Our cloud-based engine helps thousands of doctors and nurses around the country make medical decisions, so that every patient receives the highest quality and value of care based on the latest medical knowledge and data.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Aisle50
one_liner: Grocery deals.
long_description:
Aisle50 came out of the summer 2011 class at Y Combinator, the Silicon Valley accelerator.  Aisle50 builds CPG and retailer campaigns aimed to get both banner and brand incremental shoppers, bigger share and valuable brand messaging to consumers.

Our product has a two-year track record of producing baskets that are 30% larger for our retailers.  We also give our retailer partners incremental trips that, in the past, they would have lost to competitors.  Aisle50 content, because much of it is in the form of offers that are paid for through Web or Mobile, compel the consumer to head to the store sooner rather than later.  

Everybody wins: We drive trips to stores, new customers to CPGs and big discounts to consumers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer packaged goods manufacturers (who fund the discounts) and grocery retailers; shoppers redeem the offers
problem: Printed grocery coupons are wasteful and hard to target. Aisle50 let shoppers prepay for a manufacturer deal online and load it onto their store loyalty card.
business_model: Manufacturer-paid deals: the manufacturer covers the discount, Aisle50's cut and an 8 cent handling fee to the retailer
product_category: Digital grocery deals and CPG marketing
founder_names: Riley Scott; George Korsnick; Christopher Steiner
market_need_then: TechCrunch (2012) reported 26% of redeemers had not shopped at the store in over a month and 50% bought the product for the first time, evidence that manufacturers wanted trial.
outcome_analysis: Aisle50 raised $2.6M in January 2012 after launching with Lowes Foods in August 2011 and early data showing it brought lapsed and new product buyers. The YC directory lists it as acquired, but the acquirer, date and price were not confirmed by a reliable source, so the strength of the outcome is unknown.

name: Apollo
one_liner: Apollo helps engineering teams accelerate delivery
long_description: Apollo GraphQL is the leader in open source and commercial GraphQL technologies. Apollo’s open-source GraphQL client, server, and gateway are downloaded more than 17M times per month and used in production by over 30% of the Fortune 500. Customers like Walmart, Expedia, Glassdoor, Audi, and PayPal, use the Apollo Graph Platform to unify their GraphQL efforts, collaborate on graph development, and safely iterate on their graphs. Based in San Francisco, Apollo is backed by Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Matrix Partners, Trinity Ventures, Y Combinator and individual investors.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: AppHarbor
one_liner: .NET Cloud Platform as a Service
long_description:
AppHarbor is a .NET Platform-as-a-Service. Developers push code to AppHarbor using either Git or Mercurial. AppHarbor then builds the code and runs any unit tests. If everything checks out, the code is deployed to AppHarbor's scalable cloud platform.

AppHarbor lets developers spend their time coming up with ideas and developing applications, not patching servers, worrying about deployment, messing with configuration files, or scaling.

At AppHarbor, we believe that developing and deploying .NET application should be simple and fun. AppHarbor has been designed to tie in with developers day-to-day workflows. Deploying a new version to AppHarbor is as simple as checking in code when a new feature is ready.

AppHarbor will run most ASP.NET applications without modification. Moving an application to our platform requires no AppHarbor-specific code modifications nor installation of plugins or other custom software. We believe developers should be able to move applications and data to different cloud-vendors with as little friction as possible.

AppHarbor believes in giving developers access to an open ecosystem of addons and 3rd party services, not just the ones we decide to provide ourselves.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Apportable
one_liner: iOS porting
long_description: Apportable allows developers to cross-compile Objective-C apps to Android, without maintaining a separate code base in Java. It is used by many top-rated iOS games like Kingdom Rush and Osmos to deploy to Android stores using their existing Objective-C or C++ code.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mobile game and app developers with existing iOS Objective-C or C++ code who wanted Android versions
problem: Porting an iOS app to Android meant maintaining a separate Java codebase. Apportable let developers cross-compile Objective-C apps to Android.
business_model: Developer tooling (SDK and porting service), later enterprise offering Tengu
product_category: Cross-platform mobile developer tools
market_need_then: Popular iOS games such as Kingdom Rush and Osmos used it to reach Android stores, and the 2013 seed round was framed around automatically converting iOS games to Android.
outcome_analysis: Apportable solved a hard compiler problem and raised about $7.4M, including a 2013 seed from Google Ventures, but VentureBeat reported sources saying it had financial difficulties before Google quietly acqui-hired the founders and a few engineers in 2015, with most staff let go and products shut down. It fits an acquihire soft landing for a platform dependent tool.

name: Assembled
one_liner: Pivoted to TenXList, a professional network of top college engineers.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Palo Alto, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Automatic
one_liner: Automatic connects your car to the rest of your digital life.
long_description:
Our Mission: To empower drivers with knowledge about themselves and their cars so they can be safer and drive smarter. We believe you shouldn’t have to buy a new car to have a better driving experience, and that the phone in your pocket can bring the future of driving to today’s automobiles.

Who We Are: Automatic is based in San Francisco, but our team comes from every corner of the world. We obsess about creating beautiful and well-engineered products that make a real difference in people’s lives. We’re big on ideas, low on ego, and love working together.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer drivers with older cars, later fleets, insurers and dealers through partner programs
problem: Cars built since 1996 expose diagnostic data through the OBD-II port but drivers had no easy way to use it. Automatic's adapter paired with a phone app for trip logs, engine alerts and crash response.
business_model: Hardware adapter sales (Link at $69.95 in 2013), later paid Pro tier with connectivity and dealer programs
product_category: Connected car OBD-II hardware and app
market_need_then: Most cars on the road lacked connected features; the OBD-II port standard since 1996 made an aftermarket adapter feasible. Evidence of demand: retail placement in Apple stores in 2013.
outcome_analysis: Automatic launched its Link adapter in 2013, got Apple store distribution, and raised a $24M Series B in 2015 led by USAA, then sold to SiriusXM for over $100M in April 2017. SiriusXM shut the business down in May 2020 citing COVID-19; some observers doubted that cause. The real reason beyond the stated pandemic impact is not public, and unit economics of hardware is an inference not confirmed by a source.

name: Balanced
one_liner: Payments for Marketplaces
long_description:
Payments for Marketplaces.

We're obsessed with all forms of infrastructure, including communications, transportation, energy, waste management, and payments. Robust infrastructure creates a happier, more productive, and more prosperous society. You know exactly what I mean if you've traveled somewhere where you struggled to find a reliable Internet connect or even usable roads. You also know what I mean when you sit in traffic or struggle with public transportation (or lack thereof) in the US.

Balanced was created to increase the global economy (increase GDP) by enabling new commerce. Our mechanism or facility to do that is payments. Everything else we do depends on how it fits into the vision for Balanced.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Beetailer
one_liner: Facebook stores.
long_description:
Beetailer. Your online store in Facebook

Bring your store to Facebook and grow your business

Our software helps you import your existing web store onto FB. We give you tools for promoting it and detailed analytics about how well it is doing. Over a thousand stores, reaching more than 50 millions of fans, are already using our system.

https://www.beetailer.com
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Mountain View, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Caviar
one_liner: Uber for food.
long_description:
Caviar delivers the best restaurants. We partner directly with restaurants to bring food to customers across the country — whether dining for one or 100. Customers can order ahead on the web, or instantly from the Caviar app for iOS and Android.

Caviar is part of Square’s full suite of tools for businesses, enabling restaurants across the country to reach more customers, grow sales and expand reach. We deliver from the best restaurants in Boston, Brooklyn & Queens, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, Manhattan, Philadelphia & Greater Philadelphia, Portland, Sacramento, Seattle, San Francisco Bay Area (including East Bay, Peninsula, Marin & South Bay), and Washington D.C.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Urban diners and office workers ordering from premium restaurants, and restaurants that wanted delivery without their own couriers
problem: Good restaurants rarely delivered. Caviar curated restaurants, photographed dishes and ran the couriers so restaurants needed no delivery infrastructure.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on restaurant orders plus a delivery fee ($9.99 flat noted at launch)
product_category: Curated restaurant food delivery marketplace
founder_names: Jason Wang; Richard Din; Andy Zhang; Tony (Shi) Li; Shawn Tsao; Abel Lin
market_need_then: Seamless and Grubhub covered mainstream delivery but not high-end restaurants; Caviar reported 80% repeat orders and an average order of about $80 in 2014 across four cities.
outcome_analysis: Caviar launched in San Francisco in July 2012 with curated restaurants, raised a $2M seed and a $13M Series A led by Tiger Global in April 2014, and sold to Square four months later for $90M in stock. Square reportedly struggled to make it profitable and sold it to DoorDash for $410M in 2019. Success reflected a strong premium niche with 80% repeat orders against crowded general delivery.

name: Citus Data
one_liner: Real-time. Big data. PostgreSQL
long_description:
The amount of time businesses spend on their databases is altogether too much time. Citus is fixing this problem.

Citus is worry-free Postgres. Built to scale out, Citus is an extension to Postgres that is available as open source, as enterprise software that can be run on-prem or on any cloud, and as a fully-managed database as a service. Whether you have a multi-tenant application that needs to scale out, or you need performance for your real-time analytics customers, with Citus, you can focus on your app—not your database.

Founded in 2011, Citus Data is venture backed by Khosla Ventures and Data Collective. Citus is a Y Combinator alumnus and has offices in San Francisco’s SoMa district and Istanbul, Turkey.  

At Citus, we make it simple to scale out Postgres. 

Citus Data online: www.citusdata.com
Documentation: docs.citusdata.com
GitHub: github.com/citusdata/citus
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Istanbul, Istanbul, Turkey; Amsterdam, NH, Netherlands
regions: United States of America; Turkey; Netherlands; America / Canada; Middle East and North Africa; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams at SaaS and analytics companies running PostgreSQL who need to scale out, for multi-tenant apps and real-time analytics
problem: Scaling a relational database beyond one machine meant giving up transactions, joins and foreign keys or rebuilding on NoSQL.
business_model: Open source Postgres extension with paid enterprise software and a managed database service (Citus Cloud, 2016)
product_category: Distributed PostgreSQL database
founder_names: Ozgun Erdogan; Sumedh Pathak; Umur Cubukcu
competitors_at_founding: Cloudera Impala; Apache Drill; Pivotal Greenplum; Vertica, Teradata Aster, Amazon Redshift
market_need_then: By 2012 to 2013 SQL on Hadoop was crowded and fast moving, and the founders wanted scale-out SQL that kept transactions, joins and foreign keys.
outcome_analysis: Citus Data began in the Summer 2011 YC batch as scale-out SQL, launched CitusDB for Hadoop in 2013 into a crowded SQL-on-Hadoop field, then in 2016 unforked and open sourced Citus as a Postgres extension and launched a cloud service. It raised a $9.5M Series A led by Khosla in October 2015 and was acquired by Microsoft in January 2019, with terms undisclosed. The extension strategy and Postgres community goodwill explain the positive exit.

name: Clerky
one_liner: Makes legal paperwork easy for startups and their attorneys.
long_description: Clerky builds software to make legal paperwork easier for startups and their attorneys.  From formation to fundraising to hiring - everything a startup needs.  Thousands of top startups use Clerky to get legal paperwork done safely and efficiently.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startup founders incorporating and issuing stock, and the attorneys who work with them
problem: Routine startup legal paperwork (incorporation, founder stock, bylaws, board consents) consumed lawyer hours and inflated bills, and generic online services left lawyers fixing mistakes.
business_model: Per-package fees for legal paperwork software ($99 incorporation and $299 post-incorporation at 2013 launch)
product_category: Legal tech for startups
competitors_at_founding: LegalZoom and other online law sites; Traditional startup law firms
market_need_then: TechCrunch (2013) reported over 100 startups incorporated through Clerky in stealth across three YC batches; founders and lawyers wanted cheaper standardized paperwork.
outcome_analysis: Two former Orrick startup attorneys built Clerky inside YC's Summer 2011 batch, used it in stealth with YC companies, launched publicly in 2013, and reported 20,000+ startups incorporated by the 2020s. Stripe announced the acquisition in late August 2026. The founders' legal domain insight and distribution through YC explain its niche position; funding was tiny or undisclosed so it looks capital efficient.

name: Close
tags: SaaS; B2B; Sales; Sales Enablement; CRM
one_liner: CRM and sales automation suite
long_description: Modern ai-native CRM for all of your customer communication channels.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote

name: Clutch
one_liner: An easy to integrate library for native iOS applications designed to…
long_description: Clutch.io builds tools for mobile application developers. Clutch's line of tools helps developers overcome some common problems with mobile app development including A/B testing for mobile apps as well as a framework that enables developers to iterate much faster.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mobile app developers building native iOS and Android apps
problem: Shipping changes to native mobile apps meant waiting on app store review and there was no easy way to A/B test. Clutch offered native A/B testing plus a framework for faster hybrid native and HTML iteration.
business_model: Hosted developer service (A/B testing SDK), pricing not found
product_category: Mobile developer tools, A/B testing
market_need_then: App store review delays made native app iteration slow; YC and Twitter both saw value, though no customer or revenue numbers were found.
outcome_analysis: Clutch was a two person YC Summer 2011 team that launched publicly around early 2012, then was bought by Twitter in August 2012 for its IP and people. Twitter closed the hosted service on November 1, 2012 and open sourced the code, which makes it an acquihire with no continued product. Price and funding are not public.

name: Codecademy
one_liner: The leading online learning platform for technical skills.
long_description:
Working professionals are experiencing their jobs changing amidst the rise of technology and automation threatens over 800 million jobs. At the same time, software is eating the world, disrupting every major industry, and creating millions of new technology jobs that companies are eager to fill. This is the skills gap. Our mission is closing it.

In 2011, we changed the face of education by creating free interactive coding courses explored by over 45 million people. As we look to the future, we're focused on helping anyone get the skills they need for the jobs they want.  We aim to bridge the gap: between companies and the workforce, people and their dream jobs. Join one of the most dynamic technology companies in New York that is changing the way the world learns.

Headquartered in New York City, our team is filled with highly curious diverse individuals whose backgrounds span tech and education. Our team is passionate about our mission: helping people get the skills they need for the jobs they want. We seek transparency, thrive on feedback, value teamwork, love evolving and never forget it's people first. We enjoy catered lunches together, company outings, guest speakers and long walks on the beach.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Individual learners who want to learn to code, later paying subscribers and employers buying team training
problem: Learning programming meant books or courses that were passive. Codecademy let people write code in the browser from the first lesson.
business_model: Freemium consumer subscription (Pro) plus business training sales
product_category: Online coding education
market_need_then: Interest in learning to code was rising. The Code Year campaign drew 100,000 sign ups in about 48 hours in January 2012 per TechCrunch, and over 200,000 users within days according to one profile.
outcome_analysis: Codecademy rode the 2011 to 2012 wave of interest in learning to code with free interactive lessons and the viral Code Year campaign, raised a 30 million dollar Series C in 2016 and a 40 million dollar round in 2021. It sold to Skillsoft, announced in December 2021 at a headline 525 million dollars, a decent but not outsized outcome for a product that was easy to copy and had to build paid subscriptions.

name: Compose
one_liner:
We make it easy to run databases.
PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB,…
long_description: Compose is a fully-managed platform used by developers to deploy, host, and scale databases to help you conquer the data layer. www.compose.io
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; San Mateo, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies that need managed, hosted databases (originally MongoDB, later Elasticsearch, Redis, PostgreSQL, RethinkDB)
problem: Running, scaling and securing a database yourself is operational work; MongoHQ/Compose hosted and managed it for a monthly fee.
business_model: Usage/plan-based subscription for managed database hosting, also sold through PaaS add-on marketplaces (Heroku, CloudBees)
product_category: Database-as-a-service / DevOps
founder_names: Jason McCay; Ben Wyrosdick; Kurt Mackey
market_need_then: Hosted MongoDB was already being asked for in 2009 (AVC post), and by 2011 PaaS platforms (Heroku, CloudBees) integrated MongoHQ as an add-on; in 2012 the company reported being profitable with about 20% month-over-month growth for the prior year (company statement via TechCrunch).
outcome_analysis: Compose (MongoHQ) rode the growth of MongoDB and PaaS platforms, distributing through Heroku and CloudBees add-ons, reported profitability and 20% monthly growth in 2012, raised about 6.4M in total, broadened into a multi-database platform in 2014 and was acquired by IBM in July 2015 with undisclosed terms and about 3,600 customers. It is a modest but real exit; the price is not public.

name: Comprehend
one_liner: SaaS to increase speed and quality of clinical trials.
long_description: Comprehend, the leader in Clinical Intelligence solutions, is focused on accelerating treatments to patients. Our suite of software applications provide clinical operations, data management and medical review teams with the critical insights and automation they need to improve the speed, safety and quality of their clinical trials. Designed to unify, monitor and analyze clinical data across disparate sources in real-time, Comprehend's Cloud software delivers solutions for CRO oversight, centralized monitoring, risk monitoring, data review and medical monitoring. Comprehend’s investors include Sequoia Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Eminence Capital. Learn more at www.comprehend.com.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Redwood City, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharmaceutical, medical device companies and contract research organizations running clinical trials (CIOs, data management and clinical operations leaders)
problem: Clinical trial data sits in disconnected systems, so sponsors cannot see trial status, risk and data quality quickly. Comprehend layered cloud analytics and monitoring on top of existing systems.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscriptions for clinical analytics
product_category: Clinical trial data analytics software
market_need_then: In 2013 the YC blog described customers as CIOs, data management and clinical operations directors needing connected trial data; by 2017 the company reported use at five of the largest CROs and ten of the largest pharma companies.
outcome_analysis: Comprehend raised a $1.2M seed, an $8.4M Series A from Sequoia in 2013, a $21M Series B led by Lightspeed in 2014 and a $15M Series C led by Eminence in 2017, selling clinical analytics to large pharma and CROs. Saama Technologies agreed to acquire it in August 2019 with undisclosed terms. Growth was steady, but the exit size is unknown, so it is not clear whether it was a strong or soft outcome.

name: Convore
one_liner: Hosted IRC and so much more.
long_description:
Convore is an online platform that enables its users to communicate with groups in real time. Its users have the ability to join an existing group or create groups of their own.

Convore allows its users to post topics and have conversations with friends about those topics. The platform also provides its users with both public and private groups.

Convore was launched in 2011 by Eric Florenzano, Leah Culver, and Eric Maguire. It is operated from San Francisco, California.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Cryptoseal
tags: Cloud Workload Protection; DevSecOps; Next-gen Network Security
one_liner: Server key management, VPN as a Service, Privacy VPN.  Sold to…
long_description: CryptoSeal provides Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) as a service.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Mountain View, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-size businesses needing a hosted VPN without buying hardware, plus privacy-minded consumers for the Privacy VPN product
problem: Companies had to buy and run VPN hardware from vendors like Cisco and Juniper to give staff secure remote access. CryptoSeal sold VPN as a cloud service with no on-premise gear.
business_model: Subscription VPN as a service (enterprise Connect plan listed at 99 USD per month for five users) plus a consumer privacy VPN
product_category: VPN as a service, server key management, trusted computing
founder_names: Ryan Lackey; Erik Berls; Thomas Sparks
market_need_then: Businesses were moving to cloud applications and mobile work and wanted VPN access without hardware. After the 2013 Lavabit case, demand for privacy services drew attention, but the same legal risk led CryptoSeal to close its consumer product.
outcome_analysis: CryptoSeal sold hosted VPNs from 2012 and drew press when it closed its consumer Privacy VPN in October 2013 over fears of government key demands after Lavabit. The enterprise business was bought by CloudFlare in June 2014 with terms undisclosed, and the CEO joined CloudFlare, so the outcome looks like a small acquisition tied to the team and its security expertise.

name: Custora
one_liner: Custora is a predictive analytics platform for e-commerce marketing…
long_description:
Custora is an advanced segmentation platform designed to help online retailers better understand and market to their customers. We’re on a mission to remove the “mass” from marketing with software tools that focus on customers as individuals with unique needs and interests. Our software employs the state-of-the-art in customer analytics methodologies and integrates directly with marketing tools (ESPs, display, Facebook Custom Audiences, Google Customer Match) to help marketers deliver more relevant, meaningful communications. 

We’re excited to work with some of the leading retail innovators including Teleflora, Bonobos, 7 for All Mankind, and many more retailers spread throughout the world. Our offices are located in the Flatiron district of Manhattan. We work hard, work together, and care deeply about building a meaningful business, collaborative team, and exceptional culture that we’re proud to be a part of.

And yes, we're hiring. Check out https://www.custora.com/careers for details.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Online retailers and consumer brands (early customers included web apps and SaaS companies; later Teleflora, Bonobos, 7 for All Mankind)
problem: Online merchants could not tell which customers were most valuable or at risk of leaving, and lacked data teams to act on order data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for customer analytics and segmentation
product_category: Customer analytics, retention marketing, predictive segmentation
market_need_then: Ecommerce retailers had order data but few analysts; TechCrunch coverage in February 2011 framed the pain as telling lapsed buyers from lost ones and keeping customers after paying to acquire them.
outcome_analysis: Custora sold retention analytics to online retailers, raised a 2011 seed and a 6.5 million dollar Series A in 2015 led by Foundation Capital, and grew to about eleven staff on the YC page. It ended in a 2019 acquisition by Amperity with terms undisclosed, a modest exit that looks like a team and product tuck-in rather than a breakout.

name: Debteye
one_liner: Automate credit counseling.
long_description: Automate credit counseling.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers in debt who could not afford professional credit counselors
problem: Credit counseling and debt consulting were expensive. Debteye analyzed bank data via Yodlee, prioritized bills and helped fill debt management or settlement forms.
business_model: Consumer subscription planned (free at launch, monthly fee to follow)
product_category: Consumer fintech, automated credit counseling
founder_names: Paul Zhang; John Sun; Kevin Yu
market_need_then: Post 2008 consumer debt stress and expensive counselors; TechCrunch July 2011 framed it as a much cheaper credit counselor.
outcome_analysis: Debteye launched in July 2011 as a cheaper automated credit counselor built by three certified counselors, one of whom later cofounded Avant. YC lists it as Acquired, but the buyer, date and price were not found in any source. The strength of the exit is unknown, so no failure or success drivers beyond founder domain fit are asserted.

name: DrChrono
one_liner: The essential platform for modern medical practices and patients.
long_description: DrChrono develops the essential platform and services for modern medical practices to make care more informed, more interactive, and more personalized. The open platform powers telehealth, electronic health record (EHR), practice management, medical billing, and revenue cycle solutions for physicians and patients, and is fully extensible via a robust API and marketplace of applications and services. The platform is used by thousands of physicians and millions of patients, and is facilitating millions of patient appointments and is processing billions of dollars in medical billing. For more information about DrChrono, visit www.drchrono.com
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Independent physician practices that need an EHR, practice management and billing system
problem: Electronic health records were clunky desktop software. drchrono built a native iPad EHR so doctors could chart on a tablet.
business_model: SaaS subscription for EHR and practice management, plus billing and revenue cycle services
product_category: Cloud EHR and practice management
market_need_then: The HITECH Act paid physicians up to 44,000 dollars for Meaningful Use of certified EHRs, and drchrono said its iPad app was certified in mid 2011, a regulation driven demand wave.
outcome_analysis: drchrono rode the iPad launch and Meaningful Use incentives in 2011 with a tablet first EHR, raised small seed rounds from Yuri Milner and a 12 million dollar Series A in 2017, and was acquired by EverCommerce in November 2021 for roughly 182.5 million dollars. The sale price is modest relative to the capital and time, which suggests competition from larger EHR vendors capped the outcome.

name: Draft
one_liner: Making Draft. Super simple version control and collaboration for…
long_description:
Draft is a streamlined online word processor with version control.

Draft offers clean saves of drafts instead of the usual autosave jumble, clear version control between multiple users, easy importing from popular file services like Dropbox and Evernote, and something pretty unique — an editing service.

Built by one-man Y Combinator team Nathan Kontny (previously the cofounder of Inkling and Cityposh), the web app puts solo writing first. Its interface makes a point of looking nice, with the words you write appearing in large, plain-text font on a light-gray background.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Dubjoy
one_liner: Dubjoy translates and voice-overs your video to any language
long_description:
Dubjoy makes it easy for anyone to translate and voice-over any video.

Businesses that produce or host a lot of video content use Dubjoy to grow faster and go global.

People who speak at least 2 languages are able to earn some extra cash or create a job for themselves.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Earbits
one_liner: Google AdWords for music.  Allowing bands and labels to bid for…
long_description: Google AdWords for music. Allowing bands and labels to bid for airtime and have their music streamed to qualified audience.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent bands and labels paying for promotion, and music listeners who stream the free radio
problem: Independent artists had few ways to reach listeners, while internet radio was dominated by licensed major label catalogs. Earbits let artists pay for extra plays to a matched audience.
business_model: Free ad-supported artist-curated internet radio with pay-per-play promotion sold to bands and labels
product_category: Internet radio, music discovery, artist promotion marketplace
founder_names: Joey Flores; Yotam Rosenbaum; Benjamin Bryant
market_need_then: Independent artists wanted exposure and spent on promotion, and May 2011 coverage described an audience gap for artist-focused radio against crowded major label services. Spend per band was small.
outcome_analysis: Earbits built an indie focused radio with pay-per-play promotion and reported about 1.7 million dollars raised in total per Hypebot. It announced a shutdown in 2014 after running out of funding, was revived by a partner later named as You42 and was acquired by it, announced in September 2015 with terms undisclosed. The market had large streaming competitors and small per-artist budgets, so growth capital never arrived.

name: Embark
one_liner: Public transit apps. Acquired by Apple in 2013.
long_description: Embark is a mobile application designed to make it easy to get around cities using mass transit. Among other features, the iOS and Android application tells users when trains and busses are coming and will send push notifications when services are delayed. With over half a million users and rapid growth, Embark's simple and powerful mobile application is designed to bring urban transportation into the age of the smartphone. Embark is available for twelve major transportation systems in the US and the UK and is expanding rapidly. Embark won best transit and mobility app awards from the New York MTA App Quest and NYC Big Apps 3.0 contests.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Urban transit riders on iPhone and Android, monetized through advertising rather than paid by riders
problem: Riders needed accurate real-time transit directions and delay alerts per city; generic maps handled transit poorly, especially after iOS 6 dropped built-in transit directions.
business_model: Free consumer city-by-city transit apps funded by advertising
product_category: Consumer mobile app, public transit navigation
market_need_then: Smartphone riders wanted accurate transit directions. Embark's NYC app won the MTA App Quest and reported 20 million trips planned in ten months by January 2012.
outcome_analysis: Embark built polished per-city transit apps, claimed profitability from ads and 20 million trips planned within ten months by early 2012. Apple removing transit from iOS 6 sent users its way, and Apple acquired the team in August 2013 for an undisclosed price to bolster Apple Maps, after which the Android apps disappeared. A small acquisition driven by platform need and strong product design.

name: Everyme
one_liner: The #1 private social network
long_description:
Everyme is the private social network. With Everyme, you can share like you do in real life, in intimate Circles.

name: Fivestars

Fivestars is a leading payment and customer loyalty platform for small local businesses. Our mission is to help businesses and communities thrive by turning every transaction into a relationship.

Flotype licenses enterprise-grade middleware, Bridge, to customers ranging from social web and software enterprises to financial and fleet management groups.

Other offerings include NowJS, a free, open-source framework, for developers seeking real-time interactivity on Node.js and JavaScript browsers. NowCluster is available for companies seeking scalability and reliability for NowJS applications.

Established in 2010 and based in Berkeley, California, Flotype is venture-backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Ignition Partners, InterWest Partners, and Salesforce.com.

FOBO is a local marketplace for selling consumer electronics.

The app guarantees sellers will get a certain price for their devices and will be paid upfront, and ensures that their product is sold fast — within 97 minutes.

name: Freshplum

long_description: Freshplum's goal is to bring the decision-making power of data science to companies who sell goods and services electronically.

We are backed by some of the leading names in venture capital including Accel Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, Matrix Partners, NEA, SV Angel, Upfront Ventures, Webb Investment Network and Y Combinator.

name: Genius

Founded in 2009, Genius began as a platform for annotating rap lyrics. Over the years, it has expanded its mission to include more than hip-hop, and more than just lyrics. Our mission is to make a clearer world and help people find life via Glassmap!

Glassmap is backed by YCombinator and other top investors.

name: GoCardless
one_liner: We’re building the world’s bank payment network.
long_description:
At GoCardless we believe that bank payments are the best way to pay and get paid. We help businesses collect both recurring and one-off payments, without the chasing, stress or expensive fees.

We’re building a global bank payment network that lets people make and collect payments straight from their bank account, across multiple countries and currencies. 75,000+ businesses around the world trust us to power their payments. We enable them to collect payments from 30+ countries, processing over $30 billion each year.

Our suite of add-on products are helping businesses face their payment challenges head on. From automatically recovering failed payments, to challenging charge backs and fighting fraud - all without compromising their customer’s payment experience.

Our open banking leadership unlocks the ability to make and accept direct bank payments confidently and securely. And our acquisition of Nordigen means we’re also helping businesses make faster and more informed decisions by accessing and generating insights from their customers’ bank account data.

We’re also backed by some of the world’s leading investors including Accel Partners, Bain Capital Ventures, Balderton Capital, GV (formerly Google Ventures), Notion Capital, Passion Capital, Permira and Salesforce Ventures. We're a global team, with offices in London, Paris, Riga, Melbourne and New York.

business_model: Transaction fee on bank payments (early flat 1 percent capped at 2 GBP) plus add-on products
product_category: Bank payments network, direct debit and open banking
founder_names: Hiroki Takeuchi; Tom Blomfield; Matt Robinson
market_need_then: Small businesses struggled to set up direct debit with banks (TechRound profile), and a Contrary research report frames direct debit as cheaper than cards for recurring payments.
outcome_analysis: GoCardless raised steadily from a 2012 seed through a 2014 Series B, 2016 Series C, 2017 Series D and larger rounds in 2020 and 2022, reaching a reported 2.1 billion dollar valuation at the 2022 round. It grew into open banking and bank payments, and Mollie agreed in December 2025 to buy it for about 1.05 billion euros, below the 2022 valuation, so the exit is a down exit relative to the peak even though the company reached about 900 staff.

name: HackerRank

name: Imgix
one_liner: The platform for your visual media.
long_description:
Nobody should have to employ expensive imaging scientists and engineers for their business to get the most out of their visual media. This is where imgix has your back. imgix is a platform for managing, processing, rendering, optimizing, and delivering your existing visual assets so that you can meet the demands of your business and your team can stay focused on what they do best.

The business demands on web visual media can blindside even the most hyper-aware content teams and developers. Just to be competitive on the Internet, you need your images to be sized perfectly to every device, served in one of any of a half dozen web formats, optimized to the absolute best perceptual quality while maintaining pinpoint performance, and distributed to wherever your users are, anywhere in the world. And that is just the baseline. Next-level imaging concerns like copyright, licensing, accessibility, moderation, illegal or explicit content, "fake news", and more, can threaten your business at any moment if not handled properly. Get any of these things wrong and you are shedding revenue, ceding ground to competitors, and potentially exposing your business to extreme liability.

By working with imgix's powerful APIs, SDKs, user interfaces, and integrations, you can rest assured that any demands on your images and videos will always be met, now and into the future, without you having to invest in building it yourself or patching together a mishmash of open source and third-party technologies. Our platform is designed to ensure that your images are always working for your business and never against it.

imgix was launched through the famed Y Combinator accelerator program. Its customers include Google, Lyft, Kickstarter, AirBnb, Coursera, Bonobos, Spotify, Vimeo, Bustle, and many others.

outcome_analysis: imgix grew from a YC Summer 2011 company into a long lived infrastructure vendor that reports over 60,000 customers and 8 billion images served daily, after a seed from YC and SV Angel and a 2014 Series A led by RRE. name: Launchpad Toys
one_liner: Creativity at Play.  Tablet toys.   Acquired by Google, 2015.
long_description:
We're creating digital toys and tools that empower kids to create, learn & share their ideas through play.

Give a young child a couple of toys or a box of crayons and he or she is likely to play for hours, deeply engrossed in an imaginary world. In both art and dramatic play, children construct settings, create fictional characters, and act out fantastic storylines that would be the envy of many Hollywood scriptwriters. Yet, ask that same child to write out a story in a blank notebook or a word processor and you would be lucky to capture a fraction of the depth and splendor of his or her imagination. Play inspires and scaffolds the creative process from an early age, but there is a persistent gap between the origins of imaginative play (ages 4-5) and kids' adoption of the formal discipline of creative writing (ages 8-10).

At Launchpad Toys, we're using mobile devices like the iPad to bridge this gap between informal and formal learning, to harness the power of play to help children capture and share their ideas with other kids around the world. Our first product, Toontastic an app for the iPad, is a creative learning tool that blends constructionist and social development theories to empower young children to create, learn, and share their ideas through play.

outcome_analysis: Launchpad Toys built Toontastic, a children's animated storytelling iPad app released in January 2011, on well under 1.2 million dollars of reported funding. name: Scuba

name: Semantics3

name: Senic
one_liner: Simple Controls for Sonos, Philips Hue and other Smart Home products
long_description:
Our mission is to empower every family member and business to set the right ambience of sound and light for every moment. 

Our company offers simple wireless switches and remotes for products like Sonos or Philips Hue, software and simplify the installation of Smart Home systems and add-on solutions to create a great smart home experience for consumers, prosumers and professionals.

target_customer: Consumers and prosumers with Philips Hue or Sonos systems who want physical controls, plus installers and switch makers

business_model: Hardware product sales (switches, Nuimo controller) direct and through retailers, with a co-branded switch built with Gira
product_category: Smart home physical controllers
founder_names: Tobias Eichenwald; Lech Alexander Murawski; Johannes Berdin; Kai-Dominik Kuhn; Andreas Mohr
market_need_then: In 2013 smart home gear was growing but controlled by apps. The founders pitched simple physical control as the missing piece; no dated demand figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Senic found a durable niche in design led smart home controls and survived more than a decade, raising small seed rounds in 2016 and 2018 including from Gira, the German switch maker that later co-designed its Hue switches. The YC page lists the company as acquired by Gira, but its own site and search results show an independent brand and a partnership, so the exit is unclear. The outcome looks like a modest capital light hardware business rather than a venture scale win.

name: SimpleLegal
one_liner: Legal Operations for corporate legal teams.
long_description: Legal spend, matter, accrual and IP management software for in-house counsel.

name: SimplyInsured
one_liner: We sell health insurance to small businesses 100% online.
long_description:
SimplyInsured was founded with one mission: to eliminate fear from health insurance. By changing the way small business owners purchase health insurance with our 100% online platform, we’re transforming a $20 billion dollar industry and delighting thousands of customers. 

Our unique values-based culture (and extremely talented team) is our core competitive advantage, and each person on our team makes a direct, immediate impact on our business. 

We value transparency, feedback, bias to action, growth, and an obligation to dissent. Every opinion is respected, we hold each other to extremely high standards, we’re driven by the diversity in our backgrounds, and unified by 100% alignment on our mission. 

What’s best for the customer is the heart of everything we do, and our customer stories prove it: by changing health insurance we’re literally saving lives. 

Based in San Francisco, SimplyInsured was founded in 2012 and is back by Bessemer Venture Partners, Polaris Ventures, and Y-Combinator. If you’re up for the challenge of improving health insurance for millions of Americans, we’re just getting started, and we’re growing!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small businesses buying group health insurance, and the payroll platforms that embed it

business_model: Online broker: commissions from carriers on plans sold, plus embedded partnerships with payroll platforms
product_category: Small business health insurance marketplace and administration platform
market_need_then: Affordable Care Act exchanges (SHOP) and 2013-2014 reforms pushed small businesses to re-shop coverage; the launch post cites confusing plans and hidden costs. TechCrunch (2015) reported over $1M monthly sales through carriers including Kaiser and Anthem.
outcome_analysis: SimplyInsured launched from YC W13 as a plain-English health insurance quote tool, reached over $1M monthly insurance sales by 2015, and raised a $1.75M seed in April and a $5.9M Series A led by Polaris in June 2015. No later round, acquisition or shutdown was found; the site is live in 2026 under the operating entity Ten 250 Corporation with blog posts last in 2021, which suggests a small surviving business rather than a venture outcome.

Its technology was later bought by iFood, so the directory label Acquired reflects an asset sale, not a company exit.

Standard Treasury partner banks saw material top-line growth through the decreased cost of servicing their customers, decreased churn, and increased transaction volumes, while delivering tremendous value to their customers by allowing them to radically automate their treasury management and accounting processes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Banks that wanted to offer developer APIs to their corporate clients

name: StatusPage

name: Swapbox
one_liner: Stop missing deliveries. Ship to Swapbox and pick up at our kiosks.
long_description:

Take anything that you want to ship to your local Swapbox, no planning ahead necessary. Enter a few details about where your item is being shipped and how fast you want it there. We have developed a windshield protection film product line called ExoShield to help vehicle owners protect their windshields. Our ExoShield GT3 film is sold through 400+ aftermarket installers and car dealerships in 56 countries that carry and install it for vehicle owners. For Jeep Wrangler and Ford Bronco owners (google: broken windshield club), our ExoShield ULTRA DIY kits are available via our website and dropshipping partners. 

Defense - Over the last 3 years, we have been working with the Canadian Armed Forces to develop an infrared camouflage technology. We have received two contracts from CAF to develop our technology. Our solution has the ability to be integrated into the uniform directly (adding just 5-10g of weight vs. 600-18,000 kg of weight for other alternatives), has outperformed all existing NATO alternatives in multiple CAF field trials, and is receiving support from major elements of CAF for our next contract. This technology can also be adapted for other individual camouflage integrations (face paint and individual nettings) and for mobile camouflage applications (vehicle nettings and vehicle paints).

Traveling? Earn some extra cash.
Let backpack help you save that high shipping cost or earn a little extra.

Backpack is a peer-to-peer platform that connects travelers and shoppers to give people access to products across markets in all continents. 
Each backpacker, regardless of their role as a carrier or a shopper, follows a simple four-step process to either earn or save money from their backpacking experience.
Travelers share their travel information and specify what kind of items they want to carry. Then they wait to get a "backpack request" and ask their price. Finally, they confirm the deal, buy the items, deliver them and earn money. Shoppers on the other hand, search items from their favorite websites and fill out the item description. Then they give their location and find a traveler coming to their city. Finally they "request backpack" and confirm the deal. Within days they can get the product and save money.  

backpack is founded with a vision to provide every citizen of the world with a choice; the choice of buying organic, authentic, and cost effective products with minimum friction.
Whether the product is state-of-the-art consumer electronics, exotic pashmina from the south-east, or even medication that are rare in some parts of the world and not so rare in others - we promise ourselves to get those products to your doorsteps. We would like to reject the counterfeits, we would like to reject the almost-originals, most importantly, we would like to not pay the heavy expense incurred, most of which we deem to be superfluous. Help us make a better, more original globalized world.

Everyone can benefit from an objective perspective during difficult times, but the current model for supportive services is broken due to insurance gridlock, a clunky referral system, long wait times and unsustainable costs. Our web-based approach offers valuable guidance through accessible and anonymous means. Users log in to secure accounts and speak with licensed professionals on a variety of topics—relationship conflict, job stress, etc.—from anywhere at any time. With our proprietary technology, we have removed every barrier to entry and created an outlet for millions who wouldn’t have sought emotional health services otherwise, reducing stress for an increasingly stressed-out generation. This is the future of mental health. 

The shift in moving counseling services online is inevitable and our product is already in demand: After a successful pilot with Pretty Padded Room, an online therapy website specifically targeted towards millennial women, we are excited to relaunch as In Your Corner, an aspirational brand that provides the very best in counseling, coaching, and calm. In Your Corner improves on our original offering by being more gender-inclusive and convenient. In addition to developing a mobile app to provide one-tap, on-demand support in real time, users also have access not only to licensed mental health counselors, but also coaches in personal and professional development as well as instructors of meditation and breath work.

We're Lawn Love, a new type of lawn care service. We’re building a software layer on top of the very large and largely low-tech lawn care market. We solve two core problems:
 
For consumers: Lawn Love is a modern, seamless lawn care experience. Gone are the days of physical, in-person estimates, payments left under the doormat, and spotty service. We use a combination of high-resolution satellite imagery, public and private data sets, and human review to generate a personalized quote for your yard – all in under two minutes and without ever setting foot on your property.
 
From there, you are paired with a skilled lawn pro who will show up and complete the work. You can coordinate everything from your smartphone or web browser, and the entire experience is streamlined and delightful.
 
For lawn pros: We start by bringing a pipeline of new customers straight to your door. No more spending hours hanging door hangers or dealing with snake-oil SEO salespeople. Just pick up whatever jobs you want, fill out your schedule, and you’re good to go. We also handle all the customer service, accounting, and collections; freeing you up to spend less time on the back-office work and more time in the field earning money. And that’s just the start: Our advanced job clustering and routing algorithms help build you much denser routes, allowing you to do up to twice as many jobs per day while slashing your fuel expenses and idle time.
 
In short, we’re democratizing software that was previously only available to large companies in the space, and giving small business owners tools to operate more efficiently and better compete with the big guys.

name: Oklo
one_liner: Emission free, always on power from advanced fission power plants.
long_description:
About Oklo Inc.: 

Oklo Inc. (Oklo) is developing advanced fission power plants to provide emission-free, reliable, and affordable energy. 

Oklo received a Site Use Permit from the U.S Department of Energy, has performed successful prototypic fuel fabrication, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, developed the first advanced fission combined license application accepted and docketed by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and is developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and national laboratories.

Oklo has been featured in Time, Newsweek, Wall Street Journal, CNBC, Popular Mechanics, Wired, Architectural Digest, Hyperallergic, POWER Magazine, has been the subject of a Harvard Business School case, and is featured in the Oliver Stone documentary Nuclear, among other features.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Sunnyvale, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Data centers, industrial users and government sites buying long-term power, plus fuel and isotope buyers
problem: Reliable emission free power from nuclear was slow and costly to build; Oklo aims to deliver small fast fission plants and sell power under long-term agreements.
business_model: Own and operate reactors selling power under long-term agreements, plus fuel recycling and isotope sales
product_category: Advanced fission power plants
market_need_then: In 2014 clean firm power was wanted by climate focused investors, and small reactors were a funded concept; sources at the time on Oklo specifically were not found.
outcome_analysis: Oklo raised from Sam Altman linked investors and DCVC, reported as the first venture led Series A for a nuclear hardware company in 2018, then went public by merging with AltC in May 2024 with about 306 million dollars gross proceeds, below the 500 million marketed. The NRC rejected its first application in 2022 for insufficient information, but it returned in 2025 and began construction in Idaho, with AI power demand lifting its shares.

name: One Codex
one_liner: Data platform for metagenomics and the microbiome.
long_description: One Codex is a data platform for applied microbial genomics, enabling new and valuable applications in clinical diagnostics, food safety, and biosecurity. Acquired by Invitae (NVTA) in February 2021. Spun out as an independent company in September 2022.
all_locations: Boston, MA, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Researchers, clinical labs, public health agencies, and biotech and food safety teams doing microbial sequencing
problem: Identifying microbes in sequencing data was slow and clunky. One Codex built a fast search of a large microbial reference database that identifies genomic datasets in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS data platform plus sequencing services
product_category: Metagenomics and microbial genomics software
market_need_then: Sequencing costs were falling and researchers, clinicians and public health officials had sequenced over 100,000 genomes by 2014, but analysis tools were slow and hard to use per the YC blog.
outcome_analysis: One Codex built a fast microbial genomics data platform from a YC Summer 2014 start and was acquired by the diagnostics company Invitae in February 2021. Invitae sold its equity back for an immaterial amount in September 2022 in an employee buyout, so the company continues independently in biosecurity, food safety and microbiome work. The acquisition price is not reliably public, and funding beyond YC could not be verified.

name: One Degree
one_liner: One Degree is a nonprofit organization that makes it easy for…
long_description:
One Degree is a technology driven nonprofit organization that helps individuals and families access the resources they need to improve their lives and achieve social and economic mobility. 

One Degree's mission is to empower people to create a path out of poverty for themselves and for their communities. Our core product is a web and mobile platform makes it easy for low-income families to find, manage, and review nonprofit and government services. 

Our platform has become the go-to tool for help-seekers – and the people who support them, such as case managers and social workers – throughout the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles County in California, and in Gainesville, Florida.

We currently operate three major products: the One Degree website and Android and iOS apps. Thousands of people in the Bay Area and Los Angeles rely on One Degree’s website and apps to access health care, food banks, employment services, and much more. We also support communities around the country to start their own One Degree chapters.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: OpenCurriculum
one_liner: Helping K-12 teachers and school administrators build awesome…
long_description:
A library of community curated teaching and learning materials, free to the entire world. Come collaborate; we can teach better together.

OpenCurriculum, Inc. is a California based technology nonprofit organization with a mission to bring openness and innovation to K12 education around the world
all_locations: Sacramento, CA, USA; Mountain View, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: K-12 teachers (free) and later schools and districts (paid plans per company site); a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
problem: Teachers duplicated lesson-planning work and lacked free, shareable, standards-aligned materials, especially locally relevant content.
business_model: Nonprofit; free library and tools, paid school plan around $5 per user per month and network plans per the company site; early funding from grants and accelerators
product_category: Open educational resources / lesson planning (edtech nonprofit)
competitors_at_founding: Share My Lesson; BetterLesson; Teachers Pay Teachers
market_need_then: The Common Core rollout (2013-2014) created demand for aligned materials; the 2014 launch reported about 6,000 monthly users, and a beta with about 20 teachers claimed 50% saving on first-time planning time (company-sourced).

Its competitors Share My Lesson, BetterLesson and Teachers Pay Teachers were already established and it has no documented grant totals, user growth or exit afterwards; it is still listed as active with a paid school plan, so it survived as a small nonprofit without evidence of scale, and the outcome is best described as stalled or niche rather than failed.

name: Owners Circle
one_liner: Kickstarter for local businesses
long_description:
OwnersCircle provides small business owners with the online tools and financial information that they need in order to navigate the complex world of business financing.

The reality is that there is no easy way to search for small business financial products, which creates a headache for already time-strapped business owners. Recent reports show that owners spend an enormous amount of time (25 hrs on average) searching and applying for loan products, with many focusing on lenders that have high rejection rates and long, complex processes.

There's a better way! There are a growing number of banks and alternative lenders that want to work with small businesses and are willing to compete for their business. Our platform provides owners with the information they need in order to identify, compare, and apply for financial products that can help take their business to the next level.


Why Use OwnersCircle?

1. Get access to free, online tools to identify financial institutions that actively lend to growing small businesses
2. Shop and compare a variety of lenders and their loan products 
3. Use one platform to complete your financing search versus spending countless days researching and completing lender applications only to find out you're not a fit
4. Free access to our team of funding consultants to answer any questions you may have throughout the process


What Types of Business Financial Products does OwnersCircle Include?

- Lender Types: Local Banks and Alternative Lenders
- Product Types: SBA Term Loans, Bank Term Loans, Alternative Term Loans, Asset-based Loans and more


Why Would I Need Business Financing?

New location or remodel current space
Purchase inventory
Purchase equipment
Hire additional employees
Manage cash flow
Refinance/consolidate current debt
Marketing and advertising

long_description:
Paid is an API for invoicing.  Paid helps company manage their accounts receiving with a seamless integration into any tech stack.  We help you track expenses, generate & issue invoices, remind customers of outstanding payments and reconcile your accounts—all with about 30 minutes development time.

API - Automate Everything
Paid allows you to automate every step of your accounts receivable.  In a few lines of code you can create invoices, issue them, and accept payments.  Paid makes the invoicing/billing process fully automatic, freeing up time to focus on core business responsibilities.

Customize Everything
Your company, your way of doing things.  Paid is fully customizable from branding, billing terms, payment methods and more.  Paid can be adapted to any business model.

Track Everything
How much revenue is currently outstanding? How much is overdue? Who has already paid and does so on a regular basis? Everything you and your Finance Department need can be seen on our dashboard and exported for Accounting.

Grow With Paid
Whether it’s 10 or 10,000,000 invoices, Paid has a solution that will enable you to scale without the normal growing pains.

name: Payable
one_liner: Simple payments and tax compliance for your contract workforce.
long_description:
Payable is the easiest way to manage your external workforce. By simplifying and automating onboarding, payments, and 1099 compliance, Payable consolidates disparate and manual processes, while getting contractors paid faster! 

Payable is backed by Freestyle Capital, Redpoint Ventures, General Catalyst, Moment Ventures, Y Combinator, and others.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Businesses and marketplaces that pay independent contractors, especially on-demand companies using Stripe Connect
problem: Companies managing contractors had manual onboarding, payments and 1099 tax filing. Payable automated these, and 1099 reporting became its most valued feature.
business_model: B2B SaaS priced per contractor per month, reported as 8 dollars in 2015
product_category: Contractor payments and 1099 compliance
founder_names: Tad Milbourn; Kyle Kilat; Peter Terrill
market_need_then: On-demand marketplaces such as Lyft and DoorDash had to file 1099s for many contractors. The Stripe partnership brought more users in early 2016 than the previous two years combined per Payable's co-founder.
outcome_analysis: Payable began as the time tracking app Tiempo in YC Summer 2014 and turned into a contractor payments and 1099 tool. It raised about 2.1 million dollars in 2015 and found distribution through a Stripe Connect partnership that fed on-demand marketplaces like Lyft and DoorDash. Stripe bought it on July 26, 2017 to bring 1099 reporting in-house, a classic platform acquisition of a niche feature vendor. The price was not disclosed.

name: Permutive
one_liner: Rebuilding data in advertising to protect privacy

We're rebuilding data infrastructure in advertising to work with cohorts—privacy safe descriptions of users—which enable advertising use cases without the need for sharing personal identifiers. We do this by moving data processing and management out of the cloud, and on to the user's device.

name: PipelineDB
one_liner: Open-source time-series data analytics extension for PostgreSQL
long_description: PipelineDB is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that enables realtime reporting use cases by continuously aggregating large streams of time series data down into summary data. It shines the most at larger scales, where storing lots of raw time-series data and aggregating it over and over again becomes inefficient. The amount of value that PipelineDB adds is directly proportional to the amount of continuous aggregation that an analytics use case can benefit from. PipelineDB should be used for analytics use cases that only require summary data, like realtime reporting dashboards. PipelineDB is not a good fit for exploratory analytics on siloed datasets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams building real-time analytics and dashboards on streaming time-series data, using PostgreSQL
problem: Storing raw streams and re-aggregating them repeatedly is slow and costly. PipelineDB lets teams define continuous SQL views that aggregate streams on the fly and store only the summaries.
business_model: Open source PostgreSQL extension with a planned commercial enterprise version
product_category: Streaming SQL database
market_need_then: Real-time reporting such as live A/B test results was a stated use case; TechCrunch in July 2015 positioned the SQL interface as the advantage over streaming tools needing special programming languages.
outcome_analysis: PipelineDB built a streaming SQL extension for PostgreSQL out of YC Winter 2014, released it as open source in July 2015 and raised a seed from SV Angel, Data Collective and others. Its team joined Confluent on May 1, 2019 to bring continuous views to Kafka, and the open source project stopped getting new releases. The announcement said the team joined and did not describe the product's future, so this reads as an acquihire; the deal terms are not public.

Community members can submit, browse, vote and comment on daily submissions of products and collections of products. They also get the opportunity to interact directly with product creators, investors, journalists, as well as, an active community of people who are passionate about products.

name: Protocol Labs
one_liner: Protocol Labs makes internet protocols: IPFS, Filecoin, and more.
long_description:
Protocol Labs is an open-source research, development, and deployment laboratory. Our projects include IPFS, Filecoin, libp2p, and many more. We aim to make human existence orders of magnitude better through technology.

Some of our projects.

IPFS makes the web work peer-to-peer. IPFS is a protocol for storing, addressing, and transferring data, designed to replace HTTP in many contexts. IPFS uses content-addressing to uniquely identify and link to information. IPFS is one of the leading protocols of Web3, crypto, and the decentralized web movements. IPFS serves millions of end users and tens of thousands of developers. It powers the websites and applications of small startups, large enterprises, and even blockchains.

Filecoin is a decentralized storage network, designed to store humanity's most important information. Filecoin is a cryptocurrency incentivized decentralized market, where storage providers earn filecoin tokens for renting out storage space. (Think airbnb for cloud storage). Filecoin is one of the leading projects in the cryptocurrency/blockchain space.

name: Rigetti Computing

We are scientists, engineers, builders, and visionaries. We believe quantum computing is going to significantly affect health care, how we treat disease, how we generate energy, and how we feed humanity. Rigetti is the only company deploying full-stack solutions for hybrid classical/quantum computing. Our 19-qubit quantum computer is available online through our Forest platform, and the first commercially useful applications are already under exploration.

With sequencing and synthesis being mainstream now [1], 20n provides the computational systems that predict DNA design for novel industrial biotech and health applications.

At 20n, we are taking a fresh look at turning biological data into information. We approach it as a big data learning problem, and bring to bear techniques from machine learning, distributed systems, AI planning, program synthesis, data mining, and natural language processing. With the support of DARPA [2], we are building a team of computer scientists, and bioengineers to look at biology in fundamentally new ways.

Our current customers include industrial biotech firms that are leading the charge in transitioning us from traditional unsustainable means of manufacturing to sustainable biological processes leading to advanced fuels, materials, therapeutics, and flavors and fragrances. 20n’s technology helps them enter markets previously thought inaccessible for biology.

[1] Sequencing DNA costs $4k/genome (http://www.genome.gov/sequencingcosts/) and is expected to go down to $1k/genome. Synthesizing DNA is at 20cents/bp, and is expected to go down to 0.1cents/bp.
[2] DARPA in the past supported work that led to the internet, stealth planes, GPS, and even Douglas Engelbart’s mother-of-all-demos.

After a number of recent key milestones, the team is taking the technology more broadly to 50% of cancers diagnosed in the US.

name: Razorpay
tags: Banking as a Service; Fintech; Payments; India
one_liner: India's only full-stack financial solutions company for businesses.
long_description:
The journey of building Razorpay started in 2014, when Harshil Mathur (CEO & Co-Founder) and Shashank Kumar (MD & Co-Founder) witnessed the dismal state of the online payments industry in India then and understood that they have a larger and more important issue to solve. And That was democratizing online payments for Indian businesses, particularly the underserved market, Startups and SMEs. Over the last 9 years, Razorpay has evolved from a single-product company to a multi-product company, from an online payment gateway to India’s only full-stack financial solutions company, offering payments and banking solutions to businesses.  Razorpay today is transforming age-old complexities and changing every known paradigm of money movement for disruptive businesses.

Over the last couple of years, Razorpay’s growth has evolved to be an index of India’s digital economy. From a kirana shop in Kashmir collecting payments on our POS device to a textile exporter in Kanyakumari accepting dollars through our International Payments product, Razorpay has revolutionised how businesses have traditionally transacted and interacted with money. 

Razorpay became the first and only Indian fintech to build a full-stack international Payment Gateway ‘Curlec by Razorpay’ and evolved into a comprehensive provider of payment solutions, leveraging the synergy between cutting-edge technological capabilities and a profound understanding of the local payment ecosystem. The introduction of the new Curlec Payment Gateway aims to cater to a wide spectrum of businesses, expanding its reach to over 5,000 establishments. 

Be it for international expansion or solving for Indian businesses, for Razorpay, the customer has always been at the core of all disruption, from addressing evolving needs to delivering new solutions. This hyperfocus helped bring Razorpay’s several industry-first innovations into the market since 2014. Razorpay became the first to launch a completely digital on-boarding process for startups, first to launch support for UPI, first to launch support for Bharath QR, first to introduce recurring payments for businesses through Razorpay Route, automating payment receipts and later automate payouts and making the entire process seamless and optimized and many more were introduced aling the way. Other firsts include: - First to launch India’s Multi-Network Tokenisation solution, TokenHQ - Razorpay became India’s first payment gateway to support credit cards on UPI - Razorpay also became India’s largest omnichannel payment gateway for businesses post acquiring Ezetap which is India’s leading offline POS company that was founded with the aim to simplify the in-person offline payments experience.

Over the years, Razorpay’s valuation has jumped from $1 billion to $7.5 billion and has added a host of marquee investors to its captable. Razorpay is also the second Indian company to be a part of Silicon Valley’s largest tech accelerator, Y Combinator. Marquee investors such as Lone Pine Capital, Alkeon Capital, TCV, GIC, Tiger Global, Sequoia Capital India, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, Salesforce Ventures, Y Combinator, and MasterCard have invested a total of $741.5 Mn through Series A, B, C, D, E and F funding. The last financing round of Series F led the company’s valuation to $7.5 Billion signaling one of the fastest increases in valuation for an Indian Unicorn. 

Razorpay has also made acquisitions with like-minded companies over the last 9 years. In total, till date, Razorpay has made eight acquisitions, Billme in 2023 - A Digital invoice and customer Engagement, Ezetap in 2022 - India’s leading offline POS company, PoshVine in 2022 - India’s leading loyalty and reward management platform, IZealiant in 2022 - A mobile-first, API-enabled, and cloud-ready payment solution and made its first international foray in South-East Asia by announcing its acquisition of Curlec in 2022 - A recurring payments platform. TeraFin Labs in 2021 - the AI-based SaaS platform that facilitates digital financing solutions, Opfin (Now RazorpayX Payroll) in 2019 -  The payroll management solution and Thirdwatch in 2019, the first acquisition - The AI-powered fraud detection platform.

All these efforts are being done in collaboration with banks, regulators, and stakeholders so that India can build a better place for small and big businesses. Today, Razorpay powers online payments for 76 Of 100 startup unicorns and millions of businesses in India. The core premise of what Razorpay was founded in 2014 and what it is today hasn’t changed. It is to make money movement simpler and easier, whether it is for businesses to receive money, send money, or manage money.

outcome_analysis: Razorpay won by making online payments easy for Indian startups with developer friendly products, then expanded into banking, payroll, lending and acquisitions. It raised from Tiger Global, Sequoia, GIC and others, reaching a $7.5B valuation in December 2021, and moved its domicile back to India in 2025 with an IPO approved by SEBI. Growth rode UPI and digital payment adoption while competition from other gateways stayed intense.

one_liner: Quantitative Investment in Art Assets
long_description:
Arthena is a financial product that gives you access to the alternative asset class with the highest barrier to entry and strongest historical returns. We invest in the most liquid segment of the art market, with the lowest volatility, yielding tremendous growth uncorrelated to traditional investments. Arthena’s automated and data driven investment strategy regulates art investment by building traditional fund structures. HNWI’s can now securely and confidently diversify their portfolios into alternative assets focusing on the luxury market.

Arthena has designed and built a statistically rigorous model that estimates the value of artwork over time. Since the data we obtain derives from auction records and repeat sales, our model relies on a set of features about each result. These features include include the artist’s name, medium, date of creation, origin of location and size of work. After identifying groups of work that are similar to each other, we calculate the expected ROI and estimated volatility based on the distribution of gains. Using historical auction results to simulate the performance of our funds, we leverage Monte Carlo analysis to determine annualized returns and sharpe ratios. Based on this analysis, Arthena can validate the financial viability of our product and establish statistically rigorous bounds for these estimates.

We’re on a mission to optimize the agricultural industry.

These low-fidelity forecasting methods weren’t giving them a clear enough understanding of their production until it was too late, leading to waste and inefficiency throughout the supply chain.

We saw a problem we wanted to solve.

Today, Bountiful is using advanced data science to help farmers forecast more accurately, so they can make better decisions. In the last three years, we’ve combined the latest in machine learning with weather, satellite, geographic, and historical data. The result is a user-friendly platform that transforms volumes of complex agricultural information into simple, actionable insights farmers can use to run more economically and environmentally sustainable farms.

More recently, we’re working to open the dialogue between buyers and sellers, remove uncertainty, and provide clarity to the supply chain to meet global food demand.

Our ultimate goal is to close the agricultural margin of error. Not only will this make individual farms more efficient, profitable, and sustainable, but it will help optimize the global food supply chain. That means healthier people and a healthier planet.
