name: Well Principled
one_liner: The neural engine for autonomous robots
long_description:
We aren’t building AI to replace "knowledge work” that requires neither, but to bolster the working human intellect which has never failed to discover new paths to prosperity.

For all their success, mainstream approaches to AI have fundamental limitations preventing them from solving critical classes of problems. We are building a new AI architecture from first principles to break from these limitations.

The status quo has ossified around the supervised, brute-force pretraining paradigm. These systems do not, and cannot, handle the essential skills of continual learning, goal discovery, novel planning, and the creation of new knowledge.

These limitations are not trivial. Our national prosperity depends directly on overcoming these limitations, because the essential skills underlie the skilled trades. From electricians to machinists to nurses, apprentice tradespeople in all of these fields learn “skilled improvisation” where every solution is novel, and even the goal must be discovered. Prosperity demands the precise capabilities where status quo AI is structurally weak.

Worse, these limitations will not be overcome with more compute or training data. They are inescapable consequences of the underlying technologies of supervised learning, neural networks, transformers, backprop, and gradient descent. Progress requires independence from them.

We are building a new AI architecture by reverse-engineering the system that got us this far: the human brain. By triangulating between neuroscience, cognitive science, and the evolutionary elaboration of brains, we have identified the brain’s algorithms to (a) continually learn a causal world model (b) select goals to both achieve and learn to achieve more (c) plan to reach novel goals, and (d) creatively produce new knowledge.


Join us in building intelligence with ingenuity to bolster the skilled trades.

Our strategy exists at the intersection of two strong theses:
1. The AI doctor that wins will get to escape velocity using GLP-1s, the fastest growing consumer product in history.
2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.
Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026: Since April 2025 we've grown from 3k to 200k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.
Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.
Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2030: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.
Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.

We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

product_category: AI enabled consumer telehealth and online pharmacy

+ High throughput experimental measurement uniquely leverages AI/ML:  We’ve engineered cells to measure antibodies for pharmacological activity, not just structure or binding like others, 100 million at a time, 100X+ the throughput of others. With our large, proprietary activity datasets, we uniquely leverage ML to both unlock the discovery of rare hits and generate optimized hits for challenging targets, starting with G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)

+ Pharma traction: We’ve secured 3 partnerships with $3M in revenue and $125M in downstream value.

product_category: Antibody agonist discovery for GPCRs
market_need_then: Antibodies that activate GPCRs were an unmet need for difficult targets, and obesity drugs became a large market. NIH SBIR grants in 2021 and 2022 funded programs for inflammatory bowel disease and endometriosis pain.
outcome_analysis: Abalone Bio is a preclinical biotech that has won grants and pharma partners. It signed a research collaboration with Pfizer in January 2026, with Sihuan Pharmaceutical on an obesity drug in October 2025 and with the University of Pennsylvania in March 2025 per press listings. name: Altay Therapeutics

Altay develops small molecule drugs to treat chronic liver diseases like liver fibrosis and liver cancer.  Our co-founder Dr. Osman Ozes, led the first drug development program for Esbriet (Pirfenidone), resulting in the first FDA approved therapy for lung fibrosis. Esbriet is now a $1 billion/year drug and has already made over $6 billion in revenue. 

With a team that has over 70+ years of small molecule drug development experience, we intend to do the same with chronic liver diseases, which affects over 20 million Americans and represents a market size of over $30 billion. 

We know we are well positioned for success because we have shown excellent pre-clinical mouse data in several liver fibrosis models using our novel small molecule. We demonstrate a reduction in fibrosis with our drug, but more significantly, we show a reversal in fibrotic tissue back to normal tissue. 

With our current developmental strategy, we hope to have a clinic-ready compound by the end of 2021 and be in phase I clinical trials by mid of 2022.

name: Altro
one_liner: Build Credit With Your Subscriptions
long_description:
Altro (altro.io) is a platform that enables members to build credit no matter who they are, where they are from, or their history of credit access/score. We serve the 68M people in the US (mainly Women and POC) who are denied credit due to historical bias and the lack of access that current banks provide to credit building and tools. (It wasn't until The Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the 1970's that Women and "Minorities" could even get fair access to credit)!


Altro has created a mobile that allows anyone to have access to credit, using their subscriptions as a means to start building their credit score. Altro lends to members a $75 Line of Credit to pay for their subscriptions, such as Netflix, Hulu, HelloFresh, etc. This card is built to solely work on the subscriptions that the member is already paying for, allowing them to securely use their $75 credit to build their credit using things they are already paying for.

Doing this empowers folx who were denied credit a way to start building their score and financial power. Altro will service millions of people in not only building their credit, but also gaining access to the tools (such as personal loans, emergency funds, car/house loans and more) that they could not access prior.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: US consumers with thin or no credit files, mainly younger and underserved people, paying a membership fee
problem: People with no credit history cannot get credit and so cannot build a score. Altro lent a small line of credit usable only on subscriptions and reported payments to the credit bureaus; earlier it reported rent.
business_model: Consumer subscription membership with a restricted credit line and bureau reporting
product_category: Credit building fintech
market_need_then: Tens of millions of Americans lacked usable credit files, and the company cited 68 million people denied credit; credit-builder apps were gaining users in 2020.
outcome_analysis: Altro, previously Perch, joined YC in Summer 2020, raised about $22M in total including an $18M round in 2022 and a $4M strategic round in 2024, and expanded to 47 states with a credit builder card. Its site later announced it had been acquired after about seven years; the buyer, date and terms are not public in sources found, so the outcome quality is unknown.

name: Alude
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: We offer free software that automates bureaucracy for real-estate…
regions: Brazil; Latin America
target_customer: Brazilian real estate agencies and brokers, with revenue from service providers such as insurers that agencies route renters to
problem: Renting a property in Brazil involves paperwork: background checks, document collection, signatures and insurance. Alude automates this for agencies for free.
business_model: Free software for brokers; revenue from financial and home products sold to renters and owners (insurance and similar)
product_category: Proptech, rental workflow software
founder_names: Jota Junior; Alef Miranda; Alexandre Dubugras
market_need_then: Rental paperwork in Brazil is slow and manual; Startupi (Sept 2020) reports about 150 brokers on the platform and 150 on a waitlist, and a goal of 20,000 rentals in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Alude raised a 3.3 million dollar seed in September 2020 with Ribbit Capital and others and is still listed active. Its free-to-broker model monetized through partner products. No later round, acquisition or shutdown was found, so its trajectory after the seed is unclear.

name: Anatomic
tags: B2B; Digital Health; Healthcare; Data Labeling; AI
one_liner: Real-world healthcare data for medical AI
long_description: Anatomic works with hospitals and doctors to collect surgical video, doctor-patient conversations and medical imaging for AI and robotics research. Our data library includes multi-perspective surgical recordings, diarized and transcribed clinical conversations, and annotated X-ray, CT and MRI series linked to longitudinal patient records. Built through a network of 100+ hospitals and 1,000+ clinicians, with HIPAA- and GDPR-compliant data.
all_locations: Gurugram, HR, India; Noida, UP, India
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Medical AI and robotics research teams that buy clinical datasets
problem: Medical AI teams lack real-world surgical video, clinical conversations and annotated imaging linked to patient history; Anatomic collects it through hospital partners.
business_model: Data licensing and custom data collection
product_category: Healthcare data for AI training
market_need_then: Not established from sources dated at founding; the current site claims demand from AI and robotics research teams.
outcome_analysis: Anatomic is listed active with a team of three based in India and sells healthcare data for medical AI. No funding beyond YC, no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found, and sources on its history are thin, so the outcome is unclear and the company appears small.

name: Angle Health
one_liner: Health Insurance for Startups
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-sized employers buying level-funded group health plans and their employees
problem: Small employers face slow quoting, opaque pricing and clunky benefits administration; Angle built a tech-enabled insurer and administrator with fast quoting and HR system integrations.
business_model: Insurance premiums on level-funded group health plans plus administration and stop-loss economics
product_category: Health insurance and benefits platform
competitors_at_founding: Oscar Health; Sidecar Health; Bright Health; Collective Health
market_need_then: Crunchbase News (July 2020) framed small startups as underserved by slow, costly insurance quoting; Wang expected to launch the plans in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Angle raised a 4 million dollar seed in 2020, a 58 million Series A around January 2023, a 134 million Series B in December 2025 and a 200 million Series C in September 2026 at a reported 2.7 billion valuation with a 400 million tender. The company says it serves over 5,000 employers and reported positive EBITDA in recent quarters. Regulatory work and licensing gave it a path others lacked.

name: Ansa Biotechnologies
one_liner: Next-generation DNA synthesis using enzymes
long_description: Ansa Biotechnologies is developing a new way to make DNA that will be faster, cleaner, and more accurate than existing methods. Currently, DNA is manufactured via a chemical method that has remained mostly unchanged for 35 years. Our enzyme-based approach promises to dramatically accelerate innovation in biological research and biotechnology, including therapeutics, diagnostics and biomanufacturing.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Emeryville, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Researchers, biotech and CDMO teams that order synthetic DNA, especially long and complex sequences
problem: Chemical DNA synthesis is slow, dirty and limited in length; Ansa uses enzymes to make longer, more accurate DNA faster.
business_model: Product and service sales of synthetic DNA (clonal DNA, fragments, plasmids) with on-time guarantee
product_category: Synthetic biology, enzymatic DNA synthesis
market_need_then: Chemical phosphoramidite synthesis had changed little in decades per the company site; gene and cell therapy and synthetic biology were expanding demand for long DNA.
outcome_analysis: Ansa kept raising: a 7.9 million seed in 2020, 68 million Series A in 2022 and 54.4 million Series B in 2025, after a December 2018 pre-seed. It shifted from technology development to a commercial service for long clonal DNA, appointing Jason Gammack as CEO in February 2024. It remains independent and active.

name: Apartio
one_liner: Apartio offers Short Term Rentals for Business Travelers in Brazil
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Aquarium Learning
tags: Deep Learning; Developer Tools; Generative AI; Machine Learning; AI
one_liner: We help ML teams improve their models by improving their datasets
long_description:
ML models are only as good as the datasets they're trained on, and that means that most improvement to model performance comes from improvement to the quality and diversity of their datasets.

Our tooling makes it easy for ML teams to find anomalies + failure patterns in their datasets and fix these problems by editing / adding the right data. So the next time you retrain your model, it just gets better.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: ML teams at autonomous vehicle, robotics and computer vision companies
problem: Model performance is limited by dataset quality, and teams lack tools to find label errors, anomalies and failure patterns in training data. Aquarium surfaced these and helped teams fix them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for ML dataset tooling
product_category: ML data curation and dataset debugging
market_need_then: Self-driving and computer vision teams were spending heavily on labeling and found data quality was the main bottleneck, a point of rising attention in 2020 as data-centric AI emerged.
outcome_analysis: Aquarium was founded by two Cruise alumni who understood data problems in self-driving, raised a $2.6M Sequoia-led seed in February 2021 and had no reported later round. It was absorbed into Notion's AI team in 2024 and the products were shut down, which reads as a team and technology acquisition rather than a scaled outcome, with the price undisclosed.

name: Ardis AI
one_liner: Transform your text data into a searchable knowledge graph
long_description:
Ardis AI extracts information from your unstructured text data and automatically generates a knowledge graph that can be browsed and queried, by web app or by API. Users can ask complex questions about the content of your text data, and Ardis responds with the answers and the evidence -- even when the information needed to answer the questions comes from multiple documents. Ardis also provides summary views of the topics discussed in your data. 

Coming soon: an Ardis plug-in for Elasticsearch, and support for natural languages questions.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Mountain View, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Arist
one_liner: Deliver effective learning at scale
long_description:
Arist is the only message-based learning platform. 

We help over 10% Fortune 500 companies and governments rapidly teach and train employees, entirely via messaging tools like SMS, Slack, WhatsApp and Microsoft Teams.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Large companies, governments and nonprofits that train employees or learners at scale
problem: Corporate training is boring and low completion; Arist delivers short courses through text message, WhatsApp, Slack and Teams so learners engage where they already are.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for course authoring and message-based delivery
product_category: Workplace microlearning and enablement platform
founder_names: Michael Ioffe; Ryan Laverty; Maxine Anderson
market_need_then: Seed coverage (Oct 2020) says customers used it mainly for diversity and inclusion, compliance and safety training, and remote work increased demand for distributed learning.
outcome_analysis: Arist grew from a 1.9 million seed in October 2020 to a 12 million Series A in 2022 and claims use by over 50 Fortune 500 companies. A reduction in force of seven people in August 2023 shows a rough patch, and a later report of a 22.5 million Series B in August 2026 is single sourced. It remains active and independent.

name: Arketa
one_liner: Everything for your fitness or wellness business.
long_description: All in one platform for online and in-person classes, video on-demand, courses and website hosting.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Independent fitness, yoga and wellness studio owners and instructors who pay a monthly software fee
problem: Small studios and instructors had to stitch together booking, payments, video on demand and website tools, or pay for heavyweight legacy studio software.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payment processing fees
product_category: Fitness and wellness studio management software
market_need_then: The 2020 pandemic forced studios to move classes online and sell video on demand, creating sudden demand for low cost all in one tools. The seed post says thousands of studios were using the product by late 2022.
outcome_analysis: Arketa started in the 2020 pandemic, when studios suddenly needed online class and video on demand tools, and grew into an all in one platform. It raised a $7.6M seed in late 2022 and a $15M Series A in June 2025, renamed from Sutra Fitness in November 2023, and was still active with about 55 people. No shutdown or sale was found. Evidence of strong product market fit is thin beyond the company's own claims.

name: Artifact
one_liner: Personal podcasts with the people in your life
long_description: Artifact makes it easy to record stories with the most important people in your life. We set them up with a professional interviewer through our marketplace and we make it easy, from scheduling interviews to delivering a polished edit that wouldn’t sound out of place on NPR. We then host their stories in shareable, interactive listening experiences.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Atmo
one_liner: Ultra-precise AI weather forecasting.
long_description: Atmo is the leading company bringing artificial intelligence to meteorology for governments, militaries, and corporations. Atmo builds state-of-the-art AI weather forecasts that are up to 50% more accurate, 10x more detailed, and run 40,000x faster. Atmo has rapidly become the trusted AI meteorology partner for high-stakes users worldwide, such as the US Department of Defense, top aerospace companies, the Philippines, and the United Nations. Today, Atmo forecasting systems protect vital infrastructure and enhance economic activity for its partners, including disaster response, renewable energy, agriculture, transportation, and national security.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Berkeley, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Governments, militaries and weather-sensitive corporations (energy, aerospace, agriculture, transport)
problem: Traditional numerical weather prediction is slow and expensive to run at fine resolution. Atmo applied deep learning to produce faster, more detailed forecasts for high-stakes users.
business_model: Enterprise and government contracts for forecasting products and APIs
product_category: AI weather forecasting
market_need_then: Climate-related catastrophes were raising business demand for better forecasts in 2020, and TechCrunch covered Atmo in that context; forecast accuracy and resolution were limited by physics-based models.
outcome_analysis: Atmo raised an early seed after YC Winter 2020, built AI forecasting models, and won government clients including the Philippines and US defense customers. As deep learning forecasting matured, Vaisala agreed in June 2026 to pay $70M upfront plus up to $60M in earn-outs, a meaningful positive exit for a small team, with closing confirmation not found.

name: Atmos
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: The entire homebuilding process, all online
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: AtoB
tags: Fintech; SaaS; Payments; Supply Chain; Transportation
one_liner: Modernizing global transportation payments.
long_description:
The trucking and logistics industry provides the backbone of the economy, but the payments infrastructure on which it runs is broken; the existing suite of payment tools is outdated, difficult to use, prone to fraud, and saddled with hidden fee structures. 

AtoB is building Stripe for Transportation — modernizing the payments infrastructure for trucking and logistics, where capital movement occurs quickly and transparently. Our flagship product is the AtoB Fuel Card, a zero-fee fuel card accepted anywhere built for fleets of all shapes and sizes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Trucking fleets and owner operators that buy fuel and need payments and credit
problem: Trucking payments ran on outdated fuel cards with hidden fees and fraud exposure, and small fleets were poorly served.
business_model: Interchange and fuel discount economics on a fleet fuel card, plus payments and credit products
product_category: Fintech, transportation payments and fuel cards
market_need_then: Fuel is a large cost for fleets, and incumbents were criticized for fees and acceptance limits. The company says a zero fee card accepted anywhere addressed that pain.
outcome_analysis: AtoB sold a zero fee fuel card to a large trucking market dominated by WEX and Fleetcor. It raised a $155M Series B in August 2022 and $130M in September 2024, and signed distribution deals with Uber Freight, Murphy USA and others. It was still active with 75 staff. Growth looks driven by a clear customer pain and partner channels, though much of the capital includes debt and the early rounds are not verified.

name: Atomic
one_liner: API that lets companies embed investment accounts into their services
long_description: With our API any company that holds consumer deposits (e.g. savings apps) can easily embed professionally managed investment accounts into their services.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Fintechs, banks and apps that hold consumer deposits and want to offer investing
problem: Companies with consumer deposits wanted to offer managed investment accounts but lacked the brokerage, advisory and compliance setup to do it.
business_model: Usage and platform fees from an embedded investing API (advisory and brokerage)
product_category: Embedded investing infrastructure API
market_need_then: Fintech and savings apps wanted to add investing in 2020, and retail investing demand had surged, per the company's pitch. No spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Atomic raised a $25M Series A in November 2021 co-led by QED and Anthemis, launched its API from stealth, and later raised $30M in August 2025 and bought a Dutch investment firm in January 2026 to enter Europe. It remains active with about 25 staff. Its position rests on regulated licenses and custody ties, though traction numbers were not disclosed.

name: Atomized
one_liner: Enabling teams to deploy without needing a cloud expert
long_description:
Atomized helps developers launch applications in the cloud faster by deploying and managing the necessary infrastructure for you. Simply connect up your Github repo and your AWS account, and we'll handle the rest!

The best part is that all the infrastructure runs in your AWS account, and you have full ownership and visibility into it. No more black boxes that you can't troubleshoot and manage.

We want to empower engineers to build, deploy, secure, and monitor infrastructure faster than ever. Our long-term vision is to be the go-to platform to get started and to be able to manage all things cloud - no matter which cloud provider you choose.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Avion
one_liner: Avion builds and operates autonomous eVTOL drones that deliver vital…
long_description:
Avion is a drone-based digital health platform, designed to bridge the gap between remote clinics and urban healthcare infrastructures. By connecting these isolated clinics with sophisticated labs and well-stocked pharmacies in cities, Avion brings a new era of remote diagnostics and prescription fulfilment.

Avion ensures the rapid, safe, and efficient delivery of vital medical supplies and clinical samples, even to the most hard-to-reach locations. 

Avion's operation uniquely combines cutting-edge autonomous drone technology with digital health platforms. Our drones, built with advanced eVTOL capabilities, ensure seamless take-off and landing capabilities, even in challenging terrains.

Avion's digital health platform serves as the connective tissue between urban health centers and remote clinics. The platform features an intuitive interface, making it easy for healthcare providers to order necessary supplies, track shipments, and even communicate with laboratory and pharmacy staff.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Remote clinics, labs and pharmacies and the health ministries or customers who pay for medical drone delivery
problem: Remote clinics in places such as Ethiopia are hard to reach by road, so samples and medicines move slowly.
business_model: Owned and operated drone delivery service paid per delivery or contract
product_category: Autonomous medical drone delivery
market_need_then: Ethiopia has many remote clinics with poor roads. A 2021 profile says Avion got permission to expand nationwide. A VC4A profile claims a $10M exclusive delivery contract, which is unverified.
outcome_analysis: Avion is an Ethiopian medical drone startup that joined YC in Winter 2020 and is listed as active. Sources show a small YC seed and a 2021 claim of nationwide permission, but later funding, traction and status are unverified. The YC page lists San Francisco as its base. No shutdown was found, so the record is too thin to assign success or failure factors.

name: Awtomic
one_liner: Dollar Shave Club as a platform.
long_description: Awtomic powers DTC brands with an easy-to-use subscription management and discovery platform. Starting with a Shopify app, we'll give merchants the subscription product power of premium subscription brands like Dollar Shave Club and Ipsy. As we grow our support for more eCommerce platforms and merchants, we'll help customers discover new brands through cross-sells and make it easier for them to manage their subscriptions in one place.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Direct to consumer brands on Shopify that sell subscriptions, clubs and memberships
problem: Merchants found existing subscription apps limiting, with checkout friction and weak bundling. The founder cites her sister's DTC beauty brand as the trigger.
business_model: B2B SaaS monthly subscription for a Shopify app, reportedly $299 per month plus a per order fee
product_category: Ecommerce subscription management
founder_names: Emily Yuhas; Brian Singer; Adrian Andrade
market_need_then: Pandemic era DTC growth increased demand for subscriptions. Merchant reviews on the Shopify app store describe leaving Recharge over checkout friction.
outcome_analysis: Awtomic is a small Shopify subscriptions app led by a solo founder that is still active with about 11 people. No institutional round was found, only an aggregator claim of a $500K note. It competes with Recharge and Bold in a crowded market after Shopify's 2020 API change. Public evidence of traction is limited to app store reviews, so no success or failure story can be asserted.

name: BIK
tags: SaaS; B2B; E-commerce; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Agentic AI CRM for ecommerce
long_description:
A place where you can spin off commerce agents or build your automation across the funnel of acquisition, retention & support. 

The single place where you can handle everything you need for your ecommerce / retail business when it comes to marketing & support.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Ecommerce and DTC brands, first Indian small merchants, later global brands, that pay for marketing and support automation
problem: Small Indian merchants sold over WhatsApp without a store system; later brands needed automated customer engagement and support.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, freemium at the start and later priced per brand
product_category: Ecommerce CRM and AI commerce agents
market_need_then: In 2020 pandemic lockdowns pushed Indian neighborhood shops to sell over WhatsApp. An Inc42 piece dates the first product to March 2020.
outcome_analysis: Bikayi raised a $2M seed in August 2020 and a $10.8M Sequoia India led Series A in September 2021, then rebranded to BIK in September 2022 and moved toward global ecommerce brands and later AI agents. Inc42 reported a layoff of up to 90 percent of staff during the pivot, with the date unknown. It is listed active with 55 people and claims 500 brands, which is unverified. The pivot looks real but the outcome is unclear.

name: Balance
one_liner: The first digital payment experience company, built for B2B.
long_description: Balance is the easiest way for B2B marketplaces, merchants, and service providers to process payments online. We raised our last funding round from Lightspeed, Stripe, and Max Levchin to build 'Stripe for B2B'. Balance offers the first business checkout, enabling business customers to pay How they want (check, card, bank) and When they want (net terms, payment plans, invoice payments). this is achieved while the seller receives the funds instantly and easily like card payment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B marketplaces, merchants and distributors that sell to businesses and want net terms and online checkout
problem: Business buyers pay by check and invoice on net terms, so sellers wait for cash and have no consumer style checkout.
business_model: Payment and trade credit fees on B2B transactions plus software fees
product_category: B2B payments, checkout and trade credit infrastructure
market_need_then: TechCrunch in Feb 2021 describes B2B payments as analog, with checks and invoices, while pandemic ecommerce grew. Balance claimed to serve large brands later.
outcome_analysis: Balance raised $5.5M seed in February 2021, $25M Series A in August 2021, $56M Series B in July 2022 and a $350M credit facility in November 2022, then widened from checkout to trade credit and receivables tools. Named customers include Instacart, Upwork and GE Vernova. It stays active with 70 staff. Investor backing from Stripe and Ribbit and a funded credit line signal real demand, though revenue is not public.

name: Bamboo
one_liner: Bamboo ― the first online brokerage service for Africans and their…
long_description:
Bamboo is the first online brokerage service that gives wealthy Africans and their wealth managers direct access to the US and global securities. We’re building Fidelity for the African continent.
For wealthy Africans and their asset managers, investing in the global capital markets is cumbersome, expensive and practically inaccessible. In Nigeria, Africa's largest economy and home to 30% of all the wealth in Sub Saharan Africa (excluding South Africa), 99.99% of the investing population do not have access to invest globally. Even for the 0.01%, if you wanted to buy a US stock, you’d have to call your asset manager who would then call an international broker to execute a trade. This is inefficient & expensive!
We have a mobile app that allows individuals trade the US stock markets by themselves and a brokerage tool for asset managers to execute trades directly & manage multilple portfolios seamlessly.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Nigerian and wider African retail investors, and wealthy individuals via asset managers, who want US and local stocks
problem: Africans had little access to US securities, and buying one required an asset manager calling an international broker.
business_model: Brokerage commissions and fees on trades and products, via a partner broker dealer
product_category: Online brokerage and investing app
market_need_then: TechCrunch says 75 percent of users had never traded before and 50,000 joined the Ghana waitlist. In 2020, Nigerians sought dollar assets, though that point is the company's pitch rather than a sourced spend figure.
outcome_analysis: Bamboo launched in January 2020, reached over 300,000 users by early 2022 and raised a $15M Series A co-led by Greycroft and Tiger Global in January 2022. It later gained a Nigerian sub broker licence, a US broker dealer affiliate in 2024, expanded to South Africa and added Nigerian stocks and a remittance app. It claims 2.3M users. A 2021 SEC circular shows regulatory risk that it navigated.

name: Bandit ML
one_liner: Bandit ML builds machine learning tools for e-commerce companies.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: E-commerce companies and engineering teams wanting ML-driven recommendations and decisions optimized for long-term value
problem: Building production contextual bandit and reinforcement learning systems for personalization is hard for most e-commerce teams. Bandit ML offered an API that makes decisions to optimize long-term metrics such as customer lifetime value.
business_model: Usage-based ML decision API for e-commerce, with an open source core library
product_category: ML decision and recommendation API
founder_names: Edoardo Conti; Joseph Gilley; Lionel Vital
market_need_then: E-commerce growth in 2020 raised demand for personalization, while few teams had expertise in bandit and reinforcement learning methods that the founders had built at Facebook and Uber.
outcome_analysis: Bandit ML raised a small seed in 2020 on the strength of founders from Facebook AI, Uber and Twitter and shipped an open source bandit library. It did not reach a larger round and the team was acquihired by Silo Technologies in May 2022, with the product wound into a food supply chain effort, so the exit was a soft landing; the stated reason is the buyer's, and customer traction is not public.

name: Basedash
tags: SaaS; B2B; Data Science; Data Visualization; AI
one_liner: The AI-native business intelligence platform
long_description: Basedash is the AI-native Business Intelligence platform. Create dashboards and instantly understand your customers using natural language. Connect 500+ data sources, ask a question, and let Basedash visualize the answer.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startups and product teams that need internal admin tools on a production database; now teams wanting AI-native business intelligence
problem: Nearly every company builds internal admin panels from scratch; Basedash auto-generates a UI on a production database without SQL, and later became an AI analytics platform.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a free tier and team plans
product_category: Internal tools, then AI business intelligence
market_need_then: Internal tools were widely built in-house, and Retool's 2020 round signaled strong demand; Basedash spent about three years talking to thousands of companies.
outcome_analysis: Basedash began as a database admin panel in 2020, raised a $4.4M seed from Matrix in May 2023 and repositioned as AI-native BI in 2025, now claiming 5000+ teams and security certifications. It remains independent with a small team. Competitors in both categories are strong, so the pivot is promising but unproven.

name: BeGo
tags: Banking as a Service; Digital Freight Brokerage; AI
one_liner: BeGo Connects cargo shippers with truck suppliers in Mexico and US
long_description:
In Mexico and US trucking demand outpaces capacity, yet 40% of the time trucks roll empty. BeGo uses Machine Learning to reduce empty returns, deadheads, and carbon emissions. 
BeGo is co-founded by two brothers, Jasiel, with 10+ years of experience in the industry, and  Ivan, ex-Tesla engineer with experience in product design and machine learning.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Cargo shippers and independent truck carriers moving freight between Mexico and the US
problem: Trucking demand in Mexico and the US outpaces capacity while trucks often run empty on return trips, and shippers and carriers lack an efficient way to find each other.
business_model: Digital freight brokerage and marketplace taking a margin on loads, later adding software (BeGo Black fleet management), insurance and credit products for carriers
product_category: Digital freight brokerage and logistics software
market_need_then: Company states roughly 40 percent of truck trips roll empty in Mexico and the US and demand outpaces capacity. Cross border trade volume was large and Mexican freight was fragmented among small carriers.
outcome_analysis: BeGo is active and still independent. The founding brothers combined trucking industry experience with an ex-Tesla engineer, and it raised a reported $14M seed in 2021 from a broad group of US funds. It has since widened from brokerage into credit, insurance, fleet software and air freight. Public data on revenue and later rounds is thin, so its trajectory beyond the seed is unclear.

name: Belvo
one_liner: Open Finance API platform for Latam.
long_description:
We are Belvo, a financial API platform for Latam that enables any company or developer to access and interpret their end-users' financial information, through one easy-to-use API. Think Plaid for Latam.

Our vision is to power the next generation of financial services in Latam by enabling more inclusive, efficient and empowering offerings through tech and data. Latam is a very exciting and dynamic place to be right now and a great place to build infrastructure for the next generation of financial products for a huge market.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Fintechs, banks, lenders and other companies in Latin America that need access to end-user financial data and bank payments
problem: Latin American banks keep financial data siloed and offer no open banking infrastructure, so developers must build many separate integrations to access user data.
business_model: Usage and subscription based API platform for financial data and later payments
product_category: Open finance API platform
market_need_then: In July 2019 Belvo described over 600 million people in Latin America, a booming fintech sector and an absolute lack of open banking infrastructure, with banks reluctant to open data unlike Europe under PSD2.
outcome_analysis: Belvo is active and raised $10M seed in 2020, a $43M Series A in 2021 and a $15M round in 2025 from top regional and US funds. Founders had fintech and aerospace backgrounds and chose the Plaid for Latam wedge when open banking infrastructure was absent. The 2023 funding squeeze led to layoffs of roughly 27 people, and the later smaller round suggests a slower period, but the company reports 80 million connected accounts and expanded into payments.

name: Benepass
one_liner: Pre-tax and lifestyle benefits, managed in one place.
long_description:
Benepass consolidates corporate benefits onto a single card, powered by our in-house fintech payments stack. We run global benefits at scale. 

We help companies take care of their employees through tax-advantaged benefits (e.g. FSA/HSA, dependent care, commuter) and company-funded lifestyle benefits (e.g. wellness, WFH, professional development) all on a single card + mobile app.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Employers (HR and finance teams) that offer pre-tax and company-funded lifestyle benefits to employees
problem: Employee benefits such as FSA, HSA, commuter and wellness stipends are fragmented, hard to use and often underused, and debit cards tied to pre-tax accounts are frequently declined.
business_model: B2B SaaS and payments: per-employee platform fees plus card interchange on a single benefits card
product_category: Benefits card and benefits management platform

name: Breathe Well-being
one_liner: A digital well-being program to help people prevent or manage chronic…

Our online program is 3X more effective at 1/4th the cost.

The coach helps the user bust negative emotions of past failures in weight-loss and increase motivation by linking short-term achievable goals with the user's personal values. Through the program, the user is able to self-identify triggers of unhealthy habit adoption and make better decisions.

Breathe Well-being has demonstrated success in helping people lose weight, build long-term healthy habits and reduce/eliminate medication for lifestyle diseases (example - Type 2 Diabetes). We are looking for ideas to improve our sales processes so that we can get users to enrol at a higher conversion rate post our 1-week free trial. We need to identify triggers when users are most likely to pay and provide them with a seamless process for paying on-the-spot.

name: Command AI
one_liner: AI-powered user assistance platform
long_description:
At Command AI, we believe in a world where the internet “just works” for every visitor, customer, and user. As the internet has become more powerful and crowded, it has become harder for everyone to use. And the solutions we’ve come up with to date — like irritating chatbots and pestering popups — end up being ignored or even annoying users more than they help.

We sell tools to software builders and buyers to help them make their software better for users.

We call this as our User Assistance Platform, and it comes in 2 pieces:
- AI Agent — an AI chat agent that can answer users questions, perform actions for them, and even co-browse with them to teach your interface.

- Nudge Platform — AI-assisted nudges, hints, and messages to guide users in personalized ways that don’t annoy them. We do this by optimally delivering nudges based on in-product behavior not just static rules as well as measuring measuring and the extent to which users “rage close” nudges to avoid pestering them. A replacement for legacy Digital Adoption Platforms

User assistance translates into concrete outcomes like improved engagement, feature adoption, conversion, and retention, all while decreasing low-value support tickets.

We’re used by teams like HubSpot, HashiCorp, Yotpo, Thryvv, and Freshworks.

CoreCare is the leading AI-powered workflow platform helping Post-Acute and Long-Term Care (PALTC) providers achieve operational excellence. Trusted by 1,000+ locations nationwide, CoreCare increases admissions, optimizes reimbursement rates, improves collection metrics, and reduces administrative burdens—all on one intuitive platform.

At the heart of CoreCare is Collaborative Revenue Management, which unites essential data and teams on a shared platform. Our approach empowers employees—regardless of skill or tenure—to perform like experts from day one, collaborate with their peers on critical work, and give management unmatched visibility into performance across the organization.

CoreCare replaces error-prone spreadsheets and fragmented portals with streamlined workflows that drive measurable results. Trusted by leading providers, CoreCare redefines how teams work and sets a new standard for AI in long-term care.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Post-acute and long-term care operators and skilled nursing facilities
problem: Skilled nursing facilities lost revenue and time on billing, Medicaid and admissions workflows that sat across EHRs and payer systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS for facilities
product_category: Healthcare revenue integrity and workflow software
market_need_then: Skilled nursing providers bill Medicaid and Medicare through slow and error-prone processes; the 2020 seed coverage described an ML system connecting EHR data with payer data.
outcome_analysis: CoreCare raised a $3M seed in October 2020 and has since disclosed no further rounds, yet it reports over 1,000 locations using the platform. In April 2026 it moved its Pre-Admit product to ExaCare AI to focus on its revenue integrity platform. It is active, and funding beyond the seed is unknown.

name: Cortex
one_liner: Cortex is the Internal Developer Portal eliminating “developer tax”…
long_description: ​​Cortex is an internal developer portal built to accelerate the path to engineering excellence. Companies like Xero, Canva, and TripAdvisor use Cortex to catalog, score, and assign action to improve service quality and velocity, so devs can get back to work that drives the business forward.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering organisations with many microservices, such as Xero, Canva and TripAdvisor
problem: Engineering teams lost track of who owned services and whether they met quality standards, often tracking them in spreadsheets.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Internal developer portal and engineering operations platform
founder_names: Anish Dhar; Ganesh Datta; Nikhil Unni
market_need_then: Microservice sprawl left teams tracking hundreds of services in spreadsheets, which TechCrunch cites as the founder's Uber experience.
outcome_analysis: Cortex launched in 2019, shipped in March 2020 and has raised seed, Series A, Series B ($35M, 2023) and a $60M Series C reported at a $470M valuation. Sequoia backed it from seed. The company sells to large engineering organisations and has repositioned to an engineering operations platform. It remains independent and active in 2026.

name: Cradle
one_liner: B2B payments network in India
long_description: Cradle is a B2B payments network in India that lets small businesses collect online payments from other businesses for free.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Small businesses in India collecting online payments from other businesses
problem: Small Indian businesses lacked a free way to collect online payments from business customers.
business_model: B2B payments network, possibly with purchase credit; monetisation not confirmed
product_category: B2B payments
market_need_then: No dated 2020 evidence of demand was found; the YC description states small businesses lacked a free way to collect payments.
outcome_analysis: Cradle appears to be a tiny team of two. The sources opened give no funding, traction or shutdown news, and its cradle.finance domain redirects to an expired-domain listing, which suggests the original site lapsed. The YC page still shows it as active, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Cron
one_liner: Next-generation calendar for professionals and teams
long_description: Cron (acq. by Notion) is the next-generation calendar app for professionals and teams, making modern work more efficient and joyful. Our mission is to help spend time wisely through well-crafted software that streamlines workflows, integrates other productivity tools, and builds collaboration right into the core experience. In everything we do at Cron, we believe that time is our most precious resource.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Professionals and teams who live in Google Calendar and want a faster, keyboard driven desktop calendar
problem: Existing calendar apps were slow, cluttered and poorly integrated with the other tools people use to plan their day.
business_model: Freemium prosumer SaaS with paid plans for individuals and teams
product_category: Calendar app (macOS, Windows, iOS)
market_need_then: Sunrise had been shut down in 2016 and its fans lacked a loved replacement, while remote work increased calendar load. Evidence is the later TechCrunch framing of Cron as following Sunrise; no spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Cron was a tiny team that rebuilt the beloved Sunrise experience with strong design, raised a $3.5M seed in March 2020 from Initialized and notable angels, and shipped publicly in late 2021. Notion bought it in June 2022 to get a native calendar and the founder, so the exit was a product and talent acquisition by a company that wanted the wedge rather than a standalone calendar business.

name: CrowdForce
one_liner: Crowdforce is an app that allows any local merchant in Africa,…
long_description: CrowdForce is an app that allows any local merchant in Africa, starting with Nigeria to become a bank branch within minutes.
regions: Nigeria; Africa
target_customer: Local merchants, pharmacies and reseller networks in Nigeria that act as banking agents, plus the customers who use them for cash and payments
problem: Most Nigerians lived far from a bank branch and relied on cash, so access to deposits, withdrawals and transfers was poor.
business_model: Agency banking: transaction fees on payments and cash services through a distributed POS terminal and agent network
product_category: Fintech, agent banking network
market_need_then: Nigeria had a large unbanked population and heavy cash use. A 2020 EFInA agents survey and later coverage show strong agent demand; exact figures were not verified here.
outcome_analysis: CrowdForce built a merchant distribution network for agent banking in Nigeria, said it was cash positive from 2020 and raised a $3.6M pre Series A in February 2022 including $1M of debt. Facing much larger rivals like OPay and Moniepoint, its PayForce unit was sold to FairMoney in March 2023 and the CEO joined FairMoney, a modest exit that suggests a strategic sale rather than a breakout.

name: Current Foods
one_liner: Impossible foods of seafood.
long_description: Creating the next generation of seafood with plants and biotechnology. No compromises on taste and health while winning on price and consistency. First products are raw tuna and smoked salmon.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Foodservice buyers such as poke bars and restaurants, then retail and direct to consumer shoppers wanting plant-based sushi grade seafood
problem: Fish supply is unsustainable and existing plant-based seafood tasted and performed poorly versus raw tuna and salmon.
business_model: CPG and foodservice product sales of plant-based tuna and smoked salmon, wholesale and direct to consumer
product_category: Plant-based seafood
competitors_at_founding: Sophie's Kitchen; Ocean Hugger Foods; Good Catch Foods
market_need_then: Plant-based meat had mainstream traction (Beyond, Impossible) and seafood analogs were about 1.4% of plant-based meat sales, per Good Food Institute data cited in a trade report, so the need was an open gap with small current spend.
outcome_analysis: Current Foods built a plant-based tuna and salmon brand, raised an $18M seed in June 2022 and reached retail, but alternative seafood remained a small category. Wicked Kitchen acquired it for stock in May 2023, its second seafood acquisition in a year, which looks like consolidation of a sub scale category rather than a breakout win.

name: Daedalus
one_liner: AWS for precision manufacturing
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Industrial buyers of precision machined parts, such as aerospace and robotics firms
problem: Precision parts took months to get and manufacturing was manual, slow and costly; the founder waited months for spare parts for a robot hand at OpenAI.
business_model: Vertically integrated contract manufacturing with an AI-driven production platform
product_category: Autonomous precision manufacturing
market_need_then: The founder's firsthand experience of months-long waits for precision parts is cited in 2024 coverage; no 2020-dated demand data was opened.
outcome_analysis: Daedalus raised an $11.5M seed in November 2021 and a $21M Series A in February 2024 led by NGP Capital, bringing reported funding past $40M. It runs a factory in Karlsruhe and was targeting more capacity. No distress or exit appears in sources found, so the later outcome is unknown.

name: Dashworks
one_liner: Your team's intelligent start page.
long_description: Dashworks is where work begins. Where all your documents, messages, tickets, and other knowledge scattered across your company's apps and people come together seamlessly. And where you and your team can get on the same page, and get things done.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Teams at tech companies (support, sales, engineering, product) that lose time searching scattered internal knowledge
problem: Company knowledge is spread across many apps and people, so employees waste time finding answers.
business_model: B2B SaaS, tiered subscription pricing
product_category: Workplace search and AI knowledge assistant
market_need_then: Scattered knowledge across SaaS tools was a widely felt pain, but no dated spend or complaint data was found for 2020; the 2022 TechCrunch piece framed it as a search engine for internal knowledge.
outcome_analysis: Dashworks started as a start page and search tool for internal knowledge, raised a $4M seed in January 2022 and a $5M extension in July 2023 when it pivoted to an LLM assistant. With a crowded enterprise search field including Glean, it ended in an acqui-style sale to HubSpot in April 2025 to strengthen Breeze AI, with no price disclosed.

name: Datafold
one_liner: Automating manual and repetitive data engineering tasks with AI
long_description:
Datafold automates manual work in data engineering. 

We leverage agentic AI to automate both day-to-day tasks, such as testing and code reviews, and massive one-off projects, such as data platform code migrations. Companies from Perplexity to Disney use Datafold to unlock more value from their data by freeing up their data teams from manual work, accelerating developer velocity, and ensuring data quality.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data engineering and analytics teams at data-heavy companies
problem: Code changes to SQL pipelines silently broke downstream data, and teams lacked automated regression testing for data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Data quality, data diff and migration tooling
market_need_then: Launch HN in August 2020 framed regression testing of ETL pipelines as a major pain point; the founder's Lyft incident where a 4-line SQL change broke data for most of a day is the origin story.
outcome_analysis: Datafold raised a $20M Series A in November 2021 led by NEA and has stayed independent while shifting toward migration and AI agent products. It lists customers such as Disney and Databricks. Funding after the Series A is unverified, so the strength of its later growth is not shown.

name: Dataland
tags: B2B; Data Engineering; Data Visualization; AI
one_liner: AI agents for customer support.
long_description: Dataland is the applied AI lab for complex operations and customer support. In 8 months, we've grown to multi-million dollar ARR as just two founders and are highly profitable. We’re partnering with some of the fastest growing startups and public companies in the world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mid to large operations and customer support teams at fast growing startups and public companies (named logos include Upwork, Midi Health, Shippo, Fanatics)
problem: Complex support and back office work needs people who use internal admin tools without APIs and follow detailed policies. Dataland replaces that labor with custom AI agents backed by an embedded forward deployed engineer.
business_model: Enterprise services plus software: custom AI agents sold per engagement with a forward deployed engineer per customer
product_category: AI agents for customer support and operations (earlier: database viewer and internal tools for non-technical teams)
market_need_then: In 2020 many YC companies (Basedash, Stacker, Acho) targeted the same pain of non-technical teams needing database access without SQL, which shows demand but also crowding.
outcome_analysis: Dataland started as a database viewer for non-technical teams in a crowded 2020 internal tools niche and later repositioned as an AI agent lab for customer support run by two ex-Palantir founders. The YC page claims multi-million dollar ARR within 8 months as two founders and high profitability, which is self reported and unverified. No funding beyond YC, shutdown or acquisition is public, and the timing of the pivot is not documented.

name: Datasaur
one_liner: Datasaur builds private AI/agents for enterprise/government
long_description: Datasaur builds and integrates private AI and agents for enterprise organizations. We prioritize rigorous security and compliance, ensuring your most sensitive data never leaves your infrastructure. Datasaur keeps your workflows internal, so your proprietary intelligence remains a dedicated competitive advantage, and is never used to train the next generation of third-party models.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Enterprise and government teams in regulated industries (finance, health, legal) that want private AI and agents running in their own infrastructure; originally NLP and ML teams needing text labeling
problem: Teams building NLP models needed better tooling to label text data; later, regulated organizations wanted AI without sending sensitive data to third party model providers.
business_model: Originally B2B SaaS for NLP data labeling; now enterprise contracts and services for private AI deployments
product_category: NLP data labeling platform evolving into private enterprise AI
market_need_then: Growing NLP adoption meant teams needed labeled text, and the founder saw the need while managing training data at Apple. Demand for labeling later shifted with LLMs, and enterprises began asking for private deployments.
outcome_analysis: Datasaur began in 2019 as a text labeling tool from an ex Apple ML data lead, raised a 4 million dollar seed in 2023 led by Initialized, and later repositioned toward private enterprise AI with a May 2026 Forge service. It is still active with about 60 staff and no layoffs or sale found. Total funding is modest and the labeling market was crowded, so it is a survivor repositioning rather than a breakout.

name: Datree
one_liner: Datree prevents Kubernetes misconfigurations from reaching production
long_description:
Prevent Kubernetes misconfigurations from reaching production with Datree’s automated policy checks for your pipeline. 

The open-source CLI tool empowers engineers to write more stable and secure configurations, and further supports them in their roles so they can actually sleep at night. 

By revealing misconfigurations in seconds and combating the issues in early stages of the pipeline, your organization can enforce its standards and secure its infrastructure from development to production.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: DevOps and platform engineering teams running Kubernetes
problem: Kubernetes misconfigurations reach production; Datree runs automated policy checks in the CI pipeline via an open-source CLI.
business_model: Open-source CLI with paid SaaS policy management (freemium); pricing not verified
product_category: DevOps policy engine / Kubernetes security tooling
market_need_then: Not independently evidenced at founding in sources I retrieved. Datree raised $3M seed (2018) and $8M Series A (Feb 2020) on the premise that Kubernetes misconfigurations were a production risk.
outcome_analysis: Datree raised about $11M across a 2018 seed and a February 2020 Series A while joining YC W20, but the YC directory lists it as inactive and an aggregator reports it stopped operating in July 2023. No company statement of the reason was found, so failure factors are left unassigned rather than guessed. Alternatives such as Kyverno and OPA remained active, and the open-source CLI was archived.

name: Daybreak Health
tags: Mental Health Tech; Consumer Health Services; Digital Health
one_liner: The first digital mental health system for youth
long_description: Daybreak offers comprehensive and clinically-validated online mental health services designed for youth, like teletherapy, psychiatry and digital education.  We partner with schools and pediatric groups to make access to services easy, and strive to deliver zero cost to the end consumer through insurance and government funding.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: School districts and pediatric groups that contract Daybreak, with insurers and government programs paying so that families pay little or nothing
problem: Kids and teens cannot get timely mental health care because of provider shortages and cost. Daybreak delivers teletherapy and psychiatry through schools and bills insurance or government funding.
business_model: B2B2C care delivery: school and health plan partnerships, with reimbursement from insurance and Medicaid
product_category: Youth digital mental health provider
founder_names: Alex Alvarado; Siddarth Cidambi; Luke Mercado
market_need_then: Youth mental health demand rose sharply in 2020 and schools lacked counselors. Daybreak began serving California schools in 2019 and the founders targeted zero cost to families through insurance and government funding.
outcome_analysis: Daybreak sold youth teletherapy through school partnerships and funded care via insurance and Medicaid, which gave it a distribution channel and a payer path that consumer mental health apps lacked. It raised a seed in early 2021, a 10M Series A in March 2022 and a 13M Series B led by Union Square Ventures in August 2023, reaching about 25M raised. No shutdown or acquisition is reported, and the Series A lead and seed amount differ across outlets.

name: Decentro
tags: Banking as a Service; Fintech; API
one_liner: API Platform for Banking Integrations (Plaid for India and APAC)
long_description:
Almost every company that has to integrate with the legacy financial institutions, faces several challenges when it comes to the product cycle. Not only are the APIs and documentations less available, but they are also old school and ridden with errors and loopholes. 

On top of that, the lack of a single point of contact from the underlying institutions, makes the already long integration cycle of 5 months feel like a temple run between different departments. And since those services break and update over time, you can imagine the nightmare in terms of coordination between the tech teams. 

We are a full-stack platform where you can come, select your desired modules, play in the sandbox, and launch your product with the APIs and SDKs within a couple of weeks! Not only that, but we also take care of all upcoming fixes, iterations, and updates without breaking any flow.

It's that easy, as it should be. Welcome to the future.
all_locations: Bengaluru, KA, India; Delhi, DL, India; Singapore, Singapore
regions: India; Singapore; South Asia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian and APAC fintechs, lenders, marketplaces and SaaS companies that need banking, KYC and payments integrations
problem: Integrating with legacy Indian banks and financial institutions takes months, with poor APIs and no single point of contact. Decentro packages those integrations as modular APIs and SDKs.
business_model: Usage-based API platform for banking, payments and KYC, plus payment aggregator revenue
product_category: Banking as a service API platform
market_need_then: TechCrunch's demo day coverage in August 2020 described Decentro as Plaid for India, with about 1M USD gross transaction volume, about 7,000 USD MRR, four customers and 45 more in the pipeline. India's fintech boom created demand for faster bank integrations.
outcome_analysis: Decentro is an active API banking platform in India founded by a repeat founder who previously sold Mypoolin. It raised a seed in 2020, a 4.7M USD Series A in November 2022 and a roughly 3.6M USD Series B in June 2025 while expanding into payments and licensing, including a payment aggregator and a GIFT City licence. Funding has been modest relative to rivals, and no exit, shutdown or layoffs were found.

name: Deep Meditate
tags: Mental Health Tech; Consumer Health Services
one_liner: Deep Meditate is an app that helps you de-stress, sleep, and…
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers seeking stress relief, sleep and relaxation, paying through app subscriptions and in-app purchases
problem: People need quick, simple tools to calm panic and sleep better. Deep Meditate offers short guided meditations, music and sleep aids in a mobile app.
business_model: Consumer mobile app with subscriptions and in-app purchases
product_category: Meditation, music and sleep app
market_need_then: Meditation and sleep apps were a proven consumer category by 2019, with Calm reporting more than 1 million paying subscribers. A founder post on Indie Hackers cited by a search summary reported over 1 million completed meditations by March 2020.
outcome_analysis: Deep Meditate is a solo founder meditation app that entered a category already led by Calm and Headspace. It reports early usage but no verified funding beyond YC, no traction after 2020 and a single listed founder under a former founders heading on the YC page. It appears still published in app stores, so the failure factors reflect stalling against better funded rivals rather than a confirmed shutdown, and the cause of stalling is inferred.

name: DeepSource
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Unified DevSecOps platform, helping developers ship good code.
long_description: DeepSource helps developers ship clean and secure software by automatically scanning their code and fixing it with Autofix™ AI. We're trusted by 7,000+ teams, from startups to Fortune 500s.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams, from startups to enterprises, wanting automated code review, security scanning and autofix in pull requests
problem: Teams ship bugs and security issues because code review is manual and static analysis tools are noisy and hard to set up.
business_model: B2B SaaS per developer seat with a free tier for open source and a 14 day trial
product_category: Developer tools, static analysis and code review
market_need_then: Static analysis was an established category (Codacy, Code Climate, SonarCloud), showing paid demand, and the founders aimed to do for code quality what Travis CI did for CI. Dated 2020 evidence is limited to the founders' stated goal.
outcome_analysis: DeepSource grew from a developer friendly code analysis tool to an AI code review and security platform trusted by over 7,000 teams per its own page, funded by a $2.6M seed in 2020. It stayed independent for six years in a crowded space and was acquired by Harness in September 2026 to join its autonomous SDLC platform, a strategic exit with no disclosed price.

name: Depict
one_liner: GPT Search & Merchandising for fashion e-commerce
regions: Sweden; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Fashion and other e-commerce brands and retailers that want product recommendations, search and merchandising without large behavior datasets
problem: Small and mid-size online stores lack the data to build Amazon quality recommendations. Depict models products from images and descriptions instead of customers, avoiding the cold start problem.
business_model: SaaS with performance linked pricing at launch (a cut of uplift after free A/B tests), now merchandising software subscriptions
product_category: E-commerce personalization, recommendations, search and merchandising
founder_names: Oliver Edholm; Anton Osika; Lonis Hamaili
market_need_then: In the Launch HN post, Depict argued smaller stores could not use collaborative filtering like Amazon and Netflix because they lack data, and reported 4 to 6 percent top-line uplift in A/B tests with early customers Staples Nordics and kitchentime.com.
outcome_analysis: Depict raised a 2.8M USD seed in 2021 and a 17M USD Series A led by Tiger Global in February 2022 on the strength of a data-light recommendation approach and unusually young technical founders. It added search and merchandising and now claims more than 350 brands. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, and one aggregator showing headcount decline is unverified.

name: Dialect
one_liner: Making internet experiences distributable and actionable everywhere
long_description:
Dialect is on a mission to organize the internet’s experiences and make them distributable and actionable everywhere. We’re doing this with blockchain links, or blinks, a new technology that lets businesses unbundle their product experiences from their apps and sites, allowing users to take instant, no-redirect actions wherever they are.

This technology is unique to blockchain today, but as the world moves onchain, it will redefine how we interact with the internet—everywhere.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Crypto wallets and apps, particularly on Solana, that need notifications, messaging and shareable onchain actions
problem: Onchain apps could not reach users with alerts or let them act without leaving the page, making crypto experiences clumsy.
business_model: B2B infrastructure and developer tooling, monetization unclear
product_category: Web3 messaging, notifications and blockchain links (blinks)
market_need_then: Web3 apps lacked notification channels and chat, an inferred gap; no dated demand data found for 2020. The product reached mainnet in 2022 and claimed integrations across Solana apps by 2023.
outcome_analysis: Dialect began in the Solana ecosystem with messaging and notifications, raised a $4.1M seed in March 2022 and later led the blinks and Actions launch with Solana in 2024. The YC directory marks it Acquired but no acquisition announcement was found, so the outcome and timing are unverified; its dependence on a single chain's fortunes was the main structural risk.

name: Ditto
one_liner: Manage the words across your team’s product from design to production.
long_description: Manage the words across your team’s product from design to production.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product design, content and engineering teams at software companies that manage UI copy
problem: Product copy is scattered across design files, code and spreadsheets, so changes are slow and inconsistent. Ditto centralizes copy as a single source of truth from design to production.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat (editors and commenters) with free tier and enterprise plans
product_category: Product copy and content design tooling
market_need_then: The founders described copy as the most under-leveraged part of building product. The Figma plugin launched in January 2020 and was featured by Figma that April, and the Product Hunt launch was on 2020-03-10.
outcome_analysis: Ditto began as a Figma plugin for managing product copy, raised a 1.5M USD seed in 2021, and grew to a claimed 8,000 teams while rebuilding the product around AI and a new brand. It then announced a 12.2M USD Series A led by Craft Ventures in January 2026. The long gap between seed and Series A suggests slow, capital efficient growth, but this is inferred, and exact revenue is not public.

name: DocVita
tags: Marketplace; Consumer Health Services; Telemedicine; Mental Health
one_liner: Telehealth provider for India.
long_description:
We make it easy for anyone in India to access healthcare over Zoom, Meet, or WhatsApp. We provide care in 11 local languages.

For every appointment, we provide a concierge who manages all logistics for the patient & handles the back-office work for doctors. With this, we have cracked the code to make telehealth work in India.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Urban Indian consumers seeking therapy and psychiatry consultations, who pay fees comparable to in-person visits
problem: Access to doctors and therapists in India is hard to navigate and logistics heavy. DocVita runs consultations over Zoom, Google Meet and WhatsApp with a concierge who handles scheduling and back office work.
business_model: Consumer healthcare marketplace and clinic: fee per consultation, with a take from provider fees
product_category: Telehealth and online mental health clinic
market_need_then: COVID-19 lockdowns in 2020 pushed Indian consumers toward telemedicine and mental health helplines. Traxcn data cited in coverage says Indian mental health startups raised about 20M USD between 2016 and 2020.
outcome_analysis: DocVita is a small Bengaluru telehealth company that narrowed from general consultations to therapy and psychiatry delivered over WhatsApp. Its public funding is limited to unverified aggregator figures of roughly 125K to 130K USD, so it looks like a slow-growing, capital light business rather than a venture scale raise. It is listed as active with about 14 people and no shutdown, sale or layoffs were found, and its stalling relative to VC backed peers is inferred.

name: Draftwise
one_liner: Contract and negotiation AI built for lawyers
long_description: Draftwise is redefining contract work for lawyers with AI that streamlines drafting, review, and negotiation. Draftwise empowers lawyers with  intelligent, data-driven tools that use a firm’s own knowledge base—drawing from past deals, preferred language, and internal guidance to improve the entire contract workflow—from first draft to signed deal.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Large law firms and in-house legal teams doing transactional work (M&A, finance, real estate)
problem: Lawyers spend many hours drafting and negotiating contracts from precedent, with high risk of error and poor access to past deals at drafting time. Draftwise suggests language and playbooks from the firm's own knowledge base.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS sold to law firms by seat or firm-wide license
product_category: Legal AI for contract drafting, review and negotiation
founder_names: James Ding; Emre Ozen; Ozan Yalti
market_need_then: TechCrunch's August 2020 demo day coverage said Draftwise claimed it could cut credit agreement drafting from about 30 hours to 10, had nearly half a dozen letters of intent from law firms and expected to charge big law firms over 500K USD a year.
outcome_analysis: Draftwise combined ex-Palantir engineers with a Stanford-trained former Clifford Chance lawyer and sold to big law with strategic law firm backing: Orrick joined the 2023 seed and Mishcon de Reya, Jones Day and Ropes & Gray later became partners. It raised a 5M USD seed in June 2023 and a 20M USD Series A led by Index in March 2024 after a long period without public rounds. No later round, exit or shutdown is reported through late 2026.

name: Drapr
one_liner: Try on clothing online
long_description: Drapr lets shoppers try on clothing, online. Apparel brands use Drapr to make more money online.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Berkeley, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Apparel brands and retailers wanting fewer returns and higher conversion, and their online shoppers
problem: Shoppers cannot tell how clothes will fit and look online, causing returns and abandoned carts.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to apparel brands
product_category: Virtual try-on and 3D avatar fit technology
founder_names: David Pastewka; Richard Berwick; Will Drevno
market_need_then: Online apparel returns were a known cost and the pandemic in 2020 accelerated online shopping; Gap framed the deal as reducing unnecessary returns. No dated spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Drapr's founders had built and sold a 3D scanning company earlier and returned to virtual try-on. Within about a year of the YC batch, Gap acquired the team and technology in August 2021 to improve fit and cut returns, a quick strategic exit likely close to an acqui-hire given the small team and tiny disclosed funding.

name: Dripos
one_liner: The only piece of software a coffee shop needs to operate.
long_description: Dripos is the only piece of software a coffee shop needs to run their business. We offer point of sale, employee scheduling, mobile ordering, and more to the 100,000 cafes in the United States.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent coffee shops and small cafes in the United States
problem: Coffee shop owners juggle many separate tools for ordering, payments, scheduling, marketing and payroll, and general restaurant POS systems are not built around coffee workflows.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payments and hardware (pricing starts at about $160 a month per the January 2026 Sprudge piece)
product_category: Vertical POS and operating system for coffee shops
market_need_then: The company says there are about 100,000 US cafes and that owners used 10 or more tools per shop. Dated 2020 demand evidence was not found beyond the YC listing.
outcome_analysis: Dripos grew from a Summer 2020 YC company into a vertical coffee shop operating system that claims over 3% of US coffee shops and raised an $11M Series A led by Base10 in April 2024. Its wedge was a coffee-specific all-in-one product against general POS vendors, and press reported fast growth in locations. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff reports were found as of the research date.

name: Dropbase
one_liner: AI app builder for internal tools. Build back-office software faster…
long_description:
