name: Dropprint Genomics
one_liner: The better way to run single cell genomics
long_description:
Who we are?
We write software that understands the activity of individual cells as opposed to all cells. This approach is novel because we are no longer looking at average signals and can be precise. It is like a police person trying to identify the speeding car, they won’t find it if they look at all the cars at once, rather they need to look at the speed of each individual car. This is the beauty of single cell genomics, we can now identify that speeding car.

Why now?
The biggest barrier for entry into the single cell genomics market are cost and data analysis. To that end, we have reduced the cost by 10-fold and built the computational infrastructure for scalability. Although single cell sequencing has only been around for about five years, we come from one of the top single cell genomics labs and were the first to process and analyze millions of immune cells. Thanks to our software solutions, we have been able to bring big data solutions to the immune system.

Where are we and where are we going?
We have generated a database of over 1 million immune cells spanning healthy, cancerous, and autoimmune immune cells and are growing through paid partnerships. Harnessing out database and ML software, we can take a data-centric approach for better target discovery. Fortunately, as our database continues to grow, our models will continue to learn for more precise, unbiased, and automated single cell genomics.

Thank you!

product_category: Single cell genomics software and data

outcome_analysis: Dropprint was a tiny team from a leading single cell lab with a database of over a million immune cells. Immunai acquired it in March 2021, shortly after raising $60M, to fold the data and the founders into its immune atlas and ML team, so the exit looks like a data and talent acquisition rather than a revenue business.

name: Easyplan
one_liner: An AI-driven investment app for beginner investors in India
long_description:
Easyplan is an investment app for beginner investors in India (kind of a cross between Betterment and Qapital in the US). We also provide users with a credit card secured by their investments. 

We launched with money market funds and have ~40,000 customers who’ve invested (~40% MoM growth). The pandemic spurred interest among new investors, and our AUM has grown 3x since April 2020. And we’ve done this with a cost of acquisition that is 10% of the industry average. 

Here’s the problem we see. Only 10% of the 100 million middle-income Indian workers have invested in the markets. This is despite the fact that they save ~30% of their income, making this a $325B potential market in assets under management. 

However, current investment apps in India are built for active investors. With over 16,000+ mutual funds and 5000+ stocks to choose from, they are far too complicated for beginners, who make up most of the market.

We’re building an AI - driven investment planning software that is designed for beginners. Users use our conversational AI to get diversified mutual fund portfolios tailored to their goals. We also offer users a credit card secured by their investments, so they can earn return without losing liquidity.

In terms of business model, we make commissions on the asset we manage, and interchange fees on the fund. We estimate we can make $12 per user per year, which is 6x our current acquisition cost of $2 per investor.

product_category: Consumer robo-style investing app with investment-backed credit card
market_need_then: The YC profile cites only about 10 percent of 100 million middle-income workers invested in markets and a pandemic surge in new investors in 2020.
outcome_analysis: Easyplan grew to about 40,000 investing customers by its YC batch on a customer acquisition cost the founders say was 10 percent of the industry average, then was acquired by neobank Jupiter in June 2021, which reported over 250,000 users. The directory marks it Inactive because it was absorbed rather than shut down. Price is undisclosed, so whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing is not known.

name: Equator Therapeutics
one_liner: We are developing a drug to burn calories and increase metabolism…
long_description:
We are developing a drug to increase metabolism and burn calories without exercise.

Obesity and type 2 diabetes have reached epidemic proportions. There are 2.2B overweight people and 500M people with type 2 diabetes worldwide, and these numbers increase drastically every year. Existing drugs are not effective enough to reverse the trend. Our drug can solve this problem, because it addresses the root cause of metabolic disorders – the imbalance between caloric intake and expenditure.

Our drug will target mitochondria – the powerhouse of the cell – to generate heat. This approach has been proven to fully reverse obesity and type 2 diabetes in animals. However, therapeutic application for humans was impossible, because mitochondrial heat production could only be induced by highly artificial methods with side effects. This changed after our recent breakthrough discovery of the protein that mitochondria naturally use to generate heat. We have developed a unique high-throughput drug discovery platform to identify compounds that selectively activate this target protein, without side effects.

For decades people have wanted a drug that burns calories like exercise does. We are realizing this dream at Equator Therapeutics.

product_category: Therapeutics, obesity and metabolic disease (mitochondrial thermogenesis)
founder_names: Jonah Sinick; Yuriy Kirichok; Liliya Khasin
market_need_then: The YC description cites 2.2B overweight people and 500M with type 2 diabetes worldwide and says existing drugs are not effective enough; these are company claims.
outcome_analysis: Equator Therapeutics is a very small, science led obesity drug developer from YC Winter 2020 that remains active with a small team and public funding signals limited to grants and aggregator listed small rounds. It has not shown clinical stage progress in public sources opened, so its outcome is still pending rather than a success or failure. The long timelines and capital needs of drug development are the main risk.

name: Explorex
one_liner: Ecosystem Platform for Restaurants in India
long_description:
Explorex — The Memory Layer for Physical Commerce

~90% of Indian retail happens in person, yet offline venues have no memory of their customers. Restaurants run on disconnected tools, and every visit ends with zero data captured. Explorex fixes this by owning both sides of the dining transaction.

At the center is Elite, our consumer app that is redefining how people dine out. Diners see live table availability, browse dynamic menus, order, and self-checkout instantly — no waiting, no interruptions. Behind it sits our infrastructure stack: Bridge OS (the full-stack restaurant operating system), Clyro (WhatsApp-native CRM), and ReserveX — all feeding a single behavioral data layer.

That data layer is what makes Explorex fundamentally different. Delivery platforms only see orders. We capture real-world, in-venue behavior — what people order, how long they stay, how groups behave, how menus perform, how experiences shape spending. Because we operate the restaurant OS and the consumer touchpoint, this data is irreplicable.

We're now building Elara, an AI dining concierge that turns this data into real-time decision-making — factoring intent, context, availability, and historical behavior. This moves us beyond discovery into becoming the intelligence layer for offline commerce.

Today, Explorex powers 250+ partner restaurants and 3M+ diners across Bangalore and Hyderabad, processing 8M+ transactions annually (18M+ lifetime), and operates at breakeven.

Explorex is not a SaaS tool — it is the infrastructure layer for offline dining, with AI and consumer experience at its core. Think Shopify for restaurants, on its way to becoming the UPI of restaurant operations.

name: Farmako Healthcare
tags: Health Tech; Delivery; Digital Health; Healthcare
one_liner: India's fastest medicine delivery in just 30 minutes
long_description:
We are India's fastest medicine delivery service. We deliver medicines in just 30 minutes. We have built highly optimized pharmacy stores and a set of internal tools designed to process prescriptions quickly.

We also provide easy-to-integrate APIs and SDK for anyone to start a virtual pharmacy without needing a license, pharmacy, or delivery fleet. Any doctor, teleconsultation app, or EMR provider can start delivering medicines to their patients on WhatsApp or App using our service in the background. We have more than 80 B2B partners, including India's top teleconsultation apps, EMR providers, hospitals, elderly care apps, and insurance providers.

We operate 24/7 in Gurgaon, New Delhi, and Moradabad and deliver over 15,000 orders monthly. So far, we have processed more than 250K orders and done thousands of life-saving deliveries.

We started in 2020 with the vision to build a centralized health record system for India. We had an AI-powered EMR app for doctors and a SaaS for diagnostic labs to add patients' medical records to Farmako Health ID. We have more than 3M health records added on Farmako. In 2022, the Indian government launched ABHA Health ID and we became one of the first official partners with them. In 2023, we launched quick medicine delivery and decided to move forward with ABHA Health ID for medical records.

Now, we are building a safe health assistant inside our medicine delivery app, which will be connected to your Health ID and all your past medical records. Our goal is to make it a super-safe and accurate health assistant for the world, which can eliminate your doctor in the long run for all primary care issues.

founder_names: Aman Bhandula; Kaishu Sahu; Nikhil Kumar
market_need_then: Inc42 (Dec 2020) reports about 1,500 doctors onboarded in a year with over 400 on a premium plan and about 300 medicine orders a day after adding delivery, company reported.

name: Felix Biotechnology
one_liner: We’re creating programmable therapies
long_description: We are building the first end-to-end digital viral design platform to protect the world against the coming threat of antimicrobial resistance.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Fieldguide
one_liner: Vertical AI for Audit & Advisory Firms
long_description: ‍Fieldguide is a vertical AI platform for modern audit and advisory firms that digitizes the end-to-end engagement workflow on a single platform. Built by former Big Four practitioners and experienced technology leaders, Fieldguide is trusted by top CPA firms to improve margins, win new business, and build stronger client relationships. We’re based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Goldman Sachs, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Y Combinator, Floodgate, Elad Gil, Justin Kan, Qasar Younis, Eric Ries, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: CPA, audit and advisory firms, including Big Four and top 100 US firms
problem: Audit and advisory engagements run on emails, spreadsheets and disconnected tools, which hurts margins, quality and client experience.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription sold to accounting firms
product_category: Audit and advisory engagement workflow software, now agentic AI
market_need_then: Founder Jin Chang had five years at EY and said he felt the pain of managing complex audit and advisory engagements; the profession faces an accountant shortage (Bloomberg coverage cited on the company blog, not opened).
outcome_analysis: Fieldguide is a standout of the batch: a practitioner founder built engagement workflow software for audit firms, raised a 17M Series A at 100M in 2022, 30M Series B in 2024 and 75M Series C at 700M in 2026, with 125M total reported. It sells to over half of the top 100 US accounting firms. Success came from founder market fit, an enterprise motion and the AI tailwind.

name: Fig
one_liner: Fig adds visual apps, shortcuts, and autocomplete to your terminal.
long_description:
Fig is re-imagining the terminal. We make it more accessible to beginners and more productive for advanced engineers

Our first product is autocomplete, but we plan to expand into a full App Store ecosystem for the Terminal. We can do a bunch of cool stuff, check out our website.

And if you're interested, we are hiring 😀
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software developers who work in the command line, paying for team and pro features
problem: Terminals are hard for beginners and slow for experts because commands, flags and arguments must be remembered.
business_model: Freemium developer tool with paid team subscriptions
product_category: Developer tools, terminal autocomplete
market_need_then: Developers lived in the terminal and a 2020 Product Hunt launch drew strong early interest; completion tools like zsh plugins existed but gave limited descriptions.
outcome_analysis: Fig reached developers through free product led growth and a 2.2 million dollar seed in 2020, then was acquired by AWS in August 2023 as Amazon pushed generative AI coding tools. Standalone Fig was later sunset and folded into Amazon Q. The Series A mentioned in a 2022 interview is not confirmed. The exit looks like a talent and technology deal, with price undisclosed.

name: Finch
one_liner: Finch is the Employment Data Platform
long_description: Finch is the API to access employment data systems. We allow admins to connect their company in a compliant and secure manner to trusted applications. Finch integrates across data providers enabling developers to access a previously closed system and are at the source of truth for employee data and money flow. Our API powers use cases across insurance, benefits, tax, finance, and HR applications.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software companies in insurance, benefits, tax, finance and HR that need employer payroll, HR and benefits data
problem: Employment and payroll data sits in hundreds of fragmented HRIS and payroll systems with no standard API, so every app builds and maintains many integrations.
business_model: Usage-based API with per-connection pricing, free developer tier and paid plans
product_category: Unified employment data API, HR and payroll infrastructure
market_need_then: TechCrunch (Dec 2020) reports 50 percent month over month growth in revenue and employers connected, with demand from fintech, lending and benefits apps that needed payroll data. Zhang describes many systems behind each provider.
outcome_analysis: Finch raised a 3.5M seed in December 2020, a 15M Series A in June 2022 and a 40M Series B in February 2023, for about 58.5M, and reported 12x revenue growth after the Series A and cash flow positive months. It reached over 100k employers connected by its own count. The unified employment API category grew as fintech and benefits apps needed payroll data, though rivals were also well funded.

name: Finlens
one_liner: AI Accounting for Founders & Accountants
long_description:
Finlens is an AI co-pilot for QuickBooks, built for founders and accounting firms who want faster closes, real-time visibility, and clean books without the spreadsheet chaos.

We automate categorisation, GAAP schedules, and collaboration, all on top of your existing QuickBooks setup. No migrations. No change management. Just a smarter way to work with the stack you already use.

Backed by Y Combinator (W20) and Accel.
Built by second-time founders who’ve seen the finance backend break — and decided to rebuild it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Today: startup founders and accounting firms using QuickBooks Online. At the Winter 2020 batch: unclear, possibly an India account aggregator under the Authlayer name
problem: Early stage accounting is manual and messy: categorising transactions, accruals, reconciliations and month end close take too much accountant time.
business_model: SaaS subscription for accounting firms and founders with a free start tier (per company site)
product_category: AI accounting copilot for QuickBooks Online
market_need_then: For the 2025 product, the American Bazaar launch article says founders and accounting firms described messy manual early stage accounting. Demand evidence for the 2020 product was not found.
outcome_analysis: Finlens is listed as active with six people and a QuickBooks AI copilot launched publicly in July 2025, with YC and Accel named as backers. The record is thin: the YC page says it was founded in 2024 although the batch is Winter 2020, and the founder previously built Authlayer, so the company probably changed product after the batch, but no source states a pivot or its dates. No funding amounts were found.

name: Finmark
one_liner: Financial planning software for startups
long_description: Finmark is financial planning software for startups.  We make it simple for companies to manage their runway, hiring, and cash.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startup founders and finance leads at early stage companies
problem: Startups modeled runway, hiring and cash in Excel, which was slow, error prone and hard to share with investors.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Financial planning and analysis software
founder_names: Rami Essaid; Greg Lissy; Jeremy Neuberger
market_need_then: Startup finance relied on spreadsheets and the company said it replaced Excel models; investor money was abundant in 2020 and 2021, which raised planning needs.
outcome_analysis: Finmark raised a 5 million dollar seed in October 2020 and a further 6.5 million led by American Express Ventures in January 2022, then sold to BILL in November 2022 as FP&A for small companies became a feature that payments platforms wanted. The founding CEO had a prior exit. Terms were not disclosed, so whether it was a strong exit is unknown.

name: FitnessAI
one_liner: App offering AI powered workout plans with anytime access to coaches
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Gym going consumers who want strength training plans, paying an app subscription
problem: Lifters did not know what weights, sets and reps to do to keep progressing and personal trainers were expensive.
business_model: Consumer subscription app
product_category: Consumer fitness app, AI workout planning
market_need_then: TechCrunch reported it passed 1M dollars in ARR heading into Demo Day in March 2020 while bootstrapped, which shows paying demand, and home workout interest rose that spring.
outcome_analysis: FitnessAI grew an AI workout planning app to over 1 million dollars of ARR before Demo Day in March 2020 with almost no outside money, built on the founder's own lifting data set. The YC directory marks it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or price was found; the current site shows FitnessAI Inc., with a terms link pointing to Moonset Labs, which could be the buyer but is unconfirmed.

name: Flint
one_liner: Securing Nurses for Your Future
long_description: We help hospitals 🏥 hire nurses 🧑🏻‍⚕️ from all around the world 🌏 and with technology make the complexity of immigration and licensing simple.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: US hospitals and healthcare facilities that pay to hire long term foreign nurses and other clinicians; candidates apply free
problem: Hospitals struggle to staff nurses, and recruiting nurses from abroad is slowed by immigration, licensing and credentialing complexity.
business_model: Placement fee paid by facilities for long term staff; Flint covers candidate immigration and licensing costs (per company site and a directory, unverified)
product_category: International nurse recruitment with immigration and licensing technology
market_need_then: Hospital nurse shortages and a backlog of foreign nurse green cards: the AAIHR estimated at least 10,000 foreign nurses held up by retrogression (2023 reporting, after the batch); no 2020 dated demand source was opened.
outcome_analysis: Flint is active with about 50 people per the YC page and works across 20 or more states per a YC job post. Funding is poorly documented: aggregators show roughly 4 to 5M raised with a seed dated October 2025, none confirmed by a primary source. The business depends on immigration visa availability, which was hit by retrogression delays after the batch. The outcome is unclear.

name: Flowdash
one_liner: Quickly build internal tools for your ops team's manual workflows
long_description: Flowdash makes it easy to build semi-automated workflows with no code. We recognize that many business processes today simply can't be fully automated and require human intuition. But there's no reason they need to be fully manual either. With Flowdash, teams can build custom tools to manage their internal processes, leveraging automation where it makes sense, and weaving in human intuition when needed.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Operations teams at small and mid sized companies
problem: Ops teams run manual workflows that need both automation and human judgment, and building internal tools needed engineers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: No code workflow and internal tools
market_need_then: No code tooling was growing in 2020 and ops teams lacked engineering help; specific spend data was not found.
outcome_analysis: Flowdash built a no code workflow tool for ops teams and raised a small reported amount, around 300 thousand dollars per CB Insights, before Notion acquired the team and shut the product down on 30 September 2022. The shutdown notice and the deal framing suggest a team acquisition without continuing the product, though the terms are undisclosed.

name: Flowglad
one_liner: Analyze, act, and automate across systems
long_description: A unified home for your team's cross-system automations, context, and knowledge.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software developers and small teams that need billing and payments (launch product); now teams wanting to connect AI agents to their apps
problem: Developers must wire Stripe style billing with webhooks and database syncing; later, teams need a controlled way to let AI agents act across their apps.
business_model: Payments and billing provider taking a percentage fee (claimed 3.55 percent all in) built on Stripe Connect; open source code (AGPL and MIT)
product_category: Open source billing and payments, later AI agent operating layer
market_need_then: Hacker News discussion (late 2025) shows developer interest in simpler billing, 405 points on the Show HN, and complaints about webhook glue code, though critics questioned the open source and processor claims.
outcome_analysis: Flowglad is a young company: the YC page lists it as founded in 2025 although its batch label is Winter 2020. It launched an open source billing product in late 2025, drew attention on Hacker News, and has since repositioned toward AI agent automation. Funding is only seen on PitchBook, so the outcome is too early to call and the pivot reasons are not public.

name: Fly.io
one_liner: Run full stack apps close to your users.
long_description: We run app servers and databases close to end users. Developers deploy their apps to Fly.io (it's about the simplest place to deploy a Docker Image) and use our CLI to launch instances in regions that are most important for their application.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers and small to mid-size engineering teams that want to deploy full stack apps and databases close to end users
problem: Deploying app servers near users worldwide was hard and expensive on traditional clouds, and CDNs only helped static content. Developers wanted a Heroku-like experience with global placement.
business_model: usage-based cloud infrastructure (VMs, bandwidth, storage billed by use)
product_category: developer cloud platform / edge application hosting
founder_names: Kurt Mackey; Jerome Gravel-Niquet; Michael Dwan
competitors_at_founding: Heroku; Cloudflare Workers; Google Cloud Run and AWS Fargate; StackPath
market_need_then: Founders grew up on Heroku and wanted low-latency global deploys; the launch thread drew strong interest in running app servers and databases near users beyond what CDNs offered.
outcome_analysis: Fly.io joined YC in Winter 2020 as a global Heroku and raised a $12M Series A in 2021, a $25M Series B in 2022 and a $70M Series C in 2023 at a reported $467M valuation. Heroku ending free tiers in 2022 helped adoption, while reliability complaints and outages are a recurring issue. The company remains active with no exit found.

name: Fondeadora
one_liner: We are connecting every single Mexican to the financial system.
long_description:
Fondeadora is the digital alternative to the traditional Mexican banking system. We know that the current system is broken and we want to fix it. Our mission is to free people from their banks by giving them back control over their money. We want to serve the 54 million Mexicans who are unhappy with their current banks and the 65 million of Mexicans who currently do not have a bank account.

Our first product is a mobile banking app and an international Mastercard debit card so you can spend, store and move your money seamlessly, completely fee-free.

Join us in this magical mystical ride.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Unbanked and underserved Mexican consumers, freelancers and small businesses who want a fee-free mobile bank account and debit card
problem: Many Mexicans have no bank account or are unhappy with high fees and slow service at traditional banks.
business_model: digital bank (interchange, deposits and lending; fee-free accounts for customers)
product_category: consumer neobank / challenger bank
market_need_then: The founders cited 54 million Mexicans unhappy with their banks and 65 million without an account; the company reported about 150,000 accounts and roughly $20M of new monthly deposits by 2020-08.
outcome_analysis: Fondeadora pivoted from crowdfunding to a licensed neobank in 2018, joined YC in Winter 2020 and raised a $14M Series A in 2020 plus a $14M extension in 2021. It remains active with 160 staff listed. Nu and other neobanks intensified competition, and later round sizes and dates conflict across databases.

name: Foreword
one_liner: A marketplace for live, online workshops for professionals
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Formal
one_liner: Least privilege for agents and humans
long_description: Formal lets your company put AI agents to work on sensitive data without losing control. It sees every connection your people and agents make, whether they run on endpoints or in the cloud, and understands exactly what each one is doing, down to the individual network call. It identifies every agent and the person behind it and enforces least privilege on each request, all from a single control plane, with no change to how anyone works. Credentials never reach agents, private data is masked before it leaves, and risky actions are stopped before they happen. Every session is recorded and replayable. Say yes to the business without saying yes to risk.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Security and platform teams at software companies that need least privilege access control over databases, internal APIs, infrastructure and AI agents
problem: Access permissions rarely match the work people and now AI agents actually need to do, so sensitive data is overexposed and hard to audit.
business_model: B2B SaaS security platform (proxies, PAM, policy control plane)
product_category: cybersecurity / access control and PAM for humans and AI agents
market_need_then: Growing data security and access governance demand; by 2024 customers such as Gusto, Notion and Ramp were named, and the 2025 to 2026 AI agent wave created new demand for agent least privilege.
outcome_analysis: Formal began as the YC company Maytana, pivoted to access security around 2023, raised a seed round led by Thrive Capital in late 2023 and came out of stealth in November 2024 with named customers such as Gusto, Notion and Ramp. In 2026 it sells network security for AI agents with customers like Cursor. No later round or exit was found, so the outcome is still open.

name: Future Fields
one_liner: We make unmakeable proteins with radical advanced biomanufacturing.
long_description: Future Fields has developed the world's first multicellular advanced biomanufacturing platform for the production of the most challenging recombinant proteins. We help companies in biotech, life sciences, and pharma by manufacturing their proteins.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Cultivated meat producers (early) and later biopharma, diagnostics, food and agriculture firms that need hard-to-make recombinant proteins
problem: Growth factors and media are the largest cost of cell-cultured meat, so producers could not reach price parity; Future Fields aimed to make growth factors cheaply and animal-free.
business_model: B2B sale of growth factors and custom recombinant proteins (product and service revenue)
product_category: biotech inputs / recombinant protein expression for cellular agriculture
founder_names: Matt Anderson-Baron; Jalene Anderson-Baron; Lejjy Gafour
market_need_then: GFI's 2020 data work (published 2021) identifies growth factors and recombinant proteins as the bulk of cultured meat media cost, and Bee Partners reportedly mapped about 60 cellular agriculture companies by 2021.
outcome_analysis: Future Fields joined YC in Summer 2020 with growth factors for cultured meat, raised a $2.2M seed led by Bee Partners in February 2021 and then widened its market to a fruit fly protein platform serving biopharma and agriculture. It is still active; later aggregator totals are inconsistent so the funding picture is incomplete and no exit is known.

name: Gas Pos
one_liner: Modern Point of Sale for Gas Stations and Truck Stops
long_description: We have taken an incredibly monopolized, overpriced, asset-heavy industry and flipped it on its head by providing a better, modern, affordable alternative with more functionality on a SaaS model.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent gas station owners and truck stop operators in the United States
problem: Independent retailers faced card network chip (EMV) and fraud requirements at the pump that cost tens of thousands of dollars per pump to meet, and fuel card fees at truck stops were high.
business_model: SaaS and hardware retrofit with no upfront cost and a small monthly fee (about $200 per month plus 2% of card transactions for the truck stop product, per 2019 press)
product_category: fintech infrastructure / fuel point of sale and pump payment upgrades
market_need_then: Card networks required chip acceptance at the pump with an October 2020 liability shift date (later extended per some sources); independents faced estimates of $80,000 to $160,000 to upgrade, and the CEO called skimming out of control.
outcome_analysis: Gas Pos began in Birmingham, graduated from a 2018 FIS accelerator, raised $1M from Merus Capital in 2018 and joined YC in Winter 2020 with a card-network driven pump upgrade and a truck stop payments product. The company is listed as active, but no later rounds, growth data or exit were found, so the outcome is unclear.

name: Gather
one_liner: Project management software for People Operations
long_description: Gather is software that helps high-growth teams build and execute their onboarding, offboarding, and other People Operations programs. Gather replaces manual coordination with smart, automated communication powered by a deep integration with Slack.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: HR and People Operations teams at high growth, Slack based companies
problem: People Ops teams coordinate onboarding, offboarding and other programs manually across people and tools, which is slow and error prone.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: People Operations workflow software in Slack
founder_names: John Wetzel; Alex Hilleary; Brooks Sime
market_need_then: Remote work in 2020 made onboarding and offboarding coordination harder and drove adoption of Slack centered tooling.
outcome_analysis: Gather was a six person YC S20 team building Slack native People Ops workflows. It raised a small seed in September 2020 and was acquired by ChartHop in March 2022, with terms undisclosed, giving ChartHop automated workflows. The founders joined ChartHop. This reads as a modest soft landing exit with a small funding footprint rather than a breakout, and the generic name collided with other Gather companies.

name: Genecis Bio
one_liner: Makes guilt-free plastics from food waste
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Packaging, consumer goods, textile, automotive and medical manufacturers that want biodegradable PHA plastics
problem: Petroleum plastics pollute and existing bioplastics were costly; Genecis uses bacteria to turn food waste into PHA polymers at a lower target price.
business_model: Materials producer: sells PHA resin and polymer development services, plus consumer brands built on its materials
product_category: biomaterials / biodegradable plastics (PHA) from food waste
market_need_then: Regulatory and consumer pressure on single-use plastics; Genecis claimed an 80 percent emissions cut and a price target 30 to 40 percent below market PHA, and partners such as Sodexo and BASF appear in its materials.
outcome_analysis: Genecis grew out of a University of Toronto lab, joined YC in Winter 2020 with a pilot making about 1 kg of PHA per week and a Canadian government grant, then raised a Series A of $7M plus a $3M credit facility in August 2022 led by Khosla Ventures and BDC. It is still active with over 40 staff, but no exit or later round was found in primary sources.

name: General Proximity
one_liner: The next generation of induced-proximity medicines.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharmaceutical partners and its own pipeline targeting undruggable proteins in cancer, cardiometabolic disease, neurodegeneration and longevity
problem: Many disease proteins cannot be drugged by conventional inhibitors; induced proximity drugs need the right effector protein for each target, which was found by trial and error.
business_model: Biotech drug discovery platform: own pipeline plus pharma collaborations (milestones and royalties, terms not disclosed)
product_category: biotech / induced proximity drug discovery platform (OmniTAC)
market_need_then: Investors poured money into targeted protein degradation in early 2020 (Kymera $102M and Nurix about $120M in the same month), and a 2020 Business Insider piece cited over a billion dollars invested in the field.
outcome_analysis: General Proximity was a Winter 2020 YC company that stayed in stealth for years, then emerged in January 2025 with a $16M seed led by Felicis, signed an oncology collaboration with Daiichi Sankyo in November 2025 and reported a $12M round in July 2026. The founder's prior work on Abide and Vividion IP gave strong domain fit. No exit has occurred and the story is still developing.

name: Gilgamesh Pharmaceuticals
one_liner: Gilgamesh Pharmaceuticals, a Clinical stage biotechnology company…
long_description: Gilgamesh is a pioneering, clinical stage mental health science-focused biotechnology company. We have a disciplined focus on developing innovative new chemical entities (NCEs) leveraging a unique combination of medicinal chemistry, intellectual property strategy, neuroscience & neurobiology, and drug development expertise. We are an experienced team, with proven success in biotech exits and inventions.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: pharmaceutical partners and acquirers; ultimately patients with depression and other mental-health disorders
problem: Existing treatments for depression and other psychiatric disorders work poorly for many patients; the company designs new chemical entities based on psychedelic chemistry to improve efficacy and duration.
business_model: drug development funded by venture capital, with value realised through licensing and sale of programs to pharma
product_category: clinical-stage biotech: psychedelic-derived therapeutics for mental health
founder_names: Jonathan Sporn; Andrew Kruegel; Dalibor Sames
market_need_then: Depression treatment gaps and a 2020 investor wave into psychedelic medicine (Compass and MindMed listings) created demand for differentiated compounds.
outcome_analysis: Gilgamesh combined an experienced psychiatry and medicinal-chemistry founding team with new chemical entities, raised a $39M Series B led by Prime Movers Lab in December 2022, and produced Phase 2 data for bretisilocin. AbbVie then partnered in 2024 and agreed in August 2025 to buy the program for up to $1.2B, an outcome driven by technical results and IP rather than a company-wide exit; the remaining team continues in a spin-out.

name: GiveAway
one_liner: Community driven marketplace for used things
long_description: We help to get rid of the things in your house that are no longer needed without spending any time or money. Our users bid on your items with virtual coins and can often find great products up to 95% off.
all_locations: Lisbon, Lisbon, Portugal; Minsk, Minsk Region, Belarus; Remote
regions: Portugal; Belarus; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers in Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan and the US who want to give away or get used items nearby; planned enterprise product for companies
problem: People have unwanted items but no easy, hyperlocal way to pass them on; existing buy and sell or donation platforms were not built around giving.
business_model: consumer marketplace with a virtual currency (Karma coins bought in app, about 30 percent of Karma per TechCrunch) plus ads; planned enterprise recycling product
product_category: consumer peer-to-peer marketplace for used goods (giveaway and auction with virtual coins)
founder_names: Sergei Lepchenkov; Artem Artemiuk; Siarhei Stasilovich
market_need_then: Founders were inspired by a store in Austria letting customers take one free item; the app reported over 1 million users and about 400,000 completed item transactions by 2020-09.
outcome_analysis: GiveAway grew fast in Belarus and neighbouring markets, reaching over 1 million users in 2020, but the company was unprofitable in September 2020 and monetised only through Karma purchases and ads. Third-party app trackers show the iOS app removed and not actively promoted by 2022, and no later funding beyond YC was confirmed, so the outcome looks like a stall. The generic English name and weak monetisation are plausible but not confirmed causes.

name: Glimpse
one_liner: A social video chat.
long_description: Deeply engage groups of 4 to 400,000 through 1-on-1 video chats. Match back to back for round-robin chats or use typed rooms for enhanced pairings. Play games, take pictures, and more!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers and friend groups, later teams and event organizers running Zoom networking
problem: Group video calls were awkward; people wanted short one on one conversations with friends, and later events needed round robin networking.
business_model: Free consumer app, later B2B event tool
product_category: Social video chat
market_need_then: Pandemic lockdowns in March 2020 drove a surge in video chat; Houseparty reportedly grew to about 200 million users by March 2020, showing consumer demand for social video.
outcome_analysis: Glimpse began as a Chatroulette style prototype, was reworked into friend video chats, and then pivoted to group matching for events in 2020 after the pandemic lifted video demand. Twine acquired it in February 2022 and the Glimpse tool became twine for Zoom. No funding was found for the YC company and the price is undisclosed, so whether it was a success or soft landing is unclear.

name: Glimpse
one_liner: Glimpse is the system of action for CPG retail operations
long_description:
Glimpse is the leading AI platform for CPG brands - automating key back office workflows like deductions management, revenue recovery, & cash application to increase operating leverage and put millions of dollars back into a brand's pocket. 

Our agents automatically retrieve deduction data, validate charges, automate cash application, and dispute invalid claims to recover lost revenue—often starting with a lookback of the past year of deductions. For a $1B CPG, one agent reviewed 17,000 deductions in under 24 hours (work that would take an FTE ~2 years), identifying $10M+ in revenue and driving meaningful margin expansion. Pricing is simple and incentive-aligned, structured to create clear P&L impact from day one.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer packaged goods brands that lose money to retailer deductions (today); at founding, DTC brands paying Airbnb hosts to place products
problem: Today: CPG brands lose revenue to invalid retailer deductions and spend heavy manual labor on cash application. At founding: DTC brands wanted awareness and sampling, and Airbnb hosts wanted extra income.
business_model: Today: software for CPG back offices, priced to the revenue recovered. At founding: commission to hosts on sales driven from product placement in short term rentals.
product_category: AI back office automation for CPG retail operations (originally Airbnb product placement marketplace)
founder_names: Akash Raju; Anuj Mehta; Kushal Negi
market_need_then: In 2020 DTC brands wanted cheap awareness and sampling and the founders saw it at campus pop-ups. About 750 properties joined by July 2020 with many booked through September, but launch landed just before COVID travel disruption.
outcome_analysis: Glimpse launched an Airbnb product placement marketplace in March 2020 with about 750 properties, then lost momentum when COVID hit travel and, in the founders' words, never found product market fit. By 2024 it hard pivoted to AI agents that dispute invalid retailer deductions for CPG brands, raised a $10M round led by 8VC in April 2025 and a $35M Series A led by a16z in March 2026, and reports 200+ brand customers. The pivot, not the original idea, is the success story.

name: Glisten AI
one_liner: Glisten AI automatically categorizes and tags e-commerce product data.
long_description: Glisten AI automatically categorizes and tags product data. With Glisten AI, e-commerce retailers and marketplaces can taxonomize millions of products with ease to enable better search, filtering, recommendations, and analytics.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Global Belly
tags: Marketplace; Consumer; Social; Food Tech; Creator Economy
one_liner: Marketplace enabling social commerce for brands and content creators.
long_description:
Global Belly is a platform that helps creators and content companies add shoppable products to their content and monetize their audience. We drive social commerce for partnering brands, by matching their products to relevant content. 
We take care of technology, analytics and operations so that content creators can easily 
 create and start selling unique physical and virtual offerings in a matter of minutes. Global Belly has launched 100+ influencers in the food space and shipped thousands of products nationwide. Global Belly's co-founders are Ankita Sharma and Madhuri Sharma (unrelated). Ankita has a Masters in Computer Science (Carnegie Mellon) and MBA (NYU Stern) and experience working at Apple and Bloomberg. Madhuri brings the culinary and content marketing skills to the team, with a B.S in Film & Television (Boston University), a Culinary Arts degree (Institute of Culinary Education) and experience at Grey Global Group and The Food Network.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Grain
one_liner: Grain transforms the debit card you already have into a credit card…
long_description: Grain is a mobile app that transforms the debit card you already have into a credit card by linking it to a line of credit based on your cash flow. For the millennials, Gen Zs, and immigrants who are afraid of falling into crippling credit card debt, there is now a distinct market opportunity to offer an alternative to how these 100M people access and manage credit.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Oakland, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Younger and immigrant consumers with thin or damaged credit who want a credit line without a traditional card
problem: Many people lack credit history or fear credit card debt, so they cannot build credit safely. Grain linked a debit card to a revolving line of credit sized on cash flow.
business_model: Consumer revolving credit line and interest or fees, originated through a partner bank
product_category: Consumer fintech credit builder
founder_names: Christian-Robert Joseph; Carl-Alain Memnon; Patrick De Suza
market_need_then: Fair Isaac estimated about 53 million US adults lacked enough credit history to be scored (NBC News, May 2019). Grain's June 2020 Ponce Bank partnership targeted customers with little or damaged credit.
outcome_analysis: Grain launched a debit linked credit line, signed a Ponce Bank lending partnership in June 2020 and is listed as active on the YC page, but verifiable funding and revenue facts are missing. Search results suggest later stress: Ponce reported fraud related loan buybacks in 2022 and a third party blog claims the consumer app was shut down by 2025 or 2026, though another review dated April 2026 still describes the app as live. With no confirmed shutdown or rounds, the outcome is unresolved.

name: GuruHotel
one_liner: AI-native direct booking infrastructure for global hospitality
long_description:
GuruHotel is building the AI-native booking protocol that will power direct hotel reservations in the next decade, effectively becoming "Stripe for hotel bookings" and ending OTAs' $370B stranglehold on hospitality distribution.

For 25 years, hotel ecommerce has been broken. Independent hotels lack the infrastructure to sell directly online, forcing them to pay OTAs 20-40% commissions on 40-60% of their bookings. Hotel websites don't convert (<0.5% vs. 5-10% in modern ecommerce), booking engines redirect users, payments are fragmented, and inventory is trapped in legacy PMS systems.

More critically: AI agents cannot book hotels directly today. ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, none can complete a hotel transaction end-to-end because inventory isn't exposed in a machine-readable format.

GuruHotel has built the complete solution: a full-stack ecommerce platform (website + native booking engine + checkout + payments + AI-ready APIs) that integrates directly with hotel PMS systems, enabling both humans and AI agents to book directly.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Independent hotels in Mexico and the Caribbean (later US and Europe) that pay OTA commissions
problem: Independent hotels pay OTAs 15 to 40 percent commissions and lack tools to sell directly online. GuruHotel gave them a direct booking website and engine at a lower fee.
business_model: Commission on direct bookings (5 percent per Bloomberg Linea coverage) plus platform fees
product_category: Hotel direct booking platform
founder_names: Josué Gio; Stiven Martinez; Jorge Flores Acevedo
market_need_then: Hotels paid OTA commissions of about 15 to 40 percent (Bloomberg Linea Dec 2021). The pandemic hit shortly after the batch, and a pre-seed reportedly kept the company alive.
outcome_analysis: GuruHotel went through YC in early 2020, survived the pandemic on a small pre-seed, raised a $2.1M seed in December 2021 led by Anthemis and reported around 160 hotels. It is listed as active with a team of 12 and now repositions as AI native direct booking infrastructure, but no later round or exit was found, so growth since 2021 is unverified.

name: H1
one_liner: Connecting stakeholders across the healthcare ecosystem.
long_description: H1 helps connect the healthcare ecosystem by providing a global platform of every healthcare professional and healthcare organization.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Life sciences companies, payers and providers that need data on doctors and healthcare organizations
problem: Information about healthcare professionals is fragmented, so pharma and others struggle to find the right doctor for trials, outreach and network building.
business_model: B2B data and software subscriptions
product_category: Healthcare professional and organization data platform
market_need_then: Life sciences and payers wanted to identify clinicians for trials and outreach. By April 2020 H1 had more than 8 million profiles and revenue, and investors funded a $12.9M Series A within months of YC.
outcome_analysis: H1 sold data on healthcare professionals to life sciences firms, raised $12.9M Series A in April 2020 and a $58M Series B in December 2020, then a $100M Series C in November 2021 with a 2022 extension, and grew to about 500 staff. Its proprietary database and pharma sales motion drove rapid funding, and it later made several acquisitions. It is active with no exit.

name: HENRY
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; B2B; Recruiting; Latin America; Talent Acquisition
one_liner: We train AI engineers and connect them with companies.
long_description: AI Engineers, ML+ Data Scientists, AI Product Engineers. We also help companies accelerate AI Adoption.
regions: Argentina; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Spanish speaking aspiring developers in Latin America (students), and companies hiring remote tech talent
problem: Latin America has far more software openings than trained engineers, and training is unaffordable upfront. Henry trained students at zero upfront cost and recovered a share of future income.
business_model: Income share agreement bootcamp (15 percent of salary for 24 months, capped, per 2020 coverage), later a hiring fee from employers
product_category: Tech bootcamp and talent marketplace
founder_names: Martin Borchardt; Luz Borchardt; Manuel Barna Ferrés; Leonardo Maglia; Antonio Tralice
market_need_then: Henry cited about 1 million software openings in Latin America against fewer than 100,000 trained professionals (TechCrunch Dec 2020), with 800+ students enrolled within months of its March 2020 launch.
outcome_analysis: Henry launched in March 2020, enrolled 800+ students quickly, raised $1.5M seed in December 2020 and a $10M Series A in May 2022, reaching 5,000+ students and 1,000+ hiring companies. It now claims 20K graduates and sells vetted AI talent to employers. No exit or later round was found, so the story is steady growth for a Latin American edtech with a model proven by Lambda School.

name: Handl
one_liner: Handl converts documents (invoices, income stabs, custom forms, etc.)…
long_description: Handl converts documents (invoices, income stabs, custom forms, etc.)  into structured data through simple API. 100% automation implies no need for any supervision/manual work on your side and allows you to reduce costs, improve response time, and operate accurate data. Powered by the merge of ML/AI + humans-in-the-loop to work in real-time even for the most complicated cases
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Fintech, lending and insurance firms that process invoices, income statements and claims documents
problem: Companies need structured data from messy documents; Handl combined machine learning with human review behind an API for full automation.
business_model: Usage based document processing API with human in the loop
product_category: Document AI and intelligent document processing
market_need_then: Back office document entry was a known manual cost for lenders and fintechs, and Rossum raised a seed in November 2019 on the same pain.
outcome_analysis: Handl is listed as active with 29 people and a San Francisco base, but no verified rounds, revenue or exit were found. Search results show it later narrowed toward insurance claims and medico-legal documents. Without press or funding evidence the outcome is unclear and it appears to be a quiet niche document AI vendor.

name: Handoff
tags: Machine Learning; Construction; B2B; Proptech; API
one_liner: AI estimator & agent for remodelers.
long_description:
Handoff creates instant construction estimates and automates business operations for contractors with AI.

Using generative AI technology and access to localized construction costs, Handoff provides remodelers with a fast, accurate, and intuitive way to create construction cost estimates in minutes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Residential remodelers, builders and trade contractors; originally construction firms buying cost data (as 1build)
problem: Construction pricing is volatile and the industry relied on annual cost books. The company offered live cost data, then AI estimating and back office tools for small contractors.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for estimating and project operations
product_category: Construction cost data and AI estimating
market_need_then: The launch post cites lumber rising about 400 percent before crashing in 2021 and an industry still using annual cost books. Usage fell 50 percent in the first 30 days of COVID before subscription revenue rose 7x in 10 months (TechCrunch Sep 2021).
outcome_analysis: Handoff began as 1build, a cost data company, raised a seed led by Initialized and a $14.5M Series A led by Greycroft in September 2021 after subscription revenue grew 7x in ten months. It renamed to Handoff and added a $5.8M strategic round from Nemetschek and Masco in June 2025, claiming 10,000+ monthly users. It is active, small at about 20 people, with no exit.

name: Haven
one_liner: Homeownership reimagined for the 21st century.
long_description:
Haven is re-imagining the $11 trillion U.S. mortgage industry, with a focus on engaging the 53 million homeowners with a mortgage. The incumbent technologies used by mortgage lenders and servicers are decades old, and the borrowers who are served by them increasingly demand modern digital experiences and frictionless financial products throughout the home journey. Haven’s mission is to deliver them at a transformational scale, and to improve lives in one of the world’s largest asset classes.

The company is well capitalized and backed by top fintech and mortgage venture funds and led by seasoned veterans of tech startups and financial marketplaces.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mortgage servicers, subservicers and lenders (later); at founding, homeowners with a mortgage
problem: Homeowners found life after closing a black box and servicers used decades old technology. Haven built a digital relationship and servicing platform to engage borrowers and increase servicing returns.
business_model: B2B SaaS and engagement revenue shared with mortgage servicers
product_category: Mortgage servicing fintech
founder_names: Nipun Kant; Aditya Acharya; Jonathan Chao
market_need_then: The company says first time buyers found post move in a black box, and the YC description cites $11 trillion in US mortgages and 53 million homeowners with a mortgage.
outcome_analysis: Haven came through YC in winter 2020 targeting homeowners and mortgage servicing, raised an $8M Series A led by Fifth Wall in November 2022 and now sells a white label engagement platform to servicers with claims of 1.4M homeowners. It is active with 15 people and no later round was found, so it looks like a modest, capital efficient B2B business.

name: Healthlane
one_liner: Africa's Preventative Health System
long_description: Rebuilding Africa's health system, with focus on prevention this time
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Urban middle-class consumers in Lagos and Cameroon who pay out of pocket for health checkups and screening
problem: Health systems in Africa focus on treating illness late. Healthlane tried to give people preventive checkups, screening and follow-up through an app plus its own diagnostic and clinic network.
business_model: Consumer subscription and pay per checkup, plus owned physical diagnostic centers
product_category: Preventive healthcare app and diagnostic network
market_need_then: Techpoint's 2020 coverage described Africa's health systems as treatment-focused and under-supplied, and the founders argued prevention was neglected. No usage numbers were found for 2020.
outcome_analysis: Healthlane raised about $2.4 million in 2020 and opened a Lagos launch in November 2021 with owned facilities. By Techpoint's 2022 reporting, anonymous sources said there was no clear sales or marketing direction, high facility costs, unpaid salaries from December 2021, and alleged misuse of funds, which the CEO disputed. The Nigerian site closed in mid 2022, the app stopped working in September 2022, and the Cameroon office closed in early 2023. The cause is allegation based and not a formal post-mortem.

name: Hellometer
one_liner: Making fast food faster
long_description:
Hellometer helps fast food owners' grow same store sales using security cameras to improve customer wait times.

Speed of service is fast food's core value proposition (it’s literally in the name) and owners currently don't have a reliable way to measure it. We show them when and where they have slowdowns and for every 7s they improve service times, owners see 1% increase in revenue.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Quick-service restaurant franchisees and chains that run drive-thrus and dining rooms
problem: Fast food owners could not reliably measure speed of service. Hellometer uses cameras and computer vision to time each car and guest and show where slowdowns occur.
business_model: B2B SaaS per location, with camera hardware
product_category: Computer vision operations analytics for restaurants
market_need_then: The company states that every 7 seconds of service improvement lifts same-store revenue about 1%, and that owners had no reliable measurement. A QSR trade study reported timer stores were about 30 seconds faster.
outcome_analysis: Hellometer remains an operating company with a small team. It expanded from drive-thru timers to lobby timers, loss prevention and kitchen monitoring and lists customers including Subway, Carl's Jr. and Church's Chicken. Funding is not publicly verified, so growth is judged only from product breadth and a 2023 Intel partnership.

name: Hellosaurus
one_liner: Interactive video platform for kids
long_description:
[Hellosaurus](http://www.hellosaurus.com) is an interactive video platform for kids filled with stories they can actually play instead of just watch. Top kids media creators and popular YouTube stars are already making content for our platform and transforming screen time into an active and fun experience. 

Hellosaurus is developing software tools for creators of high-quality kids programming to make truly participatory shows and a single distribution platform to share these creations with families everywhere. Experts in early childhood education have long stressed the importance of play for healthy cognitive and social development, and Hellosaurus supports this by empowering content creators to build enriching, interactive shows that engage kids as active participants rather than passive viewers.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Parents of children aged 2 to 8 (subscription) and kids media creators who publish interactive shows
problem: Kids spend screen time passively watching video. Hellosaurus made shows that respond to taps, swipes and spoken answers, and gave creators tools to build them.
business_model: Consumer subscription app plus creator tools and revenue share for kids content creators
product_category: Interactive video platform for kids
market_need_then: Pandemic-era 2020 raised parent concern about passive screen time and demand for kids content, but the sources found show no hard demand data.
outcome_analysis: Hellosaurus raised a 3.5 million dollar seed from General Catalyst in November 2020 alongside its app beta and signed well known kids creators. It did not become a standalone business and was acquired by Brilliant in December 2022, which wanted the Creator Studio for interactive lessons. The price is undisclosed, so whether this was a soft landing or a real outcome is unknown.

name: HelpNow
one_liner: India's most reliable Ambulance service. (uber for ambulances)
long_description: We are creating an aggregated network of Ambulances, and "MedCabs", i.e. ridesharing cabs converted into Medical first responder network, to drastically reduce medical help arrival time in India and save 70,000+ lives daily.
regions: India; South Asia

name: Hent
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: Hent is helping land lot developers to better manage their sales…
long_description: Hent is helping land lot developers to better manage their sales receivables and streamline their processes by securing access to capital and connecting all the stakeholders involved.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Brazilian land lot developers (loteadores) and real estate developers who sell lots on installment plans
problem: Lot developers sell on long installment plans and struggle to manage and collect receivables and to get working capital against them. Hent automated collections and lent against the receivables.
business_model: Receivables management software plus credit and receivables advances to developers (fintech take on lending)
product_category: Proptech fintech: receivables management and credit
founder_names: Leo Pinho; Thiago Diniz; David Aragao
market_need_then: Brazilian lot developers depend on installment receivables and had limited access to bank credit. Press in 2020 and 2021 described fast growth as the real estate sector heated up.
outcome_analysis: Hent was founded in Recife in 2019 by repeat founders with prior exits in receivables and ticketing, and it targeted lot developers who live off installment receivables. It raised a seed led by Canary in 2020 and a small Virgo Ventures round in 2021, and press reported rapid growth. A founder bio on the YC page says it was later acquired by Arke, but the date, price and terms are not public, and the company site still showed independent branding in 2023.

name: Here
one_liner: Where friends watch, play and hang together in digital rooms
long_description: Here is where friends feel close even if they're worlds away.  We do this by providing an infinite and interactive canvas where friends watch, play, decorate, draw and hang together, all powered by our own real-time video and voice technology.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Heron
one_liner: Underwriting automation for small business finance
long_description: Heron is on a mission to eliminate the underwriting tax on American businesses. When a consumer applies for credit, a spinning wheel can return an offer in seconds; when a business applies for a loan or insurance policy, humans still spend hours reading documents, verifying the business, detecting fraud, and deciding what to offer. Heron does that work in software: lenders, insurers, and credit brokers send applications in and get declines and offers out in minutes instead of days. We have underwritten roughly 1 in 8 US employer businesses in the past year. That scale allows us to go beyond what any individual could ever do: identify cross-customer signals across millions of businesses to build new data products, and ultimately become the data layer for private businesses in the US. Backed by Insight Partners and Y Combinator.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Lenders, insurers and credit brokers (originally fintechs needing bank transaction categorisation)
problem: Understanding bank transaction and business documents takes human underwriters hours. Heron started with categorising and enriching bank transaction data and moved to automating underwriting.
business_model: B2B usage based API and SaaS
product_category: Underwriting and financial data automation
founder_names: Johannes Jaeckle; Dominic Kwok; Jamie Parker
market_need_then: Fintechs and lenders were processing raw open banking data. The launch post says Heron's founders hit the problem in their own earlier fintech, and Heron later reported 150 to 200 plus funders and fintechs as customers.
outcome_analysis: Heron raised $1.2 million pre-seed after YC in September 2020, then reportedly pivoted in 2023 from bank data categorisation to AI document automation for underwriting. A $16 million Series A led by Insight Partners followed in July 2025, with the company citing more than 150 customers and underwriting about one in eight US employer businesses. The product fit appears to have come from the pivot rather than the first wedge.

name: Hideout
one_liner: A portfolio of delivery-only restaurant brands
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Hiration
one_liner: We help job seekers quickly create resumes that get 2X more interviews
long_description:
Our SaaS product solves the different problems that job seekers face in the process of finding a new job - creating an efficient resume, writing a cover letter/email, updating their LinkedIn profile, applying to suitable jobs, interview preparation...
It's the 1st time in history that we've been able to create resumes using technology that surpass human made resumes.
This is a novel way to add active job seekers to our database of resumes as none of the incumbents are focussing on candidates' problems.
100k+ new active job seekers are added to our database every month, growing rapidly.
As the next step, we are launching a recruitment marketplace to close the loop.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Individual job seekers in India and the US who pay for resume building, reviews and interview prep
problem: Job seekers struggle to create effective resumes, cover letters and LinkedIn profiles. Hiration offers a low cost software product plus paid reviews to fix this.
business_model: B2C subscription and paid services (resume review and rewrite)
product_category: Resume builder and career platform
market_need_then: The YC page cites 100k+ new active job seekers added each month, which is the company's own claim. No third party demand evidence dated 2020 was found.
outcome_analysis: Hiration is still operating and reports millions of users. After YC in early 2020 it raised about $3 million in August 2021 from Prime Venture Partners, Venture Highway and Y Combinator to scale in India and the US. No later round was found, and the company moved from resume builder to an AI career platform.

name: HireSweet
one_liner: A talent acquisition software built for data-driven recruiting teams.
all_locations: Paris, Île-de-France, France; San Francisco, CA, USA
regions: France; United States of America; Europe; America / Canada
target_customer: Tech and data driven recruiting teams hiring engineers and other passive candidates
problem: Finding qualified candidates who are not actively job hunting is slow with LinkedIn searches and agencies.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for sourcing, CRM and candidate marketplace
product_category: Recruiting software and sourcing
founder_names: Paul Bachelier; Ismael Belghiti; Robin Choy
market_need_then: Customers named by TechCrunch in March 2020 included BlaBlaCar, Dashlane and Nokia, with about 100 US customers and about 30 employees.
outcome_analysis: HireSweet raised EUR 1.5M in October 2017 from Kima, GFC and Bpifrance, joined YC in Winter 2020, expanded to the US, and was still active with a team of 27 in 2026. Funding after the seed is unclear, so how large it became is not established.

name: Homestead
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: Homestead is a real estate development platform for homeowners
long_description: Homestead enables homeowners to become their own real estate developer. We're empowering homeowners, allowing them to take advantage of California's new $6T regulatory opportunity: SB9. SB9 allows homeowners to split their lots in half, build a new unit, and sell it on the open market. Use our website to see if a property qualifies for our services.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Hoss
one_liner: The developer experience platform
long_description: Hoss is a developer experience platform that gives teams the essential tools they need to deliver a world-class customer experience. API-driven companies like Xendit, AssemblyAI, and Zentail trust Hoss to help them better acquire, understand, and support their customers. With Hoss, teams can offer superior documentation and developer content, gain deep visibility into how customers are using their API, monitoring third-party APIs, and provide robust and customizable developer dashboards. Hoss is backed by top investors like Y Combinator, Liquid2, FundersClub, and Soma Capital.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: API-driven companies (named customers Xendit, AssemblyAI, Zentail) that need developer docs, usage analytics and dashboards
problem: Companies with APIs lacked good documentation, visibility into how customers use the API and monitoring of third-party APIs. Hoss bundled docs, analytics and developer dashboards.
business_model: B2B SaaS for API companies
product_category: Developer experience platform (API docs, analytics, monitoring)
founder_names: Cameron Cooper; Trung Vu; Matt Hawkins
market_need_then: API-first companies were growing and developer experience was a recognised pain, but sources found give no dated demand data.
outcome_analysis: Hoss was a three person team in Austin that sold developer experience tooling to API companies and raised a small seed from YC, Liquid2, FundersClub and Soma Capital. In October 2021 Niantic acquired it for an undisclosed price to speed up the Lightship developer experience, which looks like a team and product fit acquisition rather than a scaled standalone outcome.

name: Hotplate
one_liner: Online ordering platform for independent chefs and bakers.
long_description:
Hotplate is changing how people sell food across the US by giving Chefs and Bakers the tools necessary to solo launch and manage a food business online. There are talented people around the world capable of making amazing food, but either due to a lack of awareness, financial constraints, or the daunting overhead costs associated with traditional brick-and-mortar businesses, many never venture into this space independently. 

Hotplate is fueling a new model of food sales, allowing anyone to create a storefront, announce a sale, and coordinate local pickups with hundreds, or even thousands of customers—all within a 10-minute setup. 

Our aim is to make the food industry more available to everyone with the desire to enter it, consequently making food more accessible and diverse across the United States.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent chefs, bakers and pop-up food sellers in the US who sell by pre-order
problem: Solo food makers need a simple way to announce a sale, take pre-orders and coordinate local pickups without building a store.
business_model: SaaS and payments for chefs (storefront and pre-order tool; fee model not verified)
product_category: Online ordering platform for independent food businesses
market_need_then: The 2020 pandemic pushed home and pop-up bakers online; Hotplate began as a marketplace and moved to an ordering platform for pop-up chefs (Baking For Business podcast, undated). No hard demand figures found.
outcome_analysis: Hotplate is active with about 9 staff and reports only a roughly $2.85M seed in February 2022 after the S20 batch; no Series A is confirmed. It narrowed from a marketplace to a tool for pre-selling chefs, which appears to have worked well enough to keep operating, but one third-party site's revenue claim ($2.7M in 2024) is unverified. Evidence is too thin to attribute success to specific factors.

name: Hubla
one_liner: All-in-one platform for creators to sell courses and subscriptions
long_description:
Hubla is the Shopify for creators, enabling anyone to build, manage, and grow their online business. We provide powerful tools to create courses, communities, sell products, manage memberships, and deliver content—all in one platform. For example, a fitness coach can charge her audience for a unique digital weight-loss program, turning passion into profit.

Creators need simple, flexible tools to succeed. Hubla’s fully customizable platform lets them own their strategy, stand out from competitors, and create unique experiences. This approach works—our top creator earns over $8M annually.

Hubla is leading the creator economy revolution, empowering individuals to transform their expertise into sustainable, scalable businesses.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Brazilian creators and influencers who sell courses, memberships and paid communities
problem: Influencers who sold access to closed WhatsApp and Telegram groups had no easy way to charge and manage members. ChatPay handled payments for them and later became a full creator commerce platform.
business_model: Payments take rate on creator sales (PIX, card, boleto) plus platform features
product_category: Creator monetization and payments platform
founder_names: Arthur Alvarenga; Breno Oliveira; Bernardo Reis; Raphael Capelão
market_need_then: Creators sold access to WhatsApp and Telegram groups and needed billing tools. Startups.com.br described ChatPay as managing payments for influencers running closed groups.
outcome_analysis: ChatPay raised about $2.1 million in 2020 and in November 2021 renamed itself Hubla and raised R$60 million in a Series A led by Kaszek. The pivot from group payments to a full creator platform rode the Brazilian infoproduct boom, and YC lists a team of about 100 and Active status. No later rounds were found, so the growth story rests on the 2021 round and company claims.

name: Humanloop
tags: Generative AI; Machine Learning; SaaS; AI
one_liner: Humanloop is the LLM evals platform for enterprises.
long_description: Humanloop is the LLM evals platform for enterprises. Teams at Gusto, Vanta and Duolingo use Humanloop to ship reliable AI products. We enable you to adopt best practices for prompt management, evaluation and observability.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprise AI and product teams (later customers named include Gusto, Vanta, Duolingo)
problem: Teams needed labeled data and then, after GPT-3 class models, a way to manage prompts, evaluate outputs and observe LLM apps. Humanloop moved from an active learning annotation tool to an LLM evals platform.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform subscription (annual contracts)
product_category: ML data tooling, then LLM evaluation and prompt management
founder_names: Raza Habib; Peter Hayes; Jordan Burgess
market_need_then: In 2020 transfer learning for NLP made small labeled datasets useful, and the founders cited a shortage of annotated data and ML expertise. Demand for LLM tooling arrived later after GPT-3 and ChatGPT.
outcome_analysis: Humanloop began as an active learning tool, raised a 2.6 million dollar seed led by Index in 2022 and pivoted into LLM evals as foundation models took off, winning enterprise customers like Gusto and Vanta. It stayed small and was absorbed in August 2025 when Anthropic hired the founders and most of the team and the platform was shut down in September 2025. This reads as a talent driven exit in a market where model providers were bundling evals, with terms undisclosed.

name: Humanly
one_liner: We empower the world’s hiring teams to grow engaged, high-performing…
long_description:
Our mission is to empower the world’s hiring teams to grow engaged, high-performing organizations - by delivering human connection at scale through innovative technology, commitment, and fairness.

High-volume hiring is extremely broken - it is inefficient, ineffective, and biased. Our mission is to fix what is broken. We believe great hiring processes are centered around quality conversations between candidates and employers and a future where every candidate’s journey starts with a conversation - a future where candidates are considered without bias or archaic artifacts like resumes and cover letters.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Employers with high-volume and hourly hiring needs, such as retail and hospitality
problem: High-volume hiring is slow and biased. Humanly uses conversational AI to engage, screen and schedule candidates at scale.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Conversational AI recruiting platform
founder_names: Prem Kumar; Andrew Gardner; Bryan Leptich
market_need_then: The company describes high-volume hiring as inefficient and biased. No third party dated spend data was found for 2020.
outcome_analysis: Humanly raised small early rounds and a $4.2 million raise in 2021, then a $12 million Series A led by Drive Capital in 2023 and a reported $25 million Series B in 2026. It moved from a chatbot into a broader platform by acquiring Teamable and other firms. Competitor Paradox was far ahead at founding, so the roll-up strategy was its route to scale.

name: Hyper Online
tags: Augmented Reality; Entertainment; Social; Metaverse; AI
one_liner: Social avatar platform for VTubers
long_description:
Hyper is an early stage startup with a mission to build the largest avatar platform in the world.
