name: Hypermile
tags: Autonomous Trucking; Computer Vision; Logistics; Climate
one_liner: Driver co-pilot to make trucking more efficient
long_description:
Hypermile is on a mission to improve trucking efficiency, sustainability and safety by developing an AI driver assistance system 🚛 🌎🌱.

Today, fuel is the main cost component for logistics operators, accounting for >1/3 of all operating costs. Driving behavior is a key factor affecting overall fuel consumption and can increase fuel use by up to 35%. However, current solutions are not cost effective, so logistics operators are constantly looking for new solutions. 

In addition, logistics operators are under huge sustainability pressure, as Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGVs) are responsible for 16% of the UK's transport emissions but only 5% of the miles travelled. While electric vehicle sales for passenger vehicles are on the rise, the same can't be said for long-haul HGVs due to high initial cost and limited range, making it impractical for logistic purposes. 

With this problem in mind, we aim to leverage the latest AI techniques to improve the fuel efficiency of diesel trucks today, and increase the range of zero-emission trucks of the future. 

Our product Hypermile Co-Pilot is a retrofittable AI cruise control for commercial vehicles focused on controlling the speed of the truck efficiently. We have trained the AI algorithms to learn the best techniques for saving fuel: anticipating how traffic flow will change, optimising speed based on the road gradient and maximizing vehicle coasting. As a result, we can reduce diesel consumption by 11% and extend the range of battery-electric vehicles by 15%. The long term vision is to incrementally build higher levels of autonomy with the next milestone being a Level-3 autonomous trucking solution. 

The company was founded in May 2020 and raised a $1.5M pre-seed round in May 2021 from Y Combinator, Greg Brockman (CTO of OpenAI), Luc Vincent (former Executive VP of Autonomous Driving at Lyft Level 5) and others. We’ve received a number of R&D grants from Innovate UK, Department for Transport and Horizons 2020. We’re currently a team of 10 across Commercial, Product and Engineering (including 4. sub-teams cloud software, machine learning, automotive software and electronics).

It claimed 11 percent diesel savings and independent project data showed about 6.8 percent fuel savings against an experienced driver. The sources do not show large venture rounds and the YC status is Acquired with no public buyer or terms, so the story reads as a small grant funded hardware software company that exited quietly.

Our automated financial technology platform ingests revenue and alternative data sources that gives us a proprietary edge in understanding the behavior of our borrowers. As we collect continuous data, we are able to offer better financial and technology solutions, while mitigating our downside risk.

Funds are seamlessly deployed via our virtual Jenfi Wallet and MasterCard solution, giving borrowers flexibility to make payments while giving Jenfi real-time tracking of their spend.

Kernal Bio is led by a team with experience from MIT, Harvard, Merck, and BMS, boasting three FDA-approved therapies and over 120 patents. Based in Cambridge, MA, we are backed by Hummingbird Ventures, Amgen Ventures, HBM, and even NASA.

problem: Conventional mRNA therapies act in many cell types and cell therapies like CAR-T are slow, costly and limited to specialized centers; Kernal wants mRNA that is translated only inside chosen cell types, including in vivo CAR-T programming.
business_model: Therapeutics R&D company funded by venture rounds and grants, aiming at partnerships and drug approval
product_category: Cell-selective mRNA therapeutics (mRNA 2.0, in vivo CAR-T)
founder_names: Yusuf Erkul; Burak Yilmaz; Jeff Ozdemir
market_need_then: In October 2020 the founders pitched mRNA candidates for cancer and Covid-19 with cheaper production than existing therapies (Webrazzi, 2020-10-07); the Covid-19 mRNA wave created investor attention for mRNA platforms.
outcome_analysis: Kernal is a deep-tech mRNA company that raised a $25M Series A in 2022 led by Hummingbird with Amgen Ventures, then won an ARPA-H award of up to $48M in October 2025 for its in vivo CAR-T program KR-402 and joined Lilly Gateway Labs. Strengths are founders with pharma and academic credentials and a differentiated selective-translation platform; it is still pre-approval, so the outcome is open.

name: KeyDB
one_liner: The only database you'll ever need
long_description: KeyDB is a fast key value database that combines in memory caching and FLASH persistence in a single package.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams running Redis at scale who want more throughput per server, later Snap
problem: Redis is single threaded, so scaling needs many instances. KeyDB forked Redis to add multithreading, active replication and flash persistence while staying protocol compatible.
business_model: Open core database with paid enterprise features and managed offerings (features later merged into open source under BSD-3)
product_category: In-memory key-value database (Redis fork)
market_need_then: Teams ran large Redis fleets and paid for many instances because of the single thread limit; the company reported profit in Q1 2021 per its own funding update.
outcome_analysis: KeyDB was a two person Toronto team that forked Redis for multithreading, grew through open source adoption, and reported profit in early 2021 after a 1.3 million dollar seed. Snap, a heavy user, acquired it in May 2022 and merged the paid features into open source. A single report says Snap later moved to Valkey after the Redis license change and the departure of the creator, and third parties call development stagnant, so the long run outcome was a soft landing inside a user company.

name: Kingdom
one_liner: Clinically-validated ingredients from natural microbes
long_description: Kingdom creates clinically-validated Superculture® ingredients from natural microbes to improve the health of pets and people.  We’re the world’s first AI-native ingredients company, delivering industry-leading efficacy in a fraction of the traditional development time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pet food and supplement brands and consumer packaged goods companies that buy microbial ingredients
problem: Food and consumer brands want natural ingredients with proven benefits but relied on single engineered strains or chemicals; Kingdom designs communities of natural microbes into ingredients with clinical backing.
business_model: B2B ingredient supply (branded Superculture ingredients sold to CPG and pet brands)
product_category: Microbial and postbiotic ingredients
market_need_then: The Series A release (2021-10-05) cites brands wanting natural ingredients as alternatives to artificial chemicals; at founding the target was plant-based foods, fermented beverages and personal care.
outcome_analysis: Kingdom raised a $3.5M seed in 2020 including Sequoia and a $25M Series A in October 2021 led by Shine Capital, then moved toward pet health, where its postbiotic ingredients are used by over a dozen brands and have published canine studies. Founders with prior exits and microbiome science credentials and clinical validation support its story. No shutdown or acquisition found; later funding was not verified.

name: Kinter
one_liner: A new kind of power for finance teams
long_description: Kinter empowers leading organizations to supplement their workforce with AI Accountants that execute the accounting close. Trusted by global leaders including Amazon, Mastercard, and UPS, Kinter is backed by a16z, Bain Capital Ventures, Y Combinator and dozens of career operators and founders.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Finance and accounting teams at large organizations (the site names Amazon, Mastercard and UPS as customers); originally e-commerce merchants and product teams buying integrations as Alloy Automation
problem: Finance teams spend heavy manual effort on the month-end close; Kinter sells AI accountants that run close tasks inside existing ERPs with human approval. As Alloy Automation, the problem was connecting e-commerce tools without the cost of enterprise integration platforms.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (Alloy: $200 to $1,000+ per month per TechCrunch 2021; Kinter pricing not found)
product_category: AI accounting agents (formerly integration and automation platform)
market_need_then: Shopify and BigCommerce merchants wanted automations between SMS, fulfillment and other tools and found Zapier too simple and MuleSoft too expensive (TechCrunch, 2021-02-02).
outcome_analysis: Alloy Automation raised a $4M seed in October 2020 at a $20M post-money valuation led by Bain Capital Ventures and Abstract, then a $20M Series A from a16z in February 2022. Seeing integrations commoditize, Mojica pivoted the company into Kinter, selling AI accountants to finance teams, and the site names Amazon, Mastercard and UPS as customers. The pivot is recent, so its payoff is not yet established.

name: Known Medicine
one_liner: Combining 3D cell culture & AI to translate drugs to clinical success
long_description: Known Medicine combines patient-specific 3D cell culture & AI to translate drugs to clinical success. We receive patient tumors, break them down, make thousands of micro-tumors, and then treat each with different drugs to determine which they will respond best to.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Oncology clinics, hospitals, pharma and research institutions that pay for patient tumor drug response testing
problem: Few cancer drugs predict well which patient will respond. Known Medicine breaks patient tumors into thousands of micro-tumors, tests drugs on them in 3D culture and applies machine learning to predict response and find biomarkers.
business_model: B2B testing services and dataset licensing for drug development and clinical decisions
product_category: Patient derived 3D cell culture and AI for oncology drug response
market_need_then: Oncology drug failure rates are high and precision medicine funding was strong in 2020 and 2021, but sources found give no hard demand numbers.
outcome_analysis: Known Medicine raised a 7.2 million dollar seed in August 2021 led by Caffeinated Capital with Khosla and others and built a patient tumor dataset on a Salt Lake City team of about 17. The YC directory marks it Acquired but no buyer, date or price was found in any source, so the exit quality is unknown. The record cannot say whether it was a strong outcome or a soft landing.

name: Kosh
tags: Fintech; Social; India; Consumer Finance; Diversity & Inclusion
one_liner: Creating Microfinance 2.0.
long_description: Kosh is a digital lending platform in India, empowering blue-collar workers with a unique joint liability model (much like microfinance but for a different segment). The social component of their underwriting helps control credit risk significantly and lower CAC/Opex in one go, making this 150mn-strong segment credit-worthy.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Blue-collar workers in India (factory staff, drivers, delivery and service workers) in tier-2 and tier-3 cities, borrowing in small groups
problem: Blue-collar workers lack credit histories and access to formal loans; Kosh uses group joint liability and social underwriting to lend to them at lower risk and acquisition cost.
business_model: Digital lending (loans funded through partner NBFCs) earning interest and fees
product_category: Group microloans, digital lending
market_need_then: In March 2020 Kosh had made about 150 loans worth roughly $35,000 since December 2019 (TechCrunch, 2020-03-19) and the company cites a segment of about 150 million blue-collar workers lacking credit access.
outcome_analysis: Kosh started lending to groups of blue-collar workers in December 2019, joined YC W20, and has since scaled to over 100 employees according to an aggregator, with revenue reported at about INR 18.3 crore for the year to March 2024. COVID-19 moratorium confusion hurt collections in 2020 to 2021 per MicroSave. Funding is poorly documented in reliable sources, so the funding trajectory remains unclear.

name: LFcarry
one_liner: Marketplace for game boosting, carries and coaching
long_description:
LFcarry (formerly LegionFarm) is the world's top AI-powered marketplace for gamers to hire elite pros (top 1%) for coaching, carry, boosting and pro analytics in AAA games like WoW: Forever, Destiny 2, Call of Duty, GTA 6, Apex Legends and 40+ other games. Founded in 2016, YC-backed (W20) with $17.8M raised from 20+ investors, we've served 250k+ users via two web platforms and five messenger bots, creating 10k+ jobs for Pros worldwide.

Current services include WoW Forever, WoW Forever power leveling and Modern Warfare 4 pre-orders. Customers can browse options and pricing on LFCarry before coordinating with a professional player.

In Q2 2026 we've launched a specialized gaming SEO/page building AI tool that is operating on pro analytics training data and autonomous AI research&engineering loops available at https://lfcarry.com/guides and it became the fastest growing product marketing case in video games so far, recording a 60x+ organic monthly impressions growth with 2.5M weekly impressions across gaming guides, tier lists, weekly activities and game time planning in major AAA games. At the same time we have all operations automated for coaching, carry and boosting services that our customers can purchase from Pros at our marketplace at https://lfcarry.com/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Gamers who pay for coaching, carries and boosting in games such as World of Warcraft, Call of Duty and Apex Legends; supply side is professional players paid per job
problem: Casual players want help with hard content or rank, and skilled players want paid work; there was no trusted, managed marketplace connecting them.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on coaching and carry orders, plus subscriptions
product_category: Game services marketplace (coaching, carry, boosting)
market_need_then: Founded 2016 and by September 2019 it had over 2,000 active players earning up to $5,000 per month (Kommersant via EWDN); demand for coaching and carries in WoW was already established.
outcome_analysis: LegionFarm, now LFcarry, was founded in 2016, raised $1.5M in 2019, joined YC W20, then raised $6M in 2021 and an $11M extension in March 2022 despite Ukraine war disruption. It reports 525,000 completed orders and a team of 3 on YC. It looks like a durable but modest marketplace in a legally gray category; no later institutional rounds were found.

name: LSK Technologies
one_liner: A diagnostic lab in a box
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Laboratories, pharmacies and field testing providers that need low cost molecular (LAMP) and ELISA testing outside a central lab
problem: Quality disease testing normally requires a central lab and expensive equipment. LSK built a portable plate reader to run LAMP and ELISA tests where samples are collected.
business_model: Hardware instrument (PLUM-HT plate reader) plus consumables and testing workflows sold to labs and pharmacies
product_category: Point of need diagnostics hardware
market_need_then: COVID 19 in 2020 created sudden demand for decentralized molecular testing, and a CIHR grant of 500000 dollars funded field testing of the device as a COVID 19 diagnostic.
outcome_analysis: LSK started from university research on portable Zika testing and pivoted to COVID 19 testing when the pandemic created demand, funded by a 500000 dollar federal health grant and a YC place in Summer 2020. It stayed tiny at two people, sold research use only products, and was acquired by Nicoya Lifesciences in May 2022 for undisclosed terms, which looks like a technology and team purchase by a larger life science tools company rather than a venture scale outcome.

name: Ladder
one_liner: Labor Marketplace for Construction
long_description: Ladder is a recruiting platform for the construction trades.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Electrical and other construction trade contractors in the US Southeast that need skilled workers
problem: Construction firms struggle to find and verify skilled tradespeople, and tradespeople have no easy way to build a verified profile and apply to new job sites.
business_model: Recruiting and labor marketplace charging contractors for hiring and placement
product_category: Construction labor marketplace
market_need_then: Construction firms reported difficulty hiring skilled trades, and the founder saw this first hand on data center projects; the product launched during the COVID period.
outcome_analysis: Ladder was a one person YC company that grew to a reported 200 plus contractor customers and a large worker network over about five years, focused on electricians in the Southeast. With almost no disclosed funding it appears capital efficient but never raised a venture round, and Buildforce acquired it in December 2024 to gain a foothold in the Southeast, with the founder joining as a senior account executive, which reads as a small regional exit.

name: Laguna

regions: Germany; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Laylo
tags: SaaS; Messaging; Enterprise; CRM; Creator Economy
one_liner: The CRM powering iconic musicians and events
long_description: Laylo powers drops for the world’s biggest musicians and events. The platform combines landing pages, messaging, link tracking, and more to drive sales and streams around the most important moments in entertainment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Musicians, festivals, events and creators (over 10,000 per the company) who pay a monthly subscription plus messaging fees
problem: Artists depend on platforms they do not own to reach fans around releases and ticket or merch drops; Laylo captures fan contacts and sends drop notifications by SMS, email and Instagram DM.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (premium from $25 per month) plus usage-based messaging
product_category: Fan CRM and drop marketing platform for music and events
market_need_then: In 2019 Ellin said Laylo would hit revenue targets almost a year early and expected a partnership giving access to tens of thousands of artists (Built In LA, 2019-10-03); artists lacked owned audiences.
outcome_analysis: Laylo raised a $1.5M seed in 2019, a Eldridge-led strategic round in 2021 and another in October 2022 for about $8M total, and became a CRM used by major artists and events with label and agency partners, adding AI agents in 2026. It stayed small (24 team members) and venture funding was modest, so growth appears driven by artist adoption rather than large capital.

name: Lendtable
one_liner: We give employees cash advances for their 401k match and ESPP
long_description:
1 in 4 Americans do not get their full 401(k) match. That means 25 million workers are leaving $24 billion on the table in free employer contributions. The primary reason these workers cannot get their match is because they do not have enough to both cover living expenses and invest. 

Lendtable helps workers get thousands in additional income by giving them a cash advance to cover their living expenses so they can finally begin earning their employer match. Once their money has vested we take some of the match money earned in order to cover our expenses. 

Workers now have thousands of dollars more without putting any money down, and we make money helping them do so -- we win if they win.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Employees at large employers who are not capturing their full 401(k) match or ESPP; employees pay a fee, employers do not
problem: About 1 in 4 workers miss their full employer 401(k) match because they cannot afford to contribute; Lendtable advances cash for living expenses so they can contribute and then takes part of the vested match.
business_model: Consumer cash advance repaid from vested employer match with a one-time fee (6% to 20% in 2020, 10% in later examples)
product_category: Fintech, retirement match and ESPP cash advances
market_need_then: The company states 1 in 4 Americans do not capture their full 401(k) match, about $24 billion left on the table by 25 million workers (YC company page).
outcome_analysis: Lendtable launched in 2020 with a $3M seed backed by YC, SoftBank and Valor plus TikTok creators, then raised an $18M Series A in November 2021 led by O1 Advisors, bringing total venture funding to a reported $26M. It reported disbursing over $2.4M in match benefits by then. No news after 2021 was found, so later outcomes and current status are unknown.

name: Letter
one_liner: Beautifully designed banking for high net-worth individuals.
long_description: Letter is a beautifully designed banking and financial platform made exclusively for high net-worth individuals. We make it easy to give customized debit cards to family members and staff, automatically donate to charity, and get access to exclusive investment and lending opportunities through our marketplace.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Letterdrop
one_liner: Get into the competitive deals you can't see
long_description: If you beat your competitors in head to head bakeoffs, you should want to get into every active evaluation of them possible. Letterdrop makes that possible so you can sell customers on your better solution.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B marketing and sales teams that want to find accounts evaluating their competitors
problem: Sellers who win head to head bakeoffs cannot see most competitive evaluations. Letterdrop provides competitor intent signals for ads and outbound. It began as a content creation and distribution tool for B2B companies.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, listed from about 995 dollars per month by one directory
product_category: B2B content tooling, then competitor intent data and sales signals
market_need_then: B2B companies were investing in content marketing and distribution in 2020. No sourced evidence of spend specific to Letterdrop was found.
outcome_analysis: Letterdrop joined YC in Winter 2020 as a B2B content tool and later shifted to competitor intent data and sales signals, citing AI changes. It is still operating with a small team of about 10 and a SOC 2 badge. Verified funding and revenue data were not found, so the record cannot say whether it stalled or is growing.

name: Lightdash
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Analytics; Open Source; Data Visualization
one_liner: The open source Looker alternative
long_description: Lightdash is an open-source Looker alternative. It's built on top of dbt and lets users centralise all their team's business logic in one place.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data teams and analysts at companies using dbt and a cloud data warehouse; later business users who self-serve on dbt metrics
problem: Started as Hubble, a tool to test data quality in warehouses. Became Lightdash, an open source BI layer so teams define business logic once in dbt instead of in a proprietary modeling language.
business_model: Open core: free self-hosted open source, paid Cloud Pro and Enterprise plans
product_category: Business intelligence on dbt (open source)
market_need_then: Companies adopting dbt had business logic split between dbt models and the BI tool, and Looker used a proprietary language. A commenter called the product an open source Looker and the founders adopted that as positioning (founder podcast transcript via search).
outcome_analysis: Hubble pivoted in 2021 from data quality tests to an open source BI product built on dbt, riding dbt adoption. It raised an Accel led seed in 2022 and an Accel led Series A in October 2024, reporting 50x usage growth in two years and customers such as Workday and Morning Brew. The company remains active and pivoting toward AI analytics.

name: Linkana
one_liner: The leading SRM platform for LatAm
long_description: Linkana helps enterprise companies reduce lead time and costs on supplier onboarding approvals with an easy-to-use and integrated SRM platform.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Procurement and compliance teams at mid-sized and large companies in Latin America, mainly Brazil, that must onboard and vet many suppliers
problem: Supplier registration, qualification (homologacao) and approval is slow, manual and document heavy, which raises lead time and cost for enterprise buyers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for enterprise procurement teams, integrated with ERP and procurement suites
product_category: Supplier relationship management and supplier onboarding
market_need_then: Large Brazilian buyers need to qualify many suppliers against fiscal, legal and risk criteria. The company later cites a customer cutting homologation from 42 to 8 days, which is a vendor claim. No dated 2019 to 2020 demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Linkana remains active and, per its own site, sells to large Brazilian enterprises such as Suzano, Raizen and Gerdau, with over 200 procurement leaders and 1,500 users claimed. Public funding is thin: aggregators show roughly 200 thousand dollars from YC, Latitud, Endeavor and Plug and Play, so growth appears capital light. The company has stayed a niche enterprise SaaS in a single region and no exit has occurred.

name: Living Carbon
one_liner: maximizing biomass on low quality land
long_description: transforming degraded land into high quality environmental assets using end to end operational expertise and precision breeding.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Corporate buyers of carbon removal credits and landowners with degraded land
problem: Reforestation on poor land grows slowly; the company uses photosynthesis-enhanced poplar trees to raise biomass and sell carbon removal.
business_model: Carbon credit sales and land restoration projects, plus biomass supply
product_category: Synthetic biology for carbon removal and reforestation
market_need_then: Corporate demand for carbon removal credits was rising; AgFunder says the Series A would fund 4 to 5 million seedlings (January 2023).
outcome_analysis: Living Carbon raised a Temasek led $21M Series A in January 2023 with total funding stated at $36M, then signed offtake deals with Microsoft in 2025 and a $500M project commitment from Octopus Energy Generation in April 2026. Success rests on proprietary engineered trees and corporate carbon removal demand, with regulatory and public acceptance risk.

name: Liyfe
one_liner: Digital Nurse to Automate Symptom Assessment and Risk…
long_description: Liyfe remote symptom management platform utilizes Artificial Intelligence (AI) to automate oncology nurse triage pathways and high-risk patient detection. It helps you standardize procedures, streamline existing clinical protocols, reduced ER visits and hospitalizations.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New Haven, CT, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Cancer centers and oncology practices, and cancer patients directly through a telemedicine clinic
problem: Oncology nurses triage symptoms manually between visits, causing missed high-risk patients, ER visits and hospitalizations.
business_model: B2B SaaS to oncology providers plus a consumer telemedicine clinic
product_category: AI symptom triage for oncology
market_need_then: Symptom tracking improved cancer patients' outcomes in studies cited in trade press, and big vendors were buying into remote symptom monitoring in 2020.
outcome_analysis: Liyfe is a two person oncology triage startup led by a medical physicist. No priced round or later traction was found beyond accelerator money, and a directory claims PitchBook marked it out of business by 2023, which I could not confirm. The cause of any stall is not public.

name: Logarithm Labs
one_liner: Easy button to use data for your daily operations
long_description:
Easy button to use data for your daily operations. Power your business workflows with quality data.

Logarithm Labs helps you turn manual data wrangling and ad-hoc scripts into repeatable pipelines for your operational workflows. Power your workflows with quality data.

Our product and team of experts do the heavy lifting so that can focus on the business logic that drives your organization.

To learn more, contact us at hello@logarithmlabs.com.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Foster City, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and mid size businesses without a data engineering team
problem: Operational teams rely on manual data wrangling and ad hoc scripts instead of repeatable pipelines.
business_model: Managed data engineering service plus a pipeline platform
product_category: Managed data pipelines
market_need_then: Companies needed usable data without data engineers; the company's own pitch, no independent demand evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Logarithm Labs started with chip design data in mind and became a managed data pipeline service. No funding beyond the YC deal, no customers and no news were found, and the site shows no activity after December 2021, so the outcome is unclear and the cause of any stall is not public.

name: Loop Health
one_liner: Modern & comprehensive health insurance plan for employees in India
long_description:
Loop Health is a new type of healthcare provider in India combining high-quality primary care and insurance for employers. Employees get unlimited primary care visits at our asset-light clinics, alongside traditional hospitalization insurance.

During YC, we grew from 0 to $85,000 ARR with 200% MoM growth. We serve 22 companies and 5500 members across Pune. 

Employers pay us $15/member/year and we make an additional $25 on prescriptions, lab tests, and hospitalization referrals. Our total gross margins are 70%.

200MM Indians are covered with employer-funded health insurance, representing a $8 billion dollar market opportunity, growing at 27% CAGR.

Indian employers are dissatisfied with their health benefits today because insurance in India only covers hospital stays, not doctor visits – and only 8% of their employees will ever use the benefit in the year. With Loop, employers can offer a more engaging health benefit that includes doctor visits and telemedicine, alongside traditional hospital coverage, for about the same price. Because their employees have better access to doctors, we can also offer lower insurance premiums.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian employers with 100 or more employees that buy group health benefits
problem: Indian group health insurance covers hospital stays but not everyday doctor visits, so employees rarely use it. Loop bundles insurance with unlimited primary care.
business_model: Insurance brokerage commission plus per member primary care fees and referral revenue on prescriptions, labs and hospitalization
product_category: Employer health benefits and primary care
market_need_then: Company stated in YC materials that about 200 million Indians have employer funded insurance that covers hospitalization but not doctor visits and that only 8 percent of employees use it in a year. These are company claims, not independent figures.
outcome_analysis: Loop raised a seed, a 12 million Series A and a 25 million Series B within about 18 months of YC and now claims about 1,250 companies and 950,000 members on its site. It sells to employers through a repeatable channel. Revenue estimated near 8.9 crore rupees in FY24 against a large loss suggests heavy burn, so later funding is unknown.

name: Lume
long_description: Lume was a banking app for nurses with earned wage access, student loan refinancing, and travel nurse jobs. Acquired by Vivian Health (an NYSE: IAC company) in 2022.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Luminai
one_liner: Luminai is the AI platform for Health System Operations.
long_description:
Luminai helps the largest health systems like the Cleveland Clinic run their core operations. 

https://luminai.com

Grateful to be backed by General Catalyst, Craft Ventures, Y Combinator, Moxxie Ventures, Caffeinated Capital, Unshackled Ventures, Scribble Ventures, Shrug Capital, Underscore VC, Weekend Fund, Liquid 2 Ventures, Nikhil Basu Trivedi, Yuri Sagalov, Chris Golda, Basement Fund, the founders and CEOs of Dropbox, Flexport, Notion, Deel, Front, Ramp, Coda, Rappi, Twitch, Lever, Algolia, Thredup, Pagerduty, Sendbird, the COO's of Stitchfix/Rippling, and the former heads of product of Twitter, Instagram, and Uber. We’ve raised $60 million till date. 

We’re hiring across all roles!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Large health systems (Cleveland Clinic is the named flagship customer); earlier, customer support teams using help desk software
problem: Operational work in health systems and support teams spans many systems with manual handoffs. Luminai records and replays workflows, using APIs where available and RPA style automation where not.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS and automation platform sold to large organizations
product_category: Workflow automation and RPA, now AI for health system operations
market_need_then: Support agents spent time on repetitive internal tasks such as cancelling orders or filing Jira tickets. TechCrunch (2020-10) reports the founders claim agents worked about twice as fast. No customer counts were given.
outcome_analysis: Luminai raised a 3.4 million dollar seed during YC, a 16 million dollar Series A led by General Catalyst in 2022 while keeping a lean team, and a 38 million dollar Series B in 2026 led by Peak XV with Cleveland Clinic as flagship customer. The move from support automation to healthcare operations gave it a high value enterprise niche. Total raised is stated as 60 million dollars by the company.

name: Mailwarm
one_liner: Prevents your emails from landing in spam.
long_description:
Mailwarm is the email deliverability company. We help senders get into the inbox and stay there, through products, tools, and services built for both humans and AI agents.

✦ Mailwarm.com: The original email warmup tool. Build sender reputation automatically through real, positive inbox interactions across a large network of mailboxes, with built-in monitoring and deliverability insights.

✦ ThemailX.com: Instant deliverability diagnostics for AI agents and humans. Check all protocols SPF, DKIM, DMARC, Inbox placement and more via MCP, API, or web. Get specific fixes and actions, not just scores.

✦ Mailadept.com: Email deliverability on autopilot. A subscription-based, AI-native service where agents and deliverability experts collaborate to audit your setup, fix issues, and monitor inbox placement continuously.

Build reputation with Mailwarm, diagnose problems with themailX, fix and maintain with mailadept.
Doing email marketing or cold outreach? Book a call through mailadept.com, we'll show you which one fits.
regions: United Arab Emirates; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Cold email senders, agencies, founders, marketers and sales teams who need emails to reach the inbox instead of spam
problem: New or cold sending domains land in spam. Mailwarm builds sender reputation automatically by exchanging real positive engagement across a network of mailboxes.
business_model: Subscription SaaS priced per mailbox or plan, with deliverability expert services
product_category: Email warmup and deliverability
market_need_then: Cold outreach and email marketing depend on inbox placement, and senders with fresh domains need a reputation. No dated 2020 demand evidence was found in opened sources.
outcome_analysis: Mailwarm built a small email warmup business with a claimed 10,000 plus teams and little disclosed venture money. In June 2025 mailX, a deliverability firm led by Thami Benjelloun, acquired it with undisclosed terms, and the group now sells mailX diagnostics and Mailadept services beside Mailwarm. It looks like a capital efficient niche product that ended in a small acquisition rather than a venture scale outcome.

name: MarketForce
one_liner: The SuperApp for neighbourhood merchants in Africa.
long_description:
MarketForce empowers neighbourhood merchants in Africa to source, order and pay for inventory digitally and conveniently, access a banking wallet with credit facilities, collect digital payments and earn extra income by offering agency baking services and reselling digital financial services such as airtime, electricity tokens and bill payments in their communities. 

Incorporated in 2019, MarketForce is a fast-growing company running an asset-light business model and is currently operational in 5 markets in Sub-Saharan Africa, with over 200,000 merchants and 180 consumer brands trading on the platform.
regions: Kenya; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Informal neighbourhood retailers in Sub-Saharan Africa, and consumer brands selling to them
problem: Small merchants struggle to source stock, pay digitally and access credit.
business_model: B2B marketplace margins and fintech services (wallet, agency banking, airtime)
product_category: B2B e-commerce and fintech for informal retail
market_need_then: Informal retailers dominate African retail and lacked digital sourcing and credit; Series A coverage cited over 100,000 merchants in 2022.
outcome_analysis: MarketForce raised a $40M equity and debt Series A in February 2022 led by V8 Capital Partners, but cut about 9% of staff in 2022 and in 2023 reportedly scaled back after some investors reneged on commitments. It exited most markets and wound down RejaReja in April 2024 over thin margins, moving to Chpter social commerce.

name: Matter
one_liner: Building the future of reading
long_description: Matter is a powerful, modern reading app that lets you save media from anywhere, pulls in your newsletters, lets you listen to your articles in a natural voice, and much more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers who read articles, newsletters and long form web content and pay for a premium reading app
problem: Read it later tools such as Instapaper and Pocket had lagged behind how people read online today, with no good way to save media, collect newsletters, highlight and share what you read.
business_model: Consumer freemium subscription (free app, paid premium tiers)
product_category: Consumer read it later and reading app
market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2021 described first generation read it later apps as having lagged behind how people read online, and a GV partner said he was a heavy user of them. Newsletters had grown strongly in 2020.
outcome_analysis: Matter went from an angel round to a YC slot in summer 2020, a $2 million seed, and a $7 million Series A led by GV in October 2021, on the thesis that Pocket and Instapaper had stagnated. It is still active as of 2026 with app updates, though a third party tracker estimates small usage and revenue. Pocket's 2025 shutdown boosted interest in alternatives but also brought Readwise Reader into focus as the main rival.

name: MedPiper Technologies, Inc
one_liner: Instant cash payouts for delayed flights
long_description: OrbitCover (by MedPiper Technologies, YC S20) is parametric travel insurance infrastructure. We power flight delay coverage that auto-settles payouts in under 5 minutes; with zero claims filing.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Airlines and travel platforms that embed flight delay cover, and their passengers
problem: Travellers in India had to file claims for delayed flights and wait for payouts, while insurers carried slow manual claims processes.
business_model: Insurance MGA earning commission on embedded parametric policies (company states 25 to 30 percent commission economics)
product_category: Parametric travel insurance infrastructure
market_need_then: Indian insurers already sold flight delay cover embedded in travel bookings by 2018, which shows demand for the cover, though sources do not give 2020 spend or claims data.
outcome_analysis: The company is listed as active with 55 people in Bengaluru. Its history is unclear: MedPiper news in 2022 and 2023 concerns healthcare products (the MedWriter acquisition and MConnekt), while the current YC listing describes OrbitCover flight delay insurance. No shutdown or sale was found and no verified funding round exists, so no success or failure factor can be assigned.

name: Medicare Vox (fka Fair Square)
one_liner: Building an AI Health Insurance Agent.
long_description: Building and AI Health insurance agent.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Seniors choosing Medicare plans (consumer side), later Medicare carriers and brokerages buying AI voice agents
problem: Seniors found Medicare enrollment confusing, and traditional brokers favored plans paying the highest commissions.
business_model: Licensed insurance brokerage earning carrier commissions, later B2B AI software for carriers and brokerages
product_category: Medicare brokerage and AI insurance agent
market_need_then: The 2022 release cites broker churn above 40 percent and an average broker net promoter score of 34 in 2021, and says brokers favor high commission plans.
outcome_analysis: Fair Square started as a commission agnostic Medicare brokerage out of YC W20 and raised a 15 million dollar Series A in 2022, with about 19 million stated as total raised. In 2024 it pivoted toward selling AI voice tools to carriers and brokers under the Medicare Vox name. A single aggregator reports a sale to Senior Market Sales in January 2026, which is unconfirmed.

name: Memberstack
one_liner: Build a custom SaaS or membership site with Webflow or Wordpress
long_description:
3,000 companies have generate over 130 million dollars in recurring revenue. 

Companies like American Airlines, Slack, Entreprenuer.com, Webflow, and reddit use Memberstack to serve millions of members every single day.

No code if you need it, tons of APIs if you need those, and 100% design control so that you can build any frontend.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Designers, agencies and small SaaS or membership businesses building on Webflow, WordPress or custom front ends
problem: Adding logins, gated content and subscription payments to a no code site normally needs custom backend work.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers plus a transaction fee on payments (4 percent on the basic tier down to 0 percent)
product_category: Membership, authentication and payments layer for no code sites
market_need_then: Webflow users in 2019 and 2020 had no native member login or paywall, and Memberstack reached Product Hunt number one in July 2019 and over 1,000 paying customers by October 2020.
outcome_analysis: Memberstack found demand inside the Webflow community, hit Product Hunt first in 2019, passed 1,000 customers by late 2020 and raised a 2M seed from Gradient Ventures. It remains active with a team of 8 and claims over 200M processed, a capital efficient niche business with no later priced round found.

name: Memo
one_liner: Memo is modern communication that helps you get your focus back
long_description:
We all know the attention economy is damaging our ability to focus. Memo is for people that are mad as hell about their time being sold to the highest bidder.

Forget laborious old email and hyperactive Slack.  We built Memo as the feel-good alternative that will make you love communication again and get back time for what matters to you.

Memo's features make every message high value so you can communicate more effectively.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Menten AI
one_liner: Menten AI designs peptide and protein therapeutics using quantum…
long_description: Menten AI designs protein drugs and enzymes using quantum computing and machine learning. Their technology leapfrogs current computational methods making it possible to design previously intractable proteins. The team created the first protein design algorithm for current and near-term quantum computers and created the world’s first protein designed on a quantum computer. They are now working on 3 new proteins, including a peptide to prevent the spread of viruses like Covid-19. They have 2 paid pilot projects with multinational chemical companies and 4 LOI’s with pharma and biotech companies.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharmaceutical and biotech companies that co-develop or license protein and peptide drug candidates
problem: Designing protein and peptide drugs for hard targets is slow and classical computational methods cannot explore the space well, so the company applied machine learning and quantum computing to protein design.
business_model: Drug discovery partnerships with pharma plus internal therapeutic programs
product_category: AI and quantum protein and peptide drug design (TechBio)
founder_names: Hans Melo; Tamas Gorbe; Vikram Mulligan
market_need_then: Pharma spends heavily on discovery and TechCrunch in 2020 framed quantum computing plus AI as a differentiator against classical computational methods during the COVID period; no spending figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Menten AI raised a 4 million dollar seed in June 2020 from Khosla, Social Impact Capital and Uncork on a quantum plus machine learning protein design thesis with a world class protein design developer. It stays active with a focus on peptide macrocycles and says it partners with top pharma, but no later round is verified. Outcomes for drug discovery depend on partner programs that are not public.

name: Mesh
one_liner: Performance management platform that fits the way you work
long_description: Mesh is a performance management platform that makes it easy for employees to accomplish goals and get timely feedback, especially in remote teams. It looks like Facebook, and instead of filling boring HR forms, employees like & comment on each other’s progress.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; San Jose, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: HR and people leaders at mid sized and large companies, especially remote first teams in India, the US and Asia Pacific
problem: Annual performance reviews and goal tracking were disconnected from daily work, so employees got feedback late and remote teams lacked a social layer for recognition.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for performance management
product_category: Performance management and OKR software for HR
founder_names: Saurabh Nangia; Rahul Singh; Gaurav Chaubey
market_need_then: Remote work from 2020 made continuous feedback and goal visibility more pressing; the CEO told Inc42 that old systems like Workday and Lattice did not fit remote first teams.
outcome_analysis: Serial founders with a prior exit to Snapdeal and an HR consultant co-founder raised a pre-seed in 2020, a 5 million dollar seed in 2021 and an 11 million dollar Series A in 2022. In August 2025 customer contracts were assigned to Netchex in what the notice calls a reorganisation. No sale price or shutdown cause is public, so the end state looks like a soft landing rather than a venture scale exit.

name: Metamanagement
one_liner: We help SaaS companies deploy into their customer's environment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Metaplane
one_liner: Data observability for modern data teams
long_description:
Metaplane ensures everyone trusts the data that powers your business. Data teams at Bose, Ramp, and Klaviyo use our data observability platform to prevent and detect data issues — before the CEO pings them about weird revenue numbers.

We do this with ML-based anomaly detection, end-to-end column-level lineage, and tools to help prevent incidents before they occur. You can monitor your entire data stack within 30 minutes.

The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Y Combinator, and the founders of Okta, HubSpot, and Vercel.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Data teams at companies running a cloud data warehouse stack, such as Klaviyo, Ramp and Bose
problem: Data teams learn about broken or wrong data from executives or customers. Metaplane monitors warehouse tables and lineage to catch silent data quality issues early.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription priced by monitored tables or usage tier
product_category: Data observability
founder_names: Kevin Hu; Guru Mahendran; Peter Casinelli
market_need_then: The cloud data stack (warehouses and dbt) was spreading, and data teams lacked tooling to detect incidents; the data observability category was being defined around 2019.
outcome_analysis: Metaplane rode the cloud data stack wave with a fast setup monitoring product, reached 100 plus customers by 2023, raised an 8.4 million dollar seed in January 2023 and a 13.8 million dollar Series A in March 2024, and was acquired by Datadog in April 2025 as Datadog expanded from software into data observability. The exit price was not disclosed and the category was crowded, so the sale looks like a strategic fit rather than a clear market win.

name: MilkRun
one_liner: Get Food From Farmers, Delivered.
long_description: Our team of farmers and chefs curate boxes of the finest quality local food for our customers each week. From seasonal produce, to humanely-handled pasture-raised meat, to organic eggs and dairy, there's something for every family. We deliver right to your door, as often as you want. Whether your family needs a delivery once a week or once a month, we're committed to helping you shop local. Delivery includes recipe suggestions, cooking videos, and more from our team of chefs. Whether you're looking for advice on how to roast a whole chicken or what that new-to-you vegetable is, we're here for you every step of the way.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Milo
one_liner: The Family AI - a copilot for parents to tackle the invisible load of…
long_description: Milo is the Family AI. We give busy parents back time + mindshare by tackling the daily details with a behind the scenes co-pilot. By pairing a human in the loop with the latest in LLM capabilities we're able to effectively build a copilot for detailed, high context and noisy tasks, via a simple conversational SMS interface.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Vancouver, BC, Canada; Seattle, WA, USA
regions: United States of America; Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: MindsDB
tags: Developer Tools; Machine Learning; Open Source; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Connect, Unify, Respond to any data, anywhere with human-level…
long_description:
MindsDB is a fast-growing AI startup headquartered in San Francisco, California. As a leading innovator bringing AI and Data together, our passion is empowering companies to easily build AI capabilities that can Think, Understand and Orchestrate: enabling teams to move from prototyping & experimentation to production in a fast & scalable way.

MindsDB was founded in 2017 by Adam Carrigan and Jorge Torres, inspired by Ian M. Banks's Culture series, in which super AI systems called Minds collaborate with other forms of life to accomplish incredible goals. Starting as an Open-Source project, MindsDB has grown to be one of the most widely used AI-Data platforms in the world, with a growing community and more than 700 contributor developers from every corner of the globe.

We are backed with over $55M in funding from Mayfield, Benchmark, YCombinator, and nVidia. MindsDB is also recognized by Forbes as one of America's most promising AI companies (2021) and by Gartner as a Cool Vendor for Data and AI (2022).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers, data teams and enterprises that want machine learning and AI agents connected to their existing data
problem: Putting machine learning on top of operational data required separate pipelines and data scientists, so MindsDB let users query models like tables in a database.
business_model: Open source core with paid cloud and enterprise platform
product_category: Open source AI layer for databases, later an AI agent platform
market_need_then: Companies struggled to put predictions into production on data they already stored; the company released AI-Tables in October 2020 and attracted open source users at firms such as PayPal and Verizon per VentureBeat in 2021.
outcome_analysis: MindsDB used an open source community to win developer attention and raised repeated seed extensions, with the company stating about 50 million total by mid 2023 and Nvidia joining in August 2023. Timing tailwinds from the generative AI wave helped it move from ML in databases to AI agents, culminating in a 2026 rename. Competition from cloud vendors and later AI infrastructure players remains the main risk.

name: Minimum
one_liner: Helping corporates achieve Net Zero through tech solutions.
long_description: Minimum lets you calculate, report on, and reduce the carbon emissions of your business, whether you're a corporate or an investment fund.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Corporates and funds that must measure, report and reduce carbon emissions, initially via an API for businesses to calculate and offset footprints
problem: Companies wanted to reach net zero but lacked tools to calculate their carbon footprint and buy credible offsets.
business_model: B2B SaaS carbon accounting, with an early API and offsetting offer
product_category: Carbon accounting and net zero software
founder_names: Freddie Evans; Chris Winchurch; Freddie Green
market_need_then: Corporate net zero pledges were rising in 2020 and TechCrunch in January 2020 described investors and utilities seeding carbon offset startups; later EU and UK reporting rules added demand per 2026 coverage.
outcome_analysis: Minimum raised a 2.6 million dollar seed in June 2021 led by Octopus Ventures and, per BetaKit, more than 18 million dollars in venture funding by its March 2026 sale to Novisto after a three year partnership. The terms were not disclosed. It rode corporate net zero demand and reporting rules, but the many funded carbon accounting vendors and the unstated price suggest a modest exit.

name: Mito
tags: Developer Tools; Analytics; Open Source; Data Science; AI
one_liner: Cursor for data analysis
long_description:
Mito is Cursor for data science. We’re building an AI enabled IDE to 10x the productivity of data people. Data analysts use Mito to automate reports without relying on internal engineering resources. 

Mito is used by thousands of business analysts, data scientists, and automation engineers at some of the world's largest banks, private equity shops, and consulting firms. 

Open source is key to our enterprise sales strategy. Mito is open source and built on top of Jupyter. That means getting started with Mito is as simple as running `pip install` and doesn't require enterprises to manager new infrastructure. 

Check us out at: https://www.trymito.io/
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Business analysts and data scientists at banks, private equity firms and consulting firms who work in Excel and Python
problem: Analysts hit Excel's row limits and found repeatable processes hard in Python, so Mito offered a spreadsheet in Jupyter that writes pandas code.
business_model: Open source tool with paid Pro and Enterprise subscriptions
product_category: Spreadsheet interface for Python and Jupyter, now an AI data science assistant
market_need_then: Founders cited frustration with Excel's one million row limit and the difficulty of repeatable processes in Python in their March 2021 Show HN post.
outcome_analysis: Mito launched out of YC S20 with a spreadsheet in Jupyter and grew through tutorials and an open source community, then repositioned in 2024 and 2025 as an AI data analysis tool for Jupyter. Verified funding is absent: aggregators give inconsistent totals from 130 thousand to 5.7 million dollars. With a three person team on YC, the outcome so far is a small active open source company with no public exit or failure.

name: Mobius Materials
one_liner: The spot market for semiconductors
long_description: Mobius is the safe spot market for electronic components like microcontrollers and capacitors. We help electronics manufacturers buy and sell chips quickly, safely & at market prices.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Contract manufacturers and OEMs that hold excess electronic components or need to source chips quickly
problem: Hardware makers get stuck with excess chips when product plans change, and brokers pay low prices, while buyers in shortages face a counterfeit-heavy gray market. Mobius offers a vetted spot market with authenticity testing.
business_model: B2B marketplace taking a fee on trades of excess and in-demand electronic components, with authentication and an upcoming e-auction
product_category: B2B marketplace for electronic components and semiconductors
market_need_then: In 2020 EMS firms and OEMs saw long lead times and shortages, and the founder cites her own half million dollars of excess chips written off at a prior employer while brokers and a counterfeit-heavy gray market were the alternatives.
outcome_analysis: Mobius is active and small, with about 10 staff and over 1,000 regular users by late 2025. It pivoted from chip recycling to a marketplace, raised a 735 thousand dollar pre-seed in 2023 and a 3 million dollar seed in 2025. Shortages and tariffs have helped demand, but scale and liquidity are still unproven.

name: Modernbanc
one_liner: Accounting software that works for you
long_description: Simple to set-up, flexible and powerful platform to manage your business finances
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startup founders and small business owners who need accounting and finance reporting
problem: Founders keep financial data in accounting software that is disconnected from their spreadsheets and must export it by hand. Modernbanc offers fast accounting that behaves like a spreadsheet and, later, an AI assistant over live bank and accounting data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for accounting software; earlier a developer API product (ledger and vault)
product_category: Accounting software and finance infrastructure
market_need_then: The founder says he found it hard to manage finances as a tech entrepreneur and that accounting tools felt outdated. Open Banking APIs in the UK had opened bank data access by 2020.
outcome_analysis: Modernbanc is active with a team of 6 on the YC page, after several product shifts from a loyalty app to banking infrastructure to accounting software and an AI assistant. Funding is only partly public and no large round is verified, so the story is one of a small, persistent company still searching for a breakout position.

name: Momence
one_liner: Scheduling and payments for experiences
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Boutique fitness, yoga, pilates and wellness studio owners, and experience businesses that sell classes and events
problem: Studios and experience businesses needed one place for scheduling, payments, memberships, marketing and a customer app, especially when classes moved online in 2020.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus embedded payments take rate
product_category: Studio management and booking software
market_need_then: Pandemic closures in 2020 pushed studios to sell online classes and memberships, creating demand for tools combining scheduling and payments for experiences.
outcome_analysis: Momence launched in Summer 2020 as studios moved online, grew to a reported 75 person team and over 4500 business customers with hundreds of thousands of monthly bookings in its consumer app, and was acquired by Clubessential Holdings in January 2025. Terms were undisclosed and the round history is poorly sourced, but customer growth and a strategic buyer in the same vertical suggest a real product market fit exit.

name: Monosi

long_description: Monosi is an extensible data observability platform that ensures teams achieve data reliability.

name: Morphle Labs
tags: Hardware; Robotics; Health Tech; Medical Devices; Automation
one_liner: Robotic Automation for cancer diagnostics - Robotic Microscopes &…
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Pathology and hematology labs, research and education institutions, and dermatopathology practices
problem: Tissue sectioning and slide scanning in cancer diagnostics are slow, manual and expensive. Morphle builds robotic microtomes and slide scanners to automate histology workflows.
business_model: Hardware sales of robotic microtomes and slide scanners, with software and support
product_category: Medical devices and robotics for cancer diagnostics and digital pathology
market_need_then: Whole slide scanners cost tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars per one market report, and manual sectioning is a bottleneck in histology labs; a low cost automated workflow from India targeted that gap.
outcome_analysis: Morphle is active and grew to roughly 65 to 100 people, with 180 plus installations reported on its site and about 14 crore rupees operating income in FY24 per Venture Intelligence. It raised a small seed from Enzia in 2020 and a 5 million dollar Series A only in November 2025, so growth was slow and capital efficient, built on patented hardware and certifications.

name: Mozart Data
one_liner: The easiest way to set up a modern data stack
long_description: Mozart Data provides an out-of-the-box modern data stack that empowers anyone to easily consolidate, organize, and prepare their data for analysis. Spin up a data stack that’s built on a best-in-class data warehouse and ETL tool in hours, without any engineering. You can finally spend more time on generating insights and less time wrangling your data.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and growing businesses without data engineers that want a data warehouse, pipelines and transformations set up for them
problem: Modern data tools are complex and built for advanced use cases, so most startups cannot set up a data stack without data engineers. Mozart sets up and maintains a warehouse, ELT and transforms in hours.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for a managed data platform on top of Snowflake or BigQuery
product_category: Managed modern data stack and data platform
market_need_then: The YC launch post says most startups struggle to set up a data stack without data engineers. The TechCrunch seed piece (Nov 2020) reports about a dozen customers and six employees, evidence of early demand.
outcome_analysis: Mozart grew from three customers after the batch to 50 by April 2022 with a reported 500 percent ARR growth since the seed, then raised a 15 million Series A led by Craft. It rode the modern data stack wave with a managed, no engineers offer. It remains active with 24 listed staff; later rounds were not found, so its position against Fivetran and warehouse vendors is unproven.

name: Mozper
one_liner: A debit card and app designed for kids and parents in Latin America
long_description: Mozper is bringing the weekly allowance into the digital era in Latin America. About 70% of the population in the region has never received formal financial education, and do not have the right tools to teach their children. In Brazil and Mexico alone, parents give more than $10B each year in pocket money to kids. Currently, parents must choose between giving their kids cash or handing over their own credit/debit cards. Mozper is a debit card and app where parents can give their kids an allowance, set spending rules (so they can't blow it all on video games), assign chores and even create and track savings goals. Mozper is currently available in Mexico.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Parents in Mexico and Brazil who want to give children an allowance and teach money skills
problem: Parents must choose between giving kids cash or handing over their own cards, and most people in the region lack formal financial education. Mozper offers a kid debit card and app with allowances, spending rules, chores and savings goals.
business_model: Monthly subscription fee per card (reported 69 pesos in Mexico) plus card interchange, B2C2C
product_category: Kids and family fintech, prepaid debit card
founder_names: Gabriel Roizner; Yael Israeli; Pablo Klestorny
market_need_then: Mozper's YC page says about 70 percent of the region has never received formal financial education and parents in Brazil and Mexico give over 10 billion dollars a year in pocket money, while the only options were cash or lending out an adult card.
outcome_analysis: Mozper launched in Mexico in late July 2020 and raised a 3.55 million dollar seed in December 2020 led by Hetz, then expanded to Brazil in January 2022. It stayed small at 6 people on the YC page and no later round was found. Reliance on sponsor banks and a niche, regional market make its scale uncertain.

name: Multiverse
one_liner: Multiverse is a web-based game creation system inspired by Dungeons &…
long_description:
Multiverse is a web-based game creation system inspired by Dungeons & Dragons and Roblox with a marketplace for assets from A-list creators. We've already partnered with several prominent creators who have millions of followers and millions in revenue, and they're bringing their audiences to Multiverse. We charge 30-60% of those sales based on how much we help the creators make the content.

Check out our [gameplay trailer here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rPwwhw03HO7uda_YDXBfKfvCZ_fHV795/view?usp=sharing).

The best way to get Multiverse is to play it. If you're into games, creativity and representation, hit us up and we'll play with you.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Tabletop RPG players and creators; creators sell content to players through a marketplace
problem: Creators and fans of tabletop style role playing games lacked an easy digital platform to build, sell and play game content together.
business_model: Free-to-play platform with marketplace take rate of 30 to 60 percent on creator sales
product_category: Digital tabletop and game creation platform
founder_names: Sara Alfageeh; Hisham Bedri; Thariq Shihipar
market_need_then: Pandemic era demand for remote tabletop play surged in 2020, and the company said it partnered with creators with large audiences; the platform later cited financial unsustainability, suggesting demand did not translate to revenue.
outcome_analysis: Multiverse raised a $17.5M Series A in April 2021 for One More Multiverse, a digital tabletop platform with creator content, then announced its shutdown in May 2024 because the platform was not financially sustainable to run. No detailed breakdown is public; the failure factors reflect the stated sustainability problem, a niche audience and no later round found, and are partly inferred.

name: Nabla Bio
one_liner: We use AI to design antibodies for intractable diseases
long_description: Our mission is to enable pharmaceutical and biotech companies to bring more antibody therapies to patients. Using AI and massively parallel experimentation, we design antibodies that precisely bind the disease target at the right location, while minimizing manufacturability and toxicity risks. We are a well-funded, revenue-generating, bilingual company of wet- and dry-lab scientists, and are founded by AI and protein design experts from Harvard University.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharmaceutical and biotech companies that want de novo designed antibody therapeutics for hard targets
problem: Finding antibodies that bind difficult targets at the right site, with good manufacturability and low toxicity, takes slow trial and error. Nabla pairs generative AI design with large scale wet lab testing.
business_model: Pharma partnerships with upfront and milestone payments plus royalties, plus services revenue
product_category: AI protein and antibody design for drug discovery
founder_names: Surge Biswas; Frances Anastassacos; George Church
market_need_then: Pharma had antibody targets that classical discovery struggled with; by Dec 2021 Nabla reported partnerships with five unnamed pharma companies, one grown into a multi-target collaboration.
outcome_analysis: Nabla grew from a Harvard Church lab spinout into an AI antibody design company with a seed of 11 million dollars in Dec 2021, pharma collaborations with AstraZeneca, Bristol Myers Squibb and Takeda worth over 550 million dollars in upfront and milestone payments, and a 26 million dollar Series A in May 2024. Strong founder market fit and a hard technical moat drove it; it remains active.

name: Nephrogen
one_liner: Curative genetic medicines for kidney diseases
long_description:
Nephrogen is a Stanford biotech spin-out developing curative genetic medicines for kidney and pancreatic diseases. Kidney disease alone affects 1 in 7 Americans, and neither indication has any approved gene-based therapies. 

Nephrogen's underlying platform combines AI and high-throughput screening to engineer safer, more efficient, and less expensive gene delivery vehicles for reaching the kidney and pancreas, and has attracted non-dilutive funding from seven major pharmaceutical companies including Merck KGaA, Novartis, and Bristol Myers Squibb.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharmaceutical partners and, later, kidney disease patients; today pharma sponsors fund preclinical work
problem: Almost no clinical stage genetic medicines target the kidney or pancreas, which the company attributes mainly to a lack of efficient delivery vehicles. Nephrogen engineers AAV delivery vehicles and promoters for those organs.
business_model: Preclinical biotech funded by pharma sponsors and investors, aiming to develop one-time gene therapies and license delivery vehicles
product_category: Gene therapy delivery platform (AAV) for kidney and pancreas diseases
market_need_then: Kidney disease affects 1 in 7 Americans per the YC page, with no approved gene-based therapies for the kidney or pancreas; the company says 903 clinical stage genetic medicines include almost none aimed at these organs.
outcome_analysis: Nephrogen is an early stage preclinical Stanford spinout that has raised little equity publicly: TechCrunch said in October 2025 it was raising a 4 million dollar seed and the National Kidney Foundation Innovation Fund invested in October 2026. Non-dilutive money from pharma sponsors supports the work. Outcome is open and depends on proving delivery data and raising larger rounds.

name: Nestybox
one_liner: Enables Linux containers to act as super fast & efficient VMs
long_description:
Nestybox creates software that enables Linux containers to act like virtual machines. This increases the use cases for containers and gives enterprises a less expensive and more flexible alternative to virtual machines in many scenarios. 

Our first product is a "container runtime", the software that creates the containers. It's called "Sysbox" and integrates with the popular Docker and Kubernetes engines, enabling these tools to deploy containers that act like virtual machines. 

This technology provides software engineers with an alternative to VMs, one that easier to use, much more efficiency, and easily migrated across clouds.

Hacker News Launch: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=24084758
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; San Jose, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineering and platform teams at enterprises that want containers to behave like VMs for development, CI and system workloads
problem: Containers could not safely run system level workloads such as systemd, Docker or Kubernetes without privileged mode, forcing teams onto heavier and costlier virtual machines.

Today we developed the nELISA for high-throughput drug discovery scientists, enabling them profile 100s of proteins at 10x higher throughput and 10x lower cost compared to existing solutions. We're offering the nELISA through early access programs to HTS groups in top pharmas as well as pioneering biotechs in the space.

Our goal is to create a ubiquitous technology that consolidates the broad range of legacy immunoassay toolkits that scientists use today with a single platform that can carry the science end-to-end, from discovery all the way to the clinic. 

We're a team of engineers, biologists, and highly-skilled lab operators that are looking to grow quickly to keep up with customer demand but also to continue developing our core technology, scale our multiplexing/throughput, and build our software stack. We're hiring on a number of positions including engineering, software, biology, and ops. Come talk to us!

product_category: High-throughput multiplex proteomics (immunoassay platform)
market_need_then: Pharma discovery groups wanted larger protein panels at lower cost; the company said it offered 100s of proteins at 10x throughput and cost advantage versus existing solutions, with pharma pilots in 2021 cited by the CEO.
outcome_analysis: Nomic stayed independent and active. It rebranded from Nplex Biosciences, raised a $17M Series A in December 2021 led by Lux Capital after pharma pilots, and a $42M Series B in September 2024, then launched Omni 1000 in May 2025. A novel assay technology and repeat backing from Lux, SR One and Real Ventures explain its progress, while the deep science and long sales cycles slowed commercial scale.

name: Ophelia
one_liner: Medication & support to beat opioid addiction from home
long_description:
Ophelia helps people quit opioids without going to rehab. We offer online doctor’s visits, withdrawal medication prescriptions, and support for long-term recovery, using a protocol 6x more effective than most rehabs (2/3rds of which don't have doctors).

More than 3 million Americans are addicted to opioids, but 80% are not getting help, due to jobs, families, and privacy concerns. Meanwhile, there's a proven treatment that increases survival rates by 600%, and it's low cost, discreet, and convenient. It's called MAT, and it looks like treatment for anxiety or depression: medication plus therapy. However, doctors need a special waiver to prescribe the medication, which fewer than 5% of them have, so it's difficult to get, and most people are buying it on the street. Sadly, drug dealers aren't doctors: every 11 minutes another American dies of an opioid overdose, now the #1 cause of death for Americans under 50.

Ophelia is replacing rehab with telemedicine, using proven science and a consumer-first approach. The opioid treatment market in the U.S. is $15B, and 85% of opioid addicts have insurance that pays for it. We're treating roughly 400 patients with thousands more waiting.

Zack started Ophelia after losing his girlfriend to an opioid overdose, who found it easier to get medication from a drug dealer than a doctor. We are raising money to help patients in waiting, grow our footprint, save lives, and earn venture-level returns for investors.

name: Osmind

one_liner: Platform for breakthrough mental health research and treatment
long_description:
Osmind is the premier platform for clinicians and researchers advancing new life-saving mental health treatments. Today, mental health disorders are one of the leading causes of death worldwide, especially among young adults, and are tied to shortening lifespans. While there have been developments in new psychiatric medications since the first FDA approval in 1954, today there is a growing movement among clinicians, patients, and researchers who are recognizing the need to accelerate new science.

The Osmind treatment platform is the first and only solution that solves specific challenges faced by neuropsychiatric clinics, spanning general psychiatry and interventional psychiatry (transcranial magnetic stimulation, ketamine, SPRAVATO®, psychedelic medicine, electroconvulsive therapy). The core electronic health record (EHR) technology is precisely developed for interventional treatment workflows and designed to support a strong therapeutic alliance, including journaling tools and assistance with health plan reimbursement, which is a significant access hurdle for millions of patients.

Research from our platform is already helping to set new standards for mental health interventions. For example, in the largest published real-world analysis of ketamine infusion therapy for depression, we teamed up with Stanford University School of Medicine to share findings in the Journal of Affective Disorders (March 2022). We have multiple ongoing research studies leveraging our proprietary real-world data, including an even larger ketamine analysis leveraging machine learning to predict treatment outcomes.

Osmind is a San Francisco–based public benefit corporation led by scientists, technologists, and psychiatrists. We are backed by top investors including DFJ Growth, General Catalyst, Future Ventures, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator.

name: QuestDB
tags: Developer Tools; Analytics; Open Source; Time Series

QuestDB is the data platform for mission-critical workloads where data cannot be lost and batch processing is too slow. It runs real-time trading analytics, grid monitoring, fleet telemetry and mission operations at millions of events a second, with years of history kept queryable.

Data stays in open formats like Parquet, and you or any of your agents can query it in plain SQL.

QuestDB started where the problem is hardest, on the electronic trading floor, and built outward into energy, aerospace and robotics. Today 7 of the largest 20 investment banks use it, as do energy companies and makers of aircraft, rockets and satellites. Its engineers work with each customer's team on the whole solution, from the live feed to the archive.

outcome_analysis: QuestDB grew from an open source side project into a company with a $2.3M seed in 2020 and a $12M Series A in 2021, and later released version 9.0 in July 2025 with B3 and bank customers. No later round, layoff or acquisition was found; funding is reported at about $14.3M total by TechCrunch, and the open source community is its main distribution channel.

name: Recall.ai
