long_description: AgendaPro is building Shopify for Beauty and Wellness businesses in Latam. We allow business owners to charge their customers online and easily schedule appointments.
regions: Chile; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-size beauty, wellness, health and fitness businesses in Latin America (salons, spas, clinics, gyms)
problem: Appointment based businesses took bookings by phone and paper and could not take online payments. AgendaPro offers online booking, reminders, payments, inventory and marketing in one system.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payment processing and marketing add-ons
product_category: Vertical SaaS scheduling and business management
founder_names: Julio Guzman; Sebastian Hevia; Nicolas Rossi; Matias Ulloa
market_need_then: Bloomberg Linea reported 1.8M dollars ARR with 89 percent gross margins in March 2021; the YC page claims over 20,000 merchants today, and the founders said it was easier to buy a flight online than book a haircut.
outcome_analysis: AgendaPro grew from a Chilean service marketplace into a regional SaaS leader serving over 20,000 businesses in 17 countries, with 1.8 million dollars ARR in March 2021. It raised 3.7 million dollars in 2022 and a 35 million dollar growth round in August 2025, which shows capital efficient growth followed by a large later round.

name: Ahazou
one_liner: Podium for local businesses in Latam
long_description: Ahazou is a SaaS app that helps offline local businesses to connect online with their customers to promote their brand, to build their reputation and to sell more. We've reached USD100k MRR with 16k+ subscribers. Our vision is to build the next all-in-one platform for 50 million local businesses to grow online in Latam. The company is founded by Rui Miadaira - 10+ years building local businesses, 3x entrepreneur, tech background with a Harvard MBA - and has built a team from iFood, Movile, PicPay. Ahazou is backed by GFC, Monashees, Y Combinator (S21) and more.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Offline local businesses in Latin America (SMBs such as salons and shops) paying a monthly subscription
problem: Millions of local businesses in Latin America are not visible or active online and lack simple tools to build reputation, engage customers and sell.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for local businesses
product_category: Local business marketing, reputation and engagement platform (SMB SaaS)
market_need_then: The YC page claims 16k+ subscribers and about 100k USD MRR, which indicates paying demand among small Latin American businesses. The target is described as 50 million local businesses, but this is the company's own claim.
outcome_analysis: Ahazou reached a claimed 100k USD MRR and 16k+ paying subscribers by its YC listing, suggesting real demand for low priced tools among Latin American local businesses. The founder has long experience in local business and the company lists GFC and Monashees as backers. Amounts and dates of its rounds are not public in sources found, so the funding trajectory is unknown. The company was still Active with 27 people in the directory.

name: Akudo
one_liner: India's first learning-focused neobank for teenagers
long_description:
Akudo is a digital bank for teenagers in India that gets them their own sleek, personalized prepaid card that they can use independently, helps them save money and gives them exciting rewards under a gamified setup when they're good at their personal finance.  
We are crafting the concept of "Learning-first Banking" where financial learning is seamlessly intertwined with full scale banking.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Akute Health
one_liner: The medical record & infrastructure stack for digital health companies
long_description:
Akute is an automation-first electronic medical health record system (EMR). It’s a co-pilot for digital health and direct primary care companies that are growing modern practices. Akute’s platform is fully programmable and customizable that enables clinical businesses to cut admin overhead and give time back to providers so they can spend more time with patients.

In a space of legacy tech, our team and platform’s agility and exceptional customer support makes us stand out. Join a VC-backed company in its seed stage and help make real improvements to healthcare.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Digital health companies and direct primary care practices that need a programmable EMR
problem: Legacy EMRs are rigid and burden clinicians with admin work; digital health and direct primary care operators need an automation-first, API-driven record system.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per practice with tiers (Essentials 300 USD per month, Premium 550 USD per month, custom Developer tier)
product_category: Electronic medical record and health infrastructure
market_need_then: Growth of telehealth and direct primary care in 2020 to 2021 created demand for EMRs tailored to digital health operators. The company's own materials cite customers such as direct care practices. No dated quantitative evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Akute Health is still active with about four to five people and a product aimed at digital health and direct primary care operators. Revenue claims on aggregators suggest it may be largely bootstrapped, and no outside round beyond the YC deal could be verified. The story is therefore a small, slow growth software business rather than a venture scale outcome so far, but sources are thin.

name: Alba Orbital
one_liner: We make satellites to image everywhere on Earth, every 15 minutes
long_description: Alba Orbital is building the world's largest earth observation constellation, imaging everywhere on earth, every 15 minutes. We can see events within minutes such as wildfires in real time and have signed >$85m of LOIs, with both government and commercial customers paying pre-orders for imagery. To date we have launched 62 satellites into orbit (more than any all other yc companies combined), with more launching in 2026 onwards. We have launched a number of technology demonstration imaging satellites called Unicorns, which are the world's most advanced satellite under 1kg ever flown in orbit.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Space agencies, universities and companies buying PocketQube launch rides and satellite platforms, and government and commercial imagery customers
problem: Small satellites lack affordable launch access and frequent revisit Earth observation is limited; Alba builds tiny satellites to image everywhere every 15 minutes.
business_model: Launch brokerage and satellite platform sales (PocketQube rides, Unicorn platform), with a planned imagery data service
product_category: PocketQube satellites, launch services and Earth observation
market_need_then: Seed coverage cites demand for night time and frequent revisit imaging and notes competitor Satellite Vu raised 5M USD for the same idea. The company later claims over 85M USD of LOIs, which is its own statement.
outcome_analysis: Alba Orbital raised a 3.4M USD seed in May 2021 after YC and has since flown 62 PocketQubes across 11 missions, giving real flight heritage. It remains active with about ten people and a claimed LOI pipeline, but the 15 minute imaging constellation is still ahead of it, so outcome rests on future launches and funding that are not yet public.

name: Albedo
one_liner: Full-stack VLEO satellite missions
long_description:
Albedo builds and operates satellites in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) — a new orbital layer much closer to Earth than traditional satellites in LEO. Flying lower unlocks sharper imagery, faster communications, and real-time maneuverability with smaller, more efficient hardware.

VLEO is naturally self-cleaning and resilient, offering a sustainable alternative to crowded low Earth orbit - providing diversification and redundancy for critical systems that we rely on in higher orbits. 

With the only flight proven VLEO system on the market, Albedo is creating a new orbital infrastructure designed for speed, precision, and resilience.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: US government (NRO, Space Force, AFRL, NASA JPL) and commercial buyers of high resolution imagery; later operators needing VLEO satellite buses
problem: Satellite imagery resolution is limited by orbital altitude; flying in very low Earth orbit promises 10 cm optical imagery with smaller hardware.
business_model: Imagery data sales and government contracts, shifted in October 2025 to selling VLEO satellite buses
product_category: VLEO satellites and Earth observation
market_need_then: Government demand for higher resolution imagery was visible in the 2021 to 2022 contracts and licensing; the Series A coverage compares the target to 15 cm products sold by Maxar and Airbus.
outcome_analysis: Albedo raised about 97M USD across a seed, a Series A and an A-1 and flew Clarity-1 in March 2025, outperforming drag expectations by 12 percent. Founders came from Lockheed Martin remote sensing programs, which fit the government customer base. In October 2025 it dropped its imaging business to sell VLEO buses and cut some staff, so the original imagery plan stalled even as the technology proved out.

name: Aleph
one_liner: One source of truth for financial data.
long_description:
Aleph helps top finance teams work with their data in real time. Businesses can automate financial models and streamline budgeting and forecasting with the fastest-to-implement FP&A platform. Aleph eliminates the need to export data from multiple sources by syncing spreadsheet models with data from 150+ integrations, and allows teams to interact with their data in no-code dashboards.

From annual budgeting to ad hoc reporting, scale your financial processes faster with better data without expanding your team. See why over 90% of people who start a trial with Aleph become customers!
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Finance teams at startups and mid market companies (examples named on the site: Zapier, Turo, Harvey, Chess.com)
problem: Finance teams export data from many systems into spreadsheets for budgeting, reporting and forecasting; Aleph syncs spreadsheet models with live data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, spreadsheet add-ins plus web app
product_category: FP&A and financial data management software
founder_names: Albert Gozzi; Santiago Perez De Rosso
market_need_then: Finance teams were doing budgeting and forecasting in disconnected spreadsheets. TechCrunch frames Aleph as reconciling disparate financial data; no dated spend figures for 2021 were found.
outcome_analysis: Aleph came out of stealth in October 2023 with 16.7M USD from Bain Capital Ventures, Khosla, Picus and YC, and raised a 29M USD Series B in September 2025 for total funding near 46M USD. The company says it grew ten times after the first round and wins customers like Zapier and Turo. Spreadsheet first positioning and fast implementation fit the demand, though crowded FP&A competition remains.

name: Aleph Solutions (Alephee)
one_liner: We help automotive aftermarket brands to supply and sell parts online
long_description:
Aleph helps companies with thousands of products like General Motors and Bosch increase their revenue in Latin America by listing their inventory on large e-commerce sites like Mercado Libre and Amazon. Our customers sell over U$D 4M dollars’ worth of product every month using our software.

Many brands struggle with the shift to sell on marketplaces. They want resellers to be involved in their online sales strategies, but both still need to maintain 10,000 products, prices and inventory up-to-date across digital channels and Marketplaces do not provide tools to help brands and resellers on the journey.

Aleph is the best way for brands and wholesalers to replicate their offline network of resellers online. With Aleph, Brands create high-quality product catalogs to share with their resellers. Now, any seller can access their product catalogue and sell on marketplaces.
all_locations: Buenos Aires, CABA, Argentina; Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires, Argentina; Remote
regions: Argentina; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Automotive aftermarket brands, wholesalers and resellers in Latin America that sell parts on marketplaces such as Mercado Libre, Amazon and Shopee
problem: Brands with thousands of parts struggle to keep catalogs, prices and inventory current across marketplaces, which provide no tools for brands and resellers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for cataloging and marketplace automation, plus a B2B portal that Bloomberg Linea says is about 20 percent of revenue
product_category: Automotive parts catalog and marketplace integration software
founder_names: Gaston Zelerteins; Javier Neumann; Jonathan Saiegh
market_need_then: Bloomberg Linea says the company began when Mercado Livre contacted the founders for help building its auto parts category, which indicates a marketplace side need for structured parts catalogs. The company later claims customers selling over 4M USD per month.
outcome_analysis: Alephee grew from a Mercado Livre request into a platform used by about 300 brands across eight countries, with Brazil giving 60 percent of revenue, per Bloomberg Linea and the company site. It raised roughly 5M USD since founding and was preparing a 10M to 15M USD round. Experienced software founders and the Mercado Libre relationship helped, while dependence on one marketplace until 2024 is a risk.

name: AlgoUniversity
one_liner: Building Job driven Virtual Tech University for India 🇮🇳
long_description:
We are building live teaching infrastructure that enables handful of top educators (from Google, Facebook, etc) to coach a large number of students.
We train college students in a year-long live cohorts and they pay us a portion of their salary as fees once they get a tech job (Income Sharing Agreement)
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian college students who pay a share of salary after getting a tech job (income share agreement); revenue comes from graduates and hiring partners
problem: Few Indian college graduates have the algorithm and interview skills for top tech jobs, and good teachers are scarce; AlgoUniversity uses live cohorts led by a small group of expert educators.
business_model: Income share agreement: year long live cohort training paid as a portion of salary after placement
product_category: Online tech education and ISA based bootcamp
market_need_then: India produces many engineering graduates with limited access to strong tech training; the YC page states the premise but I found no dated spend or placement data.
outcome_analysis: AlgoUniversity is listed Active with about 40 people in Hyderabad, running year long live cohorts under an income share model. Public funding information is thin and unverified, and no news on layoffs, sale or shutdown was found. The ISA model defers revenue until graduates are placed, which strains cash, but outcome details are not public.

name: AlgoViral
one_liner: We help high-growth startups go viral on autopilot
long_description:
Go viral. Grow fast.

We help high-growth startups go viral on autopilot.

We run your entire social growth loop end-to-end. We create, publish, and manage organic content at scale, then turn the winners into high-performing ads.

We are not a creative agency. We are your growth engine: AI-native, data-driven, built to compound.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: High growth startups buying outsourced social media growth (organic content and paid ads)
problem: Startups struggle to produce and scale short form social content that spreads; AlgoViral runs the content and ad loop end to end.
business_model: Service plus software, managed social growth engine for startups (pricing not found)
product_category: Social media growth service
market_need_then: Short form video growth was a visible startup priority in 2021, but no dated source on spend or demand for this service was found.
outcome_analysis: AlgoViral is listed as Active with a handful of people in London, and its current pitch is an AI native social growth engine for startups. The 2021 product is not described in the sources found, the YC listing shows a 2025 founding date that conflicts with the S21 batch, and no funding or outcome news was found, so any success or failure story cannot be told from public sources.

name: Algofi
one_liner: Building the new financial system
long_description: At Algofi, we're building the new financial system. Our work will reduce barriers to entry and promote democracy in the financial system.
regions: Unspecified

name: Alinea
one_liner: Automated investing for the next generation 💸
long_description: Alinea is an app for new investors where we do the hard work for you. With Alinea you have a team of investment experts in your pocket.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Gen Z and millennial first-time retail investors, mostly women, paying a flat subscription
problem: New investors find investing intimidating and unfriendly. Alinea gives them automated, educational investing with a flat annual fee.
business_model: consumer subscription ($120 per year) for automated ETF portfolios, plus stock and crypto access
product_category: consumer robo-advisor and investing app
founder_names: Anam Lakhani; Eve Halimi; Daniel Nissenbaum
market_need_then: The 2020 to 2021 retail trading surge brought many young first-time investors; Alinea targeted women who were underserved by Robinhood-style apps. The founders cite the pandemic as a reason they built it.
outcome_analysis: Alinea raised a pre-seed after YC, a seed in January 2024 and a $10.4M Series A in April 2025, reporting over a million users and a multi-million revenue run rate. Growth came from a niche focus on young women and strong consumer marketing rather than technology. The company remains active with no shutdown or exit reported; later debt financing is unverified.

name: Alltruists
one_liner: Kid-friendly, at-home volunteer projects in a box, delivered bimonthly
long_description:
Alltruists is a subscription for at-home, kid-friendly volunteer & giving projects for families - delivered every other month.

We give kids (and grown-ups!) a way to give back anytime, anywhere. Each box is themed around one big issue in the world - from homelessness to clean water to hunger to climate action and more - and guides kids to engage with that issue in positive, meaningful ways.

In each box:

A proprietary mini-book to help kids learn about the issue at hand
1-2 empathy-building activities to help kids connect with others' experiences
1-2 unique volunteer projects designed with incredible nonprofit partners
Online giving experience where kids direct a $5 donation (included in the box) to one of three nonprofit partner projects
(There are also a few surprises in each box, little things kids can keep as reminders or touchstones so they can easily reflect on the lessons learned.)
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Alokai
one_liner: Frontend Platform for eCommerce
long_description: Alokai is an award-winning and pioneering global technology startup setting a new standard in online shopping. Alokai is a Frontend as a Service solution that simplifies composable commerce. It connects all the technologies needed to build and deploy fast & scalable ecommerce frontends.Founded in 2021, Alokai (prev. Vue Storefront) is a best-in-class composable commerce solution and market-leading Frontend as a Service currently used by 3000+ live stores around the world. With a remote, global team of 100+ people and offices in San Francisco and Warsaw, Poland, customers include Movado, SPAR Inc., or Brompton Bikes. Supported by 130+ partners and a community of 10,000+ developers, Alokai and its leaders are recipients of several industry awards, including Europe’s top tech startup prize and recognition from Forbes magazine.
regions: Poland; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mid-market and enterprise ecommerce teams and agencies building headless storefronts
problem: Headless commerce teams must stitch together backends, CMS and search and build the frontend from scratch. Alokai (formerly Vue Storefront) supplies an open-source frontend framework and a managed platform.
business_model: open-source core with enterprise subscription for managed frontend platform (frontend as a service)
product_category: headless commerce frontend platform
founder_names: Patrick Friday; Filip Rakowski; Bart Roszkowski
market_need_then: Headless and composable commerce was growing in 2020 and 2021, with Series A text citing a wave of well-funded backend module vendors that left the frontend unserved.
outcome_analysis: Alokai rode the headless commerce shift, with open-source adoption driving pipeline and a partner ecosystem driving enterprise deals. It raised a seed in January 2021, a $17.4M Series A in October 2021 and a $20M extension in March 2023, then rebranded in March 2024 and moved toward enterprise licensing. It remains active with 100 plus staff and no exit.

name: Alpas
one_liner: Software for procurement departments to find suppliers 10x faster
long_description: Alpas provides data-driven sourcing for procurement departments of mid and large-cap manufacturing companies. We use ML methods to provide 360° views of suppliers and supply chains, benchmark suppliers globally and assess geopolitical as well as supplier-specific risks.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Procurement departments of mid and large-cap manufacturers buying parts and engineering services
problem: Procurement teams find new suppliers slowly and with poor visibility into risk. Alpas uses machine learning to search, benchmark and risk-score suppliers globally.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for enterprise procurement teams
product_category: AI supplier discovery and sourcing software
market_need_then: Supply chain disruption in 2020 and 2021 pushed manufacturers to look for alternative suppliers; scoutbee's $60M round in January 2020 showed spending appetite.
outcome_analysis: Alpas is still operating as a small Berlin team with enterprise references such as ABB, Siemens Energy and SBB listed on its site. No verified funding, exit or failure was found, so its trajectory is unclear; it is competing against the better funded scoutbee in supplier discovery.

name: Alrighty
one_liner: Email that only shows you what matters.
long_description: Alrighty is a Mac mail app that fixes email. Anyone with your address can reach you, so most inboxes fill up with cold outreach, sales pitches, newsletters nobody reads and privacy-policy updates, and the few emails that matter get buried. Alrighty gets that mail out of your way and lets the AI you already use keep track of the conversations that matter. It works with the Gmail, iCloud and Outlook accounts you already have, and every AI feature is one you choose to turn on.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Individual Mac users with overloaded inboxes
problem: Inboxes fill with cold outreach and newsletters that bury important mail. Alrighty filters unwanted mail and lets users connect their own AI tools to what matters.
business_model: consumer email app, free plan with no time limit; paid tiers not described
product_category: email client with AI filtering
founder_names: Emmett Miller; Wyatt Miller; Leo Schottenstein
market_need_then: Email overload and cold outreach were widely discussed, and a market of paid clients existed in 2021, but no source on Alrighty's own demand was found.
outcome_analysis: Very little is public about Alrighty. It is listed as active with a team of two, backed by Y Combinator, and its current site markets a Mac and Linux mail app with an optional AI agent. No funding, traction or outcome was found, so the trajectory cannot be judged and the 2021 batch product may differ from the current one.

name: Amenli
one_liner: Offers insurance to customers in a convenient & transparent way
long_description: Amenli is the first licensed online insurance broker in Egypt. Egypt has one of the lowest insurance penetrations in the world with a 100m population and a $2B GWP market growing 20+% YoY and a potential TAM of $10B. Over the past few months, Amenli issued 500+ policies in less than 10 mins compared to the minimum of 3 weeks industry standard. Amenli co-founders, Shady & Adham were founding team members of Paymob, one of the fastest growing payment companies in MENA. Shady was CCO and Adham was its Tech Lead and they worked together for more than 3 years to scale-up Paymob from scratch to 50K+ merchants, 5 countries and dozens of millions of monthly transactions.
regions: Egypt; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Egyptian consumers and small businesses buying motor, health and other insurance online
problem: Insurance in Egypt is slow and opaque with very low penetration. Amenli is a licensed online broker that issues policies in minutes.
business_model: insurance brokerage commission
product_category: insurtech broker
founder_names: Shady El Tohfa; Adham Nauman; Omar Ezz El-Din
market_need_then: Egypt had one of the world's lowest insurance penetrations on a 100 million population (company statement), with policies taking about three weeks traditionally.
outcome_analysis: Amenli, founded by two early Paymob team members, was the first licensed online insurance broker in Egypt and raised a $2.3M seed in October 2021, $1M in 2023 and $2.3M in 2024 with EBRD and YC. Team size of 65 and continued rounds suggest steady growth, though no revenue data was found and no exit has occurred.

name: Anakin
one_liner: One API to get clean data from any website for your AI agents at scale
long_description:
Anakin is building web data infrastructure for AI agents and data teams. We help them get clean, structured and deterministic data from any website with one API call, at up to 10,000x lower cost than driving a browser.

We do that by collecting data and turning websites into documented, self-healing APIs that adapt when sites change. Our engine automatically delivers real-time data from thousands of websites and apps, including the world's hardest, across 100+ countries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Ecommerce and on-demand retailers (originally) and now AI agent builders and data teams needing web data
problem: Retailers needed competitor pricing and product data from websites that are hard to scrape. Anakin first sold pricing intelligence and now sells a web data API for AI agents.
business_model: usage-based credits and subscription API (Free, $19, $100 and enterprise tiers); earlier B2B SaaS pricing intelligence
product_category: web data API and pricing intelligence
market_need_then: Ecommerce retailers were paying for competitor price monitoring; TechCrunch reported revenue growing 24 percent per month and profitability before the seed round.
outcome_analysis: Anakin began as a profitable pricing intelligence business and raised a $2M seed in December 2021 from YC and others. It later repositioned its scraping infrastructure as a web data API for AI agents and now lists a team of about 70 in Austin. It remains active with no exit; its current competitive set is fast moving.

name: Ananya Health
one_liner: Portable cryoablation to prevent cervical cancer
long_description:
Building a standard-of-care medical device to freeze abnormal cells before they become cervical cancer, in any clinic, anywhere in the world, at 1/10 the cost.
--
Ananya Health is building a portable cryoablation unit designed for every primary care clinic in the world. Our beachhead application is cervical cancer prevention -- even though cervical cancer is easy to screen for, 80% of clinics worldwide lack the infrastructure and specialized staff to treat at the earliest stages. Our platform technology allows nurses and lower level health workers to treat at the point of care for 1/10 the cost of traditional ablation, and is the only cryo device that will help us achieve the WHO target to eliminate cervical cancer in our lifetime.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Primary care clinics and ministries of health in low and middle income countries treating cervical precancer
problem: Most clinics worldwide lack infrastructure to treat cervical precancer because gas-based cryoablation needs bulky consumable cryogen. Ananya builds a portable, battery-powered closed-loop cryoablation device.
business_model: medical device sales (CRCL System), not yet cleared by FDA
product_category: portable cryoablation medical device
market_need_then: WHO targets elimination of cervical cancer and recommends cryotherapy in low resource settings, yet consumable gas is a barrier; the company states 80 percent of clinics worldwide lack capacity to treat early.
outcome_analysis: Ananya is a small hardware company that has funded development mostly from grants and impact investors, including a $2.3M NCI SBIR grant in September 2024 and an ACS strategic investment in June 2025. It aims for FDA clearance and a 2026 launch; no clearance, exit or failure was found. Slow device timelines and small raises are the main risks.

name: Ancana
one_liner: Marketplace for vacation home co-ownership, fully managed
long_description: Ancana is a marketplace for fully managed, co-owned vacation homes. Owners buy a real share of a property alongside a small group of vetted co-owners, each with guaranteed usage time every year. Unused weeks can be rented out or swapped for stays at other Ancana properties, so the ownership stays useful even as plans change. Ancana handles everything behind the purchase — setting up the ownership structure, vetting and matching co-owners, and managing the transaction — then runs the property year-round, from furnishing to bookings and maintenance. We operate in Mexico, the US, and Spain, each with different legal and regulatory requirements for ownership, and solving that structuring problem market by market is what makes the model hold up as we expand.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Affluent buyers wanting a share of a managed vacation home in Mexico, the US and Spain
problem: Owning a vacation home is expensive and used for few weeks a year. Ancana sells fractional shares of managed homes with guaranteed usage and a swap network.
business_model: fractional ownership sales and management fees
product_category: vacation home co-ownership marketplace
market_need_then: Pandemic-era demand for second homes in Mexico and fractional models; Kocomo's 2021 financing showed investor interest.
outcome_analysis: Ancana is active with a 12-person team and operates in Mexico, the US and Spain per YC. Funding is unverified and no outcome was reported, so its trajectory is unclear. It competes with much better funded Pacaso and Kocomo, which is the main risk visible in the sources.

name: Anima
tags: Deep Learning; SaaS; Consumer Health Services
one_liner: The next generation care enablement platform
long_description:
Hey, thanks for reading! We founded Anima out of a very personal problem. Again and again, we saw people dying because they got bad care plans, weeks or months late. 

We build Care Enablement for care teams - combining online consultation with productivity tools in a realtime multiplayer dashboard. By doing this, we get people optimal care within 24 hours.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: NHS GP practices and other healthcare providers (clinics) that pay for patient triage and care coordination software
problem: Patients get delayed or poor care plans because intake, triage and admin are manual. Anima aims to get patients to the right care within 24 hours using online consultation plus a shared team dashboard.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to clinics and healthcare providers
product_category: Healthcare care enablement and AI triage platform
market_need_then: UK primary care faced access backlogs and delayed diagnosis; NHS adoption of online consultation was accelerated in 2020. Founders cite delayed care plans as the motivating problem.
outcome_analysis: Anima is active and independent. It raised a $2.5M seed in April 2021 after YC W21, launched paying clinics in September 2022, and raised a $12M Series A in March 2024 with deployment in over 150 NHS clinics per the round coverage. The company now claims over 1,000 providers. A doctor founder with NHS access and the tailwind of digital triage supported growth. No layoffs, acquisition or shutdown found.

name: Apollo
one_liner: The card that rewards you with stock
long_description: Apollo is a debit card that rewards you with stock. Every swipe earns guaranteed fractional shares plus a chance to win big with a full share of your favorite stocks.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: AppX
one_liner: AppX helps social media creators launch their own mobile apps.
long_description: AppX empowers creators to launch their personal apps and websites to monetise their audience via courses and premium exclusive content.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Educators and social media creators (mostly in India) with a following who pay to run their own branded mobile app and website for courses and content
problem: Creators and educators depend on YouTube and social platforms that own the audience. AppX gives them their own app and website to sell courses, memberships and live classes without coding.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for creators, plus later stakes in creator ventures (divested in 2025)
product_category: No-code creator and edtech app and website builder
market_need_then: Indian edtech and creator economy were booming in 2020 and 2021 with heavy funding; creators wanted ownership of audiences beyond YouTube. The company's own framing cites a $100B creator market (Jan 2022).
outcome_analysis: AppX is active. It raised about $1.3M seed in January 2022 led by Y Combinator, acquired Superpage that month, and reports thousands of creators on its platform. In April 2025 it exited stakes in educational YouTube channels to focus on B2B. Indian edtech funding fell hard from 2022, and the company has not publicly raised again, so growth seems bootstrapped.

name: Aqua
one_liner: The AI-Native Turnkey Alternative Investment Platform (TAIP)
long_description: One platform to put your alternative assets on autopilot.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Wealth managers (RIAs, broker-dealers, multi-family offices) and fund managers that pay for software to offer and operate alternative investments
problem: Private equity and other alternatives run on manual paper and fax processes, which keeps smaller investors out and burdens advisors. Aqua provides software for subscriptions, reporting, documents and access vehicles.
business_model: B2B SaaS and platform fees to advisors and fund managers
product_category: Alternative investment infrastructure (fintech)
market_need_then: In 2021 private equity access for individuals and advisors was a growth theme, with a TechCrunch piece (Nov 2021) citing manual processes. iCapital raised $440M in July 2021.
outcome_analysis: Aqua is active. It raised a $2.5M seed in November 2021 led by Gradient Ventures, then no publicly reported round until a $15M Series A in September 2026 led by Arthur Ventures. It moved from an investor-facing private equity marketplace to infrastructure for advisors and fund managers and reports large transaction volume. It competes with far better funded iCapital and CAIS.

name: Archbee
one_liner: TURN STATIC DOCS INTO INSTANT ANSWERS
long_description: Build beautiful knowledge portals that are easy to navigate, search, share and contribute to.
regions: Romania; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: SaaS and technical teams that pay for internal and customer-facing product and API documentation portals
problem: Documentation is scattered across wikis and generic tools that are slow and hard to keep in sync with code. Archbee offers a docs platform with API docs, diagrams, GitHub sync and, later, AI answers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per team with free trial
product_category: Documentation and knowledge portal software
market_need_then: Developer-facing and product documentation tools were in demand with API-first companies; the 2022 company post says existing customer documentation tools lacked usability and speed.
outcome_analysis: Archbee is active and independent. It raised more than $1M in July 2021 during YC S21 and a $2M seed in February 2022 for about $3M total, then no public rounds. The company claims 3,000+ customers and now adds AI answers. A small, lean team in a crowded documentation market suggests slow efficient growth rather than a venture outcome so far.

name: Arengu
one_liner: Build frictionless signup flows in minutes
long_description: Arengu allows developers to build frictionless signup flows in minutes. Large companies like Airbnb, Uber or Revolut, dedicate a full engineering team to build and optimize their signup flows. Most companies cannot dedicate these resources, and Arengu helps them deliver an optimized signup flow that boosts conversion rates by 20-30%.
regions: Spain; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product and growth teams and developers who build sign-up, login and onboarding flows
problem: Large companies assign whole engineering teams to signup flows while most cannot. Arengu offered a low-code builder for forms and flows connected to any API, claiming 20 to 30 percent conversion lifts.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription low-code form and flow builder
product_category: Developer tools, sign-up and onboarding flows
founder_names: Jacobo Vidal Abeigon; Pablo Castro Valino; Sergio Regueira
market_need_then: Signup conversion and passwordless login were priorities for product teams, and Auth0 customers needed customizable flows beyond hosted login pages.
outcome_analysis: Arengu was a Galician team of three that started in 2018, raised about 500,000 euros led by K Fund in 2020 and joined YC in Summer 2021. It reached a customer base that made it attractive to Okta, which acquired it in June 2023 (dated by CB Insights and a June 2023 report, while the K Fund post is dated February 2024). The small raise and strategic acquisition indicate a capital efficient outcome.

name: Arpio
one_liner: Recover from any outage in 10 minutes or less.
long_description: Arpio is a SaaS that eliminates downtime for AWS applications by making it easy to recover from any outage in just a few minutes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mid-size and enterprise companies running production workloads on AWS (later Azure) that pay for automated disaster recovery
problem: Recovering cloud applications after an outage or ransomware needs manual scripts and runbooks that fail when tested. Arpio maps dependencies, replicates infrastructure and automates failover and recovery in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, sold directly and through AWS Marketplace and resellers
product_category: Cloud disaster recovery orchestration
market_need_then: By 2021 many companies had moved production to AWS, and ransomware and outage concerns were rising; native tools covered servers but not the whole application environment. Founders describe an outage at Bandwidth that existing tools could not recover from (Dealroom snippet).
outcome_analysis: Arpio is active. After YC W21 it raised an $8.2M seed in August 2023 and a $15M Series A in June 2026, added Azure support in March 2026 and lists enterprise customers such as Finnair and Choice Hotels. Founders with infrastructure experience and a hard technical product that AWS partners with rather than copies helped it. No layoffs or sale found.

name: Arrow
one_liner: Modern Checkout Platform for D2C brands in Southeast Asia
long_description:
Arrow makes it easier and faster for sellers and shoppers to safely sell and buy online in Southeast Asia. It is  first in Southeast Asia to provide brands a better, more profitable checkout experience for their shoppers. Arrow was created to partner with merchants to build consistent and seamless hyperlocal checkout experiences wherever their shoppers come across their brands. 

Shoppers checkout securely with their preferred payment methods. They no longer have to set up new passwords, face multiple redirects or set up a new account every time they shop. Built specifically for Southeast Asia, Arrow works anywhere that shoppers prefer to shop from. Southeast Asian shoppers love the simple and hassle-free solution since almost everyone in this region shops on their mobile devices.

With Arrow, merchants sell more of what they are selling; and shoppers conveniently and easily checkout wherever they shop.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Direct-to-consumer online merchants in Southeast Asia that pay for a checkout layer
problem: Shoppers in Southeast Asia face account creation, redirects and fragmented local payment methods at checkout, which loses sales. Arrow provides account-free checkout supporting many local payment methods on top of existing gateways.
business_model: Checkout-as-a-service for merchants, likely per-transaction fees (not stated by sources)
product_category: Checkout and payments orchestration for e-commerce
founder_names: Liat Beng Neo; Sudhan Raj; Sebastian Roervig
market_need_then: Southeast Asian e-commerce was growing quickly in 2021 and D2C brands sold through own sites and social channels with fragmented payment methods; one source estimates $25 to 30B of regional GMV flows through such channels.
outcome_analysis: Arrow raised a $4.8M seed in April 2022 led by Sequoia Capital India, reported 100 merchants and 50+ payment methods across Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, then was acquired by Pomelo Group in January 2025 on undisclosed terms, with founders joining Pomelo. Coverage frames the deal as largely a talent purchase, so it reads as a soft landing rather than a large exit. No later rounds found.

name: Artillery
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Open Source; DevOps
one_liner: The complete production quality platform. AI-powered E2E testing,…
long_description:
Supercharge your Playwright E2E testing, run scalable load tests, and automate production monitoring with synthetic checks — all in one platform. Built for engineering teams who want to ship fast without performance & reliability risks.

Used by thousands of developer teams to help keep their production systems fast & reliable.
regions: Ireland; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering and SRE teams that pay for hosted load testing, Playwright end-to-end testing and monitoring on top of an open source tool
problem: Teams need to know their APIs and apps hold up under load and stay reliable in production, and existing tools like JMeter are heavy, GUI and XML based. Artillery offers a developer-friendly load testing CLI and a cloud service for distributed tests.
business_model: Open source core (MPL 2.0 per a search summary) plus paid Artillery Cloud SaaS
product_category: Load testing and E2E testing developer tools
market_need_then: Developers had adopted DevOps and SRE practices and wanted code-based load testing instead of GUI tools; the project already had traction as open source before YC (Grafana reviewed it in 2020).
outcome_analysis: Artillery is active and independent. The open source tool dates to 2016 and had developer traction before YC S21. Public trackers put total funding around $2M with Y Combinator, Boldstart and others but no round was verified. The company now sells a cloud product and adds Playwright testing, with a team of five on the YC page, suggesting steady lean growth rather than a large raise.

name: Astek Diagnostics
one_liner: One-hour antibiotic sensitivity testing
long_description: Astek Diagnostics is building a platform (Eugris) that guides physicians in prescribing appropriate antibiotics for patients with bacterial sepsis in one hour. It is done by detecting the oxygen consumption of the bacteria
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Urology practices, hospitals and clinics that would buy a benchtop analyzer and cartridges for rapid urinary tract infection and antibiotic sensitivity testing
problem: Doctors wait days for urine culture results and often prescribe antibiotics blindly. Astek is building a point-of-care analyzer that confirms infection and indicates antibiotic sensitivity in about one hour.
business_model: Medical device: benchtop analyzer plus disposable microfluidic cartridges (not yet on the market)
product_category: Point-of-care diagnostics and rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing
market_need_then: Antimicrobial resistance and slow urine culture turnaround were widely recognized problems; the Longitude Prize on AMR rewarded rapid tests. Founder motivation came from his grandfather's UTI treatment delay (company site).
outcome_analysis: Astek is active and pre-revenue. After YC S21 it closed about $850K in early 2022, later added seed and pre-Series A money from Maryland funds and angels, and the YC page claims over $5M raised in total. The company targeted market entry in 2025 pending FDA clearance, which is not confirmed. Hardware and regulatory timelines are the main risks.

name: Atlas
one_liner: Operating system for restaurants, focusing on Southeast Asia
long_description: Atlas is building the operating system for restaurants. Atlas is the easiest way to start, run and grow any restaurant online and offline. We are the team that previously built Grain, a venture-backed online restaurant, to millions in revenue. Team and investors are from Grain, Accenture, Microsoft, Udacity, McKinsey, Salesforce, Y Combinator and others. https://atlas.kitchen
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Restaurants and F&B groups in Singapore and Southeast Asia
problem: Restaurants juggle separate POS, online ordering, kitchen and delivery tools. Atlas bundles them into one operating system.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription from about 79 to 89 dollars per month plus payments and logistics
product_category: Restaurant operating system and POS
founder_names: Yi Sung (Sung) Yong; Shawn Liam; Ernest Sim; Surendhar Reddy
market_need_then: Covid pushed restaurants online in 2020 and 2021, and the founders say they ran Grain, a cloud kitchen, and productised its tech stack. A 2019 TechCrunch-sourced piece described the Grain Atlas stack, per a search summary.
outcome_analysis: Atlas is still operating in Singapore with named customers such as Raffles Hotel, Haidilao and SaladStop, and its founders bring operating experience from Grain. No credible funding figures or exit exist in the sources, so growth is visible only through customers and headcount, which differs between sources. It competes in a crowded regional POS market against better funded rivals.

name: Atmana
one_liner: Apps to control technology addictions/ helping startups hire engineers
long_description:
At Atmana, we help millennials cut down on technology addictions like gaming, pornography and social media. We have our solution consisting of blocking and techniques used in treating in alcohol and drug addiction like peer support groups, buddy program and psycho education. 

We also have a 2nd line of business: helping startups hire engineers from India. Hiring engineers from India can help you save cost while ensuring you have the same quality of talent in your team like you have in the US.
all_locations: Dubai, Dubai, United Arab Emirates; Remote
regions: United Arab Emirates; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Millennials and teens trying to cut gaming, pornography and social media use; secondary line sells engineers from India to startups
problem: People struggle with compulsive technology use and want blocking plus accountability.
business_model: Consumer app subscriptions (BlockerX, SocialX) plus a staffing service
product_category: Digital wellbeing and content blocking apps
market_need_then: YourStory in Nov 2021 describes demand among 15 to 30 year olds for help with phone, porn and social media addiction.
outcome_analysis: Atmana raised a reported 500K dollar seed after the Summer 2021 batch and continues to operate BlockerX, which appears in 2026 guides. There is no evidence of a larger round or exit, so it looks like a small, steady consumer app business with weak defensibility against platform tools.

name: Atomic Industries
one_liner: Software orchestrated mass production of plastics
long_description: Atomic is a vertically integrated plastics supplier. To offer parts better, cheaper, and faster than anyone on Earth, we became the best mold makers using AI. Our software helps us design and build the best possible mold for each unique geometry, with the goal of moving into production more rapidly than existing supply chains.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Manufacturers buying injection molded plastic parts and molds (automotive, medical, electronics, packaging)
problem: Mold making is slow, apprenticeship based and offshored. Atomic uses software and automation to design and build molds faster and run production.
business_model: Vertically integrated manufacturer selling tooling and molded parts
product_category: AI-driven tool and die making and injection molding
founder_names: Aaron Slodov; Austin Bishop; Lou Young Jr.
market_need_then: Reshoring and supply chain disruption during Covid raised interest in domestic tooling; a trade article notes toolmaking skills pass by apprenticeship, leaving a labor shortage (TechCrunch 2022 summary).
outcome_analysis: Atomic climbed from a 3.2 million dollar pre-seed in 2022 to a 17 million seed in December 2023 and a 25 million Series A in September 2025 while buying metal 3D printing capacity and growing to roughly 50 to 60 staff. Reshoring tailwinds and automation of tooling drove investor interest; the main risk is capital intensity in physical manufacturing.

name: Atrato
one_liner: Enabling consumers split the cost of purchases without a credit card
long_description: Enabling merchants and consumers to offer flexibility at the point of sale
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mexican consumers and the merchants that offer them installment credit
problem: Many Mexican shoppers lack a credit card, so merchants lose sales. Atrato lets them finance purchases at partner stores over up to 24 months.
business_model: Consumer installment credit (buy now pay later) with merchant fees and interest
product_category: Fintech, BNPL
founder_names: Juan Casian; Roger Rea; Alejandro Chavez
market_need_then: Low credit card penetration in Mexico left a large underbanked retail market, and Covid accelerated online commerce. Atrato claims about 100,000 customers and 2,000 merchants on its site.
outcome_analysis: Atrato raised a 2.7 million dollar seed led by Accel in April 2021 and a 15 million dollar debt facility from Architect Capital in September 2021, then grew to claims of about 100,000 customers and billions of pesos financed. It appears active in 2026 but little later funding is public, and a founder bio hints at an acquisition that no other source confirms.

name: Aurabeat
one_liner: Providing clean, safe, virus free air for homes, buildings and cars
long_description: We make Air Purifier and filters that is certified to eliminate COVID-19 and most other viruses and bacteria.  Our technology is independently lab tested, EPA certified and FDA registered.  Our air purifiers are already found in homes, businesses and government facilities around the world to help protect their customers and employees from airborne pathogens.
regions: Hong Kong; East Asia
target_customer: Hong Kong property owners, hospitals, government and households buying air purification and HVAC energy savings
problem: Indoor air carries viruses and bacteria, and air handling units waste energy. Aurabeat sells silver ion antiviral filters and a sonic HVAC retrofit.
business_model: Hardware sales (purifiers, filters, EcoSonic retrofit) to businesses and consumers
product_category: Air purification and HVAC energy efficiency hardware
market_need_then: Covid created demand for antiviral air treatment in 2020 and 2021; SCMP coverage described its lab test claim of eliminating 99.9 percent of the virus (headline), and HKTDC reports it won a government tender and public hospital use.
outcome_analysis: Aurabeat became a profitable Hong Kong air treatment company by its own site, selling to hospitals, landlords and government, and added EcoSonic HVAC retrofits after the Covid peak. Covid demand and certifications drove early sales; funding is thinly documented, and the Covid tailwind faded, so later growth depends on the energy saving product.

name: Auricle
tags: Hard Tech; Neurotechnology; Health Tech; Medical Devices; Healthcare
one_liner: Neurostimulation implant to restore hearing & speech understanding
long_description:
Auricle is a medical device company building a breakthrough neurostimulation implant to restore hearing in millions of patients who no longer benefit from hearing aids, get less than 60% on a word recognition test, but aren't prepared to make the jump to a cochlear implant. 

Our approach preserves remaining natural hearing through a reversible and less invasive surgery, addressing the key concerns that hold most patients back from getting a cochlear implant (currently the only treatment option for these patients).

The company spun out of Stanford Biodesign having completed two acute human clinical studies demonstrating the approach will work. The team is now focused on developing their full implant system for their first clinical trial. 

Auricle addresses a currently unserved profile of hearing loss that affects a growing population of 3.5 million patients in the US and represents an immediately accessible $1.2B market opportunity with existing reimbursement.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Oakland, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Patients with severe high-frequency hearing loss who no longer benefit from hearing aids but are not ready for a cochlear implant, reached via ENT surgeons
problem: Many people hear sound but cannot understand speech. Auricle is developing an extracochlear neurostimulation implant that preserves residual hearing.
business_model: Medical device, pre-clinical, intended implant sales after regulatory approval
product_category: Implantable neurostimulation medical device
market_need_then: The company says millions fail hearing aids but score under 60 percent on word recognition tests and are not ready for a cochlear implant. No dated 2021 market sizing source was found.
outcome_analysis: Auricle remains pre-clinical, supported by YC, Stanford ecosystem partners and NIH grants, with only about 500 thousand dollars of private funding reported by aggregators. Whether it is operating is uncertain because PitchBook shows it out of business while a 2024 NIH award shows activity. The technology risk and capital needs of implants are the central challenge.

name: Authologic
one_liner: Stripe for online identity verification
long_description: Authologic is an orchestration and aggregation layer for local KYC & AML methods. We allow businesses to check the identity of their clients online using video/biometrics, banking data, and government issued digital IDs. Our API  allows a flexible definition of verification scenarios based on the risk profile of the client or risk involved in the given process.
regions: Poland; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Regulated businesses (fintech, banks, gambling, telecom) needing KYC and AML identity checks
problem: Verifying customer identity across countries means many local methods. Authologic aggregates video, bank data and government eIDs behind one API.
business_model: Usage-based API and SaaS for identity verification
product_category: Identity verification and KYC orchestration
founder_names: Krzysztof Klimczak; Marek Rogozinski; Jarek Sygitowicz
market_need_then: EU AML rules and growth of online fintech required remote customer verification, and the founders ran ZenCard and Toyota Financial Services Poland where AML was their responsibility (YC page).
outcome_analysis: Authologic raised a small pre-seed in 2020, joined YC in Winter 2021 and closed an 8.2 million dollar Series A led by OpenOcean in October 2024 with offices in Warsaw, London and San Francisco. Experienced founders from a prior fintech exit, EU eID regulation and AML demand drove progress, while global verification vendors remain much better funded.

name: Avenue
one_liner: Observability platform for operations teams
long_description:
Avenue is a simple way for business teams to set up alerts from their database or data warehouse. Think Datadog / PagerDuty for operations teams.

Operations teams create set-and-forget alerts on all their data, so they can be more proactive with their time (and monitor on more nuanced triggers than just what fits on their dashboard page).

Avenue can improve response times to critical problems from several days to real-time by alerting directly on the data sources that customers already use.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Business and operations teams at companies with data in databases or warehouses
problem: Operations teams lack tools to monitor business events. Avenue lets them set alerts on database or warehouse data and run playbooks, described as Datadog and PagerDuty for operations teams.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with free trial and sales calls
product_category: Operations observability and alerting
market_need_then: Operations teams relied on spreadsheets and manual checks while data warehouses became common; Accel framed ops as lacking incident tooling.
outcome_analysis: Avenue launched from YC Winter 2021 with a $4M seed led by Accel with YC, Flexport and notable angels, building alerting for operations teams. The YC listing now shows it as acquired with a team of eight, but no buyer, date or terms are public, and the homepage still operates with testimonials. The outcome is unknown beyond the acquired status, so the cause of the exit cannot be explained.

name: Aviator
one_liner: Google-level engineering productivity suite
long_description:
Aviator is a developer tool that automates merge workflows and keeps builds healthy. Engineers save up to 5 hours a week and avoid frustration of broken builds.

Our users include Slack, Square, Benchling, Figma, Doordash and many others.

Our goal is to become the leading brand for developer experience.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams at software companies with busy monorepos and CI pipelines
problem: Merging pull requests onto a busy main branch causes broken builds and wasted engineer time. Aviator's MergeQueue serialises and batches merges so main stays green.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per team, with free tools and on prem option
product_category: Developer productivity and merge workflow tools
market_need_then: Large engineering orgs such as Google had internal merge queues and engineers elsewhere wanted the same. Customers named include Slack, Square, Figma, DoorDash and Notion.
outcome_analysis: Aviator started as MergeQueue and raised a $2.3M seed in May 2022 with only a small team, serving big engineering orgs. GitHub's native queue is a direct substitute, so the company widened into a suite and now focuses on AI generated code workflows. It has stayed small and capital efficient, with no later round found, so the outcome is unresolved.

name: Avion School
one_liner: We teach Filipinos to become remote software engineers globally.
regions: Philippines; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Aviron Interactive
tags: Sports Tech; Consumer Health Services; Gaming
one_liner: Aviron transforms workouts with game-based exercise machines, making…
long_description: Aviron, a Y Combinator-backed company, reimagines fitness with connected exercise machines powered by an immersive gaming platform. We're on a mission to build the leading fitness entertainment experience, motivating our community through game psychology, engaging content, and innovative technology.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Home fitness consumers, especially people who find workouts boring
problem: Connected fitness machines become coat racks because workouts are not engaging.
business_model: Hardware sales plus content subscription
product_category: Gamified connected fitness
market_need_then: Pandemic home fitness boom in 2020 to 2021; company claimed 2,700 percent subscriber growth year over year.
outcome_analysis: Aviron pivoted to gamified home rowers in 2021 during the home fitness boom, raised a 4.5 million dollar seed in August 2021 and an 18.5 million dollar Series A in February 2022, and reports rapid subscriber growth. Later funding and the post boom outcome were not found, so the long term result is open.

name: Avocado
tags: Fintech; Generative AI; Restaurant Tech; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: AI-Native Restaurant POS
long_description: Avocado is a modern point-of-sale system for restaurants, powered by a built-in AI agent. More than just a POS, Avocado combines order management, KDS, kiosks, and online ordering in one platform - and lets restaurants control everything with simple voice or text commands. Want to change your menu, check your sales, or optimize pricing? Just ask. Avocado’s AI understands your business and takes action instantly, freeing up owners and staff to focus on what matters most: great food and service.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent restaurants, cafes, food trucks and quick service operators that pay for a point of sale
problem: Small restaurants run on outdated POS systems or on too many badly integrated tools, and pay high monthly software and processing costs.
business_model: POS software at $0 per month with revenue from card processing fees (paid by merchant, customer or split), plus hardware and add-ons
product_category: Restaurant point of sale with AI assistant
market_need_then: The launch post says founders saw restaurants struggle with outdated POS systems and janky integrations between too many tools. No dated 2021 demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Avocado is still operating with a team of four years after its Winter 2021 batch and no public funding round, acquisition or shutdown was found. It appears to be a small, slow growing company that has added an AI agent to its POS in recent years. Without verified funding or traction data, the outcome is unclear rather than a clear success or failure.

name: Awari
one_liner: Reinventing lifelong learning for the future of work.
long_description: We're replacing masters degrees in Brazil with cohort-based courses for top talent to advance their careers in tech. The programs incorporate hands-on learning with sessions led by experts from high-profile companies like Rappi, Nubank, Apple, Google, and more.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Brazilian early-career and mid-career professionals paying for tech, product, data and design courses, with some employer sponsorship
problem: Brazilians who want tech careers face expensive or slow degrees and bootcamps with weak job outcomes. Awari sold cohort-based courses taught by practitioners, with early income share financing and a placement guarantee.
business_model: Cohort-based course tuition, initially with income share agreement (ISA) financing
product_category: Online career education and bootcamps (Brazil)
market_need_then: Strong demand for tech talent in Brazil in 2020 and 2021 and interest in pay-after-hire education. The company reported revenue growing from about R$1.2 million in 2020 to R$7.2 million in 2021 per Bloomberg Linea.
outcome_analysis: Awari grew quickly in the Brazilian tech education boom, reporting more than sixfold revenue growth in 2021 and raising small angel rounds led by education investors. It never raised a large venture round and in April 2024 sold to Fluency Academy, a General Atlantic backed language company, for an undisclosed price paid mostly in shares. The outcome looks like a modest strategic exit rather than a large win or a distressed sale.

name: Awesomic
tags: Marketplace; B2B; Recruiting; Design; Web Development
one_liner: Get matched with top 1% of talents in 24h
long_description:
Awesomic matches companies with top & vetted product talents in 24 hours. Find your designers, engineers or no-coders in a few clicks. They deliver you results through our app, every 24 business hours guaranteed, for a flat monthly subscription.

Successfully matched 4000+ companies, including 400+ YC startups, with their talents who completed over 14 000 projects in the app.

Book a live demo here: https://www.awesomic.com/demo

Portfolio – https://www.awesomic.com/portfolio
Cases – https://www.awesomic.com/case-study
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and small companies that need design, web and no-code talent on a monthly subscription
problem: Hiring and vetting freelance designers and developers is slow and unreliable; Awesomic matches vetted talent within 24 hours on a flat subscription.
business_model: Marketplace plus managed subscription, flat monthly fee per matched talent
product_category: Talent marketplace for product and design talent, later AI plus experts workspace
market_need_then: Startups needed on-demand design and no-code talent; Awesomic reports 1,000+ businesses served early 2022 and 4,000+ later (self reported, company about page).
outcome_analysis: Awesomic raised a small pre-seed, YC money, a 2 million dollar seed in December 2021 and 800 thousand dollars in March 2023, and reports serving over 4,000 companies with a team of about 150. It has stayed independent and appears to be growing modestly, with a recent move toward AI agents combined with human experts. No later priced round was found, so scale of success is limited by public data.

name: Axiom.ai
one_liner: No-code Browser RPA
long_description:
Axiom.ai is building a no-code browser automation tool. This lets anyone automate repetitive work by recording clicking and typing actions in their browser.

We think the market has huge potential - companies like UiPath built $10 billion+ businesses by automating processes on the desktop - an industry now known as Robotic Process Automation (RPA). We think RPA has a lot more potential outside the Enterprise. 

Axiom is on its way to being the industry-standard RPA tool for the browser. It now ranks alongside Selenium - the historical industry standard - as the top result when searching for ‘Browser Automation’ on Google, and is the top-result on Chrome’s extension store.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Non-technical workers and small businesses that want to automate repetitive browser tasks without code
problem: Repetitive browser work such as copying data between sites is manual, and classic RPA tools are heavy and enterprise priced.
business_model: Freemium SaaS Chrome extension with paid runtime hours and plans
product_category: No-code browser automation and RPA
founder_names: Yaseer Sheriff; Simon Williams; Alex Barlow
market_need_then: YC description argues RPA had large potential outside the enterprise; the team came from an RPA consultancy that spun Axiom out, indicating customer demand for browser automation.
outcome_analysis: Axiom.ai grew into a browser automation tool with a self reported 300,000 users and 800,000 bots run, backed by Y Combinator, and it keeps adding AI and Claude integrations. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is not verified beyond small aggregator figures, so the scale of the business is unclear.

name: Axle Health
one_liner: Scheduling and workforce management SaaS for home healthcare providers
long_description: Axle Health provides scheduling and workforce management software for home healthcare providers. The Axle platform includes a mobile app for clinicians, an operations dashboard for office teams, proprietary logistics algorithms to optimize scheduling, and a patient engagement and booking solution. Axle is integrated with a wide range of EMRs, and the entire Axle product can be customized and accessed modularly via API. Some of the biggest home health care providers in the country use Axle’s software to improve the utilization of their clinical teams, and automate the operational burden of scheduling and dispatching.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Home health and hospice agencies that schedule field clinicians
problem: Home health agencies schedule clinicians manually, with poor visibility of routes, cancellations and patient ETAs, which cuts clinician productivity.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for scheduling and workforce management
product_category: Home health scheduling and workforce software
market_need_then: Home health staffing shortage and scheduling inefficiency; the seed press release (Feb 2024) frames the need as staffing shortage. No 2021 dated demand source found.
outcome_analysis: Axle Health raised a 4.2 million dollar seed in February 2024 and a 10 million dollar Series A in May 2025 led by F-Prime, and reports 900 percent growth over its 2024 fiscal year (company reported). Focus on a narrow home health scheduling wedge and EMR integrations supported fundraising. Still independent with no exit found.

name: Axolo
one_liner: Improving Developer Experience with Streamlined Code Reviews
long_description:
Better Code Reviews, Less Hassle, All in Slack

Axolo takes your team's code review practices to the next level, integrating seamlessly with Slack to deliver real-time notifications and natural discussions.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software development teams that use GitHub or GitLab together with Slack
problem: Pull request reviews stall because discussion is split between GitHub and Slack and reviewers forget stale PRs.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat with a 2 week trial
product_category: Developer workflow Slack integration for code review
market_need_then: Review latency is a known developer pain; Axolo's Sept 2021 blog covers reminder bots as an existing category. No survey data found.
outcome_analysis: Axolo remains a two person company (YC lists team size 2) with product expansions to GitLab, an app store and a video tool launched via YC, and no public funding beyond the YC investment. It appears to be a small, stable developer tool; no acquisition or shutdown found. Growth and revenue are unknown.

name: BLUUMBIO
one_liner: We make bacteria and plants that clean up pollution.
long_description:
Our mission

-To ensure current and future generations have access to clean soil, water & air.

-To protect and restore earth's beautiful and diverse ecosystems.

-To undo the harm of industrial activity on the planet and ensure future industrial activities are more sustainable.

Our research

-We develop new bio-based solutions that break down and remove toxic chemicals from the environment.  We also develop bioreactor based solutions which remove toxins from industrial production pipelines, ensuring contaminants are never released into the environment.

-To do this, we've partnered with Nature. Specifically, we have harnessed the power of one of Nature's smallest but most powerful technologies: enzymes. Enzymes are everywhere. They break down the food in your stomach, remove dirt from your clothes, and make our beer. At BluumBio, we look for enzymes found in bacteria, algae, plants and other living organisms that naturally degrade toxic chemicals. We then make these enzymes work better in the lab and come up with develop new applications for these technologies.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Industrial site owners, environmental consultants and remediation contractors with petroleum, pesticide, plastic or PFAS contamination
problem: Contaminated soil and water are expensive to clean with conventional methods; microbial and enzymatic products can degrade pollutants.
business_model: Product and service sales of microbial products plus bench scale testing and remediation services
product_category: Environmental biotech and bioremediation
market_need_then: Contamination by petroleum, pesticides and plastics and growing attention to PFAS; the YC and EQT pages describe the need. No dated 2021 spend data found.
outcome_analysis: BluumBio spun out of a Berkeley postdoc project, went through YC in 2021 and then raised little publicly for years until EQT Foundation invested in a seed round in May 2025. Slow commercialization is typical of environmental biotech needing field validation. It is still operating with products for petroleum and PFAS contamination and no exit.

name: Baraka
one_liner: Grow Your Wealth With Baraka
long_description:
💸Hey YC, we’re baraka (S21), an investment app built for people in the Middle East.

📱 Our product

This is how we do it:
•	6,000+ stocks and ETFs – the freedom to choose the companies and industries that you want to back
•	The power of financial literacy – educational  content, digestible market news and in-depth stock analysis
•	Fractional Shares – the ability to start investing with smaller sums of money
•	Fair pricing – Transparent, low commission pricing model
•	Easy to use – intuitive user journey and interface  


🕒 What's Next?

The app is available in countries across MENA. Check out our website: getbaraka.com.

Please reach out to give us feedback, discuss product, go-to-market strategy or anything else on founders@getbaraka.com.  

Feras & Kunal
regions: United Arab Emirates; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Retail investors in the UAE and wider GCC wanting commission-free access to US and local stocks, with Sharia screening
problem: Residents of the Gulf had costly or limited access to global markets and Sharia compliant investing.
business_model: Brokerage app with commission-free trading, revenue from fees on services, FX and premium features
product_category: Retail brokerage and investing app
market_need_then: Retail investor boom in commission-free apps; coverage in 2021 says the Gulf lacked commission-free access in local currency and Arabic. Regulatory approval from the DFSA in July 2021.
outcome_analysis: Baraka received DFSA approval in July 2021, launched across several GCC markets, raised a 4 million dollar seed in August 2021 and a 20 million dollar Series A led by Valar Ventures in November 2022, totalling about 25 million dollars. It now offers US and GCC stocks, options and gold with Sharia filters. It remains independent; no later round found.

name: Baubap
one_liner: Smart micro financing for everyone
long_description: Baubap is LatinAmerica's firts AI-powered, credit-focused bank. Today we're the leading AI lending app in Mexico
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Underbanked and self-employed consumers in Mexico needing small short-term loans
problem: Many Mexicans lack access to formal credit; Baubap lends small amounts via app using alternative data.
business_model: Consumer microlending (interest and fees), funded by debt facilities
product_category: Consumer lending app / neobank
market_need_then: Crunchbase News (Mar 2021) reports loan approval around 25%, average loan about 50 pesos, 40% self-employed borrowers, expecting 220,000+ loans in 2021, indicating unmet small-credit demand.
outcome_analysis: Baubap grew from a 2018 Mexican microloan app to over two million borrowers and over half a million active loans a month by 2024, funded mainly by debt: $20M in 2022, $120M in 2024 and about $23M from BBVA Spark and SixPoint in 2026. Growth looks driven by unmet demand for very small loans from unbanked borrowers, though loans carry very high rates and equity funding beyond a $3M seed is not public.

name: BeWell Digital
one_liner: Building the operating system for diagnosis.
long_description: 4 Billion radiology scans are generated every year, but unfortunately, 1 in 5 reports are wrong and 35% of the studies are delayed. It can be primarily attributed to access and efficiency. BeWell is building the platform for access and efficiency
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Beau
tags: SaaS; B2B; Productivity; Customer Success; Collaboration
one_liner: Workflows for repetitive customer-facing tasks
long_description: Beau helps to work with people outside your company: build, visualize, and automate your customer-facing processes! 🔥 All with one, easy-to-use solution: collect forms, accept payments, keep updated, request details, and approve steps!
all_locations: Barcelona, CT, Spain; CT, Spain; Remote
regions: Spain; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Service businesses such as accounting and financial firms that collect and process client documents
problem: Collecting, extracting and verifying data from client documents (PDFs, images, forms) is manual and slow.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, Basic from $289 per month plus custom Enterprise
product_category: Document data extraction and client onboarding automation
founder_names: Mila Dayan; Kyril Kulikov; Kirill Zakharov
market_need_then: Manual document handling at service firms; no dated 2021 evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Beau is a five person company that launched Beau 2.0 on Product Hunt in October 2022 and still operates a live site with published pricing. No funding beyond YC, acquisition or shutdown was found, so traction is unknown and the outcome is unclear.

name: Beeper
one_liner: One chat app to rule them all
long_description:
We're building the best chat app on earth. Beeper connects to 15+ different chat networks. Unified search, advanced filtering and more. Available on Desktop, Android, iPhone and iPad.

The idea is simple: messaging today is painfully fragmented. We're going to fix that.   

Every time we communicate there is friction lurking under the surface. E.g. Which app did I message her on? Where's that photo gone? Why can't I join an iMessage group from my Android? Our mission is to eliminate that friction and boost the efficiency of the entire human race.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Palo Alto, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
