target_customer: Heavy messaging users and professionals juggling many chat networks, free app with an optional paid tier
problem: Messaging is fragmented across WhatsApp, iMessage, Telegram, Signal and others, so people lose messages and context. Beeper put all networks in one inbox with unified search.
business_model: Consumer subscription (Beeper Plus) on a free app
product_category: Universal chat client
market_need_then: Chat fragmentation across many apps was a widely felt complaint, and people wanted iMessage on Android. A dated 2021 competitor source was not found in this search.
outcome_analysis: Beeper was built by a founder with a prior hardware exit and YC partner experience, raised an $8 million Series A in early 2022 and gained fame in December 2023 when Beeper Mini brought iMessage to Android and Apple blocked it. Automattic acquired it in April 2024 for a reported $125 million, which is a modest multiple of roughly $16 million raised, with a team of 27 joining.

name: Betterhalf
one_liner: India’s first and only marriage super app
long_description:
Betterhalf is India's first and only matrimony app without parents.

We are the first and only marriage super app in India offering end-to-end matrimony and wedding products to urban Indians, who are the primary decision makers for their marriage and wedding decisions, unlike their parents who were in the driver's seat a decade ago.

Our ecosystem of products on marriage - matchmaking, courtship and wedding in one super app - and focused on the correct audience - high income, higher age urban working professionals of India who are located in 30 tier-1 cities of India makes Betterhalf product a winning combination. 

Our flagship product - matrimonial matchmaking - offers these users the world's fastest matching in a single click (US Patent No. 16/777,773). This matching technology is faster than Tinder and more accurate than eHarmony / Shaadi.com.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Urban, high income Indian working professionals in tier-1 cities who choose their own spouse, plus wedding service buyers
problem: Legacy Indian matrimony sites were built around parents and long manual searches. Urban professionals wanted to find and decide on a partner themselves, quickly.
business_model: Freemium consumer subscription for matchmaking plus wedding services revenue
product_category: Matrimony and matchmaking app with AI matching, courtship and wedding services
market_need_then: Indian marriage decisions shifted from parents to the urban working couple and matrimony remained a large spend category. Company claims urban professionals disliked parent driven search.
outcome_analysis: Betterhalf stayed active after YC W21, raising a reported 3 million dollar round in 2021 and an 8.5 million dollar Series A in March 2023, and reporting 500 thousand dollars monthly revenue in September 2023. Growth came from urban professionals choosing partners themselves. It is not a breakout yet; later status is not covered by sources found.

name: Bimaplan
one_liner: Affordable insurance for the next billion Indians
long_description:
Bimaplan is an affordable insurance platform for the next billion Indians.

Our vision is to provide financial security to 150 million vulnerable households through contextual life and health insurance products. The growth in mobile penetration and the evolution of digital infrastructure in India has now made it possible to reach this vulnerable population. This is an $8 billion addressable market.

We launched in February 2021, and went live with one insurance underwriting partner. We are on track to sell 1,000 policies in March 2021. We are backed by some of the best early stage technology investors, successful fintech founders, and insurance industry veterans.

The company is founded by Vikul Goyal, a second-time founder with a successful exit track record. His previous venture, Carcrew, was acquired by TVS Group, a large automotive conglomerate in India.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Low and middle income Indian households, reached through fintech, financial services and other distribution partners
problem: Over 150 million Indian households lack formal risk cover and traditional insurers avoided them because of high distribution cost and little underwriting data.
business_model: Embedded and co-branded micro insurance distribution, earning commission from insurer underwriting partners
product_category: Insurtech and microinsurance distribution
market_need_then: Insurance penetration was about 3 to 4 percent and 150 million households lacked formal cover. Mobile and internet growth to a projected 975 million users by 2025 made digital distribution viable (March 2021 coverage).
outcome_analysis: Bimaplan raised a 500 thousand dollar seed in March 2021 and 2.5 million dollars in June 2021, then reportedly a later round in 2023, and was still operating with FY25 revenue of about 24.6 crore rupees and a loss per Inc42 Datalabs. The second time founder with an exit and distribution partnerships gave early funding momentum. It has not been acquired and its scale remains modest.

name: Biodock
one_liner: Cloud AI microscopy automation
long_description:
Biodock's cloud platform accelerates microscopy analysis, automating months of microscopy analysis and infrastructure to minutes with our end-to-end AI architecture.  Scientists enjoy auto-scaling storage, GPU compute, and 30-50% more accurate analysis.

We're building an amazing experience to translate microscopy images to therapeutic insights for academic and enterprise scientists.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Academic and enterprise life science labs and biotech and pharma companies analysing microscopy images
problem: Microscopy image analysis took months of scripting and infrastructure work. Biodock offers no code AI training and analysis in the cloud.
business_model: SaaS subscription for cloud image analysis with usage and compute
product_category: Cloud AI microscopy image analysis
market_need_then: Imaging labs generated large volumes of microscopy data and lacked ML staff. The founder describes the problem from his own Stanford research.
outcome_analysis: Biodock took an early round of about 2.2 million dollars led by a16z around YC W21 and says total funding is 3.8 million dollars, a small amount over five years. It reports over 5,000 labs as users and holds SOC2 Type II. Growth looks steady and capital efficient rather than venture scale, with limited public data.

name: Birdie
one_liner: Connect LinkedIn to your CRM to automate and track LinkedIn outreach.
long_description: Birdie supercharges your sales team’s outreach productivity on LinkedIn. We do this by automating outreach workflows and providing comprehensive activity analytics. We help individual sales reps save time, while also helping sales managers get full visibility into their LinkedIn outreach efforts.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B sales reps and sales managers who prospect on LinkedIn
problem: LinkedIn outreach is invisible to the CRM, so reps copy and paste and managers cannot track activity.
business_model: Per seat SaaS subscription (site lists 40 dollars per month after a trial)
product_category: LinkedIn to CRM sync and outreach Chrome extension, now an AI social selling copilot
market_need_then: Sales teams used LinkedIn heavily for prospecting but had no native CRM logging. The YC page says reps save time and managers gain visibility.
outcome_analysis: Birdie is still operating in 2025 and 2026 with a pricing page and an AI copilot positioning, but no funding round, acquisition or traction numbers could be verified. The product competes with many LinkedIn extensions and depends on LinkedIn access, so the outcome is a small ongoing product with unclear scale.

name: Bite Ninja
tags: Food Service Robots & Machines; SaaS; AI
one_liner: Remote labor for restaurants
long_description: Our platform enables fast food and quick service restaurant workers to take orders and payments remotely
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Quick service restaurant operators and chains, especially drive-thru and front counter
problem: Restaurants struggled to staff order taking, especially during the pandemic. Bite Ninja provides remote workers to take orders and payments, shared across locations.
business_model: Labor as a service: per hour or per order fee for remote workers plus queuing software
product_category: Remote labor platform for restaurants
market_need_then: Restaurants faced labor shortages and pandemic reopening constraints in 2020 and 2021. By Aug 2022 the company said it had signed five of the top 20 US quick service chains.
outcome_analysis: Bite Ninja raised about 15.4 million dollars across 2021 and 2022 and signed major quick service chains, then was acquired by Voicify in March 2025 with the price not public. The pandemic labor shortage gave it demand, but voice AI shifted the market away from human remote labor, making an acquisition by a voice AI player a likely soft outcome.

name: BlackOakTV
one_liner: A video subscription platform serving black viewers and creators.
long_description: BlackOakTV is a subscription video platform hyper-serving black viewers and creators. We make it easy for black viewers to find, watch and engage with the content and creators that most reflect their lives and experiences.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Blink
one_liner: Same-day delivery for e-commerce companies in Europe.
long_description: Blink provides same-day delivery to e-commerce companies, helping them acquiring and retaining more customers thanks to a great delivery experience. Merchants sell on their website and Blink picks-up orders directly from physical stores or from dark stores (small urban warehouses) deployed in cities. Crowdsourced riders and transportation companies complete the delivery following routes optimized in teal time. Consumers can track and personalize their delivery.
regions: Italy; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Blixo
one_liner: Accounts receivable automation to help companies get paid faster
long_description:
Blixo is an all-in-one replacement for things like subscription management, invoicing, collections, and cash application software.

Blixo improves conversion rates, increases average order size, drives subscriber loyalty, collects unpaid bills, speeds up cashflow, and is the single source of truth for reconciled real time revenue data.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and mid sized companies with subscription or invoice based revenue that use QuickBooks, Xero, Sage Intacct or NetSuite
problem: Companies get paid slowly because billing, collections and cash application sit in separate tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for accounts receivable automation
product_category: Accounts receivable and subscription billing automation
market_need_then: Late payments and manual collections were a known SMB cash flow issue; funded AR startups raised large rounds in 2021, showing investor demand.
outcome_analysis: Blixo is still operating with a product site and customer testimonials, but no funding beyond the YC investment, no acquisition and no traction numbers could be found. It competes with well funded AR and billing vendors, so it appears to be a small bootstrapped or lightly funded business with no public growth signal.

name: Bloom
one_liner: Investing app that teaches you how to invest
long_description:
Bloom's mission is to improve the financial outcomes of all Americans by giving them the knowledge and tools they need to achieve prosperity. 

Our first product is an investing app that teaches users how to build wealth through interactive financial lessons, a gamified rewards economy as well as an investing account designed for building long-term wealth.

Since launching in April 2022, over 1 million users have joined Bloom and we have crossed $3MM in annual recurring revenue.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Beginner investors, originally teens and later 18 to 25 year olds, who pay a monthly or annual fee
problem: Young people want to invest but lack financial knowledge, so Bloom pairs interactive lessons and rewards with a brokerage account.
business_model: Consumer subscription (15 dollars per month or 120 dollars per year per TechCrunch 2023)
product_category: Investing education app with brokerage account
market_need_then: Retail investing surged in 2020 and 2021 and young users sought education. Claimed 1 million downloads within about a year of launch (TechCrunch, July 2023).
outcome_analysis: Bloom launched in February 2022, reported 1 million downloads and seven figure annual recurring revenue by mid 2023, and is still active with claims of 2 million downloads. Total disclosed funding is about 4.4 million dollars in seed. It has not raised a larger round or exited in sources found, so it looks like a modest consumer fintech.

name: Bluelight
one_liner: Analytics, built for the trades.
long_description: Bluelight gives home service contractors the power of real-time data to optimize and scale their business.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Home service contractors, such as plumbing, HVAC and electrical businesses, that run on ServiceTitan
problem: Contractors lack real time analytics, so budgets go stale. Bluelight builds revenue plans around operational drivers and updates morning huddle numbers automatically.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for contractors
product_category: Analytics and revenue planning for home services
market_need_then: Home service businesses grew fast and spent heavily on software, but spreadsheets drove budgeting. Jobber reported its users grew to 100,000 by January 2021.
outcome_analysis: Bluelight appears active in 2026 with named customers, a recent case study and a Nexstar partnership, but no public funding beyond small amounts and no acquisition were found. It narrowed from general trades analytics to ServiceTitan operators, which gives focus but dependence on one platform. Scale is not public.

name: BoldVoice
one_liner: Speech and accent coaching app for non-native English speakers
long_description: BoldVoice helps non-native English speakers to speak clearly and confidently. We combine bite-sized video lessons from Hollywood accent coaches with instant pronunciation feedback from AI, to create an effective and engaging learning experience.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Non-native English speakers (professionals, immigrants, students) who pay a subscription to reduce their accent; also a smaller business/team offering
problem: Non-native speakers understand English but are misunderstood or judged because of accent; human accent coaching costs $200 to $300 per hour per the company.
business_model: Consumer subscription mobile app (B2C) plus B2B team plans
product_category: Accent and pronunciation training with video lessons and AI speech feedback
market_need_then: Strong stated need: founders are immigrants who experienced accent bias; human coaching is priced at $200 to $300 per hour, leaving room for a cheap app (company statements via press, 2021 to 2026).
outcome_analysis: BoldVoice stayed lean (seven people at the Series A) and reached a reported $10M+ ARR and 5M downloads by January 2026 before its $21M Series A led by Matrix. Its consumer subscription model, founder-market fit with immigrant users and the distinctive Hollywood-coach content appear to explain the traction; earlier funding is poorly documented. No pivot or distress signal was found.

name: Bolster
one_liner: The platform for buying, selling and managing residential construction
long_description: We are building the Amazon for construction where contractors can give their customers an interactive shopping experience, turning the estimate into a point-of-sale, for the first time.  It is a marketplace for general contractors, subcontractors, retailers and consumers, powered by a database of over 114,000 real items.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Residential general contractors and remodelers, plus the subcontractors, retailers and homeowners they transact with
problem: Contractors estimate jobs with outdated manual processes and lack digital tools, so quotes are slow and customers cannot interactively choose materials and upgrades.
business_model: Software subscription plus marketplace take on construction purchasing (reported annualized GMV of $72M in 2021)
product_category: Construction estimating, management software and procurement marketplace
market_need_then: The company says contractors were frustrated with outdated estimating processes. TechCrunch reported $72M annualized GMV and growth of 2,203% year over year from a small base in October 2021.
outcome_analysis: Bolster, formerly CostCertified, grew out of its founder's own contracting experience and reached reported $72M annualized GMV by October 2021 when it raised an $8.45M seed led by FUSE, a record for Alberta per the company. The founder's domain knowledge and fast growth from a small base were the main strengths. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, so the long term outcome is unknown and its status is Active.

name: BotBuilt
tags: Robotic Process Automation; Robotics; Construction; Housing
one_liner: We use robots to build houses.
long_description: BotBuilt is creating flexible robotic systems to solve the housing crisis. Our cutting-edge software and cost-efficient hardware allow us to improve the world by providing beautiful construction, safer job sites, and sustainable building techniques. The $600 billion residential construction industry is facing a massive labor shortage. Our robotic systems leverage the latest in rapid prototyping, artificial intelligence, and computer vision. By taking on some of the hardest technical challenges on earth, BotBuilt is ready to help solve one of society’s biggest problems.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Residential home builders who buy framing components such as wall panels and trusses
problem: Residential construction faces a labor shortage and high costs; framing is slow, unsafe and wasteful when done by hand on site.
business_model: Robot-equipped factory producing framed components sold to builders (BotBuilt operates the factories rather than selling the robots)
product_category: Construction robotics and prefabricated framing
founder_names: Brent Wadas; Colin Devine; Barrett Ames
market_need_then: The company cites a labor shortage in a roughly $600 billion US residential construction industry and housing affordability pressure.
outcome_analysis: BotBuilt pursued a hard hardware and software problem in a large housing market, raising a $12.4M seed in December 2023 led by Shadow Ventures with strategic backers Owens Corning and Ambassador Supply. No later round or exit was found, so it is early and unproven at scale. The strategic investors suggest industry validation, but the small team and capital intensity remain risks.

name: Breadcrumbs.io
one_liner: No-code scoring engine identifying your most engaged upsell opps
long_description: Breadcrumbs analyzes customer and prospect data to identify hidden revenue opportunities. It does this through a no-code scoring engine that can be set up in minutes rather than months. Because of Breadcrumbs sales teams can now focus on the right opportunity at the right time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B SaaS revenue operations and sales teams, especially product-led growth companies
problem: Sales teams struggle to find which leads and accounts are ready to buy because scoring tools needed data scientists and months of setup. Breadcrumbs offered a no-code scoring engine that sets up in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Lead scoring and routing software
founder_names: Armando Biondi; Gary Amaral; Massimo Chieruzzi
market_need_then: Rise of product-led growth made usage signals valuable for sales prioritization, and teams wanted scoring without data science staff. Crunchbase News covered the May 2021 seed as a no-code approach to the problem.
outcome_analysis: A repeat founding team from AdEspresso raised a $5.4 million seed in May 2021 for a no-code lead scoring product. No later round was found, and in October 2024 competitor MadKudu absorbed the customers while the Italian team joined WordLift. The reasons for the sale are not public.

name: Bree
one_liner: Chime for Canada, starting with cash advances
long_description: Bree is building a challenger bank for the 11 million Canadians living paycheck to paycheck, starting with interest-free cash advances. We make money through tips and an optional, same-day express fee. By solving our customers' most urgent problem—illiquidity between paychecks —our cash advance business is a cheap, but profitable and repeatable hook that builds distribution for a broader challenger bank. This represents a $9 billion revenue opportunity in Canada.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Canadians living paycheck to paycheck who need short term cash between paydays
problem: Canadians face illiquidity between paychecks and rely on payday loans; no interest-free cash advance app existed locally.
business_model: Cash advances funded by tips, an optional same-day express fee and later a monthly subscription; aimed at growing into a challenger bank
product_category: Consumer fintech, cash advance and challenger bank
market_need_then: The YC page cites 11 million Canadians living paycheck to paycheck and a $9 billion revenue opportunity. Finder says cash advance apps launched in Canada around 2021, before which people turned to payday loans.
outcome_analysis: Bree launched in 2021 as a Canadian interest-free cash advance app and, per review sites, is still operating with a subscription fee and advances up to several hundred dollars. No funding round, exit or distress news was found, so its financial health and traction are unknown. Competition from KOHO and Neo Financial suggests the category is contested.

name: BrioHR
one_liner: All-in-one HR management platform for SMEs
long_description:
Our HR management platform helps companies instantly digitize all HR functions across the full employee journey, all in one place:
- talent acquisition: digitize and collaborate over recruitments with our ATS (applicant tracking system), then onboard your new joiners fully digitally
- HR admin: manage paid time off, employee database and documents, payroll (for Singapore and Malaysia, more to come!), expense claims, timesheets...
- Performance management: track KPIs / OKRs, manage performance appraisal, gather 360° feedback...
all_locations: Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
regions: Malaysia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and medium enterprises in Malaysia, Singapore and wider Southeast Asia
problem: SMEs run HR across spreadsheets and single purpose tools for recruiting, leave, payroll and appraisals.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per employee with payroll for Singapore and Malaysia
product_category: HR management and payroll software
market_need_then: TechCrunch (2021-03) reported 10x growth from a small base and local rivals that focus on single solutions such as payroll, indicating SME demand for an all in one tool.
outcome_analysis: BrioHR launched to early adopters in late 2019, raised a $1.3M seed led by Global Founders Capital before YC Winter 2021, and then took about four years to raise a $6.5M Series A led by Openspace Ventures in May 2025 with over 1,000 customers across ASEAN. Slow, modest funding suggests capital efficient growth in a crowded SME HR market. It remains independent with no exit.

name: Bristle
one_liner: At-home oral health testing, coaching & care
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Health conscious consumers in the US (also sold via dental offices and partners) who pay for an at-home oral microbiome test
problem: Oral health problems such as bad breath, gum inflammation and decay are treated reactively; people cannot see which microbes drive them between dental visits.
business_model: Direct to consumer test kit (about $169) with coaching and care plan; partnerships with dental offices and programs
product_category: At-home saliva microbiome testing, consumer health
founder_names: David Lin; Brian Maurer; Shivam Patel
market_need_then: The company links oral bacteria to more than 50 systemic diseases and positions preventive care against a roughly $145B US dental market (Initialized Capital blog, 2022-07).
outcome_analysis: Bristle sells an at-home oral microbiome test and raised a $3M seed in July 2022. It was still operating in 2026 with partnerships with Dentistry.One and Tiny Health, but no later funding was found and the traction figures are company claims. Whether it reached strong product market fit or remains small is unknown.

name: Brite
one_liner: Software that helps employees pick their employee benefits.
long_description: Brite is disrupting the employee benefits education space by building a platform that allows employee benefits brokerages to build digital benefit guides that drive employees to enroll in the right plans and understand their benefits better. To those who are in the industry...we are the "Employee Navigator" of benefits education software.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Employee benefits brokerages (and their employer clients) that need to educate employees about plan choices
problem: Employees misunderstand benefits and choose plans poorly; brokers educate with PDFs and slide decks.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to brokerages, with a carrier funded access pricing option
product_category: Benefits education and decision support software
founder_names: Ben Hale; Landon Fielding; Jake Parkinson; Colton Shields
competitors_at_founding: Employee Navigator; PDFs and PowerPoint decks
market_need_then: Brokers relied on static documents; Brite later reported over 3 million employees reached (company claim) and partners such as USI, Gallagher and Aon, indicating demand from large brokerages.
outcome_analysis: Brite sold benefits education guides to brokerages, raised a $1.5M seed after YC in October 2021 and a $7.8M Series A led by Elevation Capital in July 2022. It now lists large brokerage partners and reports over 3 million employees reached, so it appears to have a working sales motion in a niche. No exit or distress was found.

name: Broad
one_liner: The multicurrency account and card for Brazilians
long_description: Broad is building global financial products that enable life without borders.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Brazilians who travel, shop online abroad or live overseas and want multicurrency money
problem: Brazilians pay high fees and the IOF tax on international card spending and lack easy accounts in pounds, euros and dollars.
business_model: Currency conversion spread (2%) on a multicurrency account and Mastercard card
product_category: Consumer fintech, multicurrency account and card
market_need_then: Brazilian outlets in 2022 described demand from Brazilians living or spending abroad and high conversion costs including a 1.1% IOF tax; multiple rivals were raising money for the same need.
outcome_analysis: Broad launched in beta at the end of 2021 and publicly in June 2022 into a market where Nomad, Wise and Revolut were already well funded. YC provided the first check and a further round was mentioned but never sized publicly. The company site says it closed on March 16, 2026; the cause is not public, so the failure factors are inferred from competition and the absence of any disclosed follow on round.

name: Bueno Finance
one_liner: Building Chime for India
long_description: Credit building platform for next billion users. We offer digital credit card over UPI
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Blue-collar and gig workers in India with thin credit files, reached through employers
problem: Blue-collar workers in India lack access to formal credit. Bueno offered a UPI based digital credit card and short-term credit to build credit history.
business_model: Consumer lending and credit card interest and fees, with B2B employer tie-ups
product_category: Credit building neobank (India)
market_need_then: India has over 300 million blue-collar workers with limited formal credit access, and press in 2021 covered the segment as underserved.
outcome_analysis: Bueno raised a 3 million dollar seed in June 2021 for credit products aimed at blue-collar workers in India. It was reported unable to raise further funds during the fintech funding slump, and BetterPlace, a workforce platform already among its investors and keen to enter lending, acquired it in May 2023 for an undisclosed price.

name: Buoyant Aero
one_liner: Bringing back blimps
long_description: Buoyant Aero builds zero-emissions autonomous drone blimps to break free from existing advertising paradigms and reach new audiences in new places. Whether it’s on the beach, outside the convention center, or through the window of your target executive’s office, Buoyant’s blimps amplify your message to create measurable brand benefits.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Brands and event marketers who rent custom branded blimps (originally logistics and cargo customers)
problem: Billboards and digital ads are saturated; brands want physical attention grabbing media, and cargo operators in remote areas lack cheap middle mile delivery.
business_model: Turnkey blimp rental service for advertising (originally planned cargo airships)
product_category: Autonomous drone blimps for advertising
competitors_at_founding: Flying Whales; Hybrid Air Vehicles; Lockheed Martin; LTA Research (Sergey Brin)
market_need_then: In 2021 the founders had letters of intent worth $5M from cargo prospects including an Alaskan regional air carrier (TechCrunch). Later, advertising customers such as Amazon Prime Video rented blimps.
outcome_analysis: Buoyant started as a cargo airship company with $5M in letters of intent and four prototype flights, then moved to rentable advertising blimps with named brand clients. Funding is poorly documented (aggregators show roughly $125K to $3M), so scale and runway are unknown. It looks like a small niche business that survived by finding a nearer revenue market.

name: Buró de Ingresos
one_liner: The Work Number for LatAm
long_description: Buró de Ingresos makes it easy for consumers and businesses to share income information to financial institutions
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Banks, fintech lenders and employers in Latin America, mainly Mexico, that need verified income and employment data for credit decisions
problem: Lenders in Latin America cannot easily verify the income of applicants, many of whom work informally or in the gig economy and have no credit history.
business_model: usage-based API per verification
product_category: Income and employment verification API
founder_names: José Carlos Aguilar; Pierre Delarroqua; Antoine Nguyen Hong Duc
market_need_then: The founders ran a gig economy lending company and found they could not validate earnings, so they built integrations that proved more valuable than the lending business. Many applicants in Latin America lack credit history.
outcome_analysis: The company grew out of a failed or abandoned gig lending business whose founders knew the income verification pain first hand. It raised a 2.6 million dollar seed in January 2022, signed lenders such as Tarjeta Falabella Soriana, and in May 2026 raised 4 million dollars led by Experian while reporting about 5 million verifications in 2025. It is still active and no exit has occurred.

name: BusinessOnBot
one_liner: Automated user acquisition & selling on WhatsApp for businesses
long_description:
We help D2C brands and SMBs in India acquire customers and sell on WhatsApp. We do this by offering attribution based marketing and storefront ordering through a commerce bot with 
vernacular support.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: D2C brands and small and medium businesses in India selling over WhatsApp
problem: Indian D2C brands and SMBs struggled to acquire customers and take orders over WhatsApp, with weak attribution and no vernacular language support.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus WhatsApp messaging usage
product_category: WhatsApp commerce and marketing automation, later AI omnichannel support and marketing
founder_names: Kirushanth Kumar; Mohit Kumar; Aditya Chintapalli
market_need_then: WhatsApp was the dominant messaging channel in India and D2C brands were growing in 2020 and 2021, with the WhatsApp Business API opening commerce use cases. Demand evidence is directory level only.
outcome_analysis: BusinessOnBot raised about 1.3 million dollars in December 2021, has grown to 25 people and claims more than 1000 brands as customers, and remains active. The WhatsApp commerce market is crowded with funded rivals such as WATI, so growth has been steady rather than venture scale on public evidence. No shutdown, acquisition or large later round was found.

name: Buzzle
one_liner: Automatic voice-of-customer trends & metrics from sales conversations.
long_description:
Buzzle help product marketing teams identify competitive moats and weaknesses, marketing teams generate & understanding voice of customer and product teams gauge demand in feature requests based on customer pain points, all automatically from a company’s library of recorded sales and success calls. Buzzle is founded by alumni from the University of Michigan. Adithya operated as the NLP modeling lead at Capital One's Center for Machine Learning. Michael was the lead developer of Capital One's privacy portal, serving millions of customers. Bhairav dropped out of his PhD at MIT to found Buzzle, after publishing research on deep learning and robotics at NVIDIA Research, NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, and the Montreal Institute for Learning algorithms.
	
Buzzle was formerly named q&ai!
all_locations: Philadelphia, PA, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Byte Kitchen
one_liner: Increasing restaurant profitability through our AI Operating System
long_description: Byte is able to quickly expand the geographic footprint of any given brand with minimal up front investment by licensing their IP, and rolling out their cuisine across a network of next generation kitchens optimized for delivery, pick up, and take out.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; San Mateo, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent and regional restaurant brands wanting to expand through delivery kitchens, later restaurant operators buying software
problem: Independent restaurants struggled to expand and profit in delivery. Byte Kitchen licensed their brands into shared digital food halls called Noshery, then pivoted to selling its operating software.
business_model: Brand licensing and food hall operations, later restaurant operations SaaS
product_category: Digital food halls and restaurant operating software
founder_names: Divyang Arora; Rahul Madadi; Quinn McKenna
market_need_then: The 2020 to 2021 delivery boom pushed restaurants toward virtual brands and shared kitchens, and press covered ghost kitchens heavily in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Byte Kitchen licensed restaurant brands into Noshery food halls in San Mateo and San Carlos and raised about 6 million dollars in August 2022 during the end of the ghost kitchen boom. By 2024 it had scaled to three halls and pivoted to restaurant software. YC lists it as acquired, but the buyer, date and price were not found and the reasons for the exit are not public.

name: Bytebot
tags: Generative AI; Robotic Process Automation; SaaS; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Bytebot is the open source container for AI desktop agents.
long_description:
Bytebot simplifies and streamlines the development of computer use agents with a ready made container for desktop automation, including APIs for mouse movements, keyboard input, and screenshot capture. 

The container enables developers to build robust, dynamic computer use agents that can be configured and run anywhere.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers building computer use agents and automation (open source), originally web data extraction users
problem: Automating web tasks like data extraction and form filling needs brittle scripts. Bytebot used AI, later as an open source containerized desktop for AI agents with mouse, keyboard and screenshot APIs.
business_model: Open source with free self-hosting; paid offering unclear
product_category: AI desktop agent infrastructure
market_need_then: Demand for no-code web automation and scraping existed in 2021, but no dated evidence on Bytebot's own demand was found.
outcome_analysis: Bytebot began in YC Summer 2021 as an AI web automation tool with a team of three and a small convertible note from Y Combinator and angels. It later repositioned as an open source desktop agent container under Tantl Labs. YC lists it as acquired and PitchBook gives December 2025 and Standard Fleet, but no press confirms it, so the cause and terms of the exit are unknown.

name: Cabal
one_liner: Private workspace for founders, investors, and advisors to collaborate
long_description: Cabal helps founders get more out of their investors and advisors. We do this by providing a private workspace for founders to send asks & updates, track contributions, and get warm intros to prospects and candidates.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startup founders (free tier), with investors and advisors as the users who contribute, and paid email tooling for founders
problem: Founders get little help from investors and advisors because asks and updates are scattered across email, and investors do not know how to help.
business_model: freemium SaaS; paid Cabal Mail Pro at 19 dollars per user per month
product_category: Investor relations and founder investor collaboration workspace, now an investor update email tool
founder_names: Fahim Ferdous; Brian Murray; Varun Rustomji
market_need_then: Founders and investors both said investor help was unstructured. Cabal began in early 2020 as a side project by a founder and a venture partner who wanted it for themselves, per Forbes.
outcome_analysis: Cabal came from a side project between a founder and a Craft Ventures partner, raised an 8 million dollar seed in May 2022 led by Craft and Seven Seven Six, and won Launch of the Day on Product Hunt. Its distribution through investor networks helped, but the public product has since narrowed to an investor update email tool and Fahim Ferdous appears as a former founder in a database. The company is active with no exit.

name: Cache
one_liner: Online convenience stores fulfilled by tiny, automated dark stores.
long_description: Online convenience stores on DoorDash, UberEats. We use automated dark stores to pass items to delivery drivers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Café
one_liner: Your Workplace Engagement Hub
long_description: Café makes it easy to discover people, meet in-person, and organize internal events. Boost connection, engagement, and attendance — all in one place.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: HR, people and operations teams at hybrid companies (and their employees)
problem: Hybrid teams did not know who was in the office when, relied on spreadsheets to coordinate, rarely met colleagues in person, and found internal events hard to organize.
business_model: B2B SaaS, freemium: free plan with unlimited seats and basic features; organization-wide rollout and advanced features paid (prices not found)
product_category: Hybrid-work scheduling and workplace engagement app
founder_names: Tom Nguyen; Arthur Lorotte de Banes
market_need_then: Before building, the founders said they interviewed 150 companies that all coordinated office attendance with spreadsheets (TechCrunch, 2021-05); the return-to-office and hybrid debate of 2021 created the need, and the first paying clients named were Livestorm, Jellysmack and Yubo.
outcome_analysis: Café started as a hybrid-office scheduling app that replaced spreadsheets, raised a $1M seed from 122West and Kima in May 2021 and joined YC Summer 2021, then broadened toward meeting colleagues in person and organizing events. It is still active with about ten people and a free plan, but there is no evidence of a later round, revenue scale or exit, and competitors such as Envoy added similar features at the time, so the outcome is a small surviving company whose growth is unproven.

name: Caire Health
one_liner: Semi-Autonomous Diagnostics for Emergent Care
long_description: We believe that no emergency should have to wait. To make this a reality we build AI that instantly reads medical scans and enables critical care teams to make diagnoses better than radiologists. This saves lives by getting emergencies to treatment immediately and by discharging non-emergent patients quickly so the next emergency doesn’t have to wait either.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hospital emergency departments, emergency physicians and radiologists reading head CT scans
problem: Emergency patients wait for radiologists to read scans, which delays treatment for time sensitive conditions such as intracranial hemorrhage.
business_model: B2B software licensed to hospitals (pricing not found)
product_category: Medical imaging AI, head CT triage and interpretation (Caire ICH)
founder_names: Anmol Warman; Pranav Warman; Roshan Warman
market_need_then: Head CT triage for hemorrhage was an established use case with cleared products by 2018, indicating hospital demand and a shortage of radiologists in emergency care.
outcome_analysis: Caire Health joined YC in Summer 2021 with a head CT hemorrhage AI. Public sources show only about 125 thousand dollars from YC, peer reviewed studies including one by the founders, and no found FDA clearance, while rivals like Aidoc were cleared in 2018. The site is live in 2026 with a three person team, but its path to a venture outcome is unclear and no exit is recorded.

name: Camber
one_liner: Admin automation for healthcare
long_description:
We’re on a mission to make behavioral health more available and accessible. We're backed by a16z, YCombinator, Craft, and many others to make this dream a reality.

At Camber, we build software for clinicians to improve quality of care. We streamline and replace manual efforts so clinicians can focus on what they do best: providing high-quality care.

—

Healthcare is broken. We think this is a problem worth solving, and we think we know how to solve it. Interested? Check out https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/camber.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Behavioral health clinics, initially ABA autism therapy providers, later physical therapy, ENT, allergy, cardiology and substance use clinics that bill insurance
problem: Specialty clinics lose revenue and staff time to manual insurance billing, claims and denials.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for revenue cycle management and billing automation
product_category: Healthcare revenue cycle management and claims automation (formerly Juniper Behavioral Health)
founder_names: Christophe Rimann; Celina Qi; Nathan Lee
market_need_then: Behavioral health and autism clinics faced heavy insurance billing burden and denial work. Evidence is the product focus and a16z, Craft and YC backing; no independent 2021 spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Camber spent roughly four years largely out of public view as Juniper Behavioral Health, then announced a 30 million dollar Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz in February 2025 with total funding about 50 million dollars. It grew to 101 people by the directory listing and widened from ABA billing to many specialties. Public detail on early traction is thin, and no exit has occurred.

name: Camlist
one_liner: The super app for pets
long_description: Camlist is the super app for pets, a video-first, mobile-only, social platform that allows pet breeders and pet parents to interact, transact, and care for their furry friends all under one roof.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Pet breeders, rehoming owners and pet buyers using a mobile video marketplace, starting in the UAE and moving to the UK
problem: Peer to peer pet listings use static photos on classifieds sites, so buyers cannot judge the animal and scams are common.
business_model: marketplace with in-app payments and pet services
product_category: Video first pet marketplace and social app
competitors_at_founding: Traditional online classifieds such as eBay
market_need_then: Pandemic era pet demand and scams in classifieds. The company reported rehoming over 6,000 pets and about 2 million dollars monthly GMV in November 2021 (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Camlist raised 1.3 million dollars pre-seed in November 2021 while claiming strong GMV growth and thousands of rehomed pets, and the YC directory still lists it as active with 5 people. No later round, exit or failure was found, so the company's path after 2021 is not public.

name: Camp
one_liner: A Nouns DAO governance client
all_locations: Stockholm, Stockholm County, Sweden; San Francisco, CA, USA; Remote
regions: Sweden; United States of America; Europe; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Nouns DAO token holders, delegates and builders who vote on and discuss governance proposals
problem: Nouns DAO governance required clearer tools for browsing proposals, discussing, voting and managing funding streams than the default interfaces.
business_model: unclear; a free client funded by DAO grants (not confirmed in sources)
product_category: Crypto DAO governance client (Nouns Camp)
founder_names: Christian Södergren; Pedro Pregueiro; Olle Werme
market_need_then: Nouns DAO was a high profile NFT DAO in 2021 and 2022 with on-chain governance, so interfaces for proposals and voting had a niche audience. No independent spend evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Camp built a governance client for a single DAO, Nouns, and its public traces are community update posts rather than funding news. The product site states it stopped being active on September 30, 2026 with no stated cause. A small niche audience and dependence on one DAO's treasury and contracts are plausible reasons, but the actual cause is not public.

name: Canopi
tags: Carbon Capture and Removal; Crypto / Web3; Climate
one_liner: API to measure and eliminate carbon emissions
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Carbonfact
one_liner: Decarbonizing the fashion industry
long_description: The first apparel & footwear Carbon Management Platform.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Apparel and footwear brands, multi-brand retailers and their suppliers that need carbon accounting, product lifecycle assessments and regulatory reporting
problem: Fashion brands could not measure emissions at product level or meet reporting rules because supplier data was scattered and carbon tools were generic.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Carbon management and environmental intelligence platform for fashion
founder_names: Marc Laurent; Romain Champourlier; Martin Daniel
market_need_then: Rising pressure from regulation and brand pledges on supply chain emissions, and VC investment in carbon accounting grew from 54.6 million dollars in 2020 to 398.5 million in 2021 per PitchBook cited by Axios.
outcome_analysis: Carbonfact picked fashion as a vertical for carbon accounting while horizontal rivals chased enterprises. It raised a 2 million dollar seed in June 2022 and a 15 million dollar Series A in April 2024, grew to 45 people and over 300 brands, and bought Vaayu in May 2026 to consolidate fashion product data. Regulation such as CSRD and Digital Product Passports added a tailwind.

name: Care Weather
tags: Hard Tech; Space Exploration; Satellites; Weather; Manufacturing
one_liner: The highest-accuracy global weather data from low-cost flat satellites
long_description: Care Weather collects the highest-accuracy global weather data to help governments and shipping companies adapt to extreme weather. The data is collected by Care Weather’s unique flat-panel radar satellite, which is 1000X more cost effective because it’s vertically integrated, gets more solar power, and sails on top of the atmosphere for a closer view of the surface. Our team includes CEO Patrick Walton (NASA Earth science fellow) and CTO Alex Laraway (mach 4 rockets). In the last 4 months, we built and launched the smallest radar satellite ever. We have $35M worth of LOIs, including one from the Air Force and others from cargo shippers. Care Weather is backed by Boost VC, Kickstart Seed Fund, Y Combinator, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Governments, weather agencies and shipping companies that need frequent ocean surface wind and weather data
problem: Weather forecasts rely on aging government satellites and sparse sensors, so ocean winds are observed infrequently. Care Weather aims to give hourly, high accuracy ocean surface observations from cheap radar satellites.
business_model: Data sales to government and maritime customers from its own satellite constellation, plus government grants
product_category: Small radar satellites (scatterometer) for ocean surface winds and weather data
competitors_at_founding: Spire Global; Government weather satellites (NOAA, JTWC sources)
market_need_then: Launch post cites aging government satellites and non scalable stations as the data source, and the company reported letters of intent from the Air Force, National Weather Service and shippers (stated as $35M on the YC profile and $50M in the launch post; unverified).
outcome_analysis: Care Weather is still operating and has flown multiple Veery satellites since its 2021 pre-seed and a 2023 NSF grant. Its founders have deep satellite engineering backgrounds, which fits a hardware heavy problem. Public funding is thin and only grant and pre-seed money is found, so whether it can raise a larger round is not yet shown.

name: Careerist
one_liner: Learning platform for job seekers with job applications automation
long_description:
Careerist is an ed-fintech platform that trains job seekers for tech careers (in QA, Sales, Support & more), finances them and automates their job hunting. Our B2B2C platform aggregates job seekers, tutors and employers – streamlining training and placement.

Techcrunch: "Edtech meets SaaS in Careerist’s job placement learning platform. The startup trains job seekers through live and self-paced training taught by third-party tutors. The adaptive learning software is meant to help candidates prep for tech interviews. Once a candidate is well equipped, Careerist uses automation to help them apply for jobs."
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Career changers without tech experience who pay for training in QA, automation and related roles, often via financing
problem: People trying to enter tech jobs lack structured training, financing and help applying; Careerist bundles live training, loans or deferred payment and automated job applications.
business_model: Tuition for training programs with financing options and a job-within-a-year money back guarantee; B2B2C marketplace of tutors, job seekers and employers
product_category: Ed-fintech and job placement training
founder_names: Ivan Tsybaev; Max Gusakov; Max Glubochansky
market_need_then: Pandemic era demand for tech career switching and high bootcamp prices created need for financing and placement support; the company claims job seekers pay for it.
outcome_analysis: Careerist raised a seed in February 2021 and a reported 8M USD Series A in 2023 while many bootcamps contracted, and now reports about 100 staff. Its financing plus guarantee model and QA focus kept demand alive, though outcomes data and returns are not public, so strength of fit is unverified.

name: Cartpanda
one_liner: Global online sales platform
long_description:
As an ecommerce platform, we provide a complete ecosystem for creators and entrepreneurs to sell and promote their products and services, including tools for product management, affiliate management, payment processing and much more. Users can sell various types of products, including digital goods, services, events, and physical items.

Cartpanda help entrepreneurs scale their global sales by providing a high converting checkout page and payment solution, capable to convert to 180+ currencies and languages.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Creators and online sellers, mainly in Brazil, selling digital and physical products internationally
problem: Sellers need a high converting checkout with local payment methods and many currencies, plus affiliate and order management, without stitching together tools.
business_model: Platform with transaction fees on checkout and payment processing
product_category: Ecommerce checkout and payments platform
market_need_then: The 2022 Startups.com.br interview framed Cartpanda as a Brazilian answer to Shopify and reported monthly billing above seven figures in reais, which indicates seller demand (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Cartpanda appears to be operating with a team of about 60 according to the YC page, and press in 2022 said it grew more than five times after YC. Funding details are not public, so its position among larger checkout rivals cannot be judged from sources.

name: CashBook
one_liner: Ramp for Indian Businesses - UPI Wallets for Employee Expenses
long_description: Issue UPI wallets to employees, track and control the spend.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian businesses, including field heavy enterprises, that pay employee expenses
problem: Employees pay business expenses out of pocket and wait for reimbursement; companies lack real time control. CashBook issues UPI wallets to employees with limits and tracking.
business_model: SaaS pricing per wallet or employee, with wallets issued by a licensed PPI partner
product_category: Expense management using UPI wallets
market_need_then: India's businesses reimburse employee expenses manually and UPI was widely adopted; the founders' earlier Raseedbook app served small business bookkeeping, and CashBook says it serves 4,500+ businesses.
outcome_analysis: CashBook raised a $2.3M seed in September 2021 after YC and is still operating, claiming 4,500+ business customers. UPI adoption in India gave it a tailwind, but its dependence on a partner's wallet licence and the absence of later announced rounds make its long term trajectory unclear.

name: Catena Biosciences
one_liner: Using protein coupling to build new therapies
long_description: Catena’s technology lets us attach any two proteins together using an enzyme and the native amino acids tyrosine and cysteine within target proteins. It is a true platform technology because it enables the joining of any two soluble proteins together with minimal engineering and without restrictions due to protein size or complexity. Our work has already been used to modify cancer specific antibodies, CRISPR proteins and even cell surfaces. Our ability to produce modular protein therapeutics in a fraction of the time allows for true library creation across the therapeutics spectrum from oncology, vaccines, inflammatory disease and beyond.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Berkeley, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Biopharma developers building antibody drug conjugates and other protein therapeutics for solid tumors
problem: Conventional conjugation attaches linkers at random positions on antibodies. Catena couples two proteins at defined sites using an enzyme and native tyrosine and cysteine residues, enabling multi payload conjugates.
business_model: Therapeutics developer using its own protein conjugation platform; revenue not yet public
product_category: Protein conjugation platform and antibody drug conjugate therapeutics
founder_names: Marco Lobba; Matthew Francis; Geo Guillen
market_need_then: ADC makers sought site specific, multi payload conjugation; the company described random linker attachment as the traditional method (Berkeley and company materials).
outcome_analysis: Catena spun out of Berkeley protein chemistry research, joined YC in summer 2021, and raised a small seed extension in 2024, and added a chief business officer and chief scientific officer in January 2024. Capital raised appears modest for a therapeutics company, so progress depends on the planned Series A.

name: CellChorus
one_liner: The dynamic single-cell analysis company
long_description:
At CellChorus, we apply artificial intelligence to evaluate thousands of microscopy videos in parallel to evaluate how immune cells move, interact and perform over time. This allows our customers to discover, develop, manufacture and deliver cell therapies, antibodies, vaccines and other novel therapies faster, at lower expense, and with higher rates of success.

Our customers include top-25 biopharma companies and seed-stage biotechs that are developing cell therapies, antibody therapeutics and vaccines (including one of the few companies with an approved CAR T cell therapy).

Hear from the team at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IE9x_tm0XnI
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Biopharma and cell therapy developers who need single cell functional analysis of immune cells
problem: Bulk assays hide how individual immune cells move, interact and kill. CellChorus uses AI on time lapse microscopy in nanowell grids (TIMING) to track thousands of single cells.
business_model: Instrument and services revenue from biopharma, plus NIH and NSF grants
product_category: Single cell time lapse imaging and AI analysis platform
market_need_then: Cell therapy developers needed functional single cell readouts; NIH funded the platform via SBIR and STTR awards.
outcome_analysis: CellChorus remains active in Houston with grant funding from NIH, NSF and NCI and customers including large biopharma by its own account. Equity funding is unclear, and it looks like a grant funded tools company rather than a venture scale raiser so far.

name: Cero
tags: Machine Learning; Consumer Health Services; B2B; NLP
one_liner: Automated communication between hospitals and patients in Latam
long_description:
At Cero, we solve specific coordination tasks between hospitals and patients, such as appointment confirmations and last minute cancellations, by automatically communicating with patients over WhatsApp. For example, a patient can confirm and reschedule their appointment without needing to call anyone.

Almost half of the medical appointments in Latin America are missed because patients simply do not show up. This ranges from missing a regular dentist check to missing an expensive MRI scan. With increasing pressure to improve access to care in developing countries, optimizing communication and coordination with patients is a key task to achieve. This is a massive problem especially in places where most people don't know how to effectively use self-service mediums (or are too busy to use them).
 
We bootstrapped the company and we are profitable. As of August 2021 we have $97K in monthly revenue from 15 clients with a CMRG of 20% in the last year. We have 100% logo retention and we grow with our clients. We are currently coordinating over 600,000 medical appointments every month, just in Chile.

This problem represents a $3.5B market opportunity in Latin America only. Latin America has 650M people, each one having an average of 3 medical consultations per year. We charge for every time we effectively communicate with a patient. We plan to handle several coordination interactions with every patient for each consultation, which considers a roadmap of scheduling, confirming, booking, reimbursements, payments, among others.

We are a team mixing strong knowledge about the healthcare industry with deep technical skills. Felipe (CEO) is a former dentist that has led deep changes in healthcare payments in Chile. Mauricio (CTO) and Jorge (R&D), both PhD in Computer Science, led the creation of the most advanced Spanish Language Neural Network used daily by scientists and practitioners in LatAm (BETO: Spanish BERT).

In a weekend project, Mauricio and Jorge automated the communication with students attending a summer school obtaining impressive engagement. Felipe was struggling with contacting his patients to coordinate appointments, and saw a big opportunity in this technology. The three together have designed and run a solution that as of 2021 is coordinating over 600,000 patients per month in their home country, Chile.

name: Dailybot
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Collaboration; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Make all team work visible — people and AI agents
long_description:
Dailybot is the coordination platform for software teams where people and AI agents work side by side.

As engineering teams increasingly operate alongside multiple AI agents — coding agents, incident responders, research assistants — the gap between what's being worked on and what the team can actually see has become a critical problem. Dailybot closes that gap.

name: Digistain
one_liner: Pioneering Breast Cancer Diagnostics for a Healthier Tomorrow
long_description:
In the global fight against breast cancer, Digistain stands at the forefront, offering a beacon of hope to millions. Our journey began at Imperial College London, where ground-breaking research gave birth to a technology poised to revolutionize breast cancer diagnostics.

The Challenge: Every year, breast cancer affects 2.3 million individuals globally. Post-surgery, 60% of patients are advised to undergo genomic testing, an expensive and time-consuming process monopolized by a single lab in the U.S., costing around $4,000 and taking nearly two months. Consequently, only 5% undergo this vital testing. The rest, unable to access this crucial diagnostic step, often resort to chemotherapy—a treatment that, in one in four cases, is more harmful than the cancer itself.

Our Solution: Digistain addresses this critical gap. Our technology transforms the current diagnostic process by enabling hospitals to analyze patient samples in-house using existing equipment, supplemented with our innovative technology. This approach offers near-instantaneous decision-making data, a stark contrast to the existing month-long waits. Central to our technology is a proprietary algorithm that identifies a unique spectral fingerprint of the tumour in the infrared spectrum, providing a personalized risk score. This score guides oncologists in selecting the most effective, individualized treatment plans, potentially reducing unnecessary chemotherapy and its harmful side effects.

Impact and Potential: Our solution not only challenges the status quo in technology but also in accessibility. In a landmark government-commissioned study, Digistain demonstrated clinical evidence on par with the market leader, but at a fraction of the cost and time. Already making waves in clinical practice globally, with insurance reimbursement at leading cancer centers, our technology represents a paradigm shift in cancer care.

Recognized by the Institute of Physics, the Royal Society, and Imperial College for our innovative contributions, and supported by entities like the NHS, Y Combinator, and the European Investment Bank, Digistain is more than a company—it’s a movement towards equitable, effective cancer treatment. With the potential to democratize access to life-saving diagnostics, Digistain is not just envisioning a better future for cancer patients; we are actively creating it.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe

business_model: Per-test diagnostic fee through a UK laboratory and distributors
product_category: Breast cancer diagnostic test, medical device
competitors_at_founding: Oncotype DX (Exact Sciences); Prosigna and EndoPredict
market_need_then: Genomic tests are expensive; the company claims a low-cost alternative with results in 1 to 2 days, supported by Imperial clinical data on 800+ patients.
outcome_analysis: Digistain turned Imperial College spectroscopy research into a UKCA-marked breast cancer prognostic test, raised about 1 million dollars in August 2022, and by late 2024 had insurer adoption and an Indian distribution partnership. Evidence of scale is limited to small seed funding and press, so it is an active medtech with regulatory progress but unproven revenue.

name: Dime
one_liner: Instant E2E tests for your website
long_description: As developers, we’re constantly going through the cycle of starting to write tests, deciding we can’t prioritize them because we need to ship new features, and then running into bugs in production as a result. Autotest lets you build comprehensive integration tests for your website with basically no work on your part, so you get the benefits of testing without wasting dev time on it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Djamo
one_liner: Challenger Bank for consumers in French speaking Africa.
long_description: Djamo is a challenger Bank for consumers in french speaking Africa where less than 25% of the population is banked, we are building seamless and affordable banking solutions to break into this huge untaped market and bring millions of people into financial inclusion.
all_locations: Abidjan, Abidjan Autonomous District, Ivory Coast; Dakar, Dakar Region, Senegal
regions: Ivory Coast; Senegal; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Banked and unbanked consumers and small businesses in francophone West Africa, mainly Cote d'Ivoire and Senegal
problem: Fewer than 25 percent of people in francophone Africa are banked and traditional banks are costly.
business_model: Digital bank with interchange, card and premium tier fees, lending and business payments
product_category: Consumer neobank and fintech
competitors_at_founding: Wave; Orange Money, Moov Money, MTN MoMo
market_need_then: Company and TechCrunch cite under 25 percent banked in francophone Africa and over 55 percent of Djamo users unbanked.
outcome_analysis: Djamo reached over a million active customers in Cote d'Ivoire and Senegal, raised a 14 million Series A in 2022 and a 17 million equity round in April 2025, and gained a microfinance approval. Telcos and Wave are pressing on its prepaid card turf, and a Series C near 40 million was reported in July 2026, so the trajectory is strong but contested.

name: Dots 💸
one_liner: Developer friendly drop in payouts infrastructure
long_description: Dots is a developer-friendly API that lets businesses pay their contractors through just a few lines of code. Whether its gig workers like Uber drivers, sellers on marketplaces like Etsy, or simply your local handyman - Dots’ abstracts away the complexity of payouts completely. We manage the entire process: information collection (KYC), payments through any rail (ACH, Venmo, CashApp, Zelle, international, and many more to come), and even filing tax forms! Dots lets developers get payouts up and running over just a few hours, rather than the many months this would normally take.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Marketplaces, creator platforms and gig businesses that pay contractors
problem: Paying many contractors needs KYC, multiple payout rails and tax forms; Dots provides these through one API.
business_model: Usage-based API with per-payout fees
product_category: Payouts infrastructure API
competitors_at_founding: Stripe Connect; Tipalti; Hyperwallet and Trolley
market_need_then: Growth of gig and creator marketplaces in 2021 created payout demand; Dots later reports over 150M dollars in monthly payouts and 400 percent revenue growth, self-reported.
outcome_analysis: Dots built a developer payouts API from the 2021 batch and by February 2026 raised an 8.9 million dollar Series A led by DCM, claiming profitability, 1 billion dollars delivered and fast revenue growth. All traction figures are self-reported and earlier seed rounds were not verified, so the case is promising but thinly documented.

name: Double
one_liner: We make software for bookkeepers.
long_description:
Double makes software to help bookkeepers manage their clients' back-office.

We write the same kind of software that venture-backed bookkeepers like Pilot write internally, but instead of doing bookkeeping, we sell that software to the 1.5M bookkeepers across the US.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Bookkeeping and accounting firms in North America
problem: Firms struggle to manage client work and month-end close across tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Accounting practice management and AI close software
market_need_then: Accounting firms were adopting cloud tools; Double says it serves thousands of firms and 4,000+ per a 2025 release, self-reported.
outcome_analysis: Keeper, now Double, grew into a bookkeeping practice management tool used by thousands of firms and raised a 6.5 million dollar Series A in December 2025 after a rebrand. Earlier funding is not documented, and the YC page shows 80 staff, which suggests capital efficiency, though no source states revenue.

name: DreamWorld
one_liner: DreamWorld is a next-gen Minecraft with generative AI building
long_description:
DreamWorld is a next-gen Minecraft with generative AI building. A game and platform for 3D user generated content, DreamWorld is a digital world with one of the largest multiplayer capacities ever developed.
Our players grew up on User Generated Content games, but are now 13-40 and have aged out Roblox / Minecraft. DreamWorld provides more powerful building tools, better graphics, and massive social multiplayer.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Gamers aged 13 to 40 who want a Minecraft or Roblox style sandbox MMO
problem: Players wanted a shared persistent 3D world with stronger building tools than Minecraft and Roblox.
business_model: Game sales, free-to-play with in-game monetization, and creator tools
product_category: Sandbox MMO and UGC game platform
market_need_then: UGC sandbox games had huge audiences in 2021, but reporting shows the Kickstarter raised under 65K versus a stated need far larger.
outcome_analysis: DreamWorld pitched an infinite sandbox MMO, raised under 65 thousand dollars on Kickstarter in 2021 against heavy skepticism, launched on Steam Early Access on 10 March 2026 and was pulled from sale and its servers shut down by June 2026. The record points to scope far beyond resources and weak execution; the cause of the final takedown was not made public, and no institutional round beyond YC was verified.

name: Dressd
one_liner: Make infinite $$$ off of clothes in your closet without selling them
long_description:
Dressd is AirBnb for clothes; a P2P clothing rental marketplace. Unlike Rent the Runway, we don’t handle any inventory or deal with cleaning the items. Our initial target market is sorority girls who can have up to 3-4 events per week that they need a new outfit/dress for. One of our core theses is that this idea couldn’t have existed at scale until now because resale apps like Depop & Poshmark paved the way for a P2P model to work after familiarizing users with the process of taking pictures of items, shipping, etc. 

Advantages to our P2P model

- Entrepreneur-led
    - Similar to Depop, most of our growth will be spearheaded by a group of “top renters”
- More variety in inventory
    - Existing rental companies like Rent the Runway own all the inventory so they're limited to the brands they buy/partner with. Since we're P2P, our users can rent any item or brand that's in someone else's closet
- Better margins
    - we don’t touch any inventory or deal with the cleaning of any items
    - Unlike Rent the Runway, we don’t handle any inventory or the cleaning of items. This means people renting out their clothing on Dressd are responsible for shipping things out & returning them in good condition

Here are some of our links!

[dressd website](https://dressd.com/stylist-waitlist)

[dressd instagram](https://www.instagram.com/shop.dressd/)

[dressd tiktok](https://vm.tiktok.com/TTPdMPYFRY/)
