regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Dyte
one_liner: Real-time audio & video SDKs, ready to launch 🚀
long_description: Integrate live video calls with Dyte Video SDK with less than 10 lines of code.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers and product teams at companies that embed live video and audio calls in their apps
problem: Building reliable real-time video calls on WebRTC is slow and hard; Dyte offered SDKs to add calls in a few lines of code.
business_model: Usage-based API and SDK pricing (per participant minute, with a free tier)
product_category: Real-time audio and video SDKs
market_need_then: The 2020 shift to remote work and virtual events raised demand for embedded video; the company claims integration in under 10 lines of code.
outcome_analysis: Dyte was founded in 2020 in Bengaluru, joined YC in Winter 2021 and raised an 11.6 million dollar seed in April 2022 led by Unbound, Surge and Nexus. It reached a sale to Cloudflare, which one analyst framed as an acquihire to gain a client SDK; Cloudflare launched RealtimeKit with Dyte in April 2025. The price was not disclosed and the product is now folded into Cloudflare.

name: Eat Blueprint
tags: Anti-Aging; Fitness; Food; Health & Wellness; Food & Beverage
one_liner: Longevity Nutrition Service
long_description: Making Blueprint Protocol-inspired meals for longevity and performance. Organic, local, gluten-free, and seed oil free.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Echoes HQ
one_liner: Measure and communicate engineering activity
long_description:
Echoes gives engineering leaders visibility into the alignment of engineering efforts against the business goals and whether their deliveries are having actual business impacts.

By doing so we enable engineering leaders to make informed decisions on hiring and priorities, to communicate effectively on their team's activity to their business partners/bosses/investors, and to build engagement by putting their team's work into context.

We achieve this by offering a seamless way for engineers to connect their day-to-day contributions to their intent, creating the missing link between tech outputs and business outcomes.
regions: Netherlands; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering leaders (CTOs, VPs of engineering) at software companies who must explain engineering work to the business
problem: Engineering leaders cannot easily show how engineering effort lines up with business goals or whether deliveries had business impact, which makes hiring, priority and reporting decisions harder.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Engineering analytics and intent tracking
market_need_then: Engineering leaders were adopting engineering management platforms in 2021, shown by Jellyfish and LinearB raising rounds in early 2021, so the reporting pain was funded and visible.
outcome_analysis: Echoes stayed a three person company in Amsterdam with no verified funding beyond the YC deal and no reported exit or shutdown. It launched its product in September 2021 and a Product Hunt launch followed in May 2023. The market already had better funded engineering analytics vendors, so it has not shown venture scale growth in public sources.

name: Emerge Tools
one_liner: Supercharge your mobile apps
long_description:
Emerge is a suite of developer tools designed to supercharge mobile apps and the teams that build them.

Our tooling is already used by many of the best mobile teams in the world like DoorDash, Square, Airbnb, Duolingo, Stripe, among others. Come help us make it even better!
all_locations: Los Angeles, CA, USA; Santa Monica, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mobile engineering teams at large app companies (DoorDash, Square, Airbnb, Duolingo, Spotify) that pay for developer tooling
problem: Mobile apps bloat in size and slow in launch, and teams build custom tooling to track it. Emerge sells off-the-shelf size analysis, snapshot testing and performance tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for developer tools
product_category: Mobile developer tools
market_need_then: App size affects installs and App Store limits; a January 2021 post showed Dropbox at 269 MB with about 40 percent reducible, and large teams built custom tooling for this.
outcome_analysis: Emerge started with iOS app size analysis in 2020 and expanded to snapshots, dead code removal and launch speed, winning customers such as OpenAI, Spotify, Duolingo and Square with a very small team. Sentry acquired it on May 6, 2025 for undisclosed terms and rebuilt Size Analysis in its own product. The outcome fits a niche technical product bought by a platform that wanted mobile depth.

name: Enable Us
one_liner: Digital Sales Rooms (Acquired by MindTickle)
long_description:
Enable.us is an all-in-one workspace for the B2B Sales, Marketing, and Customer facing teams to provide a personalized and interactive buying and onboarding experience to their prospective customers. Customer facing teams have everything they need in one single location to:

- Capture Video/Audio Product demos, customer references, sales decks, white-papers, contracts, onboarding material, and other content 

- Automatically organize & contextualize  (by industry, persona, deal stage, deal size)

- Build personalized deal rooms with AI-targeted content,  simplified workflows, and 1:1 communication with the prospect and other stakeholders/influencers.

Learn more about our launch here https://www.producthunt.com/posts/referenceable or sign up here  https://www.enable.us/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B sales, marketing and customer success teams that pay for a workspace to share content with buyers
problem: Sellers scatter demos, decks and references across tools; buyers want a single personalized place to evaluate and onboard. Enable Us offers digital sales rooms with AI-targeted content.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Digital sales rooms and buyer enablement
market_need_then: Remote selling in 2020 and 2021 pushed buyers to self-serve evaluation; the company launched on Product Hunt in 2021 as Referenceable.
outcome_analysis: Enable Us began as Referenceable and became a digital sales room product, raising about 4.5 million dollars in December 2021 after YC Winter 2021. It won G2 awards in 2022 and partnered with Mindtickle, which then acquired it in May 2023 for undisclosed terms. A small raise and quick sale suggest a product-feature outcome rather than a standalone category leader.

name: Encord
tags: Machine Learning; Robotics; Enterprise Software; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: The data layer for physical AI
long_description: Encord is the data layer for physical AI. We're how the world's most ambitious AI teams turn messy, multimodal data into production systems - from humanoid robots to autonomous vehicles to smart infrastructure. 300+ teams including Toyota, Skydio, and Maxar rely on Encord to curate, manage, and align the data their models actually need. $110M raised. San Francisco, New York, and London.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: AI and machine learning teams (robotics, autonomous vehicles, medical imaging, enterprise) that need to label, curate and manage training data
problem: Teams building computer vision models spend large effort labeling and curating data with fragmented tools; Encord offers an annotation and data management platform with AI assisted labeling.
business_model: B2B SaaS and platform contracts for enterprise AI teams
product_category: Data labeling and data infrastructure for AI
market_need_then: Computer vision teams were scaling model development in 2020 and 2021, and data labeling vendors raised large rounds in early 2021 (Labelbox $40M, Scale $325M), showing funded demand.
outcome_analysis: Encord launched its product during YC in spring 2021 and raised a seed in June 2021, a Series A in October 2021, a $30M Series B in 2024 and a $60M Series C in 2026, reaching about $110M total. The AI data boom and growing computer vision and robotics demand supported growth, and the company claims 300 plus enterprise teams as customers. Strong funded rivals existed, so differentiation through AI assisted tooling and later the physical AI focus mattered.

name: Encuadrado
one_liner: Payments and scheduling for services professionals in LATAM
long_description: Encuadrado automates booking, payments, and invoicing for solo practitioners running appointment-based businesses in LATAM.
all_locations: Santiago, Santiago Metropolitan Region, Chile; Remote
regions: Chile; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Solo practitioners and independent professionals in Chile and Mexico (psychologists, doctors, nutritionists, lawyers) who run appointment based practices
problem: Independent professionals manage bookings, reminders, payments and receipts by hand over WhatsApp and phone; Encuadrado bundles scheduling, payments and electronic receipts.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (about $40 per month in 2021) plus payment processing
product_category: Scheduling and payments for independent professionals
market_need_then: The founders cited 27.2 percent of the Chilean workforce as self employed, many still managing bookings through WhatsApp, Instagram or phone calls (Bloomberg Linea, Nov 2021).
outcome_analysis: Encuadrado launched in Chile in 2019, expanded to Mexico in 2021, joined YC in Summer 2021 and raised a $1.5M seed in November 2021. Forbes Chile reported about 1,500 active professionals in 2022. It has focused on health professionals with certified clinical records and appears active, but no later round was found and the scale remains small against AgendaPro.

name: Endla
one_liner: Software that increases the value of oil & gas wells
long_description:
Endla increases the value of oil & gas wells by providing software that helps design the well that maximizes ROI.

Our product AlphaSpace, optimizes the well design by automatically producing many high-quality options which the engineer can then measure against their business objectives (auto-design). Having software that finds the optimal solution, empowers the engineer to work a layer up on understanding the problem and specifying the important objectives.

Our vision is to make auto-design and auto-operation software part of the workflow for every engineer working with physical assets.
regions: Australia; Oceania; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Upstream oil and gas operators and engineering teams (for example Senex in Queensland) that design wells and pipelines
problem: Well and pipeline design relies on manual engineering iteration; Endla's AlphaSpace generates many design options so engineers can pick the best return on investment.
business_model: Enterprise software licences (B2B SaaS)
product_category: Oil and gas engineering design automation software
market_need_then: Operators wanted lower well costs and better returns in a post 2020 cost conscious industry; customer testimonials from Senex appear on Endla's site, but dated 2021 demand evidence was not found.
outcome_analysis: Endla is a small Brisbane company that went through YC in Summer 2021 and has expanded its product from well design to a wider platform with named customers. No institutional funding, exit or shutdown was found, so its trajectory beyond a niche enterprise software business is not visible in public sources.

name: Enerjazz
one_liner: Making electric vehicle batteries affordable
long_description: Enerjazz is building a battery swapping network (like gasoline stations) for 2M+ commercial electric vehicles in India. We make batteries affordable for EV owners and enable them to earn 80% more.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Delhi, DL, India
regions: United States of America; India; America / Canada; South Asia
target_customer: Operators and owners of commercial electric vehicles in India (about 2 million vehicles cited)
problem: Battery cost is the main barrier for commercial EV owners; Enerjazz is building a battery swapping network so owners pay per use instead of buying packs.
business_model: Battery swapping network (energy as a service, per swap)
product_category: EV battery swapping
market_need_then: India pushed commercial EV adoption and the founder argued affordable storage would matter most over decades; funded rivals raised in late 2021, indicating investor demand.
outcome_analysis: Enerjazz is an early stage Indian battery swapping company founded by a former Shell strategy analyst that went through YC in Summer 2021. Public sources show little after the batch: no verified round, no exit and no shutdown. Competitors such as SUN Mobility and Battery Smart raised larger rounds in late 2021, so capital intensity and competition are the main open risks, but the outcome is not visible.

name: Enode
one_liner: Energy Orchestration Platform
long_description: Device connectivity, home energy coordination, and grid orchestration in a single platform.
regions: Norway; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Energy retailers, utilities, EV charging and smart home companies that need to connect to and control consumer energy devices
problem: Every EV, charger, battery and thermostat has its own proprietary interface; Enode offers one API to connect and optimize them for energy products and grid flexibility.
business_model: B2B API platform, usage and per device pricing
product_category: Energy device connectivity API and orchestration
market_need_then: Energy retailers needed to offer smart charging and flexibility as EVs and home batteries spread, and the energy transition drove investor interest shown by the seed and Series A.
outcome_analysis: Enode raised a $2.2M seed in July 2021 and a $15M Series A led by Creandum in November 2022, and grew to about 70 people with customers such as Vattenfall. The shift to electrification and flexible demand created a need for a unified device layer, and the company moved from an EV API to a broader energy orchestration platform. Competitors in connected car APIs existed, so breadth beyond cars was the key differentiator.

name: Enso
one_liner: Self-Service Data Prep and Blend Built for Data Teams.
long_description:
Enso Analytics is a self-service data prep and analysis platform for data teams. It transforms complex processes into repeatable workflows, saving users 7 hours weekly. With full configuration visibility, seamless environment transitions, and real-time updates, Enso caters to both non-programmers and developers, offering cloud and desktop options.

DEMO: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OBrYjpgCSEE
all_locations: Kraków, Lesser Poland Voivodeship, Poland; Remote
regions: Poland; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data teams and analysts at enterprises such as banks (HSBC, ING and Alior are named customer logos) that prepare and blend data
problem: Preparing and blending data takes slow, repeated manual work or code; Enso offers a visual and textual data preparation workflow tool that saves time.
business_model: Open source core with paid cloud and enterprise products
product_category: Self-service data preparation and blending
market_need_then: Enterprises had a large analyst population needing data preparation, shown by the entrenched use of Alteryx and Tableau Prep named in 2022 press.
outcome_analysis: Enso, previously the Luna language project, joined YC in Summer 2021 and emerged from stealth in April 2022 with a $16.5M round led by investors including SignalFire and Khosla. It positions itself as an Alteryx alternative with enterprise banking customers and about 20 to 26 staff. Founding history is long and the market has strong incumbents, but it remained active in 2026.

name: Entelexo Biotherapeutics
one_liner: Creating a New Class of Drugs to Address Incurable Autoimmune Diseases
long_description: Entelexo is creating modern treatments for immune-mediated diseases, such as psoriasis, using novel engineered exosome technology.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharma partners and patients with immune-mediated diseases such as psoriasis and multiple sclerosis (drug developer, not yet a seller)
problem: Autoimmune diseases are complex and single cytokine drugs address only one signal; Entelexo engineers exosomes to deliver multiple signals to several cell types at once.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing exosome therapeutics (future licensing or clinical development)
product_category: Engineered exosome therapeutics
founder_names: Milad Riazifar; Todd Schurr; Cameron Taylor
market_need_then: Autoimmune diseases such as psoriasis and MS have large patient populations and incomplete treatments, and exosome research was gaining attention, with Codiak already in the clinic in 2020.
outcome_analysis: Entelexo is a very small preclinical biotech that went through YC in Winter 2021, selected lead candidates in 2022 and began IND enabling animal studies in 2023. Funding found is small and inconsistent across sources, so the lack of larger rounds is not proof of failure but suggests capital is the main constraint for a capital hungry sector. No exit or shutdown was found.

name: Epinoma
one_liner: We engineer proteins that control the operating system of biology.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Clinical researchers, diagnostics developers and biopharma teams that need to measure DNA methylation, especially from blood-based liquid biopsy samples
problem: Standard methylation workflows (bisulfite conversion and similar) damage DNA and limit sensitivity. Epinoma says its EpiAmp chemistry copies DNA while keeping methylation marks, so epigenetic signals can be read at lower detection limits.
business_model: Research tools and reagents, with a path to diagnostics and epigenetic therapeutics partnerships (company site: disease detection, programmable epigenetic therapies, biopharma partnering)
product_category: Epigenetics tools and diagnostics (methyl-preserving amplification)
market_need_then: Methylation is a core signal for early cancer detection, and the Polsky Center article says currently available methylation measurement technologies have limits. Company claims a detection limit of 0.1 percent at one locus against 2 to 3 percent for current workflows (company stated).
outcome_analysis: Epinoma remains an early stage biotech tools company, still running clinical proof of concept work as of 2025 press. Its edge is a licensed methylation chemistry that is hard to copy, but no venture round is verifiable beyond a small seed reported by aggregators, so its trajectory is unclear. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found.

name: Epsilon3
tags: Commercial Space Launch; SaaS; Space Exploration; B2B; Enterprise Software
one_liner: AI-Powered ERP, MES, and Test Software for Complex Operations
long_description: Epsilon3 is the AI-Powered ERP, MES, and Test Management Software for Complex Engineering, Manufacturing, & Operations. We are a growing team of engineers from SpaceX, NASA, Google, and Stanford with unique experience planning and executing over 100 space missions. We are applying what we learned to develop web-based solutions that make building and operating advanced systems as efficient, error-free, and enjoyable as possible. Want to join a fully remote, US-based SaaS startup on a mission to solve complex problems in aerospace, energy, defense, maritime, and biotech? Apply today!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Aerospace, launch, defense and other complex hardware operators and manufacturers
problem: Launch and test teams ran critical procedures on paper checklists, spreadsheets and documents with no traceability. Epsilon3 offers software to plan, execute and track procedures, tests and manufacturing.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, sold to launch providers, space agencies and defense customers
product_category: Operations software for complex hardware (electronic procedures, MES, test management)
founder_names: Laura Crabtree; Max Mednik; Aaron Sullivan
market_need_then: Launch industry was growing fast in 2021 (TechCrunch cites analyst estimates of more than $18B by 2026) and the founder said the tools she wanted did not exist for launch operations.
outcome_analysis: Epsilon3 pairs founders from SpaceX operations with a booming launch market, signed roughly 40 customers by mid 2022 and raised a $15M Series A led by Lux Capital. It later moved from launch procedures into ERP, MES and test software with defense compliance. No Series B was found as of the sources opened, so growth after 2022 is not verified.

name: Equipt Health
tags: Sleep Tech; Consumer Health Services; Digital Health; Telemedicine
one_liner: Home medical equipment, prescribed online and delivered.
long_description: Equipt Health makes it easy for any healthcare company to offer prescription medical devices to patients. We handle the whole process: the packaging, the logistics, the clinical (via our provider network) and technical support, and the return of data from connected devices. We're starting with the diagnosis and treatment of sleep apnea at heliosleep.com.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Healthcare companies wanting to offer prescription medical devices to patients, and consumers needing sleep apnea diagnosis through its Helio Sleep brand
problem: Home medical equipment lacks an end to end stack for inventory, logistics, clinical support and device data. Sleep apnea is undiagnosed in roughly 24 million Americans (YC launch post claim).
business_model: B2B2C healthcare logistics and clinical platform plus cash pay consumer sleep apnea testing and devices (Helio Sleep)
product_category: Home medical equipment and sleep apnea telehealth
market_need_then: YC launch post cites about 24 million undiagnosed sleep apnea patients in the US and growth in home delivered care in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Equipt Health targeted home delivered medical devices, starting with sleep apnea through Helio Sleep, a consumer cash pay offering launched in March 2022. No credible funding round was found beyond a $500K convertible note listed by CB Insights, and a 2026 aggregator lists it as out of business, so the outcome and cause are not public.

name: Estoca
one_liner: The Logistics Operating System for E-commerce in LatAm
long_description: Estoca is a cloud-based logistics platform that uses AI to optimize fulfillment, warehousing, and last-mile operations for D2C brands in Latin America. Estoca provides customizable software and an integrated partner network that automate every step from storage to delivery. Our AI-driven workflows help merchants process more packages per square meter, per hour, and per person, accelerating delivery speed while reducing operational costs.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Direct to consumer and e-commerce brands in Brazil and Latin America
problem: E-commerce brands struggle with fulfillment, warehousing and last mile delivery across multiple sales channels. Estoca provides its own warehouse management, order and transport software plus warehouses.
business_model: Fulfillment with commission per processed order plus software (WMS, OMS, TMS)
product_category: E-commerce fulfillment and logistics software
market_need_then: E-commerce in Latin America grew quickly during the pandemic and brands outside marketplaces lacked fulfillment options; YC page describes AI optimized fulfillment for D2C brands.
outcome_analysis: Estoca grew from a 2020 start into a logistics operator with more than 100 clients, reported breakeven and a R$470M valuation in May 2025 led by existing investors Astella and Y Combinator. It built WMS, OMS and TMS in house, serves D2C brands and earns a commission per order, which suggests capital efficient growth in a growing market.

name: Evidence
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Analytics; Data Engineering; Data Visualization
one_liner: Business intelligence as code
long_description: Evidence is an open source, code-based alternative to drag-and-drop BI tools. Build polished data products with just SQL and markdown.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data teams and analysts who write SQL and want BI as code, from startups to large enterprises
problem: Drag and drop BI tools produce dashboards that are hard to version, review and customize. Evidence builds reports from SQL and markdown in a Git repository.
business_model: Open source core with a paid hosted product (Evidence Cloud, launched 2023) and enterprise offerings
product_category: Business intelligence as code (open source)
competitors_at_founding: Metabase; Looker; Apache Superset; Streamlit; Mode
market_need_then: Launch HN commenters in August 2021 voiced frustration with Looker, Metabase and Power BI, and the modern data stack (dbt, Fivetran, BigQuery) was growing, creating demand for code based reporting.
outcome_analysis: Evidence grew through an open source project and a Launch HN in August 2021, then raised a $2.1M seed in September 2023 led by A.Capital when it launched a hosted Evidence Cloud. It reports large enterprise users, but no later round was found and the funding is small, so scale remains modest.

name: Evidently AI
tags: Developer Tools; Machine Learning; B2B; Open Source
one_liner: Open-source monitoring for machine learning models
long_description: We are building an open-source standard to monitor ML models in production. The tool is used by enterprise data science teams to operate their models reliably and detect and resolve issues.
all_locations: London, England, United Kingdom; San Francisco, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United Kingdom; United States of America; Europe; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data scientists and ML engineers at enterprises running models in production, later AI teams evaluating LLM applications
problem: Models degrade in production through data drift and quality issues, and teams lacked a standard open source way to monitor them.
business_model: Open source Apache 2.0 library with a paid cloud and enterprise product
product_category: ML and LLM evaluation and observability (open source)
market_need_then: The July 2021 launch post pitched open source ML monitoring as a gap next to end to end platforms and proprietary tools, as production ML spread in enterprises.
outcome_analysis: Evidently built a popular open source monitoring library from a founding team with Yandex ML experience and extended it to LLM evaluation as that market grew. Public funding is thin: YC pre-seed is confirmed while a later seed of about $1M is reported only by aggregators, so its fundraising ceiling is unclear. No shutdown or acquisition was found.

name: Exa
one_liner: Web search rebuilt for LLMs
long_description: Exa is a search engine built for AIs. We enable developers to filter the internet's content with complex queries in order to bring the world's knowledge into their AI apps.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI developers and companies building agents and LLM apps that need web search and retrieval APIs
problem: Keyword search engines were built for humans. Exa builds a neural, embeddings based search engine and API so AI systems can retrieve precise web content.
business_model: Usage based search and content APIs with enterprise plans
product_category: Search API for AI agents (formerly a consumer neural search engine)
market_need_then: In 2021 the founders were building a consumer search engine on neural link prediction; demand for an AI facing search API appeared from early 2023 per Bryk.
outcome_analysis: Exa started as Metaphor, a consumer neural search engine, and pivoted around 2023 to serve AI developers just as agents and LLM apps took off. It raised a $17M Series A in 2024, $85M at a $700M valuation in 2025 and reportedly $250M at $2.2B in May 2026. Execution on its own index and the timing tailwind explain the trajectory.

name: Examedi
one_liner: Uber for Healthcare in Latinamerica
long_description: Examedi is a healthcare-at-home marketplace in Latin America that sends nurses and lab technicians directly to patients’ homes for appointments. It’s like Uber, but for medical lab work.
regions: Chile; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Patients in Chile and Mexico needing lab tests at home, plus health insurers and clinics that partner with it
problem: Getting lab exams in person is slow and costly. Examedi sends nurses and technicians to patients' homes, with online booking and digital results.
business_model: Marketplace and service provider charging per exam, with insurer and clinic partnerships (Clinica Alemana, Isapre alliances)
product_category: At-home diagnostics and lab services
founder_names: Andres Kemeny; Juan Pablo Zepeda; Ian Lee
market_need_then: Pandemic demand in 2021: COVID tests made up 41 percent of home exams in Chile by August 2021, and the company said prices were up to 80 percent below traditional labs (DF).
outcome_analysis: Examedi grew quickly on pandemic demand, raising a $17M Series A in June 2022 led by General Catalyst, then cut 25 percent of staff in April 2023 after operations became manual and inefficient, per its CEO. Further reports describe a drop from 160 to 25 employees, founder exits and a $750K round in November 2025 as General Catalyst left, so it stalled as a venture company.

name: Expent Inc
one_liner: Procure the right software 5x faster
long_description: Expent is a marketplace that accelerates software procurement for teams, while giving organizations control over the entire purchasing process.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Finance, IT and procurement teams at mid-size and larger companies that buy software and manage vendors
problem: Buying software is slow and fragmented, and organizations lack control over the purchasing process and the vendor lifecycle that follows.
business_model: B2B SaaS marketplace and workflow platform for software procurement; later vendor lifecycle and third-party risk management
product_category: Software procurement marketplace, later vendor lifecycle and third-party risk AI platform
market_need_then: Companies were adding many SaaS tools and the purchase, renewal and security review process was manual and spread across teams. Evidence is the founders' own framing on the YC page; no independent demand data was collected.
outcome_analysis: Expent started as a software procurement marketplace in the YC Winter 2021 batch with two technical founders from Workday and PlanGrid. Public funding data is thin, with only unverified aggregator figures of roughly 125 to 130 thousand dollars, which suggests a capital efficient path. The company moved toward vendor lifecycle and third-party risk management and was acquired by Hyperproof in October 2025 on undisclosed terms, so the result is a modest exit rather than a venture scale outcome.

name: Fable
one_liner: The command center for product teams
long_description: Fable is a command center for product teams - we're building for PMs what Figma has done for designers and Linear for engineers. Product teams are acting on stale information. Fable is the place that keeps everything - from specs to decisions - fresh.

name: Fathom
one_liner: The most flexible AI meeting notetaker ever built.
long_description:
Fathom captures your meetings your way – bot or bot-free, on any call. Ask questions across your entire meeting history and get instant, cited answers. Connect your intelligence to Claude, ChatGPT, your CRM, and more. Desktop, mobile, and in-person.

The real value of meetings isn't just the notes. It's the knowledge inside them.

#1 AI Notetaker on G2. Works with Zoom, Meet, and Teams.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Individuals and teams in sales, customer success and operations who record video meetings; paid tiers for teams
problem: People lose the substance of meetings and spend time taking notes. Fathom records, transcribes and summarizes calls, with a generous free tier.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with paid per-seat team plans
product_category: AI meeting notetaker
market_need_then: Zoom fatigue and the pandemic meeting load in 2020 and 2021 created demand for call recording and summaries; Fathom launched on Product Hunt on Dec 8, 2021 and was a Zoom marketplace launch partner.
outcome_analysis: Fathom launched a free AI notetaker for Zoom in 2021 and grew through a generous free tier and Zoom marketplace distribution, raising 4.7 million dollars in 2022 and 17 million in September 2024, including 2 million crowdfunded from users. It reportedly reached more than 400,000 monthly users and was bought by Superhuman on September 14, 2026 for undisclosed terms as notetakers consolidated into productivity suites.

name: Female Invest
one_liner: The world's largest financial education and community app for women
regions: Denmark; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Women, mainly in Europe and the US, who want to learn to invest and manage money; paying members of a subscription app
problem: Women invest less than men and have few approachable places to learn, so a financial gender gap persists.
business_model: Consumer subscription (about 13 dollars per month or 139 per year in 2024) for courses, a trading simulator, community and tools
product_category: Financial education and community app
founder_names: Anna-Sophie Hartvigsen; Camilla Falkenberg; Emma Due Bitz
market_need_then: Few women attended personal finance events in 2019 per the founders, and the 2020 retail investing boom increased interest. Evidence is founder statements in press, not independent surveys.
outcome_analysis: Female Invest built a subscription education and community product for women and reached tens of thousands of paying members across more than 120 countries. It raised a record Series A of about 11 million dollars in July 2024, partly through member crowdfunding, and acquired Gaia Investments in 2022 to add trading. The brand and community are the main growth drivers and the company remains active, with US expansion as the next test.

name: Feroot Security
one_liner: AI-powered Compliance Platform for PCI 4, CCPA, HIPAA, CIPA, 50+ laws
long_description: Feroot (YC W21) is the leading compliance and security platform for b2b websites that  helps you easily achieve and maintain compliance with PCI DSS 4.0.1, CCPA, CIPA, HIPAA and 50+ data privacy regulations.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Security, compliance and e-commerce teams at B2B and consumer companies with payment pages and privacy obligations
problem: Client-side scripts on websites are a blind spot for attacks like Magecart skimming and for compliance with PCI DSS and privacy laws.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for client-side security and compliance automation
product_category: Client-side web security and compliance
market_need_then: Magecart skimming attacks were rising in 2019 and 2020 per Source Defense's May 2020 release, and PCI DSS 4.0 was approaching, creating compliance demand.
outcome_analysis: Feroot sold client-side security and compliance for websites, a niche helped by Magecart attacks and the PCI DSS 4.0 requirements. It raised a YC-era seed of 2.5 million dollars, a True Ventures-led seed of 11 million in 2022 and a 14 million dollar Series A in November 2025. Customers shown on its site include Reddit, Instacart and Gusto. It remains independent and active, with compliance regulation as the main driver.

name: Ferveret
one_liner: Nuclear-inspired cooling that turns wasted power into more AI compute
long_description: Ferveret is developing Adaptive Phase Cooling, a next-generation thermal solution for AI data centers inspired by heat transfer principles used in nuclear reactor systems. Our rack-integrated design delivers 35% more usable compute from the same power envelope, with a PUE of 1.03 (vs. the 1.2 industry standard), zero water consumption, and 45°C inlet temperatures that eliminate the need for chillers. Compatible with NVIDIA MGX and HGX architectures, Ferveret's solution uses a proprietary dielectric fluid that is not part of any regulated PFAS category, giving AI infrastructure operators a scalable, water-free path to higher compute density without redesigning their facilities.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: AI data center operators, hyperscalers and crypto-mining infrastructure operators
problem: Dense compute needs cooling that wastes power and water; air and many liquid systems are complex, capital intensive or need facility redesign.
business_model: Hardware sales of rack-integrated cooling systems, with pilots; revenue not disclosed
product_category: Data center liquid cooling hardware (Adaptive Phase Cooling)
market_need_then: Crypto mining and HPC were already adopting immersion cooling in 2020 (GRC customers), and AI compute density later increased demand. The CEO traces the idea to 2017.
outcome_analysis: Ferveret is an MIT-linked hardware company applying reactor heat transfer ideas to AI data center cooling. It raised a seed round described as about 10 million dollars from investors including Aramco Ventures and Y Combinator and ran pilots with data center operators, and it is moving toward a Series A. The AI compute boom is a tailwind, while the outcome depends on converting pilots into purchases against funded rivals.

name: FifthTry
one_liner: Continuous Documentation To End Documentation Rot
long_description: FifthTry is a Notion-like documentation tool designed to end documentation rot. We integrate with GitHub and block code changes from getting deployed till documentation has been updated and approved. We call this Continuous Documentation.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Filadd
one_liner: We help students in Latin America graduate from College.
long_description:
We provide premium, personalized courses for college entrance exams (like Chile’s PAES and Brazil’s ENEM) combining engaging video lessons, live tutoring, AI-powered study plans, and downloadable resources.
Today we serve over 25,000 students annually across Chile, Brazil, Argentina, and Colombia, with a 90% YoY growth and industry-leading margins.
regions: Argentina; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: High school students and families in Chile, Brazil, Argentina and Colombia preparing for university entrance exams
problem: Quality exam preparation is expensive and in-person; students outside major cities lack affordable, personalized access.
business_model: Consumer course subscriptions and packages for entrance exam prep (video lessons, live tutoring, AI study plans)
product_category: Online exam preparation (edtech)
founder_names: Joaquin Olmedo; Guillermo Bruchmann Tanodi; Nicolás Ferrer; Agustín Trombotto
competitors_at_founding: Preuniversitario UC (online); PreUSS (Universidad San Sebastian); PreUnab (Universidad Andres Bello); Mineduc alliance with Cpech, Puntaje Nacional and Pedro de Valdivia
market_need_then: COVID-19 pushed Chilean prep online in 2020 and many universities launched free online courses, showing demand and substitutes. Paid demand was unproven at founding.
outcome_analysis: Filadd grew from a Cordoba, Argentina startup into an online exam prep provider claiming over 25,000 to 30,000 students across several Latin American countries with 90 percent year over year growth. Funding found is limited to small aggregator-reported amounts, suggesting capital efficient growth, and all figures are self-reported. It remains active and recently invested in an Indian edtech startup per a regional report.

name: Filta
tags: Augmented Reality; Crypto / Web3; Virtual Reality
one_liner: The Face Filter NFT Marketplace
long_description: Filta is the face filter NFT marketplace being built by veterans from Pixar/Oculus/Facebook. We partner with creators to release limited-edition filters for their fans to use on social media. It turns out: the face filters you see everywhere on Snapchat and Instagram are created by independent artists - not by the platforms. These artists ALMOST NEVER get money for their work - which is insane! Filta fixes this by giving these creators a marketplace and the best filter creation tool anywhere. Interested in working on the future of digital fashion, AR/VR, and web3? Hit us up. We're hiring.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Social media users who want limited-edition face filters and creators who sell filters as collectibles
problem: Face filter creators had no ownership or resale economics on social platforms; Filta used NFTs to give scarcity and creator income.
business_model: Marketplace taking a cut of face filter NFT sales, with in-app purchases
product_category: Face filter NFT marketplace and AR camera app
market_need_then: NFT trading boomed in 2021 and face filters were popular on Instagram and Snapchat, but creator payment for filters was weak. Demand for owned filters was unproven.
outcome_analysis: Filta tried to sell limited-edition face filters as NFTs during the 2021 NFT boom, with a Pixar, Oculus and Facebook veteran as founder. The YC page now lists him as a former founder with a team of 3, and no funding or press was found beyond a small YC-era amount in aggregators. The company is still marked active, but the thin trail suggests it stalled; the cause is not public, so these failure factors are inferences about the market rather than stated reasons.

product_category: Wealth tracking and investing app

It raised an 8 million euro Series A in February 2022, a community crowdfunding in March 2022 and a 25 million euro Series B in September 2025, and bought Affluent as its first acquisition. Strong distribution and brand are the main success drivers.

name: Fingo Africa
one_liner: A neobank for Africa's 500 million youth

Fingo is building a pan-African digital bank.

Today, most Africans pay 5-15% fees to transfer money to friends, family, or businesses - with Fingo these fees will be 90% cheaper. 

In 240 seconds, any young person will be able to access a full suite of financial services including personal, business, investment and savings accounts.
regions: Kenya; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Young, mobile-first retail banking customers in Kenya, with a stated ambition across Africa
problem: Young Africans pay 5 to 15 percent fees to move money and lack modern banking; Fingo promised accounts opened in minutes with cheap transfers.
business_model: Neobank: fees, interchange and interest spread, delivered with a licensed partner bank
product_category: Neobank
founder_names: Kiiru Muhoya; Ian Njuguna; Gitari Tirima
market_need_then: Large unbanked and underbanked young population in Kenya and high remittance and transfer fees as stated by the company; mobile money was ubiquitous.
outcome_analysis: Fingo went through YC in Summer 2021, raised a reported 4 million dollar seed led by HOF Capital late in 2022 and launched in May 2023 with Ecobank Kenya, with CBK approval. YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or terms were found, so the real outcome and cause of the exit are not public in sources seen.

name: Finley
one_liner: Streamline your debt capital raise and management
long_description: Finley simplifies debt capital raise and management. Our software helps companies like Ramp, Arc and Parafin automate due diligence, ensure compliance, and streamline ongoing reporting with their capital providers. Our team brings experience from Goldman Sachs, Nova Credit, and Palantir Technologies, and is backed by Y Combinator and Bain Capital Ventures.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Fintech lenders, banks and asset managers that raise and manage debt capital (early customers Ramp, Arc, Parafin); later credit funds and banks

business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for loan and credit facility administration
product_category: Debt capital management and loan administration software
founder_names: Jeremy Tsui; Kevin Suh; Josiah Tsui
market_need_then: Fintechs and private credit were raising large debt facilities in 2021 and handled diligence manually; the Series A press cited private credit at an all-time high.
outcome_analysis: Finley, founded by a former Goldman debt investor and ex Nova Credit and Palantir engineers, raised a 3 million dollar seed led by Bain Capital Ventures in June 2021 and a 17 million dollar Series A led by CRV in January 2023. It moved from fintech borrowers toward banks and credit funds and was acquired by Concord in March 2026, with the CEO joining Concord. Terms were not disclosed.

name: Fintoc
one_liner: Account-to-Account payments in Mexico and Chile.
long_description: Account-to-Account payments in Mexico and Chile.
regions: Chile; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Online merchants, subscription businesses and collection teams in Chile and Mexico that want to accept bank transfer payments

product_category: Account-to-account payments and open banking API
market_need_then: Chile lacked card alternatives and its Fintech Law was establishing open banking; Chilean merchants used transfers heavily. Evidence is the founders' own account and later press.
outcome_analysis: Fintoc built an account-to-account payments API for Chile and then Mexico, raised a 7 million dollar Series A in April 2024 led by Propel, and says over 1,200 companies use it. It obtained regulatory authorizations in Chile and Mexico and reportedly processed about 350 million dollars monthly in 2025. It remains active and independent, and its main risks are competition from Khipu and global players and regulatory change.

name: FirstIgnite

product_category: Business development and CRM for research institutions

outcome_analysis: FirstIgnite, founded in 2019 by a former university-research VC and a UIUC engineer, sold prospecting and CRM tools to universities and went through YC in Summer 2021. It stayed small and was acquired by Merit Holdings in February 2026, which had bought Inteum in 2025. The price and funding history are not public in sources found, and commentary notes the market size is a limit.

name: FirstQuadrant

In October 2025, FirstQuadrant Inc. completed a confidential agreement with a leading AI technology company that recognized long-term strategic value in components of the FirstQuadrant platform and data infrastructure and sunset the platform.

name: FirstSupport.ai
