We give AI superpowers to support agents so they can reply quicker, understand multiple languages, get information quickly from knowledge base, summarize ticket in one click, get weekly customer support report, and many more. Available on Zendesk.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Customer support teams and outsourcing firms that run Zendesk, plus e-commerce merchants and startups
problem: Support agents spend time drafting replies, translating tickets, searching knowledge bases and summarizing threads by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS app sold through the Zendesk Marketplace with a two week free trial
product_category: AI assistant for customer support agents (Zendesk app)
competitors_at_founding: Zendesk Answer Bot and macro suggestions
market_need_then: Support teams were adopting Zendesk at scale and Zendesk had already bought AI automation talent in 2021, which signals demand for agent productivity tools. No spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: FirstSupport remains active with a team of four based in Bandung and no public funding or exit. It has distributed through the Zendesk Marketplace, which is cheap distribution but leaves it exposed because Zendesk later built comparable AI assist features itself. Without disclosed revenue or rounds the trajectory is unclear.

name: Firstbase.io
one_liner: The all-in-one startup operating system
long_description: Incorporation, compliance, bookkeeping, and taxes – all in one place.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Global and non-US founders who want to incorporate and run a US company, plus a few dozen B2B enterprise clients
problem: Non-US founders find US incorporation, registered agent service, compliance, bookkeeping and tax filing fragmented and hard to do remotely.
business_model: Fee per incorporation plus recurring compliance, registered agent, bookkeeping and tax subscriptions; B2B partner deals
product_category: Company formation and compliance platform (startup operating system)
market_need_then: Remote and international founders were forming US companies in growing numbers; Firstbase reported about 6,000 incorporations by July 2021 across founders from 170 countries.
outcome_analysis: Firstbase grew from incorporation into a compliance and bookkeeping suite, reaching about 15,000 compliance customers by its YC launch post and over 30,000 incorporations per its about page. It raised a small $3M seed in 2021 and was acquired by Harbor Compliance in December 2025, which looks like a modest outcome rather than a breakout. Terms were not disclosed.

name: FitHub
one_liner: The one-stop shop for healthy products
long_description: FitHub is an online supermarket specialized in healthy products, currently operating in Colombia. We have a healthy and eco-friendly sourcing criteria for every product we offer. We are like Good Eggs for LATAM.
regions: Colombia; Latin America
target_customer: Health conscious urban consumers in Colombian cities buying groceries online or from small stores
problem: Healthy and eco friendly groceries were hard to find in one place with fast delivery in Colombia.
business_model: Online and physical grocery retail with private label products and margin on resale
product_category: Healthy online supermarket
founder_names: Jabib Char; Cristina Char; Andrés Iriarte; Alex Ramírez; María José Ramos
market_need_then: The pandemic pushed Colombian grocery shopping online, and Forbes reported FitHub grew 10x in the year to September 2021.
outcome_analysis: FitHub grew about 10x in the year to September 2021, reported more than 2,000 products across eight cities, and raised a US$1.4M seed led by Capital Energy. The online grocery space is capital hungry and crowded with Merqueo, Rappi and quick commerce entrants. No later round or exit was found, so the later trajectory is unknown despite an Active status.

name: Fitia
one_liner: Automated Meal Planner & Nutrition Tracking
long_description: Fitia is an AI meal planning and calorie counter app. Our users receive personalized weight loss or muscle gain plans that adapt based on their data, progress, and preferred foods.
regions: Peru; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Spanish speaking consumers who want weight loss or muscle gain meal plans and calorie tracking, via a freemium app with premium subscriptions
problem: People want to improve their diet but cannot afford a nutritionist, and generic calorie counters do not adapt plans to their foods and progress.
business_model: Consumer freemium app with a premium subscription for meal plans, shopping lists and advanced tools
product_category: AI meal planner and calorie counter app
market_need_then: Fitness and nutrition app use was high in 2021 and the Spanish speaking market had few localized planners; the founders say the idea came from friends who could not afford a nutritionist.
outcome_analysis: Fitia launched in July 2019 as a Peru pilot, joined YC in 2021 and says it now has over 20 million users, though that figure is self reported. A 2024 profile reports about 800,000 monthly active users, a team near 20 and a seed round from US investors without amounts. Growth looks product led and efficient, while funding disclosure is thin.

name: Flextock
one_liner: Tech-enabled fulfillment provider in the Middle East & Africa
long_description: Flextock is a tech-enabled fulfillment provider in the Middle East & Africa. For local merchants, we warehouse the stock and deliver orders directly to their customers through our network of last mile delivery partners.
regions: Egypt; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Egyptian and regional e-commerce merchants and SMEs needing warehousing, fulfilment and last mile delivery
problem: Small online merchants in Egypt had to manage storage, packing and many delivery partners themselves.
business_model: Fulfilment fees for storage and order handling plus delivery aggregation margin, with cross border and merchant financing add ons
product_category: E-commerce fulfilment and logistics operating system
market_need_then: Egypt's e-commerce was growing and TechCrunch cited a MENA e-commerce logistics market of 25 billion dollars; Flextock signed over 100 merchants within months of its January 2021 launch.
outcome_analysis: Flextock launched in January 2021 and raised a then record MENA pre-seed in 2021, then a 12.6 million Series A in February 2026 led by TLcom, expanding from Egypt to Saudi Arabia. The gap of nearly five years between rounds suggests slower capital access, though it stayed active and widened the product suite. E-commerce growth and regional logistics gaps supported it.

name: Float
one_liner: Supply chain finance for consumer brands
long_description: Float is Pipe for supply chain finance. We help fast-growing consumer brands unlock capital from their inventory. We pay their supplier invoices up front and enable them to pay for their inventory after they’ve sold it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Fast growing consumer brands that need working capital tied up in inventory
problem: Consumer brands pay suppliers up front for inventory and wait months to be paid by sales, which locks up cash.
business_model: Supply chain finance: pays supplier invoices up front and charges brands a fee when they repay after inventory sells
product_category: Supply chain finance for consumer brands
market_need_then: DTC and consumer brands in 2021 needed inventory cash and revenue based financiers were raising large rounds; no Float specific demand evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Float is listed as active with two people in Honolulu, but its float.xyz website now redirects to a domain for sale page and no funding, product news or exit was found. The outcome is therefore unclear; it may have stalled or changed name. Competitors such as Settle had raised venture funding by mid 2021.

name: Floatpays Inc
one_liner: On-demand wage access service built for the African market
long_description:
Floatpays is an on-demand wage access platform that helps employees access, spend, save and manage their money.

The problem we are solving is that more than 75% of the 12 million employed South African’s run out of money before the end of the month, 52% of those end up borrowing money to survive. Informal lending is the only option for most borrowers, with interest rates anywhere between 30-50%. The story is the same in most African countries where payday/micro-lending has become the norm amongst lower-income earners.

Our app features include financial education, a budget planning tool, cash access, and voucher purchases all from wages earned but unpaid. We are currently working on a savings product to promote long-term financial resilience.
	
We launched our product in South Africa in July 2020 and plan to extend our reach into additional African countries in 2022 and beyond.
all_locations: Cape Town, WC, South Africa; Remote
regions: South Africa; Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: South African employers (who integrate payroll) and their lower-income employees
problem: Most South African workers run out of money before month end and borrow informally at 30-50% interest.
business_model: B2B2C earned wage access and employee financial wellness platform integrated with payroll; fees on cash access and voucher purchases
product_category: Earned wage access / fintech
market_need_then: ITWeb (Nov 2020) and the YC page cite that over 75% of 12 million employed South Africans run out of money before month end and informal lending costs 30-50%; COVID-19 raised financial strain in 2020.
outcome_analysis: Floatpays launched in July 2020 after a six-month pilot, joined YC in Summer 2021 and raised a seed of just under $4 million in January 2022 for African expansion, plus about R15 million from Naspers Foundry in early 2022. It reported 43% employer growth and 70% user growth during YC. No shutdown or sale was found, but no later round or expansion was confirmed either, so the current trajectory is unclear.

name: Flok
one_liner: End to end company retreat planning
long_description: Flok offers end to end company retreat planning. Flok combines a planning dashboard with human retreat designers to provide your team with the best retreat possible. From booking hotel room blocks to planning and executing the ideal itinerary, Flok has you covered.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Remote and distributed tech companies that pay per attendee for a planned company retreat
problem: Planning a company retreat means sourcing venues, negotiating contracts, booking room blocks and running logistics, which is slow and painful for small remote teams.
business_model: Service-led marketplace: fee per retreat built around a planning dashboard plus human retreat designers; venue and travel commissions possible but unconfirmed
product_category: Corporate retreat planning
market_need_then: Remote and distributed teams grew sharply in 2020 and 2021, creating demand for in-person gatherings, but no sourced spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: YC lists Flok as acquired, but no acquirer, date or price could be found. A CB Insights entry claiming a Wix subsidiary appears to describe a different, older Israeli company named Flok, so it is not used. The flok.com site is still active in 2025 with a services-led retreat offering, so the exit may be small or an unannounced deal. Too little is public to assign causes.

name: Flow Club
tags: Consumer; Community; Productivity; Health & Wellness; Remote Work
one_liner: Virtual Co-working Community
long_description:
https://www.flow.club/ is a virtual co-working space where people work in high-intensity sprints designed to double their productivity. 

We envision a world where...
- anyone can access deep, focused flow anytime, anywhere
- working independently or remotely doesn’t have to feel like you're on your own

Our mission is to build the software that powers the most inspiring and productive work environment for knowledge workers.

Our members love Flow Club (https://www.flow.club/wall-of-love). We’re growing quickly, just presented at Y Combinator's Summer 2021 Demo Day, raised $5M, and hiring our founding team.

We are backed by Worklife Ventures, a firm investing in companies re-designing the way work gets done in the future, and 100 more of the world's best investors and operators. Among our investors are Paul Graham and the founders of iconic companies like Dropbox, Mercury, Quora, Outschool, and Sendbird. 

Finally, we are inspired by our members and hosts who we see everyday working out of Flow Club building the most incredible things. They remind us great things are built incrementally, one step at a time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Remote workers, students and people with ADHD who pay a monthly fee for hosted virtual coworking sessions
problem: People struggle to focus and start hard tasks alone, especially when working remotely.
business_model: Consumer subscription ($40 per month or $400 per year per its site) with volunteer peer hosts and employer stipend use
product_category: Virtual coworking and body doubling sessions
market_need_then: Pandemic remote work raised isolation and focus problems; the company reports over 3 million hours of coworking since 2021, and the format maps to ADHD body doubling demand.
outcome_analysis: Flow Club began as hosted coworking emails to friends in 2020, joined YC in summer 2021 and announced a 5M round led by Worklife Ventures in April 2022. It reports 400,000 sessions and over 3 million hours, and leaned into ADHD body doubling. It remains active with no exit; the pandemic tailwind and a volunteer host model kept costs low.

name: FlowEQ
tags: B2B; Customer Success; Compliance; API; Enterprise
one_liner: No-code workflow tool
long_description: FlowEQ is the trusted provider of workflow automation for teams that need to accelerate their work, especially complex processes and high-volume workflows that require human judgment. The FlowEQ Workflow Acceleration Platform includes interactive decision trees that are used by customer support, operations and product teams across all industries to improve accuracy and speed up important recurring work. Using FlowEQ customers get through high-stake recurring workflows 10x faster, saving their companies time and money every day. For additional information, visit www.floweq.com.
all_locations: Houston, TX, USA; Pleasanton, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Customer support, operations and product teams handling complex high volume processes that need human judgment, using Zendesk, Salesforce, Freshdesk or Zoho
problem: Agents handling complex tickets follow inconsistent procedures and take long to onboard, causing slow resolution and compliance gaps.
business_model: B2B SaaS priced per user and by usage
product_category: No-code workflow automation with guided decision trees embedded in CRM and help desk tools
market_need_then: Support teams were scaling remote and the company shows enterprise logos (Showtime, Tableau, fubo) and claims 50M plus actions a year; no 2021 spend data found.
outcome_analysis: FlowEQ started as BrightReps, a decision tree tool for support agents, joined YC in winter 2021 and renamed in April 2022 as it broadened to general workflow automation. No acquisition or shutdown was found, but G2 says the profile has been inactive for over a year and the site has placeholder content. Status and traction are unclear.

name: Flowbo
one_liner: Pipe for online businesses
long_description:
Flowbo provides financing to online revenue-generating companies including creators and eCommerce. 

We package assets into investable products so creators can raise money. For example, we package receivables into factoring products.
all_locations: Los Angeles, CA, USA; Seoul, Seoul, South Korea
regions: United States of America; South Korea; America / Canada; East Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Flowly
one_liner: Our mobile app reduces chronic pain for 100 million Americans.
long_description:
Flowly’s mobile app is the VR version of Calm with a focus on reducing chronic pain for 100 million Americans. Flowly subscribers receive a $5 VR headset and Heart Rate sensor that collects a user's biometric data like HR and HRV, and converts it to visualizations in virtual experiences that reduce pain by 46%. 
Flowly is backed by the National Institutes of Health.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Adults with chronic pain paying through a subscription, later patients and insurers through a virtual clinic program
problem: Chronic pain affects about 100 million Americans and many lost at-home options as opioid prescribing tightened. Flowly offers a VR and biofeedback app as a non-drug alternative.
business_model: Consumer subscription (VR headset plus heart rate sensor), later a therapist-led virtual clinic program with insurance coverage
product_category: Digital therapeutics, VR for chronic pain
founder_names: Celine Tien; Narae Kim; Julien Soros
market_need_then: The company cites 100 million Americans with chronic pain and the opioid crisis, with stricter prescribing leaving patients seeking non-drug options.
outcome_analysis: Flowly is still operating. It started as a low cost VR and biofeedback consumer app backed by NIH funded trials, and the current site presents a therapist-led virtual clinic covered by insurers. Funding is poorly documented, so no verdict on its trajectory is supported; no shutdown or acquisition news was found.

name: FlutterFlow
one_liner: Application Development Platform (Native Mobile + Web Apps)
long_description:
We're building a visual application development platform to dramatically improve the time to market and quality of digital experiences. FlutterFlow helps companies and product teams improve developer efficiency, accelerate project timelines, and reduce costs for large-scale business applications. Our customers include some of the largest banking, consulting, telecom, and manufacturing companies in the world.

We have more than 1.3M users in more than 200 countries and regions around the world.

We’re a remote first team headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. We have offices in Mountain View, New York City, and Singapore.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Product teams, agencies and enterprises building mobile and web apps, plus individual builders on self-serve plans
problem: Building native mobile and web apps takes long and needs scarce engineers. FlutterFlow gives a visual builder on top of Google's Flutter framework that exports real code.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers (self-serve plans, team and enterprise plans)
product_category: Low-code visual app builder
market_need_then: Demand for cross-platform mobile apps and for low-code tools was strong in 2020 and 2021, and Flutter was growing as a framework.
outcome_analysis: FlutterFlow grew with the Flutter ecosystem, reaching about 1 million users and roughly 10,000 paying self-serve customers by January 2024, when it announced a $25.5M Series A backed by Google affiliated funds. Founders with Google experience and a product that exports real code helped it win developers. A headcount drop reported by an aggregator is unverified.

name: Flux
one_liner: Cross border Payments infrastructure for internet businesses and…
long_description:
We are building Flux- Flux is a Mobile App for merchants, freelancers, regular users(P2P) to make and accept payments from their customers anywhere in the world using crypto or fiat.
We have built a mobile app that uses the merchants’ phone number, creates a wallet enabling them to receive payments in crypto or fiat without having to go to an exchange or pay expensive fees. Merchants can accept payments in crypto or in fiat.
Payments made in Crypto can easily convert into fiat due to the built in fast reconciliation and is made available for spending immediately.
Currently the vast majority merchants receive payments in crypto because of two issues (1) Paypal, Venmo, CashApp or Square to not exist in Africa and (2) the local currency fluctuates more than bitcoin due to inflation. But in order for merchants to receive money in crypto and exchange it into fiat they resort to crypto exchange apps and crypto addresses to receive payments which is a very complicated and expensive process. Merchants want to be paid quickly with the lowest amount of fees possible. This is why we are building Flux
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: African merchants, freelancers and consumers sending and receiving cross-border payments
problem: Merchants in Africa could not use PayPal, Venmo or Square, and receiving crypto required complicated exchanges. Flux offered a phone number based wallet for crypto or fiat payments.
business_model: Payments app with transaction fees, later banking and card services
product_category: Cross-border payments and crypto wallet
founder_names: Ben Eluan; Osezele Orukpe; Israel Akintunde
market_need_then: Founders cite no PayPal, Venmo or Square in Africa and a local currency that fell faster than Bitcoin.
outcome_analysis: Flux is still operating with about 15 staff as of June 2024. After the YC batch it had about 5,000 users and over $750,000 in volume, but Nigerian crypto restrictions forced a move to fiat banking. Funding beyond the 2020 pre-seed is not public, so its trajectory is stalled or slow rather than failed.

name: Flux Auto
tags: Autonomous Trucking; Hard Tech; Robotics; AI
one_liner: Physical AI for Warehouses and Factories
long_description:
Flux is building physical AI to automate material movement in warehouses and factories on legacy vehicle fleets. Using Flux's solutions customers can reduce their dependency on human drivers, while also increasing productivity and reducing operating costs. 

Flux is currently deploying with customers like Walmart, Daimler, Bajaj, Cummins, Mahindra Logistics across warehouses, fulfillment centers and factories.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Warehouse, factory and logistics operators running legacy forklifts, tuggers and pallet jacks
problem: Driver dependence and labor cost in material movement. Flux retrofits existing vehicles with autonomy instead of selling new autonomous machines.
business_model: Hardware and software retrofit sold to enterprises
product_category: Autonomous vehicle retrofit, physical AI
market_need_then: Aug 2017 coverage cites high cost of lidar based autonomy and demand for cheap truck autonomy in India; later focus is labor and productivity in warehouses.
outcome_analysis: Flux Auto is active with about 56 people and lists Walmart, Daimler, Bajaj, Cummins and Mahindra Logistics as deployment customers on its own site. It shifted from road trucks to controlled warehouse environments where retrofit autonomy is more tractable. Funding amounts are inconsistent across aggregators, so no funding based verdict is supported.

name: Forage
one_liner: Payments powering people
long_description: Forage is a mission-driven payments company that helps businesses accept government benefits through a single, unified API. Today, over 42 million Americans receive government assistance (ex: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP) to buy groceries. Starting with enabling EBT SNAP online, Forage builds the financial infrastructure empowering businesses to serve these shoppers online.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Online grocers, delivery apps and retailers that want to accept SNAP EBT payments
problem: Over 42 million Americans receive SNAP benefits but most merchants could not accept EBT online. Forage provides one API, checkout components and a fraud layer to do it.
business_model: B2B payments API with transaction based fees
product_category: Government benefits payments infrastructure
competitors_at_founding: Instacart (Carrot Payments); Fiserv and FIS Worldpay
market_need_then: Over 42 million SNAP recipients per the company, with online grocery growing and USDA's online purchasing pilot opening in 2019.
outcome_analysis: Forage is active and growing: it raised a $22M Series A in 2022-08 and a $40M Series B in 2026-06, and lists itself as one of three USDA approved online EBT providers. Its moat is regulatory approval in a niche large incumbents were slow to serve, plus rising online grocery demand.

name: Forage Mail
tags: Consumer; Productivity; Email; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: AI that solves email overwhelm. Not another mail app.
long_description: Forage filters low-priority emails from your Gmail. It sends you a clean, daily summary of the emails it filtered out, including a TLDR for every newsletter. It learns your preferences and gives you full control with custom rules. Works with any email app.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Forcyte Biotechnologies
one_liner: Discover drugs that control how much cells "squeeze" to treat disease
long_description:
In a nutshell: many diseases are caused by how much your cells squeeze (asthma, fibrosis, others). We discover drugs that control how much cells squeeze, with ease, to treat disease.

We use patented bioMEMS technology to turn cell strength (cells' ability to pull/ squeeze) into a quantifiable metric in drug discovery, to help find better drugs for mechanical diseases. 

We screen 100,000s of drugs against numerous contractile human cell types to comprehensively map human mechanobiology (the "contractome") and identify promising drug development starting points to deliver novel medicines to treat mechanically-driven diseases including asthma, hypertension, preterm labor, fibrosis, and others.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Formance
tags: Developer Tools; Fintech; Payments; B2B; Open Source
one_liner: Open Source Infrastructure for the Financial Internet
long_description:
Formance Platform is building open-source infrastructure for the next wave of financial services. It enables fintech engineers to build and operate complex flow of funds, weaving together multiple payment rails with internal ledger accounts.

github.com/formancehq/stack
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Fintech engineering teams, EMIs, money transmitters and stablecoin issuers that need to build and operate flows of funds
problem: Fintechs hand build ledgers and payment orchestration. Formance offers an open source programmable ledger plus connectivity, flows and reconciliation modules.
business_model: Open source core with paid managed hosting and enterprise modules
product_category: Financial infrastructure, ledger and payment flows
market_need_then: Fintech boom of 2021 created many companies needing custom flows of funds; the company says fintech engineers wanted to weave multiple rails with internal ledgers.
outcome_analysis: Formance is active and raised a $21M Series A in 2025-01 after a reported tenfold revenue increase over 12 months, with about 20 customers per TechCrunch. It builds on an open source ledger that spreads through developer adoption, then expanded into a broader platform and now targets stablecoin and AI payments.

name: Foster
one_liner: A better way to write.
long_description: Community-powered writing workflow driven by some of the internet's best writers, editors, and experts.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Writers and professionals who pay for membership, editing and community support
problem: Writing alone is slow and lonely. Foster connects writers with a network of editors and peers, through a Google Docs button, circles, cohorts and retreats.
business_model: Paid membership and professional editing services, free community events
product_category: Writing community and editing marketplace
market_need_then: The 2020 and 2021 creator economy drove demand for writing help and paid newsletters; no hard demand data was found in sources opened.
outcome_analysis: Foster is still active as a writing community led by Dan Hunt, with a team of Stewards and Contributors. Co-founder Stew Fortier moved on to Type.ai. No funding, acquisition or shutdown was found, so the outcome is a small community business and no verdict on scale is supported.

name: Fountain9
tags: Warehouse Management Tech; E-commerce; Supply Chain; Retail; AI
one_liner: Helping food brands and retailers reduce food wastage
long_description:
Fountain9 is a predictive inventory planning solution. We help food brands and retailers reduce food wastage and improve product availability by predicting their future inventory needs. 

Food wastage is a global problem that has both financial and environmental costs. An estimated $1.3 Bn tonnes of food is wasted every year and 7 - 15% of that is because of mismanaged inventory. 

We accurately predict future inventory imbalances which lead to out of stock situations or wastage, and also recommends best ways of minimising their impact. Our state of the art demand sensing and pricing engine takes into account several factors like historical sales trends, seasonality, holidays, markdown events and pricing changes to predict future inventory requirements and optimize prices. Predicted inventory demand is also aligned with supply side data to identify ideal suppliers and replenishment quantities that minimize chances of stock outs or inventory wastage.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Food brands, grocers and retailers with perishable inventory
problem: Retailers and food brands waste product and lose sales through poor inventory forecasting, especially for fresh goods with short shelf life.
business_model: B2B SaaS for demand sensing, pricing and replenishment planning
product_category: AI demand forecasting and inventory planning
market_need_then: The company's own pitch cited food waste and stockouts as costly; no independent 2021 spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: Fountain9 raised a $1.9M seed in July 2021 after YC W21 and sold its IP and team assets to Rappi, reported around September 2024, to support TURBO retailing and a B2B supply chain offering. The price is not public. A three year gap with no sourced follow-on round suggests the company did not raise a larger round, but that is inference, so no failure factors are assigned.

name: Fractional
one_liner: The place where motivated investors and entrepreneurs co-own together.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Groups of friends, families and community leaders pooling capital into investment clubs, mostly real estate and private lending
problem: Co-investing in property needs expensive legal and back office work. Fractional supplies LLC setup, compliance, bookkeeping, distributions and tax filings for clubs.
business_model: SaaS and service fees per investment club
product_category: Group investing and real estate co-ownership infrastructure
market_need_then: Retail interest in real estate investing and group investing was high in 2021; the founders cite their own high legal costs; real estate venture funding hit a record in 2021 per PitchBook as reported by search results.
outcome_analysis: Fractional raised a $5.5M seed at a reported $30M valuation in 2021-11 and a $15M Series A led by Fifth Wall in 2024-11, bringing total funding to about $20.55M. It is active and has moved toward serving operators who run investment clubs. No exit or shutdown was found.

name: Freterium
one_liner: Real-Time Collaborative Transport Management Platform
long_description:
Freterium is a collaborative SaaS platform that connects organizations, people and technologies in the logistics value chain to help them move things.

Our connected cloud platform provides real-time visibility of shipments, elastic logistics infrastructure (in-house & 3rd party fleets), proprietary routing algorithms, productivity tools, and seamless collaboration that breaks down traditional organizational silos.
regions: Morocco; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Manufacturers, distributors, retailers and logistics providers in Morocco and the MENA region that run their own fleets or hire carriers
problem: Companies in the region managed shipments with spreadsheets and disconnected tools, with little visibility across departments, ERP systems, in-house fleets and third-party carriers.
business_model: B2B SaaS transport management system sold by subscription
product_category: Transport management system (logistics SaaS)
founder_names: Mehdi Cherif Alami; Omar El Kouhene
market_need_then: In February 2022 TechCrunch reported that SaaS tools for managing shipment flows across departments and ERP systems were few in the region, and the company reported 20+ enterprise customers in its first full year and 35 percent monthly growth.
outcome_analysis: Freterium is an active Casablanca company that raised a 4 million dollar seed round led by Partech in early 2022 and, by its own site in 2026, claims 100+ customers including large retail and FMCG names. It filled a regional gap for transport management software, helped by founders with logistics and consulting backgrounds. No later round, exit or shutdown was found.

name: Friz

problem: Freelancers lacked finance tools built for them; later, small DTC marketing teams spent too much time and money producing and scheduling social content.

product_category: Freelancer neobank, then AI social media management

outcome_analysis: Friz raised a small seed ($1M, October 2021) as a freelancer neobank, then shifted to an AI social media tool for DTC brands and is listed as acquired by YC without naming a buyer or date. One Spanish language profile claims an acqui-hire by Deel, which no second source confirms. The acqui-hire is unproven, so no failure factors are assigned.

name: FrontPage
one_liner: Community for 100M Indian Financial Market Traders & Investors
long_description: Frontpage is building a community for 100M Indian traders and investors. Millions of new traders and investors are looking to participate in financial markets. FrontPage harnesses power of community where traders and investors can connect with each other, share their ideas, and learn from each other.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Retail Indian stock and commodity traders and investors, free to use with monetization unclear
problem: New Indian retail traders had no focused place to discuss specific stocks and trade ideas, and relied on scattered Telegram, WhatsApp and Twitter groups.
business_model: Free consumer community app and market tools; monetization not stated in sources
product_category: Social community and market data tools for retail traders
market_need_then: India added tens of millions of demat accounts in 2020 and 2021, creating many new retail traders seeking ideas, though the sources reviewed give no hard demand data for a dedicated community product.
outcome_analysis: FrontPage remains listed as active with a team of five and a seed backed by YC. Sources show no shutdown, layoffs or acquisition, and no independent coverage of traction or later rounds, so the outcome is unresolved; the company later describes itself as an AI first trading platform on YC job pages.

name: FunctionUp (FanPlay)
one_liner: A skill-tech platform that runs placement bootcamps
long_description: A technical placement bootcamp in the Income Sharing Model. We train top tech talent with 0 upfront fee and place them across our partner companies. regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Job seekers in India who pay a share of salary after placement; hiring partner companies
problem: Aspiring tech workers in India, including women and unemployed youth, could not afford upfront bootcamp fees, and employers needed trained engineers.
business_model: Income share agreement bootcamp: students pay a share of salary after placement (a 2022 report says 17 percent of monthly salary for 36 months)
product_category: Edtech placement bootcamp
market_need_then: Indian edtech demand for upskilling was high in 2020 and 2021, and the founders cited a gap in affordable placement-linked training; no sourced spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: FunctionUp ran an income share agreement bootcamp in India and is listed as acquired by YC, but no reliable source names the buyer, date or price. A 2023 Inc42 cap table showed the parent FanPlay Inc holding 83.9 percent, so the exit may be a parent or related party deal. Too little is public to assign causes.

name: Furmacy

target_customer: Veterinary practices and veterinarians (and pet owners filling prescriptions)

business_model: Software for vet practices to e-prescribe and run a practice-branded online pharmacy; also operated a retail veterinary pharmacy (trademark filings cover retail and online veterinary pharmacy services)

Group in an all-stock deal that closed 2022-10-24 for about $283 thousand in shares per Wag!'s SEC filing, roughly 20 months after the batch. The tiny price and the later closure of its pharmacy suggest a soft landing rather than a venture-scale exit, though the filing does not state the reason. A CB Insights entry that lists MWI Animal Health in July 2025 is unconfirmed and may reflect a later transfer or a data error.

name: GamerPay
one_liner: We are the marketplace for trading gaming skins & assets without scams
long_description:
GamerPay is a marketplace for trading gaming skins and assets without scams. We do this by integrating with games to instantly validate all trades.

We launched 3 months ago and transacted 245.000 dollars growing 30% MoM. 

Talking to 5.000 gamers we learned that 46% have been scammed more than once. Over half are minors, who are stuck trading for cash on social media due to their age. 

We are the first to build a fully compliant system for parental consent, enabling the majority of gamers to trade legally and giving the parents peace of mind.

There are 215 million trades annually in games we support. We make 7 dollars on average per trade. So a $1.5B initial market, growing fast alongside gaming and blockchain game economies.   

The team behind previously co-founded the largest transactional marketplace for secondhand high end clothes in Denmark, with 1 million users and a yearly transacted GMV north of $40 million.
regions: Denmark; Europe
target_customer: Gamers, many of them minors, who trade CS:GO and Ev.io skins; revenue from trade fees
problem: Peer-to-peer skin trades happen on social media and are scam-prone; minors often cannot legally cash out.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on skin trades (company claimed about $7 average per trade)
product_category: In-game item marketplace
founder_names: Mathias Hermansen; Martin Lykke Suhr; Morten Byskov; Peter Haldbaek
market_need_then: The company reported that 46 percent of 5,000 surveyed gamers had been scammed more than once; self reported and unverified.
outcome_analysis: GamerPay raised a $2M seed in October 2021 after YC S21 and was acquired by Finnish studio Social First in November 2025. A single source family (csdb.gg) and the site banner say the marketplace shut down on May 29, 2026, attributed to low traffic and unprofitable fees. The price of the deal is not public. Success and failure factors are not assigned because the shutdown cause rests on one referral funded source.

name: Genomelink
one_liner: DNA App Store
long_description:
Genomelink is a DNA App Store. If you’ve taken a DNA test from Ancestry or 23andMe, you can upload your data to Genomelink to unlock a wide range of DNA apps: a 2,000+ region ancestry breakdown, insights from 400+ ancient DNA samples, analysis of 350+ genetic traits, unique DNA matches, and more.

Explore our latest genealogy app, YourRoots (https://yourroots.com/), which transforms your family tree into an interactive global map visualization.

We believe consumer genomics today is where the internet was in the 1990s. Over 50 million people in the U.S. have already tested their DNA, and this number will grow into the billions globally in the coming decades. Genomelink aims to become the default DNA data hub and app store for this genomic future.

Our mission:
- Build the world’s #1 platform for consumer genomics apps
- Help people discover their family roots and unite the world  
- Create an infruscrucure for consumer genomics
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers who have already taken a DNA test at Ancestry, 23andMe or MyHeritage and want more analysis, plus genealogy hobbyists
problem: People with raw DNA data from one testing service could not easily get more ancestry, trait and matching insights without buying another test.
business_model: Consumer freemium with paid reports and subscriptions for DNA apps; later a genealogy product (YourRoots)
product_category: Consumer genomics and genealogy app platform
market_need_then: The YC page cites more than 50 million people in the US having tested their DNA, a large installed base of raw data files that people could reuse.
outcome_analysis: Genomelink is still active after nearly a decade, expanding from consumer DNA reports to a separate genealogy brand, YourRoots, launched in July 2025. Funding is only visible through conflicting aggregator data, so its financial trajectory is unclear. It shows steady survival in a small consumer niche without a visible breakout.

name: Genuity
one_liner: SaaS Platform to manage IT and buy business software
long_description: Genuity is a one-stop-shop for companies to manage IT and buy business software. Companies use Genuity to keep track of all the company laptops, manage employee support requests, and buy software at wholesale prices.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-sized businesses and their IT teams that buy software, telecom and hardware
problem: Smaller IT teams lack buying power and tooling, so they overpay for software and telecom and track assets and support requests across scattered tools.
business_model: SaaS membership (community plan advertised at 29.99 per month per company) plus marketplace commissions on software, telecom, hardware and managed services
product_category: IT management platform and group-purchasing marketplace
founder_names: Colum Donahue; Jason Noble; Zaeem Asif
market_need_then: The company's about page says it formed in reaction to predatory practices and unfair pricing in the IT market. No dated third-party demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Genuity is an active Illinois company that claims 10,000+ IT professionals as members and more than 50 million dollars of reported savings on its site. The confusable name and lack of independent coverage limit what can be said about its trajectory.

name: Geostar
tags: SaaS; B2B; Sales; Sales Enablement; Market Research
one_liner: Geostar drives inbound for companies through search.
long_description: Geostar is a platform that helps you generate more inbound revenue from AI search. Monitor your brand's AI visibility and get actionable insights to improve your search rankings.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote

name: Gerald Technologies, Inc
one_liner: Buy Now Pay Later + Cash Advance for Household Essentials
long_description:
Gerald is a Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) and cash advance app that provides users with financial flexibility without any fees—no service fees, no transfer fees, no interest, and no late fees. Unlike competitors that charge hidden fees or penalties, Gerald ensures users can shop now, pay later, and access cash advances without extra costs.

Gerald is on a mission to eliminate stress about paying bills, and provides:
Zero Fees—Ever – No interest, no late fees, no transfer fees, and no subscriptions.
Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) with No Hidden Costs – Users can shop now and pay later with no interest or late fees, making purchases more manageable.
Free Cash Advance Transfers – Users who shop using BNPL unlock free cash advance transfers with zero costs—no hidden fees, no percentage cuts, and no instant transfer fees.
Instant Transfers for Eligible Users – Unlike other apps that delay transfers or charge extra for speed, Gerald provides instant transfers for eligible users at no cost.

iOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/gerald-cash-advance-app/id1569801600
Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/dev?id=8069558551988887008&hl=en_US
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers living paycheck to paycheck who use small cash advances and buy now pay later for household essentials
problem: Short term cash advances and BNPL products charge fees, interest or tips that hit low income users hardest.
business_model: Consumer fintech: fee-free BNPL and cash advances monetized through a store (Cornerstore) where users buy essentials, plus rewards and in-app games
product_category: Consumer fintech (BNPL and cash advance app)
market_need_then: No dated source on demand was found; the company's materials argue that fee-heavy advance apps burden low income users.
outcome_analysis: Gerald is an active New York fintech whose app was still being updated in April 2026 per an app tracking listing. No independent funding, exit or shutdown reporting was found, so its trajectory cannot be judged beyond survival and a large volume of self-published marketing content.

name: GetDot
one_liner: Your AI Data Analyst
long_description:
Our mission is to help everybody in an organization to take data-driven decisions, by democratizing access to trusted high-quality data and metrics. 

**Chat with your Data Warehouse**

Answer most business questions instantly 24/7. Data teams can focus on deep work, not on answering easy questions about dashboards.

Dot understands your existing data stack: tables, SQL queries, documentation, DBT metrics or LookML are its learning material.

Users can interact via Slack, Teams or our native web app.

➡️  https://getdot.ai/
regions: Germany; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data and business teams at companies with a data warehouse such as Snowflake or BigQuery
problem: Business users depend on analysts and dashboards to answer data questions, and trusted answers take too long.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (a directory lists 180 per month billed annually)
product_category: AI data analyst (chat over a data warehouse)
founder_names: Theo Tortorici; Rick Radewagen; Sven Rudolph
market_need_then: The YC launch post contrasts Dot with searching through dashboards and says trustworthy data plus correct logic is needed for analytics; no dated demand numbers were found.
outcome_analysis: Dot, built by Snowboard Software GmbH, shifted from the Snowflake data catalog Sled to an LLM based data analyst and now lists customers including Duolingo, Airbyte and BlaBlaCar plus SOC 2 Type II on its site. Funding is not publicly confirmed, so the story is a small, active team that rode the language model wave.

name: Gigs
one_liner: The OS for Embedded Telecom
long_description: Gigs is the leader in embedded connectivity, powering global mobile infrastructure for some of the world’s largest enterprises. By bridging the gap between telecom carriers and modern digital platforms, Gigs enables connectivity for hundreds of millions of people worldwide. Gigs is backed by Ribbit Capital, Google’s Gradient Ventures, and Y Combinator. Learn more about what we do at www.gigs.com.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

business_model: Usage and platform fees on an API and operating system for embedded mobile services (connectivity, billing, compliance)
product_category: Telecom as a service / embedded mobile infrastructure
market_need_then: TelecomTV (2022) reported growing demand from neobanks, employee management platforms and hardware makers for embedded mobile service; no earlier dated metric was found.

Its position as carrier of record and the deep integration into partner products give it a structural moat, and no exit or trouble was found.

name: Gigs Live

long_description: We are the Substack for millions of artists, musicians, indie producers, extreme sports athletes and video production companies. Creators choose us because our platform is available in 4K on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, Gaming consoles and more. name: GimBooks

long_description: GimBooks offers a cloud based and Mobile First book keeping and business management platform, geared mainly towards small and micro-sized businesses of India, which is easy to use and uniquely offers domain based bookkeeping and Integrated banking.

product_category: GST billing and bookkeeping app for SMBs

name: Glitzi
one_liner: At-home spa, beauty & grooming services marketplace for LatAm
long_description: Glitzi provides at-home spa, beauty and grooming services for people in Latin America. We do this by connecting you to our network of high quality masseuses, manicurists and barbers.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Urban consumers in Mexico who book at-home massage, nails, barbering and beauty, plus businesses booking spa services for offices, events and hotels
problem: Quality spa and beauty services at home are hard to find and trust in Latin America. Providers are informal and customers worry about safety and quality.
business_model: Two-sided marketplace taking a commission on services booked through the app, plus packages, memberships, gift cards and corporate bookings
product_category: On-demand at-home beauty and wellness services marketplace
founder_names: Ana Ramos; Luis Enrique Vazquez; Leonel Campos
market_need_then: At-home services demand rose in Latin America around 2020 and 2021 as people avoided salons during the pandemic. No spend figures were found in opened sources.

It raised a 2.8M dollar round in June 2023 after YC and reported about 700 providers and 170,000 services booked. No later round, exit or shutdown was found. The pandemic shift to at-home services helped, while thin defensibility and city-by-city operations remain the open risks.

name: GoBuild (fka Brick)

name: Govly
one_liner: The #1 Market Network for Government Contractors.
long_description:
🏛 Govly makes it easier to sell to the government

You can use our advanced searching alongside our analytics dashboard to identify trends and new business opportunities.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: OEMs, distributors and VARs selling to US federal and SLED government
problem: Government contractors find it hard to track and win public-sector opportunities; fragmented data (starting with SAM.gov).
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription market network and data (free tier, paid plans); sells to OEMs, resellers, distributors and primes
product_category: Government procurement intelligence
founder_names: Michael Weiland; Nick Weiland; Jon Wright

outcome_analysis: Govly, YC S21, was built by founders with deep government-contracting experience (previously Telescope) and sold a market network linking OEMs, resellers and distributors. It raised a $9.5M Series A led by Insight Partners in November 2023 at a reported $41M post-money, with about $1.2M ARR and about 400 organizations (company-reported), then added a Carahsoft partnership (October 2024) and AI agents. No exit or shutdown found; total raised reported as $13.1M since 2019, so earlier rounds are missing from the record. Still Active at growth stage, with modest scale so far.

name: Gradia Health
tags: Consumer Health Services; Health Tech; Telehealth; Digital Health; Healthcare
one_liner: Integrated, high touch healthcare — at scale
long_description:
Our mission is simple: challenge archaic rules and implied medical conventions in healthcare to better serve patients and physicians.

Gradia is the backbone of the entire patient experience, helping patients get personalized, high-touch care while also making clinics more money. With our software patients can stay informed/educated about the status of their care, easily communicate with their providers, and get direct access to a specialized virtual care team.

Our software is currently at several clinics across the Southeastern US and helping thousands of patients get the care they deserve.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent and multi-provider clinics, starting with chronic GI conditions, that pay for software and a virtual care team
problem: Patients with chronic conditions get short clinic visits and little support in between, and clinics cannot afford concierge-style follow up for their whole patient population.
business_model: B2B software and virtual care team service sold to clinics, which earn more from ongoing patient care
product_category: Digital health, virtual care team platform for clinics
market_need_then: Pulse 2.0 describes 60 to 70 million Americans with chronic GI conditions needing follow up beyond brief visits. Clinics were being asked to deliver more continuous care.
outcome_analysis: Gradia is active. It raised a 4.2M dollar seed round in July 2023, two years after the YC batch, led by MaC Venture Capital, and works with several clinics in the Southeastern US. No later round, exit or shutdown was found. The record shows modest capital against better funded virtual care rivals, with the clinic-first integration approach as its stated difference. Too little is public to call it a success or a stall.

name: GreaseBoss
one_liner: GreaseBoss verifes industrial machinery is greased correctly
long_description:
Our hardware and software product verifies industrial machines are greased correctly. 

Incorrect greasing is the number one cause for machinery failure and costs $21bn per annum.

target_customer: Industrial sites in mining, marine, utilities and manufacturing that grease heavy machinery
problem: Incorrect greasing is a leading cause of machinery failure, and there was no way to verify that grease was applied to the right fitting in the right amount.
business_model: Hardware tags and grease gun sensors plus cloud software subscription (GreaseCloud)
product_category: Industrial IoT lubrication verification
founder_names: Steve Barnett; Tim Hall; Peter Condoleon
market_need_then: The company cites incorrect greasing as the number one cause of machinery failure and a 21 billion dollar annual cost. First installation was at Glencore and clients came from mining, marine and utilities.
outcome_analysis: GreaseBoss is active. Founders came from mining, aerospace and robotics experience and found a first customer in Glencore. After YC it raised about 2.5M Australian dollars in October 2021 led by Pipeline Capital, with Joe Montana's Liquid 2 Ventures taking a stake, and later showed an IoT endpoint product. No later round, exit or shutdown found. The niche is real but narrow.

name: Great Question
one_liner: User research on autopilot.
long_description:
Great Question puts customer research on autopilot - from recruiting participants, scheduling interviews, sending surveys or prototype tests - and sharing what you learn with your team.

Companies like Adidas Runtastic, O'Reilly Media & MainStreet use us to put their customers at the center of their product, design & marketing decisions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product, design and research teams at software companies that run customer interviews, surveys and prototype tests
problem: Recruiting participants, scheduling interviews and sharing findings is manual and slow, and existing panel providers were expensive.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, freemium at launch with paid plans at 49 and 199 dollars per month
product_category: UX and customer research platform
market_need_then: TechCrunch quotes the founders on a large research provider costing about 40,000 dollars a year. MainStreet booked eight interviews within 24 hours of signing up.
outcome_analysis: Great Question is active and grew to about 41 people. After a 2.5M dollar seed in July 2021, a repeat founder team that had sold Elto to GoDaddy stayed capital efficient and reported a total of 16.6M dollars raised after a 13M Series A led by Inovia in November 2025. Customers include ServiceNow, Brex and Asana. The long gap between rounds shows slow, efficient growth in a crowded category.

name: Greywing
one_liner: The Operating System for Maritime
long_description:
Greywing is a platform for ship operators to automate their business, through actionable intelligence, better data and communication.

Greywing today serves three product lines to customers:

*Flotilla* is a monitoring tool for vessels, enabling vessel managers to identify fleet-level patterns and optimizations and to identify risk and liability vectors in advance.

*CRY4* is an operational tool for individual vessels that allows crew managers, security officers and masters to gather intelligence about a vessels current or proposed route, making decisions about the safest and the cheapest ports of call that a vessel can be directed to.

*Landfall* is a crew management and analysis system to provide risk reporting and detailed editing capabilities about the crew on-board a vessel.

*Semaphore* is a port-agent communications tool meant to simplify the process of interfacing with large numbers of port agents while planning a port call.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Ship operators, crew managers and vessel managers at shipping companies
problem: Crew changes, port risk and port agent communication were handled by email and spreadsheets, and COVID-19 rules made crew changes hard to plan.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for maritime operations software, sold per fleet
product_category: Maritime operations software and data platform
market_need_then: Lloyd's Register April 2021 reports 25,000 seafarers helped home and over 1,000 vessels served. COVID-19 border rules created acute crew change pain.
outcome_analysis: Greywing is active. It started as a maritime security marketplace in May 2019 and pivoted at the start of the pandemic to crew change tools, which won customers like Hafnia and OSM. It raised a 2.5M dollar seed in October 2021 and later added AI assistants (SeaGPT, Proteus). No later round was found. The pivot found real demand and the company stays small, with unclear scale.

name: Gridware
one_liner: Protecting the grid today, preparing the grid for tomorrow
long_description:
Gridware exists to enhance and protect the mother of all networks: the electrical grid. The grid touches everyone and makes our modern economy possible. But it’s also fragile. When the grid is compromised, everything grinds to a halt, and the consequences can be dire: wildfires burn, land is destroyed, property is damaged, progress stops, and lives are lost.  

Our team builds smart sensors that help utility companies to immediately detect, find, and fix outages and take steps to prevent new outages, and other related disasters, from happening at all. The need for power will only increase. We protect the grid of today while we build the grid of tomorrow.  

Gridware is privately held and backed by the best climate-tech and Silicon Valley investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Electric utilities that need to detect faults, outages and wildfire ignition risks on distribution lines
problem: Utilities learn about faults and hazards late and spend hours searching lines, while failing equipment can ignite wildfires.
business_model: Hardware sensors (Gridscope) mounted on poles sold with a software subscription to utilities
product_category: Grid monitoring sensors and software
founder_names: Tim Barat; Hall Chen; Abdulrahman Bin Omar
market_need_then: Utility-caused wildfires in California and Australia drove demand. In 2021 the California Energy Commission funded five wildfire grid protection startups with 150,000 dollar grants.
outcome_analysis: Gridware is a clear winner of the batch. After a 5.3M seed in 2021 it ran a PG&E pilot starting 2023, extended the seed by 10.5M in June 2023, raised a 26.4M Series A led by Sequoia in 2025 and a 55M growth round in November 2025. The company reports 18 major utility customers and sevenfold revenue growth. Founder lineman credibility and wildfire urgency drove the utility sales motion.

name: GroMo
one_liner: App for independent agents to sell financial products in India
long_description: GroMo (YC W21) is building India's largest financial products distribution company. GroMo has built a network of 1.2 million agents on its platform. GroMo has built a tech-enabled social commerce platform that helps agents not only improve access to better financial products for consumers, but also bridge the financial literacy gap by helping them choose the right offerings. Currently, GroMo is distributing a broad spectrum of 100+ financial products across Insurance, Investments, Credit Cards, Loans, Saving & Demat accounts, etc. from brands such as IDFC Bank, Jupiter Money, Axis Bank, Freecharge, etc.

target_customer: Independent agents in India (students, professionals, homemakers) who earn commissions, and the banks, insurers and fintechs that pay for distribution
problem: Banks and fintechs struggle to reach customers in smaller towns, and individuals lack a simple way to earn by selling financial products.
business_model: Commission on financial products sold through a network of agents, shared with the agents
product_category: Fintech distribution marketplace for independent agents
market_need_then: India's insurance and credit penetration was low and PoSP rules since 2015 and 2018 allowed agent distribution at scale. Banks and fintechs paid commissions for new customers.
outcome_analysis: GroMo is active and one of the larger companies of the batch, with 100 staff and a network of 1.2 million agents. After a small 2019 seed it raised an 11M dollar Series A led by SIG in September 2022 and obtained an insurance broking licence. The company site claims 100 crore rupees paid to partners. A large agent distribution network drove traction. No later round was found.

name: H3X Technologies
one_liner: The lightest electric aircraft motors in the world.
long_description:
At H3X, we are making the lightest, high-power electric propulsion systems in the world to enable a large-scale revolution in aircraft electrification.

Our first product is a 250-kW (335 HP) integrated motor drive in an 18 kg package. It combines the electric motor, inverter, and gearbox into a single powerful unit and is the culmination of patent pending innovation in multiple areas.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Aerospace, defense, marine and heavy industry customers who need lightweight, high-power electric motors, including NASA and the US Air Force
problem: Electric aircraft and other heavy vehicles need motors with far higher power density than available motors, and separate inverters add weight.
business_model: Hardware sales of integrated motor drives plus government and strategic development contracts
product_category: Electric propulsion, integrated motor drives
founder_names: Jason Sylvestre; Max Liben; Eric Maciolek
market_need_then: ARPA-E's benchmark per New Atlas is above 12 kW/kg continuous for a Boeing 737 class propulsion system, while the best flying motors were around 4 kW/kg. Aircraft electrification was a funded priority.
outcome_analysis: H3X is active with 58 staff and products from 30 kW to megawatt class. It shipped drives for customer testing in 2023, won contracts with NASA and the US Air Force, took Lockheed Martin Ventures money in February 2023 and raised a 20M dollar Series A led by Infinite Capital in August 2024. Extreme power density and defense demand carried it, with hardware capital intensity the main risk.

name: HEO Robotics
one_liner: We visually monitor space objects for governments and defense
long_description: HEO Robotics visually monitors satellites for governments and defence. We do this by transforming existing Earth observation satellites with software to image other satellites as they fly close by.

target_customer: Governments, defence and intelligence agencies, and satellite operators that need images of other spacecraft
problem: Operators and defence agencies lack independent, timely imagery of satellites in orbit, and dedicated inspector spacecraft are expensive. HEO adds software to existing Earth observation satellites so they can image other objects as they pass close.
business_model: Imagery and analytics sold to government and operator customers, delivered through partner satellites hosting HEO software
product_category: Space domain awareness, non-Earth imaging
market_need_then: Growing government interest in space domain awareness and rising numbers of satellites around 2021, though no dated source on demand figures was opened.

Founders with aerospace and robotics PhDs fit a defence-driven space awareness market, and the software-on-existing-satellites approach kept hardware cost low. The company site also references a later US$25 million raise that was not verified with a dated source.

name: Hapi

Hapi democratizes investing for consumers in Latin America.

name: Harmonic Discovery
tags: AI-powered Drug Discovery; Biotech; Healthcare; Drug discovery
one_liner: Multi-targeted therapeutics to treat complex diseases
long_description:
We are a drug discovery company developing a new generation of therapeutics that embrace the complexity of disease. Currently available approaches for creating drugs work on the principle of finding one drug-one protein 'magic bullets'. However, diseases such as cancer and autoimmunity are often the result of several dysregulated proteins across many distinct biological pathways. 

We are building a computational-experimental platform to design therapeutics that can target several disease-causing proteins at once. By designing multi-specific drugs, we are able to create therapeutics that are more efficacious and safer than existing medicines.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Pharma partners and the company itself as a drug developer, starting with kinase inhibitors for cancer and autoimmune disease
problem: Complex diseases involve many dysregulated proteins, but most drugs hit one target. Harmonic designs drugs that hit several chosen targets while avoiding anti-targets that cause side effects.
business_model: Drug discovery platform company: pipeline assets and research partnerships (milestones and royalties not disclosed)
product_category: AI-enabled drug discovery, kinase polypharmacology
market_need_then: Complex diseases such as cancer and autoimmunity involve many pathways and single target drugs often face resistance; a 2021 crowdsourced Multi-Targeting Drug DREAM Challenge in kinase inhibitors shows research interest.
outcome_analysis: Harmonic Discovery stayed active after YC Summer 2021, launching in September 2022 with an 8 million dollar seed led by Innovation Endeavors and signing a 2024 co-development deal with Turbine on the NEK1 kinase. Drug discovery timelines are long, so success depends on clinical results not yet reported in sources found.

name: Haystack
one_liner: Delivery Analytics for Software Teams
long_description:
We are bringing the competitive advantage data-driven engineering teams like Google have - to everyone else.

Our analytics platform plugs directly into developer tools like Github to provide insights on delivery speeds, bottlenecks, and risks that impact team velocity & developer happiness. 

We're trusted by some of the world’s most innovative teams: Microsoft, The Economist, and Indiegogo and backed by Y Combinator, Soma Capital, Funders Club, and strategic angels (Founder @Optimizely, SVP Sales @Amplitude) . 

Haystack is a culture of tinkering, learning, testing and iterating. We ship quickly and help our customers do the same. We're led by founded by two technical founders who have experienced this problem first-hand after scaling their startups from 0 to 100m+ users.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering and product leaders at software teams

product_category: Software engineering analytics, delivery operations

name: Heimdal

name: Hera
one_liner: Calendar app to prepare, join and follow-up on virtual meetings

Google Calendar is built on hypotheses that are now deprecated. Now that most of our meetings are virtual, there is a massive opportunity to remove frictions at each step of the lifecycle of these meetings, and finally make calendars actionable.

From Hera, users can:
- Schedule a meeting or share availabilities
- Prepare a meeting with the right context on attendees and past discussions
- Join a meeting in one-click
- Snooze a meeting to make sure you don't forget to follow-up

All of that without leaving the keyboard.

name: HeyCharge
one_liner: Low-cost, high-scale EV charging platform for apartments (and more).
long_description: EV charging infrastructure today is expensive, difficult to install, and doesn't integrate well with existing products, services, and businesses. HeyCharge solves all of these problems with ultra-low-cost, plug-and-play EV chargers that don't require internet connections and integrate with third-party products via our SDK and APIs. Our customers are energy utilities, property operators, mobility service providers, and more.

name: Hilos
one_liner: Close and activate your customers on WhatsApp
long_description:
Platform for WhatsApp API that allows you Profile leads, automate follow-ups and integrate with your favorite tools to increase conversion.

Hilos allows startups and SMBs to run their entire business on WhatsApp, without code. We focus specifically on letting businesses build apps within WhatsApp that integrate with other systems (CRMs, Databases, Payment providers, etc.).

name: Hirebolt
one_liner: AI engineering capacity. Made simple. ⚡️
long_description:
Access a global network of verified engineers, AI-augmented teams, and expert AI evaluators with instant search that helps you start finding and interviewing talent in seconds.

To date, we’ve raised ~$1.5M from investors including Y Combinator, Entrepreneur First, world-class Venture Capital funds and industry leaders.

Index.dev announced its acquisition in March 2026 on undisclosed terms. A small team and modest funding, with no later round found, suggest a soft outcome, but the terms and the reason were not public.

name: HitPay
one_liner: Full-stack payments infrastructure for growing APAC businesses
long_description: HitPay is a full-stack payments infrastructure platform for growing businesses in APAC. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Singapore, HitPay unifies e-commerce, point-of-sale, and B2B payments — cards, PayNow, QR, digital wallets, and local rails — into a single platform, so merchants can accept, send, and reconcile money across the region from one account. More than 15,000 businesses use HitPay, which has saved SMEs over US$35M in fees (Trustpilot 4.4/5). It is regulated across six markets and backed by leading global investors, including Tiger Global, Y Combinator, Global Founders Capital, and HOF Capital.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and growing merchants in Singapore and Southeast Asia that sell online and in person

product_category: SME payments gateway and payments infrastructure
market_need_then: SME merchants in Southeast Asia were digitising sales and wanted local payment methods such as PayNow and wallets in one place; the company says more than 10,000 merchants used it by mid 2022 (fintechnews.sg).
outcome_analysis: HitPay is active and growing: it joined YC in Summer 2021, raised a 15.75 million dollar Series A led by Tiger Global in May 2022, and won an in-principle MAS licence in February 2024 followed by a full major payment institution licence reported in June 2024. Its edge is local payment method coverage for SMEs and regulatory licences in several markets; no shutdown or acquisition was found.

name: Hive Health

name: HomeBreeze

We send those scopes to our network of contractors and get homeowners quotes within minutes, rather than weeks. We started with energy-efficient upgrades (e.g. heat pumps), as our first stop toward modernizing home management.

As a pioneer in bringing AI to home services, we served thousands of customers across California and delivered an experience that both homeowners and contractors love (our reviews average 4.97 stars!).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Homebase

long_description:
Homebase provides Rent-To-Own real estate financing for buyers in Southeast Asia - the only alternative to inflexible/high-interest rate (12%+) mortgages in the region. We strive to provide more innovative, compelling, and empathetic solutions for those who aspire to own a home.

Homebase was founded in 2019 in Singapore and is backed by Y Combinator, VinaCapital Ventures, Class 5 Global, Pegasus Technology Ventures, 1982 Ventures, Iterative VC and Antler, as well as the founders and executives at disruptive real estate financing companies including Opendoor, Zerodown, 99.co and Divvy Homes.

business_model: Rent-to-own and co-investment real estate financing: Homebase buys the home, the client pays a deposit and monthly payments and later buys out its share; investor product earns monthly returns
product_category: Proptech and home financing

market_need_then: The founders interviewed over 70 customers and cited a broken home financing system with mortgage rates of 12 percent or more and heavy documentation, in a market with a young, urbanizing population.

The directory status is Active, so it is stalled rather than shut down, and the cause of the shift is inferred from a headline.

name: Houm

name: Howdy.com
one_liner: We help US tech companies hire and manage software engineers in LATAM
long_description:
Why Howdy.com?

Howdy was founded in 2018 to help Austin startups hire talented engineers who work within US time zones in Latin America.

Since then we’ve grown to a team of over 600, and our platform has enabled hundreds of companies to hire individual teammates, set up remote, hybrid or in-office teams, and manage remote equipment assets and benefits.

Join over 200 companies, like Coinbase,Truepill, Vanta, and other YC companies that have hired with Howdy to build their tech outpost in Latin America.

Better talent: Howdy is deeply involved in the Latin American tech scene, regularly hosting meetups and inviting speakers and industry leaders into our local communities called Howdy Houses throughout Latin America. We get to personally know the top tech leaders who are interested in joining product teams in the US for the long-term. These individuals are not actively seeking jobs through freelancer platforms.

98% retention: Developer churn slows teams down. That’s why, when you hire with Howdy, developers are automatically provided with premium health insurance, top-of-the-line Apple equipment, gym memberships, lunches and the use of class-A office spaces.
Your engineering culture: When you partner with Howdy, you're not just hiring individuals; you're gaining access to a skilled local workforce that becomes an extension of your team. We provide full support in all areas, from recruitment to equipment and office spaces, allowing you to build and directly oversee your engineering outpost in Latin America as your team grows.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: US tech companies, especially startups, that want to hire and manage software engineers in Latin America in US time zones
problem: US startups in Austin could not compete for engineering talent and needed vetted developers, payroll, benefits and equipment handled in Latin America.
business_model: management fee on top of developer salary, benefits and taxes (15 percent fee stated at the YC launch)
product_category: nearshore engineering staffing and employer of record services
market_need_then: US startups faced an engineering talent shortage and remote work grew in 2020 and 2021; founders said they struggled at OwnLocal to compete for talent and used Latin American outsourcing partners.
outcome_analysis: Howdy, founded in 2018 as Austin Software, joined YC in Winter 2021 as Astro and came out of stealth in August 2022 with a 13 million dollar Series A led by Greycroft, followed by a 5 million dollar extension in January 2023 at a reported 105 million valuation. It bought GeekHunter in August 2023 and reports hundreds of staff and more than 200 client companies. Remote work demand and the founders' own hiring pain drove growth; margins and later funding are not public.

name: Hudu

name: Humaans
tags: SaaS; Human Resources; B2B; Enterprise; AI
one_liner: AI-Powered HRIS for high performing teams
long_description:
Humaans is a next generation HRIS supporting globally distributed organisations. Powered by a flexible data model, deep integrations, fast APIs, and enriched by AI, Humaans removes manual work, reduce compliance risk and enhance your employee experience. Humaans reduces ongoing administrative work by 65% and onboarding time by an average of 55%.

We've raised $20 million in VC funding to date. Investors include major Tech players such as Lachy Groom; Slack founder Stewart Butterfield; Shopify founder Tobias Lütke; Figma Founder Dylan Field; Linkedin ex-CEO Jeff Weiner; Stripe COO Claire Johnson; Y Combinator; Moonfire; Frontline Ventures; Exor and more.

product_category: HRIS and people operations software, now with an AI agent layer
