name: Humance
one_liner: AI that keeps complex construction projects on schedule.
long_description:
Humance builds and integrates custom AI agents for construction teams, helping them review project documents, identify potential conflicts, and prepare next steps within the tools and workflows they already use.

Construction projects generate a constant flow of drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, change orders, and emails. Reviewing that information and connecting it across a project takes time, while overlooked details can lead to delays, rework, and unexpected costs. Humance handles the first pass through this paperwork, surfacing relevant findings and linking them to supporting project information so teams can verify the evidence and act with confidence.

Every implementation starts with understanding how a team works—its review processes, approval requirements, and existing systems. Humance then tailors and deploys AI agents around those needs, refining them through real-world use and feedback.

Construction expertise remains central. AI prepares the review; people apply their judgment and make the decisions. By reducing routine document work, Humance gives teams more time to resolve issues and keep projects moving.
regions: South Korea; East Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Construction teams and general contractors managing drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs and change orders
problem: Construction projects generate a constant flow of documents and reviewing and connecting them by hand is slow, so overlooked details cause delays, rework and cost.
business_model: custom AI agents built and integrated per customer, likely services plus software fees (pricing not found)
product_category: AI agents for construction document review and scheduling
founder_names: Soy Hwang; Sunny Kim; Yon Soo Park
market_need_then: The YC description says construction is highly coordinated and delays are expensive; no 2021 demand data such as customers or spend was found.
outcome_analysis: Humance is a very small Seoul company with three people that went through YC in Winter 2021 and is still active. Its pitch moved from AI scheduling to custom agents that review construction documents, but no funding, customers or revenue are public, so its outcome is unknown rather than a failure. The size and the lack of press suggest limited traction.

name: Humane Genomics
one_liner: A platform to make artificial viruses as cancer therapeutics.
long_description: Humane Genomics has developed a platform to engineer cancer killing viruses. We have taken a first principles approach to design and make oncolytic viral therapies. Using a highly lytic RNA virus engineered with "2 factor authentication" (using selective infection and selective replication) they have an on-target to off-target kill ratio > 1000. We are working on our first indication, pediatric liver cancer (hepatoblastoma), with our partners at Texas Children's Hospital, who are world leading experts. We have in vivo (mouse) data showing safety and currently developing efficacy data and are showing 50% reduction in tumor volume.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharmaceutical and clinical partners developing cancer therapeutics; first program aimed at pediatric liver cancer with Texas Children's Hospital
problem: Natural oncolytic viruses are expensive and error prone to manipulate. The company engineers synthetic RNA viruses with selective infection and replication to kill cancer cells while sparing healthy ones.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing oncolytic viral therapeutics, with value expected from licensing or clinical-stage milestones
product_category: Synthetic biology, oncolytic virus cancer therapeutics

In November 2025 it announced a cGMP manufacturing partnership with Genezen and moved labs to Alexandria LaunchLabs. No clinical trial was found, so the outcome is still open and the long gap between rounds suggests slow, capital-constrained progress.

name: HyperTrader
one_liner: The Trading Terminal For Crypto Traders
long_description:
Unlock your trading superpowers wtih HyperTrader. As traders, we reimagined the ultimate trading experience for you. HyperTrader is fast, efficient, accurate, and secure.

✔️ Streamline your workflow with fewer clicks.

✔️ Speed up your trading with fast execution.

✔️ Stay informed with real-time position updates.

✔️ Trade safe with secure encryption.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Experienced retail and active crypto traders who want a fast desktop trading terminal
problem: Professional-grade trading tools from traditional finance were not available to crypto traders, who juggled fragmented apps for tracking, analysis and order management.
business_model: Desktop trading terminal sold by subscription, made free of charge in June 2022
product_category: Crypto trading terminal software
market_need_then: Crypto trading volume and retail participation were high in 2021, and the founders argue crypto traders lacked tools that exist in traditional finance, per the September 2021 TechBullion interview.
outcome_analysis: HyperTrader is listed as active. After a Launch HN post in August 2021 it moved to free access in June 2022, which suggests monetization difficulty in a crowded field of exchanges and charting tools. No exit or shutdown was found, and no priced round could be sourced, so traction and runway are unknown. Founder experience in trading systems is a strength, but the outcome cannot be judged from public data.

name: Hyperbrowser
one_liner: Web infra for AI agents
long_description:
Hyperbrowser.ai is the internet infrastructure for AI agents. We provide instant, scalable browser infra with built-in CAPTCHA solving, proxy management, and anti-bot detection. 

Developers use us to power their AI agents for data collection, testing, and web automation at scale. We're backed by YC, Accel, SV Angel, and others.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and teams building AI agents, scrapers and test suites that need many remote browser sessions
problem: AI agents and automation need scalable cloud browsers with CAPTCHA solving, proxies and anti-bot evasion, which teams otherwise run themselves.
business_model: Usage-based cloud browser infrastructure with credits, plus an open-source agent framework (HyperAgent)
product_category: Browser infrastructure for AI agents
market_need_then: Demand for agent browsing grew with AI agents; the YC launch post lists web research, testing, training data collection and KYC automation as use cases, and rival Browserbase raised a Series A in late 2024.
outcome_analysis: Hyperbrowser is active and sells browser infrastructure for AI agents, competing with better-publicized Browserbase and Steel. Its public story is product launches (Hyperbrowser, MCP server, Hyperpilot, HyperAgent) rather than funding news. No verified round, acquisition or shutdown was found, so its outcome is open and traction cannot be rated.

name: Hypercontext
one_liner: Meeting agendas, notes, & goals that tie back to your OKRs
long_description:
Hypercontext helps managers run more effective meetings that tie back to their OKRs and is trusted by over 100k managers in companies like Netflix, Linkedin, and Facebook. 

Managers use our app to run their 1:1s, team meetings, and OKRs in one workflow that increases the odds of their team hitting their goals by 95%.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Hypercore
one_liner: Loan management software for private lenders
long_description:
Hypercore is a loan management software for small lenders. We help lenders automate workflows and provide them with real-time analytics and KPIs on their portfolios.
Since June we are running paid pilots ($3.5K MRR), 1 LOI ($1.5K MRR). The founding team met while serving together as officers in technological units in the Israeli Defence Forces. We then established together a software development company specialized in fintech projects such as e-wallets and open-banking projects. That’s where we discovered how archaic are the tools lenders use that are ready for disruption.
Hypercore is building the tools for private lenders who currently do everything in Excel, culminating in a 'Nasdaq of private loan books' - utilizing the platform to securitize loan books.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small non-bank lenders at founding; now private credit, venture debt and commercial real estate lenders
problem: Private lenders run loan books in spreadsheets because standard loan management systems do not fit non-standard private credit.
business_model: B2B SaaS loan management plus loan administration services
product_category: Loan management and servicing software
founder_names: Daniel Liechtenstein; Eitan Frailich; Tomer Moshe; David Yahalomi
market_need_then: At the YC profile (Aug 2021) the company had paid pilots at $3.5K MRR and one LOI at $1.5K MRR, evidence of early demand from small lenders using spreadsheets.
outcome_analysis: Hypercore stayed small for years after YC in 2021, with a seed led by Atinc in 2023 and a $13.5M Series A led by Insight Partners announced in February 2026. The company repositioned from small lenders to private credit and added loan administration services and an AI admin agent, reporting over $20B in assets and 10,000 loans managed. Persistence and a narrower, higher-value segment appear to be the drivers.

name: Hyperseed
one_liner: Zapier for billing
long_description:
Hyperseed is the Zapier for billing. 
 
We help companies handle their custom billing workflows without code and instead, with spreadsheet formulas. Hyperseed replaces manual work borne of billing system limitations and lets companies avoid spending engineering resources on homegrown systems.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Austin, TX, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Infer
one_liner: Operating system for insurance agencies
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Insurance agencies, MGAs and lead-generation operations with high call volume
problem: Insurance agencies lose leads to missed and after-hours calls and spend staff time on quoting, first notice of loss and renewals.
business_model: B2B SaaS AI voice agents for insurance front and back office
product_category: Conversational AI voice agents for insurance
founder_names: Suneel Matham; Vaibhav Saxena; Urvin Soneta
market_need_then: At founding Synth targeted knowledge workers wanting a second brain from meetings and videos; later insurance voice AI addressed agencies' call handling costs.
outcome_analysis: Synth raised a $125K YC seed in August 2021, then pivoted around late 2023 to insurance voice AI as Infer. Company materials now claim Fortune 100 and top broker customers and revenue, and a job posting claims about $6M raised, but those figures are unverified. The pivot appears to have found a paying vertical after the knowledge-base idea, but evidence is thin and mostly company or aggregator material.

name: Infina
one_liner: Leading wealth management and investing platform in Vietnam
long_description:
Infina is Vietnam's leading wealth management and investing platform (like Groww of Inida and Ajaib of Indonesia).  Its mission is to empower retail investors by make investing accessible, frictionless, and safe.  The platform is multi-asset, offering stock trading, mutual funds, and fixed-income products, with more asset classes to be added.

Infina was founded by James L. Vuong, a Silicon Valley engineer turned VC investor (IDG Ventures) and serial entrepreneur with a prior successful exit in Vietnam (Reddit of Vietnam, which was acquired by LINE corporation in 2017).

Investing apps are seeing explosive growth in many markets around the world, including in Vietnam. There is a growing middle class who are hungry to invest in assets like stocks and crypto. We are building Infina to capture this huge opportunity to democratize investing in South East Asia.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
regions: United States of America; Vietnam; America / Canada; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Young, tech-savvy Vietnamese retail investors, mostly aged 25 to 40
problem: Vietnamese consumers had little easy access to savings, funds and fixed-income products with low minimums; Infina fractionalizes them from about $25.
business_model: Retail investing platform earning distribution fees from asset managers and partners, with third-party super app integrations
product_category: Wealth management and investing app
market_need_then: Southeast Asian retail investing apps raised large rounds in 2021 and Infina reported 64% compound monthly growth in funded accounts in 2021 (TechCrunch, Feb 2022), indicating demand for low-minimum products.
outcome_analysis: Infina grew from a $2M seed in June 2021 to a $6M seed total in February 2022 backed by Surge, YC, Saison and others, then drew a strategic minority investment from JB Financial Group in March 2024. It claims over 4 million users across platforms through integrations with partners like Tiki and ZaloPay. No Series A was found, so growth appears capital-light and distribution-led.

name: Infiuss Health
one_liner: 2 sided Marketplace for accelerating medical research
long_description: We are building the world's first community of patients eager to contribute to and advance  medical research. Our patient community platform offers health management, patient support and patient health data aggregation. We offer researcher's and life science companies with the opportunity to connect with these patients for their medical research needs. They recruit real patients for clinical trials, for bio specimens sourcing and to obtaining real world patient data.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; LA, Nigeria
regions: United States of America; Nigeria; America / Canada; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Life science companies and researchers recruiting patients and data for clinical trials, with a focus on African populations; now pharma trial teams using digital twins
problem: Clinical trials under-represent African patients and struggle with enrollment; the founder aimed to connect patients to research and later to simulate trials with digital twins.
business_model: Two-sided marketplace and SaaS platform for trial recruitment, later software for protocol rehearsal with medical digital twins
product_category: Clinical trial recruitment and digital twin software
market_need_then: The founder describes a rare-disease trial enrolling a remote patient in Africa as the inspiration; no spend or regulatory data was found for 2021.
outcome_analysis: Infiuss raised a small YC investment in 2021 and an undisclosed investment from UM6P Ventures reported in October 2022. It later moved from patient recruitment toward digital twin trial simulation and shows customer logos from WHO and MHRA on its site without describing the relationships. Funding figures conflict widely, so traction and runway are unknown and the outcome is still open.

name: Inflow
tags: Mental Health Tech; Consumer Health Services
one_liner: A self-help app for people to manage their ADHD.
long_description: Inflow is a self-help app for people to manage their ADHD. They provide support through psychoeducation, habit development, and community.
all_locations: London, England, United Kingdom; New York, NY, USA
regions: United Kingdom; United States of America; Europe; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Adults with ADHD paying for a consumer subscription app
problem: Adults with ADHD have little accessible, evidence based support for building skills and habits between or instead of clinical care.
business_model: Consumer subscription app with CBT based psychoeducation and community
product_category: Digital therapeutics and self help for ADHD
founder_names: Levi Epstein; Seb Isaacs; George Sachs
market_need_then: ADHD diagnoses were rising and adults reported difficulty accessing care; the company claimed the #1 position for ADHD apps, but no independent demand figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Inflow raised a small pre-seed, a 2.3M seed in January 2022 and an 11M Series A in January 2023, then bought a telehealth clinic in late 2022 to widen its offer. It was acquired by Cerebral in March 2026 for undisclosed terms, so it reached an exit with a clear funding trail but no reported price. Success factors reflect a funded ladder and clinician involvement; sources do not show retention or revenue.

name: Infracost
tags: Developer Tools; DevSecOps; FinOps; B2B; Open Source
one_liner: Shift FinOps Left: Proactively Find & Fix Cloud Cost Issues
long_description:
Infracost shifts cloud costs left and makes FinOps proactive. It sits in the engineering workflow (CI/CD), and shows the cost impact of code changes (IaC) before the code is shipped to production. This catches costly mistakes before any money has been spent. It also checks to make sure all resources are tagged with your set tagging policy, and runs checks on the code against our FinOps policy packs, ensuring best practices are followed (e.g. using Graviton processors and storage lifecycle rules).

This creates a cost-aware engineering culture.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering, platform and FinOps teams using infrastructure as code on AWS, Azure and GCP
problem: Engineers do not see the cloud cost of infrastructure changes until after deployment, so cost problems are found late.
business_model: Open-source core with paid SaaS (Infracost Cloud) for guardrails, policies and dashboards
product_category: Cloud cost estimation and FinOps for infrastructure as code
founder_names: Ali Khajeh-Hosseini; Alistair Scott; Hassan Khajeh-Hosseini
market_need_then: Cloud spend and infrastructure as code were growing; the open-source project reached over 4,000 GitHub stars by September 2021, showing developer pull.
outcome_analysis: Infracost grew from an open-source tool left over from a failed hiring startup into a YC W21 company with a $2.2M seed in September 2021 and a $15M Series A led by Pruven Capital in November 2025. Founders had deep cloud-cost experience including a prior acquisition. Developer adoption through GitHub and CI drove growth, and it reports over 3,500 companies as users, though the long gap between rounds points to capital-efficient growth.

name: InpharmD
one_liner: We provide a curated, evidence- based answer to any clinical question.
long_description:
Every hospital hires clinical pharmacists to answer clinical questions from doctors. 

They outsource this to us because we’re more efficient.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hospital and health system pharmacy departments that need answers to clinical questions from physicians
problem: Hospital clinical pharmacists spend large amounts of time researching drug information questions; InpharmD outsources this with AI plus pharmacist review.
business_model: B2B subscription service per health system for outsourced drug information answers
product_category: AI clinical drug information service
market_need_then: Hospitals employ clinical pharmacists to answer physician questions and the company states it saves pharmacist hours; the YC pitch says hospitals outsource this because it is more efficient.
outcome_analysis: InpharmD is active and reported as profitable at its December 2023 seed, which was its first announced institutional round, led by 645 Ventures. A pharmacist founder paired with an engineer fits the niche, and growth came from selling to health systems rather than burning cash. The company site claims more than 30 health systems, but this is self reported. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown news was found.

name: InstaKin
one_liner: Financial Platform for Migrant Families in America
all_locations: Houston, TX, USA; Boston, MA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Migrants in the US, initially Pakistani, who support families back home
problem: Migrants struggle to manage tasks and spending for family back home, and traditional money transfer costs 4% to 8% per the press.
business_model: Marketplace connecting migrants to vetted vendors back home, take rate on orders (not confirmed by a source)
product_category: Diaspora commerce and payments platform
competitors_at_founding: Revolut US to Mexico remittance corridor; Paysend
market_need_then: TechTimes in August 2021 said traditional transfers cost 4% to 8%, and the founder described his own difficulty managing tasks back home.
outcome_analysis: InstaKin remains active, and the current site claims 25K users and 100K deliveries across 50 plus countries, which is self reported. No priced round beyond YC and Antler backing was verified, so its funding trajectory is unknown rather than zero. The product seems to have moved from a payments pitch toward delivery of goods, but no source explains why.

name: Instacrops
one_liner: Helping farmers maximize crop yield
long_description:
Instacrops is a simple dashboard that helps farmers maximize their crop yield. 

We give farmers IoT sensors to put in their field. We combine that data with satellite and drone data to provide analytics on the health of their farms. Farmers use this to increase their crops yield by 12% on average. 

We’re live on 300+ farms across Latam and have reached more than $200.000 in monthly revenue, growing 2X YoY. 

There’s 2.9 billion acres of farmland in Latin America which makes this a $50 billion market.

We’re instacrops. We’re bringing data driven decisions to farmers worldwide
regions: Chile; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Commercial farmers in Latin America
problem: Farmers lack field level data to decide on irrigation, frost and pests; Instacrops provides IoT sensors plus satellite and drone analytics.
business_model: Subscription for sensors and analytics dashboard
product_category: Agtech IoT and crop analytics
market_need_then: LAVCA (Apr 2021) says Instacrops sells sensor based monitoring for weather, pests and irrigation; the company reported 12% average yield gains and 300+ farms at its YC application.
outcome_analysis: Instacrops is active and expanded across Chile, Colombia and Mexico, raising about 2.8M in 2021 and an extension with SQM in late 2022. It moved from frost sensors toward software and now AI agents. The company reports over 200K monthly revenue at its YC application, which is self reported. Funding stayed modest and no later large round was found.

name: Intellect
tags: Digital Health; Healthcare; Health Insurance; Health & Wellness; Mental Health
one_liner: A modern-day mental healthcare company for global workforces.
long_description:
Intellect is the global leader in hyperlocalised mental healthcare, serving 4 million lives across enterprise employers, insurers, healthcare systems, and governments in over 50 languages and 100 countries.

With a comprehensive, AI-powered care ecosystem, Intellect seamlessly integrates digital therapeutics, virtual therapy, high-acuity crisis support, and specialty clinical treatment - delivered through its proprietary digital platforms and directly owned mental health clinics.

Headquartered in Singapore with nine global offices, Intellect is backed by top investors including Tiger Global, Y Combinator, Insignia Ventures, and HOF Capital. It is trusted by hundreds of Fortune 500 companies and industry leading organisations.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Employers, insurers and governments buying mental health benefits for workforces
problem: Workforce mental health care in Asia was hard to access and stigmatized; Intellect offers app based, coaching and clinical care for employees.
business_model: B2B enterprise subscription for employee mental health programs
product_category: Digital mental health for employers
market_need_then: TechCrunch in August 2021 reported Intellect claimed 2.5 million app users and 20 enterprise clients including FoodPanda and Shopback, during a pandemic rise in demand for workplace mental health support.
outcome_analysis: Intellect raised a chain of rounds from 800K seed to a 10M Series A and a 10M Tiger Global led extension in July 2022, and now claims 4 million lives and 200 staff on the YC page. Demand from employers for mental health benefits after the pandemic and a regional focus helped. No later round, layoff or acquisition was found, so the later funding history is incomplete.

name: Inversion Space
one_liner: Turning space into a transportation layer for Earth
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Government, defense and commercial customers needing cargo delivery from orbit
problem: Moving cargo anywhere on Earth within an hour; reentry vehicles that store cargo in orbit and return on demand.
business_model: Per mission cargo delivery and vehicle services, with government contracts
product_category: Space reentry vehicles
market_need_then: Launch costs were falling and the Department of Defense later invested in point to point space cargo; need was speculative in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Inversion raised a 10M seed and a 44M Series A in November 2024 and flew its Ray demonstrator on a January 2025 rideshare; reports say it reached orbit but a short circuit prevented its deorbit engine from firing so reentry did not happen. Arc is targeted for a 2026 first flight. Success so far rests on funding, defense interest and speed, but the main technical milestone is still ahead.

name: Invoid
one_liner: Create identity verification workflows the way you want
long_description: Invoid currently processes more than 5 million KYC’s/ month and works with over 35 companies in India, including some of the leading banks, fintechs, investment platforms & shared economy companies. Using our solution, companies see onboarding speed increase by 5x and costs reduce by >80%.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian banks, fintechs, investment platforms and gig economy companies that must verify customer identity (KYC)
problem: Physical KYC is slow and costly. After the Reserve Bank of India allowed video KYC in January 2020, companies needed a developer friendly way to run remote identity verification.
business_model: usage-based SaaS API per verification
product_category: identity verification, eKYC and video KYC
founder_names: Kunwar Raj Singh Sethi; Sarthak Goel
market_need_then: The RBI approved video KYC in January 2020 and Covid pushed remote onboarding. Inc42 (2020-07) reported daily KYCs up to over 15,000 from about 6,000, revenue up 250% in three months and over 50 clients.
outcome_analysis: inVOID rode the January 2020 RBI video KYC approval and Covid driven remote onboarding, growing fast in 2020 and joining YC in Winter 2021 with more than 35 clients and 5 million KYCs a month claimed. The market was crowded, and the company was acquired by Bureau Identity, reported in July 2023, for an undisclosed price. The YC directory marks it Inactive, which reflects the brand being absorbed, not a documented shutdown. A reported team move to Credenc for a student neobank has conflicting dates.

name: Ivella
tags: Banking as a Service; Fintech; Consumer Finance
one_liner: Banking and savings products designed for couples
long_description: Ivella builds banking and savings products that are designed for couples, no matter where they are in their relationship. Whether you've been dating for months are signing up for the The Split Account or have been married for decades and are signing up for The Joint Account and Savings Pods, we've got a product for you.
all_locations: Los Angeles, CA, USA; Santa Monica, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Couples in the US who share expenses and want joint banking and savings
problem: Couples struggle to manage shared money with accounts built for individuals. Ivella started as an expense splitting app and moved to joint checking and savings.
business_model: Consumer fintech through partner bank, earning interchange and balances revenue (inferred from banking as a service category; not stated in sources)
product_category: Couples banking and joint accounts
founder_names: Kahlil Lalji; Vishal Dubey; Eric Wang
market_need_then: Couples sharing money used workarounds such as one partner paying and Venmo; TechCrunch covered it in 2022 as the latest couples banking fintech, showing crowded interest.
outcome_analysis: Ivella raised a 3.5M seed in June 2022 for couples banking and launched joint accounts in 2023, then sunset its products and joined EarnIn. The company page does not give a reason, date or deal terms, and no post-mortem was found. The failure factors are therefore tentative: a soft landing is stated by the site, while a missing next round is only inferred from the absence of later funding.

name: Ivy Homes
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: We make instant offers to buy homes in India
long_description:
Selling a home is a super stressful affair due to the uncertainties involved. We help smoothen that process by guaranteeing a fair price and offering that value upfront for the seller. We’ve built up an information system that captures the details of all real estate transactions.
We’ve further developed a pricing model on top of it that helps determine the value of a home. We use this to offer liquidity to the seller by making an instant offer to purchase their house. We then refurb the property as necessary and further sell through our channel partners.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Home sellers in India (Bengaluru)
problem: Selling a home is slow and uncertain; Ivy makes instant offers, refurbishes and resells via channel partners.
business_model: iBuying: buy, refurbish and resell homes (spread)
product_category: Proptech iBuyer
market_need_then: Founders argue selling a home in India is slow and stressful; Inc42 cites an Indian real estate market projected to grow from $200 Bn in 2021 to $1 Tn by 2030. Demand evidence beyond the company claim was not found.
outcome_analysis: Ivy Homes is a Summer 2021 iBuyer for Bengaluru that raised about $7M in June 2022 (USD 5.75M equity plus 1.3M debt) and still operates. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, and the balance-sheet heavy model carries inventory risk that sources do not yet show succeeding or failing, so no outcome factors are assigned.

name: JABU
one_liner: B2B payments, transforming Africa's cash economy
long_description: HQ in Namibia and Zambia, Jabu is a fintech startup providing digital wallet solutions to streamline transactions in Africa's cash-dominated economy, enhancing business efficiency and financial integration.
all_locations: Cape Town, WC, South Africa; Windhoek, Khomas Region, Namibia
regions: South Africa; Namibia; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Informal retailers and suppliers in Southern Africa, later businesses and banks needing cash digitization
problem: Namibia and neighbors run on cash; JABU first digitized ordering and distribution for small shops, then moved to smart safes and digital wallets.
business_model: B2B e-commerce margin and logistics fees, later fees for smart safes, payments and wallets
product_category: B2B commerce then cash digitization and payments
market_need_then: TechCrunch in January 2022 said pandemic lockdowns hit small shops, and JABU registered about 1,000 shops with existing software, then reported GMV up 25x.
outcome_analysis: JABU raised 3.2M seed in January 2022 and 15M Series A led by Tiger Global in May 2022 on fast GMV growth in Namibia and Zambia. The current site shows a shift to smart safes and payments across Namibia, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe. A February 2026 article via search results says it is exploring local manufacturing of safes. No layoffs or shutdown were found, and funding after 2022 is unknown.

name: Jestor
one_liner: Saving OPS from SLOPS. Jestor builds internal systems that last.
long_description: Stop vibecoding internal tools nobody can maintain. Get apps, tables, forms, dashboards, and AI automations built for your process, on infrastructure that already handles permissions, data, and integrations. Your team just opens the app. Unlimited users, pause anytime.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Operations teams in small and mid sized companies, mainly in Brazil
problem: Companies run operations on spreadsheets and legacy ERPs; Jestor offers a no-code database and workflow platform with unlimited users.
business_model: SaaS subscription with a free tier and paid plans up to R$299 per month (2021)
product_category: No-code internal tools and operations platform
market_need_then: Startups.com.br in August 2021 said Jestor aimed to replace spreadsheets and ERPs, was near breakeven with 10 people and had clients like Loft and Sami.
outcome_analysis: Jestor was near breakeven in 2021 on 458K raised and, per Exame via search results, later reached profit. It continues as a no-code and AI platform with a mostly Brazilian base. No large priced round was found, so it stayed capital efficient rather than venture scale; no layoffs or acquisition were reported.

name: Jetdocs
one_liner: Collaborative ticketing that integrates into Teams and Slack
long_description:
Jetdocs is a collaborative ticketing solution that is integrated into Microsoft Teams and Slack. We allow teams to create no-code workflows that digitize your processes and connect your teams.

We empower IT and Ops teams with the interface, as well as the ability to build out workflows to handle internal tickets, requests and approvals. We eliminate the problems of bloated email chains, group inboxes and long messaging threads.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: IT, HR and operations teams at companies using Microsoft Teams and Slack
problem: Internal requests and approvals are buried in email, shared inboxes and chat threads; Jetdocs provides ticketing with workflows inside Teams and Slack.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Internal ticketing and workflow
market_need_then: Founders said the problem came from sharing information across departments; the company says teams drown in email chains and shared inboxes.
outcome_analysis: Jetdocs is still active with a live site, SOC 2 Type II and a Teams AI assistant named Gerald, but the YC page lists a team of two. No funding amount was verified, so the funding trajectory is unknown rather than zero. The stalled visible growth suggests a small bootstrapped business, though no source states this.

name: Jiga
one_liner: Source better parts by partnering directly with vetted manufacturers
long_description:
Source high-quality, cost-competitive custom parts faster by partnering directly with vetted manufacturers.

Jiga is used by engineers and supply chain managers from NASA, Siemens, Tesla, Google and many more.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel; Remote
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mechanical engineers, procurement and supply chain managers at hardware companies (aerospace, defense, robotics) who buy custom machined, sheet metal, printed and molded parts
problem: Sourcing custom parts runs through email threads and spreadsheets, and instant-quote services hide the actual manufacturer, so complex parts suffer from miscommunication, delays and higher cost.
business_model: Managed B2B manufacturing marketplace; takes a margin on parts ordered from vetted suppliers, with quoting, order tracking and quality management software
product_category: Custom manufacturing marketplace and sourcing platform
founder_names: Adar Hay; Assaf Geuz; Yonatan Wolowelsky
market_need_then: The YC launch post describes engineers managing sourcing in email and spreadsheets, and the March 2021 launch article reports 30,000 parts already shipped while bootstrapped, which shows early paid demand during pandemic supply chain stress.
outcome_analysis: Jiga bootstrapped from 2020, shipped tens of thousands of parts before YC Winter 2021, and reports being profitable. It then raised a $12M Series A led by Aleph in November 2025 after the seed funding history stayed unclear. The white box positioning gave a clear contrast with black box rivals, and the company is still operating, so no failure factors apply.

name: JoinSub
one_liner: India's first aggregator and provider of local business subscriptions
long_description:
We, at JoinSub, are empowering the Indian small and medium retailers to drive repeat purchases & maximize their revenue by building a subscription-based model. 

India has over 14 million retail outlets, and we are poised to revolutionize the Retail Sector and enhance the buying experience both for retailers and consumers. We are dedicated to co-creating a community of futuristic retailers who are ready to embrace tech for growth.

Our Subscription Programs work wonderfully for everyone who is looking to drive repurchases, right from those in the F&B industry, to Salons, Nail Salons, Spas, Gyms, Yoga & Dance Studios, Coffee Shops, Bakeries, Dry Cleaners, Florists, etc. We can help you delight your consumers and accelerate your business, the JoinSub Way!
all_locations: Delhi, DL, India; Palo Alto, CA, USA; Remote
regions: India; United States of America; South Asia; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Journey
one_liner: No code platform for sales to tell better stories and win more deals.
long_description:
Journey is a storytelling tool designed for the internet age. We've identified hundreds of opportunities to tell better stories: sales, marketing, fundraising, and many more.

Journey is a tool that allows you to combine all sorts of content into one interactive experience. We believe that the future of storytelling looks more like a video game than a slideshow.

We're an experienced senior team (the founders have worked together for 6 years across two companies) that is building a well funded and thoughtful company.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Sales teams and founders who send decks, videos and PDFs to buyers and investors
problem: Static decks and scattered links give senders no view of who engaged, and buyers get a poor experience.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (14 day trial per current site)
product_category: Interactive sales storytelling and digital sales rooms
founder_names: Peter Clark; Anil Sevim; Brendan Weitz
market_need_then: Remote selling and fundraising in 2020 to 2021 increased sending of decks and links; no spend figures found.
outcome_analysis: Journey was a no-code interactive sales page tool from founders with senior growth, engineering and sales backgrounds at AdRoll, Udemy, Quora and Facebook. It raised a pre-seed led by Susa Ventures in October 2022 and YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer or date was found, and its site still markets the product. The outcome cannot be explained beyond that, so failure factors stay empty.

name: Jovian
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Developer Tools; Education; Machine Learning
one_liner: Online University for Tech Professionals
long_description:
Jovian is an online university for software development and data science. We offer practical and industry-focused programs that help professionals learn technical skills, build real-world projects, and advance their careers.

Students learn practical skills, build real-world portfolio projects, and undergo job readiness training. Our tutors offer 24x7 guidance & mentorship over Slack & Zoom. Students also get access to jobs with 200+ hiring partners.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Working professionals and students in India and globally who pay for job-oriented software development and data science programs
problem: Learners struggle to move into data science and software careers through self-study; they need structure, mentorship and hiring access.
business_model: Paid online bootcamps and programs with mentorship, plus free courses and community as top of funnel
product_category: Online education, tech upskilling
market_need_then: Strong demand for tech upskilling in India during the pandemic; the 2022 seed coverage cites 200,000 community users in more than 180 countries.
outcome_analysis: Jovian built a free community and courses and then sold job-oriented programs, raising a $1.5M seed in May 2022 after YC. It still operates under SwiftAce Inc. with a claimed 575k learners, but no later round or exit was found, so the outcome is a modest, still-active company with limited public data.

name: Juicy Marbles
one_liner: Juicy marbles makes thick juicy and marbled plant based steaks.
long_description: We are food-tech company. We developed proprietary protein texturing technology that enables us to produce plant-based whole cuts. Our vision is to produce a variety of meat products and match animal derived counterparts by taste, price and convenience. We want to accelerate transition of meat industry into a more sustainable future - by 2030 we want to cut meat consumption in half.
regions: Slovenia; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Flexitarian and vegan consumers and restaurants buying premium plant-based whole cut steaks
problem: Plant-based meat mostly imitates ground products; whole cuts with real texture and marbling were missing, limiting meat reduction.
business_model: Consumer packaged food sold through direct online sales, retailers and restaurants
product_category: Plant-based whole cut meat
founder_names: Luka Sinček; Maj Hrovat; Tilen Travnik
market_need_then: Plant-based meat demand was high in 2020 and 2021, and the company reported selling 100,000 steaks around the Valentine's Day 2023 run up per trade coverage.
outcome_analysis: Juicy Marbles launched a plant-based filet mignon in 2021, raised a $4.5M seed from World Fund in November 2021, and later reached retail listings such as Waitrose in 2023. No later rounds, exit or shutdown were found, so it is an active company whose funding history after the seed is not public in the sources checked.

name: June
one_liner: June is the new way to do product analytics
long_description:
June is a plug & play product analytics for B2B SaaS. 

It automatically generates graphs of the metrics you should track, lets you view your company-level metrics, and zoom into them!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: KaiPod Learning
one_liner: A national network of microschools bringing school choice to every…
long_description:
KaiPod Learning is a national network of microschools bringing school choice to every community in America. We work with education entrepreneurs to start high-quality microschools to better serve students and their families.

As more families stand up for choice in education and as more educators look for alternative career pathways, KaiPod Learning is helping bring microschools into the mainstream.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Families wanting small in-person schooling for grades 3 to 12, and educators who want to start microschools
problem: Parents wanted in-person, personalised alternatives to traditional and online-only schooling, and teachers had no easy path to launch their own small schools.
business_model: Tuition from learning centers and later a network and accelerator model (Catalyst program fees, software and support for independently owned microschools)
product_category: Microschool network and education entrepreneurship accelerator
market_need_then: Pandemic school closures drove the pod and microschool trend in 2020 and 2021; KaiPod's first center opened in Newton, Massachusetts in March 2021 per CRPE coverage.
outcome_analysis: KaiPod opened its first center in March 2021, raised a $1.5M seed in November 2021, then shifted to an asset-light network and Catalyst accelerator announced in December 2022. It reports 150+ schools in 30+ states, while no later round or exit was found, so it is active with limited public funding data.

name: Kalam Labs
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Drones; Aerospace; AI
one_liner: Autonomous Stratospheric UAVs
long_description:
Kalam Labs has developed autonomous spaceplanes, capable of flying from 100,000+ ft altitude to conduct upper atmospheric sensing, currently limited to non-maneuverable balloons and expensive satellites.
We are one of the world's highest flying UAVs, and have $330 Mn+ contracts from global goverments to deploy the autonomous spaceplanes and replace traditional satellites and ground-borne UAVs
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Government and defense buyers in India (army, defense agencies) and scientific users needing near space and stratospheric data
problem: Upper atmosphere sensing relies on non-maneuverable balloons (most single-use radiosondes are lost) and expensive satellites, leaving a gap for reusable stratospheric platforms.
business_model: Hardware and contracts sold to government and defense customers; reusable stratospheric UAVs and platforms
product_category: Stratospheric UAVs and near space aerospace hardware
founder_names: Ahmad Faraaz; Sashakt Tripathi; Harshit Awasthi
market_need_then: Gap between balloons and satellites for upper atmosphere sensing; company site cites 600,000 radiosondes launched yearly with over 80 percent lost. Indian defense demand for indigenous drones grew later.
outcome_analysis: Kalam Labs took a small pre-seed in August 2021 and kept building reusable near space aircraft, then in 2025 reported altitude records and army demonstrations as it moved into defense. Reported $330M contracts on the YC page are unverified, and later raises are only reported as talks, so success so far is technical rather than financial.

name: Kanda
one_liner: Affirm for general contractors
long_description: Kanda is building Affirm for general contractors. We allow contractors to offer financing to homeowners who want to remodel but can’t pay the full price upfront.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: UK tradespeople and home improvement contractors who want to offer finance to homeowners
problem: Small contractors lose jobs to bigger firms that can offer customers credit, because they cannot access consumer finance themselves.
business_model: Credit broker model: contractors (introducer appointed representatives) introduce customers to partner lenders; Kanda earns broker commission
product_category: Point of sale consumer finance for trades
market_need_then: Founder experience of losing jobs for lack of customer credit; the FCA states Kanda ended with a network of around 700 tradespeople, showing real uptake.
outcome_analysis: Kanda built a broker network of around 700 tradespeople in the UK, then agreed to FCA restrictions on appointing new representatives in February 2026 over weaknesses in systems and controls, and its main entity entered liquidation on 6 May 2026. The FCA does not state the cause of the liquidation, so the regulatory factor is an inference from the sequence; no funding history beyond YC was found.

name: Kapacity.io
one_liner: Reducing energy costs & emissions in buildings.
long_description: Kapacity.io is building the future of smart energy grids with an electricity Load Balancing service focused on buildings.
regions: Finland; Europe
target_customer: Commercial real estate owners and, later, energy retailers and heat pump makers needing demand flexibility
problem: Buildings use electricity at expensive, high emission times and lack automated ways to shift load and sell flexibility to the grid.
business_model: Software and flexibility services sharing grid revenue
product_category: Demand response and building energy optimization
founder_names: Jaakko Rauhala; Sonja Salo; Rami El Geneidy
market_need_then: European electrification and dynamic electricity pricing created demand for load shifting; the company claimed early trials cut power costs 25% and CO2 10% (self reported, TechCrunch 2021-08).
outcome_analysis: Kapacity.io sold AI load shifting for buildings into a European market moving to electrification and dynamic pricing, then refocused on heat pumps and was acquired by EnergyHub in December 2024. Funding found is only about 125K to 130K of pre-seed on aggregators, so the exit was reached on little disclosed capital, suggesting capital efficiency but unverified.

name: Karbon Card
one_liner: Corporate Card solution for Indian businesses
long_description:
We at Karbon Cards provide corporate credit cards, vendor payment solutions and forex outward remittance products to Indian companies. We partners with banks and other FI's to provide comprehensive spend management and working capital solutions. Companies qualify for credit via a liberalized startup friendly underwriting process.

For those do not qualify, we provide payments option where companies can top up and use card/vendor payment solutions.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian startups and SMEs needing corporate cards, vendor payments, and forex remittances
problem: Indian startups could not get corporate credit cards without personal guarantees or collateral, and lacked spend management and working capital tools.
business_model: Card interchange, vendor payment and forex fees, plus interest on credit with bank and lender partners
product_category: Corporate cards and spend management fintech
founder_names: Pei-fu Hsieh; Amit Jangir; Kartik Jain; Sunil Sinha
market_need_then: India's startup boom with few corporate cards for young companies; one 2025 analysis estimates about 5 percent card penetration among 63 million MSMEs. Inc42 reports 2,000 corporates served and $30M monthly GTV in December 2021.
outcome_analysis: Karbon raised seed money in 2020, a $12M pre-Series A in September 2021 and a $15M Series A in February 2022, then took debt for lending. It reports serving 3,000 companies and kept launching products through 2025, with no exit or shutdown found, so it is an active growth stage company in a competitive Indian card market.

name: Kaya
one_liner: Marketing agency for startups: 10x cheaper, better and faster
long_description:
Kaya is on a mission to help businesses achieve rapid growth through digital advertising. With our cutting-edge technology and experienced marketers, we deliver ad campaigns 10x cheaper, better and faster than traditional agencies. In less than a year, we’ve helped 120+ businesses achieve multiple fold growth on their ad campaigns, without the steep fees typically associated with high-quality marketing services.

Check out what some of our customers have to say here: usekaya.com/reviews
all_locations: Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; Remote
regions: Malaysia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startups and small businesses buying paid advertising on Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok
problem: Startups overpay traditional agencies or lack in-house marketers to run paid campaigns efficiently.
business_model: Agency service fees (one aggregator says from $3,000 monthly) with analytics software; the current site sells a competitor ad intelligence tool at a one-time $250 Pro plan
product_category: AI-assisted performance marketing agency and ad intelligence software
market_need_then: Startups spend heavily on paid ads; the claim of 10x cheaper agency work and 120+ business customers is the company's own and unverified.
outcome_analysis: Kaya launched as an AI-assisted marketing agency for startups in 2021 and claimed 120+ clients, but no funding, revenue or exit was found. The current site sells an ad intelligence tool, which suggests a shift in offering, so the outcome is an active small company with insufficient public data to judge.

name: Keyri
one_liner: Secure fraud prevention and authentication platform for developers
long_description:
Keyri helps companies implement simple, secure anti-fraud and authentication solutions to delight users and keep bad actors off their platform. Keyri's mobile application and browser fingerprinting suite ties user identities to trusted devices, preventing fraudulent activity such as account opening, account takeovers, bot attacks, and referral/promo abuse. Keyri is able to establish an immutable device fingerprint for every device, alerting companies of any suspicious devices during sign up, log in, or subsequent authentication events.

Keyri also offers a passwordless authentication suite that leverages Passkeys, WebAuthn, and QR codes to enable biometric authentication on all platforms and devices, providing a seamless user experience, strengthening multi-factor account security, and reducing reliance on other tedious and unsecure authentication methods.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers and companies needing passwordless login and device fraud detection
problem: Passwords are weak and costly; sites need a login that resists account takeover and bots.
business_model: Developer SaaS with free and paid plans
product_category: Passwordless authentication and device fingerprinting
market_need_then: Account takeover and password fatigue were widely discussed; no company specific demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Keyri sold QR code passwordless login and later added device fingerprinting for fraud prevention, partnering with Ping Identity in 2022. Its team joined Signifyd to strengthen account takeover protection, with no date or price disclosed. Reported funding is only about 130K from YC on aggregators, so capital raised cannot be confirmed and the exit looks small.

name: Kidato
one_liner: Online school for K12 education in Africa
long_description: Parents in Africa face either public schools with student-teacher ratios as high as 50:1 or private schools with tuition fees as high as $7500 per year, per child. Kidato classes have student-teacher ratios of 5:1 and teach the same rigorous international curriculum as other private schools — but at a fraction of the price. In our second semester, Kidato has enrolled more than 30 students into our learning-from-home program as a replacement for brick-and-mortar schools. We expect to triple this enrollment by our third semester.
regions: Kenya; Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Parents in Africa, mainly Kenya, who want an international (British, IGCSE) curriculum for children aged about 4 to 18 at a price well below private school tuition
problem: Public schools in Africa can have student to teacher ratios as high as 50 to 1, while private international schools can cost up to 7,500 dollars per child per year. Kidato offers live online classes at about 5 to 1 for a fraction of that cost.
business_model: Tuition-based online school (per student subscription per semester)
product_category: Online K12 school (live classes over video)
market_need_then: COVID-19 school closures in 2020 pushed Kenyan families to remote learning. Kidato's own YC page cites a second semester with more than 30 students enrolled and plans to triple that, so demand existed but at a small base.
outcome_analysis: Kidato started in 2020 as COVID closures pushed Kenyan parents toward remote schooling, and raised a 1.4 million dollar seed in April 2021 right after the Winter 2021 YC batch. The founder had incubator experience through Nailab and a prior YC company, which helped him raise from African and US funds. The company is listed as active with about 15 staff. No later round or exit was found, so how well enrollment held after schools reopened is not public.

name: Kilobaser
one_liner: Desktop DNA Printer. The Nespresso Machine for DNA.
long_description: We combined microfluidic chip technology and a reagent cartridge to create the first personal DNA synthesizer. Until now most life scientists had to rely on out-sourced DNA synthesis, causing stagnating research. Kilobaser empowers every life scientist to synthesize DNA on their benchtop.
regions: Austria; Europe
target_customer: Life science research labs that order custom oligonucleotides (DNA and RNA primers and probes) from outside suppliers
problem: Labs wait days for outsourced DNA synthesis. Kilobaser sells a desktop synthesizer using microfluidic chips and reagent cartridges so a lab can make oligos on the bench in under two hours.
business_model: Hardware instrument sales plus recurring cartridge and reagent sales
product_category: Benchtop DNA and RNA synthesizer (life science instruments)
founder_names: Alexander Murer; Martin Jost; Bernhard Tittelbach
market_need_then: Life scientists routinely order primers and probes from outside vendors and wait for delivery. The YC description states that outsourcing stagnates research. No dated demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Kilobaser built a hard-tech desktop DNA synthesizer in Graz and joined YC in Winter 2021. Public funding data is thin: one aggregator shows an undisclosed round from Cathexis Ventures in April 2021 and about 125 thousand dollars total. CB Insights style listings report a bankruptcy filing in July 2023 and an asset sale in January 2024, but these come from aggregators only and the company website was still live, so the true status and cause are not public in sources I could verify. If the insolvency is real, long hardware development cycles with limited capital would be the likely pressure, which is inference only.

name: Kindamagical
one_liner: Create + share amazing product GIFs in minutes ⚡️
long_description: Kindamagical is a recording + editing studio for making product content. We help users record, produce, and share product GIFs in minutes, that would otherwise take hours to produce with traditional tools.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Mill Valley, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product marketers and founders at software companies who need short product demo GIFs and guides
problem: Making product GIFs and demo content with traditional tools takes hours.
business_model: SaaS subscription, Pro plan $29 per month per the site
product_category: product content and demo recording tool
market_need_then: Remote product teams needed lightweight demo content in 2021, but no demand evidence found for this specific tool.
outcome_analysis: YC lists Kindamagical as inactive with a team of one, but no shutdown post, news or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. The website still loads under the name Kindamagic selling a Pro plan for interactive product guides, so the product may have continued after pivoting. A single founder in a crowded recording tool category with easy copyability is a plausible stall, but no source states a reason.

name: Kitemaker
tags: Developer Tools; Productivity; Team Collaboration; Remote Work
one_liner: A faster and more collaborative alternative to Jira for remote teams
long_description:
Kitemaker is a faster and more collaborative alternative to Jira optimized for remote teams.

It's helping teams spend less time and effort on collaboration by providing a place for discussing and documenting initiatives, it collects activities and discussions across tools, and it's fast and simple to use.

Unlike tools like Jira and Notion, our primary focus is helping software development teams spend less time coordinating across tools and roles so they have more time figuring out and building the things their users want.
regions: Norway; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Remote software and product teams paying per seat for project management
problem: Specs, tasks, roadmaps and user feedback live in disconnected tools and Jira is slow.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat
product_category: Product development and project management software
market_need_then: Teams complained of tool fragmentation per the founders' launch post; no spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Kitemaker was a Oslo based Jira alternative combining specs, tasks and feedback. The company site states ClickUp acquired it and the service was discontinued on 1 September 2025, so the product ended rather than continuing as a brand. Funding is unverified aggregator data and no traction numbers were found, so the cause of the soft exit is not public.

name: Kiwi Biosciences
one_liner: Patent-pending enzymes to break down common dietary triggers
long_description: Kiwi Biosciences can help 18M Americans suffering from Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) enjoy a normal meal without running to the bathroom two hours later. We develop novel, patent-pending enzymes that break down common digestive triggers in food.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: People with irritable bowel syndrome who follow or want to avoid the low FODMAP diet (consumers, sold online and through retail partners)
problem: About 18 million Americans have IBS and the standard approach is a restrictive low FODMAP diet. Kiwi Bio sells FODZYME, a tasteless enzyme powder added to food that breaks down FODMAP triggers.
business_model: Direct to consumer consumable (enzyme powder bottles and stick packs) plus retail partners
product_category: Digestive enzyme supplement (biotech, food tech)
market_need_then: TechCrunch reported a founder with IBS who tried the restrictive diet for nearly three years. The company cites about 15 percent of the world and 18 million Americans with IBS, and FODZYME launched in May 2021 at 39 dollars a bottle.
outcome_analysis: Kiwi Bio launched FODZYME in May 2021 and raised a 1.5 million dollar seed after the Summer 2021 YC batch, led by a founder with first-hand IBS experience and a second founder who had already built and sold a gut health app. The product won Monash certification and clinical interest, expanded to Australia, the UK and Europe by 2022, and was still updating its formula in 2025. No later round or exit was found, so growth beyond the seed is not publicly documented.

name: Kiwify
one_liner: Create & sell online courses
long_description:
Kiwify enables anyone to create and sell their online course in Brazil.
We provide payment processing, video streaming and student management
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Brazilian infoproducers and online course creators who sell digital products, plus affiliates and buyers on the platform
problem: Creators in Brazil needed payment processing, video hosting and student management in one place at a low cost. Kiwify bundles checkout, video streaming, members area and affiliate management.
business_model: Take rate on each sale (percentage plus fixed fee per transaction), plus receivables advance financing
product_category: Digital product and online course sales platform (creator economy)
market_need_then: Online course and infoproduct sales grew during the 2020 pandemic in Brazil according to a Sebrae guide; creators wanted lower fees and bundled video hosting.
outcome_analysis: Kiwify entered the crowded Brazilian infoproduct market in 2020 against Hotmart, Eduzz and Monetizze, winning producers with free video hosting and low fees. It grew to a team of about 200 and, per a sponsored 2024 article, more than 30,000 active producers and 25 million registered buyers. The documented capital is YC's standard deal plus receivables fund debt of R$50 million in late 2024 and R$150 million in February 2025, not venture equity. Growth appears driven by the product and the creator economy rather than venture funding.

name: Kodda
tags: Consumer Health Services; Digital Health; Health & Wellness
long_description: Community that accompanies you in your transformation towards a healthy and lasting lifestyle, through guided programs made by professionals who will support you every step of the way.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Spanish-speaking consumers in Mexico paying a subscription for guided health and habit programs
problem: People struggle to keep healthy habits after crash diets; Kodda offered community plus professional-made programs to make lifestyle change lasting.
business_model: Consumer subscription app with programs from nutritionists and trainers, plus partner studios
product_category: Consumer digital health and wellness habit app
market_need_then: Growing consumer interest in wellness after 2020, and a launch write-up reported over 2,400 downloads in the first month, but willingness to pay in Mexico was unproven.
outcome_analysis: Kodda joined YC in Summer 2021 with a habit and wellness community app from Monterrey and is now listed as Inactive. No shutdown notice, post-mortem or date was found, so the cause is not public, and no failure factors are asserted.

name: Kodex
one_liner: Easiest way for companies to process data requests from governments
long_description:
Kodex makes it easy for companies to process, and respond to, subpoenas from governments around the world. Agencies, like the FBI, subpoena user data from customers like Coinbase, and thousands of other companies - without Kodex, companies largely rely on email, fax, and spreadsheets to manage them.

Kodex is a SaaS tool that helps private sector companies manage relationships, workflows, and secure file transfer with government agencies who are seeking confidential information on a company's users. We streamline compliance operations, protect the privacy of their users, reduce error, and validate the legitimacy of government agents who are requesting information.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Companies such as crypto exchanges and tech platforms that receive subpoenas and data requests from law enforcement and government agencies
problem: Companies handled government data requests by email, fax and spreadsheets, risking errors and impersonation by fake officials. Kodex provides workflow, requester verification and secure file transfer.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for companies, with a network of verified government requesters
product_category: Legal compliance software for law enforcement response
market_need_then: The founder's own account is a stalled FBI counterterrorism investigation because a social media company did not know how to answer legal requests safely. Crypto and fintech firms such as Coinbase received growing volumes of requests, and company blog posts show crypto exchanges as customers.
outcome_analysis: Kodex was founded by a former FBI counterterrorism officer who saw first-hand how platforms struggled to answer legal requests. It joined YC in Summer 2021, raised a 10 million dollar seed led by a16z in November 2023 per its own blog, and sells to crypto exchanges and other data holders. Its two sided network of verified agencies is the main moat. Sources conflict on total funding and a later Series A is only reported by an aggregator that could not be opened.

name: Kodo
one_liner: Corporate card & spend management platform for Indian startups
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian startups and growing companies that need corporate cards, vendor payments and spend management
problem: Indian startups lacked a proper corporate card and spend control product. Kodo issues cards with credit limits and later added procurement, payables and reimbursements in one system.
business_model: Card interchange and fees plus spend management software and payments
product_category: Corporate card and spend management (fintech)
market_need_then: Reported card spend growth of 45 percent month over month for the prior twelve months in the May 2021 seed coverage, and Brex invested, which signals demand from Indian startups.
outcome_analysis: Kodo joined YC in Winter 2021 and raised an 8.75 million dollar seed in May 2021 led by strategic and YC-linked investors including Brex, reported by several outlets. It later widened from cards into full spend management and says more than 2,000 companies use it. No later priced round, exit or distress was found, and aggregators disagree on total funding, so the funding trail after the seed is unverified.

name: Konta.com
one_liner: Turbotax for México and LATAM
long_description: Konta.com is a tax filing and accounting platform for small businesses in México.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mexican freelancers, individuals with business income and small businesses that must file taxes with the SAT
problem: Small taxpayers in Mexico depend on traditional accountants for filings and invoices. Konta combines software with accountants to automate tax filing, CFDI invoicing and SAT compliance.
business_model: Subscription accounting and tax service combining software and human accountants
product_category: Tax filing and accounting platform (fintech SaaS)
market_need_then: Forbes Mexico describes Konta starting as accounting service and becoming a tech-enabled accounting firm. Mexican SAT compliance is mandatory for millions of taxpayers, and Konta reported 16.5 million pesos in 2022 revenue and 61 employees per Forbes Mexico.
outcome_analysis: Konta started as Buho Contable, an accounting service in Monterrey, and rebranded to Konta.com as it built software. It joined YC in Summer 2021 and raised about 2.65 million dollars in seed funding with YC, Streamlined Ventures and Liquid 2. By 2022 Forbes Mexico reported 16.5 million pesos in revenue and 61 staff, and the YC page lists 35. No Series A or exit was found, so later growth is not documented.

name: Koshex
one_liner: Automating wealth creation for 400M Indian millennials
long_description: Koshex is building Wealthfront for India with data-driven insights around day to day finances for an individual to save more and invest well. We are automating wealth creation for 400 million Indian millennials with access to more than US$700bn of individual investable wealth.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Young Indian salaried investors (millennials) who want to track net worth and invest in mutual funds, digital gold and fixed deposits
problem: Indian millennials lack automated, data-driven help to save and invest. Koshex positions itself as Wealthfront for India, with budgeting, tracking and investing in one app.
business_model: Mutual fund distribution commissions (AMFI-registered distributor) and other investment product revenue
product_category: Personal finance and wealth app (fintech)
market_need_then: Koshex's YC description cites 400 million Indian millennials with access to over 700 billion dollars of investable wealth. A search summary reports fewer than 30 million Indians then invested in mutual funds and stocks, source not opened.
outcome_analysis: Koshex, run by Neuokosh Capital, launched in 2020 as a personal finance and investing app for Indian millennials and joined YC in Summer 2021. It raised about 2.1 million dollars in a seed round reported in April 2022, then claims over 400K users on its site. Competition from far better funded investing apps was intense and no later round or exit was found, so the long term outcome is unclear.

name: Krab
one_liner: Instant loans for trucking companies in India
long_description: A lending platform that enables truckers/trucking companies with no formal credit score to access loans from banks. Our platform creates a rich credit profile of a trucking company by pulling 200+ data points from varied sources via consent APIs and instantly offers loans from multiple banking partners in less than 60 seconds. The trucking company can also use the same product for order management, invoice generation, vendor payments, and collections.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Kredi
one_liner: Rocket Mortgage for LatAm.
long_description: Kredi is rocket mortgage for LatAm.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mexican homebuyers who need a mortgage and are underserved by banks
problem: Getting a mortgage in Mexico was slow, opaque and often denied. Kredi digitized origination and comparison so buyers could find and close a loan faster.
business_model: Mortgage broker fees at first, then own mortgage origination with interest income (from 2022 per a review)
product_category: Digital mortgage platform (fintech, Latin America)
founder_names: Javier Aldape; Juan Carlos Mercado; Fernando Nader Giacoman; Hernan Belden
competitors_at_founding: Creditas; Traditional Mexican banks and Infonavit
market_need_then: Mexico had a large mortgage gap and complaints about slow, denied applications. The founder cited his own repeated denial. The company reported over 8 million dollars of loans originated in early 2021 and 30 percent monthly revenue growth (Crunchbase News, June 2021).
outcome_analysis: Kredi raised a 2 million dollar round and a 3.1 million dollar seed in 2021 while reporting fast early growth and moved from brokerage to own lending in 2022. The company site now says it is not offering new credits, so the current state is unclear. A March 2026 ecosystem profile says it has served over 700 thousand families, but no later round was verified.

name: Kurios
one_liner: Cohort-based online courses for professionals in Latin America
long_description:
Kurios is cohort based online courses for professionals in Latin America. Our instructors are professionals coming out of tech companies like Google, Amazon, Stripe and more. 

Our course completion rate is 90% and annual customer retention rate is 100%.

We have 65 B2B customers and we up-skill their employees in product management, growth and data analytics, just to start with.

Some customers: Walmart Mexico, Banorte (2nd bank in Mexico), Mercado Libre, BCP (#1 bank in Peru), Alicorp (leading CPG in Latam), Sura (leading pension fund), etc.
all_locations: Lima, Callao Region, Peru; Lima, Lima Province, Peru
regions: Peru; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Lago
tags: FinOps; Fintech; SaaS; Open Source; Billing
one_liner: The AI Native Billing Platform
long_description:
At Lago, we're on a mission to make billing simpler, more transparent, and more adaptable for SaaS companies.

As the leading open-source billing platform, we empower businesses to build flexible pricing models and scale with confidence. We've raised over $22 million in funding from top-tier investors including Y Combinator and FirstMark, reflecting strong confidence in our vision and growth.

Our platform has garnered over 9,000 stars on GitHub, a testament to our active and growing developer community. Companies such as PayPal, Synthesia and Mistral.ai choose Lago for their billing.

We're a team of ambitious, focused individuals who work together to solve hard problems with excellence and accountability. At Lago, we value reliability and proactivity - we trust each other to own tasks, drive them to completion, and adapt quickly. While we encourage you to try fast and "fail fast", we also expect you to learn fast: make mistakes, but don't make the same one twice.

If you're excited by challenges and want to grow alongside a high-performing, supportive team, this is the place for you.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: SaaS, AI and API companies with usage-based or hybrid pricing that outgrew home-built billing
problem: Engineering teams rebuild billing in-house because off-the-shelf tools were too rigid for usage-based pricing. Lago offers an open-source metering and billing engine.
business_model: Open source core (AGPLv3) with paid Lago Cloud and premium self-hosted features
product_category: Usage-based billing and metering platform (open source)
market_need_then: Usage-based pricing was growing among SaaS and API companies, and the founders say they repeatedly tried to replace home-grown billing and found nothing flexible enough (Launch HN, 2023).
outcome_analysis: Lago took the open-source route in a crowded billing market, gaining developer attention in early 2023 and raising a 15 million dollar Series A in March 2024 with total funding reported near 22 million. It rides the shift to usage-based and AI pricing while facing Stripe and well-funded rivals. No exit as of the latest sources.

name: Lalabox
one_liner: Live stream shopping for beauty products
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Lamar Health
one_liner: Take Care of Shitty Paperwork for Expensive Drugs
long_description:
We deal with drugs that cost on average $70,000/patient per year. These patients need their medications within days but currently it takes weeks because of complex, manual workflows that were built around poor data standards. 

At Lamar Health, our mission is to get patients on therapy fast. Our customers are specialty pharmacies, infusion clinics and hospitals that are moving quickly to use AI to offset operational risks and gain competitive advantage.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Specialty pharmacies, infusion clinics and hospitals handling high cost drugs
problem: Specialty drugs averaging about 70,000 dollars per patient per year need prior authorization and benefit checks that take weeks of manual work, delaying therapy.
business_model: B2B SaaS and workflow automation sold to specialty pharmacies and infusion providers
product_category: AI prior authorization and intake automation for specialty pharmacy
market_need_then: Prior authorization for specialty drugs was a recognized bottleneck and cost center for pharmacies, with delays measured in weeks per the company.
outcome_analysis: Lamar Health, a Winter 2021 company, has grown into workflow software used by what it says are the top ten specialty pharmacies, reporting 5.5 billion dollars of medications processed and named customers such as CloudRx and NuFactor. Growth appears largely capital light, with no priced round found after the YC seed, and the traction claims are company reported. It faces well funded prior authorization competitors, so the outcome is still open.

name: Lariat Data
tags: Machine Learning; Big Data; Data Engineering
one_liner: Observability for Data Engineering Teams
long_description:
Lariat is a Continuous Data Quality monitoring platform to discover data bugs before your consumers do. Ensure data products don’t break even as business logic, input data and infrastructure change.

Use Lariat to define and then automatically extract, store and visualize data quality metrics on raw event-level data through to delivered data products.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Laudable
one_liner: App for B2B companies to find customer stories and advocates
long_description: Laudable finds happy customers and their success stories hiding in your existing data - like call recordings, NPS, salesforce logs - and auto-generates case study content.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; United States; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
