name: Milky Way AI
one_liner: Mobile app for CPG brands to connect to millions of stores globally
long_description:
We help CPG brands to understand how their products are being displayed, priced and what are their competitors are doing across millions of physical stores in real time with our computer vision powered mobile app. 

Each year these brands spend $500 bn annually buying prime retail shelf space to influence customer purchasing decisions, but they have no easy way to audit it. 

Our mobile app reduces the time of these audits by 10x and cost by 3x.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote

name: MindFi
tags: Machine Learning; Mental Health Tech; B2B; HR Tech; Health & Wellness
one_liner: Transforming Mental Health for Corporate Asia
long_description: MindFi is an app that reduces burnout and improves mental health for employees. We sell to companies in Asia such as Deutsche Bank, KPMG, PatSnap, Visa. The team is headquartered in Singapore and consists of Bjorn, (ex-Zendesk product manager), psychologist Anita Sadasivan (UMich alum, ex-Raffles Hospital), Leon 2X startup founder with 2 exits and Gangeshwar, an award-winning AI engineer.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Employers in Asia Pacific buying employee mental wellness benefits
problem: Corporate Asia has high burnout and low usage of traditional employee assistance programs. MindFi offers an app with therapy, coaching, self-help and HR analytics, localized across languages.
business_model: B2B pay-per-use and custom budget contracts with employers
product_category: Workplace mental health and wellness platform
founder_names: Bjorn Lee; Gangeshwar Krishnamurthy; Leon CK Leong
market_need_then: COVID increased demand for mental wellness services; founder Bjorn Lee discussed rising demand in a KrASIA interview. Employers such as Visa, Willis Towers Watson and Patsnap signed on.
outcome_analysis: MindFi joined YC in Summer 2021, raised a $750K pre-seed in August 2021 and a $2M seed in February 2022, and reported enterprise clients such as Visa and Willis Towers Watson. No later funding, layoffs, acquisition or shutdown was found, so the company appears to be a small active startup that has not announced a larger round. Competitor Intellect raised a $10M Series A months later, a sign the segment was crowded and well funded.

name: MindPortal
one_liner: Thought-to-Language AI Models
long_description: MindPortal is a pioneering AI research company advancing human-AI interaction by enabling people to communicate with computers and AI assistants purely through thought. As an AI company, we focus exclusively on model development rather than hardware. Our models are designed to be general-purpose, adaptable across a wide range of applications. Our flagship development, MindSpeech, is the first supervised AI model to translate imagined speech into text, enabling direct thought-to-language communication. MindSpeech has earned endorsements from leading experts, including Neuralink's former technical strategy head and DARPA’s N3 program lead scientist. Our thought-to-language AI models have the potential for transformative applications in fields such as healthcare, education, and VR/AR and our work has been featured in major publications such as Forbes, The Times, The Telegraph, and Business Insider. MindPortal has over 11 patents filed in the field and is backed by prominent investors such as Y Combinator.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Mindee
tags: Deep Learning; Developer Tools; Automation; AI; APIs
one_liner: AI Document Understanding API
long_description:
Documents are everywhere. Through all industries, understanding their content is a critical step of many processes that software builders throughout the globe want to automate.

We focus on the science, the AI, the deep learning to give these builders the one API they need to automate the understanding of documents and give their software human-like superpowers.

Based on three pillars:
- A product: a universal self-service platform where builders can train their own models
- A catalog of use-cases: We push critical use cases to the limits of human performances in critical markets such as Accounting software, AP Automation, Expense Management, KYC and many others
- A internal capability to make tailor-made AI: We answer to specific needs from large customers that needs a custom AI of their own to handle their use cases
all_locations: Paris, Île-de-France, France; San Francisco, CA, USA; London, England, United Kingdom
regions: France; United States of America; United Kingdom; Europe; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software companies and developers who need to extract data from documents such as invoices, receipts and IDs
problem: Developers building accounting, expense and KYC software need reliable document parsing but lack the AI capacity to build it. Mindee provides APIs and trainable models.
business_model: Usage-based API plus custom AI work for large customers
product_category: AI document understanding API
market_need_then: Documents are everywhere and software builders wanted to automate accounting, AP, expense and KYC workflows; in 2021 over 50 software companies used the API in production per VentureBeat.
outcome_analysis: Mindee, founded in Paris in 2018, raised a seed in 2019 and a $14M Series A in October 2021 led by GGV Capital, and says it processed over 1 billion pages in 2024. Its developer-first API and self-serve trial supported growth, while competition from cloud giants and LLM based extraction is a continuing risk. Competitor blogs claim a 2024 shift to custom OCR, which Mindee does not confirm.

name: Mindmesh
one_liner: Mindmesh is the virtual desk that puts you in control.

Mindmesh is the virtual desk that puts you in control.

regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Mindstate Design Labs
one_liner: Programmable biology company for psychoactive effect design
long_description:
Mindstate Design Labs is building the closed-loop science & engineering stack for rational psychoactive effect design.

Our molecular-experience interface links molecular biology to the human psychopharmacodynamic profile to convert informal constructs like clarity, presence, or motivation into high-dimensional design targets.

Our clinical program is a sequence of human demonstrations that psychoactive effects can be decomposed, recombined, and synthesized. The first controlled study decomposed hallucinations from the broader hallucinogen profile; the next is designed to selectively upregulate aesthetic salience to treat anhedonia in major depressive disorder.

We’re progressively digitizing the molecular interface through which biology shapes what intelligence wants.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharma partners and patients with neuropsychiatric conditions such as depression and anhedonia (future drug buyers)
problem: Psychedelics have therapeutic promise but come with hallucinations. Mindstate aims to decompose and recombine psychoactive effects to design drugs that deliver therapeutic effects without hallucinations.
business_model: Drug development, preclinical and clinical programs aimed at licensing or commercializing therapeutics
product_category: Biotech, psychedelic-inspired therapeutics
market_need_then: Depression and related disorders have large unmet need and psychedelic funding surged in 2021; hallucinations limit use of classic psychedelics.
outcome_analysis: Mindstate raised an $11.5M seed in February 2022 led by Initialized Capital shortly after the YC Summer 2021 batch and by 2024 and 2025 headlines described a first AI derived psychedelic heading to the clinic and an early FDA nod. A later Series A is reported only by aggregators, so progress and funding after 2022 are unverified; the company remains a preclinical or early clinical biotech whose outcome depends on trial results.

name: Mine
one_liner: The AI personal finance company.
long_description:
Mine is the personal finance app designed to help you get ahead.

Founded on the idea that financial independence begins with ownership — of your money, your momentum, and your decisions.

We make the credit-builder thousands know and love, with budgeting and spend tracking features meant to help your money be the best version of itself. We’re also the makers of MoneyGPT, the money assistant that’s got your back.

Young people today are stepping into a financial world built for someone else’s life.

We give young adults the confidence and control to take charge of their financial journey with simple tools, smart guidance, and a system that works for the path you choose.

Let’s build your future together. Get started at usemine.com

Backed by Kleiner Perkins, SV Angel, Liquid 2 Ventures, and the founders of Handshake, Postmates, Public.com, Motive and many more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Mixr

long_description: Mixr is a social platform for remote and hybrid teams; we host virtual game tournaments and an ongoing office competition.  Mixr tournaments have built-in audio/video chat, a library of fun games, ice breakers, and automatic breakout rooms - all built with the goal of being easy for managers and employees to use.  By participating in tournaments, players earn high scores and trophies which places them on the company-wide leaderboards.  Our goal is to bring companies together, boost employee engagement and help companies bolster a collaborative corporate culture.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: MobileBoost
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; B2B; No-code; AI
one_liner: AI SDET for mobile apps
long_description:
MobileBoost is an AI SDET for iOS and Android apps. An agent turns a plain-language test spec into test code, runs it on simulators and real devices, and fixes it when your app changes. Nobody on your team maintains test scripts by hand. The test code is accessible at any time if your team wants that level of access.

You can start runs from your CI pipeline with the MobileBoost GitHub Action, or let your coding agent start them over MCP while you build.

Mobile teams at Duolingo, Lyft, Wayfair, Flo Health, Noom, Compass, and Redfin use MobileBoost. Duolingo cut manual regression testing by 70%: https://blog.duolingo.com/reduced-regression-testing/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mobile app engineering and QA teams (customers include Duolingo, Lyft, Wayfair, Flo Health)
problem: Mobile end to end tests are slow to write and maintain. MobileBoost's AI agent turns plain language specs into test code, runs them on devices and repairs them when the app changes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (G2 lists a Standard plan at $799 per month)
product_category: AI mobile app test automation (GPT Driver)
market_need_then: Kitchenful targeted time poor consumers wanting cheap meal plans with automatic grocery orders. For the later testing product, Duolingo reported a 70% cut in manual regression testing.
outcome_analysis: The company went through YC in Summer 2021 as Kitchenful, raised about $1.9M in October 2021, then pivoted into AI mobile test automation, with GPT Driver first shipped around April 2023. It now lists customers such as Duolingo, Lyft and Wayfair. No announced round after 2021 was found, so the pivot succeeded commercially on customer evidence while funding remains unverified.

name: ModernLoop
tags: B2B; Recruiting; Productivity; HR Tech; Remote Work
one_liner: ModernLoop helps teams automate and streamline recruiting operations
long_description:
ModernLoop helps every company automate and streamline recruiting operations to deliver the best candidate experience. In 2022, the Department of Labor estimates there is a global talent shortage of 40 million workers, and that number is expected to grow to over 85 million by 2030. In order for companies to win the war for talent, they need to provide a best-in-class candidate experience to recruit top talent, and our product aims at doing just that!

Our founders Lydia Han (CEO) and Chris Triolo (CTO) both founded ModernLoop in December of 2020 after they saw the challenges recruiting teams had when it came to coordinating hundreds of interviews across various teams, all while making sure both hiring managers and candidates had the best experience possible. After spending 15+ combined years at companies like Facebook, Slack, Brex and Salesforce, they understood what it took to enable talent teams do their best work, and are building a product to scale alongside them as they grow.

We created ModernLoop to serve companies of all sizes in every industry to help Talent teams interview candidates quicker, easier, and enhance productivity of teams as they continue their search for top talent!
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; San Mateo, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Talent acquisition and recruiting operations teams at tech companies
problem: Coordinating many interviews across teams is manual and slow for recruiters, harming candidate experience. ModernLoop automates scheduling and interview logistics.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Recruiting operations and interview scheduling software
market_need_then: The founders cited coordinating hundreds of interviews across teams as painful at Facebook, Slack and Brex; they also cited a labor shortage in 2022 trade framing.
outcome_analysis: ModernLoop was founded in December 2020, joined YC in Winter 2021, raised a $3.3M seed in October 2021 and a $9M Series A led by Accel in August 2022, with customers such as Instacart, Brex and Ramp on its site. No later round, layoffs or exit was found, and it appears active in 2026 as a small Series A stage company.

name: Moichor
one_liner: AI Powered Animal Diagnostics
long_description: Leveraging AI to provide veterinarians with more accurate and affordable diagnostics.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Veterinary clinics and reference labs needing fast hematology and cytology reads
problem: Veterinarians wait on slow or costly lab diagnostics. Moichor uses AI and computer vision, with pathologists in the loop, to provide preliminary results in as little as 15 minutes.
business_model: Diagnostics service and platform sold to veterinary practices, with distribution partnerships
product_category: AI veterinary diagnostics
founder_names: Shevy Karbasi; Matthew Chen; Thanh Le
competitors_at_founding: IDEXX SediVue Dx; Zoetis Vetscan Imagyst
market_need_then: Vet clinics rely on outside labs for cytology and hematology with delays and cost; the YC pitch is more accurate and affordable diagnostics.
outcome_analysis: Moichor joined YC in Winter 2021, raised about $4M seed led by Neotribe Ventures, built the Pathview AI diagnostics product, and by February 2026 had a national distribution agreement with Zomedica. It is still active with about 29 staff. Later funding is unconfirmed, and strong incumbents in veterinary diagnostics remain the main risk.

name: Momo Medical
one_liner: We help nurses in nursing homes to be 30% more effective
long_description:
We go to nursing homes, and we put an internet-connected bed sensor underneath all their beds. Our app gives nurses valuable insights and an overview of all their residents. We reduce fall incidents and bedsores while improving evening and night shift productivity by over 30%. 

Momo Medical solves the biggest problem affecting nursing homes, staff shortages while increasing the quality of care.
all_locations: Delft, ZH, Netherlands; San Francisco, CA, USA
regions: Netherlands; United States of America; Europe; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Nursing homes and memory care facilities (mainly Dutch, later US and Canadian) that buy bed sensors plus an app subscription for nursing staff
problem: Nursing homes are short of staff and rely on walkie-talkies and sensors with many false alarms, so night shifts are stressful and falls and bedsores happen.
business_model: Hardware sensor plus B2B SaaS subscription per bed
product_category: IoT bed sensor and care-team app for elderly care
market_need_then: Staff shortages in nursing homes and high false alarm rates in existing sensors, stated by the company; Vilans is cited by a profile as estimating hours saved per day for a 90-resident home.
outcome_analysis: Momo Medical is still operating and raised a reported 6.5 million euro round led by the pension fund investor PGGM in September 2024, years after YC Summer 2021. Its founder had direct nursing home night shift experience, which fits the pain it targets. The company has reached many Dutch care organizations and now lists offices abroad, but the funding history before 2024 and revenue are not public in sources found.

name: Monet

long_description: Monet provides Instant cash-advances to employees in Latin America. We are a mobile app available to any employee with a recurring income and a bank account.

target_customer: Employees and informal workers in Colombia with recurring income and a bank account who want small advances or short loans
problem: Workers in Colombia run short of cash before payday and often turn to costly informal lenders known as gota a gota, while banks serve them poorly.
business_model: Consumer lending with fixed service fees rather than interest, funded by equity and warehouse credit lines
product_category: Salary advance and small-ticket consumer lending app

competitors_at_founding: Bancolombia; Banco de Bogota; BBVA Colombia

It moved from employer-sold advances to a direct-to-user app, scaled loans to hundreds of thousands of users and won a Bancolombia partnership, and now plans Mexico entry. Public funding between YC in 2021 and 2025 is not documented in sources found.

name: Mono
one_liner: Plaid for Africa, but better.
long_description: We allow companies to access data from their customers bank accounts and allow them to debit money from these same bank accounts.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: African fintechs, lenders and digital businesses that need customer bank data, account verification and direct debit
problem: African fintechs lacked a reliable API to read customer bank account data and debit accounts, which Plaid does in the US.
business_model: Usage-based API fees for financial data, bank payments and identity verification
product_category: Open banking API
market_need_then: Nigerian lending and personal finance apps needed bank data to underwrite and verify users, and the 2021 TechCabal coverage described API fintech as a rising wave.
outcome_analysis: Mono pitched itself as Plaid for Africa, raised a 2 million dollar seed and then a 15 million dollar Series A led by Tiger Global in October 2021, and claims 8 million linked accounts. Flutterwave acquired it in January 2026 in an all stock deal reported at 25 to 40 million dollars, below the Series A scale of funding, while rival Okra shut down. Regulation and Nigeria's open banking framework in 2025 were tailwinds.

name: Monto
one_liner: Salary on-demand platform for Latin America
long_description: Through our platform employees of our affiliated companies can access their earned wages on-demand for a low fixed fee.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mexican employers (HR and finance buyers) who offer earned wage access and other benefits to their staff
problem: Hourly and salaried workers in Mexico need cash before payday and often turn to costly informal credit. Employers want a benefit that improves retention without cost to them.
business_model: B2B SaaS and fees: employees pay a low fixed fee per on-demand salary withdrawal, employers reimburse Monto at the end of the pay period; later expanded to a benefits marketplace with modules
product_category: Earned wage access and employee benefits platform
market_need_then: Large informal and underbanked workforce in Mexico, high cost of payday style credit, and a visible wave of earned wage access startups (Minu 2019 seed, 14M USD Series A in 2021) showed employer and worker demand.
outcome_analysis: Monto is still active with a team of about 13 and claims 400,000 employees across client companies. It raised a small pre-seed and a 1M USD seed in December 2021, far below Minu's 14M and later 30M raises, and has broadened from wage access into a benefits suite. Growth looks capital light and employer driven; the lack of larger rounds leaves the outcome open.

name: Moonshot Brands
one_liner: Buy and grow profitable e-commerce companies selling on Amazon and DTC
long_description: Moonshot Brands is building the world’s largest - next-generation CPG (Consumer Product Goods) e-commerce company. We look for profitable e-commerce companies on Amazon or selling DTC on Shopify, purchase them from the founders giving them liquidity for their biggest asset, then turbocharge the growth with our proprietary data-driven technology platform and team. We scale e-commerce brands globally.

name: Moonvalley

regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Morada Uno

long_description: We screen, collect and insure residential leases; allowing brokers and landlords to close more deals with less work, and solving the biggest pain point for tenants- needing a guarantor with a property to co-sign the lease.

It is still active and expanding to more cities, but growth numbers are company statements.

name: Moving Parts
one_liner: Delightful components for iOS.
long_description:
Moving Parts is a library of components for iOS. Everything your designers and engineers are building that isn’t unique to your app, we can do better and cheaper.

We're building high-level SwiftUI components that plug right into your application, made to solve real-world problems when designing and building a native mobile app.

Our components are also highly styleable and take care of responsiveness, localization, accessibility, and follow all platform best practices around dark mode, dynamic font size etc.
regions: Germany; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote

Press and insider accounts say it scaled production before resolving technical problems and relied heavily on a few early customers, while the company cited funding and investor challenges; the exact cause is only partly public.

name: My NextDerma
one_liner: Dermatology telehealth app for LatAm
long_description:
Dermatologist 👩🏻‍⚕️ virtual clinic in LATAM, with great dermatologists that consult, prescribe and send treatment to your doorstep
In 🇲🇽 Mexico 8 out of 10 teenagers have acne, and there is only a ratio of 1 Dermatologist 👨🏽‍⚕️ per 50,000 🌎 population.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Patients in Mexico, especially teens with acne, who pay for video dermatology consultations, prescriptions and skincare products
problem: Mexico has very few dermatologists (the company cites one per 50,000 people), so patients wait long or go untreated.

product_category: Dermatology telehealth app and online pharmacy for Latin America
founder_names: Saul Armando Lepe Soltero; Luis Alberto Guevara Mendoza; Enrique Ibarra
market_need_then: Shortage of dermatologists in Mexico and high teen acne prevalence, as stated by the company on its YC page, plus pandemic-era telemedicine adoption.
outcome_analysis: My NextDerma is listed as active and its website was selling dermatology services and products in 2026, but little independent coverage exists after its 2021 YC batch. Aggregators suggest a very small seed, so it appears to have stayed small and bootstrapped-sized rather than scaling. The cause of limited growth is not public.

name: Mystic
tags: AIOps; Developer Tools; Machine Learning; AI
one_liner: Low latency API to run and deploy ML models
long_description:
Mystic’s platform allows companies to easily and reliably deploy ML models on our serverless cloud or on their own infrastructure without requiring a team of MLOps engineers. With our Python SDK, data-scientists immediately get an endpoint from their own model, or any open-source models.
Once uploaded, our platform handles routing, multi-cloud scaling, caching, GPU optimization and other features to provide the ultimate ML inference platform.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Mythia

name: Nano Technologies
one_liner: Payroll app to pay workers daily for retailers & manufacturers in SEA
long_description:
Nano is an income streaming app which pays workers daily instead of monthly for retailers and manufacturers in South East Asia. 

This is essential because these employers compete for workers with the gig economy, which pays daily with a flexible work schedule. 

Nano integrates seamlessly with any HRM/Attendance Software from employers, helping them save turnover costs and build a more engaged and productive workforce.
regions: Vietnam; Southeast Asia
target_customer: Retailers and manufacturers in Southeast Asia that need to attract and keep hourly workers, and those workers
problem: Gig platforms pay daily while traditional employers pay monthly, raising turnover. Nano lets workers draw earned pay daily.
business_model: B2B2C earned wage access, employer integration with HR and attendance systems
product_category: Earned wage access fintech
market_need_then: Employers competed with the gig economy that pays daily, and Vietnam had no specific earned wage regulation, per a market overview.
outcome_analysis: Nano raised a $3M seed in May 2021 after YC W21 and a reported $6.4M round in August 2022, with a CEO who ran Uber Vietnam and ZaloPay. It claims customers like GS25 and Annam Gourmet and remains active, though round labels and total raised vary across outlets, so the long term outcome is open.

name: Nasdisc
one_liner: A marketplace for vinyl, cassettes and cds
long_description:
Nasdisc is a marketplace for the $4B worth of records purchased every year.

The vinyl market has seen exponential growth in the past decade - the first 6 months of this year has already seen an increase of 108% in sales. Our platform takes a 12% cut, making this a $400mm opportunity that is more than doubling every year.

Pressing plants are backed up years out, bots buy limited releases in seconds, and record prices are skyrocketing in both retail and aftermarket sales. Despite this growth, the only dedicated marketplace is difficult to use, doesn’t process transactions, yet facilitates over $600mm in vinyl exchanges per year. 

This is why I finally decided to quit my job at Google and recruit my best friends from college to fix it. We’re all software engineers and have been passionate about music and vinyl since we were kids, and have $50k in records ourselves.

We started building a marketplace in July and launched our website 4 weeks ago. We now have $1k / week in sales, and $50k in listings.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Vinyl, cassette and CD collectors buying and selling records online, with sellers paying a 12 percent fee
problem: Record collectors faced a hard to use dominant marketplace that does not process transactions, with limited drops, bots and rising prices.
business_model: Marketplace take rate of 12 percent
product_category: Consumer marketplace for physical music
founder_names: Cam Korzecke; Simeon Goolsby; Christian White
market_need_then: Founders cited vinyl sales growth of 108 percent in the first half of 2021, pressing plant backlogs and bots buying limited releases; these are founder claims.
outcome_analysis: Nasdisc launched a vinyl, cassette and CD marketplace in mid 2021 and claimed 1 thousand dollars a week in sales and 50 thousand dollars of listings at the YC application. YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date, price or funding is public, and no coverage of the deal or of any shutdown was found, so the outcome and its cause are not public.

name: Nash
one_liner: Nash is the digital logistics infrastructure for commerce
long_description:
Last mile is a $500B industry powering digital commerce but managed largely with self managed API integrations. Nash approaches last mile orchestration with information completeness solutions from checkout, courier management, customer engagement, and post-purchase experience. Doing this enables merchants and customers to capture immense efficiencies, drive better customer experience, reliability and business outcomes.
We are working towards a mission of processing a double digit percentage of every physical last-mile transaction. We achieve this by providing top of the market modules for each step of the customer journey and leveraging the network effects from having more information that allows traditional competitors to collaborate. It’s a big mission, but we are already seeing strong market pull as we are already serving some of the largest retailers in the world like Walmart, 7-Eleven and Woolworths.
Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and has raised funding from top investors, including Y-Combinator and a16z, to build the world’s best logistics infrastructure platform. We are based in SF.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Merchants, restaurants, retailers and marketplaces that need same-day local delivery without running their own fleet
problem: Businesses wanting local delivery must integrate many courier networks and handle late or missing deliveries one by one.
business_model: Usage-based delivery orchestration API and software, with a courier network
product_category: Last-mile delivery orchestration platform
market_need_then: Post-pandemic growth of local delivery and small businesses wanting to match Amazon speed, per a16z (July 2022).
outcome_analysis: Nash raised an a16z-led 7.8 million dollar seed in late 2021 and a 20 million dollar Series A in July 2022, totaling 27.8 million dollars, and claimed 52 percent average month-over-month revenue growth over the prior year. It is still operating and repositioned to AI logistics by 2026. No later round was found, so growth since 2022 is unverified.

name: Navattic

Total funding is about 4 to 6 million dollars depending on aggregator, so it grew capital-efficiently or is still at an early stage. Revenue is not public.

name: Neodocs
tags: Consumer Health Services; Medical Devices; AI
one_liner: Instant lab tests on your smartphone
long_description:
Neodocs lets you perform instant lab tests on your smartphone. Our users are health optimizers and athletes who want to improve key nutritional markers for better performance.

You simply collect your sample, take a picture, and results are instantly generated.


We are the perfect team to build this. Anurag is a 3-time medical entrepreneur who’s built medical devices, Pratik has worked on AI/ML models for leading US banks, and  Nikunj comes from a consulting background at Bain & Co.

We’re building your personal lab on your phone.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Consumers and doctors in India buying smartphone-read at-home test kits such as urine kidney and UTI cards
problem: Routine lab tests are slow and inaccessible in India; Neodocs lets a user collect a sample, photograph a test card and get results instantly.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer and doctor-channel sales of test cards and kits read by a smartphone app
product_category: Smartphone-based point-of-care diagnostics
founder_names: Nikunj Malpani; Pratik Lodha; Anurag Meena
market_need_then: Limited access to routine diagnostics in India and growth of at-home testing after the pandemic; the company reports over 200,000 test cards sold by 2024.
outcome_analysis: Neodocs raised a pre-seed in August 2021 from YC, 9Unicorns and Titan Capital, then a roughly 2 million dollar seed in February 2024 led by Omidyar Network India. It reports 200,000 test cards sold and over 4,000 doctors, and its store was live in 2026. No Series A was found, and the long gap between rounds means growth has been slow or capital-light.

name: Neverland
one_liner: The first online home garden and lawn marketplace
long_description: Neverland is the first marketplace that connect buyers of everything needed for indoor and outdoor gardening with the 24,000 shops across the US. Neverland is taking this offline category online starting with this $26B market.

name: NextPay
tags: Banking as a Service; Fintech; B2B
one_liner: The digital bank for small businesses in the Philippines.
long_description:
NextPay is a digital bank for small businesses and entrepreneurs in The Philippines. They use us to send invoices, collect payments, do payroll, and pay their bills.

NextPay is the best alternative to bank accounts for small businesses and entrepreneurs in the Philippines. We help them similarly to how Brex helps companies in the US, but in a way that is more locally nuanced. We manage their finances and remove the steep barriers that Filipino banks and financial institutions typically require; no setup fees, maintaining balances, or ridiculous requirements. 

View the full context on our Launch Bookface post: 
https://bookface.ycombinator.com/posts/51999
regions: Philippines; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small businesses and entrepreneurs in the Philippines that need invoicing, payments, payroll and bill payment; later platforms and companies needing payouts
problem: Filipino banks impose setup fees, minimum balances and heavy requirements on small businesses, which pushes them toward cash and informal tools for invoicing, collecting and paying.
business_model: Fintech payments and payouts, fees on transactions and disbursements; later an API for platforms using its BSP operator of payment system registration
product_category: SMB digital banking, then payment and disbursement infrastructure
market_need_then: Bank accounts for small businesses in the Philippines were hard to open and costly per the YC description, and a Maya commissioned study (secondary, self interested) claimed 94 percent of SME transactions were in cash.
outcome_analysis: NextPay raised a 125 thousand dollar YC investment in 2021 and a 1.6 million dollar seed round in July 2021 from regional and local investors. No later round was found. It narrowed its scope from a broad SMB bank substitute to disbursements and a BSP regulated payouts API, which suggests the broader banking offer faced strong competition from wallets and digital banks. It remains active with about 25 staff per YC.

name: Nexus

long_description: Nexus offers a unified checking and investment account. Your full balance is invested to get market returns, all while retaining instant access to cash even when the markets are closed. The product appears to have shifted from a clinician facing layer to consumer programs in the UK. The story is unclear, so factors are left empty rather than guessed.

name: Novatr
one_liner: Online cohort based courses for architects, engineers and designers…
long_description:
Novatr (YC S21) offers online cohort-based courses for architects, engineers and designers in the AEC industry to advance their professional growth. We serve learners from 45+ countries including India, MENA, USA, Europe, and SEA. Our courses are delivered by professionals from global firms like Autodesk, BIG, Google, UNStudio, AECOM, and graduates are placed at top-tier architecture firms, construction companies and real estate companies.

Project-based learning and peer-to-peer interaction in cohort makes learning enriching and increases the completion rates to 84%. Learners work in groups of 2-6 on live projects and create significant outputs from scratch.

The company is led by alumni of SPA Delhi and IIT Madras.
all_locations: Gurugram, HR, India; Delhi, DL, India
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Architects, engineers and construction professionals (AEC) in India and abroad paying for cohort based upskilling courses
problem: AEC professionals lack practical training in BIM, computational design and related tools, and a masters degree is expensive.
business_model: Paid online cohort-based courses and career programs
product_category: Edtech for architecture, engineering and construction
founder_names: Harkunwar Singh; Vipanchi Handa; Chaithanya Murali; Mehul Kumar
market_need_then: Novatr positions its courses at about one tenth the cost of a masters in architecture (company claim); demand evidence beyond that is not independently sourced.
outcome_analysis: Novatr, formerly Oneistox, raised only about 1.3 million dollars across a 2021 pre-seed and an April 2023 seed round, yet grew to a team of 180 per its YC page and claims learners in 45 countries and 84 percent course completion. Founders who are architects serving their own profession fit the niche; the story is capital light, but revenue figures are not independently verified.

Funding is unknown beyond aggregator claims of roughly $125K, so progress cannot be judged beyond one partnership.

name: ODWEN

problem: Small Indian businesses struggle to find, compare and rent small warehouses at fair prices and to manage inventory in and out.

product_category: On-demand warehousing marketplace

name: Observa

name: OctiFi

The cause is not public; the macro downturn tag is a low confidence inference from the 2022 to 2023 BNPL pullback.

name: Odys Aviation
one_liner: Vertical takeoff and landing aircraft for major airlines
long_description: Odys Aviation (formerly Craft Aero) builds vertical take-off and landing aircraft for major airlines. We cut travel time in half on the world’s busiest routes by using city helipads and local airports.  The company founders are electric propulsion and automotive manufacturing experts who have spent their careers electrifying transportation systems at Virgin Hyperloop, GoogleX, Volvo, and Fisker Automotive. We’ve won two USAF Agility Prime contracts, have pre-orders and options for more than 1,000 aircraft.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Airlines and cargo operators (originally regional passenger routes); now defense, commercial cargo and civil markets
problem: Short regional air travel is slow because airports and helipads are underused; the company aimed to halve travel time with hybrid-electric VTOL aircraft.
business_model: Aircraft maker selling aircraft and hybrid power systems; pre-orders and Air Force contracts rather than recurring revenue
product_category: Hybrid-electric VTOL aircraft and cargo drones
market_need_then: Regional travel and cargo needs plus a push for electric aviation and US Air Force Agility Prime funding; the YC page claims pre-orders and options for over 1,000 aircraft.

The long gap between rounds and a shift to the Laila cargo drone suggest hardware capital intensity slowed progress, but the company has stayed active and is moving to flight tests.

name: Okani
one_liner: Preventive healthcare app for Latam.
long_description:
Okani is a low-cost wellness membership for the 50M Mexicans that spend 25B on healthcare out of pocket. 

We become patients' first point of contact with the healthcare system by providing digital primary care through chat and an app, then orchestrate the delivery of secondary healthcare with physicians, labs, pharmacies and clinics. 

We're founded by a team of 3 engineers and a doctor with a masters in clinical care. Pepe previously sold a startup to Cabify and ran engineering with Romario for Nubank's first international market.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Low and middle income Mexican consumers who pay for healthcare out of pocket and subscribe to a monthly wellness membership
problem: Mexicans without insurance spend heavily out of pocket and have no first point of contact for primary care, so care is fragmented and mostly reactive.
business_model: consumer subscription membership for digital primary care, with orchestrated referrals to labs, pharmacies and clinics
product_category: digital primary care membership (Mexico)
market_need_then: The YC description cites 50M Mexicans spending about 25B on healthcare out of pocket, which indicates large unmet primary care demand at the time of the Summer 2021 batch. This is a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Okani is listed as active and early stage with a three person team after the Summer 2021 batch. The founder has a record of three earlier exits and Nubank engineering experience, and the team includes a clinician, which fits the product. No public funding round, acquisition, layoffs or shutdown was found, so the long term outcome cannot be judged from public sources.

name: OlaClick
one_liner: Restaurant Solution (E-commerce via WhatsApp + POS + CRM/Marketing)
long_description:
OlaClick makes it easy for mass market restaurants in Latam to create a digital menu, promote it instantly with only one click and start receiving simple food orders though WhatsApp. 

We have +40000 restaurants in Latam and we increase their sales by 40%.


contact: founders@olaclick.com
all_locations: Lima, Callao Region, Peru; Lima, Lima Province, Peru; Remote
regions: Peru; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mass market restaurants in Latin America that take orders by phone, cash and WhatsApp
problem: Most small restaurants in Latin America take orders by phone and settle in cash, and they lose margin to marketplaces that charge commissions.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for restaurants (digital menu, WhatsApp ordering, POS, CRM) with commission free orders
product_category: restaurant ordering and POS software
founder_names: Carol Riboud; Ulysse Lichtle; Jose Rico
market_need_then: TechCrunch (2022) reports more than 80 percent of food delivery orders in Latin America were still made by phone and paid in cash, and the company positioned commission free WhatsApp ordering against marketplace fees.
outcome_analysis: OlaClick grew from a Winter 2021 YC company to a restaurant platform reporting 45,000 plus restaurants and over 1 million orders a month by May 2022, with a seed round led by Gradient Ventures and backing from Meta and Delivery Hero. It remains active and now sells a POS, chatbot and invoicing suite in Brazil and beyond. Its edge was commission free WhatsApp ordering for restaurants ignored by marketplaces. No later round, acquisition or layoff was found.

name: Ollama
one_liner: Get up and running with large language models.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and teams that want to run open weight language models locally or on hosted GPUs, with a growing paid cloud tier
problem: Running open language models locally required complex setup of weights, runtimes and hardware drivers. Ollama packages this behind a one command install.
business_model: free open source local runner, with paid subscription cloud service billed by GPU time
product_category: developer tools, local LLM runtime
market_need_then: Open weight models such as Llama 2 (mid 2023) created demand to run models locally for privacy and cost. The company's Show HN in July 2023 and Docker image in October 2023 show early developer pull.
outcome_analysis: Ollama launched publicly in mid 2023 as open weight models took off, and it grew through free open source distribution into nearly 9 million users. Founders with Docker experience packaged local models like containers, then added a paid cloud tier, raising a Series A led by Benchmark and a 65M Series B in July 2026 for 88M total. The remaining risks are monetization pushback and competition from other local runners.

name: OneSchema
one_liner: The AI Cowork for big data
long_description: OneSchema Studio brings AI Cowork into your private cloud. Teams can clean and validate massive datasets at 1,000x the scale of generic AI tools - data never leaves your network, you pick the AI model, and proven work becomes a skill your whole team can reuse. It self-hosts natively on AWS, Azure, or GCP, gives you granular, role-based control over who can touch what data, and connects directly to the systems you already run - from Salesforce and Workday to SAP and Snowflake.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B software companies that need customers to import messy CSV and spreadsheet data
problem: Product teams spend months building and maintaining CSV importers instead of core product.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an embeddable importer and file automation
product_category: Developer infrastructure, data import

outcome_analysis: OneSchema launched an embeddable CSV importer in July 2021 and raised a 6.3 million dollar round in November 2022 led by General Catalyst with Sequoia and YC. OSK is a preferred restaurant partner due to its innovative hyper scalable model. Consumers can mix & match multiple cuisines in a single order for dine in, pick up or delivery.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Onebrief
one_liner: Onebrief makes military headquarters run seamlessly
long_description:
Virtually everything in the military requires a plan—from everyday operations to war-time missions. With a rigorous process, many stakeholders, and rudimentary software (PowerPoint!!), planning is very slow. 

Onebrief is a collaborative software designed to make military planning fast. It turns every input into reusable building blocks and automatically keeps all planning artifacts in sync.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Military headquarters and staffs (US Army, Air Force, Marine Corps, NATO allies) that plan operations
problem: Military staffs plan with slide decks and email, which is slow and keeps plans out of sync. Onebrief turns inputs into reusable building blocks and keeps planning products synchronized.
business_model: B2G enterprise SaaS sold through defense contracts
product_category: collaborative military planning software
market_need_then: The YC description says military planning relies on PowerPoint and slow multi stakeholder processes. Company careers pages say slide workflows without version control tie up staffs for weeks or months.
outcome_analysis: Onebrief was founded in 2019 by a former Army officer and joined YC in Summer 2021. It won Army and Air Force work and raised a Series B in 2024, a Series C in January 2025 at 650M, a 20M extension at 1.1B in June 2025 and a 200M Series D at 2.15B in January 2026 while buying Battle Road Digital. Founder domain insight, accreditation and a defense AI funding wave drove the growth.

name: Onfolk
one_liner: Gusto for the UK
long_description:
We make it easy for growing teams to set up and run their payroll & HR (instead of a mess of spreadsheets, poorly integrated tools, and emails with accountants).

- 1 min to run payroll
- 2 mins to onboard new starters
- Hands-off pension & accounting integrations
- Centralised employee info, time-off, and reporting

Our team are software engineers who spent 4 years scaling Monzo from 400k to 6m customers. While at Monzo we repeatedly got paid incorrectly by their poor payroll providers. So we decided to build the product that they should have used from day 1.

We’ve gained certification as a payroll software from the UK government.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: UK small and growing businesses running payroll and HR
problem: UK payroll providers paid the founders incorrectly at Monzo; small teams wanted fast, accurate payroll with HR records.
business_model: B2B SaaS per-employee subscription (listed from 5 pounds per month)
product_category: UK payroll and HR software
founder_names: Naz Malik; Charlie Thomas; Michael Colley
market_need_then: Founders were repeatedly paid incorrectly by Monzo's payroll providers; no market spend figures found.
outcome_analysis: Onfolk was a UK payroll and HR startup built by ex Monzo engineers who had suffered payroll errors themselves. It went through YC Summer 2021, raised only a small reported pre-seed, and was acquired by Tide, which closed on 18 October 2024 for an undisclosed price. The exit fits an acquirer wanting payroll inside its small business app.

name: Onsite Pro
one_liner: Revolutionizing digital selling within HVAC
long_description: We make contractor proposal creation as simple as checking out of e-commerce. We equip HVAC distributors (who sell HVAC equipment to contractors) with digital catalogs preloaded with pricing, product details, and templates that allow contractors to create a professional proposal in under 10 minutes and sell in-person.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Ontop
one_liner: Simplifying hiring and payments for the global workforce
long_description: Ontop allows companies to hire global workers and gives those workers access to a Global Financial Account.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Companies hiring remote contractors worldwide, and the freelancers they pay, mostly in Latin America and emerging markets
problem: Companies struggle to hire, contract and pay workers abroad, and workers face slow, expensive cross border payments and limited banking access.
business_model: SaaS fee per worker (priced at 29 USD per month per employee plus 1 percent of payment in Oct 2021, 49 USD per month contractor plan later) plus payment and wallet fees
product_category: global hiring, contractor payments and payroll fintech
founder_names: Santiago Aparicio; Julian Torres; Jaime Abella

outcome_analysis: Ontop joined YC in Winter 2021 as remote hiring boomed and raised a 20M Series A from Tiger Global and Point72 in October 2021, claiming 40 percent monthly growth and a team of about 200. The company is listed as active with 186 people. Well funded rivals such as Deel were ahead, so growth depended on a Latin America focus and the wallet product. Later rounds are unclear in sources.

name: OpenCode
one_liner: The open source AI coding agent
long_description: Built by Anomaly, makers of sst.dev, opennext.js.org, openauth.js.org, models.dev, and more.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers: first AWS serverless teams using SST, now individual developers and teams using an open source AI coding agent
problem: At YC, building serverless applications on AWS was hard to set up and test. The company later moved to open source AI coding agents that work with any model provider.
business_model: open source with paid subscriptions and console (OpenCode Go from 10 USD per month, low cost model subscriptions, team tools); earlier SST Console from 20 USD per month per workspace
product_category: developer tools, serverless framework then AI coding agent
market_need_then: SST's own guide (Serverless Framework vs SST) says developers found Serverless Framework painful, and the 2021 seed announcement states demand for easier serverless apps. Dated 2021 competitor pages were not retrieved.
outcome_analysis: The YC W21 company was Serverless Stack (SST), an open source AWS framework that raised a 1M seed from Greylock, SV Angel and YC in July 2021. The same team later built OpenCode, an open source coding agent that press reports at over 13 million monthly users. Press attributes part of the growth to Anthropic limiting subscription use. A security incident and free usage controversy are reported. Later funding was not found, so the company may be bootstrapped or undisclosed.

name: Openlayer
tags: AIOps; Developer Tools; Generative AI; Machine Learning; AI
one_liner: The fastest way to ship airtight AI
long_description: Openlayer is the governance platform for AI applications.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Enterprise ML and AI teams, especially in regulated industries, that need to test, monitor and govern models and LLM applications
problem: Teams ship ML models and later LLM applications without reliable testing, so failures reach production. Openlayer provides tests that run on each commit and on live data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a free basic plan and enterprise contracts
product_category: AI evaluation, observability and governance platform
founder_names: Gabriel Bayomi Tinoco Kalejaiye; Vikas Nair; Rishab Ramanathan

outcome_analysis: Openlayer started as Unbox in the Summer 2021 batch with ML testing, raised a 4.8M seed in May 2023 as LLM applications emerged, and a 14.5M Series A in May 2025. Success depends on standing out from many observability vendors, and no exit or distress signal was found.

name: Opkit
tags: SaaS; Health Tech; Digital Health; Healthcare; Conversational AI
one_liner: AI phone calls for the US healthcare industry
long_description: Opkit uses AI to automate routine phone calls for medical practices, telehealth companies, and other leading healthcare provider organizations. Opkit's AI agent is capable of executing a wide-range of non-clinical phone call tasks, including Verification of Benefits, patient intake, and appointment scheduling, without human intervention. Opkit is HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2 Type 2 certified.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Telehealth companies and medical practices needing insurance verification and routine phone work
problem: Verifying patient insurance benefits and handling routine non-clinical phone calls is manual, slow and costly for providers.
business_model: B2B SaaS / AI call-center service
product_category: Healthcare administration AI (insurance verification, voice agents)
market_need_then: At launch in March 2023 coverage cited telehealth adoption and large US insurance billing administration spend (Rock Health, McKinsey, Center for American Progress figures per AlleyWatch).
outcome_analysis: Opkit joined YC in S21, launched an insurance-verification product for telehealth firms in March 2023 with a roughly $1M seed, and in August 2024 pivoted to a generative-AI back-office call center for medical practices. It never announced a Series A. In November 2024 directory profiles (CB Insights and others) report an acqui-hire by 11x, and the founder's own post is reported to say the platform would be wound down. No cause is stated by the founders in the sources I could open, so the failure factors are inferred from the timeline: about 18 months after launch and no follow-on round, followed by a team-only exit.

name: Orbillion Bio
one_liner: Tasty and scalable cultivated meat at price parity
long_description:
Intro to Orbillion Bio: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wAf21WXxnhw (Slush Nov 2024)

Orbillion is making cultivated beef at scale using advanced computational models to rapidly optimize the bioprocess and reduce cost. With Orbillion’s proprietary bioware, they can precisely control the microenvironment that the meat cells need. This supercharges cell growth without the need for GMO, serum, or expensive growth factors, enabling a cost of $4 per kg at commercial scale.


Orbillion’s technology addresses the industry's two main challenges: cost and scale-up. Its integrated bioprocess platform allows Orbillion to  produce at a commercial level  anywhere globally within two weeks in an asset-light fashion. Partnerships with two global food companies of combined $280B revenue, and a European partner have fast-tracked commercialization in the $211B ground beef market. Founders Dr. Patricia Bubner and Samet Yildirim are the only industry founders with scale-up experience in mammalian cells from the biopharma industry. Orbillion is backed by The Venture Collective, Y Combinator, At One Ventures, Venture Souq, and Hub71 among others.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Food companies and meat producers that want to make cultivated beef and need a cheaper, scalable bioprocess
problem: Cultivated meat is too expensive and hard to scale, mainly because of growth media cost and bioreactor scale-up.
business_model: Technology and platform partnerships with food companies, asset-light production licensing
product_category: Cultivated meat bioprocess platform
competitors_at_founding: Aleph Farms; Upside Foods (formerly Memphis Meats)
market_need_then: Cultivated meat funding peaked at about $989M in 2021 per AgFunder, driven by climate and animal welfare interest and the need for lower cost production.
outcome_analysis: Orbillion raised a seed in 2021 at the peak of cultivated meat funding and an additional round in 2024 that brought its total to about $15M, as the sector's funding fell sharply in 2023. Without a reported price or breakout commercial product, it was acquired by pork peer Fork & Good in October 2025 as part of sector consolidation, combining IP and production sites. The exit looks like a consolidation outcome rather than a clear win, and terms are not public.

name: Orderli
one_liner: Square for Europe
long_description:
Orderli is tableside ordering for bars and pubs in Europe. Orderli works without downloading an app, guests can scan a QR code on the table, browser the menu and order what they want. 

For the staff we provide a simple app which gives them a better overview who is ordering and control of the orders that are sent to the kitchen.

In the backend we use predictions to recommend restaurant owners what to purchase and make changes to the menu in real-time.
all_locations: Utrecht, UT, Netherlands; Amsterdam, NH, Netherlands
regions: Netherlands; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Bars, pubs, restaurants and hotels in the Netherlands and Europe
problem: Hospitality venues lose staff time and revenue taking table orders by hand, and menus are hard to change. Orderli lets guests scan a QR code, order and pay without an app.
business_model: B2B SaaS fixed monthly fee per venue with payment fees only for online payments
product_category: QR table ordering and payments for hospitality
founder_names: Dorus van den Oord; Maurits Franken; Sven van der Zee
market_need_then: Tech.eu (Aug 2021) says Orderli acquired the venue check-in app mycapa.city, which had over 650 locations, reflecting pandemic rules. NL Times (Sept 2021) reported QR menus used to combat hospitality staff shortages.
outcome_analysis: Orderli is a small Dutch QR ordering company that joined YC in Summer 2021 after four earlier rejections per a Dutch trade report. It acquired a check-in app in August 2021, raised 875K in February 2023 at a reported valuation of 9M, and remains active with a small team. No acquisition, layoffs or shutdown were found. Its fate depends on competing with POS vendors and other QR players.

name: Outfit
one_liner: DIY renovations in a box. Materials, tools, and instructions delivered
long_description:
We sell DIY home renovations in a box.

We format our architect-designed templates to a customer's space. We then buy all the materials needed on their behalf, and ship it to their door for them to build.

The experience is accompanied by an app that guides from start-to-completion of the project.

regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Output Labs

one_liner: The foundation for the next era of science

target_customer: Pharma and biotech teams (as Output Biosciences); as Output Labs, scientific R&D organizations that need models of complex systems
problem: Understanding and controlling the mechanisms behind complex biological systems for drug discovery, using AI that learns causal mechanisms rather than correlations.
business_model: Frontier AI research lab; no public pricing or revenue model found
product_category: AI foundation models for biology and drug discovery
market_need_then: In 2021 AI for drug discovery was drawing heavy investor interest and pharma was seeking better preclinical prediction. No company specific demand evidence was found.

No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found. Public funding evidence is almost absent, so the story of why it stalled or progressed cannot be told from sources.

name: PAYZE

long_description: Innovator of online transactions, helping businesses in former soviet union countries to accept payments from around the world through a single integration.

name: Pactima
one_liner: Live video signing for real-time agreements
long_description:
Pactima is a value-centric, fast-growing, and venture-backed company that’s transforming the manner in which businesses conduct transactions in our remote world.

Our flagship product, Live eSignatures<sup>TM</sup>, is a real-time solution that allows people to view and sign documents while simultaneously hosting a secured video call. This easy-to-use solution allows transactions that could only be done in-person to now be performed online.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Notaries, title and mortgage firms, law firms and businesses that sign agreements remotely
problem: Transactions that needed an in-person signing could not be done remotely with trust and identity verification.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription and per-transaction fees for eSignature and remote online notarization
product_category: eSignature and remote online notarization
market_need_then: The remote-work shift of 2020 and 2021 and temporary RON rules created demand for transactions previously done in person.
outcome_analysis: Pactima rode the remote transaction boom, raised an oversubscribed seed led by FundersClub in 2021 and built a broader eNotary and eSignature suite with compliance credentials. It was acquired by Snapdocs, announced in a founders letter dated September 1, 2026, and the product became Snapdocs RON. The price and exact round sizes are not public, so the quality of the outcome is uncertain.

name: Pagaloop
one_liner: Pay, Get Paid and Extend Cash Flow using your Credit Card as…
long_description:
Pagaloop helps business owners and persons in Latin America pay, get paid and extend cash flow using credit cards to finance expenses like rent, taxes, payroll and suppliers, via an extended network of relevant partnerships (federal/local governments, AMEX, HSBC, schools and universities, etc.). The Company provides a service in which a payment is made to a third party (that would typically not accept credit card as a payment method) in exchange for a fee of 4.7% (+ taxes). Additionally, Pagaloop offers payments in 3, 6, 9 or 12
months with an extremely accessible commission. All of those solutions without taking any underwriting risk, which remains at the issuer of the credit line.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mexican SMEs and individuals who want to pay suppliers, rent, payroll and taxes with a credit card, including payees that do not accept cards
problem: Small businesses in Mexico get little bank credit at high rates, and many payees refuse cards, so owners cannot use card credit to finance expenses.
business_model: Transaction fee on card payments to third parties (3.9% plus VAT in 2020, 4.7% plus taxes per the YC page), plus installment plans where credit risk stays with the card issuer
product_category: Fintech, B2B payments and card based working capital
founder_names: Gerardo Briones; Carlos Cruz; Luis Fernando Dosal G.; Alejandro Servín
competitors_at_founding: Citibanamex SME loans; BBVA business loans and credit cards
market_need_then: Expansión (2020-01) and Forbes Mexico (2019-09) describe SMEs with no access to credit or only very high rates, with bank products at CAT of 67% to 106%. Pagaloop reported about 1,100 users in 2020-01, up from about 300 in 2019-09.
outcome_analysis: Pagaloop grew from about 300 users in 2019-09 to about 1,100 in 2020-01, joined YC in Winter 2021 and is still active, with a G2 Fintech Fund seed in 2022-09 and an Unlimit acquiring partnership in 2024-11. Raised capital appears small compared with the 5 to 7 million dollars the founders planned in 2019, so scale is unproven. Serial founders and bank partnerships helped, but dependence on card rails limits defensibility.

name: PaletteHQ
one_liner: Manage sales commissions and sales performance
long_description:
PaletteHQ makes it easy for B2B companies to calculate sales commissions and boost sales performance.

We built a SaaS platform that non tech people can implement in a day, connect to their CRM, accounting software or ERPs, and calculate commissions automatically instead of using excel spreadsheets or BI tools.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Finance and operations teams at B2B SaaS and usage based companies that pay sales commissions
problem: Modern sales compensation plans tied to product led sales and usage pricing do not fit older tools, so companies fall back on spreadsheets or BI tools to compute commissions.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for commission calculation and sales performance
product_category: Sales compensation management software
market_need_then: The founder said in 2022 that none of the tools evaluated handled modern plans for product led sales and consumption pricing, and TechCrunch notes many firms still use spreadsheets.
outcome_analysis: PaletteHQ raised a $6M seed in 2022-05 from Bain Capital Ventures and others, about nine months after the batch, and remains active. It entered a category where CaptivateIQ and Spiff each raised $46M Series B rounds in 2021, so it must win on modern usage based plans. The founder came from Algolia's sales team. No later rounds or exit were found.

name: Palla
one_liner: P2P Cross border payments
long_description: Palla enables instant P2P payments from the US to other countries, a $65BN a year market. Sending and receiving remittances today is slow, time consuming and inconvenient for all parties, as it's a mostly cash based process. With Palla, senders in the US can do it in a few taps of their phone and receivers get their money in seconds.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Originally US senders of remittances to Latin America; now banks, fintechs and wallet providers that embed instant cross border P2P payments
problem: Sending money from the US to other countries is slow, cash based and inconvenient for senders and receivers.
business_model: B2B2C payments infrastructure: API, embeddable payment blocks and white label checkout for financial institutions, earning on transfers (fee model not stated in sources)
product_category: Cross border payments infrastructure
founder_names: Enrique Perezalonso; Andrew Mason; Gregory Piccolo
market_need_then: The YC page cites a $65B a year US to abroad P2P market; later coverage cites over $155B sent from the US to Latin America and the Caribbean in 2023. Remittance was cash heavy and slow in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Palla stayed active and raised a $14.5M Series A led by Revolution Ventures in 2025-05, almost four years after the batch, with about $15M raised in total per a spokesperson. It moved from consumer P2P remittance toward selling payment rails to banks across Latin America, which sidestepped consumer rivals like Remitly and Wise. Founders had banking and fintech experience. Growth looks steady but slow for the YC cohort.

name: Pandai
one_liner: Learning app for school students in Southeast Asia
long_description:
💡 What is Pandai?

Pandai is an app that helps students get better grades in school. 

Pandai provides gamified quizzes aligned to a specific school curriculum, from which students can learn, practice, get feedback, and diagnose their weaknesses.

🔥 Why do we build this? 

In Southeast Asia, the education system is competitive and exam-oriented. 

There is a huge demand for interventions (tutors, workbooks, and extra classes) to help students perform better in school. Pandai fills the demand with a solution that is better than the alternatives.

👨‍🏫 Who We Are

The three founders are based in Malaysia and have known each other since high school, 23 years ago. 

After we graduated (from MIT & other US colleges), we started our first education company in 2007, focusing on coaching school students in STEM subjects.

We worked closely with students (many of them from underprivileged backgrounds) and saw firsthand the impact we’ve had on them. 

We then realized that with technology, we could reach more students and bring more impact. Hence, we released Pandai in 2020. 

🚀 Present & Future

Currently, we have launched in our home ground Malaysia in 2020. 

So far, 280,000 students have completed 83 million questions on Pandai, and 92% of users have seen some improvement in their academic performance. 

We plan to expand to Southeast Asia and other emerging markets, a market of 100M+ school students. Pandai is designed to be scalable, and our content (also available in English) can be mapped to other curricula from other countries.
all_locations: Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
regions: Malaysia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Malaysian school students aged 7 to 17 and their parents, with modules for teachers; later other Southeast Asian markets
problem: In exam oriented Southeast Asia families spend heavily on tutors, workbooks and extra classes to raise grades; Pandai offers a cheaper curriculum aligned alternative.
business_model: Consumer subscription to a gamified learning app aligned to the national curriculum
product_category: K-12 edtech app
founder_names: Khairul Anwar Mohamad Zaki; Akmal Akhpah; Suhaimi Ramly
market_need_then: The YC page describes a competitive exam oriented system with large demand for tutors and workbooks; Pandai reported 280,000 students and 83 million questions by the batch, and school closures in 2020 drove remote learning demand (not sourced).
outcome_analysis: Pandai launched in 2020 in Malaysia, joined YC in Summer 2021 and raised about $2.03M of pre-seed and seed money announced in 2022-01, led by backers including Global Founders Capital and 500 Global. A 2025 BFM podcast description says over RM16 million has been raised and 1 million users reached, though these are not independently verified. Founders had long education experience and a prior coaching business, which supports a strong founder market fit.

name: Pangea.app

The best way to know if someone is a good fit is to work with them on a project before you hire them full-time. 

At Pangea, we make contract-to-hire easy and painless.

We'll work with you to provide a shortlist of top, interested candidates.  

Our talent have an average of 5-7+ years of experience in design, growth, ops, product, and engineering, and are primarily based in the USA (but also extend to 155 countries)
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Providence, RI, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startups and small companies hiring contract-to-hire marketing, design and operations talent; originally startups hiring college students
problem: Hiring a full-time employee blind is risky; trying someone on a project first (contract-to-hire) is hard to arrange. Originally, startups struggled to hire college student freelancers.
business_model: Marketplace: 15% take on transaction volume plus SaaS fees from some companies in 2020 (TechCrunch); later a commission-free talent marketplace (2025 company blog)
product_category: Talent marketplace for fractional and contract-to-hire work
market_need_then: In 2020-04 TechCrunch reported about 250 schools with students on the platform, five figures of contracts and 60 new schools in three weeks, as COVID reduced internships.
outcome_analysis: Pangea raised $400K in 2020-04 and a $2M seed in 2021-07 after the W21 batch, then shifted from college students to experienced fractional talent, announced in 2025-04. The company is still a team of 3 on the YC page, which suggests slow scaling despite claims of a large talent network. It competes with Upwork, Fiverr and Toptal, so differentiation rests on contract-to-hire.

name: Parallel Bio
one_liner: Using the immune system to cure disease
long_description:
Parallel Bio is pioneering human-first drug discovery by creating the first map of human biology. Using groundbreaking biological and computational tools that track real clinical outcomes, the company generates data that enable earlier, more reliable decisions about disease biology and drug development. 

Parallel Bio’s platform overcomes the core limitations of traditional animal testing, which fails to encapsulate the complexity of human biology. The company is building internal pipelines of novel disease targets and drug candidates in both cancer and autoimmune disease, while collaborating with pharmaceutical companies to evaluate therapies directly in human systems to reduce the cost and risk of clinical trials. 

Based in San Francisco, the company was founded in 2021 by two of the world’s leading experts in replacing animal models with human-first platforms.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharma and biotech companies testing drug candidates, vaccines and antibodies, plus Parallel's own internal drug pipelines
problem: Animal models often fail to predict human immune responses, so drugs fail in the clinic; Parallel builds human immune organoids to test therapies earlier.
business_model: Platform partnerships and testing services for pharma, plus internal drug discovery pipelines in cancer and autoimmune disease
product_category: Human immune organoid drug discovery platform
market_need_then: Animal model failures and the cost of drug development were widely discussed; Parallel's founders cite the 2006 TGN1412 trial as a case where their model would have flagged the risk (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Parallel Bio raised a $4.3M seed in 2022-12 and a $21M Series A in 2025-06, with nearly $30M in total, and is building internal pipelines alongside pharma partnerships. Scientific founders with Stanford and organoid backgrounds, a defensible organoid platform and tailwinds for animal testing alternatives helped. The long gap from batch to the first announced round shows slow, capital intensive progress.

name: Parsagon
one_liner: AI to track and analyze public policy
long_description:
Parsagon is an AI that can collect and analyze publications from any government body in any jurisdiction. It currently parses and analyzes legislation, press releases, speeches, meeting minutes, executive orders, and much more in 64 countries and counting.

Fortune/Global 500 companies, policy firms, and other organizations are using Parsagon to uncover policy insights in hundreds of jurisdictions that they would otherwise miss. Customers use us to:

- Analyze changes in US state education policy
- Generate reports on UK financial regulations
- Monitor vaccine policies across the EU
- And much more!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Fortune and Global 500 companies, policy firms, non-profits and public affairs teams that monitor government publications
problem: Tracking legislation, regulation and government statements across many jurisdictions is slow, keyword based and limited to few sources.
business_model: Data and API subscription for regulatory and policy data; earlier products sold data from AI generated web scrapers
product_category: AI regulatory and public policy data
market_need_then: The launch posts say existing policy tracking platforms are outdated and keyword based; no dated demand evidence for 2021 was found.
outcome_analysis: Parsagon remains active with a team of 2 and has launched at least eight products on YC Launch, moving from price indexes and scrapers to policy tracking and a regulatory data API. No funding, exit or traction figures are public. The repeated repositioning suggests a search for demand, but the sources do not say why.

name: Partnered
one_liner: The network where sales teams connect to share customer introductions.
long_description: Partnered is the network where B2B sales teams share customer introductions. Join for free and get started in less than five minutes.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B SaaS sales and partnership teams that want warm introductions through partner sales teams
problem: Sales reps lack a systematic way to request and trade warm customer introductions with partners.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for a partner introductions network
product_category: Partner ecosystem and co-selling software
market_need_then: Partner ecosystem and co-selling was a growing practice among SaaS companies, with a dedicated podcast and professional communities, but no hard demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Partnered was a two person team building a network for partner introductions and was acquired by Crossbeam in May 2022, announced at Crossbeam's conference, with its functionality merged into Crossbeam's platform. No funding or price is public, so it is unclear whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing; the acquirer was the category leader, which suggests the standalone network could not match its distribution.

name: Patterns
tags: Analytics; Data Science; Data Engineering; Data Visualization
one_liner: Next-Gen Financial Analysis and Reporting with AI Agents
long_description:
Patterns revolutionizes financial analysis by making it easy and accessible through natural language. We are seeking passionate individuals excited about simplifying financial analytics and transforming business intelligence. If you're interested in joining an innovative team in the finance space, explore our job openings and become part of our mission.

Our advanced AI transforms financial data workflows and reporting, surpassing traditional spreadsheets and inflexible SaaS solutions. By integrating state-of-the-art LLMs with autonomous querying and financial reasoning, Patterns empowers practitioners to perform complex analyses effortlessly via a natural language interface.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Initially data and AI teams building data applications; later finance teams and practitioners needing financial analysis and reporting
problem: Building data and AI applications required heavy engineering; later, financial analysis depended on spreadsheets and rigid tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform; pricing not found
product_category: Data/AI platform, later AI financial analysis agents
market_need_then: TechCrunch (March 2023) says Patterns aimed to remove routine data science work; no spend or demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Patterns raised a reported $2.5M pre-seed around March 2023 for a data and AI platform, then its site and YC listing shifted to AI analytics and financial-analysis agents. YC now lists it as inactive, but no shutdown announcement or reason was found. Pivot_failed is a tentative inference from the product change followed by inactivity, not a stated reason.
