Later-dated (March 2023) TechCrunch coverage named MLOps rivals Galileo, Qwak, Diveplane, Tecton, Arize, Iterative, Comet and Weights & Biases.

name: Payflow
one_liner: A mobile app. It allows employees to get paid their salary on-demand.
long_description: A mobile app. It allows employees to get paid whenever they want, instead of just once a month (or biweekly). We sell it to companies as an employee benefit (B2B SaaS).
regions: Spain; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Employers in Spain, Portugal and Latin America (mostly hourly or shift-based workforces) that pay a fixed monthly fee to offer on-demand salary access as an employee benefit
problem: Employees wait until monthly or biweekly payday to access wages they have already earned, which pushes some toward costly short-term credit.
business_model: B2B SaaS employer-paid fixed monthly fee, free to employees, plus a financial wellbeing super app (flexible compensation card, savings, financial education)
product_category: Earned wage access / employee financial wellbeing
market_need_then: Earned wage access was an established category in the US by 2021 and Spain had no dominant local product; Payflow said it targeted employees who wait for monthly pay. No dated Spanish demand statistic was opened.
outcome_analysis: Payflow is active and has raised repeatedly from 2021 to 2025 from Spanish and European investors while expanding from Spain into Portugal, Colombia and Peru. It sells to employers on a fixed fee and added adjacent products, and claims over 1,000 client companies. No shutdown, layoff or acquisition reports were found. The other success factor reflects debt financing used to fund advances, which the company says totals 27 million euros.

name: Payhippo
one_liner: Loans to Nigeria's SMEs in under 3 hours
long_description:
Payhippo provides loans to small businesses in Africa in under 3 hours.

We made $42k in revenue in Nigeria in July 2021, growing 25% m/m with a 97% repayment rate.
all_locations: Lagos, LA, Nigeria; LA, Nigeria; Remote
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and medium businesses in Nigeria needing short-term working capital loans
problem: Nigerian SMEs have little access to fast credit from banks; Payhippo promised loans in under 3 hours using its own scoring on SME data.
business_model: Digital lender: interest and fees on short-term SME loans, later a microfinance bank acquisition and a pivot to clean energy financing
product_category: SME digital lending, later clean energy financing
founder_names: Zach Bijesse; Chioma Okotcha; Uche Nnadi
market_need_then: TechCabal 2021 coverage cited over 40 million SMEs in Nigeria and Payhippo reported 5,000 loans disbursed worth about $1 million with a 97 percent repayment rate and $64,000 in revenue before the seed round.
outcome_analysis: Payhippo raised a 1 million dollar pre-seed and a 3 million dollar seed in 2021 from African fintech founders and bought a microfinance bank in 2022 pending central bank approval. Public sources show no shutdown, but in March 2025 it rebranded as Rivy and moved from SME lending to clean energy financing, citing the difficulty of SME lending. The company is active, and whether the pivot succeeds is not yet known.

name: Pensil
one_liner: New-Age White Label Community Platform SDKs and APIs for Games,…
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Per Diem
one_liner: The AI operating system for restaurants
long_description: Restaurants today rely on dozens of disconnected tools to manage ordering, loyalty, marketing, and operations. Per Diem replaces that fragmented software stack with AI agents that build and maintain branded apps, run marketing campaigns, manage loyalty, automate operations, and help restaurants grow first-party sales. Built natively on Square, 800+ brands use Per Diem to power more than 500,000 monthly orders as their operating system for commerce, customer retention, and growth.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Independent coffee shops, restaurants and small food brands that use Square point of sale
problem: Independent restaurants lack branded mobile ordering and loyalty apps like Starbucks and rely on third-party delivery marketplaces that own the customer relationship.
business_model: SaaS subscription (from $99 per month per the company site) for white-label branded apps, loyalty and marketing, built on the Square ecosystem
product_category: Restaurant branded app, loyalty and marketing platform (now positioned as an AI operating system)
market_need_then: Restaurants were paying high marketplace commissions and wanted first-party ordering after the pandemic shift to digital orders; Per Diem's early pitch was Starbucks-level apps for independents. No dated customer-spend figure was opened.
outcome_analysis: Per Diem raised a 2.3 million dollar seed in April 2021 led by Two Sigma Ventures and stayed small with 25 staff while building around Square's marketplace, which gave it distribution. It claims 800 plus brands and 500,000 monthly orders and is still active, with no later priced round found. The risk is dependence on Square, and a shift in 2024 to an AI operating system framing.

name: Perfekto
one_liner: Grocery subscription service against food waste in Latam
long_description:
Over 1/3 of food is being thrown away and in Latin America 72% of it prior to the consumer stage. Mainly due to physical imperfections or surplus production, despite being fresh and edible.

Perfekto offers a grocery subscription box with imperfect and surplus food, home-delivered. Thereby, consumers save time and money while reducing food waste.

The founders are experienced leaders scaling startups & grocery operations. Anahí previously led the Uber Grocery initiative for Latam. Jan scaled Swiss FinTech Sonect to pre-Series B and to Mexico. Juan led Walmart's eCommerce logistics and operations in Mexico. 

By the end of 2022, Perfekto had:
🌱 rescued over 500,000kgs of food from being wasted
🚚 delivered over 60,000 orders
📈 grown 1,120% year-over-year
🥖 gone beyond just produce and now help rescue items like bread or packaged goods from companies like Heartbest Foods, Bové, Tuny - with major multinationals in the pipeline
💚 become a beloved brand with an NPS of 70
🫂 built an online community of over 20,000 people and several thousand homes receiving Perfekto boxes
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Pesto
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: US consumers with thin or poor credit who own valuables such as gold, jewelry and watches and would otherwise use pawn shops
problem: Pawn loans carry very high rates and risk losing the item; Pesto offers a secured credit card whose limit is backed by pledged assets, with rates far lower than pawn.
business_model: Asset-backed credit card issued with a partner bank; revenue from interest and fees
product_category: Fintech, asset-backed credit card
market_need_then: Pawn lending is a large market with high rates for underbanked borrowers; Pesto's founder and press cite pawn rates far above the roughly 90 percent savings Pesto claimed.
outcome_analysis: Pesto started as PingLend in 2020 and joined YC in Winter 2021. It raised an 11 million dollar round in May 2023 and launched the Pesto Mastercard backed by gold, jewelry and watches, built on the founder's firsthand pawn shop experience. NerdWallet later shows the card as no longer taking applications, but the reason and date were not retrievable, so the outcome after 2023 is unclear.

name: Phoenix
tags: Consumer Health Services; Telehealth; Consumer; Digital Health
one_liner: Canada's digital health clinic for men
long_description: Phoenix is a mission-driven digital healthcare platform for men. We are dedicated to improving the relationship men have with their health, while building the future of patient-centric healthcare in Canada from diagnosing to delivery.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Canadian men seeking prescription treatment for erectile dysfunction, hair loss, weight management and related conditions, paying out of pocket
problem: Men in Canada face stigma and slow access when seeking care for sensitive conditions; Phoenix offers provider-reviewed virtual care with prescriptions filled by partner pharmacies.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer telehealth clinic with consultation and prescription revenue through partner pharmacies
product_category: Men's digital health clinic
market_need_then: Pandemic-era adoption of telehealth in Canada and the stigma around ED and hair loss care; Maple's 2022 interview anticipated post-peak telehealth demand declines. No dated Canadian men's telehealth demand figure was opened.
outcome_analysis: Phoenix grew from a Winter 2021 YC start to about 70 staff and a 50 million Canadian dollar Series A in March 2025 led by Valspring, with a launched sister brand and a generic semaglutide offering announced in 2026. The growth rests on cash-pay telehealth demand and unusually visible advertising. Earlier rounds and valuation are not public in the sources found.

name: Phykos
one_liner: Growing seaweed to stabilize the climate.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Corporations and governments buying durable carbon dioxide removal credits
problem: Open-ocean seaweed could remove carbon at scale if grown and sunk cheaply; Phykos proposed solar-powered autonomous vessels to cultivate and sink it.
business_model: Sell carbon removal credits generated by autonomous seaweed cultivation vessels (per a profile; not confirmed on a company site)
product_category: Ocean carbon dioxide removal hardware
market_need_then: Corporate buyers such as Microsoft and Shopify were buying carbon removal in 2021, and Phykos's launch press (Fast Company, September 2021) framed ocean seaweed as a scalable removal route.
outcome_analysis: Phykos is listed as active with two people and no website on its YC page, and no priced round, exit, shutdown or pivot was found in public sources. Press coverage in 2021 described a seaweed carbon removal concept still before proof of principle, in a field where Running Tide later closed. The outcome is not yet clear and funding is unknown rather than zero.

name: Pibit.ai
one_liner: The AI Underwriting OS for Commercial, Specialty & E&S insurance
long_description:
Pibit is the AI Underwriting OS for Commercial, Specialty & E&S insurance. Its AI agents run underwriting from submission to quote: they check submissions for completeness and chase brokers for what's missing, clear appetite, ingest documents and third-party data, analyze against guidelines, and give underwriters a risk summary with risk signals, pricing scenarios and benchmarks. Underwriters spend their time only on decisions and broker relationships.

50+ carriers and MGAs across 10+ lines run on Pibit. We guarantee 99.9% workflow accuracy in the contract from day one, go live one module at a time in weeks, and have never had a failed implementation. Pricing is per submission processed, with no license or implementation fee. Based in the Bay Area, with R&D in Bangalore.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Commercial, specialty and E&S insurance carriers, MGAs and mutuals
problem: Underwriters spend time on submission intake, document extraction and loss run analysis instead of risk decisions.
business_model: B2B software priced per submission processed, with no license or implementation fee (per the YC description)
product_category: AI underwriting platform for insurance
market_need_then: Insurers faced manual underwriting workloads and talent shortage, and Pibit's early product launched on Product Hunt in February 2021 as an API turning unstructured documents into structured data. No dated spend figure was opened.
outcome_analysis: Pibit.ai has survived and grown to about 200 staff (YC page) and announced a 7 million dollar Series A led by Stellaris in November 2025, four years after its Winter 2021 batch. Earlier funding is unclear and the long gap suggests slow capital-light growth. The product moved from a document extraction API toward an agentic underwriting platform as language models matured.

name: Pide Directo
tags: Autonomous Delivery; SaaS; E-commerce; Enterprise Software
one_liner: One-stop-shop for restaurants to operate and grow their business.
long_description:
Pidedirecto is a restaurant management platform that optimizes operations, increases revenue, and enhances customer experience. Its comprehensive toolset includes point of sale, payment terminals, online ordering, delivery management, loyalty programs, and integrations with third-party services.

All for a reasonable fixed monthly fee, without eating up margins with hefty commissions and service charges.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Local businesses in Mexico and Latin America, mainly restaurants, selling directly to consumers and wanting to avoid marketplace commissions
problem: Delivery marketplaces took roughly 25 to 30 percent of each sale; Pidedirecto offers online ordering, logistics orchestration and point of sale for a fixed monthly fee.
business_model: B2B SaaS with fixed monthly fee and delivery orchestration that connects couriers from Rappi, Uber and Didi or the merchant's own drivers
product_category: Restaurant ordering, point of sale and delivery logistics platform
founder_names: Hussein Fawzi; Antonio Nacoud; Ronni Samir Sulaka; Anders Steiner
market_need_then: Mexican restaurants complained of commissions near 30 percent and CANIRAC said pre-pandemic fees were unsustainable (January 2021); founders told TechCrunch customers lost 25 to 30 percent of each sale to marketplaces.
outcome_analysis: Pide Directo raised a 5.25 million dollar seed in October 2021 led by JAM FUND and grew to about 150 staff, with a claimed 5,000 clients and a Rappi partnership. It pitched fixed-fee software against 25 to 30 percent marketplace commissions. No later priced round, exit or shutdown was found, so growth since 2021 is funded either by revenue or undisclosed capital.

name: Pideaky
one_liner: We help offline LatAm SMBs manage and accelerate their cash-flow
long_description:
Pideaky helps offline LatAm SMBs manage and accelerate their cash flow through AI collection agents, which remind, collect, and negotiate bills on behalf of SMBS in Latam.
We focus on the massively underserved $70B/year customer segment as our wedge — Mexican corner shops and corner shop providers:
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mexican corner shops (tienditas) and their suppliers
problem: Offline corner shops and their providers struggle with cash flow and access to credit; the company began with point of sale, then inventory-based lending, then AI collection agents for supplier invoices.
business_model: Lending to corner shops against inventory, later fees on AI-driven invoice collection for suppliers
product_category: SMB fintech: inventory-based lending and AI collections (LatAm)
founder_names: Carlos Tejeda; Oscar Rydberg; Rafael Tejeda Elizondo
market_need_then: The YC launch post cites about 70 billion dollars per year of gross merchandise value in the corner shop segment and 6,000 plus shops served; a 2021 TechCrunch piece states about 86 percent of Mexican payments were cash and many lacked credit.
outcome_analysis: Pideaky is active with a very small team and no public priced round, so its funding is unknown rather than zero. It moved from point of sale to inventory lending and then to AI collections for suppliers, and claims over 14,000 loans and 6,000 shops. The founders have long ties to corner shop customers through the payphone business. Whether the latest pivot works is not yet visible.

name: Pillar
tags: Consumer Health Services; Digital Health; Healthcare
one_liner: A white-label care enablement platform
long_description: Pillar is designed to solve healthcare’s longitudinal engagement problem through a combination of our SOC 2-certified, HIPAA-compliant platform and health coach workforce. Our white-label infrastructure enables companies to guide patients from outreach and activation through to flexible microsites and automated digital pathways including content, services, vendors and forms. Together with our in-house network of 1,200+ health coaches, Pillar partners drive positive outcomes through scalable digital care programs focused on health education and care navigation to chronic condition management.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Healthcare organizations (primary care, disease management, value-based care) and employee benefits organizations that pay for white-label patient engagement and coaching
problem: Healthcare organizations struggle to keep patients and members engaged over time after outreach and activation. Pillar supplies white-label microsites, digital pathways and a coach workforce to do this.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform fees plus staffed health coach services for partners
product_category: Digital health care enablement and navigation platform
market_need_then: Value-based care and employer benefits buyers wanted ongoing engagement for chronic conditions and navigation, and the company began as a coach marketplace that placed coaches with partners before building a platform. No quantified demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Pillar is active as of the sources found. It started as a coach marketplace, then moved to a white-label platform with a large coach network and earned SOC 2 in January 2023. Funding is only visible in aggregators, so how well it has done is hard to judge. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff report was found.

name: PingPong
one_liner: Video messaging app for remote teams.
long_description:
A video messaging app for remote teams in multiple time zones—it's like Slack for video.

With PingPong, teams collaborate by exchanging short video, voice, and screen recording clips.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Remote and distributed product teams working across time zones
problem: Text chat is too limiting for detailed ideas and live meetings are hard across time zones.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat
product_category: Asynchronous video messaging
market_need_then: Remote work during 2020 and 2021 raised interest in asynchronous communication across time zones, with the founders collaborating between the US and Nigeria themselves.
outcome_analysis: PingPong launched a video messaging app for remote teams in March 2021 in a space where Loom and Slack were far larger, and was acquired by Grain about a year later with the team joining Grain. No funding amount or price is public, and the product looks like a soft landing; the lack of differentiation and an easily copied feature set probably limited an independent outcome.

name: PipeBio
tags: AI-powered Drug Discovery; Machine Learning; SaaS
one_liner: PipeBio is a SaaS bioinformatics platform to develop antibody drugs.
long_description:
Pipe|bio is the bioinformatics cloud for antibody / peptide screening & drug development.

We enable scientists to analyze and manage massive amounts of DNA sequencing data themselves without the need for bioinformaticians or programmers. The software is highly visual and enables you to overlay and filter information from different sources across your organization; be it assay data, sequence data or other process metadata. Insights from past results can be used to guide new experiments and they get better as you upload more and more data. Team leads get oversight and these capabilities combined empower organizations to find better drugs, faster.

We believe that science moves faster when scientists can curate and analyse their own data.
regions: Denmark; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Biotech and pharma antibody discovery scientists
problem: Scientists need to analyze large DNA sequencing datasets from antibody screening without relying on bioinformaticians or programmers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for bioinformatics
product_category: Antibody discovery bioinformatics platform
market_need_then: Next generation sequencing made antibody screening datasets large, and teams lacked bioinformatics staff to process them.
outcome_analysis: PipeBio was started by two founders with Biomatters and bioinformatics backgrounds, took small early funding from byFounders, Y Combinator and Acequia Capital, and sold to Benchling in October 2024, continuing as a product inside Benchling's biologics offering. Domain expertise and a clear niche helped; the deal price is not public so the exit size is unknown.

name: Pipekit
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Data Engineering; DevOps
one_liner: Pipekit scales data & CI pipelines for enterprises
long_description:
Our app manages Argo Workflows for data teams, enabling complex data &
 CI pipelines in half the time while saving companies hundreds of thousands of dollars annually. We maintain Argo Workflows, an open-source pipeline framework for Kubernetes that’s used in production by Bloomberg, Intuit, Adobe, New Relic, NVIDIA, and many other open-source early adopters.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Platform and data engineering teams at enterprises that run Argo Workflows on Kubernetes for data and CI pipelines
problem: Running Argo Workflows at scale across Kubernetes clusters needs expertise, tooling and support. Pipekit offers a managed control plane and enterprise support for it.
business_model: B2B SaaS control plane subscriptions plus enterprise support and services for Argo Workflows
product_category: Developer tools, data and CI pipeline orchestration (managed Argo Workflows)
market_need_then: Argo Workflows was in production at large firms such as Bloomberg, Intuit and Adobe per the YC description, and the founders say they came from the pain of scaling data pipelines. No quantified spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: Pipekit is active and, per third-party sources, leads maintenance of Argo Workflows with a team of about 15. Its path rests on open-source credibility rather than venture-scale funding that can be verified. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff was found, and the technical_moat tag reflects maintainer expertise only loosely.

name: Pirouette Pharma
tags: Health Tech; Medical Devices; Biotech; Healthcare
one_liner: We make injections as easy as pushing a button!
long_description: At Pirouette, we have developed a low-profile, disk-shaped, rugged injection device with a patient-centric focus on affordability, portability, and usability. The patented device, based on extensive patient input, is designed to make administering an injection as easy as pushing a button. This allows individuals with limited or no training to easily and intuitively perform an injection on themselves or others.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharmaceutical companies that co-develop or license the device for chronic injectables, and patients who self-inject; also military and first responder segments
problem: Self-injection with traditional auto-injectors is intimidating and hard for untrained users, which hurts adherence. Pirouette builds a low-profile push-button disc injector with a hidden needle.
business_model: Medical device and drug-device platform: co-development and licensing with pharma plus own 505(b)(2) and 351(k) programs
product_category: Drug delivery device (auto-injector)
founder_names: Conor Cullinane; Matthew Kane; Elijah Kapas
market_need_then: Self-injected biologics and chronic therapies were growing and needle fear affects adherence, and the founders applied for NIH-backed work on a naloxone auto-injector for opioid overdose. No quantified market data was gathered.
outcome_analysis: Pirouette remains active and has funded itself largely through retail crowdfunding, with a 2024 Wefunder round led by Safar Partners alongside Y Combinator. Its progress depends on regulatory milestones and pharma partners, with targets claimed for 2027 to 2029. No exit or shutdown was found.

name: Plai
one_liner: Create, launch, and optimize Facebook ads and ads on 10+ platforms
long_description: Plai makes it easy to create, launch, and optimize ads with AI doing the heavy lifting. Brands use Plai across Facebook, Google, LinkedIn, and TikTok. Trusted across 100,000+ campaigns and 5B+ ad impressions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and local businesses, ecommerce brands, franchises and agencies that buy and manage online ads
problem: Creating, launching and optimizing ads across Facebook, Google, LinkedIn and TikTok is complex and time consuming for non-experts. Plai uses AI to automate setup and optimization.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers including a white-label plan, plus agency billing by ad spend or retainer
product_category: AI advertising automation platform
market_need_then: Small businesses spend on Facebook and Google ads but lack expertise, and the founder came from building ad products at both companies. No quantified demand data was gathered.
outcome_analysis: Plai is active with about 20 people and claims 25K businesses and 200K campaigns launched, though these are company claims. Funding is only visible in aggregators and they disagree, so its fundraising success is unclear. No shutdown or acquisition was found.

name: Planet A Foods
one_liner: Building the next generation food ingredient champion.
long_description:
Imagine a world without chocolate. Horrifying, right? But the supply of cocoa is endangered and chocolate is as bad as meat for our planet. 

We make future-proof chocolate using precision fermentation. Doing this, our chocolate is 10x more sustainable and 20% cheaper than conventional chocolate. In order to mimic the organoleptic properties of chocolate (tender, smoothly melting taste release) we are working on the flavor itself but also on replacing the cocoa butter. 

55 Mio lbs of chocolate are consumed every day. By 2035 we will substitute a big chunk of it through our sustainable chocolate. 

In addition, we are working on extending our technology platform to additional ingredients such as palm oil.
regions: Germany; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Chocolate, bakery and confectionery manufacturers and food retailers that buy cocoa or cocoa butter
problem: Cocoa supply is under climate and price pressure and conventional chocolate has a large environmental footprint.
business_model: B2B ingredient sales and distribution partnerships (ChoViva cocoa-free chocolate ingredient)
product_category: Cocoa-free chocolate ingredient made from oats and sunflower seeds via fermentation
market_need_then: Cocoa supply was described as endangered and pricey in the 2021 pitch, and cocoa prices later surged, which raised demand for substitutes.
outcome_analysis: Planet A Foods raised a 6M USD seed in October 2021, a 15.4M USD Series A in February 2024 and a 30M USD Series B in December 2024 to expand its Czech plant from 2,000 to over 15,000 tonnes a year. Founders with food chemistry and materials PhDs, the cocoa price crisis and distribution through Barry Callebaut and retail launches such as Aldi UK explain the momentum. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff was found.

name: Platypus
tags: B2B; Workflow Automation; Data Engineering; AI Assistant
one_liner: The Distributed Data Operating System
long_description:
For Business Operators: Connect & automate processes on top of any data, crazy fast.

For Engineering Teams: Connect any data, across any stack, in any format, crazy fast.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Playmaker
one_liner: Community for fantasy sports players
long_description: We're building the social, infrastructure layer for players of fantasy sports games, to provide them with a centralised place where they can own their identity as a fantasy sports player and get additional enjoyment and engagement out of watching live sports alongside their friends.
regions: Denmark; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Pluggy
one_liner: Plaid for Brazil: we allow developers to access users' financial data
long_description:
Pluggy is a B2B Fintech that allows any developer to connect to the data from their users' bank and broker accounts, essentially Plaid for Brazil. 

We are 100% focused in Brazil. One of the largest markets in the world. Its complexity, risks and challenges require its own solution.

Local focus and our deep experience in banking tech engineering allowed Pluggy to create a product that is considered by our customers as the only one to provide reliable data at the right time to market.

We currently cover 90% of the bank accounts in Brazil a market of more than 7 billion USD. 

We are Pluggy!
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: ERPs, fintechs, accounting and financial management software companies in Brazil that need bank data and Pix payments through one API
problem: Brazilian software companies could not reliably read customers' bank and broker data or initiate payments. Pluggy provides an Open Finance API, described as Plaid for Brazil.
business_model: Usage-based and subscription API fees for data connectors and Pix payment initiation
product_category: Open Finance infrastructure API (fintech)
founder_names: Federico Miras; Gabriel Pan Gantes; Rogerio Correa; Victor Braga; Bruno Loiola
market_need_then: Brazil was rolling out regulated Open Banking from 2021 and software vendors wanted bank data access. Pluggy claimed to cover 90 percent of Brazilian bank accounts on its YC listing.
outcome_analysis: Pluggy rode Brazil's regulated Open Finance rollout, raised small rounds and reports breakeven since 2024 with about 500 direct clients. Its capital efficiency is notable, with only about $6M raised by 2026 per press, and its payment initiation license adds a regulatory edge. Rivals such as Belvo and Quanto raised far more.

name: Poliglota
one_liner: The online language school for Latam, with groups led by an instructor
long_description:
Poliglota is the online language school for Latam, where group classes are led by an instructor. Over 12,000 students have paid us $500 to learn english in order to get a higher income.
We offer an online service of personalized language sessions with small groups of people of the same level, guided by expert language coaches that we train in our social methodology.
regions: Chile; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Spanish-speaking adults and companies in Latin America who pay for instructor-led online language classes, mainly English
problem: Learning to speak a language in Latin America was taught like a school subject and in-person options were costly or inconvenient. Poliglota offers small live online groups focused on conversation.
business_model: Paid multi-month course plans in USD for individuals plus B2B corporate programs and add-ons
product_category: Online language school (edtech)
founder_names: Carlos Aravena; Nicolas Fuenzalida; Jose Sanchez
market_need_then: Chilean and Latam professionals needed English for higher income, the company said over 12,000 students had paid about $500, and the pandemic pushed the business from in-person events to online classes per Forbes Chile (2021).
outcome_analysis: Poliglota turned a pandemic shock into growth by moving classes online, scaling to about 170 people and reporting breakeven at the end of 2023 after rounds of $2.5M at a stated $50M valuation in 2021. Later money came from small crowdfunding rounds, which suggests no large venture follow-on is visible.

name: Popl
one_liner: Your AI GTM platform for In-Person Events
long_description: Popl is the AI GTM platform for in-person events — the data layer for everything that happens face-to-face. Powered by AI and its proprietary data engine, Popl helps companies worldwide turn events into a measurable, scalable growth channel: universal badge scanning, AI-powered conversation recording, real-time data enrichment, and automatic CRM sync.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Originally individual consumers and professionals buying NFC business cards; now B2B go-to-market and sales teams capturing leads at in-person events
problem: Paper business cards and trade show leads were slow to share and often never reached a CRM. Popl began as tap to share cards and became an event lead capture platform.
business_model: Hardware sales of NFC cards and devices plus B2B software subscriptions for teams
product_category: Digital business cards and event lead capture
market_need_then: Pandemic era contactless sharing and about 10 billion paper business cards printed yearly were cited as the opportunity; TikTok demand showed consumer pull.
outcome_analysis: Popl grew from TikTok driven sales of NFC cards in 2020 and 2021 into a B2B platform, then rebranded in 2025 around event lead capture. It claims 5,000 plus customer teams and 2 million users. Revenue estimates range from 15M to 34M per data vendors, and public funding appears limited to a small seed, so growth looks capital efficient but unverified.

name: Portão 3
one_liner: We are the frictionless way for companies to make payments.
long_description:
Portão 3 is Ramp for LATAM. We are the frictionless way for companies to make payments.

The company is founded by Fernando, second-time entrepreneur with past successful exit and ex-CPO of large IT consulting firms in Brazil and Bianca, experienced entrepreneur that handled payments for Cargill and funded startups in travel and growth. We've grown bootstrapped from the beginning and we were in the Y Combinator S21 batch.
regions: Brazil; Latin America
target_customer: Brazilian companies of all sizes, notably those with heavy ad spend and fuel or travel spending, that want virtual cards and expense control
problem: Companies in Brazil struggle to pay suppliers and platforms and to control spending by team or project. Portao 3 issues virtual cards and tracks expenses, described as Ramp for LATAM.
business_model: Fintech take on card spend and expense management software, reaching profitability per press
product_category: Corporate cards and spend management (fintech)
market_need_then: The company started as corporate travel software and moved toward cards after finding demand for payment control, and bootstrapped to profitability before its seed according to press. No quantified market data was gathered.
outcome_analysis: Portao 3 bootstrapped, joined YC in S21 and raised a R$19M (about US$3.6M) seed in January 2023 led by Better Tomorrow Ventures after pivoting from corporate travel to cards. It claims thousands of client companies. Co-CEO Bianca left in 2024 leaving Fernando Nery as sole CEO. No exit or shutdown found.

name: Positional
one_liner: A modern platform for content marketing & SEO.
long_description: Start, grow, and scale your inbound marketing and SEO strategy with a toolset optimized for results — not vanity metrics. Our goal is to connect the workflow from end to end, from keyword research to analytics, and the actions that users take that ultimately drive revenue for a business.
all_locations: Charleston, SC, USA; Hoboken, NJ, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Content marketing and SEO teams at startups and small companies
problem: Marketers juggle six or seven separate tools for keyword research, briefs, writing and analytics.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Content marketing and SEO platform
market_need_then: Content and SEO teams paid for several overlapping tools, evidenced by the crowded set of content optimization products named in an October 2021 Single Grain list.
outcome_analysis: Positional came from founders with ten years of inbound marketing experience who pivoted after two years on a product nobody wanted. It entered a crowded SEO content tool market against MarketMuse, Clearscope, Surfer and Frase and was acquired by Daydream in April 2025 after a few million dollars at most in reported funding. The exit price is not public and the deal looks like a small acquisition.

name: Potion
tags: Generative AI; Hard Tech; B2B; AI
one_liner: AI for product formulation
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Cosmetic and personal care brands, contract manufacturers, formulators and chemists that need ingredient search, formulation and compliance tools
problem: Developing cosmetic formulas relies on manual ingredient research, trial and error and compliance checks. Potion applies AI to ingredient management, formulation and regulatory screening.
business_model: Freemium software with a free discovery platform and sales-led premium plans and enterprise partnerships
product_category: AI software for product formulation (beauty R&D)
founder_names: Yahya Syed; Hejab Malik; Alex Stec
market_need_then: Beauty and personal care formulators faced long reformulation cycles and compliance work, and AI formulation startups such as Turing were already selling to CPG firms in 2020. No quantified spend data was gathered.
outcome_analysis: Potion is active and moved from a general AI for product formulation pitch to a beauty industry focus with a free discovery platform, patented Virtual Formulation and a KDC/ONE partnership in January 2026. How much it raised is unclear because only aggregators report funding. No exit or shutdown found.

name: PowerRouter
one_liner: PowerRouter helps sales teams with lead routing in Salesforce
long_description: PowerRouter helps sales teams assign leads and contacts to the right reps, instantly within Salesforce.  We provide a powerful automation engine with a drag and drop canvas to create routing rules, visually.  With actionable metrics to increase speed-to-lead and account based sales support, we make it very simple to stay on top of every lead in your Salesforce CRM.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B sales and revenue operations teams that run Salesforce and need to assign inbound leads and contacts to reps
problem: Leads sit unassigned or go to the wrong rep inside Salesforce, which slows speed to lead. Building routing rules in native Salesforce tooling is hard for non-developers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, a Salesforce-native app (a directory listing shows per user per month pricing, unverified)
product_category: Salesforce lead routing and assignment automation
market_need_then: Speed to lead and account based sales were common RevOps concerns in 2021, and LeanData had been selling Salesforce lead management since at least 2014, which shows paid demand. No PowerRouter specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: PowerRouter is still listed as active and I found no news of an acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Public information is thin: no confirmed funding round, no press coverage and only directory profiles, so its traction cannot be judged. It targets a real but contested wedge against LeanData and native Salesforce tooling, and it has stayed small.

name: Pragmatic Leaders (Ankai Inc)
one_liner: AI-powered Corporate Training: Faster, Smarter, and More Effective
long_description:
Ostronaut is an AI-powered, SaaS-based corporate training solution built to transform workforce learning. Its foundations come from six years of training 10,000+ product professionals through Pragmatic Leaders, which provided a faster, more cost-effective alternative to an MBA.

🚀 Smarter, faster, and designed for real-world impact.

- Initiative of Pragmatic Leaders
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mid-career product professionals in India (Pragmatic Leaders) and corporate training and sales enablement teams (Ostronaut)
problem: Professionals wanted a faster and cheaper route than an MBA to product skills, and companies want faster, more effective workforce training.
business_model: Paid online cohort courses, later B2B SaaS for AI-powered corporate training
product_category: Edtech, product management training and AI corporate training
market_need_then: Inc42 describes the course as a cheaper, faster alternative to an MBA with real product building; the company reports training over 10,000 product professionals in six years.
outcome_analysis: Pragmatic Leaders built a product management training business in India and joined YC in Winter 2021, then launched Ostronaut for AI-powered corporate training. It remains active with a small team of about 10, but no funding or revenue figures were found, so success cannot be judged. Founder experience in product and education is the main advantage.

name: Preki
one_liner: Shopify for LatAm
long_description:
Preki creates easy to use e-commerce solutions for local businesses in LatAm, you can think of us as Shopify for LatAm.

Setting up an online business in LatAm is expensive, hard to learn and time consuming.

With us, all businesses have to do is follow an onboarding process and add products - no code or design involved. This process takes less than 30 seconds and users can start selling immediately.
regions: Colombia; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small independent businesses in Latin America (initially beauty retailers buying wholesale; later small businesses building online stores)
problem: Independent LatAm retailers had to travel or wait days to restock and were limited to suppliers near them; later positioning was an easy no-code online store builder ('Shopify for LatAm').
business_model: Wholesale marketplace with supplier credit (2021), later SaaS e-commerce store builder
product_category: LatAm B2B wholesale marketplace / e-commerce platform
founder_names: Pedro Virgüez; Alex Hakim; Tahi Hakim; David Narvaez
market_need_then: In March 2021 Preki reported 226+ registered businesses, 30 suppliers and 1,000+ products sold in 18 municipalities, targeting 3,500 businesses and $1M volume by year end, which suggests early but small demand for wholesale restocking.
outcome_analysis: Preki began as a wholesale marketplace with credit for LatAm retailers and later presented itself as Shopify for LatAm. Funding found is only the roughly $125,000 YC deal, and the company was bought by Sumer in September 2023 for an undisclosed price, mainly for its Brazil user base, with founders staying only as advisors and the brand to be retired. Whether this was a rescue or a modest win is not public, so no success or failure factors are asserted.

name: Prendea
one_liner: Live afterschool classes for Spanish-speaking kids ages 4 to 15.
long_description: Prendea offers live afterschool classes to Spanish-speaking kids ages 4 to 15.  For a fixed monthly price, kids can choose as many classes as they like from our large selection that ranges from TikTok choreography to astronomy.
regions: Peru; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Prequel
one_liner: Helping B2B co's sync data to their customers
long_description: Prequel makes it easy for companies to share data with their customers. It helps you export data directly to your customer's Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Databricks, or other data warehouse on an ongoing basis.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B SaaS and data product companies whose enterprise customers want the vendor's data delivered to their own data warehouse
problem: Customers of SaaS vendors increasingly ask for raw data in Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift or Databricks, and each vendor would otherwise build and maintain a separate pipeline per warehouse.
business_model: Usage based API and platform, priced per destination rather than per row, with cloud and self hosted deployment
product_category: Data warehouse integration and data sharing infrastructure for SaaS vendors
market_need_then: Warehouse centric data stacks were spreading by 2020 and 2021, and a Snowflake guide for SaaS providers says customers increasingly ask vendors to share raw data back with them.
outcome_analysis: Prequel is active and, by its own seed announcement, signed customers including LogRocket, Metronome, Modern Treasury and Postscript, with synced destinations growing over 35 percent monthly in 2023. It raised a 5.2M seed in September 2023, more than two years after the batch, so early capital efficiency mattered. The product rides the shift to warehouse centric data stacks, while native exports from large vendors are the main threat.

name: Procoto
one_liner: Self-service RFP management
long_description: Procoto makes running RFPs, tracking contracts, and managing vendors simple and affordable. We get procurement teams out of dense systems and spreadsheets without having to drop a hefty check on SAP or Coupa.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-market companies running vendor RFPs and procurement
problem: Enterprise procurement tools like SAP and Coupa need six-figure annual agreements, leaving small firms with spreadsheets.
business_model: Self-service B2B SaaS for RFPs, contracts and vendor tracking
product_category: RFP and procurement management
market_need_then: Founders evaluated 30+ competitor products while building procurement at earlier startups and found enterprise tools too costly for small companies (YC launch post).
outcome_analysis: Procoto offered self-service RFP management to small companies and was acquired by Bedrock in an all-stock deal announced June 2024 to fold into a procure-to-pay platform. Price and prior funding are undisclosed, so it is unclear whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing.

name: Promakhos Therapeutics
one_liner: A therapeutics platform for curing inflammatory disorders
long_description: We are building a platform of bacterial molecules to awaken our body’s innate ability to control inflammation and heal. Our first indication is Crohn’s Disease, which affects over 500,000 Americans at an annual cost of $10B. After Crohn's disease, we are going for type 1 Diabetes and Multiple Sclerosis.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Patients with Crohn's disease and other chronic inflammatory conditions, reached through pharma development and licensing; today the paying parties are grant funders and investors
problem: Current treatments for inflammatory bowel disease suppress the immune system. The company aims to restore intestinal innate immune function and wound healing instead.
business_model: Preclinical drug development, with value realized through partnering, licensing or acquisition
product_category: Therapeutics, bacterial derived small molecules for inflammatory disease
competitors_at_founding: Vedanta Biosciences (VE202 with Janssen); Finch Therapeutics (FIN-525 with Takeda)
market_need_then: The company's own materials cite over 500,000 US Crohn's patients and about 10B USD annual cost. Existing immunosuppressants leave many patients without durable control.
outcome_analysis: Promakhos remains active with a team of 1 to 10 and has financed itself mostly through non dilutive grants since 2021, including an NIH SBIR and Crohn's patient foundation awards. No equity round above a small seed was verified, and no clinical data or partnership has been reported. The model needs far more capital than grants provide, so progress depends on raising a real seed or partnering.

name: Promoted.ai
one_liner: Dramatically better search and ads for marketplaces
long_description: Promoted.ai unifies search, native ads, and feed ranking for online marketplaces and scaled e-commerce apps to dramatically improve relevance (and revenue) using AI. We are a team of ex-Google, Meta, and Pinterest ads engineers. Our customers are publicly traded and late-stage marketplace companies like Eventbrite, Upwork, and Outschool. Our mission is to connect every buyer and seller.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Online marketplaces and e-commerce apps that want better search, feed ranking and native ads
problem: Marketplaces lack in-house ranking and ads systems like those built at Google and Pinterest, so relevance and revenue lag.
business_model: B2B SaaS and revenue share on marketplace ads
product_category: Marketplace search, ads and feed ranking infrastructure
market_need_then: Marketplaces wanted ad revenue and better relevance, and customers such as Upwork integrated its search and native ads engine by 2024.
outcome_analysis: Promoted was started by ex Pinterest and Google ads engineers, raised roughly $8M across two seed rounds, and landed marketplace customers including Eventbrite, Upwork and Outschool. It was acquired by Dropbox in April or May 2025; the price was not disclosed, so the strength of the exit is unknown. Deep founder expertise in ads systems and a clear customer segment drove the traction.

name: PropReturns
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: End-to-end commercial real estate transaction platform
long_description: PropReturns is an online platform to buy, sell and rent commercial real estate in India. The real estate market in India is highly fragmented and plagued by lack of transparency. We empower businesses and individuals in India to transact commercial real estate backed by data.
regions: India; South Asia

name: Prospa
one_liner: Banking for businesses
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and medium businesses in Nigeria and wider Africa, later positioned at structured African businesses with payroll and larger volumes
problem: African SMEs juggle banking, invoicing, payroll and inventory in separate tools. The founder describes the product as 10 percent banking and 90 percent software.
business_model: Fintech and SaaS with business accounts through partner banks, cards, loans and invoice financing
product_category: SME banking and business management software
founder_names: Frederik Obasi; Chioma Ugo; Rodney Jackson-Cole
market_need_then: TechCrunch reports tens of thousands of businesses on the platform growing 35 percent month on month, over 150,000 product catalogs and 360,000 invoices by September 2021, which shows demand.
outcome_analysis: Prospa raised the largest pre seed in sub Saharan Africa at the time, 3.8M in September 2021, on reported fast growth across SMEs. It is active and the YC page lists about 70 staff. No later priced round was found, so its trajectory after 2021 is unclear; it still operates in 2025 and has moved to target larger structured African businesses.

name: Protego
one_liner: We help companies recover lost revenue from chargebacks
long_description: Protego helps companies recover lost revenue from chargebacks. The company automates chargeback management and dispute processes. It provides real-time monitoring, reporting, and analytics on chargeback information for providing valuable insights into fraudulent consumer behavior.
regions: Colombia; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Protex AI
tags: Industrial Workplace Safety; Machine Learning; B2B
one_liner: Computer vision that makes the industrial workplace, safer
long_description:
Tl;dr: We’re building software that monitors existing cameras in the port, logistics, and manufacturing industries to ensure compliance and identify safety issues.

At Protex AI, we’re on a mission to protect the industrial workforce! We’re building a proactive computer vision tool for workplace safety - empowering industrial Health and Safety (HS) teams to identify risk and danger before it becomes a problem.

🤕 The Problem:
Keeping people safe at work is extremely hard. In the U.S. alone, there were over 5,000 deaths in the workplace in 2019, mainly in the heavy industry space.

Serious workplace injuries cost U.S. businesses circa $62 Billion annually. Until now, safety has been reactive, someone has to get injured, and in some cases fatally before something is done about it.

✅ Problem Solved:
Protex AI’s platform uses privacy-preserving camera monitoring software to provide companies with an always-on guardian angel, protecting their workforce.

The platform plugs into existing CCTV infrastructure and enables HS teams to flexibly translate their document-based safety rules into the real world.

Protex AI takes these rules and autonomously audits the customer’s facility to identify areas of high risk and non-compliance.

HS teams can access this data via a reporting engine and use it in weekly safety meetings, external safety audits, insurance discussions, and legal claims.

The tool integrates seamlessly with existing safety workflows to augment data produced by any manual incident logging system in place.
regions: Ireland; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Health and safety and operations teams at port, logistics, warehousing and manufacturing companies
problem: Workplace safety is reactive and relies on manual audits and incident logs. Protex turns existing CCTV into continuous audits of safety rules.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscription on top of existing cameras with edge video processing
product_category: Computer vision workplace safety analytics, later site intelligence
market_need_then: The YC page cites over 5,000 US workplace deaths in 2019 and about 62B USD annual cost of serious injuries, and Intenseye's 2021 funding signaled investor demand.
outcome_analysis: Protex went from a five person YC team in Limerick to an 18M round in 2022 and a 36M Series B in 2025 with customers such as large retailers and manufacturers named on its site. It sells to enterprise safety teams with a clear budget and a technology that plugs into existing CCTV, though Intenseye and others compete directly. It is active with offices in Dublin and Boston.

name: Pry Financials
one_liner: Finance for Founders (now at prune.com)
long_description:
Now working on prune.com

Pry makes it simple for companies to manage their budget, hiring plan, financial models, and cash runway.

Today, most people plan for their business once a quarter. It's done in Excel - buggy, boring, confusing, and really time-expensive. A lot of people have tried to solve this and only found moderate success or failed.

We're the team to do it right.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startup founders and small businesses that plan budgets, hiring and runway
problem: Founders model cash, hiring and runway in spreadsheets, which are error prone and hard to share.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Financial planning software for startups
founder_names: Andy Su; Tiffany Wong; Hayden Jensen; Alex Sailer
market_need_then: Seed funded startups had new cash to plan, and 2021 saw heavy startup funding, but demand evidence beyond press coverage was not gathered.
outcome_analysis: Pry was built by a repeat YC founder, Andy Su, raised a $4.2M seed in August 2021 and had about ten people when Brex bought it in April 2022 for roughly $90M, its largest deal at the time. A small team, a clear founder audience and a strategic fit with Brex's spend management produced a fast, high-multiple exit.

name: Purpose Finance
one_liner: Accelerating the shift to a more transparent economy
long_description: We help our users align their money with their values by giving actionable environmental, social and governance data about the companies that they shop at. And we keep it fun with perks and rewards.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Pylon
one_liner: Infrastructure management software for water & electricity companies
long_description:
Pylon provides water and electricity distribution companies, in emerging markets, with a platform for reducing their losses as well as opening new revenue streams. These losses are coming from leakages, consumption thefts, and uncollected bills, amongst others.
We have signed 11 utilities onto our platform across 2 countries and connected our systems to over 560k endpoints.
Today our average client has reduced their aggregate revenue losses by 45%
Expanding in Africa, LATAM, and SEA.
regions: Egypt; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Public and private water and electricity distribution utilities in emerging markets, starting with Egypt and the Philippines
problem: Utilities lose revenue to leakage, consumption theft and uncollected bills, and run fragmented metering systems across many meter models.
business_model: Smart Metering as a Service subscription to utilities, so cash constrained utilities avoid upfront hardware costs
product_category: Utility infrastructure management and smart metering software
market_need_then: Ashour said utility structural losses could approach 2B USD a year in Egypt alone, and the Egyptian smart meter standard and national rollout created demand.
outcome_analysis: Pylon bootstrapped from 2017 and, per TechCrunch, grew revenue 3.5 times in 2021 and claimed profitability before raising a 19M seed of equity and debt in April 2022. It serves utilities in Egypt and the Philippines with over a million endpoints and was still operating in late 2025. Founders with deep metering experience and sticky utility integrations explain the traction; no later round was found.

name: Pyroscope
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Open Source; Kubernetes
one_liner: Open source continuous profiling software to debug performance issues
long_description: Pyroscope is an open source continuous profiling platform. With just a few lines of code it will help you debug performance issues and find bottlenecks in your code.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Oakland, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software engineering and platform teams running production services who need to find CPU and memory bottlenecks
problem: Profiling was usually a one-off, manual task done on a laptop or in a short production capture. Teams lacked an always-on, low-overhead way to see which lines of code burn CPU and memory over time.
business_model: Open source (AGPL) continuous profiling with a planned paid hosted and enterprise offering
product_category: Developer tools, observability, continuous profiling
market_need_then: Observability was moving beyond metrics, logs and traces, and cloud cost pressure made code level CPU and memory waste visible. The project reached about 7.2k GitHub stars by the 2023 acquisition, per press coverage.
outcome_analysis: Pyroscope grew an open source continuous profiling project to about 7.2k GitHub stars and a Grafana integration within two years of the W21 batch. Grafana had built a competing database called Phlare, and in March 2023 it acquired the company and merged the projects under the Pyroscope name, a strategic acquisition with undisclosed terms.

name: Quadrant Eye
tags: Deep Learning; Digital Health; Telemedicine; AI
one_liner: Breaking new ground in online eyecare.
long_description:
Quadrant Eye is on a mission to improve eyecare access and fight preventable blindness. We're building the next generation eye exam... inside the average American home. 

Our team wants to enable patients' best and most visually rich lives. To this end, we're looking for curious and nimble minds to help us develop the world's first fully online eye exam and ultimately deliver high-quality eyecare at scale.

Some QE highlights:

🐝 We're a team of surgeons, scientists, venture partners, and hackers who mean business.
💸 Our backers include Y Combinator, Khosla Ventures, and the creator of Google Image Search.
🍥 We're a mission-driven company tackling an eye health market worth $USD137B.
🌟 Our core focus is currently the development of patentable deep tech, and our overall vision is to change eyecare for good.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Quadrant Health
one_liner: Analyzing EHR and messaging data to predict disease before it occurs.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Health systems and primary care practices, later outpatient clinics seeking billable care management programs
problem: Clinicians cannot see which patients are heading toward harm because signals sit in unstructured EHR notes and patient messages.
business_model: B2B SaaS to health systems and practices
product_category: Healthcare AI and predictive analytics on EHR and patient messaging data
market_need_then: Health systems were buying predictive analytics, as shown by Clarify Health's 115M raise in March 2021, but no Quadrant specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Quadrant Health appears active, with 2025 and 2026 items about a Stanford Health Care collaboration, a partnership with medent and a blood test integration. Public sources give no verified funding, traction or leadership background, and tracker totals range from 125K to 7M USD, so its outcome cannot be judged beyond survival.

name: Queenly
one_liner: Leading marketplace for formalwear
long_description:
Live on iOS, Android and our web app (queenly.com). 

Queenly is the leading online marketplace for the formalwear industry. We are a Y Combinator company and backed by some of the top VC's in Silicon Valley such as Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), NextView Ventures, The House Fund, and more. The Queenly cofounders were also recently featured on the Forbes 30 Under 30: Art and Style cover for 2022. 

At Queenly, our mission is simple: make every woman look and feel like a queen. We strive to empower women and to feel confidently beautiful in their own skin by providing cutting-edge technology, seamless logistics, white-glove customer service and unique expertise within the industry.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Women and girls buying, selling or renting formalwear (prom, pageant, quinceanera, wedding), plus small stores and designers as supply
problem: Formalwear is worn once and expensive; buyers struggle to find and afford dresses and sellers had no good resale channel.
business_model: Marketplace take rate (sellers keep about 80% of price); dresses over $300 routed through Queenly's own quality assurance
product_category: Consumer formalwear resale marketplace and search engine (iOS, Android, web)
competitors_at_founding: Poshmark; Retail stores and prom shops
market_need_then: Dresses are worn once and cost hundreds of dollars; pandemic-era event cancellations hit the category yet Queenly reported about $500K in sales during the pandemic and listings grew from 50,000 (Feb 2021) to 60,000 (Jul 2021).
outcome_analysis: Queenly grew quickly after YC Winter 2021, raising a $6.3M seed led by a16z in July 2021 and buying Mi Padrino in 2022. A secondary summary of the CTO's February 2025 post-mortem says the economics never worked: formalwear is bought rarely, acquisition was costly, late-2023 revenue was about $0.2M a year against a burn of about $0.27M a month, and a Series A was out of reach, so the company shut down around late 2024 to early 2025.

name: Quest
one_liner: Audio career advice
long_description: Quest is a Q&A app where experts answer questions in short audio clips. We’re starting with career advice, hosting founders and operators from YC and companies like Google, who share intimate and personal stories about work you've never heard before.
regions: Netherlands; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Quicknode
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Crypto / Web3; API
one_liner: Infrastructure and tools to build and scale blockchain applications.
long_description: Quicknode is an enterprise-grade blockchain development platform that helps teams build and scale high-performance onchain applications. Developers get fast and reliable access to over 75 chains, real-time and historical data, automation tools, and a unified suite of APIs. From startups to global enterprises, teams choose Quicknode for consistent performance, predictable pricing, and a platform built for growth.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Blockchain developers, crypto startups and enterprises that need reliable node access and APIs without running their own infrastructure
problem: Running and scaling blockchain nodes is slow, costly and unreliable for application teams.
business_model: Usage based API and subscription plans for RPC endpoints and data tools
product_category: Blockchain infrastructure and developer platform
founder_names: Dmitry Shklovsky; Alex Nabutovsky; Auston Bunsen; Manuel Kreutz
market_need_then: The 2021 crypto and NFT boom drove developer demand; the Series A release cites over 2 billion requests per day, nearly 20,000 developers and about 20x revenue growth since March 2021.
outcome_analysis: Quicknode joined YC in W21 just as the crypto cycle took off, raised a 5.3M seed in May 2021, a 35M Series A in October 2021 after claiming about 20x revenue growth, and a 60M Series B in January 2023 reported at an 800M valuation. It survived the downturn, expanded to over 75 chains and rebranded in 2025, though competition from Alchemy and Infura remains intense.

name: QuotaBook
one_liner: Equity management platform for startups and investors.
long_description:
Founded in 2019 by ex-VCs, Quotabook is a fintech startup building equity management solutions for startups, employees and investors. With Quotabook, founders can streamline equity data and company ownership by managing cap tables as well as running analyses and simulations. Employees are better motivated through stock option features that are aligned with the growth of the company. Investors can track performance of their portfolios with data automatically synced into the platform. Quotabook takes care of all the fuss so that founders, employees and investors can focus on building a business together. 

We are proud to be a startup helping fellow startups boost growth. Find out more about how we simplify equity management for startups around the globe from https://www.quotabook.com/en/
regions: South Korea; East Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Korean startups (freemium cap table, paid by number of stakeholders), plus venture investors who pay by fund AUM and portfolio count
problem: Korean startups and investors managed cap tables, stock options and investor reporting in Excel and older ERP tools, with no standard for securities data.
business_model: B2B SaaS, freemium for startups priced by stakeholders, subscription for investors priced by fund AUM and number of portfolios
product_category: Equity management and cap table software, fintech
founder_names: Andy Choi; Dan Hong; Pilseon Jun
market_need_then: Startups used Excel and older ERP tools for equity records (TechCrunch, August 2022). Korea had a growing venture ecosystem with no dominant local cap table standard.
outcome_analysis: QuotaBook was founded in 2019 by former VCs in Seoul, joined YC in Winter 2021, raised a round in June 2021 and an $11 million round in August 2022, and by then claimed about 40 percent of Korean startups on its cap table product. The domain insight of ex-investors and the switching costs of holding ownership records explain the traction. The company is still active and no outcome beyond growth is public.

name: R2
one_liner: Embedded lending infrastructure
long_description: R2 enables platforms to seamlessly offer capital to their SMB customers in Latin America
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Platforms and marketplaces in Latin America (ride hailing, delivery, payments) that want to offer working capital to their small business merchants and workers
problem: Small businesses in Latin America struggle to get credit, and platforms that hold their sales data lack the underwriting, compliance, servicing and capital markets stack to lend to them.
business_model: Embedded lending infrastructure, revenue-based financing funded by R2 and partner debt, earning loan interest and fees shared with platform partners
product_category: Fintech, embedded lending infrastructure
market_need_then: SMB credit in Latin America was widely described as under-served, and platforms were looking for embedded finance offerings. Specific dated evidence from 2021 was not collected beyond the company's own framing.
outcome_analysis: R2 grew by embedding revenue-based loans inside large platforms such as Uber, Rappi and PayU, raising equity from General Catalyst and Gradient Ventures and a large debt facility to fund loans. It reports more than 200,000 SMBs financed. In October 2025 Ant International made a strategic investment, which the YC page describes as an acquisition, while press releases call it an investment.

name: REGENT
one_liner: All-electric seagliders for fast, affordable regional transportation
long_description:
REGENT is building a new mode of transportation that will redefine regional mobility by 2026. Their first product, the seaglider, is an all-electric, hydrofoiling flying-boat that operates within a wingspan of the water's surface.  By flying low on a cushion of air, seagliders unlock the ability to fly twice as far as an electric aircraft, while being regulated by maritime authorities enabling market entry for a fraction of the cost.
 
REGENT has de-risked seaglider technology with a ¼-scale flying demonstration vehicle. By this summer, REGENT will fly humans on the 15,000 lb (7000kg) first full-scale prototype seaglider, which will be the largest electric-flying machine in history.

By late 2026, REGENT’s customers - airlines and ferry companies – will begin commercial seaglider service on the 12-seat initial product.  A 100 passenger version, already with firm orders, will follow several years later.

In just four years, REGENT has accumulated >$10B in pre-orders (including firm deposits) from airlines and ferry companies around the world.  Currently a team of 100, REGENT is led by MIT-trained, ex-Boeing engineers Billy Thalheimer and Mike Klinker.  REGENT has raised over $100M to date from the likes of Founders Fund, Japan Airlines, Hawaiian Airlines and Lockheed Martin, and is on contract with the US Marine Corps.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Airlines and ferry operators; defense customers (US Marine Corps contracts, REGENT Defense)
problem: Regional coastal transport is slow and costly, and electric aircraft range is short; a wing-in-ground-effect craft regulated as a maritime vessel could fly farther per charge at lower cost.
business_model: Hardware sales of seagliders (Viceroy, Squire, Monarch) to operators with orders and deposits, plus defense contracts
product_category: Electric wing-in-ground-effect seagliders (aerospace and maritime)
market_need_then: Electric aircraft range was limited by batteries; Thalheimer's 2021 paper claimed 180 miles with existing batteries and up to 500 miles with next-generation batteries for coastal routes such as Boston to New York and inter-island Hawaii.
outcome_analysis: REGENT, founded in late 2020 by two MIT aerospace engineers, raised a $9M seed in April 2021, a $60M Series A in October 2023 and a $240M Series B in August 2026 (half debt), and flew a crewed Viceroy for the first time on September 2, 2026. Original timelines slipped (prototype tests were planned for 2023 and service for 2025; manufacturing is now targeted for 2027), but investors, strategic partners, Marine Corps contracts and a built factory show strong momentum while commercial revenue is still ahead.

name: RGI Labs
one_liner: Robust & recursively self-improving general intelligence
long_description:
RGI's mission is to build the world's first robust & recursively self-improving general intelligence. We're building the environment for intelligent systems to be able to develop in such a way where they can: 
- Recursively self-improve across all modifiable planes including architecture, parameters, scaffolding, etc. 
- Continually learn from online experiences and update its parameters while maintaining robustness against catastrophic failures. 
- Use its robust general intelligence of the world to acquire new skills in few or zero shots. 
- Use its world model to predict future states and plan via multi-step rollout. 
- Operate on a learned latent space that is compressed and feature-rich, including a robust latent space for reasoning.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: none identified; research effort aimed at general intelligence, no paying customer stated
problem: Building a system that recursively self-improves, learns continually from online experience, and plans with a learned world model, per the YC description.
business_model: unknown, pre-revenue AI research
product_category: Artificial general intelligence research
market_need_then: No customer demand evidence is stated. The pitch is a research mission rather than a market.
outcome_analysis: RGI Labs is a one-person YC Summer 2021 company with a research mission to build a self-improving general intelligence. No product, customers, funding or press beyond the YC listing was found, so the outcome is unknown. The directory status is Active, but public evidence of progress is absent.

name: RMFG
one_liner: Advanced Contract MFG for fast moving hardware companies
long_description:
RMFG builds and operates advanced, software-defined factories, manufacturing precision parts and metal assemblies for fast-moving hardware teams. 

Our vertically integrated software platform automates quoting, DFM, scheduling, and machine control, and allows us to ship faster and at lower cost than traditional shops. 

We build our own computer vision models, AI agents, and custom software to solve problems inside our manufacturing facility. 

Today we primarily build complex metal assemblies using sheet, tube and CNC milled parts. We plan to continually moving upstream, offering more complex manufacturing services including electro-mechanical assembly. 

We’ve delivered critical parts for companies building custom robots, autonomous farms, PCB factories, weather modification technology, rockets, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware startups needing sheet metal, tube and CNC parts in prototype and small batch
problem: Fast-moving hardware teams wait on slow quotes and long lead times from traditional machine shops.
business_model: Contract manufacturing with instant online quoting, revenue per part
product_category: Software-defined contract manufacturing, sheet metal fabrication
market_need_then: Hardware startups needed quick small-batch metal parts; online manufacturing platforms had raised large rounds by 2019 to 2021, showing spend.
outcome_analysis: RMFG is a Fort Worth sheet metal factory run by a founder with a trades and software background, accepted into YC Summer 2021. Public funding is a reported 4.5 million round in December 2025, four years after the batch, which suggests slow capital-light growth. It serves hardware startups and remains active; no exit or shutdown found.

name: ROGER
one_liner: The Best Way to Sign Contracts Since Handshakes. Roger that.
long_description: Sending and signing contracts should be easy. So why is it that existing eSignature tools are all so janky? The last thing you need is a frustrating eSignature tool. That’s why we’re building Roger — a faster, simpler eSignature. Think of it like what Linear did to Jira.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups, SMBs and scaling teams that send contracts
problem: Existing eSignature tools such as DocuSign are slow and clunky for sending and signing everyday contracts.
business_model: Pay-as-you-go per signed contract (free for 0 to 5, 4 dollars for 6 to 20, 3 dollars above 20), enterprise plans with API
product_category: eSignature and contract management software
market_need_then: Complaints about clunky eSignature tools are the stated premise; the YC pitch compares the opportunity to Linear versus Jira. No quantified demand found.
outcome_analysis: ROGER is a small YC Winter 2021 eSignature startup that sells pay-per-contract signing to startups and SMBs. Public evidence shows a live product into 2026 but no verified funding, no exit and no traction numbers. The segment is crowded with DocuSign and consolidating rivals, so the story so far is a low-visibility, low-capital product.

name: Reclaim Protocol
one_liner: Education, Employment, Loyalty verification. Global & Compliant.
long_description:
Reclaim Protocol provides best in class conversion rates (45%+) on education, employment and retail loyalty verification. Global coverage, secure and privacy preserving.

- Global coverage : Unlike most other vendors we are global by default. No matter where in the world the user is, we can verify.
- It is 100% private : Neither you, nor us, see any private information about the user. So you carry no liabilities. No risk of your database getting hacked. 
- Best in class conversion : We have the highest conversion rates in the industry at 45%+ because users don't have to scramble for their documents to upload.
- AI fraud resistant : All the verifications happen securely using cryptography that even the most advanced models cannot fake.

Total amount raised : $10M (Series A)
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Enterprises verifying education, employment and loyalty data of users
problem: Document-upload verification has poor conversion and privacy/liability risk.
business_model: B2B usage-based verification API (per-verification pricing not stated; company says cost under $1)
product_category: Privacy-preserving identity/credential verification (zkTLS)
market_need_then: YC page claims 45%+ conversion versus document uploads; no 2021-dated demand data gathered.
outcome_analysis: Reclaim Protocol is active with 17 staff and states $10M raised in a Series A, while a May 2022 $8.3M Series A led by Lemniscap was reported under the name Questbook, which one aggregator links to Reclaim. The identity link and the $10M versus $8.3M gap are unreconciled, so the funding story is uncertain and no outcome has occurred yet.

name: Recover
one_liner: Government-funded online addiction treatment
long_description:
Recover provides more effective and affordable addiction treatment via telemedicine. We partner with local governments to save lives and taxpayer dollars.

More than 20 million Americans struggle with addiction, but less than 10% of people who need it receive treatment. For those that do, it usually does not work - only 8% get better. Most of this treatment is funded by governments, and goes to programs that are frequently predatory, and focus more on profit than people.
