name: SolarMente
tags: Solar Power; Climate; Consumer Finance; ClimateTech
one_liner: Home electrification at $0 upfront cost
long_description:
SolarMente helps homeowners in Southern Europe install solar, storage, and heat pumps with zero upfront cost, allowing them to pay through predictable monthly savings. 
Based in Barcelona, we’ve raised $5M from YC, Climate Capital, Soma Capital, Plug & Play, Leonardo DiCaprio, and others.
regions: Spain; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Homeowners in Spain and Southern Europe who want solar, storage and heat pumps without upfront payment
problem: Most households cannot or will not pay thousands upfront for solar panels, so rooftop adoption in sunny Spain lagged.
business_model: Subscription: customer pays a monthly fee (reported as about 40 EUR per month over 20 years) funded by project debt, company owns the installation
product_category: Residential solar as a service and home electrification
market_need_then: Spain had high sun and rising power prices in 2021, but few rooftops with solar; the CEO argued most Spaniards would not pay upfront.
outcome_analysis: SolarMente joined YC in Summer 2021, scaled to a reported 65 staff and about 10M USD ARR, financed with 50M in debt in 2023 and a DiCaprio backed seed in 2024. The YC directory lists it as Inactive, and one Spanish source dated May 2026 reports an insolvency filing in February 2026. No source gives the cause, so it is not public and failure factors are left empty.

name: Solo
one_liner: We help people resolve debt.
long_description: Solo, formerly SoloSuit, helps Americans resolve debt. People use our first product, SoloSuit to respond to debt lawsuits and create other legal documents. Then they use SoloSettle to connect with the collector and settle the debt. We're targeting the $35B debt resolution market.
all_locations: Salt Lake City, UT, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers in the US who have been sued over unpaid debt or who want to settle it, with collectors paying through settlement flows
problem: Most people sued by debt collectors never respond and lose by default. Solo gives a self-help way to answer the lawsuit and to negotiate a settlement without calling the collector.
business_model: Freemium consumer legal self-help (SoloSuit) plus a commission on settled debt (SoloSettle)
product_category: Consumer legal tech and debt resolution
market_need_then: The company's pitch is a roughly $35B debt resolution market and that debt lawsuits are often lost by default because defendants do not respond (YC description). A 2020 commercial launch followed an academic version in 2018 per one aggregator article.
outcome_analysis: Solo is still active with about 25 people. It raised a small $2M round in August 2024 after the YC batch and says that moves it closer to a Series A, so it has not shown venture scale growth in public sources. The move from a free lawsuit answer tool to a commission based settlement marketplace is the main strategic change. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff was found, and the CFPB dismissal story in search results concerns a different company, Solo Funds.

name: Somos
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: Internet for the urban developing world.
long_description: We use cutting-edge radio tech operating in unlicensed spectrum to rapidly build fiber-quality networks (1Gbps ) in the urban developing world.
regions: Colombia; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Households and businesses in Medellin and Bogota in Colombia, with enterprise customers such as Mercado Libre and Rappi named by the company
problem: Fixed internet in urban Latin America is slow, shared and expensive. Somos builds its own network to deliver dedicated high speed connections.
business_model: Residential and enterprise ISP subscriptions
product_category: Fixed broadband ISP

outcome_analysis: Somos kept building after YC and raised a $13.4M seed in 2023, an $18M Series A in 2025 and a $40M Series B in March 2026, with reported scale of about 70,000 homes, 900 employees and a plan to enter Mexico. Capital intensive network building is funded in stages as subscribers grow. It faces much larger incumbents, so its outcome depends on keeping unit economics and the network ahead of them. No shutdown or acquisition was found.

name: Soraban
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Robotic Process Automation; SaaS
one_liner: AI tax workflow platform for accounting firms
long_description: AI-native Tax workflow Platform for accounting firms from client request to delivery. We raised $18m from patient investors who are onboard to help us grow and serve tens of thousands of accounting firms. We're not in this market to grow fast and fail fast. We're in this to build something that'll last decades.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Accounting and tax preparation firms, about 350 firms per the company website
problem: Tax firms lose time chasing client documents, preparing workpapers and delivering returns. Soraban automates collection, preparation and delivery.
business_model: B2B SaaS for accounting firms, pricing not public
product_category: Tax workflow software
market_need_then: The company claims tax firms need less manual client chasing and prep work. Dated 2021 demand evidence was not found beyond the company's own descriptions.
outcome_analysis: Soraban is active with about 50 people and over 350 firms as customers per its site. It announced a Series A led by Altos Ventures in April 2025 and shipped an AI preparation product in 2026. Funding amounts are only partly public, so growth is hard to judge. No shutdown or acquisition was found. AI tooling after 2023 appears to have helped its positioning.

name: Spark Studio
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Education; Generative AI; eLearning; AI
one_liner: The most magical personal Voice-Led AI English Learning Buddy for Kids
long_description:
Meet Sparky, a fun and quirky AI buddy in the avatar of a friendly fox who kids can just speak with to build fluency and confidence with English speaking. 
Powered by Generative AI, and made magical with child-appropriate experience, features and topics, Sparky brings a whole world of knowledge and a judgement-free environment for kids to become comfortable with speaking English. 

142 countries (outside English dominant countries) mandate English learning as part of the national education policy. These kids have exposure to English but feel underconfident and embarrassed to speak. The biggest problem across the classes and books they get, is the lack of real conversational practice. With AI, we're making this affordable accessible and enjoyable for kids across the world. 

We're a passionate team of educators with over 30 years of combined experience in building education products for kids and have held leadership positions are India's biggest education companies - Byju's and LEAD.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Parents of children in non English dominant countries who want conversational English practice, originally parents of 6 to 15 year olds buying online extracurricular classes in India
problem: Kids learn English in school but lack real speaking practice and feel embarrassed to speak. The product offers a voice led AI buddy for judgement free practice.
business_model: Consumer subscription, originally paid online extracurricular classes
product_category: Consumer edtech
founder_names: Anushree Goenka; Namita Goel; Kaustubh Khade; Jyothika Sahajanandan
market_need_then: In 2021 press the CEO described the extracurricular market in India as fragmented and unstructured, and Entrepreneur cited a $50B figure and the National Education Policy. The YC page says 142 countries mandate English learning.
outcome_analysis: Spark Studio raised a 2021 seed from Better Capital and joined YC in Summer 2021, then moved from live extracurricular classes to an AI English tutor, still staffed by an education leadership team from BYJU'S and LEAD. It remains active with about 27 people. Public data on revenue, later rounds or exit was not found, so its trajectory is unknown. The Indian edtech downturn is mentioned by a 2023 Forbes India piece listed on its YC page but that article was not opened.

name: Spline
one_liner: Design and collaborate in multiple dimensions.
long_description: Easily create and publish 3D for multiple platforms. Build and iterate fast with production-ready results.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Designers and product teams who add interactive 3D to websites and apps; free tier for individuals, paid plans for teams
problem: Creating web ready 3D needed heavy tools like Blender or Cinema 4D and developer help. Spline offers a browser based collaborative 3D editor.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription with team and enterprise plans
product_category: 3D design tool
market_need_then: Designers were adding 3D to web projects but found existing tools hard to learn; a Figma for 3D framing appears in commentary that is not clearly dated to 2021. YC accepted it in Winter 2021 and NXTP led a seed in April 2021.
outcome_analysis: Spline grew from a 2021 seed led by NXTP into a freemium 3D design platform, raising about $15M in 2023 and a $10M Series A led by Third Point Ventures in 2024. It stayed lean at about 25 people and kept shipping, including Spline V2 and AI agent support in 2026. Browser delivery and a free tier drove designer adoption. No acquisition or layoff was found.

name: Spoken

Spoken is a website where users compare buying options for the exact same product across multiple stores. We help our users never overpay online.

name: Spokn
one_liner: AI-powered video platform for Internal Comms and HR teams
long_description:
Spokn makes it easy for People and Comms teams to make videos starring their own employees and leaders - no editing skills or special equipment necessary.  In minutes, you can create videos that feel as engaging as TikTok, and share them anywhere: Slack/Teams, your LMS, intranet, careers page, or job offer emails.  

Companies like InterContinental Hotels, Coinbase, Twilio, Opendoor, Udemy, SiriusXM, Gong and more use Spokn to create engaging videos for their learning & development, internal comms, recognition, DEI and employer branding.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: People, HR and internal communications teams at mid to large companies
problem: Internal communication through email, Slack and Zoom is ignored. Spokn made audio podcasts for work, later short employee led video, to engage employees.

product_category: Internal communications and employee video

market_need_then: AlleyWatch and TechCrunch (May 2021) describe remote work driving a need for engaging internal communications. TechCrunch lists customers such as Podium, ShipBob, Cedar, Mixpanel, ServiceNow and Superhuman.
outcome_analysis: Spokn raised a $4M NEA led seed just before the Winter 2021 Demo Day after pivoting from consumer audio to enterprise internal audio, and later moved to employee video. It is active with about 20 people and named customers such as Coinbase and Twilio on its YC page, but no later round, acquisition or shutdown was found. Its outcome is unclear from public data.

name: Sproutfi
one_liner: Latin Americas' first investing social network.  Learn. Share. Invest.
long_description:
We're on a mission to make investing in the US markets accessible and fair to everyone in Latin America.  Our social features make it seamless for investors to mingle, share investment ideas and learn from each other.   We make it super easy to invest in thousands of US stocks & ETFs, with as little as a $1 USD, no account minimums, and no fees.  

Our team is composed of highly experienced builders hailing from Goldman Sachs, E*Trade Financial, Nubank, ING, Wise...
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Retail investors in Latin America, starting with Brazil, who want to buy US stocks and ETFs cheaply and learn from other investors
problem: Latin Americans had little access to US markets with small amounts and low fees, and investing advice was fragmented, so the founders paired fractional US investing with a social layer to learn and share ideas.
business_model: Brokerage platform with fractional US stocks and ETFs from 1 dollar and no account minimums or fees, monetized later through the brokerage relationship and services
product_category: Fintech, social investing and brokerage app
market_need_then: Brazilians were already buying US stocks through Avenue, Stake, Passfolio and Nomad, which showed demand, and the founders expected multiple winners. Brazilian launch depended on legal steps in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Sproutfi, led by a former early Nubank data scientist, raised about 5.7 million dollars in 2021 to offer fractional US investing and a social network for Latin Americans, in a market where Avenue, Stake, Passfolio and Nomad were already established. It bought Passfolio's Brazilian client book in 2022, then combined with Vest, whose CEO retained leadership and later phased out the Sprout name, which he said Brazilian users did not understand.

name: SpruceID
tags: GovTech; Crypto / Web3; Identity; Privacy; Infrastructure
one_liner: SpruceID lets users control their data across the web.
long_description: SpruceID lets users control their data across the web. Instead of people signing into platforms, we imagine platforms should sign into people’s data vaults. We implement this pattern into digital wallet ecosystems for governments, enterprises, and blockchains. We believe that architectures that enable individual autonomy in the digital world are necessary for free societies and dynamic economies to thrive.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Governments (such as state DMVs), enterprises and blockchain ecosystems that need digital identity, wallets and verification
problem: People sign in to platforms that own their data. Spruce builds standards based identity and credential tools so users control their data, now sold mainly to governments.
business_model: B2B and B2G software, services and open source tooling for digital identity
product_category: Decentralized identity and digital credentials
market_need_then: Spruce worked with the Ethereum Foundation and ENS on Sign-In with Ethereum starting in September 2021, showing demand from the web3 ecosystem. Later government demand came through mobile driver's license programs such as California's.
outcome_analysis: Spruce raised a $7.5M seed in late 2021 and a $34M Series A led by a16z in April 2022, then shifted emphasis from web3 sign in to government digital identity, with the California DMV mobile driver's license program as a flagship reference. It is active with about 25 people on the YC page. No later round was found, no acquisition or shutdown reported, and the shift to public sector work appears to be what sustained it.

No shutdown post, founder post-mortem, funding record or acquisition was found, so the cause of failure is not public and no failure factors are assigned.

name: Stacksi
one_liner: Automated Answers to Security Questionnaires
long_description:
Stacksi helps companies automate the process of answering enterprise security questionnaires so they can close deals faster and save their best engineers’ time for more strategic projects.
Salespeople, CTOs, and CEOs of fast-growing enterprise startups can upload security questionnaires into our system. If the company already has written security policies, they can upload those documents, too. From there, Stacksi parses their documents, identifies gaps in their security policies vs. standards, and helps them establish a successful security program. 
Ultimately, we will help them 1) automate completion of security questionnaires, 2) quickly get through enterprise security audits and 3) improve their security posture.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Salespeople, CTOs and CEOs of fast-growing startups that must answer enterprise security questionnaires to close deals
problem: Answering buyer security questionnaires eats engineering time and slows enterprise deals; companies also lack clear written security policies.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Security questionnaire automation / compliance
market_need_then: Enterprise buyers routinely sent long security questionnaires to startups, and the YC description frames them as a drag on salespeople and engineers. No quantified spend figure was found.
outcome_analysis: Stacksi stayed tiny, a four person team with no verified institutional funding, and was bought by the trust center company SafeBase in September 2023 for undisclosed terms. The product fit SafeBase's roadmap, so the outcome reads as a small tuck in acquisition of a niche feature rather than a standalone success or a clear failure. The founder later moved to a product role at Ashby.

name: Stardex
one_liner: AI native ATS + CRM for executive search firms
long_description: Stardex is an AI native ATS and CRM executive firms and professional recruiting firms. We are AI first designed specifically for modern recruiting firms. It has a powerful client collaboration feature that helps you execute searches faster with clients. It also streamlines your searches by automating repetitive tasks, allowing you to dedicate more time to building meaningful relationships.﻿
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Boutique and mid-market executive search and professional recruiting firms, about 100 firms per the company site
problem: Search firms run on legacy ATS and CRM tools. Stardex offers an AI native system for candidate search, pipelines, outreach and client collaboration.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Recruiting ATS and CRM
market_need_then: The company says search firms are stuck on legacy tools. A job post says it targets firms moving off legacy platforms. Dated 2021 demand evidence was not found; the AI native product pitch is a later repositioning.
outcome_analysis: Stardex is a small, active team of about 8 to 9 that says it is cash flow positive, SOC 2 Type II certified and used by about 100 search firms, with customers migrated from Bullhorn, Thrive and Loxo. Funding is not publicly confirmed. The founders came from an earlier YC company, Dots, and built Stardex on search industry pain. No acquisition or shutdown found. The company site is the main source for traction, so the claims are unverified.

name: Stayflexi
one_liner: Operating System for Hotels and Vacation Rentals
long_description:
Stayflexi is a revolutionary platform designed to simplify hotel and vacation rental operations, while increasing revenues from unsold rooms and amenities. By harnessing the power of automation, Stayflexi eliminates the need for manual processes and provides a seamless, positive customer experience for guests. 

Founded by computer science majors from Carnegie Mellon and Cornell, Stayflexi was born out of the need to solve the problems experienced by hosts and travelers. With Stayflexi, you can rest assured that your guests will be given the best possible experience and that you will be able to maximize profits on your unsold rooms.

Stayflexi platform is helping over 3000 hotels in 16 different countries and growing rapidly.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent hotels, resorts and vacation rental operators, many in India
problem: Hotels lose revenue on unsold rooms under rigid 2 pm check-in and 11 am check-out, and run on fragmented manual tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for PMS, booking engine, channel manager and POS
product_category: Hotel and vacation rental property management system
founder_names: Venkatesh Sakamuri; Preetam Mohan Shetty; Krishna Sasank Talasila
market_need_then: Hotels hit by COVID-19 in 2020 needed new revenue from unsold rooms and flexible stays. The founders say the problem came from their own travel experience.
outcome_analysis: Stayflexi raised a 1.6M seed in June 2021 and, per its YC page, grew to a claimed 3,000 hotels in 16 countries with a team of 58. No later round, exit or layoff was found, and funding may be incomplete. The company appears to have grown capital efficiently, but with no sourced traction figures beyond its own claims the factors are left empty.

name: Stepful
one_liner: Online Training for Healthcare Jobs
long_description: Stepful trains people with a high school education in 4 months and places them into healthcare jobs. Healthcare is the fastest growing industry in the US accounting for 40% of all jobs added including medical assistants, nursing assistants, and phlebotomists.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: High school graduates seeking entry-level healthcare jobs (self-pay or employer and health system sponsored) and healthcare employers needing trained staff
problem: Entry-level healthcare roles such as medical assistant and phlebotomist are in short supply, while traditional trade schools and community colleges are slow and costly. Stepful trains and places people in about four months.
business_model: Tuition and employer or health system sponsored training with job placement and clinical partner network
product_category: Online healthcare workforce training and placement
founder_names: Carl Madi; Tressia Hobeika; Edoardo Serra

It rode a persistent healthcare staffing shortage and used employer and health system partnerships to broaden demand beyond individual tuition. An aggregator reports layoffs in May 2026, which is unverified and is not confirmed by a primary source.

name: Stipop
one_liner: Monetization platform for character creators
long_description:
Stipop is a monetization platform for character creators, or simply put, Patreon for character creators. We help independent character IP owners generate revenue directly from their audience with fun, dynamic features. 

Previously, Stipop was a sticker platform with 5,000 sticker creators, and 250K stickers and provided stickers to Canva, Teams, Google, and Adobe. We also provide sticker API and SDK to help chat apps improve revenue and user engagement.

Stipop has been invested by Snap (through Yellow Accelerator), YC, Translink Investment, Strong Ventures, Next Ventures, and more.
all_locations: Seoul, Seoul, South Korea; Santa Monica, CA, USA
regions: South Korea; United States of America; East Asia; America / Canada
target_customer: Chat and video apps needing sticker content (API and SDK buyers), and independent character IP creators who monetize through the platform
problem: Chat apps wanted rich sticker content without building it, and independent sticker artists had no good way to earn from their characters. Stipop later narrowed to a Patreon-like monetization platform for character creators.
business_model: Sticker API and SDK licensing to apps plus creator monetization platform (revenue share)
product_category: Sticker platform and creator monetization
market_need_then: Chat apps competed on expressive features and stickers drive engagement, especially in Asia. Stipop reported customers such as Canva, Teams, Google and Adobe using its stickers.
outcome_analysis: Stipop is still listed as active with 8 people. It was backed by Snap's Yellow accelerator and YC but no later priced round is found. It faced free incumbents in Giphy and Tenor and pivoted from stickers to creator monetization, so the story is a stalled early stage company rather than a clear success or failure.

name: Stoke Space
one_liner: Seamless mobility to, through, and from space. It starts with 100%…
long_description:
Nova: Radically improving access to and from orbit. We’re unlocking the space economy by harnessing the power of full and rapid reusability with Nova, our 100% reusable rocket. Nova offers affordable access to, through, and from space with a 20x reduced cost to orbit.

Our reusable upper-stage vehicle delivers on-demand access to any orbit at any time. Its unmatched capabilities enable dynamic space operations, including capture, reposition, long-dwell operations, and return of assets, as well as space cargo and logistics missions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Satellite operators, constellation builders, and civil and defense launch customers needing orbital access
problem: Launch is expensive because rockets are only partly reusable. Stoke is building a fully and rapidly reusable two stage vehicle, Nova, to cut cost to orbit.
business_model: Launch services per mission
product_category: Reusable orbital launch vehicle
competitors_at_founding: SpaceX; Rocket Lab; Relativity Space; Firefly Aerospace
market_need_then: Satellite constellation demand and the success of reusable boosters showed launch demand and cost pressure at the time of the Winter 2021 batch.
outcome_analysis: Stoke has raised on a steady cadence from a 2021 seed through a reported 1B raise in September 2026, driven by founders with Blue Origin engine experience and a clear technical thesis of full reuse. It has not yet reached orbit, so the outcome rests on execution risk and capital needs rather than market need.

name: Storylane
one_liner: Build Interactive Product Demo in 10 mins for SaaS companies
long_description: Storylane enables marketing and sales teams to create and share interactive product demos in 10 min. Prospective buyers can self-experience the demos without talking to sales. Our no-code platform allows teams (without any engineering help) to capture, personalize, add guides and publish a demo. These Demos can be embedded on websites, email campaigns or sales followups.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Marketing, sales and solutions teams at B2B SaaS companies that want self serve interactive product demos
problem: Buyers want to try a product before talking to sales, and engineering heavy sandboxes or video demos are slow and expensive to make.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription tiers by seats and demos, with an enterprise tier
product_category: Interactive product demo and buyer experience platform
market_need_then: In 2021 SaaS buying moved toward self serve and product led evaluation, and the company pitched demos built in ten minutes without engineering help.

It added an AI website agent called RepX in the 2025 and 2026 period. Funding is not credibly documented, so growth may be capital efficient, but traction figures are the company's own and the category is crowded with Navattic and other tools.

name: Stownest
one_liner: Flexible On-Demand Storage Space for Household, SMEs & Travellers.
long_description:
Valet self-storage solution for your personal storage needs. Be it household storage or seasonal belongings, we will pick them up and store them in our facility. You get it back when you need it. 

Service built on technology and strong customer experience fundamentals.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Urban households and small businesses in Bengaluru needing short or long term storage with doorstep pickup
problem: Urban Indian homes are small and cluttered, and traditional storage and movers are unorganised with no standard of quality or security. Stownest picks up, barcodes, stores and returns items on request.
business_model: Pay per space used valet storage subscription plus packers and movers services
product_category: Valet self-storage and moving services
founder_names: Sudhindra Subbarao; Ramesh Chincholi; Amieth Kumar; Srinivasa Murthy
market_need_then: A 2019 YourStory profile reported the Bengaluru market was served by unorganised movers with no quality or security benchmark, and Stownest had 15,000 sq ft of leased warehouse space then.
outcome_analysis: Stownest is active with about 80 people per the YC page and operates valet storage in Bengaluru. Public funding is thin: an aggregator shows only about $130K including YC, and Inc42 describes it as bootstrapped, so there is no evidence of institutional rounds. The story is a small operations heavy business with limited public data.

name: StrideQ
tags: Food Service Robots & Machines; SaaS; E-commerce
one_liner: Automated phone ordering system for restaurants
long_description:
StrideQ (formerly SliceQ) is the automated phone ordering system for restaurants which ensures no missed calls and no missed orders. Surprisingly, 33% of restaurant customers still prefer ordering via phone calls, but front desk staff is often busy and revenue is lost.

After enabling StrideQ our customers have increased their sales by over 10%, even while dealing with staff shortages in covid times.

Phone ordering is our wedge to become the point of sale system for all restaurants. StrideQ also streamlines dine-in and online orders in one single system. It helps to run restaurants more easily by effectively managing operations during weekend peak rush.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Mountain View, CA, USA; Remote

name: Striga
one_liner: Compliant Crypto and Banking Infrastructure
long_description: Striga is building infrastructure for digital assets and financial services as a single set of APIs doing the heavy lifting of security and regulatory compliance. Striga's customers include early stage FinTech's, Web3 innovators, Banking Institutions and Crypto Exchanges utilizing services spanning the range of Crypto Custody, Trading, Card Issuing and Banking. Building a crypto business today is a highly regulated space unlike a few years ago and maintaining a compliance program and building technology presents a huge barrier to entry for startups and mid-size businesses alike and the Striga platform solves the problem with a single set of APIs and a single contract to deliver services to 30 countries today.

problem: Building a compliant crypto and banking product requires licences and a compliance program that most startups and mid-size firms cannot afford to build.
business_model: Usage-based API with a single contract covering regulated services
product_category: Crypto and banking infrastructure API
market_need_then: Crypto businesses in Europe needed banking access and regulatory cover as rules tightened; Striga's own pitch says compliance had become a large barrier compared with a few years earlier. No independent demand data was found.

It reached 30 countries and a team of about 14 and was acquired by Lightspark in October 2025 for undisclosed terms, so the outcome is a licence and team driven acquisition.

name: Strive Math
one_liner: Online Coding School for Kids 8-16
long_description:
Strive Math is an online coding & math school for kids (8-16). We help students start and commit to their coding and math journeys by making the subjects fun and exciting. We focus, above all else, on making the process of learning joyful.

- Our mission is to make education more joyful and meaningful. We teach coding, math and custom STEM courses to kids aged 8 to 16, and build the tools to support teachers to deliver engaging learning experiences.
- We believe we can only make education joyful if we ourselves are joyful, so creating a fun and exciting work environment is one of our core values. We’re a remote-first company with teachers and employees from South Africa, Singapore, India, the USA, and the Philippines.
- We’re a well-funded startup backed by YCombinator and early investors of Spotify and Facebook.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote

It sells a service that larger rivals in live coding classes also offered and shows no clear breakout, so it remains a small, capital light stage company rather than a clear success or failure.

name: StudyStream
one_liner: 24/7 video platform & online community for students to study together
long_description:
StudyStream is a video platform & online community that allows students to study with others from around the world 24/7 and in real time. It brings accountability & motivation to the students from over 180 countries who study with us daily.  

We have helped over 3 million students be more productive & motivated, while also feeling less isolated. Our mission is to create a global community of students who can motivate each other to succeed.

Public information after 2021 is thin and monetization is unclear, so later outcome is unverified; it is still listed as active.

name: Sully

long_description: Sully.ai is printing labor for health systems by building a team of autonomous AI agents to run the entire hospital operations. The autonomous agents run like ClawdBot in the background (Receptionists, Medical Consultant, Triage Nurse, Scribes, Coders) collaborate to execute entire workflows. Replacing the $800B labor doing all the manual work at hospitals.

name: Supadock
one_liner: Making logistics facilities run themselves
long_description:
Supadock runs the day-to-day operations of logistics facilities with AI workers. We're not a software tool. We own the work.

We start at the gate, where someone has to check in every truck driver, verify their paperwork and decide who gets in, around the clock. Most facilities pay a security agency to do it by hand: it's expensive, error-prone and a major opening for cargo theft. Our AI workers do it 24/7 using the cameras, intercoms and systems a facility already has, at a fraction of the cost, and we've handled 12,000 check-ins since June.

The gate is where we start. Facilities that run themselves is where we're going.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Freight and logistics facilities (warehouses, yards, distribution sites) that pay security agencies for gate check-in and monitoring

business_model: AI workers sold as an operated service for facility operations (the company says it owns the work rather than selling a software tool); pricing not public
product_category: AI agents for logistics facility operations (gate check-in and site monitoring)

outcome_analysis: Supadock is listed as Active with a team of one. The YC page gives a founding year of 2025 despite the Winter 2021 batch tag and ties the founder to Javelin Robotics, whose legal name appears on the site, so the history between 2021 and 2025 is unclear. The company claims 12,000 gate check-ins since June and sells AI workers for gate operations. No funding, exit or failure was found, so the story is early and unproven.

name: Superwall
one_liner: Subscription infrastructure & paywall experimentation for mobile apps
long_description:
Superwall is a complete, standalone subscription platform for consumer mobile and web apps — backend infrastructure (entitlements, purchase APIs with server-side receipt validation, standardized webhooks, real-time revenue analytics, direct SQL access to subscription data) together with a no-code paywall and experimentation engine, and first-class tooling for AI coding agents. Superwall manages $1.6B+ in annual subscription revenue across 10,000+ apps. The infrastructure layer is free at any scale; the only meter on the platform is revenue that converts through a Superwall-rendered paywall — subscriptions sold anywhere else are never billed.

**Standalone backend:** The highest-revenue apps on Superwall like Cal AI — run their **entire subscription stack on Superwall alone: no second backend, no other subscription platform underneath**. Entitlement state is computed server-side from App Store Server Notifications V2 and Google Play Real-Time Developer Notifications, delivered by Apple and Google directly to Superwall. The largest single app runs **$43.7M ARR entirely on Superwall**; the top 10 together represent $134M+ in annual subscription revenue. Apps that previously ran a different subscription backend complete an automated migration — subscription history, entitlement state, webhook configuration — and run on Superwall alone from then on; imported subscribers are never billed.

**Pricing:** The subscription infrastructure — entitlements, receipt validation, webhooks, analytics, SQL access — is free at any scale, with no revenue threshold and no per-event fees. The paywall product is free up to $10k/month in paywall-attributed revenue, then 1% of paywall-attributed revenue, and only that revenue: an app with $50k/month in subscriptions and no Superwall paywalls in use pays $0/month for the entire platform, and revenue the platform didn't help earn is never billed. Compared with charging a percentage of all subscription revenue, the difference is the base, not the rate.

**Coverage:** Apple App Store, Google Play, and Stripe — including web checkout, external browser checkout from iOS paywalls (App2Web), and products from any external billing system via Custom Store Products. Monetization models: auto-renewing subscriptions, free trials and intro offers, one-time purchases, lifetime unlocks, and consumables. SDKs: iOS & Apple platforms, Android, React Native, Flutter, Expo, Unity, and Web — all open source on [GitHub](https://github.com/superwall). Not just for engineers: growth, product, support, and data teams run monetization from the dashboard, analytics, and SQL access day to day.

**What Superwall does not do:** It does not process payments — Apple, Google, and Stripe do. It does not run virtual-currency or coin-ledger systems, does not track ad revenue, and does not support Amazon or Roku storefronts. For consumer subscription apps on iOS, Android, and the web, it covers the monetization surface end to end.

**Experimentation:** Superwall's published research spans 100M+ analyzed paywall views and 4,500+ paywall A/B tests: multi-page onboarding paywalls convert 37% better than single-page (40M+ opens measured), Cal AI ran 123 experiments and grew monthly revenue 3x+ in 10 months, Planner 5D lifted revenue per user 83% through price testing. Build, target, test, and ship paywalls from the dashboard with no app release.

**Retention:** Free trial reminders, cancellation and decline surveys, transaction-abandon recovery offers, win-back paywalls targeted by subscription state, Apple Retention Messaging on the iOS cancel screen, automated refund protection, and a per-customer timeline for support.

**Agent tooling:** Open-source agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents; an editor MCP server for building live paywalls from the terminal; an embedded dashboard CLI; and direct SQL access to subscription data via the Query API.

name: Suplias
one_liner: We enable FMCG distributors in Africa buy inventory on credit
long_description:
Suplias helps FMCG manufacturers in Africa receive payments and finance inventory purchases of their distributors using a mobile app called Obtainly.

We launched in Nigeria, where we have been growing revenue by 32% month over month for the last 11 months

Our founding team has a combined 25+ years of experience in supply chain and ecommerce having worked for Procter & Gamble, Pepsi Co, Gap and Jumia, the #1 ecommerce company in Africa.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote

business_model: Inventory financing and payments for distributors through the Obtainly app (earlier a B2B marketplace); fee structure not public
product_category: B2B fintech: supply chain payments and inventory credit

Disclosed funding is small and inconsistent across aggregators, and no exit, failure or later priced round was found. It faced much better funded Nigerian rivals already moving into credit.

name: Svix
one_liner: Enterprise ready webhooks service, open-source and in the cloud
long_description:
Svix is the enterprise ready and open source webhooks service.

Webhooks are a pain. Developers need to worry about deliverability, retries, monitoring and security. All of which are different for webhooks compared to the rest of the stack. We turn all of that into a simple API call.

Svix is sending billions of webhooks for customers both large (Fortune 500) and small (startups), and is backed by Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Aleph, and founders and CTOs of companies such as Github, PagerDuty, Segment and Lookout.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software companies, from startups to Fortune 500, that need to send webhooks to their own customers
problem: Sending webhooks reliably needs retries, deliverability, security and monitoring that differ from the rest of the stack, and teams keep rebuilding it.
business_model: Usage and tier based SaaS and open-source core with a hosted cloud
product_category: Developer infrastructure: webhook sending service
market_need_then: Founder said customers of his previous company repeatedly asked for webhooks and a friend asked about them in a Slack community, showing recurring demand; Aleph described webhooks as the nervous system of SaaS.
outcome_analysis: Svix started as Diahook, took a 2.6 million dollar pre-seed in November 2021 from YC and Aleph, and raised a round led by a16z in February 2023. It lists customers such as Brex, Twilio, PagerDuty and Vanta, claims billions of webhooks delivered, and published the Standard Webhooks spec. It is still Active with a small team and no exit. Its success rests on a clear developer pain, an open source go-to-market and low competition at the start.

name: Swadesi Way
one_liner: Healthy organic food that creates a positive impact
long_description:
At Swadesi Way, we’re building an organic food brand movement that connects us back to real food. A few things set us apart:

1. We source exclusively from organic small farmer collectives. No traders.

2. We operate with capped margins: 60% to farmers, 30% to ops, 10% for overheads, ensuring fair value distribution 

3. We practice radical transparency: customers know where their food comes from, how it’s priced, and how much the farmer earns
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Urban Indian households in Delhi NCR and online buyers who want organic staples with traceable sourcing
problem: Consumers cannot tell where organic food comes from or how much farmers earn, and small organic farmers lose margin to traders.
business_model: Direct to consumer organic grocery brand sourcing from farmer collectives with capped margins (60 percent to farmers, 30 percent operations, 10 percent overheads, per the YC page)
product_category: Organic food D2C brand
market_need_then: YourStory estimated the Indian organic food market at about 1 billion dollars in 2020 growing at 20 to 25 percent a year; IMARC and EMR gave 815 and 849.5 million dollars for 2020.
outcome_analysis: Swadesi Way joined YC Winter 2021, originally under the name Leap Club, and now sells organic staples sourced from five farmer collectives with a stated 60 percent share to farmers. It is listed as Active with 9 staff. Public funding is limited to YC money and a small crowdfunding campaign seen only in aggregator snippets, and no exit or failure was found, so the outcome is unproven rather than clearly good or bad.

name: SwiftSku
tags: Fintech; SaaS; B2B; Analytics; Retail Tech
one_liner: Management and analytics software for convenience stores
long_description:
SwiftSku connects the $650B convenience store industry with management and analytics. 

SwiftSku’s app connects to point of sales at convenience stores in real time, enabling owners to remotely manage and monitor their stores. We take the guesswork out of running a convenience store with predictive analytics, dashboards, and reports.

SwiftSku's CEO, Mit Patel, grew up managing the inventory, pricebook, and reporting of his family’s convenience stores, and, when vendors would come by, he’d bridge the language barrier as a translator.  More than 85% of independent convenience stores are owned by Indian families like Mit’s.

Solving convenience store owners' pains of today leads to SwiftSku's greater vision of optimizing the supply chain, facilitating a retailer agnostic consumer to brand relationship, and providing real time insights to brands and retailers.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Independent convenience store owners in the US
problem: Independent c-store owners lack real-time visibility into transactions, pricing and scan data across their stores and cannot easily manage fuel prices, loyalty and brand data exchange.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for store owners (Basic and Standard plans) plus a hardware module and brand data exchange
product_category: Convenience store back-office software and analytics
market_need_then: Independent c-stores lacked remote monitoring and brand scan data programs; the founder grew up in his family's convenience stores and the company reported 250+ customers by June 2021.
outcome_analysis: SwiftSku was conceived in August 2019 by two Auburn students, one raised in his family's convenience stores. It won the 2021 Rice Business Plan Competition with a 350,000 dollar investment, joined YC Winter 2021 and reports 35 staff and thousands of customers on its site. It is Active with no exit and no priced venture round found, so funding is only partly known. Skupos was a better funded rival in the same niche.

name: Swipe
tags: Fintech; SaaS; B2B; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Super AI Accountant for SMBs
long_description: Swipe is a simple billing and payments app for small businesses in India. We make it easy for local businesses to invoice their customers over WhatsApp. With Swipe, businesses can send a WhatsApp message with a link that allows their customers to pay instantly with a variety of payment methods.

problem: Small Indian businesses need simple GST-compliant billing, invoice sharing and payment collection without complex accounting software.
business_model: Freemium SaaS; free mobile app with limited features and paid desktop plans of INR 1,299 to 2,499 as of February 2022 (Inc42)
product_category: SMB billing, invoicing and accounting software (India)
market_need_then: India's SMBs were adopting GST invoicing and WhatsApp commerce; Inc42 cited rivals at millions of users, showing established demand, while Swipe had about 10K dollars ARR in early 2022.

It is Active with no exit. Revenue figures for fiscal 2024 and 2025 are unverified. It entered a crowded market with myBillBook and Vyapar far ahead, so success relied on freemium growth and WhatsApp distribution.

name: Synder
one_liner: Financial data your AI can actually trust
long_description:
Synder reconciles every channel and processor into one ledger that ties to the bank – every fee, refund, payout, and chargeback matched to the order behind it.

Everything downstream inherits that. Your close, your margin questions, and any AI you point at your finances all read the same numbers – and every one of them traces back to the transaction that produced it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Online sellers, subscription businesses and their accountants and bookkeepers
problem: Sales, fees, refunds, payouts and taxes from many payment processors and sales channels must be reconciled by hand into accounting ledgers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for sync and reconciliation (Synder Sync) plus revenue recognition (Synder RevRec, launched 2024)
product_category: Ecommerce accounting and bookkeeping automation
market_need_then: Ecommerce growth and many payment processors made manual reconciliation painful; the company said it processed about 1 billion dollars of 2020 volume for several thousand companies (own press release, unverified).
outcome_analysis: Synder, run by CloudBusiness Inc., was already selling to several thousand ecommerce companies before YC Summer 2021, raised a 2 million dollar late seed in June 2021 and added revenue recognition in 2024 and NetSuite and AI features in 2025. It is Active with no later priced round found and says it serves thousands of businesses with strong marketplace reviews. It grew from a crowded niche with a modest raise, suggesting capital efficiency, but no Series A appears.

name: TAG
one_liner: TAG is the First Digital Bank (Chime/Revolut/N26) for Pakistan
long_description: TAG is setting new standards and changing the way Pakistan banks by building a digital bank for the masses, with an aim to encompass the entire financial life of users, from basic banking such as bank account and Visa Debit card to employer payrolls, salary advances, savings, and neo-brokerage in future.
regions: Pakistan; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Tablevibe
one_liner: Direct Ordering Software for Restaurants
long_description:
We help restaurants launch their own online ordering store and sell directly to customers.

This reduces costs by up to 80% compared to traditional delivery apps, grows sales, and gives restaurants full ownership of their customer data.

Our software automatically books riders for on-demand delivery at low, distance-based rates.

Curious to learn more? Book a demo at tablevibe.co/democall.

target_customer: Restaurants and restaurant groups in Southeast Asia that want to sell directly instead of through delivery apps
problem: Delivery apps charge heavy commissions and keep customer data, so restaurants lose margin and the customer relationship.
business_model: B2B SaaS for direct ordering, with delivery rider booking and payments
product_category: Restaurant direct ordering software
founder_names: Jeroen Rutten; Guido Caldara; Mathieu Sneep
market_need_then: Restaurants were complaining about delivery app commissions after the 2020 to 2021 delivery boom; Tablevibe's pitch claims savings of up to 80% against marketplace fees (company claim).

name: Talentdrop
one_liner: Your personal hiring page.
long_description:
When it comes to hiring, there are lots of resources to help managers get more candidates. But on average, only 1 in every 300 of these candidates actually get hired. Hiring managers and recruiters end up taking a robotic, brute force approach to sourcing - the kind of approach top talent hates.

Managers are increasingly finding that the simplest and most personable way to attract talent starts with their network. The best candidates want to work for great people, not faceless companies. Sharing open roles on places like LinkedIn, Slack, and Twitter unlocks enormous potential for a personalized recruiting approach across a curated talent pool, but these referrals are difficult to track across platforms and end up lost in the shuffle. We are changing that.

After more than a decade building teams at high-growth consumer tech companies like Instacart, Snapchat, and Uber, Maddy Nguyen turned her attention to creating collaborative tools for hiring managers and recruiters to source candidates from a wider range of networks and communities - while staying human.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Atherton, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Taloflow
one_liner: Better, faster tech vendor research
long_description:
Choosing the right tool for your tech stack is a soul-sucking exercise — countless hours in demos, endless spreadsheets, and the risk of a wrong choice. At Taloflow, our mission is to make technology selection effortless and low-risk for IT and software teams.

Taloflow is backed by Y Combinator, YC Continuity, Wonder Ventures, Plug and Play Ventures, and Voyager Capital.
all_locations: Los Angeles, CA, USA; Santa Monica, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: IT and software teams, technology consultancies and procurement groups that must choose software vendors
problem: Choosing the right tool for a tech stack takes many hours of demos and spreadsheets and carries the risk of a wrong choice. Taloflow aims to make vendor research faster and lower risk.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for vendor evaluation reports and a collaborative evaluation notebook
product_category: software vendor selection and research
founder_names: Louis-Victor Jadavji; Todd Kesselman; Jason Kim
market_need_then: Founders interviewed about 70 CTOs and engineering managers who said tech stack decisions were getting more complex and time consuming (TechCrunch 2024). In 2021 the company was in cloud cost management, which its own blog later called too noisy.
outcome_analysis: Taloflow joined YC in Winter 2021 as a cloud cost tool, pivoted into software vendor selection and by mid 2024 reported hundreds of paying customers including three Fortune 500 firms and five staff. Its only sourced round is a small 1.3 million dollar seed in June 2024, so it remains small and active without a clear breakout.

name: Talus Bio
one_liner: Discovering drugs that target the DNA regulome
long_description: We have built a platform that enables drug discovery and development for previously undruggable genome regulators ("the regulome"). We accomplish this by moving drug discovery out of artificial systems where regulome proteins fail to function properly, and back into live human cells. Our technology combines innovations in automated cell processing, next-gen proteomics, and advanced data analytics to measure a drug's effect on the entire regulome in one experiment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharma and biotech partners and Talus itself as a drug developer pursuing transcription factor and other regulome targets
problem: Many gene regulator proteins (the regulome) are hard to drug because they fail to function in artificial biochemical assays, so drug screening on them rarely works.
business_model: Platform-based drug discovery: internal pipeline plus partnerships and collaborations
product_category: Biotech drug discovery platform (proteomics, automation, AI)
market_need_then: Gene regulators and transcription factors were widely described as hard-to-drug targets, and Foghorn's 2020 IPO and Merck deal showed investor and pharma appetite for the area.
outcome_analysis: Talus is still active and has funded itself with a 2022 raise, a 2023 grant and an 2024 seed-plus round led by Two Bear Capital, then signed a pharma-style tools collaboration in December 2025. Its founders have deep regulome and proteomics training, which fits the platform. No clinical outcome is reported yet, so the story is early and unproven.

name: TaoFi

target_customer: Traders, liquidity providers and developers in the Bittensor (TAO) ecosystem

product_category: DeFi exchange and liquidity infrastructure

name: Tarsal
tags: B2B; Cybersecurity; Big Data; Data Engineering
one_liner: Data pipeline for your security data lake.
long_description: Tarsal is a data pipeline custom built for security teams. As security data grows 25% year over year, security teams desperately need access to best-in-class data infrastructure. Tarsal bridges the gap between the modern data stack and security teams, pioneering the modern security data stack.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Security teams at companies that keep security logs in data lakes such as Snowflake, S3 and Databricks
problem: Security data grows fast and is hard to ingest, normalise and route into modern data stores without custom pipeline work.
business_model: B2B SaaS data pipeline, subscription or usage based
product_category: Security data pipeline
market_need_then: The company's pitch said security data was growing about 25% a year and security teams lacked pipelines built for data lakes; Tarsal joined the Snowflake partner network in 2023 (per a PR Newswire release listed in search results).
outcome_analysis: Tarsal built a security data pipeline founded by engineers from TikTok, Uber and Plaid, raised a 6M seed in March 2024 and added a security veteran as CTO, then sold to the competitor Monad in July 2025 for undisclosed terms. It stayed seed stage in a crowded pipeline market led by Cribl, and the sale looks like consolidation rather than a breakout.

name: Taste
one_liner: Online marketplace for dinners shipped from great restaurants
long_description: Taste is an online marketplace where you can order ready-to-eat dinners from great restaurants, shipped nationwide. The next time you want to have a nice dinner at home, instead of cooking for hours or getting low quality take out, you can order a nice multi-course dinner from Taste to enjoy with friends or loved ones.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: New York City consumers ordering premium multicourse dinner kits for a special evening at home, and partner fine dining restaurants selling through the marketplace
problem: Restaurants hit by the pandemic needed new revenue, and diners wanted restaurant quality dinners at home without hours of cooking or ordinary takeout.
business_model: Marketplace taking a margin on dinner kits from partner restaurants, priced roughly 60 to 100 dollars per person
product_category: Premium restaurant dinner kit marketplace
market_need_then: In early 2021 pandemic restrictions had New York restaurants searching for delivery revenue and consumers were spending on at home dining. TechCrunch reported 16 Michelin starred or rated restaurants on the platform at launch in February 2021.
outcome_analysis: Taste launched in New York in February 2021 with Michelin rated partners and kits costing 60 to 100 dollars per person. The cause of its shutdown is not public. The likely pressures, which are inferences from the model and not sourced statements, are that kit logistics and premium pricing limited the market once restaurants reopened and Goldbelly scaled nationally, while both founders went on to other companies.

name: Tavus
tags: Generative AI; B2B; Video; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Building the human layer of AI
long_description: At Tavus, we're building the human layer of AI. Our mission is to make human-AI interaction as natural as face-to-face interaction, enabling the human touch where it has been previously unscalable. We achieve this through pioneering research in multi-modal AI models for human perception and understanding, combined with state-of-the-art human avatar rendering and conversation models that we make accessible to developers worldwide. Our models and APIs power everything from text-to-video AI avatars to real-time conversational video experiences across industries like healthcare, recruiting, sales, education, and more. By enabling AI to see, hear, and communicate with human-like authenticity, we're creating the foundation for developers to create the next generation of AI employees, assistants, and companions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and enterprises that want conversational AI video agents and digital twins (sales, healthcare, training)
problem: Producing personalized, lifelike video and human-like AI interaction at scale was costly or impossible; Tavus offers APIs for video generation and real-time conversational video agents.
business_model: Usage-based developer API plus enterprise deployments
product_category: Generative AI video and conversational AI avatars
market_need_then: In 2021 sales and marketing teams wanted personalized video at scale and Synthesia's 2021 rounds showed enterprise demand for synthetic presenters.
outcome_analysis: Tavus rode the generative AI wave from a 2021 video personalization product to a developer platform and conversational agents, raising an $18M Series A in 2024 and $40M Series B in 2025 from top investors. It remains independent. Heavy competition from well funded rivals and large labs is the main risk, and no shutdown or layoff reports were found.

name: TechBiz
one_liner: MIS on mobile for SMB's in India
long_description: SMEs find it hard to derive value from their business data which is stuck inside hard-to-access accounting softwares. We provide them an app-first MIS/Business Intelligence solution to track their business essentials (Debtors, Creditors, Sales, Outstanding etc.) and help make quicker and better decisions.
all_locations: New Delhi, DL, India; MH, India; Remote
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and medium businesses in India that use BUSY accounting software
problem: Business data sits inside hard to reach accounting software, so owners cannot easily see debtors, creditors, sales and outstanding payments.
business_model: B2B SaaS mobile subscription
product_category: Mobile MIS and business intelligence for SMBs
market_need_then: Indian SMBs ran on desktop accounting tools like BUSY and Tally with limited mobile reporting, and several mobile first apps such as Vyapar targeted them. No dated demand figures were found.
outcome_analysis: TechBiz was a three person team selling a mobile MIS layer on top of BUSY accounting data to Indian SMBs. It raised no verifiable institutional money and was bought by CredFlow in an all cash deal in June 2023, which reportedly cost under INR 10 crore per Inc42 sources. The founders joined CredFlow to transition the product, which suggests a small team and product pickup.

name: Telivy
one_liner: Automate your cyber security risk assessments
long_description: Telivy helps small and medium businesses purchase the best cyber insurance coverage. Our proprietary ML-based risk platform assesses insurability gaps, offers remediation plans and brokers insurance quotes from A+ rated carriers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and medium businesses buying cyber insurance, later managed service providers (MSPs) selling security assessments
problem: SMBs struggle to understand their cyber risk and to get suitable cyber insurance coverage and quotes.
business_model: Insurance brokerage commission plus SaaS risk assessment subscription (later sold to MSPs)
product_category: Cyber risk assessment and insurance brokerage
market_need_then: Cyber insurance demand and premiums were rising in 2021 as ransomware spread, and At-Bay raised a reported 185M Series D at a 1.35B valuation in 2021 (from a 2026 comparison article).
outcome_analysis: Telivy began as a cyber insurance broker for SMBs with an ML risk assessment, shifted toward selling its assessment to MSPs, and was acquired by Cytracom in January 2025 for undisclosed terms. Total funding appears to be about 2.5M from aggregator estimates, so it exited as a small company after leaning on the product rather than insurance brokerage.

name: Telmai
one_liner: Automated data observability and quality for Data Lake
long_description: Telmai is a Data observability and Data Quality platform designed for Open architecture. It monitors data stored/managed in any data system, such as a data lake or data warehouse, in its raw format at scale without sampling
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Foster City, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data engineering and analytics teams at enterprises with data lakes and lakehouses
problem: Data lake and warehouse data is often unreliable, and existing monitoring tools sampled data or required moving it; Telmai monitors data in place without sampling.
business_model: B2B SaaS data observability platform
product_category: Data observability and data quality
market_need_then: Data quality and observability was a hot category in 2021, shown by Monte Carlo's rounds and rising spend on data lakes.
outcome_analysis: Telmai has stayed small and independent, raising a 2021 seed and a 2023 seed and adding partnerships such as iLink Digital in April 2026. It competes against better funded observability vendors, and a third-party estimate puts revenue at a few million dollars. It is a steady but unexceptional outcome so far.

name: Tenyks
tags: Computer Vision; Video; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: The World's Most Versatile Video Answering Engine
long_description:
Tenyks (YC S21) is a Cambridge University spin-out building the World's Most Versatile Visual Intelligence Platform—think Snowflake for Vision or GPT for Video.

Problem: Companies today collect oceans of visual data (from cameras, drones, and satellites), but struggle to extract actionable insights. Current solutions rely heavily on manual analysis by call centres in locations like the Philippines or AI platforms narrowly focused on security rather than deeper operational insights. This leaves critical improvements in efficiency, customer satisfaction, and revenue growth unrealised.

Solution: Tenyks unlocks unprecedented insights by applying advanced multimodal Vision-Language Models (VLMs) capable of comprehensive video summarisation, retrieval, and visual question-answering. These VLMs are seamlessly combined with specialised analytics for emotion detection, activity recognition, object tracking, and even gait analysis. Our platform transforms ordinary visual footage into extraordinary operational intelligence.

Initial Focus: Starting with Quick Service Restaurants (QSRs), we enable operations leaders to instantly understand customer flow, kitchen efficiency, staff productivity, and quality of service using their existing security camera footage—turning previously inaccessible data into direct operational improvements and clear financial ROI. For instance, insights from Tenyks can accelerate the speed of service significantly; even a 1-second improvement in service speed could generate $30,000 additional annual revenue per restaurant. For a multi-unit owner of 100 restaurants, that's an additional $3 million per year.

Traction: We've recently secured our first Fortune 500 customer, joining other major enterprises, global system integrators, and high-growth startups trusting Tenyks for powerful, data-driven decision-making.

Why Tenyks: Our patented technology originates from the founders' PhD research at Cambridge University. Previously, we helped world-leading teams scale high-performing Vision AI in production. 

Recognition: Recognised as a Rising Star in Gen AI by Sifted, Best Product of the Year by Vision AI Alliance, and Company of the Year by Cambridge University (previously awarded to DeepMind).
regions: Bulgaria; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Originally ML engineers working on computer vision; now restaurant operators using vision AI on existing cameras
problem: Computer vision models fail in hidden ways and teams lacked tools to diagnose them; the company later applied its vision stack to restaurant operations such as drive-thru wait times and order accuracy.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: Computer vision MLOps, later restaurant vision AI
founder_names: Botty Dimanov; Dmitry Kazhdan; Maleakhi Wijaya
market_need_then: Computer vision deployments were growing in 2021 and teams complained about opaque model failures, a gap Aquarium also targeted.
outcome_analysis: Tenyks launched as a Cambridge spin-out debugging computer vision models, raised a $3.4M seed in March 2022 and by 2026 sells vision AI to restaurants, claiming 100+ customers including large chains. The cause of the shift away from MLOps is not public. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown report was found.

name: Terapify
tags: Mental Health Tech; Consumer Health Services; Telemedicine
one_liner: Online therapy platform for the Spanish-speaking market
long_description:
Terapify offers high-quality on-demand mental healthcare for individuals and businesses.

Currently, people in more than 45 countries take therapy with us on a recurring basis every month.
all_locations: Mexico City, CDMX, Mexico; Guadalajara, Jal., Mexico; Remote
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Spanish-speaking individuals and couples in Mexico seeking online therapy, plus employers through a corporate program
problem: Access to affordable, stigma-free therapy in Spanish was limited; the idea came from a founder's own years of delay before seeking help for depression.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer per-session fees plus B2B employee mental health program
product_category: Online therapy marketplace
founder_names: Juan Daniel Velez Santiago; Eduardo Velez Santiago
market_need_then: The Platzi article describes social stigma and poor access to therapy in Mexico and the company reported 30% monthly growth in 2018; the pandemic from 2020 increased online care demand.
outcome_analysis: Terapify is still operating in Mexico, driven by a founder-led story of personal need, and the company claims hundreds of psychologists and over 300,000 sessions. Funding figures conflict across aggregators, from about $190K to over $1M, so the capital story is unclear. The company has stayed focused on the Spanish-speaking market with a B2B offering.

name: Terra API
one_liner: API for developers and AIs to access health data
long_description:
Terra makes it easy to transfer health data.

The unified API makes it easy to access data from health apps, wearables, sensors, and medical equipment through one source
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers of fitness, health and wellness apps that need data from wearables and health sensors
problem: Each wearable and health app has its own API, so apps spend engineering time integrating them; Terra offers one API for all of them.
business_model: Usage-based API pricing per connected user
product_category: Health and wearable data API
market_need_then: Fitness and health apps proliferated in 2020 and 2021, and each wearable required separate integration work, which TechCrunch framed as the 'Plaid for fitness data'.
outcome_analysis: Terra raised a $2.8M seed in June 2021 from General Catalyst and Samsung Next and has kept shipping, claiming over 1,000 developers and customers such as Nutrisense and Levels. No later equity round was found, and the generic name collides with Terraform Labs in search. It looks like a durable but modest developer API business.

name: Text Blaze
one_liner: Slash commands anywhere
long_description: Text Blaze saves time and increases comms quality by automating repeated tasks. Users save smart templates and insert them anywhere on the web using keyboard shortcuts. Templates can include placeholders, logic, dynamic fields, integrations with other apps, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Knowledge workers and teams, about 70% with corporate emails at launch, who type repetitive text in Gmail, CRMs and web apps
problem: People retype the same messages and make mistakes; Text Blaze lets them insert snippets with shortcuts, forms and formulas.
business_model: Freemium Chrome extension with paid individual and business plans
product_category: Text expansion and snippets, later AI prompt templates
market_need_then: At launch in 2021 the Chrome extension had over 70,000 users, about 70% with corporate emails, and early revenue, showing organic demand.
outcome_analysis: Text Blaze grew through a free Chrome extension with product-led distribution, reaching 70,000 users before its $3.3M seed in 2021 and a claimed 800,000 users later. A four-person team was the plan at seed, suggesting capital efficiency. It remains independent and has extended into AI Blaze and Data Blaze.

name: The Breakaway
one_liner: The personal coach and companion for cyclists.
long_description:
The Breakaway is a personal performance coach for cyclists, with the product, team, roadmap and vision to extend to be the mass market coaching platform for anyone tracking their performance.

As more and more people realize that exercise is the key not only to personal performance, but to health and wellness, the inevitable future is that everyone will have an AI driven personal performance coach & companion in their pocket. The Breakaway will be that Coach.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Recreational and competitive cyclists who pay a monthly or annual subscription for ride analysis and training guidance
problem: Cyclists have ride data scattered across Strava, Garmin, Zwift and Peloton and no personalized, affordable coaching that turns it into training guidance.
business_model: Consumer subscription ($7.99 per month or $89.99 per year in June 2021)
product_category: Cycling training and performance coaching app
founder_names: Jordan Kobert; Kyle Yugawa; Christian Vande Velde
market_need_then: Pandemic era growth in cycling and indoor training. The Fitt Insider Q&A (2022-01) cites a total market in the hundreds of millions of people, and a June 2021 review shows demand for deeper power analysis than Zwift offered.
outcome_analysis: Two former Strava employees started The Breakaway in fall 2020, joined YC in Summer 2021 and raised a $2.9M seed in February 2022. It stayed small, with a six person team in the directory, and Strava bought its core assets in May 2025 without disclosed terms. The outcome is a soft strategic exit rather than a venture scale result, and the YC directory still lists the company as Active.

name: The Third Place
one_liner: Subscriptions for neighborhood businesses
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent restaurants, bars, bottle shops, retailers and arts groups that want recurring revenue from regulars
problem: Neighborhood businesses lost direct relationships with regulars to delivery aggregators and lacked simple tools for memberships, subscriptions and limited drops.
business_model: B2B SaaS with a platform fee on memberships and subscriptions (7 percent fee, waived through June 2021 per early coverage)
product_category: Community and membership software for local businesses
market_need_then: COVID-19 shut dining rooms in 2020 and delivery aggregators took margin and customer data; early coverage says the founders signed about 70 businesses by early 2021.
outcome_analysis: The Third Place rode the pandemic shift to direct membership and subscription revenue for restaurants and reportedly raised about $3.2M after YC. It remains active, but a 2025 article places it next to better funded restaurant tools such as Table22 and Dorsia, and no growth figures were found, so the long term outcome is open.

name: Therify
one_liner: Inclusive mental healthcare for companies
long_description: Therify is an inclusive mental health benefit for companies. Through our web platform, employees access culturally responsive therapists, live community sessions, and self-guided content to support their emotional well-being.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Employers buying inclusive mental health benefits for employees and families
problem: Employee mental health benefits (EAPs) are poorly used and not culturally responsive; Therify offers culturally responsive in-network therapists.
business_model: B2B employer benefit layered on existing health plans: provider network matching, covers the first sessions, pays providers market rate, group sessions
product_category: Employer mental health benefit
market_need_then: TechCrunch (2021-12): the founder found few therapists matching his background; he argues underrepresented employees leave jobs more and report symptoms more; therapy is stigmatized in some communities. Hundreds of providers signed up in the first six months. No spend or survey data cited.
outcome_analysis: Therify, YC S21, matched employees with culturally responsive therapists through employer benefits and raised a $1.3M seed in December 2021 led by SoftBank's SB Opportunity Fund. Employers such as Thumbtack and Indeed are named on its site and job posts. Aggregators list a convertible note in late 2025 and total funding of about $3.4M to $3.8M, unverified. No exit or shutdown found, so it appears to be operating small; the outcome is unresolved against much better-funded benefit platforms.

name: Tilt
one_liner: Bringing the joy of cycling to millions of Indians
long_description:
You can buy or share our bicycles and e-bikes for health, fitness, and mobility.

Today, our bikes can be found in hundreds of communities across Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi NCR and Pune.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Corporate campuses, townships and residential communities in India that deploy shared bikes and e-bikes, plus individual buyers
problem: Last mile and campus mobility in India lacks affordable, healthy options; shared bicycles and e-bikes can serve closed communities where public bike sharing struggles.
business_model: B2B2C bike and e-bike sharing deployments for enterprises and townships, plus direct bike sales and community advertising
product_category: Shared micromobility hardware and service
market_need_then: Campuses and townships wanted internal mobility, and pandemic era interest in cycling and fitness rose; Tilt reported serving over 1000 users in three months in 2019 and customers such as Tata Motors and TCS.
outcome_analysis: Tilt grew from a campus bike pool into a B2B2C shared bike and e-bike provider with named corporate customers, took the standard $125K YC deal in 2021 and shows no later disclosed funding. Retail listings in 2025 show it still selling e-bikes, so it survives but with no sourced evidence of venture scale traction.

name: Tint
one_liner: Makes it easy for tech platforms to embed insurance into products
long_description:
Tint makes it easy for tech platforms to embed insurance into their products. For example, when you go to Outdoorsy to rent an RV, the insurance that is sold with the rental is powered by our technology.

Our product provides anything that is needed from underwriting software to access to insurers to compliance, in a simple API.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Tech platforms and marketplaces such as Outdoorsy, Deel and Guesty that want to sell insurance to their users
problem: Platforms want to embed insurance but face underwriting, insurer access and compliance work they are not set up to do.
business_model: B2B API and software plus insurance program access, with revenue from platform fees and insurance economics
product_category: Embedded insurance infrastructure
market_need_then: Rental and gig platforms such as Outdoorsy already sold insurance with transactions and lacked in house underwriting and compliance; the founders saw this at Turo.
outcome_analysis: Two ex Turo operators built embedded insurance infrastructure, raised a $3.75M seed in March 2021 and a $25M Series A led by QED in February 2022, with total capital of $30M. Founder market fit and the embedded finance wave helped. The directory lists a 40 person team and Active status, and no later round, acquisition or layoff was found.

name: Tiriel AI
one_liner: The AI workforce for freight dispatch
long_description:
Tiriel is the AI workforce for freight dispatch.
