Not dispatch software. A workforce: specialized AI agents, each with one job, one standard, and one boss, the dispatcher. Scout finds freight across 14+ load boards. Closer negotiates rates with brokers by phone, in parallel, within the rate floors you set. Coordinator manages your drivers in English, Spanish, or whatever language your fleet speaks. Auditor closes the paperwork, files detention and TONU claims, and processes PODs. Analyst learns your operation and makes the team better every week.

Every call is recorded, transcribed, and attached to the load. You direct. They execute.

Built by a family that has operated trucking companies for over 20 years. Live across the United States.

Start with $99 at https://tiriel.ai
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid sized US trucking fleets and owner operators that run their own dispatch
problem: Dispatchers spend their day finding loads, negotiating with brokers by phone, managing drivers and chasing paperwork, which limits how many trucks one dispatcher can run.
business_model: Subscription for AI dispatch agents ($99 first month, then from $349 per month per the company site)
product_category: AI agents for freight dispatch
market_need_then: Not documented for 2021. The company site now cites dispatcher workload and the YC page cites a family with over 20 years in trucking.
outcome_analysis: Tiriel is a small, family run freight dispatch company that joined YC in Summer 2021 and today sells AI dispatch agents with a 10 person team. No funding amounts, exit or failure were found, and it is not clear what the product was in 2021, so the record shows an active company with unknown traction rather than a clear success or failure.

name: Titipku
one_liner: Super Hyperlocal Marketplace for SMEs in Indonesia
long_description: Local market is a traditional wet market that consist with 200 - 1000 merchants who sell groceries located in every residential area. We  digitize all these merchants into our apps and provide personal shoppers. So every household can buy groceries from multiple merchants at one local market in one single order. There are 16.000 local markets in Indonesia with 8.000.000 merchants inside.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Urban Indonesian households buying groceries and traditional wet market merchants who sell through the app
problem: Shoppers cannot easily buy from many merchants in a traditional market in one order, and merchants, often older sellers, lack digital storefronts.
business_model: Hyperlocal marketplace with personal shoppers, take rate and delivery fees, plus B2B2C partnerships with market operators
product_category: Grocery marketplace for traditional markets
market_need_then: Indonesia has about 16,000 local markets with 8 million merchants per the company, and a June 2020 Nielsen survey reported in press found 58 percent of people preferred traditional markets even during the pandemic.
outcome_analysis: Titipku digitized over 150 traditional markets and 10,000 traders in Greater Jakarta by 2025 per press, working through market operators and officials. No disclosed funding beyond the YC deal and no exit were found, so it appears to be a slow, capital light operator rather than a venture scaled marketplace.

name: Toku
one_liner: Account Receivables Platform for Latin American Enterprises
long_description: Toku helps companies increase their monthly revenue collection rate so they can focus on the their main business. Payment method management, failed payment retries, payment reminders, failed payment notifications, among others.
all_locations: Santiago, Santiago Metropolitan Region, Chile; Mexico City, CDMX, Mexico
regions: Chile; Mexico; Latin America
target_customer: Mid sized and large Latin American enterprises with recurring billing, such as insurers, schools, utilities, telecoms and real estate firms
problem: Companies in Latin America collect recurring revenue across fragmented payment methods and lose revenue to failed payments, manual reminders and reconciliation.
business_model: B2B SaaS and payment collection platform, per volume or subscription
product_category: Accounts receivable and recurring payments platform
founder_names: Cristina Etcheberry; Francisca Noguera; Enzo Tamburini
market_need_then: Tool use for subscriptions and recurring collections was growing in Latin America; the company reportedly managed about US$3M per month at the time of its 2021 YC selection (Descubre, 2021-07-28).
outcome_analysis: Toku went from a YC Summer 2021 recurring payments startup to a 150 person company with over 450 enterprise clients, raising a $7.15M seed in 2023 and a Series A of $9.3M in 2024 extended by $38.7M in 2025. Enterprise sales focus, ERP and bank integrations and early traction explain the progress; no failure signs were found.

name: Topkey
long_description: Topkey is the all-in-one financial operating platform that simplifies expense management for hospitality managers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Short term rental and vacation rental property managers, with hospitality operators as a later expansion
problem: Property managers handle many small vendor expenses and owner statements with general tools that do not fit vacation rental operations.
business_model: B2B SaaS and fintech with expense management, bill pay and corporate cards (interchange and software fees)
product_category: Financial operating system for property managers
market_need_then: Vacation rental management grew during 2020 and 2021 and managers lacked tools for expense and owner reporting; the company's own blog (2025) claims general tools were not built for vacation rental operations.
outcome_analysis: Topkey, founded by a former Airbnb Hotels partnerships lead and a full stack developer, raised a $5.2M seed in July 2023 led by Felicis and has grown through integrations and partnerships such as Guesty and Casago into 2025. No later round, exit or failure was found, so it is an active niche fintech with moderate funding and unproven scale.

name: Topline Pro
one_liner: Generative AI powered Shopify for home service professionals
long_description: Topline Pro (formerly ProPhone) is a Generative AI platform enabling home service businesses to be easily discovered, trusted and booked, directly. The AI-driven interface rapidly and affordably creates a custom, SEO-optimized website along with a application to help sync content to and from local listings, put social media communications on autopilot and enable the business owner to easily get paid online.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Boston, MA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small home service and trade businesses (plumbing, painting, landscaping, roofing, HVAC) in the US
problem: Home service pros rely on word of mouth and struggle to be found online, look trustworthy, get booked and get paid without hiring marketing help.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for local service businesses
product_category: Marketing, website and booking platform for home service businesses (originally a video-call app for plumbers)
market_need_then: The founders report that plumbers liked video calls but needed more jobs and had no way to grow beyond word of mouth (TechCrunch 2022). Home service is a large, digitally underserved segment of small businesses.
outcome_analysis: The founding video-call idea did not become the business; the team pivoted in early 2022 to a website and marketing subscription for home service pros, raised a 5 million seed in October 2022 and a 27 million Series B in August 2025 with the company claiming over 6,000 customers. The generative AI wave gave the pivot a timing tailwind. The company is still active.

name: Tractian
one_liner: Physical AI for asset-heavy industries
long_description: Tractian transforms machine data into uptime, captures shop-floor know-how, and accelerates manufacturing throughput.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Manufacturing plants and other asset-heavy industrial sites, starting with Brazilian factories
problem: Factories lose money to unplanned machine downtime but lack the networking and capital to run enterprise condition monitoring from large vendors.
business_model: Hardware sensors plus per-sensor monthly SaaS subscription (about 90 USD per sensor and 60 USD per month in 2021), later a broader industrial AI platform
product_category: Industrial IoT condition monitoring and predictive maintenance, later CMMS and physical AI
founder_names: Igor Marinelli; Gabriel Lameirinhas; Leonardo Vieira
market_need_then: Brazilian factories wanted predictive maintenance but could not afford or network the offerings from large vendors. By March 2021 AB InBev was the first customer and about 30 buyers used the sensors (TechCrunch).
outcome_analysis: Tractian started in 2019 selling cheap vibration and temperature sensors to Brazilian plants that could not run enterprise systems, joined YC in Winter 2021 with AB InBev as first customer, and grew through rounds in 2022, 2023, 2024 and a reported 2026 Series D at a 1.4B valuation. Founders grew up around plants, the offer fit an underserved segment, and it expanded to the US and into software.

name: TransAstra Corporation
one_liner: Orbital logistics: Unleashing space industry, from Earth to asteroids
long_description: With five issued patents covering our core business lines, and more than a dozen additional patents pending this year and more than $5M in revenue, TransAstra is developing the technologies that will drive the rapidly expanding space economy. Our breakthrough Omnivore propulsion system can propel spacecraft, including our Worker Bee commercial OTV with water or virtually any other fluid as a propellant using only concentrated sunlight as a power source. Omnivore is faster, cheaper, and more practical than electric propulsion while being substantially less expensive, safer, and more operationally flexible than legacy chemical propulsion systems. Our Sutter Telescope System can identify and locate resource-rich asteroids and orbital debris that existing technologies can’t find and works synergistically with our Worker Bee OTV for orbital logistics. For government customers, Sutter can identify dark fast-moving objects between Earth and the Moon which currently evade detection, a critical issue for national defense and a key need of the Space Force. We are already using Sutter in ground-based observatories and will begin commercial sales of Sutter SDA data next month having tracked dozens of faint moving objects in space already. Once launched into space, Sutter will be 300,000 times more cost effective than any other known telescope design and will revolutionize sense making in space.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Satellite operators, space agencies (NASA) and defense customers such as the US Space Force
problem: Moving satellites and handling debris or asteroid resources in orbit is expensive with chemical or electric propulsion, and faint fast-moving objects are hard to detect.
business_model: Government R&D contracts and SBIR awards now, with planned orbital logistics services and space domain awareness data sales
product_category: Space propulsion, orbital transfer vehicles and telescopes
market_need_then: In 2021 the in-space economy was growing with rideshare launches and a push for orbital debris and space domain awareness; the company cited Space Force interest in detecting dark fast-moving objects between Earth and the Moon.
outcome_analysis: TransAstra is an active, long-horizon space hardware company led by a propulsion PhD and former Momentus CTO. After YC in Summer 2021 and a reported 4M seed it has relied on SBIR, Space Force and NASA awards, including a 5M combined NASA and private round in September 2025, rather than large venture rounds. Its path depends on flight demonstrations that are still in development.

name: Treinta
one_liner: Software and AI tools for SMBs in the US and Latin America
long_description: Treinta powers 7 million SMBs across the US and Latin America with simple finance, inventory, and sales tools.
regions: Colombia; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Single-operator microbusinesses and small shops in Latin America, such as tiendas, bakeries, salons and restaurants
problem: About 90 percent of Latin America's roughly 50 million microbusinesses record sales and debts on paper, so they lack a view of their finances and cannot access credit.
business_model: Freemium mobile ledger and inventory app with paid monthly plans (Essential and Pro), expanding into payments and financial products
product_category: Microbusiness bookkeeping, inventory and POS app, later AI tools
market_need_then: TechCrunch (2021-02) reported monthly users up 400 percent since the August 2020 launch, 35,000 monthly active users in January 2021 and over 25 million dollars in gross transaction volume, with most Latin American microbusinesses still on paper.
outcome_analysis: Treinta launched in August 2020, reached tens of thousands of monthly users within months, raised a 46 million Series A in April 2022 and claims millions of businesses. A 2026 profile says it later shrank to a smaller team focused on its management software after other products were dropped. It is active, with a reported 30,000 paying customers.

name: Trela
one_liner: Your one-stop shop to eat well in Brazil
long_description: Trela is an end-to-end marketplace that connects suppliers of healthy groceries directly to our customers' homes at the lowest prices.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Brazilian households, first condominium WhatsApp groups, later online grocery shoppers wanting healthy food at lower prices
problem: Groceries pass through several middlemen so urban Brazilians pay more; Trela aimed to buy directly from suppliers and deliver to homes cheaply.
business_model: Marketplace and online grocer with take rate of about 10 percent per transaction at the start, later a just-in-time own-distribution grocery model
product_category: Social commerce and online grocery marketplace (formerly Zapt)
founder_names: Guilherme Nazareth; Joao Jonk; Guilherme Alvarenga
market_need_then: Online grocery demand jumped during the pandemic and TechCrunch (2022) reported revenue up 30x since the April 2021 seed with 45 percent average monthly growth, while members saved 20 to 60 percent versus stores.
outcome_analysis: Trela rode pandemic demand for online groceries, raised a seed in April 2021 and a 25 million Series A led by SoftBank in March 2022, then pivoted away from stock-based retail toward just-in-time delivery. Online grocery was a hard-margin field where peers Justo and Mercado Diferente also closed, and Trela announced its shutdown in April 2026 after failing to close a new round.

name: Trendpop
tags: Analytics; Social Media; Music; Creator Economy
one_liner: Discover trends as they happen
long_description:
Trendpop is the leading analytics and insights platform for short-form video marketing. We’re on a mission to help anyone go viral on social video platforms. We’re a deeply technical team that has taken a data-first approach to this problem: our core engine has collected over a billion social video posts that are analyzed with state-of-the-art algorithms to understand the recommendation algorithms that power virality. 

Trendpop was co-founded by Yoav Zimmerman (CEO) and Jonathan (Yoni) Ben-tzur (CTO) in August 2020, raising money from YCombinator (W21) to build Trendpop and growing to profitability in 12 short months. In January 2022, Trendpop was acquired by Collab, a veteran company in the digital creator space and an official TikTok creative and marketing partner. Today, Trendpop powers the TikTok marketing programs of top major record labels in North America and is quickly expanding to new markets in the film, television, beauty, and DTC eCommerce industry. Trendpop is currently used by leading marketing and A&R professionals in the music industry (both indie and major) to help their artists go viral on TikTok and hundreds of brands and creators who consistently win on social video.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Music marketers and A&R staff at record labels, plus brands and creators running short form video campaigns on TikTok
problem: Marketers could not tell which sounds and formats would go viral on TikTok, so campaigns were guesswork.
business_model: B2B SaaS analytics subscription, with a self serve plan launched in October 2022
product_category: Short form video analytics and trend insights
market_need_then: Record labels were running large TikTok marketing programs in 2020 to 2021; YC and the company state it grew to profitability within 12 months (company statement, not independently verified).
outcome_analysis: Trendpop was started in August 2020, joined YC in Winter 2021, claimed profitability after about a year using about 500K of aggregator reported funding, and was acquired by the creator platform Collab in February 2022 with the founders staying on. The TikTok boom and its record label customers made it a cheap, fast growing asset, so the exit was early and capital efficient.

name: Trestle Biotherapeutics
one_liner: Bioengineered kidneys for patients with kidney failure
long_description: We are developing an implantable therapeutic tissue that will be surgically delivered to patients suffering from end stage renal disease.  Upon implantation, this tissue will supplement the patient's renal function, eliminating their dependency on dialysis and improving their disease status. This has the potential to not only get these patients off dialysis - a significant impact for them and their families - but to greatly extend the time required before kidney transplantation is essential.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Patients with end-stage renal disease and the nephrology and transplant system that would treat them; pharma-style licensing and partners
problem: Dialysis is burdensome and transplant organs are scarce; Trestle aims to implant bioengineered kidney tissue that supplements renal function and delays or avoids dialysis and transplant.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing a therapeutic tissue product; funded by grants, prizes and venture capital, with planned clinical development and partnering
product_category: Regenerative medicine and bioprinted kidney tissue
market_need_then: End-stage renal disease patients depend on dialysis and wait for scarce transplants; the KidneyX Artificial Kidney Prize created a funded demand signal for dialysis alternatives.
outcome_analysis: Trestle is a two-founder preclinical biotech from former Organovo scientists that licensed Harvard and Kumamoto technology in 2022, won a 1 million dollar KidneyX prize in June 2023 and announced a research collaboration with Humacyte in March 2025. It is still active, with limited verified venture funding, so the outcome is unresolved and depends on preclinical and clinical milestones.

name: Triomics
one_liner: AI Agents for Oncology EHRs
long_description:
Triomics is building the AI infrastructure for modern oncology. Across the U.S., cancer care providers rely on highly trained staff to manually review unstructured patient records such as pathology reports, clinical notes, genomic panels, and scanned faxes to support workflows like clinical trial matching, visit preparation, and quality reporting. We replace that manual work with task-driven AI agents embedded directly into clinical workflows, automatically processing medical records at scale and in real time.

Our platform is trusted by 4 of the top 10 Best Hospitals for Cancer ranked by U.S. News, as well as several of the largest community oncology practices.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Cancer centers, community oncology practices and life sciences sponsors
problem: Oncology staff manually read unstructured records (pathology, notes, genomics, faxes) to match patients to trials, prepare visits and report quality data, which is slow and costly.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software sold to health systems and life sciences firms
product_category: Healthcare AI agents and LLMs for oncology EHR data (OncoLLM)
founder_names: Sarim Khan; Hrituraj Singh; Sajjan Rajpurohit
market_need_then: Cancer centers rely on trained staff to read unstructured charts for trial matching and registry work; TechCrunch (2024) says six centers were using or piloting the product by May 2024.
outcome_analysis: Triomics grew from a trial matching idea into oncology AI agents as language models matured, winning named cancer centers (MSK deployment announced November 2025) and raising a 15M Series A in May 2024 and a 22M Series B in May 2026. The LLM timing tailwind and enterprise hospital sales drove growth; it is active and independent.

name: Triplit
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Web Development; Cloud Computing; Databases
one_liner: The best database for app developers
long_description: Triplit is complete full-stack solution to data persistence, state management, and realtime synchronization for web applications that want to go fast
regions: Remote; Fully Remote

name: True3D
one_liner: Building the next generation of visual media
long_description: We're a research lab building foundation models and products for what comes after flat video.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Video creators and marketers (QuickVid, Outpaint phases) and viewers and creators of spatial 3D video (current True3D Labs)
problem: Flat video does not use depth; the company has pursued ways to turn any screen or video into immersive 3D, and in between built tools to repurpose video for short-form and any screen size.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer subscriptions (QuickVid at 10 dollars a month; a directory lists 29 dollars a month for the 3D product, unverified)
product_category: AI video tools and spatial video foundation models
market_need_then: No source dated near January 2021 describes demand for the founding product; later products targeted short-form video repurposing demand in 2022 and generative AI interest.
outcome_analysis: True3D is a very small team led by one former Meta engineer that has moved between products: a 3D video idea at YC, the QuickVid short-form tool launched December 2022, Outpaint for reframing video, and by 2025 a spatial video lab. No funding amounts, revenue or customers were found, so there is no clear success or failure story; it remains active with about five people.

name: Truss
one_liner: Truss is a banking and payments network for blue-collar trades.
long_description: Truss is an all-in-one banking and payment automation platform for construction businesses. With Truss, construction companies can manage bill payments, receivables, and corporate cards in one place. They can save time on manual data entry by integrating Truss with their existing tools and automating the full billing cycle, from invoicing and reconciliation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-size construction contractors and subcontractors in the US that pay bills and subs and collect receivables
problem: Contractors still run on checks, slow ACH and manual data entry between invoicing, payments and accounting, so cash arrives late and bookkeeping is heavy.
business_model: Fintech payments and banking on a partner bank (Thread Bank): interchange, payment and card fees, accounts with no account fees
product_category: Construction banking and payment automation
competitors_at_founding: Billd; LinqPal (now BlueTape); Built Technologies (Built Pay)
market_need_then: Construction payments were check heavy and slow, and several funded startups (Billd, LinqPal, Built Pay) launched or raised in 2021, which shows demand and investor interest in the wedge.
outcome_analysis: Truss is still operating as an Active YC company with a small team, a Thread Bank partnership announced in August 2023 and a construction only focus. No verified funding round was found, and a seed round reported by databases for the construction company appears to belong to a UK fashion startup with the same name, so funding is unknown rather than zero. The 2023 rename to Truss and the narrow trades focus are the clearest strategic moves; traction is not public, so no success or failure factors are asserted.

name: Tuli Health
one_liner: Transforming pharmacies in the UK into diagnostic centers
long_description:
Tuli health is turning all 11 000 independent pharmacies in the UK into diagnostic centers.  Our software makes it easy for these pharmacies to sell and fulfill COVID-19 tests today and other diagnostic tests tomorrow. Instead of waiting for a long time or travelling a long distance to receive the tests, customers can now receive tests in their neighbourhood, with results guaranteed in 24 hours. 

Tuli Health was launched in June, had onboarded 147 pharmacies, performed over 7000 diagnostic tests, and helped pharmacies generate $1.3 million in incremental revenue per month. 

The vision is to make every local pharmacy into a diagnostic center powered by Tuli Health.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Independent and community pharmacies in the UK that want to offer diagnostic and blood testing services
problem: Patients wait or travel far for diagnostic tests while independent pharmacies lack the clinical, lab and software setup to offer them.
business_model: B2B2C software and service: pharmacies sell and fulfil tests through Tuli, with lab partners; revenue share on tests and phlebotomy network fees
product_category: Pharmacy diagnostics platform
competitors_at_founding: Medicspot; NHS Pharmacy Collect (free lateral flow tests)
market_need_then: UK demand for private COVID PCR and lateral flow testing in 2021 and about 11,000 independent pharmacies without a turnkey testing setup, per the YC page.
outcome_analysis: Tuli launched in June 2021 selling COVID tests through 147 pharmacies and claimed over 7,000 tests, then moved to a blood testing and phlebotomy network that its site says reaches 308 pharmacy partners and is CQC registered. The company is still Active with roughly ten staff per directories. Funding is not verifiable beyond YC, so it appears capital efficient or small, and the pivot away from COVID testing is the main reason it survived.

name: Tupelo
one_liner: Marketplace for small business M&A
long_description: Tupelo is building the future of how traditional small businesses are bought and sold. We are the first small business M&A marketplace with modern integrations to make selling and buying a business quick and easy.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Business brokers, plus buyers and sellers of small businesses
problem: Buying and selling a small business is slow and paperwork heavy, with NDAs, valuations and listings handled in generic tools.
business_model: SaaS subscription for business brokers (CRM, data rooms, valuations); originally a listing marketplace
product_category: Small business M&A software and marketplace
market_need_then: Small business sales were a large fragmented market run by brokers using generic CRMs; a testimonial on the site contrasts Tupelo with generic CRMs.
outcome_analysis: Tupelo is a two person YC W21 company that still operates in 2025, now positioned as software for business brokers rather than a buyer and seller marketplace. No funding beyond YC could be verified and there is no evidence of rapid growth or failure, so the story is a small, quietly surviving company that moved to the broker workflow niche. The reason for the shift is not public.

name: Turing College
one_liner: AI-driven online tech school for busy professionals
long_description: Turing College is an online AI-driven school for busy professionals. We upskill & reskill in data science & AI, analytics, marketing and programming in 3-12 months with 1on1 support and flexibility.
regions: Lithuania; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Working professionals and career switchers in Europe paying for online data, AI, marketing and programming courses, plus government funded training buyers
problem: Traditional education and bootcamps are slow, expensive and poorly matched to job market needs for people who work full time.
business_model: Tuition for online cohort programs with 1 on 1 mentoring, including deferred payment options; government training funds; EU grants
product_category: Online tech education
founder_names: Lukas Kaminskis; Tomas Moska; Benas Sidlauskas
competitors_at_founding: Lambda School (BloomTech); Springboard; Flatiron School and General Assembly
market_need_then: Demand for data science and AI reskilling among working adults in Europe in 2020 and 2021, with few Baltic or European online options and Tech.eu coverage of a launch promising well paid jobs.
outcome_analysis: Turing College grew from a student community into a funded Lithuanian online school, was the first Lithuanian YC company, raised a 2020 initial round and a 1.05M dollar seed in 2021, won a 2.5M euro EIC grant in 2024 and bought Boom Training in 2025. It is still Active with about 50 staff. Capital raised is modest, so success rests on execution, European reach and public funding rather than venture scale.

name: Turion Space
one_liner: Moving Things Around in Space, Imaging Space Objects When We're Not
long_description: Turion Space is building spacecraft to move things around in space and image space objects when they’re not, and focused on developing the dual-use technology required to ensure a sustainable future in space. They aim to build a strong foundation selling space domain awareness imagery data while advancing their technology towards an affordable solution for orbital debris removal and eventually asteroid mining. The founding team originates from SpaceX, and after going through the Y-combinator accelerator in summer 2021 went on to raise a $6.2M seed round and is launching their first DROID satellite in early 2023.
all_locations: Los Angeles, CA, USA; Irvine, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US government and defense buyers (Space Force, NRO type agencies) and commercial space operators
problem: Tracking and imaging objects in orbit, moving spacecraft and removing debris require maneuverable satellites that are costly and slow to build.
business_model: Government contracts and data sales for space domain awareness, spacecraft and mission software; hardware manufacturing
product_category: Maneuverable satellites and space domain awareness
founder_names: Ryan Westerdahl; Tyler James Pierce; Patryk Wiatr
market_need_then: Growing orbital congestion and US defense interest in commercial space domain awareness and debris removal; later Space Force contract for debris capture technology (July 2024) confirms demand.
outcome_analysis: Turion has progressed from a three founder SpaceX alumni team with a seed round in 2021 to launching DROID.001 in 2023 and DROID.002 in 2025 per Built In, winning a Space Force debris capture contract in 2024, closing a Series A in late 2024 and a 75M dollar Series B in April 2026. Founder domain fit, hardware credibility and growing defense demand for space domain awareness explain the trajectory.

name: UPchieve
one_liner: Connecting low-income HS students with free, 24/7 online tutoring
long_description:
UPchieve is an edtech nonprofit that provides free, 24/7 online tutoring to low-income HS students. Using our app, students can request and get paired with a live volunteer in under 5 minutes. We’ve matched 100,000+ requests so far.

Right now in the US, there are 8 million low-income HS students who don’t have anyone in their home who can help them with schoolwork. UPchieve is working to change that. Our vision is simple: we want to democratize access to academic support, so that every student has an equal opportunity to attend college and achieve upward mobility.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Low-income US middle and high school students (free); funded by donors, foundations and school partnerships
problem: Millions of low-income students have no one at home to help with schoolwork and cannot afford tutoring.
business_model: 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by individual donations, foundation grants and paid partnerships; volunteer tutors
product_category: Free on-demand tutoring nonprofit
market_need_then: Pandemic learning loss in 2020 and 2021 increased demand for free tutoring; the YC page cites 8 million low-income high school students without help at home.
outcome_analysis: UPchieve is an Active nonprofit that matched over 100,000 requests by early 2021 per the YC page, and its site now claims 381,000 matched requests from 57,000 students across all 50 states. Revenue was about 2.7M dollars in 2022 per a Form 990 summary and Gates Foundation support is reported by aggregators. It runs as a donor funded nonprofit rather than a venture backed company, so success is steady mission scale rather than venture growth.

name: Udhaar App
one_liner: We're Khatabook / OkCredit for Pakistan
long_description:
We are a simple book-keeping app, to help 30M micro SMEs run their finances digitally.

I was visiting Pakistan. 1-day, asked our local store owner on plans for his next location. His response, 'never'. 

Since business operations & money flow are manual, he worked 16 hours / 7 days to minimize theft. Zero time with family. We got obsessed with identifying how we can help small business owners run their business and have a life. 

Everything in Pakistan is manual, store credit, sales, purchasing inventory, cash management, tax filings, payments, etc.

This idea got us hooked as it allows us to build a large company and have a huge impact on ~30M small businesses in Pakistan that contribute 74% of the overall GDP.

Explosion in 4G adoption (91M 4G subscribers, 720% growth in 5 years), is helping drive product market fit:
i. >1M downloads
ii. 4.6 star rating on Playstore & Appstore
iii. MAUs & GTV: get in touch :)
regions: Pakistan; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pakistani micro and small retailers (kiryana stores, mobile shops, distributors, pharmacies); YC cites about 30M micro SMEs, Profit cites 10 to 15 million MSMEs that could be digitised
problem: Small businesses in Pakistan track store credit (udhaar), sales, inventory and cash in paper ledgers and by hand, which costs owners long hours and loses money to errors and theft.
business_model: Free bookkeeping app (khata) monetized through commissions on mobile top-ups, bill payments and vouchers, with payroll, invoicing and inventory tools added
product_category: SMB bookkeeping and payments super-app (khata app)
founder_names: Fahad Kamr; Shahjahan Warraich; Myra Ali
competitors_at_founding: Digi Khata; Easy Khata; Credit Book
market_need_then: YC page: manual credit, sales, inventory and tax in Pakistan, 91M 4G subscribers with 720% growth in five years. Profit 2021-11: 1.4M registered users in 421 cities and 510,000 MAU, with MAU up 300% in three months (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Udhaar Book is still active and appears to have found real demand: it reported 1.4M registered users and 510,000 MAU by November 2021, raised a $6M seed from a mix of Pakistani and Silicon Valley fintech investors, and later claims 5.1M businesses. Growth rode cheap 4G and phones plus telecom and bank partnerships. No later priced round is confirmed, so whether the monetization via commissions supports a venture-scale outcome in a market with local competitors is still open.

name: Uiflow
one_liner: No-code platform for enterprise software companies
long_description: At Uiflow we are building a platform that allows for developers and designers to build production applications at the speed of thought. You can imagine it as a cross between Unity and Figma
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Enterprise software companies (250 plus employees) whose developers, designers and product managers build front ends
problem: Enterprise teams spend heavy engineering time hand building front end applications and keeping design and code in sync. Uiflow let developers and designers assemble production apps visually on top of an existing backend.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, pilot customers paying at launch
product_category: No-code and low-code front end app builder
market_need_then: Developers and designers wanted faster delivery of enterprise front ends. The company reported about 1,200 signups after its Product Hunt launch and some paying pilots by April 2021, during a boom in no-code tools.
outcome_analysis: Uiflow rode the 2021 no-code wave, raising a $5.2 million seed in November 2021 and a $15 million Series A in September 2022 on a Unity meets Figma pitch aimed at enterprise front ends. YC now lists the company as acquired, but no acquirer, date or price was found in public sources, so whether this was a strategic exit or a soft landing after the 2022 to 2023 funding downturn is not public.

name: Unfurl
one_liner: A virtual food hall that delivers
long_description: Unfurl is a ghost kitchen, but instead of having one type of food we enable families to order many types of food all in one order. Think of it as an upscale food court where you and your kids can order from 8-15 different restaurants all at once.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Families and groups ordering delivery from many restaurant brands in one order; restaurant brand owners as partners paying a commission
problem: Delivery orders are limited to one restaurant at a time and ghost kitchens struggle with real estate and operations; Unfurl sells a food-court style order from 10 to 20 brands cooked in one hub.
business_model: Ghost kitchen food hall operator; partner brands pay a 5 to 7 percent commission and Unfurl staff cook the food
product_category: Virtual food hall / ghost kitchen
founder_names: Chris Tara-Browne; Mikhail Kokorich; Liudmila Kokorich
competitors_at_founding: DoorDash Kitchens; Kitchen United; CloudKitchens; Local Kitchens
market_need_then: Delivery demand surged in the 2020 pandemic; Food On Demand (2022-02) described Unfurl as a 3-unit operator in the Bay Area (San Francisco, San Mateo, Hayward) planning Los Angeles, Denver and Austin. No customer-side demand data found.
outcome_analysis: YC lists Unfurl as inactive with a team of 20, but no shutdown notice, post-mortem or news about closure was found, so the cause and date are not public. In February 2022 it ran three Bay Area units and planned expansion, so it stopped sometime after. The ghost kitchen category broadly shrank after the pandemic delivery boom (Kitchen United and Epic Kitchens pulled back), but no source ties Unfurl's end to that.

name: Union54
one_liner: Developers of ChitChat, an integrated messaging and payments wallet…
long_description:
ChitChat by Union54 is an integrated messaging and payments platform designed specifically for Africa's unique needs.

Our app combines secure instant messaging with USD card capabilities and cross-border payments, making international money movement more accessible and affordable.

We're tackling one of Africa's biggest financial challenges: the high cost of sending money across borders, where African senders often pay double the fees despite sending smaller amounts.

As a Y Combinator-backed startup, we're building technology that empowers African consumers and businesses to participate more fully in the global digital economy.

Our mission is to create financial products that genuinely serve customer needs while challenging the status quo of traditional remittance providers.
regions: Zambia; Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: African fintechs and software companies issuing cards (original); African consumers and merchants using ChitChat (current)
problem: Card issuing in Africa required a bank or third party processor and was slow; consumers face high cross-border payment fees.
business_model: Card issuing API earning interchange and processing fees; later a messaging and payments super app
product_category: Card issuing API, now messaging and payments wallet
market_need_then: African fintechs needed local card issuing; over 50 companies were in the API sandbox by October 2021 per TechCrunch.
outcome_analysis: Union54 raised 3M dollars in October 2021 and 12M in April 2022, both led by Tiger Global, but in July 2022 it suspended card operations after a chargeback fraud attempt reported at 1.2 billion dollars and the halt lasted about eleven months. It relaunched in 2023 as ChitChat, launching with Mastercard in Zambia in March 2024. In September 2025 a lawsuit by Patrick Sikalinda claimed co-founder status and 33 percent equity, which the company denies. The pivot is not yet proven, so it is recorded as an unresolved risk.

name: Unschool
one_liner: Learn, Intern and become Industry-Ready
long_description: Unschool provides real-world professional education that colleges in India do not provide. We are a marketplace where college students in India can learn about technology, management and arts from high-quality courses created by experts from around the world.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: College students in India who pay for courses, internships and mentorship
problem: Indian colleges do not teach job-ready professional skills, leaving graduates unprepared for employers.
business_model: Course marketplace with revenue share to expert creators; paid courses and internship programs for students
product_category: Edtech course marketplace for students
competitors_at_founding: Newton School; AlmaBetter and Skill-Lync; KnowledgeHut (upGrad)
market_need_then: Indian graduate employability gap and the 2020 and 2021 edtech boom; a 2020 YourStory piece quotes the founder on outdated curricula.
outcome_analysis: Unschool is listed Active by YC but its own site says course access ended in June 2024, so it has effectively stopped delivering courses. Only about 125 to 145 thousand dollars of funding is recorded by aggregators (YC and a Village Capital grant), with no later round, during the 2022 to 2024 Indian edtech downturn when Unacademy cut thousands of jobs and sold to upGrad. The reason for winding down delivery is not public, so the failure factors are inferred from missing follow-on funding and the sector context.

name: V-Flow Medical
one_liner: Transforming the lives of millions of women suffering from chronic…
long_description:
Chronic pelvic pain is a debilitating condition, that impacts over 15 million US women and costs over $39 Billion each year to manage. V-Flow medical has developed a trio of products that target the root cause of chronic pelvic pain, allowing millions of women to avoid opioid use and restart living a normal, pain free life. 

The V-Flow team has successfully scaled, multiple start-up medical device companies in various clinical disciplines with a combined exit value of over $4B. We have developed a broad IP portfolio covering both device design and method of application.  A recent landscaping identified no competing IP for our indication of use. We have tested our beta prototypes and are initiating animal models ahead of a planned first in human investigation in Q1 2023. Following discussion with the NIH program advisors, we have been encouraged to apply for a phase 1 grant, call to action for the Heal initiative to find new diagnostic and non-drug treatments for chronic pelvic pain.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Interventional radiologists and hospitals treating women with chronic pelvic pain from pelvic venous disorders
problem: Chronic pelvic pain affects millions of US women and current options are opioids or limited procedures. V-Flow targeted a venous root cause.
business_model: Regulated medical device sold to hospitals (pre-revenue, not yet cleared)
product_category: Medical device, venous catheter and stent system
founder_names: Peter Balmforth; Rodney Brenneman; Paul Sobotka; Darren Spencer
market_need_then: The company cited over 15 million US women affected and 39 billion dollars annual cost, and the NIH HEAL initiative sought non-opioid pain treatments, per the company's YC description.
outcome_analysis: V-Flow Medical joined YC Summer 2021 with an experienced medtech team and a device aimed at pelvic venous causes of chronic pain. Its only funding found is a 2023 NIH grant of about 300 thousand dollars and it is now listed inactive. The cause of the inactivity is not public, so no failure factors are assigned.

name: Valink Therapeutics
one_liner: Discovering bispecific antibody drug-conjugates (BsADC) against cancer
long_description: Valink Therapeutics develops next generation antibody-based therapeutics. We identify novel mechanism of action from known targets by incorporating multiple antibody modifications at once, rapidly and scalable generating complex drug candidates (bi-/multispecificity, multivalency and drug-conjugation in a single discovery process). Our research focus is on solid tumours poorly addressed by immunotherapy.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Cancer patients with solid tumours poorly served by immunotherapy; commercially, pharma partners and biotech investors who would license or acquire drug candidates
problem: Antibody drug candidates with several modifications at once (bispecific, multivalent, drug-conjugated) are slow and hard to discover, so novel mechanisms of action against known cancer targets are under-explored.
business_model: Therapeutics R&D company: discovery platform plus internal pipeline, partnering and licensing of drug candidates
product_category: Biotech, bispecific antibody drug conjugate (BsADC) discovery
market_need_then: Solid tumours poorly addressed by immunotherapy, and strong industry interest in antibody drug conjugates; the company's own site cites the need for drugs that attack tumours while sparing healthy tissue.
outcome_analysis: Valink is an active Oxford spinout that spent about four years building its LiliumX platform, raised $7.8M in 2023 and $11.8M in 2025, and signed a discovery alliance with Nona Biosciences in December 2025. It is still preclinical, so the outcome is unresolved; the funding pace is modest for biotech, and its fate depends on pipeline data rather than on the YC batch.

name: Vapi
one_liner: Voice AI for developers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and enterprises building voice AI agents for phone and web, such as support and sales calls
problem: Building natural-sounding voice bots needs orchestration of speech-to-text, language models, text-to-speech, telephony and low latency, which is slow for a team to assemble.
business_model: Usage-based API and platform with enterprise contracts
product_category: Voice AI developer platform
market_need_then: Large voice and contact-center spend plus rapid improvement of language models in 2023 made automated phone agents newly feasible; the company later reported Amazon Ring moving its inbound support to Vapi.
outcome_analysis: Vapi is the pivoted successor of the YC W21 company Superpowered. After the November 2023 pivot to a voice API it raised a seed, a $20M Series A in December 2024 and a $50M Series B in May 2026, riding the language model wave and enterprise wins like Amazon Ring. Risks are heavy competition and reliance on third-party model vendors.

name: Varos
one_liner: AI Business Analysts to gather requirements and optimize processes
long_description:
Varos AI delivers the work of business analysts 10x faster, better & cheaper with AI agents built for discovery.

Arthur, our AI agent, acts as a Senior Business Analysts and works for you 24/7 in any language. He conducts intelligent 10-15 minutes voice or text-based interviews with your teams to rapidly capture the institutional knowledge you need to execute on projects. He learns from each conversation, cross-references information, and analyzes all the findings to deliver actionable insights. 

Arthur is an expert at capturing mapping & optimizing complex processes, gathering knowledge from employees' heads and documenting it, supporting automation projects, uncovering root causes to significant problems and more. 

All this information gathered is turned into a private, secure knowledge base that can be used by the org → turning tribal knowledge into institutional knowledge.

For example, Arthur unblocked a critical system migration for a large financial system in 3 days by interviewing 100+ operators in the org, replacing a $1m & 6 month engagement of a consulting firm.

Backed by Y Combinator, Mosaic General Partnership, and leading financial institutions ($8.5m in funding).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Enterprises in regulated and financial sectors (banks, insurers, large tech) that run process and migration projects; originally ecommerce and SaaS companies seeking KPI benchmarks
problem: Capturing institutional knowledge and business requirements normally needs months of analyst or consultant interviews; originally, marketers could not see how their KPIs compared with peers.
business_model: Enterprise project and software subscription (AI business analyst agent); originally subscription benchmarking SaaS
product_category: AI agents for business analysis and knowledge capture; originally data benchmarking
founder_names: Yarden Shaked; Lior Chen; Gil Shaked
market_need_then: Marketers and founders lacked peer benchmarks for core metrics; TechCrunch covered the February 2022 launch under the headline about showing companies how they compare to peers.
outcome_analysis: Varos launched as a peer benchmarking product, raised a $4M seed in February 2022 and later moved to an AI business analyst agent sold to large financial institutions. It is active with a nine person team; the YC page claims 8.5M raised in total, but the extra funding is not documented in other sources, so the traction is only partly verified.

name: VedaBio
one_liner: CRISPR powered Diagnostics with results in minutes.
long_description: Syndromic testing powered by engineered CRISPR enzymes. Get comprehensive results in every doctor visit. More at www.vedabio.com
all_locations: San Diego, CA, USA; Urbana, IL, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Urgent care centers and clinical labs that run syndromic respiratory tests; ultimately patients and health systems
problem: Most urgent-care respiratory patients leave without a molecular answer because PCR testing is slow and needs lab equipment and trained operators.
business_model: Diagnostic instrument plus single-use cartridges (in development, not yet for sale); strategic distribution via Siemens Healthineers
product_category: CRISPR molecular diagnostics
market_need_then: The company's site cites about 65M respiratory urgent-care visits per year and a large share of patients leaving without a molecular answer; the pandemic highlighted demand for fast molecular tests.
outcome_analysis: VedaBio came out of stealth in October 2023 with over $40M from OMX Ventures, added a Series A extension and a strategic deal with Siemens Healthineers in September 2025, and says its product is still in development and not for sale. Success depends on proving amplification-free performance and winning FDA clearance, so the outcome is unresolved.

name: Veera Health
one_liner: We treat women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome in India
long_description:
Veera Health is helping 110M women in India get treated for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS).  Our app combines evidence-backed therapy with coaching & specialist support for a subscription fee.

PCOS is the most common cause of infertility in women, and can lead to diabetes, depression and cancer. Patients spend up to 10 years and thousands of rupees searching for the right treatment, yet 90% are dissatisfied with existing options. With our program, 85% patients report feeling "in control" of their PCOS after just 1 month and are 4-times more likely to complete treatment.

The founders, Shobhita (COO) and Shashwata (CEO) got an inside view into this massive need when the former was diagnosed with PCOS. Shashwata studied data science at Yale University, holds an MBA from Wharton, and helped grow Fortune 100 and growth-stage consumer health / product companies at McKinsey. Shobhita studied Biology & Psychology at Tufts University and has worked with leading healthcare companies, such as GlaxoSmithKline, Accenture Life Sciences & UnitedHealth.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Women in India with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), paying a subscription or buying supplements
problem: PCOS patients spend years and large sums finding treatment and most are dissatisfied with existing options.
business_model: Subscription app combining therapy, coaching and specialist support; later direct-to-consumer supplements
product_category: Women's health, digital therapeutics and nutraceuticals
market_need_then: The YC page cites 110M women in India with PCOS, years of diagnostic delay and widespread dissatisfaction with treatment; the July 2021 round was covered by several Indian outlets.
outcome_analysis: Veera Health raised a $3M seed in July 2021 and is active, but its public site has shifted from a PCOS treatment app toward supplements for weight loss, skin and PCOS. No later round was found; the shift suggests the original subscription model was not enough alone, though that is inference. Outcome is unresolved.

name: Vendease
one_liner: Where restaurants in Africa buy food supplies
long_description:
Vendease is a marketplace that lets restaurants in Africa, order directly from farms and food manufacturers.

Now, instead of going through expensive - middlemen - vendors, or wasting productive man hours sending staff to open markets with hiked prices, restaurants can now get on our platform, click to order and get all their food supplies within 24hrs.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Restaurants, hotels and food businesses in Nigeria and Ghana that buy food supplies
problem: Restaurants buy through expensive middlemen or send staff to open markets with inflated prices, wasting time and money.
business_model: B2B marketplace take rate and margin on supplies, plus ERP software and buy-now-pay-later
product_category: B2B food supply marketplace and procurement
founder_names: Tunde Kara; Gatumi Aliyu; Olumide Fayankin; Wale Oyepeju
market_need_then: Restaurants faced middlemen markups and market trips; TechCrunch covered the company in March 2021 as an Amazon-style supplier for restaurants.
outcome_analysis: Vendease raised a $3.2M seed in October 2021 and a $30M Series A package in September 2022 ($20M equity, $10M debt), but then cut 9% of staff in November 2022, 68 people in September 2024 and about 120 in February 2025 while restructuring toward profitability, and its CFO left in 2025. The record points to growth that outran margins in a tough funding climate; no shutdown is reported.

name: Venu AI
one_liner: Meet qualified leads in person by automating conference production
long_description: Meet qualified leads in person by automating conference production with Venu AI. Host a conference and meet 100 qualified sales leads in person every 3 months fully automated with Venu AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Companies and organizations that host conferences and events to meet qualified sales leads, customers or investors
problem: Producing conferences that reliably deliver qualified in-person leads is labor intensive and requires event expertise.
business_model: Software subscription for event production (a directory lists $49 per month, unverified)
product_category: Event and conference production software
founder_names: Jeremy Lam; Fanny Chen; Justin Chen; Nanette Jackson; Patrick Nguyen
market_need_then: The pandemic forced events online in 2020 and event platforms raised large rounds; demand for online conferences was strong but proved temporary.
outcome_analysis: Venu launched into the pandemic virtual event boom and now sells automation for in-person conferences. No funding round is verified, the team is small, and the YC page lists five founders without bios. The category's collapse after 2022 is documented, but the company's own outcome is unclear and its status is active with little public evidence.

name: Verak
one_liner: Better Business Insurance for MSMEs in India
long_description:
Verak is now part of InsuranceDekho as of April 2023.

Verak offered next day coverage starting at ₹8 per day for MSMEs in India to insure any facility (shop, warehouse, factory etc) against 15+ natural & man-made perils. (*)

Our team worked across the entire insurance value-chain: From satellite based underwriting to machine learning based pricing to instant quotation to WhatsApp based claims.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Micro, small and medium enterprises in India, such as shopkeepers and small factories, buying property and liability cover
problem: Indian MSMEs have very low insurance penetration because cover is slow, paperwork heavy and priced for large firms. Verak sold next day cover from 8 rupees a day with WhatsApp claims.
business_model: Insurance distribution commission on premiums, with data driven underwriting and pricing
product_category: Insurtech for small business
market_need_then: In April 2021 India's insurance regulator introduced two standard MSME property products, and reports put MSME insurance penetration at about 5 percent. This created a regulatory push and a large underserved base.
outcome_analysis: Verak pivoted from the consumer BimaPe product to MSME insurance in September 2021 and reported 30 percent month on month premium growth by the time InsuranceDekho acqui-hired the team in April 2023. The price was not disclosed and most outlets call it an acqui-hire, which points to a soft landing for a small team that had raised well under two million dollars in confirmed funding.

name: Verano Health
tags: Mental Health Tech; Consumer Health Services; Healthcare IT
one_liner: Nonprofit telehealth coaches for underserved Americans on Medicaid
long_description:
We're building the nation's largest digital diabetes platform for underserved Americans. There are 80 million Americans on Medicaid and 30% or more have chronic disease. Less than 1% of patients with diabetes receive needed training.

We provide a SMS-based telehealth platform to people with chronic disease on Medicaid. Our proven Healthy at Home program uses 2-way SMS interactions, weekly diabetes coaching visits, and evidence-based health education. 

Our vision is to reach millions of Americans that lack at-home support for chronic disease. We're billing health insurance $186 for telehealth visits and have 2 contracts underway. With your support, we can be a fully sustainable nonprofit by 2023.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Medicaid enrolled patients with chronic disease, paid for through health insurance billing and contracts
problem: Under 1 percent of people with diabetes receive needed training, and Medicaid patients have little at-home support. Verano delivered SMS based coaching and weekly telehealth visits.
business_model: Nonprofit billing health insurance per telehealth visit, with contracts with plans
product_category: Digital health coaching, diabetes
market_need_then: The YC description cites 80 million Americans on Medicaid with 30 percent or more having chronic disease, and the company reported billing 186 dollars per telehealth visit with two contracts underway in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Verano Health, formerly CoachMe Health, was a three person nonprofit SMS diabetes coaching service for Medicaid patients when it joined YC in Summer 2021, with a stated goal of financial sustainability by 2023. YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or terms and no funding history were found in public sources, so the story of why or how it ended up acquired is not public.

name: Verde
one_liner: Digital lending platform for Brazilian farmers
long_description: Verde is a lending platform that offers fast loans to small-and-medium sized farmers in Brazil. Our vertical software allows independent ag loan advisors to originate loans digitally and manage their operations more effectively.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Verihubs
one_liner: AI-powered Deepfake Detection
long_description:
Verihubs is an Indonesian AI-powered verification company. We have helped more than 300 companies ranging from digital disruptors to Fortune 500 companies in Southeast Asia. Ranked #1 in Indonesia by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in terms of performance and accuracy, our AI-based face recognition (FR) technology became a staple in fraud prevention in this new era of digital acceleration. Our solutions have been trusted by BCA—the largest private bank in Indonesia, IFG (one of the largest state-owned insurance), Commonwealth Bank, Maybank, Bukalapak, FAZZ, Ministry of Finance, and many other industry leaders.

The pandemic has accelerated the digital development and adoption of products, services, and processes by 4-7 years according to recent studies. However, the verification solutions and related data to meet these digital needs are still so behind the ideal mark. We at Verihubs are on a mission to build an all-inclusive automated and instant verification platform for Indonesia.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Banks, fintechs, insurers and digital businesses in Indonesia that must verify customer identity
problem: Digital onboarding in Indonesia needs fast, accurate identity verification and fraud prevention, but verification data and tooling lagged the shift to digital services.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API usage-based identity verification
product_category: Identity verification, face recognition and deepfake detection
market_need_then: The YC page cites pandemic-driven digital acceleration and unmet verification needs; the company reports serving over 300 companies at the time of the batch and more than 400 clients later.
outcome_analysis: Verihubs raised a $2.8M seed in September 2021 led by Insignia Venture Partners and grew into an identity verification vendor for Indonesian banks and insurers, later adding deepfake detection in late 2024. It is active with 63 staff and more than 400 clients; no later priced round was found.

name: Version Story Compare
one_liner: Git for Lawyers — now within Claude
long_description: Version Story is Git for Lawyers, offering a suite of deterministic tools — compare, merge, rebase, etc. — via MCP and REST API. Easy to embed in Claude or in custom applications.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Law firms and legal teams negotiating contracts, plus AI tool builders needing redlines
problem: Managing document versions and redlines in legal work is slow and risky.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API (pricing not found)
product_category: legal document comparison and version control
market_need_then: No dated source describing demand for this product at the time of founding was found, so the market need at founding is unknown and is not inferred here.
outcome_analysis: Version Story entered YC Winter 2021 and by 2026 sells document comparison, track and merge tools through a web app, REST API and Claude and ChatGPT connectors. Customer logos are shown but no funding amounts, revenue or outcome are public, so success cannot be judged from the sources found.

name: Vibe Kanban
one_liner: Plan and review AI generated code
long_description: As AI agents become more capable at writing code, developers are spending more of their time planning and reviewing what those agents produce. Vibe Kanban helps them do exactly that, seamlessly integrating with leading coding agents like Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Software developers and engineering teams using AI coding agents
problem: As agents write more code, developers spend their time planning and reviewing agent output and need a way to run several agents in parallel and review the results.
business_model: Open source tool with paid team subscriptions (terminated at sunset)
product_category: Developer tools, AI coding agent orchestration
market_need_then: Developers in 2021 wanted better code search and navigation; by 2025 coding agents created demand for plan and review tooling, with the project reaching about 20,000 GitHub stars per a podcast title.
outcome_analysis: Bloop started as an open source code search engine and pivoted in 2025 to Vibe Kanban, which spread quickly among developers using coding agents. It did not find a business model that justified continuing, and the team announced the company shutdown in April 2026 while handing the open source project to the community. Agent vendors absorbing orchestration features and the free open source license likely limited paid conversion, though the company only stated that no satisfactory business model was found.

name: Vinco
one_liner: Retaining employees in LatAm via education
long_description: Vinco helps companies in Latin America pay for blue-collar employees’ online education. We do this by connecting employees to accessible programs (like High School, College, and Language Courses) and in turn, improve employee retention by at least 2x.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Large employers in Latin America paying for blue-collar employee education
problem: Employers in LatAm lose workers to turnover and have no easy way to fund and manage education for frontline employees.
business_model: B2B platform; support fee as a percentage of tuition paid by universities per enrolled student, plus employer programs
product_category: Employer education benefits
founder_names: Lissy Giacoman Colyer; Miriam Fernandez Guerra; Sofia Sada Segovia
market_need_then: Per the company, 185 million LatAm employees lack a high school diploma, and employee retention was a stated pain; employer paid education had proven in the US via Guild.
outcome_analysis: Vinco sold employer funded education to large LatAm employers such as OXXO, Femsa and DiDi, raising a $2.4M seed in October 2021 and reaching a claimed 100 plus companies. The team of women founders from Monterrey had consulting and elite university backgrounds, and the company reported a five year anniversary in December 2025, so it appears to be a steady, active company without a later public round.

name: Vogent
one_liner: Build Voice AI Agents
long_description: Vogent is an all-in-one platform for building voice agents by using intelligent building blocks, including IVR detection models, custom phone-ready LLMs, drag-and-drop conversational flow builders, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Businesses and developers building voice agents for phone calls, including call center and healthcare use cases
problem: Phone calls are costly to staff, and voice agents need reliable IVR navigation, turn taking and low latency to sound natural.
business_model: Usage based platform and API with enterprise plans
product_category: Voice AI agent platform
market_need_then: Outbound and call center phone work was large and labor heavy in 2021; the original Elto product targeted AI calling and parallel dialing, though no dated demand figures were sourced.
outcome_analysis: Vogent started as Elto with AI calling and dialer products, then rebranded around 2024 as a voice agent platform with IVR detection, turn detection and open model tooling, claiming over 1M calls per month with a team of three. Aircall acquired it in May 2026 for undisclosed terms, a talent and technology buy by a business phone vendor riding the voice AI wave.

name: Voosh
one_liner: Making Restaurants more data-driven!
long_description: Voosh is a Food Technology company aiming to empower Food Service brands using our proprietary visualisation tools and Data Science. One stop visualisation tool for CXOs, Operational heads or Zonal managers to get business insights and take real time decisions to help grow online sales.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Restaurant brands selling through third party delivery marketplaces
problem: Restaurants lose money to disputed orders, payout mismatches, bad promotion ROI and store downtime on delivery marketplaces.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: Restaurant operations automation
market_need_then: Restaurants in India were shifting to Zomato and Swiggy delivery in 2020, creating need for sales visibility and margin tracking.
outcome_analysis: Voosh began as an Indian virtual restaurant chain with a December 2020 pre-seed from Better Capital, then turned its internal data tooling into software and moved to the US market, with customers such as a Wendy's franchisee and KFC franchise group. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, so it looks like a quiet, active company.

name: Wabi
one_liner: We are Shopify for the $15B creator economy in LATAM
long_description: We are Shopify for the $15B creator economy in LATAM starting with online coaching businesses. For example, a fitness coach can use our no-code builder to get a branded landing page integrated with payments and a website that can host their online coaching programs and subscriber-only content.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: WarpBuild
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; SaaS; Productivity; DevOps
one_liner: Accelerate software development with WarpBuild's 10x faster CI infra.
long_description:
Accelerate software development with WarpBuild.
Get 2x faster, up to 90% cheaper CI in 30 seconds using WarpBuild for Github Actions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software teams using GitHub Actions
problem: GitHub hosted runners are slow and expensive for CI.
business_model: Usage-based CI runners
product_category: CI infrastructure
market_need_then: Complaints about GitHub Actions cost and speed, per the company's launch claims.
outcome_analysis: WarpBuild sells faster, cheaper GitHub Actions runners and now lists customers such as Sonar, Comcast, Raycast and Plex. Funding details are unclear, with only aggregator figures between $0.5M and $2M in 2021. It remains active and competes with many runner vendors.

name: Warpfy
one_liner: Building Shein of Home: tech-driven, design-mfr Home Lifestyle Brand
long_description:
The Fine Living Company (Warpfy) is on a mission to revolutionize the $800B home and kitchen market, building a tech-enabled cross-border Home Lifestyle brand from India—think Shein for Home or Williams Sonoma. 
Our Design-to-Manufacture-to-Consumer model cuts out the middlemen, delivering high-quality products directly to consumers (D2C), through marketplaces, and via our proprietary B2B channel, The India Wholesale Company). 
With a fragmented market where 70% is dominated by single-store boutiques and online penetration is just 20%, Home and Kitchen segment is ripe for disruption. India’s share of products has been minimal due to 60%+ value inflation from intermediaries. We’re changing that.
Our full-stack approach: AI Copilot-driven product design, ERP for multi-channel distribution & manufacturer retention, and optimized supply chain—offers unparalleled speed & value.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Global consumers and B2B buyers of home and kitchen products
problem: Indian manufacturers lack a design-led brand and distribution to sell home goods globally.
business_model: Direct to consumer, marketplace and B2B wholesale of own brand home products
product_category: Home lifestyle brand
market_need_then: Company cites an $800B home and kitchen market and demand for cross border goods made in India.
outcome_analysis: Warpfy pitched a Shein of home model for India made home goods and now runs The Fine Living Company and an India wholesale platform, with company reported 300 plus products. Public information is thin, funding aside from a reported $125K pre-seed in aggregators is unknown, and no outcome event was found.

name: Warrant
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Open Source; API
one_liner: Authorization and access control as a service.
long_description: Warrant is an open source authorization service that helps developers implement and enforce access control in their applications. Warrant serves as a dedicated, centralized platform for handling user authorization and access control so engineering teams can focus on building their core products.
all_locations: Los Angeles, CA, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software engineering teams that need fine grained, relationship based access control in their applications
problem: Teams hand build authorization logic that becomes brittle as products grow. Warrant offered a centralized, open source service modeled on Google's Zanzibar system.
business_model: Open source core with a hosted usage based cloud service
product_category: Developer infrastructure, authorization
market_need_then: Google published the Zanzibar paper in 2019 and developers wanted an accessible implementation. The founders said no publicly available implementation existed when they started.
outcome_analysis: Warrant built an open source Zanzibar inspired authorization service that a three person team shipped in 2021, then sold the company and product to WorkOS in April 2024, where it became WorkOS FGA. Funding found was minimal and unverified, and competing open source engines from Auth0 and AuthZed emerged, so the exit looks like a strategic tuck in rather than a venture scale outcome. Terms were not disclosed.

name: Wasp
one_liner: Configuration language for building enterprise web apps 10x faster
long_description:
Wasp is a simple configuration language for building enterprise web apps with less code and best practices. If a developer wants to build an app like Instacart, they need to know a dozen different technologies and how to make them work together - Wasp solves this problem while still letting developers use React, Node.js and their other favourite tools.

We will enable enterprises to build modern apps quickly at scale, like Databricks did for data management.
regions: Croatia; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Web developers and startups building full-stack React and Node apps
problem: Building full-stack web apps requires heavy boilerplate for auth, CRUD and jobs.
business_model: Open source framework with planned paid hosting and services
product_category: Developer tools, full-stack framework
market_need_then: Developers wanted less boilerplate; TechCrunch reported about 300 apps built on the alpha in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Wasp raised a $1.5M seed in 2021, built an open source framework and grew through the Open SaaS template to 26,000 GitHub stars. A $3.7M round closed in late 2024 and total raised is $5.2M. The team is small, about eight people, and has not shown a revenue model yet.

name: Waterplan
tags: Machine Learning; SaaS; B2B; Climate; ClimateTech
one_liner: Water risk mitigation for industrial sites
long_description: Waterplan is the world’s leading climate platform to measure, respond, report, and monitor companies increasingly changing climate water risk. Customers include multinational companies like Coca-Cola, Diageo, Colgate & Ab InBev. The platform combines companies’ operational data with local water satellite imagery to provide a continuously updated financial assessment of water risk. Based on that, it offers tailored mitigation and adaptation opportunities, from conventional infrastructure to nature-based solutions. The company was founded by a team of tech and water 2nd-time entrepreneurs with two exits and almost ten years of experience working for Fortune 500 companies in water projects. Early investors include YCombinator, Giant Ventures, David Helgason, Leonardo DiCaprio, Richard Branson's family, Manu Ginobili, among others waterplan.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Large water-dependent corporations (beverage, consumer goods, mining)
problem: Companies lack site level water risk data to measure, report and mitigate water exposure.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS with implementation and advisory support
product_category: Climate and water risk software
market_need_then: Corporate buyers faced rising water scarcity and disclosure expectations in 2021, and the company's launch pitch cited customers such as Coca-Cola, Diageo, Colgate and AB InBev needing a financial view of site level water risk.
outcome_analysis: Waterplan raised a $7M seed in April 2022 and an $11M Series A in May 2023 led by Base10, selling to large beverage and consumer goods companies. Founders had water and software backgrounds. It has expanded into carbon and AI metering and no exit or shutdown has been reported.

name: Waydev
one_liner: Engineering intelligence for AI transformation
long_description: Waydev maps AI velocity across the SDLC — built on DORA, SPACE, and DX — turning developer tool data into board-ready evidence of adoption, impact, and ROI.
regions: Romania; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering leaders at software companies
problem: Engineering leaders lack data on developer productivity and delivery.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Engineering analytics
market_need_then: Rise of remote engineering teams and DORA metrics.
outcome_analysis: Waydev was incorporated in March 2017, bootstrapped to profitability before YC W21, and sells to enterprises such as American Express and Caterpillar per its own pages. Public funding is only small YC money in aggregators. It has retooled for AI adoption analytics and remains active.

name: Waypoint
one_liner: The email API built for product teams
long_description:
Waypoint combines a modern email API with a visual template builder so teams can ship faster.

Alternative to SendGrid, MailGun, or Postmark.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product and engineering teams at software companies that send data-rich transactional email such as receipts, order confirmations and alerts
