Our aim is to make the app inclusive for all. The stock market unfortunately can be very technical and opaque and therefore isn’t always accessible for all. However, when we start allowing trading in categories such as cricket, politics and entertainment, not only do we make trading more relatable, but we also help improve their financial literacy.
all_locations: Bengaluru, KA, India; Gurugram, HR, India; Remote
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Retail users in India, mostly young mobile users, trading on event outcomes such as cricket, politics and entertainment
problem: Stock markets are technical and opaque; the product lets everyday users trade opinions on events with real money.
business_model: Opinion trading app taking a fee on trades
product_category: Prediction market / consumer fintech
market_need_then: India has a large audience for cricket and betting adjacent apps and a large retail trading base; the company reported 600,000 users trading over Rs 10 crore by mid 2022.
outcome_analysis: Better Opinions raised a small pre seed and a $2.5M seed in 2022, and reported fast early user growth in a market with strong cricket and betting adjacent demand. The outcome is still open and regulation of opinion trading in India is the main risk; later rounds were not found, so success is not established.

name: Beyond Aero
tags: Hydrogen Energy; Airplanes; Energy; Electric Vehicles; Aerospace
one_liner: First electric business aircraft designed for hydrogen propulsion
long_description: Beyond Aero is building the first electric business aircraft powered by hydrogen propulsion, enabling six passengers to fly up to 800 NM (1,500 km), a range unattainable with battery-electric aircraft. Founded in December 2020, the company is redesigning the architecture of an aircraft around hydrogen-electric propulsion, focusing on fuel cell technology, gaseous hydrogen tank integration, and advanced cooling systems. With offices in Toulouse, Paris, and Los Angeles, the company boasts a team of over 80 highly qualified engineers from leading aerospace companies. Beyond Aero has secured over $50 million in funding, backed by investors such as Giant Ventures, Bpifrance, and prior supporters like Initialized Capital, Female Founders Fund, and 7 Percent Ventures. Beyond Aero also completed Y Combinator in 2022. The company has secured $1.5bn in Letters of Intent (LOIs), completed France’s first manned, fully hydrogen-electric flight, and acquired Universal Hydrogen Co.'s assets, IP, and flight data. Beyond Aero is a member of the World Economic Forum’s First Movers Coalition and the Alliance for Zero Emission Aviation, underscoring its commitment to electrifying aviation with hydrogen propulsion.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Business aviation operators and buyers of private aircraft, including letters of intent from airlines and charter firms
problem: Battery electric aircraft cannot reach business jet ranges, so the company designs an aircraft around hydrogen fuel cells for about six passengers and 800 nautical miles.
business_model: Aircraft OEM selling hydrogen-electric business aircraft, with pre-orders via letters of intent
product_category: Hydrogen-electric aircraft manufacturing
founder_names: Eloa Guillotin; Hugo Tarlé; Valentin Chomel
market_need_then: Pressure to decarbonise private aviation and the range limits of battery electric aircraft; the company reports about $1.5bn in letters of intent (YC page, later).
outcome_analysis: Beyond Aero is an active hydrogen aircraft developer that raised a $20M Series A in October 2024 for about $44M total including debt and grants, and later reported a TRL6 propulsion system test and the acquisition of Universal Hydrogen assets. The long certification path means outcome is unresolved; the capital intensity and timeline to the early 2030s are the main risks.

name: BharatX
one_liner: Enable Buy-Now-Pay-Later in a White-Labelled Manner
long_description:
BharatX was recently acquired by Flipkart, the largest startup in India, to enable Buy Now Pay Later in their own ecosystem as well as bolster their own FinTech play via Super.money. It powers Checkout Financing in their ecosystem currently on Millions of Users.

BharatX enabled "Pay in 3" and "Pay in X" parts as a feature on over 1000+ brands, 300+ directly and the rest via Payment Gateway partners. Our product enabled Buy Now Pay Later, in a white-labelled way. For e.g. Flipkart PayLater on Flipkart. We grew 47X to $2.5M ARR in under 6 quarters straight after fumbling for 2 years around PMF and Credit Risk & Fraud. 

We started out as a platform to provide access to Credit in Developing countries without relying on traditional documentation processes by Banks, which did not give access to hundreds of millions.Over the course of BharatX, we have credit to hundreds of thousands of consumers, including many New to Credit (NTC) users.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Indian consumer brands and merchants that want to offer buy now pay later at checkout under their own name
problem: Indian shoppers, especially new to credit users, lacked credit access at checkout, and merchants lacked a white-label way to offer pay in 3 or EMI without building underwriting.
business_model: B2B2C white-label BNPL; fees from merchants and credit margin, with BharatX taking credit risk
product_category: Embedded credit / BNPL infrastructure
founder_names: Mehul Nath Jindal; Eeshan Sharma; Shyam Murugan; Siddharth Venu
competitors_at_founding: Razorpay with Capital Float; Simpl, ZestMoney, ePayLater, LazyPay
market_need_then: Indian BNPL was growing quickly in 2021 and 2022, with merchants seeking conversion lift at checkout and large new to credit populations lacking card access.
outcome_analysis: BharatX raised a $4.5M seed in May 2022 after YC and reported growing 47x to $2.5M ARR in under six quarters on white-label pay in 3 and EMI products for hundreds of brands. The founder says regulation hit the business hard and it was sold in February 2025 for an undisclosed all-cash price, with technology, IP and the team moving to Flipkart-backed super.money. It reads as a modest exit after a regulatory squeeze rather than a large win.

name: Bifrost
one_liner: Wills and Estate Management for Crypto
long_description:
We write smart contracts that can automatically transfer assets during end-of-life events.
When you hold your own keys to your own wallet, your funds are lost in worst-case-scenarios. We make an on-chain dead-mans-switch to help your loved ones claim your holdings.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: BiggerPicture
one_liner: The freight appointment network for carriers, shippers and warehouses
long_description:
BiggerPicture is a freight appointment network. Carriers, shippers and warehouses schedule from one shared shipment record, each in their own view.

Carriers and brokers automate appointment booking across customer portals and email, with an exception queue for anything that needs a person. Warehouses run their docks and yards with a live dock schedule, QR driver self check-in, detention tracking and carrier compliance scorecards. Shippers see every order across facilities and grade carriers on the same compliance standard their warehouses use.

Because every party sees the same record, a confirmed time updates everyone at once. No reconciling emails, portals and spreadsheets.

BiggerPicture runs the largest freight scheduling network. Founded in 2020 by Deema Adada and Guillaume Lo Re. SOC 2 Type I certified.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Carriers, brokers, shippers and warehouses that schedule freight appointments
problem: Freight appointments are booked through portals, email and spreadsheets, so parties lack one shared record and incur detention and delays.
business_model: B2B SaaS, network across carriers, shippers and warehouses
product_category: Freight appointment scheduling network
market_need_then: Manual appointment booking across portals and email; the YC page cites the founders' freight operations experience.
outcome_analysis: BiggerPicture appears to be an active freight scheduling company whose site claims 80,000 appointments monthly and 45,000 verified facilities, with SOC 2 Type I. Funding is unverified so the fundraising trajectory is unknown. Founder operating experience at Coyote and Uber Freight fits the domain; no shutdown or acquisition was found.

name: Birch Biosciences
tags: Machine Learning; Synthetic Biology; Biotech; Climate; ClimateTech
one_liner: We recycle plastic using engineered enzymes
long_description: Birch Biosciences engineers enzymes for plastic recycling using synthetic biology and machine learning.  Our enzymes function as high performance “molecular scissors” that efficiently break down plastic polymers into chemical building blocks that can be used to manufacture high quality recycled plastic products.   Today, plastic manufacturing  is unsustainable and a major driver of climate change.   Birch Biosciences is developing an economical end-to-end plastic recycling process that reduces carbon emissions by 70% and enables a circular plastic economy.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Plastic recyclers and brand owners buying recycled PET and polyurethane inputs
problem: Mechanical recycling degrades plastic, so engineered enzymes depolymerise PET into monomers for virgin-quality recycled resin.
business_model: Technology developer funded by grants and equity, aiming at licensing or process deployment
product_category: Enzymatic plastic recycling, synthetic biology
market_need_then: Plastic waste regulation and brand recycled-content targets; the company claims 70% lower emissions than virgin plastic (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Birch is active and funded largely by non-dilutive grants: NSF SBIR Phase I and II, a DOE Phase II, a DARPA award and an NREL licence per its site. Equity funding is poorly documented and aggregators disagree, so the trajectory beyond grants is unclear. The science is hard and capital needs are high.

name: Bitstack
one_liner: All things money, with better money
long_description:
Bitstack is building a new neobank powered by crypto. Bitstack has gone from a simple product that turns your spare change into bitcoin to a bitcoin-native neobank that is bringing a better way to manage all things money, with better money. We believe getting started with Bitcoin should be simple, fun and accessible to everyone.

Bitcoin is an unparalleled financial alternative: a radically new way to transact and store value all around the world. It is a new kind of currency that isn't centrally controlled by any business, government or bank and that cannot be debased. Bitcoin will redefine the future of finance, from payments to savings, and wealth preservation. It is the first open and borderless monetary network with a fixed supply of 21 million, making bitcoin the most scarce financial asset ever.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Retail savers in France and Europe who want to accumulate bitcoin effortlessly
problem: Buying bitcoin is intimidating, so the app turns spare change and recurring buys into bitcoin and now adds a card and euro account.
business_model: Consumer fintech: trading fees, card interchange and subscription features
product_category: Bitcoin savings app and neobank
market_need_then: Growing retail interest in bitcoin and French registration regime for crypto providers (PSAN registration granted in 2022 per company).
outcome_analysis: Bitstack grew from a spare-change bitcoin app to a licensed European bitcoin savings and card product, raising four institutional rounds ending with a $15M Series A in December 2025 and then a crowd round. Regulatory registration and MiCA approval gave a moat in France while the company expanded to four countries.

name: Blaze
one_liner: Marketing automation for the modern world
long_description: Blaze uses AI and automation to scan millions of online signals to help modern companies target the right potential customers as soon as they show interest.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Web3 and consumer product teams building communities on Discord and social channels (per a Dec 2022 post); YC page describes marketing teams
problem: Teams cannot see who in their community is engaged, so Blaze unifies social, on-chain and product data into member profiles and automations.
business_model: B2B SaaS CRM and analytics
product_category: Community growth CRM and marketing automation
market_need_then: Crypto and web3 communities on Discord were growing in 2021 to 2022 with little tooling for member analytics.
outcome_analysis: Blaze has little public record: a Dec 2022 profile, YC and angel backing, and a founder who later moved to another company per an unreliable mirror. The status in YC is active but the site was unreachable from the session, so whether it still operates is unknown. No factors are assigned because the sources do not tell a clear story.

name: Blee
one_liner: Smart, fast, and collaborative compliance reviews
long_description: Blee easily integrates across the content creation workflow, combining instant feedback and faster approvals with scalable review and recordkeeping. Helping companies maximize revenue by moving faster to market while minimizing risk
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Compliance, legal and marketing teams at financial services and other regulated companies
problem: Marketing content needs manual legal and compliance review that slows launches, so Blee reviews content with AI and logs approvals for audit.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS
product_category: AI marketing compliance platform
market_need_then: Fintech marketing claims face regulators and review queues; Blee's customers include fintechs per its site.
outcome_analysis: Blee raised a $20M Series A in September 2026 with customers such as SoFi, Brex, NerdWallet and PayPal logos on its site, and a reported 65% review-time reduction that is company-reported. Growth in AI-generated content increased review load, which is the stated tailwind.

name: Blink
one_liner: Build fully functional apps with AI.
long_description:
Blink is the fastest way to build and launch web apps—no coding required. Our AI-powered platform lets anyone create full-stack apps in minutes: just describe what you want, and Blink handles design, database, backend, hosting, and authentication instantly. Apps are fully editable, remixable, and deploy with one click to a live site, including custom domains and monetization.

Builders, startups, and creators use Blink to launch MVPs, internal tools, SaaS products, and websites up to 20× faster—no developers needed. Each app is shareable and remixable, powering viral growth. Blink is “Shopify for web apps,” making software creation as easy and fun as making a TikTok.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Non-technical builders, startups and creators who want to launch web apps without developers
problem: Building and hosting a full-stack web app with database, auth and deployment requires developers or stitching several tools together.
business_model: Subscription SaaS with usage tiers for an AI app builder
product_category: AI full-stack app builder (vibe coding)
market_need_then: By 2025 demand for AI coding and no-code app creation was strong; Blink reported (via aggregators, unverified) a community of many user built apps.
outcome_analysis: Blink is an active, very early stage AI app builder run by a repeat YC founder who previously built 1Flow. It gained Product Hunt attention in 2025 and 2026, but no verified funding or revenue data exists, and it competes in a crowded prompt to app market with little structural defensibility.

name: Blitz
one_liner: Lovable for non-tech users: Build no-code internal and customer apps
long_description:
Blitz is a no-code platform to build internal applications and automate manual tasks. Quickly build a database, integrate your logic, and scale your operations. 

Alternative to Google Sheet and Airtable, Blitz is not limited by a number of lines of records or by an API rate. 

Create your data model and set up data validation rules. Use our interface builder to create dynamic forms, and quickly onboard customer and partners. Leverage our granular permissions to share data to external users (publicly or privately). Add advanced business logic to your forms and portals, without writing any line of code. The experience is similar to creating spreadsheets, but without their limitations in terms of scalability and security. 

You can use Blitz to build an onboarding flow, an order management system or some validation workflows for compliance purposes. 

Stop using developer resources or rigid SaaS software. Start building your own tools, adapted to your needs, with Blitz.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Operations and product teams that run processes in spreadsheets
problem: Existing no-code tools do not scale for internal workflows, so operations teams go back to spreadsheets; Blitz offers a database plus forms, portals and logic without code.
business_model: B2B SaaS (pre-launch beta)
product_category: No-code internal app and database platform
market_need_then: The launch post claims many no-code tools do not work for internal operations; no hard demand data.
outcome_analysis: Blitz is listed active but the site still says the beta is coming soon with a 2025 footer, years after its 2022 launch. No verified funding or traction exists. No shutdown was found, and the shutdown stories in results concerned Internal.io, a different company.

name: Blitzllama
one_liner: A platform to collect and analyze in-product user feedback
long_description: Blitzllama makes it easy for product development teams to rapidly collect user feedback at scale. With only a simple SDK integration, teams can ask questions to their users within product journeys and get highly contextual answers in minutes. This empowers product teams to ship products that address users' real problems that increase user retention, engagement and reduce churn.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product teams at software companies, mainly fintech and retail, wanting in-app user feedback
problem: Product teams struggle to collect contextual user feedback quickly inside the product journey without building survey tooling.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with SDK-embedded surveys
product_category: In-product feedback and survey analytics
founder_names: Rahul Mallapur; Joel Koshy; Bently Nixon
market_need_then: Product teams wanted faster user research and contextual feedback, but no dated 2021 to 2022 source was found to quantify demand.
outcome_analysis: Blitzllama joined YC in Winter 2022 with a small team and a seed reported only by aggregators at about $500K in total. It built the Pulse and Eureka feedback products and was sold to Wingify in an all-cash deal announced in December 2025, with its capabilities merged into VWO. The price is undisclosed and public traction data is thin, so whether this was a strong outcome or a soft landing is unclear.

name: Blockscope
one_liner: Palantir for Web3
long_description:
Blockscope is a Web3 data platform that enables anyone interested in on-chain data to quickly spin up live or historical data pipelines (for blocks, event, transaction, wallets, token, NFTs, etc). Similar to AWS, users have access to variety of managed software services to analyze, interact with or inject captured data into their apps.

Our platform is built around the core idea of off-loading the on-chain data that our customers need for their Web3 apps, and reliably storing them for quick access/use.

We offer products on top of the core data we index for our customers. Some of these services are contract analytics, wallet profiling, events & transactions database as a service, push notifications, webhooks, and developer tools.

Our mission is to enable everyone to easily access and consume on-chain data!
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Web3 developers and teams that need on-chain data in their apps, plus compliance and security users
problem: Building and running pipelines that index blocks, events, transactions, wallets and tokens is slow and costly for small Web3 teams.
business_model: Managed data infrastructure with subscription or usage pricing (pricing not found)
product_category: Web3 data infrastructure and analytics
market_need_then: The Block reported the Summer 2022 YC batch leaned toward Web3 infrastructure during a bear market, which suggests developer demand for data tooling but weak crypto funding conditions.
outcome_analysis: Blockscope remains listed as active with four people and no public acquisition, shutdown or layoff news. It joined YC in Summer 2022 as crypto funding cooled, and no later financing, customer wins or product milestones were found. Its trajectory is therefore unknown rather than a clear success or failure.

name: BlueHill Payments
one_liner: Client management, communication, and projects in one platform.
long_description:
BlueHill replaces the patchwork of tools you use to manage clients. Instead of bouncing between a project management app, a shared inbox, a portal solution, and a spreadsheet to track onboarding — BlueHill brings it all into one platform. Your team gets built-in email, structured onboarding workflows, project management, and a complete history of every client interaction. No more lost context, no more switching between tabs, and no more wondering who said what to which client.

Your clients get a branded portal experience where they can communicate with your team, track progress, and access everything they need — without the confusion of scattered tools and login links. Whether you're onboarding a new client, managing an ongoing project, or following up on a conversation from three months ago, BlueHill keeps everything connected so your team stays aligned and every client feels taken care of.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Businesses that have outgrown a single payment processor (launch post), later small service teams managing clients (current site)
problem: Merchants with complex payment operations pay too much in processing fees and lose approvals because each transaction goes to one provider. The current site instead targets teams juggling separate tools to onboard and support clients.
business_model: B2B SaaS; pricing not public
product_category: Payment orchestration, later customer success and client management platform
market_need_then: The YC launch post says businesses outgrow single-processor setups and want lower rates and higher acceptance. No quantified spend or demand evidence found.
outcome_analysis: BlueHill is an active two person company with no verified funding beyond the standard YC deal and no news of an exit or shutdown. Its launch post pitched payment routing, while the current site sells client onboarding and support software, which implies a pivot away from a crowded orchestration niche. Public evidence of traction is limited to a self-reported claim of serving 2,000 teams.

name: Boardcave
one_liner: Building the world’s largest online surf gear store.
long_description: The one stop shop for surfers. Boardcave provides surfers with online surf knowledge and gear to accelerate their surfing. The company is reimagining how surfers progress and partake in ocean activities.
all_locations: Brisbane, QLD, Australia; Gold Coast, QLD, Australia
regions: Australia; Oceania; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Surfers in Australia and the US buying boards, wetsuits and accessories online
problem: Buying a surfboard, especially a custom one from a local shaper, was hard to do online, so surfers lacked advice and selection.
business_model: E-commerce retail with expert advice and content
product_category: Online surf gear retailer and marketplace
market_need_then: The founders report starting after struggling to buy a custom board on the Gold Coast (search summary of press); no quantified demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Boardcave began around 2012 as a surf blog before becoming a store, and joined YC in Winter 2022 with a team of six. It remains active in 2026 selling over 3,000 boards, so it has survived, but no verified funding history or growth numbers are public. Its outcome as a venture is therefore unknown.

name: Bobidi
tags: Generative AI; Machine Learning; Human Resources; AI
one_liner: Restaurant Loyalty Using Quiz
long_description:
Bobidi runs Upswell, a platform that brings new guests to local restaurants and helps turn them into regulars.

We transform restaurants’ promotional videos on social media into engaging quiz campaigns based on the video content. Winners receive cash rewards that can be redeemed at the restaurants.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: At launch, AI developers paying testers; later, local restaurants buying guest acquisition
problem: AI developers needed human testers to find model weaknesses; the restaurant product addresses getting new guests to return as regulars.
business_model: Marketplace and services; Upswell restaurant growth packages listed at roughly $700 to $30,000+ per year
product_category: AI model testing marketplace, later restaurant growth platform (Upswell)
market_need_then: The July 2022 TechCrunch launch said developers wanted faster validation of AI models and could earn $10 to $20 per hour testing; no spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Bobidi raised a reported $5.8M seed in July 2022 for an AI model testing marketplace, then appears to have moved to Upswell, a restaurant guest acquisition product. It is listed as active with about seven people and no exit or shutdown news. The cause and timing of the change are not public, so its outcome is unresolved.

name: Boostly
one_liner: Premier growth platform for restaurants
long_description:
Boostly provides everything necessary for restaurants to attract new guests and turn them into regulars. From AI-powered SEO, paid ads, behavioral-based text marketing with gamified engagement, and AI driven reputation management, Boostly provides 10x greater guest engagement when compared to others in the industry.  

Boostly’s patented processes enables them to build opted-in subscriber lists bigger and faster than anyone on the market.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent and multi-unit restaurant operators wanting repeat guests
problem: Over 60% of a restaurant's customers never return for a second visit (launch post), and owners lack time to run text marketing and feedback.
business_model: Managed SaaS and service subscription for restaurants
product_category: Restaurant SMS marketing, reviews and loyalty automation
market_need_then: The launch post cites over 60% of guests never returning and a February 2022 NRN report showed text subscribers visited 44% more often than non-subscribers.
outcome_analysis: Boostly was bootstrapped from 2017, joined YC in Summer 2022 with about $1M in revenue, and raised a $5.6M seed in August 2024 followed by a $22M Series A in February 2025. It reports serving over 1,200 locations. Its path shows revenue-led growth in a crowded SMS category, with later capital rather than early capital.

name: BotCity
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Observability and Governance for AI-Generated Python scripts.
long_description: BotCity is a centralized platform that unifies Python scripts generated by AI or humans under a single governance framework, enabling organizations to scale with orchestration, observability, security and governance.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: developers and automation teams at enterprises, mainly in Brazil and Latin America at founding, now global
problem: RPA tools were low-code and locked-in; developers wanted code-based automation. Later: AI-generated Python scripts proliferate without governance.
business_model: software platform (orchestration, observability, governance) on an open-source core; pricing not found
product_category: developer-first RPA, then automation governance
market_need_then: VentureBeat (2022-02) cited RPA market of US$1.61B in 2020 projected to US$7.64B by 2028; the CEO argued developers need code-based tooling beyond low-code RPA.
outcome_analysis: BotCity, a Brazilian developer-first RPA company, raised a US$2.5M seed in December 2021 (SoftBank Latin America and Astella) plus a US$500K YC extension, then a US$12M round in September 2025 led by Four Rivers while repositioning toward governing AI-generated scripts. The company reports over 1,000 teams in production with customers such as Bayer and LG. It survived against much larger RPA incumbents; the traction figures are self-reported.

name: Botin
one_liner: Investment super app for Latin America
long_description:
Botin a mobile app where people in Latin America can invest in US Stocks, Crypto and more. 

We are building a one stop shop product for consumers to create wealth in Latin America by giving them the investment tools of the 1%.
all_locations: San José, San José Province, Costa Rica; Remote
regions: Costa Rica; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Boton
one_liner: Accounting software with an AI agent
long_description: SMBs in Latam use Boton to get real-time financial statements prepared by an autonomous agent. We match you with a partner accountant that may review your books and answer your questions.
regions: Panama; Latin America
target_customer: Small and medium businesses in Latin America
problem: SMBs in Latam lack timely, accurate financial statements; Boton uses an autonomous agent with a partner accountant reviewing books.
business_model: B2B SaaS with accountant review; pricing not found
product_category: AI accounting software
market_need_then: Latam SMBs rely on manual or legacy systems; directories position Boton against QuickBooks, Peachtree and Zoho. No quantified demand found.
outcome_analysis: Boton joined YC in Summer 2022 as a three person team in Panama City selling AI assisted accounting to Latam SMBs, apparently following the founders' earlier product Hero, a Bill.com for Latam. No funding, traction, exit or shutdown is publicly documented, and the YC jobs page shows no open roles, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Boya
one_liner: Corporate Expense cards and Spend management for businesses in Africa
long_description:
Boya Makes it easy for businesses in Africa to issue corporate expense cards instantly and great software to control and track spending. For example, if you run a pharmaceutical company, you can use Boya to instantly issue Visa cards to sales and marketing teams and get real-time visibility and control over their spending.

50M+ businesses in Africa have no easy way to streamline and track their employee spending in real-time. So we are building a corporate card and a spend management platform that enables businesses to streamline spend workflows and provide real-time reporting. We are building the first corporate card that supports mobile money, banks and card schemes payment workflows
regions: Kenya; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: African businesses, starting with SMEs and corporates in Kenya
problem: Companies in Africa could not easily issue employee expense cards or track spending, and cards did not work across mobile money, bank and card scheme payments.
business_model: Fintech platform: card issuing with bank partners, spend management software, interchange; no monthly fee on standard plan
product_category: Corporate cards and spend management, expanded to business banking
market_need_then: African SMEs lacked corporate cards; Float and Sava raised in 2022 for adjacent products, indicating investor demand.
outcome_analysis: Boya joined YC in Winter 2022 and launched virtual Visa cards with Diamond Trust Bank and Paymentology in July 2023, later expanding to banking, payroll and books with offices in Nairobi and San Francisco. It remains active with no shutdown news. Funding is only documented by aggregators, so its trajectory relative to rivals like Float is unclear.

name: Bracket
one_liner: Two-way syncs between business tools and your database
long_description: Bracket is the two-way data pipeline between popular business tools and backend databases. When ops teams update data in Salesforce or Airtable, and engineers update data in the database, Bracket connects the two sources to reflect the same information.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Los Angeles, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering and ops teams at companies using Salesforce, Airtable or Notion alongside a backend database
problem: Ops teams edit data in business tools while engineers use the database, and keeping the two in sync required costly or hand-built pipelines.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for managed sync pipelines
product_category: Data integration, two-way sync
founder_names: Vinesh Arun; Kunal Garg; Ian Yanusko
market_need_then: Heroku Connect was costly (the company cited above $50k a year) and tied to Heroku Postgres, creating demand for cheaper hosting-agnostic sync.
outcome_analysis: Bracket was a three person YC W22 team selling two-way sync between Salesforce, Airtable and databases as a cheaper Heroku Connect alternative. Funding figures from aggregators conflict ($1M to $2.5M) and none are verified. It is listed as acquired, with Rippling named only by its LinkedIn page, and no deal date or price exists, so the soft landing label is an inference from team size and silence rather than a sourced fact.

name: Brainboard
tags: Developer Tools; DevOps; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure
one_liner: Visually design and manage cloud infrastructures.
long_description:
Brainboard is a collaborative and end-to-end solution for engineers to visually design & manage their Cloud infrastructures.
We allow companies to lower the learning curve while moving to IaC, build a self serve model, have a service catalog to not reinvent the wheel.

Both technical profiles with 25+ years of combined expertise and after working together at a major French Cloud provider, Chafik and Jeremy launched Brainboard in 2020.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Paris, Île-de-France, France; Remote
regions: United States of America; France; America / Canada; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Cloud architects, DevOps and platform engineering teams using Terraform or OpenTofu
problem: Engineers find infrastructure as code hard to learn and to keep consistent across teams; architecture diagrams drift from deployed reality.
business_model: B2B SaaS per user with a free tier; paid plans cited at 25 euros to $99 per user per month by third parties
product_category: Visual cloud infrastructure design and management platform
market_need_then: Terraform adoption was growing and the YC page frames a learning curve problem for moving to infrastructure as code.
outcome_analysis: Brainboard, started by two former Scaleway engineers, joined YC in Winter 2022 and is still active with AWS and Azure marketplace listings and blue chip logos on its site. Aggregators show only pre-seed and seed sized funding of roughly $1.7M to $2.6M, and a directory claims $1.5M 2024 revenue, which is unverified. It looks like a durable but small business so far.

name: BricksAI
one_liner: Streamlining LLM application management for enterprises
long_description:
BricksAI is an open-source AI gateway that helps you manage how each of your services is calling different LLM providers.

You can create API keys with rate-limits, spend-limits, and expiration dates, then use them to make requests to different LLMs. With our SSO dashboard, you also get (1) role-based access control, and (2) fine-grained metrics (e.g. cost, number of requests, tokens) over each API key.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Bridgecard
tags: Banking as a Service; Fintech; Payments; B2B; API
one_liner: Card issuer for Africa
long_description:
Bridgecard makes it easy for fintechs to issue MasterCard or Visa cards that work anywhere in the world. We provide easy-to-integrate APIs to issue virtual and physical cards and we can get you started in weeks instead of months.

For nearly three years, we’ve supported Africa’s top startups with stable, high-growth card solutions. Thanks to our stability, over 50% of our clients have grown their volumes by more than 5X within 6 months. Our commitment is to deliver great cards that work, provide reliable support, and unbeatable uptime so that your users can be satisfied.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Broccoli AI
one_liner: AI-native operating system for home service businesses
long_description:
Broccoli is building the AI-native operating system for home service businesses. Running a plumbing or HVAC company is chaotic: calls, scheduling, dispatch, follow-ups, marketing. We automate all of it so contractors can focus on what they do best: serving customers.

Our AI agents handle both revenue and ops; answering phones 24/7, booking jobs in real time, following up on leads, and alerting techs when emergencies hit.

We’ve grown from 0 to 800+ contractors in under 2 years, raised Series A round led by Khosla Ventures to take on one of the biggest labor automation opportunities in the country.

Together, Adi and AJ co-founded Telematica, where they built energy-management systems for large European utilities and charging-point operators. They have raised $1.5M for Telematica and $25M for Broccoli.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Home service contractors in plumbing, HVAC, electrical and related trades
problem: Contractors miss calls and leads, and follow-up on estimates and memberships is manual, so jobs are lost.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage; pricing not public
product_category: AI voice agents and operating system for home services
market_need_then: Home service firms depend on phone booking; the first customer Armstrong Plumbing became Chief Industry Officer. Demand evidence for 2022 specifically was not found.
outcome_analysis: Broccoli grew from a Winter 2022 YC company into a voice AI platform for home services, with Khosla led funding reported at $25M Series A and $52M in total across A and B by October 2026, and over 1,500 businesses served. The strong timing came from voice model progress, and an early customer became an executive. Round dates and sizes are partly unclear across sources.

name: Brown Foods
tags: Cellular Agriculture; Biotech; Climate; Food Tech
one_liner: Making 'REAL' Cow and Human Milk!
long_description:
Brown Foods is a Stanford, Rice University and IIT Delhi alumni venture creating UnReal Milk - 'real milk' made using mammalian cell culture, AI enabled. They are the world's 1st company to produce cow-free whole milk in lab (Forbes). Targeting the $700 billion dairy market and $22 billion alternate dairy market with UnReal Milk - which could be converted into butter, cheese, ice-creams etc. and has taste and texture exactly like conventional dairy - unlike any of the plant based milks like oat milk or soy milk. Also, no animal cruelty and 82% lower carbon foot-print!

Using the same technology, they have also created real human milk targeting the $80 billion infant formula market. And who knows if adults also start drinking human milk in future!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Dairy and infant formula manufacturers and food brands that would license or buy cell-cultured milk
problem: Conventional dairy carries a large carbon footprint and animal welfare costs, and plant milks do not match dairy nutrition or taste. The company wants to make real milk from mammalian cells without cows.
business_model: Biotech product company targeting B2B supply of cultivated milk and ingredients, plus licensing; pre-revenue at the time of the seed round
product_category: Cellular agriculture, cultivated dairy
founder_names: Sohail Gupta; Avhijeet Kapoor; Bhavna Tandon
competitors_at_founding: Perfect Day; Wilk; TurtleTree Labs; Biomilq; Better Dairy
market_need_then: TechCrunch in June 2022 described a large dairy market and growing investor interest in animal-free dairy; the company itself cites a 700B USD dairy market and an 80B USD infant formula market (YC page).
outcome_analysis: Brown Foods raised a small seed round in June 2022 from YC and food tech investors and unveiled its lab made whole cow milk in February 2025. It is still active, pre-revenue as far as sources show, and faces long regulatory approval timelines and funded rivals. No later rounds were found, so its trajectory is unresolved.

name: Bunkyr
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Crypto / Web3; B2B; Security
one_liner: Zero-Knowledge security without seed phrases or backup codes
long_description:
Bunkyr enables companies to protect their users’ data with a simple, hardware-secured API. When a user forgets their password, applications using Bunkyr can provide them a familiar, robust recovery method to restore access to encrypted data.

Zero-Knowledge architectures and end-to-end encryption are the only true safeguards against data breaches, but come with large user-experience burdens and engineering overhead. Bunkyr eliminates these obstacles in a way that is friendly to both developers and users, cost-effective, and extremely fast.

Users won’t even know Bunkyr exists, while their data stays protected against both breaches and lost passwords.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software companies and developers building end-to-end encrypted apps, including crypto and Web3 apps, that need user key recovery
problem: Zero-knowledge and end-to-end encrypted apps lose user data when a password or seed phrase is lost. Bunkyr offers a hardware-secured API so apps can offer a familiar recovery path without seeing user data.
business_model: Developer API sold to application companies (B2B SaaS)
product_category: Developer security API, encrypted key recovery
market_need_then: The YC description argues zero-knowledge architectures are the safeguard against breaches but impose heavy UX and engineering burdens; seed phrase loss was a known pain in crypto wallets around 2021 to 2022.
outcome_analysis: Bunkyr is a YC Winter 2022 company that raised a 1M USD pre-seed in June 2022 for a zero-knowledge key recovery API. The YC page lists it as active, but no later rounds, customers or exit were found, so the outcome is unresolved and little can be said about why it has or has not progressed.

name: Bunting Labs
tags: SaaS; Geographic Information System; B2B; Web Development; AI
one_liner: AI Models for GIS
long_description: Bunting Labs researches and develops custom AI models for surveying and GIS.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Surveyors, governments, geologists and GIS teams that digitize maps and spatial data (QGIS users); at founding, teams needing spatial data pipelines
problem: Spatial data is heterogeneous and building ETL scripts, infrastructure and analysis pipelines takes months. Later the product turned to AI tools that digitize scanned maps and deeds into vector data.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat for QGIS plugins (a listing shows 20 and 199 USD per seat per month, unverified), plus open source Mundi
product_category: Geospatial software, AI map digitization
market_need_then: The founders say they spent three months of a year-long real estate AI project building data pipelines (YC launch post), showing the pain, but no spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: Bunting Labs joined YC in Summer 2022 with a geospatial data pipeline idea and later moved to AI map digitization in QGIS, claiming 30 plus government users. Its only found round is a 100K USD pre-seed reported in March 2026 by one aggregator, so growth looks small. It remains active and its trajectory is unresolved.

name: CAPSULE
tags: Generative AI; Machine Learning; Computer Vision; E-commerce; AI
one_liner: Buy anything you find on social media
long_description:
CAPSULE is a mobile app that makes it easy to save and buy the things you find on any social media platform. Just snap a screenshot of anything you like, from any platform, and we search the entire internet to instantly give you shoppable links. 

Instead of searching hundreds of websites and sifting through thousands of products on your own, CAPSULE lets you find inspiration from anywhere and uses advanced machine learning to return results that feel like magic.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: CODEXA
tags: Fintech; Crypto / Web3; Payments; Supply Chain; AI
one_liner: The AI-native financial platform for enterprises
long_description:
Our agents run tax, customs clearance, and supply chain workflows, helping companies navigate complex regulations and reduce the cost of international trade. By running these operations, Codexa becomes the natural platform for customers’ payments and foreign exchange.

We execute transactions through our own financial institution, regulated by the Central Bank of Brazil, connecting operational workflows directly to financial infrastructure. Customers approve payments, and Codexa moves the money through traditional and stablecoin rails.

Today, 51 enterprise customers use our agents, and 84% have adopted our financial products. We process approximately $800M in monthly financial volume, including $160M settled through stablecoins. Our customers include Fortune 500 and Global 500 companies.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Brazilian industrial importers and exporters (enterprises with foreign trade operations)
problem: Import and export operations involve customs, tax, payment and FX workflows that are manual and costly. Codexa combines AI agents with a regulated financial base to run them.
business_model: Fintech and software platform earning on FX, payments and credit volume plus agent software for foreign trade
product_category: AI-native financial and foreign trade operations platform
market_need_then: The site claims clients can save about 720K USD a year from overpaid taxes, demurrage and fines (company claim, not independently verified); no dated demand evidence from 2022 was found.
outcome_analysis: Codexa is a Manaus based YC Summer 2022 company that grew into an enterprise foreign trade and payments platform. By its own claims it has 51 enterprise customers and hundreds of millions of dollars in monthly volume, backed by a regulated financial group. Independent funding and traction evidence is thin, so the outcome is mostly company reported.

name: CUTR
one_liner: The marketplace for wood manufacturing
long_description:
Look around you - everything you see that was made with wood a designer conceived and then a woodworker has made. Most of the time, something went painfully wrong.

60% of the $1.4T global woodworking market is serviced by small businesses with inefficient, manual processes - Cutr is digitising their workflow. This market is massive, chaotic and surprisingly manual. Woodworkers are mostly offline, hard to find and even harder to vet. They need help with critical back-of-house jobs like quoting and capacity planning. Customers have no idea where to find them and need help asking the right questions & providing the right info to get their job produced correctly. 

Cutr solves discovery, pricing, payments and workflow for the woodworking market. 

Our users simply upload a file, accept an instant quote, and get their parts delivered. To make that possible we do the heavy lifting: filechecks, automated quoting, matchmaking, creating job packages, tracking changes & updates, logistics and payments.

Cutr saves time, cuts costs and ensures quality with a smooth workflow.
regions: Netherlands; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Interior builders, contractors, designers and custom woodworkers who need wood parts and furniture produced on demand; supply side is small woodworking manufacturers
problem: Small woodworking businesses serve a large share of the woodworking market but work through manual quoting and file handling. Cutr digitizes file checks, quoting, matching and logistics so customers upload a file and receive parts.
business_model: Marketplace taking a margin on manufacturing jobs, with quoting, logistics and payments handled on the platform
product_category: Manufacturing marketplace for wood products
founder_names: Oscar Peppitt; Rodny Heemskerk; Jasper Mittelmeijer
market_need_then: The YC page says small woodworking businesses serve about 60% of a 1.4T USD global woodworking market, a company claim; no dated demand evidence beyond that was found.
outcome_analysis: Cutr, an Amsterdam based YC Winter 2022 company, raised a seed round in 2022 and by 2026 claims 2,000 plus projects, over 1,000 customers and 250 plus manufacturers in Europe. Funding amounts are unclear across sources, so growth relative to capital cannot be judged. It remains active.

name: Cambio
one_liner: AI-native commercial real estate operations
long_description:
Cambio is the AI-native commercial real estate operations platform, built by investors for investors. Our suite of products automatically collects building data to empower mission critical workflows like capital planning and compliance.

Cambio uses LLMs and agentic AI to reason across thousands of pages of unstructured data, run multi-stepanalyses, and continuously adapt as regulations, assets and market conditions change. With Cambio, investors can evaluate and prioritize retrofit investment opportunities across thousands of buildings at once, compressing months of work into minutes.

We're working with the largest commercial real estate private equity firms globally like Principal Real Estate, Nuveen Real Estate, BGO, LaSalle Investment Management, Oxford Properties Group, Madison International Realty and Beacon Capital Partners. Our founding team collectively has two decades of commercial real estate experience across KKR, Oxford Properties Group, JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs. We are building the solution we wished we had while working at these funds.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Commercial real estate private equity firms and asset managers with large building portfolios
problem: Building data such as leases, loan documents and condition reports is scattered across PDFs and spreadsheets, so capital planning, retrofits and compliance depend on slow, costly consultant work.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS for asset managers
product_category: AI-native commercial real estate operations platform
market_need_then: The YC launch post says capital planning and compliance depend on costly, slow consultant engagements and manual analysis of scattered documents; regulation on building emissions and reporting is increasing, though no 2022 spend figure was found.
outcome_analysis: Cambio went through YC in Summer 2022 and then built in stealth, launching publicly in January 2026 with an 18M USD Series A at a reported 100M USD valuation. Founders with deep institutional real estate backgrounds and large asset manager customers explain the traction claims, which are company reported. It is active and the outcome is unresolved.

name: Capix
one_liner: AI-powered private equity intelligence.
long_description: Capix makes finding private equity firms fast and accurate by aggregating and enriching data from multiple sources into one customizable platform.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Private equity firms, limited partners and other investors that need to find and research private companies and firms
problem: Finding private equity firms and private companies takes manual work across scattered sources. Capix aggregates and enriches data into one customizable platform, later an AI sourcing copilot.
business_model: B2B SaaS, private beta with demo requests; pricing not found
product_category: AI data and sourcing platform for private capital
market_need_then: Private equity firms already paid for deal sourcing and private company data tools in 2022, as Grata's Series A and growth claims show; no Capix-specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Capix is a YC Summer 2022 company with one named founder that moved from a private equity data platform toward an AI sourcing copilot, still in private beta in 2024 per its site. No priced rounds, customers or press were found, and funded rivals like Grata were consolidating, so the outcome is unclear.

name: Capuchin
one_liner: Search and automation for engineer-to-order companies
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineer-to-order manufacturers and defense and engineering organizations that quote, design and support custom products
problem: Engineer-to-order companies keep designs, test data, ERP records and documents in scattered systems, making quoting, compliance and onboarding slow. Capuchin makes them searchable and automates work on the customer's own infrastructure.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software deployed on customer infrastructure; pricing not found
product_category: On-premise AI search and automation for engineering organizations
market_need_then: Engineer-to-order firms spend heavily on configuration and quoting software (Tacton and Configit serve them), but no Capuchin-specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Capuchin is a one founder YC Winter 2022 company that moved from search for engineer-to-order firms to on-premise sovereign AI for engineering organizations. Its site is active in 2026 with a demo call to action and offices in several states, but no priced rounds, customers or press were found, so its trajectory is unresolved.

name: Carbon Crusher
tags: Carbon Capture and Removal; Construction; Climate
one_liner: We make carbon negative roads
long_description:
We are crushing roads in need of maintenance, reusing the old road materials, replacing heavy oil with carbon binding lignin. This is both a cheaper, more durable and net carbon negative method, removing ~1.5 tonnes CO2 from the atmosphere from every 100 feet of road. 

We offer Crushing As A Service (CRAAS) to public and private road owners and refurbishers, and are already gaining international traction. Using satellite imagery, we will monitor road status and potential, and will offer additional tech and bio enhancements to make all roads green and a solution to the climate crisis.  

We are building the road to a carbon negative future.
regions: Norway; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Public and private road owners and road refurbishing contractors, starting in Norway
problem: Road maintenance relies on heavy-oil bitumen and new aggregate, which is costly and carbon heavy. Carbon Crusher grinds the worn road layer and rebinds it with lignin.
business_model: Crushing as a service (CRAAS), project-based service contracts with road owners and refurbishers
product_category: Climate and construction, carbon-negative road repair
founder_names: Haakon Brunell; Hans Arne Flåto; Kristoffer Roil
market_need_then: Road owners faced maintenance backlogs and rising pressure to cut construction emissions; 2022 press (Fast Company, Biofuels Digest, March 2022) covered the carbon-negative claim, which is company-reported and unverified.
outcome_analysis: Carbon Crusher joined YC in Winter 2022 with an experienced serial-founder team and early positive climate press, and remains listed as active with 21 people. No verified funding round, revenue figure or exit was found, so the story is an unproven early stage company in a slow, capital-heavy road construction market. Whether it succeeded or stalled cannot be judged from public sources.

name: Cardda
one_liner: All-in-one spend management for businesses in Latam
long_description:
All-in-one spend management for businesses in Latam.
We give customers tools for bill payments, automated local transfers and corporate cards.
all_locations: Santiago, Santiago Metropolitan Region, Chile; Mexico City, CDMX, Mexico
regions: Chile; Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-sized businesses in Chile and Latin America that pay suppliers and employees
problem: Latin American companies reconcile bill payments, local transfers and expenses by hand across banks and ERPs. Cardda bundles payments, cards and ERP sync.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus card and payments fees
product_category: Fintech, spend management and B2B payments
competitors_at_founding: Brex; Ramp; Clara; Mendel; Pleo; Spendesk
market_need_then: Founders argued most company spend in Latin America flows through transfers and bill payments, not only cards; the DF article (January 2022) cites reconciliation pain, and card-led spend startups were raising money in 2021.
outcome_analysis: Cardda pivoted out of an equipment rental marketplace into LatAm spend management in 2020, joined YC in Winter 2022 and reports 350 plus client companies and a Peru launch in 2025. Funding stayed small (about 330K USD reported by the founders at YC time), while Clara and Mendel raised far more in the same niche, so growth looks capital-efficient but modest. No exit or shutdown found.

name: Cash Flow Portal
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
tags: Marketplace; SaaS; Real Estate; B2B; Proptech
one_liner: Investment management platform for real estate
long_description:
Cash Flow Portal is an investment management platform for real estate. 

We launched 5 months ago, and we have 6-figure ARR, growing 50% month over month, with 300 syndicators and 3,000 investors. 

We’ve grown quickly because I am a syndicator myself. Having raised $20MM for my own deals, I know how painful it is to manually prepare Docusigns, send wire instructions and wrangle investors. I also happen to be friends with 2,000 other syndicators just like me needing a solution for managing their investors. 

I’m not just a syndicator. I spent most of my career as an engineering leader at Lyft, Twitter, and Amazon. 

$20K ARR per syndicator gives us a $2B TAM. Having achieved my own financial freedom through real estate investing, our mission is to serve all real estate investors and help them achieve financial freedom.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Real estate syndicators and general partners who raise money from investors
problem: Syndicators manually prepare documents, wire instructions and investor reports. The platform handles capital raising, investor portal and fund administration.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per syndicator
product_category: Proptech, investor management software
market_need_then: Syndicators raised money with spreadsheets and e-signatures; the YC page reports 300 syndicators and 3,000 investors five months after launch, and a 2021 GeekWire item covered the company's early growth.
outcome_analysis: A Lyft engineering manager who was himself a syndicator built investor management software for peers, launched in 2021, claimed 6-figure ARR five months later and joined YC in Winter 2022. By 2025 the site lists roughly 6B USD of customer AUM and the company reportedly has about 26 staff. Outside funding is not verified, so growth looks founder-funded and capital-efficient.

name: Cashboard
one_liner: Inventing the solo CFO.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-sized finance teams and solo CFOs who run budgeting and FP&A
problem: Finance teams build budgets in disconnected spreadsheets and tools. Cashboard aims to let one person run planning with software and AI doing repetitive work.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, month-to-month contracts
product_category: FP&A and collaborative budgeting software
market_need_then: FP&A startups raised large rounds in 2022 (Cube, Mosaic, Abacum), showing demand for modern planning tools among mid-market finance teams.
outcome_analysis: Cashboard raised a 1.5M USD pre-seed around YC in 2022, then stayed lean for four years before a 5M USD seed led by FINTOP in July 2026 as it repositioned toward AI-assisted FP&A. The slow capital path suggests modest early traction with a later AI-driven reacceleration, but revenue is not public. Still active at six people.

name: Cashmere
one_liner: Crypto wallet for web3 startups
long_description: Cashmere is a multisig solana wallet for enterprises to manage their digital assets. Instead of running their business from one person’s wallet, startups can use our wallet to securely manage their funds.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Castia
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: Built Rewards for Latam. Pay Rent and get benefits.
long_description: Castia is the first rent payment platform in Latam that allows tenants and landlords to get benefits for one of their single biggest monthly expense. Get rewards, pay with any payment method, build your credit score and even save for your future home downpayment, just by paying rent through Castia.
all_locations: Bogotá, Bogota, Colombia; Mexico City, CDMX, Mexico
regions: Colombia; Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Castled.io
one_liner: Customer Engagement software on top of BigQuery/Snowflake
long_description:
Castled.io is a Customer Engagement Platform (CEP) that brings the power of data in the warehouse to the marketer.  

Essentially, Castled.io is similar in feature set to Braze, CustomerIO or MoEngage with a major difference - We don't store your customer data. Instead Castled sits on top of your cloud data warehouse to create segments and engage them across channels.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Cellbyte
one_liner: AI Agents for Pharma Drug Launches
long_description:
Cellbyte's AI agents help pharma companies launch new drugs worldwide. Market-leading firms are using Cellbyte to answer questions like “What price can we achieve for our new drug in the U.S. versus Germany?“.

The three co-founders have known and worked with each other for many years: Daniel brings 5+ years of industry experience from his previous job at leading global Life Sciences consultancy Simon-Kucher. Felix has sold $3m+ ACV deals to customers like H&M for his previous YC startup. Samuel holds an MSc in Information Systems from TUM, and has built enterprise AI applications from scratch as ML Engineer at Celonis.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Pharma companies running global drug launches, pricing and market access
problem: Launch teams spend weeks gathering regulatory, HTA and pricing evidence across countries; Cellbyte answers these questions with traceable AI agents.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS platform plus expert-led evidence reviews and pricing analyses
product_category: AI platform for pharma market access and pricing
founder_names: Felix Steinbrenner; Daniel Moreira; Samuel Moreira
market_need_then: Launch failure is costly and consultancies charge heavily for pricing and access analyses; the founders came from Simon-Kucher and saw this directly.
outcome_analysis: Cellbyte is the survivor of Glocally, a YC W22 delivery startup that pivoted in mid 2023 into AI for pharma pricing and market access. A consulting-sourced insight, named customers such as Bayer and Gilead, a claimed 8 of the top 20 pharma firms and a $2.75M seed in November 2025 show a successful pivot. Customer claims come from the company site, and rivals now add AI features.

name: Cerebrium
one_liner: Serverless Infrastructure Platform for AI
long_description:
Cerebrium is a serverless infrastructure platform for AI applications. We make it easier for companies to build and deploy AI based applications. We offer Serverless GPU's with low cold start times, over 12 varieties of GPU chips, allow you to run large scale batch jobs, run realtime voice applications and much more. We are used by the teams at Tavus, CivitAI, Twilio and many more. 

Customers typically experience 40% in cost savings when compared to using traditional cloud providers and can scale models to more than 10K requests per minute with minimal engineering overhead.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: AI application developers and startups that need GPU inference without managing infrastructure
problem: Deploying and scaling ML models needs costly, complex GPU infrastructure. Cerebrium offers serverless GPUs with fast cold starts.
business_model: Usage-based serverless GPU compute
product_category: AI infrastructure, serverless GPU
market_need_then: Demand for ML deployment grew with AI adoption; the founders had felt the cost and maintenance pain at OneCart per Gradient's investment post.
outcome_analysis: Cerebrium started in Cape Town, entered YC in Winter 2022 and reportedly grew to millions in ARR through partnerships before raising an 8.5M USD seed from Gradient in July 2025. It benefited from the generative AI and voice agent boom, with customers like Tavus, Vapi and Deepgram. Competition from Modal and hyperscalers remains the main risk. Active at 2026.

name: Cerrion
tags: Deep Learning; Computer Vision; Video; Manufacturing; AI
one_liner: Video AI to automatically detect and respond to production line…
long_description:
Cerrion helps manufacturers automatically detect, understand and eliminate problems on their production lines using video-based Computer Vision. Our AI leverages standard CCTV cameras and learns how a manufacturing process looks like when things are going well and can automatically detect and track problems in real-time.

For example, one of our customers, a Pepsi supplier producing 500 bottles per minute now automatically detects and reacts to a fallen bottle before it starts blocking their production line.
regions: Switzerland; Europe
target_customer: Discrete and process manufacturers such as glass, beverage and food plants
problem: Production line stoppages and defects are noticed late. Cerrion uses video AI on existing CCTV cameras to detect problems in real time.
business_model: B2B SaaS and deployment subscription per line or plant
product_category: Industrial computer vision and video AI
founder_names: Karim Saleh; Nikolay Kobyshev; Michael (surname not given)
market_need_then: Manufacturers lose large sums to downtime and scrap, and AI inspection startups were raising growth rounds in 2021 and 2022.
outcome_analysis: Cerrion, founded in Zurich in December 2021 by ETH computer vision experts, entered YC in Summer 2022, raised 5M USD in September 2024 and an 18M USD Series A led by Creandum in November 2025. Customers like Stoelzle and Sisecam expanded from one plant to group-wide rollouts with reported ROI of 6x to 8x, which supports real product-market fit in glass and beverage manufacturing.

name: Champ
one_liner: AI SDR
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B sales teams running outbound
problem: Outbound prospecting, research and personalized email take SDR time.
business_model: AI SDR product, also describes an embedded go-to-market engineering service
product_category: AI sales development
market_need_then: No sources dated near the 2022 batch were found; the company only asserts that outbound prospecting and email personalization consume sales rep time.
outcome_analysis: Champ remains active with a listed team of one and no public funding found. Its site markets an AI SDR with claimed open and reply rates, while founder Matt Sun's bio now describes a GTM engineering service, hinting at repositioning, but no dated sources confirm a pivot or outcome.

name: Chariot
one_liner: A payment network connecting nonprofits to the $326B in DAFs
long_description:
Chariot is building the financial infrastructure for the $326 billion donor-advised fund (DAF) market, the fastest-growing segment of philanthropy. Our gift processing platform is an end-to-end solution for managing DAF payments, making it easier for grantmakers to send grant payments and nonprofits to receive, reconcile, and enrich their donation data.

Chariot also powers DAFpay, the industry’s first integrated DAF payment option and a TIME’s Best Invention of 2025. It is embedded on over 100,000 nonprofits’ donation forms—including American Cancer Society, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, and University of Pennsylvania—and is a primary payment option on leading fundraising platforms like GoFundMe and GiveButter.

Hundreds of millions are already moving through Chariot’s platform, and we’re just getting started.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Nonprofits receiving donor-advised fund gifts, and DAF sponsors and grantmakers sending grants
problem: DAF gifts are slow, paper-based and hard to reconcile for nonprofits. Chariot builds payment rails and gift processing for them.
business_model: Payment processing fees and software for nonprofits and DAF sponsors
product_category: Fintech, nonprofit payments and DAF infrastructure
founder_names: Salomon Serfati; Aaron Kahane; Drew Schneider
market_need_then: DAF assets were about 326B USD and the fastest growing segment of philanthropy, but nonprofits had no easy online way to accept DAF gifts.

It launched gift processing in January 2026. No acquisition or later round found.

name: Cherry Recommends

Cherry is the only AI promotion management platform. We help online stores boost revenue and increase their marketing ROI by delivering and tracking dynamic promotions.

name: Chordio
one_liner: Claude Code design workspace built for product teams
long_description:
Designers and product managers are often locked out of prototyping on top of their existing product. Security policies, large code base, and complex build setup all stand between the promise of code-first front-end design and reality.

The Chordio Workbench helps non-technical team members prototype new experiences on top of their existing products even when they don’t have access to the source code.

The full workflow runs in Claude Code on your local machine. It starts with cloning the front-end of the product into the workbench repository directly from the browser and compiling it into code a coding agent can work with. This means anyone can start prototyping in minutes without having to worry about a complex environment setup.

The Workbench includes agent skills to help ensure prototypes meet team standards, are backed by research, and presented to stakeholders with clarity.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product teams, designers and product managers; later teams building coding agents

outcome_analysis: Chordio, a Summer 2022 company with experienced founders from the Brand.ai and InVision exit, launched a sprint planner in 2023, then repeatedly repositioned toward AI-era design workflows and a coding-agent benchmark. No funding, revenue or exit is public and the team is four people, so the company appears small and still searching for a fit, though 'failed pivot' is not established.

name: Chowdeck
one_liner: On-demand food delivery for Africa
long_description:
Founded in October 2021, currently based in Lagos, Nigeria, Africa’s most populous city, Chowdeck is an on-demand food delivery service and marketplace where people can purchase their favourite meals from a wide range of restaurants. Whether local or continental, customers can buy food in a few short steps and have it delivered to their doorstep in under 30 minutes. 

Chowdeck is on a mission to empower restaurants in Africa to deliver meals to customers anywhere and anytime. Part of our unique offering to the restaurants listed on our marketplace is that we’ll help them grow, and so far, most of the restaurants we work with can boast of this achievement. With their help and the help of an ambitious team of relentless and fearless riders, we’ve delivered over 80,000 meals in the last six months in two major cities in Lagos.

We’ve come this far because we’re passionate about understanding the teething pains of delivery service in Africa and believe strongly in a world where ordering a meal is seamless.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Urban consumers in Nigeria (later Ghana) ordering meals, plus restaurants and stores that pay commission to be listed and delivered
problem: Food delivery in Lagos was slow and unreliable, with delivery times often above 30 minutes and heavy discount dependence among rivals.
business_model: marketplace take rate plus delivery fees, later ads and subscription (Chowpass)
product_category: on-demand food and grocery delivery marketplace
founder_names: Femi Aluko; Olumide Ojo; Lanre Yusuf
market_need_then: Lagos had demand for food delivery but rivals averaged more than 30 minute deliveries and relied on discounts, per Chowdeck coverage; the YC listing cites 80,000 meals delivered in six months.
outcome_analysis: Chowdeck grew from a Lagos food delivery startup into a multi-country platform. It reached 1 billion naira monthly order value by November 2023, raised a 2.5 million seed in April 2024 and a 9 million Series A in August 2025, while rivals such as Jumia Food exited. It cut 68 percent of contract staff in 2024 citing process gains and acquired Mira in 2025.

name: Cinapse
one_liner: The Operating System of Hollywood
long_description:
Cinapse is reimagining the production schedule: the foundation of every film and TV project. We’re building the OS of Hollywood, starting with the tool that filmmakers use every day.

Besides the script, nothing is more foundational to filmmaking. There’s no accurate budget without a schedule. No execution plan without one. The schedule is the map that takes us from idea to image.

Cinapse helps filmmakers draw that map better, faster, and together.

product_category: film and TV production scheduling software
market_need_then: Schedulers and ADs worked in a decades old desktop tool where collaboration meant file passing; the company's pitch rests on that gap, and a 2024 product launch followed.
outcome_analysis: Cinapse was a two person team led by a working assistant director who targeted the scheduling tool at the heart of Hollywood production. It launched to users in February 2024 and, per an acquisition tracker and its own site, was acquired by Wrapbook in December 2025 for an undisclosed price. Funding detail is thin, so the outcome looks like a small, domain led exit.

name: Cinder
tags: SaaS; B2B; Compliance; Trust & Safety; AI
one_liner: Infrastructure to protect companies from AI abuse
long_description:
From content moderation to AI safety, Cinder empowers businesses to orchestrate and automate digital safety at scale. Cinder was founded to help organizations foster safe online spaces for everyone. Our platform empowers companies from start-ups to enterprises with end-to-end capabilities to mitigate harm, investigate abuse, and produce trustworthy and reliable AI outcomes. Building your world-class company means keeping your users and community safe—Cinder unlocks faster growth by making safety easy. We work with customers in every industry from frontier AI labs to e-commerce and social media. 

We're hiring across a variety of teams and looking for candidates based in NYC or open to relocating to NYC, and able to work in-person.

product_category: trust and safety operations and AI safety infrastructure

market_need_then: Platforms faced rising regulatory and public pressure on content moderation in 2021 and 2022 and often built internal tools; the founders saw the need at Facebook.
outcome_analysis: Cinder was founded by former Meta threat intelligence staff, launched from stealth in December 2022 with 14 million from Accel and Y Combinator, and extended into AI safety, adding customers such as Synthesia and Wizz. A 41 million Series B in May 2026 suggests growing enterprise demand driven by the AI abuse tailwind.

name: Circular
one_liner: Subscription consumer electronics for Asia
long_description:
Circular is accelerating the adoption of the circular economy by making subscriptions the best way to access and experience tech: from smartphones, laptops, and headphones to gaming, VR and wearables.

Our customers get their hands on the best tech through low-cost, convenient subscriptions. They can pay monthly, keep it as long as they want, and if they love it, buy it. If they return it, we carefully refurbish it and pass it on to the next loving owner - radically extending its useful life.

outcome_analysis: Circular is an Active Singapore device-subscription company that went through YC W22 and closed a US$7.6M seed in October 2023 led by AirTree with YC Continuity and GFC at a reported US$30M valuation. TechCrunch reported 3x growth over the prior year, and a later US$3.3M round in 2024 appears only in secondary sources. It has not been reported to reach Series A, so it is best read as a funded early-stage company with an unproven outcome.

long_description:
Ciro is an AI agent that finds prospects, researches their buying signals, and drafts personalized outreach, all from Slack.

Tell it who you sell to. It finds the right people, figures out why now is the right time to reach out, and writes outreach that sounds like your best rep did 30 minutes of research.
