A crowded AI prospecting market led to its acquisition by Reevo in July 2026, a soft consolidation exit with undisclosed terms rather than a standalone breakout.

name: Cisterna Biologics
one_liner: High quality mRNA for therapeutic application
long_description:
Founded in 2022 and based in San Diego, California, Cisterna Biologics is a technology company. It aims to solve some of the challenges currently facing the biotech industry to develop mRNA-based therapeutics – quality, quantity, longevity and cost of mRNA. As mRNA technology matures, it becomes imperative that these issues are solved so we can fully explore mRNA's endless possibilities as a therapeutic.

Cisterna uses proprietary technologies to either remove a contaminant at its source or replace the source itself. For example, to remove double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), we use ribozymes - molecular scissors - to precisely cut the mRNA at its 3’ end. This assures not only 3’ homogeneity, but also eliminates dsRNA, which are primarily produced due to self-templated additions at the 3’ end. Utilizing a PCR-like system to amplify the DNA template in large quantities eliminates the requirement for plasmid enrichment in bacteria, the prime source of endotoxin contamination. These are just a few examples of Cisterna’s powerful technologies being used to achieve our goal of 10x higher quality mRNA for therapeutic application.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: mRNA researchers and therapeutic developers buying custom or off-the-shelf high purity RNA
problem: Therapeutic mRNA suffers from impurities such as double stranded RNA and endotoxin from plasmid based manufacturing, which hurt quality, yield and tolerability.
business_model: custom RNA synthesis service and off-the-shelf RNA product sales, plus grant funded R&D
product_category: mRNA manufacturing technology
market_need_then: mRNA therapeutics surged after COVID vaccines and impurity control mattered for tolerability; the company site cites dsRNA and endotoxin problems as the target.
outcome_analysis: Cisterna is a single founder deep tech company founded in 2022 and still active per YC with a team of two. The company shows YC, NSF, NIGMS and NCATS logos, suggesting grant funding, but no verified rounds, customers or news exist in the sources found, so the outcome is unresolved.

long_description: Clearline is the AI operating system that captures, routes, and converts every revenue opportunity across your dealership without adding headcount.

They restarted as Clearline for car dealerships; the company is active with no public funding and early customer claims from a founder recap.

name: Clickpad
one_liner: The AI employee for contractors. No software to learn. Just text.
long_description:
ClickPad.com (fka WeReno) is an AI-powered back office that helps contractors take on more projects without hiring administrative staff or learning complicated software.

After 10+ years in construction and facilitating over $1B in renovations through WeReno, we've packaged everything we've learned about running a successful contracting business into an AI employee that fits in the palm of your hand.

Contractors simply text, call, or WhatsApp Click in any of 13 supported languages. Click handles leads, estimates, contracts, invoices, payments, scheduling, change orders, and client communication. We also generate AI-powered contractor websites with 24/7 lead capture.

We discovered that 95% of our trade partners had no website or CRM. Rather than build another dashboard, we built an AI agent that actually runs their back office through simple conversations.

Our mission is simple: give millions of contractors the tools and expertise of a fully staffed back office, right in the palm of their hand, so they can run bigger businesses without bigger teams.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small contractors and trade businesses (painters, roofers, plumbers, electricians, movers) who pay a monthly subscription
problem: Contractors lose time and money on quotes, contracts, invoices and payment chasing; Clickpad offers an AI assistant they text like a crew member.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, plans from US$49 per month
product_category: AI back office for contractors
market_need_then: The batch product WeReno targeted renovation and capital projects; the YC page says it facilitated over 1 billion dollars of projects. Demand evidence for the later AI assistant is limited to its pricing page.
outcome_analysis: A construction industry founder entered YC as WeReno and has since rebranded and refocused as Clickpad, an AI texting assistant for contractors with 12 team members per the YC page. name: CompUp
tags: SaaS; Human Resources; B2B; HR Tech
one_liner: Building a compensation graph to help companies optimise people spend
long_description:
With over 500M white-collared job offers rolled out annually, companies find it very difficult to be certain about what to offer. Companies rely on old compensation survey data, which are updated only once every year.

The salary expectations of candidates in the market change significantly on a quarterly basis (~7% statistically) in the startup ecosystem.

This results in more than 50% of qualified/selected candidates not joining the company due to expectation mismatch.

CompUp is an API-driven compensation benchmarking tool. We integrate with your existing HR/payroll systems, removing the need for manual data entry, and also getting updated in real-time.

CompUp provides the most accurate real-time compensation benchmarking data which helps you make the right offer to the candidate. The platform allows you to make better compensation decisions such as annual increments, candidate offers using internal and external data. 

This has the following advantages :
- All the process of compensation data submission is automatic and needs no manual intervention
- Since the job market is dynamic in nature, the offers made on CompUp's real-time benchmarks would be the most efficient
- The presentation of the offer to the candidate makes it look more appealing and explanatory to the candidate
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Funded startups and mid-size companies in India (and beyond) making hiring and pay decisions
problem: Companies rely on annual compensation surveys while candidate expectations shift quickly, so offers miss and candidates decline.
business_model: B2B SaaS API driven compensation benchmarking and management
product_category: Compensation benchmarking and HR tech
founder_names: Anurag Dixit; Ramesh Konatham; Anshul Mishra
market_need_then: The launch post and company state that salary expectations in the startup market move about 7% a quarter and more than half of selected candidates may not join due to expectation mismatch; these are company claims.
outcome_analysis: HireSure.ai, with CompUp as its compensation product, joined YC Summer 2022 and raised a 2.5M USD seed in February 2023 led by YC and Three State Capital. It lists 35 staff, more than 100 customers by its own claim and a G2 profile, and remains active. Its India focus has less direct competition than Pave, but no later rounds were found.

name: Compra Rápida

long_description:
Cone is an AI-powered work operating system that unifies accounting workflows —
proposals, tasks, billing, payments, and client engagement into one platform
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Accounting and bookkeeping firms and other professional service firms, from solo practitioners to multi-seat practices
problem: Accounting firms juggle separate tools for proposals, engagement letters, billing, payments, tasks and client requests.
business_model: B2B SaaS per user subscription (a 2024 article puts Cone Practice at 8 USD and Cone Propose at 13 USD per user per month)
product_category: Accounting practice management, proposals and billing software
market_need_then: Accounting firms had a recognized need for practice management, proposals and billing tools, shown by active vendors such as Karbon raising large rounds in early 2022.
outcome_analysis: Cone is an eight person Hyderabad company selling accounting workflow software. It raised a reported 1.65M USD pre-seed in 2023 per aggregators, launched Propose in 2024 and added Practice, and claims thousands of accountant users. It entered a crowded market against well funded vendors, so the story is still unresolved and no clear success or failure factor is supported by sources.

name: Convoy
one_liner: Webhooks Gateway for outgoing and incoming webhooks.
long_description:
We are building Convoy for engineering teams that value efficiency, especially during this bear market. 

You might already know about API Gateways. Convoy is exactly that for webhooks.

Engineering teams today use Convoy to securely send, receive and manage millions of webhooks reliably with robust support for retries, rate limiting, static IPs, circuit breaking, rolling secrets and more.

We know both receiving and sending webhooks can become a lot of work to manage, we have built a product to enable engineers to build and ship highly scalable stripe-like webhooks infrastructure.
all_locations: London, England, United Kingdom; LA, Nigeria; Remote
regions: United Kingdom; Nigeria; Europe; Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams that send or receive webhooks (SaaS and fintech developers)
problem: Reliably sending and receiving webhooks needs retries, rate limiting, secret rotation and monitoring that each team ends up rebuilding.
business_model: Open-source core with hosted/cloud and enterprise offering (usage or subscription; exact pricing not verified)
product_category: Developer infrastructure: webhooks gateway
market_need_then: The company says engineering teams struggle to run Stripe-like webhook infrastructure, and at least two other startups raised money in 2021 for the same problem, indicating developer demand and investor interest.
outcome_analysis: Convoy (operated by Frain Technologies, Lagos/London) raised a reported $473K pre-seed in January 2022, around its YC Winter 2022 batch, and remains listed Active with 8 people. It competed with better-funded webhook startups Hookdeck and Svix, the latter of which later raised from a16z; no later round, exit or shutdown for Convoy was found, so its trajectory is unresolved from available sources.

name: Coris
one_liner: AI risk and ops platform for Payment Processors, Banks, SaaS…
long_description:
Coris is the AI platform for payments risk and operations. We work with the most ambitious companies around the globe such as GoFundMe, Kajabi, Clio and Cherry to automate merchant onboarding, monitoring, and payment operations. What risk teams only imagined two years ago, Coris is delivering today with our risk platform and AI agents.

We’re backed by Y Combinator, Lux Capital, Pathlight Ventures, and other world-class investors — and we’re just getting started !
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Payments platforms, ISOs, PayFacs and sponsor banks; originally fintechs underwriting SMBs
problem: Traditional bureaus cover small businesses poorly, so risk shows up only at chargebacks or defaults, and merchant onboarding and risk operations are manual.
business_model: B2B SaaS/API for merchant risk underwriting, monitoring and fraud detection
product_category: AI merchant risk platform
market_need_then: YC launch post: bureau SMB coverage is poor, integrations painful, data unstructured; founders spent 20+ years in payments risk. VentureBeat 2024-02 cites 150,000 SMBs verified and a Mindbody case (onboarding 5x faster).
outcome_analysis: Coris is active and raised a $3.7M seed in February 2024 co-led by Lux and Exponent, with a reported 150,000 SMBs verified and named customers. Founders with PayPal, WePay and eBay risk experience give strong founder-market fit, and the product widened from an SMB data API to an AI risk platform with fraud and verification modules. Later rounds and revenue are not public, and funded rivals like Middesk and Alloy already served the same buyers at founding.

name: Corveus Medical
one_liner: Catheter-based solution to treat chronic heart failure.
long_description: Our device catheter-based device is able to safely perform a targeted nerve ablation in the upper abdomen. Cardiologists are concerned about collateral tissue damage in ablation procedures - our probe not only targets a very specific area, but also confirms that it’s done correctly.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Cardiologists and hospitals treating class III chronic heart failure patients (outpatient catheter procedure), paid by hospitals and ultimately payers
problem: Many chronic heart failure patients have limited options; the company argues that overactive sympathetic nerve signaling drives fluid buildup, and wants a safe, targeted ablation that confirms it worked.
business_model: Medical device sold to hospitals per procedure; pre-revenue and pre-clinical per sources found
product_category: Catheter-based nerve ablation medical device for heart failure
market_need_then: Heart failure is common and costly with limited device options; the neighbouring Rebalance-HF trial of splanchnic ablation was enrolling by December 2020, showing clinical and investor interest in the approach.
outcome_analysis: Corveus is a tiny Houston device startup that came out of the TMC Biodesign program, took YC in W22, and has funded itself through small private money, an NSF Phase I grant and prizes. A third party profile found no registered clinical trial or FDA authorization as of September 2026, and a competing splanchnic ablation trial reportedly showed no benefit over sham. The path to a venture sized round depends on first in human data that has not appeared.

name: Cotera
one_liner: The fastest way to build an AI agent
long_description: Cotera is an AI agent platform that connects directly to your data warehouse and APIs, enabling businesses to build agents that take actions across their systems. With built-in tools, a visual workflow editor, and fine-grained control, teams can deploy agents at scale for use cases like intelligent ticket routing, voice-of-customer analysis, and proactive customer health monitoring.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Business teams in sales, marketing, customer success, support and operations at mid-size and large companies (named customers include Peloton, SKIMS and OpenSea)
problem: Teams have customer data in warehouses and tools but cannot easily turn it into insights or automated actions; the early product surfaced insights from customer data and the current one builds AI agents that act across systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform subscription for AI agents with integrations; pricing not found
product_category: AI agent platform, previously customer analytics
market_need_then: In 2022 companies were adopting data warehouses and wanted analytics on top of them; later demand shifted to AI agents. The early description said the product surfaced interesting insights from customer data.
outcome_analysis: Cotera started on warehouse-based customer analytics, then moved to an AI agent platform, reaching general availability in December 2025 and listing named consumer brands as customers. It is still an eight person team, no priced round beyond YC is verified, and the outcome is open. Sources do not support a clear success or failure factor yet.

name: Coupl
one_liner: Banking designed for Indian couples.
long_description:
Coupl is a digital joint account for Indian households. We help couples and families easily manage their shared and household payments from one shared account.

Over 20 million Indians marry each year, creating a $300 billion market opportunity in household expenses. Couples juggle multiple accounts, cards, and expense-tracking tools. Joint accounts involve lengthy paperwork, rejections, and minimum balance requirements, making them inconvenient for modern couples. Beyond married couples, this need extends to engaged partners, live-in couples, roommates, and families seeking simpler ways to manage shared expenses.

Coupl offers a digital, zero-balance joint account with co-branded debit cards and in-app bill payments, set up in just 60 seconds. Couples can use the account for all shared expenses, with an analytics dashboard to help them stay on top of their finances.

Coupl is powered by RuPay, NPCI and IDFC FIRST Bank.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian couples and households (married, engaged, live-in, roommates) who share expenses; revenue from card interchange and partner offers
problem: Couples juggle separate accounts, cards and expense tools, while bank joint accounts involve paperwork and minimum balances.
business_model: Consumer prepaid joint account and co-branded RuPay cards issued through a licensed PPI partner, earning interchange and partnership fees (exact model not stated by sources)
product_category: Consumer fintech: digital joint account and shared expense app for couples
competitors_at_founding: Splitwise; Traditional bank joint accounts; Fibbl
market_need_then: Founders cite over 10 million Indian weddings a year and pain from joint account paperwork and minimum balances; the public launch followed in September 2023.
outcome_analysis: Coupl joined YC in S22, launched its joint account publicly in September 2023 on a partner PPI issuer and reported 8,000 accounts by its YC launch post. No verified priced round was found beyond aggregator figures, and the company remains an eight person active team. The outcome is open; the main risks are dependence on partner rails and a small paying base.

name: Courtyard.io
one_liner: Courtyard turns shopping into entertainment with instant liquidity
long_description: Courtyard.io (YC W’22) turns shopping into entertainment. Open digital packs to instantly reveal physical trading cards, comics, watches, and more. Keep what you love – securely vaulted, insured, and ready to ship – or sell back instantly at a guaranteed price. Expanding across new collectibles, fashion, and beyond, Courtyard is pioneering a new model of shopping where entertainment drives demand and liquidity backs every purchase.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Collectors and consumers who buy digital packs that reveal graded physical trading cards, comics, watches and sneakers; revenue comes from pack sales and marketplace activity
problem: Collectibles buying and selling suffers from shipping delays, scams, lost items and little digital innovation since eBay; Courtyard lets users hold, trade or redeem vaulted assets.
business_model: Consumer marketplace: sells digital packs of vaulted physical collectibles with instant buyback, and runs a trading marketplace (the company says it charges 0 percent marketplace fees)
product_category: Collectibles marketplace and tokenization of vaulted physical assets
market_need_then: NEA cited a collectibles market of over 400B USD with shipping delays, scams and lost items; Courtyard sold out 500K USD of graded Pokemon cards as physically backed NFTs in under four hours by November 2022 (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Courtyard started as a physically backed NFT collectibles platform, raised a 7M USD seed led by NEA in November 2022, then grew into pack-opening entertainment with instant buyback and raised a 30M USD Series A in July 2025. The company claims monthly volume rose from 50K to 50M USD, which points to strong demand, supported by the collectibles boom. Competition from Dibbs, Whatnot and eBay remains the main risk.

name: Coverage Cat
one_liner: Consumer Optimized Insurance
long_description:
Coverage Cat, the AI-native insurance broker, fixes your coverage limits and finds cheaper premiums. 

We provide both AI and human support so you can get fast answers on your policy and quickly get a response from a human agent so you can protect you assets or close on a new home. 

The AI-first approach drives core search, support and shopping experiences to ensure you get the best prices with the correct coverage.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: High-earning US households buying umbrella, auto and home insurance (California, Florida, New York, Texas and Washington at last check)
problem: Consumers carry wrong coverage limits and overpay because policies are hard to read and brokers or comparison sites push their own incentives.
business_model: Licensed insurance brokerage earning carrier commissions, with an AI-guided intake and human brokers
product_category: Insurtech: AI-native consumer insurance brokerage
competitors_at_founding: Jerry; Insurify; Traditional captive and independent brokers
market_need_then: Umbrella coverage is often misunderstood and underbought; the founders say policies are hard to read and incentives are misaligned. Insurance comparison startups raised large rounds in 2021, showing investor demand.
outcome_analysis: Coverage Cat is a licensed AI-assisted broker focused on umbrella insurance for high-earning households, backed by YC in S22 and described in January 2023 as moving from fundraising to growth. Funding figures exist only on aggregators, and it competes with well funded comparison sites and traditional brokers. It is still active at four people and is extending into AI agent channels; no clear success or failure factor is supported yet.

name: Cozmo AI
one_liner: End-to-end AI agents for property claims, from loss report to estimate
long_description:
Cozmo AI helps restoration franchisors, TPAs and adjusters put agents to work on US property insurance claims. Agents are autonomous AI workers that answer intake across all channels, coordinate crews and write up losses. Putting them to work means deploying across the full claim, from first notice of loss to crew dispatch and damage estimate to supplement approval. Work that took human teams days to weeks closes in minutes.

Cozmo is an operating system for the whole claim, end to end, and it runs on top of the estimating software, CRM and phone system already in place. Nothing gets ripped out and nothing gets migrated.

This allows operators to run more jobs per adjuster and send estimates that clear review the first time. On the carrier side, the same work cuts cycle time to hours and leaves a line-item record of every loss, so risk can be priced by property instead of by ZIP code.

Cozmo's platform captures context from every claim it touches and gets sharper with each one.

Go to hellocozmo.ai and book a demo to see the Cozmo AI agents in action.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US property and casualty carriers, third party administrators and restoration contractors that handle property claims
problem: Property claims take days to weeks of manual intake, crew coordination and estimating. Cozmo agents run the claim from first notice of loss to estimate and supplement approval on top of existing software.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS, AI agents sold to claims operators
product_category: AI agents for insurance claims
market_need_then: As of 2022 the demand was for youth banking in the Gulf, where the founders saw teen digital payments as underserved. The claims automation need cited today (long claim cycle times) dates from the later pivot.
outcome_analysis: The W22 listing was the teen neobank Zywa, which raised a 1 million dollar pre seed and a 3 million dollar seed in 2022 and then, per the YC page and a secondary profile, was hit by regulatory and market changes. The founders moved to San Francisco and rebuilt as Cozmo AI, selling agents to insurers. The company is active with a team of 5 and unverified customer claims, so the outcome is still open.

name: Craniometrix
one_liner: Using AI to help dementia patients age at home
long_description:
Dementia is tough – but it can be easier. Turns out, if you give families the right non-clinical coaching and support, you can avoid 30% of hospitalizations for these patients. And Medicare has recently started paying for that coaching.

We leverage AI to provide best-in-class care, alleviating the burden on providers. Come help us build!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Families of dementia patients and Medicare GUIDE model providers who pay for care navigation
problem: Alzheimer's is diagnosed late and families lack coaching. The 2022 product screened risk through a phone game; the later product provides AI assisted dementia care navigation that Medicare now pays for.
business_model: Subscription screening and care navigation, later B2B2C via Medicare GUIDE program providers
product_category: Digital health, dementia screening and care navigation
market_need_then: In 2022 Alzheimer's was underdiagnosed and families lacked guidance; Medicare later began paying for non clinical dementia coaching, which the YC page cites as the opening.
outcome_analysis: Craniometrix raised a 6 million dollar seed in 2022 on a phone based Alzheimer's screening product, then moved toward care navigation as Medicare began paying for dementia coaching through the GUIDE model. Aggregators report a 2026 Series A and a team of 64 to 100, so it looks like it grew, but the later round size is unverified.

name: Craze
one_liner: The AI video platform where creatives make something people watch
long_description:
Craze is the AI video platform where creatives make something people watch.

Brands, creators, agencies and studios use Craze to storyboard, edit, design and turn creative direction into social media content, ads, films and more.

Craze comes with a creative agent you direct, access to all top video/image/music/audio/media models, and a full premiere-like timeline editor. You can also use Craze with your Chatgpt, Claude, Muse or other personal agents via Craze MCP.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Originally Indian startups and SMEs buying payroll, HR and IT; now creators who pay for AI video
problem: Indian founders needed one place for payroll, HR and compliance. The company later restarted as an AI video maker for creatives.
business_model: SaaS subscription (original HR product); freemium subscription with Pro, Ultra and Max plans (current video product)
product_category: HR and payroll platform, then AI video creation
market_need_then: Indian startups needed compliant payroll and HR; vendor pages show an active market of products aimed at startups, but no evidence on Craze demand.
outcome_analysis: Craze entered YC in Summer 2022 as an HR and payroll platform for India and was backed by YC, Nexus Venture Partners and Soma Capital according to a profile. The founders later shut the original product and relaunched twice, ending in an AI video maker. The cause of the shutdown is not public. Funding is undisclosed, so the outcome is a restart rather than a clean success or failure.

name: CrediBook
one_liner: Faire for Indonesia
long_description:
CrediBook digitizes the MSMEs' supply chain, from wholesale to retail, through online wholesale and bookkeeping operation system.

Our online wholesale platform CrediMart aims to create an efficient inventory-sourcing. We provide online-ordering, Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) payment method, and logistic support. We help our wholesale partners earn an additional daily income stream by 50%.

Our bookkeeping app CrediBook also enables MSMEs generate financial report in less than 5 minutes and proven to speed up users’ micro-loans process from financial institutions.
CrediBook strives to encourage more MSMEs to benefit digitalization from easy and efficient platforms that meet their needs.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indonesian small shops and wholesalers who buy wholesale goods and keep books
problem: Small Indonesian retailers kept paper ledgers and bought stock through informal wholesale channels with little credit. CrediBook is a bookkeeping app plus a wholesale marketplace with buy now pay later.
business_model: Free bookkeeping app feeding a B2B wholesale marketplace with take rate and BNPL financing
product_category: SME bookkeeping and B2B wholesale marketplace
founder_names: Gabriel Frans; Dekha Anggareska; Christian Lie
market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2021 framed Indonesian wholesalers as heavily offline, with bookkeeping digitization as an entry point; the company reports 330,000+ businesses on its site, undated.
outcome_analysis: CrediBook used bookkeeping to reach small Indonesian shops and then layered wholesale and pay later on top. It raised 1.5 million dollars in January 2021 and an 8.1 million dollar Series A in March 2022 led by Monk's Hill, and the company reports 330,000+ businesses on its site. Searches found no layoffs or sale, so the company looks like a surviving niche leader with strong funded rivals.

name: Creizer
one_liner: Clear.co for LATAM. Revenue based financing for online sellers.
long_description:
Creizer is Clearbanc (Clear.co) for LATAM. We provide revenue-based financing to online sellers.

More than 80% of SMEs can’t have access to loans in LATAM, thus limiting their growth. They represent 99% of online sellers in the region.
 
At Creizer we built a unique risk model in which the requirements for these online sellers are 100% accessible since the scoring is based on the store’s metrics and collections on a percentage of their daily sales.
 
We are growing 65% MoM and experiencing overdemand every month. Helping our customers to grow up to 7x in less than a year.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mexican online sellers on Mercado Libre, Amazon and Shopify who need working capital
problem: Online sellers cannot get bank loans and need stock financing. Creizer lends against store sales and is repaid as a share of sales.
business_model: Lender: revenue based financing, credit lines and fixed loans with interest and fees
product_category: Revenue based financing for e-commerce sellers
market_need_then: Mexican e-commerce sellers lacked bank credit and the Clearco model was spreading across LATAM, with Fairplay and Divibank raising in 2021 and 2022.
outcome_analysis: Creizer copied the Clearco model for Mexican online sellers and joined YC in Winter 2022 with a small team. Public funding data is thin, a seed from Carabela in 2021 and unverified aggregate totals near 500K. Its site now shows three credit products and aggregators claim hundreds of sellers, but there is no reliable growth data, so its trajectory is unclear.

name: Criya
tags: B2B; Sales; Sales Enablement; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: AI that builds GTM assets in seconds
long_description:
Criya AI, a Y Combinator and venture backed AI startup is an intelligent content system that reads across all your data sources and in 1-click produces stunning, hyper-personalized client-ready assets, by combining research, branding, authoring and engagement analytics.

Our AI Prospector replaces 85% of your account based marketing effort in 60 seconds. From market research to email/linkedin campaigns and landing page pitch decks, personalized for your specific buyer, we do it all in 1-click.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Curacel
tags: SaaS; B2B; Insurance; Healthcare IT; AI
one_liner: AI-Powered Infrastructure for Insurance & Healthcare
long_description: Curacel builds AI-driven infrastructure to help payors, TPAs and healthcare providers automate claims processing, reduce fraud, streamline operations and enhance customer experiences. Our intelligent solutions make insurance and healthcare more efficient, accessible, and scalable.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: African and emerging market insurers, HMOs and digital platforms that embed insurance
problem: Insurance claims in Africa are slow, paper heavy and fraud prone; Curacel automates claims and offers APIs to sell insurance inside other apps.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage based API for insurers and platforms
product_category: Insurtech infrastructure, claims automation and embedded insurance
market_need_then: Pre seed coverage in March 2021 says Curacel already worked with insurers such as AXA Mansard, Liberty Health and Old Mutual and more than 800 hospitals, which shows early insurer demand for claims processing.
outcome_analysis: Curacel started as claims automation for African insurers, raised a 450K pre seed in 2021 and a 3 million dollar seed in February 2023 led by Tencent, and added APIs and embedded insurance. It claims over 100 million dollars of claims processed and serves insurers in eight countries. No layoffs or sale were found; the company is active and moderately funded.

name: CustomerOS
one_liner: Uncover high-fit leads already silently engaging with your brand
long_description:
CustomerOS uncovers high-fit leads who are engaging directly with your brand but not yet in your sales funnel. By lead scoring your pipeline against your ICP we build data-driven profiles of your best customers and provide a real-time ICP-fit indicator so your team doesn't waste time on low-value/high-cost leads. This ensures you're spending your CAC acquiring customers who are primed to renew year after year and expand as they grow.

The Top 10% of SaaS companies generate 87% of all market returns. CustomerOS gives you the data and tooling to compete with the top 10%.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Cypher
one_liner: Crypto Neo-Bank (WhatsApp moment for bank accounts)
long_description:
Internet broke physical boundaries in commerce and made it global. It never happened in finance. Almost all financial consumer apps are country specific. Stablecoins are the internet moment for finance industry.

Cypher lets an user download an app from anywhere in the world and have a bank account in 5 mins and start transacting with the crypto card. Can instantly send USDC to anywhere in the world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Crypto users wanting a self-custody wallet with a spendable Visa card, later businesses and stablecoin payments
problem: Crypto holders could not easily spend assets from their own wallet at ordinary merchants without trusting a custodial exchange card.
business_model: Card fees and subscription plans (premium plan reported at $199 per year), interchange, token incentives
product_category: Non-custodial crypto wallet and card issuing
market_need_then: Demand for spending crypto existed in 2021 and 2022 through exchange cards, but self-custody card options were few; no dated source quantified demand.
outcome_analysis: Cypher raised a $4.3M YC-led seed in January 2023 and, per the founder, reached $5M annualized revenue selling a self-custody Visa card. In July 2026 Nium acquired the wallet and issuing business at an undisclosed price while the consumer app, cards and CYPR token program were wound down by September 2026. The outcome looks like a technology and licence pickup rather than a consumer success, though terms are unknown.

name: Darsel
one_liner: Chatbot teaching K12 math in developing countries
long_description: Darsel is a AI-powered math education chatbot which is designed to supplement K12 education systems in resource-constrained environments. Darsel allows students to practice math questions & do their homework through platforms like SMS, WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger.
regions: Jordan; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Public school systems and ministries in low and middle income countries, paid by donors since Darsel is a nonprofit
problem: Students in low bandwidth settings lack personalized math help; Darsel tutors K12 math over SMS, WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger on basic phones.
business_model: Donor and grant funded nonprofit, free to students and teachers
product_category: Education technology, math tutoring chatbot
market_need_then: COVID learning loss and poor connectivity made text based tutoring attractive; the Stanford GSB article describes testing with students in Nigeria in fall 2020 and early evidence of improved test scores.
outcome_analysis: Darsel is a nonprofit math chatbot that reports 264,000 students across Jordan, India and Nigeria by July 2025. It joined the Google.org Accelerator in June 2025 and won a WISE Prize award per the prize site. Growth comes from donor and government partnerships rather than venture rounds, so success is measured in reach and an RCT registered in 2026.

name: Dart
one_liner: The work and agent management platform
long_description: Dart is a fully-featured project management tool that lets you chat with AI to create tasks, plan roadmaps, generate reports, and handle any other PM work. You can then use customizable agents to complete work across every role. Thousands of teams use Dart in order to chat with their tasks, plan better, and eliminate regular PM chores from their schedule, freeing up seven hours per week to focus on other work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Teams and startups that manage projects and increasingly work with AI agents
problem: Project management tools add overhead; Dart uses AI to create tasks, plans and reports from chat and lets agents do the work.
business_model: Freemium SaaS per seat
product_category: AI native project management
market_need_then: Dart claims to save users seven hours per week on PM overhead in its earlier YC launch; demand evidence in 2022 is not independently sourced.
outcome_analysis: Dart launched publicly in March 2024 after a 500K pre seed in 2022 and has added AI chat and agents. The site claims over 100,000 teams, which is unverified. No acquisition, layoffs or later rounds were found. It competes in a crowded category with incumbents adding AI, so the outcome is open and modest in evidence.

name: Dealls – Jobs & Mentoring
one_liner: Indonesia's #1 ATS & Job Portal to match top talents & companies
long_description: Dealls offers a curated selection of job vacancies for individuals pre-screened and curated by our team. By partnering with us, 5000+ companies have saved time and money by receiving only eligible and top candidates. Job seekers love Dealls because they can apply to multiple top companies with a single click and receive responses 21X faster than with other platforms.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indonesian employers (hiring teams, later HR departments) who pay for curated candidates and an ATS, plus young Indonesian job seekers who use it free
problem: Indonesian employers struggle to find pre-screened candidates among large volumes of unqualified applicants, and young job seekers lack guidance and fast responses.
business_model: B2B recruiting SaaS and job portal (employer vacancy and ATS fees) with free job seeker mentoring; later HRIS (KantorKu)
product_category: Job portal, ATS and career mentoring in Indonesia
market_need_then: Indonesia has a large young population entering the workforce and many employers reporting difficulty filtering applicants; the YC page claims 5,000+ employers and responses 21x faster, which are company claims.
outcome_analysis: Dealls appears to have grown steadily in Indonesia, reaching a team of about 127 per the YC page and expanding into HR software with KantorKu HRIS. No layoffs, acquisition or shutdown were found. Its growth seems tied to a free mentoring program that feeds a candidate pool and a large young Indonesian market, but funding is not verified by any primary source.

name: Decent
tags: Developer Tools; Crypto / Web3; B2B; Cryptocurrency
one_liner: Cross-chain routing + trading APIs. One-click transactions with any…
long_description: Any asset, every chain, in an instant.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Web3 developers, music and NFT creators, later apps and institutions needing cross-chain execution
problem: Creators and apps found it hard to build token-based projects and let users transact across chains in one step.
business_model: Usage-based developer APIs and protocol fees
product_category: Cross-chain routing and NFT infrastructure
founder_names: Charlie Durbin; Will Collier; Will Kantaros; Alexander Carlson
market_need_then: NFT and music NFT creators in 2021 and 2022 wanted no-code token tooling; the later cross-chain focus responded to fragmentation across chains.
outcome_analysis: Decent started in 2021 as music and NFT infrastructure, raised a $3.5M Archetype-led seed in December 2022, then pivoted into cross-chain routing and chain abstraction APIs as NFT demand cooled. MoonPay acquired it in May 2026 to power an institutional trading platform across 200 plus chains, reportedly in a high eight-figure deal that MoonPay has not confirmed. The pivot to infrastructure created the buyer interest.

name: Delegasi
one_liner: Automated accounting service for small businesses in Indonesia
long_description:
Financial statements are definitely a hassle for business owners. Many accounting software are available, yet not everyone has the capability to operate them.

Amidst this problem, Delegasi dares to provide a solution. As the first virtual financial manager in Indonesia, we assist SMB owners in putting together their financial statements and business analysis. By simply uploading receipts and bank statements, owners will receive their financial statements and business analyses with guaranteed accuracy, allowing them to make well informed financial decisions.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Delfino AI
tags: Generative AI; Machine Learning; Health Tech; AI
one_liner: Generative AI for administrative automation in healthcare
long_description: Delfino AI helps automate the repetitive phone calls that providers' offices make to payors
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Provider offices, billing companies and practices that call insurance payors for eligibility, prior authorization and claim status
problem: Provider office staff spend hours on hold and on repetitive calls to payors for benefit verification, prior authorization and claim status.
business_model: B2B AI voice automation, likely usage or subscription based (pricing not found)
product_category: Healthcare administrative automation, voice AI for payor calls
market_need_then: US providers spend heavy staff time on payor calls; the pain was a known cost center, though the 2022 text-only source set offers no spend figures.
outcome_analysis: Delfino AI remains a tiny two person team per the YC page with no disclosed funding beyond aggregator mentions of a $500K pre-seed. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. The company entered a crowded niche led by Infinitus, and its outcome is not yet visible from public sources.

name: Demo Gorilla
one_liner: Make all your live SaaS demos impactful: close more ARR faster
long_description:
Demo Gorilla is a browser extension for live SaaS demos that tells your sales team exactly what to say to sell your product.

Keep everyone on the same page with the best customer stores, competitive talking points and feature explanations. Collect insights across product, engineering, marketing, and sales experts to ensure your sales team always knows exactly what will close this deal.

- Automatically get relevant talking points for the part of the product you're on and who you're talking to
- Track notes and metrics back in to your CRM
- Share slides and images in line while demoing to set the stage
- Clean up your UI to keep attendees focused
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Seattle, WA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Denormalized
one_liner: serverless platform for real-time data
long_description: Denormalized is a serverless real-time data platform that allows users to query data quickly while eliminating the need to manage complex infrastructure. It enhances developer productivity by automating schema inference from sample data and simplifying data stream creation allowing engineers to go from idea to production fast. Denormalized supports SQL for data transformations without needing complex stream processing systems like Flink.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Dev Tools AI
one_liner: AI powered web & mobile automation
long_description: We help scale automation leveraging LLMs and computer vision
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software and QA teams that need automation of web and mobile apps
problem: Scripted web and mobile automation is brittle and expensive to maintain; the founders applied LLMs and computer vision to make it scale.
business_model: Likely B2B software subscription (not confirmed by sources)
product_category: AI powered web and mobile test automation
market_need_then: Test automation maintenance was a known pain and the founders came from test.ai, but specific demand evidence for Dev Tools AI itself was not found.
outcome_analysis: Dev Tools AI was a two person Summer 2022 team of former test.ai engineers building LLM and vision based automation, and is marked Inactive. No post-mortem, acquisition notice or funding news was found, so the cause of shutdown is not public and failure factors are left empty. Its timing preceded the 2023 to 2025 wave of well funded LLM agent automation startups.

name: Devyce
one_liner: The global mobile network for business.
long_description:
Devyce is building the global mobile network for business. Right now, we give your employees a business phone number in an app, on their personal phone, instantly, alongside a portal for analytics, management and integrations.

Nick has a background in recruiting and real estate and understands the pain points these industries face with hybrid working, while Ed has a solid tech background including a CS degree from Cambridge. Because of our relationship with a mobile network operator, we have the unfair advantage that we will actually become a mobile network, unlike other SaaS VoIP providers.

https://devyce.com/
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Businesses and recruitment teams that want employees to have a business number in an app on their personal phone
problem: SaaS VoIP providers lease numbers from carriers and pass on connection and usage costs; businesses want cheaper business numbers on personal phones with analytics and integrations.
business_model: Per-user monthly subscription (YC page says about $20 per user per month; website now lists GBP 30 and 39 plans)
product_category: Business phone system and mobile network for business (VoIP)
founder_names: Nick Browne; Edward Clayton; Leo Bartle
market_need_then: Hybrid work after 2020 raised demand for business numbers on personal phones; Tech.eu cites savings of up to 70 percent versus leasing models, a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Devyce raised a $2.7M seed in February 2023 after YC and appears operating with a recruitment-focused product and public pricing. No shutdown or acquisition was found. Its structural cost edge comes from the sister mobile operator, but traction numbers are not public so the outcome is still open.

name: Dialect
one_liner: AI copilot for forms, questionnaires & RFX
long_description: Dialect uses AI trained on your company’s internal knowledge to automate response generation for forms,  RFPs, and other complex business communications.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Palo Alto, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: DimOrder
one_liner: Toast for Southeast Asia
long_description:
DimOrder - Restaurant POS system for Southeast Asia

Founded in 2019, DimOrder is a Hong Kong-based technology company transforming the F&B industry. In addition to online payments, we allow restaurants to market to their customers, order food from their suppliers, and receive short term loans. Through one single platform, restaurateurs can easily manage their business and focus on their passion, we let the chef be chef.
regions: Hong Kong; East Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hong Kong and Southeast Asian restaurants and F&B operators
problem: Restaurants face staff shortages, costly ingredients and no data analysis; they need ordering, payments, supplier ordering and financing in one system.
business_model: Restaurant POS SaaS plus payments, delivery app commission, supplier ordering and short-term loans
product_category: Restaurant POS and F&B fintech
market_need_then: Hong Kong F&B faced labor shortages and COVID-driven shift to online ordering and delivery, per the HKTDC founder story.
outcome_analysis: DimOrder was founded by two restaurant operators, giving it founder-market fit, and now runs a team of about 70 with POS, delivery and payment products across offices in Hong Kong, Thailand, Taipei and Guangzhou. No shutdown or acquisition was found. Funding is unverified, so growth quality cannot be judged.

name: Dioptra
one_liner: Automated contract review with AI
long_description: We help founders and in-house counsels streamline their contract negotiations to close deals faster. We do this by building your contract negotiation playbooks and automating them with AI.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: In-house legal teams and law firms reviewing and negotiating contracts
problem: Lawyers spend hours redlining contracts against playbooks; Dioptra automates playbook-based review and redlining in Word.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Legal tech, AI contract review and redlining
market_need_then: Contract review is labor intensive for legal teams; the generative AI wave from 2022 and 2023 increased budgets, but no dated 2021 source was gathered.
outcome_analysis: Dioptra is a small YC W22 team that moved to AI contract review, launched PromptIQ in October 2024, partnered with LawVu and Icertis in 2025, and was acquired by Icertis in November 2025 at an undisclosed price. Its team and technology were folded into Icertis, which suggests a strategic tuck-in; funding and traction are not public. The generative AI wave and Word-native redlining fit are the likely tailwinds.

name: Disclo
tags: Human Resources; B2B; Compliance; HR Tech
one_liner: Health disclosure and accommodation management platform
long_description:
Disclo is the first software for employers to collect, verify, and manage health disclosures and employee accommodation requests (HIPAA and SOC2 compliant, of course).

We help employees secure the enhancements and protections they need to succeed in their careers without having to disclose their underlying medical condition to their employer. We handle the collection of that data, the verification, the secure data management, and much more.

Using our patent-pending medical verification system, Disclo validates that an employee's accommodation request is legitimate and required, interacting with medical providers directly, so HR managers can focus on what they do best. We help companies stay compliant with EEOC, ADA, and HIPAA guidelines.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Employers and HR teams that must manage health disclosures and disability accommodation requests
problem: Employees struggle to safely ask for and verify workplace accommodations, and employers handle them through insurers, sticky notes and shared drives while needing ADA, EEOC and HIPAA compliance.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for employers
product_category: HR compliance software, accommodation management
market_need_then: TechCrunch cites a 61 percent rise in accommodation requests tied to remote work and regulation like the ADA creating compliance pressure.
outcome_analysis: Disclo raised a $5M seed led by General Catalyst in February 2023 and claims customers like Meta, Levi Strauss and Lululemon on the YC page. Founders have lived experience and an earlier disability recruiting business, and the rise in accommodation requests supports demand. No shutdown or acquisition found; traction numbers remain undisclosed.

name: Dittofeed
one_liner: Open-source customer engagement & messaging automation
long_description:
Dittofeed is an open-source alternative to platforms like Klaviyo and Customer.io. Self-host us for free, or use our low-cost cloud offering to automate messages across email, SMS, mobile push, WhatsApp, and more. 

We also offer solutions for embedding Dittofeed in your own SaaS! Instantly provide your customers with automated messaging tools.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers and SaaS companies wanting self-hostable customer messaging automation
problem: Marketing automation platforms like Klaviyo and Customer.io are costly and closed.
business_model: Open-source (MIT) core with paid cloud and Embedded Components
product_category: Customer engagement / messaging automation
market_need_then: Self-hosting and cost interest in open-source Klaviyo/Customer.io alternatives; Product Hunt launches in 2023 and 2025 and about 3,000 GitHub stars by late 2026 show developer interest but not paying demand.
outcome_analysis: Dittofeed, an open-source Klaviyo alternative from a two-person team, wound down in 2026: Cloud closed on 2026-10-31 and the company said it could not make the business sustainable. Open-source adoption (about 3,000 GitHub stars) did not translate into enough paying customers against entrenched, funded incumbents, though the sources do not state the precise cause.

name: Diversion
tags: SaaS; Virtual Reality; Enterprise; Cloud Computing
one_liner: A scalable, cloud-native Perforce and Git alternative
long_description: Diversion is a modern alternative to Perforce and Git, designed for digital entertainment industries like games, virtual production, animation, and 3D/VR. It streamlines collaboration by providing GitHub-like version control for large files and complex projects, integrating seamlessly with tools like Unreal Engine. Built for studios handling massive assets, Diversion ensures efficient workflows, secure storage, and effortless tracking of project history, making it the go-to platform for creative teams managing evolving digital content.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Game studios, virtual production, animation and 3D teams with large binary repositories
problem: Perforce is costly and heavy to operate and Git handles large files poorly, so creative teams lack a modern, cloud-native version control system.
business_model: SaaS subscription per seat or usage for hosted version control
product_category: Version control, developer tools for games and creative industries
competitors_at_founding: Perforce; Git with Git LFS; Plastic SCM (later Unity Version Control)
market_need_then: Game studios complained about Perforce cost and operations and Git's trouble with large binaries; Diversion's own surveys and blogs cite this, which is vendor material.
outcome_analysis: Diversion has kept shipping and raised more funding, with a reported $4.5M round led by Konvoy in 2025 and about $12M in total per GamesBeat. A repeat founder with two exits targets a clear pain at Perforce, though Epic's Lore and Unity's tooling are credible competitors. No shutdown or acquisition found.

name: Dojah Inc
one_liner: Prevent Fraud and Onboard Users Faster
long_description:
Dojah is the anti-fraud infrastructure for the internet, helping businesses verify identities, detect fraud, and stay compliant with powerful APIs and no-code tools. Fintechs, banks, and digital businesses rely on Dojah’s solutions for seamless user onboarding, AI-driven fraud detection, KYC & KYB verification, and transaction monitoring.

By leveraging government data lookups, biometric authentication, and real-time risk analysis, Dojah ensures businesses can mitigate fraud risks, improve user trust, and scale efficiently while staying compliant with regulatory standards.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: African fintechs, banks and digital businesses needing KYC, KYB and fraud checks
problem: Innovators struggle to source APIs and government data to verify customer identity and prevent fraud in African markets.
business_model: Usage-based identity verification and fraud API plus no-code dashboard
product_category: Identity verification, KYC and anti-fraud infrastructure
market_need_then: Fast growth of African fintech and tightening KYC rules created demand for verification APIs; competitor rounds in 2022 reflect investor interest.
outcome_analysis: Dojah remained active with about 30 staff on the YC page and a broad KYC and anti-fraud product suite. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. Aggregators show only about $510K raised, so growth appears modest and capital efficient, but no primary source confirms funding or revenue.

name: Dr. Treat
one_liner: “One Medical for pets.”
long_description: Dr. Treat is a tech enabled modern veterinary care company offering virtual and in-clinic services to pet parents. We are building the largest pet health company powered by technology and driven by data to offer highly personalized & preventative care for every pet.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Gen Z and millennial pet owners in the San Francisco Bay Area who pay an annual membership
problem: Veterinary care is hard to access and impersonal; owners want preventative, personalized care with virtual and in-clinic options.
business_model: Annual membership (Dr. Treat One at $149 per year) plus pay-as-you-go visits ($85) and clinic services
product_category: Tech-enabled veterinary clinics and telehealth
founder_names: Rakesh Tondon; Hetal Shah; Charlie Bowman
market_need_then: Pet ownership surged in 2020 and 2021 and vet capacity was strained; an investor-funded set of premium membership clinics existed, showing willingness to pay in affluent markets.
outcome_analysis: Dr. Treat opened its San Francisco clinic in 2022 and by Dealroom a second in Burlingame in early 2024, and sells memberships. The YC page claims an acquisition in 2025 after reaching $9M ARR, but no independent source or acquirer was found, so the outcome is uncertain. Funding figures conflict across sources.

name: Drahim 💰
one_liner: WealthFront for Saudi & Middle East
long_description:
"Drahim" is a slang for money in Arabic (from the ancient Greek Drachma).

The app integrates with banks and provides individuals meaningful spending insights and generates auto savings and investment advice.

For the meaningful insights, the app integrates with banks and automatically categorizes all of your transactions (All of your accounts in one place) and spots spending patterns and behaviors.

Drahim then suggests a saving and investing plan that allows the user to continue living comfortably and to keep spending guilt-free.

Our focus is not necessarily to save you money, rather we grow your money discreetly. Drahim allows you to continue spending but feeling way better doing it.
regions: Saudi Arabia; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Saudi retail consumers who want spending insight and automated, Sharia-compliant investing; later also companies via Drahim Business
problem: Individuals in Saudi Arabia had no single place to see all bank accounts and spending, and no simple way to turn spare cash into investments.
business_model: Fee on assets under management (0.25 percent per year stated on the company site) on top of a free personal finance management app; Drahim Business for companies
product_category: Personal finance management app with robo-advisory investing
competitors_at_founding: Malaa Technologies; Abyan Capital; Mint and Truebill
market_need_then: Rising Saudi smartphone banking, Vision 2030 push for household savings and capital market participation, and a regulator creating fintech sandboxes. Pain stated by the company is lack of consolidated spending insight.
outcome_analysis: Drahim launched a Saudi personal finance and robo-advisory app, joined YC in Summer 2022, and won licenses from SAMA and the Capital Market Authority. Al Rajhi Bank acquired 65 percent in September 2024, which the bank's own release confirms, so the outcome is a majority acquisition by a strategic bank rather than a failure. Regulatory licensing and local fit were the main assets.

name: Drama Drama
tags: Payments; Entertainment; Advertising; Creator Economy; AI
one_liner: Monetization platform for AI characters and dramas
long_description:
Drama Drama is building the monetization platform for AI character and drama creators.

Creators are already building AI characters and serialized stories that attract audiences on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and other social platforms, but turning that fandom into direct revenue is still difficult.

Drama Drama lets creators monetize their existing characters and series through gated episodes, paid AI character chat across text, voice and video, personalized fan experiences and other direct-to-fan products.

Creators can bring the content and audience they already have. For selected creators who want help producing a series, we also offer optional co-production.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Creators of AI characters and serialized AI dramas who already have audiences on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, plus fans who pay them
problem: Creators build audiences around AI characters and series but cannot easily turn fandom into direct revenue.
business_model: Creator monetization platform: gated episodes, paid AI character chat, fan requests and tips, with an optional co-production model and revenue share
product_category: Creator economy monetization platform for AI characters and drama series
market_need_then: In early 2022 creators sought direct monetization beyond platform ad revenue. The current pitch about AI characters and AI dramas reflects the 2025 and 2026 AI video wave rather than conditions at the batch, and no dated source describes the original 2022 product.
outcome_analysis: Drama Drama is listed as active with a team of two more than four years after the W22 batch. Searches for funding, press, acquisition or shutdown returned nothing about it, so the trajectory is not public. The company describes a current focus on monetizing AI characters and dramas, which suggests the product was reshaped around the AI video wave, but no dated source documents the earlier pivot or any traction.

name: Drip
one_liner: Shop and pay in installments anywhere
long_description:
Drip combines the best of Pix and a credit card. We enable customers to pay with credit and earn 2%+ cashback with the speed and widespread acceptance of Pix.

Through our app customers can onboard, shop nearly anywhere and manage their payments. We're enabling transactions via  Pix's existing network (85%+ of e-comm).
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Drivingforce
one_liner: Rippling for trucking
long_description:
Drivingforce is building “Rippling for trucking”, an all-in-one workforce management solution for the trucking industry. We consolidate multiple back office functions such as compliance, payroll, and recruiting, so trucking fleets can manage their entire workforce in one place.


Check us out on TikTok!
tiktok.com/@truckingnewbie
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Dukesell
tags: Marketplace; Social; E-commerce; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Duke makes every ecommerce merchant agent-ready
long_description:
Duke equips ecommerce merchants with the tools they need to participate in agentic commerce, regardless of platform or geography.

Merchants can deploy voice agents that understand customers, recommend products and help process orders in 50+ languages. Duke connects deeply to the merchant’s catalog, inventory, customer history, orders and fulfillment, giving agents the context they need to personalize and complete transactions.

Duke also provides the agent-ready infrastructure that makes merchant products and purchasing flows accessible to external commerce agents, allowing consumers to discover and buy from merchants through the AI tools they already use.

Merchants can connect an existing Shopify store or use Duke directly. Our goal is to make every merchant discoverable, understandable and transactable by agents.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Ecommerce merchants (initially Shopify stores and social sellers in Africa) that pay for voice and AI sales agents and agent-ready storefronts
problem: Merchants lose sales because shoppers cannot easily browse and buy by talking in local languages, and merchant catalogs are not accessible to external shopping agents.
business_model: SaaS subscription with a free tier, a 15 USD per month Premium plan and custom pricing, per the company site
product_category: AI voice commerce agents and agent-ready ecommerce infrastructure
market_need_then: Catalyst Fund's January 2022 note frames demand around informal digital sellers in Ghana and the fact that WhatsApp and Facebook were adding commerce features.
outcome_analysis: The company began as Tendo, a Ghana social reselling platform, joined YC in Winter 2022, and later renamed and repositioned as Dukesell around AI voice agents and agentic commerce. It remains active with about 15 people. Public funding evidence is thin, the pivot date is unknown, and the outcome is still open, so no success or failure judgement is made beyond survival.

name: Duplo
one_liner: Venmo for B2B in Africa
regions: Nigeria; Africa
target_customer: Nigerian FMCG distributors and SME to mid-market finance teams that pay and collect from other businesses
problem: B2B payments in Nigeria involve slow settlement, manual invoicing and reconciliation; a survey cited by TechCrunch found many businesses wait over 24 hours for payments.
business_model: Payments and spend management platform earning fees on payment flows plus software and B2B credit products
product_category: B2B payments and financial operating system
founder_names: Yele Oyekola; Tunde Akinnuwa; Emeka Okwuagwu
market_need_then: TechCrunch cites a 1.5 trillion USD sub-Saharan B2B payments market and a survey of 1,000 business owners where 44 percent waited over 24 hours for payments.
outcome_analysis: Duplo launched in 2021 with FMCG distributors, raised 1.3M USD pre-seed in February 2022 and 4.3M USD seed in August 2022 for 5.6M total, and reported very fast payment volume growth. It is active and has expanded to treasury and e-invoicing with a South African arm. No later priced round was found in searches, so funding coverage is partial and the long run outcome is open.

name: Durioo
one_liner: Streaming Platform for Muslim Children
long_description:
We create and license high quality Islamic cartoons and shows that kids watch on our subscription app.

We are the right team to do this because we previously created an Islamic cartoon with more than 3 billion views on YouTube.

All parents want their kids to grow up with values and virtues close to them. The same goes for Muslim parents - but the reality is - they are struggling to get high quality Islamic content for their kids.

We are addressing an underserved market of 70 million Muslim families with internet access globally.
regions: Malaysia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Muslim parents with children aged 1 to 12 who pay a monthly subscription for Islamic-values cartoons
problem: Muslim parents struggle to find high quality children's content that matches their values, and algorithms on open platforms push unsuitable content.
business_model: Consumer subscription streaming (7.99 USD per month at launch per press release) plus planned merchandise and games
product_category: Islamic children's streaming platform and animation studio
market_need_then: Digital News Asia reports the founder's claim of 70 million Muslim families online, YouTube monetization changes for kids' content in 2020, and about 22,000 paid subscribers by early 2023, 99 percent in Malaysia.
outcome_analysis: Durioo moved a content studio with a large YouTube audience into its own subscription app, joined YC in Winter 2022 and raised a 2.85M USD seed announced in March 2023 with about 22,000 paid subscribers. It is active with about 50 to 65 staff. Later subscriber or revenue data were not found, so the long run outcome is unknown, but owned characters and an inherited audience were clear strengths.

name: Dynamo AI
one_liner: Compliant-Ready AI for the Enterprise
long_description: End-to-end privacy, security, and compliance solutions to prepare your organization for emerging AI regulations.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Regulated enterprises (banks, insurers, tech and government) that must deploy AI under privacy, security and compliance rules
problem: Companies cannot train or deploy models on sensitive data, or put LLMs into production, without leaking data or violating regulation.
business_model: Enterprise software licences for AI evaluation, guardrails and agent security
product_category: Privacy-preserving ML, then generative AI compliance and guardrails
competitors_at_founding: Owkin; Devron; Rhino Health; NimbleEdge; FedML
market_need_then: TechCrunch 2022 frames demand around privacy regulation and companies unable to use sensitive data for ML; the later LLM wave raised demand for compliant generative AI, and Experian deployed the product in 2024 per a profile.
outcome_analysis: Two MIT PhDs turned research on privacy-preserving ML into DynamoFL, raised a 4.15M USD seed in September 2022 and a 15.1M USD Series A in August 2023 as LLMs created compliance demand, then rebranded to Dynamo AI in 2024 around guardrails and evaluation. It is active with named enterprise customers. No later priced round was found, so the Series A is the last known raise.

name: Eazipay Inc.
one_liner: Eazipay powers effortless payroll and financial access in Africa.
long_description:
Eazipay is Africa’s leading payroll and payment automation platform, making it easy for businesses to pay their teams accurately, on time, and with minimal effort. Our Payroll API enables businesses, fintechs, and platforms to integrate payroll processing directly into their systems—automating salary payments, tax deductions, and compliance.

Beyond payroll, Eazipay also empowers workers by providing faster access to their earnings and financial benefits. With features like early wage access and financial wellness tools, we help employees and gig workers gain more control over their income and financial stability.

We now serve over 10k businesses, with many YC companies as customers.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Nigerian businesses of all sizes, plus fintechs and platforms using the payroll API, and workers seeking early wage access
problem: Nigerian businesses struggle with manual payroll, tax, pension and statutory remittances, and workers lack timely access to earned pay.
business_model: Payroll SaaS and API with fees on payroll and remittances, plus lending and early wage access products
product_category: Payroll and compliance platform
market_need_then: Company says it serves over 10,000 businesses (YC page) and 15,000 (2025 sponsored article); demand evidence at founding is not independently sourced.
outcome_analysis: Eazipay is a Lagos payroll and compliance platform from YC Winter 2022 that now claims thousands of business customers and a payroll API. No funding beyond YC was found in reliable sources, and growth claims come from the company and sponsored content. It appears to have grown capital-efficiently but evidence is thin.

name: Ekho
one_liner: Shopify for vehicles
long_description: Ekho's end-to-end vehicle commerce platform powers compliant, digital sales of titled vehicles. Our platform handles checkout, financing, titling, registration, signature collection, and taxes—so dealers and OEMs can sell nationwide with a seamless, Tesla-like experience. Dealers use Ekho Dealer as a “dealership-in-a-box” to capture online sales and automate in-store deals without needing large back-office teams, while OEMs use Ekho Access and Omni to extend their reach and unify dealers across sales channels.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Vehicle OEMs, dealers and dealer groups that sell titled vehicles online
problem: Franchise laws force new vehicle sales through licensed dealers, so manufacturers could not sell direct online in most states and compliance with titling, registration and taxes was hard.
business_model: Licensed dealer and software platform charging per transaction and subscriptions to OEMs and dealers
product_category: Vehicle commerce and compliance platform
market_need_then: YC launch post cites franchise laws, direct sale illegal for manufacturers in most states, and dealer commissions of 20 to 30 percent plus; EV makers wanted online sales.
outcome_analysis: Ekho began as Ekho Dealer, a licensed distribution layer letting OEMs sell online, and broadened into a platform for dealers and OEMs with an AI sales agent. It raised a 15M USD Series A led by Activant in July 2025 (17.3M total with seed) and remains active with about 30 people. Licensing and per-state compliance are the moat; scale beyond that is not yet shown.

name: Elementary
tags: Developer Tools; Analytics; Open Source; Data Engineering
one_liner: Open-source data observability for data teams
long_description: Elementary enables data teams to detect problems in their data before their users do. An open-source solution that any data engineer can deploy in minutes without sharing sensitive data.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Data engineers and analytics engineers at companies using dbt and cloud data warehouses
problem: Data teams learn about broken or anomalous data from their users instead of detecting it first.
business_model: Open-source core with a paid managed cloud product (launched 2024 per press) on subscription
product_category: Data observability and data quality
market_need_then: Monte Carlo raised 60M USD in August 2021 on rapid growth, showing budget for data observability as dbt and cloud warehouses spread.
outcome_analysis: Two Unit 8200 alumni built an open-source dbt-native observability tool, raised about 8.5M USD by end of 2022 and added a paid cloud product in 2024. It was acquired by Boomi in October 2026 for roughly 40 to 45 million USD with 17 staff. That is a modest exit relative to funding, delivered by open-source adoption of about 1,500 data teams.

name: Elessar
one_liner: AI-powered engineering productivity tools
long_description: Elessar boosts engineering productivity by integrating with your existing ecosystem of tools to automatically generate changelogs, streamline communications, and provide AI-powered reporting to engineers & managers.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Palo Alto, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams and engineering managers at software companies using GitHub, Slack and Linear
problem: Engineers spend time documenting code changes and keeping up with teammates, and managers lack visibility into where engineering time goes.
business_model: B2B SaaS (pricing not found)
product_category: Engineering productivity and automated documentation
market_need_then: Engineering analytics was a funded category in 2021 and 2022 (LinearB and Swarmia rounds), showing manager demand for visibility. Demand for automated changelogs specifically is not evidenced by sources opened.
outcome_analysis: Elessar was a two person YC S22 company building automatic changelogs and AI reporting for engineering teams. No funding beyond a reported YC note, no exit and no shutdown were found. The founder later started another YC company (NeoStrand, W27 per his profile), which suggests Elessar stalled or was set aside, but no source states this.

name: Elevate (formerly Bloom)
one_liner: US based USD accounts for non-US residents
long_description: We provide US based USD deposit accounts that sit with a licensed banking partner. Elevate's FDIC-insured USD accounts offer ACH, wire inbound and outbound payments, and a free Mastercard debit card. Our regional payout partners enable our users to send their money back home at very low cost.  We're targetting non-US residents in emerging markets who struggle to get paid in USD.
regions: United Arab Emirates; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Freelancers, remote workers and founders in emerging markets (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Philippines) who need USD accounts to get paid
problem: People in emerging markets struggle to receive USD from employers and platforms; incumbents like Payoneer charge high fees and lack FDIC insurance.
business_model: Fintech accounts with FX, payout and card fees, built on a sponsor bank
product_category: Cross-border USD accounts and debit cards
market_need_then: About 100,000 people used the first Sudan focused products between late 2021 and mid-2022; after the 2024 pivot over 150,000 signed up in the new markets, showing demand for USD accounts.

name: Emobi

Emobi is a unified legal, financial, and technical infrastructure that delivers seamless, secure, and reliable EV charging across networks—powering apps, fleets, and automakers while maximizing charger utilization. Our secure, fully automated charging technology, JustPlug, works instantly with no special hardware, software, or setup, making EV charging effortless.

With 122,000+ EV chargers integrated across the U.S. and Canada, Emobi is recognized as the largest EV charging ecosystem in North America. Backed by two provisional patents and 15+ enterprise customers, Emobi's technology is also trusted by the Department of Energy (DoE) and the Department of Transportation (DoT). To learn more, visit www.emobi.ai.

outcome_analysis: Emobi is a YC W22 EV charging infrastructure company that built JustPlug Plug and Charge roaming and reports integration of over 122,000 chargers and pilots with large automakers. name: Engage Bio

outcome_analysis: Engage Bio was a YC W22 preclinical biotech that built the Tethosome non-viral DNA platform on aggregator-reported seed money of about $4M from SciFounders, Pioneer Fund, YC and others plus NIH and Gates grants. The lean capital use and technical differentiation drove a strategic exit.

name: Entvin
