name: EthosX
tags: DeFi; Fintech; Crypto / Web3; Consumer; B2B
one_liner: The protocol for derivatives on blockchains
long_description:
EthosX is a decentralized finance platform creating end-to-end financial derivatives on blockchains. No centralized exchanges, clearinghouses, depositories, clearing banks, CSD participants etc. required.

We are starting with cryptocurrency options first, with the intention to move towards other crypto derivatives and traditional finance derivatives eventually.

For example, one can buy a bitcoin hedging token directly from EthosX without involving any exchange or counterparty and earn profits when the bitcoin price is falling (similar to a put option). It is perpetual and is completely on-chain, end-to-end. It is held as a token in wallets and can be sold/transferred to anyone at any time.

At institutional level, using EthosX’s options infrastructure two hedge funds can trade high-value on-chain options with each other directly without involving any banks or brokers with zero counterparty risk and zero settlement risk.

We are also providing derivatives infrastructure to other crypto companies who want to use these products as a part of a larger package to their customers.

Global derivatives ecosystem is broken. Derivatives trading in traditional finance has way too many gatekeepers and intermediaries. Crypto was supposed to be free of these issues and a solution to all of this, but it is itself getting more and more centralized with disastrous consequences.

We at EthosX intend to pick the best of both worlds and change the way retail and institutional financial derivatives are traded world over.
all_locations: Claymont, DE, USA; Bengaluru, KA, India; Mumbai, MH, India; Remote
regions: United States of America; India; America / Canada; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Crypto institutions, hedge funds, DeFi protocols and retail traders wanting on-chain options and derivatives
problem: Derivatives trading has many intermediaries and crypto derivatives are centralized; EthosX aims to run the full derivatives lifecycle on-chain without exchanges or clearing banks.
business_model: Protocol and trading platform fees on options and perpetual options (OPerps), institutional OTC platform and infrastructure for other crypto companies
product_category: DeFi derivatives protocol, on-chain options
market_need_then: Crypto options volume was concentrated on centralized venues and on-chain options had small TVL; the founders cite centralization risk after 2022 failures.
outcome_analysis: EthosX entered YC in Summer 2022 with an on-chain derivatives protocol during a crypto bear market. It raised a reported $1.8M in December 2023 and launched perpetual options (OPerps) in 2024, but a search summary showed zero TVL on DeFiLlama at the time of the snapshot. The company is listed active; no exit or shutdown found, and traction looks limited.

name: Eugit Therapeutics

long_description:
Eugit Therapeutics targets the issue of non-specific drugs that cause toxicity and clinical trial failures, affecting millions with tissue-specific inflammatory diseases. Our initial focus is on the 3.1 million U.S. individuals with Inflammatory Bowel Disease, aiming to initiate clinical trials within two years.

Cofounded by George Church (Harvard) and funded by Y Combinator (S22).
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; South San Francisco, CA, USA

name: Eventual
one_liner: Building the AI data engine for any modality and scale
long_description:
Every breakthrough AI application, from foundation models to autonomous vehicles, relies on processing massive volumes of images, video, and complex data. But today’s data platforms (like Databricks and Snowflake) are built on top of tools made for spreadsheet-like analytics, not the petabytes of multimodal data that power AI. As a result, teams waste months on brittle infrastructure instead of conducting research and building their core product.

Eventual was founded in 2022 to solve this. Our mission is to make querying any kind of data, images, video, audio, text, as intuitive as working with tables, and powerful enough to scale to production workloads. Our open-source engine, Daft, is purpose-built for real-world AI systems: coordinating with external APIs, managing GPU clusters, and handling failures that traditional engines can’t. Daft already powers critical workloads at companies like Amazon, Mobileye, Together AI, and CloudKitchens.

We’ve assembled a world-class team from Databricks, AWS, Nvidia, Pinecone, GitHub Copilot, Tesla, and more, quadrupling our size within a year. With backing from Y Combinator, Caffeinated Capital, Array.vc, and top angels from the co-founders of Databricks and Perplexity, we’re looking to double the team now. Join us—Eventual is just getting started.

Please note we are looking for someone who is willing and able to come into our San Francisco office in the Mission district 4 days / week.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: ML and data engineering teams at AI companies, robotics and autonomous vehicle firms processing images, video, audio and text at scale
problem: Data platforms like Databricks and Snowflake were built for tabular analytics, so teams waste months on brittle infrastructure for petabytes of multimodal data.
business_model: Open source engine (Daft, Apache 2.0) with a commercial cloud platform (Eventual Cloud waitlist opened June 2025)
product_category: Multimodal data processing engine and distributed dataframe
market_need_then: AI workloads in 2022 moved toward images, video and embeddings, which tabular data platforms handled poorly. The founders hit this problem at Lyft Level 5 (TechCrunch coverage 2025).
outcome_analysis: Eventual built Daft as open source and let usage lead, with customers like Amazon and Together AI named by 2025. It raised a $7.5M seed led by CRV and a $20M Series A led by Felicis in June 2025, about three years after YC. The multimodal AI data wave and the founders' autonomous vehicle data background fit the timing.

name: Fini

name: Finku

Our help to others includes:

regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Lenders, banks and fintechs in Southeast Asia, later any document-heavy regulated business
problem: Lenders review bank statements and loan documents by hand, which is slow and lets fraud through. Fintelite extracts and checks the data automatically.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for document extraction and analysis, plus AI consulting
product_category: AI document processing for lending
market_need_then: Southeast Asian digital lenders were scaling loan approvals and fraud checks on bank statements; Fintelite's site cites customers such as KoinWorks speeding loan processing about 10x.
outcome_analysis: Fintelite is active with about 20 staff and a customer list of regional banks and fintechs, but no priced round after a 2021 pre-seed of the sibling Sribuu was found. Public funding data is thin and aggregator figures conflict, so its trajectory is unclear. It appears to be a bootstrapped or lightly funded B2B tool that has broadened from lending to general document AI.

name: Firecrawl
one_liner: Building the library for superintelligence.
long_description:
Supercharge your AI agents with data from the web and beyond. Building the library for superintelligence. 🔥

Search and scrape the web, then access more sources through Alexandria’s library of data providers and specialized indexes. With more data to draw from, your AI agents can dig deeper and find answers that would otherwise stay out of reach. Use Firecrawl through your AI tools or build with our web data API.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents and LLM apps that need clean web data
problem: AI applications need reliable, LLM-ready data from websites, but scraping, rendering and cleaning the web is brittle infrastructure.
business_model: Usage-based API with open-source self-hosting (AGPL) and a managed cloud
product_category: Web data API for AI (search, scrape, crawl)
founder_names: Caleb Peffer; Eric Ciarla; Nicolas Silberstein Camara
market_need_then: At the 2022 batch the product was Mendable, an embeddable chat search for developer docs; demand came from the GPT-3 era and developer experience teams. The scraping need emerged later from Mendable's own data ingestion problems.
outcome_analysis: Firecrawl is an example of a successful pivot. The YC batch product, Mendable, was an AI docs chat tool used by Snapchat, MongoDB and DoorDash. The team turned its internal scraper into an open-source API, grew to hundreds of thousands of developers, raised a $14.5M Series A in August 2025 and a $75M Series B in September 2026. Open-source virality and the AI agent boom drove growth.

name: Firezone
tags: DevSecOps; Next-gen Network Security; B2B; Security; Open Source
one_liner: Reach any device, network, or SaaS app without opening firewall ports
long_description:
Firezone connects your workforce to the computing resources they need, wherever they are, securely. Unlike traditional VPNs, Firezone uses a least-privileged approach to access control known as Zero Trust Access.

Connect your identity provider and define granular policies in minutes, then rejoice in the IT support requests you won't receive due to our lightweight, WireGuard-powered clients which work great on all platforms.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: IT and security teams of companies of any size that want a VPN replacement with zero trust access
problem: Traditional VPNs are hard to set up and give broad network access. Firezone offers WireGuard-based, least-privilege access tied to identity providers.
business_model: Open-source (Apache 2.0) with a paid managed cloud and self-hosted plans
product_category: Zero trust network access (ZTNA) and VPN alternative
market_need_then: Remote work made VPN sprawl and firewall exposure a pain for IT teams; the open-source Firezone repo started as a self-hosted WireGuard VPN server and its first release was announced on Hacker News per the company timeline.
outcome_analysis: Firezone is an active open-source ZTNA company. Its seed round after YC is confirmed by the company timeline but the amount is not public in a reliable source; aggregators give $125K to $500K and one unreliable total of $12M. No Series A was found. It competes against far better funded Tailscale and Cloudflare. The story is a small open-source team with unproven commercial traction.

name: Flagright
one_liner: AI-native AML compliance platform for fintechs & banks
long_description: Flagright helps fintechs & banks monitor, screen, investigate, and report their transactions & customers against financial crime risks with a best-in-class AML compliance software. Catering to a diverse clientele across various financial sectors, we serve customers across 6 continents. Flagright is a pioneer in the application of generative AI for AML compliance operations with its AI suite, Flagright AI, delivering unmatched scalability and extreme performance. Our products are designed to help our customers scale volume without scaling headcount and grow faster.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Fintechs, banks, payment processors and other regulated firms that need AML and financial crime compliance
problem: Startups and banks need transaction monitoring and AML case management but legacy tools are costly and slow to integrate. Flagright started as an API-first, usage-priced transaction monitoring tool.

product_category: AML compliance and transaction monitoring software

outcome_analysis: Flagright raised a $2.8M pre-seed in July 2022, a $4.3M seed in 2025 and a $12.5M Series A in June 2026, and grew to about 58 staff and a claimed 100+ customers. Funding came slowly for three years after YC, but the shift from a startup-focused API to a full AML suite with AI agents widened its market. Competition from Unit21 and Sardine remains heavy.

name: Flair Labs

long_description: Flair Labs is the leading AI communications platform for lending, empowering teams to build autonomous agents that execute complex workflows across voice and text. Its early concierge pitch was repositioned as voice AI digital workers for mortgage teams as voice models improved, with a claimed West Capital Lending deployment of 44,194 leads. Public traction data is limited to its own press release and trade coverage.

outcome_analysis: FlatX is a two person company from the founders of Shelf, also YC S22, building a broker-free flatmate and rental marketplace in Bengaluru. No public funding, exit or shutdown was found, and the YC page lists it as active with two people. The site says it launched in 2025, so traction is early and unproven.

name: Fleek

name: FlowDeploy
tags: Developer Tools; Drug discovery; Data Engineering
one_liner: Bioinformatics pipelines in the cloud
long_description:
FlowDeploy helps bioinformaticians manage their data analysis pipelines. We provide everything they need to try, run, develop, and share their pipelines. That includes integrations with AWS, Snakemake, Nextflow, GitHub, Slack, SSO, and more, as well as a clean API and web app for launching and monitoring pipelines and managing their data.

FlowDeploy is built for bioinformaticians: it doesn't restrict how pipelines are built and managed, as long as a bioinformatics workflow manager like Nextflow or Snakemake is used. But it does eliminate several footguns like idle spend and accidental data egress, and it reduces the potential for users accidentally sharing credentials.

FlowDeploy runs the pipelines in either our managed cloud or the customer's cloud – eliminating the need to transfer data externally.

Non-computational biologists can use FlowDeploy, too: features like pipelines templates decrease the complexity to launch a new pipeline, which reduces user error and decreases the need for advanced cloud training for non-computational users.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Mountain View, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: FlyCode
one_liner: Recover failed subscription payments to increase retention and LTV
long_description:
FlyCode helps subscription merchants maximize revenue. We reduce involuntary churn by managing payment failures intelligently.

We’re Jake, Etai, and Tzachi and we’re building FlyCode.

TL;DR: If you sell SaaS or B2C subscriptions, we’re here to help you recover lost revenue due to failed payments and involuntary churn.

‘Involuntary’ or ‘Passive’ churn is a hidden Revenue Killer 💳 for Subscription Businesses

❌ THE PROBLEM: Recovering Failed Payments is Complex
Involuntary churn refers to the loss of subscribers due to payment failures, not due to them actively canceling. While it is both possible and a worthwhile strategy to attempt to win back a customer during the cancellation process — involuntary churn is not intentional and in most cases, your customers aren’t even aware that their payment failed.

💰 Bottom line?
Effective payment optimization does reduce involuntary churn and will increase ARR by as much as 5-10%

FLYCODE SOLUTION 💡
FlyCode leverages ML and AI to provide Payment Optimization and smart payment retries to maximize subscription revenue and reduce churn. We apply a unique model tailored to each Merchant and their customers to ensure optimal results.

⚡️Automatically recover failed subscription payments and reduce passive churn

⚡️Use ML & AI based payment optimization to find the best time to charge your customers

⚡️ Improve customer experience by coordinating payment retries with customer emails/SMS

🛠️ We support OOTB + Custom Integrations for Merchants and White-Label for Platforms
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

business_model: Usage-based, charges on recovered revenue (per company site)
product_category: Failed payment recovery and dunning software
founder_names: Tzachi Davidovich; Etai Avrahami; Jake Vacovec
competitors_at_founding: Baremetrics Recover; Stripe Smart Retries; Churn Buster
market_need_then: The YC launch post cites 8 to 10 percent of ARR lost to payment failures; these are the company's own industry figures, unverified.
outcome_analysis: FlyCode is a three founder company from YC S22 selling failed payment recovery to subscription merchants and has expanded its product line to Recover, Reach, Retain and Agents, with a Stripe app launched in May 2026. No verified funding or exit was found, so its trajectory is unclear; it faces incumbents such as Stripe Smart Retries and older dunning tools.

name: Fogbender
one_liner: Customer support tool purpose-built for companies that sell APIs
long_description:
Fogbender helps B2B companies support customer teams: think Intercom meets Slack's shared channels.

Today, all customer software is explicitly or implicitly designed for helping individuals, not teams. This is forcing B2B companies - who sell products to teams, not individuals - to augment their default customer support platform (Zendesk, Intercom, Front, etc) with a second, "unofficial", system: Slack's shared channels.

This causes a number of operational and logistical difficulties for both vendors and their customers, resulting in added costs, inefficiencies, and lost opportunities.

With Fogbender, B2B vendors embed a team-to-team messaging widget directly on their customer dashboard, where all users belonging to an account can - with no additional authentication - 1) see a list of currently-open issues 2) participate in conversations with their own team and the vendor, and 3) search all historical discussions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B companies, especially API sellers, that support customer teams
problem: B2B vendors support teams, not individuals, and fall back on Slack shared channels alongside Zendesk or Intercom, creating cost and operational mess.
business_model: B2B SaaS embeddable team messaging widget for customer support
product_category: B2B customer support software
competitors_at_founding: Zendesk; Intercom; Front; Slack Connect shared channels
market_need_then: The YC description says B2B vendors were bolting Slack shared channels onto their support stack; no quantified demand evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Fogbender sold an embeddable team support widget for B2B vendors and went through YC W22 with six people. No verified funding round, exit or shutdown was found, so its progress is unknown; later Slack-native competitors suggest the wedge was real but crowded.

name: FoodCourt

long_description:
FoodCourt (CoKitchen) is Africa's leading virtual restaurant company. We've served over 350,000 meals in the last 12 months & our goal is to make good food and quick convenience goods more accessible across Africa, through virtual restaurants & dark stores.

Understanding the unique problems of the African on-demand/ food delivery market, we've taken a full-stack approach by controlling different areas of the value chain such as technology, production & delivery to give users a seamless & consistent experience while giving us unlimited flexibility for growth.

name: Fresh Factory

name: Gauss
one_liner: AI agent that helps consumers lower the cost of debt automatically

Gauss is building an AI credit agent that automatically lowers the cost of consumers’ debt.

The product connects to a user’s credit profile, continuously monitors balances and available offers, and executes refinances or restructurings when it can materially improve terms.

For credit card debt, Gauss can track and automatically pay off any expensive balance on connected cards from an instantly originated line of credit, saving users thousands of dollars on interest charges and helping them pay off faster.

target_customer: Government contractors (GovCon firms) that bid on federal work
problem: Contractors spend two to four weeks per proposal on manual drafting or consultants, which caps how many bids they can submit; GovDash automates capture, proposals and post award work.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a pilot offer for government contractors
product_category: AI proposal, capture and contract management software for GovCon
founder_names: Sean Doherty; Timothy Goltser; Curtis Mason
market_need_then: US government spends over 650B USD per year on contracted work, nearly all through formal RFPs; proposals take two to four weeks each (Northzone and company sources).
outcome_analysis: GovDash raised a 10M Series A in April 2024 and a 30M Series B in January 2026, and now has about 56 people. The company claims 16x revenue growth over the past year and top 100 contractor customers. Generative AI made proposal drafting a strong wedge in a large, document heavy government market, and the company expanded into capture and contract management.

name: Grai
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Analytics; Open Source; Data Engineering
one_liner: Open source version control for metadata
long_description: Grai is open source version control for metadata. We can determine how database changes will affect deployed machine learning models, apis, and dashboards because we understand how data relates across systems which don’t otherwise talk to each other.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; London, England, United Kingdom; St. Louis, MO, USA
regions: United States of America; United Kingdom; America / Canada; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Grey
one_liner: Banking services for remote workers and digital nomads
long_description: Grey provides US, EU, and UK accounts for remote workers in emerging markets. For the first time, western companies feel comfortable recruiting skilled workers from anywhere and Grey is making it easy for these workers to receive their salary, save in foreign currency, convert to local currency and spend.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; LA, Nigeria; Remote
regions: United States of America; Nigeria; America / Canada; Africa; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Remote workers, freelancers, creators and small businesses in emerging markets (initially Nigeria and Kenya) paid by foreign clients
problem: Workers in emerging markets struggle to receive foreign currency pay, hold it, and convert it to local currency; Grey provides USD, EUR and GBP accounts, conversion, cards and transfers.
business_model: Fees and foreign exchange spread on conversions and transfers, virtual cards, plus a business product (Grey Business)
product_category: Cross border payments and multi currency accounts
market_need_then: Remote work for foreign clients grew and Nigerians needed to convert foreign currency to naira; Grey started in July 2020 as an instant exchange service and had about 100,000 users by August 2022.
outcome_analysis: Grey began in 2020 as an instant exchange service for Nigerians, rebranded in February 2022 around foreign accounts, joined YC, and raised a 2M seed in August 2022 with about 100,000 users and 200 percent volume growth in 2022. A 2024 headline reports over 1 million users. Searches found no layoffs, shutdown or regulatory action, so it appears to have grown with the remote work and cross border payment wave.

name: Groundmail
one_liner: Email for your app and your agents
long_description: Groundmail is email for apps and the agents that build and run them. Send sign-in codes, password resets and receipts from IPs kept separate from marketing mail. Give an agent a real mailbox it can read and reply from. Your coding agent can set it all up through our API, SDKs, CLI or MCP server.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: At batch time: shippers and carriers of flatbed and open deck freight. Today: developers and AI agent builders needing email infrastructure
problem: Batch era company (EXO Freight): open deck freight was poorly served by general freight marketplaces. Current Groundmail: apps and agents need reliable transactional email and mailboxes.
business_model: Batch era: managed marketplace and brokerage taking a margin on loads, later managed transportation software. Current: usage and tiered subscription email API (free, 15 USD per month, 249 USD per month per company site)
product_category: Freight marketplace (as of batch); email infrastructure (current)
market_need_then: Open deck freight was described as about 20 percent of domestic truckload spend and under served because of higher insurance costs and exception handling (FreightWaves, Oct 2021).
outcome_analysis: The Winter 2022 company was EXO Freight, which raised a seed in October 2021 and a 15M Series A in May 2022, with 33 percent monthly revenue growth and 50 enterprise shippers. Later it closed an office, laid off 19 people, and shifted from unprofitable spot brokerage to managed transportation software. The YC listing now describes Groundmail, an email infrastructure startup with 3 people. Whether EXO was wound down is not confirmed, so unit economics and the failed spot market bet are the likely factors.

name: GrowthBook
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Analytics; Open Source
one_liner: Open source feature flagging and A/B testing
long_description:
GrowthBook is an open source platform to help companies make data-driven product decisions with feature flags and A/B tests.  

Existing SaaS solutions like LaunchDarkly require a company to send all of their data to them. This results in high costs, data compliance issues, and vendor lock-in.  As a result, many companies end up building their own platforms in-house, which can take thousands of hours of work and lots of headaches.  To solve this, GrowthBook uses a company's existing data infrastructure and business metrics.

We believe feature flags and experimentation are the right way to build products at scale and that they will become a standard part of the development process.  GrowthBook is well positioned to be a leader in this growing market.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product, engineering and data teams at software companies that want feature flags and A/B tests on their own data warehouse
problem: SaaS experimentation tools such as LaunchDarkly make companies send data to a vendor, adding cost, compliance issues and lock in, so many build in house; GrowthBook runs experiments on a company's existing data infrastructure.
business_model: Open source core with paid cloud and enterprise (self hosted or cloud) plans
product_category: Feature flagging and experimentation platform
market_need_then: Companies complained about sending data to LaunchDarkly style vendors and many built tools in house, costing thousands of hours (YC description of the problem).
outcome_analysis: GrowthBook began as an in house experimentation tool, was open sourced in 2021, and joined YC in Winter 2022 with experienced founders from Education.com. It grew through open source adoption, claims over 4,000 companies on its site, and raised a 22.6M Series A in mid 2025. No acquisition or layoffs were found.

name: Guardian Bio
one_liner: Dendritic cell-based platform for cancer therapy
long_description:
Your immune system is your body’s best weapon and defense against cancer. It is only when it is overcome that cancer develops into full blown disease. Dendritic cells sit at the helm of the immune system, directing and dictating immune responses. Data has shown dendritic cells are often dysfunctional in cancer patients, and that this dysfunction is a bottleneck for other therapies. 

Guardian Bio’s approach is focused on creating a dendritic cell-based product which drives anti-tumor activity through activating the killers of the immune system AND training them against multiple cancer targets. We take stem cells from cancer patients, turn them into specific therapeutic dendritic cells specially trained against that patient’s tumor, and re-introduce them back into the body. 

Our therapeutic dendritic cells revitalize the killers of the immune system and give them the kickstart they need to fight - and win - against cancer.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Oncology patients with late stage solid tumors, via future clinical partners and biopharma
problem: Dendritic cells are often dysfunctional in cancer patients and limit other immunotherapies. The company aimed to make patient specific therapeutic dendritic cells from stem cells to restore anti-tumor immunity.
business_model: Therapeutics development, pre-revenue, aiming at clinical milestones and partnerships
product_category: Cell therapy, dendritic cell oncology
market_need_then: Cell therapies for solid tumors remained an unmet need in 2022, and dendritic cell dysfunction is described by the company as a bottleneck for other immunotherapies.
outcome_analysis: Guardian Bio was a two founder dendritic cell therapy startup in YC Summer 2022 that raised a small pre-seed with Brazen Capital and other backers and went through Creative Destruction Lab. A 2024 BIO listing said it was seeking a 3M seed round, and a directory says the founders put it into hibernation in November 2024, which suggests it could not raise the capital that cell therapy development needs. This is based on a single third party note and the cause is not public.

name: Gullak Money
one_liner: Gullak automates savings & invests these in gold
long_description:
Gullak is a mobile app that automates savings & invests these in Gold. We launched in India 60 days ago and have grown from 0 to 40k transacting users and hit a monthly GTV of $280K already. We are growing 25% week on week.

India is a nation of savers but the way the majority of India saves is non-smart & does not create wealth. There are 200 Mn Indians who save manually in bank deposits, the returns from these instruments do not even beat India's inflation. 

Gold is an instrument that India loves - 30Bn worth gold is purchased in India every year by middle income households. Gold has great cultural significance in India & there is high familiarity with the asset class. Despite gold being a familiar asset class & giving 5% higher returns than bank deposits, 200 Mn Indians still save manually in these non wealth creating bank deposits. This is largely because the ways to save in Gold required painful discrete activities such as manually accumulating money to buy gold, going to offline stores to buy this gold, incurring storage charges & more. The minimum ticket size for purchasing gold at these stores is $50 adding to more friction to saving in Gold.

Using automated savings, Gullak now makes it extremely easy for users to save small amounts regularly($1/day) in digital Gold.This was not possible a year ago because the underlying infrastructure(UPI Autopay) was missing. 

With 50 Mn Indians saving $2/day & with gold backed lending, this is a $1.5Bn market opportunity.

Gullak’s Founding team is the team which built BHIM UPI App(10Mn Downloads in 10 Days), this was launched by the PM of India. We built large scale payment systems for partners like GooglePay / Amazon, processing more than 30Mn payments/day. This is the same team that has built more than 40+ consumer brands & their initial growth strategy.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Middle income Indian savers who buy gold
problem: Indians love gold but buying it requires lump sums, store visits and storage; most savers use low return bank deposits.
business_model: Upfront margin per transaction on digital gold bought via UPI Autopay, plus jeweller partnerships
product_category: Fintech, micro-savings into digital gold
founder_names: Dilip Jain; Manthan Shah; Naimisha Rao
market_need_then: The company cites 200 million Indians saving manually in bank deposits, about 30B dollars of gold bought yearly by middle income households, and fast early uptake (40k transacting users in 60 days per the YC profile).
outcome_analysis: Gullak launched in India with fast early growth in automated gold savings, then raised a pre-seed in 2022, a seed in 2023 and a Series A in 2025 from Better Capital, Stellaris, YC, Chiratae and others. Founders with UPI and payments product experience fit the problem, and the company is still operating. The main risks are that gold and payments are supplied by partners and that Jar and payment apps compete in the same segment.

name: Gym Class
tags: Virtual Reality; Consumer; Gaming; Social; AI
one_liner: Connecting the world by simulating it
long_description: Gym Class is a social platform where you can play games, make friends, and create and share your own experiences. Join a community of millions across virtual reality and mobile.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers, mainly teens and young adults on Meta Quest, plus licensing partners such as sports leagues
problem: Social VR needed a sports-first game that people actually want to play together; the company started as a social basketball game on Meta Quest and grew into a broader social games platform.
business_model: Free to play VR and mobile social platform monetized by in-app purchases, passes and league licensed content
product_category: Social VR gaming platform
founder_names: Justin Hubert; Paul Katsen; Matthew Harris
market_need_then: Meta Quest 2 headset sales and social VR growth in 2021 and 2022 created a user base seeking multiplayer games; the demand evidence is the headset base, not a stated customer pain.
outcome_analysis: Gym Class began as a social basketball game on Meta Quest, raised an 8M seed from a16z in August 2022, and expanded to more sports, NBA and MLB licenses and a 2026 mobile launch. It is still active with about 20 people. Strong Quest ratings suggest product market fit, while dependence on the Meta platform and a small VR market remain the main risks. No later round was found.

name: HOAi
one_liner: AI agent for community management
long_description: HOAi (acquired by Vantaca in Fall 2024) is a fast-growing startup revolutionizing the community association management industry. Our AI workforce platform integrates machine learning technology to streamline labor-heavy processes, eliminating inefficiencies and driving scalability. With rapid growth in the AI space, we are pushing boundaries to redefine industry standards.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Community association (HOA) management companies
problem: Community managers spend large amounts of labor on routine tasks such as onboarding, board packets and month end financials.
business_model: B2B SaaS and AI agent subscriptions sold to management companies
product_category: AI agents for community association management
market_need_then: Management companies were labor heavy, which is the company's own framing. No dated third party demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: HOAi built AI agents for HOA management companies in a niche where the dominant platform was a natural buyer. Vantaca acquired it in November 2024 and kept HOAi as an independent product, and by 2026 the HOAi brand anchored Vantaca's AI offering. Terms, customer counts and funding are not public, so the strength of the company's own traction is unknown.

name: HOKALI
one_liner: After School & Enrichment Activities Marketplace
long_description: HOKALI is the marketplace for buying after-school programs and enrichment activities with high-quality, vetted vendors in the US. We simplify the process of booking, organizing, and managing after-school programs and camps for schools.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: US K-12 schools and districts that buy after-school and enrichment programs, originally parents booking lessons
problem: Schools and parents struggle to find, vet and manage enrichment instructors and activities; HOKALI supplies staffed programs and a platform for enrollment, payments and attendance.
business_model: B2B program delivery and marketplace commissions on bookings, plus management software for schools
product_category: Edtech marketplace, after-school enrichment
market_need_then: Schools reopening after the pandemic needed enrichment and aftercare providers; the sources give no spend figures, so demand evidence is limited to the company's growth claims (240+ to 1,099 school and district partners, sources disagree).
outcome_analysis: HOKALI started as a consumer marketplace for lessons and shifted to selling onsite enrichment and aftercare to schools and districts, which the company says has grown to hundreds of partner schools. It is still active with 12 people, but funding is only visible through aggregators, so how well capitalized it is remains unknown. The B2B shift and school relationships are the main positives; the commodity nature of booking software is the risk.

name: HOMLI
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: Sell your home without brokers
long_description: HOMLI is building the first fully autonomous real estate broker, enabling homeowners to sell without agents.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Homeowners in Greece (initially framed as Europe) selling, renting or buying property
problem: Real estate brokerage has very low consumer satisfaction in Europe per the launch post; HOMLI offers data driven valuation and a tech enabled brokerage, using its own capital to speed sales.
business_model: Brokerage commissions plus principal investment in properties, with free valuation tools as lead generation
product_category: Proptech, tech enabled real estate brokerage
founder_names: Antonis Mitropoulos; Tim Ioannidis; Nikos Legbelos
market_need_then: The founders cite the lowest consumer satisfaction of any industry for brokerage in Europe; Greek press in October 2022 describes demand for faster sales, but these are company claims.
outcome_analysis: HOMLI is a Greek focused tech enabled brokerage founded by three MIT trained Greek founders and entered the Greek market in 2022 with press coverage. It is active with about 20 staff, offices in Athens and Thessaloniki and a recently sold listings page. Funding is only in aggregators and the amounts conflict, so capital strength is unknown.

name: Happl
one_liner: Your personalised benefits and engagement platform for global teams
long_description:
Happl - Personalised benefits for employees to choose what’s right for them, and tools for managers to engage their teams, whilst we take care of all the compliance and admin.

Founded in 2020 and based in London, UK, Happl works with some of the UK’s leading employers to bring their hybrid working culture to life!

https://www.happl.com/
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: UK employers with hybrid teams, later multinational employers needing global benefits
problem: Employers struggle to give staff personalised benefits and recognition and to run compliance and admin across countries.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for employee benefits and engagement platform
product_category: Employee benefits and engagement platform
market_need_then: Hybrid work after 2020 raised demand for engagement and flexible benefits per the YC description; no hard spend or complaint data found.
outcome_analysis: Happl is active, grew from 11 staff at the W22 batch to an $11M Series A in May 2026 led by Portage with YC and others returning, after a small seed. It repositioned from UK hybrid-team perks to global benefits infrastructure and AI. Progress looks slow for a YC company (Series A about four years after the batch), and early revenue and traction are not public, so the record does not support strong claims about why it worked.

name: Hedgehog
tags: Robotics; Climate; Food Tech; Agriculture; AI
one_liner: Building robotic mushroom farms
long_description:
Hedgehog builds robotic mushroom farms. Our robots eliminate labor and our AI optimizes grow conditions to increase yield. We’ll soon grow mushrooms and fungi for <1/3rd the cost of leading growers. 

Fungi may address our food system’s biggest problems: they transform agricultural waste into protein-rich foods with near-zero environmental impact. Hedgehog’s technology is unleashing fungi as our next major food source.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mushroom buyers (food distributors and retailers); the company itself grows and sells mushrooms
problem: Mushroom farming is labor-intensive; the founders claim robots and AI can cut cost by 70% or more.
business_model: Vertically integrated grower selling mushrooms and fungi, using proprietary robotic farms
product_category: Agtech robotics / indoor mushroom farming
market_need_then: Founders' stated pain: labor costs and fungi as a protein source; no dated demand evidence (customers, orders) found in sources.
outcome_analysis: Hedgehog, founded in 2022 and in YC S22, raised about $4M of seed funding and, per aggregator listings, a Series A in 2024, and is Active with a 50-person team. As of April 2024 it was testing machinery in an R&D space and planning a first commercial farm within 12 months, so there is no verified commercial traction yet; the story is still open and success or failure cannot be judged from public sources.

name: Heptabase
one_liner: An AI visual knowledge base to understand and create knowledge.
long_description: Heptabase is an intelligent, visual knowledge base to understand and create knowledge. It is backed by Y Combinator, HOF Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Moving Capital, Tonic Fund, and other investors, including the founders of Socialcam, Triplebyte, Codementor, and more.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Students, researchers, knowledge workers and creators who learn from many sources
problem: Linear note apps make it hard to understand and connect complex material; Heptabase offers whiteboards of cards to build understanding visually.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer SaaS subscription with a 7 day trial
product_category: Visual note-taking and knowledge base software
founder_names: Alan Chan; Yeefun Lin; Ethan Wu
market_need_then: Note-taking and tools for thought drew heavy investor interest by 2020, shown by the 9M seed for Roam Research, and Heptabase's early community grew to about 6000 members in 82 countries by March 2023.
outcome_analysis: Heptabase grew a loyal visual note-taking user base, joined YC W22 and raised a 1.7M seed from YC, Kleiner Perkins and others, then kept a small team while adding AI and mobile apps. It is active in 2026. Revenue and user numbers in third party profiles conflict, so scale is uncertain, but there is no sign of distress.

name: Heyfood
one_liner: Doordash for Africa
long_description:
Heyfood is building the “Doordash for Africa”.  But unlike Doordash in America, we make a profit on every single delivery, from day 1. 

We are targeting Millennials and Gen Z urban professionals in Africa’s top 70 cities, withing 10 years there will be 140m number of these people, we assume they will want to order food once a week, we make $1 per delivery, this represents a $51B market.
regions: Nigeria; Africa
target_customer: Urban millennial and Gen Z consumers in Nigerian cities outside Lagos, plus restaurants that use its ordering software
problem: Restaurants in secondary Nigerian cities were underserved by delivery platforms; Heyfood delivers meals and sells restaurants ordering and delivery software.
business_model: Marketplace delivery fees and commissions, plus SaaS for restaurants
product_category: Food delivery marketplace, Africa
market_need_then: Nigeria had millions of young urban professionals and active delivery platforms in Lagos; the company projects a 51B market but that is its own claim.
outcome_analysis: Heyfood focused on Ibadan and other cities outside contested Lagos, raised a seed from YC, Voltron, Goodwater and Ventures Platform, and was expanding to Abuja and Benin in 2024 with about 40 staff. Jumia Food and Bolt Food exited Nigeria in December 2023, which helped. Funding size is unverified, so capital strength is unknown.

name: HippoBuild
one_liner: The Operating System of the construction industry
long_description:
Hippo Build is building the Operating System for the Construction industry.   
We automate and optimize back office functions and the supply chain of Small and Medium Construction Companies. We save our customers hours everyday, and 1000’s of dollars every month on better sourced materials. And it takes only minutes for them to onboard

We charge a small SaaS fee, + 1% transaction fee for the materials sourced. We are integrated with multiple marketplaces and providers, letting us automatically source better priced materials. This allows us to stay affordable for the SMB, whilst earning $20-100K per company.
regions: Colombia; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and medium construction companies in Latin America, starting in Colombia
problem: Small contractors overpay for materials and run back office work on spreadsheets; HippoBuild pools demand to buy from large manufacturers and provides an ERP and financing options.
business_model: Small SaaS fee plus a 1% transaction fee on materials sourced (company says 20K to 100K dollars per customer)
product_category: Construction ERP and materials procurement marketplace
market_need_then: The company claims small contractors lack IT tools and overpay for materials; Construction Dive reported record contech funding in 2021 but no source here quantifies LatAm SME spend.
outcome_analysis: HippoBuild is a five person Bogota based startup selling construction ERP software and pooled materials purchasing to small contractors, listed Active in the YC directory. Funding figures are aggregator only and conflict, and no revenue or customer count was found, so there is not enough public evidence to say whether it is succeeding or stalled.

name: HomeRoom
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
tags: Machine Learning; Real Estate; Proptech; NLP; Data Engineering
one_liner: We Rent Your Property by the Room.  You earn 50% more Rent.
long_description:
Homeroom helps investors provide affordable housing while making a 22% ROI.

We do this by sourcing properties, arranging capital, managing construction, vetting tenants and collecting rent by the room. To date, Homeroom has brought on 85 property investors, growing 6X annually, are bringing in 420K in annualized net-revenue

How it works:
We help investors buy homes in cities that are attractive to young people, but lack affordable housing options.  We then renovate and after about 20 days, the home is ready and we find qualified renters by the room.

We launched in 2018 in Kansas City with 1 home. We now have 105 homes in 31 cities. In 2021, we grew rental GMV to $1.8M (300% YoY growth). Our average rent across every property is $458, which is about 50% lower than market comps, and our investors see returns up to 50% higher.

We are HomeRoom. Johnny is the financial analyst/domain expert. Thomas is a cereal entrepreneur with a PHD in ML, and Mike hacked growth for Airbnb and Facebook.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; San Jose, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Real estate investors who buy single family homes and want higher rent, plus renters who want a cheap room
problem: Affordable housing is scarce in young person cities, and investors earn less renting a whole house than renting by the room.
business_model: Master lease with guaranteed rent to the investor; HomeRoom keeps about 15 percent of collections (per Dealroom)
product_category: Co-living and rent by the room property management
founder_names: Johnny Wolff; Thomas Hornbeck; Mike Tich
market_need_then: The company reported 105 homes in 31 cities, 1.8M USD rental GMV in 2021 (300 percent YoY) and rents about 50 percent below market comps; all self reported on its YC page.
outcome_analysis: HomeRoom grew a rent by the room model from one Kansas City home in 2018 to 105 homes by 2021, raised a 1M USD pre-seed around YC W22 and a further seed in March 2022, then was acquired by Bungalow. The deal price and exact date are not public, so it is unclear whether it was a strong exit or a soft landing.

name: Housewarming
one_liner: Share casual moments with the people you care about
long_description:
Housewarming is social media and AI designed to bring you closer to your friends, not replace them or keep you isolated in an algorithm.

We've been building mega-viral consumer AI experiences since 2020. From the music discovery app Discz (1.5M users) to creative expression with Verse & Internet Bedroom (0-10 million users in 30 days, one of the fastest growing products of all-time) we like building at the frontier of technology in ways consumer truly love.

Housewarming is our latest and most delightful product ever. Check it out, share moments with your friends, and let us know what you think :)
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers, mainly young people who want to share casual moments with close friends
problem: Mainstream social media is driven by algorithms and polished posting; people want a low-pressure way to keep up with close friends.
business_model: Consumer app, no revenue model found
product_category: Consumer social app with AI features
market_need_then: Public evidence of demand in 2022 is thin for this specific product; the team's earlier apps Discz and Verse reported large user counts, which suggests consumer appetite for their creative products.
outcome_analysis: Housewarming is still active after the W22 batch with a four person team. The founders have a record of building viral consumer apps (Discz, Verse, Internet Bedroom), which is the main asset, but no funding round, revenue or exit is verifiable. The story so far is serial consumer experimentation rather than a clear breakout, and the product has moved from creative tools to a close-friends social app.

name: Hubble Network
tags: Developer Tools; Hard Tech; Hardware; IoT; Satellites
one_liner: Bluetooth to Space
long_description: Hubble is building a global satellite network that any Bluetooth-enabled device can connect to, even without cellular reception.  Our mission in life is to get a billion devices connected to the network and unlock a new era of human-machine collaboration.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Device makers and IoT operators that want connectivity for Bluetooth chips without cellular
problem: Low-power devices lose connection outside cellular and gateway range; Hubble lets standard Bluetooth chips connect to satellites after a firmware update.
business_model: Connectivity service with free sandbox and paid usage tiers, plus full-service deployment
product_category: Satellite IoT connectivity
founder_names: Alex Haro; Ben Wild; John Kim
market_need_then: Billions of Bluetooth devices exist, but trackers and asset tags depend on phones or gateways nearby; cellular IoT needs special modems and subscriptions.
outcome_analysis: Hubble remains active and has raised repeatedly, with a $20M Series A in 2023 and a $70M Series B in September 2025. Success so far rests on a hard technical result, connecting off-the-shelf Bluetooth chips to satellites, and founders with wireless and consumer-scale experience from Amazon Sidewalk and Life360. The risk is capital intensity: constellation build-out continues to 2028 and requires further raises.

name: Humand
tags: Generative AI; SaaS; B2B; Productivity; AI
one_liner: All-in-one app for internal communication and HR
long_description:
Humand transforms how companies digitize their internal communication, culture, and HR processes within one user-friendly app. As a result, Humand provides every company with a digital Community to centralize every company-employee interaction.

Humand's digital Communities are powerful, customizable and easily adapt to the needs of every company, no matter the industry, size or region. Companies that implement Humand benefit from the following suite of Mini Apps, which are getting smarter thanks to the power of AI:

+ Forms & Smart Workflows 📋
+ Internal Social Network ❤️
+ Chat 💬
+ Time Off 🏝
+ Magazine 📰
+ Surveys 📊
+ Smart Intranet 📲
+ Kudos 👏🏻
+ Learning 📚
+ Onboarding 🎉
+ Org chart 👥
+ Company Files and Employee Documents 📂
+ Perks & Benefits 🥂
+ Birthdays & Work Anniversaries 🥳
+ Employee Development 🥇
+ Electronic Signature ✍🏻
+ Smart Tickets 📧
+ Marketplace 🛍
+ Calendar & Events 📆
+ Agenda 🔎
+ Integrations 🔗

More than 1,000 companies use Humand. Implemented by ArcelorMittal (biggest steel producer in the world), Tenaris (global leader in steel pipes production), NSG group (among the biggest glass producers in the world), and many other organizations across different countries.

Humand enables all workers, particularly those without direct access to a computer at their desks, to stay connected with their company anywhere, anytime. Humand enhances internal communication speed, streamline information flow between collaborators, and enable instant, targeted reach to all employees with push notifications tailored to their needs.

Companies that adopt a digital Community powered by Humand experience an enriched work environment, heightened employee camaraderie, and a surge in productivity, all contributing to a thriving and connected workforce.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Large employers with frontline, deskless workers, mainly in Latin America
problem: Companies cannot reach operational workers who have no desk or email; internal communication and HR processes are fragmented.
business_model: B2B SaaS per employee
product_category: Employee app for internal communication and HR
market_need_then: Frontline workers are about 80 percent of the workforce per a 2026 outlet, yet most software targets desk workers; the founders first sold to an industrial plant (ArcelorMittal Acindar) after a request for better internal communication.
outcome_analysis: Humand reports more than 2,500 customers and about 2 million employees on its own site, and in February 2026 raised a $66M Series A described by outlets as a regional record. The company grew mostly through enterprise sales to frontline-heavy employers in Latin America after the 2022 YC batch, and the large round came years after the batch.

name: Hydra
tags: Developer Tools; Analytics; Open Source; Data Engineering
one_liner: Serverless Analytics on Postgres
long_description:
Hydra is a real-time analytics database management system for Postgres. We seperate compute from storage to offer software engineers serverless analytics with autoscale, write isolation, automatic caching, and more.

Shipping scalable projects on time series and event data has never been easier. Hydra is available for local development, cloud, and bare metal deployment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software engineers and data teams who run Postgres and need analytics on event and time series data
problem: Analytics queries on row based Postgres are slow, forcing teams to stand up a separate warehouse.
business_model: Open source Postgres extensions with a hosted serverless analytics cloud
product_category: Analytics database on Postgres
market_need_then: Postgres was already widely adopted by developers, and the founders chose it as a base for that reason, but dated demand evidence is thin.
outcome_analysis: Hydra raised a 3.1 million seed after Demo Day and built open source columnar Postgres, later co-developing the pg_duckdb extension with DuckDB Labs, which also took a stake in 2024. Supabase announced in February 2026 that the team was joining to lead its Open Warehouse Architecture work. Terms were undisclosed, and one community comment called the older columnar extension abandoned, so the exit looks like a team and maintainership move rather than a revenue story.

name: HypaHub
one_liner: A Cloud-Based Bioinformatics and AI Platform
long_description:
HypaHub is a Cloud-Based Bioinformatics and AI Platform. It is the first HIPAA-compliant Bioinformatics SaaS that runs natively on users' clouds, providing both operation- and price-transparency. 

Our product is a one-stop shop to access complex technologies designed for scientists building data applications or performing data analytics to extract insights. It automates the creation and manages the operation of computing resources, eliminating the need for enterprises to set up and maintain a high-end R&D cloud infrastructure.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Sunnyvale, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Biotech, diagnostics and pharma teams running bioinformatics and multiomic analysis who need HIPAA compliant cloud tooling
problem: Genomics tools and algorithms are hard to access and costly to operate, so scientists lose time standing up and managing compute for analysis.
business_model: B2B SaaS running in the customer's own cloud with usage transparent pricing
product_category: Cloud bioinformatics and AI platform
market_need_then: The YC launch post cites high cost and access barriers in genomics for diagnostics and pharma, with testimonials from small biotech users. No spend data found.
outcome_analysis: HypaHub sold a HIPAA compliant bioinformatics platform to small biotech teams but was a six person company against established platforms. The company's site now says it no longer offers products as an independent company and that its IP was acquired by GaudiBio, while PitchBook marks it out of business in November 2025. The cause of the wind down is not public, and no funding beyond accelerator money was verified.

name: Hype
one_liner: Trade memecoins
long_description:
Trade memecoins, crypto and send crypto to your friends
Download Hype here: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hype-trade-memes/id6477802830
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Retail crypto traders, mostly young mobile users interested in memecoins
problem: Trading and sending memecoins across chains is fragmented across wallets and exchanges.
business_model: Trading fees on a mobile and web trading app (not stated by sources)
product_category: Crypto trading app
market_need_then: Not documented for 2022; the product launched on the App Store in October 2024 per a newsletter, in a memecoin boom.
outcome_analysis: Hype is listed as Active with a team of three and shows an app on the App Store that rates 4.9 on its own site. No funding beyond YC, no revenue and no outside press about the company were found, so its traction is unknown. Competition was heavy from larger crypto apps and the name collides with other Hype brands.

name: HyperDX
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; B2B; Open Source; Infrastructure
one_liner: Open-source, dev-friendly observability.
long_description:
HyperDX assists engineers in resolving production bugs more quickly with simple workflows that take you from alert to resolution. You can get set up in a matter of minutes and correlate debug telemetry all in one place, including logs, metrics, traces, and browser session replays, allowing you to resolve issues faster than ever before.

HyperDX is open source and built on top of Clickhouse and S3, so customers can enjoy ten times the savings when compared to traditional vendors like Datadog.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams that want production debugging and observability at lower cost than Datadog
problem: Traditional observability vendors are expensive and split logs, metrics, traces and session replays across tools, slowing engineers who debug production issues.
business_model: Open core: MIT licensed open source plus a paid hosted cloud
product_category: Open source observability platform
market_need_then: Vendor cost was the stated driver, with the company claiming about ten times savings over Datadog. No dated third party spend data found.
outcome_analysis: HyperDX built open source observability on ClickHouse and won a following of developers and early customers such as Lovable, plus ClickHouse itself as a user. The database vendor acquired it in March 2025, framing it as an acceleration, with deal terms undisclosed. Funding is unverified, so how capital efficient the path was cannot be stated.

name: Hyperbeam
tags: Developer Tools; eLearning; Virtual Reality; API; Remote Work
one_liner: API for shared embeddable web browsers
long_description:
Emebedding third-party apps and websites can often be a nightmare due to incompatible platforms, security issues, and poor UX. Adding multiplayer functionality to these embeds makes this problem exponentially more difficult.

Enter Hyperbeam—an API that lets you embed virtual computers anywhere, including web, mobile, VR, and even VSCode. You can then open any third-party website or application, synchronize audio and video flawlessly among multiple participants, and add multi-user control with just a few lines of code. Uses cases and customer segments include remote learning, virtual offices, online casinos, productivity, watch parties and more.

We are three technical founders from the University of Waterloo, and worked as engineers at Facebook, Yahoo, and Lyft. Our technology is battle-tested–we currently stream over 1.25M hours of video per month across every continent. https://hyperbeam.com?ch=yc
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers who want to embed shared browsers or remote computers in apps; consumers for the watch party app
problem: Screen sharing is single player; developers need a cloud browser that many participants can control together.
business_model: Usage-based API per participant minute ($0.007 per minute per the site) plus consumer watch party product
product_category: Virtual computer and multiplayer browser API
founder_names: Philip Scott; Ambareesh Balaji; Declan Goncalves
market_need_then: Remote watching boomed during the pandemic; Hyperbeam's blog claims 1.5 million sign-ups and 150K monthly users for the watch party product, and Rabb.it's shutdown left a gap.
outcome_analysis: Hyperbeam grew from a Waterloo capstone watch party site into a developer API for embedded virtual computers and is still active. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is unclear: a 2022 company blog calls it bootstrapped, while aggregators list a $500K YC note, so the capital story is unresolved. The API faces newer well-funded cloud browser startups.

name: Hypestream
one_liner: We help livestream sellers get more sales.
long_description: We help livestream sellers get more sales.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Sellers on the Whatnot live shopping platform
problem: Livestream sellers spend time on buyer messages, refunds and reviews; Hypestream automates this to protect ratings and sales.
business_model: Freemium SaaS for sellers
product_category: Seller tools for livestream commerce
market_need_then: Not documented for 2022; the current product targets Whatnot sellers, a platform that grew strongly (Series E in January 2025, Series G in August 2026 per press).
outcome_analysis: Hypestream is listed as Active with a team of two and a product for Whatnot sellers. No funding, customers or exit were found. The YC listing has a founding year of 2025 against a 2022 batch, suggesting the current product came long after the batch, and its dependence on Whatnot makes it exposed to the platform.

name: IMT Care
one_liner: Disrupting Indian Insurance space by empowering distrubutors
long_description:
India’s insurance market is filled with bygone products, which do not cater to 95% of the market's demand for specific products such as illness-specific insurance, primary care with insurance, and surgical insurance to name a few. 

We, at IMT, aim to target this white space by creating innovative products that fulfill this new demand by empowering the agents. Agents are the largest insurance distribution channel in India and cover 85% of the premium collection. 

Agents collect 20B premium every year. With a 5% take rate, it’s a 1B dollar market opportunity growing at 22% CAGR.

Kunal has 15+ years of experience working with insurance companies and building agent networks, while he scaled his brokerage business to 3M dollars in revenue. Rachit has 12+ years of experience in building tech products, he was a founding engineer at Payu (stripe of India).
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Insurance agents, brokers and employers managing employee benefits in India
problem: Insurance intermediaries in India lack technology to sell and manage employee health and benefit policies.
business_model: B2B SaaS and distribution platform for insurance intermediaries
product_category: Insurtech and employee benefits
market_need_then: The YC page says agents are India's largest insurance distribution channel and many products are underserved; no dated data on spend was found.
outcome_analysis: IMT Care is listed as Active with a team of 23 and says it has an insurance technology platform for intermediaries. No funding beyond an unverified $500K YC note, no exit and no layoffs were found. Revenue figures online conflict and are unverified, so traction cannot be judged.

name: IOMETE
one_liner: Self-hosted data lakehouse platform
long_description: The IOMETE self-hosted data lakehouse platform unifies all data - regardless of where the data resides - enabling large-scale analytics (BI/ML/AI) on the entire data set. IOMETE runs always in the customer's environment, whether on premises, on public cloud or private cloud thereby maximizing data security, data privacy and data ownership while reducing cost.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Enterprises, financial institutions and government bodies wanting a data lakehouse inside their own environment
problem: Teams want large-scale analytics without sending data to SaaS platforms, and building lakehouse infrastructure in house is complex and costly.
business_model: Self-hosted software license plus forward-deployed engineering services
product_category: Data lakehouse platform
founder_names: Vusal Dadalov; Piet Jan de Bruin
market_need_then: Data privacy and sovereignty concerns plus cloud cost drove demand for self-hosted analytics; the company's own pitch stresses ownership and lower cost versus SaaS.
outcome_analysis: IOMETE has stayed independent and active since YC Winter 2022 with a self-hosted lakehouse aimed at regulated and sovereignty-minded buyers, a team of about 25 and public customer logos. Funding is small and poorly documented, so its stage is hard to judge, and the main risk is competition from large lakehouse vendors.

name: Illuminant Surgical
tags: Medical Robotics; Augmented Reality; Robotic Surgery; Medical Devices; Navigation
one_liner: A new way of seeing inside the human body.
long_description:
Illuminant Surgical is building a new way of seeing inside the human body.

Our breakthrough platform, Skylight™, is the first real-time anatomical projection system, displaying images directly on the patient to give doctors an x-ray vision view for safer interventions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Spine surgeons and interventional radiologists, bought by hospitals
problem: Traditional surgical navigation is costly, slow to set up and takes the surgeon's eyes off the patient; Skylight projects anatomy onto the patient.
business_model: Medical device capital equipment (pre-commercial, not FDA cleared per site)
product_category: Surgical navigation and projection
market_need_then: Spine navigation is an established category with large vendors; the company argues existing systems are costly and disruptive to workflow.
outcome_analysis: Illuminant Surgical is active and raised an $8.4M seed in April 2026, about half of it federal grants per Fortune, nearly four years after the S22 batch. That slow capital path is typical for device companies, where clearance and clinical validation come before sales. Its main risks are regulatory timing and well-resourced navigation incumbents.

name: Impossible Metals
tags: Hard Tech; Robotics; Mining; ClimateTech; AI
one_liner: Underwater robotic vehicles that collect  battery metals responsibly
long_description:
Impossible mining is building underwater robotics vehicles which collect battery metals from the seabed without harming the environment. We have $500M+ in off-take LoI’s and have signed a partnership with a global offshore logistics company which holds a seabed mining exploration permit. We have also built the 1st PoC underwater robotic arm.

Polymetallic nodules are rocks which are rich in critical battery metals. Specially nickel, cobalt, manganese and copper. These metals are the the most expensive part of EVs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Seabed mineral license holders, offshore logistics operators and battery metal off-takers (nickel, cobalt, manganese, copper) who want lower-impact nodule collection
problem: Polymetallic nodules on the seabed hold critical battery metals, but existing collector designs plow the seafloor and draw environmental opposition. The company proposes robots that pick individual nodules selectively.
business_model: Technology and collection services for seabed nodule mining, with off-take letters of intent and partner-held exploration permits
product_category: Autonomous underwater robotics for seabed mineral collection
founder_names: Oliver Gunasekara; Jason Gillham; Renee Grogan
competitors_at_founding: Global Sea Mineral Resources (DEME); Allseas with The Metals Company
market_need_then: Demand for nickel, cobalt and manganese for EV batteries, and rising objections to bulk seabed collection, created a niche for a selective approach; the company reported over $500M in off-take letters of intent on its YC page.
outcome_analysis: Impossible Metals is active. It raised a reported $10.1M seed in June 2022, built and tested successive Eureka robots, and in 2025 postponed a planned 2026 test and applied for a US lease off American Samoa, which drew opposition. The founders combine semiconductor deal experience, underwater imaging and permitting expertise. Commercial deep sea mining has not yet occurred anywhere, so the outcome rests on regulation and permits.

name: Impractical
tags: Generative AI; Sales; Sales Enablement; AI
one_liner: Your autonomous motion designer that turns every feature into a…
long_description:
Impractical is your team's autonomous motion designer - trained off of hours of motion design courses, examples - built to ship stunning videos while your team ships features. 

Instead of hiring an agency, getting a freelancer, or getting subpar results with claude code, Impractical can make superior videos faster, and for much less. 

Signup at motion.impractical.ai for free!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software and product teams that need launch videos, explainers and social clips without hiring an agency or freelancer
problem: Product teams want polished motion graphics for each feature release but agencies and freelancers are slow and costly, and general AI coding tools give weaker video results.
business_model: Self-serve AI motion design product with free signup; pricing not found
product_category: AI motion design and video generation for product marketing
market_need_then: In 2022 the founders targeted outbound sales automation, a large existing spend category; no source found with demand evidence specific to the company.
outcome_analysis: Impractical is still active with a two person team. The 2022 YC page focus was sales automation with generative AI, while the current site sells an autonomous motion designer, which suggests a change of focus though no source states a date or reason. No funding was found, so its trajectory cannot be judged from public data.

name: InVision Medical Technology
one_liner: AI Diagnosis of  Heart Disease
long_description: At InVision, we use AI to help streamline the interpretation of ultrasounds and identify diseases that may have been missed by human readers. Our models have been tightly integrated into the clinical workflow to allow easy usage by clinicians. Our work has previously been peer-reviewed and published in several top medical venues, including Nature (2020), Nature Medicine (2021), Lancet Digital Health (2021), JAMA Cardiology (2022). Results from our blinded and randomized clinical trial on evaluating cardiac function have also been recently presented as a Late Breaking Clinical Trial at the European Society of Cardiology.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hospitals, cardiology echo labs and ultrasound device or reporting software vendors that read heart ultrasounds
problem: Echocardiogram interpretation is variable and diseases such as cardiac amyloidosis are missed by human readers; the company packages peer reviewed AI models into the clinical workflow.
business_model: Clinical AI software licensed to health systems and imaging software partners; FDA cleared algorithms
product_category: AI diagnostics for cardiac ultrasound (medical device software)
market_need_then: Echo is a high volume test with reader variability, and several AI echo vendors had obtained FDA clearances by 2021, showing clinical and regulatory demand.
outcome_analysis: InVision is active and has turned its founders' published echo research into products: Precision LVEF (FDA 510(k) K232331) and Precision Cardiac Amyloid cleared on 2025-05-21 (K243866). A distribution partnership with HeartLab for Australia and New Zealand was announced on 2025-10-13. Funding is not publicly stated, so the financial trajectory is unknown.

name: Industrial Next
one_liner: IndustrialNext builds the AI brain for manufacturing –…
long_description:
We're building the brain for the factory floor, developing AI-driven robotic systems powered by a proprietary foundation model for the difficult, contact-rich manufacturing tasks where conventional automation falls short.

Founded by veterans of Tesla, Waymo, Ford, and GM who built the systems that brought modern autonomy into manufacturing, IndustrialNext is bringing that same intelligence to the factory floor: autonomous factories that are cost-competitive at any scale, anywhere.

Backed by Y Combinator, Khosla Ventures, Lenovo, AlphaX Partners, and Plug and Play.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Automakers, EV suppliers and electronics manufacturers that want flexible automation for contact-rich factory tasks
problem: Conventional factory automation is rigid and slow to reprogram, so tasks with product variation and contact stay manual. The company sells AI driven robotic work cells and smart factory equipment.
business_model: Modular equipment, custom software and follow-on service sold per production unit or per factory (2022); AI robotic work cells (current)
product_category: AI robotics and smart factory automation
market_need_then: EV makers were building new factories in 2022 and TechCrunch reported procurement talks with Rivian and Nio; Tesla's automated factory was the cited benchmark.
outcome_analysis: Industrial Next is active. It raised a reported $12M in June 2022 led by Lenovo, then a Khosla led Series A of tens of millions reported in April 2025, and announced a BMW evaluation partnership in October 2026. Its founders came from Tesla and Waymo factory and autonomy teams. Commercial deployment scale is undisclosed.

name: InferEdge
tags: Fintech; Finance; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: AI solutions for investment firms under a forward deployed model
long_description:
InferEdge provides agentic AI solutions to buy-side firms under an outcome-based, forward-deployed model. We build systems that fit customer workflows for research, portfolio analysis, risk and client servicing. Everything can be hosted inside a private cloud, and the system comes with citations, traceability and guardrails.

Our team has deep quantitative finance and technology experience, enabling us to deliver outcomes effectively.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Buy-side investment firms such as asset managers, hedge funds, wealth platforms and mutual funds
problem: Investment teams need research, portfolio analysis, risk and client servicing workflows that generic AI tools do not handle reliably; InferEdge builds custom agentic workflows inside the client's cloud.
business_model: Forward deployed engineering with outcome based pricing for agentic AI workflows
product_category: Agentic AI for investment management (fintech enterprise software)
founder_names: Aditya Mehta; Amal Dani; Omkar Ghaisas
market_need_then: Asset managers already spent heavily on research and data tools (the AlphaSense and Sentieo market); the current pitch is that generic AI tools rarely hold up in real investment workflows.
outcome_analysis: InferEdge is active with about 20 staff in Mumbai and Singapore. Its founders come from Goldman Sachs, hedge funds and Paysense, and the company now sells agentic AI to buy-side firms with named customers such as Temasek and Mahindra Manulife. Funding is essentially undisclosed and the original 2022 product is not documented, so the path to this model cannot be reconstructed from public sources.

name: Instalab
tags: Consumer Health Services; Health Tech; Telemedicine; Health & Wellness; AI
one_liner: Proactive Testing and Treatments
long_description: Instalab gives you direct access to all the preventative tests you need to do this year to stay on top of your health. Trusted by tens of thousands of top-performing founders, executives, and professional athletes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Health conscious consumers, founders, executives and athletes who pay for preventative lab tests, imaging, medications and physician consults
problem: Preventative testing is hard to order and interpret through the traditional system; Instalab lets consumers order tests directly and builds a personalised plan with physician guidance.
business_model: Direct to consumer testing and telemedicine with a membership; pricing pages conflict ($499 per year on one page, $42 per month on another)
product_category: Consumer preventive health testing and telemedicine
market_need_then: Direct to consumer testing was an established category with companies such as Everlywell and LetsGetChecked raising capital before 2022, indicating consumer demand.
outcome_analysis: Instalab is active and claims over 10,000 patients, a catalog of 600 plus lab tests and a nationwide at-home collection partnership with Getlabs announced in April 2024. No disclosed venture round was found, so growth appears bootstrapped or lightly funded, but this cannot be confirmed from public data.
