Its position faces competition from larger consumer testing brands.

name: Instant
one_liner: The best backend for AI-coded apps
long_description: Give your AI a real backend. You get auth, permissions, storage, presence, and everything you need to ship apps your users will love.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers building realtime, collaborative and AI coded apps who want a Firebase style backend
problem: Firebase style backends lacked relations and offline realtime sync, and developers had to hand build sync, permissions and optimistic updates for collaborative apps.
business_model: Open source database with a hosted cloud with free tier and paid plans
product_category: Realtime backend and client side graph database
market_need_then: Developers wanted Firebase like productivity with relational queries and collaboration features; the HN launch drew over 1,000 points in 2024, but dated 2022 demand evidence is thin.
outcome_analysis: Instant built an open source realtime backend and gained strong developer attention, raising a 3.4 million seed in October 2024 and reporting over 17,000 users and 400,000 apps. In August 2026 the four person team joined OpenAI as the hosted cloud was set to shut down by August 2027, with no terms disclosed. That looks like a talent move rather than a continuing product outcome, though the open source code lives on.

name: Instant Labs
one_liner: Instant Labs builds modern tools to help you find and buy domain…
long_description: Instant Labs started in 2005 by building the fastest domain search engine on the internet: https://instantdomainsearch.com. People have performed over 2.5M searches and purchased 250K domains with our free tool.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: People and businesses searching for and buying domain names (affiliate commissions); at the 2022 batch, software companies buying creator marketing through Strobe
problem: Finding an available domain name quickly; the YC launch product Strobe aimed to help software companies find influencers who already like their product.
business_model: Affiliate commissions on domain purchases through partner links, now also an ICANN accredited registrar; Strobe was a subscription web app
product_category: Domain search tools (consumer and developer tools), plus an AI creator marketing tool at the batch
market_need_then: The site reported over 2.5M searches and 250K domains purchased from its free tool by the time of the YC page, showing steady consumer demand for domain search.
outcome_analysis: Instant Labs is active. Its domain search business, started in 2005, kept growing (the company reports 2.5x growth in the last year as of its instant.ai post) and in 2026 it moved into registrar services and an API under the instant.ai brand. The YC era Strobe creator marketing product appears peripheral. Investors are named by the company but amounts are not disclosed.

name: Integrated Reasoning
tags: Developer Tools; Hard Tech; Hardware; SaaS; AI
one_liner: Faster processors for solving NP-complete problems
long_description: Integrated Reasoning builds efficient computer processors that are tailored to the memory access patterns of Karp's 21 NP-complete problems. We’re making it 100x - 10,000x faster to perform computations like scheduling airline pilots or optimizing packing layouts for shipping containers.
all_locations: San Diego, CA, USA; Kilauea, HI, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Companies running logistics, scheduling, routing and packing optimization, such as airlines and shippers
problem: Combinatorial optimization jobs (scheduling pilots, packing containers) run slowly and expensively on general purpose cloud hardware; the company proposes processors shaped to the memory access patterns of Karp's 21 NP-complete problems.
business_model: Cloud deployed optimization hardware, sold as scalable capacity without hardware or firmware expertise needed
product_category: Custom processors and hardware for combinatorial optimization
competitors_at_founding: Fujitsu Digital Annealer; Toshiba Simulated Bifurcation Machine (SQBM+)
market_need_then: Logistics optimization is expensive on cloud solvers (the launch post cites Google OR-Tools cost) and TechCrunch's batch coverage said there is clearly a customer base, though the claim is ambitious.
outcome_analysis: Integrated Reasoning is active with a one person team and was called a moonshot by TechCrunch in its Summer 2022 batch coverage. Aggregators report roughly $0.5M pre-seed and $1.9M total, not confirmed by a primary source. No customers, benchmarks by third parties or funding announcements were found, so its progress against Fujitsu and Toshiba optimization hardware cannot be judged.

name: Integration Labs
one_liner: The Unified API for Business Financial Data
long_description:
Integration Labs makes it easy to interact with your business customers' financial data.

Leading SaaS, payments, and financial service companies use a single API to seamlessly retrieve and sync data across their customers' accounting, commerce, and payments platforms.

With Integration Labs, B2B companies integrate once to connect to 30+ accounting, payments and e-commerce integrations and build innovative business tools for invoice financing, digital lending, expense management, automated AP/AR reconciliation, and more.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: SaaS, payments and financial-services companies (lenders, invoice-financing, expense-management and AP/AR tools) that need their business customers' accounting, commerce and payments data
problem: Fintech and SaaS builders must write and maintain separate integrations to many accounting, e-commerce and payments platforms to read their customers' financial data.
business_model: usage/subscription-based unified API (B2B developer API); exact pricing not found
product_category: unified API for business financial data (accounting, commerce, payments integrations)
founder_names: Ishwar Gogineni; Parth Shah; Sidharth Rao
market_need_then: Lenders, invoice-financing and expense-management fintechs needed programmatic access to SMEs' accounting data; the existence of funded unified-API vendors in 2022 (Rutter, Codat) shows active demand.
outcome_analysis: Integration Labs (formerly RootFi) raised a roughly $1.5M seed from YC and angels, built a unified financial-data API with 30+ integrations, and was eventually acquired by its first customer, Commenda, which says the product and team continue. The deal price is undisclosed and the YC directory marks the company Inactive, so it reads as a small, quiet exit in a market crowded with better-funded rivals rather than a clear success or failure.

name: Intuned
tags: Developer Tools; Robotic Process Automation; B2B; API; AI
one_liner: Code-first scrapers and RPAs — built and maintained by AI
long_description: Intuned is a code-first browser automation platform with an AI agent that builds and maintains your automations. Developers use Intuned to deploy scrapers, RPAs, and crawlers as production-ready TypeScript or Python projects — with stealth, CAPTCHA solving, proxies, auth, and scheduling handled out of the box. The agent builds projects from a prompt, fixes failed runs, and can self-heal automations autonomously when websites change.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and engineering teams that need integrations, scrapers or RPA for websites that have no API
problem: Browser automations break when sites change and are costly to maintain; teams need reliable, code-owned automations.
business_model: usage-based developer platform with tiered subscriptions
product_category: browser automation / RPA platform
market_need_then: Founder says he left UiPath frustrated with brittle RPA; his own blog post describes frustration at a job in summer 2022 before applying to YC. No dated spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Intuned is active as of 2026 with a small team and an AI agent that builds and repairs browser automations. No public funding beyond the standard YC deal was found, so its trajectory is unknown. The product moved from a code-first automation platform to an agent-assisted one as AI browser agents emerged, and no exit, layoff or shutdown has been reported.

name: Invert
tags: Cellular Agriculture; Machine Learning; Synthetic Biology; Biotech
one_liner: Data analytics software for biomanufacturing.
long_description: We build software to manage, analyze, and optimize bioprocessing data. Our initial customers are bio-industrial companies, who produce various products in bioreactors.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Bio-industrial and biopharma manufacturers running bioreactors
problem: Bioprocess data is scattered across instruments and files, making it slow to analyze and optimize runs.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: bioprocess data analytics software
market_need_then: Bioprocess teams were generating large volumes of bioreactor data in spreadsheets; the YC description says initial customers are bio-industrial companies. No dated spend figure found.
outcome_analysis: Invert has stayed active and grown, with a roughly $20 million raise in mid 2024 per an SEC Form D summary and a customer list including large biopharma. Founders had prior YC and engineering leadership experience but no stated bio industry background in the sources. Success rests on being an early dedicated bioprocess data platform; the evidence for traction beyond case studies on its own site is thin.

name: Invofox
one_liner: Invofox is the document parsing and data extraction API for software…
long_description:
Software teams in 150+ companies solve their document processing needs using Invofox.
We are a good option for you if:
- Great accuracy is a requirement in your business (we guarantee +99% as part of our SLAs, written in our contracts)
- You want a simple and easy to understand pricing (we charge per page, and any documents were you report back an error are completely free)
- You want a system that just works, and that gets better over time (Invofox learns automatically with feedback)

You can try it with this link and get an extra 250 pages for free: https://go.invofox.com/ooVVIw
all_locations: Madrid, Community of Madrid, Spain; Remote
regions: Spain; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software companies and developers that need document data extraction embedded in their products
problem: Extracting accurate structured data from invoices, payslips and other PDFs is slow and error prone for software teams.
business_model: usage-based API priced per page
product_category: document parsing and data extraction API
founder_names: Alberto Gimeno; Carmelo Juanes; Adrian Ramirez
market_need_then: Founders say they served several segments until reaching about $1 million in annual revenue, then focused on software companies (founder profile, yespress). No dated spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Invofox remains active, reports 150 plus software teams and an accuracy guaranteed pay per correct page model, and says it reached about $1 million revenue before narrowing to software companies. Funding is uncertain across aggregators. The main structural risk is that cloud and LLM based extraction made the core capability cheaper to replicate.

name: IoTFlows Inc
one_liner: Plug-and-play AI platform with sensors and dashboards that makes…
long_description: IoTFlows combines AI-powered hardware and software to give manufacturers real-time visibility into machine utilization, downtime, and workflow efficiency. Our plug-and-play platform analyzes data, generates actionable insights, and automates maintenance and operational tasks, helping teams optimize performance and achieve ROI in less than a month. Trusted by companies like Parker Hannifin, IoTFlows delivers high-margin, subscription-based value that scales seamlessly.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and mid-size manufacturers and machine shops
problem: Manufacturers lack real-time visibility into machine utilization and downtime.
business_model: hardware sensors plus per device SaaS subscription
product_category: manufacturing machine monitoring (IIoT)
market_need_then: Manufacturers report downtime and utilization blind spots; the company claims 35 percent less unplanned downtime for customers (company site, undated).
outcome_analysis: IoTFlows is active with a reported 60 person team and a broad customer list on its own site, including large industrials. Public funding appears small and conflicting across aggregators, so scale of capital is unclear. The story is a hardware plus software monitoring product selling per device subscriptions into manufacturing.

name: Jamble
tags: Marketplace; Consumer; Social; E-commerce; Creator Economy
one_liner: Live shopping for collectibles in Brazil
long_description:
Jamble is a live shopping marketplace for collectibles in Brazil. Collectors discover products, meet sellers and buy together in interactive live shows, from Pokémon and other trading cards to Hot Wheels and diecast miniatures.

Buyers see items live, ask questions and make offers in real time. Sellers turn their expertise and inventory into live storefronts, build an audience and grow a community of returning customers.

Jamble brings live video, chat, checkout, payments via PIX and cards, and tracked shipping into one app. Available on iOS and Android.

Explore Jamble: https://www.jamble.com/
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Collectors and sellers of trading cards and diecast in Brazil (originally secondhand fashion buyers and sellers)
problem: Collectors lack a trusted live venue to see items, ask questions and buy; sellers lack an audience.
business_model: marketplace take rate on live shopping sales
product_category: live shopping marketplace
founder_names: Louis de Jenlis; Aymar Dumoulin; Jeremy Gozlan
market_need_then: Brazilian press in 2023 described live shopping as a coming channel; Shopee's 2022 launch shows platform demand. Collectibles demand evidence is from 2026 reports.
outcome_analysis: Jamble is active and has focused on collectibles in Brazil, reporting over 3,000 active buyers and 400 sellers in a few months of operation in a 2026 article, and R$4 million of April sales in another headline. Funding found is small and from aggregators only. It moved from a French secondhand fashion live app to a niche where platform rivals are less specialized.

name: Jamsocket
one_liner: Run compute-intensive apps in a browser
long_description:
We are a platform for high-performance browser-based applications. We make it easier for developers to deploy apps that give every user a dedicated backend.

This is a system design that apps like Figma and GitHub codespaces use, but it's currently difficult for others to replicate it. We make it as easy as deploying a traditional web server.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers building browser based, compute intensive or collaborative apps that need a dedicated backend per user session
problem: Giving each user a dedicated, short lived backend, as Figma and GitHub Codespaces do, is hard to build and operate for most teams.
business_model: Usage based infrastructure platform plus open source tools (Plane, Y-Sweet)
product_category: Session backend and realtime sync infrastructure
market_need_then: The founders pointed to Figma and Codespaces as proof the architecture works but is hard to replicate; no dated third party demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Jamsocket raised a 2.5 million seed in August 2022 and built session backend infrastructure with open source Plane and Y-Sweet, later adding ForeverVM for AI code execution. Modal acquired it in July 2025, saying the platform suits AI heavy workloads, with undisclosed terms and no traction numbers. The AI shift gave the infrastructure a new audience, but the company stayed small and was absorbed.

name: Jasmine Energy
tags: Solar Power; Energy; Renewable Energy; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Claim solar incentives with AI
long_description: Jasmine makes it easy to register, sell, finance, and retire RECs (renewable energy certificates). Our AI can "read" unstructured data (CRM notes, PDFs, images, etc) and use that information to complete webforms and filing document. This takes previously manual error prone process and makes it automatic and self-healing.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Joe
one_liner: We let customers "Buy Now Pay Later" on any store in Europe.
long_description:
Joe is building a innovative and flexible DtoC Buy Now Pay Later App  in Europe powered by Tech📲.
In Europe, only 15% of e-commerce have integrated BNPL solutions and consumers don’t have access to installments very easily. 

Within Joe app and our virtual card you can buy now pay later on any store  without any technical integration. And if you already made your purchase, you can be refunded and get 3 installments
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: French and European online shoppers who want installment payments at any store without merchant integration
problem: Only about 15 percent of European e-commerce offered buy now pay later, so most shoppers could not split payments.
business_model: Consumer fintech earning a commission from the buyer or merchants, with a virtual card for payment and a refund and repay feature
product_category: Consumer buy now pay later app
market_need_then: French and European BNPL was growing quickly in 2021, with Klarna entering France and Alma and Pledg raising money; Joe itself claimed only about 15 percent of European e-commerce had BNPL.
outcome_analysis: Joe launched in early 2021 after a 1 million euro angel seed, reporting over 10,000 users, and joined YC for Winter 2022 in a crowded French BNPL market. The business was sold to La Banque Postale in late 2022, about two and a half years after founding, with terms undisclosed. Whether it was a success or a distressed sale is not public.

name: Joon Health
tags: Mental Health Tech; Consumer Health Services; Consumer
one_liner: Pediatric digital therapeutic for the +100M families in the US
long_description:
Joon is an integrated pediatric digital health platform for kids, starting with behavior disorders like ADHD, autism, anxiety, and depression. In Joon, kids access a game-based digital therapeutic where they level up when they do real-life behaviors that are managed by parents and clinicians. 

Over the next 10 years, we plan on being the first-line vertically integrated digital treatment for pediatric behavior disorders, leveraging the first of its kind technology to drive behavior change.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Oakland, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Parents of children with ADHD and behavior disorders paying subscriptions, with clinicians as a channel
problem: Parents struggle to get kids with ADHD and related disorders to build daily routines. Joon gamifies real-life tasks that parents assign and kids complete.
business_model: Consumer subscription app (reported 89.99 dollars per year), moving toward clinician-integrated digital therapeutic
product_category: Pediatric digital health, gamified behavior app
founder_names: Isaac Eaves; Brad Brenner; Kevin Bunarjo
market_need_then: ADHD and behavior disorders affect large numbers of US children and prescription digital therapeutics had just been cleared by FDA, creating interest. No hard spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Joon is still early stage, with about 10 staff and a reported 6.4 million dollar seed in 2023. It sells a quest-based routine app rather than a cleared therapeutic, and no outcome events are reported. Evidence of product market fit is not public, so it cannot yet be judged as a success or a stall.

name: Juicebox
tags: Generative AI; B2B; Recruiting; HR Tech; AI
one_liner: AI Agents for Recruiting
long_description:
Juicebox is on a mission to help teams win the talent war.

In the age of AI, human ingenuity is the ultimate scarce resource. Recruiting is a zero-sum game where you either compete or lose.

Teams at Ramp, Notion, and leading AI labs use Juicebox to power their hiring, alongside 5,000+ customers from early-stage startups to Fortune 500 companies.

We’re on the path to $100M in ARR with 20%+ monthly growth, powering thousands of searches every day and making Juicebox one of the fastest-growing AI SaaS companies in the world. In 2026, Juicebox was named to Forbes’ Next Billion-Dollar Startups list and LinkedIn’s Top Startups list.

Juicebox has raised $116M in funding, including a $30M Series A led by Sequoia Capital and an $80M Series B led by DST Global. NFDG lead out seed round, and additional investors include Y Combinator, Coatue, BOND, Lux Capital, Verified Capital, and Committed Capital.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Recruiting teams, staffing agencies and companies sourcing candidates outbound
problem: Finding qualified candidates by keyword search on profile databases is slow; recruiters need natural language search and automated outreach.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat subscription
product_category: AI recruiting and candidate sourcing
market_need_then: Original idea was a talent marketplace (shut October 2022); founders said message market fit came before product market fit. LLM search demand followed in late 2023.
outcome_analysis: Juicebox shut its first idea in October 2022, then rebuilt around LLM search for recruiting, launched PeopleGPT in late 2023, and raised a $6M seed, a $30M Series A led by Sequoia in September 2025 and an $80M Series B at $850M in March 2026. Growth claims of 5,000 plus customers are company reported. Success reflects a pivot timed with the LLM wave and fast execution.

name: Julius
one_liner: Build and analyze things with AI
long_description: Julius is an AI workspace that turns ideas and data into finished work. Analyze spreadsheets and files with AI data analysis, turn research and insights into editable slides with the AI presentation maker, or bring ideas to life with the AI website builder, all in one interface.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Analysts, students and business users who want to analyze spreadsheets and data in plain English
problem: Non programmers struggle to analyze and chart data without coding; Julius provides chat based data analysis.
business_model: freemium subscription
product_category: AI data analysis workspace
market_need_then: Founders said they began Julius after seeing limits of Code Interpreter; mid 2023 launch reached 300k plus users per one source.
outcome_analysis: Julius pivoted from a logistics idea to chat based data analysis in 2023, grew to a million users by one account, and raised a $10M seed in July 2025 led by Bessemer. It benefits from LLM timing and founder visibility but competes with ChatGPT's own data analysis features. Funding beyond the seed is unverified.

name: JumpWire
one_liner: Dynamic access controls for all data and databases
long_description:
JumpWire is a data protection platform that adds advanced data security controls between APIs, applications and databases. JumpWire automatically identifies sensitive properties inside large data sets and gives developers full control over which people and applications can access or update records containing sensitive info.

Examples uses include restricting who can read customer PII to members of the customer service team, giving on-call engineers elevated access to production, or splitting user records between regions for GDPR purposes.

JumpWire’s approach to securing data in-place minimizes the risk of data leaks exposing sensitive information or mishandling by other applications and vendors. The exact security scheme applied to data is defined by policies that align with an organization’s existing InfoSec program.

JumpWire helps companies who maintain information security with compliance programs such as SOC or HIPAA. They are processing sensitive data, often from their own customers, and exceed security best practices as a competitive advantage. JumpWire provides defense at depth to data and sits alongside access controls and Layer 4 encryption to provide a comprehensive data security solution.

JumpWire is unique from solutions such as data vaults by installing inside our customers’ own infrastructure and clouds. It is interoperable with existing applications and databases, which eliminates the need for large data migrations or code refactoring. Lower-level approaches to data security, such as encryption at rest, are too blunt and lack the ability to differentiate between properties in the data itself. Its scope is limited to physical storage, and security is lost as soon as an application or query loads the data.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering and security teams at companies handling sensitive customer data under SOC 2, HIPAA or GDPR programs
problem: Sensitive fields in databases and APIs are readable by too many people and applications, and encryption at rest is too blunt to control access per property.
business_model: B2B software deployed inside the customer's own infrastructure, sold as a data security platform
product_category: Data security and field-level access control
market_need_then: Compliance programs such as SOC 2, HIPAA and GDPR pushed companies to restrict access to PII, and the company's own pitch cited customer PII exposure and production access as common pain points.
outcome_analysis: JumpWire was a one founder data security startup from Winter 2022 that was acquired by WorkOS, reported as January 2024, after about two years. The buyer needed data access governance next to its enterprise identity products, so the exit looks like a small tuck in deal. No price, funding history or post-mortem is public, so the story beyond the acquisition cannot be told.

name: Jutsoo
tags: FinOps; Fintech; SaaS; B2B; Enterprise Software
one_liner: All your corporate bank accounts connected under one platform
long_description:
Jutsoo is a modern treasury management platform that helps finance teams work smarter by having efficient, reliable, real-time visibility and control over their financial data across their different banks and bank accounts.

We do this by unifying data from internal systems, integrating directly with banks for your money movements, and reconcile them automatically.

Money movements, reconciliations, cash forecasting, and identifying liquidity trends will be a breeze using us.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Finance teams at companies with multiple bank accounts (later small teams needing bookkeeping)
problem: Finance teams lack unified real time visibility and reconciliation across banks.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: treasury management, later AI bookkeeping
founder_names: Mario Gaw; Kristian F H Sinaulan
market_need_then: Indonesian corporate clients wanted direct bank to ERP and treasury links (Asian Banker article, undated).
outcome_analysis: Jutsoo, previously Bananas, raised a reported $1.5M seed in February 2022 and pivoted from grocery delivery to treasury software, with its site now describing an AI bookkeeper. Total funding of about $1.49M per PitchBook suggests modest capital. No exit or shutdown found; later positioning changes indicate continued search for fit.

name: Kaagaz
one_liner: 'Office' Suite for Mobile-first Businesses in India
long_description:
Kaagaz is an 'Office' Suite for Mobile-first Businesses in India. With Kaagaz, these users can manage all the document requirements for their business using their smartphone itself, without needing a Desktop.

We have an active user base of 3Mn+ users and paid users north of 60,000+ - growing every month.

With over 200M such businesses in India, at $15/year subscription price, this a $3B opportunity in India & much larger globally.

We are a team of 2nd time entrepreneurs having scaled the pervious startup to $1M in GMV. We are backed by YCombinator, Goodwater Capital, Pravega Venture, Better Capital & other investors including Alan Rutledge (TrendMD) and Farid Ahsan (Sharechat)
all_locations: Gurugram, HR, India; New Delhi, DL, India
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Mobile-first individuals and small businesses in India who need to scan, edit, store and share documents on a smartphone
problem: India's small businesses run on documents but mostly have only a phone, not a desktop. India blocked the popular CamScanner app in June 2020, leaving a gap for a trusted local scanner and document suite.
business_model: Freemium consumer and SMB mobile app suite with a paid subscription tier (company states roughly 15 USD per year) and pay per use AI tools
product_category: Mobile document scanner and office suite
founder_names: Snehanshu Gandhi; Tamanjit Bindra; Gaurav Shrishrimal
market_need_then: CamScanner's June 2020 block in India created sudden demand; the founders cite more than 200 million small businesses in India and 3 million users by YC time.
outcome_analysis: Kaagaz launched a free scanner a day after India blocked CamScanner in 2020, which gave it a one time distribution tailwind and millions of installs. It raised a small seed in November 2020, joined YC in Winter 2022, and reports 3 million users and 60,000 paying users at the time of the batch. It remains active and has widened into a poster and AI suite. No outcome event such as an exit or shutdown was found.

name: Kable
one_liner: Usage-based billing for API companies
long_description:
Kable makes it easy for developers to add usage-based billing, invoicing, analytics, and authentication to their API products with just three lines of code.

We help API companies bring their products to market faster, more securely, and with flexible billing tools that help businesses scale. We provide everything needed to create a delightful experience for developer communities and to optimize revenue while giving time back to engineering teams to focus on what matters most.
all_locations: Los Angeles, CA, USA; Santa Monica, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Kamion
one_liner: Uber for Trucks for Turkey
long_description:
Turkey is MENA’s largest economy, with ~850,000 independent truckers and a logistics market of 73 Billion USD. However, in its current state, freight forwarding for trucking relies on many phone calls, emails, and f2f conversations. Trucking is also fragmented, with SME fleets having ~95% market share. 

Kamion is the Uber for Trucks for Turkey. We connect businesses that are looking for trucks, with trucks that are looking for loads. We also utilize technology to do more with fewer people and collect data.
regions: Turkey; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Turkish shippers who need trucks, and the small fleets and independent truckers who supply them
problem: Freight forwarding in Turkey runs on phone calls, emails and face to face deals, and SME fleets hold about 95 percent of a fragmented trucking market.
business_model: Freight marketplace and brokerage with a margin on loads (FTL contract and spot)
product_category: Digital freight marketplace
market_need_then: YC launch post cites about 850,000 independent truckers and a 73 billion USD Turkish logistics market run on phone and email brokering.
outcome_analysis: Kamion built a trucking marketplace in a market of fragmented small fleets, joined YC in Summer 2022 and closed a reported 2 million dollar seed in December 2022. Its site now claims over 50,000 drivers and more than 10,000 loads shared daily, and a 2023 article reports about 10 million dollars of revenue. It remains active with no shutdown or acquisition found, so its outcome so far is steady growth.

name: Kapital Bank
one_liner: Empowering businesses to grow.
long_description:
Cash management solution that offers debit & credit solutions for Enterprise/SMBs in LATAM. 
- 24/ Multi-treasury: FX, multiple debit global accounts, payroll & services payment to all the world 24/, wires
- Corporate Expenses: dashboard and prepaid cards to control your employee's budget & expenses
- Credit Card: flexible global line where you can decide to use it as a revolving line or as a simple amortizable credit in installments.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mexican and Latin American SMBs and enterprises needing treasury, expense cards and credit
problem: Mexican SMBs had poor access to multi currency business accounts, payments and flexible credit from traditional banks.
business_model: Banking and credit: interest income, FX and payments fees, card interchange
product_category: Business neobank and credit
market_need_then: SMBs in Mexico were underserved by banks for treasury, FX and credit; the YC page notes demand and the company expanded to Colombia and the US.
outcome_analysis: Kapital grew from a YC Winter 2022 cash management startup into a Mexican financial group by buying Banco Autofin in 2023 and Intercam assets in 2025. It raised a Series B in December 2023 and a Series C in September 2025 at a reported 1.3 billion dollar valuation, then a 125 million dollar round in 2026. The license strategy plus credit growth explain the outcome.

name: Karate Labs
one_liner: Open-source API & UI test automation
long_description:
Karate is an open-source unified test automation platform combining API testing, API performance testing, API mocks & UI testing. 
1.5 million monthly downloads, used by 500+ companies including 76 of the Fortune 500, are a testimony of Karate removing friction from the developer experience (DX). We did this by making it exceptionally simple to write tests (low code), simulating end-user workflows accurately, re-using API tests as performance tests, parallel execution, and collaboration via Git. 
Staying true to Karate’s “LOCAL-FIRST” approach (user data remains within the customer's firewall, ensuring security and addressing any concerns), we launched the official Karate plugins (IntelliJ and VS Code) for frictionless onboarding, simplified installations, configuration, and maintenance. Our plugins include all Karate open-source features, including exploring of APIs, and premium features (testing for Async APIs, API documentation, API data importer and more).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software engineering and QA teams at enterprises (500+ companies claimed, incl. 76 of the Fortune 500) that pay for premium plugins and support around the open-source Karate framework
problem: API and UI test suites are hard to write and maintain; Karate offers low-code, Gherkin-style tests that reuse API tests for performance testing.
business_model: Open-source core with paid premium plugins (IntelliJ, VS Code) and enterprise features
product_category: Test automation / developer tools
market_need_then: Company claims 1.5 million monthly downloads and 500+ users (YC page, self-reported); the framework originated inside Intuit in 2017 to replace a harder in-house tool (secondary account).
outcome_analysis: Karate Labs commercialises an open-source test framework its creator built at Intuit. The company is active and reports 500+ company users and 1.5M monthly downloads, which suggests strong developer pull, but no verified funding history or revenue is public, so its trajectory beyond a small team of two remains unclear.

name: Kashin
one_liner: Credit for the emerging economy in Latam
long_description:
Credit for the emerging economy in Latam.
We have 10K users and nearly $2M in annualized revenue, from our small loans to micro-merchants and individuals in the informal economy.
We do our underwriting with our proprietary AI risk model processing 250+ variables from the user's smartphone and credit bureau.
all_locations: Lima, Callao Region, Peru; Lima, Lima Province, Peru; Remote
regions: Peru; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Underbanked individuals and micro merchants in Peru's informal economy
problem: People in the informal economy have no credit history and little access to formal loans; the founders aim to underwrite them with phone data and a network of endorsers.
business_model: Consumer nano loans (S/50 to S/800, 30 day term) with interest, plus a digital wallet
product_category: Digital microcredit and wallet
market_need_then: Launch post says default rates in this segment are around 15 percent traditionally versus Kashin's under 8 percent claim; the company reports 10K users and nearly 2M USD annualized revenue at batch time.
outcome_analysis: Kashin, founded in Peru in 2020 by two ex Easy Taxi and Cabify executives, joined YC in Summer 2022 with small loans to micro merchants. It reports about 2 million dollars of annualized revenue then and was approving more than 1,000 loans a day in 2025 per a Peruvian outlet, and Grupo RPP invested in 2025. It stays active; the funding history is thin in public sources so success is only partly evidenced.

name: Kaso
tags: Marketplace; Supply Chain; Food Tech; AI
one_liner: AI group purchasing for restaurants
long_description:
Independent restaurants pay ~12% more than chains for the exact same food supplies because they buy alone.
Kaso uses AI agents to aggregate purchasing demand from restaurants and negotiate chain-level pricing with suppliers.
regions: United Arab Emirates; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Independent restaurants and food suppliers in the UAE and Saudi Arabia
problem: Independent restaurants buy food supplies alone and pay more than chains, and ordering from suppliers is manual.
business_model: B2B procurement marketplace with supplier fees, plus invoice financing and buy now pay later
product_category: Restaurant procurement marketplace
market_need_then: Company cites independents paying about 12 percent more than chains; a Gulf food service market with manual ordering by phone and WhatsApp (company framing).
outcome_analysis: Kaso, renamed from Elkaso, raised a 2.1 million dollar pre-seed in 2021 and joined YC in Winter 2022. It added a 10.5 million dollar seed in July 2023 and now claims over 5,000 restaurants and 2,000 suppliers across MENA. Serial founder experience and regional investors helped; it remains active with no shutdown or acquisition found.

name: KemNet
tags: Marketplace; B2B; Digital Health; E-commerce; Therapeutics
one_liner: KemNet supplies reformulated drugs for specific groups of patients.
long_description: KemNet supplies pharmacies with premium reformulations of popular drugs that are more useful for specific groups of patients. For example, more than 30 pharmacies rely on KemNet to supply reformulated products for erectile dysfunction that work up to 8 times faster than alternatives. In addition to sexual function, products reformulated for novel drug delivery and supplied on KemNet include medications for hair growth, pain, weight loss and women's health.
all_locations: Victoria, BC, Canada; Edmonton, AB, Canada; Remote
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Pharmacies in Canada (Alberta first) that want reformulated versions of common drugs for specific patient groups
problem: About half of patients do not take medications as prescribed, often due to unpleasant formats; pharmacies lack a supply of reformulated products.
business_model: B2B marketplace supplying compounded reformulated drugs from compounders to pharmacies
product_category: Pharmaceutical reformulation supply platform
market_need_then: In Sept 2022 KemNet supplied three compounders and 30 Alberta pharmacies (Taproot Edmonton). Pharmacies typically compound only when no Health Canada approved product exists, which constrains demand.
outcome_analysis: KemNet joined YC in Summer 2022 with an Alberta pharmacy supply platform for reformulated drugs and had 30 pharmacies and three compounders at that time. No funding round, exit or shutdown is reported publicly, and a third party estimate puts revenue at about 880,000 dollars in 2025. The story is unclear: regulatory limits on compounding may cap growth but there is no evidence of failure.

name: Kenobi
tags: SaaS; B2B; Sales; Sales Enablement; AI
one_liner: Personalize your landing site for each vistor, in one line of code.
long_description:
Kenobi is personalizing the internet. Your marketing site is your front desk to the internet, but its content has to be applicable to all of your ICPs and potential visitors, usually resulting in fragmented and blunt brochure content.

Kenobi acts as your concierge, ensuring each of your visitors receives content that is tailored to _them_ so that they actually convert and progress along your sales journey. You can install Kenobi with one `<head />` tag in your site's markup -- everything else is taken care of using our AI research + content generation pipeline.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: B2B companies with marketing sites that want visitors to see tailored content
problem: Marketing sites speak to everyone at once, so most traffic does not convert; the founders claim 98 percent of web traffic does not convert.
business_model: B2B SaaS with a free plan and paid tiers
product_category: Website personalization widget
market_need_then: Launch post claims opted in visitors engage 3x longer and convert 2x better (company figures); B2B marketers were funding personalization tools in 2021 and 2022.
outcome_analysis: Kenobi pivoted from Verdn into website personalization and joined YC in Winter 2022 as a three person London team. A single aggregator reports a seed round in March 2022 and about 1 million dollars raised in total, while larger rivals Intellimize and Mutiny raised tens of millions. It is still listed active with no exit; the company site now describes a different design systems product, so its outcome is unclear.

name: Keylika
tags: AI-powered Drug Discovery; Medical Devices; Drug Delivery; Nanotechnology; Therapeutics
one_liner: Redefining the Standard of Care for Iron Deficiency Anemia
long_description:
Keylika is an early stage biopharma startup developing metal-based drugs using a platform synthesis technology to treat unmet medical needs. We then administer these drugs using proven delivery technologies to effect the best clinical outcomes. 

Our first product is a small molecule iron drug (new molecular entity) delivered by a wearable skin patch to treat Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA), with significantly higher safety, efficacy and tolerability over existing treatments. This is poised to be a best-in-class, potentially breakthrough therapy for treating iron deficiency without any GI side-effects (eg. nausea, constipation, diarrhea, etc.) typically associated with oral iron supplements, and without the risks, costs and side-effects associated with IV iron infusions. When approved, Keylika’s proprietary transdermal iron will be the world's first prescription iron patch. Iron deficiency is a hugely understated problem affecting about 1.6 billion people worldwide and more than 30 million in the US alone, translating to a $17B US market.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Walnut Creek, CA, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Patients with iron deficiency anemia, starting with women with heavy menstrual bleeding; commercially pharma partners and payers
problem: Oral iron causes GI side effects and IV iron needs infusions and carries risks; the company wants a patch that avoids both.
business_model: Biopharma drug development aiming at licensing or partnering and eventual prescription sales
product_category: Metallodrug and drug delivery patch (NistuFe, KYLK01)
competitors_at_founding: Fe3 Medical; Accrufer (Shield Therapeutics); Injectafer (American Regent)
market_need_then: Company cites about 1.6 billion people with iron deficiency worldwide and over 30 million in the US; oral and IV iron both have known drawbacks.
outcome_analysis: Keylika is a one person biotech that joined YC in Summer 2022 to develop an iron patch for iron deficiency anemia. Public sources show animal studies and promotional press in 2024 and 2025 but no priced funding round, clinical trial or exit. The product framing shifted from a skin patch to a buccal patch, and the long timeline of drug development means the outcome is still open.

name: Knowtex
tags: Health Tech; B2B; Productivity; Digital Health; AI
one_liner: Making doctors 2x more efficient with AI note-taking & charge capture
long_description:
We’re on a mission to leverage AI and voice technology to solve inefficiencies and revenue leakage in our healthcare system. With the rise of EHRs, the manual documentation burden on doctors has never been higher, leading to burnout and fatigue and high attrition rates. Assigning the correct diagnosis and billing codes is crucial for proper reimbursement and patient care, but medical coding is becoming more and more complex each year with growing numbers of codes (over 145,000 now), and doctors are unsupported by current technology to keep up with its ever increasing requirements. $125 billion is left on the table each year by healthcare organizations due to improper documentation and coding. 

Knowtex creates visit notes with up-to-date and accurate reimbursement codes from doctor-patient conversations, allowing the doctor to focus on patient care and preventing revenue leakage for hospital systems through standardized, transparent, and accurate documentation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Health systems and specialty physician practices that pay for clinical documentation and coding software

It competes in a crowded scribe market with Microsoft DAX, Suki and others, and has moved to a broader clinical AI lab positioning.

name: Koala

name: Koko

We provide free digital mental health technologies for millions of people struggling online — particularly young people. 

For example, we partner with online communities to help find and treat at-risk individuals directly on their platform.

name: Kombo

Execution speed and a focused developer wedge explain the growth.

name: KorrAI
one_liner: Traceable AI for billion-dollar infrastructure.
long_description:
KorrAI began in 2021 as a Canadian Space Agency research spin-off. We spent four years on ground deformation monitoring and geotechnical studies for mines and infrastructure, and kept running into the same problem: engineers who sign off on a site's safety have to synthesize reports by hunting for docs and data received from consultants, contractors, and site teams by hand.

Over the last two years, we built TRAIL, a platform informed by interconnected data, powered by specialised AI agents, and supported by our experts. With TRAIL deployed at multiple mine sites across the US and Canada, we envision turning risk management into a proactive process. When records span decades, a wrong answer has regulatory and safety consequences; it is necessary to have complete knowledge of risks and take action in time. 

Our team of satellite data experts, geoscientists, and AI engineers monitors more than $100 billion in assets across the globe. TRAIL reads a site's full record: reports, drawings, inspection notes, monitoring data, satellite imagery, and ground deformation, etc. It builds a location-based knowledge graph. AI Agents run defined risk passes over the graph, flag contradictions, cross-link data, and present findings. Every finding cites its source page and data point, so a regulator or Engineer of Record can review it. Where no evidence supports a claim, TRAIL says so.

TRAIL is used by closure professionals, geotechnical engineers, and Engineers of Record in mining, and by risk engineers and underwriters on data centers and other critical infrastructure. We work with organizations including Agnico Eagle, Hecla, Eldorado Gold, Stantec, AECOM, Ramboll, Amazon Web Services, and Zurich North America.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mining companies, geotechnical and engineering consultancies, insurers and infrastructure owners that must assess ground stability and site risk
problem: Engineers who sign off on site safety must manually hunt through consultant, contractor and monitoring reports; early on the company sold satellite ground deformation monitoring to mines.
business_model: B2B software subscription and monitoring services; started as satellite monitoring studies and moved to the TRAIL AI platform
product_category: Satellite InSAR monitoring and AI risk analysis for mines and infrastructure
competitors_at_founding: TRE Altamira; Descartes Labs; Sixense (Atlas InSAR)
market_need_then: Mine and tailings safety carries regulatory and safety consequences; satellite InSAR for mining was an established method before 2022, per industry sources.
outcome_analysis: KorrAI is active with about 20 people and works with large mining and insurance customers, including Zurich and AWS per its site. Disclosed funding is small, around 1.6M in 2022 plus grants, and a 2026 article says it is raising a seed round. It moved from satellite monitoring services to an AI platform called TRAIL. Domain founders and enterprise customers help, while capital remains limited.

name: Krave Mart

long_description: Krave Mart is the Rappi for Pakistan. We’re an online grocery store that delivers within minutes.

It grew in Karachi, Lahore and Rawalpindi, drew an inDrive investment in December 2024 and was acquired by inDrive in March 2026 with terms undisclosed. name: Kular
one_liner: AI Lead Generator
long_description:
Kular is an AI Lead Generator, generating leads for busy professionals and business owners and only charging for results. Today, Kular generates leads for over 1000 companies via email and LinkedIn. 

Kular is being built by a team of MIT, IIT, Cambridge and Oxford grads, backed by some of the best investors in the world, including Y-Combinator, Entrepreneur First, Acequia Capital and angel investors behind companies like Ironclad, OpenSea and Stripe.

market_need_then: B2B teams spent heavily on outbound tools in 2021, as shown by large rounds at Apollo.io and Outreach; the company claims leads for over 1,000 companies.
outcome_analysis: Kular is listed Active with about 12 people and claims leads for over 1,000 companies on a pay-for-results model. No verified funding round, revenue or exit was found, so its trajectory cannot be judged. The offer sits in a crowded outbound market with low defensibility, where larger funded tools already existed at founding and new AI outbound entrants came after.

name: Lamin

We make it easy to query, trace, and govern R&D data in the age of AI, serving big pharma enterprises, biotech, and academia.

Our core product is an open-source, lineage-native, format-agnostic lakehouse for agents and teams.

name: LanceDB
tags: AIOps; Machine Learning; Open Source; Data Engineering
one_liner: Open-source, serverless vectordb for production-scale generative AI
long_description: LanceDB is a new open-source vector database that can support low-latency billion-scale vector search on a single node. Built around a new columnar data format, LanceDB makes it incredibly easy to build applications for generative AI, recsys, search engines, content moderation, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

market_need_then: Generative AI adoption in 2022-2023 increased demand for vector search; the YC description targets generative AI, recsys, search and moderation. Dated demand figures not found.
outcome_analysis: LanceDB is active, raised an $8M seed in May 2024 and a $30M Series A in June 2025 led by Theory Ventures, with total funding reported around $38-41M. Success factors are the hard Lance format technology, the generative AI tailwind and founders with pandas and ML infrastructure experience; adoption by companies like Netflix and Midjourney shows traction. No exit yet.

name: Landeed
one_liner: Landeed is India’s digital infrastructure for property intelligence,…
long_description:
Landeed is the AI-native digital infrastructure for property intelligence, verification, and transactions in India. We provide read/write rails that transform fragmented property and regulatory systems into continuously verified, machine-interpretable state. Powered by Terra, our proprietary property intelligence engine, Landeed converts messy, multi-source records into structured, queryable knowledge that supports legal-grade due diligence, collateral verification, title search, transfers, and property payments. With coverage across 24 states, enterprises go live nationally from day one. We are trusted by Fortune India 500 companies across BFSI, real estate, and retail.

Landeed is the blue tick for property.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Banks and NBFCs, real estate developers, retailers, law firms and consumers in India who need property records, title checks and registry services

It has moved from a consumer records app to enterprise APIs and AI title reports used by banks and developers, helped by repeat founders from GoLorry and a messy, high-need records market.

name: Layerup

name: Lenk

name: Levers

product_category: Legal AI assistants
founder_names: Pedro Jahara; Pedro Calderon; Guilherme Delai; Lucas Kawazoi

name: Lotus

Lotus is an open-core pricing and billing engine. We enable API companies to automate their custom usage-based pricing for any metric. Rather than guess on how to charge their customers, Lotus provides companies with powerful new tools from metering to invoicing to testing new pricing.

name: Lovage

It later pivoted to Lumibot automation and then to manufacturing video AI, so the original job platform story did not become the lasting business. It remains active with a team of 12; whether the pivot succeeded is not yet visible in public data.

name: LunaJoy Health
tags: Mental Health Tech; Digital Health; Femtech
one_liner: AI-powered scalable infrastructure + mental health services, starting…
long_description:
LunaJoy is building the AI-powered care platform for precision mental health—starting with women.
We integrate intelligent automation with specialized clinical services to deliver scalable, life-stage-specific care—from adolescence to pregnancy, postpartum, infertility, miscarriage, perimenopause, and aging. By embedding AI agents into care navigation, triage, and decision support, we reduce costs, accelerate outcomes, and personalize treatment at scale.

Our hybrid care model blends targeted psychotherapy, psychiatric medication management, genetic testing, coaching, and holistic wellness—delivered by a curated workforce of women’s mental health specialists. Through continuous feedback loops, AI segmentation, and predictive insights, LunaJoy is built to scale.

We’re expanding our in-network footprint to make this care accessible across commercial and Medicaid populations—closing equity gaps for women of color, LGBTQ+ individuals, and those most at risk.

Women are twice as likely to experience mental health conditions, and 3x more likely to endure trauma. Yet the system is still built for the “average” patient—ignoring the biological, emotional, and social complexity of women’s lives. LunaJoy is rearchitecting that system with AI at its core—because when we invest in women’s mental health, entire communities thrive.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Women seeking therapy and psychiatric care, paid via insurers, employers and provider partners
problem: Women's mental health needs across life stages, such as perinatal and postpartum, are poorly served by generic providers; LunaJoy offers a virtual clinic with specialists.
business_model: Virtual clinic billing insurance payers, plus employer and provider partnerships
product_category: Women's virtual mental health care
market_need_then: The founders started after their own postpartum depression experiences and launched the telehealth clinic in October 2021 (Florida Trend, February 2023); virtual mental health demand was elevated in 2021.
outcome_analysis: LunaJoy is a clinician-founded virtual clinic for women's mental health that raised a $2.4M seed in January 2023 and $4.2M in April 2024 alongside the LunaCare launch. It grew to over 15 payers and a dozen-plus states by 2024 and remains active. Funding is modest and no later round was found, so the outcome is still open.

long_description: Lyra is a crypto-native virtual card provider that allows users to easily create cards and fund them with cryptocurrency. Create virtual cards directly from your browser through our Chrome extension for all your purchases and subscriptions.

target_customer: Crypto holders who want to spend crypto at online merchants that only accept cards

outcome_analysis: Lyra launched Visa virtual cards funded with crypto in August 2022 as a three-person S22 team, entering a segment that Crypto.com, Wirex, Uphold, BitPay and Coinbase already served. No funding round, traction or exit is publicly confirmed, and its official domain no longer serves the product when fetched, so the outcome is unknown. The 2022 crypto downturn is a plausible headwind but no source states it.

name: Magna
one_liner: Carta for Web3: token vesting and DeFi investment management.
long_description:
Magna is building a platform to turn DeFi investments into financial primitives. Our first product is Carta for Web3, where companies can manage their cap tables and distribute their token equity to employees, advisors, or investors. We’re also building investor infrastructure for institutions to custody investments with on-chain execution and intelligence. Our ultimate goal is to use locked tokens as composable building blocks to power collateralized lending, liquid secondary markets, and other DeFi applications.

Launching a token? Let's chat. Are you receiving tokens from your investments? We can also be helpful.


What are our companies saying about the problem?

> Having it all bundled together would make life easier. We have a million things to do. If you have an off-the-shelf thing, we’d use it.
> This wouldn’t be a nice to have, it’d be a have to have.
> Terrible process. We’re manually sending out transactions, going to solscan and manually check that they received our token. Takes hours every week.
> Everything we do is potentially very dangerous. We have to check it thoroughly. I’ve spent several hours a day on this since launch. I imagine every month, it’ll take us at least 1-2 days.
> Manual process every month for the ops team. They likely burn a week.... every month to pay out 150+ addresses.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Crypto projects and token issuers distributing vested tokens to employees, investors and advisors, plus investors receiving tokens
problem: Token vesting and distribution was done by hand with spreadsheets and manual transactions, taking ops teams days each month and carrying the risk of costly errors.
business_model: B2B SaaS for token vesting, claims and distribution, with custody and on-chain execution services
product_category: Web3 token management and cap table software
market_need_then: Founders interviewed for the YC pitch described hours or days of manual work each month to pay out token holders, and the 2021 to 2022 token boom produced many projects with vesting obligations.
outcome_analysis: Magna rode the 2022 token boom into a 15 million dollar seed at a reported 70 million dollar valuation and became a standard tool for token vesting, claiming 160 plus projects and a 60 billion dollar peak value locked. It survived the crypto downturn and was acquired by Payward, Kraken's parent, in February 2026, continuing as a standalone brand. Terms were not disclosed.

product_category: Digital wealth management and retirement in Pakistan

name: Malama Health
tags: Health Tech; Digital Health; Healthcare; Femtech
one_liner: Making motherhood safe, not scary
long_description:
Malama offers doula-led holistic support during and after pregnancy at no cost to patients. Malama is in-network with Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, Anthem, Kaiser, and several Medicaid Managed Care Plans. 

Malama is backed by the Stanford d.school, Y Combinator (S22), Alpine Investors and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Medicaid health plans and health systems paying for doula-led maternity support, serving pregnant and postpartum Medicaid members at no cost to them
problem: Medicaid mothers face poor maternal outcomes and gaps in follow-up; Malama pairs doula-care navigators with a gestational diabetes app and insurer contracts.
business_model: B2B2C care services reimbursed by insurers and Medicaid managed care plans, plus grants
product_category: Doula-led maternal care and digital diabetes-in-pregnancy support
founder_names: Mika Eddy; Orlando Li; Daniela Bahamon Arango; Shalmali Bane
market_need_then: The founders' project began at a Stanford biodesign course around gestational diabetes; the company cites poor outcomes among Medicaid mothers and the launch post for a diabetes-in-pregnancy app described real patient need.
outcome_analysis: Malama began from a Stanford biodesign project on diabetes in pregnancy and grew into a Medicaid-first doula care model with about 35 staff, in-network contracts and a randomized trial result. It was slow to raise institutional money: the first sizable priced round found is a 9.2M seed in March 2026, after a 2.4M NIH grant in 2025. It is active and growing but remains early stage.

long_description:
Marathon Education provides live interactive tutoring classes to K-12 students in Vietnam, we're the fastest-growing edtech player disrupting the $5bn offline tutoring market by allowing students to learn online with the best teachers in large-class or small-class format.

The company is founded by Duc, former education private equity investor at TPG Capital - where Duc invested in K-12 education and edtech businesses in Vietnam & Southeast Asia. name: Markaz Technologies
one_liner: Reselling marketplace for social media entrepreneurs in Pakistan
long_description:
We enable WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram-based micro-entrepreneurs to source wholesale products from across Pakistan. Our marketplace enables these micro-entrepreneurs to start their business without any investment while we facilitate them by offering their customers a great experience. We do this by taking care of their delivery operations, payments, and customer services. 

Pakistan is one of the youngest populations globally and is expected to become the 7th largest consumer market by 2030. Our vision is empowering 5 M + people, especially women, to start their businesses while working from home and supercharging the eCommerce rails of Pakistan.
regions: Pakistan; South Asia
target_customer: Pakistani micro-entrepreneurs selling over WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, and their end customers
problem: Social media sellers in Pakistan lack wholesale sourcing, delivery, payments and customer service; Markaz provides these so they can resell without upfront investment.
business_model: Reselling marketplace earning margin and fees on wholesale orders, with cash on delivery fulfilment
product_category: Social commerce reselling marketplace
founder_names: Umair Aslam; Shoaib Khan; Sameel Hayat; Fawad Hussain
market_need_then: Pakistan has a young population and heavy WhatsApp and Instagram commerce; investors funded several social commerce startups in late 2021 and 2022, such as Zarya and DealCart.
outcome_analysis: Markaz is a four-founder Islamabad team that raised a 2.4M seed led by Indus Valley Capital in May 2022 and grew to about 55 staff. It rides a real shift to social commerce in Pakistan, and its site now describes a broader marketplace. No Series A, layoffs or exit were found; the funding gap since 2022 means the later path is unclear.

name: Massdriver
one_liner: Internal developer platform for Terraform, OpenTofu and Helm
long_description:
Massdriver is an internal developer platform and platform orchestrator. Platform teams publish the Terraform, OpenTofu, and Helm they already write to a catalog; developers and AI agents provision from it with policy enforced before every deploy. Self-hosted or managed.

Platform teams encode their security, compliance, and cost requirements into the modules once. Developers and AI agents pick from the catalog, policy runs before anything is created, and every deploy is recorded with who proposed and who approved it.

Massdriver generates an ephemeral pipeline per deploy, so there are no standing CI/CD pipelines to maintain. Run it self-hosted, on-prem, or in your cloud.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Platform and DevOps teams at companies that want developers to self-serve cloud infrastructure
problem: Developers wait on ops for cloud infrastructure while ops teams struggle to enforce standards; Massdriver packages Terraform modules into a catalog with policy and diagrams.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with managed and self-hosted options
product_category: Internal developer platform and platform orchestrator for infrastructure as code
founder_names: Cory O'Daniel; Chris Hill; Dave Williams
market_need_then: In 2022 companies were adopting Terraform and Kubernetes widely, and platform engineering was emerging; the company reported six-figure ARR and about 35 organizations soon after its March 2022 soft launch.
outcome_analysis: Massdriver is an infrastructure-as-code platform founded by experienced cloud operators that reported six-figure ARR within months of its March 2022 launch. It raised a 4M seed in 2022 and an 8M Series Seed in August 2023 led by Builders VC, and it remains a small active team. It competes in a crowded platform engineering market with strong incumbents, so scale is unproven.

name: Materee
one_liner: E-commerce platform for construction materials in Indonesia
long_description:
Materee is an e-commerce platform for construction materials in Indonesia. 

Construction is one of the most important industries in Indonesia. Despite its importance, procuring raw materials for construction work involves many phone calls, text messages, as well as back and forth communications. Materee aims to transform and simplify construction material procurement process while assisting contractors to focus on the most important activity, completing their projects.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Contractors and construction material stores in Indonesia that buy raw construction materials
problem: Procuring construction materials in Indonesia relies on many phone calls, text messages and back and forth, with manual price and stock checks, expensive credit, poor delivery visibility and out of stock items caused by a fragmented value chain.
business_model: B2B marketplace with product margin or commission, plus planned buyer credit and manufacturer demand planning
product_category: B2B e-commerce for construction materials
market_need_then: The YC launch post describes manual price and stock checks, costly credit and unreliable delivery in a fragmented Indonesian construction supply chain. Construction is described as one of the most important Indonesian industries.
outcome_analysis: Materee is active as of the sources found. Founders came from GudangAda, BCG's construction practice and Kargo Tech, which gave domain and engineering credibility. It raised a reported 3 million USD seed in June 2023 from Alpha JWC, January Capital and YC, in a year when several Indonesian construction materials marketplaces raised rounds. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found; outcome remains open.

name: Material Depot
one_liner: India's Fastest Growing Home Decor destination for Floor & Wall Decor
long_description: Material Depot is reimagining home interiors for the next generation of Indian homeowners. We bring design-forward materials: tiles, laminates, wall panels & more - straight from manufacturers to customers, cutting out the old, broken supply chain. Our online engagement fuels real-time trend insights, enabling us to launch new designs faster, in smaller batches, and at unbeatable prices. The result: beautiful homes built smarter, quicker, and more affordably. With over 10,000 homes served and a rapidly growing digital-first ecosystem, Material Depot isn’t just selling materials—we’re building the future of how India designs and lives.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Indian homeowners and contractors buying floor and wall materials (tiles, laminates, wall panels)
problem: Home decor materials go through layered traditional distribution, so prices are high and design choice is slow to refresh.
business_model: online direct-from-manufacturer ecommerce marketplace plus offline experience centres
product_category: home decor materials ecommerce (India)
market_need_then: YC page says it has served over 10,000 homes (company claim). Reported revenue Rs 13.7 Cr in FY24, up 89.5% from Rs 7.2 Cr in FY23 (Inc42 profile), which shows demand grew after founding.
outcome_analysis: Material Depot (Winter 2022, Active) grew into a team of about 50 with revenue of Rs 7.2 Cr in FY23 and Rs 13.7 Cr in FY24, then raised a 10M USD Series A co-led by Accel and Stellaris in February 2026, about four years after YC. It combined a digital catalogue with offline experience centres in Bengaluru; the main caveat is that profitability is unknown and earlier rounds are only partly documented.

name: MaverickX
one_liner: Engineering the future of chemistry for natural resource extraction
long_description:
MaverickX is a chemical technology company advancing natural resource extraction. The company was founded by Eric Herrera, former Department of Defense scientist,  and Jesse Evans, former startup operations manager. 

As resources become more difficult to extract across the energy and mining sectors, new technologies are needed. MaverickX has a portfolio of chemical solutions -- PetroX and LithX -- to enhance recovery of oil from shale reservoirs and metals from low-grade ores. 

More oil. More metal. Better chemistry.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Oil and gas operators (shale producers) and mining companies that need better recovery of hydrocarbons and metals
problem: Only about 20 percent of oil in unconventional shale wells is recovered and operating costs are rising, while metals in low grade ores are costly to extract.
business_model: Chemical products sold to operators and miners, with pilot programs, field trials and production scale manufacturing in Texas
product_category: Specialty chemistry for natural resource extraction (PetroX, LithX, HydroX)
market_need_then: The launch post cites low shale recovery of about 20 percent and a projected 40 percent rise in operating costs over a decade, and a Department of Energy request to turn old oil wells into mines led to the discovery.
outcome_analysis: MaverickX began in mining chemistry and extended to oil and gas after a Department of Energy project showed the chemistry freed hydrocarbons. It stayed small for about three years, then raised a reported 19 million USD seed in April 2025 and a strategic investment from Chord Energy in May 2026, opened a Texas production facility in April 2026, and remains active with no exit.

business_model: Clinic partnerships and insurance-reimbursed care programs (per YC page and company site); earlier telemedicine expert-consult platform
product_category: Preventive care / longevity health services

No funding beyond YC's investment, no exit and no layoffs were found, so there is no sourced outcome yet; the stage and traction are unknown.

name: Mercator
one_liner: AI-assisted data analytics
long_description: Mercator is your AI-assisted data analytics platform for writing faster, cheaper, and smarter SQL. Co-founders Andrew and Dayton met on the Instacart data science team. Dayton earned a physics PhD at UC Berkeley before entering DS. Andrew spent six years as a SWE at Uber, where he developed pydeck, a geospatial data visualization library with over 12M downloads. Mercator is backed by Y Combinator, Tribe Capital, Soma Capital, Valor Equity Partners, Amplify Partners, and Rebel Fund.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data teams and analysts writing SQL (B2B)
problem: Writing SQL and analyzing data is slow and costly; generative AI could write it faster.
business_model: B2B SaaS (AI SQL editor, Dubo)
product_category: AI-assisted data analytics / text-to-SQL
market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand was found in sources; the premise was that generative AI could cut the cost of writing SQL, and the founders came from Instacart data science and Uber.
outcome_analysis: Mercator joined YC in S22 with two founders, built Dubo and published a record-setting Dubo-SQL paper, and pivoted to an SQL editor in March 2024. YC lists it as Inactive and a co-founder's profile describes it in the past tense, but no shutdown announcement, funding amount or cause is public, so the cause of the failure is not public.

name: Metriport
tags: B2B; Digital Health; Healthcare; API; AI
one_liner: Healthcare data infrastructure for next generation care delivery.
long_description:
Metriport provides real-time access to medical data for 340 million individuals across the US. Its open-source platform turns scattered patient records across all major healthcare IT systems into structured information that gives clinicians what they need, exactly when they need it, to provide the best possible care. 

Metriport manages dozens of connections across all national HIEs and QHINs, state and regional HIEs, ADT networks, pharmacies, labs, and EHRs. It then matches, extracts, standardizes, deduplicates, and enriches records, and converts them into a unified data model, accessible through a single API, data warehouse, or apps directly within an EHR.

In addition to providing longitudinal patient clinical data at the point of care, Metriport offers ambient monitoring, alerting providers in real time as patients are moved through the healthcare system to assist with transitions of care. Metriport also delivers insights on top of the data, like AI medical record summarization, condition suspecting, and surfacing care gaps.

Founded in 2022 and headquartered in San Francisco, Metriport processes 4.2 billion network requests a month and returns the first structured record in under 15 seconds. Teams across care delivery, value-based programs, and health tech platforms build on Metriport, including Amazon One Medical, Strive Health, Color, Sollis Health, and Canvas Medical.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Digital health companies, providers and payers that need patient medical records and health data through one API
problem: Patient records are scattered across health information exchanges, EHRs, labs and pharmacies, and each digital health company had to build and maintain these connections itself.
business_model: API and platform subscription with usage pricing, open source core, plus AI summarization and monitoring products
product_category: Healthcare data infrastructure and interoperability API
market_need_then: Digital health companies repeatedly rebuilt record retrieval; the 2022 launch coincided with push toward national exchange networks. By 2026 the company reports Amazon One Medical, Color and Sollis Health as customers.
outcome_analysis: Metriport raised a 2.4 million dollar seed on post money SAFEs at a stated 20 million valuation in December 2022, shifted from a wearables API to clinical record retrieval in 2023, and by 2026 had a 29 person team, named healthcare customers and a 26 million Series A led by Matrix. The company is active and growing, with the open source posture and exchange network connections as its main assets.

name: Midplane
tags: Generative AI; B2B; Productivity; Data Engineering; AI
one_liner: The safety layer between AI agents and your database
long_description: Companies are connecting AI coding agents like Cursor and Claude directly to their databases — where one wrong command can delete data or leak customer records. Midplane sits in between and controls what each agent is allowed to do: it blocks dangerous queries, hides sensitive data, and keeps a record of everything the agent touches. It’s open source, and runs either as a hosted service or on your own servers.
regions: Germany; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering and data teams that connect AI coding agents and assistants (Cursor, Claude) to production Postgres databases
problem: Connecting AI agents directly to databases risks destructive queries and leaks of customer records. Midplane checks each SQL statement against policy, hides sensitive fields and logs activity.
business_model: Open source (MIT) gateway with a paid hosted Midplane Cloud tier adding team approvals, SSO and shared rules
product_category: AI agent database access control (MCP gateway for Postgres)
market_need_then: No evidence of demand in mid 2022 was found for the current product. The YC page lists earlier launches by the founders (IvyCheck) around text classification and prompt injection protection, so the present description reflects a later period.
outcome_analysis: Midplane is a two person Berlin team of former Amazon scientists that is active as of the sources found. Its current product, an open source safety gateway between AI agents and Postgres, fits a recent agent adoption wave, but no funding beyond YC, no revenue and no customers were found, so the outcome is too early and too thinly documented to call.

name: Miggos
one_liner: Wholesale marketplace for mom & pop clothing shops in LATAM
long_description:
Miggos is a wholesale marketplace for the 5 million+ mom & pop clothing shops in Latin America.

We're on a mission to make the lives of these mom & pop store owners in Latin America easier, connecting brands and manufacturers to small retailers and facilitating the entire process of purchasing, selecting, and discovering new products, credit, logistics, and service.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mom and pop clothing retailers in Latin America (about 5 million shops per the company) and the brands and manufacturers selling to them
problem: Small clothing retailers buy wholesale through fragmented, manual channels with limited credit and logistics. Miggos connects brands to retailers and handles purchasing, discovery, credit, logistics and service.
business_model: Wholesale marketplace with take rate plus credit and logistics services
product_category: B2B wholesale marketplace for fashion retail
