market_need_then: The YC description cites more than 5 million mom and pop clothing shops in Latin America, and the company's own job posting cites about a 220 billion dollar annual market. No independent demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Miggos remains listed as active with a team of 20 as of the YC page, but no press, funding amounts or traction figures were found, and the company site could not be loaded. The Latin American wholesale marketplace space drew several funded rivals in 2022, so the outcome is unclear and not a documented success or failure.

name: Mintlify
one_liner: The intelligent documentation platform
long_description: Self-updating documentation for startups, enterprises, and agents.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software companies, startups, enterprises and AI agent builders that need developer and API documentation
problem: Writing documentation is hard and hosting and maintaining the platform is harder. Mintlify offers markdown based docs with analytics, search and AI features, later self-updating docs for agents.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers with a free plan, enterprise plan with self-hosting
product_category: Documentation platform for developers
market_need_then: The YC launch post says writing documentation is hard and building the hosting platform is harder, and claims users see about 40 percent higher conversion. No independent demand data from 2022 was opened.
outcome_analysis: Mintlify is a clear success so far. It raised a 2.8 million USD seed in May 2022 with a three person team, an 18 million Series A led by a16z in September 2024, and a 45 million Series B at a reported 500 million USD valuation in April 2026. It reports documentation for more than 20,000 companies, with growth driven by AI agents reading docs, and it acquired Helicone in March 2026.

name: Mistle
one_liner: Open source background agents
long_description: Mistle is the open source alternative to Stripe Minions, Ramp Inspect and Shopify River. Instead of spending months building an internal platform, teams use Mistle to run collaborative background agents from day one.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Momento
one_liner: Building a full-stack auto insurer for the underserved in LatAm
long_description:
In Momento we are going through a challenging regulatory process to become a fully-licensed insurance carrier. By doing so, we will be able to underwrite risk, set prices and, ultimately, become owners of the product.

Once approved, around summer 22, we will be in a great position to size the $13bn untapped opportunity of +30 Mn uninsured vehicles – just in Mexico! As we will be able to attack the main pain points in the market: i) antiquated underwriting models and ii) payment conditions only adapted for the affluent.

To succeed, we have assembled an elite team with both innovative and experienced profiles. We are three cofounders, two ex-McKinsey and one ex-P&G, and we managed to attract two heavyweights of the Mexican insurance industry: the previous CUO of Zurich Mexico and the previous CFO and VP of Finance of ING and AXA Mexico.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Underserved Mexican car owners, including rideshare drivers, who lack affordable auto insurance
problem: Mexico has tens of millions of uninsured vehicles because underwriting models are outdated and payment terms suit only affluent buyers. Momento became a licensed carrier to underwrite risk and price digitally.
business_model: Licensed auto insurance carrier selling policies through a mobile app and brokers, with monthly payments from 249 MXN
product_category: Digital auto insurance carrier (insurtech)
founder_names: Lois Rogel Vence; Leon Bartolome Carreno; Andres Guerrero Alvarez
market_need_then: The launch post cites over 30 million uninsured vehicles in Mexico and a 13 billion dollar untapped opportunity, with antiquated underwriting and payment terms for the affluent as pain points. Figures are the company's own.
outcome_analysis: Momento took roughly a year longer than its stated summer 2022 target to obtain a carrier license, then launched in August 2023 with a 10.5 million USD seed and raised a 10 million Series A in August 2025 with more than 10,000 active customers claimed. It is active, regulated by the CNSF and rated by AM Best, so it is a slow but advancing regulated business.

name: Moneco
one_liner: Neobank for African migrants in Europe
long_description: Moneco is a neobank targeting the migrant communities in Europe, starting with the African diaspora. We are making banking easier and more affordable for underserved communities, starting with a current account, a payment card and free remittances. The long term vision is to turn Moneco into a one-stop-shop where all of their financial needs will be addressed.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: African migrants and diaspora in Europe, plus freelancers, e-merchants and small importers who move money between Europe, the US and Africa
problem: Migrants face costly remittances and poor access to European bank accounts. Moneco offers a euro account, a card and low cost transfers aimed at them.
business_model: Consumer fintech app: card interchange, FX and remittance fees
product_category: Neobank and remittance app for diaspora
founder_names: Shams Radjabaly; Bilal Dahlab; Kuassi Jimmy Kumako
market_need_then: The YC page frames migrants as underserved with expensive banking and remittances. No dated spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Moneco is still active with a team of about 15. Funding evidence is thin and conflicting, including a small Wefunder crowdfunding raise in 2025, which suggests slow capital progress. No shutdown or exit was found, so the outcome is unresolved and the license and distribution questions remain open.

name: Mono
one_liner: Embedded finance infrastructure for LatAm enterprises.
long_description: Mono provides an API-first platform that lets any company in LatAm offer financial capabilities, wallets, real-time payouts (Bre-B), Visa cards, and multi-rail bank transfer without becoming a fintech.
regions: Colombia; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: LatAm companies, starting with Colombian startups and SMEs, that move recurring high volume money (payouts, wallets, cards)
problem: Opening business bank accounts and moving money in Colombia was slow and hard for startups; Mono started as a business account and became embedded finance infrastructure.
business_model: API-first embedded finance: fees on payins, payouts, card and wallet usage
product_category: Embedded finance infrastructure
founder_names: Salomon Zarruk; Sebastian Ortiz; Juan Camilo Poveda; Jose Tomas Lobo
market_need_then: TechCrunch (June 2022): founders describe the pain of opening business accounts; 300 customers and $1M payment volume by March 2022.
outcome_analysis: Mono is active with about 30 people. It raised a $6M seed from Tiger Global in 2022 and later repositioned from SME banking to infrastructure, joining Bre-B in 2025 and claiming over $2B processed. The CEO changed from Zarruk to Poveda. Later rounds were not verified, so the funding picture is partial.

name: Monterey AI
one_liner: Turn user feedback to product insights
long_description: Monterey AI helps companies understand what actions to take to improve engagement and reduce churn by setting up user feedback channels, auto-collecting, and analyzing qualitative feedback and quantitative data from multiple sources.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product, support and customer teams at software companies
problem: Customer feedback is scattered across calls, emails, chats and surveys; Monterey aggregates and analyzes it into product actions to cut churn.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: AI customer feedback analytics
market_need_then: Not evidenced by a dated source; the product ties to the long-standing problem of scattered feedback, and Monterey's own docs philosophy page frames it that way.
outcome_analysis: Monterey AI was a small Summer 2022 YC team led by Chun Jiang that built feedback analytics and was acquired by Reforge around January 2025, becoming Reforge Insight Analytics. Terms and funding are not public, so it is unclear whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing; the founder moved into a Reforge product lead role. A later vendor guide says the standalone Insights product is being wound down after Miro bought Reforge in 2026, which is unverified.

name: Morf Health
one_liner: Workflow automation for healthcare providers
long_description:
Morf is an integration platform that allows healthcare providers to sync patient data and automate workflows across their tools. For example, when a patient submits an intake form, Morf creates a patient record in an EHR and sends insurance information for an eligibility check. You can think about it like Segment + Zapier for healthcare providers.

Morf helps their customers eliminate tedious administrative tasks and empowers them to focus on patient care as they grow.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Digital health and telehealth practices that need to sync patient data across EHR and other tools
problem: Healthcare providers manually move patient data between intake forms, EHRs and insurance checks.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a free tier
product_category: Healthcare integration and workflow automation
market_need_then: Founders cite problems faced at Parsley Health; the pitch is Segment plus Zapier for providers.
outcome_analysis: Morf is active and raised a $3M seed in November 2023 led by Kindred Ventures, about 16 months after the batch. It now sells to digital health practices with an AI workflow builder. No exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is still developing.

name: MosaicVoice
one_liner: We make it simple for call centers to automate quality assurance.
long_description: MosaicVoice makes it easy for call centers to automate their Quality Assurance function. Our software listens to customer conversations in real-time and identifies and alerts agents and managers to any compliance violations as they happen
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Oakland, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and mid size contact centers, especially healthcare, utilities, hospitality and BPO
problem: Manual call quality assurance covers few calls and misses compliance breaches.
business_model: B2B SaaS for contact centers
product_category: Contact center AI, real time agent assist and automated QA
market_need_then: Founder's prior consulting and banking work in call centers is the stated insight; no dated spend data found.
outcome_analysis: MosaicVoice is alive and listed by aggregators as a small private company with about 11 employees. No funding announcement or exit was found. Aggregators disagree on raised capital. The story is a slow bootstrapped path without verifiable traction metrics.

name: MovingLake
tags: SaaS; B2B; Analytics; API; Data Engineering
one_liner: Realtime Data Connectors
long_description: MovingLake is Fivetran for event-driven architectures. Companies such as Casai use our product to obtain orders and price changes in real time.
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software teams at hospitality and ecommerce firms that need real time data from ERPs, CRMs and property systems
problem: Getting real time events from third party systems into warehouses and services requires custom connectors.
business_model: B2B SaaS flat monthly fee per a listing
product_category: Real time API integration and ETL
market_need_then: YC page says customer Casai uses it for real time orders and price changes; no broader spend data found.
outcome_analysis: MovingLake is active with a team of three and shows no public funding beyond YC. It serves hospitality and ecommerce customers and added an AI data insights product. With no verified rounds or traction metrics, the outcome is unresolved.

name: Munily
one_liner: Access control management app for Latam´s gated communities
long_description:
There are three key roles among a community:

The security Guard
The resident 
The administrator 


When a visitor tries to access a designated community, the security guard must require an ID previously to allow entry. 

He proceeds to communicate with a specific resident through a intercom which is almost always broken or under repair, delaying the visitor’s entry to the compound 


WE come in, by interconnecting the security guard with the resident and the administrators through an app and a tablet we provide to make all the process of access pretty smooth and easy.


When a visitor comes in, the security guard must only:

Take a picture of its ID, using the tablet, 
Select the apartment, so the resident receives a pop up notification through which they can deny or approve the access. 

Last but not least, An even easier way has been developed by Munily which utilizes QR codes generated through Whatsapp. Which visitors just show and security guards scan to allow entry.
regions: Panama; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Property administrators and security companies running gated communities and buildings in Latin America
problem: Gated community access, visitor control and administration are manual and paper based.
business_model: B2B SaaS per community
product_category: Proptech access control and community management
founder_names: Khaled Alhaj; Marwa Hage; Mitchell Contreras; Carlos de la Guardia
market_need_then: Forbes Colombia Dec 2021: targeting 2000 communities by Q1 2022; no spend data.
outcome_analysis: Munily is active, claims 950 plus properties and 190K residents across several countries, and has about 30 staff. Funding is small and sources conflict, which fits a capital efficient regional business. Traction numbers are company claims only.

name: MySivi
one_liner: MySivi - AI English Speaking Practice App
long_description:
MySivi is an AI-powered English learning app.

Learn English Speaking The Fastest Way (AI + Human) 😀
Practicing with AI English Tutor and Human is the fastest way to learn to speak. Try now to feel the change within a week.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: English learners in India and emerging markets who want speaking practice
problem: Learners lack affordable speaking practice with feedback.
business_model: Consumer subscription app
product_category: AI English speaking tutor
founder_names: Akshay Sanghai; Shivam Gupta; Anoop Jaiswal
market_need_then: No dated demand evidence was found; the founders targeted Indian learners who want affordable English speaking practice.
outcome_analysis: MySivi is active and Inc42 reports over 1 million downloads and 200K monthly users. Its YC page says it raised minimal funding, so it appears capital light. Revenue and funding claims are unverified.

name: Myria
one_liner: A marketplace of luxury services for the ultra-wealthy
long_description:
Myria is a private community and concierge for off-market goods & services — the things you can't Google. 

Ultra-high net worth individuals spend $390 billion per year ($1.3 million each) on lifestyle, but they still struggle to find everything they want. Why?

Because the best of any category — homes, boats, restaurant reservations — the best stuff is never listed online. Likewise, the best people don’t need the internet to find a new client or job. 

The best is always off-market.  Myria is the Off-Marketplace. 

Myria helps off-market sellers reach the nicest and wealthiest buyers. In turn, we help the world’s most successful people access the best of everything, give back, and get the most out of life. 

If it’s off-market, it’s on Myria!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Ultra high net worth individuals seeking off market luxury goods and services
problem: Wealthy buyers cannot easily find trusted off market experiences and services.
business_model: Membership marketplace and concierge
product_category: Private luxury marketplace
market_need_then: Launch press release March 2022 limited to 1,000 members with KYC checks; no spend data.
outcome_analysis: Myria launched in March 2022 with a 1,000 member cap and remains active. A reported $20M Series B in 2025 appears only on PitchBook, so it is unverified. Funding totals conflict widely across aggregators.

name: NFTScoring
one_liner: The NFT exchange for traders
long_description: All NFT liquidity in a single exchange. Designed with pro traders in mind.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Namecard.ai
one_liner: AI-powered business matchmaking
long_description:
In the fast-paced world of business, your success often hinges on who you know. But finding the right people to grow your business shouldn't be left to chance or countless hours of networking.

At Namecard.ai, we're transforming how businesses connect and grow. We harness the power of generative AI to understand your unique business DNA - your goals, challenges, strengths, and needs. We then connect you with the right people who can truly catalyze your growth.
regions: Taiwan; East Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Professionals, founders and event organizers who want warm introductions and pre-scheduled meetings (individual subscriptions and per-event conference pricing)
problem: Finding the right people to meet for business is left to chance, cold outreach and conference wandering. Namecard.ai uses AI to match people by stated needs and offers.
business_model: Freemium SaaS: free tier, $49 per month Professional plan, per-event conference pricing of $199 to $299 (company site)
product_category: AI professional networking and event matchmaking
market_need_then: Conference and networking matchmaking was an established category before 2022, and the company site cites low cold email response rates as the pain.
outcome_analysis: Namecard.ai is listed as active with a small team. The YC launch post describes the Web3 background check product Chainsight, and the company site now names Chainsight Pte. Ltd. as the operator, so the team appears to have moved from crypto risk checks to AI networking. No exit, shutdown or layoff was found, and public funding information for Namecard.ai itself is absent, so the trajectory is unclear.

name: Nara
tags: Sales; Customer Service; Customer Support; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Answer 70% of your support and sales questions. Instantly
long_description: We make it easy for small and medium businesses to build an AI sales agents for their websites and social media, augmenting their sales capacity. This assistant provides personalized shopping recommendations to customers and is available 24/7 to answer their questions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and medium online merchants, especially Shopify stores, paying for an AI sales and support assistant
problem: Small merchants cannot staff 24/7 sales and support, so shoppers leave with unanswered questions and no product guidance.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an AI sales assistant embedded on websites and social channels
product_category: AI sales and customer support assistant
founder_names: Felipe Abello; Oscar Rojas; Angela Castillo
market_need_then: Merchants wanted automated answers and product recommendations, but no dated evidence of paid demand was found in sources.
outcome_analysis: Nara was a three person AI sales assistant for small merchants, renamed from Helloguru, that was acquired by an unnamed buyer. Neither the buyer, date, price nor funding history is public in the sources found, so the reason for the exit, whether a soft landing or a real product acquisition, is not known.

name: Nash
tags: Banking as a Service; FinOps; Fintech; B2B
one_liner: All in one finance platform for borderless businesses in Africa
long_description:
Nash enables finance teams to manage all their finance flows in one place and craft their money flow experiences globally.  Our ledger-based operating system allows your borderless business to connect all your money accounts, accounting systems, payment service providers, treasury operations, spend management in one place. 

Our mission is to enable borderless commerce in Africa. We achieve this initially by providing your team with all the finance tools needed to build, scale, and grow your borderless business without the need for a costly and complex in-house infrastructure.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Nairobi, Nairobi County, Kenya
regions: United States of America; Kenya; America / Canada; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Finance teams at borderless African businesses that move money across accounts, payment providers and currencies
problem: Finance teams in African cross border businesses juggle many bank accounts, payment service providers and accounting tools without one ledger. Nash offers a ledger based finance operating system to connect them.
business_model: B2B SaaS finance platform (pricing not found)
product_category: Finance operations and treasury software for Africa
market_need_then: The YC description states a mission of enabling borderless commerce in Africa. No quantified demand evidence was found in sources opened.
outcome_analysis: Nash joined YC in Winter 2022 with a solo founder from finance backgrounds. The YC directory still lists it as active, but its website domain now redirects to a domain sale page, which suggests the product may no longer operate, though no shutdown report was found. Funding is only seen on aggregators, so the trajectory is unknown and no cause of failure can be asserted.

name: National Finance Olympiad
one_liner: The SAT of Financial Education in India.
long_description:
NFO is building India’s financial education platform for students.

We make financial education structured, engaging and competitive through age-appropriate curricula, AI-proctored assessments and nationally recognised certification. Our platform enables schools to introduce financial education without adding to their academic workload, while giving students a measurable way to learn, apply and demonstrate financial knowledge.

We’re building toward a future where financial education is a standard part of every Indian student’s education.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Indian schools and parents of students in Grades 5 to 12, who pay for olympiad registration, study toolkits and handbooks
problem: Indian students get little structured financial education. NFO runs a national competition with curricula, proctored assessments and certification that schools can adopt without extra workload.
business_model: Consumer and school fees for olympiad registration, toolkits and handbooks (company site)
product_category: Financial education and competitions
founder_names: Mitul Mehta; Shiv Bidani; Balaji R
market_need_then: A survey by the company of 1,333 students in 2021 found only 16.7 percent met a basic financial literacy benchmark, which it used to argue demand (reported in press).
outcome_analysis: The team started as Streak, a teen neobank that raised an undisclosed seed in July 2021 led by Inflection Point Ventures, and used a financial literacy quiz as a growth engine. The olympiad grew to over 100 schools in its first two editions and the site now claims 500 plus schools. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, so the company appears to be a small active education business with undisclosed economics.

name: NearWave
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; SaaS; Medical Devices; AI
one_liner: Helping physicians select the right therapy for breast cancer patients
long_description: NearWave makes a handheld imaging device that helps physicians select the right therapy for their breast cancer patients. This prevents patients from suffering through months of side effects caused by unsuccessful treatments.
all_locations: Austin, TX, USA; South Bend, IN, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Oncologists and breast cancer centers that choose and monitor neoadjuvant therapy; currently research institutions and hospitals under investigational use
problem: Patients can endure months of ineffective chemotherapy before response is known. NearWave makes a handheld near infrared imager to show early whether a therapy is working.
business_model: Medical device sales to hospitals and researchers (pre-commercial, investigational use only)
product_category: Handheld fdNIRS medical imaging device with iOS app
competitors_at_founding: Boston University Roblyer group wearable diffuse optical probe
market_need_then: Breast cancer therapy response is uncertain for months; academic papers dating to 2007 showed diffuse optical spectroscopy can predict response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
outcome_analysis: NearWave grew out of a Notre Dame class and won $100K in university competition prizes in April 2020 before joining YC in Winter 2022. The device is still investigational as of its site, with a team of three, and no priced equity round, exit or shutdown was found. It is a slow medical device path where regulatory clearance and clinical evidence, not software growth, set the pace.

name: Neosync
one_liner: Neosync is an open-source anonymization and synthetic data platform.
long_description: Neosync is an open-source platform that allows you to create anonymized or synthetic data and sync it across all environments for testing and machine learning. Companies in highly regulated industries such as FinTech, HealthTech, InsureTech and those with sensitive data can use Neosync to create production-like data to use for debugging and building features in lower-level environments without the security and privacy risk of using production data.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams in regulated industries such as fintech, healthtech and insurtech that need production-like test data without exposing real PII
problem: Developers need realistic data in staging and test environments, but copying production data is a privacy and compliance risk.
business_model: Open-source core (MIT) with a hosted commercial offering
product_category: Data anonymization and synthetic data orchestration
market_need_then: Regulated teams needed safe test data; no quantified demand evidence found for 2022.
outcome_analysis: Neosync built a small open source data anonymization project that reached about 4,000 GitHub stars and a few named enterprise customers, then was bought by Grow Therapy in September 2025 for its anonymization capability, with the founder joining as a product manager. Price and funding are not public, and the shutdown of its own site suggests an absorbed product, so its commercial scale is unclear.

name: Nest Genomics
tags: SaaS; Health Tech; Digital Health; Genomics; Primary Care
one_liner: Software to launch and integrate genetics into clinical care
long_description: Nest is a lab-agnostic, comprehensive solution for organizations to launch and implement large-scale genomic programs. The platform includes the ability to triage, consent, and counsel patients for genetic testing, provide EMR-integrated clinical decision support for providers managing patients with genetic results, and manage patients’ clinical needs across the continuum of care.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Health systems, hospitals and public programs launching large scale genomic testing programs (customer logos on site include Geisinger, Mount Sinai, Dana-Farber and the State of Florida)
problem: Health systems struggle to triage, consent, order and follow up on genetic tests inside the EHR, so genetic results rarely change care. Nest provides lab agnostic software with EHR integrated decision support.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to health systems and genomic programs (pricing not found)
product_category: Clinical genomics software and clinical decision support
market_need_then: Genetic testing volume was rising while health systems lacked tools to deliver counseling and decision support at scale; the company's seed announcement cited expansion to pediatrics, polygenic risk and pharmacogenetics.
outcome_analysis: Founders who had already sold Clear Genetics to Invitae in 2019 built Nest in 2021 and joined YC in Winter 2022, then closed an $8.5M seed led by B Capital in January 2023. The product reports health system and state customers and EHR and lab integrations, and no layoffs, Series A or exit were found, so the company appears to be an independent, growing enterprise software business.

name: Netmaker
tags: DevSecOps; Next-gen Network Security; Open Source; Kubernetes
one_liner: Automated WireGuard networks for distributed systems and Kubernetes
long_description: Netmaker is an open source virtual networking platform based on WireGuard. With Netmaker, you can bridge, clouds, the edge, IoT devices, and Kubernetes clusters. Netmaker provides the fastest possible virtual networks, with an average speed 10x faster than standard alternatives. Think of Netmaker like your VPC for distributed systems.
all_locations: Austin, TX, USA; Asheville, NC, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: DevOps and platform teams, managed service providers, IoT companies and Kubernetes users who need private networks across clouds and edge devices
problem: Connecting servers, clouds, edge devices and clusters in different places with conventional VPNs is complex and slow. Netmaker automates WireGuard mesh networks managed from one control plane.
business_model: Open source core (Apache-2.0 per profiles) with paid Enterprise Edition and SaaS tiers
product_category: WireGuard based virtual networking and zero trust access
market_need_then: WireGuard adoption was growing and distributed, multi-cloud and IoT estates needed simple overlay networks; the open source project drew about 1,200 users before a paid version.
outcome_analysis: Netmaker began as an open source WireGuard project in 2021, joined YC in Winter 2022 and raised a $2.3M seed in October 2022 with about 1,200 users and a paid beta. It faces better funded rivals in Tailscale and ZeroTier. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, so it is an active small company with modest funding and a community driven distribution model.

name: NewsCatcher
tags: SaaS; Enterprise; Big Data; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Turning the web into a structured database of real world events.
long_description:
NewsCatcher turns global news and web coverage into structured, ready-to-use data. We index 140,000+ sources in 50+ languages, so teams can monitor any company, market, topic or real-world event continuously, and act on it before it reaches them elsewhere.

Two ways in, on one key. The News API returns ranked articles in any language, grouped into stories so repeated coverage of one event arrives as one event, plus boolean search across the last 12 months when you need every match rather than the best ones. The Agent handles the questions no single page answers like every funding round, regulatory action, product launch or cybersecurity incident in a window, or the news about every company on a list. It retrieves a large candidate set from the web, validates which pages actually match, and returns a table with a source on every row.
regions: Ukraine; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data, risk, media monitoring and enterprise teams (banks, PR firms, investment firms, research and government groups) that pay for structured news and web data; the company states 100 plus paying customers
problem: Monitoring global news in many languages as structured, deduplicated data is hard to build. NewsCatcher indexes news and web sources and exposes them as APIs and monitors.
business_model: Usage and tier based API subscriptions, with enterprise contracts
product_category: News and web data API (later a web search agent)
market_need_then: Companies wanted news as structured data for risk and monitoring; the YC launch post lists risk intelligence, in app news and media monitoring as top use cases.
outcome_analysis: NewsCatcher began as a data side project in 2020, joined YC in Summer 2022 and took backing from YC and TinySeed. By 2023 and 2024 it reports enterprise and government customers and 100 plus paying customers, with a team of about 22 and a shift from the v2 developer API to enterprise and an agent product. No exit, shutdown or later priced round was found, so it looks like a small profitable style business with undisclosed economics.

name: Nira Energy
tags: Solar Power; Climate; Energy; Renewable Energy; ClimateTech
one_liner: Software to find the best sites for renewables on the electrical grid
long_description: Nira is a map tool, built for renewable energy developers, that shows available capacity at every interconnection point on the electrical grid. Customers like AES and Cypress Creek use Nira to find the most profitable points on the grid to site new projects.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Renewable energy developers (solar, wind, storage), plus transmission planners, utilities and ISOs; customers named include AES, Cypress Creek, Doral Renewables, Orsted and BW Solar
problem: Developers waste time and money siting projects at grid points where interconnection capacity or upgrade costs make them uneconomic. Nira maps capacity and models ISO style studies to find viable sites.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscriptions for developers and grid stakeholders; reported as profitable from its first year
product_category: Grid interconnection capacity mapping and study software
founder_names: Chris Ariante; Andy Chen; Andrew Martin
competitors_at_founding: Pearl Street Technologies; Siemens PSS/E and GE PSLF
market_need_then: Interconnection queues were swelling; Berkeley Lab reported solar as the largest share of queued capacity at end of 2021, and developers needed early cost visibility.
outcome_analysis: Nira started in 2021, reportedly turned a profit in its first year, joined YC in Winter 2022 with a 500K investment and grew to customers including major developers while bootstrapping. Energize Capital announced a strategic growth investment in May 2025 with undisclosed terms. The company is active with a growing team, and no shutdown or exit was found.

name: Nophin
tags: Generative AI; SaaS; Real Estate; Proptech; AI Assistant
one_liner: AI Deal Screening Analyst for Commercial Real Estate Acquisitions
long_description:
Nophin helps commercial real estate professionals screen deals faster with Cresa, an AI Analyst that automates multifamily deal screening and diligence processes, freeing up time for what truly matters—closing the best opportunities.
 
Acquisition teams are overwhelmed with manual tasks, from screening countless deals that don't meet buying criteria to analyzing complex documents and conducting market research. These inefficiencies lead to missed opportunities and slowed decision-making, making it difficult to focus on high-potential opportunities.

Cresa is the first fine-tuned multimodal Agent capable of handling various workflows for acquisition teams around the clock so they can focus on high-potential deals that align with their buying criteria. Cresa can screen deals, analyze documents, and generate comprehensive reports.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Northwind
tags: Consumer Health Services; Health Tech; Digital Health; Healthcare; Telemedicine
one_liner: Tele-dermatology for chronic skin conditions
long_description:
Northwind is a tele-dermatology start-up changing how chronic skin conditions Psoriasis and Atopic Eczema are treated. 

We connect 31 million American patients to specialists in under 12 hours, and provide a tailor-made treatment plan with our proprietary line of clinically tested vegan OTC and Rx products. 

Patients register and go through our digital questionnaire, uploading pictures of their affected skin. In under 12 hours the patient receives their own specialised dermatologist who then decides the correct treatment plan required - with monthly checkpoints where the plan is adjusted based on patient feedback and results. 

Today, thousands of users rely on, and love Northwinds proprietary Swedish formulas. The company is led by a patient suffering from 20 years of severe Psoriasis.
all_locations: Los Angeles, CA, USA; Stockholm, Stockholm County, Sweden
regions: United States of America; Sweden; America / Canada; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Notebook Labs
one_liner: Decentralized, anonymous, and accountable identity on Web3.
long_description:
Notebook solves the Web3 identity problem by using Zero-Knowledge to provide both anonymous proof-of-humanity and credential aggregation. Notebook initially verifies users’ identifying information to ensure that each person has just a single Notebook. Neither Notebook, nor any other company knows the link between a user’s personal information and their Notebook. Once a user’s Notebook account is created they can begin proving their humanity and aggregating their credentials across wallets.

Notebook can be used to increase the safety of DeFi, governance, and airdrops. With Notebook, creators and communities can run Sybil-resistant airdrops, DAOs can verify the humanity and aggregate the credentials of participants, and lending protocols can build credit scoring systems to offer lower-collateralized loans.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Novig
one_liner: America's #1 Sports Trading App
long_description:
Novig is building America's #1 sports prediction market. Founded by Jacob Fortinsky and Kelechi Ukah, we are the only platform to offer commission-free sports trading. We deliver better pricing, full transparency, and a more efficient market structure for users by eliminating the traditional sportsbook model.

Backed by the best - Novig has raised over $100M from some of Silicon Valley’s top investors including Pantera, Forerunner, Lux, NFX, Paul Graham, and Joe Montana.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US sports bettors, later a broader retail audience trading sports event contracts
problem: Traditional sportsbooks set prices with a built-in margin and limit or ban winning bettors. Novig offers a peer to peer exchange with commission free trading and tighter pricing.
business_model: exchange and prediction market, fee and spread based (marketed as commission free to users)
product_category: sports prediction market and betting exchange
market_need_then: Legal US sports betting was expanding after 2018 and sportsbooks restricted winning bettors, creating demand for exchange style pricing. Source is the YC page description of the founder as a banned bettor.
outcome_analysis: Novig started as a small exchange in the YC Summer 2022 batch and raised $6.4M pre-seed in 2023, then $18M Series A in 2025 and a $75M Series B in 2026 at a reported $500M valuation. It rode the rise of regulated prediction markets and gained CFTC designation, while also fighting state regulators in court. The main risks are state level legal action and larger rivals such as Kalshi and Polymarket.

name: NuMind
tags: Documents; Machine Learning; Data Engineering; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: The LLM provider for Document Extraction
long_description:
We make NuExtract, a VLM specialized in extracting structured information from documents (JSON output). It is used by banks and insurances such as AXA to do automatic data entry for their incoming documents.

NuExtract outperforms general-purpose LLMs while being small enough to be deployed on-premises.

Try it here: https://nuextract.ai/
all_locations: Paris, Île-de-France, France; Cambridge, MA, USA
regions: France; United States of America; Europe; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises in banking, insurance and healthcare that process documents, plus developers wanting custom NLP models
problem: Turning unstructured text and documents into structured data usually needs ML teams and labeled data. NuMind builds small specialized models for extraction that can run on premises.
business_model: SaaS platform and API plus private enterprise deployments of its models
product_category: document extraction and custom NLP models
market_need_then: Enterprises had large volumes of documents needing manual data entry. Customers listed on the company site include AXA and Credit Mutuel.
outcome_analysis: NuMind started as a no code platform for custom NLP, raised a $3M seed in March 2023 and later refocused on NuExtract for document extraction with enterprise customers such as AXA. It remains small and active. The open question is whether specialized small models stay ahead of general LLMs.

name: Nullstone
one_liner: An easier way to deploy and manage cloud apps
long_description:
Nullstone is a suite of tools delivered as a single product that enables developer self-service while accommodating flexibility and control that platform engineers need to maintain secure, compliant, performant, and reliable infrastructure.


Nullstone provides a simple developer experience that guides developers through the architecture and release of cloud apps. By default, infrastructure launched through Nullstone is compliance-certified and vetted for security best practices. The software delivery process can be customized per app through external CI/CD tools or IaC tools like Terraform to meet the specific needs of customers or to optimize developer workflow.


Nullstone comes with many quality-of-life features that are hard to build with an in-house DevOps/Platform team: Auto-Build/Deploy, Preview Environments, GitOps, and Automatic Secrets Management.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Growing engineering teams that want developer self-service on their own AWS or GCP account without a large platform team
problem: Teams either use closed PaaS tools that do not scale to larger businesses or build in house DevOps platforms. Nullstone gives developers a simple deploy workflow on top of compliant, customizable infrastructure.
business_model: B2B SaaS internal developer platform
product_category: developer tools, internal developer platform
market_need_then: Platform engineering and developer self-service were growing pains for scaling teams. The company page cites SOC 2 compliance and customers such as Atlas, IOU Financial and Wick.
outcome_analysis: Nullstone is a small, still active platform engineering startup run by two brothers with enterprise platform experience. Public funding is limited to an undisclosed angel round in 2021 and about $500K reported by an aggregator, so the scale of the business is unclear and it has not raised a visible institutional round.

name: Numida
one_liner: Working capital for African micro businesses
long_description: Numida provides working capital loans to African micro businesses. Instead of borrowing from informal lenders or family, micro business owners download the Numida app, apply in minutes, and receive capital within a day. We have figured out how to score and disburse unsecured loans to cash-based businesses that have no digital transaction history, while maintaining excellent collection rates. Since 2021 we have provided $23M in working capital to 32,000 businesses in East Africa.
regions: Uganda; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Cash based micro and small businesses in Uganda needing short term working capital
problem: Micro business owners borrow from informal lenders or family because they have no digital transaction history. Numida scores and lends to them through an app.
business_model: lender earning interest on unsecured working capital loans, funded by equity and debt
product_category: fintech, SME working capital lending
founder_names: Mina Shahid; Catherine Denis; Ben Best
market_need_then: In 2017 Numida was raising from angels and winning Seedstars Kampala, targeting credit constrained Ugandan entrepreneurs who relied on informal lenders. Loans of $100 to $5,000 were later repaid in a month at 10 to 16 percent interest per TechCrunch.
outcome_analysis: Numida is the first Ugandan YC company and kept growing, lending $20M in working capital by September 2022 and raising $12.3M in equity and debt, with monthly issuance growing from $250K to $2M. Founder market fit in East Africa and proprietary repayment data helped, while macro and currency risk in Uganda remain. It is active with 115 staff.

name: Nyckel
one_liner: Classify Anything
long_description: Use Nyckel to train and integrate state of the art machine learning into your application. Our ML platform can be used by anyone and it only takes minutes to train your first model. Once trained, your functions is immediately deployed to production grade infrastructure.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers and small companies without ML staff who need image, text or tabular classifiers behind an API
problem: Training and deploying a custom classifier requires ML expertise and infrastructure. Nyckel turns a few labeled examples into a hosted classification API in minutes.
business_model: usage-based API with a free tier, charged per invoke
product_category: AutoML classification API
founder_names: Oscar Beijbom; George Mathew; Dan Ott
competitors_at_founding: Google Cloud Vision AutoML; Hugging Face; Roboflow; Microsoft Custom Vision
market_need_then: The Launch HN post cites uses such as photo tagging for a used car marketplace, support ticket triage and fake profile detection, showing demand from developers without ML skills.
outcome_analysis: Nyckel is a four person YC W22 team building a self serve classification API for developers. It launched on Hacker News and Product Hunt, added pretrained classifiers in 2023 and remains active. No institutional funding was found, and the AutoML category faced strong cloud incumbents and later general models, so its scale is unclear.

name: Offbeast
tags: Clean Meat; Cultured Meat; Climate; Food Tech
one_liner: We make plant-based steaks with an authentic texture
long_description: We add authentic meat-like textures to plant-based and animal proteins. By upscaling low-value minced meat into higher-value whole cuts, we increase meat producers' margins by 50-300%, while maintaining a clean label and protein content.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Meat producers wanting to upgrade low value minced meat into whole cuts, plus foodservice and direct to consumer buyers of plant-based steaks
problem: Plant-based and cultivated meat lacked authentic whole cut texture. Offbeast adds fibrous whole muscle texture to plant and animal proteins to raise producer margins.
business_model: B2B technology and ingredient partnerships with some direct sales of plant-based steaks
product_category: food tech, whole cut meat alternatives
market_need_then: Whole cut texture was the unsolved gap in plant-based meat in 2022, noted in several trade pieces on whole cut competitors.
outcome_analysis: Offbeast, previously Mooji Meats, raised a $3M seed in May 2022 and developed whole cut texture technology. Plant-based demand weakened after 2022 and the company shifted toward hybrid beef products with meat producers, with a further reported investment from Global Brain. It is active and small.

name: Ole
one_liner: Fashion shopping with delivery and return on demand
long_description:
Ole brings fashion with delivery and return on-demand.
Customers use our app to order clothes from nearby stores, try them at home while the driver is waiting, take only what they like and return to the driver what they don't.

We already have $35k monthly GMV, growing 35% MoM.

What’s unique about our business is our average order value which is 7X higher than typical on-demand business. While their average order is $30, ours is $200, which is why we are already positive in unit economics.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa

name: Olympian Motors
tags: Consumer; Manufacturing; Climate; Transportation; Electric Vehicles
one_liner: Next-generation, modular electric vehicles
long_description:
⚡️Olympian manufactures timeless, art-deco electric vehicles. We challenge today’s mundane, over-standardized car designs produced by the traditional automotive industry.

► Olympian EVs are powered by an open, modular EV architecture. We are pioneering a new modular production model in the U.S., delivering 85–90% reductions in tooling and machinery costs, and achieved 60–80% faster production-lead-times compared to legacy automakers in the U.S.

💸 Revenue Backlog: $61M+
🚗 Number of Orders: 790+
🏭 Production Capacity: 2,400 units in 2026
✅ Backed by: YC, NVIDIA, Climate Capital, Mobility Vision, Amazon AWS, Soma & Collaborative.

--
Olympian has two pillars:
1) Art-deco, aesthetic, but simple electric cars
2) Modular EV architecture that enables rapid, cost-efficient production.

Olympian rejects today's mundane and over-standardized car experience.   We challenge the 40-year status-quo in automotive design, and bring aesthetic, simplicity and color back to the cars. 

We are manufacturing electric vehicles with our innovative 'modular' vehicle & drivetrain architecture (MVDS), providing Olympian with strong cost and lead-time advantages compared to legacy automakers like Tesla and Ford. Olympian is disrupting 120+ years old automotive industry and targeting to capture 7% market share in the U.S. automotive market by 2030.

Olympian developed a fully-decoupled, modular, EV drivetrain system (eMVDS) that provides a 'Lego-like' vehicle architecture. Built on 4-core-hardware and 2-core software modules, Olympus eMVDS platform unlocks 80% reduction in tooling & machinery costs and built ~60% faster production lead time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers buying design led electric vehicles, plus suppliers and regional partners joining its modular platform
problem: Electric vehicle startups face huge tooling and factory costs; Olympian claims a modular architecture cuts tooling and labor costs so small runs of distinctive vehicles become viable.
business_model: vehicle sales with deposits and preorders, plus platform partnerships with suppliers and joint ventures; funded in part by retail crowdfunding
product_category: Electric vehicle manufacturer with modular platform
market_need_then: Consumers and press showed interest in retro styled EVs; the company reports 790 plus orders and a 61M plus revenue backlog on its own YC page (self reported, deposits).
outcome_analysis: Olympian Motors is an active YC W22 EV startup using a modular platform and art deco styling to stand out in a capital hungry market. Press in early 2024 and retail crowdfunding gave it visibility and investor numbers, but sourced evidence of deliveries or production is missing, and funding totals are unverified, so its outcome is still open. The business faces the usual hardware and capital risks that sank earlier EV startups.

name: Omoi (formerly Azuki)
one_liner: Japanese comic subscription service
long_description: Omoi (formerly Azuki) is Netflix-style Japanese comic subscription service where users can subscribe for $4.99 a month to unlock access to all the manga on the service. Free users have access to select chapters with ads.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: English language manga readers who pay about $4.99 a month, plus free ad supported readers
problem: Fans wanted legal, affordable, global access to many licensed manga series in one place. Azuki offers a Netflix style subscription of officially licensed titles.
business_model: consumer subscription plus ads on a free tier
product_category: digital manga reading app
founder_names: Abbas Jaffery; Adela Chang; Evan Minto; Krystyn Neisess; Ken Urata
competitors_at_founding: Shonen Jump Vault (Viz Media); Manga Plus (Shueisha)
market_need_then: Launch coverage in June 2021 describes demand for a global all you can read manga service, with over 170 Kodansha series at launch for about $5 a month.
outcome_analysis: Azuki launched in June 2021 with Kodansha titles and joined YC in Winter 2022 with a $500K investment. It stayed small with licensing dependence on publishers and competition from Manga Plus and Viz, then rebranded as Omoi in November 2025 partly because the name was shared by unrelated companies. It remains active with a catalog above 500 titles.

name: Onboard.io
tags: SaaS; B2B; Productivity; Customer Success; Collaboration
one_liner: Manage & automate customer onboarding and implementation
long_description: Onboard is a SaaS which automates & streamlines the customer onboarding & implementation process. Easily create dynamic launch plans (customized per customer), which are collaborative with clients and visible to all stakeholders.  Onboard is built for onboarding by a team that spent a better part of the last decade onboarding some of the worlds largest brands.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B SaaS customer success and implementation teams that onboard customers
problem: Teams run customer onboarding in spreadsheets, email and generic project tools. Onboard gives shared launch plans, a customer portal and automation.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with tiers from $25 to $1,000 per month
product_category: customer onboarding and implementation software
founder_names: Jeff Epstein; Will Stevenson; Matt Majewski
competitors_at_founding: Google Docs, email, Asana and monday.com; GuideCX; Rocketlane
market_need_then: The 2021 press release says onboarding teams relied on Google Docs, email, Asana or monday.com, and the founders cited poor customer launches as the pain.
outcome_analysis: Onboard was founded by Ambassador alumni, raised a $1.25M pre-seed in February 2021 and joined YC in Winter 2022. It stayed a small SaaS in a category with better funded rivals such as GuideCX and Rocketlane, and in August 2025 Zelkova Ventures, an early investor, took a majority stake.

name: Oneleet
one_liner: YC's most popular security compliance platform (SOC 2, ISO 27001,…
long_description:
Oneleet helps companies become secure and compliant through an all-in-one solution that combines automated tools and human expertise.

Oneleet has built the second generation of security compliance automation software, providing tools that go beyond what is classically provided for just compliance alone. Tools like a code security scanner, attack-surface management, access reviews and trust portal are all built in.

As the most popular, highest rated and most frequently used platform in the YC community, Oneleet has quickly established itself as the preferred and superior alternative to other incumbents.

The founder behind Oneleet has spent the past 10+ years helping companies become more secure by performing penetration tests.
regions: Netherlands; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and SMB software companies that need SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR or PCI compliance and a real security program
problem: Compliance automation tools sell a checkbox; buyers still need penetration tests, code scanning, device management and an auditor-ready program from several vendors.
business_model: B2B SaaS flat annual fee bundling compliance automation, pentests and vCISO services
product_category: Security compliance automation plus human pentesting
founder_names: Bryan Onel; Ora Onel; Erik Vogelzang
market_need_then: Startups were required by enterprise buyers to hold SOC 2 and similar attestations, and Vanta and Drata raised large rounds in 2021 and 2022, showing strong demand.
outcome_analysis: Oneleet pairs security expertise from founders who were penetration testers with a bundled compliance product, positioned against checkbox tools. It says it reached eight figure revenue profitably before raising its $33M Series A in October 2025 led by Dawn Capital, which points to capital efficiency and a founder market fit story.

name: Onyx Private
one_liner: A modern and more accessible private bank for the new generation
long_description: Onyx is a modern, accessible private bank for the next generation of affluent young professionals. We offer a unified digital-native premium banking and wealth management experience tailored for the overlooked groups of young high-earners and illiquid entrepreneurs, investors, and tech employees. Onyx aims to be the next-generation UBS.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Affluent young professionals, tech employees and entrepreneurs underserved by traditional private banks; later community and regional banks as a B2B platform
problem: Young high earners lack access to private banking and wealth management, which are built for the already wealthy.
business_model: Consumer premium banking and wealth management subscription and fees, pivoted to B2B white-label banking platform in 2024
product_category: Digital private bank
founder_names: Victor Santos; Douglas Lopes; Tiago Passinato
market_need_then: Young high earners with illiquid equity were poorly served by premium banks; the founders cited the group as overlooked, with no quantified spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Onyx Private raised 4.1 million dollars in May 2023 to build a private bank for young high earners, then closed customer accounts in March 2024 to pivot to a B2B banking platform. The YC page later lists it as acquired, with a founder bio naming Citizens Bank. No deal date, price or confirming announcement was found, so how the company ended is partly unknown.

name: OpenScale
tags: Developer Tools; API; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: The cheapest, fastest way to run open models and agent sandboxes
long_description: Latent Space develops AI applications specifically designed to address the unique challenges and opportunities in emerging economies. Our products are Halo AI (an AI universal concierge for SEA enterprises), GoVisa (an AI-enabled online visa and permit application), and Supa (a hyperlocal knowledge AI for 280M+ Indonesians).
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and companies running open weight AI models via API and agent sandboxes (current website); the original YC listing describes AI apps for Southeast Asian enterprises and consumers
problem: Running open models and agent sandboxes is costly and slow; the original Latent Space listing targeted AI apps for emerging economies.
business_model: Usage-based API with pay as you go and subscription plans
product_category: Open model inference API and agent sandboxes
founder_names: Faza Fahleraz; Gery Nugraha; Albert Sahala
market_need_then: No sourced evidence of demand at founding was found beyond the company description of AI apps for emerging economies.
outcome_analysis: The sources do not show a funding history or outcome. The YC listing describes the earlier Latent Space apps while the live website sells an open model API and sandboxes under the OpenScale name, which suggests a later pivot whose date and reason are not public.

name: Optery
tags: SaaS; Consumer; Security; Privacy; Enterprise Software
one_liner: Opt out software that removes your private info from the internet
long_description:
Optery is automated opt out software, and we serve individuals, families and businesses.  With Optery, you can remove yourself from hundreds of data brokers that are posting and selling your home address, phone number, email and other private information on the internet.  

Optery received the “Editors’ Choice” award by PCMag as the most outstanding product in the personal data removal category in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2026 and 2026, the Cybersecurity Excellence Awards for Attack Surface Management, Digital Footprint Management, and Employee Privacy Protection in 2024 and 2025, Cyber Defense Magazine’s Top InfoSec Innovator and Best Attack Surface Management awards in 2024 and 2025, the 2025 Fortress Cybersecurity Award for Privacy Enhancing Technologies, and Fast Company’s Next Big Things in Tech award for security and privacy in 2023. In 2025, Optery was also listed by Business Insider as one of 30 early-stage startups most likely to become a unicorn.

Optery prevents phishing and social engineering, identity theft and fraud, online stalking and harassment, ransomware, doxxing, and prevents people's private information from showing up in Google search results. 

Anyone can create a free account to receive a personalized Exposure Report with live screenshots summarizing where your information is being posted and sold online.  Optery then provides free tools for self-service removals, or you can upgrade to a paid plan, and Optery will remove the profiles for you.

Optery for Business serves enterprises removing personal information from the internet for their employees and executives, and offers an API enabling application developers to embed data broker scanning and removal technology into their applications.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Individuals and families paying for data broker opt-outs, plus businesses protecting employee and executive privacy
problem: Hundreds of data brokers publish and sell home addresses, phone numbers and emails, and manual opt-out is slow and repetitive.
business_model: Consumer and business subscriptions for automated data broker removal, with a free exposure report as the funnel
product_category: Personal data removal and digital footprint management
market_need_then: Privacy law growth and rising doxxing and phishing concern drove demand for broker removal, and reviewers later rated the category as in high demand; no figures dated to 2021 were found.
outcome_analysis: Optery grew a consumer and business data removal product to a team of about 55, won repeated PCMag Editors' Choice awards and raised only a few million dollars. In September 2026 Surfshark bought a majority stake, keeping Optery standalone next to its Incogni brand. Terms were not disclosed; the capital efficient path ended in a strategic majority sale.

name: Orca
one_liner: Banking for Gen Z, on steroids.
long_description: Orca is banking built for Gen Z from the ground up. Send money instantly, split bills with groups, access local discounts and perks, spend and save, and do everything else you could ever ask on Orca — the only financial hub you'll ever need.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Austin, TX, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Gen Z consumers, initially university students in Austin
problem: Banking for young people lacks social features such as group bill splitting and local perks.
business_model: Consumer neobank app
product_category: Gen Z neobank
market_need_then: Neobanks aimed at young users raised large rounds in 2021, showing investor demand, but no sourced user evidence for Orca.
outcome_analysis: No outcome is documented. The company is listed as Active on YC, the website returned no readable content, and no funding, shutdown or acquisition reports could be tied to it, so its trajectory is unknown rather than a failure.

name: Ordinary Seafood
one_liner: We are doing for seafood what Impossible did for meat
long_description: We are a consumer facing biotech company using the power of plant protein and biotechnology to deliver the next generation of sustainable seafood. Our mission is to bring balance back into our food system by empowering people to make greener choices one bite at a time.
regions: Germany; Europe

name: Origami Therapeutics, Inc.
one_liner: Oral drugs to halt neurodegeneration
long_description: Origami Therapeutics, Inc. is a biotech company developing novel protein degraders with potential to delay or halt disease progression by eliminating toxic proteins from the body. Our drug discovery platform leverages our proprietary human disease models developed to select the small molecules with the best chance of clinical success. Our first indication is Huntington’s disease, a debilitating, progressive and ultimately fatal disorder caused by a genetic mutation. We have already identified small molecules that reduce the toxic mutated protein, suppress mutant protein-induced toxicities in human disease neurons and get into the brain. We anticipate that this approach will be broadly applicable to traditionally “undruggable” targets in other neurological diseases.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Patients with Huntington's disease and other neurodegenerative disorders; pharma partners through licensing and collaboration
problem: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Huntington's are driven by toxic misfolded proteins that existing drugs do not remove.
business_model: Preclinical biotech; licensing and collaboration deals with pharma
product_category: Small-molecule protein degraders and correctors for neurodegeneration
market_need_then: Huntington's disease has no disease-modifying treatment; MedCity News (Nov 2021) notes most degrader programs were in oncology, leaving neurodegeneration open.
outcome_analysis: Origami was founded by a veteran neuroscience drug-discovery executive, ran largely self-funded, and joined YC in Winter 2022 aiming to close a seed round at Demo Day. Its lead ORI-113 for Huntington's remained preclinical. A global collaboration with Ipsen on its protein degrader program was announced in early 2026, a meaningful validation, but equity funding and deal terms were not found, so the financial outcome is unknown.

name: Oto
tags: Consumer Health Services; Health Tech; Digital Health
one_liner: Digital program for tinnitus
long_description:
Oto’s digital programs are the best way to manage tinnitus, and at a fraction of the cost of in person treatment. 

Tinnitus or ringing in the ears affects 1 in 8 people, and before Oto effective therapy was only available via expensive meetings with a specialist.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Adults with tinnitus, paying directly, via clinics or through health system partners
problem: Effective tinnitus therapy such as CBT was available only through expensive specialist sessions with long NHS waits; Oto delivers it as a digital program with audiologist support.
business_model: Digital therapeutics program with audiologist sessions, sold direct to consumers and through partners
product_category: Digital health, tinnitus therapy
founder_names: Edmund Farrar; George Leidig; Jameel Muzaffar
market_need_then: Tinnitus affects roughly 1 in 8 people per the YC page, and press at the 2021 launch cited NHS waits of up to 9 months for CBT.
outcome_analysis: Oto, founded by tinnitus sufferers who were military doctors, joined YC in Winter 2022 after a pre-seed and raised a roughly $3.3M seed in July 2022 led by Octopus Ventures. It built clinical credibility through a randomized trial run with Cambridge and regulatory certification, and remains active. Founder insight into patient pain and long NHS waits helped; no later round was found.

name: Overwatch
tags: Cybersecurity; Fraud Prevention; Fraud Detection; AI
one_liner: Enterprise software for enterprise risk and cyber fraud intelligence
long_description: Overwatch Data offers real-time AI agents to scale fraud, cyber, and security teams. Our agents automate the threat intelligence and brand protection workflow, while also conducting risk reviews at scale to detect fraud and financial crime.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Cyber, fraud and risk teams at banks, payments and enterprises
problem: Teams drown in noisy threat and risk signals; originally the company monitored news and satellite imagery for global risks to operations and supply chains.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscription for AI threat intelligence
product_category: AI threat intelligence and risk operations
market_need_then: The YC launch described demand for automating global risk detection across operations, supply chain and reputation; no quantified spend evidence was gathered.
outcome_analysis: Overwatch started with global risk monitoring and moved to AI agents for threat intelligence and fraud. It is active, lists Visa and FS-ISAC as customers or partners, and reported a $15M Series A in October 2026, but earlier round data is inconsistent so its funding path is only partly known.

name: Ozone
one_liner: Figma for video
long_description: Ozone is the world’s first collaborative video editor in the cloud. We are making the world a more creative place by building the next generation of creative tools.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Content marketers and short form video creators and teams making TikTok, Instagram and YouTube content
problem: Professional video editors such as Premiere Pro are hard to learn, run offline and make team collaboration painful. Ozone aimed to put editing, AI assistance and real time collaboration in the browser.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription for a browser based video editor
product_category: Collaborative cloud video editing with AI features
market_need_then: Short form video demand from marketers and creators was high in 2022, and the founder argued Adobe tools were hard to use, offline and lacked collaboration. Figma style multiplayer tools had just proven that model in design.
outcome_analysis: Ozone raised a $7.1M seed in November 2023 and launched out of beta, but YC lists it as Inactive. No source found states when or why it stopped, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned. The category was crowded with funded editors such as Veed and Descript, and the browser editing wedge was easy for rivals to match with AI features.

name: PINA
one_liner: WealthFront of Indonesia
long_description:
At PINA, we are designing and building the future of personal finance with a mission to help everyone achieve financial freedom by providing products and advice that make complicated financial decisions simple and relevant. 

We seamlessly integrate money management and investing into one app to allow people to manage their finances holistically. Users can see their net worth, monthly cash flow and how their budget has changed over the past several months. All of this is automated and designed to help them achieve the savings goal which they have set .

In addition to money management, we focus on making investing easy with pre-built portfolios and automatic rebalancing. When you sign up for an account, it offers the option to pick an expertly built portfolio, or you can choose to build your own.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Middle to upper class Indonesians wanting money management and investing
problem: Indonesian investment apps serve first time investors; affluent users lack affordable personalized advice and one view of their finances.
business_model: Free money management tools; revenue when customers invest through the platform
product_category: Personal finance and wealth management app
founder_names: Daniel van Leeuwen; Hendry Chou; Christian Hermawan; Fajar Kuntoro
market_need_then: Indonesian investment apps raised large rounds in 2021, showing demand for retail investing; PINA targeted an advice gap among affluent users per TechCrunch.
outcome_analysis: PINA raised a $3M seed in July 2022 and, per CB Insights, no later round appears. It is listed as active but the website returned no readable content, so traction is unknown; the stall in funding may reflect a tough Indonesian fintech climate but no source says so.

name: Paces
one_liner: Agentic AI for Power Projects and AI Infrastructure
long_description:
Energy demand is skyrocketing, and renewable energy is the most scalable path forward. But today’s development process can’t move fast enough to meet global goals.

Paces exists to change that. We are building AI agents, software and services to accelerate power and data center deployment and lower costs - unlocking one of the greatest opportunities of our time: transforming how infrastructure gets built and ensuring it’s built with renewable energy.

Paces automates early-stage due diligence and provides the expertise to accelerate late-stage diligence, fast-tracking projects from siting to construction-ready. Our platform supports renewable energy and data center developers, real estate firms, and more by streamlining siting, interconnection, and permitting. With Paces, teams can de-risk decisions, shorten timelines, and get more renewable energy projects built.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Renewable energy and data center developers
problem: Developers start projects without deep zoning and interconnection diligence; the launch post says roughly 80% of such projects never get built.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus expert services and reports
product_category: Site selection and due diligence software for energy projects
market_need_then: Launch post cites about $17B of cancelled clean energy projects a year and expensive diligence data.
outcome_analysis: Paces focused on siting and diligence for clean energy projects and expanded into data center power. It raised an $11M Series A in July 2024 led by Navitas Capital and now has a team of about 48, which suggests solid product demand riding the energy and data center buildout.

name: Palitronica Inc
one_liner: Detect cyber attacks on critical physical infrastructure
long_description:
Palitronica builds and deploys cutting-edge solutions to defend critical physical infrastructure and its supply chain.

By using side-channel information from endpoints, Palitronica provides a safe attack detection capability retrofittable to critical systems.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Defense, aerospace and critical infrastructure organizations needing electronics supply chain assurance
problem: Compromised or counterfeit hardware is hard to detect; the company uses side channel and echo response signals to detect attacks on physical devices.
business_model: Enterprise and government hardware testing product and contracts
product_category: Hardware and supply chain cybersecurity
market_need_then: The company won an In-Q-Tel and SVB innovation award in 2022 and landed Canadian defense contracts by 2021 per Velocity Incubator.
outcome_analysis: Palitronica spun out of University of Waterloo research and sold to defense buyers. It closed a BDC led Series A in 2026 and was selected by Bell Textron for cyber assurance on the MV-75, signalling slow but real enterprise traction in a long sales cycle market.

name: Pana
one_liner: A Global Bank on Chain
long_description:
The first secure, end-to-end global USD account, seamlessly integrating fiat and stablecoins across 125 countries for direct-to-bank settlement—no liquidity providers, no SWIFT, no intermediaries.

Both sender and receiver use the Pana app and wallet for a frictionless, real-time cross-border payment experience.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Latino immigrants in the US and their families in Latin America
problem: Remittances are expensive and slow and Latino immigrants are poorly served by banks.
business_model: Fintech app: account and card fees, low-fee remittances, FX on stablecoin rails
product_category: Stablecoin-based neobank / remittances
market_need_then: Large US-Latin America remittance flows and fee pain; a Bloomberg Linea Aug 2022 piece covers the company's YC-era pitch.
outcome_analysis: Pana is a Miami neobank for Latinos built around stablecoins, with 14 staff and still active. A Privy post (undated) cites 150,000 users and 7.2M dollars of monthly volume, and the company joined Visa Fintech Fast Track in 2026 and launched a card in Dec 2025. Funding is unclear; conflicting aggregator figures prevent a firm assessment.

name: Pantore Pay
one_liner: Working capital for Brazilian restaurants
long_description: Pantore Pay is the solution for restaurants cash flow issues and allows restaurants to shop for supplies and pay any other bills using Pantore's credit line.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Paragon AI
one_liner: Turns your sales calls into CRM data, automatically.
long_description: Paragon AI is a tool for sales representatives which automatically turns call recordings into structured information that directly updates the CRM. Instead of spending hours going over call recordings to pull out key information to populate the CRM, sales representatives can focus their time doing what they do best and sales leaders can rest assured that pipeline data is up to date.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; San Juan, San Juan, Puerto Rico; Remote
regions: United States of America; Puerto Rico; America / Canada; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B sales reps and sales leaders
problem: Reps spend up to 20 minutes after each call writing notes and updating CRM fields.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat
product_category: AI sales call notes and CRM automation
market_need_then: TechCrunch reports a customer used it to fill 15 CRM fields, replacing a write up of up to 20 minutes.
outcome_analysis: Paragon AI, formerly Pilot AI, remains active with a small team and an angel round of $2.2M reported in March 2023. No later round or exit was found, and the market is crowded with conversation intelligence incumbents, so its outcome is still unclear.

name: Partna
one_liner: Unlock African payments
long_description: Stablecoin-powered payment infrastructure, to collect, convert, and settle between Africa and global markets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Global fintechs, wallets and businesses that need to collect, convert and settle money between African local currencies and USD or stablecoins
problem: Moving money into and out of Africa is slow and fragmented. Partna offers on and off ramp APIs that convert local currency to stablecoins and settle in USD, citing cases that went from days or months to same day.
business_model: usage-based payments API with FX and settlement spread
product_category: stablecoin payment infrastructure for Africa
market_need_then: Cross-border payments into Africa were costly and slow, and stablecoin rails were a growing alternative by 2021 and 2022. The company cites customers such as MiniPay, Cenoa and HyperVerge, but those are later claims.
outcome_analysis: Partna is still active and focuses on B2B stablecoin rails between Africa and global markets.
