market_need_then: The company expected to help about 42,000 people find jobs in 2022 and positioned itself in operational hiring in LatAm; no independent market data retrieved.
outcome_analysis: HoyTrabajas raised a pre-seed from angels and Rockstart, joined YC Winter 2022 and announced a $5M seed in October 2022 with Newtype Ventures and many others, bringing reported capital to $5.5M. It is Active with 35 to 64 staff and 290 clients per the company, which supports a traction story, but later rounds and the date and reason for the rebrand to AI recruiting were not found.

name: Tank Payments
tags: Fintech; SaaS; Payments; Logistics; Supply Chain
one_liner: Modern financial infrastructure for the trucking industry.
long_description: Tank Payments is building modern financial infrastructure for the trucking industry. We offer payables automation software for logistics businesses that make hundreds of payments to trucking businesses every day. For trucking businesses, we provide a best-in-class banking platform, designed to meet the unique financial needs of the trucking sector.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Freight factoring companies, brokers and platforms that pay many trucking carriers, and the small trucking businesses that get paid
problem: Small trucking companies wait 30 days or more to be paid after delivery, and factors and brokers run slow, manual payables. Tank offers payables automation plus banking for carriers.
business_model: Fintech infrastructure: software and payment fees to factors and brokers, banking and card interchange for carriers
product_category: Trucking neobank and payables automation
founder_names: Dane Cook; Jad Rahbany; Matthew Rybak
competitors_at_founding: Relay Payments; RoadSync; CloudTrucks; TriumphPay / HubTran
market_need_then: Carriers are often paid 30 days or more after delivery (per Tank's own descriptions), and FreightWaves in September 2021 documented heavy investment in freight payments fintech.
outcome_analysis: Tank Payments remains active and independent. It started as a neobank for trucking and now sells payables automation and banking to factors, brokers and carriers, with SOC 2 Type II and named factor customers on its site. It won the 2023 Ron Conway award and raised a reported $3.3M seed. No acquisition, layoffs or shutdown were found; public traction numbers are absent, so outcome beyond survival is unknown.

name: Taro
tags: Developer Tools; Education; Community; Video; Creator Economy
one_liner: Help high-growth tech companies hire strong engineers
long_description:
Taro is a community of 150k+ software engineers looking to grow their careers. High-growth tech companies leverage the Taro platform to hire engineers who can grow the company. 

Taro's education platform offers online courses and discussions with leaders at top tech companies. These resources attract many top engineers seeking their next career move.

Taro supports the hiring process at startups through sourcing and feedback on engineers. If you're looking to expand your engineering team quickly, without compromising on quality, book time here: https://www.jointaro.com/enterprise/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individual software engineers paying for career courses and Q&A, plus companies paying for engineer hiring support
problem: Engineers lack candid, level specific guidance on getting promoted, negotiating and changing jobs.
business_model: Consumer subscription and courses plus recruiting services
product_category: Career education community for software engineers
market_need_then: The founders already ran a community of about 17K to 50K engineers (figures differ by page), showing demand for tech career advice.
outcome_analysis: Taro grew out of the founders' Tech Career Growth community and YouTube audience, giving it unusually cheap distribution, and joined YC in Summer 2022. YC lists it as acquired, and one aggregator names Handshake in February 2026. No funding history or deal terms are public, so the outcome is a likely small acquisition built on audience and founder fit.

name: TeamOut
one_liner: Online marketplace for team retreat venues
long_description: TeamOut is a retreat platform for team managers. We offer easy-to-book venues for team retreats. Managers spend months planning for a retreat. We help them do it in just a few days. How? We offer 20+ bedroom private places with robust Wifi that companies can book in a few clicks. This is an incredibly exciting time to meet with your team again, build memorable experiences that your team will remember forever.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Team managers and HR or people ops at companies, especially remote and distributed teams, who book retreats and offsites
problem: Planning a team offsite takes months of venue search, vendor vetting and quotes. TeamOut offers bookable venues and planning help in days.
business_model: Marketplace and service revenue on booked retreats (venue commission and planning fees; exact take rate not found)
product_category: Corporate retreat marketplace and planning
market_need_then: Return to in person gatherings after COVID and the rise of remote teams created demand; the YC page cites customers such as Netflix, Brex, Kayak and Cloudflare and the YC launch post says planning offsites is a headache that can be a full time job.
outcome_analysis: TeamOut is active with named customers such as Netflix, but funding and revenue are not public. Its own November 2026 post admits the large event model had low repeat business and thin margins, so it is adding small group offsites. Whether this is a stall or a healthy adjustment cannot be judged from public sources, so no factors are assigned.

name: Terraferma
tags: Machine Learning; Synthetic Biology; Manufacturing; Automation; Biotechnology
one_liner: TSMC for protein manufacturing.
long_description: Terraferma's high-titer platform bridges the gap between computational protein design and commercial production, combining AI/ML-guided strain engineering with ultra-high-throughput genetic screens to make more proteins faster, at lower economic and environmental cost.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI protein design, food, enzyme and therapeutic teams that need high yield production strains; first customer is its sister brand Ten Lives
problem: Computationally designed proteins are hard to make at commercial yield and cost. Terraferma combines ML guided strain engineering with ultra high throughput genetic screens to raise titer.
business_model: Services and licensing: feasibility studies, custom screening, strain licensing or co-development
product_category: Microbial strain engineering platform for protein manufacturing
market_need_then: AI protein design was producing candidates faster than they could be manufactured, and precision fermentation startups needed higher titer hosts; evidence comes from the company's own pitch and trade coverage, not a quantified source.
outcome_analysis: Terraferma is active with six people and an NSF SBIR award. Its first product proof is Ten Lives cat food, on shelves since 2024, and in 2026 it opened the platform to outside partners. Founders have strong ML and genetics credentials. Funding is small and partly unverified, and commercial traction beyond Ten Lives is not public, so the outcome remains early.

name: The Ankler
one_liner: Subscription entertainment news
long_description: The Ankler is subscription news for the entertainment industry so good that everyone from CEOs to creators pay to consume it every day.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Entertainment industry executives, agents, creators and fans who pay for insider Hollywood news; also sponsors and event attendees
problem: Trade press is seen as too deferential; the Ankler offers sharper, subscription funded insider reporting on the industry.
business_model: Paid newsletter subscriptions plus events, sponsorships, podcasts and a radio partnership
product_category: Subscription media, entertainment news newsletter
market_need_then: TheWrap (June 2022) reported about 22,000 total subscriptions with paid subscriptions up 92 percent after Janice Min joined, and a profitable run of over a year per Min.
outcome_analysis: The Ankler is a profitable, independent media company by its own account. Rushfield built the newsletter from 2017, Min joined in January 2022 with Hollywood Reporter and Billboard credentials, and paid subscriptions rose 92 percent. It raised a $1.5M seed through YC in June 2022 and expanded into events, podcasts and radio. Main risks are dependence on a few journalists and competition from Puck and the trades.

name: Theneo
one_liner: Stripe-like API Docs in just a few clicks
long_description: Next-Gen API Documentation with AI Brilliance. Generate Stripe-like API docs in just a few seconds.
regions: Georgia; United States of America; Middle East and North Africa; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering, product and technical writing teams at API companies, mostly fintech, with 20 or more developers
problem: API documentation is time consuming to build and maintain and existing tools are limiting. Theneo generates and keeps interactive Stripe like docs up to date, using AI.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with free tier and paid plans (prices not published on homepage)
product_category: API documentation and developer portal platform
market_need_then: The founder was frustrated by time consuming documentation tools (TechCrunch, October 2022). Caucasus Business Week reports the beta in August 2021 spread by word of mouth to over 1,000 companies and developers.
outcome_analysis: Theneo is active and says more than 18,000 companies use it, up from about 3,000 in October 2022, with customers such as Ticketmaster. Free sign up and word of mouth growth fit product led growth. Funding is small and inconsistently reported, and it has strategic backing from Atlassian Ventures since 2023. No acquisition, layoffs or shutdown were found; customer counts are self reported.

name: Thera
one_liner: AI-Native Finance OS
long_description:
Thera is an AI-native ecosystem of apps to run a modern business: global payroll, treasury, spend management, invoicing/payments.

Thera works with hundreds of the world's leading companies like Oceans, 20four7VA, Landed, Zendrop, Oneleet, Codingal and Meru to supercharge their growth.

Backed by Y Combinator, Amino Capital, Zillionize, 10x Founder, and many more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups, small businesses and global teams that need US payroll, contractor payments in 150+ countries and employer of record services
problem: Paying employees and contractors across countries is slow, costly and fragmented across tax, compliance and payout rails. Thera bundles payroll, treasury, spend and invoicing in one product.
business_model: B2B SaaS and payments: per employee or per contractor fees plus payment and FX revenue
product_category: Global payroll and payments (fintech)
market_need_then: Remote hiring across borders grew in 2020 to 2022 and funded rivals such as Deel, Remote and Papaya Global competed for it, which shows demand for global payroll and contractor payments.
outcome_analysis: Thera raised a 4 million dollar seed in August 2024, two years after its YC batch, and sells payroll and payments to startups and small teams against much larger and better funded rivals such as Deel. It remains active with a small team and a points rewards product in preview, and no Series A, layoffs or sale were found. The slow path to a seed and the crowded market suggest a modest outcome so far.

name: TigerEye
one_liner: AI for Construction
long_description:
TigerEye eliminates bullsh*t so construction professionals can focus
on building the infrastructure that makes our world work
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Sales, finance and marketing leaders at B2B companies
problem: Go to market teams struggle to forecast pipeline and plan territories and quotas because data lives in disconnected CRM and spreadsheet tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Go to market analytics and sales forecasting
market_need_then: Revenue forecasting was a funded category in 2022, with Clari raising 225M and BoostUp 28.5M that year.
outcome_analysis: TigerEye was started by the PlanGrid founders, raised a 5 million seed and a 30 million Series A in 2022 and joined YC in Summer 2022. It was acquired by homebuilder Lennar in January 2026 for undisclosed terms. Strong founder credibility drove funding, while the crowded forecasting category and the non software buyer suggest an exit below the capital raised is possible but unconfirmed.

name: Toko
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Education; Generative AI; Machine Learning; Consumer
one_liner: AI English Tutor
long_description:
Toko helps English learners in East Asia achieve speaking fluency. Through our mobile app, learners engage in short, realistic conversations with an AI and receive feedback on their grammar.

With over 500 topics, learners can practice real-world scenarios ranging from small talk to workplace discussions. Toko offers a low-pressure environment to help learners build up their confidence.

We make language fluency accessible to everyone - not just those with the means to meet 1:1 with a tutor.

In Taiwan (our first market), Toko is ranked top 3 in the App Store for Education!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Consumer English learners in East Asia, first in Taiwan, who pay a subscription
problem: Learners lack affordable speaking practice with feedback. Toko offers short AI conversations with grammar and pronunciation feedback.
business_model: Consumer subscription app with a 7 day free trial
product_category: AI language learning app
market_need_then: English learners in East Asia want speaking practice and tutoring is expensive; the YC page says Toko reached top 3 in Education on the Taiwan App Store.
outcome_analysis: Toko is an active consumer app that says it passed one million downloads and ranked in the top of Taiwan education charts, a sign of local product market fit. Public funding information is thin, so its fundraising path is unknown. The risk is that larger language apps and general AI assistants add speaking practice and compete for the same learners.

name: Tola
one_liner: The simple, fast and free tool for businesses to pay and get paid
long_description: Tola is the simple tool for SMBs to pay bills and get paid. On top of that, we help companies better manage their cashflow by allowing them to buy now and pay later expensive bills in exchange for a small fee.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and medium businesses that pay bills and invoice customers
problem: Small businesses lose time on accounts payable and receivable and face cash flow gaps on large bills.
business_model: Free payments tool with fees on buy now pay later financing of bills
product_category: SMB payables, receivables and cash flow fintech
market_need_then: SMBs commonly handled AP manually, but no dated 2022 demand source was retrieved.
outcome_analysis: Tola was in the Winter 2022 batch, raised a roughly 10 million seed led by Sequoia in October 2024 and was absorbed by Square within ten months, in August 2025. Square framed it as welcoming the team to build cash flow tools, which fits an acquihire after a strong seed rather than a standalone outcome.

name: Top Road
tags: Fintech; Generative AI; Payments; Analytics; AI
one_liner: Payments & analytics for apps in the OpenAI GPT Store
long_description: Top Road provides no-code analytics & payment tools so creators can monetise their AI apps ("GPTs") in the OpenAI ecosystem.
regions: Australia; Oceania; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Creators who build custom GPTs in the OpenAI GPT Store and want to charge for them
problem: GPT Store creators lacked direct monetization and usage analytics. Top Road adds paywalls, subscriptions and analytics through a no code action.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers (Free, Pro 10 dollars a month, Business 90 dollars a month) plus a seller fee of 20 to 30 percent on creator revenue
product_category: Creator monetization and analytics for AI apps
market_need_then: At the GPT Store launch in January 2024 builders complained of weak analytics and no payments, per VentureBeat and WIRED coverage; the company claims 300K dollars in subscription revenue enabled by January 2025.
outcome_analysis: Top Road is a two person team whose current product serves creators on OpenAI's GPT Store, a market the press describes as having weak monetization. It depends on a platform that could add the same payment and analytics features, and no outside funding was found. It remains listed as active, so the failure factor reflects structural risk, not a confirmed failure.

name: Topship
one_liner: Flexport for African Merchants - Building the OS for Global Logistics
long_description:
Topship is the easiest way for African businesses to export/import cargo, freight and parcels to their suppliers, distributors and customers.  We are building Flexport for Africa.

Our goal is to build a Global Distribution System that makes delivery of parcels, cargo and freight easy for African businesses.
regions: Nigeria; Africa
target_customer: African merchants importing and exporting goods who need shipping, freight and parcel services
problem: African merchants find international shipping and freight forwarding hard and costly. Topship aims to be a Flexport for African businesses.
business_model: Logistics service with margin on freight and parcel shipping (asset light)
product_category: Digital freight forwarding and cross border logistics
market_need_then: African merchants were importing and exporting through informal channels; Topship began as an Instagram parcel business and moved to import export tooling in March 2021 per TechCabal, and logistics drew heavy investment in 2020 to 2022.
outcome_analysis: Topship grew from an Instagram parcel service into a YC backed digital forwarder and raised a 2.5 million dollar seed led by Flexport in May 2022, which fits the Flexport for Africa pitch. Founders had logistics, tax and engineering backgrounds. No later round, layoff or shutdown was found, so its current stage is unclear beyond being active.

name: Torpedo Therapeutics
one_liner: High-precision, closed-loop neuromodulation devices
long_description: We are building high-precision implantable neuromodulation devices that can sense and stimulate neural activity in the brain with the goal of transforming the efficacy and adoption of deep brain stimulation (DBS), an existing  FDA-approved therapy used to treat Parkinson’s, essential tremor and epilepsy.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Neurologists, hospitals and device makers treating Parkinson's, essential tremor and epilepsy with deep brain stimulation
problem: Current deep brain stimulation electrodes are large and open loop. Torpedo builds micro electrode leads that sense and stimulate, with a chip and machine learning for closed loop control.
business_model: Medical device development, expected product sales or licensing after regulatory approval
product_category: Neuromodulation medical devices
market_need_then: DBS is FDA approved for Parkinson's, essential tremor and epilepsy and incumbents were adding sensing, which shows clinical interest in closed loop stimulation.
outcome_analysis: Torpedo Therapeutics is an early stage device company led by a neuroscientist founder, aiming at closed loop deep brain stimulation. Public sources show no priced round, only aggregator mentions of YC money, so its financing and progress are unknown. The path is long and capital heavy, and Medtronic reached closed loop DBS approval in 2025.

name: Touch and Pay Technologies Limited
one_liner: Digitizing and processing Microtransactions in Africa
long_description: We process cash-based microtransactions across Africa's informal sector, an example of microtransaction is payment for bus rides today we help over 300k people make this payment.
regions: Nigeria; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Informal-sector transport operators, passengers, merchants and institutions in Nigeria/Africa
problem: Cash-based micro-transactions (e.g. bus fares) in Africa's informal sector are untracked and leak revenue.
business_model: Transaction commission: 3% on each processed fare transaction, with TAP funding top-up points and card readers (How We Made It in Africa, 2023)
product_category: Fintech / NFC payments
founder_names: Olamide Afolabi; Michael Oluwole; Kabir Yabo
market_need_then: Informal and government buses in Lagos handled cash fares; the CEO cites about 300,000 daily riders on government buses and an estimated 7 million daily danfo passengers as the opportunity, and 64 million Nigerian adults lacking bank access per one outlet.
outcome_analysis: Touch and Pay turned a 2019 pivot into transport fare payments into the Cowry card, winning the Lagos BRT contract in 2020 and growing from one million to nearly five million users by 2024 with over 20 billion naira processed, and says it is profitable. Outside funding is murky: Crunchbase-based reports cite $4 million from Unicorn Growth Capital and a stalled 2023 raise, so government dependence and a thin funding record are the main risks.

name: Trackingplan
one_liner: Automated QA for your Digital Analytics
long_description:
Trackingplan automatically discovers and monitors all the information your applications and websites are collecting, ensuring that you can trust your BI, analytics, marketing, and sales tools. 

You can think of us as Segment Protocols but totally transparent, where developers can keep using Google Analytics, Amplitude, Hubspot, Intercom, Braze, etc. as they are used to. 

Installed in minutes in using your Tag Manager or adding just one line of code to your web or apps, we model all the data being sent to third parties. Since Trackingplan understands what each piece of data means, it identifies patterns, detects anomalies, and automatically connects the dots to create value from data that was hidden in plain sight:

- An always up-to-date single source of truth and data governance tool. To discover, understand and document your data and improve communication across teams.
- Automated notifications when something breaks or changes. To make sure that integrations are always well implemented: Schema errors, traffic anomalies, rogue events... 
- Easy to understand, customizable, cross-service alerts. To detect trends, insights, and problems without using complex, engineer-oriented solutions.
all_locations: Barcelona, CT, Spain; CT, Spain; Remote
regions: Spain; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Digital analytics, paid media and compliance teams and agencies that depend on tracking data from websites and apps
problem: Analytics and marketing tags break silently, so reports and ad spend rest on bad data. Trackingplan monitors real traffic to find broken tags, missing properties and consent breaches.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a free trial and an agency partner program
product_category: Analytics observability and data quality
founder_names: Alexandros Andre Chaaraoui; Jose Padilla; Jose Luis Perez; Pedro Trujillano
market_need_then: Companies rely on analytics and ad tags for decisions and consent compliance and broken tracking was a known cost, which created demand for QA tooling.
outcome_analysis: Trackingplan is a Barcelona company with a technical and entrepreneurial founding team that pre-seeded in 2021 with Spanish funds and angels and joined YC in winter 2022. It claims over 750 customers including large agencies and has repositioned as a digital analytics agent. No later priced round, exit or layoffs were found, so growth is capital efficient or undisclosed.

name: TradeX
one_liner: Prediction Market exchange for Asian market
long_description:
TradeX is a prediction market platform for people to bet on their every day events like no of ebola cases, winner of super bowl, rainfall in nyc or the next president. 

5+ users combined did more than $300m in annual trading volume. Founded by 3 engineers and repeat founders from IIT Delhi and Roorkee, one of the most prestigious college in India. 

We run direct to consumer prediction market exchange as well provide broker APIs for casinos, stock broking apps to integrate out exchange and facilitate events trading inside their platforms.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Indian retail users who bet on event outcomes, and brokers or gaming apps that integrate its exchange by API
problem: People wanted to trade on opinions about news and events, with no regulated Indian venue. TradeX runs a prediction market exchange and offers broker APIs.
business_model: Exchange fee on real money event trading plus B2B API
product_category: Prediction market and opinion trading app
founder_names: Divij Goyal; Indrajeet Roy; Ankit Shrivastava
market_need_then: Indian users already engaged with real money gaming and trading apps and early opinion trading apps raised venture money in 2021 to 2022.
outcome_analysis: TradeX raised 1 million dollars in early 2022 for an Indian prediction market and never raised a verified later round. Real money trading was shut down in 2025 after state bans and SEBI scrutiny, and it moved toward a free to play model. The legal status of the product, not demand, was the binding limit.

name: Tranch
one_liner: Tranch is the invoice to payments platform for enterprises.
long_description:
Tranch is the invoice to payments platform for enterprises who want to optimize cash flow by offering their business clients an unparalleled payment experience.

Based out of New York City and London we enable Services firms, software and marketplaces to be paid faster via our automated invoice to payment solutions. Our frictionless payment methods include Pay Now via FedNow, Pay by Card, Pay by Crypto and Pay Later from 2 to 12 months up to $1M.

Find out more about how we simplify and accelerate accounts receivables for enterprises with the most innovative workflows and payment solutions at www.tranch.com.

Tranch is backed by leading investors including: Global Founders Capital, TracVC, UpHonest Capital, Soma Capital, FoundersX and Y Combinator.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: SaaS and professional services providers, later law firms, that want upfront payment while offering buyers flexible terms
problem: Providers wait for large invoices to be paid while business buyers want to spread payments over months.
business_model: Fees on B2B buy now pay later and invoice payments, funded by credit facilities
product_category: B2B buy now pay later and invoice payments
market_need_then: Providers wanted upfront cash on large invoices; the 2022 press coverage describes BNPL moving into B2B, but no dated spend figures were retrieved.
outcome_analysis: Tranch raised a 3.5 million pound pre-seed in May 2022, then a roughly 5 million seed with a 95 million credit facility in January 2023, while its payment volume with large law firms more than tripled in 2024. Elite acquired it in January 2025 to embed payments in law firm billing, a vertical fit exit with undisclosed terms.

name: Transfez
one_liner: Brex for small businesses in Indonesia
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indonesian consumers and small remittance users, later businesses needing local disbursement and business banking
problem: Sending money abroad from Indonesia was slow and awkward; the CEO says a bank errand to send money to a relative took over two hours. Transfez built a remittance app and later business tools.
business_model: Remittance fees and FX margin, plus B2B payments and spend products under the Jack brand
product_category: Cross border remittance and business payments (fintech)
market_need_then: Indonesia has a large diaspora and SME base and the company claimed 30x transaction growth during the pandemic and a 105 million dollar total volume run rate in 2021 per e27.
outcome_analysis: Transfez raised an undisclosed seed from East Ventures and BEENEXT in May 2021, joined YC in winter 2022 and extended into business payments with the Jack brand in 2023. It holds a Bank Indonesia license per its site. No later priced round or exit was found, so scale and funding after seed are unknown.

name: Trebu
one_liner: AI coworker that automates freight tendering and shipment monitoring…
long_description: Trebu is an AI coworker for road freight. Tendering and tracking loads still run on emails, calls and WhatsApp messages between shippers, brokers and carriers. Trebu reads those messages, pulls out load details, matches loads to carriers and handles the back-and-forth until each load is covered. Once a truck is moving, Trebu monitors the shipment, follows up with drivers and flags delays or incidents before they become problems. Ops teams move more freight with fewer people, and every load is tracked in one place from tender to delivery.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Shippers, 3PLs and carriers in Latin American road freight (originally digital lenders in Latin America)
problem: Tendering and tracking loads runs on emails, calls and WhatsApp messages, so ops teams spend their time copying load details and chasing carriers and drivers.
business_model: B2B SaaS AI agent for logistics operations; pricing not stated
product_category: AI agent for freight tendering and shipment monitoring
market_need_then: The YC launch post at the batch targeted LATAM digital lenders fighting fraud and default. Demand evidence for the later freight use case is the company's own claim that tendering runs on messages.
outcome_analysis: Trebu is listed as active with a team of 5. Sources show a change from a lender data network at the batch to a freight and logistics AI agent, with no dated pivot reason. No outcome news such as an acquisition, shutdown or layoffs was found, and funding beyond aggregator entries is unknown, so the story is unclear.

name: Trellus
tags: SaaS; B2B; Sales; Sales Enablement; AI
one_liner: Power and parallel dialing with AI coaching, inside your CRM
long_description: Trellus is a Chrome extension that power dials or parallel dials up to five lines inside the CRM or sales engagement platform a sales team already uses, and saves each call's outcome, notes and callback back to the record the rep called from. Reps rehearse objections with AI practice calls, and teams on the Business plan add real-time AI coaching, team analytics and a virtual sales floor. Plans start at $99.99 per seat per month.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B sales teams and SDRs that cold call from a CRM or sales engagement tool
problem: Outbound reps lose time dialing one line at a time and get little coaching during live calls.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat per month (Power $99.99, Power + Parallel $149.99, Business plan adds coaching)
product_category: Power and parallel dialer with AI call coaching (Chrome extension)
market_need_then: The company's own pages cite sales teams wanting more dialing volume inside their existing CRM, with G2 and Chrome Web Store ratings as later evidence of adoption.
outcome_analysis: Trellus is active with a team of 8 and a product that adds parallel dialing, coaching and SOC 2 compliance, with customer logos on its site. No acquisition, layoffs or shutdown was found, and funding is not verified, so the trajectory is only partly visible and no strong success or failure factor can be assigned.

name: Trendex - Connect with stars
one_liner: Bringing fans closer to the world’s greatest athletes
long_description:
Trendex is the world leader in digital solutions for fans in the football ecosystem.
We partnered with Zinedine Zidane, Karim Benzema, Luis Suarez, Luka Modric, Blaise Matuidi and many other ballon d'or winners and superstars (1B+ followers on Instagram totalized).
Recently, we opened NBA, F1 and Hollywood partnerships including names like Jean Claude Van Damme, Rudy Gobert (3x NBA All-Stars), Marcus Smart (Lakers) and many others.
We build digital experiences for fans and organize exclusive events for our most selected partners.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Sports fans who buy athlete tokens and play fantasy games, plus athletes and celebrities who partner with the platform
problem: Fans cannot share in the careers of athletes they follow, and athletes lack ways to monetize their audience directly.
business_model: Tokenization platform selling athlete tokens backed by image rights, plus fantasy game and events
product_category: Athlete and creator tokenization (Solana)
market_need_then: Fan tokens and sports NFTs were a visible crypto segment in 2021 and 2022 per the Chiliz and Cointelegraph coverage found, though demand durability was not shown.
outcome_analysis: Trendex stayed active, signed athlete partners and acquired the Web3 streaming platform Gummys in May 2024 per CB Insights and press listings. It later ran a small crowdfunding raise per Kingscrowd, which suggests limited venture momentum, but funding sources conflict, so the trajectory is not clear.

name: TrueBiz
one_liner: Instant Background Checks for Businesses
long_description:
TrueBiz helps financial service providers reduce manual review during business onboarding.

We add color to the company's background with 250+ data points on the company from around the web (such as industry and address), and summarize key risk indicators.

The process takes seconds – not days, so financial service providers can efficiently meet risk requirements and onboard new businesses faster.
all_locations: Miami, FL, USA; New York, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Financial service providers (banks, fintechs, payment firms) onboarding business customers
problem: Know-your-business onboarding checks require slow manual review; TrueBiz compiles 250+ web data points and risk indicators in seconds.
business_model: B2B SaaS / API (per-check, pricing not found)
product_category: KYB / business identity verification (regtech)
market_need_then: Seed backers (Flourish Ventures) framed it as building KYB infrastructure; the YC page cites manual review of business onboarding as the pain. No dated spend figures found.
outcome_analysis: TrueBiz is active with a small team and raised a $2.4M seed in January 2023 led by Flourish Ventures, after the Summer 2022 batch. No Series A or exit was found, so it has neither clearly succeeded nor stalled. Hiring for sales and enterprise roles suggests an effort to scale go-to-market, but sources do not give revenue or customer traction.

name: Trueplace
one_liner: Supercharging humans
long_description: Preparing individuals for important interviews

name: Typewise
one_liner: Customer service AI that resolves requests end-to-end.
long_description:
Typewise resolves customer service requests end-to-end. Someone sends a request; it reads the message, looks up the real order or account in your own systems, takes the action, and replies. Anything it shouldn't touch goes to a human. It works across email, chat, WhatsApp and social, and is MCP-native.

Until now, that took a proper setup project, which is why it was mostly larger companies using it. Nova does the setup for you. You describe how you want things handled, in plain sentences:
- "Handle refunds under €50 yourself."
- "Anything about enterprise pricing goes to a human."
- "Turn bug reports into Linear issues and assign them to the Excellence team."

Nova connects the tools, configures the agents, tests them against your past conversations, and shows you what it got wrong before anything goes live. Nothing ships without your approval. First deployment takes 15 minutes. After that, it keeps going: it surfaces what customers keep complaining about, proposes fixes, and ships the ones you approve. We call it an AI Operator because it doesn't just answer customers; it keeps the entire operation working and improving. Across live accounts, that means 90% of requests resolved without human involvement.

Your team stays in control of what it may do on its own. Hybrid intelligence handles partial hand-offs, review-before-send, and context-preserving resumption.

We're YC S22 and work with companies like Superhuman and Unilever. Fortune 500 brands such as Unilever and DPD use Typewise to cut support effort by 50%+ while increasing CSAT and NPS. Run it natively in Typewise Ticketing or inside Zendesk, Salesforce or Freshdesk, with a CRM-embedded copilot for your human agents. EU-hosted, ISO 27001 certified.

name: Velt
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Collaboration; Compliance; AI
one_liner: SDK for adding an agent and human governance layer to your product
long_description:
For most of software's history the hard part was making things. Writing the code, drafting the document, putting the report together. That is the part that is getting cheap. An agent can now produce in an afternoon what used to take a team a month.

What doesn't get cheaper is verifying it. Someone still has to look at what the machine did, decide whether it's right, and answer for that decision later. Output goes up, review capacity doesn't, and that is where the work now piles up.

Velt is the infrastructure for that step, and it treats agents and people as the same kind of reviewer. A review agent takes the first pass and catches what a machine can catch. A person makes the call on what actually matters. Both work on the same object, in the same thread, under the same rules. Only after approval is the change applied, through your own webhook, and every decision is recorded, so you can always show who allowed what and when.

Teams build this themselves and it takes about two quarters. Comments, approvals, review agents, notifications, audit trails: the boring parts nobody thinks about until they're three months in. With Velt it's a few components you drop into a React, Next, Vue, or Angular app.

market_need_then: Figma and Google Docs raised user expectations for collaboration, and two funded rivals had launched around 2021, which implies demand for embeddable collaboration infrastructure.
outcome_analysis: Velt sells an SDK for embedding collaboration and now AI review flows, and lists customers such as Google, Pendo and HeyGen on its site. regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Tattoo artists and studios (current product); remote-first employers running recurring company meetings (original Venue.live product)
problem: Tattoo artists lose time to booking admin, chat and payment collection. The original product addressed dull recurring remote meetings such as all hands and town halls.
business_model: Booking fee on client payments (a third party reports about 10 percent, free for artists), unverified
product_category: Booking and payments software for tattoo artists; formerly remote meeting software
market_need_then: Accel describes remote-first employers struggling with engaging recurring meetings, and cites Shopify and PwC adoption and over 100K employees served in August 2022.
outcome_analysis: Venue raised a 4M seed led by Accel in August 2022 for its remote meetings product, with Shopify and PwC as early users. The company later moved into a tattoo booking app and claims over 1,000 artists, a self-reported figure. No later rounds were found, so the story after the pivot is unclear.

name: Versa
one_liner: Smart receipts for your business spend
long_description: Versa is a merchant-owned network, through which merchants securely send purchase details to buyers. You'll automate government-mandated receipt capture, reduce chargebacks, and grow sales.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; New York, NY, USA
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Merchants who send itemized digital receipts to business buyers, and finance teams that need receipts in expense systems
problem: Business buyers must collect receipts for tax and expense compliance, which is manual, and merchants face disputes and chargebacks.
business_model: Free to buyers at launch per the YC post; merchant-side monetization not stated. Later hotel invoice reconciliation product.
product_category: Smart receipts network, later AI hotel invoice reconciliation
market_need_then: The launch post cites IRS receipt requirements for transactions over 75 dollars and European VAT reclaim rules as the compliance pain.
outcome_analysis: Versa started as a merchant-owned receipt network and its website now sells hotel invoice reconciliation with a SOC 2 badge, which suggests a narrower pivot. No funding, traction or outcome data was found, so the company's progress is unknown beyond still having a live site.

name: Versable
one_liner: AI powered product description enhancement for the auto parts industry
long_description:
Auto parts retailers get product data from hundreds of manufacturers that is inaccurate and inconsistent, often with big gaps in key values. They currently have a team of "catalog managers" who are required to process and enhance this data line by line, resulting in a week to months long lag between receiving product data and actually being able to start generating revenue from those products. 

Versable leverages AI to scan the web for tens of millions of auto parts listings, and uses a fine-tuned LLM with RAG to instantly process, enhance, and transform data. With just a part number, Versable is able to generate market-ready titles, product descriptions, and specs, in any format that's needed.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Auto parts retailers and ecommerce sellers with inaccurate supplier product data
problem: Supplier part data is inconsistent and incomplete; retailers need titles, descriptions and specs per marketplace guidelines.
business_model: B2B SaaS for catalog enhancement (pricing not found)
product_category: AI product-data enrichment for automotive aftermarket
market_need_then: Auto parts ecommerce growth and industry-standard data (ACES/PIES) that suppliers adopt voluntarily leave gaps; the founder describes a 500B+ dollar market.
outcome_analysis: Versable is a three-person company serving auto parts retailers with LLM-generated product data, and went through a private beta before a public launch around July 2024. Reported funding is small and mostly from YC and angels. There is no evidence of large traction or an exit, so it is a slow-growing niche startup whose outcome is unresolved.

name: Vessel
tags: Sales; API; Marketing; Customer Support; CRM
one_liner: Developer-first, native integration platform for GTM tools
long_description:
Vessel is the developer-first, native integration platform for GTM tools. We make it easy for developers to integrate with your customer’s CRMs, Sales Engagement, Marketing Automation, Chat, Dialers, and more. Integrate in different ways customized for your use cases: 

- Speed: Use our Unified APIs to roll out many integrations quickly through a common data model and unified interface.
- Depth: Use our actions API to build deeper integrations when working with entities custom to each app.
- Ease: Use ETL to let us handle pulling and pushing customer data to your DB
- Extensible: Support any integrations through our open-source integrations library

Breadth and depth, make your integrations limitless.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Vimmerse
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Video; Advertising; AI
one_liner: Bring your photos to life with Vimmerse
long_description: Designers, branding agencies, and on-line stores can use Vimmerse’s AI creators platform, Apps, and API to animate their images at scale making their business stand out from the crowd.
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; San Jose, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Designers, branding agencies and online stores that animate images at scale; now creators, agencies and developers
problem: Static product and brand images do not stand out; producing animated or immersive content is costly.
business_model: Subscription and API usage (a third-party listing shows pricing from 29 dollars a month)
product_category: AI image animation, later AI video workflow platform
market_need_then: Not evidenced in sources opened beyond the YC pitch that agencies and stores want animated images.
outcome_analysis: Vimmerse is still active and has moved from photo animation to an AI video workflow platform. It claims 20,000 daily activations on its own site. Funding and growth are not verifiable from public reporting found.

name: Vinci Games
one_liner: Creating genre-defining multiplayer VR games.
long_description:
Vinci Games (YC S22) is building the next generation of social multiplayer VR games.

Our first title, Blacktop Hoops, became one of the highest-rated sports games on Meta Quest with a passionate global community and critical acclaim.

Our second title, Ruffnauts, is already one of the fastest growing F2P releases of 2025 on Meta Quest, with 30K+ reviews at 4.9 stars in its first month of Alpha Early Access. Ruffnauts combines creature catching, chaotic physics, and Gorilla Tag style locomotion into a groundbreaking VR adventure.

The company is led by CEO Nathaniel Ventura (ex-Oculus, Google, Meta) and CTO Maciej Szcześnik, former lead gameplay designer at CD Projekt Red for The Witcher series. Our mission is to create genre-defining VR experiences that bring millions of players together.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Meta Quest, Pico and PC VR players who buy or play multiplayer VR games
problem: VR lacks sports and social franchises with depth comparable to NBA 2K or Madden on flat screens.
business_model: Premium game sales ($29.99 for Blacktop Hoops) and free to play with in-game purchases for Ruffnauts (monetization details not sourced)
product_category: Multiplayer VR games
market_need_then: Growth of Meta Quest 2 in 2021 to 2022 created a base of headset owners; the YC pitch compares VR sports to console franchises with no VR equivalent.
outcome_analysis: Vinci shipped Blacktop Hoops, raised a 5.1M seed in April 2023, and by 2025 reported its second title Ruffnauts was among the fastest growing free to play Quest releases. The studio is a 7 person team with founders from Oculus and The Witcher. Whether the growth converts to revenue is not documented in sources found.

name: Vizzly
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; B2B; Analytics; API
one_liner: Customer-Facing Analytics for Modern SaaS.
long_description:
Vizzly provides customer-facing analytics for modern SaaS.

The platform offers the same level of flexibility as an in-house development process with minimal technical overhead required.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: SaaS product teams that want to give their own customers embedded analytics and dashboards
problem: Embedded analytics tools are rigid, and building customer-facing dashboards in house distracts SaaS teams from their core product.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription embeddable analytics platform
product_category: Embedded analytics and customer-facing BI
market_need_then: SaaS companies increasingly needed to expose analytics to customers, and the YC launch post framed existing tools as rigid.
outcome_analysis: Vizzly was a four person London team in YC Summer 2022 selling embeddable dashboards to SaaS companies in a crowded field with funded rivals such as Explo and Cube. Only an aggregator reports a small raise, and the exit appears to be a late 2024 sale to Gain Theory, described by one unverified profile as an acquihire with product support ended. The pattern fits a small team that could not out scale better funded competitors.

name: Vobi
one_liner: All-in-one project management software for construction SMBs in Latam
long_description:
Vobi is a project management platform for small construction businesses, like home remodeling companies, contractors, and architects.

We help them save up to 50% of their time spent on manual work, mainly on the procurement and estimation processes, so they have more time to focus on their core activities. Through Vobi, they can manage projects from start to finish, collaborate with their customers, plan, quote, and make purchases or payments to suppliers, all in one place. No more spreadsheets and papers!
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small construction businesses in Brazil such as remodelers, contractors, architects and engineering firms
problem: Small builders manage estimates, purchasing and projects with spreadsheets and paper, losing time on manual procurement and estimation.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscriptions with a free tier, plus planned supplier marketplace and construction insurance
product_category: Construction project management software
founder_names: Ythalo Silva; Murillo Freitas; Guilherme Guerra; Fabio Witt
competitors_at_founding: Obra Prima (01 Tecnologia); Juntos Somos Mais
market_need_then: Brazilian small builders relied on spreadsheets and paper; the company reported a little over 35 thousand customers including free users at the end of 2021.
outcome_analysis: Vobi grew from a remodeling marketplace into a construction management SaaS with a free tier and over 35 thousand users by the end of 2021. It raised about 7 million reais in February 2022 led by Y Combinator with MAR Ventures and angels. By 2026 it claims nationwide presence and AI agents, with a 45 person team; no later round was found.

name: Voltic
one_liner: Electric cargo ships
long_description:
Voltic is launching US-built cargo ships that are 4x more profitable than diesel vessels. 

We have $100M+ in sales to companies including the largest US shipping company and the largest global shipper by volume. We are on pace for our first commercial deployment in early 2026. The team previously started two shipping lines and has decades of experience in maritime innovation. Our patented battery & solar tech stack was spun out of MIT’s Ocean Engineering department. We are backed by top investors like the largest maritime VC in the world.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Container shippers and cargo owners buying ocean transport on short sea routes
problem: Diesel container ships carry high fuel cost and emissions (the launch post cites shipping at 2.2 percent of world CO2).
business_model: Operating shipping lines with owned electric vessels; sales contracts with shippers
product_category: Electric cargo ships and shipping line
market_need_then: Launch post cites zero emission regulation pressure, fuel as a major operating cost and Department of Energy grants supporting the tech stack.
outcome_analysis: Voltic is active, claims over 100M dollars in sales contracts and targets first commercial deployment in early 2026, a self reported figure. Its website now describes a shipping line with diesel backup rather than a pure electric ship. Funding is only supported by aggregators, so capital strength and delivery risk are unverified.

name: WANTD
one_liner: A direct to consumer marketplace and influencer network for brands
long_description:
WANTD is a D2C consumer marketplace for fashion and footwear brands to launch and sell product. We do the things Shopify is unable to do; we provide multiple channels to sell (e.g. live commerce, marketplace, auctions), influencer networks, and order fulfillment in a mobile-first experience. 

We solve the cold-start problem for brands and enable them to remain focused on product creation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Fashion and footwear brands, and consumers shopping live and mobile; early focus on sneaker power resellers
problem: Brands depend on Shopify without built-in demand; resellers juggle spreadsheets and several platforms.
business_model: Marketplace take rate and fulfillment fees (not sourced)
product_category: Direct to consumer marketplace with live commerce and influencer network
market_need_then: Employbl describes sneaker resellers using spreadsheets and several platforms; the YC pitch says brands face a cold start problem outside Shopify.
outcome_analysis: WANTD pitched a mobile first marketplace for fashion and footwear brands with live commerce and influencer channels, and had a 4 person team. No funding, traction or exit was verified, and sources conflict on whether it still operates. Strong incumbents in resale and live commerce make the wedge hard, but no failure cause is public.

name: Wagetap
one_liner: Access up to $2,000 of your wage in advance
long_description: Wagetap is a mobile app that allows users to get an advance of up to $2,000 on their next payday and pay their bills in more manageable instalments.
regions: Australia; Oceania; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Australian wage earners (18+, regular employer-paid income) who run short before payday and pay bills
problem: Workers face cash gaps between paydays and bill due dates; Wagetap advances up to $2,000 of the next pay and splits bills into instalments.
business_model: direct-to-consumer wage advance lending with a 5% withdrawal fee plus interest (24% p.a. on loan term) and bill split instalments
product_category: earned wage access and bill buy-now-pay-later app (Australia)
market_need_then: Pay-on-demand customer payments in Australia grew about 40 fold from Aug 2020 to Jan 2022 per an academic paper cited by search results, indicating rising demand.
outcome_analysis: Wagetap remains Active with a team of about 40 and claims over 300,000 users and more than 1.5 billion dollars lent, which implies real demand for wage advances in Australia. Its YC seed is only seen in aggregator listings, and no later rounds were found, so the capital story is unclear. Competition from Beforepay and Wagestream existed before the batch and the model faces regulatory scrutiny risk, but nothing sourced shows a setback.

name: Wand Solar
tags: Solar Power; Real Estate; Climate; ClimateTech
one_liner: We enable landlords to generate income from solar panels.
long_description: Wand Solar enables Solar Revenue for Income Properties owners. By empowering landlords to sell solar energy directly to tenants, we make it a no-brainer for landlords to adopt solar energy.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Landlords of rental properties that have or plan to install solar panels
problem: Landlords pay for rooftop solar but tenants capture the savings (the split incentive), and landlords have no easy way to bill tenants for solar energy.
business_model: software and services fee of 10% of the solar energy bill collected from tenants, plus optional financing and maintenance through installer partners
product_category: solar billing software for rental properties
market_need_then: YC launch post cites the claim that 55 percent of US electricity is used in rental properties and describes interviews with dozens of landlords; solar adoption by landlords was constrained by the split incentive problem.
outcome_analysis: Wand Solar is still listed as Active with a team of two, and no priced round, customer count or press coverage was found, so its trajectory is unclear. It targets a real structural gap (the landlord tenant split incentive) but entered a space where Ivy Energy already sold billing software, and its public footprint is thin.

name: Weltio
one_liner: First LatAm W3 WealthTech for AutoInvesting in securities & crypto
long_description: Weltio gives users access to a fully fledged brokerage account in USD, through unique features such as local instant cash rails, a robo-advisor, and tailored portfolios for the LatAm user.  Starting with MX we’re going after a market with a potential in AUM of >$60B and 40M accounts
regions: Mexico; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote

name: WhiteLab Genomics
tags: Gene Therapy; Cell Therapy; Genomics; AI
one_liner: Unleash the potential of genomic medicine using AI
long_description:
WhiteLab Genomics is a TechBio company using artificial intelligence to design the building blocks of genomic medicines. Its proprietary ALFRED platform designs viral and non-viral delivery vehicles and programmable genetic payloads, which are then experimentally validated and tested in vivo to identify candidates with the properties required for therapeutic development. 

Through this integrated approach, WhiteLab Genomics is building a portfolio of validated bio-assets that it advances independently and with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners developing the next generation of genomic medicines.

Founded in 2019, WhiteLab works with industrial and academic partners including Sanofi, Cytiva, the University of Massachusetts, the Vision Institute in Paris and the Paris Brain Institute, alongside additional collaborations with biotechnology companies. The company is part of Y-Combinator, Station F and Future4Care and is a French Tech 2030 laureate.

WhiteLab Genomics operates from Paris, Boston, and Montreal.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharma and biotech companies developing gene and cell therapies, plus academic partners
problem: Designing viral and non-viral delivery vehicles and genetic payloads for genomic medicines is slow and trial-and-error; WhiteLab uses machine learning to predict the best molecular designs before lab testing.
business_model: AI-enabled drug design: partnerships and collaborations with pharma plus an internal portfolio of validated bio-assets
product_category: TechBio, AI design of gene and cell therapy delivery vectors and payloads (ALFRED platform)
market_need_then: Gene and cell therapy developers needed better vector and payload design; Dyno raised a 100M Series A in 2021, showing investor appetite for AI in this space.
outcome_analysis: WhiteLab Genomics is Active and growing: it raised a 10M Series A in 2022 led by Omnes Capital and Debiopharm, then a 26M Series B in October 2026 led by AVP with both existing investors returning. Founders pair a healthcare executive with a genetics PhD, and pharma partnerships (Sanofi, Cytiva) validate the platform. The long gap between rounds and strong rivals like Dyno are the main risks.

name: Whiz
one_liner: Transforming Finances, Maximizing Your Money Potential.
long_description: Whiz revolutionizes the way you manage finances, providing innovative solutions for a wealthier future—where your money earns more, fully insured by Indonesia Deposit Insurance Corporation (IDIC). Join us on this journey toward financial empowerment.
regions: Indonesia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Wibond
tags: Banking as a Service; Cashierless Checkout; Fintech
one_liner: Affirm for LATAM
long_description:
Under "Buy Now, Pay Later" business model, Wibond is a 100% flexible digital payment method enabling the 200 million underbanked consumers without credit cards to shop online for the first time. 

We integrate directly into the purchase flow of online merchants, and we offer consumers a credit, when they have already made up their mind that they want to acquire a specific product.
We provide financial and digital access to a large community of people offering payment options according to their possibilities and profile. Wibond is an inclusive and simple solution:
 - Consumers can create their free account to quickly access and pay without banks, in installments, and without a card.
 - Merchants with e-commerce channels increase their sales and integrate Wibond in a very agile way by offering a new form of payment and expanding their markets.

We’re also integrated in the purchase flow of more than 500 merchants, including Samsung, Musimundo (one of the Biggest retailers in LATAM) , and Motorola. And up to 65% of the payment transactions on these sites go through us.
regions: Argentina; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Online merchants and platforms in Argentina, later also Chile and Mexico, and underbanked consumers without credit cards
problem: Many Latin American consumers have no credit card, so they cannot buy in installments online. Wibond offers buy now pay later at checkout, and later white-label wallet, payments and lending modules for other companies.
business_model: BNPL with merchant fees and consumer credit interest, later white-label fintech as a service
product_category: buy now pay later and fintech infrastructure
founder_names: Ezequiel Bucai; Lucrecia Porta; Alejandro Silvestre
market_need_then: Wibond cited 200 million underbanked consumers without credit cards. In 2021 and 2022 Argentine outlets ran explainers on buying in installments without a card, which shows public interest.
outcome_analysis: Wibond raised 2.25 million dollars in January 2022 and extended to about 6 million in June 2022 after YC, with Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph among backers. It claimed 500 merchant integrations at YC time and later repositioned as white-label fintech infrastructure in Argentina, Chile and Mexico. No newer round, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is continued operation with unclear scale.

name: Windmill
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; B2B; Workflow Automation; Open Source
one_liner: Open-source platform to turn scripts into internal apps & workflows
long_description:
Windmill is an open-source developer platform that turns scripts into workflows, internal tools, and full-stack apps.

Write scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, Bash, Rust, SQL - Windmill auto-generates UIs from their parameters, handles dependencies, credentials, permissions, and scheduling so you focus on business logic, not infra.
                                                                                     
Open-source alternative to Airflow, Temporal, Retool and n8n. Chain scripts into flows with branching, parallelism, retries. Build dashboards with the app builder. Trigger via cron, webhook, or UI. All-in-one runtime, editor, secret manager, and OAuth platform - enterprise-ready out of the box.
                                                                                                                            
Stack: Rust / TypeScript + Svelte / PostgreSQL. Self-hostable, easy to deploy, built for performance and DX.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams that want self-hosted internal tools, scripts and workflow orchestration
problem: Teams build internal apps and background jobs either with rigid no-code tools or with custom code that is slow to build and maintain; Windmill turns scripts into workflows and UIs.
business_model: open source (AGPLv3) core with paid Enterprise commercial license, support and hosted team plans
product_category: open source developer platform: workflow engine and internal tool builder
market_need_then: Launch post cites reliance on rigid no-code tools or custom scripts, risky live SQL on production, and many narrow SaaS tools; Launch HN thread of 2022-08 drew comparisons to Airplane, Pipedream, n8n and Temporal, showing interest in the category.
outcome_analysis: Windmill is Active, backed by YC, Bessemer and others per its site, and raised a reported 5M Series A in October 2024. A solo technical founder shipped an open source Rust platform that earned Hacker News attention in 2022 and 2023. Licensing debate (AGPL plus enterprise code) and crowded adjacent tools are the main risks; scale and revenue are not public.

name: Wingback
one_liner: Wingback provides tools and APIs for SaaS pricing and packaging.
long_description: Wingback provides tools and APIs for SaaS pricing and packaging. We are infrastructure that allows SaaS startups to deploy any set of features of their product using any pricing model. It enables non-technical teams to implement pricing and packaging changes and execute product-led growth campaigns without engineering involvement.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Winter
one_liner: Credit card checkout for NFTs
long_description: Stripe for NFT purchases. Easily buy/sell NFTs with a credit card.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: NFT marketplaces, launchpads and creators who want buyers to pay by card without a crypto wallet
problem: Buying an NFT required crypto and a wallet, which blocked mainstream buyers. Winter offered an embeddable checkout accepting card or bank payments.
business_model: Payments take rate on NFT sales through an embeddable checkout and API
product_category: NFT payments infrastructure
market_need_then: NFT trading boomed in 2021 and early 2022 and card payment was a known onboarding barrier, but demand collapsed through 2022 and 2023.
outcome_analysis: Winter built card checkout for NFTs in YC Winter 2022 just as the NFT market peaked and, within weeks, MoonPay shipped the same feature. NFT volume then fell sharply, the team widened into claim APIs, and Crossmint bought it in February 2024 with undisclosed terms and without the founder joining. That looks like an asset and customer pickup rather than a successful outcome.

name: Wolfia
one_liner: We help security, legal and sales teams answer customer questions
long_description:
We help security, legal and sales teams get answers in seconds without depending on subject-matter experts.

Our AI agent connects to every source that already holds the truth (Google Drive, Notion, Slack, email, website, trust center, SOC 2 docs, etc.). It keeps that knowledge graph fresh on its own and drafts, validates, and formats responses to customer questions, security questionnaires, and RFPs, all in the background, so your team just reviews and ships.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Security, legal, GRC and sales teams at B2B software companies that must answer customer security questionnaires and RFPs
problem: Answering customer security questionnaires and RFPs depends on scarce subject matter experts and slows deals; Wolfia's AI agent drafts cited answers from the company's own knowledge sources.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: AI agent for security questionnaires, RFPs and customer contract review
market_need_then: Security questionnaires were a recurring sales bottleneck for B2B vendors; evidence at the time of founding was not found in dated sources.
outcome_analysis: Wolfia is Active and still publishing in 2026, with named customers such as Amplitude, Miro and Handshake on its site and integration partnerships with Oneleet and AmplifyGRC. Funding beyond a YC convertible note is not public, so growth scale is unknown. Crowded competition from Conveyor, Loopio and Vanta and LLM commoditisation are the main risks.

name: Wondercraft
one_liner: Create video by chatting to AI
long_description: Wondercraft introduces vibe creation, creating video through natural conversation.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Creators, marketers, brands and enterprise teams (marketing, HR, L&D) producing podcasts, audio ads and business video
problem: Producing studio quality podcasts and audio is slow and costly (script, voice, recording, outsourcing); Wondercraft generates scripts and AI voices, later extended to video.
business_model: SaaS subscription with usage tiers, sold to creators and enterprises
product_category: generative AI audio and video studio
founder_names: Youssef Rizk; Dimitris Nikolaou; Oskar Serrander
market_need_then: Podcast creation was growing, with high production cost and time per YC launch post; the Hacker News Recap podcast built with the tool reportedly reached the top 40 tech podcasts on Spotify within a month.
outcome_analysis: Wondercraft is Active and raised a 3M seed in January 2024 led by Will Ventures with ElevenLabs and Steven Bartlett, reporting more than 30,000 users after a 2023 beta. It has since broadened from podcasts into video. Low defensibility on third party models and strong rivals like Descript are the main risks; later rounds or revenue are not public.

name: Workflow86
one_liner: Agentic workflows for complex, long running business operations
long_description:
Workflow86 provides a complete end-to-end platform for building agentic workflows and automating complex business processes and operations. 

Workflow86 provides users with a complete suite of tools to build and deploy custom agents and orchestrate them to perform complex, long-running workflows including human-in-the-loop steps, custom code, agent tools, and integrations with your existing systems. 

Build using a visual canvas, or simply describe the workflow in natural language with agents able to self-configure tools, prompts, and integrations, and even build the multi-agent workflows.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-size businesses and operations teams that need to automate complex, long-running business processes without coding
problem: Business processes with approvals, forms and integrations are managed in spreadsheets, CRMs or ERPs; Workflow86 lets teams build them in a no-code platform, later with AI that designs the workflow from a description.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a 14-day free trial
product_category: no-code and AI workflow automation platform
market_need_then: Businesses relied on spreadsheets, CRMs and ERPs for processes (per the YC launch post); no-code workflow companies in the region raised rounds in early 2022, indicating demand.
outcome_analysis: Workflow86 is Active with a team of about six based in Sydney and has kept shipping, now positioned around AI agents and human in the loop workflows. Public funding is limited to YC style small notes in aggregators, so growth, revenue and runway are unknown. A crowded no-code and AI automation market is the main constraint.

name: Wyvern
one_liner: High-res hyperspectral pictures of Earth from space
long_description: Wyvern is a space data company that will capture the highest resolution hyperspectral images from satellites that cost 100X less than satellites using traditional telescopes.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Organizations needing hyperspectral Earth imagery: agriculture, forestry and ESG, energy, mining, peace and security, plus governments and researchers
problem: Hyperspectral satellite imagery was scarce and expensive because it needed large telescope-based satellites; Wyvern builds small satellites with deployable optics to supply it at lower cost.
business_model: data sales and tasking of hyperspectral imagery (archive, tasking, open data program), with government and commercial customers
product_category: satellite hyperspectral Earth observation data
founder_names: Chris Robson; Kurtis Broda; Kristen Cote; Callie Lissinna
market_need_then: Hyperspectral data demand for agriculture, mining and climate monitoring was growing, and Canadian public funding (SDTC 2022-02) backed the technology; Pixxel's 25M raise in 2022 shows investor interest.
outcome_analysis: Wyvern is Active with about 26 people and has flown its first hyperspectral satellites in 2023 and signed with Loft Orbital to extend capacity. It combined grant money (SDTC in 2022), a 7M USD seed-plus in November 2022 and a 6M round in October 2024, reaching about 16M in private capital per Payload. Founders came from the Alberta student satellite programs, which fits the hardware challenge. Capital intensity and rivals like Pixxel remain risks.

name: Yezza
one_liner: Storefronts on WhatsApp in Southeast Asia
long_description:
Yezza makes it easy for small businesses in SE Asia to create storefronts on WhatsApp. Our MRR is $40K with $3M monthly GMV, from 1500 orders every day. We are profitable.

Not only for selling goods & products, Yezza also built features to fit with many use cases in WhatsApp Commerce. For example, social media influencers use Yezza to deal with brands using WhatsApp. We found that customers also make table reservations through WhatsApp.

Merchants pay us $12 per month & up to $0.25 per order. With 50M WhatsApp Business downloads in SE Asia, this creates a $7.2B market opportunity. Interestingly, a similar buying-via-WhatsApp behavior exists in Latin America & Africa.

Previously, we bootstrapped a tech-enabled travel company to $12M in annual revenue, by selling travel packages using WhatsApp. We built & used this product for 4 years in our previous company. During COVID19, we offshoot it to become a standalone business called Yezza.

Yezza is now backed by Y Combinator & angel who worked at Facebook/WhatsApp.
all_locations: Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
regions: Malaysia; Southeast Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small merchants in Southeast Asia who sell through WhatsApp; today also clinics and other service businesses
problem: Small businesses already take orders by chat on WhatsApp but manage them by hand. Yezza gives them a storefront, orders and payments inside WhatsApp.

name: autone
tags: Sustainable Fashion; Consumer; Supply Chain; Retail
one_liner: Inventory management SaaS for Retail & Consumer brands

Today, Retailers have to make 1000s of complex operational decisions every day, all impacting their bottom line.This problem is being currently tackled with excel or legacy systems, both no longer fit for purpose.

We make a platform that lets retailers make optimal decisions, easily and quickly. We ingest a retailer's data, generate recommendations and then allow users to approve a given action. Our platform covers topics including product pricing, inventory replenishment and re-ordering with the goal of covering all operational processes.

name: goodfin
one_liner: Building the next generation of wealth
long_description:
GoodFin is reimagining private wealth in the era of AI. Our mission is to empower a new generation to build wealth, starting with their investments in alternative assets. 

Our AI-native platform combines a design-forward experience with a backend powered by a system of intelligent agents. We are building a future where AI unlocks financial hyperpersonalization, automation and optimization for sophisticated financial products, which are typically gated by advisors and reserved for very wealthy clients. This highly fragmented $1.25T global services market will undergo a sea change in the coming years, as trillions pass in the largest intergenerational wealth transfer to date.  

In a world where most financial decisions will become automated, we believe the next category-defining wealth company will still be human-driven at its core – powered by a high-value community like our membership base of professionals, founders and investors. The next generation financial giant will be an AI-native platform that makes wealth creation seamless, personalized, and social. That’s what we’re building.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

business_model: Membership fees plus deal and fund fees; Goodfin pools investor capital into vehicles and is not a broker-dealer or registered adviser per its site
product_category: Private wealth and alternative investments platform
market_need_then: YC description argues alternative assets were gated by advisors and reserved for the very wealthy, with a large intergenerational wealth transfer ahead. No independent demand evidence from 2022 was opened.
outcome_analysis: Goodfin is still active and expanding its product, launching the Goodfin Go AI system in January 2026 and a QSBS venture fund in July 2026, and it appeared at FinovateSpring 2026. Its funding is not credibly documented, so the traction and outcome are unclear. It competes with established private market platforms such as EquityZen and Yieldstreet.

name: voize
tags: Machine Learning; Speech Recognition; Healthcare; NLP
one_liner: We build the AI companion for nurses, to create time for care.
long_description:
At voize, we believe the greatest gift to frontline workers is time - time to care, connect, and be present. Today, that time is lost to admin work that pulls nurses away from what matters most: people. 

We’re changing that by building the AI companion that frees nurses from admin, giving them back up to 30% of time. We don’t replace humans - we support and amplify their impact. Today, 1,500+ care facilities trust voize, and over 100,000 nurses rely on our AI companion** to ease their daily workload.

Our mission is backed with a $50M Series A funding led by Balderton Capital, with support from HV Capital, Y Combinator and other leading VCs.

name: Accend

name: Aglide
one_liner: Connect every disconnected app to your SSO.
long_description:
Our mission is to secure access to every enterprise application.

Aglide SSO lets security and IT teams connect non-standard and legacy apps - from banking portals to social media logins - directly to their existing identity provider (Okta, Entra, OneLogin, Ping, etc.), with no need for app-side integration.

Once connected, these apps behave like any other IdP-managed service: policies like MFA, Conditional Access, RBAC, and audit logging just work, and end users access them through SSO only.

Customers use Aglide to secure both individual apps (e.g., legacy banking portals, Discord, Squarespace) and sensitive shared accounts (e.g., AWS root, social media). Our agentic identity technology means Aglide works with any app out of the box - no integration catalog, no custom scripting.

Today, companies from public fintechs like Gemini to media companies like The Motley Fool rely on Aglide’s zero-trust, end-to-end encrypted platform to complete their identity stack.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Security and IT teams at companies that use Okta, Entra, OneLogin or Ping and have apps without SAML or SCIM support
problem: Many apps are outside an identity provider because they lack SSO support or gate it behind an SSO tax, so MFA, access policies and audit logs do not reach them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for identity connection
product_category: Enterprise identity and SSO
market_need_then: The SSO tax, where vendors charge more for SSO, drew public backlash and left non-standard apps unmanaged; a search shows a 2023 era discussion by 1Password and Cerby about apps outside SSO.
outcome_analysis: Aglide is an active London company with named customers such as Gemini and The Motley Fool on its own site, and a six-person team per YC.
