No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is only seen on aggregators, so capital efficiency and stage cannot be assessed reliably.

name: AiSDR
one_liner: AI that finds the right buyers and books sales meetings
long_description:
AiSDR builds Ami, an AI sales agent that helps B2B companies find customers and book meetings.

Give Ami your website. It researches your business, recommends who to target and why now, and builds an outreach plan. Once you approve, it runs personalized campaigns across email and LinkedIn, follows up, handles replies, and books meetings.

Ami keeps working after launch. It monitors results, spots problems with targeting or messaging, and recommends changes or applies them within the rules you set. It remembers your decisions and campaign results, so each campaign builds on the last.

Built on lessons from 17,000+ real AiSDR campaigns, Ami gives founders and small teams sales strategy and execution in one place, without having to manage every step themselves.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B companies and small sales teams that want outbound prospecting and meeting booking automated
problem: Outbound sales development is repetitive and costly; AiSDR uses generative AI to find prospects, write personalized email and LinkedIn outreach and book meetings.
business_model: Usage-based and subscription, pay as you go at $1.50 per person prospected, with team and managed-service plans
product_category: AI sales development agent
market_need_then: Outbound sales is a large spend and generative AI made cheap personalization possible in 2023; AiSDR's YC launch post reported 24 customers within two months.
outcome_analysis: AiSDR raised a $3M seed after YC Demo Day in November 2023, reported 4x revenue growth in 2024 and a team of 21, and launched the Ami agent. Founders were repeat founders with a prior YC exit. No shutdown, layoffs or acquisition were found. The category is crowded, so durability depends on product quality rather than structural moat.

name: Airgoods
one_liner: The modern distributor for grocers.
long_description:
Trusted by independent grocers across America, Airgoods is the AI-native distributor transforming how stores discover, order, and sell the products their customers want. 

By combining proprietary data with automation across discovery, purchasing, receiving, and merchandising, Airgoods gives independent grocers the intelligence and operating leverage once reserved for the largest retail chains.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent grocers and specialty food and beverage retailers in the continental US, plus emerging food and beverage brands as suppliers
problem: Independent grocers struggle to discover new products and order from many small brands, while brands struggle to get into independent stores.
business_model: Wholesale marketplace and distributor, earning margin on goods with net 30 or net 60 terms for retailers
product_category: Food and beverage wholesale marketplace and distribution
founder_names: Aaron Farr; Paolo Carroll; Elian Haddock
market_need_then: Independent grocers lack tools available to big chains, per the YC page; no dated external demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Airgoods is an active New York company that has moved from a marketplace for functional beverages to what it calls an AI-native distributor, with named retail customers on its site. Funding is not verified from any primary source, and no shutdown or acquisition was found, so the outcome is undetermined. Unit economics of distribution with credit terms are the open question.

name: Alaan
one_liner: Ai-native finance platform for the Middle East
long_description:
Alaan is an AI-native finance platform for businesses in the Middle East. One platform for corporate cards, expense management, cross-border payments, accounting automation, treasury, business banking, and more, with AI doing the work finance teams used to do by hand: coding transactions, chasing approvals and receipts, flagging policy breaches, placing treasury deposits and closing the books.

Our mission is to simplify finance for businesses so they can save time and money.

Over 3,000 businesses use Alaan, from first-time founders to enterprises like Careem, G42, Tabby, Al Barari, and Rivoli. Since 2022, they have saved more than 2.2 million hours of manual finance work.

Alaan raised one of the largest Series A rounds in Middle East history, backed by Peak XV (formerly Sequoia India), Y Combinator, 468 Capital, and 885 Capital, among others. Headquartered in Dubai, Alaan has more than 250 employees across its Dubai, Riyadh, and Bangalore offices, with a team that comes from Careem, McKinsey, BCG, Goldman Sachs, Amazon, Revolut, Rippling, and the world’s leading firms.

Alaan has been named to the UAE Future 100 list, selected as an Endeavor company, and ranked the No. 1 spend management platform in EMEA by G2.
regions: United Arab Emirates; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Businesses in the UAE and wider Middle East, from startups to enterprises, that need corporate cards, expense management and payments
problem: Finance teams in the Middle East handle expenses, approvals and reconciliation by hand and with cash; Alaan offers cards and software to automate it.
business_model: Fintech: card interchange, SaaS fees and payments, with cards issued by NymCard and the business account by Ruya Community Islamic Bank (Alaan states it is not a bank)
product_category: Spend management and corporate cards
market_need_then: Qashio and Pemo describe UAE businesses as underserved in corporate cards and spend management (PYMNTS items, undated in results), and Alaan names a seed of $2.5M in March 2022.
outcome_analysis: Alaan raised a $2.5M seed in March 2022, a reported $4.5M round in 2023, and a $48M Series A in August 2025 led by Peak XV. It reports over 3,000 customers and more than 250 employees, expanding from cards to business accounts and AI automation. The founders' consulting and banking backgrounds fit the enterprise finance buyer, and the pace of funding suggests strong traction.

name: Alguna
one_liner: AI-Native CPQ & Billing for Modern Pricing Models
long_description:
We are Alguna, building a modern platform that helps B2B companies price deals, send quotes, bill customers, and collect payments - all in one place.

Our mission is to create the most efficient revenue engine for B2B SaaS.

Today, many companies run these processes with spreadsheets and a patchwork of separate tools. That leads to slow approvals, manual work, mistakes, and missed revenue—especially as pricing gets more complex.

Alguna replaces that mess by connecting the entire flow from **quote to cash**: what sales sells becomes what finance bills, automatically. We help teams automate invoicing, handle usage-based or custom pricing, and reduce back-and-forth between sales, finance, and engineering.

The result: growth-stage startups and enterprises can close deals faster, bill accurately, and scale revenue operations without adding headcount or building internal systems.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B SaaS, AI and fintech companies with complex or usage-based pricing, from growth-stage startups to enterprises
problem: Companies run pricing, quotes, invoicing and collections across spreadsheets and disconnected tools, causing slow approvals, billing errors and missed revenue.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for quote-to-cash and billing, with a free starter tier
product_category: Quote-to-cash, CPQ and billing
market_need_then: Usage-based pricing was spreading across SaaS and AI in 2023, as shown by Orb's $19.1M raise in March 2023 for pricing and billing.
outcome_analysis: Alguna went from YC S23 to a $4M seed announced October 2025, led by Mango Capital and Atlantic Labs, a slow two years between YC and its first confirmed round. It lists named customers such as Evervault and ComplyAdvantage and has added AI collections and an MCP server. The founders came from payments companies Dojo and Primer. Competition is intense, so the outcome is still open.

name: Alloy
one_liner: AI prototyping tool for product managers
long_description: Alloy is an AI prototyping tool for product managers. Clone any page of your live product with the Chrome extension to turn ideas, wireframes, and Figma designs into interactive, high-fidelity prototypes your team and customers understand. Alloy's Cloud Agent connects to your codebase and takes changes from prototype to production, and its AI chat can redesign any existing website. Design to code, no engineers required.
regions: Australia; Oceania
target_customer: Product managers and product teams at software companies that want interactive prototypes of new features built on top of their real product UI
problem: Product managers can plan features but lack a fast way to show them in the real product without designers or engineers, so ideas are validated slowly with static mockups.
business_model: B2B SaaS with a free tier and paid pro plans
product_category: AI prototyping and design-to-code tool
market_need_then: The team's own framing is that PMs could plan features but had no quick way to validate them; the original Index product was product planning and the prototyping focus came later. No independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Alloy, formerly Index, is active and raised a seed round of A$3.5M in February 2025 led by Blackbird and Bain Capital Ventures, then relaunched as an AI prototyping product in September 2025. Early signs include trade awards, but independent traction data is absent and it faces a crowded field of AI prototyping tools.

name: Alphawatch AI
tags: Generative AI; Finance; Enterprise; AI Assistant
one_liner: Data Layer for Modern Builders
long_description: Enrich leads, automate sourcing, monitor competitors, and power your product with structured data from sources across the web.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Financial research teams, hedge funds, private equity and enterprises that want structured data pulled from across the web
problem: Analysts spend time collecting and structuring information from many web and document sources for lead enrichment, sourcing and competitor monitoring.
business_model: B2B SaaS or API providing structured data (pricing not found)
product_category: AI data layer and research assistant
market_need_then: Financial research and sourcing is a large spend category and generative AI made structured extraction from documents newly feasible in 2023. No company-specific demand evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Alphawatch AI is listed as active with a three person team. Public information is thin and inconsistent across directories about whether it is a hedge fund chatbot, a document agent or a web data layer, which suggests the product positioning has shifted, but no dated pivot source was found. No shutdown, acquisition or later funding was reported.

name: Andromeda Surgical
tags: Hard Tech; Machine Learning; Medical Robotics; Medical Devices; AI
one_liner: Autonomous surgical robots
long_description: We're building autonomous robots to make surgery safe, easier and more efficient. Robots currently perform about 1/4 of surgeries but only help with the physical aspects. We use AI to make surgery cognitively easier. This has far greater potential to improve outcomes and reduce costs. Founded by 3x founders from medtech and autonomous vehicles, we're on track to be the fastest surgical robot to market of all time. First indication is prostate enucleation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hospitals and urologists performing endourology procedures, starting with HoLEP prostate enucleation
problem: Surgical robots help with the physical side of surgery but not the cognitive side; surgery remains hard to learn and outcomes vary by surgeon.
business_model: Medical device capital equipment and procedure-linked sales (details not found)
product_category: Autonomous surgical robotics and surgical AI
market_need_then: The company states robots perform about a quarter of surgeries but only help physically, and prostate enlargement is a large urology procedure. Demand evidence beyond the company's own framing was not found.
outcome_analysis: Andromeda is active. It performed what it calls the first robotic assisted HoLEP in Chile in December 2024, started the ASTRA trial, signed partnerships with Richard Wolf and Quanta System in 2025, and reported a $15M Series A led by Standard Capital in August 2026. Repeat founders with medtech and autonomy experience and clinical progress explain the raise, while commercialization and regulatory risk remain.

name: Apoxy
one_liner: Simpler and cheaper multi-cloud and cross-platform deployments.
long_description: Apoxy is the programmable edge platform that simplifies connectivity, security, and custom logic deployment for distributed applications. Our platform combines secure site-to-site networking with a high-performance runtime for custom TypeScript and Go filters, allowing developers to deploy business logic at the edge without complex infrastructure. Whether you need instant HTTP/TCP/UDP connectivity, advanced access controls, or custom data processing, Apoxy meets you where you are - from Kubernetes clusters to simple processes - with powerful observability and sub-second troubleshooting built in.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Platform and infrastructure engineers running Kubernetes clusters, clouds and sandboxes that need private connectivity, gateways and edge logic
problem: Connecting and securing workloads across clouds, clusters and platforms is complex and expensive, and running custom logic at the edge needs heavy infrastructure.
business_model: Usage and tiered SaaS (Free, Standard at $250 per month, Premium)
product_category: Programmable edge and networking platform
market_need_then: Multi-cloud and edge deployments were growing pain points, and WebAssembly at the edge was an established trend by 2021 per industry coverage. No company-specific demand evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Apoxy is active as a very small team. Its product has moved from a multi-cloud and edge deployment pitch toward private networking for Kubernetes, clouds and agent sandboxes, with one named customer case study and an invite-only beta. No later funding, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is undetermined.

name: Aqueduct
tags: Developer Tools; Gaming; Design Tools; AI
one_liner: Create, edit, and share procedural material graphs.
long_description:
Aqueduct is a procedural material engine, editor, and CLI.

Technical artists and environment artists use Aqueduct to create PBR materials and VFX textures from composable GPU shader nodes.

Aqueduct's MCP server is optimized for frontier models to create high quality, legible, adjustable procedural materials.

Because Aqueduct runs in the browser, it is easy to share links to procedural material graphs. For instance, see: https://aqueduct.sh/examples/g/marble-003.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Technical artists, environment artists and game or VFX studios that author PBR materials and textures
problem: Authoring procedural materials is slow and specialist work, and sharing material graphs between artists and tools is awkward.
business_model: Software subscription for a browser-based procedural material engine and editor (pricing not found; early access)
product_category: Procedural material and texture authoring tool
market_need_then: Game and VFX studios use procedural materials widely, and incumbents are subscription priced; the company's own pitch is browser sharing and agent-friendly graphs. No independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Aqueduct is a one person company that remains active, now offering a browser procedural material engine with an MCP server so AI agents can build materials. No funding announcement, exit, shutdown or traction numbers were found, so the outcome is undetermined and the data suggests a small, bootstrapped or lightly funded effort.

name: Arcimus
one_liner: A stream of engineering candidates who ship.
long_description: We send founders and recruiting teams  a steady flow of engineers filtered with real engineering judgment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Founders and recruiting teams at companies hiring engineers (current product); earlier, insurance carriers buying workers compensation premium audits
problem: Recruiters struggle to find engineers with real engineering judgment using resumes and keyword searches; earlier the problem was costly manual workers compensation premium audits.
business_model: Recruiting service delivering filtered candidate flow to client recruiting teams (pricing not found); earlier per-audit service combining LLMs and human auditors
product_category: Technical recruiting service
market_need_then: Workers compensation audits are a mandatory insurance process; the founders say they interviewed about 50 premium auditors and claim LLM plus human audits cost half as much. Demand evidence for the recruiting product was not found.
outcome_analysis: Arcimus pivoted from AI meeting notes to insurance premium audits during the 2023 batch and later to a recruiting service for engineers. Repeated pivots with no disclosed funding or traction suggest it has not found a venture-scale wedge, but it remains active and no shutdown was reported. The pivot_failed label is tentative since the latest pivot is recent.

name: Ariglad
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; B2B; Customer Success; Customer Service; Customer Support
one_liner: Knowledge base maintenance on auto-pilot
long_description:
Founded in Vancouver, British Columbia, Ariglad The first AI platform that integrates with support channels and release notes to auto-maintain your knowledge base. Ariglad suggests new articles, updates existing ones, detects duplicates, and merges them. Basically, it puts your knowledge base maintenance on auto-pilot.

This is led by Co-Founders Sophie and Ali. They are both completely obsessed with this problem and their customers, who have partnered with Ariglad to become immensely more efficient.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Customer support and success teams (current product); earlier, HR and people teams at companies
problem: Knowledge bases go stale because maintaining articles by hand is slow; earlier the problem was HR teams handling employee questions and sentiment.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (pricing not published)
product_category: AI knowledge base maintenance
market_need_then: In 2023 the product was an HR platform to spot burnout and handle employee questions; knowledge base maintenance became the focus later. No independent demand data found, though customers named on the site include Everbridge and Arise Health.
outcome_analysis: Ariglad launched in 2020 as an HR platform, raised a $1.3M seed led by Y Combinator in April 2023, and then repositioned toward AI knowledge base maintenance for support teams around mid 2024. It is active with named customers and claimed usage figures, but no later rounds were found, so the success of the pivot is unproven.

name: Arroyo
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Open Source; Cloud Computing
one_liner: Cloud-native stream processing
long_description:
Arroyo is a serverless stream processing platform built on top of the open-source Arroyo streaming engine. We allow companies to transform, filter, aggregate, and join their Kafka streams in real-time just by writing SQL. We charge purely based on usage, with no fixed costs or clusters to manage.

In 2025, Arroyo was acquired by Cloudflare and now powers Cloudflare Pipelines
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data and platform engineering teams running Kafka who pay usage-based fees for managed stream processing in SQL
problem: Stream processing with Apache Flink is hard to operate. Arroyo offered SQL pipelines on streams without managing clusters.
business_model: Open source engine plus usage-based managed cloud service
product_category: Stream processing engine
market_need_then: Streaming SQL demand was visible in a Show HN post in June 2023 with 115 points. Teams wanted lower operating burden than Flink.
outcome_analysis: Arroyo was a two person team with deep streaming experience from Lyft and Splunk, shipping an open source Rust engine. It gained developer attention in 2023 and was acquired by Cloudflare in April 2025, which folded it into Pipelines. The engine remains open source. Price is not public and external funding beyond YC is unverified.

name: Artie
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Data Engineering; Enterprise Software
one_liner: Software that streams data from databases to warehouses in real-time
long_description: Artie is software that streams data from databases to data warehouses in real-time. Today, most companies run their ETL process every few hours or overnight, so their data warehouse is always out of date; with Artie, the warehouse always has live production data.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data and engineering teams at software companies that run production databases and a cloud data warehouse
problem: Warehouses are loaded every few hours or overnight, so analytics and AI features see stale data. Artie streams row level changes from production databases to warehouses in near real time.
business_model: Usage based managed SaaS for change data capture, plus managed Kafka and enterprise BYOC tier
product_category: Real time data replication and change data capture
market_need_then: Batch ETL left warehouses hours behind production. Artie's customers include ClickUp, Substack and Alloy, which the company says process over 700 billion rows a year through it.
outcome_analysis: Artie is active with named customers such as ClickUp, Substack and Alloy, a $3.3M seed in February 2024 and a $12M Series A led by Standard Capital in January 2026. Real time data needs for AI features are a tailwind and the product has clear demand, while competition from Fivetran, Airbyte and open source Debezium keeps defensibility modest. Final outcome is not yet known.

name: Atla
one_liner: The improvement engine for AI agents
long_description:
Find and fix your agent’s most critical failures in hours, not days.

Atla helps developers cut time spent on manually reviewing traces. Atla’s LLM judge evaluates your agent step-by-step, uncovers error patterns across runs, and suggests specific fixes—so you know exactly what to fix and why.

Atla supports the most popular agent frameworks teams build with, including LangChain, CrewAI, and OpenAI Agents. With real-time monitoring, automated error detection, and prompt experimentation, Atla gives teams the visibility and control needed to confidently ship agentic systems that work. 

We’re a team of researchers, engineers, entrepreneurs and operational leaders. Our expertise in evals was honed through training our own purpose-built LLM Judges, Selene and Selene Mini, which are available open-source and have been downloaded 60,000+ times.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe

name: Atmeto
tags: Machine Learning; Climate; Energy; ClimateTech; AI
one_liner: Building a frontier world model for power
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Owners and operators of grid-scale batteries and power plants, asset managers and utilities
problem: Battery assets must decide when to buy and sell power at dynamic prices, and rule-based or human-run dispatch leaves value on the table.
business_model: Software for energy asset operators, likely revenue share or subscription (not found)
product_category: AI for energy dispatch and power plant operation
market_need_then: Grid battery capacity was expanding quickly in California and operators needed better dispatch; the founder's launch post frames RL as replacing hard-coded rules. No independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Atmeto, formerly Keeling Labs, applies reinforcement learning to grid battery dispatch and, per a profile, achieved CAISO certification in fall 2023 and began trading in California markets in 2024. The tagline later widened to a world model for power. It is active with YC, Pioneer Fund and Collab Fund listed as backers, but no verified round sizes or revenue figures were found.

name: Automat
tags: Documents; Developer Tools; Robotic Process Automation; Automation; AI
one_liner: Agentic automation that understands context, recovers, and improves.
long_description:
Automat is an AI automation company that replaces slow manual work and brittle legacy RPA with agents that understand context, recover from errors, and improve over time. Backed by a forward-deployed engineering team and enterprise-grade security (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001), Automat runs reliable, human-in-the-loop automation for document-heavy industries — mortgage & lending, banking, insurance, healthcare, and manufacturing. It delivers this through two products: Automat Workforce and Automat Core.

Workforce - A digital teammate you onboard like a new hire. 
Meet Ace, a digital teammate with its own email, Slack, phone, and logins that works across the tools your team already uses. You reach it like a colleague (a text, a channel mention, an email, a doc comment) and it does the work end to end, asks when it needs judgment, and leaves an audit trail for everything it touches.

Learn more here: https://runautomat.com/workforce 


Core - Managed agentic automation for enterprise 
Managed, AI-powered process automation for the enterprise. Automat Core replaces legacy RPA with self-healing agents that combine UI automation, AI document extraction (IDP), and API workflows in one platform. Automat's team builds, tests, and monitors every automation, so operations go live in days (not months), run reliably at scale, and cut operational costs — with human review wherever precision matters.

Learn more here [https://runautomat.com/capabilities](https://runautomat.com/capabilities)
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Operations teams at document-heavy enterprises (mortgage and lending, banking, insurance, healthcare, manufacturing) and, for the Workforce product, teams of 2 to 50
problem: Manual back-office work and brittle legacy RPA scripts break when screens or documents change. Automat sells agents that operate computers the way people do and self-heal.
business_model: Managed enterprise automation with a forward-deployed engineering team, plus per-agent Workforce subscriptions
product_category: Agentic process automation (AI-driven RPA and document processing)
market_need_then: Legacy RPA is described by the company as slow, expensive and fragile. Large language models and vision models in 2022 and 2023 made text-to-action automation newly possible, which the founders cited as the opening after working on robotics at Google X.
outcome_analysis: Automat is active and has raised about $19.25M, ending with a $15.5M Series A led by Felicis in November 2025. It rode the LLM and vision model wave to attack legacy RPA, and the forward-deployed engineering model suggests an enterprise sales motion. Customer counts and revenue are not public, so product market fit cannot be measured from sources. It remains early with no exit.

name: Automorphic
tags: AIOps; Deep Learning; Developer Tools; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Infuse knowledge into language models with just 10 samples
long_description: Automorphic has invented a way to infuse knowledge into LLMs via fine-tuning (surpassing context window limitations), enabling developers to rapidly iterate on and successively improve custom models cheaply and efficiently.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and AI teams that want custom fine-tuned language models
problem: Infusing new knowledge into LLMs without relying on context windows. Automorphic pitched fine-tuning with as few as 10 samples.
business_model: Developer platform and API for fine-tuning (Conduit), in private beta
product_category: LLM fine-tuning and model maintenance infrastructure
founder_names: Govind Gnanakumar; Maaher Gandhi; Mahesh Natamai
market_need_then: Developers hit context window limits when giving LLMs private knowledge in 2023, and wanted cheaper custom models. The company's YC page frames the demand but no spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: Automorphic is active but small, listed with three people. Its public funding record is thin and conflicting, with aggregators citing about $600K including a Thiel Fellowship grant. Its homepage in 2026 offers only a private beta and a repositioned tagline, so there is no evidence of strong traction or of a clear failure. Not enough public evidence to assign success or failure factors.

name: Autotab
one_liner: AI agents reliable enough to do real work
long_description:
Autotab is a drop-in AI knowledge worker that uses a mouse and keyboard like you—so anything you can do, it can do. Show it how to perform your task, train it to be hallucination-proof by adding examples and providing feedback, and then run it on demand or on a schedule—either locally or in the cloud.
 

It achieves superhuman reliability, and can scale up on demand so your team doesn’t have to.
 

Autotab is already handling complex tasks thousands of steps long, from messaging customers to triggering payments and updating data across core systems of record like Salesforce, HubSpot, Google Sheets, and Jira.

 
Download the beta version of the app and get started right away, or sign up for a personalized onboarding: https://www.autotab.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprise and tech-forward teams that pay for an AI agent that operates existing software like a human
problem: Repetitive knowledge work across systems like Salesforce, HubSpot and Jira lacks APIs, so automation needs fragile integrations.
business_model: SaaS subscription for a desktop and cloud AI agent (pricing not found)
product_category: Computer-use AI agent
market_need_then: Strong interest in AI agents in 2023, but the YC page claims on reliability are the company's own marketing and no independent usage data was found.
outcome_analysis: Autotab built a computer-use agent for enterprise work in 2023, early for the underlying models and in the path of the major labs. YC lists it as acquired, but no buyer, date or price was found, and the website footer names an entity called Planetary Computers, Inc. Whether this was a win or a soft landing is not public.

name: Avoca
one_liner: AI-powered Sales Agent for Service-Based Industries
long_description: We specialize in voice and can close customers across every channel 24/7.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Home and field service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, pest control and similar), plus franchise groups
problem: Service businesses miss inbound calls and leads outside business hours and have no way to score or coach their call handling. Avoca uses voice AI agents to answer, book and nurture.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage-based AI agents (Convert, Nurture, Coach) sold to service operators
product_category: Vertical voice AI front office for service businesses
market_need_then: Home service operators lose bookings to missed calls and rely on answering services. Avoca's own materials claim it is on track to book $1B in jobs. At W23 the company started with restaurants before narrowing to the trades, per one profile.
outcome_analysis: Avoca narrowed to home services voice AI and reached a reported $1B valuation in April 2026 with more than $125M raised across seed, Series A and Series B. The site claims 1,000 plus service leaders as customers and integrations with the main field service platforms. The pivot to a vertical with clear missed-call pain and the voice model tailwind appear to explain the growth. Revenue is not disclosed.

name: Backdrop
one_liner: Building your AI coworkers for any team, workflow, or industry.
long_description:
Backdrop is a platform for building AI coworkers around the work you actually need done.

Start with an existing coworker or create your own for almost anything. Research a market, prepare client updates, run outreach, create campaigns, analyze customer feedback, build dashboards, monitor orders, coordinate projects, test products, handle recurring admin, or build a workflow completely specific to your business.

Connect the systems where the work already happens, including Slack, Gmail, Google Drive, HubSpot, Shopify, Jira, Asana, Linear, GitHub, Notion, and more. You control what each coworker can access, what it can do, and which actions need approval.

Backdrop works just as well when one person wants to hand off a job to AI. But it is also built for something today’s 1:1 AI doesn’t handle well: working together.

Employees, AI coworkers, clients, and partners can collaborate in shared conversations and workflows. One agent can bring in another. Work can move between people and agents without everyone starting a new chat and rebuilding the context from scratch.

Backdrop builds shared company memory from the work happening across your company. Decisions, conversations, feedback, documents, project history, and activity across connected tools can become context that people and AI coworkers can use later. A coworker can understand what happened before, another agent can build on what was already learned, and a teammate can understand why something was done without digging through old threads or systems.

The result is AI that works for an individual when that’s all you need, but can also become part of how the whole company works.

Backdrop can support businesses ranging from agencies and e-commerce companies to manufacturers, service businesses, SaaS teams, and more, because you build the coworkers around your work, not a fixed template.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Originally film, TV and music production finance teams; now small and mid-sized businesses (agencies, e-commerce, SaaS, service firms) building AI coworkers
problem: Production expenses were reconciled with spreadsheets and paper receipts. The company later moved to AI coworkers that share memory and work across tools.
business_model: Originally expense and payments software for entertainment; now per-coworker subscriptions with a free tier
product_category: AI coworker platform (earlier: expense management and payments for the entertainment industry)
market_need_then: The company's YC launch pitch described film, TV and music production reconciliation as slow and error-prone. No spend or regulation evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Backdrop is listed as active with two people. It started in entertainment production finance and by 2026 repositioned as an AI coworker platform, a crowded and fast-moving category. No verified funding, customer or revenue data was found, so its trajectory cannot be rated. There is no clear success or failure story supported by sources.

name: Baserun
one_liner: Observability and evaluation platform for LLM apps.
long_description: LLMs are incredibly powerful, but latency, cost, and unpredictable outputs have made productionizing LLM features challenging. Baserun is a testing and observability platform that helps AI teams streamline their development cycle from identifying an issue to evaluating their solution, so that teams ship faster with confidence.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI engineering teams building LLM features
problem: Latency, cost and unpredictable outputs make LLM features hard to productionize. Baserun offers testing, prompt versioning and observability.
business_model: Developer SaaS for LLM testing and observability
product_category: LLMOps testing, evaluation and observability
market_need_then: Teams moving LLM prototypes into production in 2023 lacked ways to test prompts and watch quality, which created demand for eval and observability tools. No Baserun-specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Baserun was a two person YC S23 LLM testing and observability startup that publicly launched in September 2023 per one aggregator. The category filled quickly with Langfuse, LangSmith, Helicone and Braintrust, and Baserun shows up only in passing in later comparisons. Its website returned an error when checked and one directory marks it acquired, but nothing confirms an exit or shutdown, so its outcome is unknown.

name: Benchmark
one_liner: Decision infrastructure for investment firms
long_description: Benchmark is the trusted AI platform for investment firms. Today, leading firms use Benchmark to screen deals, extract insights from unstructured data, and automate workflows. Our platform combines cutting-edge AI with deep industry expertise to help investment firms make smarter, faster decisions across their entire deal lifecycle.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Investment firms in credit, private equity, real estate and secondaries that pay for AI over their deal documents
problem: Deal memos, models, emails and data room files pile up unsearchable, so firms lose institutional knowledge and screen deals slowly.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS (pricing not found)
product_category: AI deal screening and knowledge platform for investors
market_need_then: Private markets firms hold decades of unstructured deal data. The company later cited customers representing over $2 trillion in assets under management, self reported.
outcome_analysis: Benchmark, earlier called BidSight, built AI over investor deal data with a founder from real estate investing. It reached an acquisition by Harvey in July 2026, roughly three years after its batch, which Harvey framed as extending across the deal process. Price and funding amounts are not public, so the strength of the exit is unknown.

name: Berry
one_liner: AI Renewal Agent for Your Long Tail.
long_description:
Berry is the AI Renewal Agent for B2B SaaS. We help you retain and grow long-tail revenue while cutting labor costs.

Your long-tail customers are too costly for dedicated rep coverage, but their collective revenue is too valuable to ignore.

Berry fully manages your long tail, freeing your reps to grow top accounts. It drives value realization, closes renewals, and unlocks cross-sells and upsells. From proactive outreach to commercial negotiation, it engages your customers across channels and languages, 24/7.

Built for revenue and CS leaders who want higher NRR at a lower cost to serve.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B SaaS revenue and customer success leaders with a long tail of small accounts
problem: Long-tail customers are too costly for dedicated rep coverage but together hold valuable revenue. Berry's AI agent drives adoption, renewals and cross-sell for them.
business_model: B2B SaaS selling AI agents for post-sales (renewal, support, onboarding, training)
product_category: AI customer success and renewal agent
market_need_then: Customer success teams were stretched on long-tail accounts and companies sought to cut cost to serve; evidence is the company's own pitch, no third-party spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Berry remains active with about 8 people and an AI renewal agent aimed at SaaS long-tail accounts. Funding is small and conflicting across aggregators, and there are no named customers on its site, so traction cannot be judged. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff was reported. Not enough evidence for success or failure factors.

name: Bland AI
one_liner: The enterprise platform for AI phone calls
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises with high phone call volume (customer support, sales, appointment setting)
problem: Enterprises handle huge call volumes with expensive, slow phone operations. Bland sells AI phone agents that run inbound and outbound calls.
business_model: Usage-based enterprise platform for AI phone calls with self-hosted infrastructure
product_category: Enterprise voice AI agents
market_need_then: Call centers and enterprise phone operations were costly and large language models made natural phone conversation newly feasible in 2023. Early proof was a San Francisco billboard asking 'Still hiring humans?' whose phone number connected to Bland's own agent.
outcome_analysis: Bland raised $16M (August 2024), $40M (February 2025) and $50M (June 2026), passing $100M in total. It grew to about 65 people. Viral billboard marketing drew early attention, then enterprise sales took over, with customers such as Better.com and Sears per one report. Voice AI timing helped, but Wired reported its bots could be programmed to deny being AI, a reputational risk, and many competitors exist.

name: Bluebirds
one_liner: Automate outbound with signals
long_description:
Bluebirds helps GTM teams automate outbound targeting with signals. Save your reps 2 hours a day from list building and prospect research. 

Create custom intent signals from trusted data sources in 3 minutes. Bluebirds continuously scans your market and delivers ready-to-prospect Leads to your CRM.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B sales and GTM teams that pay for automated lead lists driven by buying signals such as champion job changes
problem: Reps spend hours on list building and prospect research, and miss warm leads such as past champions who moved to new companies.
business_model: B2B SaaS with a free base tier and paid tiers (about $1,000 a month for extras per a summary of press coverage)
product_category: Sales signals and outbound automation
market_need_then: Job change alerts were a known sales motion sold by vendors, and sales teams were adopting signal-based outbound. Investors backed the pitch with a $5M seed in October 2023.
outcome_analysis: Bluebirds had LinkedIn-trained founders, a $5M seed led by Lightspeed in October 2023, and a signals product that grew from job-change tracking into broader intent signals. Salesforce acquired it in 2025. Price and exact date are not public, but a major funded round before the exit points to a stronger outcome than a pure team acquisition.

name: Bluedot
one_liner: Bluedot is a single payment platform for EV drivers and fleets.
long_description:
Bluedot makes EV charging payment easier and simplifies expense management for drivers and fleets. They're growing 40-45% weekly and made $110K GMV last week.

Over 50% of vehicles sold will be electric by 2030. The payments management infrastructure for EV charging and the expenses doesn’t exist at the moment. The founders operated 100+ EV charging stations, worked in companies like Zipcar, Bosch, and Mercedes, and faced this problem through their own experiences. They built a team with a strong fintech background and publicly launched their Bluedot card on Dec 14th, 2022.

Bluedot has raised their pre-seed from Y Combinator, Axel Springer, Porsche, Ford, TechNexus, DRF, and Pritchard Automotive.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: EV drivers, rideshare drivers and fleets (Rivian, Hertz and the City of San Francisco later cited as customers)
problem: EV charging payment is fragmented across many networks and apps, and fleets lack expense management for charging. Bluedot offers one card and app with a flat rate and cash back.
business_model: Fintech card interchange and charging margin, later fleet charging management software
product_category: EV charging payments and fleet expense platform
market_need_then: TechCrunch in January 2023 described founders citing charging station utilization of 5 to 8 percent and fragmented payment across networks. The company reported at YC about 40 to 45 percent weekly growth and $110K weekly GMV, per the YC long description (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Bluedot started with a debit card for EV drivers, then moved toward fleets, and raised more than $5 million total from strategic backers including Porsche, Ford and Axel Springer. Epic Charging acquired its brand, technology and team on May 1, 2026 at an undisclosed price, giving access to over 80 percent of US public charging ports. That looks like a modest outcome with no disclosed return; the founders' automotive background fit the EV timing.

name: Blyss
one_liner: End-to-end encrypted AI.
long_description:
Blyss is an AI model provider built on strong security guarantees. We run AI workloads in GPU-based secure enclaves, which keep data encrypted even while it's being processed. Our customers get a privacy model similar to on-premises deployment, without ever having to think about AI infrastructure or GPU supply.  

The Blyss team has strong experience in cryptography and AI from Stanford, Apple, Nvidia, and more. We think data privacy is fundamental to safe, trustworthy AI, so it's our job to make end-to-end encrypted AI a no-compromise option - just like Signal and WhatsApp did for messaging.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: Bolto
one_liner: AI Powered All-In-One Payroll, HR + Recruiting
long_description: AI-powered payroll, hr, and recruiting platform. Hire and scale teams easily in the US and globally.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and mid-size companies that hire in the US and abroad and want payroll, HR and recruiting in one system
problem: Small and growing companies stitch together separate recruiting, payroll, HRIS and global hiring tools, which creates manual work and compliance risk when hiring across borders.
business_model: B2B SaaS, subscription for payroll, HR and recruiting, plus global payroll and payout services
product_category: AI-native HR, payroll and recruiting platform
market_need_then: Not directly sourced for 2023. Product positioning cites fragmented HR stacks and cross-border hiring complexity, but no dated demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Bolto joined YC in Summer 2023, then public records show a $5.1M seed in March 2025 and a $12M Series A reported in April 2026 led by Standard Capital with YC and General Catalyst. The company site lists named customers and a new instant payout product, so it appears to be growing, but there is no sourced revenue or churn data. The gap between the 2023 batch and the 2025 seed suggests slow early funding, and large incumbents remain the main risk.

name: Booth AI
tags: Generative AI; E-commerce; Marketing; Retail; AI
one_liner: Generative AI Photographer for E-Commerce
long_description: Booth AI enables companies to supercharge their creative output with a generative-AI powered image production platform. Booth AI replaces complicated, labor intensive, time consuming and expensive commercial product lifestyle photoshoots. Brand managers, merchandisers, and marketers can produce beautiful lifestyle images in a matter of seconds at a fraction of the cost of traditional photoshoots.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: E-commerce brands, merchandisers and marketers who need lifestyle product images
problem: Commercial lifestyle product photoshoots are slow, labor intensive and expensive. Booth AI generated lifestyle images from product photos in seconds.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for generated product imagery
product_category: Generative AI product photography
market_need_then: Brands pay for lifestyle product photography and generative image models had just become good enough in 2022 and 2023 to substitute for some shoots.
outcome_analysis: Booth AI joined YC in Winter 2023 with a three person team selling generated lifestyle product photos. The YC page lists it as acquired but no buyer, date or price is public, and an archive site reads the outcome as a possible acqui-hire, which is unconfirmed. The category was crowded within months of founding, the product had little defensibility, and the booth.ai domain now redirects to a sale page, so the cause and terms of the exit are not public.

name: Boundary
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; Machine Learning; AI
one_liner: The programming language for AI
long_description:
Boundary is building BAML -- a programming language to build AI agents.

We used to code in assembly, and moved on to C.
From C, we moved on to higher level languages like Python.
Now we are going from Python to natural language.

What does the code look like when 50% of the business decisions is decided by an AI agent / prompts? How do you test these AI components? We made BAML to address these problems.

BAML helps has built-in tools to test, observe, and work with structured LLM outputs / tool calling natively in the language 10x faster. With BAML you can also instantly parallelize LLM Calls, or react to certain events or changes in your pipelines, without having to write any boilerplate. It's like using 'React' for AI.

BAML code can used from any other language -- providing a standardized way to organize and declare any LLM or AI code.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineering teams building LLM-powered applications and agents
problem: Developers building with LLMs struggle to get reliable structured output, test prompts and observe AI pipelines using ad hoc tools.
business_model: Open-source language (Apache 2.0) with a paid cloud for tracing and observability
product_category: Developer tools, programming language for AI
market_need_then: LLM app building was exploding after ChatGPT in late 2022, and the company's own writing describes developer pain testing and parsing prompt outputs, but no dated third-party demand figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Boundary entered YC in Winter 2023 after many earlier pivots and settled on BAML, an open-source language for LLM applications. Growth appears developer-led, with 1,000+ active developers reported by its 2024 recap and named enterprise users on its site. Funding is thinly disclosed: seed from YC and angels, with no verified amounts, so the funding trajectory is unknown rather than weak.

name: Branch AI
one_liner: AI Overview Search, as a Service
long_description:
Boost conversions & organic SEO traffic by adding AI to your search box, unlocking personalized answers, suggestions, comparisons & more

Solutions
- Add AI Overviews to Search (Boost Conversions) 
- Save Answers as Landing Pages (Boost Organic SEO)
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia

name: Bretton AI
one_liner: AI-native operations for the banks
long_description:
Bretton runs AI-native operations for the financial back office. OCC, Fed and FDIC regulated banks use Bretton to run compliance, risk, fraud operations on one platform, on their own data and policies, with every output traced, cited, and audit-ready.

Bretton has pioneered AI use in financial services with its proprietary Trust Infrastructure — a system of model validation, governance and auditability guardrails that enables AI use in key regulated workflows.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: OCC, Fed and FDIC regulated banks, fintechs and payment platforms with financial crime compliance backlogs
problem: Banks and fintechs spend large headcount on AML investigations, KYC reviews and sanctions alert reviews that are repetitive and backlogged.
business_model: Enterprise software and managed services for AI agents that complete compliance investigations, sold to regulated institutions
product_category: AI agents for financial crime compliance (AML, KYC, sanctions)
market_need_then: Not separately sourced for 2023. The company later cites large manual review backlogs and customer results such as an 87% review time reduction, which are company-provided.
outcome_analysis: Bretton, founded as Greenlite AI in the Summer 2023 batch, rode the shift to LLM agents in regulated back offices. It raised a $15M Series A led by Greylock in May 2025 and a $75M Series B led by Sapphire in February 2026, when it rebranded. Named bank customers and company-reported savings support strong traction, though results are self-reported and well-funded rivals remain.

name: Brewit
tags: Analytics; Data Visualization; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Conversational data analytics for every team
long_description: Brewit helps companies to create their role-specific BI agents, trained on their database (through feeding sample queries, metric definitions, column descriptions, etc. to create a semantic layer) that can answer data questions/provide data insights (write SQL, generate plots) through a natural language experience.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Data and business teams at companies with SQL databases who want self-service analytics
problem: Business users depend on analysts to answer data questions. Brewit built role-specific BI agents on a semantic layer that write SQL and charts from natural language questions.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a free tier and demos
product_category: AI business intelligence and analytics
founder_names: Leo Lu; Mark Ding; Sam Ding
market_need_then: Companies had backlogs of analyst requests and large language models had just made natural language to SQL plausible in early 2023.
outcome_analysis: Brewit joined YC in Winter 2023 as a four person team building a conversational BI agent. The YC page lists it as acquired but no buyer, date or price was found in any source, and directory data on funding is thin. The text to SQL space attracted funded rivals and incumbents quickly, so the exit is best read as a small outcome whose terms are not public.

name: Briefer
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Data Science; Data Engineering; Data Visualization
one_liner: The collaborative data platform.
long_description:
Briefer helps data scientists and analysts build interactive visualizations and data apps using a Notion-like interface.

Connect to your data sources, write SQL or Python, collaborate through comments and multiplayer editing, and run code in whichever compute environments you need.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Data scientists and analysts at startups and mid-size companies (named customers VTEX, Whop, Incognia)
problem: Analysts need one place to write SQL and Python, collaborate in real time, and publish interactive data apps without stitching together notebooks, BI tools and docs.
business_model: Freemium open-source collaborative notebook with paid cloud and enterprise tiers
product_category: Collaborative data notebook and data app platform
market_need_then: Teams wanted collaborative, AI-assisted analytics workspaces in 2023; the category was already served by several venture-backed notebook products.
outcome_analysis: Briefer built an open-source collaborative notebook with real open-source traction and a few named customers, but raised only a small YC-era round and competed against better funded notebook products. In August 2025 Resend acquired the team to work on its data infrastructure and the product was shut down in November 2025, which reads as a soft landing rather than a product outcome. Founders' own reasons for not continuing independently are not public, so the failure factors are inferred from the facts.

name: Bronco AI
one_liner: AI for ASIC Design Verification
long_description:
Bronco is an applied AI lab helping chipmakers keep Moore’s law going. Our mission is to build AI silicon verification engineers that find bugs, drive functional coverage, and help companies ship working chips on time.

We're currently deployed alongside verification teams at leading chip companies building next generation hardware (4 nm process node).

We are well-funded and backed by tier-1 investors, including YC, 8VC, Elad Gil, SV Angel, and Contrary Capital. We have also established strong relationships with the leading academic and industry researchers in the field of AI for chip design. Our advisors have won multiple Best Paper Awards at leading conferences, been cited tens of thousands of times, and received some of the highest honors in the microelectronics and EDA industries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Chip companies with ASIC design verification teams, including startups and large chipmakers
problem: Verification is a major bottleneck in chip design: engineers spend days on debugging and coverage closure so chips ship late or with bugs.
business_model: Enterprise software deployed on the customer's own compute, sold to chip design teams
product_category: AI agents for ASIC design verification
market_need_then: Verification is widely described as the main bottleneck in chip design, but no dated 2023 evidence was gathered in this research.
outcome_analysis: Bronco AI joined YC in Summer 2023 to build AI verification engineers for chip design and now claims deployments at leading chipmakers on 4 nm designs. No funding rounds could be verified, so the data is incomplete rather than evidence of weakness. Secondary profiles suggest a small team and modest revenue, with strong later competition from EDA incumbents and funded startups.

name: BuildJet
one_liner: High-performance computing cloud
long_description:
BuildJet makes CI faster by running its own cloud on top of Gaming CPUs

Today, BuildJet offers a CI product that makes GitHub Actions 2x faster and cheaper, by plugging in BuildJet's Gaming CPU Cloud into GitHub Actions. Simply change 1 line, and enjoy the speed-up.
regions: Germany; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software teams and open-source projects paying for GitHub Actions minutes who want faster, cheaper builds
problem: GitHub-hosted Actions runners were slow and relatively expensive for CI workloads, so teams waited on builds and overpaid.
business_model: Usage-based, per-minute pricing for managed CI runners
product_category: Managed GitHub Actions runners (CI infrastructure)
market_need_then: Not separately sourced for 2023. The company's pitch rested on GitHub-hosted runners being slow and costly; later vendor comparison pages show many alternatives appearing for the same pain.
outcome_analysis: BuildJet sold faster, cheaper GitHub Actions runners and entered YC in Winter 2023 with two founders, with funding of roughly 500K reported only by aggregators. Its site now says the product was shut down, with job processing ending around March 2026. The sourced reason is that GitHub narrowed the performance gap, leaving a product dependent on GitHub's platform with a one-line switching cost and many competing runner vendors.

name: Bujeti
one_liner: The Finance Control Centre for African Businesses
long_description: Control spending, process payments, manage payroll, and multi-currency operations with approval workflows, total visibility and control, from one unified platform
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: African SMEs and startups, mainly in Nigeria and Kenya, with finance teams managing spending, payroll and payments
problem: African businesses lack integrated tools for corporate cards, expense approval, payroll and multi-currency payments, so spending is hard to control and track.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payments and card revenue, with banking provided by licensed partner banks
product_category: Spend management and corporate cards for African businesses
market_need_then: TechCrunch coverage says the founder saw the pain at Paystack and that nearly 1,000 businesses onboarded within eight weeks of the 2023 raise, indicating demand; no independent market sizing was gathered.
outcome_analysis: Bujeti began as a diaspora personal finance app and pivoted to B2B spend management in 2022, then joined YC in Winter 2023. It raised a $2M seed led by Y Combinator in December 2023, onboarded about 1,000 businesses within eight weeks and later reported 5,000 finance professionals across Nigeria and Kenya. A founder with Paystack experience and a pivot into a clearer need explain the traction, while no later round has been found.

name: CORE
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; SaaS; AI
one_liner: Your AI butler that understands you really well and proactively acts…
long_description:
CORE is your AI personal assistant that learns who you are, connects to your apps, and does the work before you ask. 

Open source. Self-hostable. Fully yours.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Individuals and developers who want a personal AI assistant or portable memory layer across AI tools (open source, self-hostable)
problem: AI assistants forget user context and cannot act proactively across apps; CORE keeps a user-owned memory graph shared with AI tools and apps.
business_model: Open source with hosted offering (monetization not found)
product_category: AI memory layer and personal assistant
market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand from 2023 was found; the 2025 launch posts claim a benchmark result and positions CORE as a user-owned memory layer.
outcome_analysis: HeySol started as Sol, an AI personal assistant, and surfaced CORE, an open-source memory graph, in mid-2025; the YC listing now uses the CORE name with a three-person team in Bengaluru. No funding, customer figures or exit were found, and the directory's founding year (2025) conflicts with the Summer 2023 batch, so the record is thin. It competes with better-funded memory-layer startups such as Mem0 (raised $24M in late 2025) and Letta.

name: Cair Health
tags: Health Tech; Healthcare; Health Insurance; AI; ML
one_liner: AI Agents for Healthcare RCM
long_description:
Cair Health empowers billing companies, care management platforms, EHRs, offshore BPOs, provider groups, and specialty pharmacies with AI-driven RCM solutions.  Our suite of AI Agents helps RCM teams streamline operations, reduce manual costs, and improve consistency—while maintaining full control over core workflows. Cair is trusted by 100+ practices across the country — including iconic VC-backed digital health startups, leading specialty EHRs, and some of the largest billing companies and BPOs

Backed by Y Combinator, Foundation Capital, Soma Capital, Translink Capital & many others..
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Billing companies, care management platforms, EHRs, offshore BPOs, provider groups and specialty pharmacies
problem: Healthcare revenue cycle work such as coding, eligibility checks, claims, denials and payment posting is manual, costly and inconsistent.
business_model: B2B software of named AI agents for revenue cycle tasks, sold to billing organizations and providers
product_category: AI agents for healthcare revenue cycle management
market_need_then: Not separately sourced for 2023. A founder remark in a 2026 Stedi interview says claims and reimbursement were consistently the bottleneck for providers.
outcome_analysis: Cair Health joined YC in Summer 2023 to build AI agents for healthcare billing and now claims 100+ practices and named customers. Its backers include Foundation Capital and Soma Capital per its own site, but no round size could be verified, so funding is unknown rather than low. The AI RCM market is crowded with heavily funded rivals, which is the main risk.

name: Cakework
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure
one_liner: API that adds cloud hosting to any developer platform
long_description: We make it possible to build a serverless cloud platform that hosts custom user code with just APIs and no infrastructure team. For example, an open source framework can build a cloud offering that deploys their users code from Github or local dev environments in days instead of months.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developer tool and SaaS companies whose users need to run custom code (for example on webhooks) and that did not want to build a serverless platform themselves.
problem: Building a secure serverless platform that packages and runs customers' code takes months and an infrastructure team, and AWS Lambda has timeout and protocol limits.
business_model: Usage based API for hosting customer code, sold to developer platforms
product_category: Developer infrastructure, serverless code hosting API
market_need_then: The launch post cites an early customer that gave up on an in house serverless system and launched on Cakework in about a week and a SaaS tool whose users run custom code on webhooks.
outcome_analysis: Cakework was a two person YC Winter 2023 team of former AWS engineers selling a serverless hosting API to developer platforms, with early access customers but no public traction numbers. The YC directory lists it as inactive and a Wayback copy shows its domain later served an unrelated blog, but no shutdown announcement or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. The failure factors are an inference from the crowded cloud infrastructure market and the absence of any reported follow on funding, not a stated reason.

name: Campfire
one_liner: The AI Native ERP for the fastest growing companies.
long_description: Campfire is the modern accounting platform for startups and mid-size tech companies. The fastest growing YC companies such as Replit, Posthog, SpeakAI run on Campfire. Our product includes an accounting general ledger that has multi-entity support and advanced financial reporting such as P&L by department and contribution margin by customer. Migrate from legacy accounting software to Campfire for your accounting and financial reporting to automate manual tasks and streamline workflows to unlock financial insights and accelerate the monthly close process.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Fast-growing startups and mid-size tech companies moving off QuickBooks, Xero or NetSuite
problem: Startups outgrow QuickBooks but find NetSuite and other legacy ERPs slow and costly, so month-end close and reporting stay manual.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for accounting and ERP, plus implementation and migration services
product_category: AI-native ERP and accounting platform
market_need_then: Not separately sourced for 2023. Later case studies and a tracker estimate of 20 to 30 percent of customers migrating from NetSuite point to demand from startups outgrowing QuickBooks.
outcome_analysis: Campfire entered YC in Summer 2023 with a founder who came from Invoice2go and Bill.com, and sold a modern general ledger to startups leaving QuickBooks and NetSuite. It raised a $35M Series A led by Accel in June 2025 and a $65M Series B about 12 weeks later, reportedly 100M+ in total, with named fast-growing customers and case studies. Self-reported growth and a crowded AI-native ERP field are the main caveats.

name: CandorIQ
one_liner: Headcount & Compensation Management
long_description:
CandorIQ is software to manage Headcount and Compensation planning. Employees are +70% of all OPEX and yet still managed in sheets & email. We manage all people spend in 1 platform, integrated into your Finance & HR stack.

Product capabilities include:
- Headcount & backfill planning
- Headcount budget scenarios across departments
- Merit cycle planning
- Analytics including employee churn, hiring win/loss, cash burn
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Finance, HR and People leaders at growth stage companies that plan headcount and run merit cycles in spreadsheets
problem: Employees are the largest operating expense, yet headcount and compensation planning is managed in sheets and email with no link to finance and HR systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with advisory and compensation data services
product_category: Headcount planning and compensation management software
market_need_then: The company states employees are over 70 percent of operating expense and were managed in spreadsheets and email in 2023. This is a self reported claim from the YC page.
outcome_analysis: CandorIQ remains active and raised a 4.8 million dollar seed in July 2025 led by Array Ventures after the 2023 YC batch. The founders came from Checkr and Salesforce, giving some founder market fit for people and finance software. The company claims hundreds of customers but is in a crowded category with strong suites.

name: Capi Money
one_liner: Helping businesses in emerging markets make pay their international…
long_description: Capi helps businesses in emerging markets make international payments. Importers in emerging markets pay up to 10% to settle invoices and wait weeks for payments to arrive. We’re on a mission to give businesses in emerging markets the same price and speed as we expect in the US and Europe.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Importers and SMEs in emerging markets, mainly in Africa, paying overseas suppliers
problem: Importers in emerging markets pay up to 10 percent to settle international invoices and wait weeks for funds to arrive.
business_model: Cross border payments with FX and fee margin, licensed money transmitter
product_category: Cross border B2B payments
founder_names: Mitch Riley; Scott Liddle; Tom (surname not listed)
market_need_then: Capi's launch post says importers paid up to 10 percent in fees and waited weeks, and it booked over 1.5 million dollars in payments in its first two weeks after launching in Senegal.
outcome_analysis: Capi launched in Dakar in August 2023 and raised a Series A of about 17.9 million dollars in February 2025 led by Creandum. The founders came from Taptap Send and knew African corridors, and Capi built licenses in several jurisdictions. It is active and scaling.

name: Cardinal
tags: Generative AI; SaaS; B2B; Productivity; Analytics
one_liner: Your AI product backlog
long_description: Cardinal is an opinionated feature backlog. It pulls in your customer feedback, CRM data, and task management issues and uses AI to assess which customers want which features, how important is it for them, and how much are they worth
all_locations: Austin, TX, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product managers and product teams at software companies
problem: Teams struggle to know which customers want which features and what they are worth. Cardinal pulled feedback, CRM data and issues together and used AI to rank the backlog.
business_model: B2B SaaS for product teams
product_category: AI product management and feedback analysis
market_need_then: Product teams in 2023 faced scattered customer feedback across tools and large language models made automated synthesis feasible.
outcome_analysis: Cardinal went through YC in Winter 2023 with founders who had already sold Houseparty and worked at Epic Games and had product depth in this exact workflow. It was acquired by Miro in May 2024 and became Miro Insights, with Weizmann joining as a VP of Product. Price and terms are not disclosed, and no priced funding round was found, so the outcome looks like a team and product acquisition by a company that owned the product workspace.

name: Cardinal Gray
tags: Enterprise Software; Consumer Finance; Automation; AI; Automotive
one_liner: Streamlined DMV lien filing for auto lenders
long_description: When a lender gives out a car loan, they need to file a lien with their borrower’s DMV. This is difficult because the process varies dramatically by state and county. We've handled over $10B in filings and are helping lenders like Capital One and OneMain file liens on around 30k cars each month.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Auto lenders such as banks, credit unions and finance companies that must file and release liens with state DMVs
problem: Filing a lien with a DMV varies by state and county and is manual, slow and error prone for auto lenders.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API priced per filing or contract
product_category: Auto lien and title automation
founder_names: Jack Chapman; Muhammad Khattak; Grant Pease
market_need_then: Lenders must file liens on every secured auto loan across inconsistent state processes. The company later claimed over 10 billion dollars in filings and customers such as Capital One and OneMain, as stated on the YC page.
outcome_analysis: Cardinal Gray is an active four person YC S23 company serving large auto lenders with lien filing automation and a MeridianLink partnership. Funding is not publicly verified, so the scale of its progress is unclear, but the customer list claimed by the company suggests real traction.

name: CareOasis
tags: Consumer Health Services; Healthcare; Health Insurance
one_liner: Get Paid for Family Caregiving
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Ohio families who provide unpaid in-home care to a relative and may qualify for Medicaid paid caregiving
problem: Family caregivers do not know how to qualify for Medicaid programs that can pay them, and enrollment, training and billing paperwork is complex.
business_model: Medicaid reimbursed care coordination and services provider paid through Ohio Medicaid programs
product_category: Paid family caregiving navigation
founder_names: Anuhya Vajapey; Juan M Ochoa Ortiz
market_need_then: Many Ohio families provide unpaid care and Ohio Medicaid waivers can pay relatives. A 2026 report says the Ohio House considered banning such payments, a policy risk.
outcome_analysis: CareOasis is a two person company serving Ohio only, with a live site in 2026 and no verified funding after YC. Its fate depends on Ohio Medicaid policy and competition from other structured family caregiving providers. No clear success or failure story is public.

name: Cargo
one_liner: Build your GTM workforce
long_description: We’re redefining how teams execute GTM by making them leaner, faster and engineer-driven. In an AI-first world, we’re replacing SDR-heavy models with a hybrid approach, empowering full-cycle AEs through a blend of manual effort and automation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Revenue operations teams and GTM engineers at B2B companies that keep customer data in a warehouse
problem: Revenue teams cannot easily use warehouse data to segment, score and route leads and automate sales operations without heavy engineering.
business_model: Usage and credit based B2B SaaS
product_category: GTM orchestration and revenue operations infrastructure
market_need_then: In 2023 revenue teams sought warehouse based automation as reverse ETL tools spread. The YC launch described a revenue architecture on top of the customer warehouse.
outcome_analysis: Cargo is a small YC S23 company that moved from a warehouse based revenue architecture toward AI agent era GTM infrastructure. No verified funding beyond YC and no exit were found, and the category is crowded, so its trajectory is unclear.

name: Casca
tags: Conversational Banking; Fintech; Machine Learning; Finance; AI
one_liner: Make Banking Magical
long_description:
Casca is building AGI for Banking.

Our first product is an AI-native platform transforming small business lending by enabling banks and lenders to originate 10x more loans with 90% less manual effort. We’ve found product market fit already serving top 10 US banks and are scaling our team very quickly.

Small businesses are the heart of the American economy. Many banks shy away from providing funding because of the manual effort in pursuing those deals. With us, that changes. We unlock affordable, quick bank funding for the 30M+ small businesses in the US who would otherwise be subject to the high interest rates from predatory online lenders.

We are a world-class team of banking & AI experts from Stanford, MIT & Y Combinator. We like to win and we know that the only thing between us and the title is our own ability to improve every day.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US community, regional and national banks and non-bank lenders making small business and SBA loans
problem: Banks avoid small business loans because manual origination and underwriting effort is too high relative to loan size.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS sold to banks and lenders
product_category: AI loan origination system
market_need_then: Banks shy away from small business loans because of manual effort. Casca's first customer was Bankwell Bank per its Series A coverage.
outcome_analysis: Casca raised a 3.9 million dollar pre-seed in February 2024 and a 29 million dollar Series A in August 2025 led by Canapi, with banks as both customers and investors. Stanford founders with banking and ML backgrounds sold into top US banks and SBA lenders riding the generative AI wave, a strong enterprise sales engine.

name: Catamaran
tags: Machine Learning; Finance; Analytics; Insurance; Investing
one_liner: A regulated marketplace and analytics platform where investors buy…
long_description: CatX is a Bermuda regulated digital marketplace for insurance risk. With more than $500m of opportunities listed, it gives hedge funds and other sophisticated investors a direct way to access, analyse and transact insurance risk. Insurance risk is an uncorrelated alternative asset class with a broad range of return profiles. CatX's Catamaran platform helps institutional investors, insurers and risk managers quantify the impact of a risk and decide whether to hedge it or invest in it.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hedge funds and institutional investors buying insurance risk, plus insurers, brokers and risk managers placing it
problem: Insurance risk is an uncorrelated asset class but hard for investors to access and analyze. CatX offered a Bermuda regulated marketplace and the Catamaran analytics platform.
business_model: Regulated marketplace with transaction fees plus analytics software
product_category: Insurance risk exchange and analytics
market_need_then: Institutional investors wanted access to insurance-linked risk and the reinsurance market still placed risk through slow manual broker processes.
outcome_analysis: CatX built a Bermuda regulated risk exchange and the Catamaran analytics tool, joined YC in Summer 2023 and raised a $2.7M seed that November, with Oxford trained founders from reinsurance and finance. It kept shipping integrations with Moody's RMS and Verisk and in September 2025 merged with Cactus, with the site now promoting 80 plus insurers and 50 plus funds. YC lists the outcome as acquired, but press describes a merger of equals with no stated acquirer or terms.

name: Cedalio
one_liner: AI agents that automate AP, procurement, and finance
long_description: Cedalio is the AI agent platform for the Office of the CFO. We automate procurement, AP, and the data flows behind them — from invoice intake to 3-way match to payment — so finance teams stop doing the work and start governing it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Finance and procurement teams at companies with 200 to 5000 employees in Latin America
