name: Miracle
one_liner: Accelerate clinical trials with real-time, actionable insights
long_description:
Miracle is building the control room for clinical trials. Today, biotech companies rely on fragmented software systems, spreadsheet trackers, and manual processes to manage complex clinical trials. Miracle integrates and consolidates data from disparate sources into a single platform, giving teams real-time visibility, helping them identify risks early, and streamlining workflows to make faster, better decisions.

By unifying clinical trial data, we're also laying the foundation for AI-powered analytics and automation.

Our mission is to modernize how clinical trials are run so new treatments can reach patients faster.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Clinical operations and data teams at biotech and pharma sponsors
problem: Clinical trial data sits in separate EDC, lab, vendor and spreadsheet systems, so teams compile trackers by hand and spot risks late.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per study
product_category: Clinical trial data consolidation and operations software
market_need_then: YC page claims over 80 percent of trials are delayed by recruitment and ops teams spend about 15 percent of time compiling reports; company claims, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Miracle is active and says it works with several Nasdaq listed biotechs. An AWS case study in 2025 reports growth from one trial to over a dozen studies, so traction appears real. Funding is not publicly verified, so investor validation cannot be judged.

name: Mocha
one_liner: Build and publish web apps in minutes. No coding required.
long_description:
What if you could build web apps as easily as you make a Figma design or edit a Google Doc?


Enter Mocha. We've reimagined app development with a state-of-the-art coding agent that builds for our users.

Want to launch that app idea? Need to build something for your community? Looking to prototype faster? Start here. We've removed the barriers between idea and execution.

Our mission is to empower everyone to build for the web, our vision is personal software.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Non-technical individuals and small teams who want to build web apps without coding
problem: Building a web app requires coding skill, so ideas for personal software never ship.
business_model: Subscription for an AI app builder with usage costs
product_category: AI no-code app builder
market_need_then: Interest in AI coding rose quickly in 2023 to 2025, but sustained paying demand and margins proved hard.
outcome_analysis: Mocha started as the Srcbook developer tool, pivoted to a no-code AI app builder in mid 2025 and announced a shutdown for August 1 2026. Secondary sources say user acquisition was expensive, AI token costs hurt margins and the founders could not raise more capital, while funded rivals like Bolt and Lovable led the category. The YC directory labels it Acquired but no acquirer exists in any source found.

name: Modulari-T
tags: Gene Therapy; Cell Therapy; Synthetic Biology; Biotech; Oncology
one_liner: We teach your immune system to attack and cure cancer
long_description:
Cell and gene therapy promises to one day cure any disease; Modulari-T’s Platform produces the tools to fulfill that promise.

Modulari-T has designed a new family of synthetic genes that can reprogram cells to better sense their environment and modify their behavior accordingly. This can be used to engineer immune cells to efficiently recognize and kill cancer cells or to create stem cells able to regenerate any tissue.

Modulari-T looks to expand its technology to reach every area of cell therapy and become the platform of reference for cell engineering.
all_locations: Montreal, QC, Canada; San Francisco, CA, USA
regions: Canada; United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharma and biotech partners for cell and gene therapy, and ultimately cancer patients
problem: First generation CAR-T has toxicity, exhaustion and limited solid tumor reach; the company designs synthetic receptors and delivery vehicles to address this.
business_model: Preclinical platform company seeking partnerships and licensing
product_category: Cell and gene therapy platform (MARC receptors, MoVe delivery vector)
market_need_then: Cell therapy for solid tumors was an open unmet need; the company cites a market growing past 50B USD, a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Modulari-T remains a preclinical company. In April 2026 it named Tanya Borsuk as CEO and moved the founder to President and CSO as it shifts to a partnership driven model. Equity funding is unverified; the only confirmed money is a small Canadian government grant.

name: Nango
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Open Source; API
one_liner: A single API for all your integrations
long_description:
Customers expect your SaaS to integrate with all the software they use.

With Nango, you ship integrations your customers love, fast.

Leverage hundreds of pre-built integrations and unlimited customization.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: SaaS and AI companies that need product integrations with customers' other software
problem: Building and maintaining OAuth and API integrations for each third party tool takes engineering months.
business_model: Open source with hosted cloud, usage-based pricing
product_category: Integration infrastructure (auth, syncs, unified API, MCP tools)
market_need_then: Founders cite experience of how hard SaaS integrations are to build; the product began as an open source OAuth handler for 40 APIs.
outcome_analysis: Nango grew from an open source OAuth tool into an integrations platform with named customers such as Replit and a reported cash flow positive state when it raised a 7.5M seed in April 2026. Growth was bootstrapped on a small convertible raise, which points to capital efficiency, and the 2026 round is its first verified one.

name: Nanograb
tags: AI-powered Drug Discovery; Nanomedicine; Biotech; Drug Delivery; Therapeutics
one_liner: Deliver genes to any cell with AI
long_description: Nanograb is a computational drug discovery company that uses AI to create novel targeted non-viral gene therapy vectors. Our platform designs unique combinations of small peptide binders attached to nanoparticles to safely deliver genetic medicines to specific cells and tissues in the body at scale.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Biopharma companies developing genetic medicines that need targeted delivery
problem: Non-viral gene therapy vectors mostly reach the liver; delivering genes to specific cells and tissues is unsolved at scale.
business_model: Partnerships and early access agreements with biopharma, drug discovery platform
product_category: AI drug delivery design (peptide binders on nanoparticles)
founder_names: Debesh Mandal; Christopher Lau; Shanil Panara
market_need_then: Non-viral delivery beyond the liver was widely described as a gap; company claims paying biopharma partners for early access, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Nanograb is active as a five person London team with an Imperial College founding group. No public funding, partnership or shutdown news was found, so its progress is unknown and no outcome can be judged.

name: Narrative
one_liner: AI agents for end-to-end testing
long_description:
Narrative is the easiest way to create end-to-end tests, replacing Playwright, Selenium, and Cypress with self-healing tests.

Record your user journeys to deploy tests in minutes, and let our agents handle flaky selectors and timing issues. When a test fails, you get a bug report in plain English that's easy to triage.

Trusted by Nanonets, Commenda, Drumkit, Metal, and Vega.

Learn more at www.trynarrative.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software teams that maintain end-to-end browser tests
problem: End-to-end tests in Playwright, Selenium and Cypress break on flaky selectors and timing, which costs engineering time.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, pricing from 1,000 USD per month
product_category: AI end-to-end testing
market_need_then: The product replaces flaky Playwright, Selenium and Cypress tests; dated demand evidence was not found.
outcome_analysis: Narrative is active and has rebranded as Zorro with named customers such as Nanonets and Commenda, and a stated price from 1,000 USD per month. The name Narrative collided with other companies, and the rebrand points to that. Funding is unverified and the crowded AI testing market shows rising competition.

name: Nectar
one_liner: Manage energy cost & usage with AI for facility & sustainability teams
long_description: Nectar is the modern AI energy management platform. We automate utility data analysis to optimize energy costs, manage buildings, and report energy efficiency metrics for energy and sustainability teams. Our utility data API uses in-house AI agents to deliver the most accurate granular usage and cost data on the market.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Facility, energy and sustainability teams at commercial building owners; carbon accounting platforms via the utility data API
problem: Utility bill and usage data is messy and hard to analyze, making energy cost management and efficiency reporting manual.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus utility data API
product_category: energy management software / utility data API
market_need_then: Climate and sustainability reporting (Scope 1 and 2 carbon accounting) needs utility data; Nectar's partner pages target carbon accounting platforms, and UtilityAPI raised a $10M Series A in May 2022, showing dated demand.
outcome_analysis: Nectar (Summer 2023, Active) is an AI utility-data company with MIT-trained technical founders. Verified funding is absent: aggregators suggest about $500K (pre-seed or seed, Aug-Sep 2023) with YC, Eight Capital and others. It entered a niche already served by UtilityAPI and Urjanet; no shutdown or exit has been reported, so the story is early and unresolved.

name: Neptyne
tags: Generative AI; Data Science; Data Visualization
one_liner: The programmable spreadsheet.
long_description:
Neptyne is the first natively programmable spreadsheet, with a full Python environment, just like a Jupyter notebook. And we built in AI to make it easy to use, even if you’re not a Python expert. Neptyne turns anyone who can use Excel into a programmer.

At Google, Douwe launched products to millions in Search, Mobile and workplace. He founded multiple startups, and published a book on deep learning. 4 years ago Douwe rejoined Google, where he met his cofounder Jack and the rest of the team.

Neptyne launched on Hacker News in February 2023, and since then users have made thousands of spreadsheets.  People have built everything from option trading systems to machine learning classifiers using Neptyne.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Spreadsheet users who want Python (data scientists, analysts and Excel users)
problem: Spreadsheets cannot be programmed with a real language; users move between Excel and notebooks.
business_model: Freemium SaaS spreadsheet and Google Sheets add-on
product_category: Programmable Python spreadsheet
market_need_then: Demand signal is thin: no revenue at the March 2023 TechCrunch article, Hacker News launch Feb 2023, and the company says users made thousands of spreadsheets.
outcome_analysis: Neptyne launched in 2022-23 as a Python spreadsheet, raised a $2M pre-seed in March 2023 and shipped a Google Sheets add-on, then Microsoft announced Python in Excel in August 2023. YC lists the company as Inactive, but no shutdown notice, post-mortem or acquisition announcement was verified, so the cause and form of the end are not public.

name: No Cap
one_liner: AI startup investor, No Cap
long_description: The world's first AI agent that coaches founders & invests in them. Currently led by a repeat AI founder Alexander Nevedovsky (exit to Farfetch), who joined post-YC batch: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ednevsky 👋
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Early-stage founders seeking coaching and a small investment from an AI agent; later solo AI entrepreneurs
problem: Founders struggle to get investor feedback and early checks; the product tried to coach them and invest automatically using an AI trained on startup data.
business_model: AI-run investor and coach that writes small checks (reported up to $100K) in exchange for equity
product_category: AI startup investor and founder coaching
founder_names: Slava Solonitsyn; Mika Melchanka; Dmitry Starodubtsev; Alexander Nevedovsky
market_need_then: Founders in 2023 were seeking investor feedback during the generative AI surge; demand for an AI investor itself was unproven and mostly novelty-driven.
outcome_analysis: No Cap rode the 2023 interest in generative AI with a memorable AI investor stunt and a slang name, but the sources show little revenue or durable moat. Public funding data is thin and unverified. The company was acquired by Audos.com in March 2026 at an undisclosed price, which looks like a soft landing for a small team and its brand. The same people moved on to other projects such as Intently.

name: Novelcare
tags: Health Tech; B2B; Healthcare; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Empowering every doctor and every patient to participate in research
long_description:
Novelcare addresses the primary bottleneck in drug development: recruiting patients into clinical trials.

We analyze electronic health records to help doctors find clinical trials for their patients, and to help trial sites find patients for their studies. 72% of doctors want to inform their patients of clinical trials, but only 5% do. We're on a mission to close that gap, ultimately bringing safer, more effective drugs to the patients who need them.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Healthcare providers and practices (free for most), with revenue from trial sponsors and sites that need patients
problem: Few patients learn about clinical trials they could join, which slows patient recruitment for drug development. Novelcare scans electronic health records to match patients to nearby studies.
business_model: Free to most practices; trial sites and sponsors pay for patient identification, practices can earn revenue from chart review on some studies
product_category: Clinical trial patient matching from EHR data
market_need_then: The company cites that 72% of doctors want to inform patients of trials but only 5% do, and calls patient recruitment the primary bottleneck in drug development. These are company claims.
outcome_analysis: Novelcare is listed Active with a team of five and no found coverage of funding, exits or shutdowns. The problem of trial recruitment is large and the founders have Palantir life sciences experience, but sources opened give no traction or round data, so the outcome cannot be explained yet. The outcome search returned nothing about the company.

name: Nowadays
one_liner: AI-native platform for corporate meetings and events
long_description:
Nowadays is the AI-native platform for corporate meetings and events. Our AI doesn't just assist planners, it does the work: it emails and calls venues, negotiates rates in 22 languages, and parses 50-page hotel proposals into clean apples-to-apples comparisons. Clients routinely save 20-30% vs. booking direct, and one Fortune 500 VP uncovered $18M in unmanaged meeting spend just by turning Nowadays on.

We started out working with small startups. Today, Google, Airbnb, BlackRock, Anthropic, Pylon, and Mintlify use Nowadays to bring their people together, from one epic kickoff a year to thousands of meetings annually.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Corporate teams, people teams, executive assistants and event marketers who plan offsites, kickoffs and meetings, from startups to large enterprises
problem: Planning corporate events means weeks of emailing venues, comparing long hotel proposals and managing vendors. Nowadays uses AI to source venues, contact them, compare proposals and track budgets.
business_model: Event planning platform and service, commercial terms not stated in sources opened
product_category: AI corporate meetings and events planning
market_need_then: Corporate event planning was manual and slow. The company cites 20 to 30 percent savings versus booking direct, from its own site, and early use by startups; demand evidence at founding is mostly founder experience planning large events.
outcome_analysis: Nowadays started with small startups and moved toward enterprise customers, with its site listing large logos. It raised a $2M seed in December 2024 after saying fundraising was hard. AI language models made automated venue outreach newly feasible, which helped timing, while incumbents and other AI event startups are a continuing threat.

name: Noya Software
one_liner: Product design tool that lets everyone design like a designer
long_description:
Noya is a new kind of product design tool for non-designers. This is our second time co-founding a design tools company – our first company was acquired by Airbnb in 2017 and we became the design tools team there.

At Airbnb, we built the design infrastructure that the entire company relied on to scale design without increasing headcount costs. We did this by letting non-designers (such as marketing, PMs, and engineering) design screens and websites.  Now we're making these tools available to every company.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product teams and non-designers who need designs and UI code without a professional designer
problem: Non-designers such as engineers and marketers cannot easily produce good product designs. Noya started as a wireframe tool that produced high-fidelity designs and React code using a design system.
business_model: Design software, pricing not stated in sources opened
product_category: Product design and collaborative app tools
founder_names: Devin Abbott; David (surname not given on YC page)
market_need_then: The founders' own experience building design tools at Airbnb showed demand to let non-designers design within a design system. No external demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Noya is active with a team of two per the YC page. The founders had already sold a design tools startup to Airbnb in 2017 and worked on its design tools team, which is strong founder market fit. The product has moved from wireframing to a broader platform of collaborative apps, and no verified funding or traction data was found, so the outcome remains open.

name: Numen
tags: Machine Learning; Biotech; Healthcare; Diagnostics; AI
one_liner: Engineering a future without cancer deaths.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Consumers and clinicians who want early cancer screening at home; payer and channel not stated in sources opened
problem: Cancer screening is slow and needs lab visits. The company is building rapid at-home urine tests with results in about 30 minutes, starting with prostate, bladder and ovarian cancers.
business_model: Diagnostics product, commercial model not stated in sources opened
product_category: At-home cancer screening diagnostics (synthetic biology, machine learning, computer vision)
market_need_then: Screening gaps exist for cancers such as prostate, bladder and ovarian, and the company pitches the test as easy as a pregnancy test. No third-party demand data was opened.
outcome_analysis: Numen, formerly Cleancard, is active with 18 people per the YC page and is developing rapid at-home cancer tests. Technical risk and regulatory path are the main unknowns, and no verified funding, clearance or shutdown information was found. The outcome search surfaced no coverage of the company.

name: Numeral
one_liner: The AI-native sales tax solution.
long_description:
Numeral is the trusted solution for U.S. sales tax, VAT, and GST compliance, used by 3,500+ global businesses, including Eight Sleep, Supabase, and Brex.

Our end-to-end platform keeps our customers compliant wherever they sell, with registrations, filings, calculations, and ongoing compliance support.

Numeral’s AI-native solution covers more than 90 countries and tens of thousands of jurisdictions and is built for accuracy and scale.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: E-commerce and SaaS companies that sell across US states and countries and must handle sales tax, VAT and GST
problem: Growing online sellers face state by state sales tax registration, calculation, filing and remittance. Numeral automates the lifecycle with software plus human experts.
business_model: SaaS subscription for tax calculation, nexus monitoring, registration and filing
product_category: Sales tax, VAT and GST compliance software
market_need_then: Online sellers were exposed to state economic nexus rules and wanted simpler compliance. Company reports 3,500+ customers and 327 percent year over year transaction growth by 2026.
outcome_analysis: Numeral grew from a 2022 start to 3,500 customers claimed by 2026 and raised a $18M Series A in March 2025, a $35M Series B in September 2025 and a $100M Series C in September 2026, with Benchmark and Y Combinator staying in. Sales tax was a painful, regulated job where incumbents were criticized for cost and service, and founders came from Stripe, Notion and e-commerce. Competition from Avalara, TaxJar and many startups remains the main risk.

name: Obento Health
tags: B2B; Medical Devices; Healthcare; CRM; AI
one_liner: CRM Co-Pilot for Medtech Sales
long_description: Obento Health is redefining the CRM experience for medical field sales. Designed specifically for healthcare, we are saving reps time from documentation and empowering reps to create more personalized interactions with their customers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Medical device and medtech companies and their field sales representatives
problem: Medtech field reps lose time logging visits and follow-ups in CRM systems. Obento offers a mobile, voice-driven CRM co-pilot that automates documentation and follow-ups.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to medtech sales organizations, pricing not stated in sources opened
product_category: Mobile CRM co-pilot for medtech sales
market_need_then: Medtech field sales reps carry heavy documentation work, which is the pain the company cites; no independent demand data was opened.
outcome_analysis: Obento Health is listed Active with a team of two per the YC page and has no found coverage of funding, exit or shutdown. The idea targets a clear workflow pain for medtech reps and the founder has Verily medtech and biopharma product experience, but incumbents like Salesforce and Veeva sell medtech CRMs. Too little public information exists to explain the outcome.

name: Odigos Technologies Inc.
one_liner: Enterprise-Grade OpenTelemetry
long_description:
Odigos leverages eBPF technology to create an open-source solution that can automatically generate distributed traces for any application without any engineering work.
Developers are struggling with extracting and delivering high-quality monitoring data.
Currently, building a pipeline is a manual process that takes months to implement, is an error-prone process that requires tons of code changes across multiple R&D teams, and demands collaboration.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering, platform and security teams running production services, mostly on Kubernetes, in mid-size and large enterprises
problem: Distributed tracing and OpenTelemetry instrumentation require code changes and per-language setup, so adoption was low. Odigos instruments applications automatically using eBPF and OpenTelemetry without code changes.
business_model: Open source core with a commercial platform and 14-day trial
product_category: OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation and observability control plane
market_need_then: TechCrunch says the CTO saw low adoption of distributed tracing, and OpenTelemetry was growing as a vendor neutral standard.
outcome_analysis: Odigos raised a SAFE around YC Demo Day and a $13M round in September 2024 led by Venture Guides with Salesforce Ventures, and now lists customers such as T-Mobile and Merck. An open source, vendor neutral approach rode the OpenTelemetry wave, but eBPF instrumentation is also being built by larger vendors and standards bodies.

name: OfOne
one_liner: AI-powered order taker for restaurant drive-thrus
long_description:
OfOne is building software to automate order taking at fast-food drive-thrus. Using conversational AI, we help restaurant chains operate more efficiently and level-up their customer experience.

OfOne can answer questions, intelligently upsell - like suggesting ice cream on a hot day - and always says please and thank you.

There are 200,000 drive-thrus in the US and they are the industry's largest order channel.

Our mission is to deliver human centric experiences that help restaurant operators prosper, deliver delight for their customers, and empower their workers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Quick service restaurant chains and franchisees that run drive-thrus
problem: Drive-thru order taking is labor heavy and inconsistent; the product takes orders with conversational AI, upsells and writes to the point of sale.
business_model: B2B SaaS priced per store for AI order taking
product_category: Voice AI for restaurant drive-thrus
competitors_at_founding: Presto Automation; SoundHound; Hi Auto; Wendy's FreshAI with Google Cloud
market_need_then: Fast food chains faced labor costs and drive-thru speed pressure; the company cited about 200,000 US drive-thrus and a claimed saving of about $60,000 per store per year.
outcome_analysis: OfOne launched in the 2023 wave of LLM voice agents with founders who had scaled a frontline worker app at Crew. It reached pilots at national chains and SOC 2 compliance, but faced Presto, SoundHound and chain in-house efforts in a crowded market. It raised little publicly and was acquired by Deepgram in January 2026, alongside Deepgram's $130M Series C, to anchor a restaurant offering. The price is undisclosed.

name: Ohm
one_liner: Ohm helps engineering teams accelerate hardware development & testing.
long_description: Ohm’s AI platform helps Fortune 100 engineering teams accelerate the engineering and testing of complex hardware, including wearables, electric vehicles, and batteries. Launched in 2025, Ohm's platform is used by leading teams to compress development cycles, optimize test programs, and launch better products, faster.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering and test teams at battery, automotive, aerospace and electronics companies, including Fortune 100 firms
problem: Battery and hardware labs run experiments on specialized equipment and struggle to collect, clean and analyze test data. The company began as Byterat, software to automate battery lab data collection and analysis, and now sells agentic AI for hardware test programs.
business_model: Enterprise software, pricing not stated in sources opened
product_category: AI platform for hardware test data and engineering analysis
market_need_then: TechCrunch in October 2023 describes industry battery scientists facing the same lab data problems Jones saw as a student. Battery development was expanding with EV demand.
outcome_analysis: The company launched as Byterat, raised a $4M seed in October 2023 led by Giant Ventures, and later renamed to Ohm with a broader hardware test and AI agents pitch aimed at Fortune 100 engineering teams. It is active with a team of seven on the YC page. Growth evidence beyond positioning is thin, so the outcome is still open.

name: Ohmic Biosciences
tags: Synthetic Biology; Biotech; Climate; Agriculture; Genetic Engineering
one_liner: Genetically engineering plants for disease resistance.
long_description: Pests and pathogens cost the world hundreds of billions of dollars every year. Existing technologies like agrochemicals are no longer working. Ohmic Biosciences uses protein engineering to design resistance genes for crops that are robust to pathogen evolution.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Row crop growers and seed or trait companies that need durable disease and pest resistance, starting with soybean growers hit by soybean cyst nematode
problem: Pests and pathogens cause very large crop losses, agrochemicals are losing effectiveness, and natural resistance genes are overcome as pathogens evolve.
business_model: Trait development and licensing of engineered resistance genes (pre-revenue R&D, no pricing public)
product_category: Agricultural biotech, protein-engineered plant disease resistance traits
market_need_then: The company cites hundreds of billions of dollars in annual losses to pests and pathogens, and its first target, soybean cyst nematode, is said by the company to cost over 1.5B USD a year in US yield; agrochemicals were described as no longer working.
outcome_analysis: Ohmic is still active as of the latest sources, with two PhD founders who met on a DARPA plant biosensor project. Its only recorded funding is a small pre-seed tied to YC, so it remains early, with long trait development timelines and no public sign of an exit, layoffs or a larger round.

name: Olio Labs
one_liner: Combination therapeutics for the world's toughest diseases
long_description: Olio labs uses AI to develop combination therapeutics that consider the thousands of interacting proteins in your body rather than targeting just one or two. Their lead combinations target obesity and are more effective with fewer side effects than Ozempic, the fastest growing drug of all time. Their custom ML built from real-world expertise and cutting edge AI searches trillions of combinations to find the perfect one.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Pharmaceutical partners and eventually patients with obesity (therapeutics developer; no revenue model sourced)
problem: Single-target obesity drugs such as GLP-1 agonists have limited efficacy and side effects; Olio uses ML to find multi-target drug combinations.
business_model: Drug development (pre-commercial); monetization route not found
product_category: AI-driven combination therapeutics / biotech
market_need_then: YC description (2023) frames Ozempic as the fastest-growing drug ever and targets better efficacy and fewer side effects; demand for obesity drugs was high at founding.
outcome_analysis: Olio Labs is active with a 5-person team and a reported seed of about $4.5M in March 2025, two years after founding. The founders ex-Loyal and Neuralink bring computational biology depth. No exit or clinical milestone was found, and funding totals conflict across databases, so the outcome remains open with high execution risk typical of therapeutics.

name: Omnistrate
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Build your control plane to deploy your product in your customer VPC…
long_description: Omnistrate helps software companies to build their own private-label control plane to deliver your product as vendor-hosted SaaS, inside customer cloud accounts/VPCs/Kubernetes clusters, on-premises, in air-gapped environments, and through cloud marketplaces.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: B2B software vendors, especially infrastructure and database companies, that need to deliver their product as hosted SaaS, bring-your-own-cloud, on-premises or air-gapped
problem: Software vendors must build and operate a control plane to provision, upgrade and bill deployments in many environments, which takes large platform engineering teams.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform (generated private-label control plane), pricing not public
product_category: Developer tools, SaaS control plane and BYOC deployment infrastructure
market_need_then: Enterprise buyers increasingly demanded vendor software inside their own cloud accounts or VPCs for data control, while vendors had to hand build each deployment model; the company's own pitch centers on this gap.
outcome_analysis: Omnistrate remains active with a team of about 25 and a customer wall that includes DataRobot, Percona and Liferay. Its founders came from AWS Aurora and Confluent cloud engineering, which matches the product. Funding is only visible through aggregators, so how far it has raised beyond the 2023 seed is not established.

name: OneText
one_liner: Frictionless payments via SMS
long_description:
OneText is disrupting SMS marketing and payments. We win incremental sales for direct to consumer brands by making every purchase as effortless as paying with your hotel room number. OneText shoppers literally reply and buy with one text.

In our first year, we’ve onboarded 50 fast-growing e-commerce brands and have added as much as 14% in incremental revenue to their bottom lines. In March, we generated $597,000 dollars in payments. In April, we’ll book $50,000 dollars in revenue. 

Founders Jonathan Fudem/CEO and Daniel Brain/CTO met at PayPal Checkout where we designed and launched some of the world’s best checkout experiences. We left PayPal to build a payments company that actually helps merchants acquire customers and win sales.

The CMO of our largest customer, a $90M clothing brand, says we have revolutionized marketing for his company, and are, quote: “the best thing that’s happened to SMS marketing in forever.”

We are excited to share what you can do with OneText.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Direct to consumer ecommerce brands that run SMS marketing and want shoppers to buy by replying to a text
problem: Checkout friction loses sales from SMS marketing, because shoppers must click out to a web checkout and enter details.
business_model: Payments and SMS commerce, take rate on text-to-buy payments plus marketing fees
product_category: Fintech, text-to-buy payments and SMS commerce
market_need_then: Direct to consumer brands relied on SMS marketing and wanted higher conversion; the company reported 50 brands onboarded in its first year and up to 14 percent incremental revenue for brands, per YC page.
outcome_analysis: OneText is active and raised a 4.5M USD seed in July 2025 from Khosla, Coatue, Citi Ventures and YC, about two years after its batch. Founders came from PayPal Checkout, which fits the product. Large SMS platforms launched text-to-buy in 2022, so differentiation depends on its own wallet and merchant network.

name: Onshore
one_liner: AI for corporate tax
long_description:
Onshore uses AI to prepare corporate R&D tax credits.

With our technology, anyone can prepare an R&D Tax Credit accurately and fast. To provide some background, the R&D Credit is often cited as the most complex and audited tax credit in the United States. With that in mind, we set out to create software to achieve two primary objectives:

1. Ensure that any credit computed with our software is exactly what the IRS is asking for in terms of quality.

2. Democratize the ability to perform high quality R&D Credit studies extremely fast.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: US companies in agriculture, engineering, manufacturing and oil and gas that claim R&D tax credits, 179D deductions and cost segregation
problem: Corporate tax incentive studies are slow and expensive when done by CPA firms, so many eligible companies never claim them.
business_model: Tax services with AI automation, fees per study delivered by credentialed tax professionals
product_category: AI enabled tax credit and incentive services (formerly SPRX)
market_need_then: R&D credits and similar incentives are widely underclaimed because studies are costly; the company launched its first product in December 2022 as a simple, fast and affordable R&D credit tool, per a StartupIntros listing.
outcome_analysis: Onshore, formerly SPRX, grew to a stated 500 plus clients and over 600M USD in incentives delivered, and announced a 31M USD Series B in February 2026 with FPV leading. It combined AI with credentialed tax staff in a large underserved services market. Earlier rounds are not confirmed in primary sources.

name: Onward
one_liner: Intelligent meeting automation for ambitious teams.
long_description: Onward is a new take on conversational intelligence. We streamline follow-ups, CRM updates, ticket creation, and other tasks after every meeting—helping you connect this knowledge to the rest of your tools.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: sales and support teams
problem: Post-meeting work (follow-ups, CRM updates, ticket creation) is manual; Onward automated it and connected to other tools.
business_model: SaaS for sales/support teams (pricing not found)
product_category: AI meeting automation
market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand found beyond the YC launch description.
outcome_analysis: Onward was a YC S23 meeting-automation startup by a former Midjourney product lead and a Chick-fil-A operator. YC lists it Inactive and its website no longer resolves here, but no shutdown notice, post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned.

name: OpenInt
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Open Source; AI
one_liner: Open Source Embedded Product Integrations
long_description: OpenInt helps teams ship product integrations in hours, not weeks, using no or low code. Read and write data using unified APIs or sync it straight to your database.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software companies that need to ship customer-facing product integrations with third-party services
problem: Building and maintaining integrations to many outside apps takes engineering weeks each; OpenInt offered unified APIs and syncs with low or no code.
business_model: Open source core with a hosted commercial platform (usage or seat based, details not found)
product_category: Embedded integrations platform (developer tools)
founder_names: Amadeo Pellicce; Philip London; Mark Pfluger
market_need_then: SaaS companies repeatedly rebuilt integrations; embedded integration platforms were an established category by 2022, shown by multiple vendors in later comparison coverage.
outcome_analysis: OpenInt was a four person team of ex-Blockchain.com engineers selling open source embedded integrations to developers in a crowded category. Public funding was small. Replit acquired it around September 2025 and folded it into Replit Connectors, so the outcome reads as a strategic team and technology acquisition at an undisclosed price. The success factor is a weak inference.

name: OpenMeter
one_liner: Usage Metering, AI & API Monetization
long_description: OpenMeter's mission is to standardize metering with the goal of becoming the data source for AI and API monetization. We've built an open-source platform that processes billions of events into our usage lake in a matter of seconds, which acts as the backbone that serves revenue and efficiency teams.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software companies and developers who need usage metering and usage-based billing for APIs and AI products
problem: Companies that bill by usage must collect and aggregate billions of events accurately and in real time; most build this in-house.
business_model: Open source core (Apache 2.0) plus paid managed cloud and enterprise plans
product_category: Developer infrastructure: usage metering and billing

name: Orbio Earth

Orbio uses satellite imagery to track methane emissions from the oil & gas industry. We sell the data to financial companies that want to invest into the best performing energy companies.

Until today, oil & gas companies use excel-based emission factors to calculate and report their emissions. As these excel-based emission factors underestimate actual emissions by ~70%, the finance companies that invest into oil & gas can’t mitigate against incoming risks from new regulations, 

We have built a technology that can for the first time use satellite images to track methane from every single oil & gas facility on the planet, replacing emission factors and allowing finance companies to make the best bets on oil & gas companies that will withstand a wide avalanche of incoming regulation. In the summer 2023 our satellite-based technology got ranked #1 both in terms of accuracy and sensitivity of methane emission events by Stanford University in a peer-reviewed study, beating a range of multi-bn dollar competitors like Maxar.

Learn more at https://orbio.earth
regions: Remote; Fully Remote

product_category: Climate tech, satellite methane emissions monitoring using public satellite data
market_need_then: Methane regulation and investor scrutiny of oil and gas assets were rising in 2022 and 2023, and the company cites a 70 percent underestimate in spreadsheet based reporting; early funding came from the climate VC Satgana and the ESA BIC.
outcome_analysis: Orbio Earth is active and raised a pre-seed in 2022 from Satgana and a 4M USD seed in March 2024 led by Initialized Capital after YC. It relies on public satellite data and proprietary detection, selling to finance and oil and gas, with regulation tailwinds. business_model: Developer infrastructure, Code Storage sold as an embeddable Git service (pricing not found)

name: Pigeon
one_liner: AI-powered document automation: collect, review, extract, and sync.
long_description: Pigeon automates the entire document lifecycle: collecting documents from clients, reviewing and extracting data with AI, and syncing with CRMs or storage systems. Pigeon eliminates the manual back-and-forth of document handling and eliminates thousands of hours of manual tasks.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Accountants, fund administrators, insurance brokers and claims processors who collect documents from clients
problem: Collecting documents from clients is a manual back-and-forth of emails and chasing; Pigeon automates collection, AI review, data extraction and syncing to CRMs or storage.
business_model: B2B SaaS (pricing not found)
product_category: Document collection and automation
market_need_then: The YC launch post pitched it as DocuSign for document collection, letting clients upload into a secure checklist without an account.
outcome_analysis: Pigeon appears to be a small, still active team of about five with an expanding AI document pitch and an open lead engineer role. No funding, customers, acquisition or shutdown could be verified from sources, so its trajectory is unknown rather than failed or successful.

name: Pincites
one_liner: Close deals faster with AI for contract negotiation
long_description: Pincites makes contract negotiations faster and more consistent for legal teams. Using LLMs, Pincites takes a first pass at reviewing contracts, helping lawyers focus on riskiest parts of their negotiations.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: In-house legal teams and law firms negotiating contracts in Microsoft Word
problem: Lawyers redline contracts by hand against internal playbooks, which is slow and inconsistent; Pincites applied a company's playbook with large language models inside Word.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for a Word add-in
product_category: Legal AI contract redlining and negotiation
founder_names: Sona Sulakian; Mariam Sulakian; Grey Steil
market_need_then: Legal teams faced high volume contract review in Word; the GPT-4 wave in 2023 made automated first-pass review newly feasible. The founders had direct transactional law experience.
outcome_analysis: Pincites paired a lawyer-founder with an engineer from GitHub and Meta to build a Word-native redlining tool as large language models became usable, raised a $3M seed in September 2023 and sold to Filevine in a competitive process around December 2025. Filevine renamed the product LOIS for Word, so the brand ended while the team and technology continued. The price is undisclosed.

name: Pirros
one_liner: AI Platform for Architects and Engineers
long_description:
Pirros is reshaping and revolutionizing how Architecture and Engineering firms manage design details. Our software empowers AECO design professionals (Architects, Engineers, Contractors, and Owners) to streamline their detail management process more effectively, reduce errors, and speed up project delivery. We’re building the system of record for detail management in a $12T+ industry that’s been underserved by technology for too long!

About Us

Backed by top-tier investors and angels (YC, Funders Club, PlanGrid, Elephant) - We closed our Series A of ~$17 million in 2025 - PROFITABLE, ~$6M ARR and growing revenue at +10% month-over-month - 300+ firms using us today, growing 10% MoM, 120% NRR - Co-founders both come from structural Engineering, so we have industry experience!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Architecture and structural engineering firms that need to manage and reuse design details and Revit content
problem: Firms repeatedly redraw design details because past work is hard to find; Pirros searches firm content by condition and places vetted details into Revit.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription to AECO firms
product_category: Design content management and AI for architecture and engineering
market_need_then: Architecture and engineering firms had underinvested in software for managing design details; the company cites a $12T plus industry underserved by technology.
outcome_analysis: Two structural engineers built a niche tool, took a $2M seed in August 2023 and say they were profitable since. They raised a $15M Series A in December 2025 led by Elephant Ventures and claim 450 firms. The company-reported figures are unaudited, but the path shows capital efficiency and domain fit.

name: PlayAI
one_liner: Our mission is to make Voice AI accessible and useful to all.
long_description: Play is a Voice AI company that specializes in building conversational voice models capable of cloning any voice or accent and generating speech in real-time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and enterprises building voice agents, narration and dubbing, paying for a text to speech and voice cloning API and studio
problem: Synthetic speech sounded robotic and could not hold a natural, low latency conversation or clone a voice and accent easily.
business_model: Usage-based API plus subscription web studio
product_category: Generative voice AI, text to speech and conversational voice models
market_need_then: Demand for natural synthetic voice was rising in 2023 with generative AI, for narration, dubbing and agents; the company says it focuses on conversational voice. No dated spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: PlayAI rode the 2023 to 2025 generative voice wave, raised a 21 million dollar seed in November 2024 and shipped conversational models, which attracted Meta. Meta announced the purchase in July 2025 at an undisclosed price, folding the team into its AI organization, so it reads as a talent and technology exit rather than a stand alone scale outcome.

name: Pledge Health
tags: SaaS; Health Tech; B2B; Workflow Automation
one_liner: AI RCM assistant that handles any insurance task on payer portals for…
long_description: Our AI browser assistant automates insurance tasks like verifying benefits, submitting prior auths, checking claim statuses, and more across all payer portals, directly from the clinic's EHR. It does exactly what the admin team is doing today, just helps them do it 10x faster and as thoroughly as a seasoned teammate.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent clinics and their admin teams that handle patient billing and insurance tasks
problem: Clinics lose time and revenue on manual insurance verification, prior authorization and claim status checks on payer portals, and cannot tell patients what they owe at the visit.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for clinics
product_category: Healthcare revenue cycle automation
market_need_then: Insurance admin work is a known cost for clinics; no dated spend or complaint figures were found in this research.
outcome_analysis: Pledge Health stayed a two person team after YC W23, repositioned from patient billing estimates to AI assistants for payer portal tasks, and was acquired by Collectly in March 2026 at undisclosed terms. Public evidence of traction or funding scale is thin, so whether this was a strong outcome or a soft landing is not known.

name: Plutis
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers seeking on-demand mental health support, plus therapists wanting tools to grow their practices
problem: Access to therapy and coaching is fragmented; Plutis combined AI journaling and coaching, licensed therapists and peer support groups in one app.
business_model: Consumer app, listed free on iOS with services through therapists and coaches (pricing not verified)
product_category: Digital mental health platform
market_need_then: Demand for digital mental health was high after the pandemic; the founders had prior telemedicine experience. No product-specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Plutis launched an iOS app in 2023 and a Product Hunt page in September 2023, and no funding, acquisition or shutdown could be verified. One tracker says the Android app left Google Play in July 2024 and the current plutis.io page shows an unrelated POS product, suggesting it stalled, but this is not confirmed and the cause is not public.

name: Pointhound
one_liner: Earn and redeem credit card points for free flights
long_description:
Pointhound makes it easy to earn and redeem your credit card points for free flights. 

We're driven by our mission to make the world more accessible through travel.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers with credit card points who want cheaper flights
problem: Redeeming points is complex. Pointhound searches many airlines and transfer partners and explains how to book.
business_model: Credit card affiliate fees, Premium subscription and paid concierge booking
product_category: Travel points and award flight search
founder_names: Jay Reno; Jake Malone; Samantha Clark
market_need_then: Points redemption is widely seen as confusing, though no dated 2023 source was gathered here.
outcome_analysis: Pointhound is an active S23 company run by repeat founders from Feather that earns affiliate and subscription revenue. A 2026 report summarized by RuntimeWire says four staff served 750,000 users in 2025, but funding and revenue are not disclosed, so its trajectory cannot be judged.

name: PoloTab
tags: SaaS; Payments; B2B; Analytics; Food Tech
one_liner: Restaurant software that actually works
long_description:
The ecosystem coffee shops and restaurants in Mexico run on.

From point of sale, to inventory management, payments and much more for the most demanding. 

Our tech is as user-friendly as an iPhone, yet powerful enough to power Starbucks. 

PoloTab is led by a team driven by the vision that things should be different, with the skills to make it happen. We were born from the food & beverage industry and are here to make a difference, not merely be part of the crowd.
regions: Mexico; Latin America
target_customer: Cafes, coffee shops, restaurants and bars in Mexico, from single locations to chains
problem: Mexican restaurants ran on clunky legacy POS and sales-heavy vendors; PoloTab offers modern POS, inventory, payments and invoicing that keeps working offline.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription from 990 MXN plus IVA per month, payment processing quoted separately
product_category: Restaurant POS and payments software
founder_names: Aldo Piaggio; Andres Richardson; Juan Chomali
market_need_then: Mexico's restaurant software market was served by sales-heavy traditional vendors, per a VC Mexico interview; no hard demand metrics from 2022 or 2023 found.
outcome_analysis: PoloTab says more than 1,200 venues in 70 plus Mexican cities use it, up from about 800 in a 2025 profile, with a design-led product and founders from the food and beverage trade. Funding is unclear, with a reported small pre-seed and a 2024 seed whose size is not public, so growth may be largely self-funded.

name: PoplarML
tags: AIOps; Machine Learning; B2B; API; AI
one_liner: Deploy Machine Learning Models with One Command
long_description: PoplarML lets you deploy any machine learning model to a fleet of GPUs as a ready-to-use and scalable API endpoint with one command.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: ML engineers and startups deploying custom models to GPU inference endpoints
problem: Deploying ML models to scalable GPU API endpoints requires heavy infrastructure work.

product_category: ML model deployment and inference infrastructure

outcome_analysis: PoplarML is a two person YC W23 team that launched one command GPU model deployment in early 2023. Aggregators show only a small convertible note, and its website returned an error with no news of an exit or shutdown. The outcome is not public; the space was crowded and moats were thin, but the cause of any stall is not documented.

name: Portalform
one_liner: Build and host internal tools
long_description: Coming soon
