A propulsion engineer founder with SpaceX and Impulse experience and demand for cheap interceptors helped. Products are not yet publicly specified, so delivery risk remains.

name: Sirdab
one_liner: Cloud warehousing & supply chain platform in MENA
long_description: Sirdab is a tech-ops focused startup offering cloud warehousing and transportation / logistics solutions. We have built an end-to-end logistics platform that allows businesses to acquire dry, ambient, chilled and frozen warehousing space within 48 hours as well as manage, optimize and distribute inventory via a single platform.
regions: Saudi Arabia; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Businesses in Saudi Arabia that need warehousing and transport, from SMEs to large firms and government bodies
problem: Warehouse space in Saudi Arabia was hard to get quickly and on flexible terms; Sirdab says demand exceeded supply by 30 to 50 percent.
business_model: Warehousing as a service with month to month, 6 month and 12 month contracts, plus transport and WMS and OMS software
product_category: Cloud warehousing and logistics platform
market_need_then: Sirdab cites demand above warehouse supply by 30 to 50 percent in Saudi Arabia; a Knight Frank item in search results noted warehouse occupancy nearing saturation (later date, not opened).
outcome_analysis: Sirdab grew from a cloud warehousing startup in the Winter 2023 batch into a broader logistics platform and in September 2026 raised a 10 million dollar Series A co-led by Elm and BECO Capital to expand across the GCC. It claims 20x revenue growth since the batch and profitability, which are company figures. A local market with supply gaps and large named clients supports its traction.

name: Skyhook
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; B2B; Kubernetes; DevOps
one_liner: PaaS-like experience with the power of Kubernetes, on your cloud
long_description:
We make running services on Kubernetes as easy as Heroku, but on your cloud and with all the flexibility and power of Kubernetes. Companies use Skyhook so that they don't have to hire dedicated infrastructure engineers.

Although 50-70% of organizations have already adopted Kubernetes, most developers agree that it is too complex and difficult to manage. It is intended to be extremely flexible in order to solve pretty much everyone’s needs, but it can take a ton of work and many auxiliary tools to get there.

As companies grow, they spend a lot on DevOps or Platform Engineers that try to reduce the burden on developers by gluing together all the 3p tools via custom internal tools.

We are building an “internal developer platform” out of the box, with best practices and golden paths for building and operating services on Kubernetes.

We do the research on the latest and greatest tools in the extremely vibrant ecosystem, and automatically integrate for you the tools you want to use.

We operate on our customers code and in your Cloud environment, so they never locked in and never restricted, as is common with classic PaaS offerings.

If you prefer a fully hosted environment like Heroku, Fly or Vercel, we’ll host a cluster for you and offer you a one-click migration to your own cluster when you want.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and engineering teams running services who want a Heroku like experience on their own Kubernetes without hiring platform engineers
problem: Kubernetes is powerful but complex, and companies spend heavily on DevOps and platform engineers to glue tools together.
business_model: B2B SaaS internal developer platform that runs in the customer's cloud, with an optional hosted cluster and an open source tool (Radar)
product_category: Kubernetes internal developer platform
market_need_then: The company states 50 to 70 percent of organizations have adopted Kubernetes while most developers find it too complex.
outcome_analysis: Skyhook is active with about seven people and sells a Kubernetes internal developer platform, and it released an open source Radar tool in 2024. Funding is unverified: aggregators list a 500K dollar pre-seed from Y Combinator and others and total raised between 2.5 and 3.5 million. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found, so its position is early stage in a crowded platform engineering market.

name: Skyvern
tags: Robotic Process Automation; Workflow Automation; Open Source; API; AI
one_liner: Open Source AI Agent to automate browser workflows via an API
long_description:
Skyvern helps companies automate browser based workflows using LLMs and Computer Vision, fully automating manual workflows and replacing brittle or unreliable scripts.

Examples include:
1. Automating materials procurement from commerce websites
2. Completing complex multi-step workflows (ie getting an insurance quote from Geico.com)
3. Automatically logging into portals and downloading invoices
4. Navigating legacy content systems to do data extraction or data entry
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Companies and developers with manual or brittle browser-based workflows such as procurement, invoice download, insurance quotes and legacy portal data entry
problem: Browser automation with scripts breaks whenever a site changes. Skyvern uses LLMs and computer vision so agents can operate unseen websites without per-site selectors.
business_model: Open source (AGPL) core plus paid managed cloud, usage-based API and enterprise plans
product_category: AI browser automation agent / RPA
market_need_then: RPA and scraping scripts were known to be brittle and costly to maintain, and LLM tool use arrived in 2023, creating a chance to replace per-site scripts. Demand evidence in the sources is the company's own claimed usage numbers.
outcome_analysis: Skyvern rode the 2023 shift to LLM agents with an open source browser automation tool and by December 2025 announced a 2.7 million dollar seed round, while claiming large GitHub and customer numbers. Raising only a seed more than two years after the batch and facing model lab entrants and many open source rivals suggest a still contested position. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff was found.

name: Slicker
one_liner: Recover payment failures and maximize subscription Revenue
long_description: Slicker eliminates involuntary churn through AI-powered retries, tailored for your business. Our proprietary engine automatically monitors, detects, and recovers failed recurring payments, so you can convert past due invoices into revenue.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Subscription businesses in SaaS, media, health and fitness, e-commerce and e-learning that bill recurring payments via Stripe, Chargebee, Adyen or PayPal
problem: Failed recurring card payments cause involuntary churn. Slicker uses AI driven retry timing and dunning to recover them.
business_model: Performance based pricing on recovered revenue (company states if it does not outperform, customers do not pay)
product_category: Failed payment recovery / payments analytics
market_need_then: Involuntary churn from failed card payments is a recognized subscription problem and processors offered only generic retries. Evidence in sources is vendor claims only.
outcome_analysis: Slicker remains active as a two person London team that sells payment failure recovery on performance pricing, and by its site has widened into a payments data platform. No priced round beyond the YC deal could be verified and no exit or shutdown was found, so the story is still unresolved with limited evidence of traction beyond company claims.

name: Smobi
one_liner: Send texts your customers actually want over RCS
long_description: Smobi is the AI-powered platform for branded, interactive business messaging, starting with RCS. We help businesses send rich, personalized messages that drive engagement, build trust, and create real conversations.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Sohar Health
tags: Health Tech; Digital Health; API; Data Science; AI
one_liner: AI-powered insurance verification to boost patient conversion.
long_description:
Sohar Health is an AI-driven front-end RCM solution that transforms insurance verification processes for healthcare providers, enabling faster patient conversions and reducing administrative workloads.  With a 95% automation rate, our API-first platform seamlessly integrates into existing workflows to provide real-time claim accuracy and eligibility checks. 
Key performance metrics showcase the power of our technology: Median latency of just 6 seconds, ensuring real-time eligibility; over 90% of checks returned within 30 seconds for increased patient conversion; 96% accuracy in identifying and verifying benefits details; Industry-leading 99% accuracy for eligibility determination; >90% carve-out detection rate, mitigating surprise billing risks; a 60% success rate with our Insurance Discovery API, helping identify coverage for self-pay patients.

Our customers include outpatient clinics, specialty practices, and digital health platforms looking to streamline front-end claim management. By reducing errors and maximizing clean claim submissions, Sohar Health empowers healthcare organizations to convert and retain more patients, reduce operating costs, and increase their top-line revenue.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Outpatient clinics, behavioral health practices and digital health platforms that must verify insurance before care
problem: Manual insurance eligibility and benefits checks are slow and error prone, which delays patient conversion and causes surprise billing.
business_model: Usage-based API for eligibility, benefits and insurance discovery
product_category: Healthcare front-end revenue cycle, insurance verification API
market_need_then: Insurance verification is a daily cost for providers; dated spend figures were not found.
outcome_analysis: Sohar raised a 3.8 million dollar seed in March 2025 led by Kindred Capital, signed customers such as Talkiatry and Zocdoc, and was bought by Zocdoc in October 2026 at undisclosed terms. Founders with Quit Genius experience in payer integration and compliance helped, and the sale formalized an existing partnership.

name: Sola
tags: Robotic Process Automation; Workflow Automation; Automation; AI
one_liner: Copilot for Robotic Process Automation
long_description:
Sola is copilot for workflow automation. 

We help automation-minded teams build robust robotic agents to handle tedious tasks via LLMs and computer vision, smoothly integrated into their standard workflow. 

Our tooling makes it easy for companies to automate data entry/scraping in manual filing and processing flows. Go from a screen recording to a bot in any desktop or browser workflow; develop logic and watch logic self-develop in the face of new events!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises and mid-size firms in logistics, legal, healthcare, banking and similar sectors with manual back office data entry and filing workflows
problem: Traditional RPA bots are brittle and expensive to build and maintain. Sola records a process once and uses LLMs and vision to create bots that adapt when systems change.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an automation platform with enterprise contracts
product_category: AI process automation / RPA
market_need_then: RPA was an established multi billion dollar category with known maintenance pain, and generative AI in 2023 opened a chance to rebuild it. Demand evidence is mainly that incumbents were adding AI.
outcome_analysis: Sola entered a large RPA market just as LLMs made bots cheaper to build, raised a 3.5 million seed led by Conviction and a 17.5 million Series A led by a16z in August 2025. Enterprise customers in legal and logistics are named on its site. Risk remains from UiPath and agent startups, but no shutdown or exit was found.

name: Solve Intelligence
one_liner: AI patent drafting, prosecution, litigation and more for legal teams.
long_description:
Solve Intelligence is the AI platform for helping legal professionals with every part of the patent process.

With $55M backing from Y Combinator, Microsoft, Thomson Reuters, 20VC, Operator Collective, Visionaries, and others, they have assembled a world-leading team of patent attorneys, AI PhDs, and software developers to build products for patent application drafting, office action responses, invention harvesting, claim charting, infringement analysis, FTO, validity challenges, patent litigation, and more.

They are now selling their 100% secure and confidential software to 700+ IP firms and in-house teams across the US, Europe, and Asia (e.g. DLA Piper, Siemens, Perkins Coie, Amgen - see customers https://www.solveintelligence.com/#customers).

Solve customers are reporting 60-90% efficiency and quality improvements (see testimonials https://www.solveintelligence.com/#testimonials).

See a demo today: https://www.solveintelligence.com/contact-us
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Patent law firms and in-house IP teams, about 700 teams per the company
problem: Drafting patent applications and responding to office actions is slow and done in Microsoft Word with little software support. Solve uses AI to speed drafting, prosecution and later litigation analysis.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat subscription
product_category: Legal tech / AI patent drafting and prosecution
founder_names: Chris Parsonson; Sanj Ahilan; Angus Parsonson
market_need_then: Patent attorneys lacked software beyond Word for drafting, and TechCrunch in November 2023 reported over 25 IP firms already using it with claimed 60 to 90 percent efficiency gains and roughly 100 thousand to 1 million dollars in recurring revenue.
outcome_analysis: Solve launched in July 2023 into a profession with weak software, signed 25 firms within months, and raised a 3 million seed, a 12 million Series A in April 2025 and a 40 million Series B in December 2025 for 55 million total. The company reports eight figure recurring revenue growing tenfold, then expanded by acquiring Palito.ai and ClaimWise in 2026.

name: Sorted
one_liner: Instant SaaS management
long_description:
The first completely automated SaaS management software. 
Scrap the spreadsheets and avoid slack surveys when you need to run compliance audits, provisioning users, or track unused licenses. Sorted provides visibility to admins in 2 minutes without sacrificing employee flexibility.
regions: Denmark; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote

name: SpecCheck
tags: SaaS; Payments; Health Tech; B2B; API
one_liner: Unifying how the optical industry does business.
long_description: SpecCheck is an all-in-one solution that provides accurate prescription eyewear ordering and tracking, seamless billing, and streamlined communication between patients, eye doctors, and their lab partners. SpecCheck’s users work more efficiently and make fewer costly errors, increasing productivity and improving their overall workflow.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Opticians and optometry practices placing prescription eyewear orders, plus optical labs and enterprise optical chains
problem: Eyewear prescription orders between opticians and labs are error prone and poorly tracked. SpecCheck provides validated order entry, status tracking, billing and lab chat in one place.
business_model: B2B SaaS and payments (order platform with Lab Pay billing portal)
product_category: Vertical SaaS for the optical industry
market_need_then: Opticians and labs communicated through error prone processes, per the company's own founding story. No third party demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: SpecCheck is an industry insider led vertical SaaS company that raised a 3.7 million seed led by Initialized Capital in October 2023 and has since added lab network partnerships with Ocuco and Hoya. No later priced round was found, and the optical software market is crowded with entrenched suites, so the outcome is still open.

name: Speedy Labs
one_liner: Maximize profits with AI-powered rebate management.
long_description:
Speedy Labs helps manufacturers and distributors ditch error-prone spreadsheets that cost them millions in missed rebate opportunities for an AI-powered solution that not only tracks rebate payments and their performance but also unlocks insights from their financial data silos that uplifts their bottom-line profit margins.

$1 trillion worth of rebates are exchanged every year in North America alone.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Manufacturers and distributors, now focused on foodservice distributors and buying groups handling rebates
problem: Rebates are tracked in error prone spreadsheets and short payments go uncollected. Speedy Labs uses AI to track and reconcile rebates and surface margin insights.
business_model: B2B SaaS for rebate and margin operations
product_category: AI rebate management / finance operations
founder_names: Jatin Mehta; Ranti Dev Sharma; Ayush Jasuja
market_need_then: The company states about 1 trillion dollars of rebates are exchanged yearly in North America and that spreadsheets cause missed rebates; this is a company claim without third party verification.
outcome_analysis: Speedy Labs is an active small team that has narrowed from general rebate management to AI agents for foodservice distributors, with named customers and a UniPro selection on its site. No priced funding round could be verified, though the site says it is backed by Y Combinator and Google Ventures, so traction beyond company claims is unclear.

name: Spine AI
one_liner: Manage a swarm of AI agents to get real work done
long_description:
Spine AI is a visual workspace where a single prompt spins up a swarm of AI agents that plan, delegate, and execute complex tasks together — with humans fully in the loop.

Instead of chatting back and forth with one model, Spine breaks work into visible steps on a shared canvas. Agents collaborate in parallel, ask clarifying questions, use connected tools, and show their reasoning and intermediate outputs as they work.

Every agent’s work stays inspectable, auditable, and editable — reducing hallucinations and giving you real control over the outcome.

Spine connects to leading AI models and your existing tools, but the real power comes from orchestration: you act as the team lead, Spine runs the swarm.

Chat is great for answers. Spine is built for execution.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Knowledge workers such as founders, consultants, investors and analysts who want multi-agent AI research and deliverables
problem: Single chat threads handle complex work poorly. Spine gives a visual canvas where many agents plan and execute in parallel with human oversight.
business_model: SaaS subscription for Canvas, with a local first orchestrator product (Medley)
product_category: AI agent orchestration / visual AI workspace
market_need_then: Demand for generative AI assistants rose sharply in 2023, but no dated evidence of demand for a visual multi-agent workspace was found near the batch.
outcome_analysis: Spine AI moved from an early AI copilot description to a visual AI canvas and later a multi-agent swarm product, launching on Product Hunt and Hacker News. No verified priced round, customer count or exit was found, and it faces model labs and workspace tools entering the same space, so the trajectory is unclear.

name: StackAI
one_liner: The Enterprise AI Transformation Platform
long_description:
Acquired by Asana (NYSE:ASAN) in May 2026.

StackAI partners with enterprises to deploy custom AI agents to automate their most complex back-office workflows. Teams at BAE Systems, Monzo, Morgan & Morgan, and Goodwill work with StackAI to bring AI Agents to their operations.

Enterprises use StackAI no-code to automate large compliance audits, knowledge work, legal intake, due diligence research, and insurance claim underwriting.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises that want no-code AI agents for back office workflows such as compliance audits, legal intake and claims underwriting
problem: Building and governing LLM powered workflows across enterprise systems took engineering teams months.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscription with services-led deployments
product_category: No-code enterprise AI agent platform
market_need_then: Interest in LLM apps surged after late 2022, and enterprises sought no-code ways to deploy them; no dated spend figure found.
outcome_analysis: StackAI caught the enterprise agent wave, raised a small seed then a 16 million dollar Series A in 2025, signed customers such as Monzo and BAE Systems, and was bought by Asana in May 2026 for a price outlets put at 75 million dollars but the parties did not confirm. Strong founders and an enterprise motion drove a mid sized exit while competition from platforms kept the standalone path hard.

name: Stellar Sleep
one_liner: We help people with chronic insomnia sleep better, using psychology.
long_description: 25 million Americans with chronic insomnia are getting inadequate and superficial care advice (e.g. cutting coffee, meditation etc.), when in reality, their sleep problems are often driven by deeper psychological challenges like unresolved anxiety. Stellar Sleep uses psychology to help these people break the insomnia cycle.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Adults with chronic insomnia paying for a CBT-I based program, plus clinicians and employers
problem: Chronic insomnia is often driven by psychological factors, while sleep clinicians have long waits and generic apps target occasional sleep trouble. Stellar Sleep delivers psychology based therapy through an app and specialists.
business_model: Consumer subscription (TechCrunch reported 60 dollars per month in 2024) plus clinician network and employer offering
product_category: Digital health / CBT-I insomnia therapy
market_need_then: TechCrunch reported founders were told of six to twelve month waits for sleep clinicians, and the company cites 25 million Americans with chronic insomnia. Existing sleep apps mostly targeted occasional problems.
outcome_analysis: Stellar Sleep, started from personal chronic insomnia, raised a 6 million seed led by Initialized in February 2024 and now reports 100 thousand patients and a clinician network with an employer channel. No later priced round, exit or shutdown was found, and the pay-per-month consumer model still has to show durable retention.

name: Storyboarder
one_liner: Tool and platform to create and sell webcomics
long_description:
Storyboarder is a tool and a platform for anyone to create, share, and sell webcomics.


In East Asia, the webcomic (or digital manga) industry is an $12B market and rapidly growing to the rest of the world. Webtoon, the largest company in the space, generates $100M / month in revenue. However, their addressable market is limited by their content creators, who need know how to draw. Readers are desperate for a greater variety of stories in webcomics.


Through years of working with filmmakers, we’ve built extremely easy to use storyboarding software  that has 700K users. We’re democratizing visual storytelling to everyone. We’re working on the next generation that, through advances in video game interfaces, ubiquitous 3D compute, and AI, will allow anyone to easily create scenes, pose characters, to create webcomics. 


Storyboarder is backed by Y Combinator (W23), David Karp (Tumblr Founder), Andrew Kortina (Venmo Founder), and other product focused investors.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Hobbyist and aspiring webcomic creators who cannot draw, plus readers who pay per episode
problem: Webcomic platforms are limited by creators who can draw. Storyboarder wanted to let anyone build scenes, pose 3D characters and publish episodes as webcomics.
business_model: Creator platform with transaction fees on paid webcomic episodes (readers pay after a free set of episodes)
product_category: Webcomic creation tool and publishing marketplace
market_need_then: YC page cites a $12B East Asian webcomic market growing worldwide and says readers want more story variety. Evidence of demand from creators who cannot draw is the founders' claim, with no independent source.
outcome_analysis: Storyboarder entered YC W23 with an existing storyboarding tool of about 650K users and a notable founder from OMGPOP, then pitched a webcomic platform. No funding amount is confirmed by a primary source, no exit is reported, and the web domain now redirects to a product called Sumugi from Storyboarder Inc, so the company appears to have continued under a new brand. The outcome is unclear, with no public traction figures after 2023.

name: Strada
one_liner: AI agents that run insurance operations
long_description: Strada automates insurance operations with AI agents. We deploy agents that handle policy servicing and claims operations end-to-end for some of the largest insurance carriers and brokers in the US. With native integrations into core policy, claims and agency management systems, we automate complex workflows with the domain expertise and compliance guardrails the industry demands.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US insurance carriers, TPAs, MGAs and brokers that pay for automated policy servicing and claims operations
problem: Insurance back offices rely on phone, email and legacy portals for servicing and claims work. Strada deploys AI agents that handle those tasks inside existing systems.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software sold to carriers and brokers, deployed in about four weeks per the company site
product_category: AI agents for insurance operations (voice, email, chat, SMS and browser automation)
market_need_then: Insurance operations are labor heavy and many carriers use systems without APIs; the company reports vendor claims of 80 percent end-to-end resolution, unverified. No dated 2023 demand source was found.
outcome_analysis: Strada appears to have grown into an enterprise product with named insurance customers such as Clearcover (March 2026) and about 16 staff per the directory, but funding is unconfirmed by any primary source, so the strength of its progress after YC S23 cannot be judged. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found in searches.

name: Stralis Aircraft
tags: Hard Tech; Hydrogen Energy; Airplanes; Climate; Electric Vehicles
one_liner: Emission free hydrogen electric aircraft
long_description: Our planes fly 10 times further than battery electric alternatives, with a lower operating cost than fossil fuel powered aircraft. Our first product is a 15 seat aircraft with a range of 800 km that enters service in 2026 with launch customer Skytrans. Our team has over 85 years of aerospace experience and have developed, flight tested and certified aircraft at Google X, magniX, Heart Aerospace, Ampaire, Airbus, Boeing, Bombardier and Gulfstream. We have $145M in aircraft LOIs from 7 airlines in the US, Europe and Australia.
regions: Australia; Oceania; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Regional airlines and aircraft operators buying hydrogen-electric propulsion systems or converted aircraft
problem: Battery electric aircraft have short range and fossil fuel aircraft emit carbon. Stralis aimed to retrofit and later build hydrogen-electric aircraft with ten times the range of battery electric.
business_model: Aircraft and propulsion system sales and conversions, with letters of intent from airlines; funded by grants and equity
product_category: Hydrogen-electric aircraft propulsion and retrofit
market_need_then: Airline decarbonization pressure and regional routes poorly served by battery electric range. YC page cites $145M in LOIs from 7 airlines (letters of intent, not orders).
outcome_analysis: Stralis built technical demonstrators and won grants and LOIs, but the August 2026 shutdown coverage says it could not raise enough equity and the hydrogen aviation market, certification costs and fuel infrastructure were not ready. A larger seed target of $8M was stated but no close was found. It ended weeks after a successful taxi test, with no acquirer.

name: Struct
one_liner: Multi-lingual AI Voice Agents
long_description: Struct is the platform for multi-lingual AI voice agents for any phone-based task. Our agents are already live doing tens of thousands of calls daily across the globe and in multiple languages.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote

name: Structured Labs
one_liner: The publishing layer for the agentic internet
long_description: Waldium is an AI-driven platform for researching, writing, and publishing technical knowledge in formats that both humans and AIs can understand. We help developers create technical guides, resources and tutorials — structured, durable knowledge that AIs can learn from, cite, and build upon.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Studdy
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Education; Consumer; Edtech; AI
one_liner: An AI tutor that helps you study
long_description:
At Studdy, our mission is to unlock the full potential of the next generation by providing a personalized AI tutor for every student.

Studdy is a multilingual tutor that uses AI, as well as advanced speech, text, and image recognition technology to supercharge students' ability to learn new subjects.

We believe that making self-learning as easy as possible for as many students as possible (no matter their cultural, social, or educational background) is the key to unlocking the full potential of students around the world.

We're a passionate team of AI experts, educators, and builders - if you also have a passion for transforming education we'd love to hear from you.

Shoot us a message at team@studdy.ai!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Students, mainly in high school and university, who pay for an AI tutor app
problem: Students lack affordable personal tutoring. Studdy teaches uploaded notes and homework on a virtual whiteboard with voice and image input.
business_model: Consumer subscription with a free first lesson and trial
product_category: AI tutor consumer app
market_need_then: Large student demand for homework help (Photomath, Chegg) and a new technology shift from GPT-4. No dated demand figures for Studdy were found.
outcome_analysis: Studdy was a four person YC S23 AI tutor team with founders from Photomath and Speak that still has a live product and mobile app. Funding is not confirmed by any press release, so its fundraising progress and traction after the batch are unclear. A crowded AI tutoring category with low defensibility is the main risk, but no shutdown or acquisition was found.

name: Subsets
tags: Machine Learning; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: AI-driven Retention Automation for subscription media businesses.
long_description:
Subsets is the leading lifecycle growth platform for consumer subscription teams.

We are building the AI decisioning layer that unifies and powers the existing growth stack, enabling teams to automate and scale lifecycle experimentation, orchestrate personalized user journeys, and measure impact across retention, engagement, and LTV without engineering support.

Trusted by consumer subscription businesses like The Atlantic, NBCUniversal, Daily Mail, Matas Group, and Hearst.

Subsets has raised $6.1m and launched out of Y Combinator’s Summer 2023 batch in San Francisco, and is now based in Copenhagen.
regions: Denmark; Europe
target_customer: Consumer subscription media businesses such as publishers and streaming services (The Atlantic, Daily Mail, Hearst, NBCUniversal)
problem: Subscription media teams struggle to run retention experiments and personalized journeys without engineering help. Subsets predicts churn risk and automates lifecycle experiments.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for retention and lifecycle automation
product_category: AI retention and lifecycle growth platform
founder_names: Martin Johnsen; Oliver Brandt; Nikolai Skelbo; Matias
market_need_then: Subscription media competes on churn and lifetime value; named customers publish retention goals. No dated 2023 source on the market was found.
outcome_analysis: Subsets moved from San Francisco to Copenhagen after YC S23, raised a confirmed $1.65M pre-seed in February 2024 and lists premium publishers as customers, with a seven person team. The YC page claims $6.1M raised but only the pre-seed is sourced, so later rounds are unknown. It remains active with no exit.

name: SuperAPI
one_liner: Programmable API gateway that makes APIs cacheable
long_description:
SuperAPI is a programmable API gateway that makes all your fetch APIs cacheable, reducing the response time 10x. 
Our customers use SuperAPI to cache their critical APIs without spending 6-9 months rewriting their code.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Engineering teams with high traffic fetch APIs that want caching without rewriting code
problem: Caching APIs correctly takes months of engineering to handle invalidation. SuperAPI sits in front of APIs and invalidates cache entries by watching writes and database changes.
business_model: Usage-based developer infrastructure subscription with pricing page
product_category: Programmable API gateway and cache
market_need_then: Founders cite scaling API latency at their prior company. No dated third party source on demand was found.
outcome_analysis: SuperAPI remains a two person YC W23 team with a live website showing a 2026 copyright and a pricing page. No funding beyond YC is confirmed, no customers are named, and no exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is unclear and traction cannot be rated.

name: SuperKalam
one_liner: AI-Powered Super Mentor for Test Prep
long_description: Every student deserve personal attention. With AI, we can infinitely scale personalised learning experience at scale to every student. That's what we are building at SuperKalam.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: UPSC civil services aspirants in India who pay for an AI mentor instead of coaching
problem: Quality UPSC coaching costs more than Rs 1 lakh a year and offers little personal feedback. SuperKalam offers doubt solving, Mains answer evaluation and practice at a lower price.
business_model: Consumer subscription (SUPER plan priced at Rs 6,499 until Mains per the site) with a limited free trial
product_category: AI test prep mentor for UPSC
market_need_then: Millions of UPSC aspirants spend heavily on coaching. The site compares its price to coaching at Rs 1 lakh and ChatGPT Pro at about Rs 20,000. No dated third party demand figure was opened.
outcome_analysis: SuperKalam focused on one exam, UPSC, and led by a former Unacademy growth leader raised a $2M seed in May 2024 led by YC and FundersClub with a team of 20. The product is live with pricing and no exit or layoffs were found. Growth data is not public, so the strength of product market fit is unverified.

name: Surface Labs
tags: Sales; Marketing; Advertising; AI; Conversational AI
one_liner: We deploy agent teams that run critical business operations on your…
long_description:
Surface Labs is an applied AI lab that enables autonomous companies. 

We help enterprises hand critical operations to agent teams instead of adding another tool or another headcount. 

Our agent teams run real work on the systems a company already uses, from inbound, pricing and FP&A to supply chain, KYC reviews and AML alerts.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B revenue and marketing teams that pay to capture, qualify and convert inbound leads with agents
problem: Inbound lead forms lose conversions and teams lack staff for marketing operations. Surface Labs started with intelligent forms and now sells agent teams for marketing and other operations.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software sold through demos, with agent based workflows
product_category: AI agents for marketing and revenue operations
market_need_then: Founders cite conversion work at Snowflake as the origin and later customers report conversion lifts, all self reported. No dated 2023 market source found.
outcome_analysis: Surface Labs pivoted after YC S23 into intelligent forms and then agent teams, and now names customers such as Nextiva, Juicebox and Valley with a ten person team. Funding is not confirmed by a primary source, no exit or shutdown was found, and customer lift figures are company claims, so traction is unverified.

name: Sweep
one_liner: The best AI coding assistant for JetBrains
long_description: Use your favorite JetBrains IDE without compromising on AI. Sweep is the best autocomplete and agent in JetBrains: https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/26860-sweep-ai
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Professional developers who work in JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ, PyCharm, Android Studio) and pay for AI autocomplete and an agent
problem: Developers who prefer JetBrains IDEs got weaker AI tooling than VS Code users. Sweep started as a GitHub bot that turned issues into pull requests and later rebuilt itself as a native JetBrains plugin.
business_model: Subscription for a developer tool plugin, per seat
product_category: AI coding assistant
market_need_then: Developer interest in AI coding agents was surging in 2023. The GitHub repo reached several thousand stars according to a secondary source, which shows early demand for the open source bot.
outcome_analysis: Sweep raised a small seed in late 2023 at a reported 25 million post money after the open source issue to pull request bot drew attention. It then moved to a JetBrains plugin with autocomplete and an agent, still a four person team in the YC directory. It is active with tens of thousands of plugin installs per secondary sources, but no later round was found and the real outcome is still open.

name: Sweetspot
one_liner: AI for Government Contracting.
long_description: Sweetspot is an all-in-one government sales platform, powered by AI. We help businesses find, manage, and respond to government opportunities.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Government contractors and businesses selling to federal, state and local government, who pay a subscription
problem: Finding, tracking and responding to government contract opportunities is slow and fragmented across SAM.gov and other portals. Sweetspot uses AI to search, manage the pipeline and draft responses.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: GovCon sales and proposal software
founder_names: Sachin Subramanian; Philip Kung; Andrew Arkhipov
market_need_then: Federal procurement is a very large spend and opportunity search was hard. Semafor covered Sweetspot's AI search for the contract maze in August 2023, which indicates demand existed at launch.
outcome_analysis: Sweetspot launched with AI contract search in 2023, raised a 2.2 million seed led by 1984 Ventures in August 2024 and kept building toward capture and proposal tools. It now cites compliance credentials and many customer logos on its site. No later round or exit was found, so it looks like a growing niche vendor whose outcome is still open.

name: Synch

long_description: Your Sales and Sales Ops team in a unified platform. No setup, Salesforce SSO and go.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Syncly
tags: Generative AI; SaaS; B2B; Social Media; Marketing
one_liner: Social listening for the video era
long_description: Syncly co-founders (former founders of Sualab, a video AI startup, $200M exit) are building agentic AI to automate video marketing for the world’s largest CPG brands (Tiffany, Clorox), a market where brands spend hundreds of billions on agencies today. At $2.1M ARR, grown 2x in 6 months, 4x in 12 months, and 142% NDR. Backed by YC, SoftBank, and John Kim (Sendbird CEO).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Brand, social and consumer insights teams at large consumer brands and their agencies
problem: Text based social listening misses what is said and shown in short form video on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. Syncly analyzes speech, on screen text and visible products.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Social listening and video analytics
founder_names: Joseph Lee; Jongsoo Keum; Kwan Yoon

name: Tennr
one_liner: Fast, Transparent Patient Experiences
long_description:
Tennr is solving the black hole problem in healthcare by leveraging models to digitize the flow of paperwork between healthcare providers.
--
Today, when you go to your doctor and need to be referred to a specialist (e.g., for sleep apnea), your doctor sends a fax (yes, in 2024, 90% of provider-provider communication is a 1980s fax). These are often converted into 20+ page PDFs, with handwritten (doctor’s handwriting!) notes, in thousands of different formats. The problem is so complex that a person has to read it, type it up, and manually enter your information. Tennr built RaeLM™ (7B—trained on 3M+ documents) to read these docs, talk to your doc to ensure nothing is missed, and text you to help schedule your appointment so you can get better, faster.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Healthcare providers and provider groups (specialty practices, infusion, DME, hospitals) that receive patient referrals by fax and PDF
problem: Referrals between providers arrive as faxes and multi-page PDFs in thousands of formats and a person must read and key them in, so patients fall into a black hole before scheduling.
business_model: B2B SaaS for healthcare administrative teams, configured per provider
product_category: Healthcare AI referral intake and patient flow automation
founder_names: Trey Holterman; Diego Baugh; Tyler Johnson
market_need_then: YC page states about 90 percent of provider to provider communication still ran over fax, and staff retyped referrals manually, a large labor cost and patient leakage problem.
outcome_analysis: Tennr targeted a concrete, ugly workflow, fax referral intake, with a purpose-trained model and sold it to providers who measure lost patients. It raised an $18M Series A in March 2024, a $37M Series B in October 2024 and a $101M Series C at a reported $605M valuation in June 2025, with the company saying revenue more than tripled after the Series B. The homepage now claims 200+ provider customers. No acquisition or distress was found.

name: Terminal
tags: Developer Tools; Logistics; API; Supply Chain; Transportation
one_liner: Plaid for Telematics Data in Commercial Trucking
long_description: Terminal builds telematics data infrastructure for the commercial fleet industry. Commercial auto insurers and fleet software companies, including industry leaders like Intact Insurance, depend on our platform to access GPS, speeding, and vehicle data from 330+ telematics providers. We recently raised our Series A led by Battery Ventures and are backed by Y Combinator, Golden Ventures, Penske Transportation Solutions, and Intact Private Capital. Our team works together in person in Toronto, combining early-stage speed with late-stage maturity while processing many terabytes of vehicle data every day.

product_category: Unified telematics data API
market_need_then: Betakit (2023-12): 150,000 trucks committed to integrating, via FreightWaves; later Series A coverage says commercial auto insurance is about half of revenue and customers include Intact.

Insurance buyers pulled demand, and the integration work is a real moat against casual copying. Risks are telematics vendors opening their own APIs and a narrow vertical.

name: Terracotta AI
one_liner: AI-powered Infrastructure as Code PR reviews
long_description:
Terracotta AI is an AI-powered Infrastructure as Code PR reviewer for Terraform, OpenTofu, and CDK-TF code, making Infrastructure as Code changes more transparent, less risky, and faster.

Terracotta stops your Infrastructure as Code deployments from becoming ticking time bombs every time you modify your environment with AI-driven, contextual feedback delivered directly to your pull requests.

target_customer: DevOps and platform engineering teams that manage cloud infrastructure with Terraform, OpenTofu or CDK-TF
problem: Infrastructure as Code changes are hard to review, and a bad merge can cause drift, outages or cost spikes; reviewers need context beyond the diff.

product_category: AI code review for Infrastructure as Code

outcome_analysis: Terracotta AI is an active three person company selling AI review of Terraform pull requests. It has a HashiCorp partnership listing and named customers on its YC page, but no verified funding, revenue or traction numbers were found. The category is crowded with IaC platforms and general AI code reviewers, so the outcome is still open and nothing here supports a success or failure story yet.

name: Texel.ai

long_description:
Theya is the world’s simplest Bitcoin self-custody app for users who find crypto exchanges risky and hardware wallets overwhelming. We are making the self-custody UX seamless with our multi-sig wallet that users can set up using smartphones, giving them the functionality and convenience of centralized exchanges without sacrificing control and security of hardware wallets.

We aim to be the default consumer app for Bitcoin - offering products like accumulation, lending, investments and payments - all built on top of our intuitive self-custody platform.

name: Trackstar

name: Trainy
tags: Developer Tools; Machine Learning; SaaS; Infrastructure
one_liner: Infrastructure for managing GPU clusters for training/serving.
long_description:
Goodbye Slurm, Hello Konduktor.

Trainy Konduktor is a software platform for AI teams to schedule workloads with priority, control resource allocation, and improve GPU reliability. With Konduktor, teams submit jobs to a healthy pool of GPUs, assign job priority with a simple user interface, and never worry about hardware faults again.

product_category: GPU cluster scheduling and AI infrastructure software

outcome_analysis: Trainy remains a small company selling GPU cluster scheduling and, from 2026, an experiment tracker aimed at Neptune users. Its site claims over 5 million GPU hours managed and logos including DigitalOcean, Paperspace and Linum, all self-reported. Funding appears limited to about 500 thousand dollars from Y Combinator per aggregators, so the story is early and unproven rather than a clear success or failure.

name: Trayd
one_liner: A construction payroll and compliance platform built for specialty…
long_description:
Trayd is building the operating system for commercial construction: payroll, compliance, and back office workflows that actually work in the real world.

Construction is one of the biggest industries in North America (valued at $2T+), and it still runs on a messy mix of spreadsheets, legacy payroll providers, and manual processes that break the moment things get even slightly complex. The people doing the work are the hardest working people in the country, and the companies running crews are forced to spend hours every week fighting systems that were never built for them.

We’re changing that.

Trayd started with a simple promise: construction workers should be able to access the money they already earned faster, and subcontractors should be able to run payroll without chaos. Today, we’re building deeper infrastructure across payroll, union rules, job costing, and accounting workflows so our customers can run their businesses with confidence.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Specialty trade subcontractors in commercial construction, including union shops with prevailing wage rules
problem: Construction payroll, union rules and certified payroll reports run on spreadsheets and legacy providers, and workers wait days to be paid.
business_model: B2B SaaS charged per employee per month, expanding into an ERP style back office
product_category: Construction payroll, compliance and back-office software
market_need_then: The July 2023 YC launch post says workers could get earned wages 7 to 10 days sooner than legacy providers, a stated pain for subcontractors and crews; the company's own claim, no independent data.
outcome_analysis: Trayd started with fast pay for subcontractors and expanded into payroll, union compliance, job costing and accounting for specialty trades. It raised a $4.5M seed in February 2025 and a $10M Series A led by White Star Capital in March 2026, with Suffolk and Y Combinator following on, and its site claims hundreds of contractors and 34 employees. Growth looks real, though traction figures are company or aggregator claims.

long_description: React components to build charts and dashboards

outcome_analysis: Tremor built a popular open source React library from founders' dashboard work at Accenture, joined YC S23 to build a paid visual builder, then was acquired by Vercel in January 2025 to invest in open source components and the Vercel dashboard. The outcome was a team and community absorption with undisclosed terms rather than a commercial scale win.

name: Trigger.dev
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; B2B; Open Source; AI
one_liner: Build and deploy fully‑managed AI agents and workflows
long_description:
Trigger.dev is the open source platform for building AI agents and workflows in TypeScript. Long-running tasks with retries, queues, full observability, and elastic scaling.

Previously, the founders built JSON Hero, an open source JSON viewer that is currently used by more than 35k developers a month. Eric was CTO of Code School, an early code learning platform that was acquired in 2015. Matt created two iPad apps that won Apple’s App of the Year.

business_model: Open source core with usage-based managed cloud and self-hosting option
product_category: Developer tools, background jobs and durable workflow platform
founder_names: Matt Aitken; Eric Allam; Dan Patel; James Ritchie
market_need_then: Developers on serverless stacks such as Vercel lacked long-running job support, and the company reported early open source traction of over 4,000 GitHub stars by August 2023.
outcome_analysis: Trigger.dev grew from an open source Zapier-style tool into a background jobs framework and then an AI agent workflow platform. It raised a 3 million dollar seed in August 2023 on open source traction, then a 16 million dollar Series A in December 2025 led by Standard Capital. Reliability incidents in late 2025 and June 2026 are a risk, but the sources found show no layoffs or exit.

name: Trigo
one_liner: Rent verification API for landlords and lenders
long_description:
Trigo aggregates consumer rent history to help landlords approve better tenants and lenders write more loans. No solution exists to consistently furnish this rent verification to landlords and lenders today. The largest database has only 3% coverage of rent data.

Trigo is a Consumer Reporting Agency (CRA) that provides this missing rent data set through a real-time API and web application. We are repeat founders with consumer data and finance experience across Harvard, Citigroup, Experian, and Amazon.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Landlords, property managers and lenders who pay for verified rent payment history
problem: Landlords and lenders had no consistent source of rent payment history, since the largest database covered about 3 percent of rent data.
business_model: Usage-based API and web app sold as a Consumer Reporting Agency
product_category: Rent verification data, proptech and fintech API
market_need_then: The company says the largest rent database covered only 3 percent of rent data and landlords lacked verification; this is the company's own claim.
outcome_analysis: Trigo built a rent history CRA from founders with finance and Amazon data backgrounds, stayed very small with little disclosed funding, and partnered with Snappt before Snappt acquired it in August 2025 at an undisclosed price. The deal fit Snappt's applicant trust platform, so this reads as a strategic tuck in rather than a scaled independent business.

name: Truewind
tags: Fintech; Generative AI; SaaS; B2B; AI
one_liner: AI-Powered Accounting
long_description:
Truewind is a technology company based in San Francisco developing a digital staff accountant. Powered by AI, Truewind is a digital staff accountant that never sleeps, never gets sick, and always does its work. Completely predictable capacity planning. 

Automate data categorization, supporting documentation collection, and client follow-up. Truewind’s AI agents will follow up on outstanding action items while the accountant can work on strategic tasks. This is fully integrated and unified across your accounting operations. We make it easy to get work done and get visibility into your team’s processes. 

Trusted by over 100 customers, including accounting firms EisnerAmper and Frank Rimerman, along with fast-growing companies such as Wefunder, StartPlaying and Mozart Data. We’re backed by the industry leaders of accounting and AI, Rho Capital, Thomson Reuters Ventures, Pathlight Ventures, Fin Capital, and Y Combinator.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and accounting firms that need faster bookkeeping and month-end close

product_category: AI accounting software
market_need_then: Accounting firms faced staffing shortages and manual work, and the 2022 to 2023 arrival of capable language models created a technology shift.
outcome_analysis: Truewind started building in late 2022, joined YC in Winter 2023 and raised a seed in September 2023 and a $13M Series A in December 2024 co-led by Rho and Thomson Reuters Ventures. It rode the language model wave in accounting, selling to startups and firms such as EisnerAmper, and remains active. Many AI accounting rivals make defensibility modest.

name: Turntable

name: Twine

Twine helps service businesses turn more leads into revenue by bringing their entire sales process into one workspace.

We connect calls, texts, website inquiries, Google, Yelp, and other lead sources into one shared inbox where inside sales teams, field reps, and AI agents work together to qualify leads, book jobs, and follow up with customers.

Twine also connects customer conversations, sales activity, marketing attribution, and revenue data so businesses can understand what's working, where opportunities are being lost, and what to do next.

We're starting with pest control, building alongside some of the industry's leading operators to create the sales infrastructure for the next generation of service businesses.
