regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent authors, screenwriters and creators writing long-form fiction, paying individually
problem: General chat tools handle long creative documents poorly; writers want an editor with AI that remembers characters and style.
business_model: Consumer SaaS subscription with a free tier
product_category: AI document editor for creative writing
market_need_then: The 2023 generative AI wave created demand for writing tools; the company states 300k+ writers use it (company site, undated).
outcome_analysis: Type raised a 2.8 million dollar pre-seed in June 2023 and narrowed from a general AI editor to fiction writers, claiming 300k+ users. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, and its reliance on third-party models leaves defensibility thin.

name: Unhaze
one_liner: The right leads at the right time for B2B sales
long_description:
Unhaze is a revenue optimization tool for mid-market B2B teams.

Unhaze finds the leads that sales teams are most likely to close right now. We do this by analyzing previous deals and continuously monitoring for similar traits among all our collected company data.

By focusing on the right leads (at the right time!), we can almost double win rates.
regions: Denmark; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Unify
tags: Reinforcement Learning; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Models that keep learning
long_description: Building the next frontier of models that continually learn from a stream of experience.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: AI engineering teams building LLM applications and agents
problem: Teams struggle to pick the best model per prompt for quality, speed and cost, and later that frozen models do not improve from usage.
business_model: Usage-based API (router) moving to continual learning platform
product_category: LLM routing, then continual learning infrastructure
market_need_then: Few LLM applications existed at founding; the need for model routing grew with the 2023 model proliferation.
outcome_analysis: Unify raised an 8 million dollar seed in May 2024 on an LLM routing pitch with notable backers, then repositioned toward continual learning. Routing became a crowded category, so the pivot is a hedge. No exit, shutdown or later round was found.

name: Univerbal
one_liner: Language learning with a conversational AI Tutor
long_description:
Univerbal is an AI-powered language learning app that helps people boost their confidence simply by talking. In unscripted and dynamic conversations, users can talk about anything they’d like using the microphone, with the AI responding as it adapts to their level and skills. Each user gets a personal AI Language Tutor that creates a custom learning plan based on the language goals they’d like to work towards and their own interests, offers instant corrections after every message and helps users in their own language.
Based in the country with 4 official languages, Switzerland, in 2024 we were selected as one of WIRED’s Hottest 100 Startups in Europe.
regions: Switzerland; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Language learners who want speaking practice without a human tutor, paying by subscription
problem: Learners understand a language but freeze when speaking and lack affordable low-pressure conversation practice.
business_model: Consumer subscription with free trial
product_category: AI conversational language tutor app
market_need_then: Speaking practice is the main pain for learners and LLMs made conversational tutors feasible in 2023.
outcome_analysis: Quazel, an ETH Zurich spin-off, raised seed money from Khosla Ventures in July 2023 and rebranded as Univerbal. It claims 250k+ downloads and a 4.7 App Store rating on its site, and was named to a Wired list in 2024. No exit, shutdown or later round was found.

name: Unstatiq
tags: Health Tech; Finance; B2B; Supply Chain
one_liner: Single source of truth for your clinic's finances and supply chain.
long_description: There are billions of dollars of hospital waste caused by inefficient, disconnected supply chains and finance data. Today, clinics are facing unprecedented backorders, recalls, and purchase verticals (medical devices, SaaS, security, commodities). We are building a single product to 10x a fragmented industry with each tool built almost 20 years ago.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Clinics and hospitals (originally finance and supply chain teams; now hospital managed care teams)
problem: Clinic finance and supply chain data is fragmented across old tools, causing waste; the current site targets slow review of payor contracts and policies.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold via demos
product_category: Healthcare finance and supply chain software, now AI contract review
market_need_then: The founders pitched hospital waste from fragmented supply chain and finance data and recalls and backorders in 2023.
outcome_analysis: Unstatiq is a two-person company that appears to have moved from clinic finance and supply chain tooling to AI review of payor contracts. No public funding beyond an unverified aggregator figure, no customers and no exit were found, so the outcome is unknown and no factors are asserted.

name: Untether Labs
one_liner: Scheduling software for digital health clinics to do more with less.
long_description: Digital Clinics are facing an existential problem - fix margins, or die. We’ve built a clinic, and seen the tech they need to fix their margins. Now we’re bringing this tech back to other clinics. For our first customer, we’re projected to generate $2.5M in revenue.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Digital health clinics and healthcare employers that schedule clinical staff
problem: Digital clinics have thin margins and inefficient manual scheduling and callout handling for care teams.
business_model: B2B SaaS for AI workforce management in healthcare
product_category: Healthcare scheduling and workforce management
market_need_then: The founders had run a digital clinic and said margins forced the need; the YC page projected 2.5M revenue from the first customer.
outcome_analysis: Untether Labs sells AI scheduling and callout coverage to digital health companies and names customers such as Iris Telehealth, Dialogue and Headspace on its site. Funding beyond an unverified aggregator figure is not public, and no exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Upfront
tags: Marketplace; Consumer; Home Services; AI Assistant
one_liner: A personal assistant for every homeowner
long_description: Upfront is a personal assistant for home projects, powered by AI and partnerships with local businesses. Instead of sifting through reviews and playing phone tag, homeowners text us, and we connect them with a curated set of home service professionals in their neighborhood.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Upstream
one_liner: The inbox that handles itself
long_description: Your inbox, handled for you. Upstream's agents sort the noise, draft replies in your exact voice, follow up at the right time, and do what you ask - like finding receipts or scheduling meetings - so you can fly through your inbox and have fun doing it.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Individual professionals and small teams who live in Gmail and pay for a faster, AI-run inbox
problem: Email triage, replying and follow-up take hours each week. Upstream puts agents inside the inbox to sort, draft in the user's voice and chase follow-ups.
business_model: Freemium AI email client with a paid Pro subscription
product_category: AI email client / inbox agents
market_need_then: Email overload was a long-standing pain, and the 2023 LLM wave made drafting in the user's voice and automated triage newly feasible.
outcome_analysis: Upstream is still active and early. It spent nearly three years after the S23 batch in invite-only beta before general availability and a $3M pre-seed in June 2026. Its seasoned product and engineering founders and the strong angel list are positives, but it faces Gmail, Outlook, Superhuman and Shortwave, so the outcome is open.

name: Vaero
one_liner: AI for Human Writing
long_description: Vaero's AI produces the most human sounding writing in the world. User's input their own writing, and Vaero automatically trains custom models to write exactly like the user. It writes emails, reports, brand content, and anything else. Vaero bolts on to any existing foundation model, such as GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 3.5, so you can always use the latest model in your writing style.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Content marketing teams and brands that want AI articles in their own voice
problem: Generic LLM output sounds machine-written. Vaero trains a model per user or brand on their own writing so output matches their style.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for brand-voice AI content
product_category: AI writing / brand voice personalization
market_need_then: After ChatGPT's late 2022 launch, users complained about generic AI prose and wanted output in their own voice.
outcome_analysis: Vaero is still active as a one-person company. It moved from personal-style writing to brand-voice content for marketers, with aggregators also listing a patent-drafting angle that the YC launch post mentions. No public traction, round or outcome is verifiable, so the story is unclear.

name: Vango AI
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; Design; Gaming; AI
one_liner: Development platform that makes it 10x easier to improve visual models
long_description:
We built Vango excited by the future where generative visual AI models like stable diffusion dramatically reduce the barrier to create content. While spending 8 months building products for creatives, we found ourselves building hacky tools to address many of frustrations we had with visual AI. 

So we decided to build the devtool we needed: Vango is a flexible evaluation platform that makes it 10x improve visual models. Developers using visual AI models at scale use Vango to learn quantitative ways to improve their model, saving them ~10 hours per week. 

Major companies building visual products have already begun integrating diffusion models, including Adobe, Disney, Activision Blizzard, Canva, and Snap. By 2025, it is estimated that 1 billion images per day will be AI-generated.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Variance
one_liner: AI Agents for Fraud Review and Investigations
long_description: Variance builds AI agents for fraud, identity, and investigations for Fortune 500s, Marketplaces, and regulated financial services.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Fortune 500 companies, marketplaces and regulated financial institutions with fraud, KYC and compliance review teams (originally trust and safety teams at online platforms)
problem: Fraud, identity and compliance investigations need large amounts of manual evidence gathering. Variance agents collect evidence and produce audit-ready case traces.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software sold to fraud and compliance teams
product_category: AI agents for fraud, KYC/KYB and transaction monitoring investigations
market_need_then: Platforms faced rising trust and safety obligations and fraud volume, and founders had seen the problem at Apple and Discord.
outcome_analysis: Variance began as Intrinsic, a trust and safety startup in W23, and pivoted around 2025 to AI agents for financial crime investigations. The shift to regulated buyers and the LLM agent wave supported a $21.5M Series A led by Ten Eleven Ventures in March 2026. It is active with a team of about a dozen.

name: VaultPay
one_liner: Digital banking platform for the 30 million smartphone users in DRC.
long_description: Vaultpay is building a digital banking platform for 30 million smartphone users in DRC and the country's largest agent network. For example, a young Congolese entrepreneur who just won a subcontract with a major mining company can now easily open a personal and business account, receive payments, all from their smartphone, instead of spending hours at bank branches.
all_locations: Kinshasa, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
regions: Democratic Republic of the Congo; Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Smartphone users and small businesses in the Democratic Republic of the Congo who lack easy access to bank accounts and cards
problem: Opening a bank account and getting a card in the DRC means hours at branches. VaultPay offers accounts, Visa cards and an agent cash-in cash-out network from a phone.
business_model: Fintech fees on card, account and agent banking transactions
product_category: Digital banking / neobank for the DRC
market_need_then: The DRC has over 100 million people but few bank accounts; the YC page cites 30 million smartphone users and long branch waits.
outcome_analysis: VaultPay is active and early. It launched its product in Q4 2025 with 17,000 plus users and about $20K MRR claimed on its YC page, and says it holds a full Central Bank of Congo payment license and is raising a seed. Outcome remains open; regulatory position and agent network are strengths, small revenue and entrenched telecom wallets are risks.

name: Vector
tags: Generative AI; SaaS; B2B; Marketing; Enterprise
one_liner: Advertising for the new internet
long_description: B2B advertising is broken: poor targeting, wasted ad spend, bot traffic, and 3rd party-cookies. Vector helps marketers drive pipeline with contact-level targeting and revealing who's seeing your ads (even if they never convert).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B marketing and demand-generation teams
problem: B2B ads cannot be targeted to named contacts or show which accounts saw them; Vector offers contact-level ad targeting and relationship intelligence.
business_model: B2B SaaS / ad platform
product_category: Contact-level B2B advertising
market_need_then: No dated source collected; founders came from Drift's sales organisation, which sells to the same marketing buyers.
outcome_analysis: Vector, a 2022 Boston company from Winter 2023, was run by two former Drift sales-engineering leaders and raised a US$10M Series A in May 2026 led by SignalFire and HubSpot Ventures. The long gap from YC to Series A suggests slow, capital-light growth; revenue and customer data are not public (an aggregator revenue estimate is unreliable).

name: VectorShift
one_liner: AI Operating System for Private Market Investors
long_description: VectorShift is the AI operating system for private market investors.VectorShift is the AI operating system for private market investors. We capture a firm's institutional knowledge across every deal, decision, and diligence finding, and put it to work across data room analysis, IC memos, portfolio company monitoring, and LP reporting.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Private market investment firms (originally teams building internal LLM tools)
problem: Deal teams lose institutional knowledge across data rooms, memos and diligence. VectorShift captures it and applies AI to data room analysis, IC memos, monitoring and LP reporting. At launch it was a no-code builder for LLM workflows.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS
product_category: AI platform for private market investors (formerly no-code LLM workflow builder)
market_need_then: Companies in 2023 wanted to build internal LLM tools quickly without engineers after ChatGPT; the later focus targets private equity diligence workloads.
outcome_analysis: VectorShift is active with a team near 30. It raised a $3M seed in February 2024 as a horizontal no-code LLM builder and has since narrowed to private market investors with SOC 2 and single-tenant offerings. No later round was found, so traction of the vertical pivot is unproven in public sources.

name: Vellum
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Product and engineering teams at companies building production LLM applications (later enterprises and operations teams; in 2026 consumers for a personal assistant)
problem: Teams struggled to prompt, evaluate, version and deploy LLM features reliably. Vellum offered a platform for prompt engineering, evaluation and workflow orchestration.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscriptions with enterprise plans; consumer subscriptions for the 2026 assistant
product_category: LLM development platform / LLMOps
founder_names: Akash Sharma; Sidd Seethepalli; Noa Flaherty
market_need_then: After ChatGPT in late 2022, companies needed tooling to move LLM prototypes into production; the founders had built such apps at Dover.
outcome_analysis: Vellum rode the 2023 LLM tooling wave, kept going through a crowded LLMOps market and raised a $20M Series A in July 2025 on enterprise compliance offerings. In 2026 it shifted to a personal assistant and then announced the hosted assistant would close in November 2026 for weak distribution and fierce competition, so the company's current direction is unsettled.

name: Velos
tags: Reinforcement Learning; Robotic Process Automation; Insurance; Automation; AI
one_liner: AI BPO for Specialty Insurance MGAs
long_description:
Velos helps insurance carriers and MGAs automate complex, manual back-office tasks with AI workers instead of overseas teams.

We take over workflows with the same responsibility of a traditional overseas Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) firm: mapping the customer’s existing process, creating the SOP, building the automation, and continuously improving the workflow after launch. 

Unlike other "automation platforms" we don't rely on our customers to build and manage the workflow, we take over it for them like a traditional outsourcing firm.

We're automating the repetitive work people hate to do.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Specialty insurance MGAs, program managers and carriers that pay for back-office work
problem: Specialty insurers run manual post-bind work such as data entry, bordereaux reporting, billing and month-end close, usually with overseas outsourcing teams that are slow and error-prone.
business_model: Service-priced AI BPO: Velos maps the process, builds the automation and runs it, replacing outsourced labor
product_category: AI back-office automation for insurance
market_need_then: Insurers and MGAs outsourced back-office work to overseas BPO firms. Source for demand is the company's own positioning, no dated third-party source found.
outcome_analysis: Velos is a tiny YC W23 company (team of three listed) that stayed active through 2026 and has focused on specialty insurance MGAs with a done-for-you AI outsourcing model. The site mentions NVIDIA Inception and a 2026 cyber pitch result. No funding, customers by name or exit could be verified, so the story is unclear and sources do not show strong traction.

name: Vendah
one_liner: Vendah is building a Faire-style marketplace for LATAM’s +50M…
long_description:
Vendah is building a marketplace that connects digital-first beauty brands to a network of individual sellers across Brazil, powered by embedded microcredit. Brazil is one of the largest beauty markets globally (~$30B), with millions of individuals already selling through fragmented, offline channels that lack modern infrastructure.

After pivoting to a marketplace + credit model, traction has accelerated: GMV is growing ~30% MoM, we’re approaching 1,000 active sellers, and risk-adjusted margins are now positive and improving. We’re building a network of sellers powered by a proprietary credit engine.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Individual resellers in Brazil (mostly women) who sell beauty and wellness products through WhatsApp and social media, and the digital-first brands that supply them
problem: Millions of Brazilians resell products through fragmented offline channels without modern infrastructure, credit or catalog access, and need low-cost entry without upfront investment.
business_model: Reseller marketplace with take rate on sales plus embedded microcredit and installment payments
product_category: Social commerce reseller marketplace with embedded credit
founder_names: Luis Felipe Franco; Marcelo Canovas; Ilana Nasser; Pedro Pedruzzi
market_need_then: Brazil is a large beauty market and direct selling was moving to social commerce in 2022, with millions of informal sellers, per Brazilian press; the YC page cites a market of about 30 billion dollars.
outcome_analysis: Vendah raised a pre-seed in 2021, joined YC in Winter 2023, raised a R$12 million seed in August 2023, and later pivoted from home goods to beauty with credit, claiming 45,000 resellers and 30 percent monthly GMV growth. It stated a goal of a 2024 Series A but none was found, so the story is a promising but unproven pivot.

name: Vendora
one_liner: All-in-One Software for the $1T Grocery Industry
long_description:
Vendora is building a generational company in one of the largest industries out there - grocery. We build software to serve the $1 trillion dollar (over 3% of US GDP) grocery industry. This ranges from point of sale, payments, e-commerce, inventory management, loyalty, and advanced analytics with more on the horizon. 

We’re taking bleeding edge technology and an AI-focused approach to modernizing an industry stuck in legacy software and practices. Backed by Y Combinator and investors with deep expertise in retail, we are a team of operators from Amazon, Uber, Tesla, Figma and McKinsey in transforming a sector that touches us all.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent grocers and grocery chains, from mom and pop stores to large chains
problem: Grocers run on disconnected legacy systems and lack e-commerce. Vendora began with e-commerce enablement and storefronts and expanded to POS, payments, inventory, loyalty and analytics.
business_model: Vertical B2B SaaS for grocery with payments
product_category: Grocery management software / e-commerce enablement
market_need_then: Grocery is a very large industry on legacy software, and the post-2020 online grocery shift left independents without e-commerce capability.
outcome_analysis: Vendora is active in New York with a very small team. It started with grocery e-commerce enablement and now markets a full grocery platform covering POS and payments. Public funding evidence is limited to an unverified small seed, so traction and outcome cannot be judged; the founder's grocery operating background is the main strength.

name: Venta AI
one_liner: The compliant AI colleague for sales teams in Europe
long_description: Venta AI supports sales teams in Europe with targeted outreach. Our AI employee can access the best companies and contact details and carry out automated outreach in compliance with EU regulations.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B sales teams at European manufacturers, distributors and wholesalers
problem: Outbound prospecting in Europe is manual and legally risky under GDPR. Venta AI finds companies and decision-makers and runs compliant personalized outreach over email, LinkedIn and letters.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI outbound sales platform
product_category: AI SDR / outbound sales automation
market_need_then: European sales teams wanted automated outbound but faced GDPR and competition-law limits that US tools ignored, and LLMs in 2023 made personalized outreach cheap.
outcome_analysis: Venta AI is active in Munich with named European customers such as ARNO and UnternehmerTUM and vendor-claimed gains of 30 percent more meetings. It raised a $2M pre-seed in July 2025 led by Gradient, two years after YC. Compliance positioning helps in Europe, but the AI SDR space is crowded, so the outcome is open.

name: Verata
tags: Fintech; Generative AI; SaaS; HR Tech
one_liner: Network Intelligence for Investors
long_description: Source Proprietary Deals Through Your Network. Verata combines relationship intelligence with private company data to help PE firms find targets, identify warm paths, and get to companies before they hit the market. We also empower firms to leverage their extended network for back-channeling and due diligence on prospective investment targets.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Private equity firms and executive search firms serving PE
problem: PE firms struggle to source proprietary deals and to find warm paths and backchannel references into target companies and executives.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (inferred from product positioning; pricing not found)
product_category: Relationship intelligence and executive research for private equity
market_need_then: PE firms compete for proprietary deal flow and rely on personal networks for diligence; no dated 2023 source on spend was found.
outcome_analysis: Verata is a two person company that remains active with no public funding announcement, customer names or exit. Its current site has moved toward executive intelligence for PE talent teams, building on the founders' prior executive search software companies. There is too little sourced evidence to say whether it is stalling or growing.

name: Versive
tags: SaaS; B2B; Design Tools; Market Research; AI
one_liner: AI-first user research platform
long_description:
Versive is an all-in-one research platform that helps teams make faster customer-informed decisions.
- Collect richer insights: AI-moderated studies that deliver interview-quality results at the survey speeds
- Accelerate your analysis: AI-assisted analysis that instantly turns transcripts into shareable insights
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product, design and research teams at startups, enterprises and research agencies
problem: Customer research is slow: recruiting, moderating interviews and synthesizing transcripts take weeks.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (pricing not verified)
product_category: AI user research platform
market_need_then: Teams wanted faster synthesis of interview data as generative AI emerged in late 2022 to 2023; no dated spend figures found.
outcome_analysis: Versive is a three person company that still operates, expanding from interview synthesis to AI moderated studies and AI persona tests. No priced round, exit or customer count is publicly sourced, and rivals like Outset entered at the same time, so its trajectory is unclear.

name: Versori
tags: SaaS; B2B; API; No-code; Data Engineering
one_liner: Agentic integrations & automations for enterprise
long_description:
Orchestrate custom integrations, workflows & agents in hours, not months. Take control of your integration strategy and breathe easy with maintenance on AI Autopilot.

For Product Teams: Build better integration libraries. Build a feature-rich integration library, for your users to enjoy. Offer out-of-the-box integrations that work for you and your customers. Embedded IPaaS typically locks you into connector or endpoint limitations. Versori gives you to tools for limitless customisation. Proactive, self healing agents, scan your connected apps for endpoint or schema changes. You get alerted, Versori AI fixes the change. Embed Versori built integrations into your app with the Versori SDK. Flexible to your development approach with advanced user management.

For Operations Teams: Get your internal systems speaking the same language. Deliver integrations for new software in days, not months—so you can start unlocking value immediately. Versori’s speed to value reduces typical deployment fees by half—or more. Low code for speed. Full code for control. No more limits from inflexible integration platforms.

For GTM & Sales Teams: Say yes to any prospect's integration request. Stop bouncing between teams to get integrations built. With Versori, Sales can go straight to yes. No more escalations or delays. Versori offer fully managed custom-builds, so your customers get exactly what they need, without compromise.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software product teams, operations teams and enterprise sellers that need system integrations built quickly, including ERP and ecommerce users
problem: Building and maintaining integrations between business systems takes months and heavy professional services. Versori set out to cut that to days or hours.
business_model: B2B SaaS integration platform with fully managed custom builds
product_category: Integration platform as a service (iPaaS), later agentic integration
market_need_then: Versori's own launch material argues that integration cost comes from professional services time and that deployments take months. A vendor claim says a Sephora integration dropped from 9 weeks to 2 hours.
outcome_analysis: Versori started as a Manchester integration platform, took YC money in 2022 and a 3.5 million dollar seed in June 2023, and later added AI agents that generate and maintain connectors. Partnerships such as SYSPRO in 2025 and a clear pitch against slow iPaaS projects led to its acquisition by Avalara in March 2026, with terms undisclosed and the founders staying on.

name: VetRec
one_liner: AI Scribe for veterinarians. Saving time and improving patient care.
long_description: VetRec automates the process of taking clinical notes for veterinarians in a matter of seconds. Veterinarians should just review clinical notes, not spend time creating them. A visit with a pet is precious and 100% of the focus should be spent on the pet, not on notes. VetRec is the veterinarian's best friend.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Veterinary clinics, hospital groups and individual veterinarians
problem: Veterinarians spend large amounts of time after visits writing clinical notes, which causes burnout and takes attention from patients.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per veterinarian, with a free trial
product_category: AI medical scribe and practice assistant for veterinary medicine
market_need_then: Documentation burden and burnout among veterinarians, described by the founders as coming from family and friends who were vets, plus the 2023 arrival of capable speech and language models.
outcome_analysis: VetRec pivoted from developer AI tools into a veterinary scribe at the start of the 2023 generative AI wave and has expanded into intake, phone and an AI receptionist (July 2026) with named hospital group partnerships from 2024 to 2025. The company is active with a reported team of 45, but funding beyond aggregator-listed pre-seed money is not public, so its trajectory against a crowded scribe market is unproven.

name: Viddy
one_liner: A new way to create landing pages that is video-native.
long_description:
A brand new way to create landing pages that's video-native. Traditional ways of building landing pages are too costly (money & time) and brands want to experiment more. Our landing pages rely on video content to do the heavy lifting from a dev & design perspective.


Our landing pages convert well (+15-30% across channels such as paid ads, email, and sms) and take <20min to create. This means brands can test over 10x what the currently do with Viddy.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Direct to consumer ecommerce brands running paid social, email and SMS campaigns
problem: Traditional landing pages cost too much money and time to build, so brands cannot test enough variants. Viddy built landing pages around video so they could be made in under 20 minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS with Viddy building the first pages for customers
product_category: Video landing pages and shoppable video storefronts for ecommerce
market_need_then: Ecommerce brands were spending heavily on paid social and wanted more landing page tests. The company's own claim is a 15 to 30 percent conversion lift, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Viddy was a two person team selling video landing pages to ecommerce brands, with a Postscript SMS integration as its visible distribution. YC lists it as acquired, but the buyer, date and price are not public in the sources found, so the cause and quality of the outcome cannot be judged.

name: Vitalize
one_liner: Transforming how health systems optimize labor
long_description:
Vitalize is solving the most pressing operations problems for health systems, starting with optimizing staffing and scheduling. We help hospitals dramatically reduce labor spend, improve operational efficiency, and unburden clinical leaders from hours of work per day.

We're partnered with some of the country's most innovative health systems, and are excited to share more details soon!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hospital and health system operations, staffing and nursing leadership
problem: Health systems spend heavily on labor but staffing and scheduling is manual and reactive, burdening clinical leaders.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus forward deployed operating partner teams
product_category: AI hospital labor, scheduling and capacity platform
market_need_then: Hospitals faced high labor costs and manual scheduling; a symplr survey cited in coverage found 41 percent of respondents had fully manual scheduling (date not verified).
outcome_analysis: Vitalize pivoted from a clinician wellness app into hospital staffing and scheduling, sold with forward deployed teams to named systems such as MemorialCare and Hendrick Health. It reached 28 people and a $31M Series A in October 2026, about three and a half years after the YC batch.

name: Vizly
tags: Privacy; Data Science; Data Visualization; AI
one_liner: Data to insights in seconds
long_description:
Vizly helps you get the most out of your data by turning it into actionable insights in seconds. Whether you're a researcher, professor, data analyst, or business leader, Vizly's AI capabilities enable you to visualize, analyze, and interpret your data effortlessly.

For example, Vizly can automatically generate interactive visualizations, perform detailed statistical analyses, and offer predictive insights, making your data analysis workflow seamless.

Before Vizly, Ali built out people-based AI recommendations at Apple and Sami built mission-critical data visualization systems at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Vocode
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; Open Source; Conversational AI
one_liner: Open source Voice AI
long_description:
Open source voice AI.

Check out our docs for more information: https://docs.vocode.dev
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and businesses building voice-based LLM applications, e.g. automated inbound and outbound phone calls
problem: Building real-time voice agents required stitching together speech recognition, LLMs and speech synthesis plus telephony by hand.

name: Warp
tags: B2B; HR Tech; Payroll; Operations; AI

long_description:
Warp is the AI-native employee management platform for high-growth companies. We run payroll, HR, compliance, benefits, and IT on a single platform for companies from 5 to 10,000 employees, using AI agents to complete the work that legacy systems leave to people.

We've raised $85M from Battery Ventures, Peak XV, Sound Ventures (Ashton Kutcher), Sapphire, A-Star, SV Angel, and Homebrew Capital.

Some of the fastest growing companies of today trust Warp to reduce HR and admin overhead so they build faster. We're proud to serve top startups like Serval, Bland, Greptile, Reducto, Corgi, Campfire, alongside our mid-size and enterprise customers.

We're humbled to have the backing of people who have built some of the most important companies of the last two decades: Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke, former Stripe COO Claire Hughes Johnson, Dropbox co-founders Drew Houston and Arash Ferdowsi, former Coinbase CTO Balaji Srinivasan, Eventbrite founder Kevin Hartz, former Cruise founder Kyle Vogt, and Replit founder Amjad Masad.

target_customer: High growth startups and mid-size companies from 5 to 10,000 employees
problem: Payroll, HR, compliance, benefits and IT admin are manual and built for HR admins rather than founders.
business_model: B2B SaaS per employee payroll and HR platform (pricing not verified)
product_category: AI native payroll and employee management platform
market_need_then: Warp argued that payroll tools were built for HR admins, not founders, and its CEO says payroll was the biggest time sink at his first company.
outcome_analysis: Warp started as payroll for YC startups in 2023 and broadened into an AI native employee management platform. It raised an $18M Series A in June 2025 and a $60M Series B in June 2026, reporting doubled ARR and growth from 15 to over 50 staff in six months.

Xeol enables enterprises and Fortune 500s to create a proactive EOL management program that directly contributes to better vulnerability management and lower cyber insurance.

name: Yuma AI
tags: Customer Support; AI; Conversational AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: The AI Support Agent for Ecommerce
long_description:
## What is Yuma AI?

Yuma is automating customer support by providing an AI Support Agent orchestration platform. Yuma provides autonomous AI agents dedicated to customer service and e-commerce.

We integrate directly with help desk software (Zendesk, Kustomer, Gorgias, etc.) and focus on helping large Shopify brands deal with their high volume of support requests.

Top merchants using Yuma can automate up to 80% of their support tickets fully autonomously.

## Why do Shopify merchants need Yuma?

There are thousands of large Shopify merchants around the world generating $10M+ a year. Most of them have taken over some niches and are great at what they do: selling their products.

But they all have one thing in common: they all hate customer support. It's a burden for them and a huge source of cost, as they receive hundreds of requests per day. Some of them have dozens of support agents on staff, usually offshore, and the overall quality is still often pretty poor while staff turnover remains high.

Those merchants have been promised automation for years but have always been disappointed by the outcome. As customers, we have all had to live through a terrible support automation experience before, so this is no secret, and everyone knows that the current state of the technology is quite bad.

## Yuma is solving this in a few ways:

Yuma isn't just another RAG chatbot. Our platform provides autonomous AI agents dedicated to support and ecommerce.

These agents are powered by knowledge, follow processes, and are managed by our in-house AI orchestration technology. This ensures safety, control, and quality at every step.

We believe that to truly automate customer support, we must develop a platform that mimics the actions of a human support agent. That's exactly what we've been doing.

Currently, our top merchants are automating 60% of their support tickets through Yuma. Yuma can fetch information from external services and take actions in other apps as needed to resolve each ticket.

We are laser-focused on building the best AI support agent platform and aim to achieve 80% true automation in the next few months.

## Fun Fact

Yuma got started by accident. This is my third YC startup after Socialcam (W12) and Triplebyte (S15). I released Yuma as a prototype for fun in mid-December 2022 and was overwhelmed with demo requests. That's when I knew I was onto something and had to turn this into a real company, once again.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Large Shopify merchants with high support ticket volume that use Gorgias, Zendesk or Kustomer
problem: Ecommerce brands spend heavily on offshore support staff with high turnover and poor quality, and earlier automation was disappointing.
business_model: Usage-based B2B SaaS, brands pay per ticket fully resolved
product_category: AI customer support agents for ecommerce
market_need_then: Company says merchants with $10M plus revenue hate support and had been promised automation for years; a prototype released in Dec 2022 drew a flood of demo requests.
outcome_analysis: Yuma began as a prototype on the Gorgias app store in late 2022 and joined YC W23. It reports 100 plus paying customers and over 1 million tickets resolved by October 2024 and 140 plus brands by 2026, with a team of 26. A $5M round was announced in October 2024 and a prior seed closed in spring 2023. The serial founder with two earlier YC companies, ChatGPT timing and a narrow Shopify wedge helped. Helpdesk incumbents adding their own AI is the main risk.

name: refine
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Web Development
one_liner: Open-source Retool for enterprise
long_description:
refine is an open-source, headless React framework for rapidly building enterprise web applications. It eliminates many repetitive tasks like

➡️ CRUD operations
➡️ State management
➡️ Routing
➡️ Authentication
➡️ Access Control
➡️ i18n

and saves days of development time.

So far, thousands of great projects have been built by 15,000+ monthly active refine developers. Use cases are ranging from admin panels, dashboards, and internal tools to B2B solutions and complex SaaS interfaces. 

refine is backed by a strong community featuring 16K GitHub stars ⭐️, 180+ contributors and 2,500 Discord members. 

Thanks to it's unique "Headless UI" approach, refine works with any custom design. It has also ready-made integrations with 4 most popular UI frameworks: Ant Design, Material UI, Chakra UI and Mantine. refine is totally backend agnostic and it can connect to 15+ backend services out-of-the-box, incl. custom REST & GraphQL API's.

With refine, developers always have 100% control over their projects as they build, style and deploy the way they like.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developer teams building internal tools, admin panels and B2B web apps in React, with an enterprise tier for companies needing SSO, access control and audit logging
problem: Building CRUD heavy internal apps repeats the same work on routing, auth, state and access control, and low-code tools like Retool lock teams into a hosted platform.
business_model: open-core: free open-source framework with paid enterprise and AI cloud features
product_category: open-source React framework for internal tools
founder_names: Civan Ozseyhan; Omer Aplak; Eren Erkalkan
market_need_then: Retool's growth to $82M ARR by end of 2022 showed heavy spend on internal tools, and some buyers wanted open-source and self-hosted options.
outcome_analysis: Refine built a large open-source community that gave it low cost distribution, then raised a $1M seed in 2022 and a $2.8M seed in May 2024 and pushed toward enterprise and AI products. Sacra notes converting free users to paid has been difficult, so monetization against Retool and Appsmith remained the open question.

name: rex.fit
tags: Hard Tech; Computer Vision; Consumer Health Services; Fitness; AI
one_liner: Automating nutrition tracking.
long_description: The DROP by Rex.Fit is an AI wearable camera that automates nutrition tracking using computer vision. It has garnered more than 93k USD in preorders (~450 units) since its launch last month. The nutrition estimation and recommendation tech behind the DROP is already integrated as an API for fitness chains, generating hundreds of thousands of dollars in yearly revenue for them. The DROP is built by brothers, sports nutritionists and computer vision engineers from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH Zurich).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers who want automated calorie and nutrition tracking, plus fitness chains that license the nutrition API

business_model: consumer hardware sales (The Drop wearable), consumer subscription for the Rex WhatsApp coach, and a B2B nutrition API
product_category: AI nutrition tracking wearable and coach

outcome_analysis: Rex.fit sells an AI nutrition wearable and a WhatsApp coach out of a two person team with press coverage and preorders, but no verified funding or shipping data was found. The photo calorie category became crowded, so durable advantage will depend on the hardware and the B2B API.

name: rift
one_liner: B2B lead routing made simple
long_description:
rift is B2B lead routing made simple.

Inbound workflows leak revenue at every step. Routing is manual. Calendar links are generic. No-shows go unrecovered. The handoff between form fill and booked meeting is where pipeline quietly dies.

rift fixes that. One system for the full inbound lifecycle:
> Capture. Custom web forms that collect and qualify leads in real time.
> Route. Instant validation, enrichment, and assignment to the right rep.
> Schedule. Top prospects get the best calendar slots, matched to real availability.
> Recover. No-shows and ghosted leads are automatically re-engaged.

rift is built by growth engineers who ran inbound at high-velocity B2B companies and got tired of watching pipeline fall through the cracks.

rift is the system we wished existed — opinionated, fast, and wired into the tools sales teams already use: HubSpot, Apollo, Google Calendar, Gmail, Slack, Zoom, Stripe, and more.

Backed by Y Combinator (W23) and Sequoia Capital.

never lose an inbound lead → rift.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: sizeless
tags: Computer Vision; Real Estate; Construction; AI
one_liner: The spatial AI to plan, build and maintain the world's infrastructure
long_description:
sizeless is the spatial AI to plan, build, and maintain the world's infrastructure by automating the 3D documentation and planning of the world’s underground infrastructure. Construction crews capture a short smartphone video of a construction site and get an automated, millimeter-precise digital twin with automatic part identification. We compress weeks of manual surveying and back-office planning work into hours. Our documentation and planning platform is currently in production: we have signed 7 paid pilots in 3 months with a potential ACV of $1.4M. 

sizeless (https://sizeless.co) spun out of research in robotics and spatial AI: co-founders Cornelius von Einem (PhD, ETH Zürich) and Roger de Belsunce (Physics & AI postdoc at MIT) lead the technology, while Julius Schilling (insurance, Aon) leads the commercial side. sizeless is building the proprietary training-data layer that all construction robots will run on.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

problem: Documenting underground infrastructure as built takes weeks of manual surveying and back-office planning.
business_model: B2B SaaS and per-project documentation, with paid pilots
product_category: spatial AI and construction 3D documentation
founder_names: Julius Schilling; Cornelius von Einem; Roger de Belsunce
market_need_then: Utilities and district heating builders need accurate as-built records, and the company reports seven paid pilots in three months with potential ACV of $1.4M, self reported.
outcome_analysis: sizeless focused on underground infrastructure documentation after earlier positioning that varied across directories, and reports paid pilots with German utilities and builders. No funding or independent traction data was found, so its stage beyond YC is unknown.

name: sudocode
one_liner: orchestrate your coding agents with sudocode
long_description:
sudocode automates the logistics of managing context windows and orchestrating agents so you can direct the work instead of babysitting agents.

Fully open-source. Try it at sudocode.ai or https://github.com/sudocode-ai/sudocode
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineers and small teams who run AI coding agents such as Claude Code and need durable context and task tracking
problem: Coding agents lose context between sessions and developers spend time babysitting them. sudocode keeps specs and issues as context inside the git repo and orchestrates agents against them.
business_model: Open source developer tool (Apache-2.0 per aggregator metadata); commercial model not stated in sources found
product_category: AI coding agent orchestration and context management
market_need_then: The YC description at the S23 batch is generic. The current product responds to the 2025 surge of coding agents, where context window management became a daily pain. No dated 2023 demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: sudocode is still active with a team of two and no verified funding history. The listed product is an open source context manager for coding agents, apparently built or relaunched in late 2025, long after the 2023 batch, which suggests an earlier idea was reworked, though no source states a pivot. Outcome is too early and too thinly documented to judge.

name: truemetrics
one_liner: We show couriers where to park and enter a building.
long_description:
truemetrics helps logistics companies to find their customer's faster. By detecting and mapping entrances, we help GLS, a key logistics company in Europe, save 32.7 seconds on each delivery.

The way couriers navigate is broken.

“You Have Arrived At Your Destination!” — or so Google Maps thinks. In reality, the way couriers navigate is broken: No parking, hard-to-find entrances, and labyrinth-like apartment and office complexes can turn the last meters of delivery into a time-consuming puzzle.

truemetrics provides parking positions and entrance locations to enable faster drop-offs. Our data is generated by analyzing sensor data from drivers' smartphones, allowing truemetrics to identify precise parking and entrance locations, thereby simplifying the last meters of delivery.
regions: Germany; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Logistics and parcel delivery companies (named customer GLS)
problem: Maps stop at the street address, so couriers lose time finding parking and building entrances.
business_model: B2B data/API licensing for parking and entrance locations derived from driver smartphone sensor data
product_category: Logistics geodata / last-meter delivery navigation
founder_names: Ingo Boegemann; Jan Bischof; David (surname not found)
market_need_then: Company reports saving GLS 32.7 seconds per delivery (self-reported); delivery cost pressure is the stated driver. No independent spend data retrieved.
outcome_analysis: truemetrics, a Berlin YC Summer 2023 company, announced a seed round in September 2023 with Pioneer Fund, Soma Capital, Rebel Fund and Hatcher+ and lists GLS as a customer, remaining Active with 5 people. Round size is unknown (an aggregator shows $500K total), and no later funding, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is unresolved.

name: withHuman
one_liner: The Approval Layer for AI Agents
long_description:
withHuman is an open source approval layer for AI Agents.

When you want agents to take consequential actions like refund a customer, that's when withHuman is useful.

It is a centralized point where you can encode rules like "refunds < $10 can be done automatically, anything more than that, send it to the on-call from customer support". You write your rules once and connect all of your agents, no changes needed, its transparent to the agent.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Teams deploying AI agents that take consequential actions such as refunds or payments and need human sign off
problem: Agents can take costly actions unchecked. withHuman holds tool calls, applies approval rules and routes hard cases to a human reviewer with an audit log.
business_model: Open core with a hosted version; core described as source available or open source
product_category: AI agent human approval layer
market_need_then: Agents taking real actions created need for approval gates; the founders say the approval step they built for their earlier AI SRE product became this concept (Dealroom).
outcome_analysis: withHuman is active and very young. The YC page shows Summer 2023 batch but a 2026 founding year, and the founder's earlier company Metoro appears in the S23 batch elsewhere, so the batch and company history are inconsistent. No verified funding or exit exists, so no outcome story can be drawn yet.

name: 1849 bio
tags: Hard Tech; Synthetic Biology; Biotech; Climate; Mining
one_liner: Engineering microbes for miners to unlock billions in trapped metal
long_description:
1849 bio designs microbes enabling cheap metal extraction allowing miners to unlock value from low quality copper and gold ores. Surprisingly, the mining industry is one of the largest scale users of biotech in the world with biomining processes accounting for ~1% of global copper production. Biomining is ultra-low cost, running around ~$1/ton of ore vs ~$7/ton for conventional processes. 

Unfortunately, while biomining is cheap, it can’t be applied to over 80% of copper ores, leaving vast resources without profitable extraction methods. An estimated ~$800B of copper sit today in waste materials and stockpiles with negative unit economics.

While a great deal of effort has been spent on optimizing microbial metal extraction processes, very little effort has been spent on optimizing the microbes themselves. 

To change that, we’re creating new biotech tools and platforms applied directly to the types of biology most relevant to miners. This enables us to develop new microbes and tackle some of the most difficult problems in biomining, unlocking billions in value from unprofitable resources while being more environmentally friendly than conventional processes.

We’re world class microbial engineers. We met while doing our PhDs in synthetic biology, where we spent our time applying and developing the most advanced bioengineering technologies to engineer living cells.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Copper and gold mining companies running heap or stockpile leaching on low-grade ores
problem: Conventional bioleaching cannot be applied to most copper ores such as chalcopyrite, so large volumes of copper in waste and stockpiles stay unrecoverable.
business_model: Ore-specific engineered microbe solutions deployed through pilots with miners (pricing not public)
product_category: Synthetic biology for mining and biomining
market_need_then: The company states biomining is about 1 percent of global copper output at roughly $1 per ton versus $7 per ton conventional, yet cannot be applied to over 80 percent of ores. These are company figures from the YC page.
outcome_analysis: 1849 bio is an early-stage Summer 2024 company with no public acquisition, shutdown or verified funding round found. Its edge rests on two MIT synthetic biology PhD founders applying engineered microbes to a well-defined mining pain, but real-world heap results are unproven in the sources and new biomining entrants appeared by 2026.

name: Abundant
one_liner: Agent simulation and RL for researchers
long_description:
Hello! 👋

We are a team of former ML engineers, founders, roboticists and ops leads who obsess about data and its impact on safe, reliable AI.

We specialize in creating environments and datasets for RL by leveraging our experience in simulation and model training.

By the numbers:
  • Powering 3 of the top 6 global AI labs and multiple Fortune 500 enterprises
  • Billions of training tokens generated each month, 2x month over month
  • Exclusive, global network of over 500 domain experts

We believe humans are inherently creative, and thrive by pushing the frontier.

We are working towards an abundant future--one where everyone has access to infinite intelligence, services and goods.

Based in San Francisco, CA. We enjoy good food and good company.

-- more info below --

Abundant is building the NVIDIA of training data. AI models rely on two fundamental ingredients: compute and data. NVIDIA, the leader in compute, has a peak market cap of $5T and generated $130B in revenue last year as the need for scaling compute has exploded. We believe the need to scale data is just beginning, as we move beyond SFT and human supervision to RL and Learning from Experience.

Our founding team consists of second-time founders, ML engineers and data leads from Waymo, Google, Meta and AWS. Our team has previously collaborated with DeepMind to classify hate speech in YouTube videos, trained SOTA models for self-driving, and scaled data pipelines with thousands of human annotators. Our pioneering work in human computation, synthetic data, imitation learning and RL give us a solid advantage in delivering results to our customers.

Why now? Training data is more important and more scarce than ever before. Scaling laws dictate that linear improvement in model performance demands an exponential increase in training data. But there is only one World Wide Web and most of it has already been trained on. The next advances will require new, diverse, and high-quality datasets, making training data more important and scarce than ever before.

What happens if we succeed? Abundant will be the core enabler for AGI and beyond. Most of the challenges in model training are already solved. What’s missing is the data necessary to move from general knowledge to domain expertise; from chatbots to agents; and from digital intelligence to physical AI. Ask any AI researcher or roboticist: the core bottleneck to progress is the availability of data, i.e. “abundant data”.

Abundant works with the most advanced AI labs and startups, as well as F500 enterprises.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and enterprises that train models with reinforcement learning
problem: Model improvement needs new high quality training data and simulated environments, and the web is largely exhausted.
business_model: Services and data sales: custom RL environments and datasets for AI labs (pricing not public)
product_category: AI training data and RL environments
founder_names: Jesse Hu; Meji Abidoye; Ke Huang
market_need_then: Company says training data is scarce and scaling laws demand more of it. Demand surged in 2025 per later coverage; the YC page claims three of the top six labs as customers.
outcome_analysis: Abundant is a Fall 2024 company listed active. It rode the RL environments wave that grew in 2025, and claims major lab customers, but no verified funding or outcome was found. Funding aggregators conflict, so its trajectory is unknown.

Adapted is an AI physical therapist for athletes. Tell it your injury history, your sport, and your goals - it builds a personalized program to rehab and prevent injuries, bulletproof your body, and improve mobility and flexibility. No generic exercises. Just training and prehab that actually adapts to you.

Available now on the iOS App Store.

name: Afternoon.co
one_liner: Bookkeeping, compliance and tax for founders
long_description:
Afternoon.co empowers founders to make better business decisions with real time financial metrics. We pair managed AI bookkeeping and tax services, to reduce administrative burden on founders. 

Accountants struggle serving 4 million+ of ecommerce brands & startups in the US, because of complexity in sales tax, multiple sales channels and inventory management. name: Agentic Labs
one_liner: AI system design tools for dev teams
long_description:
Agentic Labs is making software design and architecture less painful by building AI into the process. Today, developers have no shortage of tools for instantly creating chunks of code, but designing the systems that integrate this code is the hardest and most manual part of software engineering.

Our first product is Glide, an AI-first editor purpose-built for writing technical design docs. It connects to your codebase and saves your engineering team time on triage, planning, and implementation of complex code changes.

It launched Glide on Hacker News in March 2024 as a design doc editor, then its own site repositioned the product as a context engine for AI agents, which suggests a pivot toward the agent infrastructure wave. Funding is only visible through aggregators, so success or stall cannot be judged from the sources found.

name: Aidy
one_liner: Mobile app helping people better manage chronic health conditions
long_description:
Aidy is a mobile app that helps people live fuller lives with chronic health conditions, beginning with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn’s Disease and Ulcerative Colitis). Our app lets users easily log their symptoms, diet, and treatments, then uses clinical indices to track disease severity and trends over time. Aidy excels at identifying patterns between diet, treatment adherence, and symptoms, giving our users a much more comprehensive and up-to-date picture of their condition to supplement clinician care. 

Previously in our careers, both Max and Peter worked in health in different capacities. At the Rockefeller Foundation and the United States Senate, Max worked in public health policy and COVID-19 response, while Peter worked as an ML researcher for a number of biotech companies. After a lengthy “pivot hell” we decided to finally listen to a friend with IBD who insisted that there weren’t any decent apps to help people live with the disease. Pretty quickly, we discovered how LLMs and regular structured questionnaire responses could provide a level of patient empowerment not possible before for chronic diseases. From there, Aidy was (re)born!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: People with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, free to them; revenue is planned from health plans, employers and researchers per the company site.
problem: People with IBD lack a good way to log symptoms, diet and treatment and to see patterns over time to share with clinicians.
business_model: Free consumer app with planned B2B revenue from health plans, employers and researchers; the App Store lists in-app purchases
product_category: Digital health, chronic condition self-management app
founder_names: Max Williamson; Peter Crocker; Greg Miller
market_need_then: The founders say a friend with IBD insisted no decent apps existed. A review cited in search results found most IBD apps lacked clinician input and guideline coverage.
outcome_analysis: The company is active as a two to ten person team. After a long pivot period it settled on an IBD tracking app, launching under three names during 2025 before settling on Aidy in October 2025. No traction figures or verified funding were found, so the story is still early and cannot be classed as success or stall.

name: Alai
