long_description: Alai makes it easy and quick to create high quality presentations with AI. Our users bring in their context and get a great first draft with 4 options for each slide in minutes. Alai has a responsive canvas made up of high-level build blocks which makes it easy for both humans and AI to iterate together to get to a polished presentation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Professionals and teams who build presentations and branded content, paying via subscription.
problem: Making a polished presentation from raw context is slow; Alai produces a first draft with options per slide and keeps edits on brand.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription plus an API
product_category: AI presentation and design tool
market_need_then: Slide decks were a universal workplace task and several AI presentation startups raised rounds in 2023, showing buyer interest.
outcome_analysis: Alai is active with about five people, launched through the YC W24 batch, and shipped a 2.0 release in mid 2026 focused on brand-true slides. Funding is only seen on aggregators and the market has strong funded rivals, so the company is neither clearly stalled nor clearly succeeding on the sources found.

name: Alex
tags: SaaS; B2B; Recruiting; HR Tech; AI
one_liner: Alex is the AI recruiter for hiring great people.
long_description:
Alex interviews, screens, and schedules every candidate – over voice, video, and text – so talent teams hire more great people, faster, without adding TA headcount. The recruiter stays in control: every shortlist is approved by a human, and every relationship and offer is owned by the customer's team.

We're past 1M+ interviews, integrate with 33+ ATS platforms, and 96% of candidates prefer interviewing with Alex. We're revenue-generating, well-funded, backed by premier investors, and are focused on enterprise customers: selling to VPs of Talent Acquisition, CHROs, and CFOs at large employers who are rethinking how hiring gets done at scale.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Large employers: VPs of Talent Acquisition, CHROs and CFOs, plus staffing firms and high volume hirers.
problem: Screening and interviewing every applicant is slow and costly for recruiting teams, so most candidates never get a real interview.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS, likely per usage or per interview; pricing not found
product_category: AI recruiter and voice interviewer
market_need_then: Recruiters faced large applicant volumes, and the company says it reached over 1M interviews and 33+ ATS integrations. A 2025 Bloomberg piece described fast adoption of AI interviewers.
outcome_analysis: Alex rode the voice AI wave to $3M seed and a $17M Series A from Peak XV in September 2025, with about 30 people and large enterprise customers by 2026. The company claims over 1M interviews and strong candidate satisfaction. Risks are well funded rivals such as Paradox under Workday and rising legal scrutiny of AI hiring tools.

name: Alex
one_liner: The Cursor for Xcode
long_description:
Tired of switching tabs to cursor every time you're building your iOS app in Xcode?

Worry not!

Alex is a sidebar app that works directly with Xcode, and has the same Cmd+L, Cmd+K, and Apply Code commands as Cursor. And, it's super fast.

Check it out: https://alexcodes.app
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: iOS and macOS developers using Xcode (individual subscriptions)
problem: Xcode lacked Cursor-style AI chat and editing, forcing developers to switch tabs to another editor.
business_model: Subscription developer tool (pricing not verified)
product_category: AI coding assistant for Xcode
competitors_at_founding: GitHub Copilot for Xcode; Apple Swift Assist; Cursor
market_need_then: Cursor's popularity in 2024 and Swift Assist delays left iOS developers without comparable AI tooling inside Xcode.
outcome_analysis: Alex launched in Oct 2024 as a Cursor-style sidebar for Xcode and gained enough traction that OpenAI hired the team into Codex in Sept 2025, with the product closed to new downloads after Oct 1 2025. The exit was an acqui-hire rather than a priced acquisition, and Apple adding model support to Xcode in 2025 shows the wedge was exposed to the platform owner.

name: Aluna
one_liner: Data for biomedical AI
long_description: We work with health organizations, to build curated datasets and evals for health AI. Currently focused on Oncology.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Health AI and life science AI teams that need curated datasets and evals, currently in oncology.
problem: Biomedical AI models lack curated, expert-annotated data and standardized benchmarks, especially in oncology.
business_model: Data licensing and evaluation benchmarks sold to AI developers and health organizations
product_category: Biomedical AI data and evals
market_need_then: The company says foundation models in health need curated human data. Demand evidence near mid 2024 was not found in the sources opened.
outcome_analysis: Aluna is a three person team that went through YC in Summer 2024 and now sells datasets such as PathFoundry and Duplex plus an OncoBench benchmark still listed as coming soon. No funding, customers or traction were found publicly, so its trajectory cannot be judged. The same YC page carries a Fortress database orchestration launch whose relation to Aluna is unclear.

name: AminoAnalytica
one_liner: The AI scientist for always-on biodefense
long_description: We design point-of-care diagnostics for emerging biological threats - in days, not 12+ months.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Biodefense and public health buyers for diagnostics; later biopharma scientists for the Amina protein engineering agent.
problem: Point-of-care diagnostics for emerging biological threats take over a year to develop; the company aims to design them in days with AI.
business_model: Diagnostics development for biodefense buyers, later a software platform for protein engineering; pricing not found
product_category: Biotech and AI protein engineering, biodefense diagnostics
market_need_then: Biodefense diagnostics have government demand, with defense funding programs appearing in search results, but no direct demand evidence for this company was found.
outcome_analysis: The company is active in London with three people. It positions around AI-designed diagnostics and has launched Amina, an agent for protein engineering, which suggests a broadening toward a software product. No funding or traction was publicly verified, so the outcome cannot be judged.

name: Anara
one_liner: AI for researchers
long_description:
Anara is AI for scientific advancement. We help researchers find, understand and write scientific documents, together.

We started working on Anara two years ago. In that time:
- we’ve grown to 3M users spanning hundreds of major colleges and research-led companies,
- we are fast approaching $10M in yearly revenue,
- 600M+ people have seen our content across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube,
- and we raised $3M from YC and the founders of Github and Reddit.

We're a small, tight-knit team with huge ambitions. As a founding member, you'll be instrumental in helping us scale revenue from $10M to $100M and then $100M to $1B+.

If you’re excited by the idea of being a part of that, definitely reach out.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Students, academics and research-led companies (consumer and B2B subscriptions).
problem: Researchers struggle to find, understand and write scientific documents across hundreds of millions of papers and their own files.
business_model: Freemium subscription with team and API products
product_category: AI research assistant
market_need_then: The YC page claims 3M users across hundreds of colleges and research companies and approaching $10M in yearly revenue, all company claims.
outcome_analysis: Anara grew quickly through short social video distribution, reporting 3M users and nearing $10M in annual revenue according to its YC page, then rebranded from Unriddle in March 2025 and shipped Anara 3.0 in April 2026. The funding picture is thin and aggregator figures conflict, and the space is crowded, so the strength rests on distribution rather than a technical lead.

name: Andon Labs
one_liner: Autonomous organizations without humans in the loop
long_description:
Safety from humans in the loop is a mirage. We evaluate, research, and apply AI control in our own real-world deployments of autonomous organizations.

We are building the Safe Autonomous Organization. We iteratively launch and scale autonomous organizations, while bridging AI control research with real-world testing.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI labs and operators who want evals and real-world deployments of autonomous AI agents; later outside operators via the Pion platform waitlist.
problem: Safety of AI agents is hard to judge without testing them running real organizations with no human in the loop.
business_model: Research and evals, own deployments of AI-run businesses, and a planned platform (Pion) with revenue share according to press; not confirmed by the company site
product_category: AI safety research and autonomous organizations
market_need_then: At founding in 2023 the company argued that AI safety needs real-world testing; demand rose as labs sought long horizon agent evals, shown by Vending-Bench in February 2025 and Project Vend in June 2025.
outcome_analysis: Andon Labs turned a benchmark (Vending-Bench, published around February 2025) into a collaboration with Anthropic (Project Vend, June 2025) and then into real AI-run businesses, including a San Francisco store opened in April 2026 and a Stockholm café, with an 11 person team. Early store operations drew critical coverage about overstocking and staffing, and funding is only on aggregators, so commercial traction is unproven.

name: Andy AI
tags: SaaS; Health Tech; B2B; Healthcare; AI
one_liner: Faster clinical documentation for home health nurses
long_description:
Andy is AI software that completes documentation for nurses doing home visits. Our software saves $8B a year; Tiantian was previously a PM at Google’s healthcare business and Max was a staff engineer on the health team at Apple. 

Andy benefits nurses and the agencies that employ them. Agencies that use Andy see up to 45% more detailed charts, 2x greater nurse productivity, and timely submission (no more billing delays!) With Andy, clinicians get their evenings back. 

Home health is the fastest growing segment of healthcare, doubling to $251B by 2031. Combined with recent nursing shortages and burnout, we’re seeing not just urgency, but excitement and joy, around adopting AI for home health.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Home health agencies and the nurses and therapists they employ
problem: Home health clinicians spend roughly 90 minutes per visit on documentation, which causes burnout, billing delays and thin charts.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to home health agencies
product_category: Ambient AI scribe, quality assurance and coding for home health
market_need_then: Home health nursing shortages and burnout, heavy OASIS documentation burden and billing delays; the company cites a home health market growing to 251 billion dollars by 2031 (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Andy AI is active and selling to named home health agencies, with founders from Google health and Apple health. No verified round, acquisition or shutdown was found, so its trajectory cannot be judged. The wedge is real but crowded as the EHR vendor WellSky and funded startups entered ambient scribing from 2025.

name: Anglera
tags: Machine Learning; SaaS; B2B; E-commerce; AI
one_liner: AI-Powered Product Data Enrichment
long_description:
At Anglera, we're developing a suite of AI agents to help e-commerce companies run their operations more efficiently. Our flagship agent helps our customers onboard, enrich, and manage their product data, reducing time per product from 15 mins down to 5 seconds.

We previously developed ML to automatically enrich millions of products at Uber Eats, and we're now on a mission to automate the most common manual workflows for every e-commerce business.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: E-commerce retailers, distributors and brands with large product catalogs
problem: Onboarding and enriching product data by hand takes about 15 minutes per product and hurts search and discovery.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI product data enrichment
product_category: E-commerce product data and AI agents
market_need_then: Catalog data quality limits search and discovery and the founders had seen the problem at Uber Eats scale. Customer evidence beyond company claims was not found.
outcome_analysis: Anglera joined YC in Summer 2024 with founders who ran catalog AI at Uber Eats and pitched agents for product data enrichment. It reached SOC 2 and enterprise positioning and Coveo acquired it in October 2026 to add enrichment to commerce search, with existing customers staying on the Anglera platform. Terms were not disclosed.

name: Anthrogen
one_liner: We work on generalizable tools for the next era of biotech.
long_description:
Anthrogen is engineering post-modality biology.

Today's modalities reflect historical contingencies in biological progress, not fundamental categories. We develop the AI systems that design modular biological machines and the experimental infrastructure to instantiate them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Biotech and pharma teams that need new proteins and biologics (stated direction); earlier plan targeted chemical producers
problem: Biological design is limited by existing modalities and slow trial and error; Anthrogen trains large protein models on its own lab data to design programmable molecular tools.
business_model: AI research lab and platform for biologics discovery; commercial model not publicly stated
product_category: Protein foundation models and biology AI
founder_names: Ankit Singhal; Connor Lee; Vignesh Karthik
market_need_then: Rapid progress in protein language models in 2023 and 2024 (ESM3, AlphaFold lineage) created demand for generative biologics design; the company itself first pitched carbon capture microbes.
outcome_analysis: Anthrogen pivoted from a carbon capture microbe idea to protein foundation models and raised a 4 million dollar seed in November 2024, then published the 102 billion parameter Odyssey in October 2025. No later round or exit was found, so its outcome is open; it competes against far better funded protein model labs.

name: Apolink
one_liner: 24/7 satellite connectivity in low Earth orbit
long_description: Apolink is a next-generation data relay network designed to provide real-time, low-latency connectivity for satellites in low Earth orbit. By enabling efficient data aggregation and relay through our hybrid RF-optical inter-satellite link (ISL) architecture, we support scalable and resilient space infrastructure across commercial, federal, and defense applications.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Satellite operators in LEO across commercial, federal and defense markets
problem: LEO satellites can only downlink data when passing over sparse ground stations, causing long delays; Apolink plans an always-on relay in orbit.
business_model: Data relay as a service sold to satellite operators, also resold through partners
product_category: Space infrastructure, inter-satellite data relay
market_need_then: Growth in LEO satellite fleets and limited ground station coverage creating delays; the company claims 150 million dollars in customer commitments since 2024 per a January 2026 report (unverified summary).
outcome_analysis: Apolink raised a 4.3 million dollar seed at a reported 45 million dollar post-money in July 2025 and signed a relay reselling partnership with RBC Signals in January 2026, with a demo cubesat planned for 2026. The company is early and hardware dependent, so the outcome is open; it faces Kepler and the megaconstellations.

name: Apten
one_liner: Omnichannel AI agents that engage leads across SMS, voice, and email
long_description:
Apten is an omni-channel AI agent that engages and nurtures leads across text, call, email, and webchat. 

We help enterprises in consumer services convert more leads.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises in consumer services such as insurance, home services, healthcare and education enrollment that need to convert inbound leads
problem: Leads go cold because follow-up across text, calls and email is slow and inconsistent; Apten runs AI agents that reply across channels with shared memory.
business_model: B2B SaaS with a dedicated implementation team per customer
product_category: Omnichannel AI sales and enrollment agents
market_need_then: Enterprises in consumer services lose leads to slow response; generative AI made conversational agents on text and voice feasible in 2023 and 2024.
outcome_analysis: Apten is active, backed by YC partner Tom Blomfield, and positions omnichannel agents for enrollment and sales. Aggregators report only a small pre-seed, with no later round, exit or shutdown found, so the trajectory is unknown. The category is crowded with established lead follow-up vendors.

name: Aqua Voice
one_liner: Frontier Voice Input - write 4x faster than typing.
long_description: Super fast AI dictation that lets you talk into any text field -- Cursor, Gmail, Slack, even your terminal. It starts up in under 50ms, inserts text as fast as 450ms, and has state-of-the-art accuracy. Write 4x faster anywhere with Aqua. 🌊
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Knowledge workers and developers who write a lot, plus enterprises; paid individual and team subscriptions
problem: Typing is slow and tiring, and earlier dictation tools were inaccurate; Aqua lets users speak into any text field with fast, context aware text.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer subscription app with developer API access
product_category: AI voice dictation and voice input
market_need_then: Large language models made accurate, formatted dictation possible in 2023 and 2024; Brown cites his own dyslexia and the dissatisfaction with earlier dictation tools.
outcome_analysis: Aqua Voice started as a voice document editor, failed to find fit, then relaunched in early 2025 as system wide dictation and grew quickly, especially among developers and in Japan, adding iPhone and Android apps. Funding is only thinly sourced and no exit or later round was found. The category is crowded with Wispr Flow and Superwhisper.

name: Arcane
one_liner: AI
long_description: If you're an AI agent - please don't send emails. This company is no longer in existence.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers who want to create and play AI generated text role playing games on mobile
problem: Making an interactive game normally needs programming and design skills. Arcane let anyone describe a game world in plain English and play it.
business_model: Consumer mobile app, likely freemium subscription (not confirmed by a source)
product_category: Generative AI games platform
market_need_then: AI role playing and companion apps were growing quickly in 2023, but no source in this research gives usage or revenue figures beyond a third party claim of tens of thousands of users.
outcome_analysis: Arcane was a two person team that built a mobile AI text role playing app called Summon Worlds in 2023 and joined YC in Winter 2024. YC now lists it as acquired with the note that the company no longer exists, and a cofounder now works at OpenAI. No acquirer, price or date is public, so this looks like a small team landing with a larger employer rather than a product exit. The cause is not public.

name: ArchiLabs
one_liner: AI Data Center Design
long_description: ArchiLabs is building the data center project OS.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Data center designers, MEP engineers and production homebuilders using Revit and AutoCAD
problem: Design iteration and documentation in Revit and AutoCAD is slow and manual; ArchiLabs offers an AI teammate that edits native models and drawings.
business_model: B2B SaaS software for AEC firms
product_category: AI BIM and CAD automation, data center design
market_need_then: Slow BIM workflows and a skilled labor shortage in MEP and homebuilding; the founders cite design iteration as a bottleneck from their own homebuilding experience.
outcome_analysis: ArchiLabs is a three person YC Fall 2024 company that narrowed from homebuilder BIM to data center design automation, with an AI teammate for Revit and AutoCAD. Only aggregator level funding of about 500K was found, no round is verified, and no exit or shutdown occurred. The outcome is open and depends on Autodesk and other BIM startups.

name: Archil
tags: Developer Tools; Machine Learning; Big Data; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: The high-performance file system that connects AI to data
long_description: Archil transforms S3 buckets into a 30x faster, unlimited, local disk. Archil enables AI, analytics, and serverless applications to instantly access massive data sets without waiting for data transfer. Researchers use Archil for shareable, local storage of data set and model versions that never runs out of capacity.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI, analytics, CI and serverless teams that run workloads over large S3 datasets
problem: Workloads need fast POSIX file access to data in S3 without copying it; Archil exposes buckets as a fast, shared, unlimited disk and now sells sandboxes and durable disks for agents.
business_model: Usage-based cloud storage and compute infrastructure
product_category: Cloud file system and agent runtime, developer infrastructure
market_need_then: AI and analytics workloads store large datasets in S3 but need file semantics and speed; the pain was long standing (the company calls it a 20 year problem) and boosted by AI training and agents.
outcome_analysis: Archil, formerly Regatta Storage, raised a 6.7 million dollar seed led by Felicis in June 2025 and cites customers such as Clay, Gamma and Depot. A Series A of 11 million dollars is reported only on aggregators. The founder's EFS experience is a strong fit, though AWS shipped S3 Files in April 2026, pushing Archil toward agent infrastructure.

name: Aren
tags: Generative AI; Digital Health; Healthcare; AI
one_liner: Powering Successful Nursing Shifts
long_description: Empowering nurses to execute successful shifts, while illuminating their critical role in health system financial performance.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hospital and health system nursing departments, buying for inpatient nurses
problem: Nurses hand off patients with paper report sheets and verbal reports that waste time and lose information; Aren digitizes handoff, tasks and charting and links nursing work to financial performance.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to hospitals and health systems
product_category: Nursing workflow software, AI handoff and charting
competitors_at_founding: HCA Healthcare Nurse Handoff with Google Cloud
market_need_then: Nursing shortages and burnout and the cost of handoff errors; hospitals seeking AI to reduce paperwork, shown by HCA building its own handoff tool.
outcome_analysis: Aren, formerly Kabilah, is an active two founder Stanford team selling nurse handoff and shift software to hospitals, with Epic and Meditech integrations and advisors from health systems. Only a small seed of about 500K is reported by aggregators, no named customers or exit were found, so the outcome is unknown. Large systems such as HCA are building similar tools.

name: Ares Industries
one_liner: Building low-cost cruise missiles
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: US Department of Defense and allied militaries buying low-cost, mass-producible cruise missiles
problem: Existing anti-ship cruise missiles cost around $3 million each, which the founders argue is unaffordable at the volumes a conflict would need. Ares aims for missiles roughly 10x smaller and 10x cheaper.
business_model: Defense hardware sales of munitions to government customers
product_category: Defense, low-cost cruise missiles
market_need_then: In 2024 US officials and the founders pointed to missile stockpile shortages and the cost per round, with YC making its first weapons investment in this company (TechCrunch, Aug 2024).
outcome_analysis: Ares Industries is active as of the latest search with no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs found. It drew early attention as YC's first defense investment and flight tested prototypes in 2024, and its site now lists two products named Maverick and Goose. Public funding detail is thin, and no later round or program award was found, so the stage reached is unknown.

name: Argil
one_liner: The video generation engine for the creator economy
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Content creators, educators and businesses that want to publish talking head and short form video using an AI clone of themselves
problem: Producing regular video content is slow and expensive. Argil lets a user clone themselves from about two minutes of footage and generate edited videos from a script.
business_model: Subscription SaaS (Pro from 50 USD per month) plus enterprise custom pricing and an API
product_category: Generative AI video, avatar clones
market_need_then: Creator economy demand for fast video output and the 2023 to 2024 rise of generative video models, which the founders say made video accessible (YC launch post).
outcome_analysis: Argil is active and raised a combined 4.9 million euros across a 2023 pre-seed and a November 2024 seed led by EQT Ventures. It rode the generative video wave with founders who had earlier video and startup experience, and it sells to creators rather than enterprises. No later round, exit or distress was found, so its durability against model vendors and larger avatar platforms is still open.

name: Argon AI, Inc.
one_liner: AI for Pharma Intelligence
long_description:
Argon AI is a platform where biopharma and life sciences professionals can execute complex and data driven workflows using natural language. We help professionals get thorough answers to questions about clinical trials, existing treatments, healthcare landscape, and the competitive market in minutes rather than months. 

Prior to starting Argon, Samy was responsible for Flatiron Health’s (Roche) first data analytics project which eventually led to the start of the Flatiron Services business unit. There, he saw first-hand the heavily manual process that biopharma companies struggle through to get the insights they need to drive forward their drug development programs. He also helped close over $6M+ in ARR and is an expert in enterprise pharma sales.

Cyrus previously led engineering teams and built 0 to 1 across pre-seed and unicorn startups, managed mission-critical trade generation systems at Bridgewater, and held AI advisory roles at various startups. Cyrus has a duel degree in EE and CS from USC.

Breakthroughs in AI present an opportunity to reinvent biopharma and life science workflows to reduce the time and cost of bringing treatments to patients where delays in bringing a drug to market can cost a pharma company $3M / day.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Biopharma and life sciences teams and the consulting firms that serve them
problem: Answering questions about clinical trials, treatments and the competitive landscape takes analysts months. Argon offers a natural language workspace that returns answers in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS workspace sold to pharma enterprises and consultancies
product_category: AI workspace for pharma intelligence
market_need_then: The company site states that bringing a therapy to market can take 15 years and cost over 2 billion USD, and YC description cites about 3M USD per day of delay cost to pharma.
outcome_analysis: Argon AI is active and announced a 5.5 million USD seed on July 2, 2025, co-led by Crosslink Capital and Wireframe Ventures, roughly 16 months after the batch. The CEO's pharma enterprise sales background fits the buyer, and the company claims licensed analyst research as a data edge. No later round or exit was found.

name: Arini
tags: Health Tech; Dental; Call Center; AI
one_liner: The single platform to run all healthcare operations
long_description:
Arini is building the single platform to run all healthcare operations.

Healthcare has spent the last decade consolidating, but operations are still fragmented, manual, and expensive. A large group runs dozens of disconnected systems for scheduling, billing, insurance, payables, and reporting, with people moving data between them by phone, fax, and spreadsheet.


We partner with some of the largest healthcare enterprises in the country through a Forward Deployed Engineering model. Engineers sit with the customer, find their biggest operational problems, and ship systems that solve them end to end. The best of that work becomes the platform that scales across enterprises.

Our goal is to deliver the operating leverage healthcare consolidation has promised for decades, so providers can focus on patient care. We obsess over improving patient outcomes, and we are building the platform to run all operations for a $620B industry.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Dental service organizations and large healthcare groups
problem: Dental practices miss calls and run fragmented manual operations. Arini started as an AI phone receptionist and now positions as an operations platform delivered with forward deployed engineers.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus forward deployed engineering services for enterprise healthcare groups
product_category: AI voice agents and healthcare operations
market_need_then: Dental offices miss patient calls and depend on front desk staff for scheduling; the YC page describes answering calls and booking appointments around the clock.
outcome_analysis: Arini is active with 17 people listed and a stated expansion from a dental AI receptionist to a forward deployed engineering model for large healthcare groups. Profiles report about 15,000 patient calls handled per day. Funding is only visible on aggregators, so the capital behind its growth is unclear.

name: Artisan
tags: B2B; Sales; Automation; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: AI employees that take on real work, starting with sales
long_description:
Artisan builds AI employees, called Artisans, that take on real work and help teams accomplish more. Our mission is to build AI employees that can take responsibility for work across a broad range of roles and industries.

Our first three Artisans focus on sales:

Ava is our outbound AI BDR. She finds and researches prospects, runs personalized outreach, handles replies, and books meetings.

Aaron is our inbound AI SDR. He engages website visitors, answers questions, qualifies leads, and books meetings with the right person.

Aria is our AI account executive. She delivers personalized product demos, handles objections, and helps prospects take the next step.

These first three employees are the starting point for a much broader AI employee company. We're building toward a future in which businesses can delegate meaningful work to AI employees across their organizations, with people setting direction and collaborating where their judgment matters.

We're a small team with offices in San Francisco and New York. We value technical ambition, fast iteration, and taking responsibility for results. We're hiring people who want to help build the next generation of AI employees.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B companies that want to automate outbound and inbound sales prospecting
problem: Sales teams spend heavy effort on prospect research, outreach and qualification. Artisan sells AI employees, starting with Ava the outbound BDR.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI employee agents
product_category: AI sales agents (AI BDR, SDR, AE)
market_need_then: Outbound sales is labor intensive and generative AI in 2023 to 2024 made automated outreach feasible; the company reports 250 customers and 5M USD ARR by April 2025 (TechCrunch).
outcome_analysis: Artisan is active and the best funded of this shard, with a 7.3M USD seed in May 2024, a further seed near 11.5M USD in September 2024 and a 25M USD Series A in April 2025 led by Glade Brook Capital. Its provocative billboard campaign produced outsized awareness while the product matured after early hallucination problems. Rivals in AI SDR are numerous, so durability depends on product reliability.

name: Artos
one_liner: Authoring documents for life sciences in minutes, not months.
long_description: Artos is an AI-based document-drafting platform that helps life sciences companies turn their data into critical documents in minutes. These submissions currently take months and are the final hurdle before life sciences companies are allowed to sell their product.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharma, biotech, CROs and medical writing firms preparing regulatory submissions
problem: Regulatory submission documents such as INDs and clinical study reports take months to write and are the last hurdle before sale. Artos drafts them from company data in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for regulatory document authoring
product_category: AI regulatory and medical writing
market_need_then: Regulatory documents are slow to author and gate market entry, per the company description; the company reports users among large pharma, which is self-described and unverified.
outcome_analysis: Artos is active with a seven person team and a niche focus on life sciences regulatory documents, with conference presence through 2025. Public funding information is limited to aggregator pre-seed entries, so there is no verified evidence of a priced round. The market has several funded competitors and large pharma in house builds.

name: Arva AI
one_liner: AI for critical banking operations
long_description: Arva AI is a Google backed research company deploying AI Agents for critical banking operations with industry-leading accuracy, from financial crime compliance to lending. Combining proprietary models with adaptive decisioning infrastructure, Arva enables large banks and financial institutions to automate high-risk decisions with greater consistency, effectiveness and control. Always hiring.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Banks, credit unions, fintechs and crypto firms running financial crime compliance and lending decisions
problem: Banks run slow, manual KYB, AML and enhanced due diligence reviews. Arva deploys AI agents to automate high risk decisions with auditability.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS for banking operations agents
product_category: AI agents for financial crime compliance and banking operations
market_need_then: Financial crime reviews are labor heavy for banks; the company cites named customers such as Ionia and OakNorth Bank and claims up to 92 percent of reviews can be automated (vendor claim).
outcome_analysis: Arva AI is active with 20 people and a 3 million USD seed in January 2025 led by Google's Gradient. name: Assembly HOA

Assembly is an AI-native HOA management company on a mission to fix homeowner associations. Traditional HOA management is often reactive, confusing, and inefficient. Assembly takes a different approach by combining professional expertise with intelligent software to make communities run smoothly and decisions easier.

We exist to build trust, create transparency, and ensure well-run communities that protect and enhance property values.

Assembly simplifies day-to-day operations, automates routine tasks, and delivers the right knowledge at the right time. Our platform gives boards and homeowners clarity to make smarter, more confident decisions. 

We manage HOAs in San Francisco Bay Area and Greater Los Angeles.

name: Astro Mechanica

long_description: Astro Mechanica is reinventing supersonic aircraft by innovating on engine, airframe, and systems that industry hasn’t in over 50 years. Our electric combined cycle engine, Duality, is the world’s first jet engine that's engineered for efficiency from takeoff to Mach 3+. This new propulsion technology enables the delivery of people and payloads anywhere on Earth in just hours, laying the foundation for a new operational paradigm: an affordable point-to-point global travel network that will make on-demand, high-speed air transport the new standard of travel.

name: AutoPallet Robotics
tags: Hard Tech; Machine Learning; Warehouse Management Tech; Swarm Robotics; Automation
one_liner: We make robots that move boxes in warehouses
long_description:
We’re building the next generation of warehouse robotics.

In the US today, retailers spend approximately $10B per year paying human laborers to pick up and move cardboard boxes in warehouses. Existing solutions for automating this are expensive and difficult to install, which is why manual operation is still so prevalent.

Our solution is different. We make swarms of small mobile robots that install into existing warehouses to provide a low-cost and robust automation solution for case picking and mixed-SKU palletization. Our novel technology allows these robots to be installed and operate at significantly lower cost than existing solutions while being both flexible and robust.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Retailers, 3PLs and grocery or foodservice distributors running distribution centers that move cases between pallets by hand
problem: Manual case picking and mixed SKU palletizing costs US retailers about $10B a year in labor, and existing automation costs too much and is hard to install in existing warehouses.
business_model: Hardware robot swarm sold or leased to warehouses as a retrofit, design partner pilots first
product_category: Warehouse robotics, case picking and palletizing

outcome_analysis: AutoPallet is an early stage Active company that joined YC in Summer 2024 with a six person team and a differentiated robot architecture aimed at a very large manual labor pool. No exit or shutdown is reported, and public funding information is thin, so the outcome is still open. The main risks are hardware reliability at scale, long warehouse sales cycles, and well funded palletizing vendors.

name: Autumn Labs

name: AveryIQ

Avery helps property managers fill vacancies faster and resolve maintenance requests automatically. Our AI property manager and leasing agents can be assigned to complete many common tasks, from getting tours scheduled to following up with vendors.  

There are nearly 300,000 third party property management companies across the US, many of whom are overwhelmed by dozens of repetitive tenant requests streaming in through antiquated software every day. Avery modernizes the property manager’s toolkit with a two-way contact center to provide an excellent resident experience.

Learn more at https://averyiq.com

name: Avora

long_description: Avora helps dental groups (DSOs) boost case acceptance and institutionalize clinical excellence. We deploy agents that listen to appointments, identify coachable moments, and chart notes to save provider time.

name: Azalea Robotics Corporation
one_liner: Automating airport baggage handling with robots.
long_description:
Azalea Robotics automates airport baggage handling with intelligent robot operations. The global market for airport baggage handling systems is $20+ billion and growing, presenting a significant opportunity for innovation and market disruption in this sector.


Passenger air traffic volume is increasing, driving demand for efficient and reliable baggage handling at airports and putting immense pressure on existing infrastructure. In 2023 alone, airports processed approximately 4.5 billion bags, highlighting the need for advanced solutions to manage this load effectively. Azalea Robotics provides state-of-the-art robotic systems that enhance efficiency, reduce mishandling, and improve passenger experience through more reliable operations.


Baggage handling is a critical component of airline ground operations, yet it is fraught with challenges. The work is physically demanding, often leading to long-term injuries among workers. Traditional baggage handling involves repetitive lifting and maneuvering of heavy loads, which can result in long-term health issues. Azalea Robotics addresses these challenges by automating the most strenuous tasks, thereby reducing the risk of injury and enhancing operational efficiency.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Airlines, ground handlers and airports that run bag rooms and load ULDs and bag carts
problem: Loading and unloading airport baggage is physically punishing manual work that causes injuries and mishandled bags, while passenger volumes keep rising.
business_model: Robotic hardware and fleet software sold or leased to airport and airline baggage operations
product_category: Industrial robotics, airport baggage handling automation
market_need_then: The company cites about 4.5 billion bags processed in 2023 and a $20B plus baggage handling systems market; the work is repetitive lifting that causes long term worker injury.
outcome_analysis: Azalea is active and early. It raised a reported 3.5 million dollar seed in April 2025 after YC S24, launched the ARC 1 cobot and began commercial deployments in late 2025 per aggregator reports. Founder market fit is strong because one founder is a manipulation roboticist and the other worked in airline operations. Later suction based peers such as Journey Robotics and Cobot Lift show a contested but real market.

name: Basalt
one_liner: Constellations as a Service
long_description:
Basalt is building Constellations as a Service, self-flying satellite constellations tailored for private enterprise and the government without any prior aerospace experience needed! Powered by our Diamond AI, Basalt provides a seamless experience, enabling users to fly and stream data and images from their own dedicated satellite constellation onto their phones and laptops.  

Basalt received its seed investment as part of the Y Combinator W24 batch, and has since launched Spirit-EEL, the world's first AI-controlled satellite constellation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Private enterprises and government agencies that want dedicated satellite constellations without aerospace expertise
problem: Operating satellites needs large teams of human operators and bespoke flight software for each spacecraft, which blocks non aerospace customers.
business_model: Constellations as a Service: satellite operating software (Dispatch) plus AI operations, sold as a managed service
product_category: Space software and autonomous satellite operations
market_need_then: Satellite operations were labor heavy and hardware specific; the company argued software defined operations would open space to non specialists. A 2026 article called AI replacing operators essential but unproven.
outcome_analysis: Basalt is active. It raised a 3.5 million dollar seed led by Initialized in May 2024 and has been flying its Spirit-EEL demo CubeSats, with one launched on a Falcon 9 rideshare in May 2026 per tracking sources. Founders with SpaceX and Aerospace Corporation experience and strong seed backers helped, but the central claim of autonomous operations remained unproven and no later round was found.

name: Baseline AI

We use AI to automate the process of creating everything from the protocol, saving not only spend on headcount but also months of time which can translate to up to $27M in direct costs + lost revenue saved for a single phase 3 trial.

The claims AI field drew several funded rivals in 2024 and 2025.

name: Bayesline
one_liner: Highly customizable and blazingly fast analytics for asset managers.
long_description:
Bayesline is building a GPU-powered financial analytics suite for institutional investors, like hedge funds. 

Clients use our cloud deployed solution to build custom analytics in seconds, having previously been frustrated with off the shelf solutions that don't generate any alpha. What used to take weeks or months now happens near instantly. 

Sebastian, CFA (ex Bloomberg Quant & AI Research) and Misha, PhD (ex BlackRock Managing Director) met while working at BlackRock in 2016. With a combined 20 years of experience in the space they set out to change the way the industry uses analytics - from one size doesn't fit all to truly tailored to clients' needs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hedge funds and institutional asset managers that use equity factor risk models
problem: Incumbent risk-model vendors' toolkits are slow and rigid (called 20-year-old by the founders); Bayesline fits custom equity factor risk models in seconds on GPUs, deployed in the client's cloud.
business_model: B2B enterprise software for asset managers (pricing not published; demo request only)
product_category: Portfolio risk and attribution analytics
market_need_then: Founders cite slow, rigid vendor toolkits; no spend or customer data sourced. MSCI's own brochure advertises custom factor attribution, indicating demand for customization.
outcome_analysis: Bayesline is an active two-to-three person YC S24 company led by former BlackRock Aladdin and Bloomberg quants selling faster, customizable equity factor risk models to asset managers. It is too early for an outcome: no verified funding, customers or revenue were found, and incumbents MSCI and SimCorp already sell customizable models.

name: BeeBettor
one_liner: Robinhood for sports prediction markets
long_description: BeeBettor makes sports betting simple. Currently, sports bettors download more than 40 sports betting apps to get the full experience. At each one, they must go through a long KYC process. BeeBettor aggregates all these accounts into one app and automatically gives sports bettors the best price.

product_category: Sports betting aggregation, +EV betting platform

name: Beglaubigt.de

- Beglaubigt.de: Germany's leading platform to found, register and manage a company. GmbH/UG formations in ~7 days instead of 6-8 weeks.
- firma.de: the operating system for running a company - accounting, tax, business address and ongoing compliance.
- Registercheck.de: real-time Handelsregister data via API. Every company, every change.

Through Germany's first fully automated incorporation API, partners like Qonto and Sevdesk embed company formation directly into their products. 30,000+ customers served so far.

target_customer: Founders of German companies, fintech and accounting partners (Qonto, Sevdesk) embedding company formation, and businesses needing register data
problem: Founding a GmbH or UG in Germany takes weeks of notary and register paperwork.

It closed a 3.3 million dollar seed in April 2026, then bought firma.de out of insolvency in June 2026 and agreed to buy registercheck.de in September 2026, funded from its own cash. Partner distribution and experienced founders explain the traction; there is no exit.

name: Benchify

name: Biblo

name: Bilanc

name: Biocartesian

name: BiteSight

name: Blacksmith
one_liner: The fastest way to run your GitHub Actions
long_description:
Blacksmith helps companies run their continuous integration (CI) up to twice as fast, at half the cost. We do this by running their CI on high performance gaming CPUs.

- Engineering productivity is often marred by slow CI that grows quadratically with the size of the engineering organization.
- On top of this, companies pay high markups to run CI on the hyperscalers.
- Consequently, companies have to run their CI on spot instances to keep costs in check. Since spot instances can get pre-empted at any point, running CI reliably on them requires [significant engineering investment](https://www.rippling.com/blog/how-rippling-used-spot-instances-to-save-and-scale-ci-cd).

Blacksmith offers CI compute that is more performant, cheaper, and reliable. With Blacksmith, companies do not have to think about CI as they scale.

We are starting with GitHub Actions - today's most popular and fastest-growing CI system. With a one-line change, companies can run their CI up to twice as fast on our high-performance hardware. In addition to this, Blacksmith provides colocated warm caches along with optimizations for common CI workloads (like building and pushing Docker images).

Aayush, JP and Aditya have gained deep systems and product knowledge from their time at Cockroach Labs and Faire respectively. Both these companies, with several hundred engineers, were spending in the order of millions of dollars on their CI. Yet they were riddled with slow CI and actively seeking out cheaper and faster alternatives. Blacksmith offers exactly this alternative, at a time where being lean is table-stakes for most companies.

long_description:
Bucket Robotics builds deployable computer vision systems for manufacturing — without labeling, long pilots, or fragile rules.
We turn CAD and sample data into production-ready vision models that run on existing cameras and edge hardware. No manual labeling. No cold-start problem. Models deploy in minutes and adapt as parts, defects, and lines change.

Our roots are in self-driving cars (Argo AI, Uber ATG, Stack AV), where we learned how to ship perception systems that operators trust in messy, real-world environments. We’re applying that playbook to factories: robust sensing, fast iteration, and tooling engineers actually enjoy using.

Manufacturers struggle with inspection because parts are too variable for rules-based vision and too expensive to inspect by hand. Legacy systems are rigid, hardware-locked, and slow to customize. We take the opposite approach: software-first vision that fits into existing automation and scales across SKUs, facilities, and workflows.

American Manufacturing is in the middle of a $700B automation push — but quality is still a trust problem. Bucket Robotics is building the vision infrastructure that lets factories automate inspection with confidence.

name: CTGT
one_liner: The deterministic layer for frontier intelligence
long_description:
CTGT is an applied AI research laboratory fundamentally solving the alignment and reliability bottleneck for enterprise AI.

For enterprises, especially highly regulated industries, deploying Generative AI is historically a compromise between capability and catastrophic risk. Standard enterprise approaches, such as RAG, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering, operate at the wrong abstraction layer. They are inherently probabilistic, carry massive engineering overhead, and fail to deliver the mathematical certainty required by the Fortune 500.

We focus on the science of representation engineering and have productized mechanistic interpretability. By opening the "black box" of neural networks, CTGT has developed a proprietary architecture that intervenes directly at the model's representation layer. We convert complex corporate SOPs, SEC/FINRA regulations, and strict editorial rulebooks into machine-readable "Policy as Code," enforcing deterministic constraints and defensible audit trails without requiring expensive model retraining.

The result is a step-function breakthrough in enterprise AI economics and capability. Our fundamental architecture allows organizations to run secure, self-hosted open-source models that mathematically match the reasoning and performance of frontier models. Benchmarks from our enterprise deployments demonstrate a 96.5% prevention of hallucinations, up to a 3.3× accuracy multiplier in complex domain-specific tasks, and an 80-90% reduction in human-in-the-loop manual review.

Backed by an $8M seed round from Gradient Ventures (Google), General Catalyst, and Y Combinator, CTGT is currently deployed with Fortune 500 companies, including Tier-1 financial institutions and global media conglomerates, giving them the deterministic control necessary to deploy enterprise AI with zero margin for error.

business_model: Enterprise software and platform licensing with self hosted open source models; pricing not public
product_category: AI reliability and interpretability, policy engine for LLMs
market_need_then: Regulated enterprises were slowed in deploying generative AI by hallucination and compliance risk; TechCrunch covered CTGT at Disrupt in October 2024 on making models safer.
outcome_analysis: CTGT raised a 7.2M dollar seed in early 2025 led by Gradient Ventures after YC Fall 2024 and a Disrupt appearance, and claims Fortune 500 deployments. Strength comes from research depth and the compliance wedge; risks are model labs adding native controls and long enterprise sales cycles. No exit or distress was found.

name: Carma
one_liner: The agentic workspace that runs construction operations for profit
long_description:
Carma is the agentic workspace that runs construction operations for profit.

Our customers are the $100M+ contractors building America’s data centers.

The AGI race is a construction race. More than 40% of America’s 2026 data centers are late, and every month of delay is a gift to the CCP. They’re late because contractors still coordinate every jobsite by phone and spreadsheet.

Contractors sell their work at fixed prices, so every hour a crew waits comes out of their margin. One broken machine stops every crew behind it, and the repair invoice shows only a fraction of the cost. The rest lands in idle crews and higher bids on the next job.

Adam, our AI operator, runs equipment operations for the whole company’s profit. He prices every idle hour, picks the repair with the lowest total cost, audits every bill before it’s paid, reallocates idle machines to the jobs that need them, and tells the company which machines to buy, repair, or sell. Managers approve every cost and Adam handles the coordination in between.

In three months, Adam increased operating profit by $4.21M a year for a $500M electrical contracting customer: a 12% increase. Across customers, the time people spend coordinating each repair fell 93%, and equipment downtime fell 30%.

We crossed $2M ARR three months after our first invoice, with five enterprise customers and a five-person team. Customers pay annually upfront, so we’re cash-flow positive. Carma sells no parts, rentals, or machines, so Adam’s only incentive is our customer’s profit.

Whoever builds faster wins. We will make sure it’s America.
