name: Gecko Security
one_liner: Security that understands your company
long_description: We built Gecko for teams that want to build secure code quickly without wasting time on security tools that don’t deliver results, or relying on one-time human pentests that quickly become outdated. Gecko uses AI to understand how your application should work, simulates relevant attacks to find critical vulnerabilities, and then verifies these vulnerabilities by exploiting them. It also helps you understand the risk of these vulnerabilities and applies a working fix to keep your code secure.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering and security teams at software companies (named customers include Cal.com, Guardant Health, b.well, Avora)
problem: Traditional static analysis produces many false positives and misses business logic and multi-step flaws, while pentests are one-time. Gecko models how an app should work, verifies exploits and proposes fixes.
business_model: B2B SaaS, AI-native SAST and code security platform sold to engineering and security teams
product_category: AI application security (SAST)
market_need_then: Static analysis tools are criticised for false positives and missed logic flaws, and AI coding increases code volume to review. No dated source near the batch was found; evidence is the founders' own launch claims.
outcome_analysis: Gecko Security is a two person London security startup from Fall 2024 YC that builds AI-native static analysis and claims 30+ CVEs found in open source projects. It lists recognizable customers and a seed round from YC and several funds, but the amount is not stated by the company. No exit or distress was found, and larger security vendors compete for the same wedge.

name: General Learning
one_liner: AI tutors for students.
long_description:
General Learning builds AI-powered learning platforms for the world's major curricula.

RevisionDojo, the AI study platform for the IB; OnePrep, the premier AI platform for SAT, ACT, and AP; and MathsGenie, the leading AI platform for GCSE and A-level.

Each brand houses pre-loaded question sets, study notes, mini-lessons guided by an AI tutor that adapts to each student individually.
regions: Hong Kong; East Asia
target_customer: Secondary school students and teachers preparing for IB, SAT, ACT, AP, GCSE and A-level exams, paying as consumers, with school adoption following
problem: Students lack affordable, curriculum-specific practice and feedback; the company positions its AI platforms as an alternative to human tutors and to general chatbots.
business_model: B2C subscriptions for exam prep platforms (RevisionDojo, OnePrep, MathsGenie) with growing school and teacher use
product_category: AI exam preparation and tutoring platforms
founder_names: Bowen Liu; Janet Liu; Michael Tong
market_need_then: StudyDojo's launch post reported 2,000+ paying customers, mid-six-figure ARR, an NPS above 75 and customers in 180 countries (company claims), showing demand for exam prep among students.
outcome_analysis: General Learning grew from the StudyDojo and RevisionDojo IB study platform into a multi-brand AI exam prep company. Its YC launch reported paying customers, mid-six-figure ARR and fast weekly growth, and it now runs about 35 people across three platforms. Funding is not confirmed by a primary source, and it is active with no exit, so the long-term outcome is open.

name: GetCrux
one_liner: AI Creative Strategist
long_description:
GetCrux is the AI Creative Strategist to launch winning ads.

Creatives have become the biggest lever to win on ad platforms. Yet, there is no clear way to figure out why something works. Marketers end up guessing and replicating the best performing ad, only to see it fail - with high CAC & wasted dollars.

GetCrux helps performance marketers find winning patterns in their ad creatives across 100+ parameters like hooks, messaging, storyline, music, pacing, and recommend exactly what to launch next.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Performance marketers and creative teams at paid social advertisers, including B2B SaaS and consumer app companies, who pay for creative analytics and ad generation
problem: Marketers cannot tell why one ad creative works and another fails, so they copy top ads, see them fail, and waste ad spend with high customer acquisition cost.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an AI creative strategist and ad creative platform
product_category: AI ad creative analytics and generation
founder_names: Himank Jain; Atharva Padhye; Prabhat Singh
market_need_then: Creatives were widely described as the biggest lever on paid social after targeting automation, and the company's own pitch cites wasted spend from guessing which creative elements work. No independent demand data was opened.
outcome_analysis: GetCrux is active and raised a 2.6 million dollar seed in February 2024 around its YC Winter 2024 batch, with IIT Bombay founders and a team of about 9. Its own site lists named customers and four AI agents, which suggests early traction, but no revenue figures were found. It faces crowded creative analytics rivals and ad platforms building the same features, so durability depends on execution speed.

name: Getcho
tags: SaaS; Delivery; Logistics; E-commerce; Retail Tech
one_liner: The reliability platform for last-mile delivery
long_description:
Getcho is a local delivery platform for high-value goods. 

We are building a high-reliability delivery network on top of high-volume, unreliable fleets, just like how TCP builds reliable end-to-end networking on top of an unreliable base network (IP).
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Retailers, brands and 3PLs, especially Shopify merchants, who need same-day delivery and reliable shipping for high-value goods
problem: Gig courier fleets such as Uber Direct and DoorDash Drive are cheap but unreliable, and merchants lack tracking, proof of delivery checks and claims handling on top of them.
business_model: Usage-based per delivery fees plus subscriptions, with a free plan
product_category: Last-mile delivery orchestration
founder_names: Jack Considine; Mike Considine; Evandro Nadal
market_need_then: Retailers wanted same-day delivery but found gig fleets unreliable for high-value goods. Evidence is the company's own pitch and customer quotes on its site, such as on-time rate claims, which are unverified.
outcome_analysis: Getcho is active in the Fall 2024 batch with a team of 3 and named retail customers such as Eataly and Janovic, plus Shopify certification and a claimed 58 city same-day footprint. No funding amount is public, and the thin defensibility on top of rented courier networks is the main risk. Too early to call an outcome.

name: Givefront
one_liner: Nonprofit Financial Management
long_description:
The world’s most important organizations deserve the world’s best financial infrastructure. We’re here to make sure they do.

At Givefront, we've built a modern financial management platform designed specifically for nonprofits. With real-time budgeting, built-in compliance, and easy integrations, we replace the spreadsheets and guesswork with smart, automated systems.

By transforming financial operations from reactive to real-time, Givefront empowers nonprofits to control every dollar, protect every grant, and move their missions forward faster — with greater efficiency, transparency, and trust.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and mid-size nonprofits, churches, foundations and HOAs that pay for spend management cards and financial tools
problem: Nonprofits lack cards and spend tools built for grants and compliance, and they struggle with personal credit checks, receipts and manual reporting.
business_model: Fintech spend management with card interchange and software fees
product_category: Nonprofit spend management and financial management
market_need_then: Nonprofits often cannot get cards without personal guarantees and rely on spreadsheets. Demand evidence is the company's traction claims: hundreds of organizations onboarded within about six months of card launch and over 200 percent monthly growth, per TechCrunch in Dec 2025.
outcome_analysis: Givefront went through YC Winter 2024 as a six-person team and raised a 2 million dollar seed led by Script Capital in December 2025 after launching cards. Company stated traction of hundreds of organizations and fast monthly growth suggests early fit in a niche that larger spend platforms underserve. Risks are interchange margin dependence and Ramp or Brex moving down market.

name: Glasskube
one_liner: Ship self-hosted software with Distr
long_description:
Managing enterprise software deployments shouldn’t feel like a balancing act. At Glasskube, we make deploying, managing, and updating software in on-premises, VPC, and air-gapped environments easier than ever.

Our Mission:
We empower software vendors to deliver exceptional customer experiences with less complexity. Whether you’re onboarding new clients, rolling out updates, or troubleshooting issues, our Software Distribution Platform streamlines every step.

The founders have been best friends for over 15 years, lived together in college, and even had a startup together. Philip was the CTO of a European Kubernetes-based company that was acquired in 2022.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software vendors (ISVs) that must deploy and update their product in customers' on-prem, VPC, BYOC and air-gapped environments
problem: Vendors shipping self-hosted software struggle to deploy, update and support it inside customer environments.
business_model: Open source core (Distr) with a commercial software distribution platform
product_category: Developer tools, software distribution for self-hosted software
market_need_then: Kubernetes users reported pain points with Helm, per the founders' launch posts. Later the company reported 200 plus organizations and 1,200 plus GitHub stars for Distr, its own claims.
outcome_analysis: Glasskube launched an open source Kubernetes package manager in early 2024, joined YC Summer 2024, then repositioned to Distr, a software distribution platform for vendors shipping on-prem. Open source traction is claimed with 200 plus organizations and 1,200 plus stars, but no verified funding was found and the open source license limits defensibility. The pivot suggests the package manager alone did not find a paying market.

name: Glimmer
one_liner: AI search for massive PDFs
long_description:
Glimmer is a new way to search massive PDFs using AI.

If you've ever dealt with massive PDFs (i.e. over 1,000 pages), you know how broken search can be. You have no choice but to use “Cmd-F” and manually sift through thousands of search results to find specific information. Professionals in construction, law, finance, and healthcare spend hours doing this every day.


Glimmer makes searching these large documents 10x easier. 


When you upload a PDF, Glimmer uses AI to intelligently index your documents. You can then search your PDF in natural language and get answers with verifiable page sources.


You can get started with Glimmer for free with any kind of PDF at withglimmer.com.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: GloGlo

Our mission: eradicate type 1 diabetes.

We are developing AI research agents that continuously analyze scientific literature and biological datasets, generate and challenge hypotheses, design experiments, and run them in a wet lab to learn from experimental results.
We are building a tight "in silico <> in vitro/vivo" feedback loop that helps us identify better targets, run experiments more efficiently, and move faster toward therapies for type 1 diabetes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

business_model: Consumer product subscriptions for gummies; therapeutics R&D with no revenue model yet
product_category: Consumer health brand turned AI-driven drug discovery
market_need_then: Type 1 diabetics need fast glucose and tablets are widely disliked, per diabetes community pages in search results, not opened. One source says Michael Fester is a type 1 diabetic.

name: GovernGPT

For money managers to raise their next billion, they dedicate entire teams to spend days filling diligence questionnaires with recycled content. We do it in minutes using AI.

This approach enables a new class of treatments with the potential to transform diseases ranging from cancer to autoimmunity.

name: Greenboard
one_liner: Modern OS for the financial back office.
long_description:
At Greenboard, we're building the future of financial compliance. Greenboard is the unified, AI-native compliance operating system for RIAs, fintechs, private funds, hedge funds, and more. By centralizing data and workflows, Greenboard helps firms reduce regulatory risk, simplify their technology stack, modernize how they run compliance, and save money. 


Greenboard's mission is to enable financial institutions to operate their back office teams at a higher standard, with half of the headcount. We’re starting with compliance

name: Greptile

Top YC companies like PostHog, Raycast, Vouch, Podium, and YC's own internal software team use Greptile to review millions of changes every week. 

When companies start using Greptile, they catch more bugs and merge PRs 4x faster, on average

Greptile can be used via the cloud, or be hosted 100% on your cloud in an air-gapped VPC.

problem: Code review is a bottleneck and reviewers miss bugs because they lack context on the whole codebase.

product_category: AI code review agent

name: Guardian RF
one_liner: Drone detection for US defense and national security
long_description:
The rise of low-cost commercial drones has introduced a new class of asymmetric threats to U.S. national security. Off-the-shelf platforms now deliver ISR, contraband, or payloads with precision, while operating below radar coverage and beyond line-of-sight. These systems—often costing under $1,000—are capable of neutralizing multi-million-dollar defense assets. For drone detection to be viable at scale, sensors must achieve cost parity with the threat.

In response, the Department of Defense established multiple initiatives to counter the rapid proliferation of uncrewed aerial systems. The Joint Counter-small UAS Office (JCO) coordinates policy and acquisition across services. The Base Defense Cross-Functional Team enables persistent perimeter security for CONUS and OCONUS installations. Falcon Peak, Red Sands, and related exercises are accelerating deployment of counter-UAS technologies in complex environments.

This threat is no longer exclusive to military operations overseas. It now directly targets the U.S. homeland. In 2025, an executive order designated the protection of American airspace sovereignty a national priority, recognizing that uncrewed systems present both surveillance and kinetic risks within the United States. That same year, a domestic extremist plotted to destroy a Tennessee power substation using a drone rigged with C-4 explosives—a plan disrupted by undercover federal agents. In July 2025, an unauthorized drone collided with a rescue helicopter during disaster response operations in Kerr County, Texas, forcing an emergency landing and halting flood relief efforts. These are not isolated incidents—they reflect a broader shift in drone-enabled threats against homeland infrastructure and public safety.

Guardian RF builds passive, radiofrequency-based drone detection systems for force protection and critical infrastructure defense inside the United States. Our systems are fielded under an AFWERX Direct-to-Phase-II SBIR with the 30th Security Forces Squadron at Vandenberg Space Force Base, deployed by local and state law enforcement, and integrated into commercial security operations. We were selected as a finalist for Falcon Peak 25.2, the Department of Defense’s premier counter-UAS exercise.

Scout is a passive RF sensor for fixed, mobile, or temporary deployments. It detects and classifies drone control signals—including modified variants of DJI, Crossfire, and ExpressLRS—at standoff ranges. Scout supports direct integration into TAK and other operational APIs and is managed through GRF-SECURE, our secure interface for live monitoring, threat alerting, and forensic review.

Mosaic extends coverage in austere environments, enabling persistent low-altitude monitoring and classification of non–Remote ID drones across complex terrain—without active emissions or mesh dependency.

Built in the United States, Guardian RF delivers scalable, automated, and cost-aligned drone detection—passive by design and hardened for real-world deployment across the homeland.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US military installations, federal agencies, state and local law enforcement, stadiums and critical infrastructure operators that need to detect hostile or unauthorized drones
problem: Cheap commercial drones can surveil or attack sensitive sites, while existing counter-drone detection is expensive and bulky. Detection has to cost about as little as the threat.
business_model: Hardware sensors plus software subscription and government contracts (AFWERX SBIR)
product_category: Passive RF drone detection and pilot geolocation (counter-UAS)
founder_names: Lucas Raskin; John Andrzejewski; Eli Kerstein
market_need_then: Founders cite the DoD Joint Counter-small UAS Office, homeland drone incidents and Ukraine drone warfare. Demand for cheap detection grew through 2024 and 2025 (company long description and Georgetown article).
outcome_analysis: Guardian RF is active and still early. The team won attention by building a hardware prototype in days after a defense hackathon, then landed an AFWERX Direct-to-Phase-II SBIR at Vandenberg, a DIU low-cost sensing challenge win at Falcon Peak 25.2 and a February 2026 partnership with Picogrid. Funding is reported only by aggregators, so capital strength is unverified. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown news was found.

name: Guide Labs
one_liner: Frontier models and agents you can learn from, audit, and steer.
long_description:
Guide Labs builds frontier AI models and agents that you can learn from, audit, and steer. 
Our first model, Steerling-8B, is the first and largest inherently interpretable model: it can trace any output to training data, concepts inside the model, and the input, all without sacrificing performance.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises, regulated industries (such as finance) and scientific users that need AI models whose outputs can be audited and traced; no named customers yet
problem: Large language models are opaque; users cannot trace an output to training data or internal concepts, which blocks debugging, auditing and trust.
business_model: Interpretable foundation models, open-sourced base model (Apache 2.0) with a platform called Clarity and planned API and agent access (pricing not found)
product_category: Interpretable and auditable AI models

outcome_analysis: Guide Labs, a Winter 2024 YC company, raised a $9.3M seed led by Initialized in November 2024 and in February 2026 open-sourced Steerling-8B, an 8B-parameter model that traces every output token to training data and concepts. It is still early: no named customers, no later round found, and no exit, so the outcome is open; its strengths are the founders' interpretability research and a research-grade technical lead, while the open license and well-funded frontier labs and interpretability rivals are the main risks.

name: Gumloop
one_liner: The multiplayer AI agent builder. Let anyone build, IT controls access
long_description:
Gumloop is the multiplayer AI agent builder. Let anyone at your company build agents with any AI model and any integration, while IT controls access and spend.

Agents reflect on their own runs and improve over time, drawing on one shared company brain: your internal knowledge, the skills your team runs on, and live context from every tool you use.

Disclaimer: Gumloop is not a visual workflow builder. It is an agent builder.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies whose employees build AI agents and automations, with IT controlling access and spend (customers named include Shopify, Ramp, Gusto, Samsara, Instacart, Opendoor)
problem: Non-technical employees want to automate work with AI but lack tools, while IT needs governance over models, data and spend.
business_model: SaaS subscription with usage credits, enterprise plans
product_category: AI agent and workflow automation builder
market_need_then: In 2023 non-technical users in a Discord server wanted to use Auto-GPT without coding (TechCrunch). Interest in AI automation rose sharply with GPT-4.
outcome_analysis: Gumloop grew from a Vancouver side project into a YC W24 company, then raised a 3.1M seed in July 2024, a 17M Series A in January 2025 and a 50M Series B led by Benchmark in March 2026. Success came from riding the AI automation wave, a deliberate rename, fast shipping and enterprise customers. No shutdown or acquisition news exists.

name: HYBRD
tags: Health Tech; Consumer; Fitness; Digital Health; AI
one_liner: coaching agents for athletes
long_description:
The mission of HYBRD is to take world-class coaching and make it universally available. 

Health data has never been more abundant. GPS watches track pace and heart rate, wearables monitor sleep and recovery, and voice logging has made it easier than ever to capture weightlifting and HYROX. 

And yet most athletes are still following static PDF plans they found online, or "adaptive" apps that fall apart the moment cross-training enters the picture.

Existing tools feel disappointing because they don’t actually know your goals and constraints, so they can’t do anything meaningful with the data they collect. 
HYBRD can. 

We aggregate your wearable data, fill the gaps with a simple AI logger, and use that complete picture to build personalized training programs from the best coaches in the world, like Alex Viada, who coined the term "hybrid athlete." 

From there, the HYBRD agent keeps you on track, adjusting your schedule around weather, travel, and fatigue as you progress. Everything you'd get from a $500/month coach, at a 50x lower price. 

Founded in 2024 by WHOOP and AWS alumni, HYBRD is built by hybrid athletes. Join us for a workout every Monday morning in San Francisco and Boston.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer hybrid athletes (HYROX, running plus lifting, triathlon) who pay for a training app
problem: Athletes follow static PDF plans or apps focused on only cardio or strength, which cannot adapt around cross-training, travel and fatigue.
business_model: Consumer subscription (free tier, paid premium plans, 7 day trial)
product_category: AI coaching and training app for athletes
founder_names: Ben Katz; Matt Ruiters; Caroline Shoemaker; Mats Terwiesch
market_need_then: Founders say existing products cover only cardio or strength and athletes rely on static plans. HYROX participation was growing (founder and company statements; not independently measured here).
outcome_analysis: HYBRD is active and early. It launched on iOS in May 2025 after a six month invitation-only beta, built by ex-WHOOP and AWS staff who are themselves hybrid athletes. No funding amounts, shutdown or acquisition were found, so outcome is unresolved and the crowded HYROX app market is the main open risk.

name: Hamming AI
one_liner: Complete QA platform for voice agents
long_description:
Hamming AI is the complete QA platform for voice agents from pre-deployment testing to production monitoring. 

4M+ calls tested. 10K+ agents monitored. Trusted by public companies and the fastest-growing voice AI teams.

Connect your agent, auto-generate test scenarios, and run thousands of test calls in minutes. In production, monitor every call with 50+ built-in metrics and get alerts before customers notice.

Sumanyu (CEO) was previously Head of Data at Citizen and Senior Staff Data Scientist at Tesla, where he grew AI-powered sales to hundreds of millions in revenue per year. 

Our engineering team ranks #1 on Weave (https://workweave.ai) across 10,000+ engineers and 100+ teams.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Companies building voice agents, such as healthcare and enterprise voice AI teams (Luma Health, Netomi, Maven AGI named)
problem: Voice agents fail in unpredictable ways and teams test them by phoning them by hand; they need automated pre-launch testing and production monitoring.
business_model: SaaS subscription, usage based, enterprise plans
product_category: QA, testing and monitoring for AI voice agents
market_need_then: Voice agents were exploding in 2024 and Sharma's Citizen and Tesla experience showed testing AI at scale mattered. Customers reported ad hoc manual call testing.
outcome_analysis: Hamming is active, raised a 3.8M seed in December 2024 led by Mischief and now claims SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance, offices in four cities and customers like Luma Health and Netomi. Strength comes from the voice AI wave and the founders' scale testing background. Competition from Cekura, Coval and platform vendors is the main risk. No Series A found.

name: Handled
tags: B2B; Workflow Automation; Logistics; E-commerce; AI
one_liner: AI teammate for finance and operations teams at consumer brands
long_description:
Consumer brands run finance and operations across ERPs, commerce platforms, 3PLs, accounting systems, email, and spreadsheets. Because these systems do not share context or complete work, teams still spend hours assembling reports, reconciling numbers, entering orders, monitoring inventory, processing invoices, and chasing exceptions. Problems are often discovered only after they have cost the business time, margin, or revenue.

Handled is an AI teammate for finance and operations. It connects to the systems and unstructured information a brand already uses and learns its data, rules, and workflows. Handled answers questions about the business, proactively catches issues, and takes on recurring manual work across financial reporting, inventory, procurement, wholesale order-to-cash, and AP/AR. It works across systems and brings a person in when judgment or approval is required.

Handled gives lean teams more operating capacity without adding another tool to manage, more outsourced support, or more headcount.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer packaged goods and e-commerce brands with lean finance and operations teams
problem: Brands run finance and ops across ERPs, commerce platforms, 3PLs and spreadsheets that do not share context, so teams spend hours reconciling data and chasing exceptions.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an AI teammate
product_category: AI operations and finance automation for consumer brands
market_need_then: At the Zimi stage, Shopify's Black Friday map showed little African selling activity and founders said cross-border merchants lacked US fulfillment and compliance help (TechCrunch, Dec 2024).
outcome_analysis: Handled began as Zimi, raised a 2M seed in December 2024 led by Fearless Fund, then repositioned to AI finance and operations for consumer brands, with CPG customers listed on its site. Team is three per YC and a secondary profile says one founder remains. No shutdown or acquisition found. Success is unproven; the pivot's quality cannot yet be judged from public data.

name: Haplotype Labs
one_liner: Personalized prevention using genetics and AI
long_description:
We're building the HaploHub: a SaaS platform for genetic testing labs, concierge medical practices, and payer/providers to: 
 * predict disease risk for their patients based on proprietary or publicly available genetic models
 * securely host, manage, and interrogate the genetic data of their population
 * generate reports and run the most common inference algorithms (phasing, imputation, ibd, etc.) without writing code
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Genetic testing labs, concierge medical practices, payers and providers
problem: Labs and clinics lack software to host genetic data, run population genetics algorithms and predict disease risk without writing custom pipelines.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform (HaploHub)
product_category: Genetics analysis and polygenic risk SaaS
market_need_then: Labs and clinics wanted polygenic risk and population genetics tools without bespoke software (company site); Polcari saw this at 23andMe.
outcome_analysis: Haplotype Labs is a one person company led by a former 23andMe chief architect. It reportedly closed about 1.1M in seed money in early 2024 and remains listed as active. No shutdown, acquisition or larger round was found, and no customer traction is public, so outcome is unresolved and scale is limited by team size.

name: Happenstance
one_liner: People search powered by AI
long_description:
Happenstance is people search powered by AI.

For example, you ask Happenstance "find people who work on notification systems at big companies", and it comes back with two who follow you on Twitter and five who are connected to your partners. That kind of thing you just can't do on LinkedIn.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Individual professionals and teams doing sales, hiring, job search, fundraising and investing who want warm introductions
problem: People cannot search their own extended network by natural language; LinkedIn does not surface who follows you or connects to your partners.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer freemium (pricing not verified)
product_category: AI people search and network intelligence
market_need_then: YC description says LinkedIn cannot answer queries like who works on notification systems and follows you on Twitter. Early product validated by YC testimonials, which are the company's own claims.
outcome_analysis: Happenstance is active, small and claims over 500,000 users plus an API, CLI, iPhone app and integrations with ChatGPT and Claude. Funding is not verified; aggregators suggest a small seed. A founder with a prior AI startup and strong YC endorsements helps, but LinkedIn and well-funded people search startups compete. Outcome is unresolved.

name: Hatchet
one_liner: The orchestration platform for teams who ship.
long_description: Hatchet is an orchestration platform for managing and observing AI agents, background tasks, and mission-critical workflows. Our mission is to provide developers with a simple, powerful, and reliable orchestration layer, enabling them to focus on building great applications.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and engineering teams running background tasks, AI agents and workflows (customers listed include Cursor, Linear, Motion, SpaceX)
problem: Teams need reliable, observable task queues and workflow orchestration without running Celery, Temporal or custom infrastructure.
business_model: Open source core (MIT) with usage-based cloud and enterprise support
product_category: Task queue and workflow orchestration platform for developers
market_need_then: Developers complained about Celery and heavy workflow engines; the Show HN drew 578 points in early 2024, showing demand for a simple Postgres queue.
outcome_analysis: Hatchet, an open source Postgres task queue launched on Hacker News in early 2024, grew into an agent and workflow orchestration platform. The company announces a 5.7M seed with v2 and lists logos such as Cursor, Linear and SpaceX, plus 170M tasks run daily. Open source distribution and AI workload growth drove adoption. No shutdown or acquisition found.

name: Haystack
one_liner: Replay real customer journeys against every change before you ship
long_description:
Haystack automatically learns real customer journeys from production traffic, figures out which ones a code change could affect, and replays them in isolated copies of production to catch regressions before they ship.

When something breaks, Haystack shows exactly what changed across the UI, network calls, and events, then gives the failure back to your coding agent to fix and rerun. Teams get high-fidelity QA without having to write or maintain test cases.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineering teams shipping code, increasingly with coding agents
problem: Code changes cause regressions that teams catch late because writing and maintaining test cases is costly.
business_model: B2B developer tooling, pricing not public (early access and demos)
product_category: AI testing and code verification for developer workflows
market_need_then: Developers in 2024 were adopting AI coding assistants and complaining about navigating large codebases. The team later moved toward code review and then change verification as AI generated more pull requests.
outcome_analysis: Haystack is an active two person company that launched a canvas code editor in August 2024, then shifted toward code review and now toward verifying changes by replaying production journeys for coding agents. No funding beyond the standard YC deal is verifiable and no exit or shutdown was found, so the story is still early. The shift reflects the crowded editor market and the new problem of reviewing large volumes of AI generated changes.

name: Hazel
one_liner: AI-enabled procurement for government
long_description: Hazel builds AI-powered procurement software for U.S. state, local, and federal government agencies. We automate the full procurement process including requirements generation, market research, solicitation drafting, and proposal evaluation. Agencies use Hazel to save time and money while improving compliance.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: US state, local and federal government procurement teams
problem: Government procurement staff are overloaded drafting requirements, solicitations and evaluations by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to government agencies, also via Carahsoft reseller
product_category: GovTech AI procurement software
market_need_then: Founders cite roughly 30 percent of procurement roles unfilled and $2.7 trillion of annual public procurement, both unverified company claims.
outcome_analysis: Hazel pivoted from a marketplace for government bidders to selling AI procurement software directly to agencies, and won the City of Dallas in July 2025 plus a Carahsoft listing. Funding is not verified beyond small pre-seed reports, so the stage is early, and the outcome is still open given government sales cycles.

name: Healia
one_liner: Modern health insurance for dual income families
long_description:
Healia is reinventing health insurance for dual income families. Our product enables companies to pay for the out of pocket costs of any employee that enrolls in their spouse's health insurance plan. This saves customers $10k per enrollee while providing an incredible employee perk: 100% coverage of a family's health costs.

We’re now up to 50+ customers coast-to-coast with over 40k employees using our product!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Employers that want to cut health benefit costs for employees with a working spouse
problem: Dual income families pay duplicate premiums and out-of-pocket costs; employers pay too much for coverage that spouses could get elsewhere.
business_model: B2B subscription for a spousal health reimbursement arrangement plus claims service
product_category: Health benefits, spousal HRA (Total Care Option)
market_need_then: Employers face rising premiums and families routinely pay duplicate coverage. The company reports 50+ customers and 40k+ covered employees by early 2024 and the funding announcement cites about $33M in added family coverage enabled.
outcome_analysis: Healia grew from a single founder with Root and Olive experience into a company with 50+ customers by early 2024 and a $14M Series A in July 2026 led by 111 West Capital, with reported total funding of $18M. The wedge is concrete employer savings, which supports strong product-market fit. Earlier funding rounds are not detailed in public sources, so the funding history is only partly known.

name: HealthSpark
tags: Health Tech; Digital Health; Healthcare; AI
one_liner: Empowering Physical Therapists to Go Independent
long_description: HealthSpark empowers physical therapists (PTs) to start, run, and grow their own independent practices. Our AI-native “business-in-a-box” takes care of the administrative work—credentialing, insurance billing, patient onboarding, documentation, and scheduling—so PTs can focus on patient care, not paperwork.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Physical therapists who want to run independent practices; patients (Medicare, in home)
problem: Therapists lose time to credentialing, billing and documentation, which keeps many employed by large clinics.
business_model: Services and software platform for independent PTs; revenue model not stated
product_category: Healthcare practice enablement, AI EHR and billing for physical therapy
market_need_then: Independent PTs face administrative overhead and Medicare billing complexity; no dated spending evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: HealthSpark joined YC in Fall 2024 with one listed founder and has since presented itself as an in home PT provider in greater Los Angeles, suggesting a shift from software toward delivering care. No verified funding, exit or traction numbers were found, so the outcome is unknown and the record is early stage.

name: HeartByte
tags: Generative AI; Consumer; Entertainment; Social Media
one_liner: GenAI Interactive story. Creator write fictions 10x faster.
long_description: Storio is a content platform where creators can create original fiction or derivative works based on other fictional worlds. Creators write fictions 10 times faster on Storio. It's a place for community to fully indulge in the fictional world that they wish they were in.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Fiction writers and fans of derivative fiction; readers (consumer)
problem: Writing long fiction and fanfiction is slow; fans want to indulge in fictional worlds.
business_model: Consumer content platform, monetization not stated (tool described as free)
product_category: Generative AI interactive fiction and writing platform (Storio)
market_need_then: Large fanfiction readership exists, and generative AI lowered writing cost in 2023 and 2024; no company spend or usage data found.
outcome_analysis: HeartByte, now marketed as Storio, is a two person company from the Winter 2024 batch with founders experienced at Wish, Instagram and Google, building AI assisted fiction. No verified funding, exit or growth numbers were found, and the status is listed as active, so the outcome remains open.

name: Helium
one_liner: Self Improving Software
long_description:
Helium is building self-improving software — AI that continuously experiments on key moments in the user funnel to boost revenue. Our first customer, a social app with 20M MAU, uses Helium to test new in-app paywalls to get more users to subscribe. 

Zach previously made $100M+ in growth experiments at Uber, Shishir led the first LLM features for Alexa, and Anish worked at Meta building ML to automatically experiment on ads, increasing Instagram ads conversion by 10%.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mobile app companies with subscription paywalls
problem: Apps lose revenue because paywalls and funnels are tested slowly and manually.
business_model: B2B SaaS for paywall building, testing and analytics
product_category: Mobile app monetization and automated experimentation
founder_names: Zach Witzel; Shishir Jakati; Anish Doshi
market_need_then: Subscription apps depend on paywall conversion; pilot customer Locket reports over 75% subscription revenue growth per the company blog.
outcome_analysis: Helium is an active company with Uber, Alexa and Meta experience that sells paywall tooling and plans an AI experimentation layer, citing customers such as Locket and Wispr. The company blog reports a $2M raise from YC, Gradient Ventures and Daybreak. It competes in a crowded paywall tooling market, and no exit or setback was found.

name: Henry
tags: Generative AI; SaaS; Real Estate; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Automating Deal Decks for Commercial Real Estate Brokers
long_description: Henry is an AI copilot for commercial real estate (CRE) brokers that seamlessly integrates a brokerage’s internal data set with external sources to generate custom presentations and financial modeling for deals. Our mission is to help CRE brokers close more deals faster, earning more while doing less repetitive work. We’re initially focusing on enabling brokers to generate deal decks in seconds—a task that typically consumes 20+ hours a week across multiple departments within a brokerage.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Commercial real estate brokerages and investment teams
problem: Brokers spend 20+ hours a week building deal decks, underwriting and marketing materials by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS with proprietary data, pricing not public
product_category: AI copilot for commercial real estate (Henry Deal, Henry Decks)
market_need_then: CRE brokers build many pitch decks manually; the founder says he built dozens as an analyst. Company reports 150+ firms and $150B of deal value by 2026.
outcome_analysis: Henry went from a June 2024 launch to 150+ brokerage customers, a $4.3M seed in February 2025 and a $16.5M Series A in 2026 led by FirstMark. Founder market fit from a CRE analyst turned Lev executive and a repeat founder drove a focused wedge on deal decks that then widened to underwriting. The main risk is generic AI tools and portals like Crexi copying the feature.

name: HeroUI
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Design Tools; AI
one_liner: The UI framework for AI agents and developers to build beautiful apps.
long_description: HeroUI makes it simple for AI agents and developers to build beautiful, accessible, production-ready interfaces for web and mobile. In the AI age, design matters more than ever. Every micro animation, color, and interaction shapes how users experience your product. HeroUI makes that level of creativity and craft simple
all_locations: Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires, Argentina; Remote
regions: Argentina; Latin America; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Frontend developers and AI coding agents building React and mobile apps
problem: Teams want accessible, well designed UI components quickly without building a design system.
business_model: Open source library with paid Pro components, templates and AI builder
product_category: UI component framework and developer tools
market_need_then: React teams were adopting Tailwind and wanted prebuilt components; adoption shows demand (site cites 38k+ GitHub stars and 31M monthly npm downloads).
outcome_analysis: HeroUI grew from the NextUI open source library into a YC S24 company with large GitHub, npm and Discord numbers, and added a Pro product and AI tooling. Distribution through open source is the main asset, while revenue and funding remain undisclosed. It was renamed in January 2025 and rewrote the library as v3 in 2026.

name: Hestus, Inc.
one_liner: An AI-powered CAD software
long_description: Hestus is AI-powered CAD software that speeds up hardware development. While engineers are typically quick at coming up with initial design concepts, they are bogged down getting from idea to the final design due to countless tedious and repetitive tasks. We are building CAD software that automates these mundane tasks and speeds up the design execution process, while letting engineers spend more time on the creative part of the design process.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mechanical and hardware engineers using CAD software
problem: Engineers waste time on repetitive sketching, constraints and dimensioning in CAD.
business_model: Software plugin for CAD, free beta for Sketch Helper; later pricing not announced
product_category: AI autocomplete for CAD (Autodesk Fusion plugin)
market_need_then: Engineers do repetitive sketch work; the company reports 1,000 engineers on its tool at launch and its site now claims 5,000.
outcome_analysis: Hestus is an active company founded by repeat founders from Cruise and SpaceRyde. It shipped a free Sketch Helper plugin for Fusion, reached about 1,000 and later 5,000 engineers, raised $1.5M in January 2025 and a $7.4M seed led by Insight Partners in October 2026. Founder market fit and a narrow wedge drove progress; Autodesk remains the main risk.

name: Hexclave
one_liner: The user infrastructure platform
long_description: https://hexclave.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and startups building web and mobile apps who need user authentication and related user infrastructure without writing it themselves
problem: Teams lose time building login, organizations, roles, payments hooks and user data plumbing, and closed vendors lock them in. Hexclave sells open-source, self-hostable modules for these jobs.
business_model: Open-source core with a managed cloud tier, usage-based pricing (tier details not verified)
product_category: Developer tools, authentication and user management infrastructure
market_need_then: Auth is a recurring pain for app builders, and the README positions the product as an open-source Clerk and Auth0 alternative, implying demand for pricing and lock-in relief. No dated spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Hexclave is active with a small team of seven and no sourced exit or distress. It started as Stack Auth, an open-source authentication product launched around the Summer 2024 batch, and has widened into a user infrastructure platform under a new name. Funding is not verifiable from primary sources, so the trajectory is unclear.

name: Hey Revia
one_liner: Voice AI to automate complex phone calls for healthcare providers
long_description: Hey Revia is a voice AI that handles complex phone calls for healthcare providers. Our software automates complex menus, reduces hold times, and handles tedious phone calls—verifying provider details, updating insurance info, and securing approvals. We offer Revia as web app, mobile app and API.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Healthcare providers and clinics that spend staff time on phone calls with insurers and pharmacies
problem: Staff lose hours navigating phone menus and holds to verify insurance, get approvals and update records. Hey Revia uses voice AI to handle those calls.
business_model: B2B software offered as web app, mobile app and API
product_category: Healthcare voice AI
market_need_then: The founding story says the founders' daughters' pediatric clinic spent hours on calls with insurers and pharmacies. Insurance and prior authorization calls are a known administrative cost for providers.
outcome_analysis: Hey Revia was a four person voice AI team from Summer 2024 aimed at healthcare phone calls. It was acquired by OpenLoop, announced around 2026-06-30, with undisclosed terms, and both cofounders took engineering leadership roles there while the product moved into OpenLoop's Launchpad platform. Little funding is public beyond the YC deal, so the exit looks like a capital efficient strategic buy that relies on the founders' Google and AI background.

name: HumanLayer
one_liner: The multiplayer control plane for your software factory
long_description: HumanLayer is a multiplayer coding agent IDE+cloud that works seamlessly from your workstation to anywhere you want to run background agents. It brings agent sessions, plan artifacts, and code diffs together in one place for you team to collaborate and ship. It's built in composable pieces to meet software factory builders where they already are - you can BYO compute, dev environment setup, and harness, or use our full integrated stack.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams using AI coding agents who want shared sessions, plans and reviews (originally developers building AI agents who needed human approval steps)
problem: Agents need human sign-off to be trusted in production, and later coding agents lacked team collaboration. HumanLayer first sold an approval API, then a multiplayer coding agent IDE and cloud.
business_model: SaaS per seat (free Starter, Pro 100 USD per user per month, custom Enterprise) plus open-source SDK
product_category: Developer tools, AI agent infrastructure and coding agent collaboration
market_need_then: In late 2024 teams were wiring LLM agents to real actions and needed approvals and audit steps; the launch drew attention on Hacker News in November 2024. No spend data found.
outcome_analysis: HumanLayer launched in Fall 2024 as an approval API for AI agents, gained developer mindshare through the 12-Factor Agents work, and moved into a coding agent IDE. It was acquired by Factory, reported November 4, 2026, with undisclosed terms, plans to open source the product and refunds to recent paying customers. The exit looks like a team and product absorption, but terms are not public so the outcome quality is unknown.

name: Hyrex
tags: AIOps; Developer Tools; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure
one_liner: The COLD Task Framework
long_description:
Hyrex is a task orchestration framework that uses PostgreSQL (or Hyrex Cloud) as a durable task queue. Define tasks in Python or TypeScript, send them to be processed asynchronously, and let Hyrex handle the rest.

Hyrex tasks are COLD: Controllable, Observable, Large-Scale, and Durable!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Backend and AI engineers who run asynchronous background tasks in Python or TypeScript on Postgres
problem: Existing task frameworks are hard to configure or debug, need code rewrites, or are unmaintained. Hyrex uses Postgres as a durable queue with an open-source core and a paid cloud.
business_model: Open-source framework with Hyrex Cloud subscriptions (200 and 400 USD per month tiers per the YC page)
product_category: Developer tools, task orchestration and queues
market_need_then: Developers on Postgres want one fewer system to run. An HN commenter on the Hatchet launch noted many teams already use Postgres, and Celery's Postgres support issue had been open for years.
outcome_analysis: Hyrex is a small team of three in a crowded task queue market. No funding, exit or shutdown is reported. The company site returned an HTTP 402 error on fetch, which may indicate a billing or hosting problem, but that is not confirmed and nothing else suggests distress.

name: ISSEN
one_liner: AI realtime voice companion for language learning
long_description: ISSEN is an AI conversational language app that helps you become fluent. Your on-demand voice tutor is personal to you, adapting lessons and chats to your particular interests, learning style, and goals. Our mission is to transform language learning by offering a level of connection, effectiveness and fun that, until now, only human teachers could provide.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Adult consumers learning a foreign language who want spoken practice, paying a monthly subscription
problem: Human tutors are expensive and hard to schedule, and gamified apps build streaks without fluency. ISSEN offers an adaptive real-time voice tutor with long-term memory.
business_model: Consumer subscription (20 minute free trial, then 20 to 29 USD per month per the launch post)
product_category: Consumer AI, language learning
market_need_then: Language learners pay for conversation practice; Speak reported over 10 million downloads and a 1B USD valuation by December 2024, showing demand for AI speaking tutors.
outcome_analysis: ISSEN is an active two-founder consumer voice tutor from Fall 2024 in a market where Speak and Praktika were already well funded. The Hacker News launch drew attention but also criticism of beginner quality, and no revenue or retention figures are public. App store updates continued into April 2026, but outcome is undetermined.

name: InQuery
one_liner: Intelligent Medical Record Reviews
long_description:
InQuery is a fully-automated medical record review platform that indexes, labels, and summarizes patient medical records so that physicians and attorneys can understand patient journeys at a glance. 

Our proprietary technology reasons about each record to surface key insights that could make or break your medical legal case.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Personal injury and plaintiff law firms, medical-legal service providers and claims organizations (originally physicians, attorneys and insurance claims teams)
problem: Retrieving, indexing and summarizing patient medical records for legal and claims cases is slow and manual. InQuery automates record review and now also retrieves records.
business_model: Service plus software per case or per page (pricing not verified)
product_category: Legal tech and health records AI
market_need_then: Personal injury firms and carriers spend heavy staff time on medical chronologies, evidenced by funding of Wisedocs in early 2024.
outcome_analysis: InQuery is active and has narrowed from generic medical record summarization toward records retrieval for personal injury firms, claiming over 1M pages processed. It faces heavily funded legal AI rivals that cover similar workflows. Funding amounts are inconsistent across aggregators, so scale of traction and runway cannot be judged.

name: Indemni
tags: Identity; Logistics; Supply Chain; Fraud Prevention; Fraud Detection
one_liner: Cargo Theft and Fraud Prevention Platform
long_description: We are building a safer supply chain. Cargo Theft has been increasing yearly, and the supply chain industry is urgently looking for ways to solve this. Using experience fighting fraud at the largest delivery marketplaces and logistics tech companies, we are building solutions to stop Cargo Theft and improve profit margins and revenue for warehouses and freight brokers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Freight brokers, shippers and 3PLs moving high-value freight
problem: Strategic cargo theft, where criminals pose as legitimate carriers or drivers, costs brokers and shippers loads and insurance. Indemni verifies drivers and shipments and offers theft coverage.
business_model: B2B SaaS verification per shipment or driver plus an insurance program (details not verified)
product_category: Logistics fraud prevention and insurance
market_need_then: Freight fraud surged in 2024; Truckstop reported reported loss values above 34M USD in Q2 2024 alone, and trade press described brokers shutting out carriers.
outcome_analysis: Indemni targets a worsening freight fraud problem and raised a 4M USD seed announced in October 2026, well after its Winter 2024 batch, while building an insurance offering backed by Chaucer and Lloyd's. The long gap suggests slow capital efficient growth. The founder's DoorDash fraud background fits the wedge, though regulation and incumbents are risks.

name: Infinity
one_liner: Business banking for cross-border SMBs & Startups
long_description: Infinity is a banking and payments platform for cross-border businesses in India. We help our customers make cross-border payments that are 70% cheaper than traditional methods and earn income on idle cash by investing in government securities.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Indian freelancers, agencies, exporters and startups that earn in foreign currency
problem: Receiving international payments in India is slow and costly with hidden fees. Infinity offers multi-currency accounts and INR settlement at a flat fee.
business_model: Transaction fee (flat 0.5 percent all-inclusive per its site) plus yield on idle cash in government securities
product_category: Fintech, cross-border payments and business banking
market_need_then: Indian freelancers and exporters faced delays and fees on international receipts, per founder stories, and Infinity claims 15K customers and 20M USD monthly volume on its site (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Infinity is an active brother-led team of 15 in Bengaluru that raised a 1.9M USD pre-seed announced in February 2025 and claims 15K customers on its homepage. It competes with Skydo, which was already funded in 2022. Regulatory status as a payment intermediary is the main risk, and no later round is reported.

name: Innate
tags: Developer Tools; Hard Tech; Robotics; AI
one_liner: Personal AI Robots
long_description:
We make personal AI robots - general-purpose physical machines that anyone can teach with code, language and demonstrations.

We believe building open platforms like the first PCs this is the only way to bring the robotics future that we all want, where everyone can participate in the robotics revolution.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers, robotics hobbyists and builders who want an affordable programmable personal robot
problem: Capable general-purpose robots are expensive and closed. Innate sells an open, teachable robot (MARS at 995 USD per its site, listed near 2000 USD at the launch) with an agentic OS and cloud software.
business_model: Hardware sales plus software subscription (a commenter cites a 50 USD per month software plan)
product_category: Consumer robotics and developer tools
competitors_at_founding: Hello Robot Stretch; Unitree G1; K-Scale Labs
market_need_then: Builders were buying low cost robot arms and kits; the Show HN post got 123 points with some orders, but price and subscription drew criticism.
outcome_analysis: Innate is an active robotics startup that shipped an affordable programmable robot, MARS, and an agentic OS. Hacker News reception was positive with price and subscription objections. Funding is unverified, so runway is unknown, and low cost competitors such as Hugging Face's robots emerged in 2025.

name: InspectMind AI
one_liner: AI agent for construction drawings review
long_description: An AI agent that catches issues in construction drawings before they become costly rework and project delays
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: General contractors, architects, engineers and developers who review construction drawings
problem: Errors and conflicts in construction drawings cause expensive rework, delays and change orders; manual plan review is slow.
business_model: usage-based per review run with a free tier, plus enterprise use
product_category: AI construction plan review
market_need_then: Company says drawing errors cost six to seven figures per job and cites a 2 million dollar rework save on a 100 million project; claims are self-reported. Advances in AI models made automated review feasible.
outcome_analysis: InspectMind AI is a Winter 2024 YC company that is still active. It reports 600 plus firm users and has expanded from field inspections toward drawing review with an agent called Sherlock. Founder domain insight from a construction engineering business and the AI model shift helped, but funding is only a small reported pre-seed and competitors are arriving.

name: Integuru
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; API; Automation; AI
one_liner: Generate fast, reliable APIs for any platform
long_description: Integuru turns any platform into a reliable, low-latency, and high-throughput API. Requests complete in 3 seconds with 99.9%+ success, including deployments above 1M requests/month/platform. No RPA or browsers. No data caching needed. (By Taiki, Inc.)
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software startups and operators that need programmatic access to web platforms that offer no public API, such as healthcare and logistics software companies
problem: Many platforms have no usable API, so teams fall back on slow, brittle browser automation or RPA. Integuru reverse-engineers a site's own network requests to generate direct, fast integrations.
business_model: usage-based API and generated integrations, with an open-source CLI
product_category: developer tools, API generation, integration infrastructure
market_need_then: Platforms without APIs force browser automation, which the company says is slow and brittle. The company site lists about 16 startup customers and claims more than 10 million API calls per month, which is self-reported.
outcome_analysis: Integuru is an active early stage company from Winter 2024 with five people, a stated customer list and an open-source agent that gave it developer visibility. No funding round, exit or failure signal was found, so the outcome is still open and the data gap is about funding rather than performance.

name: Intryc
tags: Customer Success; Analytics; Customer Support; Operations
one_liner: Intryc is the unified quality assurance, governance, and training…
long_description: Enterprises have millions of customer interactions every year but are only able to monitor less than 2-5% of those. The rest 95% is unmonitored risk across compliance, customer experience, product defects, and agent performance. With AI agents widely deployed across customer support organisations this problem increases exponentially. Every company needs a unified layer that allows them to monitor and govern all customer interactions with customer support teams, humans and AI. Intryc is building this layer.

name: Keye
one_liner: The Smartest Private Equity Investor
long_description:
Keye is an AI software that lets private equity firms do due diligence for acquisitions faster and more accurately. Our customers can evaluate 10x more deals and fund better companies which leads directly to better returns/more alpha.
--

Our system is the first of its kind to instantly generate complex, comprehensive data packs from raw data in any format, directly from the data room. This enables investors to gain an 80% understanding of a potential deal within moments, empowering them to say No to a deal earlier in the process and focus on high-potential opportunities. Traditionally, creating these detailed data packs—like cohort or retention analyses and customer roll-forwards—takes weeks, during which critical details may be overlooked, potentially costing funds millions in missed insights and poor decisions.
--

Keye combines cutting-edge AI with deep private equity expertise to deliver powerful, multi-layered insights that go far beyond the simple summarizers and search functions offered by other tools. Our platform dives deep into both quantitative and qualitative due diligence data, offering high-impact analytics crafted specifically for private equity workflows. This isn’t just automation—it’s a purpose-built solution that uncovers actionable insights, fueling smarter decisions and driving true alpha.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

business_model: B2B SaaS subscription sold to PE funds
product_category: AI due diligence analytics for private equity
founder_names: Rohan Parikh; Conor Brown; Lalit Lal
market_need_then: PE funds screen many deals and diligence analysis by hand takes weeks; generative AI in 2024 made automated analysis of raw files plausible.
outcome_analysis: Keye is active and raised a seed round in July 2025, about ten months after its Fall 2024 batch. The founders come from private equity and banking, which gives domain insight and access to buyers. It rides the timing of generative AI, but the segment drew several competitors, so durability is untested.

name: Keystroke

Keystroke is an all-in-one platform for building internal agents and workflows.

It is too early to call an outcome, and the pivot suggests the first idea did not produce a clear market position.

name: Kilvin

long_description:
Kilvin is an AI-native agency that builds custom software solutions for non-technical teams.

With AI, the future of software is democratized. Every team deserves tools built exactly for them, not off-the-shelf SaaS products they need to adapt to. Kilvin makes it a reality, delivering a private, secure workspace of custom applications, built around your workflows and ready in days, not months.

No engineers needed on your side. Just software that fits exactly how you work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

Self-serve plans are reported by a low-confidence source, and the agency model faces many AI app builders, so the story is unclear.

name: Kontigo
one_liner: USDC-Smart Neobank for Latinos.
long_description:
We’re building Kontigo, a USDC Smart Neobank for Latinos in the U.S. and Latin America.

We launched our Peer-to-Peer onramp 20 days ago and we’ve already had $540k in deposits, 10k active users and a +300k waitlist. 

The founding team has built and scaled fintechs in Latam, and it’s ex-Venmo, Nubank, Rappi, MercadoLibre, Ualá, Platzi, and Yuno. 

We’re already backed by DST Global, Soma Capital, Pioneer Fund, Transpose + 10 YC alums.

Sending money to Latin America is just as painful as holding it due to the region's fragmentation into 33 countries with 39 different currencies. 

On one hand, cross-border payments to Latam are absurdly expensive (up to 20% per transaction). Conversely, over the past decade, currency depreciation across the region has become unsustainable. (some countries surpassing the trillion percent ). 

Kontigo solves this with a USDC global wallet & a BTC savings account. 

- Like Venmo, but on-USDC.
- Like Zelle, but for cross-border payments. No limits.
- Like Nubank & Revolut, but without inflationary currencies. Bitcoin-backed.

User wallets are connected to an AI-private banker on WhatsApp to execute international USDC transactions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Latinos in Latin America (notably Venezuela) and the U.S. who want dollar-denominated savings and cheap transfers
problem: Cross-border payments to Latin America are costly and local currencies lose value, so people want to hold and send USDC.
business_model: Consumer stablecoin wallet and card with fees and spreads, plus merchant payment links and APIs
product_category: Stablecoin neobank
founder_names: Jesus Alberto Castillo Ferrer; Gino Guatavita
market_need_then: Venezuelan inflation made dollar-denominated apps a daily need; the company reported $540k deposits, 10k active users and a 300k waitlist within 20 days of its P2P onramp launch (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Kontigo grew fast from its Summer 2024 batch, reporting 1M users and over $30M annualized revenue by December 2025 when it announced a $20M seed. Founder fit with Venezuela and demand for dollar savings drove growth. Risks include sanctions scrutiny, loss of U.S. banking partners and a January 2026 security breach that was reimbursed.

name: Legora

name: Lighthouz AI

name: Lightscreen AI
one_liner: Voice + video AI interviewer
long_description:
Lightscreen’s voice + video AI interviewer enables companies to identify and invest in genuinely skilled candidates. It's already being used by high-growth startups and recruiting agencies to screen technical candidates. 

We provide companies with a voicebot that can run a full-length technical interview, does smart interruptions, and multi-modal cheating detection. The AI provides the company rubric-based, rich candidate evaluation in minutes and can be fully customized to ask questions and evaluate based on the company's needs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Startups and recruiting agencies screening technical candidates; the current site also targets high-volume frontline hiring
problem: Technical screens consume engineering time and are vulnerable to cheating. Lightscreen runs a voice and video AI interviewer with cheating detection and rubric-based evaluations.
business_model: B2B SaaS for AI interviewing and hiring workflows (pricing not found)
product_category: AI recruiting and interviewing
market_need_then: Technical screening is a recurring engineering time cost and the company cites cheating as a problem; no spend or customer-count data from 2024 was found.
outcome_analysis: Lightscreen began in 2024 as a voice and video technical interviewer and by 2026 its site describes a broader hiring pipeline with 20 plus customers (vendor-claimed). Only aggregator funding data exists (about 500K USD around December 2024), the team is small, and no exit or shutdown appeared. Many AI interview rivals make its outcome unclear.

name: Ligo Biosciences
tags: Deep Learning; Synthetic Biology; Biotech; Climate; AI
one_liner: Enzyme design models.
long_description:
We are building the next generation of deep-learning models for enzyme design to slash the cost of chemical manufacturing. The $6 trillion chemical industry is flawed: It produces 20% of industrial greenhouse gases, and is responsible for 15% of global energy usage. 

Enzymes offer a far more sustainable alternative to chemical synthesis and have already revolutionised how a select few chemicals are produced. The problem is each enzyme takes years of trial and error to develop. Our enzyme models learn the principles of catalysis, allowing us to design enzymes for each reaction, in days not years.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Chemical manufacturers and industrial biotech groups that could replace chemical synthesis with enzymes
problem: Developing an enzyme takes years of trial and error. Ligo builds deep-learning models that aim to design enzymes for specific reactions in days.
business_model: Model and tooling company for enzyme design, commercial model not found (YC page implies selling designs or tools to chemical makers)
product_category: Generative AI for enzyme and protein design
founder_names: Ed Harris; Emily Egerton-Warburton; Arda Goreci
market_need_then: The YC page says the 6 trillion USD chemical industry produces about 20 percent of industrial greenhouse gases and enzymes are a cleaner route but slow to develop; no customer spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Ligo Biosciences joined YC S24 with a four person research team, got press attention for an open-source reimplementation of a DeepMind structure model, and remains active with no verified public round beyond aggregator mentions of about 500K USD. The outcome is open: the science is hard and well funded rivals exist, but no failure or exit news was found.

name: Lilac Labs
one_liner: We automate the person taking orders at drive-thrus with a voice AI
long_description:
At Lilac, we automate the person taking order at the drive thru with a voice AI. We're building this for Quick Service Restaurants (QSRs) dealing with an historical labor shortage and rising wages.

Previous attempts at drive-thru voice ordering are costly to implement and have failed to deliver the accuracy and latency needed. It's now possible to build a voice interface that passes the threshold for a great customer experience.

In the United States, there are 200,000 Drive-Thrus handling 6 Billion visits a year. At 3 minutes per order, that's 34,000 human years spent on taking orders annually. Per location, on average we can deliver around $100,000 of value in terms of labor savings, upsell revenue lift, and training costs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Lingo.dev
one_liner: The Localization Engineering Platform
long_description:
Lingo.dev is the localization engineering platform: the best way to translate with LLMs, measure translation quality, and proofread with native speakers.

Lingo.dev is built for teams accountable for quality in languages they can't read. Teams configure localization engines, stateful translation APIs that hold the glossary, brand voice, and per-locale model preferences, and every request retrieves that context at inference time through retrieval augmented localization. Every translation is scored before it goes live, scores and corrections tune the engine, and the localization team runs the localization infrastructure. Integrate through the API, CLI, CI/CD, or native integrations with the code repository and the CMS. 

Lingo.dev is the standard localization infrastructure for modern enterprise teams scaling into new markets – including Mistral, Solana, SoSafe, and Cal.com. Over 300M words processed, SOC 2 Type II compliant.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Software and product teams that localize apps and content into many languages, from startups to enterprises
problem: Shipping software in many languages is slow and hard to quality check. Lingo.dev lets teams translate with LLMs, score quality and proofread with native speakers.
business_model: Open-source tooling plus paid hosted localization platform (API, CLI, CI/CD, integrations)
product_category: AI localization engineering platform
market_need_then: Developers wanted LLM translation without rewriting localization workflows; the founders won a hackathon prize in 2023 for the concept and customers such as Mistral, Solana and Cal.com adopted it (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Lingo.dev started as Replexica in December 2023, won attention through an open-source CLI and React compiler, rebranded in December 2024 and raised a 4.2 million USD seed led by Initialized in February 2025 with a team of about three. By 2026 it lists enterprise customers, SOC 2 Type II compliance and a v1 launch. Developer-led distribution and LLM timing explain the traction; incumbents with AI features are the main risk.

name: Loombotic
one_liner: Wire Harnesses in as little as 7 days
long_description: Loombotic is automating wire harness manufacturing.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware teams in robotics, EV, medical devices, aerospace and consumer hardware that need custom wire harnesses in low to mid volumes
problem: Custom wire harnesses normally take 5 to 7 weeks and need sales callbacks for quotes. Hardware teams lose schedule waiting on them.
business_model: Manufacturing service with instant online quoting, priced per order
product_category: Automated wire harness manufacturing
market_need_then: The company's own site cites 5 to 7 week traditional lead times against its 7 day claim, and a customer testimonial says short lead times are a real unlock. No independent dated demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Loombotic is an active Fall 2024 YC company with 25 people on the YC page and a live ordering site. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found. Funding is unverified, so the trajectory beyond the batch cannot be judged from public sources yet.

name: Lore
one_liner: Transform your iMessage conversations into shareable stories
long_description:
Transform your iMessage conversations into shareable stories

Founded by a team of ex-Google Photos and AI engineers, we’re bringing the same “turn personal data into something you actually come back to” loop to relationships
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers on Mac and iPhone who want to relive and share their iMessage conversations
problem: People have years of meaningful messages that are hard to revisit. Lore turns them into visual highlight reel stories.
business_model: Consumer app; pricing not stated on the site
product_category: Consumer AI app for messaging history
market_need_then: Spotify Wrapped style recaps had proven viral appeal, but no dated source shows demand for message recaps in mid 2024.
outcome_analysis: Lore is an active Summer 2024 YC company with a two person team and a shipping Mac app. No outcome news or verified funding was found, and the same founders also list a separate customs product, Passage, on YC. The record is too thin to assign success or failure factors.

name: Lucible
one_liner: Combined checking and investment account
long_description: Lucible is a combined checking and investment account that allows you to invest 100% of your money while still being able to spend it. Whenever you spend, we issue a loan in real time, using your investments as collateral, to cover the cost. This is the most capital and tax efficient way to manage your money. It's what the ultra wealthy already do to finance large purchases, and now you can do it for every day spending.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Affluent consumers who want their whole balance invested but still spendable
problem: Money in checking earns little while invested money is illiquid. Lucible issues a real time loan against investments at each purchase.
business_model: Account with interest on margin loans (the site cites 8% APR) on an S&P 500 invested balance
product_category: Consumer fintech, checking plus brokerage
market_need_then: The YC description frames this as how wealthy people already finance purchases; no dated demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Lucible is an active Summer 2024 YC company listing two people. The site was a pre launch waitlist and no funding or outcome news was found, so nothing supports a success or failure judgment yet.

name: Lucite
one_liner: Supercharging Insurance Brokers & Advisors
long_description: Lucite is building the first AI-native platform to help insurance brokers and advisors automate the most complex and time consuming parts of their job. We ingest unstructured carrier documents to accurately extract and analyze data, create insights, and generate deliverables, saving firms hours of time each day.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Canadian group benefits brokers and advisors
problem: Benefits advisors spend hours reading unstructured carrier documents (booklets, contracts, quotes, renewals) and rebuilding comparisons and client decks by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS for brokerages
product_category: AI document extraction and deliverable generation for insurance and benefits brokers
founder_names: Jason Spector; Richard Greenbaum; Michael (surname not given on YC page)
market_need_then: Group benefits brokers handle document heavy quoting and renewals manually; the founders first built tooling for investment banker presentations, then moved to benefits after meeting a veteran advisor. No sourced spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Lucite was a four person Winter 2024 team that moved from banker presentation automation to Canadian group benefits after adding a veteran advisor as co-founder. It reportedly raised about 500K dollars and became a key tool for Sterling Brokers, one of its largest customers, which acquired it in November 2026 with undisclosed terms and the CEO staying on. The outcome looks like a customer led strategic exit rather than a venture scale outcome.

name: Lumetric
one_liner: The AI Analyst For Deal Teams
