long_description: An AI coworker for business professionals that actually does the work. Models, decks, data cleanup, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Business professionals on deal teams in finance and real estate, later small and medium businesses buying embedded AI engineering
problem: Deal teams spend large amounts of time on models, decks and data cleanup that an AI coworker could produce.
business_model: B2B SaaS and AI engineering services
product_category: AI coworker for finance and deal workflows
market_need_then: Finance teams were beginning to adopt generative AI for analyst work in 2024, but no sourced spend or customer figures for Lumetric were found.
outcome_analysis: Lumetric was a two person Winter 2024 team building an AI analyst for deal teams, in a space with well funded rivals and low defensibility on top of general models. No external funding was found. In May 2026 Factory acquired it and said the team would help shape its desktop app, which reads as a talent led soft landing with undisclosed terms rather than a product outcome.

name: Lumona
one_liner: AI-enabled search engine featuring insights from social media.
long_description: Lumona is an AI-enabled search engine featuring insights from social media. When you’re looking to buy a new phone, instead of adding reddit to the end of your search and opening tabs of threads that take forever to get through, you can search on Lumona to get all of that processed for you on one page so you can make the best decision while saving time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Luthor
one_liner: Real-time governance for enterprise communications
long_description:
Luthor replaces fragmented compliance workflows with a single system that reviews, enforces, and logs every piece of marketing content the moment it’s created.

Generative AI has made content production effortless. Manual compliance review has not kept up. This gap is now the largest and fastest-growing source of risk in the enterprise.

Luthor closes that gap completely. Every claim is checked against your policies, your regulations, and your approved sources before it goes live. Marketing teams move faster. Compliance teams gain complete confidence, with every message verified and fully auditable.

Trusted by asset managers, RIAs, lenders, banks, and credit unions to operate at AI-era volume while meeting SEC, FINRA, FTC, UDAAP, and more.

Luthor eliminates the gap between what companies say and what they can stand behind.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Registered investment advisers, asset managers, banks, credit unions and lenders that must pre approve marketing content
problem: Generative AI makes marketing content fast but manual compliance review cannot keep up. Luthor checks content against rules and logs the decision.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for compliance review
product_category: Marketing compliance AI
market_need_then: The company says generative AI has outpaced manual compliance review; regulators such as NASAA later issued guidance on AI content, but sources are dated 2025 and 2026.
outcome_analysis: Luthor is an active Fall 2024 YC company with three people and named customers in wealth management on its site. No outcome news was found and funding is unverified, so only the early customer traction claim is available.

name: Mage Legal
one_liner: Automatic AI Legal Diligence
long_description: Comprehensive AI coverage across your entire data room. Surface red and yellow flags, draft memos, compare redlines, and ensure nothing falls through the cracks.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Law firms and attorneys running M&A and venture financing due diligence
problem: Reviewing data rooms for liability caps, change of control triggers and other issues takes days of attorney time. Mage automates classification, extraction and memos.
business_model: B2B SaaS for law firms
product_category: Legal AI for transactional diligence
market_need_then: Diligence is a heavy billable task for lawyers, and the founder came from the work, but no dated demand statistics were found.
outcome_analysis: Mage Legal is an active Summer 2024 YC company with a lawyer founder and a live product site. No outcome news was found, and well funded legal AI rivals are consolidating the space, so the record shows no clear result yet.

name: MagiCode
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; SaaS; B2B; Enterprise Software
one_liner: A Reliable AI Frontend Engineer
long_description: MagiCode is an AI-powered frontend agent that writes, reviews, and rigorously tests code before pushing a PR—helping busy frontend teams offload complex, repetitive tasks from their workload.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontend engineering teams that want an AI agent to write, review and test code before a pull request
problem: Frontend work involves repetitive changes and testing. MagiCode proposes an agent that opens tested pull requests.
business_model: Developer tool subscription (one directory lists from $49 per month, unverified)
product_category: AI coding agent for frontend
market_need_then: AI coding assistance was a fast growing category in 2024, but no dated source was retrieved in this research to quantify demand.
outcome_analysis: MagiCode is listed active from the Summer 2024 batch with three people. The company site could not be fetched here, no outcome news exists in the results, and funding is unverified, so its trajectory is unknown beyond onboarding users per its launch page.

name: Magic Hour
tags: Generative AI; Video; Media; API; Creator Economy
one_liner: AI media creation platform for creators and developers
long_description: Magic Hour is a browser-based creative platform and API for generating and editing video, images, and audio. Creators and teams use more than 100 tools, including face swap, lip sync, image-to-video, text-to-video, image editing, and voice generation. Developers integrate the same capabilities through our REST API, official SDKs, and hosted MCP server.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Creators, marketers and developers who generate video, image and audio with AI
problem: Making video takes ideation, shooting and editing time. Magic Hour gives point and click AI tools and an API.
business_model: Freemium credits and subscriptions plus usage based API
product_category: AI media creation platform
market_need_then: Creators wanted faster video production and generative models had just become usable in 2023. The founders cite their own parents' small business video pain.
outcome_analysis: Magic Hour is an active Winter 2024 YC company that shipped many tools, an API and press release launches through early 2026. It claims 5.2M creators, which is self reported and unverified. Its growth is attributed to viral content distribution, while funding totals across aggregators conflict.

name: Maia
one_liner: AI relationship app that keeps couples together
long_description: Maia helps couples connect more each day. Trained by relationship experts, Maia offers daily activities, personalized advice, proactive insights, quizzes and games through AI and relationship science.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Romantic couples who want AI coaching and daily connection activities
problem: Couples therapy is expensive and static relationship content does not adapt. Maia offers always available AI advice, quizzes and voice help.
business_model: Consumer subscription with in app purchases
product_category: AI relationship coaching app
market_need_then: Couples therapy cost and access are real pains, and the YC launch post contrasts Maia with static content apps, but no dated demand figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Maia is an active Winter 2024 YC company with apps on both stores and a voice feature launched in 2024. No outcome news was found, user numbers are not stated, and funding is unverified, so only product progress can be described. Many competing couples AI apps appeared in the same period.

name: Mango Health
one_liner: AI Therapy for OCD
long_description:
Mango Health is building the market-leading AI Guide for OCD. OCD is often hidden in plain sight, with research showing it takes an average of 12 years to diagnose, and nearly 2% of the world population affected.  We are on a mission to improve accessibility to the best resources available. With a focus on ERP like sessions, 24/7 support, and countless AI-guided lessons - we are looking to bring motivation and meaning back to the lives of millions at a fraction of the cost of traditional treatment. 

Start today at TheMangoHealth.com :)
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: People with OCD (consumers), and earlier primary care practices that referred patients to therapists
problem: OCD is often hidden and takes years to diagnose, and ERP therapy is costly and hard to access. The first version also tackled the gap between primary care and therapists.
business_model: Started as a referral and billing service for primary care practices with insurer claims; later a consumer AI guide for OCD (pricing not found)
product_category: Digital mental health, AI therapy guide
market_need_then: YC page cites research that OCD takes about 12 years to diagnose and affects nearly 2 percent of people. NOCD's 2021 raise shows paying demand for OCD care at the time.
outcome_analysis: Mango Health began as a primary care referral service in early 2024, then repositioned as an AI guide for OCD. YC now lists it as Inactive with a team of two, but no source states a shutdown date or cause, so the cause is not public. The only failure code supported by the record is a pivot that did not visibly find traction; funding history is unknown rather than zero.

name: Manifold Freight
one_liner: Aggregating Spot Freight Opportunities for Carriers
long_description:
Manifold is revolutionizing the spot freight procurement process for Carriers, Brokers, and Shippers. Our inaugural product transforms the booking process for spot shipments, significantly reducing empty miles and increasing revenue.  We do this by aggregating spot shipment opportunities from a variety of shipper and brokerage sources into a single location.

Andrew and Oliver bring deep domain expertise of freight from their pivotal roles at Convoy, where they were engineering leaders automating processes that were scaled to handle over 10,000 weekly shipments. This background has been instrumental in shaping Manifold's innovative approach.

In just two months since launching Manifold has achieved $5,100 in monthly revenue, showcasing the pressing demand for our product. Manifold is poised to transform this $100+ billion industry. Not only will we streamline spot freight procurement operations but we will also redefine the industry's cost structure for the better.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Trucking carriers and freight brokers buying and bidding on spot loads
problem: Spot freight opportunities are scattered across shipper portals and email, causing empty miles and slow bidding.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: Freight pricing and automation software
market_need_then: Convoy's Oct 2023 collapse left carriers without a spot-freight channel; GeekWire (May 2024) frames spot freight as scattered one-off loads across brokers, and the YC launch post claims $5,100 monthly revenue two months after launch (company-reported).
outcome_analysis: Manifold Freight was founded in Seattle by two early Convoy engineers (employees #12 and #50) in YC W24 and raised a $1.9M seed in May 2024 led by New Stack Ventures and YC, while Convoy's collapse in October 2023 and Flexport's revival of its load board shaped the market. It remains listed Active with 2-10 employees; its domain moved to getmanifold.ai and the site now stresses pricing automation and AI agents, an undated broadening of scope. No exit or later round is public, so it reads as an early company with founder-market fit and unproven traction.

name: Marblism
one_liner: AI Employees who love overtime
long_description:
We've built several businesses over the years, and each time, we faced the same challenges. We knew we needed to send sales emails, post regularly on social media, keep an eye on Google Ads, or simply manage the endless flood of emails—but somehow, these tasks always slipped through the cracks. The intention was there, but reality always got in the way.

That's why we created Marblism: AI Employees who seamlessly handle the tasks you keep putting off. No complex setups or prompts needed—just tell them about your business once and let them work quietly in the background. Suddenly, those tasks you knew you should be doing actually get done, giving you more time and mental clarity to focus on what truly matters.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Solo founders and small business owners who need sales, social, SEO, inbox and call handling work done without hiring
problem: Small business owners know they should send outreach, post on social media, watch ads and clear email, but these tasks slip. Marblism sells software agents framed as named employees that do the work in the background after a one time business briefing.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, one plan covering a roster of AI employees (a reviewer source cites about 24 USD per month billed yearly, unverified)
product_category: AI agents as employees for small business operations
market_need_then: Founders in the YC pitch say recurring marketing and admin tasks slipped through the cracks across several businesses they had built. Enthusiasm for AI assistants in early 2024 supported demand, but no independent spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: Marblism is active and reports tens of thousands of business customers in its own press release and site, with a team described as 18 people on its about page snippet. Public funding data is thin and conflicting, so no round is recorded. The wedge of persona based AI employees is easy to copy, so durable success depends on distribution and reliability, which the sources do not settle.

name: Marr Labs
one_liner: AI-voice agents that are indistinguishable from humans.
long_description:
Marr Labs is making AI-voice agents that are indistinguishable from humans. Han and Dave previously created speech tech company Vlingo that powered the first Siri app and was acquired for $225M. 


Now they are taking voice to the next level by making AI-voice agents that can handle virtually any phone-based job, from answering calls to schedule appointments to call center sales and support jobs—all at a fraction of the cost of a human agent.
 

In the US alone, businesses handle 17 billion calls a year at an average cost of $5 per call–an $85 billion addressable market.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Call heavy businesses, later focused on mortgage lenders and regulated lenders, insurers and healthcare operators
problem: Phone based jobs such as scheduling, sales and support are costly to staff. Marr Labs built voice agents meant to sound human, later adding compliance, document intake and warm transfers to licensed staff.
business_model: B2B software for voice and workflow automation, priced per deployment (pricing not found)
product_category: Conversational voice AI agents
market_need_then: The YC description cites about 17 billion US business calls a year at roughly 5 USD each, an 85 billion USD addressable market. That figure is the company's own claim.
outcome_analysis: Founders with a prior speech company sold to Nuance gave Marr Labs strong founder market fit in voice AI, and the product narrowed toward regulated lending. The company ended in September 2026 when PayNearMe bought its technology assets and hired key staff for an undisclosed price. The terms are not public, so whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing cannot be judged.

name: Matcha
tags: Machine Learning; Marketplace; Recruiting; Healthcare; AI
one_liner: The best way to hire clinical talent.
long_description:
We're building Matcha, the faster, smarter way to hire clinical talent—helping hospitals find active, qualified candidates at a fraction of the time and cost of job boards or headhunters.

Matcha engages candidates at scale, matching them to your organization by qualifications and cultural fit. Recruiters save time, hospitals save money, and candidates get a better experience—a radically better hiring model for everyone involved.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Mathos
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Education; Generative AI; Edtech; AI
one_liner: Ultimate AI Math Problem Solver to Revolutionize Personalized Learning
long_description:
Mathos AI (Formerly MathGPTPro) is the leading AI math solver that enables academic performance and productivity of both students and teachers. It has empowered over 1M students from over 200 countries in the past year, which turns the previously mission-impossible personalized learning into real. Our advanced math AI model achieves roughly 20% higher accuracy in mathematical and quantitative problem-solving capabilities then GPT4o. 

As we move forward, we will tackle the hardest problems in the educational sector, personalization, adaptive learning, and shortages of teachers, with our trial runs in schools. By automating grading, providing insightful analytics, and generating adaptive assignments, our model empowers teachers to understand what their students need and what should be provided accordingly.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Students, with teachers as a secondary user; consumer subscription
problem: Students get stuck on math homework and want step by step help. Mathos (formerly MathGPTPro) offers photo based solving, tutoring hints and progress tracking, with grading tools for teachers.
business_model: Consumer subscription app and web, with teacher tools (pricing not verified)
product_category: AI math tutor and solver
market_need_then: Students searched for math help before generative AI, and 2023 chat models made step by step explanations cheap, though they also made frequent arithmetic errors, which created room for specialised tools.
outcome_analysis: Mathos is active with a team of about five and self reported user counts ranging from one million to five million students, which are unverified marketing claims. Public funding data is limited to aggregator listings of a small YC check, so the fundraising trajectory is unknown. It competes with free chatbots and established solvers.

name: Melder
one_liner: AI formulas and document support for Microsoft Excel
long_description:
Melder is an Excel add-in that brings AI functions and document support into your spreadsheets. Upload files directly into cells, use smart formulas like =GEN, and build automations—all without leaving Excel.

Core features:
- File-to-Sheet: Drop PDFs directly into cells, then reference them in formulas.
- AI-Powered Functions: Write formulas like =GEN() or =EXTRACT() to summarize, classify, and analyze content.
- Chat Assistant: Use our AI assistant to help build your sheets or answer questions from your data, live in the workbook.

Business users use Melder to:
- Accelerate diligence by extracting insights from data rooms
- Review contracts by identifying key terms and clauses instantly
- Run market research by pulling information from competitor websites
- Synthesize transcripts by generating summaries from interviews and calls

Melder brings the power of structured spreadsheet logic to the messy, unstructured data world—no coding needed.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Excel users in finance, operations and analysis who work with documents and unstructured data in spreadsheets
problem: Excel users cannot easily run AI over PDFs, web pages and text inside cells. Melder adds AI formulas such as GEN and EXTRACT, file uploads into cells, web scraping and a chat assistant, with citations.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription via Excel add-in (pricing not found)
product_category: AI add-in for Microsoft Excel
market_need_then: Excel is the default tool for analysis, and users often paste in documents and text they cannot process with formulas. LLMs made extraction and classification inside cells newly feasible in 2024.
outcome_analysis: Melder is an early stage Excel add-in from a two person New York team that joined YC in the Fall 2024 batch. It launched publicly on Product Hunt in August 2025. Public funding data is limited to an aggregator figure, and Microsoft's own AI features in Excel pose the main risk to the standalone add-in. There is no evidence yet of a strong outcome or a failure.

name: Mem0
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: The Memory layer for AI Agents
long_description: Mem0 enhances AI assistants and agents with an intelligent memory layer, enabling personalized AI interactions. It remembers user preferences, adapts to individual needs, and continuously learns over time - ideal for customer support chatbots, AI assistants, and autonomous systems.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents and apps that need persistent memory across sessions
problem: Language models are stateless, so apps forget users between sessions. Mem0 provides an open source and hosted memory layer that extracts, stores and retrieves memories using vector, graph and key value stores.
business_model: Open source core with hosted usage based API and enterprise deployment options
product_category: Memory infrastructure for AI agents
market_need_then: The founders say users of their meditation style app kept complaining that it did not remember their progress, which led the move from Embedchain to a memory layer. Developers building agents in 2024 needed persistent context.
outcome_analysis: Mem0 pivoted from the Embedchain RAG framework to a memory layer in July 2024, rode the agent boom with an open source product and a large developer following, and announced a combined 24 million dollar seed and Series A in October 2025 led by Basis Set Ventures. TechCrunch reported API calls growing from about 35 million in the first quarter of 2025 to 186 million by the third. Rivals and model vendors add memory features, so durability is not settled.

name: Merlin AI
tags: SaaS; Construction; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: AI powered ERP for Construction
long_description:
Merlin is an AI-powered ERP for construction companies. 

We provide construction companies with a single, AI-powered platform to manage their entire business operations. Our platform unifies project management, materials management, finance, estimating, and CRM—traditionally scattered across multiple systems—into one cohesive solution. For the first time, construction firms can automate and oversee every aspect of their projects in a single, intuitive system. Today, construction companies pay for 8-17 different tools - that we eliminate the need for. 

We reduce 

- Manual work by 60%
- Cut software costs by $10,000 monthly
- Complete projects 3x faster. 

Why Now?
We're witnessing a perfect storm of factors: decades of stagnation in traditional ERP systems, a multi-billion-dollar industry built on misaligned incentives, and the transformative potential of AI. This confluence creates a rare cyclical opportunity for market upheaval. The last major shift in this space occurred in the 1990s with the advent of digital systems, and now, 30 years later, we're on the cusp of another seismic change. Customers are crying out for innovation and as AI reshapes the landscape, early customer signals indicate an eagerness for smarter, more efficient systems. It's a unique window of opportunity that opens perhaps once in a multi-decade chance to redefine an entire industry's operational backbone.

Team:
KS, a BITS Pilani grad and successful startup co-founder, and Ayantika, an IIT alumni and tech expert, bring extensive coding and product development expertise together bringing about over a decade of technical expertise. Sneha ( that’s me), with over a decade of experience in supply chain management and lean manufacturing within the construction industry, has lived the pain of using ERPs in this industry.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Construction companies (including modular and prefab builders) running 8-17 separate tools
problem: Construction firms scatter project management, materials, finance, estimating and CRM across many systems; Merlin unifies them in one AI-driven ERP.
business_model: B2B SaaS ERP (pricing not found)
product_category: AI ERP for construction
founder_names: Sneha Kumari; Ayantika Dey; Kumar Siddhartha
market_need_then: YC page says construction firms use 8-17 tools and claims 60% less manual work; the founder says she lived the pain of construction ERPs. Company claims, not independently verified.
outcome_analysis: Merlin AI went through YC Summer 2024 with a founder who spent a decade in construction supply chain and two engineers from Rippling and Swiggy. Aggregators report a roughly $500K seed and the company is active with a team of 19 (YC) in a crowded field of AI back-office tools for construction. No priced customer traction, later round or exit was found, so it has neither clearly stalled nor clearly succeeded.

name: Meticulate
one_liner: Making it easy for B2B sales teams to send stellar outbound
long_description: Meticulate is an AI-native sales platform. We make it easy for sales teams to send stellar outbound messaging at scale. Instead of using boilerplate campaigns, Meticulate codifies your rules and strategies (e.g. “CFOs want to hear an ROI calc upfront”) and combines them with deep research to send custom sequences to every lead. We’re serving leading GTM teams today (incl OpenAI, Noda, ThreeKit), and are backed by leading AI investors: Y Combinator, Link, Cervin Ventures.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B sales teams, especially industrial and energy sellers, running outbound
problem: Outbound sequences are generic. Meticulate encodes a team's sales rules and combines them with prospect research and buying signals to generate individual outreach.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription: about 950 USD per month for founder led sales with 2 seats, from 18,000 USD per year for AE and BDR teams (company site)
product_category: AI prospecting and outbound sales platform
market_need_then: Sales teams were already paying for outbound tooling, and the company's customer list on the YC page names OpenAI, Noda and ThreeKit as users, though the demand figures are company claims.
outcome_analysis: Meticulate is an active five person company selling AI outbound tooling to industrial sellers, with named customers including OpenAI. Public funding data is limited to aggregator listings of a small YC check, so the trajectory beyond the batch is unknown. The category is crowded and consolidating, which is the main risk.

name: Metofico
tags: SaaS; Data Science; No-code; Data Visualization
one_liner: No Code Data Analysis for Life Science Research
long_description:
Metofico provides a no-code data analysis tool tailored for the life sciences. Our platform enables life scientists to analyse complex/massive datasets and extract necessary insights without needing advanced programming skills. This accessibility helps both researchers new to data science and experts save months of work.

Metofico aims to be the leading centralized platform for data analysis in life science research, covering a wide range of applications from brain activity analysis (like photometry and EEG) to AI-powered detection and tracking of research animals. Our vision is to accelerate research processes and enhance the quality of research outputs across the board. By streamlining complex data analysis and making it more accessible, we’re committed to driving forward scientific discoveries and innovation.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Academic and industry life science labs analysing neuroscience and animal behaviour data without programmers
problem: Bench scientists spend months writing custom code to analyse fiber photometry, EEG and animal video data, and the analysis is inconsistent between labs.
business_model: SaaS subscription for no-code analysis tools
product_category: Scientific data analysis software (life science)
market_need_then: Founders describe labs analysing complex datasets in a tedious, inconsistent way; open-source GUI tools appearing in 2021 to 2023 show demand for non-programmer analysis.
outcome_analysis: Metofico is an active two person London company from the Winter 2024 batch with a tiny reported raise and a niche scientific market. No exit or shutdown is reported, so the outcome is still open; the main risks are a small market and free academic tools, while strength is the founders' direct lab experience.

name: Metreecs
one_liner: AI-powered demand forecasting for retail
long_description: Metreecs helps retailers plan, buy, and allocate products using AI-demand forecasting. We prevent overstock and out-of-stock situations, allowing clients to eliminate waste, free up capital, and drive higher sales.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Retailers in Europe and the United States that need to plan purchases and reorder stock
problem: Retailers carry too much stock or run out. Metreecs forecasts demand with a mix of over 30 statistical and machine learning models and automates replenishment and reallocation.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Retail demand forecasting and inventory optimization
founder_names: Thibaut Pellegrin; Martin Dimitrov; Elie Dufeu
market_need_then: Overstock and stockouts are costly for retailers; the company reports cutting inventory by up to 15 percent and raising turnover by up to 5 percent (company claims, unverified).
outcome_analysis: Metreecs, a Paris based team in YC's Fall 2024 batch, announced a seed round of about 2.7 million euros in October 2025 from YC, Kima Ventures, Bpifrance, Monte Carlo Capital and Founders Future, alongside a launch in Italy. It claims European and US customers without naming them. It is early, so no strong outcome or failure can be assigned.

name: Mica AI
one_liner: Turn employees' AI skills into shared company infrastructure
long_description:
Today, as employees teach AI how to perform valuable company work, the resulting capabilities often remain trapped on individual laptops or scattered across chats and repositories. 

Mica gives each company a managed, agent-native internal marketplace where employees can publish capabilities, discover them by describing the task they need help with, and install them through the AI tools they already use. Mica tracks ownership, requirements, permissions, and team customizations while letting employees contribute improvements back to the shared version for evaluation and approval.

The result: employees stop rebuilding workflows their coworkers have already solved, useful improvements spread across the organization without overwriting team-specific customizations, and security gains visibility without blocking bottom-up innovation. Mica turns scattered AI work into institutional knowledge that compounds.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies whose employees build prompts, skills and agents that need sharing and governance (current product); B2B sales teams (original product)
problem: Useful AI capabilities built by employees stay on one laptop. Mica provides a managed internal marketplace to publish, discover, install, verify and improve them. The original launch product automated B2B sales follow up from call recordings.
business_model: B2B SaaS (pricing not found)
product_category: AI capability distribution and governance layer; originally AI sales follow up agents
market_need_then: Sales teams record calls but follow up poorly; the founders built the first product around that gap. For the later product, the site's argument is that employee built agents die on one laptop, which is a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Mica launched in the YC Summer 2024 batch with a sales follow up product and now presents a different product, a governed marketplace for company AI capabilities, with a three person team. The company site shows Y Combinator, General Catalyst and Zero Knowledge Ventures logos. No amounts or dates are public, so the funding trajectory and the reason for the pivot are unknown.

name: Miden
one_liner: Card issuer processor and banking stack for businesses in Sub-…
long_description:
Miden is building a modern infrastructure that facilitates the launch of card programs and various financial products for businesses in Sub-Sahran Africa. Just by reducing integration time, card fraud, improving stability, and being customer focused we quickly rose to top 5 in TPV among card issuing Fintechs in Sub-Saharan Africa within 8 months of launch.

We’re going to build the first comprehensive fintech and banking software stack for Africa, based on modern technology. We’re starting with a card issuer-processor.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Businesses, fintechs and financial institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa that need to issue cards and run payment products
problem: Card programs and financial products in Sub-Saharan Africa are slow to launch, fraud-prone and unstable on legacy processors. Miden sells an API-first issuer-processor and banking stack.
business_model: B2B API infrastructure, card issuing and processing fees tied to card volume
product_category: Card issuing and payments infrastructure (fintech)
market_need_then: Account ownership in Sub-Saharan Africa had risen but the region was under one percent of global card volume (per company positioning). Union54's July 2022 halt left fintechs looking for virtual card providers.
outcome_analysis: Miden remains active as of March 2026, shipping NFC tap to pay and wallet support, and claims top five card issuer volume in Sub-Saharan Africa within eight months of launch. Those traction figures are self reported and differ across sources, and no verified funding round was found, so the outcome is still open and the data on funding is thin rather than negative.

name: Midship
one_liner: AI for SOX testing
long_description: Midship is rebuilding internal audit from the ground up. We're starting with SOX testing by building AI agents that perform audit work end to end, giving auditors leverage to focus on higher-value risk and advisory work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Internal audit and SOX compliance teams at public companies
problem: SOX control testing is repetitive, document heavy manual work done in spreadsheets, with talent shortages and rising compliance cost.
business_model: B2B SaaS (web app plus Excel add-in)
product_category: AI agents for SOX testing and internal audit
founder_names: Kieran Taylor; Aahel Iyer; Max Maio
market_need_then: Public companies must test internal controls annually under Sarbanes-Oxley and the work was manual; by 2024 incumbents were launching AI features, signaling demand.
outcome_analysis: Midship was a three person Summer 2024 team applying AI agents to SOX testing, a regulated and recurring workflow with budget. It reported use at large public companies, raised a 4.15 million dollar seed led by Costanoa in January 2026, and four months later was acquired by Optro, the market leader formerly called AuditBoard, with founders joining the product team. Terms were undisclosed.

name: Million
one_liner: Tools for agent verification
long_description:
Remember the first time you hit  and your code actually worked? Something that didn't exist before, now alive on your screen.

Today, coding agents can do that, orders of magnitude faster. But their verification is shallow at best. The faster agents generate code, the wider the gap grows. Nothing verifies software at the speed agents ship code.

We believe verification unlocks long-horizon coding agents: agents that run for days and prove their work as they go.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Frontier coding agent labs and frontend developers (originally React developers wanting faster apps)
problem: Coding agents generate code faster than it can be verified, and React apps were slow. Million began as a React optimizing compiler and now sells environments and evals for coding agents.
business_model: Open source developer tools with a commercial layer, now data, environments and evals for agent labs
product_category: Developer tools and AI agent verification
market_need_then: React performance complaints were common and Million.js had adoption in open source projects (85 per the founder's 2023 paper snippet). Later demand shifted to agent verification as coding agents spread.
outcome_analysis: Million is active and has pivoted from a React performance compiler toward verification data for coding agents. Developer goodwill from open source and star counts is the main asset, but no verified funding or revenue data exists, so the trajectory is unknown rather than good or bad.

name: Mineflow
one_liner: Mineflow predicts the shape and location of mineral deposits
long_description:
Mineflow is an AI platform for mineral exploration. We generate predictions for mineral deposit shapes and locations, empowering mining companies from initial exploration to advanced feasibility studies.

Geologists need to know precisely where their deposits are because drilling is expensive. In early trials with a lithium mining company, we found that Mineflow predicts the shape of hard rock lithium deposits more than an order of magnitude more accurately than our competitors.

Ryan received a BS in Artificial Intelligence from Carnegie Mellon's School of Computer Science where he helped teach both the grad-level Deep Learning course and the grad-level Search Engines course. He built ML models at Google in the Display Ads optimization org for 2 years and launched products that generated ~125m USD in ARR.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Exploration geologists, junior miners and mining companies
problem: Drilling is expensive and geologists need to know where deposits are. Mineflow builds custom AI models and a searchable database to predict deposit shape and location.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for exploration data and prediction models
product_category: AI mineral exploration software
market_need_then: Mineral exploration drilling is costly and the energy transition raised demand for lithium and critical metals. The company's own page cites an A$337K estimate for ten RC holes, a company figure.
outcome_analysis: Mineflow is a two person Summer 2024 company that appears active, with a public database product and a subscription listing. No news of acquisition or shutdown was found, and funding is unconfirmed, so the outcome cannot be judged beyond early stage.

name: MinusX
tags: Machine Learning; Analytics; Data Science; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Open source agentic BI for founders
long_description: MinusX is a state-of-the-art data agent that can build the best dashboards for your data, and notify you when something's up. You can interrogate all your data on our open source BI platform via Slack or MCP. Connect your data, and put agents to work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Founders and small data teams using Metabase or other BI tools
problem: Business users cannot get trustworthy answers from data without analysts. MinusX offers an AI data analyst agent, first as a Chrome extension for Metabase and Jupyter, now an open source agentic BI platform.
business_model: Open source core with managed cloud subscription
product_category: AI business intelligence
market_need_then: Generative AI made natural language data analysis feasible in 2024 and BI users wanted self serve answers. Evidence is mainly product positioning and the YC launch on Hacker News.
outcome_analysis: MinusX is active, open sourced its product in September 2024 and now claims SOC 2 Type II and a top ranking on a Berkeley data agent benchmark as of June 2026, all company claims. Funding is only reported by aggregators, so success or stall cannot be judged yet.

name: Miru
one_liner: Config Management for Robotics
long_description:
Miru makes it easy for robotics teams to manage, version, and deploy robot configurations. Developers use our well-documented APIs and UI components to automate configuration updates for both engineers and operators.

In the long term, we're building software infrastructure to accelerate the automation of the physical world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robotics and IoT companies running fleets of devices
problem: Teams scaling robot fleets struggle to deploy software and manage configuration across devices. Miru provides config management, deployment and access control for robots.
business_model: B2B SaaS for robotics fleet configuration
product_category: Robotics deployment and config management infrastructure
founder_names: Armel Talla; Vedant Nair; Benjamin Smidt
market_need_then: Robotics deployments were growing and teams built config tooling in house. Evidence is positioning on the YC launch post, which drew about 235 upvotes per an aggregator.
outcome_analysis: Miru is an active three founder team from UT Austin that previously built Clips AI and now sells robot fleet config tooling. It has shipped features such as access control per its CEO's LinkedIn activity, but funding is only reported by aggregators, so the outcome stage is early and unproven.

name: Mito Health
tags: Consumer Health Services; Digital Health; AI
one_liner: At-cost preventive health: Labs, Scans, Genetics, Supplements and Rx
long_description:
Mito Health is a U.S. service that lets individuals order 12,000+ lab tests, scans, supplements, genetics, home kits, and Rx without a traditional doctor’s visit. Members pay $9 per month to access every product at cost and get itemized receipts with no hidden markups.

The average member saves about $300 a year on a full baseline panel.

What the $9/mth Mito membership gets you:

- 11,000+ practitioner-grade supplements at 35% below Amazon (Thorne, Pure Encapsulations, Life Extension, Ritual, Momentous, Seed)
- 1,200+ lab tests from Quest, Labcorp and BioReference at cost · 49 states · HSA/FSA eligible
- DEXA body composition, bone density, coronary calcium (CAC), whole-body MRI, 30x whole genome sequencing, gut microbiome, multi-cancer early detection
- Every result in one longitudinal record, ordered and reviewed by a partner clinician over concierge
- No markups on tests. No commissions from labs or brands.
- No padded "wellness panels," no upsells, no annual contract; you can cancel anytime.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Health conscious consumers wanting at-cost preventive testing, starting with executives in Singapore and then the US
problem: Preventive labs, scans and genetics are expensive and hard to interpret. Mito sells testing at cost plus clinician review with a membership.
business_model: Membership ($9 per month or $99 per year) plus at-cost tests, consults and at-home draw fees
product_category: Consumer preventive health and longevity marketplace
founder_names: Kenneth Lou; Joel Kek; Tee-Ming Chew; Ryan Ware
market_need_then: Rising consumer interest in longevity and preventive screening; founder says his father's cancer motivated the focus (podcast summary). No quantified demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Mito raised a US$1.3M pre-seed in April 2023 and a US$2.2M seed in March 2025, for about US$4M in total per the company. It exited in person services in Singapore in March 2025 to go digital first and focus on the US, showing a market shift, but the company remains active so the outcome is still open.

name: Model ML
one_liner: The AI for Financial Services.
long_description:
Team:
Chaz: Founder of Fat Llama YC S17 - Acquired by Hygglo. Responsible for Business and Sales 
Arns: Founder of Fancy S20 - Acquired by Gopuff, Responsible for tech and product.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Investment banks, private equity firms and consultancies
problem: Finance professionals spend huge time on manual research, analysis and building decks and models in Excel and PowerPoint.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS for AI workflow automation inside Microsoft Office
product_category: AI workspace for financial services
market_need_then: Banks and PE firms spend heavily on junior analyst time for research and slide production; LLM advances in 2023 to 2024 made automation feasible.
outcome_analysis: Model ML, founded by two repeat YC founders, emerged from stealth in February 2025 with a 12 million dollar seed and raised a 75 million dollar Series A in November 2025 led by FT Partners. Strong founder track record, timing with LLM adoption in finance and quick enterprise traction explain the rapid growth, though it faces well funded finance AI rivals.

name: Modus
tags: Finance; B2B; HR Tech; Operations; AI
one_liner: Unlock revenue per employee with AI-powered headcount management
long_description:
Modus helps companies hire and retain only the people they need instead of becoming bloated messes. Modus connects your HRIS, ATS, and analyzes extensive data across your organization so leaders can detect, inspect, and correct their workforce plans - without relying on spreadsheets or complex systems. 
 
Lin experienced these challenges firsthand as a VP BizOps at HashiCorp, scaling from 100 employees to IPO, while Chris and Amar faced similar issues scaling 40+ person teams as a fractional CTO. They’re motivated by the belief that companies should have the least number of employees possible.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Finance, people and revenue leaders at growing companies, especially sales organizations
problem: Companies over hire and miss sales ramp, coverage and coaching gaps because headcount data sits in separate HRIS, ATS and CRM systems. Modus joins the data and flags issues early.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: AI headcount and sales planning management
market_need_then: Post 2022 efficiency pressure made headcount cost control a priority. Evidence is the company's own positioning of revenue per employee; no external data found.
outcome_analysis: Modus is a three founder Summer 2024 company with an ex HashiCorp CEO that is listed as active. No funding, customers or outcome news was found, and several unrelated companies share the name, so search visibility is a risk. The data supports only that it is early stage, not that it failed.

name: Momentic
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Mo, the AI QA engineer that bug-bashes your app before every release
long_description:
Momentic makes Mo, the AI QA engineer. Point Mo at your app with a goal and a swarm of agents bug-bashes it the way your team would, then reports every bug with repro steps, logs, and a video replay.

Notion, Whatnot, Retool, Webflow, Framer, and 1,600+ teams use Momentic.

Teams also use Momentic to write end-to-end tests in plain English, run them in CI, and let agents triage and maintain the suite across web and mobile.

Learn more at momentic.ai
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineering teams that need end-to-end and QA testing (web and mobile)
problem: Tests are brittle and slow to write and maintain, so bugs reach production; Momentic uses AI agents to write, run and maintain tests and bug-bash apps.
business_model: B2B SaaS (usage/seat-based; pricing not found)
product_category: AI software testing / QA automation
market_need_then: Wu says testing was the biggest pain point on every team he worked on; the company argues AI coding increased code volume while verification lagged. Dated founding-era evidence not found.
outcome_analysis: Momentic is active and growing: a $3.7M seed in March 2025 and a $15M Series A in November 2025 led by Standard Capital, with reported 2,600 users and customers like Notion, Webflow and Retool. Success factors are visible traction and the AI coding tailwind that raised demand for verification. Open-source frameworks and model vendors remain competition.

name: Monumint
one_liner: Conversational AI purpose-built for financial services
long_description: Monumint is conversational AI for financial services. We help banks, credit unions, and lenders build lasting customer relationships across the entire customer journey from account opening and loan origination to servicing and collections. Our AI agents are omni-channel, take action inside the systems financial institutions already use, and are built with compliance at their core.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Banks, credit unions and lenders buying conversational AI agents for customer service, origination and collections
problem: Financial institutions handle account opening, loan origination, servicing and collections through slow, manual, call-center workflows. Monumint builds compliant AI agents that act inside their existing systems.
business_model: B2B enterprise software, per-deployment or usage contracts
product_category: Conversational AI for financial services
market_need_then: Credit unions were moving to AI chatbots in 2024, with nearly 3 in 10 planning investment per a survey reported by eMarketer, and delinquency and service costs pushed demand.
outcome_analysis: The founders raised about 3.2 million dollars as OmniAI, then spent roughly ten months rebuilding as Monumint for banks, drawing on their banking backgrounds. A report cited by aggregators claims 20 paying customers, unverified. The company is early with crowded incumbents, so the outcome is open.

name: Moonset Health
one_liner: AI for Post-Acute Senior Care (Hospice, Home Health, Skilled Nursing…
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hospice, home health and skilled nursing providers
problem: Clinicians in post-acute care spend hours on documentation and compliance. Moonset records visits and IDG meetings, writes notes and writes them back to the customer's EHR.
business_model: B2B SaaS for care agencies
product_category: AI clinical documentation for post-acute care
founder_names: Tyler Rich; Kevin Bao; Sherril Wang
market_need_then: Documentation burden in hospice is high per company claims such as 1 to 2 hours saved per nurse per day at one hospice customer. No independent data found.
outcome_analysis: Moonset is active and claims 50,000 hours saved and a named hospice case study, all self reported. Larger EHR vendors launched competing scribes in 2025 and 2026, a risk, but no outcome event or funding was verified, so this is an early stage company with an open result.

name: Moonshine
one_liner: The platform for automated hiring and workforce decisions.
long_description: Moonshine creates a platform that connects to applications where hiring, employment, and contracting decisions are made and takes care of notices, explanations, recourse, and risk assessments.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Employers and HR software vendors making automated hiring decisions (per the YC directory description); the YC launch post instead targets developers needing video understanding APIs
problem: Companies using automated tools for hiring and workforce decisions must give notices, explanations, recourse and risk assessments under new laws. The sources conflict on whether the company actually works on this or on video search.
business_model: B2B software or API, pricing not public
product_category: AI compliance for hiring decisions (directory) / video understanding API (launch post) / legal text as structured data (current website title)
market_need_then: Laws such as NYC Local Law 144 (enforced from July 2023) required bias audits and notices for automated employment decision tools, creating compliance demand.
outcome_analysis: Moonshine is an early stage Fall 2024 company with only two people and no verifiable funding, so no outcome has occurred. Its public descriptions conflict: the YC directory text describes hiring compliance, the YC launch post describes a video understanding API, and the website title now describes law as structured data, which suggests repeated repositioning that I cannot date.

name: Moreta
tags: Fintech; Payments; Consumer; Travel; Consumer Finance
one_liner: Payments made easy for international travelers.
long_description:
At Moreta, we simplify payments for international travelers, letting you pay for anything using just your phone. Done is the hassle of searching for the best cash exchange rates or ATMs on your next trip. With Moreta, paying local merchants is easy.

We came up with Moreta while on our own backpacking adventures. Watching locals pay with a simple scan while we fumbled with cards and cash. So, we created a solution. By syncing with local payment networks, Moreta lets you pay like a local securely and digitally, without needing a bank account in every country.

We’re starting in Asia, where QR code digital wallets are taking over and are now the top choice at checkout. As these wallets start to join forces for cross-border payments, Moreta is the first to bridge the gap for international travelers from card-centric markets to tap into these local networks. Moreta will target 200 million travelers arriving in the region each year, who together have $410 billion in everyday expenditure.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: International travelers from card-centric markets spending in QR-wallet countries
problem: Travelers cannot easily pay local QR wallets without a local bank account, so they rely on cash, ATMs and card fees.
business_model: Consumer payments app with a 1.5% fee per payment (company website)
product_category: Travel payments wallet
market_need_then: QR wallets were becoming dominant at checkout across Asia while foreign cards were often unaccepted; YC page cites 200 million arriving travelers a year (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Moreta is an active Summer 2024 company that has launched in about 15 countries and reports 250,000 users and $70 million in processed volume in a September 2026 press release, which is company-reported. Funding disclosure is thin, so the traction cannot be compared with capital raised; the main risks are Alipay+ style incumbents and licensing across many countries.

name: NanoCorp
one_liner: Autonomous Companies Run by AI Working While You Sleep.
long_description: NanoCorp is the platform to create and run autonomous companies. In just one prompt, get an autonomous company run by an agent that maximizes revenues while trying to avoid bankruptcy with no human intervention.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individuals and small teams who want AI agents to run a business on a budget
problem: Starting and operating a business requires many repeated tasks; NanoCorp lets an owner set a mission and budget and have agents handle content, outreach, ops and ads.
business_model: Usage-based credits for agent runs
product_category: Autonomous AI business platform
market_need_then: Agent frameworks were emerging in early 2024 but demand for fully autonomous companies was unproven.
outcome_analysis: NanoCorp is a one-person Winter 2024 company that still operates. A single interview summary says it has been profitable since summer 2026 with about 1.7 million agent runs, but that is unverified and no funding data was found. The outcome cannot yet be classified, and competition from similar autonomous company products emerged later.

name: Navier AI
one_liner: Agent-Driven Engineering
long_description:
Navier AI is building the first Agent-Driven Engineering platform.

We believe engineers should focus on designing great products, not wrestling with simulation software.

Navier AI makes it simple to run CFD simulations at scale through our web-based platform built on OpenFOAM, the industry-standard solver for CFD. Our AI agents autonomously handle the complex, time-consuming steps of simulation—from geometry cleanup and meshing to solver configuration and cloud resource management.

By automating the tedious parts of the workflow, we enable engineering teams to move faster, explore more design possibilities, and spend their time on high-value engineering decisions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware and aerospace engineering teams running CFD and other simulations
problem: Engineers spend most of their time on geometry cleanup, meshing, solver setup and cloud management instead of design.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform plus desktop app, pricing not public
product_category: AI agents for engineering simulation
market_need_then: CFD workflows are slow and expert dependent; partnership with Rescale in March 2024 showed cloud demand for simulation compute.
outcome_analysis: Navier raised a $5.6M seed led by GV and HCVC with YC in December 2025, almost two years after its Winter 2024 batch, so it stayed small before launching from stealth. Founders from SpaceX and Aurora give strong domain credibility. Success now depends on agent reliability and displacing entrenched simulation suites.

name: NetworkOcean
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Cloud Computing; ClimateTech; AI
one_liner: We build floating solar data centers
long_description: We build floating solar data centers to reduce time-to-first-power by 10x. We powered an H100 in the bay, from a paper sketch to serving a customer within 60 days.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI compute customers needing fast access to powered GPU capacity
problem: Land based data centers wait years for grid power; floating solar data centers aim to cut time to first power by 10x.
business_model: Compute hosting on self-built floating infrastructure
product_category: Floating solar data centers
competitors_at_founding: Microsoft Project Natick; Nautilus Data Technologies
market_need_then: AI data center demand outstripped grid capacity in 2024, with permitting and interconnect delays a common complaint.
outcome_analysis: NetworkOcean began with a 2024 underwater data center plan that drew regulator scrutiny for lacking permits, then pivoted to a floating solar design and by October 2026 reported running a customer H100 workload on a 20kW array. No funding was confirmed, so it is unclear whether capital can support the 1MW at sea goal for 2027.

name: Newton
one_liner: AI-powered phone platform for dentists
long_description: Newton is the AI phone system built for retail healthcare practices—starting with dentists. We replace outdated phone systems and clunky communication tools with a modern agentic platform that handles scheduling, billing, and patient communication.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Dental practices and dental service organizations (DSOs)
problem: Dental front offices miss calls and lose revenue to slow scheduling, insurance checks and unmanaged patient outreach.
business_model: B2B SaaS to dental groups, pricing not public
product_category: AI front office and phone platform for dentistry
market_need_then: Dental offices commonly miss calls and have unfilled schedules; the YC page frames old phone systems and clunky communication tools as the pain.
outcome_analysis: Newton started as the Hemingway scheduler and became a broader AI front office platform used by roughly twenty dental groups listed on its site. It raised a $3.8M seed in October 2025, nearly two years after the Winter 2024 batch. The next test is whether it can win DSOs against a crowd of AI receptionist entrants.

name: No Logo
tags: Consumer; Manufacturing; E-commerce; Supply Chain; AI
one_liner: Turn ideas into physical products
long_description:
No Logo is building the orchestration layer for creating viral consumer products. The manufacturing world is full of capable, underutilized overseas factories with the machines, tooling, and engineers to build winning products – but no way to connect them to the creators and brands with the ideas and distribution. As a result, bringing a new product to market has traditionally taken 6-12 months, tens of thousands of dollars, and a team of 20-30 people.

No Logo collapses that. Using generative AI, we take a creator's product idea, visualize it, break it into core components and manufacturing processes, and match each step to the right factory in our network – turning an idea into a shippable product in just a few weeks.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Creators and brands with product ideas and audiences
problem: Bringing a physical product to market takes 6 to 12 months, tens of thousands of dollars and a large team; creators lack access to capable overseas factories.
business_model: Product development and manufacturing orchestration, revenue from products sold or services, details not public
product_category: AI assisted consumer product manufacturing platform
market_need_then: Creators with large audiences had product ideas but no manufacturing access; the company claims it launched hundreds of products and reached creator audiences over 90M people.
outcome_analysis: No Logo is an active Summer 2024 company with 15 people that connects creators to overseas factories. The YC page reports $5M raised to date, which is a good sign for a hardware oriented consumer company, but no round detail was verified. Its edge is creator distribution and factory relationships, which are replicable by sourcing platforms.

name: Nuanced
one_liner: the AI coding app for thinking.
long_description:
Nuanced is a desktop app for building software. 

Agents help developers turn rough ideas into clear specs, then stay connected to the work as agents build.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers who build software with AI agents
problem: Agent coding threads bury context and decisions; Nuanced turns rough ideas into specs and keeps agents connected to the plan. Originally the company targeted detection of AI-generated images for platforms like dating apps.
business_model: Prosumer desktop software; earlier API for image detection with pricing on request
product_category: AI coding workspace (earlier AI image detection API)
market_need_then: Deepfake and synthetic profile images worried dating apps and marketplaces in 2024, but the sources show established vendors already serving them.
outcome_analysis: Nuanced is an active two person YC W24 company that has changed direction from AI image detection to coding-agent tooling and now a desktop planning app. Only about $500K of YC-stage money is shown by aggregators, and no traction metrics are public. The story is still unresolved, with a crowded AI coding market and a generic name as headwinds.

name: Octolane AI
one_liner: Revenue Superintelligence
long_description: Every account gets an agent that finds the next best action, does it once you approve, and gets smarter with every deal.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B sales teams and revenue organizations that currently use Salesforce or HubSpot
problem: Reps spend time on manual CRM updates and deciding next actions; Octolane's agents propose and perform sales actions after approval.
business_model: B2B SaaS (AI CRM); pricing not found
product_category: AI-native CRM / sales automation
founder_names: One Chowdhury; Md Abdul Halim Rafi
market_need_then: Press coverage (April 2025) says customers were eager to switch from Salesforce and HubSpot; the company reported about 200 customers and a 5,000-person waitlist. No demand evidence dated at founding was found.
outcome_analysis: Octolane is still active as of the YC listing, with a 4-person team. It raised a $2.6M seed in April 2025, about a year after the Winter 2024 batch, and reported about 200 customers with a waitlist. Founders have prior small exits. Outcome is unresolved; no later round or exit was found, and the seed figure varies by database ($3M elsewhere).

name: Ocular AI
tags: Machine Learning; Speech Recognition; Data Engineering; AI
one_liner: Applied AI Data Research Lab Encoding Human Expertise into Machines…
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and large enterprises buying expert and audio training data and evaluations (current); mid-market and enterprise companies buying enterprise search (at launch)
problem: AI models lack real conversational and expert data; Ocular supplies expert networks, datasets and benchmarks.
business_model: Data and evaluation services plus datasets
product_category: AI data research lab (expert network, voice data, benchmarks)
market_need_then: Companies struggled to find information across scattered SaaS apps, and generative AI copilots were a new category in early 2024.
outcome_analysis: Ocular AI launched in Winter 2024 as enterprise search, then reoriented to selling expert and voice data and benchmarks to AI labs, and announced a $2M pre-seed led by Drive Capital in October 2026. It reports seven-figure revenue without precise figures, so traction is promising but unverified. The pivot moved it away from a crowded Glean and Microsoft dominated market.

name: OddsView
one_liner: The Bloomberg Terminal of Sports Betting
long_description:
OddsView is the one-stop-shop for sports betting tools and media. 

The OddsView terminal allows users to browse millions of odds updated in real time to find the best bets. Users can access familiar features like positive expected value and arbitrage finders, as well as exclusive tools such as historical odds charts, all within a single platform.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Odo
tags: SaaS; Productivity; Email; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Your email assistant because you deserve a better morning
long_description: Odo is your email assistant because you deserve a better morning. Odo can help you organize, draft emails, and follow-up effortlessly after meetings.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Busy professionals and founders who live in Gmail and want help triaging, drafting and following up on email
problem: Email triage and follow-up consume the morning. Odo sorts the inbox, flags priority messages, drafts replies in the user's voice and sends a daily brief.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per user (pricing not found)
product_category: AI email assistant
market_need_then: Email overload is a long-standing pain and generative AI made drafting and triage feasible in 2023 and 2024. No company specific demand evidence (customer counts, revenue) was found.
outcome_analysis: Odo is an active two person YC Summer 2024 company building an AI email assistant. No funding round beyond YC, no exit and no traction figures were found in public sources, so the outcome is undetermined. The category was crowded and the product easy to copy, which makes differentiation and distribution the main open risks.

name: OffDeal
one_liner: AI-native investment bank for small businesses
long_description: OffDeal is an AI-native investment bank, offering small business owners a faster, cheaper way to sell their companies at premium prices. Our AI technology automates most of the grunt work typically done by analysts at larger Wall Street banks, enabling our in-house M&A advisors to focus more on strategic client interactions, leading to better outcomes for both sellers and buyers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Owners of small and mid-sized businesses (company says $5M to $100M in sales) who want to sell, plus institutional buyers
problem: Small businesses are too small for traditional investment banks and are left to brokers or going it alone. OffDeal uses AI to do analyst-style buyer matching and outreach so a small advisor team can run auction-style sales cheaply.
business_model: Success fee on the transaction (TechCrunch reported 5% to 10% of transaction value in Sept 2024); no upfront fee per company site
product_category: AI-enabled M&A advisory (sell-side investment bank for small businesses)
market_need_then: Traditional investment banks ignore small deals and brokers are fragmented. The company claims a database of 2 million US small businesses that may sell (TechCrunch, Sept 2024).
outcome_analysis: OffDeal raised a $4.7M seed in September 2024 and a $12M Series A in July 2025 led by Radical Ventures, within about ten months, which signals fast traction in AI-enabled small business M&A. It remains active and no exit or Series B was found. Success rests on a founder who lived the problem, an engineering partner from large tech and a model where AI supplements human advisors.

name: Offstream
one_liner: Vanta for carbon compliance
long_description:
Offstream is Vanta for carbon compliance. 

Today, every new infrastructure project, from data centers to biomass power plants has a complicated mess of local, state, federal, and private sector standards that they must understand and comply with to make their projects profitable.

Offstream solves this by using LLMs to parse regulations, generate technical reports for customers, and manage 100,000+ operational data points on project’s lifecycles. We cut the time customers spend on compliance by 90% and at 1/5th of the cost of alternatives.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Carbon removal project developers, especially industrial biochar and other biogenic pathways, that need certification, life cycle assessment and registry reporting
problem: Carbon removal projects must satisfy a messy set of local, state, federal and voluntary registry standards, and developers do this with spreadsheets and consultants. Offstream uses LLMs to parse rules, generate technical reports and manage operational data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for project developers (pricing not found)
product_category: Carbon compliance and dMRV software
market_need_then: Carbon removal developers face growing certification burden as 45Q and 45Z incentives and voluntary standards expanded; the company claims it cuts compliance time by 90% at one fifth of the cost (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Offstream is an active Denver YC Summer 2024 company with about ten people selling compliance and dMRV software to biochar and carbon removal developers. No verified funding round, exit or traction numbers are public, so the outcome is undetermined. Registries and MRV vendors were shipping overlapping tools, which makes the niche focus on biochar the main source of advantage.

name: Oma Care
one_liner: Get paid for taking care of your parents.
long_description: We are building the technical infrastructure to train and pay the 53M family caregivers in the US.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Unpaid family caregivers in the US who could qualify for Medicaid or Medicare compensation programs; payers and agencies are possible later buyers
problem: Millions of family caregivers are unpaid because enrolling in state and federal compensation programs is confusing. Oma Care uses an AI agent to check eligibility, handle enrollment calls and forms, and then run training, payroll and billing.
business_model: Likely a share of Medicaid or Medicare reimbursement through payroll and billing services; the sources do not state the take
product_category: Digital health, family caregiver enrollment and payment infrastructure
market_need_then: KFF reports that all responding states pay some family caregivers through Medicaid home care programs, and the company cites 53M US family caregivers; the gap is enrollment friction and awareness.
outcome_analysis: Oma Care is an active two person YC Winter 2024 company with no verified funding beyond YC, no traction figures and no exit. The founders lived the caregiver problem, which supports founder market fit, but the model depends on state Medicaid rules and funding, which KFF flags as at risk. A site footer shows the company entity as RestAssured MD Inc. in 2025, suggesting a possible name or entity change that sources do not explain.

name: OneGrep
tags: Generative AI; B2B; DevOps; Conversational AI
one_liner: AI Agent for DevOps Workflow Automation
long_description:
OneGrep is a DevOps Agent that helps engineers automate manual devops tasks. It works across integrations that teams have to search, correlate, and operate automated tasks like runbook automation during incidents.

OneGrep specializes across devops tools to help teams release code faster and more reliably so that engineers can spend more time building rather than being trained in bespoke tools like Observability, Ci/Cd, or Infra.
    
Achintya and Brian are technical co-founders who have deep domain expertise in building and operating systems at scale at Coinbase, Disney, and Amazon. Achintya led the Search Team at Disney enabling DisneyPlus to scale to 70M users in two weeks. Brian was a founding engineer on the team that built the Incident Management Platform at Amazon that helps 30k DAUs in Amazon resolve critical incidents every day.
    
https://www.onegrep.dev
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering and platform teams at software companies that run incidents, CI/CD and observability across many tools
problem: Engineers lose time searching and correlating across observability, CI/CD and infrastructure tools during incidents and release work. OneGrep is an agent that automates these tasks, such as runbook automation during incidents, and helps reduce observability costs.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (pricing not found)
product_category: AI DevOps and SRE agent
market_need_then: On-call and incident work is a recognized cost for engineering teams and LLM agents made automation of investigative steps plausible in 2023 and 2024. No company specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: OneGrep is an active two person YC Winter 2024 company from founders with large company infrastructure experience at Disney Streaming, Amazon and Coinbase. No verified funding beyond YC, no traction figures and no exit were found. The AI SRE category later became crowded with better funded entrants, so execution speed and integration depth are the open questions.

name: Ontra Mobility
tags: Civic Tech; GovTech; Climate; Transportation; AI
one_liner: Platform for cities to optimize transit
long_description: Ontra Mobility is founded by two former Googler engineers with PhDs in operations research. Ontra helps cities and other transit agencies increase ridership through data-driven planning and real-time optimization. The founders developed the software that powered MARTA Reach in Atlanta, GA and CAT SMART in Savannah, GA.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Public transit agencies and city transportation departments that plan routes, on-demand zones and service levels
problem: Transit agencies decide what service to run with slow, manual planning. Ontra generates and compares fixed routes, on-demand zones and frequencies with projected ridership, and adds dispatching and a rider app.
business_model: B2B and government SaaS subscription (one profile states a subscription model)
product_category: Transit planning and operations software (GovTech)
market_need_then: Agencies faced ridership recovery pressure after 2020 and states funded planning tools (Virginia 2023). No company specific demand figures found.
outcome_analysis: Ontra Mobility is an active two person YC Summer 2024 company led by PhD founders with prior transit software experience. Its site lists public sector customers and a Transit Tech Lab 2026 cohort, but no verified funding round, revenue or exit was found. The main risks are a long government sales cycle and a larger incumbent, Via, with an established planning platform.

name: Onyx
tags: Open Source; NLP; Enterprise; Search; AI
one_liner: Open Source AI Chat
long_description:
Onyx is the open source chat UI connected to your company’s docs, apps, and people. We ingest and sync from all sources of information (Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Confluence, Salesforce, etc.) to provide a centralized place for users to ask about anything. Imagine your most knowledgeable co-workers, all-rolled into one, and available 24/7!

Check us out on Github: https://www.github.com/onyx-dot-app/onyx
Or visit our website: https://www.onyx.app/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies and technical teams that want a self-hostable AI chat and enterprise search layer over internal tools
problem: Employees cannot find answers spread across Slack, Drive, Confluence, GitHub and Salesforce, and many firms cannot send confidential data to closed cloud tools.
business_model: Open source core (MIT) with paid cloud and proprietary enterprise edition
product_category: Open source enterprise search and AI assistant
market_need_then: Enterprise search over scattered SaaS data was a recognized pain, and the open source plus self-host angle addressed confidentiality concerns around closed LLM tools; demand evidence is visible in GitHub traction reported later.
outcome_analysis: Onyx, formerly Danswer, grew through open source distribution, reaching tens of thousands of GitHub stars and a 20 person team, then raised a 10 million dollar seed led by Khosla and First Round in March 2025. In autumn 2026 Zoom acquired it for undisclosed terms to gain a self-hostable enterprise context layer. The exit follows traction and strategic fit rather than distress.

name: Open
tags: Generative AI; Customer Service; Customer Support; Conversational AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Enterprise AI customer support
long_description:
Open is an AI-powered, all-in-one customer support and communication platform — used in production by:

Print.com, Mollie.com, Viva.com, More.com, Orderchamp.com, OneCarNow.com, and other major enterprise companies.

We specialize in solving and automating complex support cases across email, web, phone, SMS, and WhatsApp.

We’re a research-based company currently working on releasing Support-Bench, the world’s most comprehensive AI customer support benchmark.

Our team consists of +3 programming language builders, a nationwide cybersecurity competition winner at age 16, and a dentist.
regions: Jordan; Middle East and North Africa; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Enterprise and mid-market companies with high support volume across email, chat, phone, SMS and WhatsApp (customers named include Print.com, Mollie, Viva, TicketSwap, MoneyGram)
