problem: Support teams are overloaded with repetitive and complex cases across many channels. Open sells an AI agent that resolves interactions end to end, with handoff to humans, and says it automates about 77% of interactions on average.
business_model: Usage-based per automated resolution (site lists $0.90 per resolution, no per-seat fee)
product_category: AI customer support and communication platform
market_need_then: Support is a large labor cost and generative AI made automated resolution feasible in 2023 and 2024. The YC page lists enterprise customers in production, which suggests early demand in Europe.
outcome_analysis: Open is an active Amman-based YC Winter 2024 company that reached enterprise customers in Europe, raised a $1.52M pre-seed in January 2025 and a $7M seed in January 2026 with YC and Gulf investors. It claims 77% automation of interactions and security certifications. It competes in a very crowded and well funded AI support category, so the outcome is still open.

name: Openbenchmarks
one_liner: We help humans & agents pick tools via Independent Benchmarks
long_description:
Openbenchmarks runs open, independent benchmarks across APIs, vendors and tools. 
Helping teams fairly evaluate vendors.

We offer private benchmarking & analytics tools to help you measure your product against competitors, see exactly where you fall short, and fix it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: API and tool vendors that pay for private benchmarking and analytics, and teams and AI agents that use the free public benchmarks to choose vendors
problem: Teams and agents picking among APIs, vendors and tools lack independent, current comparisons. Openbenchmarks runs open benchmarks (search, document processing, enrichment, inference, voice) refreshed hourly, and sells private benchmarking so vendors can see where they lose to competitors.
business_model: Free public benchmarks as distribution (CC-BY-4.0 data, API) with paid private benchmarking and analytics for vendors
product_category: Independent benchmarking and vendor evaluation for AI agent tooling
market_need_then: AI agents and teams were choosing among fast-multiplying APIs in 2024 with little neutral comparison data. No company specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Openbenchmarks is an active four person San Francisco company from YC Fall 2024 run by founders who previously built OpenFunnel. It publishes free hourly benchmarks across search, document processing, enrichment, inference and voice, and sells private analytics. No verified funding, revenue or exit was found. Outcome is undetermined; the main questions are whether vendors will pay and whether the benchmarks are seen as independent.

name: Opencall
one_liner: Practice admin run by AI
long_description: OpenCall makes medical practices more profitable and enables owners and operators of their rollups to hit their KPIs.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: Medical, dental and dermatology practices and their rollups that pay for AI phone and text agents
problem: Practice front desks miss calls and spend staff time on scheduling, intake and insurance checks, which costs revenue and labor.
business_model: B2B SaaS, AI voice and text agents sold to healthcare practices
product_category: AI receptionist and practice administration for healthcare
founder_names: Oliver Silverstein; Eric Mei; Arthur Silverstein
market_need_then: The company claims its agents cut labor cost and raise booking rates. These are company claims on the YC page. Independent demand evidence from 2024 was not collected.
outcome_analysis: OpenCall is active with a seven person team and named healthcare customers on its site. Its early positioning was call centers for any business and it later narrowed to healthcare practices. Funding is unclear, with aggregators giving conflicting totals, so strength of traction cannot be judged from verified rounds.

name: Openmart
one_liner: Local business data intelligence platform
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Sales teams, agencies and enterprises that sell to local and small businesses
problem: Reaching local businesses is hard because data on them is scattered across maps, filings, reviews and websites and goes stale.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for a local business database with enrichment and API
product_category: Local business data and sales intelligence
market_need_then: Press frames it as an alternative to ZoomInfo for sales leads on local businesses. The company claims over 10,000 companies use it. No dated demand evidence beyond that was collected.
outcome_analysis: Openmart is active, raised a 2.75M seed in August 2024 after YC Winter 2024 and claims over 10,000 customer companies. It has since broadened from a lead database to enrichment, an API and an AI sales agent. Funding after the seed was not found, so growth after 2024 is not verified.

name: Opslane
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Enterprise; DevOps; AI
one_liner: AI Code Review tool that runs your app
long_description: Opslane catches the bugs code review misses. On every PR, it runs your app against realistic copies of the services it depends(from Stripe to Slack). Then it tries what breaks in production: a service failing, two requests at once, a restart mid-job.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams that ship code with AI assistance and want PRs verified at runtime
problem: Code review and unit tests miss bugs that only show up at runtime, such as service failures, concurrent requests and restarts mid job.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, listed Pro plan at 150 dollars per month and custom enterprise
product_category: AI code review and runtime verification (originally open source on-call alert triage)
market_need_then: On-call alert fatigue was the pain stated in the July 2024 YC launch post. Independent dated spend evidence was not collected.
outcome_analysis: Opslane is active with a one person team listed. It launched as an open source on-call tool in July 2024 and later shifted toward verifying AI generated code. No named paying customers or rounds beyond the standard YC deal were found, so traction is unknown.

name: Orca Client
one_liner: Orca lets you build, discover, and play Minecraft games with friends.
long_description: Orca is a game launcher for Minecraft. Players browse games and experiences and join with one click, no mod installation, no setup. We handle hosting and mod delivery for server owners and game creators, who earn revenue from their games. Think Roblox, but built on top of Minecraft's 312M player base.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Minecraft players, plus server owners and game creators who earn revenue from hosted games
problem: Joining modded Minecraft games needs mod installation and setup, and creators lack a simple way to host and earn from games.
business_model: Platform with creator revenue share and hosting, pitched as Roblox style on top of Minecraft
product_category: Game launcher and creator platform for Minecraft
market_need_then: The YC page cites 312M Minecraft players as the base. Independent evidence of demand for a mini game launcher was not found.
outcome_analysis: Orca Client is listed as active with a team of two. No funding, user numbers or press were found, so its traction is unknown. It appears to have continued product work into 2026, possibly moving to a browser based AI modding product, but that identification is uncertain.

name: OrgOrg
one_liner: Organizational productivity suite for companies
long_description:
OrgOrg is a suite of apps that keeps teams productive and healthy regardless of the size of your organization. Founded by the creator of Zenter (YC 07, acquired by Google and became Google Slides), OrgOrg is designed to be a natural extension of Google Workspace Apps to help run organizations collaborate better leading to higher productivity.

Today the suite includes apps like:
  
• Go links: Go links allows anyone in the org to easily name any link so team members can jump directly to the information that matters most: go/sales, go/production, go/anything-you-want.
• Profiles with Personality: OrgOrg profiles are as insightful as they are delightful. They not only show you the expected org chart data, but also highlight accomplishments, how you like to work, and who you are as a person.
• Goal tracking: Track, share, and collaborate on "big rock" goals on the cadence that makes sense for your team from daily to annually.
• Branded New Tab: Keep the team focused the next major milestone, broadcast announcements, and keep important links top of mind every time a new browser tab is opened.
• All Hands Q&A: Crowdsource questions, anonymously if desired, for large team meetings to make sure everyone's voice is heard, and the most top of mind questions are answered and recorded.
• Smart Groups: Create rules based groups of people and use them to make sure the right people are in the right conversations and have the right access. For example, anyone with the title of "Software Engineer" should be in the #eng slack channel and eng@ google group.
• On-call: Schedule smart rotations that take into account balancing the load and using signals from calendar schedules to make sure you don't waste time figuring out who can cover what in a fair way. Easily page the on-call from slack, API, or OrgOrg directly.
• And more...

All the tools you need so you can spend more time focusing on your core business, and less time focusing on the complexity that comes from running an organization.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startups and small to mid size teams, especially Google Workspace users
problem: Companies cobble together many small internal tools (go links, directories, goals, on-call, all-hands Q&A) that an all in one suite could replace.
business_model: B2B SaaS per person subscription with a free tier (about 5 dollars per person per month at launch)
product_category: Internal productivity suite
market_need_then: The launch pitch says companies need many internal tools at each stage. No dated external demand evidence was collected.
outcome_analysis: OrgOrg is active with a two person team led by a founder with a prior Google acquisition and a funded startup exit. It keeps adding apps to its suite. Trackers report a small seed of about 500K in 2024 but the company discloses nothing, so traction is unclear.

name: Origami
one_liner: Enter your domain & Origami gets you customers.
long_description:
Origami is the first AI that automatically gets customers for you. Enter your domain, and let it start working.

Used daily by 10,000+ businesses, Origami gets smarter everyday - learning from your campaigns to find better buyers and drive more revenue for you. On average, customers get 3-6x more positive replies than traditional outbound.

Origami combines Outbound, Lead Generation, Website Visitors Identification, Viral Content & more, starting at $99/month. Every paid plan includes built-in email and LinkedIn sequencing. New organizations can try Starter for 7 days with $66 of usage; a card is required, and the trial renews at $99/month unless canceled before it ends. Current plans: https://origami.chat/pricing.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B sales teams and businesses doing outbound, from small teams to large enterprises
problem: Sales reps spend hours researching prospects and finding people with a reason to buy now.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, Starter 99 and Pro 299 dollars per month per site
product_category: AI sales research and outbound agents
market_need_then: VentureBeat coverage of the seed describes demand from property management and real estate sales teams. A report cites 50,000 dollars in monthly recurring revenue during beta, which is a secondary claim.
outcome_analysis: Origami is active with about 10 people, raised a 2M seed in January 2025 and claims over 2,000 businesses use it, with large brand logos on its site. It began with property management and real estate customers and widened to other B2B sectors. Traction numbers are mostly company claims.

name: Outerport
one_liner: Design automation for industrial electrical controls
long_description: We’re about to see an influx in the AI-led discovery of new medicines, specialty chemicals, and materials. This means the bottleneck will shift from R&D, to the scale-up of these new recipes. Unfortunately, designing these production systems and making sure they can be operated safely is an expensive and labor-intensive ordeal that involves thousands of pages of drawings where one mistake can cause millions of dollars in rework or even disasters. Outerport solves this by helping engineering firms automate the design of the industrial control systems needed for production scale-up, using a domain-specific language for electrical design with thousands of unit tests that verify performance, and building simulators that can ingest already built schematics of plants to help automate comissioning and help train operators to prevent costly mistakes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering firms and machine builders that design industrial electrical control systems
problem: Designing electrical controls, power distribution and P&ID documents is slow and manual, which limits how fast manufacturers can scale production.
business_model: B2B software, AI design agents for engineering firms (pricing not found)
product_category: Design automation for industrial electrical controls (originally GPU model weight swapping infrastructure)
competitors_at_founding: Modal and Baseten (positioned as adjacent platforms)
market_need_then: The Launch HN post in August 2024 claimed simulations projecting about a 40 percent GPU cost cut from faster model swaps. This was a company simulation claim, not customer evidence.
outcome_analysis: Outerport is active with a small team. It launched in August 2024 selling model weight hot swapping and has since turned to design automation for industrial electrical controls, with a named Daikin case study and investors including Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund. Round sizes are not public in the sources found.

name: Overeasy
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams building computer vision models that need labeled visual data
problem: Labeling images and video and iterating on annotations is slow and expensive, which delays building computer vision models.
business_model: B2B software, AI agent (IRIS) that auto labels, trains and deploys vision models (pricing not found)
product_category: AI data labeling and computer vision model building
market_need_then: The YC launch post pitched going from idea to a vision model 100 times faster. Dated demand evidence was not collected.
outcome_analysis: Overeasy is listed as active with a team of two. It started from an open source vision pipeline project and launched through YC in 2024 with the IRIS labeling agent. No funding, customers or press were found, so traction is unknown.

name: Overheard
tags: SaaS; Design; Feedback; Market Research; AI
one_liner: AI-run customer research at scale
long_description:
Overheard supercharges your team’s capacity for high-quality customer research. Tell it what you’re deciding, like why customers churn or which launch to back. It interviews dozens of people at once by voice, from your own customers or a research panel, and comes back with answers.

Most teams have more decisions than research capacity, so many still get made on gut feel. Overheard helps research teams cover far more of them, and gives teams without researchers a way to start.

Teams use Overheard to find out why customers churn or don’t convert, choose between ideas before a launch, set pricing, and run win/loss interviews.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Product, marketing and research teams at companies that need customer research faster than their researchers can run it
problem: Teams have more decisions than research capacity, so many are made on gut feel. Overheard runs voice interviews with dozens of customers or panel members at once and returns answers with supporting quotes.
business_model: B2B SaaS for AI moderated customer research (pricing not found)
product_category: AI customer research and voice interviewing
market_need_then: At batch time (W24) the company was building open source AI infrastructure, so the market need for customer research is a later pivot thesis. The YC page says teams have more decisions than research capacity. No dated demand evidence for the original idea was found.
outcome_analysis: Overheard is active with a team of two and has no confirmed outside funding. It entered YC W24 as OpenFoundry, an open source AI infrastructure tool, and pivoted by September 2026 into voice based customer research. The new market is crowded with funded players, so the story is still unresolved and any success rests on the pivot finding traction.

name: Overlap
one_liner: Multimodal AI agents for video
long_description:
Overlap builds multimodal AI agents that can do literally anything you want related to video, such as finding specific moments, generating clips, or analyzing your video library. 

What takes media companies thousands of hours, we do in seconds.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Media companies, podcasters, marketers and creators that want short social clips from long videos
problem: Turning long form video into captioned short clips and publishing them takes media teams thousands of hours.
business_model: Performance priced AI clipping service, priced on views the clips earn per the company site
product_category: AI video clipping and publishing agents
market_need_then: Podcast and long form video publishers wanted short clips for social distribution. The site cites iHeartMedia and morning show case studies, which are company claims.
outcome_analysis: Overlap is active with nine people and shows named media customers on its site, but no verified funding or revenue was found. It competes in a crowded AI clipping market where larger editors added similar features. Its performance based pricing and ownership pitch are differentiators, yet the outcome is still unresolved.

name: Oway
one_liner: Building the open operating system for the automated physical economy.
long_description:
The physical economy still operates without a common language. Enterprise systems, factories, trucks, and robots generate enormous amounts of data, but most remains fragmented across legacy software and incompatible formats. Without a shared understanding of what is happening, even the most advanced AI cannot reliably coordinate how goods are made, moved, and delivered.

Oway is building that common language. Our protocol, IOI, connects enterprise systems and physical hardware, cleaning messy legacy data and live telemetry into a standardized schema that AI can understand and act on. Through a shared API, businesses can query their operations, identify inefficiencies, and automate actions across systems without replacing their existing software.

Our first model, Juno, applies this intelligence to unused truck capacity. It tracks empty space on trucks and sells it at a 50% discount to businesses shipping in the same direction. By moving freight directly on trucks already making the trip, Oway reduces shipping costs, damage, and transit times while generating additional revenue for carriers.

Every connected system and shipment expands our understanding of capacity, pricing, routes, facilities, and industrial operations. As this network grows, Oway is building toward a future where enterprise software, automated factories, self-driving vehicles, and robots can communicate and coordinate through one shared layer, making the physical economy programmable.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Shippers of small pallet freight and, later, manufacturers and logistics firms using its data layer and AI agent
problem: Carriers run with empty trailer space while shippers overpay for less than truckload freight. Oway matches pallets with live empty truck capacity, and now sells an operations data layer and agent.
business_model: Freight marketplace margin plus software for enterprise operations data (IOI, Juno, Oway OS)
product_category: AI freight marketplace and industrial coordination software
market_need_then: Empty miles and costly LTL pallet shipping were known pain points. The company claims it can cut cross country pallet costs by half, from about $350 to $140 on one lane (TechCrunch, Aug 2025, company claim).
outcome_analysis: Oway raised a $4M seed in August 2025 backed by General Catalyst and Y Combinator and grew to about 12 to 16 people, with named enterprise users on its site. The founder has a prior operating company and the company has broadened from a freight marketplace into software. Larger freight players are pursuing the same wedge, so the stage is early and unresolved.

name: Paasa
one_liner: Invest in Global Equities from India
long_description:
Paasa helps wealthy Indians invest in global equities - without middlemen, hidden fees, or paperwork.

While high-net-worths in India often have international expenses from children's education to healthcare, most still save in INR, a currency that depreciates ~2–5% per year against the USD. Why?

- Broken outward remittance process
- Fear of making mistakes in tax or compliance
- Paper-heavy onboarding processes of international brokers
- Lack of trustworthy guidance

Paasa offers a mobile app that enables Indians to trade worldwide, invest via advisory, and automate every cross-border tax filing.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Indian residents, NRIs and tech employees who want global equities, ETFs and tax compliant reporting
problem: Indians investing abroad face paperwork, remittance rules and cross border tax filing, which Paasa automates on top of Interactive Brokers accounts.
business_model: Fintech platform with fees on managed strategies and services; assets held at Interactive Brokers (fee detail not found)
product_category: Cross border investing platform for India
market_need_then: Indian investors increasingly sought US stocks, with LRS remittance and tax filing as known frictions per consumer guides; no dated figure was opened for 2024.
outcome_analysis: Paasa is active with nine people in Gurugram and a regulated, content led product for cross border investors. Funding is unclear across sources, and no traction numbers were verified. Competition from established Indian platforms makes the result unresolved and dependent on trust and compliance execution.

name: Palmier
one_liner: Video editor built for AI
long_description: Palmier Pro is a video editor built for AI, where Claude and Codex can edit your timeline directly: trimming, reordering, and generating footage. We used it to make 15+ cinematic AI launch videos for YC companies and it's now open-source and free to download at palmier.io.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Creators, editors, agencies and teams who want AI agents to edit video
problem: Video editing is manual; Palmier Pro lets coding style agents such as Claude, Codex or Cursor operate a timeline through an MCP server while humans finish the cut.
business_model: Free open source editor with paid plans for AI generation credits and a managed per video service
product_category: AI native video editor
market_need_then: At batch time (S24) the company reportedly built an AI that understands codebases, per YC launch listings, so the video need is a later pivot thesis. No dated demand evidence for video was found.
outcome_analysis: Palmier is active with two founders and no verified funding. After a codebase understanding product it launched Palmier Pro in mid 2026, an open source Mac editor for AI agents, claiming over 100K downloads on its site. Incumbent editors are adding agent features, so traction and monetization remain unproven.

name: PandasAI
one_liner: PandasAI is an open-source conversational data analysis platform with…
long_description:
PandasAI is an open-source library for conversational data analysis. Enterprises can connect their dataframes, databases or datalakes and do data analysis in plain english.

For example, PandasAI can be used by everyone in the company to visualize data or to ask complex queries and extract valuable insights for better data-informed decisions.
regions: Germany; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Data teams and enterprises wanting conversational analysis of their data, starting from Python developers
problem: Analyzing data requires code or analyst time; PandasAI lets users ask questions in natural language over dataframes, SQL and data lakes.
business_model: Open source core with enterprise and cloud plans
product_category: Conversational data analysis
market_need_then: In 2023 LLMs made natural language data analysis feasible; the company said several Fortune 500 firms approached it about pilots (tech.eu, Sep 2023) and the repo had over 8,600 GitHub stars.
outcome_analysis: PandasAI grew from an open source library into a company that raised $1.1M in September 2023 and joined YC W24. It rode the LLM wave with strong GitHub adoption and now sells enterprise plans, though revenue claims on aggregators are unverified. Larger assistants offer similar features, so the stage is early but with a real developer community.

name: Panelytic
one_liner: Payment infrastructure for machines
long_description: Payments, identity, and financial controls for autonomous machines.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Operators and developers of autonomous machines and agents that need to pay and be identified
problem: Machines and agents lack payment, identity and financial controls; Panelytic positions itself as infrastructure for that machine economy.
business_model: Infrastructure software, pricing not found
product_category: Machine payments and identity infrastructure
market_need_then: At W24 the agent payments market was nascent and no dated demand evidence was found. The current pitch is a later positioning, so need at founding is unknown.
outcome_analysis: Panelytic is listed as active with a team of two. The homepage is a single page pitching infrastructure for machine payments, and no press, funding or customers were found. Too little is public to judge the outcome, and the name suggests an analytics origin that was not documented.

name: Panora
one_liner: Turning messy inboxes into ERP-Ready Data
long_description: Panora automates PO entry for distributors, manufacturers and wholesalers. Stop wrong shipments, block duplicates, reclaim ~80% of your order-entry time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Distributors, manufacturers and wholesalers that receive purchase orders and quotes by email
problem: Order entry teams retype purchase orders from inboxes into ERPs, causing wrong shipments and duplicates. Panora reads the emails and posts validated orders to the ERP.
business_model: B2B SaaS for order automation, pricing not found
product_category: AI purchase order automation
market_need_then: Manual order entry from email is a long standing cost for distributors, but no dated evidence from 2024 was opened. At launch the company sold an open source integration API for LLMs, so this need came with a later pivot.
outcome_analysis: Panora is listed active with one person and no verified funding. It appears to have moved from an open source integration API to purchase order automation, and its current site contains placeholder metrics and mismatched testimonials. With little public traction and a name shared with another funded company, the outcome is unresolved and the signals lean weak.

name: Paradigm
one_liner: A reimagined workspace with AI at its core
long_description:
Centered around the primitive of a spreadsheet, Paradigm puts swarms of intelligent agents at your fingertips. Paradigm is the default AI agent orchestration platform for structured data.

Try it now at paradigmai.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Finance, consulting and tech professionals who do research and data gathering in spreadsheets, and firms in credit, private equity and sales
problem: Research workflows that pull facts from the web and internal files into tables are slow and manual. Paradigm puts an AI agent behind every spreadsheet cell so rows and columns fill themselves.
business_model: Subscription SaaS, early business pricing reported at 500 dollars a month, self serve from 20 dollars a month after the August 2025 public launch
product_category: AI agent spreadsheet and research workspace
market_need_then: In 2024 generative AI made automated research feasible and finance and consulting teams spent large manual effort on spreadsheet based diligence. Early customers named later include EY, Etched and Cognition.
outcome_analysis: Paradigm is still active. It emerged from stealth in September 2024 with a 2 million dollar pre seed, grew a user base it says is above 20,000, and raised a 5 million dollar seed led by General Catalyst in August 2025 together with a public launch. The wedge rides the generative AI shift, but rivals and spreadsheet incumbents can copy it, so the later outcome depends on data connectors and finance workflow depth.

name: Parahelp
tags: Customer Success; Customer Service; Customer Support; AI; Conversational AI
one_liner: Build an AI support agent that securely uses all your tools
long_description:
Build and run an AI support agent that resolves even your most complex tickets end-to-end.

If a tool has an API, you can securely connect it to your agent - just by chatting with Parahelp. For example, you can connect Stripe so your agent can resolve billing questions and refund requests.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software and AI companies with technical support queues, such as Perplexity, Cursor, Replit and Bolt
problem: Support teams for software products spend time on complex tickets that need actions in billing and other tools. Parahelp runs an agent that resolves tickets end to end by using those tools.
business_model: Usage based, per auto resolved ticket (about 1 dollar shown on the site), no seat or platform fee
product_category: AI customer support agent
market_need_then: In 2024 LLM quality made automated resolution plausible and support is a large cost line for software companies. Parahelp reports customers resolving roughly 46 to over 80 percent of tickets.
outcome_analysis: Parahelp is active and growing. After a mid batch pivot from the founders' NFT business into AI support, it raised a seed in September 2024 and an 18 million dollar Series A led by Alt Capital in September 2025, within about thirteen months, and lists Perplexity, Cursor and Replit as customers. The category is crowded with large funded rivals, so execution speed and results on technical support are the differentiators.

name: Parallel
one_liner: AI agents for healthcare admin
long_description: We build AI agents that automate healthcare admin workflows. Our agents navigate legacy hospital software like humans (using mouse and keyboard) and automate end-to-end workflows (starting with medical coding), freeing medical professionals from manual tasks.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: French public and private hospitals, with expansion to Europe and the US
problem: Hospital coding and administrative work is manual and runs on legacy software. Parallel agents operate the existing software like a person to code stays, capture missed revenue and automate tasks.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services sold to hospitals, deployed in days or weeks without back end changes
product_category: AI agents for healthcare administration, medical coding
market_need_then: French hospitals face a complex billing coding system (PMSI) and administrative burden; LLMs made structuring medical text feasible in 2024. The company reports over 850 healthcare clients and a 10 to 1 average return on its own site, which is unverified.
outcome_analysis: Parallel is active and rising. It began inside the Hexa studio as Kiosk, pivoted in September 2024 to hospital coding agents, raised a 3.5 million dollar seed in April 2025 and a 20 million dollar Series A led by Index Ventures in March 2026. The pivot found a clear paid pain point in French hospitals, and the main open risk is expanding beyond coding and beyond France.

name: ParcelBio
tags: Gene Therapy; Synthetic Biology; Biotech; Therapeutics; Drug discovery
one_liner: Elevated mRNA for transformative medicines.
long_description: ParcelBio is engineering a new class of mRNA medicines designed to deliver unprecedented potency and durability. Its proprietary APEXm™ platform uses novel RNA domains to enhance protein expression and extend activity, enabling therapies that reach the thresholds required for meaningful, and potentially curative, clinical outcomes. The company is advancing programs in autoimmune disease, oncology, and encoded protein therapeutics.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharma partners and patients, a preclinical biotech developing mRNA therapies for autoimmune disease, oncology and protein therapeutics
problem: Existing mRNA medicines do not express enough protein for long enough to reach therapeutic thresholds. ParcelBio's APEXm platform adds RNA domains to boost and prolong expression.
business_model: Therapeutics development, pipeline value and partnerships, no product revenue yet
product_category: mRNA therapeutics platform, in vivo CAR-T
market_need_then: mRNA therapies beyond vaccines are limited by short expression and dose. Interest in in vivo CAR-T for autoimmune disease was rising by 2024 and 2025, though sources I read do not give 2024 funding figures for that area.
outcome_analysis: ParcelBio is a preclinical platform company that stayed quiet after its Winter 2024 YC batch and publicly launched in May 2026 with a 13 million dollar seed led by Breyer Capital. Founders with senior RNA platform roles at Orbital and Freenome give strong founder market fit. The outcome depends on whether APEXm shows durable expression in animals and humans, which is not yet proven.

name: Parley
one_liner: Legal Agent that delivers finished work
long_description: Parley is the Legal Agent built for the AI era. Legal teams know that getting the work done isn't just drafting or researching. It's also managing your cases, loose threads, and team. Parley is the all-in-one workspace that structures all of that information so that AI can actually deliver finished work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Immigration law firms and, after broadening, legal teams in general
problem: Immigration petitions such as O-1A and EB-1 take lawyers long hours to draft. Parley drafts them in Word and has grown into a legal agent with case management.
business_model: B2B SaaS for law firms, free trial and self serve launched in 2026 per a secondary summary
product_category: Legal AI agent, immigration legal tech
founder_names: Philip Smart; Ian Edwards; Jackson Perry
market_need_then: Immigration firms bill flat fees and gain directly from faster drafting, and O-1 and EB-1 petitions needed by AI and tech founders were rising. Company claims of 100 plus legal teams are unverified.
outcome_analysis: Parley is active. It launched an O-1A petition writer in June 2024, took a reported 500 thousand dollar pre seed from Y Combinator in October 2024, partnered with Boundless, and by 2026 positioned itself as an all in one legal agent with self serve access. Funding is small and public detail is thin, so the story so far is early traction with unproven scale in a crowded legal AI field.

name: PartnerHQ
one_liner: A marketplace for B2B businesses to buy warm intros.
long_description:
PartnerHQ is building the next generation LinkedIn. We are creating the world’s most valuable and accurate professional network graph by capturing and indexing vast quantities of relationship signals. 

Individuals use PartnerHQ to grow and monetize their networks. B2B companies use PartnerHQ to buy warm intros and drive high-value sales. 

PartnerHQ was created during Y Combinator’s W24 cohort and launched in February of 2024. Since launch we have signed on hundreds of paying companies, domestic and international. 97% of all users have come inbound or word-of-mouth.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B sales teams that buy warm introductions; individuals with large networks earn the bounty
problem: Cold outreach converts poorly, and people with valuable networks have no way to monetize introductions.
business_model: Marketplace with per-introduction bounty (average reported as $500)
product_category: Warm introduction marketplace
market_need_then: Company reports hundreds of paying companies within weeks of its February 2024 launch and 97 percent inbound or word of mouth; these are self-reported.
outcome_analysis: PartnerHQ is a Winter 2024 company that launched in February 2024 and reports hundreds of paying customers and a 97 percent inbound user base, all self-reported. No funding beyond YC was verified and no exit or failure signal exists, so the story is too early to attribute to specific success or failure factors.

name: Party
one_liner: Secure multiplayer workspace for teams building with agents
long_description:
Party is the secure workspace for your team and agents to build together, in the open. Agent Flows handle 95% of the work and your team can see it all happen and step in when needed to steer. It's built for teams and collaboration first, but caters to the solo builder as well. Use any harness/model - your keys or ours. Cost observability. Memory. Dual-level session sandboxing.
Slack/Teams are comm-first with agents as second-class citizens. Party is work-first and the communication happens where the work is being done. Party is for teams who want to build better and faster than their competition.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software teams and solo builders who build with AI coding agents
problem: Chat tools treat agents as second class and keep work and talk apart. Party is a shared workspace where teams and agents plan, build, review and ship in one thread with budgets, sandboxing and memory.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with credits: free, 20 dollar starter, 200 dollar pro, custom enterprise
product_category: Multiplayer AI agent workspace for software teams
market_need_then: In 2024 AI coding agents were spreading but team collaboration around them was weak; the founder's pitch is that comms first tools treat agents as second class. No quantified demand evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Party is active with a working product, public pricing and community events, but no public funding or traction numbers were found, so no clear success or failure story can be told. It competes in a fast moving area where chat platforms, coding agent vendors and other YC companies are building similar multiplayer agent workspaces.

name: Patched
one_liner: Reliable AI for Regulated Ops
long_description: Patched executes regulated workflows in hours instead of days, with full auditability and control.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Regulated operations teams in banking, fraud and risk, and law enforcement; originally software developers
problem: Regulated workflows such as fraud review and reconciliation take days. Patched executes them in hours with audit trails, human approvals and policy enforcement. Originally it automated code review and patching.
business_model: Volume based enterprise pricing, with SLA ownership of outcomes
product_category: AI workflow execution for regulated operations (earlier open source developer workflow automation)
market_need_then: In 2024 AI code review and patching tools were crowded; later the company targeted regulated operations where it reports 30 thousand to 2 million items processed monthly by customers, which is a self reported claim.
outcome_analysis: Patched is active but its story is unclear. It launched open source developer workflow tools in September 2024, then repositioned to AI for regulated operations and now cites customers in fraud, banking and reconciliation. Company site lists Y Combinator, IQT and SG Innovate as backers but no amounts or dates were found, so funding stays unknown and no success or failure verdict is supported.

name: Patchwork
one_liner: Your team’s AI powered communication tool
long_description: Patchwork replaces your inefficient Slack with an intelligent feed personalized for each team member with all of their daily updates, design and engineering discussions, and announcements.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: PathPilot
one_liner: AI Agents for Lending Operations
long_description: Today, onboarding, servicing, and collections still depend on large human teams — which means operations scale linearly with loan volume. PathPilot deploys specialized AI agents that handle 60–80% of high-volume operational workflows, turning human-heavy processes into scalable software. These agents operate alongside internal teams — embedded directly into existing systems. This allows lenders to grow loan volume and revenue without proportional headcount growth.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer lenders, fintechs, BNPL and collections firms in the US and Latin America
problem: Lenders need to scale origination, servicing and collections without adding staff proportionally.
business_model: B2B SaaS of AI agents for lending operations
product_category: AI agents for lending operations
market_need_then: Lenders face high operating cost in origination and collections; no dated demand data was found for 2024.
outcome_analysis: PathPilot joined YC in Summer 2024, first launching a session replay AI model and later positioning as AI agents for lending operations, with a pre seed round in May 2025 from Alaya, Unpopular and Network.VC. It is active with three people and no later round found, so the outcome is too early to judge; crowded competition in lending agents is the visible risk.

name: Pax
one_liner: AI Native Operating System for Global Trade
long_description:
Pax is the AI-native broker that automates and maximizes tariff refunds through duty drawback. We've helped enterprises recover millions in duties and manage their entire trade compliance operation from one platform.

Each year, 80% of eligible refunds—equivalent to $15B—go unclaimed. Pax is the first AI-first broker that makes this process transparent and streamline while maximizing all duty saving opportunities.

We are two technical founders: Penny got her PhD from MIT and, and was a former research scientist at Amazon & Flexport, where I encountered the problem firsthand. Chris is a second-time founder and former software engineer at Amazon, Brex, and TikTok.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Importers and exporters, plus customs brokers and service providers that do not yet offer duty drawback
problem: About 80 percent of eligible duty drawback refunds go unclaimed because filing is manual and slow and most brokers ignore small claims. Pax acts as an AI native broker that prepares and files claims.
business_model: Broker take on recovered duties, plus a channel model with other brokers
product_category: AI native customs broker, duty drawback and trade compliance
market_need_then: Drawback recovers duties paid on imports later exported, and the company says 80 percent of eligible refunds, about 15 billion dollars, go unclaimed. The 2025 tariff wave and a CBP decision that reciprocal tariffs are drawback eligible expanded demand after the batch.
outcome_analysis: Pax is active. It went after a large and overlooked service market in duty drawback, raised a reported 4.5 million dollar seed in April 2025 with General Catalyst, Initialized and Soma, and benefited when 2025 tariffs and CBP's drawback eligibility ruling enlarged the pool. The risks are Charter's scale, Flexport's AI offering and dependence on government processing times.

name: Pazi
tags: Developer Tools; Security; Web Development; AI
one_liner: Platform where autonomous companies are built
long_description: Pazi enables people to build agents that run all operations in a company. You create an agent for a position (eg. developer, devops, social media manager, SDR, etc.), you give it a goal (eg. reach 10k followers on X) and let it create a plan, start checking in with you, oversee how the goal is coming up.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Individuals and small teams who want AI agents to design, launch and sell a product or small business
problem: Starting and running a business needs many roles at once. Pazi packages AI agents as role holders that plan, execute and report progress against a goal.
business_model: Freemium SaaS for AI agent workflows (pricing tiers not shown on site)
product_category: AI agent platform for building and running businesses (formerly AI app builder Pythagora with the open source GPT Pilot)
market_need_then: Strong interest in autonomous AI agents and AI app builders in 2024, shown by GPT Pilot's open source star count reported on the YC page and by the seed round coverage.
outcome_analysis: Pazi is active with a 2024 seed of 4 million dollars and no reported exit or shutdown. The team brought open source credibility from GPT Pilot and a prior acquired startup, and rode the 2024 agent wave. The rename and shift from a coding agent to company agents is unexplained, and the product faces fast moving model labs, so its outcome is still open.

name: Pearson Labs
one_liner: AI agents to automate corporate transactions
long_description: Pearson builds AI agents to automate corporate transactions. Large law firms use us to run gigantic books of businesses with AI, reducing their cost of delivery 40-60%.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Large law firms and companies running corporate transactions such as M&A, IPOs and financings
problem: Corporate deals need armies of lawyers for diligence and document work. Pearson builds AI agents that automate that work inside Word and Outlook.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software sold to law firms (pricing not public)
product_category: Legal AI agents for transactional work
market_need_then: Law firm leaders were seeking AI cost reduction in 2024; the YC page claims a 40 to 60 percent delivery cost reduction, a company claim not independently verified.
outcome_analysis: Pearson Labs is a very young company with no public exit or shutdown. It has an experienced solo founder with a prior acquired startup and early design partner interest, but the legal AI market is crowded with heavily funded rivals. Public evidence of traction beyond company claims was not found.

name: Penciled
one_liner: AI front office assistant for physical therapy
long_description: Penciled (W24) is an AI front office assistant for physical therapy. Penciled's AI assistant schedules out plans of care, sends reminders and processes last-minute cancellations, and fills openings with an automated waitlist. Penciled books thousands of appointments for physical therapists each month and integrates directly into EHRs like WebPT.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Outpatient physical therapy clinics, mostly WebPT users in the US
problem: Front desks lose revenue to cancellations, phone tag and unfilled openings. Penciled texts patients, books plans of care and fills cancellations from a waitlist.
business_model: B2B SaaS per therapist seat annually plus $1,200 per location onboarding fee
product_category: AI front office for healthcare clinics
market_need_then: Front desk staffing and cancellation losses are real in PT; the company reports 14.8 percent more visits and 27 percent fewer calls at one customer (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Penciled, run by a Harvard trained solo founder with health data experience, claims 200+ providers across 50+ clinics through a WebPT integration. It reports about $2.6M raised from YC, Initialized and healthcare founders. The traction figures are company claims and the company remains active with a two person team on YC's page.

name: PermitPortal
one_liner: AI Operating System for Pre-construction
long_description: We are building workflows to help developers go from finding and closing development sites to getting a building permit faster. PermitPortal accelerates the most critical parts of the pre-construction phase: finding the right sites, understanding entitlements and navigating local development sentiment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Real estate and infrastructure development teams, including data center, energy and logistics developers, and utilities
problem: Finding sites, judging entitlement risk and tracking permit schedules is slow and manual. PermitPortal uses AI agents and data to speed pre-construction.
business_model: B2B software plus services (platform, reports and data API); pricing not public
product_category: AI pre-construction and entitlement intelligence
market_need_then: Permitting and entitlement delay is a known cost for developers, and the data center build out raised demand for fast site screening; only secondary sources found.
outcome_analysis: PermitPortal is active with no reported exit and no public funding detail. The team has repeated founders with a prior YC company, and the site now targets data center and energy developers. A generic name, a small team and a better funded permitting rival make the path uncertain.

name: Pharos
one_liner: Helping hospitals identify and prevent avoidable harm using AI
long_description:
Pharos automates hospital quality reporting, saving millions in labour costs and helping to prevent avoidable patient harm. 

Today, clinicians spend thousands of hours manually pulling complex facts out of medical records for mandatory reporting and quality improvement.

Our AI pulls those facts out of unstructured medical records automatically. We automate reporting and show staff where avoidable patient harm is happening.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US hospitals and health systems that report to clinical quality registries
problem: Nurses and staff manually read patient charts to fill registry fields, which is slow and costly. Pharos automates chart abstraction and real time quality monitoring.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to hospitals
product_category: Clinical AI for hospital quality reporting
market_need_then: Quality reporting is a manual, labor heavy cost for hospitals; the company says it saves millions in labour, and LLMs made chart reading feasible in 2024.
outcome_analysis: Pharos raised a 5 million dollar seed in October 2024 led by Felicis after a Moxxie led pre-seed and reports deployment across over 100 hospitals. Founders with healthcare data experience and a clear manual cost problem helped it win a niche in registry abstraction. No exit or trouble is reported, and the company claims are self reported.

name: Phonely
one_liner: AI call centers
long_description: Phonely uses existing call recordings to create a 'AI vocal twin' that can answer customer support calls and match or outperform call center agents. On top of that we've built a Zapier like workflow that lets businesses connect to software or transfer calls just like a person would. Our platform sits on proprietary deterministic LLM that is both cheaper and more accurate than gpt-4o for call center inquiries.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Businesses and call centers handling inbound phone support, bookings and sales calls
problem: Call centers are costly and slow; businesses want AI agents that sound human and integrate with their software.
business_model: Usage/seat-based SaaS AI voice agents
product_category: AI voice agents for phone calls
market_need_then: Call center spend is large; Phonely reports customers replacing hundreds of agents (company claims, 2026).
outcome_analysis: Phonely spun out of University of Melbourne AI research, joined YC S24 with about $500K, and raised a $16M Series A in April 2026 led by Base10 with enterprise customers investing. It reports millions of calls a month. It rode the 2024 voice-AI wave and crowded competition remains the main risk.

name: Pinnacle
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Sales; E-commerce; SMS
one_liner: API & SDK for RCS (the next-generation of texting)
long_description: Pinnacle is an API for RCS, the new standard for SMS for app-like text messages.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and businesses that send app-like text messages (RCS, iMessage, MMS, SMS) through an API
problem: RCS adoption needs carrier and compliance setup that is hard for developers. Pinnacle offers one API and SDKs that handle it.
business_model: Usage-based messaging API
product_category: Communications API (RCS and multichannel messaging)
market_need_then: RCS was becoming the SMS successor on Android, with Apple support announced in 2024; developers lacked simple access.
outcome_analysis: Pinnacle is active and now advertises multichannel messaging with many named customer types and an MCP server. Strong Harvard and big tech founders, but no verified funding and a market where Twilio and other carriers shipped the same wedge within months. Outcome is still open.

name: Pipeshift
one_liner: Inference for real-time agents
long_description: Pipeshift offers ultra-low latency infrastructure for engineering teams to run real-time inference in production. We offer latency-optimized runtimes for voice, chat, and physical AI, paired with distributed orchestration that routes and auto-scales across clusters and regions — typically 3 to 5X lower time-to-first-audio, so teams serve 2x the users on the same hardware.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Companies and AI product teams deploying open source or custom LLMs in production
problem: Running open source models at low latency and cost needs GPU orchestration expertise. Pipeshift sells managed inference infrastructure.
business_model: Usage-based managed inference cloud plus VPC deployments with custom SLAs
product_category: AI inference infrastructure
founder_names: Arko C; Enrique Ferrao; Pranav Reddy
market_need_then: Demand for open model deployment grew in 2024 as enterprises wanted cost and control; reports cite GPU cost savings claims by the company.
outcome_analysis: Pipeshift raised a 2.5 million dollar seed in January 2025 and is active with partnerships announced in 2026. Its focus drifted from fine-tuning to real time inference. The inference market is crowded with well funded providers, so growth depends on a performance edge and enterprise deals.

name: Piramidal
one_liner: Foundation Models for the Brain
long_description: An API into your mind.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hospitals and neurologists that review EEG, starting with epilepsy and ICU monitoring
problem: Reading EEG recordings is slow and specialist heavy. Piramidal trains a foundation model on EEG to flag and review recordings in real time.
business_model: Clinical software and enterprise AI infrastructure for hospitals (pricing not public)
product_category: Brain foundation model and clinical EEG AI
market_need_then: EEG review is a known specialist bottleneck, and foundation model methods were newly applicable; academic EEG foundation model work was emerging.
outcome_analysis: Piramidal raised a 6 million dollar seed in August 2024 and partnered with Cleveland Clinic. A domain expert CEO and a data heavy approach give it a technical and regulatory moat, but clinical clearance is still pending and the company has not disclosed accuracy metrics. No exit or trouble is reported.

name: Pivot Robotics
one_liner: AI for Robot Arms in Factories
long_description: Pivot Robotics makes AI software for robotic arms that helps manufacturers automate their most labor intensive tasks. We are starting out with the dangerous task of metal grinding and are currently deploying our software on 10+ robots in a cast-iron foundry.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Manufacturers and foundries with labor-intensive finishing work such as metal grinding
problem: Grinding and similar finishing work is dangerous, labor-intensive and high-mix, so traditional robot programming does not fit.
business_model: Software and robot-cell deployments for manufacturers (Proteus); pricing not found
product_category: AI software for industrial robot arms
market_need_then: Most grinding still manual and hazardous; a foundry made it a 10+ robot pilot (YC page).
outcome_analysis: Pivot Robotics (YC W24) targets metal grinding with foundation-model vision and has a 10+ robot deployment at a cast-iron foundry. A July 2024 seed from NuVentures was reported without an amount. It is Active at 8 people; no later rounds were found, so it is early and unresolved. Founders have strong robotics and AI backgrounds, a plausible but unproven edge.

name: Planbase
one_liner: AI workforce management for healthcare
long_description: Planbase has everything health clinics need to manage their team in one place: capacity planning, employee scheduling, credentialing and payroll.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Healthcare clinics, especially mid-sized and large ones
problem: Clinics juggle capacity planning, scheduling, credentialing and payroll across disconnected tools. Planbase combines them into an AI-native workforce platform.
business_model: B2B SaaS for clinics (pricing not public)
product_category: Healthcare workforce management
market_need_then: Clinic staffing and admin burden is a recurring pain; the company claims clinics save hundreds of hours a month (press release claim).
outcome_analysis: Planbase launched publicly in November 2025 with a 2.1 million dollar seed and is still active in 2026 coverage. Repeat founders with forecasting experience from Elando give it execution credibility. It targets a crowded workforce management market and has little public traction data yet.

name: Plume
tags: Solar Power; B2B; Energy; AI; Industrial
one_liner: Renewable infrastructure deployment at scale.
long_description:
Plume is an AI-powered geospatial platform for site selection in energy infrastructure projects. 

Selecting the right sites requires analysis of +50 geospatial, grid, and regulatory constraints across fragmented data sources. 

Plume changes the process by enabling users to interact with geospatial data using natural language.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers of renewable and energy infrastructure projects, mainly in Europe, who must find and vet land and grid access
problem: Choosing a site means checking dozens of geospatial, grid and regulatory constraints spread across fragmented data sources, which takes developers months.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform for energy developers
product_category: AI geospatial site selection for energy infrastructure
market_need_then: Renewable developers faced slow permitting and grid queue bottlenecks in 2024; company cites calls with about sixty French renewable developers as basis for its ROI model.
outcome_analysis: Plume is active and raised a reported 3.3 million euro seed in April 2026, about twenty months after its Summer 2024 batch, led by AENU with YC and Kima. It sells to renewable developers facing permitting and grid bottlenecks across several European countries. No exit, layoffs or shutdown were found. Direct competitors such as Nira Energy existed earlier, so differentiation rests on natural language access and European coverage.

name: PointOne
one_liner: AI Time Platform for Law Firms
long_description: PointOne is the leading AI Time platform. With automated time entry, compliance, and analytics, PointOne offers AI-native
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Law firms (boutique, midsize, large) and public sector legal departments that bill by time
problem: Lawyers hate timekeeping, partners spend hours reviewing time entries, and firms lose billable hours and break outside counsel billing guidelines.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for law firms
product_category: AI timekeeping, billing review and compliance for legal
market_need_then: Founders began by asking lawyers what they hate most, and timekeeping was the top answer; firms still used paper processes and old software.
outcome_analysis: PointOne is active and has raised a 3.5 million dollar seed in 2024 and a 16 million dollar Series A in March 2026 led by 8VC, with the company reporting tenfold revenue growth over six months. It attacked a clear pain with AI passive capture in a crowded niche. No negative outcome news was found, so the story is steady execution with institutional backers.

name: Poka Labs
one_liner: Helping industrial manufacturers win more business at the best price.
long_description:
Poka Labs builds AI agents for pricing and sales at industrial manufacturers. Manufacturers sell thousands of products, and most customer requests are still priced by hand: reps search the catalog, check past prices and chase approvals while the customer keeps shopping.

Poka's costing, pricing, quoting and follow-up agents share one view of each manufacturer's products, customers and deal history from their ERP, CRM and email. Sales teams answer requests faster and price consistently across every customer.

Malay and Andrew met during their MBAs at Harvard Business School. Poka works with manufacturers ranging from a few million to billions of dollars in annual sales.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Industrial and chemical manufacturers and distributors, from a few million to billions of dollars in sales, that price and quote thousands of products
problem: Most customer requests are still priced by hand: reps search the catalog, check past prices and chase approvals while the customer keeps shopping.
business_model: B2B SaaS on top of customer ERP, CRM and email
product_category: AI pricing, quoting and sales agents for manufacturing
market_need_then: Manual pricing is slow in industrial sales; a vendor survey in 2025 says six in ten manufacturers rank AI pricing tools a top goal (vendor source, later than founding).
outcome_analysis: Poka Labs is active with a small team and a customer logo list that includes Thermo Fisher Scientific. It moved from production scheduling for chemical makers to pricing and quoting agents. Funding is unclear, so the stage of traction cannot be judged. Founders have chemicals domain experience and Harvard MBAs, which fits the target market, but no outcome has been reported.

name: Polar
tags: Fintech; Crypto / Web3; Investing; Remittances; Neobank
one_liner: The smarter way to manage USD earnings globally
long_description: Polar helps remote workers, freelancers, and online sellers outside the U.S. who get paid in dollars get better exchange rates when moving earnings to their local bank. We give them a U.S. dollar account in their name to receive USD earnings and let them withdraw through local bank transfers or stablecoins instead of the expensive options they use today.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Remote workers, freelancers, online sellers and ship crew outside the US who are paid in US dollars
problem: People paid in dollars abroad lose money on exchange rates and fees when moving earnings to a local bank.
business_model: Consumer fintech: USD account with fees or spread on withdrawals and interest products (not confirmed)
product_category: Cross-border USD account and neobank
market_need_then: Freelancers outside the US pay withdrawal and conversion fees through existing tools; vendor blogs cite fees of roughly 0.3 to 4 percent (2026 sources, unverified for 2023).
outcome_analysis: Polar is listed as active with a team of two and an iOS app for USD accounts. No funding round, press coverage or customer numbers were found, and search results are dominated by other companies named Polar. The record cannot support a success or failure judgment; the corridor is crowded with Payoneer, Wise and Deel.

name: Polished
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; B2B; Advertising; AI
one_liner: Generate ads. Iterate till perfect.
long_description:
With Polished, you create finished ads (video or static) in minutes.
Then you refine it in plain English, until it's exactly what you had in mind.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Marketers and small businesses that need finished video or static ads quickly
problem: Producing ads takes agencies or editors time and money; Polished generated finished ads from a brief and let users refine them in plain English.
business_model: SaaS subscription for AI ad generation (pricing not found)
product_category: Generative AI advertising creative
market_need_then: Advertisers needed cheaper creative; generative models made automated ad creation feasible in 2023, and several rivals launched. No hard demand data found for Polished itself.
outcome_analysis: Polished joined YC in Winter 2024 with an AI ad generator in a crowded category and its website now returns 404. The founders' YC page lists a later launch for a different product, Pillar, in February 2026, which suggests they moved on, but no source states this. Funding and traction are unknown, so no outcome judgment can be made beyond stalled visibility.

name: Polymet
one_liner: AI Product Designer
long_description:
Polymet uses AI to help non-designers create production-ready designs and front-end code. They explain what they want or provide an image, and Polymet designs the interface.

Our customers use Polymet instead of hiring designers and save thousands of dollars every month. Even their managers can design with English instead of writing design specs.

This helps these teams move faster and cover design function on their own instead of contractors at early stages and when they start to scale their can produce a lot more design work, just like Midjourney.
regions: Turkey; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Startups and product teams without in-house designers, and teams that want faster design to code
problem: Non-designers and small teams cannot afford designers or contractors for interface work, and design specs are slow to turn into front-end code.
business_model: SaaS subscription for an AI product design tool (pricing not found)
product_category: AI UI design and front-end code generation
market_need_then: Small teams use no designers and pay contractors; the founders cite customers saving thousands of dollars monthly (company claim on YC page).
outcome_analysis: Polymet is active with a team of three, backed by YC and Metis Ventures (February 2025), selling an AI product designer. It operates in a field where v0, Galileo AI and Uizard were already shipping, and later large players like Figma and Google moved in. No traction numbers or round size were found, so no outcome judgment beyond early stage is possible.

name: Powder
one_liner: AI Agents for precise document analysis
long_description:
Powder is an AI tool that helps wealth advisors rapidly create sales proposals that are personalized for each prospective client.  Using LLMs, Powder is able to automate a series of manual tasks such as understanding documents and conversations to create mind-blowing analysis that builds immediate trust.


Powder has 3 main features to automate sales workflows -

1. Brokerage, tax and estate document parser thats fast and accurate.
2. Meeting notetaker thats able to capture personalized insights.
3. Portfolio analysis tool that optimizes portfolio returns, risk and fees.

Our app saves hours of time and creates a pinpoint proposal that lifts a firm's ability to win new business.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Wealth advisors and RIA firms, mostly mid-sized, that build sales proposals for prospects
problem: Advisors spend hours reading brokerage, tax and estate documents and building personalized proposals for prospective clients.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to RIAs (pricing not found)
product_category: AI document analysis and proposal generation for wealth management
founder_names: Kanishk Parashar; Soo Yung Cho; David Goerz; Dominic Tully
market_need_then: Advisors rely on manual proposal work; Powder launched at the T3 conference in January 2024 with 20 mid-sized RIA clients per trade press.
outcome_analysis: Powder is active and raised a 5 million dollar seed announced July 2024, about six months after launch, with YC and General Catalyst among about 40 investors. The founding team came from RCI Navigator, which Addepar bought in 2021, giving domain access and sales credibility. Rivals later entered proposal automation, and no later round was found, so it remains early with unproven scale.

name: Praxos
one_liner: Team messaging with built-in memory
long_description: Praxos is team messaging where customer conversations, product decisions and agent conversations stay in context.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small teams of 2 to 10 people where one person handles customers while others build with AI coding tools
problem: Customer conversations, product decisions and agent conversations are scattered across tools, so context is lost between people and AI agents.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat: free for personal and family use, 23 USD per user per month for commercial use (company site)
product_category: Team messaging with built-in memory for humans and AI agents
market_need_then: Not evidenced for team messaging at founding; the YC page offers the first 10 teams free for six months, suggesting early search for customers.
outcome_analysis: Praxos is listed as active with a three person team and has changed product direction more than once, from insurance AI to a personal assistant and then to team messaging with memory. No funding round was confirmed and no customers are named, so traction is unknown. It competes with Slack and newer AI-native workspaces, so the outcome rests on whether memory is a real wedge.

name: Pre
one_liner: The AI accountability agent for startup founders
long_description:
Pre is an AI-powered execution system for startup founders who are serious about building real companies.
Set a 10-week goal, connect your tools, and get pushed to do your highest-impact work every week.
Pre doesn’t track effort… it tracks outcomes, and it holds you to a higher standard.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Early-stage startup founders who pay a monthly subscription for weekly accountability and investor-update reporting
problem: Founders drift from their highest-impact work and report poorly to investors. Pre sets a 10-week goal, connects the founder's tools and pushes weekly outcome-focused check-ins.
business_model: B2C/prosumer SaaS subscription for founders (listing shows about $84 per month)
product_category: AI accountability and execution coach for founders
market_need_then: Founders buy coaching and accountability programs, and the founder's own Pre-Accelerator coaching page shows paid demand for a human version, but no source quantifies demand for the AI product.
outcome_analysis: Pre came out of a serial founder's YC S24 run, which began as the kids AI app Genie and then moved to a founder accountability agent. The YC directory marks it Inactive, but no shutdown post, cause or date is public, so the cause is not public. The funding found is a roughly $650K pre-seed that GeekWire tied to Genie, not Pre. The product was a thin, easily copied coaching layer in a niche that later attracted other small entrants, which is consistent with a stall, but the cause is unconfirmed.

name: Precip
one_liner: High precision AI weather
long_description:
Precip uses deep-learning to make the most accurate rain forecast in the US. We started by using high-resolution radar to measure what actually fell, and built our minute-by-minute forecast on top of it. The result is a forecast that's 85% more accurate than Apple Weather and 52% more accurate than Google Weather, plus an API (with MCP) for developers.

Our highly rated mobile app is the best way to see rain and snow totals anywhere.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers who care about rain and snow timing and totals, plus developers and agriculture or construction users who buy weather data through an API
problem: Standard weather forecasts are coarse and often wrong about when rain starts and how much falls. Precip measures what actually fell from radar and builds minute-level forecasts on top.
business_model: Consumer mobile app plus usage-based API for developers
product_category: AI weather forecasting and rainfall measurement
market_need_then: At FarmLogs the rainfall feature was the most popular and quadrupled daily signups overnight per the founder blog dated 2024-01-15. Non-farm users such as loggers and construction workers signed up just for rain history. Dark Sky had also left a gap for map-first weather apps.
outcome_analysis: Precip is Active and still small (team of 3 per YC). It builds on the founders' FarmLogs experience, where a rainfall feature drew outsized demand, which gives real founder market fit. Funding is not verifiable from primary sources, and there is no exit or failure signal. The main risk is that big platforms and nowcasting rivals already ship similar forecasts.

name: Preloop
tags: Deep Learning; Developer Tools; Machine Learning; Data Science; AI
one_liner: Translate your experimental scripts into production ML services
long_description: Only 2 out of 10 ML models make it from experiment to production. Preloop helps automate the process of deployment, helping companies realize more value from their machine learning teams, while focusing teams' attention on science instead of engineering.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Presti AI
one_liner: Helping furniture companies create product visuals with AI
long_description:
Furniture companies spend millions and months each year on photoshoots or CGI to create product images as these visuals are crucial for driving sales.

Presti offers a faster and cheaper solution powered by generative AI. Unlike other generative AI tools, our core model is optimized for furniture products and includes multiple features tailored to the unique needs of furniture industry.
 
We have 100 paying B2B users with a 10% growth week over week.
We raised a $3.5M seed round
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Furniture brands, retailers and marketplaces that need large volumes of product visuals
problem: Furniture companies spend heavily on photoshoots or CGI to produce product images. Presti generates them with AI trained on furniture.
business_model: SaaS subscription with credits (free, Pro and enterprise tiers per the site)
product_category: Generative AI product photography
founder_names: Nabil Toumi; Saad Bencherif; Hamza Bennis; Abdellah Lamrani Alaoui
market_need_then: Tech.eu and the Partech release describe furniture visuals as a major cost center versus photoshoots and CGI. Presti reported doubling monthly revenue after launching in February 2024 and a partnership with Maisons du Monde.
outcome_analysis: Presti is Active with a Partech-led $3.5M seed in July 2024 and a claimed 400 plus customers on its site. The generative AI wave helped, and a vertical focus on furniture gave it a clear wedge and a named retail partner. No shutdown, layoffs or acquisition were found. Later rounds were not found.

name: Pretzel AI
one_liner: AI tooling
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Data scientists and analysts who work in Jupyter notebooks
problem: Jupyter notebooks have long-standing usability problems. Pretzel is an open-source JupyterLab fork with built-in AI code generation and chat.
business_model: Open-source developer tool, monetization unclear
product_category: AI-enhanced notebook environment, later cloud coding agents
market_need_then: Jupyter is widely used by data scientists and AI coding assistants were spreading in 2024, but no hard evidence of paid demand was found.
outcome_analysis: Pretzel is Active with a 2 person team. Its notebook product is a thin fork in a crowded market, and the company site now leads with a different product, Cord, which suggests a shift toward coding agents. No funding beyond YC could be verified and there is no exit. Not enough evidence for a clear success or failure story.

name: ProSights
tags: Fintech; Analytics; Enterprise Software; Investments; AI
one_liner: Data services for finance and operations at PE-backed companies.
long_description: ProSights is a data services firm for finance and operations at PE-backed companies. It reconciles the data across a company's ERP, CRM and operating systems, then builds the reporting, migrations and finance workflows that run on it. Typical engagements are job-level profitability across a roll-up's acquired businesses, consolidating acquired CRMs and ERPs after a deal, contract terms reconciled into Salesforce and ARR, and AP and bank reconciliation across subsidiaries. Clients include Thoma Bravo, Vista and Blackstone portfolio companies. The New York team combines private equity and consulting experience with senior engineers, and works inside the client's own systems, with every number traced to the record it came from.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Finance and operations teams at private equity backed portfolio companies and the PE firms that own them
problem: Portfolio companies have data scattered across ERP, CRM and operating systems, which makes reporting, post-deal migrations and reconciliations slow and manual.
business_model: Services-led data engagements with milestone-based pricing after a two week diagnostic
product_category: Data services and AI workflow automation for finance
market_need_then: PE firms and their portfolio companies spend heavily on finance data cleanup after acquisitions. The founders came from PE and sourced clients including Thoma Bravo, Vista and Blackstone portfolio companies per the YC page, though this is self-reported.
outcome_analysis: ProSights is Active with 14 people, a large team for its YC batch, and sells services to PE-backed companies using the founders' private equity networks.
