Its positioning moved from a software platform to data services. Funding could not be verified from primary sources, and there is no exit. Founder market fit is the clearest success factor.

name: ProhostAI
tags: SaaS; B2B; Travel; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: AI Property Manager for Airbnb & Short-Term Rental Hosts
long_description: ProhostAI is building an AI Property Manager for short-term rental hosts on Airbnb and other platforms. Our team consists of an ex-Airbnb Staff Data Scientist and Dropbox Sr Software Engineer who are also Superhosts with 9 properties worth $15M making $1.5M/yr.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Short-term rental hosts and property managers, from small hosts to teams managing over 100 properties
problem: Hosts spend large amounts of time on guest messaging, cleaner coordination and maintenance. ProhostAI offers an AI property manager and workspace to automate it.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with AI employees and integrations
product_category: AI property management for short-term rentals
market_need_then: The founders ran 9 properties worth $15M per the YC description and built the tool for their own coordination pain, then outside teams asked to use it per the company about page.
outcome_analysis: ProhostAI is Active and positions itself as an AI workspace with 250 plus teams on its inbox app per its own site. The founders are real hosts, which gives founder market fit. The company reports $2.6M raised, but aggregators show lower totals, so the funding picture is unclear. Incumbent PMS vendors are adding AI messaging, which is the main risk.

name: Promi
one_liner: Providing quick product and design feedback via digital twins
long_description:
Promi provides product feedback in the form of customer interviews, URL walkthroughs, heatmaps, and more by creating digital twins of your existing customers. We ingest data from Posthog, Intercom, Stripe, etc. to create your personas from real product usage data. By factoring in how your customers actually interact with product features, we provide much more relevant and insightful feedback on what you are building.

We aren't trying to replace user research, but in our experiences most products don't have the time or budget to talk to real users. Getting synthetic feedback is the next best thing, and can/should be a part of launching any products.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Product and design teams that cannot interview customers often
problem: Teams lack fast customer feedback; Promi builds digital twins of existing customers from usage data for simulated interviews and walkthroughs.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: AI customer research and simulation
market_need_then: Teams cannot afford frequent user research per the founders; no dated external evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Promi is a two person Summer 2024 company led by former Uber product and AI people, building digital twin customer personas. It is active with no later funding found, so there is no outcome to explain yet and early stage risk is the main story.

name: PromptArmor
one_liner: LLM Security and Compliance
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprise security and vendor risk teams assessing AI vendors, including law firms, healthcare and SaaS companies
problem: Companies adopt AI vendors and agents without visibility into prompt injection, data training and exfiltration risk. PromptArmor assesses and monitors third-party AI risk.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI vendor risk intelligence
product_category: AI security and third-party risk
market_need_then: LLM adoption in 2023 raised new security concerns, and press such as Axios in September 2023 described a startup market forming around AI security.
outcome_analysis: PromptArmor is Active and sells to named enterprise and law firm customers, and its public threat research builds credibility. The AI security category is consolidating through acquisitions of rivals, which raises both competitive pressure and exit odds. Funding could not be verified from primary sources.

name: Propaya
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
long_description: Propaya is an AI-powered commercial real estate intelligence platform that transforms leases and property documents into structured, actionable data. It extracts key terms, obligations, costs, and critical dates with source citations, while identifying legal, operational, environmental, and biological property-risk signals. Teams can customize risk taxonomies, track portfolio-level issues, export structured data, and route flagged findings to property managers, legal teams, or domain specialists for review.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Commercial real estate investors, brokers, property managers and data centers
problem: Reading leases and property documents for key terms, costs, dates and risks is slow and manual. Propaya extracts structured data with citations and flags risks.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: AI lease abstraction and property risk intelligence
market_need_then: Lease abstraction was a long-established paid service. The CTO and CEO's family property experience motivated the focus on building health risks such as mold and pests per the product site.
outcome_analysis: Propaya is Active as a two person team selling lease review to CRE firms, with named logos on its site. Only aggregators report about $500K in pre-seed funding. The market has established vendors that added AI features, so differentiation is the open question. There is no exit or failure signal and not enough evidence for a clear story.

name: Proxis
one_liner: The platform for enterprise AI agent automations, starting with email.
long_description:
Proxis is the AI automation platform built for enterprises.

Proxis is creating AI email agents that empower brands and enterprise teams to close deals automatically. Think: your inbox, on autopilot.

We initially fine tuned and distilled LLMs for enterprise use—and quickly realized that companies need more than just smarter models. They need full-stack automation. So Proxis built AI agents that handle the tedious, time-consuming work—everything from autonomous sales closers to customer service agents.

The mission is bold: to build the world’s most capable team of AI agents for every enterprise. Proxis imagines a future where a single founder can run a billion-dollar company—backed by a custom-built army of agents. Proxis is rethinking how agents are built, trained, and deployed from the ground up.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprise teams in sales, marketing and customer service wanting AI email agents, now internal AI tooling for companies
problem: Enterprise teams spend hours on email and routine work. Proxis builds AI agents that draft and send replies and automate workflows.
business_model: B2B enterprise AI services and software
product_category: Enterprise AI agents, starting with email
market_need_then: Interest in LLM automation of enterprise email was rising in 2024, but no hard evidence of demand for Proxis specifically was found.
outcome_analysis: Proxis is Active with a solo named founder and a team of 3. Its message moved from email agents to broader internal AI tools, and it released a consumer app called Gabber, which suggests a search for a market. No funding beyond YC could be verified and no exit is reported. There is not enough evidence for a clear success or failure story.

name: Pulse
one_liner: Production-grade unstructured document extraction

name: ReactWise
one_liner: AI Co-Pilot for Chemical Process Optimization
long_description:
Our Mission: 
We aim to accelerate and automate chemical process development by equipping wet-lab chemists with the power of data-driven optimization and robotic execution of experiments.


The Problem: 
The discovery of novel pharmaceuticals is one of our most important weapons in fighting disease. However, the drug development pipeline is often held up for many months during the design of chemical processes to manufacture these drugs at scale, delaying FDA trials and lengthening the time until drug launch. Designing chemical processes involves the identification of suitable parameters such as catalyst/temperature/solvent. Currently process development is often done via tedious trial-and-error experimentation (slow) or exhaustive screening (expensive and wasteful).


Our Approach: 
In our research, we have developed algorithms for chemical process optimization, which leverage transfer learning and Bayesian optimization. We validated the algorithms in the wet lab, showing an up to 95% reduction in required experiments and cost compared to exhaustive screening. We have made our approaches accessible to chemists through our user-friendly no-code software platform and to automated laboratory equipment with our API.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Process chemists and innovation heads at pharma and biotech companies, and lab equipment makers
problem: Chemical process development relies on trial and error or exhaustive screening, delaying drug manufacturing scale-up.
business_model: B2B software platform and API plus consulting, HTE plates and data services
product_category: AI and Bayesian optimization for chemical process development
market_need_then: TechCrunch reports 12 pilot trials with pharma companies, some Big Pharma; the company says process design delays FDA trials for months and claims up to 95 percent fewer experiments.
outcome_analysis: ReactWise, founded by two Cambridge PhDs in machine learning for chemistry, raised a 3.4 million dollar pre-seed in March 2025 including YC money and an Innovate UK grant, ran pilots with pharma customers and now lists Pfizer and Pharmaron in testimonials. No later round or exit was found, so it is an active early company with credible domain fit.

name: Redouble AI
tags: Generative AI; B2B; Workflow Automation; Enterprise; AI
one_liner: Java-native multi-agentic AI operating system for enterprise
long_description:
At Redouble AI we have developed Silverlake, a Java-native agentic AI operating system for enterprise. While other AI solutions force enterprise stakeholders to embrace unfamiliar concepts in an unfamiliar language, we do the opposite: we slot agentic AI right into the enterprise comfort zone - by mapping all agentic concepts onto established enterprise primitives in their own language, their own security model, their own infrastructure. It’s like moving from Bitcoin to Stablecoin, just for agentic AI. 

When we did YC we realized there was no framework or platform that gave us as enterprise and workflow automation veterans what we needed to build truly secure, reliable, and scalable agentic solutions for mission-critical workflows. That’s why we spent the past 18 months building Silverlake from the ground up. 

We empower the 12 million Java engineers worldwide to write and deploy their own AI, securely, at scale. They define an agent in a few lines of code, and our platform does everything else, from orchestration to permission control, from auditability to rate limiting, from long-running agents to autonomous coordinated networks that perform the work of entire departments. 

Silverlake has been developed with design partners across biopharma, insurance and financial services. For example, our agentic workflows write submission-ready Clinical Study Reports that are hundreds of pages long, analyze entire datarooms full of financial and operational data for private equity investors, and automate claims processing for a large insurance player. 

We are backed by Y Combinator, Exponential, Transpose Platform, Tiny VC, and the Oxford Seed Fund and advised by Java inventor James Gosling and automation guru Professor Christian Terwiesch.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Enterprises in biopharma, insurance and financial services with Java engineering teams
problem: Enterprises lack a secure, auditable agent platform in their own language and security model; Redouble maps agent concepts onto Java enterprise primitives.
business_model: Enterprise platform licensing plus forward-deployed engineering for turnkey solutions
product_category: Java-native agentic AI operating system (Silverlake)
market_need_then: At founding (S24) the company pitched quality control and human-in-the-loop for AI in regulated industries; the Java-native positioning came later after about 18 months of build.
outcome_analysis: Redouble AI is active and still early: a YC S24 company that moved from human-in-the-loop QA for regulated AI to a Java agent platform. Founders have enterprise and pharma automation credibility and a famous advisor, and design partners exist in biopharma, insurance and finance. No priced round is verified, and newer Java agent frameworks narrow its niche.
