Growth came from product fit with BPOs and contact centers, an experienced ex-ByteDance, Meta and Google team, and timing. Competition from Vapi, Bland and others is intense and moats are thin.

name: Reticular
tags: Generative AI; Consumer Health Services; Biotech
one_liner: Scaling Genomic AI for Embryo Selection
long_description:
Reticular is scaling polygenic prediction for embryo selection, helping IVF couples plan their families today while building a platform to unlock cures for complex heritable diseases long-term.

John competed Biology Olympiads before spending 4 years at MIT publishing ML/bio research in NeurIPS and Nature. We believe biological models encode far more information than anyone is currently using - our goal is to unlock this potential.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: IVF couples who pay for polygenic and reproductive genetic screening, and earlier pharma teams for interpretable protein AI
problem: IVF patients choosing among embryos have limited genetic information. Reticular offers polygenic prediction and reproductive gene screening, with a longer-term aim of using biological models to find cures for heritable disease.
business_model: direct-to-consumer genetic test and embryo report sales (about 399 to 749 USD per panel per its site)
product_category: genomic AI, reproductive genetic screening
market_need_then: IVF patients and clinics were adopting embryo screening, and Orchid launched whole genome embryo reports in December 2023. Public criticism (NPR and others) shows contested demand and ethics.
outcome_analysis: Reticular is a two-person company from Fall 2024 that appears to have moved from interpretable protein AI to embryo polygenic prediction and now sells an at-home reproductive gene panel. No priced round beyond the standard YC deal is verifiable. Outcome is unknown at this point, with ethical and scientific controversy around embryo selection a risk.

name: RetroFix
one_liner: Automate any workflow using plain english
long_description:
RetroFix is an automation platform designed to be extremely intuitive to use, making it much easier and faster to automate manual work. 

To create or modify workflows you can describe them in natural language and our agent will create them end-to-end for you. We allow you to connect with 2000+ applications and use our pre-built actions for your workflows. In the case we don't have a pre-built step, our agent can instead write code to access the full APIs of all the apps we integrate with.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Non-technical users, freelancers, agencies and ops teams who automate workflows; originally NYC building owners and contractors seeking energy-efficiency subsidies
problem: Automating manual work normally requires coding or complex tools. RetroFix lets users describe a workflow in plain English and an agent builds and monitors it. Earlier the team targeted the paperwork for building energy rebates.
business_model: SaaS subscription for workflow automation (early access); earlier concept was a service for rebate applications
product_category: AI workflow automation agent
market_need_then: Demand for automation was proven by large incumbents like Zapier, and LLMs made natural language workflow creation newly possible in 2024. For the original rebate idea, YC launch copy pitched it as a TurboTax for building rebates.
outcome_analysis: RetroFix launched in summer 2024 as a rebate paperwork tool, then repositioned to plain English workflow automation in a crowded category led by Zapier. It remains in early access with two MIT founders and no verifiable funding beyond YC. Outcome is undetermined; a thin moat and heavy competition are the main risks.

name: Revyl
one_liner: The Mobile Development Platform
long_description:
Revyl is the mobile development platform for agents, developers, product, and design. It brings development, build infrastructure, verification, and application intelligence together in one platform, giving teams and agents a shared source of truth for every mobile application.

Teams can build and run mobile applications in the cloud, understand how their applications work, collaborate across functions, and verify changes against the running app. AI agents gain the context and runtime they need to move beyond simply generating code and understand whether their work actually works.

By connecting the people and agents building software to the application itself, Revyl helps teams move faster, collaborate more effectively, and build mobile with confidence.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mobile engineering teams and AI coding agents that need to build, run and verify mobile apps; customers shown include Zillow, Tinder, Faire and RevenueCat
problem: Mobile app tests are brittle and slow to maintain, and AI agents cannot verify whether mobile changes work. Revyl started with natural language end-to-end mobile tests and expanded to cloud runtimes and app intelligence.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage-based cloud runtimes for testing and verification
product_category: mobile testing and development platform for agents
market_need_then: Uber reported its DragonCrawl LLM mobile tester saved over 25M USD in four months (per BetaKit), showing large spend on mobile QA. Manual and scripted mobile tests were widely seen as flaky.
outcome_analysis: Revyl raised a 1.1M USD pre-seed in September 2024 on the strength of its CTO's Uber DragonCrawl experience and has since broadened into agent verification infrastructure, with well-known app companies listed as customers on its site. No later round is verified, so traction is undocumented beyond company claims. Competition in AI testing is crowded.

name: Rewbi
tags: B2B; Energy; Renewable Energy; Cloud Computing; ClimateTech
one_liner: We build data centers 10x faster
long_description: Rewbi deploys 1-10MW distributed data centers in existing industrial buildings with surplus power, which is 10+ times faster than standard data center deployment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI labs and inference providers renting compute or buying tokens, and earlier battery storage owners
problem: Standard data centers take years to build because of power and permitting. Rewbi places 1 to 10 MW compute in existing industrial buildings with surplus power and says first tokens ran 39 days from inception at its pilot.
business_model: compute rental on 1, 3 or 5 year terms plus per-token inference
product_category: distributed AI data centers and inference compute
market_need_then: AI compute demand and grid interconnection delays made fast deployment valuable; the company cites a 39 day pilot as proof.
outcome_analysis: Rewbi is a four-person company from a repeat YC founder whose earlier startup was acquired by Stem. It appears to have shifted from battery storage optimization to fast data center deployment for inference. No funding round is verifiable, so traction and survival beyond its 39 day pilot claim are unknown.

name: RiskAngle
one_liner: AI medical summaries in minutes
long_description: RiskAngle delivers fast, accurate summaries of unstructured medical records for insurance companies and law firms. Our AI-powered platform enables users to streamline underwriting, expedite claims processing, and prepare cases with confidence.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: RiskCube
one_liner: AI commercial insurance brokerage for startups.
long_description:
RiskCube enables startups to close enterprise deals with top-rated insurance.

Mission: Building insurance products & services focused on lowering the protection gap for the innovation economy on a national and global scale. 

Today, we operate an insurance brokerage focused on startups. Through the brokerage, we see firsthand where traditional insurance products fail, from AI liability and autonomous systems to defense technology and new space risks.

We are now building proprietary risk models that can price risks even when little historical claims data exists. Our approach uses stochastic simulation, then applies traditional, explainable models to make the output transparent to underwriters and regulators.

This allows us to create new insurance and reinsurance products for emerging industries much faster than traditional carriers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Venture-backed startups in AI, SaaS, defense, fintech and space that need D&O, cyber and tech E&O coverage to close enterprise deals
problem: Startups struggle to get vendor-ready insurance quickly, and carriers lack models for emerging risks like AI liability. RiskCube brokers coverage and plans to build its own risk models.
business_model: insurance brokerage commissions, with planned proprietary risk models and new insurance products
product_category: AI-native commercial insurance brokerage
market_need_then: The CEO says startups struggled to get coverage while he worked at WTW, and enterprise buyers require proof of insurance. The company reports a case where a D&O premium fell from 11,000 to 4,400 USD (company claim).
outcome_analysis: RiskCube is a one-founder brokerage from Fall 2024 led by a former WTW and Munich Re risk analyst. It sells coverage to YC-backed startups and plans proprietary risk models, but no priced round is verified and it competes with funded digital brokers. The outcome is undetermined.

name: Risotto
one_liner: Risotto auto-solves IT support requests using AI
long_description:
Want to apply AI to your IT Helpdesk queue? Risotto helps you grant software access, limit access/permission grants by time, serve knowledge, and get approvals from people like managers. All using natural language directly in chat (AKA "ChatOps")

IT teams spend too much time manually provisioning software and answering the same question repeatedly. We help them improve resolution times, reduce SaaS spend, and enhance security with 24/7 automated software access and IT support. Check us out at: https://www.tryrisotto.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mid-size and growth-stage tech companies whose IT teams handle internal support requests (named customers include Gusto, Instacart, ThoughtSpot, Jobber, Retool)
problem: IT teams spend time provisioning software access and answering repeat questions. Risotto auto-solves tickets and access requests in Slack, Teams and email, with time-limited permissions and approvals.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI IT help desk
product_category: AI IT help desk and access management
founder_names: Aron Solberg; Alex Confer; Chris Paul
market_need_then: IT teams were overloaded with repetitive access and support tickets, and SOC 2 requires access reviews. Customers report Gusto auto-resolving about 55 to 60 percent of tickets (company and press claims).
outcome_analysis: Risotto's founders came from HelloSign, Dropbox and Gusto IT and product roles, and the product won well-known customers such as Gusto, Instacart and Retool. A 10M USD seed led by Bonfire arrived in January 2026, long after the Winter 2024 batch, which suggests capital-light growth. Moveworks and ITSM incumbents are the main threat.

name: Riveter
one_liner: Turn the web into structured data
long_description:
Riveter fully automates web data extraction, end to end. With a single API, agents can search, scrape, and structure data from the web. 

Customers like Snapchat and OpenAI use us to enrich datasets using Riveter's AI search agents that combine data from the web with third party or internal data.  

Their AI agents, custom scrapers, and integrations pack the power of browser use and automation for search, at a cost that allows for scale. 

You can even create a custom data API for repeated searches live in your app or internal databases. 

Perplexity and ChatGPT are great for single questions, but they can’t handle large amounts of data at once. And they’re working with a single agent and context window instead of one in every cell.

And Riveter’s web browsing can go further—even reading PDFs and images that may contain answers. 

Most teams still spend hours (or hire UpWorkers/contractors) to manually copy product specs, check competitor pricing, pull custom KYB/KYC data to assess customer risk, or scrape filings. Or they spend months building web scrapers, and when that still doesn't work, they come to Riveter.

Our founding team (Cody Watters - CTO, Abby Grills, CEO) brings deep product and engineering expertise from to YC-backed companies Gusto, Retool, and Middesk.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data, growth and ops teams and AI companies that need structured web data (customers named include Snapchat and OpenAI per YC page; Zeffy and others in testimonials)
problem: Teams spend hours copying data from the web or months building scrapers. Riveter runs AI search agents that find, read and structure web data at scale through one API.
business_model: usage-based API and app subscription for web data extraction
product_category: AI web search and data extraction agents
market_need_then: Companies were paying contractors or building scrapers to gather product, pricing and KYB data, and LLM browsing made automation viable. Claygent had been introduced in 2023 by Clay per Clay's own guide.
outcome_analysis: Riveter is a two-person Fall 2024 company founded by ex-Gusto, Middesk and Retool staff that sells AI web data agents and says OpenAI and Snapchat are customers. No priced round is verifiable and competition from Clay, Firecrawl and Exa is strong, so the outcome is undetermined.

name: Roundabout Technologies
one_liner: Software for AI-powered traffic lights
long_description: Roundabout Technologies makes AI-powered traffic lights, allowing cities to reduce pedestrian deaths, improve traffic, and reduce resident complaints. Our founding team has experience building safety-critical embedded systems and AI at Waymo, Zoox, Google, and Verily.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Municipal governments and traffic departments that operate signalized intersections
problem: Most traffic signals run on fixed timing plans and old loop detectors, which causes delays and unsafe crossings and generates resident complaints. Studies and retiming are manual and expensive for cities.
business_model: B2B and government software and hardware subscription per intersection (pricing not public)
product_category: AI traffic signal control using cameras and computer vision
competitors_at_founding: Miovision Surtrac; NoTraffic; Rhythm Engineering InSync
market_need_then: Cities face pedestrian deaths and resident complaints about specific intersections; the San Anselmo pilot at The Hub, running since August 2025 per local news, was driven by complaints. Adaptive systems cost an estimated 30,000 to 60,000 USD per intersection per one analyst, which leaves room for cheaper entrants.
outcome_analysis: Roundabout is an early stage YC Fall 2024 company with an active first deployment in San Anselmo, California, and founders with autonomy and perception experience from Waymo, Zoox and Google. No exit, shutdown or later round was found. Outcome is open: selling to cities is slow, but the claim of no special hardware could lower cost against incumbents.

name: Rove
one_liner: Earn airline miles on hotels and everyday spend.
long_description: Earn flexible airline miles on booking travel, shopping, and dining, all on top of your credit card rewards.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers, especially Gen Z and young travelers, who want airline miles without relying on a premium credit card
problem: Earning transferable airline miles usually requires premium credit cards and juggling many loyalty programs. Rove pools earning across hotels, shopping and dining into one mile that transfers to airlines.
business_model: Affiliate and hotel commission share: merchants pay Rove commissions and Rove passes part to users as miles; margin retained
product_category: Travel rewards and universal airline mile
competitors_at_founding: Rocketmiles; Rakuten; American Express Membership Rewards
market_need_then: Travel loyalty is large and card-driven; the founders said they flew to dozens of countries using points. The offer targets people without premium cards. Demand evidence is mostly founder claims and travel blog coverage.
outcome_analysis: Rove is an active YC Winter 2024 company that launched its universal airline mile publicly in May 2025 with partnerships across about 11 airlines and has since added dining, an app and gift cards. It raised about 2 million USD. No shutdown or exit was found. Success depends on airline partnerships and affiliate economics.

name: Rowboat Labs
one_liner: Open-source AI coworker with memory
long_description: Rowboat is an AI coworker for everyday work - email, meetings, projects, and people. It builds a local knowledge graph from your work and uses it to draft emails, prep meetings, track projects, and get work done on your own computer. It comes with batteries included - meeting note capture, in-app browsing, search, and app integrations - plus MCP support for custom tools.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Knowledge workers and developers who want a local, open-source AI assistant; earlier, developers and companies building multi-agent support systems
problem: AI assistants lack persistent memory of a person's email, meetings and projects. Rowboat builds a local knowledge graph and uses it to draft emails, prep meetings and track projects.
business_model: Open source Apache-2.0 product with hosted or enterprise offerings (monetization details not found)
product_category: Open-source AI coworker with memory
market_need_then: Developer interest in multi-agent systems was high in 2024, shown by the popularity of CrewAI, LangGraph and AutoGen. Demand for the later coworker product is shown by GitHub stars and repeated Hacker News front page posts.
outcome_analysis: Rowboat is an active YC Summer 2024 company that moved from customer support agents to an open-source multi-agent IDE and then to a local AI coworker, gaining over 16,000 GitHub stars. Funding and revenue are only on aggregators, so the company's financial strength is unproven. Platform vendors compete directly.

name: Rulebase
tags: Customer Success; Customer Service; Customer Support
one_liner: AI customer operations for regulated industries.
long_description: We run customer operations for regulated industries with AI. Our QA layer reviews every interaction, human and AI, cutting manual QA by 99%. On top of it sit specialist agents for onboarding, remediation, reactivation, and retention that own accounts from approved to transacting, chasing customers over WhatsApp, email, and SMS
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Fintechs, digital banks and regulated financial services running customer operations
problem: Manual QA reviews only 3 to 5 percent of customer interactions, leaving compliance gaps. Rulebase reviews every interaction and runs back office agents for onboarding, remediation and retention.
business_model: B2B SaaS and agent subscription for regulated companies (pricing not public)
product_category: AI customer operations, QA and compliance for fintech
market_need_then: Traditional QA reviews only 3 to 5 percent of interactions per the company, and regulated firms face compliance risk. Customers named by the company include Qonto, Rho, Kuda, Nala and Lesaka.
outcome_analysis: Rulebase raised a 2.1 million USD pre-seed in September 2025 led by Bowery Capital after YC Fall 2024 and sells to fintechs such as Qonto and Rho. It narrowed from voice fraud defense to QA and then to back office agents. It is active with a tiny team and faces well funded competitors.

name: RunLocal AI
tags: Developer Tools; Computer Vision; AI; ML
one_liner: AI agent that optimizes inference for embedded compute like Jetson
long_description:
RunLocal is an environment that specializes AI agents to optimize model for onboard compute platforms like NVIDIA Orin/Thor and Qualcomm → www.runlocal.ai

RunLocal is built for Physical AI engineering teams across autonomous vehicles, robotics, smart cameras and more.

It tracks every experiment and continuously refines experimentation data into an understanding of what drives performance on your target hardware.

This environment means that a generic coding agent (e.g. Codex or Claude Code) can experiment and iterate better, faster and cheaper. 

With RunLocal, you hit performance targets faster and ship more optimized models – without hiring inference optimization specialists. 

We’re working with leaders in autonomous vehicles and robotics. We're backed by investors like Y Combinator and 468 Capital.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Physical AI teams (autonomous vehicles, robotics, smart cameras) and silicon vendors that need models optimized for embedded chips
problem: Porting and optimizing models for onboard compute such as NVIDIA Orin and Thor and Qualcomm needs rare specialists. RunLocal uses agents plus a device farm to do it.
business_model: Recurring platform subscription plus fixed price optimization jobs paid only if targets are met
product_category: Edge AI inference optimization
market_need_then: Edge deployment of vision models in robots and vehicles was growing, with a shortage of inference optimization specialists claimed by the company.
outcome_analysis: RunLocal AI joined YC in Summer 2024 from London and remains active with 468 Capital, Ritual Capital and YC listed as backers. Its offer has shifted toward a service with outcome based pricing. Round sizes are not credibly sourced, so no performance judgment is made.

name: Ryse
tags: Fintech; Machine Learning; Marketplace; B2B; Proptech
one_liner: The secondary market for real estate leases
long_description: Ryse is the only marketplace where investors who want to buy leases can trade with real estate operators who want to sell leases.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Originally real estate operators selling leases and investors buying them; now property managers and owners taking rent advances
problem: Real estate operators wait months for rent while capital markets investors have no easy way to buy lease cash flows. Ryse launched as a secondary market for leases and now advances up to about 11 months of rent to owners through property managers.
business_model: Fee on rent advances (owner pays 10 percent per company site) plus 2 percent commission to property managers; originally marketplace
product_category: Proptech and fintech: lease marketplace and rent advances
market_need_then: The YC launch post frames a 1.5 trillion USD lease market and the founders came from REZI, a property manager. The company's site claims 120 million USD funded to date, a self-reported marketing figure.
outcome_analysis: Ryse is an active YC Winter 2024 company by founders of the failed YC W17 company REZI. It raised an estimated 5.9 million USD seed in March 2025 and its website now sells rent advances rather than the lease marketplace described by YC. It reports large funded volume, unverified.

name: Ryvn
one_liner: Easy and secure customer cloud deployments
long_description: Ryvn provides the devtools and infrastructure to easily deploy any workload, on any cloud, and on-prem. Run apps in your own cloud and offer Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) to your customers in minutes, with built-in observability designed for sensitive industries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: SaaS and AI software vendors who must deploy into enterprise customers' clouds or on-prem
problem: Enterprise buyers in regulated industries demand software run in their own cloud, which is hard for small vendors to ship and support. Ryvn gives one control plane for BYOC and on-prem deployments, updates and observability.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform for software vendors (pricing not public)
product_category: Developer tools: BYOC deployment platform
market_need_then: Vendors cite data privacy and sovereignty and enterprise security requirements as reasons customers demand deployment in their own clouds. Ryvn's site names customers such as Archil and Athena Intelligence and quotes one founder.
outcome_analysis: Ryvn is an active YC Fall 2024 company by two former Palantir engineers selling a BYOC deployment control plane to AI and SaaS startups. No public funding announcement, exit or shutdown was found. Direct competitor Nuon raised 16.5 million USD in December 2024, so competition is well funded.

name: Saga AI
one_liner: AI agents for patient access: referral intake, eligibility, and prior…
long_description: Saga deploys AI agents onto the back office of patient access for medical practices, physician groups, and health systems. The agents read every inbound referral, fax, and form, then complete the work inside the practice's EHR: they enter intake data, verify insurance eligibility with real-time X12 270/271 checks, submit and track prior authorizations through payer portals, and request missing records. Saga works in Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, MedENT, and other EHRs, with staff approval on sensitive actions. HIPAA-compliant, BAA included.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Medical practices, physician groups and health systems
problem: Patient access back offices spend labor on referral intake, insurance eligibility, prior authorization and phone calls inside EHRs. Saga agents do this work in the EHR with staff approval.
business_model: B2B SaaS for healthcare providers (pricing not public)
product_category: Healthcare AI agents for patient access
market_need_then: Prior authorization and referral intake are well known administrative pain points in US healthcare, shown by many funded startups in the space. Saga's own demand evidence is limited to an anonymous testimonial on its site.
outcome_analysis: Saga AI is an active YC Winter 2024 company with a small team led by a former Palantir product manager, selling EHR-based agents to medical practices. No funding, customers or exit are publicly documented in sources opened, so the outcome is unknown. Competition from well funded prior authorization vendors is heavy.

name: Sagaland
one_liner: AI entertainment platform
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Consumers who play interactive fiction and AI generated games, with in-app purchases
problem: Interactive stories are costly to author and static. Sagaland uses AI to let players generate, play and remix story games.
business_model: Consumer app with in-app purchases
product_category: AI interactive fiction and user generated games platform
market_need_then: Consumer demand for AI character and story apps was visible in 2023 and 2024 with Character.AI and AI Dungeon. Sagaland self reports 200K USD ARR in four weeks on its YC listing, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Sagaland is an active YC Winter 2024 company with a two-person team building an AI interactive fiction app with in-app purchases and a claimed 200K USD ARR. No funding, press or exit is documented, so the outcome is unknown and the consumer AI story market is crowded.

name: Sage Care
one_liner: Automating home care agency operations with AI
long_description:
Sage is a HIPAA compliant, AI-native communication platform that makes home care agency client-intake handling smarter, faster, and more reliable.

Teams that use Sage can save over 100 minutes of busywork per prospect, freeing up their teams to manage a larger, faster growing business.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-sized home care agencies that pay for client intake and communication software
problem: Home care agencies lose prospects and staff time on slow, manual client intake calls, notes and follow-up. Sage says its software saves over 100 minutes of busywork per prospect.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold through demos, no public pricing
product_category: AI receptionist, CRM and scribe for home care agencies
market_need_then: Home care agencies are small, phone-heavy businesses with intake handled by staff. The company's own description cites 100 minutes of busywork per prospect; no independent demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Sage Care is an early YC S24 company with a three person team and no verifiable funding or customer scale beyond one testimonial. The outcome is open: no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found, and one fetch of the company site suggested a banner about joining another company, which could not be confirmed by any search, so no exit is recorded.

name: Saldor
one_liner: Making procurement easy
long_description: Saldor is the AI-native procurement and accounts payable platform that takes every purchase from request to paid.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and mid-sized companies that run purchasing and accounts payable on email and spreadsheets
problem: Purchases move from request to approval, vendor contact, purchase order and invoice matching through manual steps. Saldor automates procure-to-pay with an AI agent.
business_model: B2B SaaS procure-to-pay platform
product_category: AI procurement and accounts payable
market_need_then: Procurement and AP automation is a long-standing software category; the founders' Crusoe background gave them a view of fast-growing companies buying heavily. No independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Saldor is an early YC S24 procurement company with a two person team. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found, and no funding beyond YC could be verified, so the outcome is still open and the competitive set of well funded procurement platforms is the main risk.

name: Salvy
tags: SaaS; B2B; Latin America; Telecommunications; AI
one_liner: Mobile carrier for businesses in Brazil
long_description:
Salvy is a mobile carrier for businesses in Brazil. Over 1800 companies use Salvy to manage over 20,000 mobile lines, cutting costs by over 50%.
The founders have worked many years together in Brazil's largest fintechs (Nubank and EBANX).

Today, every carrier in Brazil has roughly the same network quality - it isn't a differentiator. If you're an IT manager who needs to deploy 2k lines, you want an integrated and seamless solution. You need to deploy this resource, fast. Salvy provides a software layer that makes deploying and managing mobile lines a fast and efficient process, integrated with HRIS, ERPs, and others.

This is a massive market: there are 55 million b2b mobile lines in Brazil, which adds up to 5 billion dollars in ARR in just one country.
regions: Brazil; Latin America; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Brazilian companies that need to deploy and manage many employee mobile lines
problem: Corporate mobile lines in Brazil are bought from large carriers with little software for onboarding, HR and ERP integration. Salvy resells network access as an MVNO with a management layer.
business_model: MVNO subscription per line (R$29.90 to R$99.90 per line per month on the site) plus software features
product_category: B2B mobile carrier (MVNO) with management software
founder_names: Artur Negrao; Hudo Assenco; Maria Eduarda Kumlehn; Lucas Rosa
market_need_then: The YC description cites 55 million B2B mobile lines in Brazil and says network quality is similar across carriers. Early customers were SMBs; sources say it began as telephony as an employee benefit before focusing on corporate lines.
outcome_analysis: Salvy is a Curitiba MVNO selling business mobile lines. Founders from Nubank and EBANX raised a seed in February 2024 with YC and SaaSholic, followed by a larger extension reported by Brazilian press after Demo Day, and the company reports more than 1,800 business customers and 20,000 lines. It is active with product launches into 2026, so the story is steady growth without an exit.

name: Sample
one_liner: Flexible systems for clinical reasoning.
long_description:
Sample Healthcare transforms healthcare operations from a burden into a competitive advantage. 

Our users build copilots in Sample to support processes like patient intake and reimbursement. These copilots don't just speed up work – they capture valuable ground-truth data that make our models smarter over time.

We work with leading national providers, already have data from 76% of US oncology clinics, and our network is rapidly expanding across the nation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Healthcare providers such as oncology clinics and revenue cycle teams doing intake, record abstraction and prior authorization
problem: Clinical and administrative staff spend hours reading medical records and handling intake and reimbursement paperwork.
business_model: B2B SaaS and AI automation with human review
product_category: AI document workflows and copilots for healthcare operations
market_need_then: Prior authorization and intake were widely cited administrative burdens with several startups seeded in 2023; no Sample specific demand figures were verified.
outcome_analysis: Sample was a five person Winter 2024 healthcare AI company automating record abstraction, intake and prior authorization for clinics, with engineering rather than clinical founders. No funding was found publicly. In April 2026 TELCOR, owned by Accel-KKR, acquired it for undisclosed terms and the team stayed on, which suggests a strategic tuck in to a revenue cycle platform rather than a standalone venture outcome.

name: Sandra AI
one_liner: Building AI employees for car dealers
long_description: Sandra AI is building the AI operating system for car dealerships, replacing clumsy legacy software with an AI-native, automation-driven platform. Founded by 3 McKinsey, HEC & MIT alumni who met 10 years ago at Ecole Polytechnique, the company’s AI agents already automates all customer interactions across calls & messages, and increasingly run dealership operations by automating sales and aftersales workflows end-to-end. This operational footprint naturally extends into a proprietary software layer that unifies billing, scheduling, inventory, and CRM into a single dealership OS.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Car dealership groups, mainly in France
problem: Dealerships miss calls and lose leads and service bookings. Sandra AI sold AI agents that answer calls and messages and automate sales and aftersales workflows.
business_model: B2B SaaS for dealerships with custom pricing by size
product_category: AI voice and messaging agents for car dealerships
founder_names: Badr El Idrissi Mokdad; Ismail Majjad; Skandere Sahli
market_need_then: Dealerships take many phone calls, and French dealer groups such as Autosphere deployed the product, per French business press. No independent measure of spend found.
outcome_analysis: Sandra AI sold AI agents to French dealership groups after YC Fall 2024 and signed a network deal with Autosphere, per French press. In November 2026 trade press reported it would end European operations, with clients told service stops after February 2027. The cause is not public, so no failure factor is assigned.

name: Saphira AI
one_liner: The Enablement Layer for Physical AI
long_description: Saphira is the easiest way for hardware products to get safety certified and reach market faster, such as industrial robots and heavy machinery.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Robotics and heavy machinery makers that need safety certification
problem: Hardware companies spend months and consultant fees producing safety reports and getting certified (UL, CE, ISO, TUV). Saphira uses AI to generate safety analysis and requirements.
business_model: B2B software and services sold to hardware companies
product_category: AI safety and compliance for hardware and physical AI
market_need_then: Humanoid and industrial robot makers face ISO 10218 and similar standards; YC's launch post and early customers (Raise Robotics, 1X, RobCo) point to demand, though no revenue was found.
outcome_analysis: Saphira is an active YC S24 company that moved from a certification report generator toward AI agents for engineering physical systems, with named robotics customers and SOC 2. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found; funding beyond a reported small seed is unverified, so the company's outcome remains open.

name: Saturn
one_liner: Compliance and back office workflows for Wealth Managers.
long_description:
At Saturn, our mission is to make financial peace of mind more accessible by building the best operating system for wealth managers. 

Wealth and Asset Management is one of the world’s highest revenue-generating industries, yet it remains painfully inefficient. The sector relies heavily on disjointed legacy systems, manual human tasks, and a complex web of intermediaries, all of which increase costs. 

Saturn is an AI-powered operating system for wealth management built to automate investment research, streamline operations, and ensure compliance. Saturn creates the best version of truth, empowering investment advisors to work more efficiently, navigate complex regulatory landscapes, and deliver personalised, high-value services to their clients.

Today, Saturn supports over 200 firms globally that manage more than £35bn in assets under management (AUM) and over 200,000 clients.

As the industry grows, it faces massive operational challenges like bad tech, advisor retirements, regulatory pressure, an increased cost base, and transformational opportunities like great intergenerational wealth transfer and changing consumer needs.

Saturn aims to be at the forefront of this transformation, driving the future of wealth management.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent wealth management and financial advice firms, mainly in the UK
problem: Advice firms spend large amounts of adviser time on admin, reports, suitability letters and compliance checks. Saturn automates this with AI so each adviser can serve more clients.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for advice firms
product_category: AI operating system for wealth management compliance and back office
founder_names: Amal Jolly; Michael Ettlinger; Rohit Vaish
market_need_then: UK advice firms face high cost to serve, adviser shortages and regulatory pressure. The founders cite an advice gap and the company says it reached cashflow positive in its second month in market.
outcome_analysis: Saturn is active and grew fast: its site claims 500 plus advice firms and the October 2025 press release 600 plus, and it raised a $15M Series A led by Singular. The company cites cashflow positive status in its second month. Success factors are early product market fit with advice firms, the generative AI tailwind and a repeatable firm by firm sales motion. Final outcome is not yet known.

name: Scape
one_liner: The intelligent inbox that works for you
long_description: Scape is the intelligent email inbox, built for the one billion professionals who spend most of their workday in email. Designed to work proactively, Scape surfaces only the emails that need attention and prepares drafted responses, ready to review and send.
regions: Sweden; Europe
target_customer: Professionals and teams who spend much of their day in email
problem: Email overload: important messages get buried and replies take time. Scape is a desktop email client that surfaces what needs attention and drafts replies.
business_model: Subscription email client, pricing not published
product_category: AI email client
market_need_then: Email overload is widely felt and AI drafting was a clear 2024 technology shift; no hard demand metric for Scape was found.
outcome_analysis: Scape began in YC Summer 2024 as a customer support tool, pivoted to an AI email client, and emerged from stealth in July 2026 with a $3.2M seed from YC, General Catalyst and FundersClub. It is early with five people in Stockholm, and the main risk is that mail platform owners and funded AI clients compete for the same wedge.

name: SchemeFlow
one_liner: AI Report Generation for Engineering & Environmental Review
long_description:
SchemeFlow uses AI to generate technical reports for engineering and environmental review  for construction projects.

Two brothers + high school friend, with great combo of skills: Mayor’s Chief of Staff, Arup construction engineer + AI software engineer.

LLMs allow fast generation of reports & handling local regulatory complexity which wasn’t feasible before.

Working across Transportation, Air Quality, Noise, Flood Risk, Environmental review in the US and the UK, with major engineering companies such as Stantec, Buro Happold and Royal Haskoning.

$9B US opportunity (143k consultants x $64k/yr report-writing work), $23B worldwide.

www.schemeflow.com
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Engineering and environmental consultancies in the US and UK that write technical reports
problem: Consultants spend long hours drafting transportation, noise, air quality, flood risk and environmental reports for construction projects. SchemeFlow generates first drafts with AI.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to engineering firms, web app and Microsoft Word add-in
product_category: AI technical report generation for engineering and environmental review
founder_names: Andrew Browning; Jonny Browning; James Griffith
market_need_then: The YC description sizes report writing at 143k US consultants times $64k a year; the company's founders include a construction engineer and say LLMs made local regulatory handling feasible. Cambridge coverage cites over 4,000 reports generated, claim unverified.
outcome_analysis: SchemeFlow is an active YC S24 company selling AI report drafting to engineering consultancies, with named customers across the UK and US and a Cambridge profile citing thousands of reports. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found; funding beyond YC could not be verified.

name: Scout
one_liner: AI insights for consumer products
long_description: Scout is an AI insights tool for consumer products companies to increase topline revenue. It ingests data from retailer portals and syndicated sources (such as SPINS, NielsenIQ), and tell sales teams exactly where they can grow. Brands use Scout to figure out which accounts to expand, which SKUs to prioritize, and which promotions drove incremental sales.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Sales and retail teams at consumer packaged goods brands, from emerging to enterprise by revenue band
problem: CPG brands receive fragmented data from retailer portals and syndicated panels and struggle to decide which accounts, SKUs and promotions to prioritize. Scout ingests the data and recommends actions.
business_model: Engagement based pricing tiered by customer revenue (under 5M, 5M to 50M, 50M and up), with consulting alongside software
product_category: AI analytics and workflows for CPG sales
market_need_then: CPG brands pay for syndicated data and manually pull retailer portal reports, and vendors such as Crisp and Daasity market portal ingestion as a pain point; the need was established though dated 2024 sources were not found.
outcome_analysis: Scout is a very young company from Winter 2024 with a three person team, a solo founder with Wayfair and Menlo Labs experience, and a product aimed at CPG sales teams. No funding, customer counts or outcome events were found in public sources, so there is no story yet to attribute to success or failure factors.

name: Scritch
tags: Consumer Health Services; Health Tech; B2B; Healthcare; AI
one_liner: AI operating system for veterinary care
long_description: Scritch is building the leading AI systems for veterinary medicine, starting with voice agents that automate front-desk operations in veterinary practices.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent veterinary practices that pay for front-desk automation
problem: Vet front desks are overloaded with calls for appointments, triage and prescription requests. Scritch's AI receptionist Emily answers calls 24/7 and integrates with practice systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS for veterinary practices
product_category: AI voice receptionist for veterinary care
market_need_then: Vet clinics are staff-constrained and phone-heavy; a customer on the site reports human-handled calls dropped over 50%, a company-published testimonial.
outcome_analysis: Scritch is an active YC W24 company selling an AI voice receptionist to vet practices, with four named practices on its site. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found and no verified funding beyond YC, so the outcome is open and depends on beating broader AI receptionist vendors.

name: Selera Medical
one_liner: One-time, device-based treatment for heart failure
long_description: Heart failure impacts millions worldwide and is associated with poor quality of life and high mortality rates. Because the heart cannot pump efficiently, fluids buildup around the body. Fluid overload is the main driver behind patient symptoms (shortness of breath, fatigue, chest pain, etc.) and hospitalizations. Our minimally invasive device leverages the body's innate fluid management system to offload trapped fluid and prevent subsequent rounds of buildup. The one-time procedure has sustained effect -- keeping patients healthier, happier, and out of the hospital.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Sensei
tags: Hard Tech; Marketplace; Robotics; Data Engineering; AI
one_liner: Robotic Training Data at Scale
long_description: Sensei helps robotics companies scale and outsource their training data collection. Our hardware platform enables the collection of human-demonstration data at a tenth of the cost and twice the speed of current teleop approaches. Our software platform acts like Scale AI for robotics data: a large network of paid human operators use our low-cost collection platform to fulfill data-generation requests.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robotics companies and labs that need human demonstration data to train robot policies
problem: Robot learning is bottlenecked by scarce, expensive and low variety demonstration data, since teleoperation needs robots costing $40,000 or more and lab-bound collection. Sensei sells data collected by paid operators using a low-cost device.
business_model: Data collection service, per request pricing, plus hardware and a marketplace of paid operators
product_category: Robotics training data marketplace
market_need_then: The launch post argues data scarcity is the main bottleneck in robot AI and that teleoperation fleets of 5 to 20 collectors are slow and costly. Demand is asserted by the company, not shown by customer numbers.
outcome_analysis: Sensei is an active two person YC S24 company selling robot training data collected by paid operators. No outcome events were found, no round could be verified beyond aggregator listings, and the market of robotics data vendors grew crowded after its batch. It is too early to call it a success or a failure.

name: Senso
one_liner: Control what AI says about you
long_description:
Senso is building the infrastructure for the agentic web.

As AI agents replace websites as the primary interface for discovery, decisions, and commerce, enterprises need a new way to control how agents understand, reason over, and act on their data. 

Senso enables companies to register agent-first domains, ingest first-party enterprise data, and publish verified, structured ground truth that AI agents can safely answer from, recommend with, and transact against. 

Our platform continuously evaluates how models use this context and adapts it to gain authority across leading LLMs.

We are building the System of Record for Verified AI—powering AI discovery, agentic commerce, and post-transaction resolution across regulated and enterprise environments.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Financial institutions, first credit unions, now enterprises that want to control how AI models describe them
problem: Enterprises lack a verified source of truth for AI agents and answer engines; early on, credit unions lacked a way to answer member and staff questions from their documents.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for knowledge bases and generative engine optimization
product_category: Enterprise knowledge base and GEO platform
market_need_then: Credit unions and banks wanted accurate answers from their own documents; by 2025 enterprises worried about how AI answer engines represent them, creating the GEO category (the company launched a GEO tool in 2025 per BetaKit).
outcome_analysis: Senso started in 2017 selling retention analytics to financial institutions, nearly did not survive by 2022 according to its CEO, then joined YC in 2024 and rode the GEO wave. In October 2026 Zeta Global agreed to acquire it after its technology already powered Zeta's GEO offering; the price is undisclosed and the deal was announced, not shown as closed.

name: Sepal AI
tags: AIOps; Reinforcement Learning; Data Labeling; AI
one_liner: Data Development for Advanced AI
long_description:
Sepal is a data research company on a mission to advance human knowledge and capabilities through safe AI.

We partner with the world’s leading AI labs and enterprises to help their models get better at the tasks people actually want them to do.

We’ve built a Cloud-Native Agent Dataset Factory which turns the process of generating evaluation and training data from manual, inconsistent, and labor-intensive into something automated, standardized, and scalable.

Sepal AI was founded in 2024 by engineers and operators from Vercel and Turing. We went through Y Combinator, raised several million dollars from leading investors, and already count multiple Fortune 500s and top AI research labs as paying customers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: AI labs and enterprises that need evaluation benchmarks and training datasets built by experts
problem: Frontier models and enterprise deployments need high quality expert built evals and training data that generic annotation vendors cannot supply.
business_model: Services and data sales to AI labs (project based dataset and benchmark development)
product_category: Expert data development for AI evaluation and training
founder_names: Robi Lin; Kat Hu; Fedor Paretsky
market_need_then: AI labs were buying expert generated data and evals at growing volume in 2024, evidenced by the rapid growth of vendors in the space; no Sepal specific revenue was found.
outcome_analysis: Sepal AI was founded by two ex Turing operators who knew the expert trainer business, entering the data market as demand from AI labs surged. It grew to about 15 people and an expert network of over 20,000, and was acquired by Mercor on February 6, 2026 for undisclosed terms. Funding is only reported on aggregators at roughly 500K to 1M dollars, so the exit looks like a consolidation of expert supply rather than a distress sale.

name: Serve AI
one_liner: AI for Field Service Enterprises
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Field service operators (website: pest control operators with $150M+ revenue); YC launch post also shows a consumer refund app (pap!)
problem: Field service companies lose calls and leads; voice/AI agents answer calls, qualify leads, book appointments.
business_model: B2B SaaS AI agents for field service (per website)
product_category: AI call and booking agents for field service
market_need_then: No sourced evidence found for demand at the time; website claims are product mockups.
outcome_analysis: Serve AI is listed Active with 6 people. The YC profile mixes a field-service tagline with a consumer refund app (pap!), and the website sells AI agents to pest control operators, suggesting a pivot whose timing is unsourced. No funding, traction or press was found, so the story is unknown and any stated factors would be guesses.

name: Sharpe
tags: Finance; Analytics; Big Data; Data Engineering; AI
one_liner: Agents for quantitative research and financial data science.
long_description: Sharpe helps traders go from idea to profit in minutes with AI, bundling petabytes of market data with high-performance infrastructure.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Quant funds and traders who need data science on large market datasets
problem: Quant researchers spend time wrangling data and infrastructure; Sharpe offers an AI research agent that runs multi step analyses and outputs reproducible notebooks.
business_model: B2B SaaS, enterprise sales with pricing page
product_category: AI research agent for quantitative finance
founder_names: Vivek Hazari; Daniel DiPietro; John McCambridge
market_need_then: The YC page claims Sharpe helped a top 5 quant firm find $10M or more of profit within hours of deployment; this is a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Sharpe is an early stage quant research agent from the Lumenary team, which also built the Solar app builder. No outcome event or verified funding was found, and large incumbents moved into agentic finance research in 2026, so its position is still unproven.

name: Shepherd
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Education; Generative AI; Marketplace; AI
one_liner: Every student's personalized learning assistant
long_description: Shepherd is a Learning assistant for schools to provide to their students. Shepherd seamlessly combines AI-enabled self-study, affordable tutoring, peer collaboration, and analytics for a personalized learning experience that is both efficient and effective.
regions: Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Schools that provide a learning assistant to their students
problem: Students need affordable study help and tutoring; Shepherd bundles AI self study, tutoring, peer collaboration and analytics for schools.
business_model: B2B2C, sold to schools, with a consumer app
product_category: AI learning assistant for education
founder_names: Moyosoreoluwa Orekoya; Marcella Imoisili; Kehinde Williams
market_need_then: The founders say they were former students; the maker says the web version had over 100,000 early users before the April 2025 Product Hunt launch (Product Hunt listing). No dated spend evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Shepherd is an active small team selling an AI learning assistant to schools and students. Public evidence is thin: no verified funding, no exit, and a crowded edtech AI market led by Khanmigo. There is not enough information to explain a success or failure.

name: Shiboleth
one_liner: Shiboleth automates lending compliance for financial institutions…
long_description:
Shiboleth automates consumer lending compliance for financial institutions using AI.
Banks and fintechs use us to save months of manual work by automating audits and drafting reports for the governments. 

LLMs allow whole categories of manual compliance processes to be automated in ways that weren’t possible until recently.

We are excited to automate back-office operations and enhance consumer protection in one of the most litigious industries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Banks, fintechs and non-bank lenders that need consumer lending compliance
problem: Compliance teams manually review calls, complaints and marketing for violations and draft regulatory reports; Shiboleth automates monitoring and reporting.
business_model: B2B SaaS for regulated lenders and bank partners
product_category: AI compliance and quality assurance
market_need_then: Regulators scrutinise bank fintech partnerships and lenders; Axios and Crowd Fund Insider covered the company's February 2025 emergence from stealth as a bank fintech compliance play.
outcome_analysis: Shiboleth is an active YC W24 company with a founding team from security and bank fraud detection. It emerged from stealth in February 2025 with a reported $1.5M seed, and no later round, exit or distress was found. Findability suffers from its name, and competition from call QA vendors is growing.

name: Silogy
one_liner: An AI-powered test and debug platform for chip developers
long_description: Silogy is building an AI-powered platform for chip developers to simulate and debug their designs.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Chip design and verification teams
problem: Chip developers spend a large share of time on testing and debugging failing simulations; Silogy first offered cloud test running and now sells Viv, an AI agent that finds root causes.
business_model: B2B SaaS, on premise capable
product_category: AI chip verification and debug
market_need_then: The launch post cites a claim that chip developers spend 70% of their time on testing; AI chip design interest was rising.
outcome_analysis: Silogy is an active three person YC W24 company that moved from a cloud test running tool to an AI verification agent, Viv. No funding could be verified, no exit was found, and large EDA vendors and other AI chip verification startups are active in the same wedge.

name: Silurian
one_liner: Foundation models to simulate Earth, starting with weather.
long_description: Silurian is building foundation models for simulating Earth, starting with weather. From assessing the risk of wildfires to predicting the energy grid load, we provide an infrastructure layer for our planet. Our frontier models push the boundaries of what can be simulated on Earth and improve decision making across vital sectors including energy, insurance, agriculture, and logistics.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Energy, insurance, agriculture and logistics firms needing high resolution weather forecasts
problem: Traditional numerical weather prediction is expensive and slow; Silurian sells AI foundation models that forecast weather and can be tailored to customer data.
business_model: API and custom model contracts, enterprise
product_category: AI weather foundation models
market_need_then: Hurricane forecasts and energy and insurance risk are costly; the GFT launch claimed up to 30% better than NOAA and ECMWF on some variables (company claim); partners include Disaster Tech (June 2025) and NOAA AOML.
outcome_analysis: Silurian is an active YC S24 company led by the Microsoft Aurora researcher, launching GFT in 2024 and winning pilots such as Disaster Tech in 2025 and NOAA AOML collaboration. Funding is not verifiable, and Google, Microsoft and ECMWF competitors give it a hard technical race.

name: SimCare
one_liner: AI avatars to scale healthcare training.
long_description: SimCare is an all in one solution for training clinical skills in healthcare and behavioral health. From AI avatars that you can speak with, feedback systems trusted by the top programs in the country, to site placements tools that help you show your skills and find a job. SimCare is used across the board to train counselors, social workers, doctors and nurses.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Universities, counseling and social work programs, teletherapy companies, training organizations
problem: Counselors and clinicians have few ways to practice patient conversations at scale before real sessions.
business_model: B2B/B2edu per-institution licence (can be passed to students as a lab fee); a directory lists $49 a month for individuals (unverified)
product_category: AI patient simulation for healthcare training
market_need_then: YC launch post cites a doctor shortage and government mandates to expand medical school seats, which schools struggle to staff with actor-based patient simulations. Early tool reached 2,500 users and $5k MRR in three weeks (YC launch post, company-reported).
outcome_analysis: SimCare (formerly Soma Lab), YC S24, grew from an AI communications coach into AI patient avatars for medical, counseling and nursing training. After being rejected once for S24 and reapplying, it raised a $2M seed in February 2025 co-led by YC and Drive Capital and reported 30 pilots, with University of Pennsylvania as a pilot customer and Touro and The Chicago School using it (2026 coverage). No later round, exit or shutdown found; the outcome is early and unresolved, with several AI patient-simulation startups entering the same space.

name: Simple AI
one_liner: AI voice that sells
long_description: Simple AI is building AI voice that sells. Our voice agents know every detail about every product SKU. They’re trained on the best reps, so every call is handled at top-performer quality. Simple AI agents already outperform trained live reps by 30% on conversion and upsell.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer facing businesses with high volume phone sales and support, such as retail, home services and insurance
problem: Inbound and outbound phone sales rely on costly human agents and seasonal hiring; Simple AI voice agents answer calls, know product catalogs and close orders.
business_model: Outcome based pricing for voice and omnichannel AI sales agents
product_category: Voice AI sales agents
market_need_then: Omaha Steaks reportedly cut seasonal hiring from 5,000 to 692 and call abandonment from 16% to 3% per the company case study (company claim). The founders' consumer phone assistant led to the Omaha Steaks interest.
outcome_analysis: Simple AI began with consumer assistants and moved into enterprise voice sales agents, landing Omaha Steaks and other named customers. It raised a $14M seed in February 2026 led by First Harmonic. Competition from voice agent platforms is intense but it shows early enterprise traction.

name: Simplex
tags: Machine Learning; Robotic Process Automation; B2B; AI
one_liner: AI agents to enroll providers with payors
long_description: Simplex builds AI agents to handle provider enrollment end-to-end. We automate pulling provider data from CAQH, filling out enrollment forms + uploading licenses via payor portals/email/phone, updating applications when returned for corrections, and performing effective date follow-ups until a final determination is made, all autonomously.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Healthcare provider groups, clinics and RCM or health tech companies that must enroll clinicians with payors; later developers needing browser automation for legacy portals
problem: Provider enrollment with insurers is slow manual work across CAQH, payer portals, PDFs, email and phone. Simplex agents run it end to end and follow up until a determination.
business_model: Flat fee per completed enrollment plus an annual fee for CAQH profile management (per company site); developer web agent platform positioning later
product_category: AI agents for healthcare administration and browser automation
market_need_then: Payer enrollment is a known manual back office burden for provider groups. Dated 2024 evidence beyond the company's own pitch was not found; market evidence is from the company site and YC page.
outcome_analysis: Simplex is an early stage YC S24 company run by two MIT engineers. It positioned first around healthcare provider enrollment agents and later as a developer web agent platform for legacy portals, shown by YC launch pages and a Launch HN post. No funding, exit or shutdown was found, so there is not enough public evidence to call a success or failure. Competition from AI native credentialing startups funded in 2025 is a later development.

name: Smooth
one_liner: Fast, simple, reliable AI browser agent
long_description: Smooth is an AI browser agent that can perform actions autonomously on the web using mouse and keyboard. It’s the most reliable browser agent yet, while also being 5 times faster, and 7 times cheaper than any other browser agent on the market.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need to automate web tasks via API/SDK
problem: Browser agents are slow, expensive and unreliable; Smooth offers a faster, cheaper agent with API and CLI.
business_model: Usage-based API/SDK for browser agents (inferred from docs and PyPI SDK)
product_category: AI browser agent API
market_need_then: Growing demand for web agents in 2024 is plausible but no dated source on spend or complaints was found.
outcome_analysis: Smooth is a two-person Fall 2024 YC company building a browser agent API. No funding, revenue or customer figures were found, so no judgement can be made about success or failure; the only evidence is vendor-reported benchmarks claiming 5x speed and 7x cost advantage over Browser Use.

name: Solari AI
tags: Workflow Automation; Team Collaboration; Chatbots; No-code; AI
one_liner: Gives non-technical team members agents that work right out of the box
long_description: Solari gives non-technical team members access to agents that work right out of the box.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Non-technical team members inside companies who want ready to use AI agents
problem: Teams without engineers cannot build or deploy workflow agents. Solari offers agents that work out of the box.
business_model: Not stated; likely B2B software subscription (unverified)
product_category: No-code AI workflow agents
market_need_then: Demand for no code AI agents was rising in the 2024 AI wave, but no Solari specific evidence of customer pain or traction was found.
outcome_analysis: Solari AI is a one person YC W24 company in Mumbai or New York with no public funding, exit or traction data found. The YC page lists it as active. Without customer or revenue evidence, and with the product category crowded by larger platforms, the outcome cannot be judged from public sources.

name: Sonatoria
one_liner: Helping Startups Grow Organically
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Fast growing startups and brands that buy UGC creator video campaigns
problem: Brands want creator video content without agency fees of tens of thousands of dollars per campaign. Sonatoria matches vetted creators, writes briefs and tracks video performance.
business_model: Per creator monthly fee plus management fee starting at $200 per month (company site)
product_category: AI assisted UGC creator marketplace and campaign management
market_need_then: Demand for UGC video ads was visible across TikTok and Instagram marketing in 2024, but no Sonatoria specific traction evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Sonatoria is a two person YC S24 company whose public descriptions vary: the YC page lists a launch of Winford Wealth, an AI meeting assistant for financial advisors, while the website sells UGC creator campaigns. No funding, exit or traction figures were found, so the outcome is not assessable. The shifting product story suggests early stage searching for a market.

name: Sonia
tags: Consumer Health Services; Digital Health; AI
one_liner: Validated mental health support in your pocket, anytime.
long_description: We're on a mission to build safe, voice-based AI that makes high quality mental health support accessible to anyone. Founded by a team of MIT and ETH researchers who published papers at top AI conferences like NeurIPS, ICML, EMNLP and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers seeking mental health support (subscription), plus employers, providers and payers via enterprise deals
problem: Therapy is expensive and hard to access. Sonia offers voice and text AI coaching built on cognitive behavioral techniques, later with licensed therapist video sessions.
business_model: Consumer subscription ($20 per month or $200 per year at 2024 launch per TechCrunch) plus enterprise partnerships
product_category: AI mental health coaching app
market_need_then: Therapist access and cost problems are well documented; Sonia reported about 8,000 users at its June 2024 launch coverage and cited demand from mental health organizations.
outcome_analysis: Sonia raised a roughly $3.35M seed in June 2024 after YC W24 and launched a paid voice AI therapy app with about 8,000 users. It later added couples coaching and licensed therapist sessions in California plus enterprise offers. The generative AI wave was a tailwind, while general chatbots and AI therapy criticism are risks. No later round, exit or shutdown was found.

name: Sorcerer
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Climate; Aerospace; AI
one_liner: Building a nervous system for the atmosphere
long_description: Sorcerer is deploying a global network of persistent airborne sensors to fuel advanced weather forecasting. Our high-altitude balloons collect 1000x more data than existing systems and are already used daily by meteorologists to track extreme weather across the US and Central America.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Meteorologists, forecasters and government or commercial weather-data buyers
problem: Atmospheric observation is sparse, especially over oceans and remote areas, which limits forecast accuracy.
business_model: Weather data and forecast products from a persistent balloon fleet
product_category: Long-duration weather balloons and atmospheric data
founder_names: Austin Tindle; Maxmillion McLaughlin; Alessandro Vecchi
market_need_then: Government forecasting faced budget cuts (2025 coverage) and AI weather models create demand for more observations; the YC page says meteorologists use the data daily.
outcome_analysis: Sorcerer's founders came from Urban Sky's stratospheric balloon work and joined YC in Summer 2024. They raised a $3.9M seed in June 2025 and report daily use by meteorologists. A competitor (WindBorne) is already larger, so scale and funding are the open questions; the company is Active.

name: Soundry AI
tags: Social Media; Music; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Remix any song into any style
long_description: We build generative AI tools that enhance the fan engagement experience. Want to remix Taylor Swift in the style of Slayer? Now you can with our new product Groove.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Spaceium Inc
tags: Hard Tech; Robotics; Space Exploration; Aerospace
one_liner: In-Space Refueling
long_description:
Spaceium builds fully automated space stations to refuel and repair spacecraft. We have secured $86.1 million in binding commercial contracts and have an additional $230 million in the pipeline. Additionally, we have 1 billion dollars in letters of intent. We have successfully tested our hardware, which will launch to space next year. 

Our fully automated space stations will efficiently store and transfer both cryogenic (extremely cold) and non-cryogenic fuels with zero loss during storage and transfer. And they can transfer fuel seamlessly to any spacecraft design using our proprietary modular robotic arm.

Our customers include launch vehicles, orbital transfer vehicles, moon landers, and spacecraft that benefit from increased payload capacity and extended travel capabilities. Our long-term vision is to build service hubs along the space superhighway to connect Earth to Moon and Mars and help humanity to become multi multi-planetary species
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Launch vehicle, orbital transfer vehicle, lunar lander and spacecraft operators that need in orbit fuel

name: Speck

name: Sphinx

name: Spur

name: Stacksync

name: Starcloud
tags: Hard Tech; Satellites; Climate; Cloud Computing; AI
one_liner: Data centers in space
long_description:
Starcloud is building data centers in space, initially to provide GPU compute to other satellites, and later to address the rapidly growing demand for energy caused by the deployment of AI. Falling launch costs give Starcloud access to abundant energy, radiative cooling, and the ability to rapidly scale in space.

In November 2025, just 21 months after founding, Starcloud launched its first satellite, Starcloud-1 to space. This has an Nvidia H100, which is 100x more powerful GPU than has ever been operated in space before. With this, they became the first entity to train an LLM in space and the first to run a version of Gemini in space. Starcloud will soon also run high-powered inference on Capella SAR data on orbit for the first time. 

Starcloud is launching its second satellite in Q1 2027, which will have 100x the power generation of the first and generate more cash than it costs to build and launch. Starcloud expects that within 10 years, most new data centers will be being built in space for the energy.

In March 2026, Starcloud raised a $170M Series A led by Benchmark, becoming the fastest unicorn in YC history, just 17 months after demo day. In August Starcloud raised an additional $250M at a $2.3bn valuation with participation from Nvidia and Cisco.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

business_model: Space-based compute capacity sold as a service, with a later plan for large orbital training clusters
product_category: Orbital data centers, hard tech
founder_names: Philip Johnston; Ezra Feilden; Adi Oltean
market_need_then: In 2024 AI compute demand was driving data center power shortages and permitting delays, and falling launch costs made orbital infrastructure plausible; no customers existed yet for space compute at scale.
outcome_analysis: Starcloud launched its first satellite with an H100 in November 2025 and raised a 170 million Series A in March 2026 and a 250 million extension in August 2026 at 2.3 billion dollars, among the fastest unicorns from YC. Success rests on a complementary founding team, the AI power narrative and launch cost declines; risks are schedule slips (second satellite moved to 2027) and entry by SpaceX and Google.

name: Storia AI
tags: Developer Tools; Machine Learning; SaaS; AI
one_liner: Open source AI copilot that knows your company's code and its context
long_description:
With AI increasingly automating away code generation, software engineers will spend more time reading, judging, and architecting code rather than writing it. Storia is building an open-source copilot that knows a company's codebase and its context.

We are starting with Sage, a Perplexity-like agent for helping developers understand, judge, and generate software. Given an existing codebase, developers can ask Sage questions such as:
1) Given my project’s SLA and latency constraints, what is the appropriate underlying vector database to use? How would I incorporate it into my existing codebase?
2) Why should I pick Redis over Milvus as my underlying vector store?
3) Does this codebase in our organization still work and what steps are required for a complex integration with another library?

Sage’s answers are directly supported by documentation and external references like GitHub, Stack Overflow, technical design documents, and project management software, preventing hallucinations. Today, Sage has up-to-date knowledge about open-source repositories (indexed daily). Tomorrow it will have a deep understanding of every line of code on the Internet. For teams, Sage will know about your private codebase too.

No group has yet solved how to build an AI system that comprehends a codebase and its context and can empower every developer to architect better code, faster. This requires new research advances because vanilla RAG and out-of-the-box LLMs aren’t going to cut it. 

We have 20+ years of software engineering and AI research experience. Julia worked on precursors of Gemini using contextual neural techniques before they were called “RAG” (and applied it to products like Google Keyboard and Pixel phones). Mihail built the earliest LLMs at Amazon Alexa and launched the first contextual deep learning conversational AI system in production at Alexa.

name: SureBright
