problem: Training new frontline employees on real customer scenarios is costly and risky; practice with real customers leads to mistakes.
business_model: B2B SaaS for enterprise training simulations
product_category: AI voice roleplay training
market_need_then: Insurers face turnover in claims adjusters and need faster onboarding; the company says it was live with 2 of the top 3 North American auto insurers at launch (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Symphony joined YC in Fall 2024 with early insurer customers and later narrowed to insurance frontline teams. Funding is only reported by aggregators, no exit or shutdown was found. The outcome is undetermined; the main risk visible is a crowded AI roleplay category and a generic, colliding name.

name: Synnax
one_liner: Unified Hardware Control and Data Processing Software
long_description: We build software that helps hardware teams quickly and clearly evaluate how a component (engine, battery, valve, etc.) or process (assembly line, manufacturing plant) performs. We prevent mistakes, reduce costs, and accelerate time-to-market. Our platform unifies industrial control with sensor data storage and automated post-processing, delivering an end-to-end operations and observability stack. To put it comparatively, take LabVIEW, InfluxDB, and Grafana, wrap them into a single package, add a bit of magic, and you get Synnax.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware engineering teams in aerospace, energy, automotive and manufacturing that test engines, batteries, valves and plants
problem: Hardware teams stitch together LabVIEW, a time-series database and dashboards, which causes missed failures and slow test review.
business_model: Software platform with free desktop download and paid enterprise offering; pricing not found
product_category: Hardware control, data acquisition and test observability software
founder_names: Emiliano Bonilla; Patrick Dotson; Elham Islam
market_need_then: Founders saw outdated control software and poor data review lead to costly hardware failures; the founders were the first beta users on a university rocketry team per YC.
outcome_analysis: Synnax is an active five person company from YC Summer 2024 whose founders come from SpaceX, NASA JPL and Firefly, which gives strong domain fit for aerospace test teams. No verified funding, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is undetermined. Its path depends on displacing entrenched LabVIEW workflows.

name: SynsoryBio
one_liner: "If-then" conditional logic for protein drugs
long_description: SynsoryBio is creating next generation, protein therapeutics that sense where they are in the body and only activate at diseased tissue. This technology platform has the potential to expand the therapeutic window of highly potent drugs and apply to many diseases such as cancer and autoimmune disorders.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Biopharma partners and drug developers working on protein therapeutics for cancer and autoimmune disease
problem: Potent protein drugs such as immunotherapies are too toxic because they act in healthy tissue; drugs that only turn on at diseased tissue would widen the therapeutic window.
business_model: Therapeutics platform; likely partnering or pipeline development (not stated)
product_category: Conditionally active protein therapeutics
market_need_then: Toxicity limits potent cancer immunotherapies, per the company's YC description; masked and conditionally active biologics were an active area with clinical programs by 2023.
outcome_analysis: SynsoryBio is an active two person biotech from YC Winter 2024 building conditionally activated protein drugs. Only a small grant and aggregator-reported pre-seed money were found. Biotech needs far more capital than the early rounds provide, so the key milestone is a priced seed or partnership, which is not yet sourced.

name: Synth
one_liner: Prompt and Context Optimization for Coding Agents
long_description: Choose a coding agent harness, model, and task dataset and optimize context and prompts to get the best performance for long-horizon tasks
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams building AI and coding agents who want better performance on long-horizon tasks
problem: Agents fail in repeated ways and hand-tuning prompts, context and models is slow; teams want automated optimization against their own task data.
business_model: Developer platform with free and paid tiers (a 2026 profile lists 20 and 200 dollars per month plans)
product_category: Agent optimization and reinforcement learning tooling
market_need_then: Agent builders in 2024 faced unreliable performance and manual prompt tuning; the company reports a 33% relative gain on SWE-Bench for SWE-Agent with 100 training points (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Synth is a one-founder research-led company from YC Fall 2024 that has reframed its offer from vertical agent training to coding-agent optimization and managed research. It still ships a product in 2026 per a profile. No verified funding or exit was found, so the outcome is undetermined and the key risk is open-source and lab-provided optimization.

name: Syntra
one_liner: Faster healthcare payments
long_description:
Syntra’s mission is to make healthcare faster, starting with healthcare payments.

Syntra Autonomous, our first product, automates pre-bill chart review, claim review, and submission.

In the 12 months since launch, Syntra Autonomous has processed more than 1 million patient encounters and over $200 million in insurance collections across hundreds of practice locations nationwide.

If you’re interested in building toward infinitely fast healthcare, reach out!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Specialty medical practices and clinics that bill insurers
problem: Claims go out with missed revenue and compliance errors because charts and claims are reviewed manually before billing, delaying payment.
business_model: B2B SaaS tied to claim review and collections, pricing not found
product_category: Healthcare revenue cycle automation
market_need_then: Billing errors and delayed collections cost practices revenue; the company reports over 1 million encounters and 200 million dollars in collections processed in its first 12 months (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Syntra reports fast early volume across hundreds of practice locations in its first year after YC Summer 2024, with an 8 person team. Funding is only seen on aggregators and no exit or shutdown was found. The outcome is undetermined but traction claims point to real early demand in a space with well-funded coding competitors.

name: Tabula
one_liner: Autonomous Accounting Software
long_description:
We build autonomous accounting software. 

Every company should have financial insights at a fingertip – not just big enterprises with dedicated finance teams. For the first time, AI makes this possible. In the intelligence age, business owners with no financial expertise will get access to all the latent knowledge hidden in their books. Businesses will operate with a level of clarity, confidence, and speed that is almost unimaginable today.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: German tax and accounting firms (Steuerkanzleien) and their SME clients
problem: Accounting firms spend hours on manual bookings, receipt splitting and chasing missing documents, and staffing shortages limit how many clients they can take on.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to accounting firms, integrated with DATEV
product_category: AI accounting automation
founder_names: Tim Hermes; Markus Jungnickel; Kilian Justus
market_need_then: The YC launch post says customers turn away 5 to 10 new clients weekly because of staffing shortages, and a 40-person firm customer quoted saved hours each week on split receipts. No revenue figures are given.
outcome_analysis: Tabula is an active Summer 2024 company with no shutdown, acquisition or layoff news found. The founders came from Taxfix and Trade Republic and sell an AI bookkeeping layer to German tax firms, a niche with clear labor pain. Funding and traction are only visible through aggregators and job posts, so its trajectory cannot yet be judged.

name: Tamarind Bio
tags: AI-powered Drug Discovery; SaaS; B2B; Biotech; AI
one_liner: AI Inference Platform for Drug Discovery
long_description:
Tamarind Bio is a website and API which allows scientists to use computational biology tools at scale using a simple interface. On Tamarind, scientists can use ML models like AlphaFold to design and simulate molecules by simply selecting inputs instead of or setting up a high performance computing environment or dealing with DevOps.


Tamarind is used by tens of thousands researchers in large pharma companies, top biotechs, and academic institutions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Computational biologists and drug discovery teams at pharma, biotech and academic labs
problem: Scientists who want to run models like AlphaFold must set up high performance computing and DevOps, which blocks wet lab researchers from using them at scale.
business_model: Usage-based web app and API subscriptions for computational biology tools
product_category: AI inference platform for drug discovery
market_need_then: AlphaFold and related protein models spread widely after 2021 and wet lab scientists lacked easy access; the founders began by serving a Stanford lab and the YC launch post cited more than 1,000 scientists.
outcome_analysis: Tamarind raised a 13.6M Series A in February 2026 led by Dimension Capital after starting with one Stanford lab and growing to a claimed 8 of the top 20 pharma companies. The wave of open protein design models gave it a tailwind, while its main risk is that cloud vendors and free tools copy the access layer.

name: Tandem
one_liner: AI-native office leasing broker
long_description:
Tandem is an AI-native office leasing platform. We’re using technology to unlock an easier leasing process.   Our AI co-pilot provides a white-glove-quality B2B office search experience, with a fraction of the human labor typically required.

Today we’re serving three primary markets — NY, SF and BOS.  We’ve helped more than 750 companies find great office space and have seen double-digit month-over-month growth.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and small to mid sized companies looking for office space; revenue paid by landlords as broker commission
problem: Finding and leasing small, short term or shared office space is slow because inventory is fragmented across landlords and brokers.
business_model: Brokerage commission paid by landlord on signed leases, free to tenants
product_category: AI office leasing brokerage
market_need_then: YC page and company copy say traditional brokerage serves big long term leases well, while smaller, short term and shared space is hard to find; post-COVID office demand shifted, and Sands researched that at Stanford.
outcome_analysis: Tandem is an active Summer 2024 company that raised a 6.1M seed in February 2025 including an earlier 750K pre-seed, and operates in New York, San Francisco and Boston. No negative outcome news was found. Its path depends on turning AI search into broker economics against established commercial brokerages.

name: TaxGPT
one_liner: AI tax assistant for professionals and businesses
long_description: TaxGPT AI co-pilot for accountants and tax professionals increases tax firm's productivity and profitability by 10x by automating tax research, client communication, onboarding flows and secure document collection.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Accounting and tax firms, CPAs, enrolled agents and tax lawyers, plus individuals and businesses
problem: Tax professionals spend large amounts of time on research, memos, client emails and document collection, and there is a labor shortage in the profession.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscriptions for tax firms with a consumer tier
product_category: AI tax research and preparation assistant
competitors_at_founding: Blue J (Ask Blue J); Thomson Reuters Checkpoint Edge with CoCounsel
market_need_then: Generative AI made tax research assistants feasible in 2023, and the company cites a workforce shortage; it reports over 10,000 professionals using it at the 2025 seed.
outcome_analysis: TaxGPT is active and raised a 4.6M seed in February 2025 after pivoting from a consumer tool to firms, riding the generative AI tailwind. Its main risk is that Thomson Reuters and Blue J launched competing AI research in 2023 and 2024, so growth depends on speed and workflow depth.

name: Tekton Dynamics
one_liner: AI control layer for welding robots
long_description:
Our mission is to empower every manufacturer, no matter their scale, to invent and build anything using intelligent robots.

Today’s industrial robots are fast but "blind". They struggle with any task that isn't perfectly repetitive. We are building the eyes and brain (a proprietary vision system and AI model) that allow industrial robots to see, reason, and perform complex work with sub-millimeter accuracy and the adaptability of a human expert.

We are witnessing the start of a new industrial revolution: an era of advanced manufacturing powered by AI and robotics. We aim to lead this shift by putting these tools into the hands of every manufacturer, ensuring the power to invent and build at scale isn’t a privilege of the few.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Small and mid-size manufacturers and fabricators that run welding robots on high-mix work
problem: Industrial robots need extensive programming and cannot adapt to variation, so high-mix welding stays manual.
business_model: Hardware plus software: a vision system and AI edge device installed on an existing robot cell, sold to manufacturers (pricing not public)
product_category: AI control layer for industrial welding robots
market_need_then: Welder shortages and the poor fit of traditional robot programming for small batches were the demand drivers cited by this class of startups. No Tekton specific demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Tekton Dynamics is a Winter 2024 YC company led by an Oxford machine learning PhD, still active with a three person team. Funding is unclear, with conflicting unverified figures, and no exit or shutdown was found, so there is no outcome to explain yet beyond a crowded AI welding market.

name: Terrakotta
tags: Real Estate; Sales; Telecommunications; Home Services; Conversational AI
one_liner: AI platform for phone-first sellers
long_description: Terrakotta is a power-dialer that lets sales reps leave AI-generated voicemails.  Our first customers are Commercial Real Estate brokerages that use Terrakotta to clone their brokers voices, dial prospects and when no one answers, leave an A/B tested, personalized voicemail that gets a callback.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Commercial real estate brokerages and brokers doing phone prospecting
problem: Brokers make many cold calls that go to voicemail, and generic voicemails rarely earn callbacks.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat for a calling and data platform
product_category: AI power dialer and CRE data platform
founder_names: Vincent Wilson; Kusiima Boswell; Gabriel Wilson
market_need_then: Brokers rely on cold calling and voicemail callbacks; company copy says its first customers are CRE brokerages. No dated demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Terrakotta is an active Winter 2024 company that started as an AI voicemail dialer and now sells a CRE calling and data platform with named brokerage logos on its site. No shutdown or acquisition news was found, and outside funding is unclear, so the stage of its growth is unknown.

name: Tesseral
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; Security; Open Source; API
one_liner: The open source platform for managing identity in business software
long_description:
Tesseral is the open source platform for managing identity and access in business software. It provides enterprise-grade capabilities, including SAML single sign-on, SCIM provisioning, role-based access control, managed API keys, and audit logs, implemented in just a few lines of code. 

Tesseral unifies access management for employees, customers, services, and AI agents, giving organizations the flexibility to adapt to any deployment model and the authority to enforce security policies with precision.

You can learn more by reading our docs at https://tesseral.com/docs or by checking out our GitHub at https://github.com/tesseral-labs/tesseral.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: The Forecasting Company
tags: B2B; Supply Chain; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Foundation models for time series
long_description: The Forecasting Company builds planning systems based on our in-house foundation models for time series.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Enterprises needing demand, energy, retail and workforce forecasts, plus researchers using open weights
problem: Forecasting usually requires per series feature engineering and model tuning; a pretrained time series foundation model aims to give calibrated forecasts with no fine tuning.
business_model: Usage-based API and web app on proprietary foundation models, with open weights releases
product_category: Time series foundation models and planning systems
market_need_then: Forecasting underpins supply chain and energy planning, and 2023 to 2024 saw a wave of foundation model attempts for time series; the company lists Engie, Netflix and Shake Shack as users on its site.
outcome_analysis: The company is active, ships an open weights forecasting model and lists known enterprise users, but funding beyond a small 2024 note is not publicly documented. It competes with Google, Amazon, Salesforce and Nixtla models that appeared at the same time, so its future depends on model quality and product delivery.

name: The New Money Company
one_liner: Invoicing that pays you even if your buyer doesn’t
long_description:
The New Money Company protects invoices with insurance.

We help businesses expand to buyers in new markets or industries by offloading the risk of buyers not paying their bill.

Support number: +18889975745.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Businesses selling to buyers in new markets or industries who want protection against nonpayment
problem: Sellers expanding to new buyers face the risk that invoices go unpaid, limiting growth into new markets.
business_model: Invoice insurance plus trade credit and cross border payments, fees and premiums
product_category: Embedded trade credit insurance and B2B payments
founder_names: Derrick Wolbert; Reuben Balik; Q Carlson
market_need_then: Credit insurance premiums grew 6 percent in 2023 per the AU Group survey, and the sellers' nonpayment risk when entering new markets is the stated pain; no company traction data found.
outcome_analysis: The company is listed as active with a team of four and has repositioned from contractor banking toward invoice insurance and trade credit. No shutdown or acquisition news was found, and funding is only visible in a paywalled aggregator, so its success or failure is not yet determinable.

name: The Synthesis Company
one_liner: 100x faster scientific evidence synthesis
long_description:
We enable research that was previously impossible—systematic reviews of 20,000+ papers in weeks with 98% accuracy.

We collaborate with researchers at Stanford, Harvard, and Johns Hopkins to ask the big questions they've been forced to scale down.

Pharma companies get complete evidence awareness in weeks — not years.

AI labs get the same reviews as RL environments with expert-validated reasoning traces—scientific synthesis as the next frontier after math and coding benchmarks. 

We're former DSPy core contributors who built the production infrastructure to make total evidence awareness actually work at scale.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharma companies, CROs and academic researchers needing systematic reviews, and AI labs buying expert validated synthesis data
problem: Systematic reviews of thousands of papers take months or years of manual screening and extraction.
business_model: Enterprise services and software for AI driven systematic reviews plus data for AI labs
product_category: AI evidence synthesis agent (Eva)
market_need_then: Systematic reviews are a slow bottleneck for pharma evidence and research; the company cites Stanford, Harvard and Johns Hopkins collaborators and a 2026 validation poster exists, but no dated demand evidence from 2024 was found.
outcome_analysis: The company is active, now sells an agent called Eva for systematic reviews, and lists General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Amplify Partners and Essence VC as backers on its site. Round sizes are not public, and a validation poster supports its accuracy claims, but the commercial trajectory cannot yet be judged.

name: The Vibe Company
one_liner: AI-native agency that scales like software, run on our own AI agents.
long_description:
The Vibe Company (formerly Quivr, YC W24) is an AI-native agency. We build custom products and internal tools for companies, deploy agentic automations (agents, skills, workflows), and train teams on AI adoption.

Our bet: agencies don’t scale because they sell hours. We’re building one that does, by automating our own internal processes with AI agents. Every workflow we automate for ourselves becomes something we can ship to clients.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mid-size and large companies, media groups and healthcare firms that pay for custom AI products, agents and training
problem: Companies want working AI products and agent automations but lack the in-house skill to build and run them; agencies sell hours and do not scale.
business_model: Project and services agency fees, positioned as AI-native
product_category: AI agency, custom AI development
market_need_then: Strong 2023 and 2024 demand for chat-with-your-documents tools after the generative AI wave; Quivr gathered a large open-source developer following per its YC page description.
outcome_analysis: Quivr gained attention as an open-source chat-with-your-data tool, but model vendors and many open frameworks absorbed that wedge, and the company repositioned as The Vibe Company, an AI-native services agency with named clients such as AFP, Monka and Theodo and a France 2030 funded media project. It remains active with five people, so the outcome is unresolved. Funding is not confirmed by any primary source.

name: Theseus
one_liner: GPS Denied Navigation for Drones
long_description: Theseus builds visual navigation software for GPS-denied drone operations. Using onboard cameras, inertial sensors, and satellite reference imagery, our system computes position fixes entirely passively. The system is entirely self contained, can't be jammed and has no RF signature.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Drone OEMs, defense program offices and operators needing navigation without GPS
problem: Drones lose position when GPS is jammed or spoofed; Theseus provides camera based visual positioning that works passively.
business_model: Software licensing to drone OEMs and defense programs
product_category: Defense tech, visual navigation software
market_need_then: Heavy GPS jamming in Ukraine and other conflicts and US interest in low cost drones created demand; Defense One reported Army special operations interest in 2024.
outcome_analysis: Theseus grew from a hackathon demo posted on X in February 2024 into a YC company with a reported first special operations customer and a $4.3M seed in April 2025. Demand is tailwind driven by GPS jamming, but a March 2026 564 km flight claim lacks independent verification and competitors raised money in late 2025, so the outcome is open.

name: Thorntale
one_liner: The world's best presentation editor, powered by AI.
long_description:
Thorntale is the easiest (and prettiest) way to create your next presentation. We've built a super capable AI assistant that can directly edit your slides, and coupled it with an advanced slide design system to keep things beautiful and professional.
Thorntale AI is designed to work alongside you as an AI collaborator. It can modify slide design and content, as well as give suggestions on what to improve to make your points clearer for your audience. We've also built tons of enterprise level features into Thorntale, like integrated data connections and send as email.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Thornwick
one_liner: Buy-side M&A Advisory
long_description: We work with 7 of the top 15 private equity firms by AUM as well as over 150 of the most active acquirers in the US to support their M&A efforts.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Private equity firms and corporate acquirers seeking buy-side deal sourcing
problem: Acquirers struggle to find and approach off-market targets; Thornwick runs outreach on their behalf using a proprietary dataset.
business_model: Advisory fees for buy-side M&A sourcing, paired with Revi deal origination software
product_category: M&A advisory and deal origination software
market_need_then: Buy-side sourcing is a paid service by boutique advisers; the company claims 7 of the top 15 PE firms by AUM and over 150 active acquirers as clients (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Thornwick sells buy-side M&A advisory and surfaces its Revi product, with self reported clients including most of the largest private equity firms. Revi's first version dates to September 2023 per YC, so the company predates the batch. No funding, exit or failure is documented, so the trajectory is unknown.

name: Thunder Compute
tags: Developer Tools; Data Science; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: The GPU sandbox company
long_description: Thunder Compute is the GPU sandbox company. We build GPU sandboxes for AI agents and GPU instances for developers, and help partners get more out of their GPU fleets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: ML engineers, researchers and AI agent builders needing cheap GPU instances and sandboxes
problem: GPUs are scarce and expensive and sit idle; Thunder virtualizes GPUs over the network to lower cost and raise utilization.
business_model: Usage-based GPU cloud, billed per hour or second
product_category: GPU cloud, GPU virtualization
market_need_then: GPU shortage and high rental prices during the 2023 and 2024 AI build out; the founders cite Georgia Tech researchers struggling to get GPUs (podcast summary).
outcome_analysis: Thunder Compute turned a low cost GPU cloud for developers into a $13M Series A led by Matrix Partners in August 2026, riding GPU scarcity. Its virtualization technology is the claimed edge; sources disagree about enterprise traction and some aggregators show an earlier seed that is unconfirmed, so the outcome remains open.

name: Thyme
one_liner: The OS for financial advisors
long_description:
There are 300k+ financial advisors in the US using a digital Rolodex to manage their client relationships, and it's time for a makeover.

At Thyme we are building the OS for financial advisors that allows them to automatically take notes in meetings (in-person, online, and phone calls), manage their client records with the help of AI, and offer a client portal where clients can track their assets, manage tasks, and even pay for their services. 

Our users have replaced their legacy CRMs and billing solutions with us while deepening their clients' relationships thanks to our client portal and AI tooling that puts rich context at their fingertips.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Independent financial advisors and RIAs who pay per seat for meeting notes, CRM and a client portal
problem: Advisors spend hours on meeting notes, CRM entry and client follow-up in legacy CRMs and billing tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS per advisor seat
product_category: AI meeting assistant and CRM for financial advisors
market_need_then: About 300 thousand US advisors rely on legacy CRMs per Thyme's own pitch. Funded rivals such as Jump in 2024 show investor and buyer interest in advisor notetaking.
outcome_analysis: Thyme was a two person team building an advisor operating system in a category where Jump and others raised money in 2024. It was acquired by Altruist in June 2025, under a year after its batch, and renamed Hazel. The price is unknown, so the outcome reads as a distribution-minded acquisition of a small product and team.

name: Tiny
tags: SaaS; B2B; Workflow Automation; Manufacturing; Enterprise Software
one_liner: A new kind of ERP system for factories
long_description: At Tiny, we’re building a new kind of ERP system for factories where AI agents automate repetitive workflows. Made for the four million factories still primarily relying on Excel. LLMs now unlock their troves of siloed unstructured data. We see a massive opportunity to build a compound startup and, beyond that, tap into network effects to unlock just-in-time manufacturing across entire supply chains.
regions: Singapore; Southeast Asia; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small and mid-size factories (initially automotive and electronics suppliers in Indonesia, Vietnam and India) that still run on Excel
problem: Four million factories run on spreadsheets and siloed unstructured data; enterprise ERPs like SAP can cost over $1M.
business_model: B2B SaaS ERP with AI agents (pricing not found)
product_category: AI ERP for manufacturing
market_need_then: YC launch post says four million factories rely on Excel and claims work with several factories in Indonesia, Vietnam and India; company claims, not verified.
outcome_analysis: Tiny is a Fall 2024 YC company building an AI ERP for factories in Southeast Asia and India, started by two ex-Zenefits and Addepar colleagues with an Apple infrastructure engineer. It is active with three people and a few factory pilots. Aggregators report only about $500K raised and no outside press or priced traction was found, so it is early and unproven.

name: Titanio
one_liner: AI Employees for Distributors
long_description:
Titanio is a suite of AI Employees for Wholesalers & Distributors. Instead of relying on humans to quote, take orders, collect payments, place purchase orders and enter data into ERPs. We build AI Employees that do these manual repetitive tasks for the 700k wholesalers in the US.

We’re a team of three Computer Science majors, and Fernando launched and grew AT&T in Mexico to $120M ARR. Previously, we all worked together at our last YC-backed startup, building it to over $6M in revenue. It was there that we placed thousands of purchase orders with wholesalers.

We realized that almost every physical product comes from B2B sales in the supply chain. However, it turns out that most of these operations are still done manually through phone and email, involving tasks like quoting, taking orders, collecting payments, entering data into ERPs, and providing support. By automating these tasks with AI agents in a human-like manner, we are creating a massive opportunity to convert $100B of payroll expenses into software spending.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Wholesalers and distributors and their sales reps and counter staff
problem: Distributors handle quotes, orders, calls and ERP entry manually; Titanio uses AI agents to handle them.
business_model: B2B SaaS and AI agent services
product_category: AI sales and ordering for distribution
founder_names: Luis Mario Garcia; Heber Garza; Javier Gonzalez; Fernando Huerta
market_need_then: Wholesale distribution is a large industry run on phone and email order desks; the team's earlier Orchata experience exposed the problem (RuntimeWire profile).
outcome_analysis: A team of repeat founders from Orchata built AI agents for distributors and has widened from order entry to field sales, contact center and commerce. No funding round, exit or failure is documented by an opened primary source, and the field is getting well funded competitors, so the outcome is open.

name: Tivara
one_liner: The AI workforce for medical groups
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Toma
tags: Marketplace; B2B; Productivity; HR Tech; AI
one_liner: AI Applied Research
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Automotive dealerships, mainly service and sales departments
problem: Dealerships miss inbound calls and lose service appointments; Toma voice agents answer calls and book work.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per dealership
product_category: Voice AI for auto dealerships
market_need_then: Dealership service departments lose revenue on missed calls; the manifesto and press describe thousands of AI calls daily and 100+ dealers by 2025.
outcome_analysis: Toma reached seven figure ARR in under a year, approached eight figures with over 100 dealerships, and raised a $17M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in June 2025. Strong early traction and a clear vertical help, though Numa has a much larger dealer base, so scale versus competition decides the next outcome.

name: Toolify
one_liner: Build internal tools with AI
long_description:
Toolify is dev-first internal tooling. At some point, companies using low-code builders hit a brick wall, and are bogged down by their limitations rather quickly.

We offer:
- A starter kit with sensible defaults,
- A VSCode extension which has AI that creates the internal tool for you, end to end, and,
- A web app where you can deploy your tools.

This gives you the best of both worlds -- everything you need to build tools just as fast as low-code, and an escape hatch when you need it.
regions: India; South Asia

name: Topo
one_liner: All-in-one AI platform  for outbound sales
long_description:
We are helping B2B companies reach the right leads with an AI Outbound agent. 



The goal is to reproduce the behavior of a sales top performers:

- They know the product, the industry, the pain points, and the company's value proposition perfectly (trained on datas from your knowledge base, calls transcript, CRM...). 

- They will find the right leads, ready to buy, based on buying signals in the industry-specific channels (Linkedin, G2, Github...) or on the company's website visitors.


That's exactly what the agent can do!

Think of it as an expert SDR in your industry, ramp up in minutes.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: B2B sales teams running outbound prospecting
problem: Outbound prospecting is manual and noisy; Topo's agent finds leads from buying signals, drafts messages and books meetings.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus outbound consulting
product_category: AI outbound sales platform
founder_names: Dan Elkaim; Léonard Henriquez; Robin Philibert
market_need_then: Founders saw outbound demand at Aircall; the company claims 150+ customers and 200+ teams (self reported on its site).
outcome_analysis: Topo pivoted from a digital sales room to AI outbound agents in 2023, raised a roughly one million euro pre-seed and joined YC in Winter 2024. It claims 150+ customers, but the AI SDR category is crowded with better known players, and no later round is confirmed, so the outcome is open.

name: Tower
tags: Workflow Automation; Legal; LegalTech; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: M&A due diligence platform powered by AI
long_description: Tower accelerates transactional due diligence via an AI-powered, centralized diligence platform. By consolidating disparate diligence workflows, Tower helps deal teams stay organized, spot issues earlier, and close deals faster.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: M&A lawyers, serial acquirers, asset managers and real estate diligence teams
problem: Due diligence means sorting thousands of files in data rooms; Tower organizes them, flags gaps and answers questions with citations.
business_model: B2B SaaS for diligence workspaces
product_category: AI legal and M&A due diligence platform
founder_names: Adam Dorfman; Andy Zhang; Noah (surname not listed)
market_need_then: M&A diligence is document heavy and billed hourly by law firms; the company claims 1000+ use cases and AmLaw 50 firms as customers (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Tower moved from an in-house legal request assistant to an M&A due diligence platform, with a lawyer cofounder and engineers from Waterloo. Only YC funding is known, and a crowded legal AI field with funded incumbents makes the path uncertain; the outcome is open.

name: Tracecat
tags: Open Source; Cybersecurity; Enterprise; Automation; AI
one_liner: Open-source agentic security automation platform
long_description:
Tracecat helps AI-native security teams build agents and automate work. All-in-one platform with agents, skills, prompt-to-workflows, and case management. Scale cyber defense with agents you own.

Open source and community-driven at it's core: https://github.com/TracecatHQ/tracecat
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Security operations teams at mid-market and enterprise companies that want to build and run automation and AI agents themselves
problem: Security teams drown in repetitive alert triage and response work, and legacy SOAR tools are closed and costly. Tracecat offers an open source, self-hostable platform for workflows, agents and case management.
business_model: Open source core (AGPL v3.0) with paid enterprise edition (multi-tenant, SSO-style controls, SLAs, forward deployed engineer) and hosted cloud
product_category: Security orchestration, automation and response (SOAR) with AI agents
market_need_then: SOAR was an established category with incumbents that customers found costly and rigid, and the 2023 to 2024 generative AI wave created demand for AI-assisted security automation. A public alpha open source alternative to Tines and Splunk SOAR was listed in March 2024.
outcome_analysis: Tracecat is active and shows signs of traction: customer logos including Depop, Verkada and NinjaOne on its site, SOC 2 Type II, an enterprise tier and open roles. The open source distribution model and the AI agent wave helped it position against Tines and Splunk SOAR. Funding is not verifiable from reliable outlets, so the financial outcome is unknown.

name: TradeFlow
one_liner: AI-powered settlement for financial securities
long_description: TradeFlow is AI-powered settlement for financial securities. During her time in financial services, Taryn saw firsthand how inefficient and costly it is to settle trades. Historically, it’s been difficult to improve this process because it’s heavily reliant on manual emails, disparate systems, and inconsistently structured data. However, the advent of powerful AI technology allows us to unlock greater automation than ever before. TradeFlow empowers back offices to do more with less by offloading these time-intensive tasks to AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Broker-dealers and financial firms that settle securities trades
problem: Settlement depends on manual emails, disparate systems and inconsistently structured data; the US moved settlement from T+2 to T+1.
business_model: B2B software / AI agents for settlement operations (inferred)
product_category: FinTech settlement automation
market_need_then: T+1 settlement rule in the US (YC launch post: from two days to one) increases pressure on operations teams.
outcome_analysis: TradeFlow is a two-person Summer 2024 company automating securities settlement, with founders from Goldman Sachs and Meta. No funding beyond an unverified aggregator figure, no customers and no outcome event were found, so the company's success or failure cannot be judged from public sources.

name: Treblo
tags: Generative AI; Social Media; Music; AI
one_liner: Create hit songs with AI
long_description: Treblo is an AI music editor that turns prompts, lyrics, or melodies into full songs in any style. People use Treblo to have fun and express themselves, and some have even made Hot 100 hits.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers and hobbyist creators who want to make songs with AI for fun and sharing
problem: Making a full song with vocals requires skills, tools and time. Treblo (launched as Sonauto) turns prompts, lyrics or melodies into full songs in any style.
business_model: Consumer freemium subscription for AI music generation and editing, details not confirmed
product_category: Generative AI music creation and editing
market_need_then: Generative AI music had a viral moment in early 2024 with Suno and Udio drawing mass consumer interest, which showed latent demand for song creation by non-musicians.
outcome_analysis: Treblo, launched as Sonauto in March 2024, remains active with a four person team. It competes with far better funded Suno and Udio in AI music, and has renamed itself, with the date and reason not public. Funding is unverified beyond one aggregator, so the outcome is unclear.

name: Trellis AI
tags: B2B; Data Engineering; Infrastructure; AI; Databases
one_liner: Accelerate Medication Access with AI
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Specialty healthcare providers and pharmacies handling referrals, prior authorizations and appeals
problem: Patient intake and prior authorization require manual document handling that delays treatment. Trellis agents extract referral data, draft medical necessity letters and submit authorizations.
business_model: B2B SaaS and agent platform sold to healthcare providers via demos, pricing not disclosed
product_category: Healthcare administrative AI agents
market_need_then: Prior authorization is a widely criticized administrative burden, and 2023 to 2024 LLM advances made document automation newly feasible.
outcome_analysis: Trellis is active, with team size growing from around 25 to 55 per YC listings, many open roles, and a focused healthcare agent suite. It focused from general data structuring onto prior authorization. Investors are named (YC, General Catalyst, Telesoft) but no round sizes or dates are public, so the funding outcome is unknown.

name: Trieve
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; API; Search; AI
one_liner: All-in-one API for search, RAG, & recommendations
long_description:
Infrastructure for search teams building retrieval and RAG. Trieve combines search language models with tools for tuning ranking and relevance.

Building excellent search is difficult and can take months to implement then even more time to maintain. Trieve offers production-ready infrastructure that works out of the box to help search teams build adjustable AI search and RAG into their products. With tools for custom models, relevancy weighting, date-recency biasing, semantic full-text hybrid search, recommendations, and more Trieve covers the full spectrum of what a team wants from their discovery infrastructure.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developer and search teams that pay for hosted or self-hosted search, RAG and recommendations infrastructure
problem: Building good search and RAG takes months to implement and more to maintain.
business_model: Usage-based cloud API plus paid self-host licenses, open source core
product_category: Search and RAG infrastructure API
market_need_then: RAG demand rose after 2023 as teams added AI search to products. Trieve's customer Mintlify used it as the backbone of docs search.
outcome_analysis: Trieve raised a seed round of $3.5M in September 2024 and sold to Mintlify in July 2025, a customer that already relied on it for docs search. The open source core and a real anchor customer made it a natural tuck-in, while the crowded search market made an independent path hard. Terms are not public.

name: Triply
one_liner: Operating system for travel businesses in Africa with embedded finance
long_description: Triply (Formerly Tripitaca) is the operating system for travel businesses in Africa. We eliminate operational chaos by unifying payments, Invoicing, payroll, accounting, operations, and more into a single platform allowing travel businesses to execute and sell more efficiently.
regions: Kenya; Africa
target_customer: Travel agencies, tour operators and travel businesses in Africa, starting in East Africa
problem: African travel businesses run on fragmented tools for payments, invoicing, payroll and accounting. Triply unifies them in one operating system with embedded finance.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus payments and embedded finance fees
product_category: Vertical operating system and fintech for travel businesses
market_need_then: The company said Africa's travel market is worth 300 billion dollars and 66 percent of spend is domestic. Earlier, Tripitaca had over 2,000 guest house operators on its marketplace per one investment memo, indicating operator fragmentation.
outcome_analysis: Triply moved from a consumer guest house marketplace as Tripitaca to a B2B operating system in March 2024, joined YC W24 as the first African travel tech investment, and has expanded with bank and payments partnerships in 2025. Founders had prior BNPL and rental management experience. It is active and funding beyond YC is not verified.

name: TrueClaim
one_liner: Transparent, AI-powered healthcare TPA.
long_description: TrueClaim is rebuilding health plan administration software from the ground-up, with modern technology and AI. Most health plans and third-party administrators (TPAs) still operate on outdated legacy technology that’s slow, error-prone and costly. We’re the modern alternative: AI-powered claims review, API-first architecture, and a platform that makes operating great health plans radically simpler. Think Shopify, but for health plans. We're on a mission to modernize how health plans operate to make the healthcare system more transparent, efficient and affordable for everyone.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Self-insured employers and health plans that need a third party administrator
problem: Legacy TPA technology is slow, error prone and opaque, so self-funded employers overpay on claims they cannot see into.
business_model: TPA administration fees plus claims savings from AI review
product_category: AI powered health plan and TPA administration software
market_need_then: Self-funded plans cover roughly two thirds of the US workforce per one source, and employers face rising claims costs and billing errors; TrueClaim says its AI review saves about 7 percent of claims (company claim, unverified).
outcome_analysis: TrueClaim raised a 2.1M USD pre-seed announced in April 2024, partnered with Rezilient Health in January 2025 and says it has processed 50M USD of claims, but no employer customer is named and no later round was found. The founders bring healthcare operations and health tech engineering experience. Outcome is still open; the main risk is raising a seed against fast moving AI native TPA and payment integrity rivals.

name: Tuesday Labs
one_liner: Delightful robots
long_description: Tuesday makes delightful robots that tidy your home for you
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Affluent households buying a home robot, with reservations open from October 2026
problem: Household tidying is a constant chore that existing robots like vacuums do not address. Tuesday Labs is building Voxel, a legged home robot that tidies, finds items and tends plants.
business_model: Hardware sales with refundable 200 dollar reservations and an expected price near 20,000 dollars, deliveries targeted for 2028
product_category: Consumer home robotics
market_need_then: Home chores are a broad pain point, robot vacuums proved households pay for automation, and 2023 to 2024 progress in learned manipulation revived interest in general home robots.
outcome_analysis: Tuesday Labs is active and pre-revenue, after unveiling the Voxel Series-1 prototype in October 2026 with refundable reservations and 2028 delivery targets. The sources do not support success or failure judgments yet. The venture needs a large hardware raise, and its funding outside a small early round is not public.

name: Tusk
one_liner: AI agent that generates unit and integration tests
long_description: Tusk (YC W24) is an AI agent that helps developers generate unit and integration tests with codebase context. Tusk sits in CI and provides automatic coverage whenever software engineers raise a PR. Engineering teams use Tusk to prevent critical regressions while increasing test coverage.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Typa
tags: Generative AI; Social Media; Marketing; AI
one_liner: The content engine that wins attention and drives growth.
long_description:
We help businesses capture what resonates, make it repeatable, and turn attention into lasting momentum. With Typa, you can build a scalable inbound growth engine with content that compounds.

We make this possible through three pillars:

1. A tone of voice that always sounds like you. Typa learns your style, cadence, and perspective so every piece of content reflects your authentic voice.

2. A knowledge base that updates in real time. Your digital clone continuously absorbs everything you say and create, ensuring your content always reflects your latest thinking.

3. A personal ghostwriter that’s always just a call away. Puff is your 24/7 AI ghostwriter and strategist, available via phone or WhatsApp whenever you want to brainstorm, plan, or execute.

Currently supported channels: X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, and blog/newsletters.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Creators, companies and agencies that need consistent content in their own voice
problem: Producing consistent on-brand content for X, LinkedIn and blogs is time-consuming. Typa drafts content in a user's voice from voice notes and links, with approval before publishing.
business_model: B2B and prosumer SaaS subscription, pricing not shown
product_category: AI content and ghostwriting engine
founder_names: Andrew Chung; Hyun Jie Jung; Junyoung Park
market_need_then: In 2024 the Weavel prompt optimization tool aimed at LLM developers, while the later Typa content engine targets the broad demand for founder-led content. The 2025 pivot is described by aggregators only.
outcome_analysis: Weavel launched Ape as an open source prompt engineer in August 2024 and joined YC S24, then rebranded as Typa and moved to AI content for creators and companies. It is a very small team in a crowded field with no verified revenue or large funding. There is no clear success or failure signal in public sources yet.

name: Ubicloud
one_liner: Open source alternative to AWS
long_description:
Ubicloud is an open source cloud that can run anywhere.

Our cloud services include elastic compute, block storage, virtual networking, managed Postgres, K8s, AI inference, and powerful IAM. Ubicloud provides these services on bare metal providers, such as Hetzner, Leaseweb, or AWS Bare Metal.

You can self-host our software or use our managed service to reduce your cloud costs by 3-10x.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams that want lower cloud bills and control, including GitHub Actions heavy teams and Postgres users
problem: Public cloud costs and lock-in are high. Ubicloud provides an open source cloud that runs on cheap bare metal providers, claiming 3 to 10 times lower cost.
business_model: Usage-based managed cloud services (compute, Postgres, GitHub Actions runners) plus open source self-hosting
product_category: Open source cloud infrastructure
founder_names: Umur Cubukcu; Ozgun Erdogan; Daniel Farina
market_need_then: Cloud bills were a widely discussed pain point in 2023 to 2024, with cost repatriation and bare metal growth, and GitHub Actions runner cost was a clear acute spend.
outcome_analysis: Ubicloud raised a 16 million dollar seed on the strength of founders with a prior YC exit, then shipped compute, Postgres and cheap GitHub Actions runners and gained named customers like Felt and Hatchet. A 2026 ClickHouse partnership and a 26 percent price rise suggest traction and cost pressure; some outages were recorded. No later round is reported.

name: Ultra
one_liner: Practical, general-purpose robots for repetitive industrial tasks
long_description:
Ultra builds practical, general-purpose robots that are deploying—and producing ROI—today.

Unlike traditional industrial automation that’s rigid and complex, our robots are zero integration (able to be installed in hours, not weeks) and are highly flexible, capable of quickly learning new tasks and delivering immediate value to customers.

Founded by a team of three-time entrepreneurs with a decade of collaboration, Ultra moves fast. We already have robots in the field generating revenue and data, with plans to rapidly scale deployments this year.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: E-commerce fulfillment warehouses, 3PLs and large brands that need order packing, sorting and kitting
problem: Warehouse packing is repetitive and hard to automate with rigid industrial systems. Ultra's stationary dual-arm OP1 robots install in hours and learn tasks.
business_model: Robots as a service: upfront integration fee plus a monthly fee for hardware and software support
product_category: Warehouse robotics for order packing
founder_names: Jon Miller Schwartz; Max Friefeld; Oliver Ortlieb; Chetan Parthiban
market_need_then: E-commerce fulfillment faced labor shortages and high volumes of poly bag and mailer packing, and rigid automation did not fit variable items.
outcome_analysis: Ultra, founded by repeat founders from Voodoo Manufacturing and Layer By Layer, joined YC S24, raised a 12 million seed and then a 50 million Series A in October 2026, with 62 million total. Its robots-as-a-service model reportedly generates meaningful revenue, and a Physical Intelligence tie-up supplies the AI models. The company claims over 500,000 packed orders, unverified.

name: Unbound
one_liner: Use AI tools without fear of data leakage
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Enterprise security and IT teams that need to govern employee use of generative AI tools and coding agents
problem: Employees paste sensitive data into AI tools and adopt unsanctioned AI apps, while security teams lack visibility, policy control and cost tracking.
business_model: B2B SaaS, enterprise AI gateway and governance; later positioned as governance for coding agents, free for teams of 50 or more developers per the current site
product_category: AI security and governance (AI gateway, data leakage prevention)
market_need_then: In 2024 enterprises were rapidly adopting gen AI tools and raising data leakage and shadow IT concerns; the seed coverage cites company claims of 7,000 prevented leaks.
outcome_analysis: Unbound is active and raised a 4 million dollar seed round in May 2025 led by Race Capital, about a year after its Summer 2024 YC batch. Founders with data security product experience at Palo Alto Networks and Imperva suit the market, and enterprise anxiety about gen AI leakage is a tailwind. The positioning has moved toward governing coding agents, which shows adaptation. Whether it can stay ahead of large security vendors is not yet known.

name: Undermind
one_liner: An AI agent for scientific research
long_description:
At Undermind, we're building a search engine that can handle extremely complex questions. It’s geared at experts, like research scientists and doctors, who need to find very specific resources to solve high-stakes problems. 

We’ve rebuilt search from the ground up to address this. Our new approach employs high-quality LLMs to adaptively explore a database, mimicking how a human researcher carefully discovers information. This approach dramatically outperforms (by 10-50x) traditional keyword search and other modern AI-based retrieval methods.

Our first target users are the 50 million researchers searching for scientific literature on PubMed and Google Scholar every month. We’ve have paying users across fields like medicine, ML, biotech, finance, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Research scientists, doctors and enterprise R&D teams that search scientific literature
problem: Keyword search on PubMed and Google Scholar misses relevant papers for complex, specific questions.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription (Pro, Team per seat, Enterprise custom)
product_category: AI literature search agent
market_need_then: The company cites about 50 million researchers searching PubMed and Google Scholar monthly and says it had paying users across medicine, ML and biotech at the batch.
outcome_analysis: Undermind is active with scientist founders and visible adoption, including a claimed GSK deployment of over 1,000 scientists and DOE national lab users. Funding appears small and unverified, so its trajectory is hard to judge. The main risk is that general AI deep research tools absorb the use case, which is not yet evidenced.

name: Understood Care
tags: Health Tech; Healthcare; Health Insurance; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Healthcare personal assistants for Medicare patients.
long_description:
The American healthcare system is complicated. 88% of US adults cite difficulties navigating the healthcare system. 

The good news is patient advocacy became a covered benefit by Medicare in 2024. 

Understood Care matches Medicare patients with a healthcare personal assistant (known as a Patient Advocate) at little to no cost to the patient. Patient Advocates help patients patients access care - finding resources, helping fill out paperwork, and much more. 

Understood Care uses AI and healthcare expertise to deliver the highest quality patient advocacy to the 68 million Medicare patients in the US.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Medicare beneficiaries (billed to Medicare for most patients) and Medicare Advantage plans
problem: Medicare patients struggle to navigate care, paperwork and costs; patient advocacy became a covered benefit in 2024 but is hard to deliver at scale.
business_model: Services billed to Medicare (principal illness navigation) and Medicare Advantage plan relationships, with AI co-pilot for advocates
product_category: Virtual patient advocacy and care navigation
market_need_then: Medicare created principal illness navigation billing codes in 2024; the company cites that 88 percent of US adults report difficulty navigating healthcare.
outcome_analysis: Understood Care is active. It launched patient care in March 2025, reports reach across all 50 states within eight months and ties with three Medicare Advantage plans, then announced 8.4 million dollars of total funding in March 2026. The 2024 Medicare navigation billing codes were a regulatory tailwind. Risks include reimbursement dependence and a crowded navigation field.

name: Unsloth AI
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Open-Source Reinforcement Learning (RL) & Fine-tuning for LLMs.
long_description:
Unsloth helps builders create custom models better & faster using RL and custom kernels. We're developing the all in one solution to help you create highly-accurate custom models 30x faster with 90% less memory use.

With over 10 million monthly model downloads and 40K GitHub stars, our mission is to make training and open-source the best it can be!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers, researchers and companies fine-tuning and running open LLMs, from hobbyists to enterprises
problem: Fine-tuning and reinforcement learning on LLMs is slow and memory hungry. Unsloth rewrote kernels to make it faster with less VRAM.
business_model: Open source library with a planned paid product and enterprise offering (monetization details not found)
product_category: Developer tools: LLM fine-tuning and RL training
market_need_then: Open model releases created demand for cheap fine-tuning, and the project reports over 10 million monthly model downloads and 40K GitHub stars (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Unsloth grew quickly as an open source tool, claiming 40K GitHub stars and 10M monthly downloads, was cited in NVIDIA posts, and joined the PyTorch ecosystem in 2026. It stayed independent and active with about 12 people. Funding is thinly documented, with only small totals in aggregators, so how much capital it holds is unclear.

name: Unusual
one_liner: Market to AI agents
long_description:
AI agents are the newest audience brands need to speak to, but go-to-market teams don't have the tools to understand how they form opinions or make decisions.

Unusual helps brands in the Fortune 100 and scale-ups like Change.org and Astronomer drive more sales and win more market share by shifting how AI models perceive their offerings.

We work closely with every brand to (1) identify the root cause of AI misperception, (2) align on marketing, sales, and product strategies that appeal to agents, and (3) build infrastructure and content that makes their strongest proof more legible to agents.

Our methodology centers on applying black-box interpretability techniques to AI agents like ChatGPT and Claude to understand how they form opinions about a brand and its competitors. Seeing the *why* behind each opinion gives us the ability to create targeted interventions that change them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Brands, from Fortune 100 companies to scale-ups, that want to shape how AI models describe them
problem: AI models form opinions about brands that go-to-market teams cannot see or influence.
business_model: Agency services plus software (Agent Analytics free trial, AgentDesk per seat)
product_category: AI visibility and generative engine optimization services
market_need_then: Brands began asking how ChatGPT and Claude describe them as AI search grew; customer logos on the site (Reducto, Astronomer, Stats Perform) show demand later on.
outcome_analysis: Unusual is active with a team of four at the batch and raised a 3.6 million dollar seed in January 2026. Timing helped as brands rushed to manage how AI models describe them. The category drew many entrants quickly and the service model is easy to copy, so durability is uncertain. Customer logos suggest early enterprise traction.

name: Upsolve AI
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Analytics; Big Data; AI
one_liner: Deploy trustworthy data agent that know your business
long_description: Upsolve AI is the analytics platform for deploying governed, grounded, and trustworthy data agents that know your business. Data teams use Upsolve's Agent Studio to get to AI-ready data foundations fast, unify and curate their context layer, and test, tune and monitor their Upsolve Data Agent to their benchmark. The company is founded by Ka Ling Wu and Serguei Balanovich, who built a similar product at Palantir before (featured in Palantir's S-1), growing it to 50+ enterprise customers and 8-figures of annual revenue in 2 years.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mid-market and enterprise data teams and AI innovation teams
problem: Companies want conversational analytics but need governed, grounded answers they can trust.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform for building and deploying data agents
product_category: AI analytics agents (originally embedded analytics)
market_need_then: Enterprises were piloting natural language analytics in 2024; founders say they built a similar product at Palantir with 50+ enterprise customers (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Upsolve AI is active. Its early blog positioning targeted embedded analytics versus Sisense, and its current site sells governed data agents, though the exact pivot date is not sourced. Founders from Palantir give enterprise credibility. Funding is thin and unverified, and no outcome news exists, so the story is incomplete.

name: Usul
one_liner: AI Platform for Winning Defense & Government Contracts
long_description:
Usul helps companies win government contracts in 60+ nations. 

Our AI monitors $8 trillion in annual government spending and instantly matches you to contracts across defense, IT, energy, healthcare and more.

Learn more at https://usul.com/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Defense and government contractors, from startups to Fortune 500 companies
problem: Government spending data is fragmented, so contractors miss opportunities and struggle to find teaming partners.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for contract intelligence
product_category: GovTech contract discovery and capture management
founder_names: Jarren Reid; Oliver Gomez; Joonghyun Lee
market_need_then: Defense contractors need contract intelligence; the company cites roughly 8 trillion dollars in annual government spending and Stanford Hacking for Defense origins.
outcome_analysis: Usul is active with a team of 15 and a 3.3 million dollar seed in May 2025 led by Scout Ventures, a year after the Summer 2024 batch. Palantir and Stanford defense backgrounds fit the buyer and the defense spending climate is a tailwind. Customers are claimed to have won over 12 billion dollars through the product, which is unverified. Competition from established GovCon suites remains.

name: Variant
one_liner: Creative intelligence
long_description: Creative intelligence
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Designers and developers who want many AI generated UI design directions
problem: Prompt-to-UI tools demand long prompts and blank canvases; designers want to explore many directions quickly.
business_model: Freemium SaaS (free tier of 300 designs a month, Pro at 20 dollars a month per a 2026 review)
product_category: AI UI design exploration
founder_names: Benjamin South Lee; Daniel Bulhosa Solorzano
market_need_then: Demand for AI UI design tools was growing in 2024; no company-specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Variant is active as of the YC listing with a team of five and a product with a free tier by 2026. Founders bring Postmates and Cruise experience. Funding is only supported by aggregators at about 500K, and the crowded prompt-to-UI market with well-resourced entrants is the main risk. Too little is sourced to explain outcomes.

name: Vaya
one_liner: Rank, Log, & Share Places
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers, mostly young adults who log and share places with friends (current site); YC page and App Store listing describe a travel and flight deals app
problem: People want to keep and share ranked lists of places they have visited with friends rather than scattered notes and reviews.
business_model: Consumer app, monetization not stated
product_category: Consumer social app for logging and ranking places
market_need_then: Beli's growth among Gen Z in 2023 to 2025 showed interest in social restaurant ranking; whether Vaya serves a separate need is unclear.
outcome_analysis: Vaya is a two person Fall 2024 YC consumer company whose public identity is unclear: the YC profile text and an App Store listing describe flight deals, while the dataset one liner and its website describe a social app for ranking and sharing places, run by Fix AI, Inc. No funding, traction or exit data is public, and the main contemporaneous competitor, Beli, had already gained traction, so no outcome can be judged.

name: Veles
one_liner: CPQ for humans and agents
long_description:
You closed your first few deals on handshakes and Stripe links. Now a customer wants a ramp-up, custom terms, or annual billing — and suddenly you're duct-taping spreadsheets to your CRM.

Most CPQ tools are built for 500-person sales orgs with a dedicated RevOps team. Veles is built for you. AI agents handle quoting, approvals, and deal docs end-to-end so you can run a real sales motion without hiring a deal desk.

It's free for founders just getting started, and pricing scales with the number of active contracts you manage — so we only grow when you do. No CRM consultant, no six-month rollout. Just connect Salesforce or HubSpot and start closing.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Early-stage and mid-sized B2B sales teams without a dedicated deal desk
problem: Growing startups need custom terms and approvals but enterprise CPQ tools are heavy and slow to implement.
business_model: B2B SaaS priced on active contracts, free for early founders
product_category: AI CPQ (configure, price, quote)
market_need_then: Founders describe duct-taping spreadsheets to CRM once deals need custom terms; the YC launch post positions Veles as a cheaper alternative to enterprise CPQ.
outcome_analysis: Veles is active with a team of five and claims over 4,000 users and customers including Procore, where the founders previously worked. Funding is only supported by aggregators with totals from 500K to 1.42M, so the funding path is unclear. The product pivoted its framing toward agents, but timing of that shift is not dated.

name: Velorum Therapeutics
tags: Biotech; Healthcare; Therapeutics; Drug discovery; Oncology
one_liner: Breakthrough medicines unlocking the biology of heme
long_description: Velorum Therapeutics is developing breakthrough medicines by unlocking the biology of heme.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Patients with porphyrias and cancers where heme biology is dysregulated, reached through eventual pharma partners or direct drug sales
problem: Heme is an iron-containing molecule involved in oxygen transport, energy generation and detoxification that the company says is largely overlooked as a drug target. Disease areas listed are porphyrias, cancer and heme-related tissue injury.
business_model: Therapeutics developer: preclinical drug discovery funded by equity and grants, with value realized through clinical milestones, partnering or acquisition

name: Village Labs
one_liner: Helping America's businesses become employee owned
long_description:
At Village Labs, we help America's businesses become employee owned by helping them set up and manage an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP). 

ESOPs are a federal retirement plan that enable businesses to give their employees a stake in the company in exchange for significant tax benefits. 

With 2.9M Baby Boomer business owners set to retire in the coming years, there's a growing "Silver Tsunami" of businesses across the country in search of new ownership. For many of these owners, selling to their employees is a socially-minded yet financially pragmatic solution.

By selling ownership of their business to an ESOP, owners get a fair price, tax benefits, and the satisfaction of knowing their employees and legacy will be taken care of — things not guaranteed with traditional buyers like private equity. In turn, employees retain their jobs and get shares in the business that can help them create life changing wealth by the time they retire — imagine an office secretary retiring as a millionaire. 

Thousands of businesses across America like Bob's Red Mill, Harpoon Brewery, and Recology already have an ESOP, benefiting over 14 million workers and creating 2.1 trillion in employee wealth. We're excited about the opportunity to massively grow these numbers by making it simple for every business to become employee owned.

product_category: ESOP fintech and AI software
market_need_then: YC description cites 2.9 million baby boomer owners set to retire and ESOPs covering 14 million workers (company figures).

name: Wordware
one_liner: AI agents you can rely on
long_description:
Every tool you use was built as an island, so you became the glue between them. You carry a name from Gmail into the CRM, a time from the CRM into Calendly, a note from Calendly into a doc. AI showed up and mostly became an eleventh window to paste into. 

Sauna is a hybrid of AI and software standing on one shared brain. It holds your context and hands you real software built on top of it. You talk to it like a chatbot and use what it builds like an app: software for the path you repeat, AI for the edge that never repeats. Keep it to yourself, or share the brain with your team. 

The clearest way to see it is a tool doing what its whole category cannot. An ordinary Calendly shows a stranger your free slots. Your Calendly writes the invite email itself, because it knows how the two of you know each other, and it offers a board member the slot over your gym block, because it knows which of your busy hours bend and for whom. 

Wordware is the team behind it, 15 people backed by Spark Capital, Felicis, and Y Combinator with a $30M seed, the largest in YC's history. We build from an office in the Presidio, fifty metres from Crissy Field beach, and we work absurdly hard because we can see and feel the outcome every day.

name: Zoa Research
one_liner: Powerful quantitative forecasting models
long_description:
Historically, quantitative models are domain specific. Brilliant people spend their best years testing features, tuning hyperparameters, and iterating architectures within a narrow domain. But scale is the panacea: large models will find patterns people, and specialized models, could not. 

Forecasting generalizes. Zoa trains cross-domain event forecasting engines. 

*Automating Iteration*

LLMs—embedded in multi-agent optimization loops and evaluated against fixed policies—can automate the build-test-improve modeling cycle. Think AlphaEvolve for forecasting problems.

*Sample-Efficient General Models*

Today’s forecasting models are narrowly crafted with deep human priors. But larger models will outperform state-of-the-art specialized models.

Unlike existing event models, our models leverage data from across contexts and rely less on human intuition. And compared to LLMs, our models are built with more inductive priors and rely more heavily on inference-time compute—improving sample efficiency.

*Why It Matters*

In the real economy, our models could be useful for forecasting supply chain volatility, energy supply and demand, even earthquake risk.

Science is, Ian Hacking writes, the taming of chance. It is the process of iteratively updating priors (something like: identify uncertainty, conceive experiment to reduce uncertainty, execute, update). If science is uncertainty-reduction, forecasting is a critical measure of progress. 

Better forecasting improves our ability to select interesting experiments (roughly those with greatest expected uncertainty reduction) and update priors. Our models will be used by labs and academics in data-heavy domains. 

Sam's ex-girlfriend introduced him to Greg back at Carnegie Mellon in 2017, and while that relationship didn't last, their friendship has. After college, Greg went to Harvard Law School, while Sam worked for three years at Jane Street on their Options desk, building & leading a satellite dev team.
