market_need_then: Game and 3D studios faced long asset creation cycles, and generative 3D was a fast moving category in 2024; the company itself cites faster concept to production assets as the pain.
outcome_analysis: Ideate.xyz stayed active and early stage with a two person team and a freemium 3D generation product. It moved from thumbnail design tooling to generative 3D, and no funding beyond the YC deal, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is still open and no strong success or failure factor is supported by sources.

name: kater.ai
one_liner: Deliver complete data analysis from a single question
long_description:
1. You explain your problem.
2. Kater identifies the most important data questions to ask.
3. Kater writes the code.
4. You get insights in seconds rather than weeks.

Kater.ai flips the script on enterprise analytics by making every user an expert analyst. It uses a continuous classification engine to turn a single business question into a contextualized package of questions that is specific to your needs.

Kater puts the power of data into the hands of business experts while ensuring they use trusted data that is specific to their persona. No more waiting for data analysts. No more wasted time on analysis misfires and rework.

Yvonne was a data engineer and analyst who built the entire data stack at CREXi. Robin led engineering in Microsoft.  


Data is the new oil. Companies are data-rich, insight-poor. We're helping companies become insight-rich. This is the future of data.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Business users and data teams at enterprises
problem: Business users wait weeks on data analysts and often use untrusted data, causing misfires and rework.
business_model: B2B SaaS, AI agent for enterprise analytics
product_category: AI data analyst, natural language analytics
market_need_then: The founders cite long waits for data analysts and untrusted data; broad interest in LLM analytics in early 2024 supported demand.
outcome_analysis: Kater.ai remained a small early stage company after YC Winter 2024 with two founders who had real data engineering backgrounds. No disclosed funding beyond the YC deal, exit or shutdown was found, and the space of AI analytics was crowded, so the outcome is unresolved and not attributable to specific factors.

name: malibou
tags: B2B; Productivity; HR Tech; Payroll; SMB
one_liner: the first all-in-one payroll and HR software for French SMBs
long_description:
malibou is a web application helping French SMBs to manage employees, run payroll and track compliance in a single app.

When processing payroll in France, you either have the choice between an accountant with good advice but no way to connect an HRIS with him, or a good HRIS that does not include payroll services. It was time for a change, to finally bring payroll and HR at the same place. 

Due to increasing competition in the space, French payroll engines have just opened their APIs. This allows us to offer a unified payroll and HR solution, which wasn't possible before.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: French small and medium businesses of about 5 to 300 employees
problem: French SMBs had to choose between an accountant with no HRIS link or an HRIS without payroll services; malibou combines HR software, payroll engine and a dedicated payroll expert.
business_model: B2B SaaS per employee per month (one comparison cites 26 EUR all included), bundled with a dedicated payroll expert
product_category: Payroll and HR software
market_need_then: The YC description states that French payroll engines had just opened their APIs and that SMBs lacked a unified payroll and HR product, which is what enabled the wedge.
outcome_analysis: Malibou raised a seed round of about 3 million euros in June 2024 from FCVC, Y Combinator and Breega, helped by a founder who was a Breega partner and by payroll engine APIs opening up. It is active with named SMB customers, but no later round is confirmed, so the outcome is still developing.

name: mdhub
one_liner: AI-native operating system for behavioral health clinics.
long_description:
mdhub is the AI-native operating system for behavioral health. 

We combine AI workers with a purpose-built EHR, CRM, and RCM into one platform where clinical teams and AI collaborate across every workflow.

Mid to large-sized behavioral health clinics run on disconnected legacy systems that weren't designed for today's demand. The result: clinician burnout, admin bloat, and patients waiting weeks for care. mdhub replaces the entire fragmented stack with a single AI-first platform.

Our AI workers:

Emma, AI Clinical Assistant: automates documentation and gives clinicians back hours every day.
Sarah, AI Admissions Coordinator: handles 100% of inbound calls, verifies insurance, and books patients 24/7.
Eric, AI Billing Agent: manages coding, claims submission, and denial management same-day.

Our platform:

mdhub EHR: the first clinical workspace built for AI from day one. Documentation, intake, treatment planning, e-prescribing, and billing in one place.
mdhub CRM: every lead captured, every follow-up automated, nothing falls through the cracks.
mdhub RCM: end-to-end revenue cycle management. From claim submission to collections, AI-powered and fully integrated.

We're not another EHR with AI bolted on. We're not a point solution. We're the full operating system where AI workers and human teams run a clinic together. Hundreds of mid to large-sized behavioral health clinics use mdhub today, including some of the largest organizations in the country. One platform, less overhead, more patients seen.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mid to large behavioral health clinics
problem: Clinics run on disconnected legacy systems, causing clinician burnout, admin load and long patient waits.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform (EHR, CRM, revenue cycle management) with AI workers
product_category: AI native EHR and operations for behavioral health
market_need_then: The company cites burnout, admin bloat and waits; the founders position AI workers against legacy systems. No dated demand data was found beyond the company's own claims.
outcome_analysis: Mdhub grew to a reported team of 25 and claims hundreds of clinics and over 10,000 clinicians, per its own site and YC profile, but these figures are self reported and no priced round beyond the YC deal was found. The outcome is still open and sources do not support specific success or failure factors.

name: nCompass Technologies
tags: Developer Tools; Hardware; Open Source; AI
one_liner: Optimize performance on GPUs - 10x faster
long_description:
Identifying performance bottlenecks and strategizing ways to solve them takes 4-8x longer than actually writing the code to fix them. We're building an agent that is an expert at analyzing the performance GPU systems like inference engines at all levels of the stack - from CPU-GPU interactions down to GPU kernels. 

Pairing our agent with Cursor / Claude Code allows you to automate both the reasoning and code implementation steps of performance optimization. What used to take weeks can now be done in days. 

Along with our AI agent, we have features such as running diffs on system traces as well as sharing and collaboration features that make our VSCode extension the most powerful way to work on performance optimization.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: AI platform and ML infrastructure teams running LLM serving, ranking and recommender workloads on GPUs
problem: Finding and fixing CPU-GPU performance bottlenecks takes far longer than writing the fix.
business_model: Developer tooling (VSCode extension and AI performance agent), engineer-led sales
product_category: GPU performance optimization tools
market_need_then: The YC description says profiling and strategizing fixes takes 4 to 8 times longer than writing code; demand for GPU efficiency was high with the 2023 to 2024 LLM boom, though no dated source was found.
outcome_analysis: NCompass remained a small team of about three after YC Winter 2024 and moved its positioning from model serving toward an agent for GPU performance engineering. No disclosed funding beyond the YC deal, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is unresolved and no factors are supported by the sources.

name: omnidock
one_liner: OS for global e-commerce expansion of brands & manufacturers
long_description:
Expanding to other geographies and marketplaces is a massive growth lever for brands and manufacturers, but it’s complex and resource-intensive.

Omnidock makes it effortless for merchants to sell on multiple marketplaces by acting as their merchant of record. 

Brands simply plug into our operating system, which reads their catalog, assesses marketplace eligibility, and auto-launches their products through our pre-vetted marketplace accounts. We handle all transactions on their behalf, removing the challenges and complexities of multi-marketplace selling
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Brands and manufacturers wanting to sell on multiple geographies and marketplaces
problem: Expanding to other marketplaces is complex and resource intensive; omnidock acts as merchant of record using pre-vetted marketplace accounts and handles transactions.
business_model: Merchant of record marketplace expansion service, take rate on sales (not stated in sources)
product_category: E-commerce cross-border marketplace expansion
market_need_then: Founders came from Razor Group, an aggregator that expanded across marketplaces, so the pain was first hand; no dated external demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Omnidock launched after YC Summer 2024 with two founders who had worked at Razor Group, giving direct marketplace expansion experience. It is listed active with a very small team, no verified round beyond the YC deal and no exit or shutdown news, so the outcome is unresolved.

name: renderlet
tags: Developer Tools; Design Tools; Data Visualization
one_liner: Build interactive applications that run anywhere
long_description:
renderlet is a framework that makes it easy to develop interactive applications.

Building applications with high-performance graphics is very hard – existing tools are cumbersome and aren’t truly platform agnostic, leading to frequent rework. 

With renderlet, developers can write high-level code to describe 2D and 3D graphics without having to use low-level, platform-specific APIs.

renderlet automatically compiles graphics code to WebAssembly and embeds a portable rendering engine inside any app, enabling graphics to safely and automatically render on any platform’s GPU.

Our runtime is open-source: https://github.com/renderlet/wander
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers building interactive and real-time 3D applications, games, digital twins and visualization
problem: High performance graphics need low level platform specific APIs, causing rework; renderlet compiles graphics code to WebAssembly with a portable GPU runtime.
business_model: Open source runtime with a commercial compiler and tooling in closed preview
product_category: Developer tools for cross-platform graphics
market_need_then: The launch pitch says graphics tools are cumbersome and not truly platform agnostic; WebGPU and WASI GPU standards work were emerging, but no dated demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Renderlet grew to a small team with a head of design and a founding engineer and moved from a graphics framework toward a procedural 3D design tool. No funding beyond the YC deal, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is unresolved and sources do not support specific factors.

name: supercontrast
one_liner: AI Co-Pilot for Design
long_description: At Hive we worked on a product called Gencraft, an ai art generator we ramped from 0 to $1M ARR in 6 months. This inspired us to build supercontrast, an AI Copilot which empowers anyone to create and refine high quality designs and assets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

name: sync.
one_liner: AI lipsync tool for video content creators
long_description:
at sync. we're making video as fluid and editable as a word document

how much time would you save if you could *record every video in a single take?*

no more re-recording yourself because you didn't like what you said, or how you said it.

just shoot once, revise yourself to do exactly what you want, and post. that's all.

this is the future of video: *AI modified >> AI generated*

we're playing at the edge of science + fiction.

our team is young, hungry, uniquely experienced, and advised by some of the greatest research minds + startup operators in the world. we're driven to solve impossible problems, impossibly fast.

our founders are the original team behind the open sourced wav2lip — the most prolific lip-sync model to date w/ over 10k+ GitHub stars.

we 
[1] train state-of-the-art generative models, 
[2] productize + host them for scale
[3] grow virally through content
[4] upsell into enterprise
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Video creators, filmmakers and studios, plus developers and enterprises that use the API for dubbing and personalized video
problem: Fixing what a speaker said or how it looked in a finished video normally means re-recording. sync. edits the mouth movement so the video matches new audio.
business_model: Usage-based API plus subscription apps (studio app, Premiere plugin, ComfyUI node), with enterprise upsell
product_category: Generative AI video, lipsync and visual dubbing
founder_names: Prady Modukuru; Prajwal K R; Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay; Pavan Reddy
market_need_then: Creators and studios spend time on re-takes and dubbing. The company's launch pitch was that video could be edited like a document. Public evidence of paid demand at the time of founding was not found beyond the Wav2Lip research reach (open source repo popularity claimed by the company).
outcome_analysis: sync. is active and raised a $5.5M seed led by GV in August 2024, about five months after the W24 batch. Its strength is founder market fit, since the founders authored the Wav2Lip model, and the generative video wave helped. The main risk is that lipsync becomes a feature inside larger video platforms. No later round, acquisition or shutdown was found in searches.

name: telli
one_liner: intelligent interactions
long_description: telli is build AI to run customer-facing operations
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Large B2C companies in Europe (energy, telecom, insurance, media, e-commerce) with high phone call volumes
problem: Customer-facing operations such as sales calls, support and appointment booking need many human agents. telli runs AI agents that handle these calls and other channels.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage-based AI voice platform for enterprises
product_category: AI voice agents and customer operations automation
founder_names: Finn zur Muehlen; Philipp Baumanns; Seb Hapte-Selassie
market_need_then: Founders ran large contact center operations at Enpal and saw the cost of phone-based sales and support. TechCrunch reported in April 2025 more than 50 percent month over month revenue growth and nearly a million processed calls.
outcome_analysis: telli raised a $3.6M pre-seed in April 2025 and a $15M seed in July 2026 led by redalpine, with enterprise customers across Europe. Success factors are founder market fit from running Enpal's call operations, voice AI timing and an enterprise sales motion. The risk is a crowded field of well funded voice agent platforms.

name: vly.ai
one_liner: The Lovable & Replit killers
long_description: The world's best AI web app builder, implementing a radically unique architecture that lets us completely outperform the competition in complexity, reliability, scalability, and more. We are 7x cheaper and are positioned to take down Lovable, Replit, Base44, Bolt, Emergent, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Non-technical builders and developers who want to generate full stack web apps from prompts
problem: AI app builders such as Lovable and Replit were seen as expensive and limited for complex apps. vly.ai pitched a cheaper full stack builder with a built-in database and hosting.
business_model: Subscription and usage-based AI app builder (pricing listed inconsistently, from free to $3 per month)
product_category: AI web app builder
market_need_then: AI app builders were a fast growing category in 2024 and 2025. Evidence of demand specific to vly.ai is limited to self-reported testimonials and reviews on its own site and Trustpilot, which marks the vly.ai rating as unavailable due to a guidelines breach.
outcome_analysis: vly.ai launched in the crowded AI app builder market in late 2024 with a price-led pitch against Lovable, Replit, Bolt and Base44. Its own site now says it was acquired by Freebuff and subscriptions were cancelled. No priced round was found, so this reads as a small team absorbed by a coding tool maker, but the terms and the cause are not public.

name: winfunc
one_liner: ai-native security engineering for mission critical codebases
long_description:
Winfunc (winfunc.com) is an AI Hacker that autonomously finds, verifies, and patches security vulnerabilities in codebases, just like a human security engineer would. 

Winfunc can find business logic errors with context-aware scanning and automate the full auditing cycle to generate reports with zero false positives.

Winfunc's agent has found vulnerabilities in Google, Supabase, Sentry, Cal, Gumroad, Bun, Hoppscotch, etc.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software and security teams that want automated vulnerability finding and patching in their codebases
problem: Manual security audits are slow and static scanners produce many false positives. winfunc runs an AI agent that finds, verifies in a sandbox and patches vulnerabilities.
business_model: B2B SaaS security tooling (pricing not found)
product_category: AI security engineering and code auditing
market_need_then: Security audits are costly and slow, and the company reports its agent found vulnerabilities in widely used open source projects. No dated customer or spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: winfunc, formerly Asterisk, joined YC in Summer 2024 and is still active with a tiny team. No priced round, acquisition or shutdown was found. The founders have security and open source credibility, but the AI pentest field drew large funding for competitors, and with no disclosed funding the outcome remains unclear.

name: xPay
one_liner: International Billing Ops, Sales Tax and Payments for SaaS businesses
long_description: We're building a commerce solution for SaaS companies globally that have overseas customers. We especially help them with streamlining billing operations like invoicing and reconciliation, managing foreign sales tax and accepting payments.  We abstract out the complexities of compliance, remittance and integration for these merchants by running all that machinery in the background.
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian and other internet businesses, especially SaaS, edtech and consumer apps, that sell to overseas customers
problem: Indian businesses struggled to accept international card payments and handle foreign tax and bank settlement. xPay offers a cross-border payment gateway with billing, sales tax and local bank accounts.
business_model: Payment gateway with transaction fees plus billing and tax services
product_category: Cross-border payments and billing operations
market_need_then: Indian SaaS and consumer apps faced difficulty onboarding with global processors in 2024, per vendor guides in search results (these are vendor content from competitors). The company claims 1,200 plus customers and 400M dollars in annual transactions on its own site, which is unverified.
outcome_analysis: xPay joined YC in Winter 2024 as a cross-border payments company in Bengaluru and was still listed as active with three employees in an October 2026 directory. No priced round, acquisition or shutdown was found. It claims strong volumes on its own site, but there is no independent evidence of traction or a later raise, so the outcome is unclear.

name: Ångström AI
tags: AI-powered Drug Discovery; Biotech; Drug discovery; AI
one_liner: Gen AI molecular simulations that reproduce wetlab results
long_description:
Angstrom AI builds GenAI-based molecular simulations to substitute wet lab experiments in the pre-clinical drug development pipeline. We are a team of 2 PhD's and 2 Professors from the University of Cambridge who decided to start a company together after we realised how to combine breakthoughs in our research in quantum-accurate models of physics and generative AI models.

Our Biotech/Pharma clients can verify the efficacy and safety of new drug candidates using our computer simulations, which match the accuracy of wet lab experiments, but are over 100x faster. We achieve this accuracy by constraining our genAI-based simulations to obey the laws of physics, avoiding the hallucinations seen in other GenAI technologies.

Since joining YC, Angstrom AI has developed the first physically accurate gen-AI based simulation of multiple molecules interacting. We have published the first molecule water solubility results with accuracy within the error range of wet lab experiments. We have also kicked-off a 150K pilot project with a pharma company to apply our tech to estimating solubility in their drug development pipeline.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharma and biotech companies running pre-clinical drug development
problem: Wet lab experiments for properties like solubility are slow and costly. Angstrom AI simulates them with physics-constrained generative models that claim wet lab level accuracy.
business_model: B2B pilots and licensing to pharma (a 150K dollar pilot is mentioned by the company)
product_category: AI molecular simulation for drug discovery
founder_names: Laurence Midgley; Jose Miguel Hernandez Lobato; Gabor Csanyi; Javier Antoran
market_need_then: Pharma spends heavily on wet lab property testing. The company reported a 150K dollar pilot with a pharma company in its YC profile and the company site lists AstraZeneca as a collaborator on a 2026 paper.
outcome_analysis: Angstrom AI is a Cambridge spinout that joined YC in Summer 2024 with unusually strong research founders and early pharma pilot work. No priced round, acquisition or shutdown was found, and a profile reports directors leaving the UK board, so team stability is unclear. The company stays active with research output, but its commercial traction is not independently confirmed.

name: .Wave
one_liner: Inference for real-time AI
long_description:
.Wave provides dedicated inference capacity for real-time workloads, alongside serverless streaming models for speech and conversation.

Our Dedicated Lanes give you the guarantees of a dedicated endpoint (latency, capacity, locked-in price) without paying for idle GPUs. Capacity is matched to your traffic on an agreed schedule: more during peak hours, less during quieter periods, or none when you don’t need service. You only pay for the capacity and time windows you reserve.

Our .wave Live API, powered by our WPK inference engine, provides streaming speech recognition and full-duplex voice.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: AI developers and companies running real-time voice and speech products that need low latency inference
problem: Real-time AI workloads need guaranteed latency and capacity, but dedicated GPU endpoints cost money while idle and serverless gives no guarantees.
business_model: Dedicated inference capacity reserved on a schedule, plus usage-based serverless streaming speech APIs
product_category: Real-time AI inference infrastructure
market_need_then: Voice agents were a fast growing use of AI with latency as the main complaint, per vendor and developer pages. The sources seen are mostly vendor material.
outcome_analysis: dotwave (.Wave) is a Winter 2025 YC company that is still active with two founders from finance and open-source speech work. No verified funding or exit was found and the YC page gives a founding year that conflicts with a directory, so no outcome can be assigned beyond continued operation.

name: 10x
one_liner: AI Sales Teams for Dental Practices
long_description: 10x helps dental practices turn missed revenue opportunities into booked appointments. We connect to a practice’s patient database, identify overdue recalls, lapsed patients, and unscheduled treatment plans, then use AI calling and texting to bring those patients back into the chair.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Dental practices that lose revenue from overdue recalls, lapsed patients and unscheduled treatment plans
problem: Practices have patient lists with missed revenue but front desks lack time to call them, so appointments go unbooked.
business_model: Monthly subscription per practice, Hygiene Recall listed at 970 USD per month on the company site
product_category: AI outbound calling and texting for dental recall
market_need_then: Vendor guides cite recall reactivation as a large revenue gap for practices; the company reports over 30k USD per month incremental revenue for one Miami practice (self reported).
outcome_analysis: 10x pivoted from GradeWiz into dental recall and, per founder posts reported by an aggregator, reached seven figure ARR with no outbound sales. The company is active and hiring. Revenue claims are self reported, and funding beyond YC is unknown, so the pivot is the main supported factor.

name: A1Base
one_liner: The social network layer for AI apps
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: College students and communities building and sharing AI powered apps (A1Zap); earlier, developers who need AI agents to have phone numbers and email
problem: People and AI agents lack a social layer for creating, sharing and using AI apps together, starting on campuses.
business_model: Consumer social AI products; earlier an API for agent identity and messaging. Revenue model not stated in sources.
product_category: Consumer social AI apps and agent identity API
market_need_then: The AI agent wave created demand for agent contact identity, but sources show only vendor positioning. No usage figures for A1Base were found.
outcome_analysis: A1Base is a Winter 2025 YC company run by founders with a prior acquired startup, Forage. It is active. Its product moved between agent infrastructure and consumer social AI, and no verified funding, traction or exit was found, so no outcome can be assigned yet.

name: Absurd
tags: Generative AI; Entertainment; Video; Media; Marketing
one_liner: The production canvas for AI film teams
long_description:
Absurd is an online whiteboard where filmmaking teams generate, organize and review AI video and images together. It runs all the leading models in one place, and it works with the tools teams already use, like Blender and DaVinci Resolve.

We use it for our own work: our Kalshi spot "Election Day" did 1M+ views.

Try it at absurd.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Filmmaking teams, studios and brands producing AI generated video and images
problem: AI film teams juggle many generation models and tools with no shared place to generate, organize and review work together.
business_model: Usage priced AI generation per minute of video and per image on a collaborative canvas; earlier positioned as an AI ad production studio
product_category: AI video production software and studio
founder_names: Philip Ho; Damian Chng; Daniel Kathein
competitors_at_founding: Flora (FloraFauna); Weavy (now Figma Weave); Higgsfield and Runway
market_need_then: Brands and filmmakers adopted AI video quickly; the company cites an AI ad for Kalshi with over 1M views and clients such as Hims, Kalshi, Replit and Brex per its YC listing.
outcome_analysis: Absurd is a Fall 2025 YC company in Los Angeles, active with a team listed as 10 and a viral client ad it made for Kalshi. It moved from an ad studio toward software. No verified funding or exit was found, and rivals such as Flora and Figma Weave are well resourced, so no outcome can be assigned.

name: Acolite
one_liner: AI Native Commercial Insurance Broker
long_description: Acolite is an AI-powered insurance brokerage purpose-built for the construction industry. We combine modern technology with dedicated, licensed brokers to help contractors get the right coverage faster and at better rates than traditional brokerages can offer.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Contractors and construction trades businesses buying commercial insurance
problem: Contractors struggle to get coverage fast, shop carriers and manage certificates of insurance and contract insurance requirements.
business_model: Insurance brokerage paid commission by the carrier when a policy is bound, with AI tools for submissions and compliance
product_category: AI enabled commercial insurance brokerage
market_need_then: Contractors need certificates of insurance, many carriers and contract compliance; the company says it serves contractors in all 50 states through carrier partners.
outcome_analysis: Acolite is a Spring 2025 YC company that is active with a founder from machine learning and legal tech. It is positioned as an AI native broker for contractors, while an earlier launch post found only on a mirror site described AI teammates for insurance agencies. name: Acrely
one_liner: Enterprise Voice Agents
long_description: Acrely enables enterprises to build and deploy enterprise-grade voice agents. With both cloud and on-prem offerings, Acrely empowers organizations to leverage AI for customer service, sales, operations, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Home-services businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical) and enterprises needing AI call agents
problem: Missed and slow-handled inbound calls lose bookings; staffing call centers is expensive.
business_model: B2B usage/subscription voice agents, cloud and on-prem
product_category: Enterprise voice AI agents

Sources do not establish that Lupitor is the same company, so the Inactive directory status may reflect a rename rather than a failure. Cause and date are not public.

name: Adam
one_liner: AI Powered CAD
long_description: Applied AI lab building end-to-end agents for mechanical engineers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Makers and hobbyists first (consumer text-to-3D), moving toward mechanical engineers and hardware teams using Onshape and Fusion
problem: CAD tools are powerful but very hard to learn, so making a parametric part from an idea takes hours of expert work.
business_model: Freemium subscription (Standard and Pro tiers from about $5.99 and $17.99 per month); enterprise copilot not yet monetized as of Oct 2025
product_category: AI CAD copilot and text-to-CAD
market_need_then: CAD is widely seen as complex and expensive to learn; TechCrunch reports tens of thousands of users and over 10 million social impressions from the text-to-3D app, showing consumer pull.

It is moving from hobbyist 3D generation to professional CAD copilots, where incumbents and several text-to-CAD rivals compete. It remains active with no exit or distress reported.

name: Adaptional
tags: AIOps; Insurance; Enterprise; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: AI-powered insurance claims review
long_description:
Adaptional is building agentic AI for insurance claims. Claims are 75% of every dollar in the $1T insurance industry -- and one of the most under-optimized areas, still managed by adjusters working hundreds of files by hand. We're changing this with AI claims review agents, already deployed at some of the major P&C carriers. 

In the future, claims will be powered by an intelligence layer that manages files and escalates actions to human adjusters. Adaptional is building the AI system that will be the foundation for every claims department across P&C insurance.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: P&C insurance carriers, MGAs and brokers whose claims departments run quality assurance reviews
problem: Claims QA samples only a few files per adjuster per month, so leakage, compliance and coverage errors go unnoticed on most claims.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS for continuous claims review integrated with Guidewire and Duck Creek
product_category: AI claims review for insurance
market_need_then: The company cites claims as about 75 percent of every insurance dollar and reviewed by manual sampling; the Reuters-sourced headline reports a 10 million dollar seed and operations with several large MGAs and carriers within about a year.
outcome_analysis: Adaptional, founded by two repeat insurtech founders who previously sold Savvy, raised a reported 10 million dollar seed around its Summer 2025 batch and says its agents already run at large P&C carriers. The thesis rides the shift to agentic AI in claims. It is early, active and unexited, with competition rising from other funded claims AI startups.

name: Adentris
tags: Health Tech; B2B; Compliance; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Real-time AI Compliance & Revenue Integrity for Medical Providers
long_description: US healthcare providers lose billions every year to denied claims, most of them traced back to documentation and coding gaps no one catches until the payer says no. Adentris is an AI revenue integrity platform that catches them first. Our AI agents read EHR and payer interfaces directly, no API integration required, across five modules: documentation, coding QA, prior authorization, appeals and denials, and discharge summaries. name: Alter
tags: AIOps; Developer Tools; DevSecOps; Security; AI
one_liner: Privileged Access Management for AI Agents
long_description:
Alter is a zero-trust identity and access control platform purpose-built for AI agents. It wraps every tool call in strong authentication, fine-grained authorization, and real-time guardrails, so agents can move fast without breaking things.

Each request is verified at the parameter level, authorized against granular policies, executed with least-privilege access, and fully audited in real time. Unsafe actions, whether it’s a rogue DROP TABLE or a payment above policy limits, are blocked before they touch production. Behind the scenes, Alter manages credentials, issuing ephemeral, scope-narrowed access for every interaction, then rotating or expiring it in seconds. The result: no long-lived secrets, no blind spots, and no surprises in audit.

With Alter, teams can move fast on AI agent initiatives while staying fully compliant with SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, and internal security standards. A CISO-ready dashboard delivers real-time visibility, detailed audit logs, and compliance-ready controls, removing silos, eliminating excessive permissions, and providing complete oversight of every agent workflow.

problem: AI agents often hold long-lived credentials and broad permissions, so a mistaken or hijacked tool call can touch production systems. Alter wraps each call in authentication, policy checks and audit.
business_model: Freemium developer platform: free plan with 10,000 API calls per month, paid tiers via demo (not listed)
product_category: Identity and access control for AI agents (auth proxy, privileged access management)
market_need_then: In 2025 agent adoption raised concern over agents holding long-lived secrets and acting with excess permissions. Press at the time described non-human identities outnumbering human ones in enterprises.
outcome_analysis: Alter is an active two person company from the Summer 2025 batch selling agent access control as the market for agent security formed. A prior exit by the CTO and infrastructure experience of the CEO fit the problem. Funding beyond a DeVC investment is not confirmed, and well funded agent identity entrants appeared within months, so the outcome is still open.

product_category: AI continuous pentesting and offensive security

outcome_analysis: Antigen is an active team of five from the Fall 2025 batch, run by founders with Google and Tesla backgrounds who appear to have moved from AI review agents (Zag) to offensive security. It says it is backed by Lightspeed, DST Global and Susa Ventures, a strong investor set, though no amount is public. Crowded competition from XBOW and Horizon3 leaves the outcome open.

name: Anto Biosciences
tags: Generative AI; Biotech; Genomics; Drug discovery; AI
one_liner: A Foundation Model for Microbial Communities.
long_description:
Anto is building a foundation model for microbial communities, making the gut microbiome computable for the first time. We predict drug toxicity and efficacy across diverse populations and fix drugs so they work for everyone — solving the hidden root cause of most drug failures. 

Founded by Arvid (Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Nature-published researcher who pioneered quality-aware, goal-directed sparsification) and David (Harvard Medical School Gastroenterology, J&J), second-time founders who published the breakthrough at leading machine learning AI conferences and Nature.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharmaceutical and biotech R&D teams that need to predict drug toxicity and efficacy across populations
problem: Gut microbial communities change how drugs are metabolized and tolerated, but this variation is not modeled in drug development, so many drugs fail for people with different microbiomes.
business_model: Foundation model and platform for pharma R&D, with potential partnerships and microbial therapies (not confirmed)
product_category: AI foundation model for microbial communities and drug-microbiome interactions
founder_names: Arvid E. Gollwitzer; David Alexander de Gruijl
market_need_then: Pharma attrition from toxicity and variable response is well known, and AI foundation models for biology were attracting investment in 2025. Whether pharma paying demand exists for microbiome models is unproven in sources.
outcome_analysis: Anto Biosciences joined YC in Fall 2025 with two scientist founders from Broad, ETH and Harvard building a foundation model for gut microbial communities. It is still early: directories list a roughly 500K seed or pre-seed in December 2025 with gumi named in a Japanese report, and Tekedia Capital announced an investment in June 2026. No customer, revenue or later round is public, so no outcome can be judged yet.

name: Aravolta
one_liner: Software to monitor, control, and optimize data centers.
long_description:
Aravolta provides a single pane of glass software for data centers to increase uptime, reduce costs, and improve performance.

A single utility node onboards every asset within an hour and detects hardware failures, hotspots, and other issues.

It also generates reports on important metrics like Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), energy metering, resource utilization, and much more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Colocation, modular and AI data center operators and infrastructure lenders
problem: Data center operators juggle separate BMS, EPMS, SCADA, NOC and DCIM tools that take months to roll out. Aravolta combines them in one platform deployable in days.
business_model: B2B software with per-device pricing, no per-point fees (quotes on request)
product_category: Data center infrastructure management and monitoring software
market_need_then: The AI build out drove rapid data center construction, and operators faced months long DCIM rollouts, with capital raises for data center tech startups reported in 2025.
outcome_analysis: Aravolta is active and raised a reported 5.1 million dollar seed in December 2025 after the Spring 2025 batch, riding the data center build out. The CEO's Microsoft data center experience fits the problem, and it lists many colocation customers. Entrenched DCIM vendors with AI features keep risk high, so the outcome is open.

name: Archon
one_liner: We help software companies sell to government.
long_description:
Archon helps software companies sell to the government by cutting the required federal compliance timeline (called FedRAMP) down from 16 to 6 months and cuts costs by $1M per company. 

Email us at inquiries@archon.inc
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software companies that want to sell to the US federal government and need FedRAMP authorization
problem: FedRAMP certification is slow and costly for software vendors. Archon claims its SDK cuts the timeline from 16 to 6 months and saves about $1M per company.
business_model: B2B developer SDK and compliance service for software vendors
product_category: GovTech compliance automation (FedRAMP)
market_need_then: FedRAMP is widely described as a long and expensive bottleneck for software vendors selling to government, and the YC page states the 16 to 6 month claim.
outcome_analysis: Archon is an active early-stage company from Winter 2025 with a team of three. A seed round in 2025 is reported only by a secondary profile site, so no round is recorded. No shutdown, acquisition or layoffs were found. It competes against better-documented FedRAMP players such as Knox Systems and Paramify.

name: Artifact
one_liner: An Collaborative, AI-native IDE for Hardware Engineers
long_description:
Artifact is a collaborative IDE for hardware engineers - accelerating every step in the engineering lifecycle:

Design → Procurement → Manufacturing → Integration → Test → Sustainment

We've raised $3.5M to build an integrated, verifiable AI copilot with an intuitive UI that reflects how hardware actually gets built. Every artifact is auto-generated and traceable to a single-source of truth.

We believe hardware engineering should be rigorous, deliberate, and system-aware. We work directly with customers solving the world's hardest technical problems to modernize how complex hardware is engineered.

If you're interested, send your resume & contact info to: careers@artifact.engineer
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware engineering teams in aerospace, robotics, automotive and related fields doing electrical and avionics system design
problem: Electrical system design for complex hardware is done in fragmented tools. Artifact offers a collaborative, version-controlled ECAD environment that generates diagrams, pin tables, harness drawings and BOMs from one system definition.
business_model: B2B SaaS for engineering teams (pricing not found)
product_category: ECAD and electrical systems design software with AI copilot
market_need_then: Aerospace and defense hardware startups were scaling quickly in 2024 and 2025 and relied on manual harness and wiring documentation. The company shows logos from many such customers on its site.
outcome_analysis: Artifact is active and small. The founders come from avionics and aerospace work, a good fit for the target buyers, and the site shows many aerospace customer logos. It announced a 3.5M seed in August 2025. No shutdown or acquisition was found. Competition from AI-first and legacy ECAD tools remains.

name: Artificial Societies
one_liner: Foundational model of human societies for consequential decisions
long_description:
Simulate decisions that matter.

Artificial Societies builds a foundational model of human societies so enterprises and sovereigns can explore how people may respond before making consequential decisions. We combine behavioural science with simulations grounded in real-world behaviour to understand individual perspectives and how opinions develop across connected groups.

Teams use our simulations to test communications, prepare for crises, explore new markets, and assess investor and public-policy reactions. They can run surveys, focus groups, interviews and experiments with simulated audiences, including stakeholders who are difficult to reach through traditional research, and decisions too sensitive to test otherwise.

Our mission is to pioneer socially intelligent technology that shape the decisions that shape the world.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Enterprises, communications and consulting firms, and public affairs teams that want to simulate audience reactions before decisions
problem: Testing communications, crises, markets and policy reactions with real panels is slow and sometimes impossible for sensitive topics. The company simulates audiences with AI personas.
business_model: Bespoke enterprise simulation services and platform (earlier prosumer product discontinued)
product_category: AI audience simulation and market research
founder_names: James He; Patrick Sharpe; Tom Whittle
market_need_then: Brands and consultancies spend on panels and focus groups, and LLM agent research in 2023 and 2024 suggested simulation might substitute for hard to reach audiences.
outcome_analysis: Artificial Societies raised a pre-seed and a 3.35M seed led by Point72 Ventures within months of its Winter 2025 batch, riding interest in LLM agent simulation. It ended its prosumer Reach product in February 2026 to focus on enterprise work, which is a narrowing of scope rather than failure. It remains active with growing competition such as Aaru.

name: Artil
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Messaging; Email; AI
one_liner: Let your agents message teammates and other agents
long_description: Artil Connect connects different AI agents and people on your team. It gives your agent its own identity, contacts of other agents and teammates, and gives an interface to message them. Artil Connect works on any popular harness and across channels — via direct HTTP, email, Telegram, Slack (beta) and SMS.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Developers and teams running AI agents that need to message people and other agents across channels
problem: AI agents lack identities and contact channels. Artil Connect gives each agent an identity, a contact directory and messaging over HTTP, email, Telegram, SMS and Slack (beta).
business_model: Developer infrastructure, likely usage or subscription based (pricing not found)
product_category: AI agent communication and identity infrastructure
market_need_then: Agent frameworks were multiplying in 2025 and agents needed ways to reach humans and each other; demand evidence for a standalone product was not found.
outcome_analysis: Artil is an active two person company in the Winter 2025 batch building messaging infrastructure for AI agents. No funding, press, shutdown or acquisition was found in public sources, so its trajectory is unknown. The footer entity Fira Finance suggests the company may have changed direction after starting, but no source confirms a pivot.

name: Aside
one_liner: The browser built to do real work for you
long_description:
Aside is an AI browser that completes real work across the websites you already use. It can sign in through your browser, work inside email, dashboards, internal tools, docs, and spreadsheets, and keep going when a task takes minutes or hours.

Unlike agents that depend on integrations, Aside uses the web the way you do. Browsing history becomes local memory, so it knows which tools and context matter. Its password manager lets agents autofill credentials without exposing secrets to the AI. Sensitive actions like payments, posts, and messages wait for your approval.

We achieved state-of-the-art on agentic browsing benchmarks, surpassing OpenAI and Anthropic's result- Aside ranked #1 across Mind2Web, Odyssey, bu-bench-v1.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Knowledge workers and professionals who want an AI agent to do multi-step work inside the sites they are logged into
problem: Agents that rely on integrations cannot reach most tools. Aside is a Chromium based browser whose agent works through the user's logged-in sites, with local memory and a password manager that hides credentials from the AI.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer subscription with credits (a third party lists Free, Pro 20 and Max 200 dollars per month; unverified)
product_category: AI agentic browser
founder_names: Jun Kim; Chanhee Lee; Sanghun Lee
competitors_at_founding: Comet (Perplexity); Dia (The Browser Company); Opera Neon
market_need_then: Interest in agentic browsing surged in 2025 with Comet, Dia and other launches, and many tasks live behind logins where API integrations are absent.
outcome_analysis: Aside is an active Fall 2025 company that moved from a sales call assistant to an AI browser, which launched publicly in mid 2026 and has shipped frequent updates and a Windows version. The market is crowded with Perplexity, OpenAI and The Browser Company, and no verified funding round is public. Outcome is open.

name: Aspect
one_liner: Intelligent media storage for creative teams.
long_description:
Aspect helps creative teams consolidate 5 media tools into one platform. We provide everything a media team needs: file ingest, local file streaming, review and approval, sharing, and archiving. 

Aspect workspaces come with an agent that has complete understanding of your asset library including comments and revisions. Ask the agent to complete any task in the background: searching for files, setting up folder structures, labeling and organizing footage, and much more.

Check out https://aspect.inc/use-cases to see how different media teams use Aspect to deliver content faster.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Creative and media teams such as agencies, production and e-commerce content teams
problem: Media teams juggle several tools for ingest, review, sharing and archiving. Aspect consolidates these into one platform with drive mounting and an AI agent, and now markets itself as an AI studio for creative teams.
business_model: B2B SaaS for creative teams (pricing not found)
product_category: Media asset management and AI creative studio
founder_names: Gurish Sharma; Edison Chiu; Bright Xu
market_need_then: The founders say they spent over 10,000 hours with in-house content teams at their previous company and saw teams stitching together five tools.
outcome_analysis: Aspect is an active three person New York company from Fall 2025. Its founders came from a post-production company and know the media workflow problem. The site has expanded from storage and review into an AI generation studio with named customers. No verified funding or exit exists. Name collisions with other Aspect companies make public coverage thin.

name: Asteroid
tags: Robotic Process Automation; Health Tech; B2B; Automation; AI
one_liner: The integration layer for healthcare: EHRs, payer portals & more
long_description: Asteroid is the AI-powered integration layer for healthcare. One connector for EHRs, payer portals, and legacy desktop systems, with 100+ pre-built integrations that go live in days, not months. Built for developers and operations teams, with integrations that maintain themselves.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Healthcare operations and software teams (providers, payers, care coordination companies) that need to connect to EHRs, payer portals and legacy desktop systems without APIs
problem: Healthcare workflows depend on portals and desktop systems with no usable API. Asteroid generates browser and desktop agents, and APIs from private endpoints, so teams can automate intake, eligibility, scheduling and credentialing.
business_model: Usage-based platform, starting at 300 dollars per month per the company site
product_category: AI browser agents and integration layer for healthcare
market_need_then: Healthcare back-office work relies on portals without APIs, and LLM browser agents had just become feasible in 2024.
outcome_analysis: Asteroid is active with a small team and says more than 100 healthcare and operations teams use it, with a Thyme Care case study. Focus narrowed to healthcare, a regulated vertical where generic browser agent vendors are weaker. Funding visible publicly is small and only in aggregators. Customer figures are self reported and unverified.

name: Astor
one_liner: Your personal investing agent
long_description:
Astor is a personal investing agent for serious investors.

Founded by Bruno Koba (Nubank, monashees) and Daniel Tulha (Stripe, Robinhood), Astor gives every active investor an AI investment advisor working around the clock to surface their next great investment. We’re backed by YC (S25).

Retail investors now account for 25% of all U.S. trading volume, nearly double from 2012. But over 56% still say they don’t feel confident in their investment decisions. Astor fixes that. 

Our AI agents uncover opportunities, decode emerging trends, and deliver analysis tailored to you. Instead of drowning in noise, investors gain a clear edge, shifting from guesswork to confident decision-making.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Active retail investors with brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts
problem: Retail investors cannot watch their holdings around the clock or cut through noise. Astor connects to accounts, monitors holdings and sends alerts, briefs and scenario analysis, with trades only after user approval.
business_model: Consumer subscription: Free, Pro 19 dollars per month, Max 29 dollars per month per the company site; SEC registered investment adviser
product_category: AI personal investing agent
market_need_then: Retail investor participation was high and AI research tools were emerging, while personalised advice was costly and mostly reserved for larger accounts.
outcome_analysis: Astor is active and raised a 5M seed announced in April 2026 about eight months after its Summer 2025 batch, led by Monashees with several fintech funds. Founders with Nubank, Monashees, Stripe and Robinhood backgrounds fit the space, and it is an SEC registered adviser. Risk is that brokerages like Robinhood ship similar AI features.

name: Astro
tags: Solar Power; Energy; Renewable Energy; ClimateTech; AI
one_liner: Power-ready land for AI data centers
long_description: Astro develops power-ready land for AI data centers. Power is now the bottleneck for new data centers, and Astro’s models find the sites that have it. Founder Alex Fuster traded grid congestion at Citadel across US power markets, predicting where the grid would run out of room.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Larger energy companies and developers that buy development-ready renewable projects; AI data center builders short on power
problem: Grid interconnection and power availability are the bottleneck for new data centers and renewable projects, and finding land with grid capacity is slow and manual.
business_model: Project development: acquire land and grid connection agreements, then sell development-ready projects to larger energy companies
product_category: Energy project development with AI site selection
market_need_then: Industry coverage in 2025 and 2026 describes power availability as the main obstacle in data center site selection, with developers shifting to power-first siting.
outcome_analysis: Astro is a very early solo-founder company from the Winter 2025 batch with no public outcome. The current website describes Texas utility-scale solar and storage development with landowner leases, which differs from the YC page pitch of power-ready land for AI data centers, suggesting an evolving focus. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff reports were found, and the funding history could not be verified beyond aggregator claims.

name: AthenaHQ
one_liner: Be the Answer in AI Search - AI SEO across SEO, GEO & AEO
long_description:
Make sure your brand doesn’t get left behind as search shifts from traditional SEO to generative AI search.

AthenaHQ is an AI SEO platform for GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) and AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), helping brands show up in AI-generated answers across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, and more.

AI search is expected to overtake traditional search within the next few years. AthenaHQ fills the gap with a system to measure visibility, identify what AI engines cite and recommend, and help your team improve content and brand presence for AI-first discovery.

Team of former product manager on Google Search's information acquisition team, Deepmind Generative Media team, and ChatGPT superusers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Marketing and SEO teams at brands and enterprises that want visibility in AI-generated answers
problem: Search is shifting from links to generative answers, and brands cannot see or influence whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude or Gemini cite or recommend them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, reported at about 295 to 499 USD per month entry pricing
product_category: Generative engine optimization and AI search visibility analytics
market_need_then: In early 2025 marketers faced the shift from traditional search to AI-generated answers and had no tools to measure brand presence in them; a wave of funded GEO startups followed during 2025.
outcome_analysis: AthenaHQ rode the 2025 shift to AI search, raising a seed of about 2.2M USD during its Winter 2025 batch and signing named enterprise logos. Founders came from Google Search and DeepMind, which fits the problem. The YC page now lists it as acquired by Bloomreach, but no independent source confirmed the deal, so the exit stays unknown here.

name: AtlasGrid
one_liner: Accelerate Product Iteration
long_description: AtlasGrid automatically builds a visual graph of your mobile app UI and displays analytics directly on your screens. Additionally, our fleet of AI-powered agents will continuously analyze thousands of mobile apps, gathering design insights and identifying growth opportunities + actionable product improvements.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mobile app product, growth and design teams
problem: Mobile analytics sit in dashboards detached from the UI, so teams cannot see funnel and conversion data in the context of the actual screens.
business_model: B2B SaaS analytics subscription (pricing not found)
product_category: Mobile product analytics and growth intelligence
founder_names: Oleg Kostour; Anton Krutiansky; Aram Aghababyan
market_need_then: Mobile teams use fragmented analytics tools; the founders cite their own growth experience at Dropbox and Life360, and AI coding tools raise iteration speed so measurement is the bottleneck.
outcome_analysis: AtlasGrid is a Fall 2025 company run by repeat YC founders with prior exits to Dropbox and Life360 and deep mobile growth experience, which is a strong founder-market fit. It is too early for an outcome. Funding is unverified and the market for mobile analytics is crowded with established vendors.

name: Atlog
one_liner: Outbound voice and text AI without a prompt
long_description: Atlog creates voice agents with built-in compliance purpose built for Outbound. Companies use Atlog to automate their calls and texts without worrying about getting sued.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies running outbound collections, payment reminders and renewals calls, notably rent-to-own and lease-to-own retailers and lenders
problem: Outbound AI calling creates TCPA, FDCPA and state law exposure and prompt-based agents are hard to control for operations teams.
business_model: B2B usage-based voice AI for outbound calls and texts (pricing not found)
product_category: Outbound voice and text AI with built-in compliance
market_need_then: The FCC ruled in February 2024 that AI voices count as artificial voices under the TCPA, raising legal risk for outbound AI calling, which creates demand for compliance-first tooling.
outcome_analysis: Atlog is a two-person company from the Spring 2025 batch, with a YC launch post framing it as an AI employee for furniture stores serving rent-to-own retailers, and a later site pitching promptless compliant outbound voice. The founders say their families used rent-to-own furniture. Named customers on the site include Uown Leasing and Hometown RTO, but figures are labeled illustrative. No outcome events were found.

name: Attune
one_liner: Faster builds, zero effort.
long_description:
Attune makes blazingly fast build tools that require zero migration effort.

As AI enables developers to write code faster than ever, slow builds are increasingly becoming the bottleneck in development velocity. Developers regularly lose hours of productivity every day waiting for their builds. Imagine being able to write code in 1 minute, but needing to wait 30 minutes to compile, deploy, and test it.

Existing solutions either require painful migrations to new tools (e.g. Bazel) or rely on just using bigger servers to run your builds. Instead, we do native, first-class integrations into compilers and build systems.

With Attune, you don't need to integrate a new tool. Just make a one-line change from `cargo build` to `hurry cargo build` for 20x faster builds.

Eliza (ex-Google) and Xin worked together for 3 years at FOSSA, where Eliza was Head of Engineering and Xin was Head of Product. Eliza brings a decade of programming languages and build systems expertise, while Xin brings a decade of experience building developer tools products, most recently as VP of Product at Teleport (S15). Having experienced the pain of slow builds firsthand across hundreds of production codebases, we're building the solution we've always wanted.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineering teams with slow builds, starting with Rust developers
problem: Build and compile times are the bottleneck as AI speeds code writing; existing fixes need migration to Bazel or just bigger servers.
business_model: Developer tools, likely subscription (pricing not found)
product_category: Developer tools, build acceleration
market_need_then: Developers lose hours to builds and AI code generation shifts the bottleneck to compile and deploy loops, per the YC launch pitch.
outcome_analysis: Attune's founders worked together at FOSSA on build systems, which fits the problem. The current website no longer mentions hurry and instead lists AI engineering tools, which suggests a shift of focus. No funding, exit or shutdown reports were found, so the outcome is still open.

name: Atum Works

regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Semiconductor makers (for example high-bandwidth memory), plus biotech, sensing and advanced materials users
problem: Scaling chips by stacking 2D layers is increasingly costly; 3D multi-material nanostructures at wafer scale could scale complexity with materials instead.
business_model: Hard tech: nanomanufacturing tools and process, commercialization model not stated
product_category: 3D nanolithography for semiconductor manufacturing
founder_names: Lucas Pabarcius; Matteo Kimura; Malcolm Tisdale
market_need_then: High-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging costs were rising by 2025, and coverage cites a claimed 90 percent cost reduction as the pitch, which is a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Atum Works is an early hard tech company from the Spring 2025 batch with a three-person team and a strong advisory board. Job postings describe it as well funded, but no amount or round could be verified. Technical risk is very high since the claimed resolution is far from leading-edge logic requirements.

name: Auctor
one_liner: The agentic operating system for modern system integrators.
long_description: Auctor brings alignment and intelligence to software implementation, enabling every project to deliver its intended value with clarity and precision.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: System integrators, consultancies and professional services teams that implement enterprise software (Oracle, SAP, Salesforce, Atlassian ecosystems)
problem: Enterprise software implementations lose time and money in requirements gathering, documentation and project coordination.
business_model: B2B SaaS and agents for implementation partners (pricing not found)
product_category: AI agents for enterprise software implementation / professional services automation
founder_names: William Sun; Matthew Blackburn; Anthony Sky Ng-Thow-Hing; Xinan Rahman
market_need_then: Launch post: the team ran over 300 customer calls; named customer Valiantys (Atlassian's largest partner) calls Auctor core to how it operates (company site).
