It is too early to know whether integrators will pay at scale or whether model vendors will absorb the wedge.

name: Automax.ai
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: AI native real-estate appraisal firm
long_description: Automax.ai does property appraisals faster and more transparent. Our mobile app uses LiDAR and computer vision to capture property details automatically, and our custom-trained AI agents combine that data with all the analysis and aggregation required to to generate a complete appraisal report in minutes. The result is a clear, grounded valuation, fully Fannie Mae & Freddie Mac compliant — done in under 20 minutes from start to finish.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mortgage lenders ordering residential appraisals, plus appraisal firms
problem: Residential appraisals take about a week and are slow and manual; AI plus LiDAR capture can compress report production.
business_model: AI-native appraisal firm charging per appraisal, with licensed appraisers reviewing and signing reports
product_category: Proptech, AI property appraisal
market_need_then: The UAD 3.6 appraisal form became mandatory for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac conventional loans in 2026, and appraiser capacity is limited, increasing demand for automation.
outcome_analysis: Automax.ai grew from the founder's family appraisal business and claims 3,000 reports a month, giving real domain insight. A 2025 seed with Pioneer Fund and YC followed. A 2026 lawsuit from True Footage is a legal risk, and competition from other AI appraisal tools is rising. Outcome is still open.

name: Autonomous Technologies Group
one_liner: Superintelligent financial advisor
long_description:
Autonomous is a superintelligent financial advisor at 0% advisory fees. 

Today, managing your money means one of two bad options:

DIY your money: You end up with accounts everywhere (401k, IRAs, brokerage, crypto, savings, equity, secondaries). Your spreadsheet is always wrong. You make expensive mistakes because this isn't your full-time job.

Hire a financial advisor: They'll manage your money and charge 1-2% of assets annually. Run that math over multiple decades and you're handing over half your net worth to fees.

Neither path can economically deliver the sophisticated, personalized strategies the ultra-wealthy use to compound wealth: strategic tax-loss harvesting across individual securities, systematic risk management, portfolio-backed borrowing to defer capital gains, access to alternatives, etc.

These aren't secret – they're just economically impossible to deliver at scale through traditional human advisors.

Robos were supposed to fix this, but they were designed in a pre-AI world. In practice they just manage cookie-cutter portfolios. They don’t coordinate across your 401(k), taxable accounts, mortgage, equity, and cash flow, they don’t help with real decisions like job offers, windfalls, or concentrated stock, and they don’t deliver institutional strategies. That’s why, even after a decade plus, the biggest robos are still <$100B AUM while old-school advisors like Raymond James / Edward Jones sit on trillions.

We’re doing for financial advising what Robinhood did for brokerages. Think of it as a full-stack, AI-native wealth strategist that brings billionaire-style playbooks to ordinary investors.

Autonomous is built around a frontier-scale reasoning engine—an AI that perceives global events as they unfold, understanding their deeper implications for markets and and most importantly, how these events will impact your investments.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Affluent retail investors with fragmented accounts who want tax aware, personalized advice without a 1 to 2 percent advisory fee
problem: People either manage money themselves and make costly mistakes, or pay human advisors 1 to 2 percent of assets a year. Robo advisors offer cookie cutter portfolios.
business_model: Zero advisory fee AI wealth manager that earns from optional paid features such as personalized direct indexing, custodian Apex
product_category: AI wealth management and financial advisory
market_need_then: The company cites about $250B a year in advisory revenue and the fact that the biggest robos are still under $100B in AUM while traditional advisors hold trillions. Demand for low fee personalized advice and tax optimization is long standing.
outcome_analysis: Autonomous came out of stealth in January 2026 with a $15M pre-seed, unusually large for a Fall 2025 YC company, driven by founders who already sold Paperspace to DigitalOcean for $111M. It is Active and still pre launch pending regulatory approval, so the outcome is open. Risks are regulation, crowded robo advisor competition and proving the economics of a zero advisory fee model.

name: Autosana
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: AI agents for E2E testing across mobile & web
long_description:
Autosana is the end-to-end testing layer for your coding agents, across iOS, Android, and Web apps.

Step away from your laptop. Come back to full-stack features built and tested end-to-end, production ready.

Autosana creates, updates, and runs tests automatically from your code diffs. Locally, it loops with your coding agent until every test passes. In PRs, it loops with cloud agents and shows video proof of your new feature or bug fix working end-to-end.

No setup, no maintenance, just tests evolving with your codebase. Ship with confidence.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams building iOS, Android and web apps, especially teams using coding agents
problem: End-to-end testing is brittle and slow to maintain, and coding agents ship features faster than teams can verify them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for agent-run end-to-end tests
product_category: AI end-to-end testing for mobile and web apps
market_need_then: Coding agents sped up feature output in 2025, making testing the bottleneck; roundups in 2025 describe agentic mobile test tools as a fast-growing category.
outcome_analysis: Autosana raised a 3.2M USD seed in February 2026 led by YC after the Summer 2025 batch, shows named customers like Life360, Kalshi and Partiful, and acquired Meadow in June 2026. Timing with coding agents helps. Competition from many AI testing tools is the main risk, and company growth claims are unverified.

name: Autumn
one_liner: Billing infrastructure for AI
long_description:
Autumn is open-source infrastructure over Stripe that allows AI startups to build their pricing plans quickly, and flexibly. We act as your app's DB and manage who's paying for what, track usage and manage customer feature access.

YC companies use us because we make it easy to handle common pricing models like usage-based, credits, subscriptions, rollovers and more in 3 functions and no webhooks. 

As you scale, you get reliable billing, that you can change however you want without wrangling code (we handle versioning, migrations etc), and manage custom pricing too. Everything you could down the line (credits, multiple subscription groups, rollovers, referral program, usage analytics, centralized team billing etc), you can drop in at any point.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: AI startups and B2B software companies that sell usage-based, credit-based or subscription plans and run on Stripe
problem: Teams building AI products with credits, usage limits and changing plans have to wire Stripe webhooks, metering and feature access by hand, and every pricing change means new code and migrations.
business_model: Open-source billing layer over Stripe with a hosted paid tier; free starting tier and demo-led sales for larger contracts
product_category: Billing and pricing infrastructure
market_need_then: AI products shifted pricing from seats to usage and credits in 2024 and 2025, and founders interviewed about billing by the company (a January 2025 post on talking to 30 YC founders) reported rebuilding pricing often.
outcome_analysis: Autumn is active and growing as of late 2026, with named customers such as Mintlify, Firecrawl, Mastra, Browser Use and T3.chat on its site. It pivoted out of a banking software idea in the F24 batch into AI billing, rode the shift to usage and credit pricing, and spread through open source, Product Hunt and Hacker News. The main risk is that Stripe and well funded billing vendors cover the same wedge, and Metronome was reportedly bought by Stripe in January 2026.

name: Avallon AI
one_liner: AI agents for insurance claims operations
long_description: Avallon automates insurance claims operations with AI agents that handle routine calls and documents processing.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Insurance carriers and third-party administrators (TPAs) that run claims operations
problem: Claims teams spend adjuster time on routine intake calls, status calls, outreach and document data entry, and have high turnover and limited capacity.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS for AI claims agents, started as bespoke services in workers' compensation and auto lines
product_category: AI agents for insurance claims operations
market_need_then: Claims operations have high turnover and heavy manual calls and data entry; the company says revenue grew tenfold during the YC batch and customers include Athens Administrators and Johnston and Associates.
outcome_analysis: Avallon began as bespoke services in workers' compensation and auto claims, reported tenfold revenue growth during the Spring 2025 batch and raised a $4.6M seed in November 2025 led by Frontline Ventures. The company is active with named TPA customers. The main risks are that claims system vendors such as Five Sigma bundle similar agents and that a seed at this size needs enterprise contracts to scale.

name: Avelis Health
one_liner: We audit medical claims for self-insured employers and health plans.
long_description:
𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐰𝐞 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬:
I (Angel) have had three knee surgeries since my mid-teens and was billed more than $250K for care that should have cost a fraction of that. Fighting those inflated charges was so painful that we set out to build a consumer-facing AI agent to do it for others. In less than five months, we helped sixty patients erase or reduce over $300K from their medical bills.

This inspired us to fix the problem farther upstream: stopping bad payments before the patient ever sees a bill. So we launched payment integrity, machine-learning models that audit every medical claim for self-insured employers and health plans in real time.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦:
• Self-insured employers waste $60 B+ each year on claims that never should have been paid. Healthcare is the 2nd largest company expense after payroll.

• Manual audits are slow and partial: Reviewers focus only on high-dollar claims, letting millions more slip through unnoticed.

• Existing audit software is static: Decades-old rule engines can’t keep pace with evolving codes, contracts, or billing tactics.

• Incentives are misaligned: Third-party administrators are paid to process claims, not to police them, so accuracy checks are minimal.

𝐎𝐮𝐫 𝐒𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧:
Our models audit medical claims before and after payments have been issued. We catch nuanced billing, coding, and contract errors to save 3-7% on annual claims spend. We work with self-insured employers and health plans.

𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐔𝐬:
Angel Onuoha (CEO) and Ahmad Shehu (CTO) have worked together for 4 years. Before Avelis Health they built Zuvy, a Lagos-based fintech company that provided invoice factoring to small businesses. Zuvy was acquired by The BAS Group in 2025.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Self-insured employers, third-party administrators and health plans that pay medical claims
problem: Self-insured payers overpay on claims because manual audits cover only high-dollar claims and TPAs are paid to process claims, not police them.
business_model: Contingency fee on realized savings with zero implementation fee
product_category: Healthcare payment integrity
market_need_then: The YC page says self-insured employers waste over $60B a year on claims that should not have been paid; this figure is the company's own claim.
outcome_analysis: Avelis Health is early and active. The founders sold a prior fintech (Zuvy) in 2025 and moved from a consumer bill dispute agent to B2B claim auditing sold on contingency. Funding beyond the YC deal is thin: one outlet reports a round with Tekedia Capital in November 2025 with no amount. It is too early to call an outcome.

name: Avent
one_liner: AI agents for industrial commerce
long_description:
Avent helps manufacturers and industrial distributors run quoting and order entry on autopilot. 

Our AI agents manage sales inboxes, build quotes from past pricing and tribal knowledge, and keep records up to date in existing ERPs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Manufacturers and industrial distributors that quote and enter orders from email, fax and phone
problem: Distributor growth is capped by the number of inside sales staff who build quotes and key orders into ERPs by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS and AI workforce for quote-to-cash work
product_category: AI agents for industrial distribution
market_need_then: The company says it generates over $200,000 in quotes per day for distributors in North America and the UK; this is self-reported.
outcome_analysis: Avent is a one-founder company in the Summer 2025 batch selling AI quoting and order entry to industrial distributors. Founder fit is credible from the YC page, and the self-reported quote volume suggests early traction, but no priced funding or customer names are public. It is too early to call an outcome.

name: Aviro
one_liner: RL Environments for Long Horizon Work
long_description: We design challenging worlds where AI models learn to explore and solve problems. We turn these worlds into post-training datasets and reinforcement learning environments to train the next frontier of AI. We're research partners with four top frontier AI labs, several Fortune 100 companies, and leading RL data vendors.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs, Fortune 100 companies and RL data vendors that buy training environments and post-training datasets
problem: Models need hard, long-horizon, verifiable tasks to improve at coding, computer use, knowledge work and research, and labs lack enough high-quality environments.
business_model: Custom RL environments and datasets sold to labs under research partnerships
product_category: RL environments and post-training data
market_need_then: In 2025 labs shifted spending from labeled data toward RL environments, with a TechCrunch article in September 2025 describing the rush; Aviro says it has partnerships with four top labs, which is a self-reported claim.
outcome_analysis: Aviro is a two-person Spring 2025 company that renamed from Tropir and now sells RL environments to labs, riding the 2025 surge in demand for environments. No priced round, customer name or exit is public, and well funded environment vendors compete with in-house lab efforts, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Axal
one_liner: We assemble PCBs in under 48 hours for quantities under 10
long_description:
Axal is a quick-turn PCB assembly shop in San Francisco. Samai and Nand build every board themselves, and both are IPC certified. For quantities under 10, we assemble boards in under 48 hours. Order online in 2 minutes at axal.ai.

Send us your board files and we handle the parts, bare boards, assembly, inspection, and delivery.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware teams (drones, robots, medical devices) needing prototype and low-volume PCB assembly
problem: Small teams wait weeks and navigate overseas suppliers to get a few assembled boards; Axal assembles runs of under 10 boards in under 48 hours in San Francisco.
business_model: Per-order PCB assembly service with online quoting, plus sourcing and production handling
product_category: Quick-turn PCB assembly
market_need_then: The YC launch post argues that designing and getting PCBs from China is slow; no dated demand data was found in sources opened.
outcome_analysis: Axal appears to have changed direction at least once, from legacy code analysis and manufacturing AI workers to a hands-on PCB assembly shop run by its two founders. It is active with beta production customers sought. No funding, customers or exit are verified, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Axial
one_liner: Accelerated Physics Kernels for Computational Engineering
long_description:
Axial develops accelerated software for geometric computation, physical simulation, and manufacturing.

Our GPU-native kernels provide programmable building blocks for the computational engineering cycle. They make existing workflows faster and less expensive while enabling engineering teams to explore substantially larger design spaces.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams in aerospace and robotics that do geometric computation, simulation and composite part design
problem: Computational engineering workflows run slowly on CPU tools; the company site describes GPU-native kernels as programmable building blocks to speed geometry, simulation and manufacturing.
business_model: Software kernels and hardware cell; model not stated
product_category: Computational engineering kernels and composite manufacturing
market_need_then: Not established from sources opened; the company claims GPU kernels cut cost and expand design space exploration.
outcome_analysis: Axial is a very early Fall 2025 company whose YC page and company site describe different products, a composite manufacturing cell and GPU kernels, which suggests a pivot or a data mismatch. No verified funding, customers or exit exist, and NVIDIA's open-source Warp covers part of the kernel wedge, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Axiom
tags: Fintech; Crypto / Web3; Consumer Finance; Trading
one_liner: Trade memecoins, perpetuals, and earn yield.
long_description: Axiom is the trading platform for decentralized finance and currently offers memecoins, perpetuals, and yield. Since launch we've hit 10M MRR and 5M monthly net profit.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Retail crypto traders on Solana memecoins and Hyperliquid perpetuals
problem: Traders wanted faster token discovery and execution across chains without juggling bridges and several apps.
business_model: Trading fees on swaps and perpetuals
product_category: DeFi trading terminal
market_need_then: The 2024 to 2025 Solana memecoin boom created heavy retail trading demand; The Block reported in May 2025 that Axiom reached about $100M in revenue four months after launch.
outcome_analysis: Axiom grew very fast on the 2025 Solana memecoin boom, with The Block reporting about $100M of revenue four months after launch and the founders saying they are profitable and not raising beyond the YC check. Risks are dependence on memecoin cycles, Hyperliquid and Solana infrastructure, and allegations from February 2026 that staff used internal wallet data to trade ahead of users, which are not independently confirmed.

name: Beluga
one_liner: Creator marketing that scales like paid ads
long_description: Using our 6+ years of creator marketing experience to help companies run their creator campaigns at scale. Fully managed solution to drive real, attributable results to their marketing efforts.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Tech and consumer companies that want to run creator ad and sponsorship campaigns without an in-house team
problem: Companies find creator marketing hard to scale because sourcing, negotiating, contracting, paying and tracking creators is manual and results are not attributable.
business_model: Managed service fee of 20% of creator ad spend or creator pay, from $15K a month
product_category: Creator marketing agency
market_need_then: Creator spend was growing and brands wanted attributable results. The company reports clients such as Clay and sponsor results like 3,800 signups from two creators, which are company claims.
outcome_analysis: Beluga is a small active creator marketing agency from YC Spring 2025 with named startup clients and a high monthly minimum, and no public funding. It shows early traction claims but a services model with low defensibility and a name shared with several unrelated brands, so its path to venture scale is unproven.

name: Besimple AI
one_liner: Voice data for AI
long_description:
We are building the data layer for AI, starting with audio.  

We start with data collection, curating our own proprietary set of diverse conversational data covering a wide range of languages, dialects and accents.  We then leverage human expert audio annotators and our own annotation platform to process audio data for Automatic Speech Recognition.  

With human level transcription and diarization, our data help push the audio model frontier.  Today we have over millions of hours of conversational data, and growing. 

If you need audio data for training or evaluating your voice models or voice agents, reach out!  We offer flexible licensing deals that work for startups and enterprises, with minimal process.  

Audio data should besimple :)
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and voice AI builders that need licensed conversational audio, annotation and evaluation data
problem: Speech and voice models need diverse, accurately transcribed conversational audio across languages and accents, which is hard to collect and label at human level quality.
business_model: Data licensing plus annotation and evaluation services
product_category: AI training data for audio
market_need_then: Voice AI and speech model training drove demand for conversational audio data in 2025. The company says frontier labs are customers, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Besimple raised a reported 3 million dollar seed after YC Spring 2025 and positions as an audio data research lab for frontier labs. Founders came from Meta annotation teams, which fits the market, while competition from Scale AI and Surge is strong and the company is still early.

name: Better Auth
one_liner: The authentication framework for TypeScript
long_description:
Better Auth is a comprehensive authentication framework for TypeScript that lets you implement everything from simple auth flows to enterprise-grade systems directly on your own database, embedded in your backend. It’s loved by developers all over the world and endorsed by leading voices in the ecosystem.

On top of the framework, Better Auth also provides an infrastructure layer to help you scale with user management and analytics, bot and fraud detection, transactional email and SMS, global session storage and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: TypeScript developers and companies that want auth on their own database, with paid enterprise and infrastructure add-ons
problem: Developers had to choose between hosted auth services with lock-in and cost, or older libraries with gaps, instead of a comprehensive framework they own.
business_model: Open source framework with paid infrastructure layer and enterprise features (dashboard, audit logs, security detection)
product_category: Developer tools, authentication framework
market_need_then: Developers wanted ownership of auth data and lower cost than hosted services. TechCrunch reported 150,000 weekly downloads and 15,000 GitHub stars by June 2025.
outcome_analysis: Better Auth grew through open source distribution, raised a 5 million dollar seed in June 2025 from Peak XV and YC, absorbed the Auth.js project in September 2025 and was acquired by Vercel in July 2026, about a year after the seed. Developer pull and a hot category led to a quick exit, with terms undisclosed.

name: Bezel
one_liner: Digital AI humans that model clothes for e-commerce brands.
long_description:
Bezel helps fashion brands create virtual photo/video shoots with AI. 

Upload images of clothes, select the human you want to model it, and Bezel generates pictures and videos that rival a full studio production. 

Every detail of the clothing is rendered flawlessly. Try it for yourself.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: E-commerce fashion brands (original product); private equity portfolio companies (current site)
problem: Fashion brands pay for costly photo and video shoots with models. Bezel generated virtual on-model photos and video from clothing images.
business_model: Original: AI generated model imagery sold to brands. Current: consulting style AI transformation engagements for private equity platforms.
product_category: Generative AI for fashion e-commerce, now AI transformation services
market_need_then: Fashion brands wanted cheaper imagery, and press in January 2025 covered AI replacing photographers and models. Several startups raised on the same thesis.
outcome_analysis: Bezel started as a one person YC W25 company selling AI models for fashion imagery in a crowded space with better funded rivals. By late 2026 its site sells AI transformation work to private equity portfolio companies, which suggests the original product did not find enough traction, though no source states why. No verified funding exists.

name: Bild AI
one_liner: AI estimating & detailing for Division 8 doors, frames & hardware
long_description:
Bild AI automates Division 8 estimating — doors, frames, and hardware — end to end. Bild AI reads blueprints and specs, generates opening (door) schedules automatically, prices the bid, and exports it directly into the ERPs Division 8 shops already run on, including Comsense, Avaware, and ProTech.

Division 8 estimating is the brutal trifecta of nitty-gritty details, where typos cost hundreds of thousands, and timelines are tight. Thousands of pages of specs, hardware sets cross-referenced by hand, and a single missed opening that can sink a bid's margin. Bild  AI collapses days of takeoff into hours, and clients have bid 50% more with smaller estimating teams.

Backed by Khosla Ventures (YC W25).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Division 8 (doors, frames, hardware) distributors and estimators in construction
problem: Estimators manually read blueprints and specs to build door schedules and bids, which is slow and limits how many bids a team can submit.
business_model: B2B software for AI takeoffs and estimates
product_category: Construction AI, blueprint takeoff
market_need_then: Estimators were capacity constrained. Company reports clients bidding 40 to 60 percent more with the same staff, which is a claim.
outcome_analysis: Bild AI raised a 3.1 million dollar seed from Khosla Ventures in July 2025 and narrowed to Division 8 takeoffs where its site lists about 18 distributor customers. Technical founders plus a construction founder fit the problem, and a focused wedge helps against broader takeoff tools.

name: BitBoard
one_liner: Let your agent build dashboards and reporting.
long_description:
Data analysis with AI agents is great until you realize you want to set up a recurring report or collaborate with your team. We built an agent-first workbook so you don’t have to roll your own dashboards or fumble around in a rigid BI tool.

Connect your agent of choice to BitBoard and it can generate connected charts, SQL, code, and commentary in a notebook-style UI you can share with your team.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams that use AI agents such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor to analyze business data and want shareable dashboards
problem: Analysis built through agent chats is hard to share, rerun and trust, so results need a workspace where sources, queries and code stay attached.
business_model: Subscription software with free trial, pricing not published
product_category: Analytics workspace for AI agents
market_need_then: Agent use for data work was rising in 2025 and 2026, but the product direction changed from healthcare back office agents to analytics, suggesting the first need was weaker.
outcome_analysis: BitBoard began in YC Spring 2025 selling AI workers for clinic back offices, then moved to an analytics workspace for agents in 2026, with two founders ex-Forward. No funding is verified and no outcome is yet known, so the story is an early pivot into a crowded analytics space.

name: BitPatrol
one_liner: AI-powered code security
long_description: Leverage cutting-edge AI to detect exposed credentials in real time and protect your organization from high-impact data breaches.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering and security teams that need to find exposed credentials in code
problem: Leaked keys and tokens in commits cause breaches, and regex based scanners produce noise and miss secrets that lack a known format.
business_model: B2B SaaS secret scanning via a GitHub App and CI integration
product_category: Code security, secrets detection
market_need_then: Leaked credentials were an established breach vector and regex scanners were known for false positives, which is the gap the company's pitch targets; no spending data was retrieved.
outcome_analysis: BitPatrol was a solo founder YC Spring 2025 company selling ML based secrets detection and reportedly raised $500K from YC and Caffeinated Capital. Snyk acquired it, per the company's own site banner, and one profile says the engine now powers Snyk Secrets. Terms and exact date are not public, and the GitHub App was reportedly deprecated on October 6, 2025, which fits a talent and technology buy rather than a scaled business.

name: Bitrig
one_liner: Build and ship native Swift apps with AI
long_description: Made by co-creators of SwiftUI, Bitrig is an AI development environment for Apple platforms. It works with real Xcode projects, features built-in simulators, and automates the App Store Connect busy work. You can add in-app purchase and publish to the App Store with just a prompt. Bring your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individual developers and indie makers who want to build and ship native Swift apps to the App Store with AI
problem: Vibe coding tools mostly produce web or cross platform apps, while building native Apple apps requires Xcode expertise and App Store setup.
business_model: Subscription with credits, plus bring your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription
product_category: AI development environment for Apple platforms
founder_names: Kyle Macomber; Tim Donnelly; Jacob Xiao
market_need_then: AI app builders were booming in 2025 and the YC x Bitrig hackathon and RevenueCat Shipaton partnership show indie developer interest.
outcome_analysis: Bitrig is an active Summer 2025 company from three SwiftUI veterans with strong credibility, press and community use. It expanded from iPhone to Mac in 2026. Funding is unverified and Apple's own tooling is the main strategic risk.

name: Bizzy AI
one_liner: Bizzy works 24/7 so you never miss a lead.
long_description: Bizzy handles your calls, captures and qualifies leads, and books appointments directly into your CRM. It understands your services better than a receptionist would, routes and escalates calls, and syncs with your existing tools to incorporate complex workflows, all so your team can focus on servicing leads, not qualifying them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small service businesses that miss inbound calls (per the YC page); the company site in late 2026 instead pitches banks and fintechs that want bill negotiation built into their products
problem: Missed calls and slow lead qualification cost service businesses leads; the later site positions phone agents that negotiate bills with live representatives.
business_model: Success-based fee on confirmed savings (bill negotiation, per company site); earlier positioning was AI receptionist software
product_category: Voice AI agents
market_need_then: Roundups of AI receptionist tools in 2026 show a crowded demand for call answering and lead qualification, but no dated pre-batch evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Bizzy is an active YC Summer 2025 company with no public funding or exit information found. The YC page describes an AI receptionist, while the company site later describes bill negotiation infrastructure for banks and fintechs, which suggests a repositioning whose timing and reasons are not public. With no revenue, round or customer data, no verdict on success or failure can be drawn yet.

name: Blank Bio
one_liner: RNA intelligence for precision medicine
long_description:
Blank Bio is an applied AI research lab focused on increasing the success rates of clinical trials. We do this by training RNA foundation models that learn the patterns that shape disease progression and patient response to treatment. We aim to help pharma make more informed decisions in clinical trials by capturing the biology that makes each patient’s tumour unique. 

We’re a technical team of AI scientists and engineers from companies including Recursion, Deep Genomics, DeepMind, and Amazon, and institutions including Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Centre, Stanford, and the Vector Institute.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharma and biotech clinical development teams, and diagnostic partners, who pay for patient selection and disease trajectory predictions
problem: Clinical trials fail often and cost a great deal, partly because sponsors cannot predict which patients will progress or respond. Blank Bio trains RNA foundation models on tumour transcriptome data to inform those decisions.
business_model: Applied AI research lab selling model access and collaborations to pharma and diagnostics; revenue plan not disclosed by the CEO
product_category: RNA foundation models for precision oncology and clinical trial design
founder_names: Jonny Hsu; Philip Fradkin; Ian Shi
market_need_then: Pharma loses large sums on failed trials, and the company frames patient selection and disease trajectory prediction as the unmet need. Cheaper sequencing and foundation model methods made RNA modelling feasible by 2025.
outcome_analysis: Blank Bio is an active, very young company. After the Summer 2025 batch it raised a $7.2M oversubscribed seed in May 2026 and announced a PacBio sequencing collaboration. Founders carry direct RNA model research credentials from Toronto and ex Deep Genomics and Recursion experience, which supports founder market fit. The open questions are revenue model and whether pharma will pay for model predictions.

name: Blaxel
tags: Developer Tools; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: The infrastructure for autonomous agents
long_description:
Blaxel is the infrastructure foundation for autonomous agents.

Engineered for the way agents actually run, Blaxel gives builders deep control over compute (sandboxes), storage (shared filesystem), and networking as built-in infra primitives.

Unlike traditional sandboxes that expire or suffer from cold starts, our sandboxes automatically scale to zero after 1s of inactivity and resume in under 25ms with full memory state preserved — allowing you to keep millions of secure sandboxes on standby indefinitely.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies running AI agents that need secure sandboxes, storage and networking
problem: Agents need isolated compute that starts instantly and keeps state, which traditional cloud and ephemeral sandboxes handle poorly.
business_model: Usage based infrastructure for agent sandboxes, storage and hosting
product_category: AI agent infrastructure and sandboxes
founder_names: Paul Sinai; Charles Drappier; Mathis Joffre; Nicolas Lecomte; Christophe Ploujoux
market_need_then: Agent builders in 2025 needed safe code execution environments; the company said it was processing billions of agent requests by its seed announcement per VentureBeat, which is a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Blaxel joined YC in Spring 2025, raised a $7.3M seed led by First Round, and sold to Baseten on September 10, 2026 with terms undisclosed. A team with prior cloud infrastructure exits built differentiated microVM sandboxes during the agent infrastructure boom, then joined an inference company that wanted compute, storage and networking next to inference. The product keeps operating.

name: BlindPay
tags: Developer Tools; Fintech; Crypto / Web3; Payments; API
one_liner: Stablecoin API for global payments
long_description: BlindPay is a stablecoin API that enables companies to send and receive money worldwide using fiat money, stablecoins and multiple blockchains. We handle all the complex compliance and regulatory requirements, so companies can focus on their core business.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies, especially tech and fintech firms, sending or receiving cross border payments with a focus on Latin America
problem: Moving money across borders is slow and costly, and compliance is complex. BlindPay offers one API that connects fiat, stablecoins, blockchains and local rails such as Pix, SPEI and PSE with compliance handled.
business_model: usage-based API with transaction fees
product_category: stablecoin payments infrastructure API
founder_names: Bernardo Simonassi; Joao Borges; Gustavo Marinho; Gabriel Lyra
market_need_then: Stablecoin payments were growing fast and Latin American companies needed local currency access. The company reported $900,000 in total payment volume in 2024, according to a Brazilian outlet.
outcome_analysis: BlindPay is active and growing in the sources found. It raised a $3.3M seed in August 2025 from YC, 468 Capital, Circle Ventures, Bitso Business and angels, and has kept shipping through 2026 with new rails and banking partners. The tailwind is stablecoin adoption and Brazilian fintech experience in the founding team, while the risk is heavy competition from better funded orchestration providers.

name: Bloom
one_liner: Build and share mobile apps in seconds
long_description:
Bloom lets you vibe code cross-platform apps and test them on your phone natively in seconds. Unlike other vibe code tools, Bloom deploys a backend for you, so you can build functional MVPs and personal apps, not just toys.

https://youtu.be/oeJCk_nwDZg
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Non coding individuals and makers who want to build and share native mobile apps with AI
problem: Building a native mobile app normally needs coding, backend setup and App Store accounts. Bloom lets people vibe code cross platform apps, test them on a phone in seconds and deploys a backend.
business_model: consumer and prosumer subscription for an AI app builder (pricing not shown on the site)
product_category: AI mobile app builder (vibe coding)
market_need_then: Vibe coding was a fast growing behaviour in 2025, and the founders argue other tools produce toys rather than apps with a backend. No customer or revenue figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Bloom is a two person company that entered YC in Spring 2025 and is still active with no public outcome. No verified funding round, revenue or user figure was found, so its trajectory cannot be judged. The founders had earlier consumer app experience and turned down an acquisition of a prior product, while the main risk is a crowded vibe coding market that platforms like Replit entered.

name: Blue
one_liner: AI rebuilt coding. We’re rebuilding the phone
long_description:
AI changed coding when it got its own environment instead of a chat window. Developers stopped typing every line and started handing off whole tasks. The phone is next, and it needs the same rebuild.

Blue is that rebuild: a phone that’s also your chief of staff. It reads every notification, text, and email for you. Then it either handles each one and leaves you an FYI, or drafts a reply and waits for your OK. Anything else is one button away: say what needs doing, and Blue gets it done in the background, using the right apps.

It knows you from day one. Switch from your iPhone and Blue brings over your apps, messages, photos, and passwords, so it already knows who matters to you, how you write, and which card to use. No logins to hand over, no context to explain.

An app can’t do this; it takes owning the phone. Blue runs our own OS on Google Pixel today, with our own hardware in development. We sold out our first batch at YC’s Alumni Demo Day in September.

The team brings complementary experience at scale: Omar Abdelaziz led Google Assistant’s transition to LLMs and holds one of the earliest patents in LLM-based computer control; Peter Krogh spent decades designing voice-first dialog systems and before Blue was a design lead at Google DeepMind building actions for Gemini Live; Muhammad Farhan Hossain helped ship Apple Vision Pro, is named on dozens of hardware and systems patents, and has led products from prototype to mass production.

We’ve built systems used by billions. Now we’re building the phone that comes next.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Busy professionals and iPhone switchers willing to pay for a phone with a built in AI chief of staff
problem: Phones are collections of apps that demand constant attention and data entry. Blue puts an assistant across apps that triages notifications, handles routine messages and runs background tasks.
business_model: hardware plus software; Blue Phone on Pixel hardware priced at $1,299 in beta, own hardware planned
product_category: AI native phone and operating system
founder_names: Omar Abdelaziz; Farhan Hossain; Peter Krogh
market_need_then: AI hardware gadgets from 2024 (Humane, Rabbit) showed appetite and failure modes. The founders bet that an assistant inside a full phone beats a separate gadget.
outcome_analysis: Blue is active and moving fast: a dictation keyboard in September 2025, then a public beta of the Blue Phone on Pixel 10 Pro with its own hardware planned for Q3 2027. The team has Google Assistant, DeepMind and Apple Vision Pro experience that fits the product. Funding is not confirmed by a primary source, and the main risk is that Apple, Google or OpenAI ship assistant phones.

name: Bluebook
one_liner: AI for accounting
long_description:
Bluebook is building AI agents for accounting firms to accelerate research, reconciliations and monthly closings. We allow professionals to serve 200 clients instead of just 20. With research time cut by 30% accountants can provide more strategic advice to help their clients thrive. The 30 leading firms in the Nordics already use Bluebook.

The accounting industry faces a perfect storm: a massive CPA retirement wave (75% in the coming 15 years), increasing complexity from globalization and new regulations, and private equity consolidation driving productivity demands. LLMs enables software that can understand context, adapt to new scenarios, and handle complex accounting tasks with human-like reasoning - capabilities that traditional rule-based software lacks.
regions: Sweden; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Accounting firms in the Nordics that want to serve more clients per accountant
problem: Accountants spend time on research, supplier invoice processing, reconciliations and monthly closings. Bluebook builds AI agents that automate this so a professional can serve about 200 clients instead of 20, per its YC page.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to accounting firms
product_category: AI agents for accounting firms
market_need_then: Nordic accounting firms face staff shortages and repetitive work. EQT Ventures reports 20+ pilots and work with 8 of the top 10 accounting firms in Sweden within months of founding.
outcome_analysis: Bluebook is active. It raised about $3M pre-seed in February 2025 led by EQT Ventures and reported 30 Nordic firms as users on its YC page. Early pilots with large Swedish firms suggest real pull and the AI timing helps. No later round was found, and the risk is that local incumbents and new entrants build similar agents.

name: Bluejay
one_liner: Test, monitor, and improve your voice and chat AI agents
long_description: Bluejay’s mission is to engineer trust into every AI interaction, becoming the trust layer between businesses and their customers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams deploying voice and chat AI agents in customer support, healthcare, financial services and logistics
problem: AI agents fail in production in ways teams do not catch. Bluejay simulates customer conversations before release, monitors production calls and evaluates latency, hallucination and tool calls.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold through demos
product_category: QA, simulation and monitoring for voice and chat AI agents
market_need_then: Voice AI agent deployments were growing in 2025 and teams lacked ways to test them. Bluejay's website cites customers such as DoorDash and Google, which are the company's own claims.
outcome_analysis: Bluejay is active. It raised a $4M seed in August 2025 led by Floodgate and, per its site, serves enterprise voice AI teams. The tailwind is fast growth of voice agents and founders from Amazon and Microsoft AI teams. The risk is a crowded testing category where rivals and platforms can bundle similar features.

name: Blueshoe
one_liner: The AI-Native Consumer + Plaintiff Law Firm
long_description:
Blueshoe is a full-stack law firm that helps people with everything from everyday legal issues to high-stakes litigation and trial.

People can access legal guidance directly through our web app or the AI interfaces where they are already seeking answers. If representation is needed, Blueshoe attorneys handle many cases all the way to resolution, equipped with cutting-edge data, AI-native tools, and operational support.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individuals and small businesses with employment, housing, injury, consumer and commercial disputes, plus attorneys who license the platform
problem: Legal help is expensive and billable hour driven. Blueshoe is an AI native law firm where AI agents handle intake, records and drafting and licensed attorneys review each matter.
business_model: law firm fees (contingency and fixed style, 'no billable hours') plus platform services to attorneys
product_category: AI native consumer and plaintiff law firm
market_need_then: Many individuals cannot afford lawyers and plaintiff firms are adopting AI. Blueshoe's thesis is direct to consumer access; no client or revenue numbers were found.
outcome_analysis: Blueshoe is a two founder company that launched an AI native consumer and plaintiff law firm in 2025 and remains active, with an Arizona firm structure and an attorney managing partner. No verified funding or traction was found. A lawyer and an MIT trained engineer give relevant skills, while regulation of law practice and cost of client acquisition are the main risks.

name: Bluma
tags: B2B; Social Media; Video; Marketing; Advertising
one_liner: Canva for short-form video ads
long_description:
Bluma is the first AI short form content engine.

In a post-AI world, attention is the most valuable commodity. Social media is only growing faster and faster, and we're still early.

We automate your entire consumer marketing strategy by cloning your competitor's viral videos.

Everything that a growth team would plan, script, produce, and edit, Bluma can clone end-to-end and at scale.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Social teams, performance marketers, agencies, creators and brands producing short-form paid video ads
problem: Making TikTok and Reels ads is slow and costly. Bluma lets users clone competitors' viral videos, recreate scripts and visuals, and edit in a canvas based editor.
business_model: SaaS subscription for an AI video ad tool (pricing requires a sales call per one review)
product_category: AI short-form video ad creation
market_need_then: Brands increasingly buy paid short-form video creative, and AI UGC tools were popular. No customer or revenue figures for Bluma were found.
outcome_analysis: Bluma is a two person Fall 2025 company with a beta product that is free to try. No verified funding, revenue or outcome was found. The founders have engineering backgrounds, but the AI video ad category is crowded with established tools and defensibility is weak, so the story is unknown rather than failing.

name: Bolna AI
one_liner: Voice AI to enable India's next billion
long_description:
Bolna handles the complexity of voice infra, so enterprises can automate calls faster, better, and cheaper, at scale

Bolna is a Voice AI Orchestration platform purpose-built for Indian enterprises.
Businesses in India run tens of thousands of calls every day - across sales, support, collections, recruitment, and more. Bolna gives them the power to build and deploy Voice AI Agents directly from their transcripts and FAQs, so they can start automating calls immediately.

With Bolna, enterprises get:

1. Full control over agent intelligence, tone, and workflows
2. Cost efficiency at scale with smart routing across providers and price points
3. Enterprise-grade performance on latency, interruptions, multi-language, and multi-accent understanding
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Indian enterprises and developers that run high volumes of phone calls (BFSI, e-commerce, recruitment, education) and want voice AI agents
problem: Building production voice agents requires stitching together speech-to-text, LLM, text-to-speech and telephony, and many voice applications stall before production, especially for Indian languages and accents.
business_model: usage-based per-minute orchestration fees plus forward-deployed engineering for large enterprise contracts
product_category: Voice AI orchestration platform
market_need_then: Indian businesses run tens of thousands of calls a day across sales, support, collections and recruitment; cheaper and better speech models in 2025 made automation viable. Company claims over 200,000 daily calls and near 700K dollars ARR per TechCrunch, unverified independently.
outcome_analysis: Bolna pivoted from application-layer tools to voice orchestration in mid-2025, used the improving speech and language model stack, and reported fast growth in calls and revenue, mostly from self-serve users with a few enterprise pilots. After YC Fall 2025 it raised a 6.3 million dollar seed led by General Catalyst in January 2026. It is early, so the main risks are competition from global orchestration platforms and model providers.

name: Bond
tags: B2B; Workflow Automation; Productivity; AI Assistant
one_liner: Your AI Chief of Staff
long_description: Bond is an AI Chief of Staff that gives CEOs and busy executives real-time visibility into what’s happening across the company and tells them what to focus on. Saving execs 10+ hours a week.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: CEOs, founders and busy executives at startups and companies using Slack, Jira, Notion, GitHub and Salesforce
problem: Executives lack real-time visibility across the company's tools and spend hours chasing status; Bond connects those tools and tells them what to focus on.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with free tier, individual plan at 49 dollars per month and custom enterprise pricing (per bondapp.io)
product_category: AI chief of staff assistant
market_need_then: Executives juggle many tools; the product launched on Product Hunt in 2025 per search listings and the company shows founder and executive testimonials, but no hard demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Bond is a three person Spring 2025 YC company building an AI chief of staff for executives. The sources opened show a live product with paid plans and testimonials, but no verified funding round, traction data or exit. A search for acquisition, shutdown or layoffs returned only unrelated companies named Bond, so the outcome is still open and any success or failure judgment would be a guess.

name: Boom AI
one_liner: AI agents that recover lost revenue through real conversations.
long_description:
Boom reaches out to your customers before you lose them.

We run proactive outbound conversations at scale: recovering churned users, re-engaging drop-offs, and protecting revenue you thought was gone. AI agents hold real conversations with your customers over SMS, email, WhatsApp, or phone, in their language, on the channel they actually answer.

Every month, companies lose 5-15% of revenue to churn, and more walks out through abandoned signups and failed onboarding. The tools built to fix this don't work. Win-back emails get ignored. Cancel flows only catch people at the door. Hiring humans doesn't scale. Boom does the one thing that works: a real conversation. 1,000x the reach of manual outreach, and the customer can reply.
regions: Mexico; Latin America
target_customer: E-commerce and subscription businesses that lose revenue to churn, abandoned signups and failed onboarding
problem: Companies lose 5 to 15 percent of revenue monthly to churn and drop-offs, and win-back emails and cancel flows do not work; Boom runs proactive outbound conversations over SMS, email, WhatsApp and phone.
business_model: B2B SaaS / AI agent platform, pricing not found
product_category: Conversational AI agents for revenue recovery and customer engagement
founder_names: Juan Casian; Sergio Garcia; Jose Toscano
market_need_then: Subscription and e-commerce firms face churn and abandoned carts; the company's origin story at Atrato reportedly involved not being able to interview enough customers (YesPress, May 2026 update, unverified).
outcome_analysis: Boom is a three person Fall 2025 YC company by repeat founders from Atrato, a YC W21 company that scaled to about 20 million dollars annualized revenue and was acquired according to the YC page. It sells AI agents that recover churned and abandoned customers and names a few customers. No verified funding, traction or exit data was found, so the outcome is open.

name: Boost Robotics
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Robotics; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Robots for the inspection and maintenance of data centers
long_description:
Boost Robotics is building autonomous mobile manipulation robots to remotely perform manual tasks in data centers. 

The surge in AI applications is pushing data centers to scale faster than they can manage, leading to suboptimal operations and staffing shortages amid rising power and compute demands.

We save data centers millions in insurance premiums and SLA violations by increasing the frequency of inspection and maintenance while reducing the time it takes to triage and address failures.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data center operators who dispatch technicians for inspection, cable checks and hardware swaps
problem: Data centers need physical remote-hands work and monitoring; Boost builds autonomous mobile manipulation robots that inspect and physically work on infrastructure.
business_model: Robot hardware and service via pilots with data centers; pricing not found
product_category: Mobile manipulation robots for data centers
market_need_then: Rapid AI data center buildout increased demand for inspection and maintenance labor; Boston Dynamics reported rising data center interest in 2026 coverage.
outcome_analysis: Boost Robotics is a two person Spring 2025 YC company founded by CMU robotics graduates, one of whom worked on Spot at Boston Dynamics, building robots for data center remote hands work. No verified funding, customers or exit were found, and the product was described as a prototype seeking pilots, so the outcome is unknown.

name: BootLoop
one_liner: Firmware in minutes, not months - rigorously tested on real hardware
long_description: BootLoop is building the first AI agent to write and test firmware on real hardware. Existing AI coding assistants fail completely with embedded systems, but our agent ingests datasheets, schematics, and other design files to write firmware in your style and automatically test it on your hardware.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware production teams in deep tech, aerospace and defense, medical device, robotics and IoT that write and test embedded firmware
problem: Firmware and embedded development is slow and hardware-in-the-loop testing is out of reach for most teams; BootLoop's agent reads datasheets, schematics and code, then writes, flashes and tests firmware on real hardware.
business_model: B2B software and pilot program with forward-deployed engineers; pricing not found
product_category: AI agent for firmware and embedded development and hardware-in-the-loop testing
market_need_then: Embedded teams face long firmware cycles; trade press in 2026 says hardware-in-the-loop testing stays out of reach for most teams (company-authored framing).
outcome_analysis: BootLoop is a three person Summer 2025 YC company led by founders with SpaceX firmware and Accenture AI research experience. It launched BootLoop Test in May 2026 with trade press coverage and exhibits at Embedded World. No verified funding or customer data exists, and no exit or shutdown news was found, so the outcome is still open.

name: Bramante
one_liner: Life sciences reagents and software
long_description: We make reagents and software that are purpose built for AI, automated labs, and personalized medicines.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Biotech and pharma companies and research labs that need reagents, or US drug developers needing contract manufacturing without relying on Chinese CDMOs
problem: Labs overpay for reagents and drug developers lack fast US-based manufacturing capacity; Bramante sells lab reagents and media and pitches shipping-container microfactories for contract drug manufacturing.
business_model: Reagent catalog sales (made to order, per unit) plus planned CDMO services
product_category: Life sciences reagents and contract biomanufacturing (CDMO)
founder_names: Scott Stankey; Mike (surname not on YC page)
market_need_then: Many US drug developers contract with Chinese manufacturers according to the YC launch page; trade press describes modular cleanrooms as a growing alternative to building facilities.
outcome_analysis: Bramante is a two person Spring 2025 YC company from founders who previously built Protein Evolution. It sells reagents through its site while its YC launch pitches shipping-container drug manufacturing, and no source dates a shift between them. No verified funding, customers or exit were found, so the outcome and any success or failure factors cannot be judged.

name: Bravi
tags: B2B; Manufacturing; Automation; Home Services; AI Assistant
one_liner: AI operating system for home improvement manufacturers
long_description:
Bravi helps manufacturers of windows, doors, and other home improvement products turn fragmented technical and commercial data into tools their teams can use instantly. 

Our AI platform helps sales, customer service, and field teams answer technical questions, configure complex products, generate quotes, and retrieve order information by connecting to existing documentation, catalogs, ERP, CRM, and pricing systems.

Bravi is already live with leading installers and manufacturers across Europe and the US, turning missed demand into revenue.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Home improvement and joinery manufacturers (windows, doors, shutters) and home service companies that field technical questions, quotes and calls
problem: Field sales reps and installers lose deals waiting for answers to technical, compatibility and pricing questions; Bravi connects product docs and ERP systems so AI can answer questions, configure products, prepare quotes and answer calls.
business_model: B2B SaaS for manufacturers and installers, pricing not found
product_category: AI operating system, assistant and receptionist for manufacturers and home services
market_need_then: Window and door makers have complex catalogues and little modern software; the founders tested the product on their own shutter business and report about 20 manufacturer clients mainly in France (Dealroom, Runtimewire).
outcome_analysis: Bravi was founded in January 2025 in Cholet, France by repeat founders from Snipfeed, entered YC in Fall 2025 and reported about 20 manufacturer clients. Two outlets report a 1.8 million dollar round in September 2026 with YC and funds. It is early with limited traction data, so the main risk is competition from configurator and CRM vendors adding AI agents.

name: Brickanta
tags: Machine Learning; Construction; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Agentic AI for Society Builders
long_description: Brickanta  – agentic AI for society builders. Hundreds of construction-specific AI agents for project analysis, insights, tenders, procurement, and more. Combine the latest AI technology with your organization's project data, templates, and workflows to identify risks and opportunities early and produce better decision support. Brickanta has raised $8 million from leading AI, construction, and real estate investors behind companies like OpenAI/ChatGPT, Airbnb, Klarna, Spotify, and Plangrid-Autodesk, as well as star investors such as Mario Götze, Anton Osika, and Northzone (see movie and press). The founding team has been building and implementing AI in construction and industry since 2018 at companies such as ABB, Fabege, Husqvarna, IKEA and Konecranes.
regions: Sweden; Europe
target_customer: Construction contractors, developers and procurement teams, mainly in Sweden and the Nordics, with customers in several countries
problem: Construction estimating, tendering and project documentation are slow and miss risks and change orders; Brickanta reads project documents and flags missing items, compliance risks and cost issues.
business_model: B2B SaaS per user (Quickstart plan listed at about 890 euros per user per month, enterprise custom)
product_category: Agentic AI platform for construction estimation, tendering and project management
market_need_then: Customers report missed risks and change orders as costly; company reports hundreds of users in eleven countries and four customer stories (Rover, H2, Sakofall, Spentab).
outcome_analysis: Brickanta, a Stockholm AI construction platform founded in 2025, joined YC in Fall 2025 and announced an 8 million dollar seed led by Northzone on January 27, 2026. It reports hundreds of users in eleven countries and named customers, and a team of about 25 to 30. It is early, with risk from global estimation tools and general AI assistants.

name: Brickwise
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: AI property manager for landlords and estate agents
long_description:
We've built an AI property manager that automates maintenance requests, handling tenant calls and messages 24/7, following up by chasing contractors and resolving issues.

We're based in London, but have over 10 customers throughout the world, from San Francisco to Dubai. We have a reliable sales pipeline, including a >$1m cARR enterprise contract. Since our formation 6 months ago, we have raised over $3M in funding.

Ismail, co-founder & CEO, is an ex-Founder at LiveLink AI, where he raised $3M, growing the platform to editing 150k videos per month. He also built his own prop firm to $500k ARR.

Elias, co-founder & CTO, was an early engineer at a YC backed company, acquired by Google. While a senior engineer at Google for 5 years, he took the product from $50k ARR to >$100m. CS at Bristol, MBA from Imperial.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Letting and estate agents, property management companies and institutional landlords (multifamily, single-family rental, student housing, build-to-rent)
problem: Landlords and agents are swamped by tenant calls and maintenance requests, and chasing contractors until a repair is closed is manual and slow.
business_model: B2B SaaS, AI agent handling tenant communication and maintenance, integrating with Yardi, AppFolio, Buildium, Xero and QuickBooks
product_category: AI property management and maintenance coordination
market_need_then: The YC page says the company had over 10 customers and a pipeline including a contract it describes as over $1M cARR within six months of formation. Maintenance handling is a recurring cost for landlords.
outcome_analysis: Brickwise is a young Fall 2025 company with no exit or failure signal. It claims early enterprise traction and more than $3M raised in about six months, backed by founders with prior startup and Google experience, riding the shift to AI agents for operations. Defensibility is the open question because incumbent property platforms are adding AI.

name: Bron
tags: Sports Tech; Analytics; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: TikTok for Sports Betting
long_description:
Bron is the Tiktok for sports betting. Scroll through recommended bets across 150+ sportsbooks and prediction markets and place them automatically.

Download Bron on the App Store here: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/bron-ai-sports-analysis/id6761323087
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer sports bettors, 18+, in the US
problem: Bettors struggle to compare odds across many sportsbooks and prediction markets and to find good bets.
business_model: Consumer app, freemium with Bron Pro subscription (monthly and annual, 7 day trial)
product_category: Sports betting research and recommendation app
market_need_then: Sports betting and prediction markets were growing in the US in 2025; the app lists 150+ books and markets. No usage numbers found beyond 19 App Store ratings averaging 4.2.
outcome_analysis: Bron is a two person Fall 2025 company with no outcome yet. Its main public event is a viral ad that triggered a cease and desist from LeBron James, which brought attention but also legal risk. The category is crowded with AI picks apps and sportsbooks building their own tools.

name: Browser Use
one_liner: Agents that use the browser.
long_description:
We enable AI to control the browser. 
Browser-use is the biggest open-source web agent project with 110k+ Github stars.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need to operate websites, plus enterprises automating web workflows
problem: AI agents cannot reliably navigate and act on websites, especially behind logins and bot checks.
business_model: Open source core (MIT) with usage-based cloud for agents and stealth browsers, plus enterprise plans
product_category: Browser automation infrastructure for AI agents
market_need_then: Demand surged after the Manus agent, which relied on Browser Use, went viral in early 2025 per TechCrunch; the repo grew past 110k stars per its YC page.
outcome_analysis: Browser Use rode the 2025 agent wave with an MIT licensed repo that became the most starred web agent project and raised a reported $17M seed within the YC batch. It has since added a paid cloud and enterprise features. Risks are model labs shipping native browser agents and the generic name.

name: Bud
one_liner: Agent with a computer
long_description: Bud is an agent with a computer. You can use it from web, text, or telegram. Bud can build & code, fully use a browser, do professional work (research, slides, docs, excel), use skills, and run completely autonomously.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers and professionals who want an autonomous AI agent; earlier developers and designers using a vibe coding app builder
problem: Users want an AI that can actually do computer work end to end, such as coding, browsing and producing documents, rather than only chat.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer AI subscription (pricing not found)
product_category: AI agent with a computer, previously AI app builder (Orchids)
market_need_then: AI coding and agent tools saw strong adoption in 2025; the founders' own claims of traction were not independently verified.
outcome_analysis: The team built Orchids as a vibe coding builder in the YC W25 batch, then repositioned to Bud as a general computer using agent. In July 2026 Figma acqui-hired the team and both products closed by 18 July, with undisclosed terms. That is a soft landing without a standalone product outcome, in a segment crowded by Lovable, Bolt, Replit and v0.

name: Butter
one_liner: Embedded Sandboxes for Agents
long_description:
Butter is building bVisor, an incredibly lightweight sandbox runtime for AI agents.
It embeds directly into your local process, providing a safe bash environment without the overhead of VMs or remote infra.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers building AI agents that need a safe local shell
problem: Agents need a safe bash environment, but VMs and remote sandboxes add overhead and infrastructure.
business_model: Developer infrastructure, open source runtime (bVisor); no revenue model found
product_category: Agent sandbox runtime
market_need_then: AI agents running code needed isolation; comparison pages in 2026 show a crowded sandbox market, but no dated demand evidence from early 2025 was found.
outcome_analysis: Butter descended from Pig, whose Windows agent product found no demand, then moved through an agent cache to a Zig sandbox runtime. In April 2026 Modal announced Butter was joining it, with the founder and a researcher joining Modal's Sandbox team. Price was not disclosed and the product was an early proof of concept, so this reads as a team acquisition. The directory status Active is out of date.

name: Bystreet
one_liner: Connect with hotel owners around the world.
long_description: Identify and connect with the owners and key decision-makers behind 300,000+ hotels globally. Our customers include the world's leading hospitality firms: Marriott International, Choice Hotels, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Hotel Equities, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hotel brands, franchisors, operators and vendors that sell to hotel owners (customers named: Marriott, Choice Hotels, Wyndham, Hotel Equities)
problem: It is hard to find who owns and operates a given hotel and how to reach them, which slows franchise development and vendor sales.
business_model: Data subscription per seat or regional data license
product_category: Hotel ownership and contact data platform
founder_names: Corey Anderson; Charlie Maki; Cameron Hake
market_need_then: Big hotel brands are paying customers per the company site, with testimonials from Marriott and Choice executives. Launch coverage was about 16,000 hotels in Caribbean and Latin America, later claimed 300,000+ globally.
outcome_analysis: Bystreet is an active Winter 2025 company selling hotel owner data to large brands. Named enterprise customers suggest early product demand. No funding amount, exit or failure signal was found, so the outcome is unresolved.

name: CLODO
tags: B2B; Recruiting; Sales; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Planet-scale people discovery.
long_description: Clodo is the planet's best people discovery. Used in GTM, Recruiting, Marketing, and Ops at AI Natives, B2Bs, and Fortune 500s in SaaS, Manufacturing/Industrials, BioTech, Healthcare, Fintech, Compliance, and more
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Recruiters, sales and GTM teams at startups and enterprises (named users include Mercor, Hud, Eragon, Corgi)
problem: Finding exact target people for recruiting or outbound is a slow manual process.
business_model: SaaS subscription, third party listing says from $75 per user per month (unverified)
product_category: AI people search and outbound prospecting
market_need_then: Outbound and recruiting teams spend heavily on prospecting tools; the company site claims 17,700 meetings booked and 1.5B+ people indexed, self reported.
outcome_analysis: Clodo is an active Summer 2025 company in a crowded AI prospecting category with a two person team. It reports a customer list of YC startups and a partnership with a similarly named people search company, but no funding or outcome is verifiable.

name: Cactus
one_liner: All-In-One AI Growth Partner. Built for Trades.
long_description:
HVAC, plumbing, roofing, and electrical companies spend $3K–$25K every month making the phone ring - then lose 10–20% of those leads to slow response times, missed calls, and zero follow-up. The revenue was already there. It just walked out the back door.

Cactus closes that gap on both sides.

Inbound: Every call answered in under 60 seconds, 24/7 qualified and booked directly into Housecall Pro, Jobber, FieldEdge, or ServiceTitan. No voicemails. No missed jobs.

Outbound: Warm leads, dormant customers, and unworked estimates get proactively contacted - driving repeat jobs, cross-sells, upsells, and referrals without adding headcount.

The result: 20–30% more jobs from the ad budget you're already spending.

What that looks like in practice:

→ Roofing company, NC | $299K collected in 10 weeks. $1.41M pipeline created. 199× ROI. $48K of that revenue came in after hours — while the office was closed.

→ Plumbing & HVAC company, UT | $180K confirmed revenue in 4 months. 90× ROI. 58% of captured leads came after hours — jobs that would have gone to voicemail now go straight into the CRM.

→ General contracting company | Grew from 11 jobs/month to 72 in a single month — 555% growth. $2.09M invoiced. $1.82M collected. Zero new hires.

→ Roofing & siding company | $228K pipeline in 75 days. 92% of calls converted to hot leads. $804K in net sales during the Cactus period. 49 spam calls filtered automatically — hours of staff time saved.

→ Commercial signage company | $398K pipeline generated in 10 weeks. 111× ROI on $3,597 invested. Grew from 0% to 30% share of total company pipeline in a single month.

If we don't add revenue, we don't stay. That's the only way this works.

The $150B home services industry is still running on voicemail and spreadsheets. We're building the system that changes that - one answered call at a time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical and construction businesses
problem: Trade businesses pay thousands per month for leads and then lose many to missed calls and slow follow up.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services, AI phone agent plus outbound and marketing management, with a never-miss-a-lead guarantee
product_category: AI call answering and growth platform for home services
market_need_then: YC page and site cite $3K to $25K monthly lead spend and 10 to 20 percent leads lost; the site reports 53K+ calls handled and 90%+ retention, self reported.
outcome_analysis: Cactus narrowed from a general AI assistant to home service trades and raised a reported $7M seed in November 2025 led by Wellington Management and YC, within months of its Spring 2025 batch. Repeat YC founders and reported customer ROI support the story. Competition from receptionist vendors and field service platforms is the main risk.

name: Cactus Compute
tags: Developer Tools; Hard Tech; Open Source; AI
one_liner: Automation Foundation Models For Tiny Devices
long_description: On-device AI for phones, wearables, smart home and small robots.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: App developers and device makers running AI models locally on phones, wearables and small devices
problem: Running AI models on low power devices is hard because of memory, latency and power limits, and cloud inference adds cost and privacy concerns.
business_model: Open source or source-available inference engine and small models with cloud fallback; commercial terms not found
product_category: On-device AI inference engine and tiny models

name: Candor

Candor helps defense and deeptech companies navigate the government procurement process with AI. We inject agents into the procurement process - agents that not only surface opportunities but actively pursue them - giving anyone the same capabilities as large contractors. 

When we met at Stanford 4 years ago, it was rare for startups to work with the US Government. In the years that we’ve been involved in the burgeoning Defense Tech ecosystem, a lot has changed. Silicon Valley and the US Government are closer than they’ve been in decades.  

As fellows in Stanford’s Center for National Security Innovation, we’ve had the privilege of speaking with dozens of government officials who have come to Silicon Valley looking to fund and scale startups solving their most urgent problems. 

However, we’ve seen firsthand the struggles these startups face in securing gov funding. Marcus, having spoken with dozens of defense startups in his time helping lead the Stanford Defense Tech Club and trying to set up a national security startup accelerator has seen this especially.

That’s why we’re making it easier to find and apply for opportunities, taking the application process from weeks to days.

We’re only going to see more cooperation in the coming years. With that, there will be increasingly more funding going towards companies in defense, energy, biotech, quantum, etc. Candor lets you unlock that funding potential.

name: Cardamon

Cardamon is an AI powered platform that ingests relevant regulation, understands what applies to each regulated financial firm, and gets compliance officers from regulation, to obligations, to product requirements in minutes - not weeks.

Financial firms face a host of complex regulations that make it incredibly painful to launch and maintain products in a compliant way. As a Product team at Revolut, we felt this pain deeply ourselves - we had products ready to launch but stuck in compliance limbo, often for weeks. Turns out, getting compliant took as long as building the product itself. 

Frustrated, we dug in and were shocked by how manual and inefficient the processes were. That’s when it clicked: there’s a huge opportunity to automate the boring stuff (and solve our own problem!). Compliance teams win because they ditch the tedious tasks. Product teams win because they ship faster. Everyone’s happy.

name: Cenote
