long_description:
Cenote helps online D2C brands convert more shoppers through AI sales reps that can call and text.

Online stores rely on static websites, one-way email and SMS campaigns, and inside sales teams with limited availability. But many purchases are better suited to a conversation: shoppers have questions, need guidance, or simply are not excited to buy based on what's on the site alone.

Today, those shoppers are poorly served. Abandoned-checkout campaigns are generic, call centers close, and slow human follow-up allows high-intent leads to go cold. Our customers often see conversion rates below 1% from traditional abandoned-checkout outreach.

Cenote's AI reps reach shoppers immediately, remember their context, and continue the conversation across channels and over time. This gives every interested shopper access to a personalized sales rep and helps brands recover revenue from leads they have already paid to acquire.

name: Certus AI
one_liner: Replacing the restaurant phone line with Voice AI
long_description:
Certus AI is replacing the restaurant phone line with Voice AI.

Restaurants lose up to $100,000 per year per location from missed calls, lost orders, and abandoned hold lines. Staff are overwhelmed. IVRs frustrate customers. Call centers are expensive and impersonal.

It’s 2025. Guests don’t leave voicemails or wait on hold. They just move on.

Certus is an AI voice agent built for restaurants. It answers every call, 24/7 — taking orders, processing deliveries, booking reservations, upselling, and handling complaints in English, Spanish, French and more. Certus is built to manage the phone line end to end, from the customer call to the restaurant tech stack, with zero human intervention required. It currently integrates with industry-leading systems like Toast, Square, Clover, UberEats, DoorDash, and more.

We’re building the voice layer of the modern restaurant — the employee they’ll never fire.

We started Certus because we lived the pain. Gurveer (CEO) grew up answering phones in his family’s restaurant and helped operate them, growing from 1 to 11 locations in 7 years. Later, he and Adam (CRO) ran a restaurant growth startup to help others increase revenue, but kept watching clients bleed cash because no one picked up the phone. So we built the solution the industry always wished existed.

Until now, this problem was considered unsolvable. But Voice AI has finally crossed the conversational chasm and 72% of consumers now prefer AI over humans as long as it means faster and better service.

More importantly, the market is begging for this. The North American restaurant industry crossed $1 trillion in 2024, and it's projected to hit $1.5 trillion in 2025. Yet over $100 billion is still lost annually to missed calls, human error, and outdated tech. As the market continues to grow, so do the losses!

Our customers say it best:

- “Certus changed my life overnight.”
- “We were losing the ability to give great in-house service — the phone was killing us.”
-  “70% of my business comes through the phone. That’s mine and my 16 staffs livelihood.”
- “Before Certus, I used to lose 40 - 60 calls a day…. now my printer just stays printing!”
-  “I’ve been in the business 38 years. I’ve been waiting for this since then.”

Certus is here to fix the $120B phone problem — one call at a time.

And in doing so, we’re redefining how the restaurant industry communicates forever, starting with the phone line.

name: Channel3
one_liner: Database of every product on the internet
long_description:
Channel3 is building a database of every product on the internet.

Google and OpenAI maintain vast product graphs, but keep that valuable data to themselves. Channel3 gives every developer access, opening a world of possibility for new shopping experiences across any vertical. For instance, developers could build AI fashion stylists or give their agents shopping capabilities.

We don’t just collect product data; we actually understand it. With the latest image classification and reasoning models, we can match products across merchants—even when listings and images differ—recognize variants, and surface the perfect matches for every search. As we grow, we’ll capture unique insights into what users want, click, and buy.

As AI models get smarter and cheaper, our flywheel accelerates: our catalog will improve, and it will be even easier for developers and vibe-coders to build on our infrastructure. To further incentivize building on Channel3, we provide built-in monetization; developers earn commissions on sales they drive.

Alex discovered this need while building an AI tutor that could recommend products and earn affiliate revenue. When no solution existed, he persuaded his smartest friend from Duke and former co-founder George to leave Palantir and build Channel3 together.

name: Clicks Health

name: Clidey
one_liner: Turn scattered data into one platform for decision-making
long_description:
WhoDB is an open-source platform for modeling organizations and running decisions on top of their data.

It lets teams define their core entities (customers, accounts, assets, workflows), the relationships between them, and the rules and objectives that govern how decisions should be made. WhoDB continuously ingests operational data and keeps this model up to date in real time.

Instead of building dashboards, writing ad-hoc queries, or maintaining scattered business logic, teams express decisions declaratively—what should happen, under what conditions, and with what constraints. WhoDB evaluates those decisions automatically as data changes and produces actions, recommendations, or state updates.

Everything is transparent and inspectable: data models, decision logic, and outcomes are fully auditable and can be extended in code.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers and mid-size operating businesses in manufacturing, retail, distribution and logistics
problem: Data and decision logic are scattered across systems; Clidey offers an open source database explorer and a data platform that models entities and runs decisions on live data.
business_model: Open source core (WhoDB) with commercial ERP and AI assistants; pricing not stated

outcome_analysis: Clidey grew out of the open source WhoDB database explorer, launched in mid 2024, and entered YC in Spring 2025 pitching a decision platform now sold as an ERP. There is no public funding or revenue data, and the product scope has widened considerably. Outcome unknown.

Code Four slashes the administrative burden on law enforcement through AI-driven automation. Officers spend up to a third of their shifts manually transcribing body camera footage, creating inaccuracies, reducing transparency, and cutting into frontline duties. We're here to eliminate these inefficiencies by integrating with body cameras, record management systems, and digital evidence management systems—acting as a software layer for data processing. 

We free the most overworked and underappreciated people in the world: police officers.

name: Codevisor

name: Codyco
one_liner: The AI Reservation Team for Hotel Groups
long_description:
€5,000 in additional bookings. In 4 weeks. For a 53-room hotel.

We help hotel groups turn missed calls into bookings.

This it how it works: 

- They send their missed calls to us.
- Our AI answers and takes the booking.
- The booking goes right into their PMS.

Even with call centers and central reservation departments they are still losing 5% of calls. 

That is a seven figure revenue leak. 

Why us? 
We used to build software that can’t fail for massive companies. We started Codyco after a friend told us how much money he was losing from missed calls. We built the first version just for him.

Now we give hotel groups the reliable AI they need, so they never lose a booking on the phone again.

name: Compyle
one_liner: The coding agent that actually collaborates with you
long_description:
Compyle is a less autonomous coding agent that asks before it acts. We're like Cursor or Claude Code - but you won't need to rewrite your codebase every time you use it for more than a small task.

We built Compyle because we were frustrated with the direction other coding agents are headed. They're all racing to be more autonomous, running for hours without human input.

This doesn't work for real production code. When agents run autonomously, they make countless small decisions that pile up in your codebase. Engineers lose ownership - they don't know what was implemented, can't effectively debug or maintain it, and struggle to build on top of it. The code becomes a black box, and they're forced to throw it away.

Compyle keeps engineers in the driver's seat.

product_category: AI coding agent, now AI for environmental due diligence

outcome_analysis: Compyle (Fall 2025, Active) launched a coding agent in October and November 2025 and by November 2026 its site describes only environmental due diligence automation, so the coding-agent wedge appears to have been dropped within about a year. The reason is not public; the crowded market against Cursor and Claude Code is a plausible but unsourced factor, so no failure factors are asserted.

name: Conntour
one_liner: Query mission-critical video
long_description:
Conntour enables government agencies to query their video - from security cameras, body cams, and drones.

Users can search past footage (“Find a man with tattoos on his left arm”), configure real-time alerts (“Notify me if someone climbs over the wall”), and extract data (“How many pickup trucks entered yesterday?”).

Unlike traditional video analytics solutions, which are limited to fixed parameters (like a weapon, bag, or car color), Conntour supports an unlimited range of highly specific scenarios described in plain language. This enables a single human to monitor thousands of cameras, or find a specific moment in minutes instead of days.

What makes Conntour's technology unique is its ability to process video using natural language at scale, fully on-premises, with minimal hardware requirements. The system is deployed with mission-critical teams at leading intelligence and homeland security agencies.

Conntour is backed by top-tier investors including General Catalyst and Y Combinator, was selected for the first-ever Palantir Fellowship, and has the former CTO of the CIA on its advisory board.
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Government, defense, homeland security and corporate security teams with camera, body cam and drone footage
problem: Security teams cannot search large volumes of video without predefined rules; Conntour lets them query it in natural language, on premises.
business_model: Enterprise and government software, deployed on premises, pricing not stated
product_category: Video intelligence and natural language video search
market_need_then: Existing video analytics required predefined rules; defense and homeland security buyers had massive unsearched footage, and a paying Singapore government customer was claimed on the YC page.
outcome_analysis: Conntour is active with a team of 20 and emerged from stealth in March 2026 with a 7M seed led by General Catalyst. Founders come from Israeli military surveillance, matching their defense and government buyers, and one has a prior exit. The main risk is camera vendors such as Verkada bundling similar search.

name: ContextFort

ContextFort gives security teams visibility and controls for AI browser agents.
It’s a Chrome extension that:
Detects when an AI agent takes control of the browser
Records every action during the session (pages visited, clicks, text entry) 
Provides controls to prevent risky actions and cross-site data leakage

product_category: AI agent security and observability
market_need_then: Agentic browsers such as Comet showed indirect prompt injection flaws in August 2025, and the founder says enterprise adoption of browser agents is slow because of that risk.
outcome_analysis: ContextFort is an active two person Summer 2025 company that appears to have moved from construction drawing review to browser agent security and now to coding agent monitoring. No primary funding or traction data was found. The repeated product change suggests searching for fit, but the outcome is unknown.

name: Contrario
one_liner: AI hiring platform powered by expert recruiters
long_description:
Contrario is an AI recruiting and hiring platform on a mission to help companies build generational teams.

In the age of AI, the best teams are still built by the best people. Recruiting has become a zero-sum game where speed and quality decide who wins.

Contrario is a network of expert recruiters supercharged by vertical AI agents purpose-built for hiring. Teams at Wispr Flow, Listen Labs, Slash, and 200+ of the fastest-growing companies use Contrario to power their hiring.

In under six months, Contrario has crossed $6M in annualized revenue, paid out $1M+ to recruiters, and placed 150+ candidates — making it one of the fastest-growing AI recruiting platforms on the market.

Backed by Y Combinator, Nexus Venture Partners, Goodwater Capital, and Inventum Ventures, alongside angels including David Chen (ex-HRT), Abhijeet Dwivedi (OpenAI), Hank Couture (DoorDash), and Jerry Cain (Stanford CS). Built by Stanford dropouts. Headquartered in San Francisco.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Fast growing startups hiring across roles, paying placement fees

business_model: Recruiting marketplace with placement fees, pairing independent expert recruiters with AI agents
product_category: AI recruiting platform and recruiter marketplace
market_need_then: Company reports 200 plus customers and about 6M USD annualized revenue within six months, plus 1M USD paid to recruiters, which suggests real demand from startups for hiring help (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Contrario grew quickly after YC W25 by combining a vetted recruiter network with AI agents, reporting about 6M USD annualized revenue in under six months and then a 2.3M USD seed led by Nexus in May 2026. The traction is self reported and unit economics are unproven, and the Series A and 25M USD ARR goals are only company targets.

name: Convexia

An AI-maximalist pharma platform. We use agents to buy drugs, run clinical trials, and sell for a profit. 10x faster and 20x leaner than incumbents.

Sourcing Agent: Mines public/private databases and unstructured global data to surface overlooked preclinical candidates.

Commercial Agent: Analyzes FDA incentives, pricing dynamics, TAM, competitive landscape, and payer alignment.
Clinical Agent: Runs digital twin simulations, evaluates CRO/CMC risk, and builds trial plans to Phase 1.
PoS Agent: Evaluates the most critical factors that impact the likelihood of clinical trial success. 

Built by 2 Stanford CS students who have built 3 startups together before.

name: CopyCat AI
one_liner: AI for Commercial Insurance Agencies
long_description: CopyCat builds AI for commercial, personal & benefits insurance brokers. It turns carrier quotes and policy documents into branded proposals, quote comparisons, and coverage reviews, and helps teams check policies and review insurance contracts, flagging discrepancies and documenting findings with source references.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent commercial, personal and benefits insurance agencies and brokers
problem: Brokers manually rekey carrier quotes and policy PDFs into proposals, comparisons and ACORD forms, and check policies by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS for insurance agencies, pricing not verified
product_category: AI workspace for insurance brokers
market_need_then: Brokers face repetitive document work and AI document extraction became practical in 2024; the company claims 4000+ deals won and 7+ hours saved per broker weekly (self reported).
outcome_analysis: CopyCat is active as of November 2026 with a growing broker customer base claimed on its site and blog posts through October 2026. It has named investors but no verified amounts. Direction appears to have narrowed from generic automation to insurance brokers, a crowded space, so the outcome is still open.

name: Corsair
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Workflow Automation; Open Source; Personalization
one_liner: OpenRouter for Integrations
long_description:
Corsair connects your app to any other API. 

Use Corsair to build custom agents, dashboards, and workflows with hundreds of different integrations. 

Get started here: https://docs.corsair.dev/quick-start
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers building AI agents and apps that need many third party integrations
problem: Connecting agents to many third party APIs means maintaining each integration, auth and permissions.
business_model: Open source core (Apache-2.0 per aggregator) with hosted hub and pay-per-call pricing for some tools
product_category: Integration layer for AI agents
market_need_then: Demand for agent tool access grew with MCP in 2025; dated sources for the batch period were not found.
outcome_analysis: Corsair is an active Winter 2025 company with a two person team, backed by YC, with no verified raise. No shutdown or acquisition was found. It competes in a crowded integration tooling market with well funded vendors, so its outcome is undetermined and depends on open source adoption.

name: Cortex AI
one_liner: Large-scale real-world robot & human data for embodied AI
long_description:
Cortex AI builds the world’s most diverse and large-scale real-world workplace robot & egocentric dataset — where the physical world becomes the next training and evaluation set for embodied AI.

We power frontier labs developing robotics foundation models and general-purpose robots by providing the data they need:
1️⃣ Egocentric Data — real-workplace human video with hand/body pose, depth, and subtask labels.
2️⃣ Robot Data — trajectories collected from manipulators and humanoids in real industry settings.
3️⃣ Human-in-the-Loop Rollouts & Evals — real-world deployments with remote operators who recover robots when they fail, capturing data that feeds back into training and continuously improves models.

Additionally, through the Cortex Marketplace, workplaces get paid to host data-collection and evaluation sessions, while labs access the in-the-wild data that truly matters. This draws on Lucas’s previous experience as co-founder of Carousell, a C2C marketplace that scaled to a $1B+ valuation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Robotics labs, humanoid companies and foundation model teams buying training and evaluation data
problem: Embodied AI models lack large, diverse real workplace human and robot data.
business_model: Data sales plus a marketplace paying workplaces to host collection sessions, and human in the loop eval services
product_category: Robotics training data
market_need_then: Research in 2025 showed gains from human egocentric video for robot training, driving data demand; vendor sources.
outcome_analysis: Cortex AI is active with an experienced repeat founder from Carousell and reports of a seed of roughly 6M from aggregators. It publishes product posts through October 2026. The market for robot data has many entrants and a shutdown of a peer, Eidon AI, was noted, so the outcome is open.

name: Cotool
one_liner: Security operations optimized for agents.
long_description:
Cotool builds AI agents and the infrastructure around them to help security teams detect threats, investigate alerts, hunt for attacks, and respond.

Our agents work across a team's security tools and data. They investigate alerts, write and tune Python detections, and turn threat intelligence into hunts and new coverage. Teams can customize agents around their workflows, inspect the evidence, edit detection logic, and bring humans in when judgment or approval matters.

Underneath the agents, Cotool provides log storage and search built for their workloads, with access to data where it already lives. The goal is to give security teams more capacity to defend their companies as their environments and workloads grow.

Teams at Ramp, EliseAI, ClickHouse, Legora, and many more use Cotool.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Security teams at tech companies (customers include Ramp and EliseAI)
problem: Security teams face alert volume and limited capacity for triage, detection engineering and hunting.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform with agents plus log storage and search; pricing not verified
product_category: AI agents for security operations
founder_names: Max Pollard; Eddie Conk; Logan Carmody
market_need_then: Security teams face alert overload and talent shortages; early users reported time savings per the YC profile (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Cotool is founded by three Material Security alumni and raised a 7.4M seed led by a16z in March 2026, with Ramp and EliseAI named as users. It operates in a crowded AI SOC market, so its outcome depends on keeping agent quality ahead of well funded rivals.

name: Cranston AI
one_liner: AI Tax prep and accounting software for CPA firms
long_description:
Cranston is AI tax prep and bookkeeping for CPA firms.

Our tax agents prepare returns the way a strong staff accountant would: they read the source documents, work the return in your tax software, and hand your reviewer a return that holds up, with workpapers attached. Our bookkeeping agents keep client books current all year, so tax season starts from clean numbers instead of cleanup.

Prep and books are the start. We're building Cranston into the system a firm runs on: the place where prep, review, client requests, and the rest of the practice get done.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: CPA firms (solo to multi-office) paying per prepared return
problem: CPA firms face a labor shortage and heavy tax prep and bookkeeping workloads.
business_model: Usage based, 40 USD per prepared return for tax prep per website; planning and research by quote
product_category: AI tax prep and bookkeeping for CPA firms
market_need_then: CPA exam candidates fell from over 100,000 in 2016 to about 67,000 in 2024 per search summary of AICPA data, creating labor shortage.
outcome_analysis: Cranston is an active Fall 2025 company with a founder who ran a tax practice and a technical co-founder, and it sells per return to CPA firms. No shutdown or acquisition was found. The segment is crowded with well funded rivals, so the outcome is undetermined.

name: Crimson
one_liner: The AI Associate for Litigation Lawyers
long_description: Crimson is the case intelligence platform for complex litigation. We help litigators build a complete picture of each case – every argument, entity and event understood in context – and support them with analysis, drafting and case management across the lifecycle of the dispute.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Litigation and arbitration teams at law firms, from Magic Circle and Am Law firms to disputes boutiques
problem: Complex disputes involve thousands of documents, and general purpose AI tools lack the factual, procedural and strategic context of a case. Litigators need a case model with cited answers, chronologies and drafting.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to law firms
product_category: Legal AI, case intelligence for litigation
market_need_then: Law firms were adopting generative AI in 2024 and 2025 and litigation document review is a large billable pain point. Early customers included large firms such as A&O Shearman and Dentons per the company site logos.
outcome_analysis: Crimson is active and early. A former litigator and an AI engineer built a case model product for disputes lawyers, joined YC in Spring 2025, signed large firm customers and raised a $2.5M seed in May 2026 with a New York office. No shutdown or exit news exists, and the main risk is the crowded legal AI field.

name: Crunched
one_liner: Excel AI analyst for Power Users
long_description:
Crunched is the Excel AI analyst for power users - in consulting, investment banking, and private equity. It error-checks workbooks end-to-end, builds models from scratch, and handles grunt work like extracting and linking data from IMs to template models - all within Excel so teams can review and iterate as usual.

Agents struggle with tabular data - getting reliable, multi-step execution over thousands of interlinked formulas, sheets, and ranges is hard. Making Crunched good enough for people who live in Excel means knowing the pain points deeply.

Michael and Philip has 10,000+ hours in Excel across consulting and finance. Markus and Lars bring deep expertise in scaling AI and enterprise solutions.

We've had easy access to first customers and are already live with firms across six European countries - we now plan to expand into the US. With >1bn total Excel users, we focus on the top 2%, highest-value Excel users globally. 

We're solving one pain point at a time to create a product that doesn't just look good in a demo but actually works in production.

Excel is here to stay, but the way experts model is fundamentally changing - with Crunched.
regions: Norway; Europe
target_customer: Power Excel users at consulting, investment banking, private equity, advisory and audit firms
problem: Experts spend hours checking workbooks, building models and linking data from documents into templates, and general AI agents struggle with interlinked formulas, sheets and ranges.
business_model: B2B SaaS, access granted firm by firm
product_category: AI agents for Excel and PowerPoint, finance workflows
founder_names: Philip Borge; Lars Gjardar Musæus; Michael Sakowski; Markus Skagemo
competitors_at_founding: Microsoft Copilot Agent Mode in Excel; Shortcut
market_need_then: Excel has over a billion users and finance and consulting teams spend large time on model building and checking; the founders cite early access to customers in six European countries.
outcome_analysis: Crunched is active and early. Two ex-McKinsey finance founders and two Norwegian AI engineers joined YC in Fall 2025 and reportedly raised a 6M dollar seed led by First Round within months. The main threat is Microsoft and model labs shipping Excel agents, so it relies on firm specific depth and security credentials.

name: Cua
one_liner: Give every agent a cloud desktop
long_description: Give every agent a cloud desktop. Built for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and any computer-use agents.

product_category: Developer infrastructure, sandboxes for computer-use agents

Funding is not confirmed by a primary source and labs keep expanding computer-use offerings, so outcome is open.

name: Cuckoo Labs
one_liner: Real-time AI translator for global sales and marketing
long_description:
Cuckoo is a real-time AI translator for global sales, marketing, and support. Companies like Snowflake and PagerDuty use Cuckoo in Zoom and in-person meetings for even the most technical discussions.

Cuckoo instantly learns the technical details of your conversation from your keywords and documents and interprets into over 20 languages—customized for your specific industry and organization.
regions: South Korea; East Asia
target_customer: Global B2B sales, marketing and support teams, plus companies holding multilingual meetings and webinars
problem: Technical sales and customer conversations across languages need interpreters who know industry vocabulary, which is costly and hard to book; generic machine translation fumbles jargon.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for real-time AI interpretation
product_category: Real-time AI interpretation for meetings
market_need_then: Cross-border sales and distributed teams needed live interpretation, and human interpreters are expensive; the company cites customers such as Snowflake and PagerDuty on its site.
outcome_analysis: Cuckoo Labs is active with a two person team in Seoul. It joined YC in Winter 2025, launched publicly in March 2025, signed technical software customers and raised a 1.8M dollar seed in November 2025. The main risk is that Microsoft, Zoom and Google bundle interpretation, so its edge is terminology customization.

name: Cyberdesk
tags: Developer Tools; Robotic Process Automation; Workflow Automation; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Self learning computer use agent for developers
long_description:
Cyberdesk is the first self learning computer use agent for developers to automate desktop workflows. 

For example, one of our customers is building an AI agent for hospital patient intake, and they’re using us to automate an entire team of people manually clicking and typing into a desktop app to book appointments. 

We launched mid July, and our agent is already operating in production environments, creating appointments in electronic health record apps and processing files in legacy ERPs.

We’ve built the first computer use agent that memorizes tasks and repeats them quickly while still adapting to unexpected changes on the screen. A good analogy is to how humans use computers: once we get used to an app, we use it much faster, while still adapting to random popups and crashes. This new paradigm for computer use will be needed by every company automating human workflows on computers.

Mahmoud previously built robotic process automation solutions impacting 20K+ employees at a Fortune 100 company. He also built AI & ML solutions at Baylor College of Medicine Neuroscience & Texas Children's Hospital + co-published a paper at the Rice Networks Group. 

Alan is ex-NASA and previously dropped out to be the first founding engineer at a PearX startup. He is a second time founder, having previously built and scaled a consumer AI app to thousands of paying users.

Computer-use agents will automate the $6T dollars spent on enterprise knowledge work and Cyberdesk will be the platform to power this.

We’d love to talk with you!
https://cal.com/mahmoud-al-madi-klrs5s/30min
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and software companies in healthcare, finance and logistics who automate legacy Windows desktop apps for their own clients
problem: Legacy desktop software such as EHRs and ERPs has no good API, so teams use brittle scripts, legacy RPA tools or people clicking and typing.
business_model: Usage-based developer API and SDKs with a Windows driver
product_category: Computer use agent, desktop automation for developers
market_need_then: Healthcare and logistics firms rely on legacy Windows apps without APIs and the founders report a customer automating hospital patient intake in production; computer-use models matured in 2024 and 2025.
outcome_analysis: Cyberdesk is active with two founders in San Francisco. After a pivot from open source virtual desktops to a Windows legacy app agent, it joined YC in Summer 2025 and reports production use in healthcare. No funding is confirmed and labs and RPA vendors are moving into the same space, so the outcome is open.

name: Dalus
one_liner: AI-Powered Hardware System Design Software
long_description:
Dalus is an AI-powered systems engineering software to model/validate complex systems for aerospace/defense/robotics and other mission-critical industries. 

With Dalus, engineers can seamlessly trace requirements, perform analyses, and update information in real-time. This ensures that every team member stays aligned and informed, reducing inefficiencies and enabling faster iterations. 

With AI at our core, users can analyze hundreds of pages of existing engineering documentation and requirements to generate or retrieve information about the system model they are building in Dalus.

We started working together on Dalus in spring 2024 after Eliot quit his job at Aerojet Rocketdyne (L3Harris) where he worked as a test/systems engineer. He experienced first-hand how silos and poor communication reduced the productivity and efficiencies in the teams he worked at.

We love working with companies tackling complex engineering systems, whether they be startups just getting their feet wet or large organizations like Israel Aerospace Industries (Our design partner and biggest aerospace/defense company from Israel)

Read why we started Dalus: https://dalus.io/articles/why-dalus
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Systems engineering teams at aerospace, defense, robotics, energy and automotive companies, from startups to large organizations
problem: Engineering teams building complex hardware keep requirements, architecture, analysis and tests in silos and in heavy legacy MBSE tools, which slows iteration and hurts alignment.
business_model: B2B SaaS, cloud MBSE subscription
product_category: AI-native model-based systems engineering software (SysML v2)
competitors_at_founding: Cameo Systems Modeler (Dassault Systemes); Innoslate (SPEC Innovations)
market_need_then: Aerospace and defense programs were adopting model-based systems engineering and the founder lived the silo problem at Aerojet; a design partner named in company materials was Israel Aerospace Industries.
outcome_analysis: Dalus is active with a three person team in San Francisco. An ex Aerojet engineer and a serial hardware founder launched a cheaper cloud MBSE tool in early 2025, joined YC in Winter 2025 and report defense customers such as DefendTex. Funding is not confirmed, so the trajectory beyond early traction is unknown.

name: Dartboard
one_liner: AI-native remote operations center for hardware fleets
long_description: Dartboard is the modern remote operations center for hardware fleets. We pair expert operators with AI agents to identify, diagnose, and fix issues faster.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Originally owners and operators of grid-scale batteries; later hardware fleet operators; the current site targets field service technicians and the contractors who employ them
problem: Battery owners lose revenue to missed market opportunities and compliance gaps, and field service crews lose time and billable detail documenting jobs by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services; remote operators paired with AI agents (YC description), voice AI subscription (current website, pricing not seen)
product_category: AI analyst for electricity markets, then remote operations for hardware fleets, then voice AI for field technicians
market_need_then: Texas battery revenues were under pressure and operators wanted benchmarks and analysis; Modo reports that average ERCOT battery revenue in 2025 was 84 percent lower than 2023 highs.
outcome_analysis: Dartboard is active with a two person team. A data scientist with battery market experience started as Dartboard Energy, an AI analyst for battery revenue, joined YC in Winter 2025 and has since shifted its description twice, ending at voice AI for field technicians. Funding is unconfirmed and nothing indicates traction yet, so the outcome is open and pivot risk is notable.

name: Darwin Robotics
tags: Hard Tech; Machine Learning; Robotics; AI
one_liner: Robot technicians for AI infrastructure
long_description:
Darwin Robotics is building general-purpose robot technicians that assemble and maintain the machines civilization runs on.

We're starting with AI infrastructure, automating physical work across data center assembly, commissioning, and maintenance. Our robots learn complex tasks from human demonstrations and improve through real-world deployment.

Initial deployments targeted for early 2027.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data center builders, operators and infrastructure equipment manufacturers
problem: AI data centers need skilled technicians to assemble, commission and maintain equipment, and the physical labor is scarce and slow to scale.
business_model: Robots deployed as technicians for data center operators; pricing model not stated, initial deployments targeted for early 2027
product_category: General purpose robot technicians, robotics and AI infrastructure
market_need_then: AI data center buildout in 2025 created a shortage of skilled technicians and commissioning labor, and the founders pitch automating assembly, commissioning and maintenance.
outcome_analysis: Darwin Robotics is active and very early. Two brothers with Stanford AI research and a payments startup background joined YC in Fall 2025 and raised a 3.6M dollar pre-seed led by Link Ventures in November 2026, with deployments targeted for early 2027. Coverage notes no completed deployment yet, and later entrants such as Exclaim Robotics, which emerged from stealth in August 2026, show growing competition.

name: Datafruit
one_liner: The AI workspace for software implementations
long_description: Datafruit helps enterprise delivery teams understand their customers deeply and deliver more profitably. We build AI agents capture every conversation, structure scope from day one, and use past projects to make every engagement sharper.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: System integrators and enterprise services teams that run software implementation projects
problem: Implementation projects fail in the gaps between sales, discovery calls and delivery, because scope, decisions and assumptions are scattered across conversations and documents.
business_model: B2B SaaS, enterprise sales (pricing not public)
product_category: AI workspace for professional services and software implementation delivery
market_need_then: Implementation overruns are a known pain for services firms and vendors, and 2025 vendor coverage cites high failure rates of enterprise AI and software projects. No customer evidence for Datafruit itself was found.
outcome_analysis: Datafruit is an early stage S25 company that launched on Hacker News as an AI DevOps agent and now presents itself as an AI workspace for software implementation teams. Only a small pre-seed is reported by aggregators, no customers are named, and no exit has occurred, so there is not enough evidence to call a success or failure. The pivot between two enterprise AI products within months is the main thing to watch.

name: Dedalus Labs
tags: Developer Tools; DevOps; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Persistent computers for AI agents
long_description:
Dedalus Labs builds persistent compute for AI agents. Our flagship product, Dedalus Machines, gives agents isolated computers where they can run software, keep files and state, and do useful work over time.

We build across virtualization, distributed storage, networking, scheduling, and orchestration. Our goal is to make persistent compute dependable and straightforward to use through APIs and developer tools, so developers can build agents that work with real software and maintain a working environment across sessions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need tool access and persistent compute
problem: Building agents that use many models and tools, and giving them isolated computers that keep state across sessions, requires stitching together infrastructure.
business_model: Usage-based developer platform with free and Pro ($20 per month) tiers
product_category: AI agent infrastructure (MCP gateway, SDK, persistent VMs)
market_need_then: In 2025 the Model Context Protocol and agent tool use were spreading quickly, and developers needed hosted gateways and isolated compute for agents. Evidence of demand for Dedalus itself is the $11M seed and open source SDK adoption claims.
outcome_analysis: Dedalus Labs rode the 2025 surge in agents and MCP, launching on Hacker News in August 2025 and announcing an $11M seed in October 2025 co-led by Kindred and Saga, which is a fast raise for a two founder S25 company from Princeton with DeepMind and Voyage AI experience. Its focus later moved from a gateway to persistent machines, entering a crowded sandbox market, so the outcome is still open.

name: DeepAware AI (Robotics Center of Silicon Valley)
tags: Machine Learning; Robotics; Supply Chain; Data Engineering; AI
one_liner: Robots, parts & RL envs & evals - delivered in 48 hrs / pickup in SF.
long_description:
DeepAware (Robotics Center of Silicon Valley, https://roboticscenter.ai/) is the fastest way for enterprises and researchers to get robots and robotics parts in the US — 72-hour delivery or Bay Area pickup.

Beyond hardware, we help teams collect teleoperation data, build reinforcement learning environments, and deploy robots into production. Customers include AI labs, industrial operations, research teams, and event producers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: AI labs, university research teams, industrial operators and event producers that need robots, parts and robot data fast
problem: Teams building physical AI struggle to buy robots and parts quickly in the US and to collect teleoperation data and deploy robots.
business_model: Hardware resale plus services (data collection, deployment) and a data marketplace
product_category: Robotics hardware distribution and physical AI data services
market_need_then: Demand for humanoid and arm hardware and robot learning data rose with the 2025 physical AI wave; no company specific demand evidence beyond the site's claim of university customers.
outcome_analysis: DeepAware joined YC S25 with a data center energy product and now operates mainly as a robotics hardware and data seller under the Robotics Center of Silicon Valley name. Funding is unclear beyond an unverified roughly 500K total, there is no exit, and the business is active with open job listings, so the story is an early pivot into physical AI supply with no confirmed traction metrics.

name: Deeptrace
one_liner: AI agents for on-call
long_description:
At Deeptrace, we’re building AI agents that investigate and resolve production alerts end-to-end. Deeptrace cuts through the noise, pinpoints root causes instantly, and gives engineering teams back what they need most: the freedom to build instead of firefighting.

In production, we're already seeing a reduction in time spent triaging, investigating, and resolving alerts with some of the fastest growing companies in the world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams at startups and enterprises that carry on-call burden for production alerts
problem: Engineers lose time triaging and root-causing noisy production alerts across logs, traces, metrics and code.
business_model: B2B SaaS with Startup and Enterprise tiers and trials
product_category: AI SRE and incident investigation
market_need_then: On-call load and alert fatigue are long standing complaints; the YC launch and customer testimonials (Mintlify, Opendoor named on the company site) indicate early paid or trial use.
outcome_analysis: Deeptrace is a Fall 2025 company with founders from Tesla, SpaceX and Parafin who turned the 2025 agent wave into an AI SRE product with named startup customers and a $5M seed announced on its own site. The seed investors and the March 2026 date come from a directory. The wedge is crowded with Datadog, AWS and several startups, so durability depends on accuracy and integrations.

name: Delineate
one_liner: Agents for Accelerated Clinical Trial Design
long_description:
Delineate is building AI agents to design better clinical trials faster.

This is a $10B dollar market, where saving even 1 day along the process is equal to $1-5M in revenue potential.

We process existing clinical trial research into specialized datasets saving scientists months of effort.

Delineate is working with two of the largest pharmaceutical companies. With one of our customers, we are helping them get to the next phase of trials faster by creating the largest dataset on a drug class ever constructed.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Large pharmaceutical companies designing clinical trials
problem: Designing clinical trials requires scientists to spend months assembling evidence from prior trial research into usable datasets.
business_model: B2B enterprise data and AI agent services for pharma
product_category: AI agents for clinical trial design and quantitative evidence
market_need_then: Trial design delay is costly (the company claims one day saved is worth $1 to 5M); the company reports work with two large pharma customers, self reported.
outcome_analysis: Delineate, a Winter 2025 company with a pharma modeling CEO and a robotics CTO, sells agent built evidence datasets to large pharma and reports two big customers plus a team of 20 on YC, but no priced rounds or press confirm that traction. It is active with no exit, and the main risk is that larger clinical data vendors add agentic trial design, so the evidence supports only a cautious early stage view.

name: Den
one_liner: Make real life a video game
long_description: We are turning real life into a video game

problem: Launch pitch: make AI agents ten times easier to build for non-engineers. Current product: interactive AI stories where the reader plays the lead.
business_model: Free consumer app, monetization not stated
product_category: AI agent workspace, later consumer AI interactive story app

No funding, traction or outcome is public, so the record shows an early stage company with unclear direction.

name: Denki
one_liner: The full-stack AI financial audit firm
long_description:
Automate internal auditing (planning, testing, documenting) to comply better with financial regulations.

Denki performs audit work with 99% software, 1% services:

✔️ Works on existing systems (e.g. Auditboard, Workiva, ERPs)
✔️ Automates Control processes (e.g. collects evidence, runs walkthrough interviews, tests)
✔️ Records every step for traceability (workpapers w/ full audit trace)

Focused on SOX programs and financial regulations (SEC Rules etc.)
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Internal audit and SOX compliance teams at public companies, and their auditors
problem: Internal audit planning, control testing and workpaper documentation are manual and costly, and auditing talent is short.
business_model: Software-led audit service, described as 99 percent software and 1 percent services
product_category: AI financial audit and SOX compliance automation
founder_names: Felipe Jin Li; David Jin Li
market_need_then: The company cites large audit spend and a talent shortage, which are unverified company claims. Public company SOX compliance is mandatory, which sustains demand.
outcome_analysis: Denki, founded in 2025, raised a 4.1M seed in March 2026 co-led by Base10 and Shine Capital within months of the Fall 2025 batch. Founders with McKinsey and financial data pipeline experience fit the problem. Competing AI SOX startups raised similar money in the same period, so execution speed will decide the outcome.

name: Design Arena
one_liner: World's largest crowdsourced benchmark for AI-generated design
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs that buy human preference data and evaluations, plus consumers who use the free arena
problem: AI model benchmarks do not capture taste or aesthetics in generated designs, and labs need human judgments of visual quality.

Social networks are dead. Social media became more media than social. My friends aren't on social media anymore - it's one third ads, one third content from strangers, and one third AI slop. name: DiligenceSquared
one_liner: AI-powered market due diligence for investment decisions
long_description:
DiligenceSquared delivers AI-powered market due diligence for investment decisions - like the $500k McKinsey reports, but automated, auditable, and at a fraction of the cost.

When Private Equity funds evaluate deals, they pay firms like McKinsey, BCG, and Bain $500K-$1M for market due diligence. The process takes weeks, and the output is a static PowerPoint that's impossible to audit. A single large-cap PE fund can spend >$30M annually on this and the total market is $10B per year.

Our AI agents conduct expert interviews and synthesize insights with every claim linked to source transcripts. No black box, no "trust me" slides, and no 10x mark-up for human labor.

Frederik bought these reports as a Principal at Blackstone. Soren sold them as a Principal at BCG. Harshil is a repeat founder and former Software Engineer at Google. We've seen both sides and know what matters in due diligence - and now we automate it.

Our clients already include 8 leading private equity funds with over $2.4 trillion in combined AUM.

name: Duranium
one_liner: Reshoring critical metal production
long_description:
China and Russia control the world’s critical minerals. We can produce Titanium, Magnesium, Aluminum, Zirconium & Hafnium in the U.S. more profitably than any existing process, and carbon neutrally via co-production.

Carbochlorination is the primary process for producing critical metals like titanium, hafnium, and zirconium, and was once the standard for magnesium. The problem: conventional carbochlorination relies on purchasing carbon feedstocks, wastes valuable byproducts, and is highly CO₂-intensive.

Duranium changes this with a novel reactor that recycles CO₂ emissions back into feedstock (CO) while generating a valuable co-product (bleaching agents). This closed loop slashes emissions and delivers Chinese-level metal pricing without subsidies — unlocking the full potential of carbochlorination for U.S. critical mineral production.

outcome_analysis: Duranium is a Summer 2025 hardware heavy startup claiming a 15 tonne per year magnesium pilot in Oakland with titanium, hafnium and zirconium targeted for 2027 and 2028. Tailwinds are the collapse of US Magnesium and reshoring policy; risks are capital needs and Chinese pricing. Our vision is to transform education by facilitating AI’s safe and effective integration across all institutions and applications. Not using AI to replace teachers but rather to empower them—providing them with all the time and resources they need to develop their students.

name: Elip AI

Elip sends you the jobs a friend would send you, and gives a company the shortlist a friend would write.

For people: add your resume and say what you want and what you'd never take. Each morning Elip reads millions of jobs from across the internet with that in mind. It sets aside what you said no to and sends the few that fit, each with why and what's missing. Some mornings, none. When one is right, Elip rewrites your resume for that role and you approve every change. Free.

For companies: tell Elip the role. Within minutes you get a short list of people who fit, each with the reason. You meet once they say yes, and pay 10% of first-year base salary only when you hire. Nobody can pay to appear on a shortlist.

Where Elip is going: a world where nobody has to start from zero with a stranger.

Elip is based in San Francisco.

Our vision is to build a personal workspace where you own your data, choose your own AI models, and replace siloed apps with open, interoperable alternatives. All while preserving authenticity and being free and open source. ❤️

Ergo is backed by Y Combinator and FundersClub, and trusted by sales teams at Pylon, Rho, Retell AI, Warp, Oneleet, and Whop.

name: Excellence Learning

Excellence an after-school maths and science program. We replace/supplement private tutoring and long-term study programs such as Kumon (over 30B TAM). US Parents are our primary customers. 

Our web and iPad software serves both ambitious and struggling students. As we believe each student is unique, we adapt our high quality courses and exercises to their knowledge and learning style in a very granular way. To facilitate learning, they get detailed text, voice and graphical explanations, can craft study plans, revise and memorize, and received human mentorship if needed. We believe LLMs have made edtech interesting, as technology now allows us to replicate a tutoring learning experience.

In addition, we offer a program with daily courses and exercises, detailed feedback on their worksheets and more (super Kumon).

Finally we sell the AI tutoring and exercise databases to schools in a B2B and B2B2C model and already work for the most prestigious institutions in France (Ecole polytechnique, college Stanislas...).

We're a passionate team of ex-quants, mathematicians and physics champions devoted to improving science education.

name: Exin Therapeutics
one_liner: Agentic platform for predictive neuro drug discovery + data foundry.
long_description:
We are developing therapies for disorders driven by dysfunctional neural circuits. To develop these therapies, we are building an agentic discovery platform that learns from experiments in our own in vivo lab.

Our agents use CircuitATLAS to connect disease phenotypes with the neural circuits, cell types and molecular mechanisms, identify therapeutic targets and design experiments to test them. Our cross-species models learn from large-scale neural activity data to identify conserved circuit states and help predict how an intervention’s effects may translate from preclinical models to humans.

At our Data Foundry in Manila, our team of RAs test these hypotheses in vitro and in vivo. The results refine our models and guide the next set of experiments. This lab-in-the-loop approach allows our agents to develop and test ideas against experimental evidence throughout discovery.

We are starting with epilepsy, with the goal of developing first-in-class therapies across a full spectrum of disorders driven by dysfunctional brain activity.

Publications:

- CircuitATLAS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09643). Target discovery platform which combines mechanistic reasoning with an in vivo lab-in-the-loop. AI agents identify therapeutic targets and design experiments that our research teams execute in the lab. The resulting biological data feeds back into the discovery process to iteratively refine hypotheses and validate new interventions.

- Cross species representation learning (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11222). Aligning mouse and human neural activity to predict clinical drug efficacy from preclinical data.

product_category: AI drug discovery, neurotherapeutics

It establishes a live baseline of normal behavior, so when something silently regresses, it catches the deviation immediately, pins it to the exact commit that caused it, and opens a fix PR. name: F2
one_liner: The AI platform for private markets investors
long_description:
F2 is the AI platform for private markets investors. Purpose-built for private credit, private equity, and commercial banking, F2 accelerates diligence, underwriting, and portfolio monitoring, helping teams evaluate deals over 60% faster. 

F2 turns unstructured deal data into investment-grade analysis and polished memos in minutes. Unlike general-purpose AI, F2 is built with the domain expertise and depth to handle the most complex financial analysis. Already trusted across thousands of deals, F2 makes collaboration easy and retains historical context, so past work compounds into future wins. 

Headquartered in New York City, F2 is backed by leading investors including NFX, Left Lane Capital, and Y Combinator.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Private credit funds, private equity firms and commercial banks
problem: Deal diligence, underwriting and portfolio monitoring rely on manual work over unstructured documents.
business_model: B2B enterprise software (pricing not found)
product_category: AI platform for private markets underwriting

It benefited from Arc's lender relationships and the founder's finance background, and shows named lender customers. The category has well funded rivals, so outcomes depend on enterprise adoption.

name: F4 Industries
one_liner: The GD&T Analysis Platform for Engineering Drawings
long_description:
GD&T takes years to master. Engineers must encode their design intent into a dense syntax that manufacturers must decode, and not everyone gets it right. 

Put ten engineers in front of the same drawing and you may get ten different interpretations. Which means errors often surface later in interface stack-ups, manufacturing, or in the field - when they’re far more expensive to fix.

That’s why we built F4 - the platform that analyzes GD&T to determine whether your designs are ready for production.

Drop in your drawing and 3D file. F4 analyzes every element of your GD&T to assess whether your design is clear, manufacturable, and production ready. To make the drawing easier to understand, engineers can visualize their datums, reference frames, and tolerance zones directly on the 3D model. F4 also calculates tolerance stack-ups instantly - directly from the drawing. What once took hours of manual work now takes seconds.

When issues are found, F4 flags them and guides engineers toward resolving the problem.

After analyzing your drawing, F4 also automatically generates design and inspection reports - stack-up tables, FAI reports - ready to share with your team.

And it does all of this locally on-device with no AI used for analysis. Producing deterministic results engineers can trust.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering, manufacturing and quality teams, including aerospace and defense, that review drawings
problem: GD&T callouts are interpreted inconsistently, so errors surface late in stack-ups, manufacturing or the field.
business_model: Software licences (F4 Review, Pro, Enterprise tiers); prices not listed
product_category: Engineering drawing GD&T analysis software
market_need_then: Founders cite late-found GD&T errors as costly; comparison pages show demand for drawing checking tools, though dated early evidence was not found.
outcome_analysis: F4 is an active YC Summer 2025 company with two founders from Tesla and SpaceX selling a deterministic GD&T analysis platform. No funding round, customer or outcome is documented beyond aggregator figures. Its no-AI positioning is a distinct angle versus AI drawing review tools, but adoption and sales traction are unknown.

name: Fernstone
one_liner: AI-native insurance brokerage.

name: Feyn
one_liner: Custom models trained on your data
long_description:
Feyn is an end-to-end service for building custom models from your data. Our models learn how your product actually works, handle the rare cases that are costly to get wrong, and grow sharper the longer they run.

Our engineers start by reviewing your current setup and agreeing on what quality means for your workflow. Then we train a model on your data. Once it ships, new cases feed back into training so the model keeps improving. 

The result is a model that runs faster, improves with use, and is yours to own.

name: Fifth Door

long_description: Fifth Door unlocks the power of imagination by making it easy for everyone to create, share, and play games anywhere, with anyone. We exist to stimulate the creativity, connection, and joy that people get when they play games.

name: Finbar
one_liner: Financial intelligence for every investor
long_description:
Finbar is high-quality financial data and intelligence, used by several of the world's largest hedge funds. It automates financial modelling, research, and data analysis so multi-million-dollar decisions can be made 100x faster.

Our services include: company primers and prebuilt models; AI tools for analysts to create their own research; Excel tools to build financial models in minutes and update them in seconds; API streams to integrate our worldwide data into any programmatic or agentic system.

outcome_analysis: Finbar is an active London company with hedge fund customers claimed on its own site and no exit. name: Finto
one_liner: AI accounting for enterprise finance teams
long_description: Finto builds AI accounting software for enterprise finance teams. We automate the invoice-to-pay process from their email inbox to their ERP. Cutting out 80% of the accountants daily work in invoice recording, account coding and  invoice approvals.

name: Flai
one_liner: We Bring Customers to Your Dealership
long_description:
The problem we solve: 56% of dealership leads arrive after business hours, and most dealers lose these potential customers to competitors who happen to be available 24/7. Missing after-hours calls alone costs the average dealership $1M annually in lost revenue.

We built Flai to fix this - AI assistants that answer dealership calls 24/7, scheduling test drives, oil changes, or running outbound recall campaigns so no opportunity slips away.

The result: No more missed opportunities, no more losing customers to competitors.

Our founding team has built voice AI products at HappyRobot, scaled infrastructure at Uber for millions of users, and applied data science at Netflix to solve operational challenges.

We're not just answering phones, we're helping dealerships win in an AI-first world where availability determine who gets the sale.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

outcome_analysis: Flai raised a seed after YC and a $27M Series A in October 2026, reporting about 20x revenue growth and 50,000 monthly appointments, which are company claims. It entered a field with Numa and Toma but won dealer groups and dealer investors. The founders previously worked at HappyRobot, a voice AI company.

name: Fleetline
tags: Logistics; Supply Chain; Data Science; AI
one_liner: Optimizing fleet planning with data driven algorithms
long_description: Fleetline is building the first complete-context algorithmic load planner for mid to large-sized trucking fleets. Today’s dispatchers face an overwhelming task: balancing regulations, customer demands, live fleet data, and individual driver needs, all while coordinating across siloed tools and teams. Mistakes run rampant, and each mistake is thousands of dollars. Even the select fleets using algorithms that have fleet-wide context struggle: the outputs are rigid, hard to interpret, and are blind to real-world nuances like driver preferences and schedule exceptions. Fleetline solves this by combining advanced optimization with LLMs that can easily adapt algorithms to each fleet’s needs and capture driver-specific information. The result is smarter planning truly optimized for every fleet and its drivers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mid to large trucking fleets whose dispatchers plan loads
problem: Dispatchers balance regulations, customer demands, live fleet data and driver preferences across siloed tools, and each planning mistake costs thousands of dollars; existing algorithmic planners are rigid and hard to interpret.

name: Flick
one_liner: We Handle AI. You Direct Films.
long_description:
Flick is an AI filmmaking software that lets people create Hollywood-level short films completely using AI end-to-end.

There are many AI tools that can give you 8-second casual clips to post on social media, but when it comes to creating truly high-quality films with coherent storylines, consistent characters, and cinematic aesthetics, they don’t come close due to their lack of flexibility, creative control, and fragmented creative flow.

Founded by an award-winning filmmaker and a founding engineer at Instagram, Flick defines an interface specifically designed for native AI filmmaking that feels natural and enables end-to-end creative flows. Think of Flick as Figma for AI filmmaking.

There are 4 complete AI short films created using Flick that got 20+ awards in international film festivals already and our early creator residency community are generating several AI short films every week.

We are also building a community where we produce our own AI films as well as collaborating with other well-known filmmakers to share their “behind-the-scenes” workflows as resuable templates to inspire users in our community. We not only build product, we also build world-class content.

The whole film industry will be revolutionized by AI and our goal is to be “the product” that defines this category.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote

problem: AI video tools give little director control; Flick offers a node canvas for scripts, scenes, characters and edits, plus a distribution platform, Flick TV.
business_model: Subscription software plans plus a content platform
product_category: AI filmmaking software

outcome_analysis: Flick raised a $6M seed in May 2026 from True Ventures, GV and others after YC. It combines an Instagram engineer with an award-winning AI filmmaker and builds community through residencies, a festival and Flick TV. Competition from larger AI video tools is the main risk. No exit.

name: Floot
one_liner: The app platform inside Claude and ChatGPT.
long_description:
Floot is the layer where vibecoded software runs.

SaaS is dead. Hundreds of millions of people already spend their day in Claude or ChatGPT - and increasingly, when they need an app, they won't buy one. They'll describe it, and it will exist.

We're building the infrastructure that makes that real. When Claude creates an app, it needs somewhere for that app to live: a backend, a database, hosting, a domain, the ability to scale, various services, maybe even to be able to work as a mobile app. Floot is that place - a full stack purpose-built for AI to operate, from a specialized framework that defines how AI writes and runs code, down to scalable hosting on AWS.

This means you can now build and ship real apps directly inside Claude and ChatGPT. Connect Floot, and the model you already pay for writes and debugs the code, shows a live preview, and publishes to your own domain. No need to wire up git, vercel, supabase and a dozen other providers. And no AI credits - every message runs on the subscription you already have, because we charge for the platform, not for a token markup.

We built Floot this way because we've watched the model layer commoditize - every serious builder writes good code now, including us. The lasting value isn't another agent between you and the model. It's the layer underneath, from wherever people already are. We're building Floot to be the home for all operation software, for the decades where most new software on earth is written by AI.

✨ Try it: floot.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Non-developers and builders who use Claude or ChatGPT to make apps
problem: AI-built apps need backend, database, hosting and publishing; Floot provides that infrastructure so the user's own AI subscription builds the app.
business_model: Flat platform plans for infrastructure, with optional credits for its own agent and image generation
product_category: App platform for AI assistants
market_need_then: Vibe coding demand rose sharply in 2025, with builders needing hosting and backend; Floot-specific demand not independently documented.
outcome_analysis: Floot is a one-founder company in the crowded AI app builder market that repositioned as the app platform inside Claude and ChatGPT, launching an MCP connector around September 2026. No verified funding, revenue or exit is public, so its outcome is unknown.

Flott’s AI agents act as an extension of fleet managers — automating repetitive tasks and optimizing workflows.This lets companies focus on what truly matters: growing the business.

name: Frekil

name: Freya

name: Frizzle

Frizzle uses AI to grade handwritten math assignments for teachers and transform them into rich analytics and differentiated assessment to help personalize instruction for every student. Teachers spend over 10 hours a week or 25% of all their work grading - Frizzle does it in minutes. Frizzle is the most valuable piece of software for teachers ever, as it eliminates the most time-consuming part of their workflow so they can focus on teaching.

Frizzle shifts education from waterfall to agile learning. Instead of waiting for end-of-unit tests to discover gaps, teachers get continuous, real-time insight into student thinking from everyday work. Feedback becomes immediate, instruction adapts weekly, and learning iterates (measure, adjust, improve) so every student progresses faster with less teacher burnout.

Frizzle was named an official White House AI Education Partner alongside OpenAI and Meta: https://www.whitehouse.gov/edai/.

Frizzle was co-founded by Abhay Gupta and Shyam Sai, who met in high school over 10 years ago.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: K-12 teachers (free individual tier) and school districts (enrollment-priced plans)

product_category: AI grading and assessment analytics for K-12

outcome_analysis: Frizzle is a two person Summer 2025 company that grades handwritten work for free to teachers and sells to districts. It is Active with named districts on its site and a claimed White House AI education partnership, but no verified funding beyond aggregator listings and no exit. The free teacher tier is a bottom up distribution wedge, while defensibility depends on district integrations since model access is commoditized.

With powerful integrations and intelligent workflows, FuseAI doesn’t just help you run campaigns. It turns every signal into pipeline, and every rep into a top performer.

name: GETASAP

long_description:
Founded in 2023, GETASAP is a San Francisco–based technology and supply chain infrastructure company transforming fresh produce distribution and freight.

GETASAP Fresh provides same-day delivery to thousands of restaurants and retail locations across the USA, sourcing directly from farms internationally and operating global cold-chain infrastructure. It also operates an AI-native freight carrier and brokerage, delivering reliable reefer LTL and FTL services powered by VoiceAI dispatch, optimized scheduling, and real-time operational intelligence.

name: Gale

We've simplified the visa application process, streamlined compliance, and can integrate with HR systems - saving teams time, money and headaches. Through automation, we enable the independent attorneys we coordinate with to maintain quality whilst being more efficient.

name: Galen AI
one_liner: Personal AI healthcare agent, powered by clinical and wearable data.
long_description:
Galen is an AI-powered personal healthcare companion. We enable patients to securely connect their medical records from over 800 healthcare institutions across more than 12,000 locations in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada. We also connect with over 20 popular wearable devices including Apple Watch, Fitbit, and Dexcom, bringing all your medical records and health data into one unified space. 

We founded Galen because for over four years, Viraj struggled to navigate several conditions related to chronic low back pain. He often found himself waiting weeks for responses from his care team, received little guidance or education about new diagnoses, and was overwhelmed trying to manage overlapping conditions and medications.

His experiences are not unique. Our healthcare system is overloaded and fragmented, and often, patients are left to navigate their care on their own. Everyday there are nearly 1 billion health-related Google searches, but the responses to such queries are generic and impersonalized, because the searches lack any insight into a users personal health background.

By leveraging your own data and state-of-the art LLM memory capabilities, Galen delivers personalized insights, proactive health recommendations, and 24/7 on-demand medical support — empowering patients to be an active part of their health team. We are a consumer app in beta testing and will be available on the App Store soon!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers managing chronic conditions who want their records and wearable data in one assistant
problem: Patients wait weeks for care team replies and face fragmented records; generic health searches ignore their own history.
business_model: Consumer app (beta) with no stated pricing
product_category: Consumer AI health companion
market_need_then: The company cited about 1 billion health related Google searches daily with impersonal answers, and the founder's own multi year struggle with chronic back pain.
outcome_analysis: Galen AI joined YC in Spring 2025 with two Stanford founders and a beta health companion linking medical and wearable data. Oura announced on April 17, 2026 that it acquired the technology and the team, following its purchases of Doublepoint and Veri; terms are undisclosed and the app's future is not stated. With a small round and a crowding field after ChatGPT Health, this reads as a talent and technology acquisition.

name: Gentle Health
tags: Telehealth; Social Media; Marketing; Advertising; AI
one_liner: The healthcare you want without the hassle
long_description:
Gentle Health is a patient-first telehealth clinic founded on four values:

Upfront, Competitive Pricing: We spend nothing on traditional marketing, work closely with pharmacy partners, and maintain highly efficient operations to keep prices among the lowest on the market. Our price is a single monthly subscription fee, with no hidden fees, surprises, or add-ons.

Frictionless Experience: Our onboarding process is fast, painless, and easy – most patients have their initial appointment booked for the next business day. Our HIPPA-compliant patient portal makes getting refills and talking to their care team fast and secure, with doctor replies typically within the hour. Prescriptions arrive in mere days via overnight shipping straight to their doorstep.

Patient Autonomy: We work closely with patients to make sure they’re armed with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions about their health. We’re clear about what we provide so they can decide what best fits them.

Trust: We offer only evidence-backed medicine, offered by a real MD. We make it clear to patients what these drugs can and cannot do, where the research is, and prioritize treatments and lifestyle advice supported by the latest data.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US adults seeking GLP-1 weight management, cash pay
problem: GLP-1 care is costly and opaque. Gentle Health offers a doctor reviewed online service with transparent pricing and pharmacy shipping.
business_model: Cash-pay subscription: compounded drugs from 135 USD per month or a 28 USD per month care fee for brand-name drugs bought direct (October 2026 listing)
product_category: Telehealth GLP-1 weight management
market_need_then: GLP-1 demand was high and cash-pay telehealth boomed in 2025, but branded pricing converged at 499 USD in April 2025 and regulatory pressure on compounding followed.
outcome_analysis: Gentle Health is a four person Fall 2025 company in the most crowded and regulation exposed corner of telehealth. It lists transparent cash prices and a doctor led model, but no funding, customer counts or news were found. FDA action on compounded GLP-1 marketing in 2026 is a risk to the compounded side. The outcome is too early to call.

name: GhostEye
one_liner: Your always-on red team.
long_description: We emulate the attacks real adversaries run today: help-desk vishing, deepfaked executives, MFA fatigue, and the payloads that follow. We run them against your people and the controls around them to reveal what is actually exploitable, not what looks compliant. Then we close the gap, retest until the fix holds, and give your leadership the evidence that risk actually went down. From initial access to remediation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

business_model: B2B security SaaS and managed testing; a first campaign is offered at no cost
product_category: AI social engineering and breach and attack simulation
market_need_then: Search results from vendor and trade pages describe rising AI-driven vishing and deepfake attacks and many security awareness vendors adding simulation, which indicates demand. No dated spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: GhostEye is an active Summer 2025 company with a single listed founder who led red teams at BlackRock and worked on offensive operations at MITRE, which fits the product. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. Funding is not verified beyond an aggregator figure, so the outcome so far is unknown and the company is early.

name: Goldbridge

long_description:
Goldbridge is building the financial operating system for the largest asset class in the world – real estate. More than $1T in rent flows through landlord bank accounts annually, with roughly a quarter locked in idle reserves and security deposits – and billions more leaking from unnecessary property expenses. And with $2.5T in real estate loans about to mature in 2027/28, property owners are desperate to boost their income ASAP. 

Goldbridge solves this problem by creating the first AI-powered banking platform for real estate owners. We are backed by Y Combinator and other world-class investors, and our founding team includes a 2x YC founder, former White House advisor, and 100-unit real estate owner/operator with deep industry expertise. Come help us redefine the future of real estate.

product_category: Banking and finance software for real estate owners
market_need_then: The launch post cites over $1T in annual rent flowing through landlord accounts and $2.5T of real estate loans maturing in 2027 and 2028, framing owners as eager to raise income. These are company claims.

A spotlight article says it had one pilot customer by June 2026. Competitors in landlord banking already existed. No exit or failure has occurred, and funding is unverified.
