name: Golpo
tags: Education; eLearning; Video; Sales Enablement; Marketing
one_liner: Create Whiteboard Explainer Videos with AI from a Prompt or Document
long_description:
Golpo AI is the world's best platform to create fully produced whiteboard explainer videos from just a prompt or document. Instead of hiring an agency, you simply input a prompt or document explaining what you want, and in minutes you get a whiteboard explainer video in a style similar to Khan Academy or RSA Animate. After creation, you have the ability to edit all aspects of the video with just prompts. 

It's perfect for training, faceless YouTube, marketing, technical, and educational videos — any video where understanding is important. Trusted by over 170,000 users as of July '26, Golpo features include but are not limited to: 

1) Convert your narration into an explainer video (with your narration as audio and the video time aligned) 
2) Input your document or prompt. Document can be of virtually any format or type (text, audio, video etc.) 
3) Script-to-video with matching audio
4) Videos up to 10 minutes
5) 50+ languages
6) dead-simple editing after generation
7) Insert your own videos and images into the generation, used as-is without alteration.
8) 10+ visuals styles, including pen in hand, voice cloning, vertical video, custom branding and more! API access available.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Educators, corporate training and marketing teams, and creators who need narrated whiteboard explainer videos from documents or prompts
problem: Explainer videos are costly and slow to produce; general video models make short cinematic clips that struggle with technical accuracy. Golpo generates narrated, animated whiteboard videos from a prompt or document.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with credit tiers (Creator $99.99/month per HN thread) plus enterprise API
product_category: Generative AI video (explainer)
competitors_at_founding: Google Veo; Google NotebookLM; OpenAI Sora
market_need_then: Press cites school districts, corporate training, sales decks and internal comms using it; no figures. Launch HN had 116 points and 46 comments.
outcome_analysis: Golpo, founded by two Stanford-dropout brothers, launched on HN in August 2025 and announced an oversubscribed $4.1M seed led by BNVT Capital in October 2025, with Golpo 2.0 in February 2026. It rides the generative-video wave and targets a niche that cinematic models serve poorly, but Google ships adjacent features and no revenue or retention is public, so it is too early to call.

name: Goodshelf
tags: Marketplace; E-commerce; Retail Tech; Retail; AI
one_liner: The online retailer for AI shopping agents
long_description:
Goodshelf is an AI-native online retailer built to help people and AI shopping agents discover, understand, recommend, and buy the right products.

Goodshelf sells curated products across electronics, home goods, travel, beauty, furniture, everyday essentials, and more. Unlike traditional online marketplaces, Goodshelf prioritizes product quality, transparent comparisons, and evidence-backed recommendations over sponsored rankings and advertising.

Goodshelf brings together products from brands and suppliers, combining detailed product specifications, real-world use cases, independent reviews, testing insights, and evidence-based comparisons. We make pricing, availability, product strengths, limitations, and tradeoffs clear upfront, giving AI agents and consumers the information they need to evaluate alternatives and choose the products that best fit their needs.

Goodshelf is built for both human shoppers and AI agents like ChatGPT, Gemini, Muse, and Instinct. Our structured product catalog, machine-readable product pages, and agent-compatible shopping tools make it easier for AI assistants to research products, compare alternatives, and help customers complete purchases.

Our mission is to help AI agents find the right product for every consumer, while giving brands and suppliers a new distribution channel as shopping shifts toward AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Online shoppers and AI shopping agents buying curated products
problem: Online product search is cluttered by sponsored rankings. Goodshelf sells curated products with machine-readable pages and transparent comparisons.
business_model: Ecommerce retail: buys from brands and suppliers and sells at listed price, margin is the revenue (per its site)
product_category: AI-native online retailer
market_need_then: The pitch rests on AI shopping agents becoming buyers. No dated evidence of demand was found in the sources opened.
outcome_analysis: Goodshelf is an active Winter 2025 solo-founder retailer with 115 products from 60 brands listed on its site. Its founder has a data engineering background at Scale AI and AWS. No funding, press, shutdown or exit information was found, so the outcome is unknown and the story is too thin to assign factors.

name: GroundControl

long_description:
GroundControl builds mission-critical software for manufacturers in highly-regulated industries (aerospace, defense, medical)

Our core product automates lengthy, complex, and regulated quality documentation in aerospace manufacturing.

As an example, the Boeing 777 is made up of over 3 million parts sourced from manufacturers around the world. These manufacturers must complete quality documentation for every part on this aircraft (machined parts, printed circuit boards, wire harnesses, assemblies, and more).

GroundControl helps manufacturers complete this required documentation accurately, in minutes instead of days.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Quality teams at aerospace, defense and medical manufacturers and their suppliers (customer logos on its site include Protolabs, Sanmina, Precision Castparts and Boom Supersonic)
problem: First Article Inspection Reports under AS9102 are slow manual paperwork. GroundControl extracts characteristics from drawings and automates the reports, supplier submissions and purchase order review.
business_model: B2B SaaS for quality teams; pricing not found
product_category: Quality software for regulated manufacturing (AS9102 FAIR automation)

market_need_then: AS9102 reports are required in aerospace supply chains and the company reports 70+ facilities as customers and nearly 1,000 reports per month on its YC page, which shows demand. Spend figures were not found.
outcome_analysis: GroundControl is an active Spring 2025 company whose founders came from a PCB manufacturer and from InspectAR, which Cadence acquired, giving real domain access. Its site claims hundreds of quality teams and government-cloud readiness. Funding is not verified, and the generic name collides with several other companies, but no failure or exit has been reported.

name: HUD

long_description:
HUD is the platform for building high quality post training datasets. Over 50 businesses use HUD to build RL environments, sell them to AI labs, or train their own models from them.

Our mission is to enable a generation of data entrepreneurs. The previous generation built apps to impact the world. We believe people will build infrastructure around data, both digital and physical, that align AIs to their specific goals.

Aggregators report a roughly $14M to $16M Series A in June 2026 with conflicting leads, which was not confirmed by a primary source. Competition grew fast, and no failure or exit has been reported.

name: Halluminate
one_liner: Data and RL environments to automate knowledge work
long_description:
AI today is capable of solving the world’s most complex math problems, writing the majority of our software, and soon automating research itself. The world of verifiable domains is being mastered at a stunning rate.

However, these same systems still struggle to build realistic financial models, deliver client ready powerpoint presentations, or grasp the nuance of well-balanced strategic analyses. Generally intelligent AI coworkers across finance, consulting, insurance, operations, and other forms of knowledge work will transform our economy. But they haven’t arrived yet.

The good news is that we have the recipe to build them.

Halluminate is a data research lab building the benchmarks and RL environments needed to push the frontier of AI in knowledge work. Our first area of focus is financial services, but we are rapidly expanding to adjacent verticals.

In the last 10 months we have:

- Grown from $0 to a mid-eight-figure revenue run rate while remaining strongly profitable
- Built and scaled RL environments with four of the five leading closed-source U.S. AI labs
- Released Westworld Due Diligence, a leading frontier benchmark for realistic financial work
- Built an interdisciplinary team of former founders, researchers, particle physicists, experts, and engineers from Meta, Scale AI, Capital One Labs, McKinsey, Goldman Sachs and more

If that excites you, join us!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying RL environments, benchmarks and expert-led evaluations for knowledge work, starting with financial services
problem: Computer-use agents need realistic sandboxes and graded tasks to learn knowledge work such as private equity due diligence. Halluminate builds the environments and benchmarks.
business_model: Data and RL environment sales to AI labs; the YC page claims a mid-eight-figure revenue run rate, profitable (company claim)
product_category: RL environments and benchmarks for knowledge work
market_need_then: TechCrunch reported on 2025-09-16 that labs were seeking RL environments to train agents, and the YC page says finance practitioners wrote the benchmark problems, indicating strong buyer demand.
outcome_analysis: Halluminate shifted in 2025 from agent evaluation to RL environments just as labs began buying them, and claimed a mid-eight-figure revenue run rate with five people while profitable. It raised a $30M Series A in October 2026 led by Oak HC/FT, per Fortune and another outlet, bringing reported total funding to $38.5M. Success rests on timing, a pivot and finance expert data.

name: Harper
one_liner: AI-native commercial insurance brokerage
long_description:
At Harper, we are building a fully autonomous commercial insurance brokerage powered by AI. Our initial focus is on mid-sized businesses with complex insurance needs, but our vision is to eventually serve every business in the country.

By leveraging AI to automate key workflows in the insurance process, we efficiently secure optimal coverage for each client's unique requirements at competitive prices and with rapid turnaround. Our AI system learns from the expertise of our brokers, accumulating not just knowledge but also the specific workflows, data, and capabilities that pave the way to full autonomy.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and mid-sized US businesses buying commercial insurance (daycares, manufacturers, dealerships, restaurants)
problem: Buying commercial insurance through traditional brokers is slow and manual; Harper automates forms, carrier matching and client communication.
business_model: Insurance brokerage earning carrier commissions, with an AI workflow platform (Harper Hub)
product_category: AI-native commercial insurance brokerage
market_need_then: Commercial insurance for small businesses is slow and phone based; the founder's family brokerage gave direct insight. YC page reports over $6M annualized premiums by the batch.
outcome_analysis: Harper grew from a Winter 2025 batch company to over 5,000 customers and a $46.8M seed and Series A led by Emergence Capital in February 2026. Family insurance experience, fast customer acquisition and the AI timing wave helped. Risks are crowded AI broker competition and commission economics. No exit has occurred.

name: HealthKey
one_liner: AI-powered Patient Identification for Clinical Trials
long_description:
HealthKey helps doctors offices generate more revenue by finding eligible patients for their clinical trials. We match at-risk patients with cutting-edge treatments, ultimately getting patients access to potentially life-changing treatments faster.

Big Pharma pays a lot of money to clinics for each patient they enroll, but finding patients who qualify is an entirely manual process today. We use AI to prescreen doctors’ existing patients against Clinical Trials’ eligibility criteria, making enrollment fast and easy.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Clinical trial sites and doctors offices that enroll patients in pharma trials
problem: Finding eligible patients for clinical trials is manual; HealthKey prescreens existing patient records against eligibility criteria.
business_model: Success fee per qualified patient identified, no upfront cost
product_category: AI patient identification for clinical trials
market_need_then: Pharma pays sites per enrolled patient and prescreening is manual (company claim on YC page). A urology practice reportedly found hundreds of eligible patients, self-reported.
outcome_analysis: HealthKey is an early Austin company from the Winter 2025 batch led by a single named founder with a product background at AWS and Plate IQ. Its pay per patient model lowers adoption risk. No exit, shutdown or disclosed funding was found, and the site claims dozens of sites using it without verification. Competition in AI trial prescreening grew quickly during 2025.

name: HelixDB
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI; Databases
one_liner: The fastest & most scalable graph-vector database on the market
long_description: As AI agents replace traditional software, they need a way to store, recall, and reason over contextual data. HelixDB gives them all of that in one system. We’re building the knowledge infrastructure every AI agent will depend on.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and AI teams building RAG and agent memory applications
problem: Retrieval systems needed separate vector and graph databases kept in sync; HelixDB combines them.
business_model: Open source (Apache 2.0 per site) database with hosted cloud
product_category: Open-source graph-vector database
market_need_then: RAG adoption in 2025 created demand for combined graph and vector retrieval, per founders' launch posts.
outcome_analysis: HelixDB launched on Hacker News in May 2025 during Spring 2025 YC and gained open source attention, with a hosted cloud and a 2026 object storage redesign. Funding is not publicly confirmed; the site lists Y Combinator, Nvidia and Vercel as backers. No exit or failure signal found. Outcome depends on converting developer interest into paid cloud usage against incumbents.

name: Helonic
tags: Construction; B2B; Workflow Automation; Architecture; AI
one_liner: Automatic Construction Drawing Clash Detection
long_description:
We help construction teams eliminate rework, delays, and drawing confusion before construction starts. We analyze PDF plans, detect clashes and inconsistencies across disciplines, and create draft RFIs so teams can resolve issues early.

This saves construction companies hundreds of hours and millions of dollars.

What we do:
- Automatically detect clashes, missing information, and drawing mismatches
- Align architectural, structural, and MEP plans so everything matches across sheets
- Generate draft RFIs from issues we find
- Replace long page-turn meetings with instant drawing analysis
- Reduce rework and prevent schedule delays before boots hit the ground

We integrate with: Procore, Autodesk, email, and the tools teams already use

Teams use us to:
- Save hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars per project
- Catch design and coordination issues early
- Reduce RFIs and prevent field fixes
- Keep projects on schedule with fewer surprises

Contact us at founders@helonic.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Architects, engineers and general contractors reviewing 2D PDF plan sets
problem: Drawing sets contain coordination conflicts and omissions that cause rework and RFIs.
business_model: B2B SaaS (pricing not public)
product_category: AI construction drawing analysis
market_need_then: Rework cost is a known construction pain; the site claims $500M+ rework avoided, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Helonic is a two person Fall 2025 company that analyzes construction PDFs for clashes and drafts RFIs. It was previously called Articulate. Funding is unconfirmed and no exit news exists. Success will hinge on accuracy and distribution into contractors against several similar AI drawing review tools.

name: Hemut
one_liner: AI-powered operating system for trucking companies.
long_description: Next-generation truck management software to automate back-office operations for trucking companies. Features include AI agents to automate inbound/outbound calls, AI document upload to reduce manual data entry, load sourcing tools, automated accounting, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US trucking carriers and fleets
problem: Trucking back office work (dispatch, load entry, invoicing, settlements) is manual and software is dated.
business_model: SaaS priced by AI credits per truck
product_category: AI operating system and TMS for trucking
market_need_then: Talk Business says most trucking software is outdated with slow support; Hemut approached $1M booked revenue and grew from 4 to 20 staff (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Hemut graduated Spring 2025, reportedly raised a $1.8M seed at about $30M valuation, and says it approaches $1M booked revenue with a Series A under discussion in March 2026. It benefits from a founder with trucking dispatch experience. No exit or failure was found. Many AI TMS rivals launched in 2025.

name: Hera
one_liner: The AI-native creative canvas
long_description:
Hera is an AI motion designer that turns 5-hour projects into 5-minute tasks. 

When you're a YouTuber making an infographic animation, instead of spending hours manually clicking buttons in Adobe After Effects, you can create the same animation in minutes in Hera. 

Through talking to our users, we realized that 95% of time spent on motion graphics is manual button clicking, not creative work. This insight led us to focus on automating the tedious parts while giving the user all creative control.

We launched in May 2025, got 100k waitlist signups in 8 weeks, and we're doubling revenue monthly.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Designers, marketers and creators who need motion graphics
problem: Motion graphics take hours in tools like After Effects; Hera generates and edits them from text.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription with API
product_category: AI motion graphics and creative canvas
market_need_then: YC page reports 100k+ waitlist signups in 8 weeks and 50,000+ animations at launch (company claims); a WHU article calls it the most visited S25 startup.
outcome_analysis: Hera launched in May 2025 and claims fast waitlist and animation growth, then broadened from motion graphics to an AI creative canvas with API access. Funding is not publicly confirmed. No exit or failure news found. The crowded AI video space and large design incumbents are the main risks.

name: Hey Telo
one_liner: Voice AI for Home Services
long_description: Voice AI for Home Services
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: German building services and craftsman businesses (SHK, electrical trades)
problem: Craft businesses miss calls and lose time to admin; Hey Telo answers calls, books appointments and writes into trade software.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Voice AI phone assistant for trades
market_need_then: Handwerk businesses miss calls while on jobs; founders cite 1 million German craftsman businesses (YC launch post). Site claims 300+ customers, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Hey Telo is a two person brother led company in the Winter 2025 batch selling German language voice AI to trades, and its site claims over 300 businesses. A software vendor integration is a distribution plus. No funding amount, exit or failure was found. Local competitors target the same niche, so execution on integrations decides the outcome.

name: Human Behavior
one_liner: Understand your users beyond the numbers
long_description: Human Behavior uses vision models to watch all user web sessions so you know exactly how users use every part of your product.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Product, engineering and design teams at fast-moving Series A and B software startups
problem: Dashboards show numbers but not why users stay, leave or pay; watching session replays by hand does not scale. Human Behavior uses vision models to watch every session and turn the findings into actions.
business_model: B2B SaaS, usage-based analytics
product_category: AI product analytics and session replay analysis
founder_names: Amogh Chaturvedi; Chirag Kawediya; Skyler Ji
founder_ages: Amogh Chaturvedi: 20; Chirag Kawediya: 22; Skyler Ji: 22
competitors_at_founding: PostHog; Mixpanel; Contentsquare, Quantum Metric, FullStory, LogRocket
market_need_then: Teams already spend on analytics and replay tools, and complain that dashboards do not explain why users behave as they do. Cheaper vision models in 2025 made automated replay review practical.
outcome_analysis: Human Behavior raised a $5M seed in September 2025 within two days, helped by cheap vision models and a young repeat-founder team with a prior small exit. It is early and active. The main risk is that incumbents such as PostHog already ship AI replay analysis, so durability depends on execution speed.

name: Humoniq
one_liner: Airline customer service, fully automated.
long_description:
Humoniq is fully automating customer support for travel & transport industries, which outsource $20B of customer support each year. Our AI-native approach improves speed, accuracy, and satisfaction.

We handle support requests across phone, email and chat. And because we connect directly to Sabre and Amadeus, we don’t just answer questions, we fully resolve complex issues. As a result, airlines need far fewer people and travelers get help much faster.

Our team is uniquely equipped to solve this challenge. We previously grew a travel management company, Flightfox (YC S12), to $25M/yr. We handled thousands of customer requests each month, which exposed the limitations of traditional outsourcing.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Airlines, airports, online travel agencies and travel management companies that outsource customer support
problem: Travel support is outsourced to large human contact centers that are slow and costly. Humoniq resolves rebooking and disruption requests across phone, email and chat by connecting directly to Sabre and Amadeus.
business_model: AI agent service priced per resolution or usage, sold to airlines
product_category: AI customer support for travel
market_need_then: Travel and transport firms outsource an estimated $20B of support yearly per the company's own claim, and disruptions create spiky load that human centers handle poorly.
outcome_analysis: Humoniq is a young company from founders who built Flightfox, a YC S12 travel company that reached over $20M in annual sales, giving unusual domain insight into airline support. No shutdown or acquisition news exists. Its outcome is open, with well-funded general agent vendors entering airlines as the main risk.

name: Hypercubic
one_liner: Agentic AI for Mainframe Operations and Modernization
long_description:
Hypercubic is an AI-native platform for mainframe operations and modernization.

We help enterprises understand and modernize their mission-critical legacy systems. About 70% of the Fortune 500 companies still rely on them to run their core business applications in banking, insurance, telecom, airlines, retail, and more.

These systems, originally built in the 1960s–90s, still power trillions in global infrastructure today but have become increasingly opaque as original developers retire or leave the workforce. 

We are pioneering a new class of intelligence capable of understanding, reasoning about, and rebuilding the world’s foundational infrastructure.

Learn more at hypercubic.ai
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Large enterprises and governments running COBOL mainframes in banking, insurance, telecom, airlines and healthcare
problem: Mission-critical mainframe systems are opaque as original engineers retire. Hypercubic documents, operates and modernizes them with AI agents.
business_model: Enterprise software license and services
product_category: AI for mainframe operations and modernization
competitors_at_founding: IBM watsonx Code Assistant for Z; AWS Transform for mainframe; Large IT services firms (Cognizant, Infosys, Capgemini, HCLTech, Wipro)
market_need_then: The company cites about 70% of the Fortune 500 relying on mainframes, with the workforce retiring. Surveys cited by press show most organizations shifted modernization strategy in the past year.
outcome_analysis: Hypercubic announced a $5.3M seed led by CIV in August 2026, about a year after its Fall 2025 batch, with angels from Opendoor and Walmart Labs. It targets a clear retiring-workforce pain. Risk is that IBM and AWS ship competing AI modernization tooling.

name: Hyperspell
tags: Machine Learning; SaaS; Data Engineering; AI
one_liner: Your Company Brain
long_description: Hyperspell is your Company Brain. AI agents are brilliant and clueless. They ace any test and still have no idea how your company works. Hyperspell connects your tools and synthesizes documents and conversations into a live, permissioned context graph. Any agent can read from it and write back to it like a filesystem, with every fact traced to source.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and startups building AI agents that need company context and memory
problem: AI agents lack knowledge of how a company works. Hyperspell connects tools such as Slack, Gmail and Notion into a permissioned context graph that agents can read and write.
business_model: Usage-based API and SDK
product_category: Context and memory layer for AI agents
market_need_then: Agent builders in 2025 repeatedly hit the problem of agents having no persistent or company-specific context, driving funding into memory startups.
outcome_analysis: Hyperspell is an active Fall 2025 company with two experienced founders, one with prior exits, in the hot agent memory category. Verified funding is absent, so its trajectory is unknown. Heavily funded rivals like Mem0 are the main competitive pressure.

name: IRBC
one_liner: AI-native financial institution for global businesses + agents.
long_description: IRBC is a financial technology company building an AI-native financial institution for global businesses and their AI agents. We believe stablecoins are to finance what AI is to software. IRBC enables businesses across 160 countries to bank, earn yield, spend with Visa credit cards, make instant global payments, and process payments like a local. All powered by programmable money and accessible through chat interfaces and a CLI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Global businesses and AI agents needing banking, yield, cards and payments across 160 countries
problem: Businesses outside major banking hubs lack easy access to dollar accounts, cards and instant cross-border payments.
business_model: Fintech fees on payments, cards and yield products (stablecoin based)
product_category: Stablecoin neobank for businesses and agents
market_need_then: Stablecoin supply and agent payments growing; claims of cost and access gaps for businesses in 160 countries come from the company, unverified.
outcome_analysis: IRBC is a three person New York company from Spring 2025 pitching a stablecoin based bank for businesses and AI agents. No funding, traction figures or exit were found, so the outcome is open; compliance burden and well funded rivals are the main risks.

name: Icarus
one_liner: Stratospheric birds for defense
long_description: Icarus is building the modern-day U2 spy plane: autonomous, solar-powered, low-cost. Flying at 60,000 ft, our birds deliver persistent intelligence and communications for the military at a fraction of the cost of existing systems. The stratosphere is the forgotten frontier.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Military and defense agencies buying persistent intelligence and communications from the stratosphere
problem: Persistent surveillance and communications are costly with satellites and crewed aircraft. Icarus builds autonomous solar-powered aircraft flying at 60,000 ft for weeks.
business_model: Hardware platform sold or leased to defense customers
product_category: Stratospheric solar aircraft (HAPS) for defense
competitors_at_founding: Airbus Zephyr; BAE Systems PHASA-35; Skydweller, Aalto, Sceye, Stratospheric Platforms; Aerostar
market_need_then: Defense buyers sought cheaper persistent ISR and comms, and 2025 industry material described HAPS moving from proof of concept to commercial debut, with a 2025 defense readiness framework white paper.
outcome_analysis: Icarus is an active Fall 2025 hardware company with an aerospace founder and active factory hiring in Los Angeles. No verified funding was found, so its stage is unknown. The core risks are hardware R&D cost and entrenched Airbus and BAE programs.

name: Imagine AI
one_liner: We reverse engineer B2B growth, starting with LinkedIn.
long_description:
Imagine AI is a research and software company reverse engineering modern B2B growth, starting with LinkedIn.

As companies get more automated, more of B2B growth will happen between agents, and the companies that connect will compound each other's output. We're building the connective layer between them. We start with content because it's still the fastest way to build B2B relationships at scale.

Today our content agent decides what your team should post based on data from 1M+ people (who posts what, who engages, where they work and how they're connected). It drafts the posts and graphics, schedules them for your execs and company page, and maps engagement back to your pipeline.

Rippling, MarqVision, Slash, Corgi and Fondo use Imagine AI. Customers have generated $40M in revenue, 100M impressions and 14,341 MQLs.

Free public benchmark of how 1,000+ B2B companies and their execs perform on LinkedIn: https://benchmark.useimagine.ai
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B companies and their executives who want LinkedIn content that drives pipeline
problem: B2B teams lack data-driven LinkedIn content; the agent decides what to post from engagement data, drafts and schedules posts and maps engagement to pipeline.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (pricing not sourced)
product_category: AI content agent for LinkedIn / B2B marketing
market_need_then: Company claims 50+ B2B customers and $40M customer-generated revenue; earlier launches cited $31M and $10M, so figures are inconsistent and unverified.
outcome_analysis: Imagine AI is a Fall 2025 YC company selling a LinkedIn content agent to B2B teams, with self-reported traction that is inconsistent across launches. No verified funding or outcome exists yet, and the generic name and crowded LinkedIn tool market are visible risks.

name: Imprezia
one_liner: The World's First AI Ad Network.
long_description: The first advertising infrastructure designed specifically for AI apps. Seamlessly integrate contextual brands & products that enhance user experience while generating revenue to pay the inference bills.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Advertisers seeking intent-rich placements, and AI app developers who want to monetize without subscriptions
problem: AI apps have high inference costs and subscription fatigue, while advertisers lack native inventory inside chatbots. Imprezia matches contextual ads inside AI apps via an SDK.
business_model: Ad network revenue share
product_category: AI-native ad network
market_need_then: AI app developers faced inference bills and wanted alternatives to subscriptions, and advertisers wanted AI-context placements; Kontext's seed and Koah's seed in 2025 show investor interest.
outcome_analysis: Imprezia is an active Summer 2025 company with a solo founder from Amazon and Meta ads. It claims 10M+ network users and early payouts, but no verified funding or independent traction. It faces better-funded Kontext and platform-owned ads.

name: Infinite
one_liner: Global B2B Stablecoin Processor
long_description: Infinite is a stablecoin payment processor. We offer businesses turnkey APIs and SDKs to instantly move money anywhere in the world at a fraction of the cost of traditional solutions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Payment providers, neobanks, marketplaces and treasury teams moving money across borders
problem: Moving money globally is slow and costly on traditional rails. Infinite offers APIs and SDKs for stablecoin payments, later adding bank accounts and compliance agents.
business_model: Usage-based payments API with fees
product_category: B2B stablecoin payment processing and compliance
market_need_then: Stablecoin volumes and investor interest rose through 2024 and 2025 and regulation became clearer, with B2B cross-border payments a core use case.
outcome_analysis: Infinite is an active Winter 2025 company from payments veterans, one with a prior exit to Coinbase. It launched bank accounts through Erebor in April 2026, widening the product. Funding is unverified. The main risk is well-funded Stripe-Bridge and BVNK in the same wedge.

name: Instinct Space
one_liner: Building lunar landers
long_description: Instinct is making the Moon the new LEO. Our small lunar lander is designed to be launched as a regular LEO rideshare, enabling higher mission cadence at a lower cost.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Governments and companies sending payloads to the Moon
problem: Lunar delivery is expensive and needs dedicated launches; no lunar navigation equivalent to GPS.
business_model: Per-kg lunar payload delivery service
product_category: Small lunar landers
founder_names: Alex Pinel Neparidze; Joaquim Dickson; Ashwin Iyer
market_need_then: NASA CLPS buyers and countries lacking lander access seek low-cost delivery (Payload, 2026-06).
outcome_analysis: Instinct Space is an early-stage London hardware startup that joined YC W25 as a lunar navigation constellation and pivoted to small landers, targeting a first mission in late 2028. It has not flown yet and no verified round beyond YC exists; hardware complexity and capital needs are the main risks.

name: Interfere
one_liner: Give engineering, product, and design teams insight into unseen issues
long_description: Interfere empowers engineers, product managers and designers with real-time understanding of previously unseen bugs and issues.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering, product and design teams at software companies
problem: Bugs and UX issues reach users before teams notice. Interfere monitors production apps, flags behavior changes, finds root causes and suggests fixes linked to the codebase.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: AI production monitoring and issue triage
market_need_then: Teams pay for monitoring and replay tools and AI coding raised release volume, increasing demand for automated detection of unseen issues.
outcome_analysis: Interfere is an active Summer 2025 company with one named founder and no verified funding. It enters a market where Sentry and LogRocket already ship AI triage, so outcomes depend on execution and differentiation. Too little reliable data exists to judge success or failure.

name: Inversion Semiconductor
one_liner: Manufacturing the most powerful chips, 15x faster
long_description:
Inversion Semiconductor is developing the next-generation chip fabrication machine, to create the most powerful chips 15x faster. Our vision is to reshore advanced chip fabrication capabilities in the West.

We're building a lithography machine. Lithography uses light to pattern circuit features on silicon. We're scaling transistors to their physical limits by shrinking particle accelerators 1000x, to create a high power light source. 

Using our light source we will double transistor density for a given numerical aperture and 3x throughput.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Semiconductor fabs and chipmakers that buy lithography tools
problem: EUV lithography light sources are power limited and a single supplier dominates the tool market, which caps wafer throughput and transistor scaling and makes Western fab capacity hard to reshore.
business_model: Hardware tool sales (lithography machine built around a compact laser wakefield accelerator light source)
product_category: Semiconductor lithography equipment
market_need_then: Chip demand and Western reshoring policy in 2024 and 2025 created interest in alternatives to the single lithography supplier; the company states its aim is to reshore advanced fabrication in the West (YC page).
outcome_analysis: Inversion is an active Winter 2025 company with a very hard research stage hardware plan. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff reports were found. Press attention (Tom's Hardware, TechSpot) is strong for its size, but the outcome depends on proving a laser wakefield EUV source, which no source shows done yet. Competing light source startups such as xLight raised much larger sums in 2025 and 2026.

name: Iron Grid
one_liner: AI-Native Data Center Engineering
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data center developers and operators that need facility engineering and design work
problem: Engineering design for AI data centers (cooling loops, power and layout) is slow and manual, delaying capacity builds.
business_model: Software and engineering services for data center design (exact pricing model not stated)
product_category: AI-native data center engineering
market_need_then: AI data center construction boomed in 2025 and several startups (Marengo, P-1 AI, Unlimited Industries) targeted design and engineering speed, indicating demand.
outcome_analysis: Iron Grid is an Active Summer 2025 company with two founders and almost no public coverage. No acquisition, shutdown or funding news was found, so there is no outcome to explain yet. The space is crowded with funded design automation startups, which makes execution speed the key variable.

name: IronLedger.ai
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: AI-enabled Corporate Cards and Invoice Processing for Real Estate
long_description:
IronLedger automates property accounting for property managers, developers and contractors, starting with accounts payable. We streamline busywork and audit spend against 100K+ units to improve NOI.

https://www.ironledger.ai/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Property managers, developers and contractors, starting with multifamily operators
problem: Property accounting teams spend hundreds of hours on invoice coding, card expenses and billbacks, which inflates headcount and delays closes.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus corporate card (card interchange implied, not stated)
product_category: AI accounts payable and corporate cards for real estate
market_need_then: Property managers rely on manual AP coding; vendor sources cite roughly $3 per invoice automated cost and several funded real estate AP tools existed by 2024.
outcome_analysis: IronLedger is an Active Summer 2025 company that its own site says raised $2.5M and has named property management customers across 100,000 plus units, though these are company claims. Founder real estate and Rippling backgrounds fit the product. No exit or distress was found; the open question is displacement of entrenched AP vendors.

name: Janet AI
one_liner: Agents that learn your company and work 24/7
long_description:
Janet AI lets you deploy reliable, cost-efficient 24/7 agents across every workflow, powered by custom agent memory and decision infrastructure we built for company operations. Janet remembers everything it sees and does across all your tools, and recalls exactly the right context at the moment it's needed.

Connect your tools and scope permissions in a few clicks, describe your flows in plain English, and always-on agents handle the work, all while learning what's going on across your company.

Janet AI is backed by Y Combinator, Formosa Capital, Paul Graham, Charles Ferguson, and others.

Check us out at janet.ai!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software and operations teams that want always-on AI agents across their tools
problem: Agents forget company context and are unreliable across workflows; Janet pitches persistent memory and decision infrastructure so agents recall the right context.
business_model: B2B SaaS agent platform (pricing not stated)
product_category: AI agents with company memory
market_need_then: Enterprise interest in agents was high in 2025, and agent memory was an active startup category (for example Mem0 raised $24M in October 2025).
outcome_analysis: Janet AI is an Active Summer 2025 company that launched in July 2025 as a Jira ticket triage layer and now describes company-wide always-on agents. It has almost no coverage, and no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Large platform vendors are shipping the same memory features, so differentiation is the central risk.

name: Jarmin
one_liner: AI Employees for human-level roles
long_description:
Jarmin.ai builds AI employees for human-level roles. It learns its responsibilities, understands your data, embeds into your systems, and becomes part of your team's day-to-day workflow. Completely hand over full initiatives or individual tasks.

Hire AI ML Engineers, Account Executives, Paralegals, Financial analysts, Compliance analysts, and more.

Jarmin’s founding team is from Meta SuperIntelligence Labs (Staff Engineers), Apple (Machine Learning Engineer), AWS (scaling infra), Lockheed-Martin (Research), and JPMorganChase (SWE) with experience building AI/ML and automating complex work of Researchers, Data Scientists, ML Engineers with AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies that want to hire AI employees for roles such as ML engineer, analyst, account executive or paralegal
problem: Teams lack ML and analyst capacity; Jarmin offers AI employees that learn a role, embed in company systems and take over tasks or whole initiatives.
business_model: Per-role AI employee subscription plus managed AI and ML engineering services
product_category: AI employees, autonomous ML engineer
founder_names: Chalmers Brown; Shir Halder; Zack Leman
market_need_then: Demand for AI employees in 2024 and 2025 was shown by Artisan's rounds and the broad enterprise agent push; Jarmin's own demand evidence is not public.
outcome_analysis: Jarmin is an Active Fall 2025 company with a strong ML founding team but no public traction, customers or priced round. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. It competes in the crowded AI employee category where Artisan raised first and model vendors expand into agents.

name: Jeevy Fabrication
one_liner: AI Driven EPC - Weld Fabrication Contractor
long_description:
Jeevy Fabrication is an AI-powered contractor that connects complex weld jobs to the best-fit shops—fast. We deliver top-tier QA and total transparency, all at better traditional outsourced pricing.

Our software reduces bid and scheduling time for our in-network shops by over 80%. It converts manufacturing drawings into an accurate bill of materials and a resource-loaded, high-fidelity schedule—eliminating costly errors and rework. Using this our in-network fabricators can bid on more jobs and deliver more reliable results than their competitors. 

We also offer our clients a streamlined purchasing and project tracking experience. Clients submit purchase requests, track schedules, access key documents, and receive real-time photo updates—all in one place. We provide traceability for easy material review and maintenance of domestic content standards as required. Faster decisions, fewer delays, complete visibility.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Industrial buyers of welded assemblies (pressure vessels, skids, pipeline systems), including aerospace and energy
problem: Complex weld jobs are slow to bid and schedule and quality is inconsistent; Jeevy acts as the contractor, routes jobs to a network of shops and gives clients schedule and QA visibility.
business_model: Fabrication contractor with software, margin on jobs routed to network shops
product_category: AI-driven weld fabrication contractor
market_need_then: Welded fabrication for aerospace and energy needs certified shops and code compliance; a trade feature argues existing quoting marketplaces do not cover it, and the company claims bid time cuts of over 80%.
outcome_analysis: Jeevy Fabrication is an Active Spring 2025 company run by two brothers with SpaceX and Rondo Energy backgrounds, operating as a weld contractor out of Texas. No exit, distress or priced round was found. The stage label of Growth in the directory is not supported by any source I found.

name: Juxta
one_liner: Building a GPS alternative 100x more powerful with no hardware needed.
long_description:
Juxta is creating the first Universal Positioning System (UPS) — a GPS alternative that can monitor movement anywhere on earth with no new hardware, minimal internet connection, and remote deployment. Using custom machine learning models and a first-of-its-kind synthetic fingerprinting technology, Juxta can make any indoor, outdoor, or underground space location-aware in minutes for a fraction of the cost of any other geospatial technology.

Juxta's UPS can be leveraged across industries — from securely tracking soldiers in combat zones to providing offline positioning for robots to offering asset tracking in warehouses and ports around the globe.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Defense teams, logistics and warehouse operators, robotics and hospital networks needing positioning where GPS fails
problem: GPS does not work indoors or underground and beacon systems (BLE, UWB) are costly to install; Juxta offers infrastructure free positioning from device sensors.
business_model: SDK licensing plus NODE1 asset tags (hardware and software)
product_category: GPS alternative, inertial positioning with synthetic fingerprinting
market_need_then: GPS jamming and spoofing in conflict zones and the cost of beacon systems (quoted at upward of $250,000 per site in a search summary of interviews) drove demand for alternatives.
outcome_analysis: Juxta is an Active Summer 2025 company that reportedly raised about $5M seed within weeks of the batch, with early revenue claimed in interviews. No exit or distress was found. The result depends on whether synthetic fingerprinting delivers the claimed accuracy in real sites, and on defense and logistics sales cycles.

name: KERNEL
tags: Developer Tools; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Crazy fast, open source infra for AI agents to use the Internet
long_description:
Kernel is crazy fast, open source infra for AI agents to access the internet 🧠🕸️
- Built on unikernels for crazy fast cold starts and low resource usage
- Sub-150ms cold starts on managed headful browsers
- Built-in stealth mode with residential proxies and automatic CAPTCHA solving
- Full observability: session recording, live view, and full logs
- Persistent sessions that maintain cookies and auth across invocations
- Native support for all browser and computer use frameworks
- SOC 2 compliant and HIPAA-ready

Trusted by Cash App, Rye, and 1000+ others. Backed by Accel & Y Combinator (S25).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need to use websites (for example Cash App and Rye)
problem: Agents that must operate websites with no API need fast, stealthy, observable cloud browsers that keep sessions and logins.
business_model: Usage-based cloud browser infrastructure with an open source core
product_category: Browser infrastructure for AI agents
market_need_then: Browser and computer use agents grew in 2025, and the company reports use by Cash App and Rye and over 11,000 teams by September 2026.
outcome_analysis: Kernel raised a combined seed and Series A of $22M led by Accel in October 2025, within months of the Summer 2025 batch. Repeat founders (a prior YC exit) and the rise of browser agents drove fast traction, with 11,000 plus teams reported by September 2026. Competition from Browserbase and others and an open core keep defensibility moderate.

name: Kaelio
one_liner: The open-source context layer for data agents
long_description:
Kaelio is the company behind ktx, the open-source context layer that makes data agents reliable. 

Data agents today fail because they lack structured context and determinism. Metrics are defined in five places, governed in none. Teams spend months on semantic layer projects that never finish.

ktx fixes that. Connect your warehouse, BI tools, and docs. ktx builds the context layer automatically. Your team governs it. Any agent can query it. One context layer across your entire data stack.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: Data teams at companies that want AI agents to query warehouses and BI tools reliably; open source users first, ktx Cloud buyers for governance
problem: Data agents fail because metric definitions are scattered and ungoverned, and semantic layer projects take months. Kaelio builds the context layer automatically from the warehouse, BI tools and docs.
business_model: Open source core (ktx, Apache 2.0) with a paid hosted ktx Cloud and a managed Data Agent product
product_category: Context layer and semantic layer for data agents
market_need_then: Companies were rolling out text to SQL agents in 2025 and hit inconsistent metric definitions. Semantic layer vendors reported momentum in February 2025, which shows spend and demand for governed definitions.
outcome_analysis: Kaelio is active and early. It joined YC in Spring 2025 and open sourced ktx, aiming at the gap where data agents lack governed context. Semantic layer vendors and warehouse native layers were already moving toward agents, so the key risk is incumbents absorbing the wedge. No outcome search result showed an acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.

name: Kaigo Health
tags: Health Tech; Digital Health; Healthcare IT
one_liner: AI outpatient care workforce
long_description: Kaigo Health provides an AI-powered outpatient care management platform that automates and scales remote care management for Medicare patients including post-discharge followups, ongoing check-ins, and monitoring. Using phone calls as an age-friendly interface, we aggregate patient responses, voice biomarkers, and remote patient monitoring data for powerful preventative and proactive healthcare.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Originally Medicare care management programs; the current website instead targets skilled nursing facilities buying an outsourced business office
problem: Remote follow up and monitoring of older Medicare patients is labor heavy; the later site describes skilled nursing facilities losing money to overcharges and missed reimbursement.
business_model: AI plus services; per the current site, recovery of money on behalf of facilities (fee basis not stated)
product_category: AI care management, later AI back office for nursing facilities
founder_names: Peter Chien; Lukas Klaiber; Kazuki Shin
market_need_then: CMS chronic care and remote monitoring programs pay for care management, and phone calls suit older patients. A search summary says CMS launched the ACCESS model in July 2026, later than founding.
outcome_analysis: Kaigo Health is active and early, with a three person team from Neuralink, NVIDIA and SAP backgrounds. Its website now describes a different business than the YC listing, which suggests a pivot toward nursing facility back office work. No funding beyond the standard YC deal and no exit were found, so the story is too early to read.

name: Kairos
tags: AIOps; Machine Learning; Reinforcement Learning; AI
one_liner: Specialized AI for Critical Industries
long_description:
Kairos closes the last-mile reliability gap in AI deployments. 

We bring frontier techniques to companies in critical industries, deploying specialized agents that encode operator expertise and reliably automate their most manual workflows.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Category leaders in regulated or critical industries that want reliable agents for manual workflows
problem: Generic AI deployments lack last mile reliability in critical industries; Kairos encodes operator expertise into specialized agents.
business_model: Service plus software subscriptions (a directory profile says service subscriptions)
product_category: Specialized AI agents and learning layer (Telos)
market_need_then: Search results cite a Gartner outlook from January 2025 projecting 40 percent of power and utility firms deploying AI operators in control rooms by 2027, which suggests demand for specialized agents in critical industries; the Kairos company itself gave no customer evidence.
outcome_analysis: Kairos is active and early with one listed founder and a three person team in Spring 2025. Its site now shows a product called Telos and a Janus AI legal entity. No outcome news, funding amount or exit was found, and the name collides with many other companies, so it is too early to judge.

name: Kaizen
one_liner: Automate anything on the web.
long_description: Kaizen is a digital employee that helps healthcare providers get patients into care faster. It processes referrals, verifies insurance benefits, manages prior authorizations, and handles provider credentialing across the systems teams already use. Kaizen works with $100M+ healthcare providers to drive seven-figure ROI with AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Healthcare providers and operations teams (company says $100M plus providers) with back office work across payer portals
problem: Referrals, benefit verification, prior authorization and credentialing happen across legacy web portals without APIs and consume staff time.
business_model: Usage based pricing, which the company says is about one third of the labor cost it replaces
product_category: Browser automation agents for healthcare operations
market_need_then: Prior authorization and insurance verification were widely reported pain points in 2025, with several startups funded to automate them. Kaizen says healthcare was its fastest growing vertical and that it reached HIPAA compliance in its first month.
outcome_analysis: Kaizen is active and early. It started as general browser automation for sites without APIs and narrowed toward healthcare back office work, citing it as the fastest growing vertical. Well funded prior authorization startups are neighbors, so the risk is crowding. No funding beyond a reported YC check and no exit were found.

name: Kalinda
one_liner: Deep research for class action law firms
long_description:
Kalinda helps class action law firms qualify potential cases in minutes with AI.

The nature of class action/mass torts involves thousands of cases for a single lawsuit. For every plaintiff (injured person), law firms involved in these cases compile everything from the products they used to the injuries they have. This data is extensive, granular, and buried deep in thousands of pages of medical, financial, and employment records and others.

Kalinda extracts, summarizes, and aggregates data from these records for attorneys with AI.

When scaled across an entire litigation, Kalinda works tirelessly and in parallel—turning a process that once took months into just a few hours. 

Kalinda provides firms with the equivalent manpower of hundreds of paralegals and legal nurses, allowing them to quickly determine which claimants are eligible and helping them file faster and in greater volume.

To date, we’ve processed 600k pages of records and are live with 2 of the largest plaintiff law firms in the U.S!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Plaintiff law firms running class action and mass tort cases
problem: Qualifying thousands of claimants means reading thousands of pages of medical, financial and employment records; Kalinda extracts and aggregates that data with AI.
business_model: B2B software subscriptions or per case fees to law firms (pricing not stated)
product_category: Legal AI for mass tort record review
market_need_then: Mass tort firms process thousands of claimants per case. The founders reported 600k pages processed and an interview in September 2025 reported about $60K revenue in four months from three large plaintiff firms (company reported).
outcome_analysis: Kalinda is active and early, a two founder team that reports live deployments at large plaintiff firms and early revenue. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is thinly documented, and competition from other legal AI vendors is the main risk, so the story is too early to read.

name: Kalpa Labs
one_liner: Scaling Generalist Speech models
long_description: We are an audio research lab building steerable voice models. Our conversational models are among the most human-like voice models, ranking ahead of ElevenLabs and Cartesia on Design Arena's AudioRealismBench, and have access to the whole conversation history to deliver the most natural experience over long conversations.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies buying speech APIs and voice agents, plus creators using a studio tool
problem: Voice models sound unnatural over long conversations and are split across separate tools; Kalpa aims for one model for all audio tasks.
business_model: Usage based speech API plus studio and realtime products (open beta per a profile)
product_category: Speech and audio foundation models
market_need_then: Voice agents were a fast growing category in 2025; companies paid for realistic, low latency speech. Kalpa's Hindi support targets a language market underserved by English first vendors, per its bilingual site.
outcome_analysis: Kalpa Labs is active and early, a small team from Google Assistant and trading infrastructure backgrounds building a generalist speech model. It reports a beta ranking and a public beta in 2026. Competition is intense and well funded, and funding is thinly documented, so no outcome can be read yet.

name: Kanava AI
tags: Sales; Supply Chain; AI; AI Assistant; Industrial
one_liner: Your First AI Sales Hire for Wholesale Distributors
long_description:
Distributors face a shrinking workforce and rising call volume.

Kanava AI builds voice-based agents that act like junior sales reps — starting with routine inbound calls, stock and price checks, field note logging, and CRM updates using live ERP data.

As the system learns from top reps and real workflows, it levels up: managing full sales calls, surfacing upsells, coaching teams, and reactivating dormant accounts.

We help distributors scale sales output without adding headcount — by automating the work reps shouldn’t be doing in the first place.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Karoo
one_liner: AI native consumer lending platform for underserved Americans
long_description: US consumers within the risk appetite of prime lenders are served by the most competitive and efficient consumer lending marketplace globally. However, once you fall outside of this as a borrower, market efficiency breaks down and incumbents take advantage of low levels of competition to price gouge. We're fixing this.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Canadian consumers needing small personal loans (site: $500 to $5,000 in Ontario, BC, Manitoba and Alberta); YC page targets underserved Americans
problem: Borrowers outside prime lending are served by low competition incumbents that price gouge; Karoo offers faster, fairer online loans.
business_model: Consumer installment loan interest; site states APRs of 31.99 to 34.99 percent
product_category: Consumer lending platform (fintech)
founder_names: Jeanot Dawson; Hugo Markland; Oliver Lambson
market_need_then: A source cited by a search summary says over 100 million Americans have scores below 670 and the subprime personal loan market exceeds $200 billion. That is from low quality sources, so it is weak evidence.
outcome_analysis: Karoo is active and early. The founders come from Lendable, which lends to similar borrowers, and launched in Canada first while the YC page targets Americans. No funding beyond a reported YC check, no exit and no outcome news were found, so the story cannot yet be read.

name: Karsa
one_liner: Stablecoin neobank for emerging markets
long_description: Karsa is a stablecoin neobank for over 100M people in emerging markets. We enable people to buy dollar-denominated stablecoins, save money in US bank accounts, and spend anywhere with a Visa card.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Freelancers, remote contract workers, crypto traders and small business owners in emerging markets such as Pakistan, India, Nigeria, Kenya and Paraguay who want dollar savings
problem: People in countries with inflation and capital controls cannot easily hold or spend dollars, and crypto onramps assume technical knowledge.
business_model: Consumer neobank with fees on stablecoin purchases, card use and peer to peer trader matching
product_category: Stablecoin neobank for emerging markets
market_need_then: In early 2025 stablecoin supply and usage were growing, and users in Pakistan, Nigeria and similar markets faced currency devaluation and limits on dollar access. The company cites inflation and capital controls in its launch post.
outcome_analysis: Karsa is a two person W25 company that says it is live with sellers in five countries. Public coverage is limited to launch posts and listings, with no confirmed institutional round, revenue or user numbers. The category is attracting large players, including Visa and Bridge, so the open question is whether local liquidity and trust can outrun partners that own the rails.

name: Karumi
one_liner: The Waymo of Personalized demos
long_description:
Karumi is an AI agent that joins a live video call with your prospects to deliver personalized product demos, 24/7, in any language.

It bridges the gap between your landing page and your sales team by engaging visitors at the peak of their interest, turning curiosity into conversion. For those not ready to talk to sales but eager to explore, Karumi offers the next generation of interactive, self-guided demos.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: B2B software companies whose prospects, new users and support teams need product demos
problem: Prospects want to see the product at peak interest but sales teams cannot staff live demos 24/7; Karumi joins a live video call and demos the real product.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscriptions (pricing not found)
product_category: AI demo agent for sales and onboarding
market_need_then: Companies were adding AI agents to sales in 2025. Karumi said it ran 3,000 plus demos of its own product in the week after its YC launch (company reported, per a search summary).
outcome_analysis: Karumi is active and early with a six person team led by two StackAI alumni. It launched in November 2025 with a demo spike and has several live video demo competitors. No outcome news or confirmed funding beyond a reported YC check was found, so the story is too early to read.

name: Kashikoi
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; Machine Learning; AI
one_liner: Simulation Engine for Benchmarking AI Products
long_description: Kashikoi is a simulation engine to benchmark AI agents. We generate CPU friendly world models that autonomously interview agents and generate deep behavioral assessments. We built a similar technology at Moveworks which was used to ship 250+ enterprise agents to customers daily.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams building and shipping AI agents that need pre-release testing
problem: Teams cannot cheaply and systematically benchmark AI agents before customers meet failures.
business_model: B2B SaaS, demo-led sales
product_category: AI agent simulation and evaluation
market_need_then: Agent launches surged in 2025 (Spring 2025 YC batch had about 70 agent startups per a trade report) and teams needed testing before production.
outcome_analysis: Kashikoi is a two-person Spring 2025 company selling agent simulation to AI teams. No exit, shutdown or layoff was found as of 2026-11, so the outcome is still open. Its edge is founder experience building similar simulation at Moveworks, while the weak points are crowded rivals such as Coval and Cekura and thin public traction data.

name: Kestral
one_liner: We automate your entire product development lifecycle.
long_description:
Kestral makes it clear what your customers want most, prioritizes those tasks for highest leverage, and closes the loop with those customers.

We (Brian and Bernard) have been close friends since university, and most recently worked together at Asana, leading AI and Authorization efforts. There we realized AI can completely disrupt the $50B Work Management Market, but it required a fresh start.

What work we even choose to manage in the first place is critical, and the most important insights from customers are silo-ed in sales/CS while R&D gives their best shot at roadmaps meant to deliver impact. Significant requests sit in a backlog, duplicate asks flood the system, months wasted on "strategic investments". We want to bridge this gap.

This message is resonating with heads of sales, heads of product, CEOs, as well as individuals, all trying to make sure the most important things get done, with less wasted effort and more revenue/retention.

Kestral works by automatically take in customer data like sales call transcripts & feature request messages and a team of agents:
1. analyze them for actionable takeaways, deal blockers, and nice to haves
2. consolidate them and manage all the asks with citations
3. prioritize them by impact and frequency to cut through the noise so you can see the biggest opportunities clearly
4. connect them to your existing strategic roadmap so when the work gets done, we can automatically follow back up with your customers and win them over

This is just step one of our mission to revolutionize how work gets done -- starting with what we choose to work on, and hope you follow us along for the ride!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Product, sales and customer success leaders at software companies
problem: Customer requests sit in siloed sales and support tools and product roadmaps are prioritized without them.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: AI product management and feedback prioritization
founder_names: Brian Kim; Bernard (surname not on YC page)
market_need_then: Founders cite duplicate asks and wasted roadmap bets at Asana; no dated external market data was captured.
outcome_analysis: Kestral launched in Spring 2025 as an AI tool that turns customer feedback into prioritized work, and its site now sells Project Brain for agent coordination, which suggests repositioning. No funding beyond the YC deal, exit or shutdown was verified as of 2026-11. The market is crowded with feedback tools and the product is easy to copy, so durability depends on integrations and speed.

name: Kestrel AI
one_liner: AI Agents for Platform Engineering
long_description:
Kestrel is the AI automation layer for platform engineering teams.

Platform teams use Kestrel to automate incident response, cloud provisioning, CI/CD, security, and developer requests across their stack.

Kestrel turns natural-language prompts into deterministic, production-ready workflows with 40+ integrations, 200+ pre-built actions, and support for custom HTTP and webhook actions.

Developer-first, with a CLI, Python SDK, and MCP server to manage workflows from where platform teams already work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Platform engineering and DevOps teams
problem: Platform teams spend time on incidents, provisioning and developer requests that could be automated.
business_model: Subscription priced per workflow or per cluster, plus forward-deployed services
product_category: AI agents for platform engineering and incident response
market_need_then: No dated source captured; competitor pages show an active AI SRE market in 2025 to 2026.
outcome_analysis: Kestrel AI joined YC in Fall 2025 with an AI platform engineering product and had no verified funding, exit or shutdown as of 2026-11. The batch is recent so outcome evidence is minimal. The space has well funded AI SRE rivals, so differentiation through deterministic workflows is the main bet.

name: Kestroll
one_liner: AI video editor
long_description: AI video editor with taste.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Video teams, creators and editors with large footage libraries
problem: Logging, searching and cutting raw footage is slow and manual.
business_model: B2B and prosumer SaaS
product_category: AI media asset management and video editing
market_need_then: No dated demand source captured; asset management and AI editing roundups exist but are 2026.
outcome_analysis: Kestroll started as AI media asset management and now markets itself as a chat-driven AI video editor integrated with Premiere and DaVinci. No verified funding beyond YC, exit or shutdown found as of 2026-11. The company is early and its direction has broadened, with thin evidence on traction.

name: Kirana AI
one_liner: AI manager for physical stores
long_description:
Kirana AI is building the first full-stack AI store manager.

With 100 years of family experience owning and operating grocery stores, we are starting there to prove our impact.

Our first product utilizes an on-premise GPU that monitors the store 24/7, scans for theft, looks for workplace health and safety issues, and optimizes customer service. 

With future POS/ordering data integrations, our manager will automate many of the day-to-day tasks of running a store, such as ordering, pricing, assortment, and delegating.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent grocery store owners in the US
problem: Small grocery stores lose money to theft, safety incidents and out-of-stocks and cannot afford staff to watch the store or run ordering and pricing.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus on-premise GPU hardware for camera monitoring
product_category: Computer vision retail operations software
market_need_then: Retail theft and shrink were a widely covered concern in 2024 and 2025 and independent grocers run thin margins. The founders cite their own family's store as the source of the pain.
outcome_analysis: Kirana AI joined YC in Spring 2025 with a two person team and a pitch that mixed camera loss prevention with a longer term AI store manager. The YC directory lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or press coverage could be found, and one YC listing still shows it as active. The cause and terms are not public, so no failure factors are recorded.

name: Klavis AI
one_liner: RL environments and training data for frontier AI labs
long_description: Klavis AI builds RL environments and high-quality training data at scale for frontier AI labs.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and AI application developers
problem: Agents need reliable tool access and realistic environments and data for reinforcement learning.
business_model: Usage and contract revenue from AI labs; earlier hosted MCP API
product_category: RL environments and MCP integration infrastructure
market_need_then: MCP launched late 2024 and agent tool access was a hot need in 2025; the company's open-source repo drew thousands of GitHub stars per directory listings.
outcome_analysis: Klavis launched in Spring 2025 with open-source MCP integrations, gained developer attention, then moved toward selling RL environments and training data to AI labs, a market that press described as booming in late 2025. No verified round beyond the YC deal, exit or shutdown found as of 2026-11. Risk comes from crowded integration platforms and labs building environments in-house.

name: Knowlify
one_liner: Done-for-you AI video paid ads and Meta campaign management
long_description:
Knowlify is a done-for-you video ads agency for B2B and B2C companies running paid social. We concept, script, produce and edit AI UGC ads, Pixar-style character animation ads and AI commercials, with a human quality check before delivery.

Our team starts with a 20-minute kickoff call, sends creative direction for approval within 48 hours, and delivers the first batch five days after the first call. New batches arrive weekly, with about 25 finished ads a week on a monthly plan.

We also offer end-to-end Meta advertising for Facebook and Instagram, combining creative production with campaign management. Creative-only engagements are available for teams with their own media buyer. Media spend is separate, and clients keep every finished ad.

See examples and book a call at https://knowlify.com/.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B and B2C companies running paid social ads
problem: Brands struggle to produce enough video creative for Meta ads.
business_model: Agency-style subscription starting at $5,000 per month; earlier SaaS plans for explainer videos
product_category: AI video ad creative agency
founder_names: Ritam Rana; Jonathan Maynard; Arjun Talati; Ritvik Varada
market_need_then: Founders say they ran Meta ads and could not produce enough creative; ad creative volume is a known bottleneck.
outcome_analysis: Knowlify began as an AI explainer video tool and moved to selling done-for-you Meta video ads at a high monthly price. Press reported a $3M raise in October 2025 but named no investors. No exit or shutdown found as of 2026-11. The pivot toward services suggests the self-serve tool market was crowded with well funded rivals.

name: Koyal
tags: Generative AI; Entertainment; Video; Media; Creator Economy
one_liner: Agentic AI Filmmaking Platform
long_description:
Koyal is an Agentic AI Filmmaking Platform that allows you to seamlessly convert script or audio into personalized, visually compelling stories. We’re a team from Carnegie Mellon, MIT and Meta, with experience in AI video generation.

https://koyal.ai builds directly upon our published research at the AI conference NeurIPS in December. We’ve been covered in the international press for our patented secure personalization protocol CHARCHA: the genAI captcha.

Announcement: https://x.com/meh_agarwal/status/1965866965425348687
Demo: https://x.com/meh_agarwal/status/1965137062119752099


We currently have paid pilots with the biggest global music labels, podcasts and production houses, and just launched our public beta at beta.koyal.ai

We recently concluded a pilot with Universal Music and T-Series (world’s largest music label) alongside Bollywood production houses like Maddock Entertainment, and Collective Artists Network! As part of that, we launched 5 music videos for Grammy and Oscar winning artists like A R Rahman, Ricky Kej and Shankar Mahadevan all crossing 1.5 million views!

We've recently built SOTA capabilities in (i) multilingual script to audio to video, (ii) Agentic lip-sync with dynamic movement & (iii) Multi-character consistency.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Music labels, studios and creators who want AI-generated video from audio or scripts
problem: Producing music videos and short films is slow and costly, and AI video raises likeness-consent issues.
business_model: Paid pilots with entertainment companies plus a public beta
product_category: Agentic AI filmmaking platform
market_need_then: Paid pilots with Universal Music, T-Series and others are company-reported on the YC page; unverified independently.
outcome_analysis: Koyal is a Fall 2025 brother-sister company building agentic AI filmmaking with research roots at CMU and MIT. It reports paid pilots with music companies and a public beta, but no verified funding beyond YC, exit or shutdown as of 2026-11. Strengths are research depth and entertainment access; risk is fast-moving video model providers and unproven revenue.

name: LLM Stats
one_liner: Independent AI evaluations lab
long_description:
We build independent and contamination-proof benchmarks that measure real world performance.

LLM Stats is the most complete LLM leaderboard. We have the most complete archive of LLM benchmark results and also run independent evaluations that are not the classical ones that are already in the training data of most models.

Our mission: become the biggest community dedicated to AI transparency.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI developers and companies choosing or evaluating LLMs
problem: Teams cannot easily compare models by independent benchmark, speed and price.
business_model: Free leaderboard funnel to paid custom benchmarking, data labeling, API and evaluation tooling (ZeroEval)
product_category: LLM benchmarking and evaluation
market_need_then: YC post reports about 60k monthly users and a third of a million unique users before the batch; demand for model comparison was high as models multiplied.
outcome_analysis: LLM Stats built an LLM leaderboard with substantial organic traffic before YC Summer 2025 and added ZeroEval evaluation tools as the paid product. No verified funding beyond the YC deal, exit or shutdown found as of 2026-11. The traffic is a real distribution asset, while the core risk is that leaderboards are easy to copy and monetization is unproven.

name: Labric
one_liner: The data layer for scientific research
long_description: Labric is building the data layer that makes AI work for science. We capture messy lab data from instruments and tools, clean it, and connect it—so researchers can actually use AI to accelerate discovery.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprise and academic research labs that run instruments from vendors such as Bruker, Thermo Fisher Scientific and Waters
problem: Lab data sits in instruments, spreadsheets and notes in inconsistent formats, so researchers cannot search it or use AI on it.
business_model: B2B SaaS data infrastructure for labs (pricing not public)
product_category: Scientific data infrastructure and lab data capture
