market_need_then: Labs generate data in fragmented formats and the AI wave in 2025 raised demand for clean, structured research data. No spend figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Labric is a very young company from Spring 2025 with no reported exit, layoffs or shutdown. It sells into a crowded lab data space with established vendors, and its main assets are a CTO with direct lab data infrastructure experience and the timing of AI demand for structured data. No traction or round figures could be verified, so the outcome is open.

name: Ladder
tags: Sales; Sales Enablement; Home Services; AI
one_liner: AI personal assistant for in-home sales
long_description: Ladder is an AI personal assistant for in-home sales. It takes notes on the in-person conversation and helps reps close more deals, improve with each pitch, and deliver and generate more leads.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Home services companies such as roofing contractors whose reps run in-home sales appointments
problem: In-home sales reps get little coaching or follow-up support and spend time on CRM entry, while managers cannot see which reps need help.
business_model: Outcome-based pricing, a flat fee per sold project
product_category: AI sales assistant for field and in-home sales
market_need_then: Home services firms run large volumes of in-home sales; the company claims about $106 million in sold projects handled, a self-reported figure on its site.
outcome_analysis: Ladder is a Winter 2025 company with two founders from robotics and computer vision and no reported exit or shutdown. Its flat per-sold-project pricing and early customer logos suggest some traction, but no verified funding or revenue was found. The name is generic and shared with other firms, which could hurt search discoverability.

name: Lakonia
one_liner: Delivering AI-powered situational awareness in tactical environments.
long_description: Lakonia is building an AI-powered command and control platform for law enforcement and the military. Our AI transcribes radio communications, analyzes them, and then synthesizes information for commanders/dispatchers and operators to act on.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Law enforcement agencies, dispatch and 911 centers, and military units
problem: Commanders and dispatchers miss critical information in busy radio traffic, and manual monitoring does not scale.
business_model: B2B and government software sales (pricing not public)
product_category: AI command and control and radio intelligence for public safety and defense
market_need_then: Public safety agencies were adopting AI transcription in 2025, and defense interest in AI command and control was rising. No procurement figures were found.
outcome_analysis: Lakonia is a Fall 2025 company with two young founders and no reported exit or shutdown. It targets a market where Motorola, Prepared and others already offered radio transcription in 2025, so its edge must come from tactical and disconnected deployment and speed of iteration. No verified funding or customers were found, so the outcome is open.

name: Lanesurf
one_liner: Book any load in 10 minutes
long_description:
Over a million loads move via trucks in the US every day and even in 2026 they are still booked through endless negotiations over calls and emails.

Lanesurf solves this with an army of AI agents that find nearby empty trucks, call/email them in parallel, negotiate rates, and book the best available truck.

Live Demo: https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7394069447327555584/

Our self-improving voice AI stack is built for the messy reality of logistics - noisy calls, compliance checks, constant exceptions and turns them into faster bookings at better margins.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US freight brokerages that book truck capacity for loads
problem: Loads are still booked through long calls and emails negotiating with carriers, which costs brokers hours per rep per day.
business_model: B2B SaaS for freight brokers (pricing not public)
product_category: Voice AI carrier sales agents for logistics
market_need_then: Over a million loads move by truck daily in the US and are booked mostly by phone and email; the company says brokers book 60 to 80 percent of loads with AI-sourced capacity (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Lanesurf is a Summer 2025 company with a team of 14 and named broker customers including a rollout across 130 plus offices at Logistic Dynamics, according to its site. Trade press coverage and a quick headcount ramp suggest early traction, but it competes with better funded HappyRobot and Vooma. No verified rounds were found, so the funding story is unknown.

name: Lapel
tags: Customer Success; Sales; Customer Support; AI
one_liner: Infrastructure to power every customer interaction.
long_description:
Lapel is bringing hospitality to the internet.

Great service means knowing your customers and making every interaction count. Online, that gets harder as a company grows. Customer context is scattered across systems, leaving teams to piece it together.

Lapel unifies that data into a real-time picture of every account and helps teams turn what they know into coordinated action across the customer journey. The result is faster decisions, more proactive service, and interactions that feel personal at scale. We call it hospitality at scale.

Learn more at lapel.com.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies from fast-growing startups to enterprises that need to coordinate sales, success and support across the customer journey
problem: Customer context is scattered across systems, so teams piece it together by hand and service gets impersonal as the company grows.
business_model: B2B SaaS infrastructure (pricing not public)
product_category: Customer data unification and customer operations
market_need_then: A Salesforce State of CRM figure cited by one source says 90% of companies want a unified customer view but only 32% have one. Secondary and unverified.
outcome_analysis: Lapel is a Spring 2025 company with experienced second-time founders from Midjourney and Chick-fil-A, a team of 14, and no reported exit or shutdown. It says it is well funded but no round was verified. It enters a crowded customer success market, so differentiation through the hospitality framing and data unification will decide the result.

name: Lapis
one_liner: AI that creates and runs ads, end-end
long_description:
Lapis builds, launches, and scales paid ad campaigns for DTC and SaaS businesses.

Lapis agents handle every step of the paid ads journey: writing ad copy (headlines and descriptions), generating the static images used in ads, deploying campaigns across paid channels, creating a custom landing page for each ad, and feeding real user interaction data back into a self-improving ads engine that gets better every day.

With Lapis, businesses can rapidly iterate on ads and A/B test at scale, free from the human design and creative bottlenecks that slow teams down. Using Lapis, companies can quantitatively improve their paid ads performance by up to 20x.

Lapis is used by 1,500+ marketing teams and 30+ enterprises, from Fortune 500 businesses to fast growing DTC businesses, and supports 10 languages including English, Spanish, and Italian.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: DTC brands, SaaS companies and growth teams that buy paid advertising
problem: Creating, testing and managing paid ads across channels is slow and bottlenecked by human design and copy work.
business_model: Self-serve subscriptions ($99 and $599 per month) plus managed plans with a strategist
product_category: AI advertising agents (ad creative, campaign deployment, landing pages, ads in ChatGPT)
competitors_at_founding: Amazon Ads agentic creative tool; Nativeads.ai
market_need_then: Paid ads spend is large and teams want faster creative testing; the company claims 1,500 plus marketing teams and 30 plus enterprises, self-reported and unverified.
outcome_analysis: Lapis is a Fall 2025 company with a small team that already moved from AI search analytics to ad generation. It faces large platforms shipping similar tools, and its traction numbers are self-reported. No exit or shutdown was found and no round was verified, so the outcome is open.

name: Lark
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; DevOps; Automation; AI
one_liner: The E2E testing layer for AI-driven development
long_description: Lark lets teams write end-to-end tests in plain English. Validate dashboards, APIs, SDKs, and full product flows without maintaining fragile test code. Run continuously on feature branches, in CI, or in production.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams shipping software with AI coding agents that need continuous end-to-end tests
problem: End-to-end tests are fragile and costly to maintain, and AI-driven development ships faster than teams can test.
business_model: B2B SaaS for developer teams (pricing not public)
product_category: AI end-to-end testing for developer tools
market_need_then: AI coding agents increased code volume in 2025 and created demand for automated testing; no spend figures found.
outcome_analysis: Lark is a Summer 2025 company that pivoted from billing to testing and carries ex-Stripe credentials. It enters a field where Momentic, Functionize and others had raised money in 2025. No exit or shutdown was found and no round was verified; the shared name with ByteDance's Lark adds search confusion.

name: Layers
tags: Consumer Health Services; Health Tech; Beauty; Health & Wellness; AI
one_liner: Improve your appearance by measuring, understanding, and tracking…
long_description:
Improving how you look and feel leads to better outcomes in life (career, relationships, first impressions, opportunities, etc). 

Improving your health and appearance is an engineering problem - the body can be optimized like any other system
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Image and health conscious consumers, shown by tech worker testimonials, who pay for measurement and treatment visits
problem: People cannot easily measure and track skin, hair and body metrics in one place, so appearance improvement is guesswork.
business_model: Consumer clinic visits and recurring quarterly assessments plus prescribed treatments
product_category: Consumer health and aesthetics measurement studio
market_need_then: Consumer demand for preventive scans and longevity services grew in 2025, evidenced by Function Health buying Ezra and Prenuvo raising $120M. No skin or hair measurement demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Layers is a Fall 2025 company whose YC page also shows a launch post for Telemetron, a hardware support platform, so its direction is unclear; the website describes a San Francisco studio for body measurement and treatments. No exit or shutdown was found and no round was verified. It sits in a market where Function Health and Prenuvo are well funded.

name: Leadbay
one_liner: Qualified leads for agentic workflows.
long_description:
Leadbay qualifies leads for agentic workflows.

Teams at L'Oréal, Saint-Gobain, Gerflor USA, Corgi, and Nespresso B2B have 3x'd their addressable market and 10x'd what they defined as "qualified leads". Talking to our customers, we used to hear, "10 minutes on Leadbay beats 6 months with Clay and a GTM agency."

Co-founders are Milan Stankovic (CTO) - PhD to make AI work with limited data, and Ludovic Granger (CEO). 

Create an account.
A new market is yours.
leadbay.ai.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B sales teams selling to data-scarce SMB markets, including enterprises such as L'Oreal and Saint-Gobain
problem: Standard lead databases miss most small businesses, so sales teams cannot find or qualify them.
business_model: Per-user SaaS subscription (free, 100 and 400 USD per user per month tiers, custom enterprise) with forward-deployed engineers
product_category: AI lead qualification and sales intelligence
market_need_then: Founders cite incumbents missing roughly 70 percent of US companies; customers report 3x addressable market. These are company claims, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Leadbay entered YC in Fall 2025 with named European enterprise customers and raised a reported 4.3 million dollar seed in May 2026. It is early and active; success rests on an ML founder and a niche in data-scarce SMB markets, while crowded incumbents are the main threat.

name: Leaping AI
one_liner: AI voice and texting agents
long_description:
Leaping AI is the best platform to deploy voice and texting AI agents for customer service, lead qualification and appointment scheduling. We target mid-market and Enterprise companies and industries are: home remodeling, roofing, pay per call, travel, retail, health insurance, Medicare, health and real estate.

We automated contact centers employing >100 human agents and now handle their incoming customer support and appointment scheduling calls, end-to-end. All while maintaining 90% customer satisfaction score.

Pain points that we solve: missed calls, insufficient speed to lead, not enough call center resources, call center inefficiencies, agents not sticking to the script, etc.

At its core, we have a multi-channel outreach campaign feature, whereby our customers can call and text potential leads over an arbitrary time period. If end customers call or text back, the Leaping voice or text AI agent can autonomously schedule appointments and resolve service requests.

Some of our differentiating features: most-human like voice in the market, CRM integrations in place (Salesforce, Hubspot, MarketSharp, AccuLynx, JobNimbus, LeadPerfection, Google, etc.) and white-glove onboarding (in-person for larger accounts). Our AI agents can hold 100+ conversations at once, speak multiple languages and be equipped with company specific FAQ. Lastly, we have our own number health monitoring and DNC software.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mid-market and enterprise contact centers and home services sellers (remodeling, roofing, windows, HVAC), plus airlines such as Eurowings
problem: Missed calls, slow speed to lead and contact center capacity limits make customer service and appointment booking costly.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage-based voice and text AI agents with CRM integrations
product_category: Voice and texting AI agents
founder_names: Kevin Wu; Arkadiy Telegin; Shraey Bhatia
market_need_then: Contact centers with 100+ human agents were automated by the company per its YC description; the company states about 90 percent customer satisfaction (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Leaping AI is active and raised a 4.7 million dollar seed in August 2025 after the Winter 2025 batch, riding the voice agent wave with named customers like Eurowings and Thompson Creek Window Company. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found. The market is crowded, so durability depends on enterprise contracts and integrations rather than technology alone.

name: Leeroo
one_liner: AI Building AI For Enterprise
long_description: Our platform connects to every system you operate, learns your business into one living model, and ships agents that turn it into outcomes.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Large enterprises with many legacy systems (the site cites a 1B dollar company with 35+ systems)
problem: Enterprises hold fragmented systems and data, so value and conflicts across systems stay hidden.
business_model: Enterprise platform (Uniforge) deployed in customer cloud or on premises
product_category: Enterprise AI agent platform
market_need_then: Enterprise appetite for AI agents grew in 2025; evidence of spend specific to Leeroo is limited to a single unnamed case on its site.
outcome_analysis: Leeroo is an early stage London company from the Spring 2025 batch with a strong research team from Meta AI, LinkedIn and BYJU'S. No exit or shutdown found and no confirmed round amount, so its trajectory is unknown. Its main risk is competition from Palantir and hyperscaler agent platforms.

name: Lemma
tags: Developer Tools; Analytics; Infrastructure; Monitoring; AI
one_liner: Production Monitoring for AI agents
long_description: Lemma is production monitoring for AI agents. We catch the silent failures your observability tools and evals miss (think bad tool calls, lost context, and infinite loops) before your users find them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams from seed to Series B running AI agents in production
problem: AI agents fail silently (bad tool calls, lost context, loops) in ways observability tools and evals miss.
business_model: B2B SaaS monitoring with integrations (SOC 2 Type II)
product_category: AI agent production monitoring
market_need_then: Agents were moving into production in 2025 and teams reported tests passing while real use failed, per the funding coverage.
outcome_analysis: Lemma raised a 2.3 million dollar pre-seed in August 2026 after the Fall 2025 batch, backed by Matrix and others, with named customers such as Modus and Boardy. It is early with two founders and no exit found. Competition from established observability vendors is the key risk.

name: Lexi
one_liner: AI Operating System for Legal Teams
long_description:
Lexi is an AI operating system for legal teams, law firms, and in-house counsel. It brings legal research, drafting, document review, contract redlining, case workflows, translation, knowledge management, and AI associates into one secure platform.

Lexi is built for enterprise legal work with end-to-end security, role-based access controls, audit trails, encrypted document handling, private workspaces, and deployment options for sensitive legal environments. Legal teams use Lexi to process high-volume legal documents, find answers with verified citations, draft in their preferred style, review contracts, and manage legal workflows from intake to output.

Lexi has processed 5,000,000+ documents across 200,000+ cases for 200+ organizations and law firms, helping lawyers save 10+ hours every week and handle more matters without adding headcount.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Law firms, in-house legal teams and solo lawyers, with focus on Asia and India
problem: Legal research, drafting, document review and workflows consume many lawyer hours.
business_model: B2B SaaS AI legal platform
product_category: Legal AI
market_need_then: Legal tech funding surged in 2025 and legal AI platforms expanded to Asia, per Law360 and Artificial Lawyer coverage.
outcome_analysis: Lexi is an active legal AI company from the Fall 2025 batch that claims 1,000 plus organizations and compliance certifications. Funding is not confirmed by any press release, and it competes with far better funded Harvey and Legora. The similar name to Alexi and LexisNexis forced a disclaimer on its site.

name: Lightberry
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Robotics; Design; Conversational AI
one_liner: Robots with soul
long_description:
We build brains for robots.

We work with manufacturers like Unitree to make robots listen, speak, and act. You can program your robot out of the box by literally talking to it, no coding involved.

Robots running Lightberry are emotionally intelligent, always on, and fully autonomous. Just like in Star Wars!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Humanoid robot makers such as Unitree and buyers of interactive robots
problem: Robots lack natural conversation and perception; programming them requires code.
business_model: Software and robot bundles (Lightberry OS, Lumi robot at about 39,990 dollars reservation)
product_category: Robot AI software and social humanoid
market_need_then: Humanoid robot interest peaked in late 2025 events but with skepticism about hardware reality.
outcome_analysis: Lightberry is an early company from Fall 2025 that signed a deal with Unitree and launched the Lumi humanoid in 2026. It reportedly closed a seed early but amounts are not public. It depends on partner hardware and faces larger humanoid players.

name: Lilac
tags: Machine Learning; Cloud Computing; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Lilac helps neoclouds operate quality GPUs at scale.
long_description: Lilac helps neoclouds operate quality GPUs at scale: provisioning, burn-in and validation, monitoring, repair, usage records and white-label consoles.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Neoclouds and GPU cloud operators
problem: Mismanaged GPU clusters stall operators; provisioning, burn in, repair and usage records are hard to run at scale.
business_model: B2B platform for GPU operations, white label consoles, capacity partnerships
product_category: GPU cloud operations software
market_need_then: Neocloud buildout in 2025 created demand for operations tooling.
outcome_analysis: Lilac is an active Summer 2025 company that partnered with Saturn Cloud in 2026 and lists MiniMax and Moonshot AI as partners. It reportedly raised a 2.5 million seed in October 2025 but only an aggregator says so. Positioning has shifted from pooling idle GPUs to operating neocloud clusters.

name: Linewise
one_liner: Industrial data layer for physical RSI
long_description: We capture how physical things are made, from the first design to the final assembly, and turn it into training data for frontier AI and robotics models.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI and robotics labs buying training data
problem: Physical manufacturing knowledge is not captured in data usable for robotics and engineering models.
business_model: Dataset sales (robotics, engineering, research)
product_category: Industrial data for physical AI
founder_names: Tanachart (James) Kujareevanich; Zhichu Ren; Will Wenbo Zhang
market_need_then: Robotics labs sought egocentric and manipulation data; Nvidia reported benefits from first person video (2025 coverage).
outcome_analysis: Linewise raised a 1.1 million pre-seed in September 2025 as a factory AI engineer and has since repositioned as a data supplier for physical AI, now with 25 staff. No exit or distress was found. It competes with other robotics data collectors and must prove labs will pay.

name: Liquid Compute
one_liner: Pending CFTC regulation to be the first cash and physically settled…
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Buyers and sellers of AI compute capacity (labs, cloud and GPU owners, financial firms)
problem: AI compute is bought through opaque bilateral deals; Liquid Compute (formerly Pluto) builds a marketplace and a CFTC-regulated exchange for cash-settled and physically settled compute contracts.
business_model: Exchange and marketplace (trading and clearing fees, market data; assumed)
product_category: Fintech infrastructure: compute exchange and derivatives
market_need_then: Compute scarcity and price volatility; the CFTC later sought comment on whether compute is standardized enough for futures. No dated 2024-2025 evidence fetched.
outcome_analysis: Liquid Compute, formerly Pluto, went through YC and in September 2026 announced a $15M seed co-led by FirstMark and Chemistry while its CFTC applications remain pending. It rides AI compute scarcity but depends on regulatory approval and faces ICE and CME entering compute futures. Too early to judge success.

name: Liva AI
tags: Marketplace; B2B; Data Labeling; Big Data; AI
one_liner: Building socially intelligent AI
long_description: Helping to build more socially intelligent AI, starting with voice.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: AI labs and companies training voice and video models
problem: Existing voice datasets lack diversity in accents, emotions and languages for socially intelligent AI.
business_model: Consented human voice and video data sold as datasets
product_category: AI training data
market_need_then: Voice AI labs needed diverse real human data; privacy suits over voice training were rising in 2026.
outcome_analysis: Liva AI is an early Summer 2025 company with six staff building consented voice and video datasets. Funding is unverified, with aggregators claiming either 500K pre-seed or 3M seed. No exit was found. Its path depends on selling data to labs against established marketplaces and synthetic voice.

name: Locata
one_liner: AI Referral Automation for Primary Care Clinics
long_description:
Locata is an AI referral management platform for Primary Care. We deploy AI agents to automate every step of the referral process that back-office staff face daily, from submitting prior authorizations to broadcasting updates and following up with patients. This frees up staff to focus on patient care.

Primary care back-offices are severely understaffed and overburdened by administrative work associated with referrals. Additionally, patients suffer navigating the complex referral process, which can have disastrous health effects if they don’t get the care they need. These factors point to a glaring gap in the system—where out of over 100 million specialist referrals issued annually in the US, only half are actually completed. Locata is tackling this problem head-on, saving administrative staff hours each week and ensuring that the referral process goes as smoothly as possible for patients and their providers.

Alejandro and Josh met at Stanford where they graduated with BS degrees in Computer Science. Alejandro was a senior software engineer at Meta’s Reality Labs where he led development of several AI features for wearable products and prior to that conducted AI research at Stanford Medicine. Josh graduated with a masters in Computer Science, specializing in AI, before working as a software engineer at Google where he developed AI products that served over 1 billion users.

Within two weeks of building our product, we signed a major regional health center and have saved them over 100 hours of work in our first month live.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Primary care clinics and community health centers whose back offices manage specialist referrals
problem: Referral work such as prior authorizations, record sending and patient follow up is manual and understaffed, so many specialist referrals are never completed.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to clinics and health centers (pricing not public)
product_category: AI agents for healthcare referral management
market_need_then: The company cites over 100 million specialist referrals per year in the US with only about half completed, and understaffed primary care back offices. This is the company's own claim.
outcome_analysis: Locata is an early stage company, active as of 2026-11. It signed community health center customers soon after launch and shows five named customer logos on its site. Funding is not verified beyond aggregator claims, so no outcome can be judged yet; the main risk is a crowded set of referral and prior authorization automation vendors.

name: Locus
one_liner: Payment infrastructure for AI agents
long_description:
We make your agents pay.

As agents evolve from tools into dependable, autonomous actors, they’ll need the ability to execute open-ended workflows end-to-end.

This inevitably means payments: accessing paywalled data, transacting for services or with other specialist agents. But autonomy requires guardrails. Businesses and developers will need a way to ensure their agents only spend how much and on what they’re supposed to.

The machine economy is coming, and Locus (YC F25) is building the connector businesses will need to participate. We connect agents securely to funds, letting you define permissions and limits for every transaction. Each payment is traceable, auditable, and fully reconcilable with your existing financial stack.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI platforms and developers whose agents need to pay for APIs and services under spending limits
problem: Autonomous agents need to transact for data and services, but businesses need permissions, limits and audit trails on every payment.
business_model: Usage-based payments and API billing layer plus subscription tiers (Free, $200 and $1,000 per month)
product_category: Payment infrastructure for AI agents
market_need_then: Agents were moving from tools to autonomous actors in 2025, creating demand for controlled payment rails; evidence is the company's own framing and the number of entrants.
outcome_analysis: Locus is an early stage, active company. It started with agent wallets and later added an API billing layer reported by RuntimeWire, widening scope toward platforms. No outcome yet; funding beyond the YC investment is not verified and competition in agent payments is dense.

name: Logical
tags: Consumer; B2B; Productivity; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Proactive AI that knows what's important
long_description: Logical is a desktop AI that acts as a proactive and largely promptless copilot, designed to reduce the friction of using AI for everyday tasks. It transfers context across apps, and allows taking action on many apps with just a few clicks. Logical can assist with drafting emails, writing docs, noting meetings and can even automatically detect action items. Need to prompt? Logical can understand intent in much fewer words than a regular chatbot. Plus, user data is never sent to Logical servers. Logical is the AI resurrection of Clippy, but actually good.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Knowledge workers and operations teams using Mac desktop apps, paying from about $29 per month
problem: Using AI chatbots for everyday work needs constant prompting and context copying across apps; Logical proactively suggests actions and carries context between apps.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription (starts around $29 per month per one aggregator)
product_category: Desktop AI assistant
market_need_then: AI chatbot friction and context switching were widely felt in 2025, and demand for desktop copilots was visible in products like Cluely, but no Logical specific demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Logical is a two person team in YC Fall 2025 building a privacy-first proactive desktop copilot with a Clippy-inspired tagline. It is too early for an outcome: only a small pre-seed is reported by aggregators, the space has well known rivals and platform incumbents, and no traction metrics were found.

name: LogosGuard
one_liner: The sensitive data redaction layer for AI
long_description: Use AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini safely without leaking sensitive data. LogosGuard redacts your private information before the prompt ever leaves your device.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individuals and enterprises using ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini who must not leak sensitive data, including regulated teams
problem: Employees paste private data into AI tools; redaction before the prompt leaves the device prevents leaks.
business_model: Browser extension with free trial and enterprise tier
product_category: AI data loss prevention browser extension
market_need_then: Enterprises worried about leaking data into AI tools in 2025; evidence is the company's HIPAA and privacy positioning, no spend data found.
outcome_analysis: LogosGuard is an early stage active company with two Stanford trained founders with Apple backgrounds. No funding amount, press or outcome is public, and the product faces many look alike extensions and platform native controls, so no conclusion about success can be drawn yet.

name: Lopus
one_liner: Headless Data Team
long_description:
Pointing an AI at all your data is a recipe for disaster - it will confidently lie, hallucinate, and drive your business into the ground.

What if you could trust your AI the way you trust a calculator?

That's Lopus.

We build a self-healing semantic layer that captures your business logic.
Including every metric, every definition, every edge case.
Defined once, and trusted everywhere.

No SQL. No dashboards. No waiting on the data team.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Growth and revenue teams at startups wanting trusted AI analytics over CRM, billing and product data
problem: Pointing an AI at raw data produces confident wrong answers; teams wait on data teams for metrics.
business_model: B2B SaaS analytics platform (pricing not found)
product_category: AI analytics with semantic layer
market_need_then: AI text to SQL tools were known to hallucinate business definitions, creating demand for governed metrics; evidence is vendor writing, not spend data.
outcome_analysis: Lopus is an active early stage company whose positioning moved from a headless data team to an AI analytics product with named startup customers such as Glean and Numeral per its testimonials. Funding beyond YC is not public in the sources found, and competition from semantic layer vendors is strong, so no outcome is established.

name: Lotas
tags: Developer Tools; Data Science; Data Visualization; AI
one_liner: AI for quantitative trading
long_description: Quantitative trading
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Quantitative researchers and data scientists working in R and RStudio
problem: Quant and data workflows in R lack an integrated AI coding assistant.
business_model: Subscription for an AI enabled IDE (launch pricing $20 per month for 500 queries)
product_category: AI coding assistant for data science and quantitative trading
market_need_then: Cursor style assistants did not serve R users well per the founders' Show HN framing; no spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Lotas launched an RStudio based AI assistant on Hacker News in July 2025 and describes itself as AI for quantitative trading. The site is sparse and no funding, customers or outcome are public, so the story is too early to read; the product's thin moat is the main visible risk.

name: Lua Global Inc
one_liner: The mid-market agent platform
long_description:
Lua is the mid-market agent platform.

We deliver enterprise reliability with the speed, flexibility, and economics that mid-market companies demand - helping them deploy AI agents that drive sales, support, and operations across everyday channels and tools.

We scale through developer agencies and channel partners, enabling rapid distribution without a large enterprise sales motion or scaled forward deployed teams. We think of Lua as an agentOS that abstracts all of the complexity required to launch enterprise grade agents and combine it with the tools needed for these agents to succeed in the real world.

Lua was founded by Lorcan O Cathain (CEO) and Stefan Kruger (CTO)- experienced founders who have spent 15 - 20 years each scaling technology companies across emerging markets.

We sell to mid-market enterprises and developer agencies in the US and internationally. Developers are increasingly our primary ICP but we run SMB & enterprise sales motions to accelerate our learnings and further develop our product:
- SMB ($25- 1k per month): fully automated self-serve agents that handle sales and support for eCommerce companies, hotels, restaurants and general service businesses. If you’ve been on our website you’ve likely seen this.
- Enterprise: We directly sell to mid-market (~ $50M- $1BN) businesses across the US and internationally to eat our own dog food and strengthen our platform.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mid-market companies, developer agencies and SMBs deploying AI agents, with many customers in emerging markets
problem: Mid-market firms lack the engineering or forward deployed teams needed to run enterprise grade AI agents.
business_model: Platform subscriptions (SMB $25 to $1k per month) plus enterprise contracts and channel partners
product_category: AI agent platform
market_need_then: Agent adoption was rising in 2025; Lua cites mid-market demand and lists customers such as CIB and Naivas on its site.
outcome_analysis: Lua raised a $5.8M seed in April 2026 led by Norrsken22, about seven months after the batch, and lists named customers across Africa and the Middle East. Founders bring prior fintech scaling experience including Paystack engineering leadership. It is a promising early company, but outcomes depend on a crowded agent platform market.

name: Lucid
one_liner: interactive video models
long_description:
We are building universe simulations powered by interactive video models.

We train video models that simulate hyper-realistic environments with immersive control, replacing hard-coded game or physics engines with dynamic neural networks.

We built the fastest action-conditioned diffusion video model (running at 20+fps on a 4090 gaming gpu) to simulate minecraft. It is 5x faster than other minecraft World Models and was trained with 100x less resources. Our unique insight was relying on aggressive compression in our tokenizer (128x versus the traditional 8x), and because attention scales quadratically with # of tokens our model can run blindingly faster.

Now we’re training a hyper realistic world model!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Game developers and robotics teams that want fast learned world simulators instead of hand coded engines
problem: Hard coded game and physics engines are expensive to build, and existing neural world models are too slow and compute hungry to run interactively on consumer hardware.
business_model: Not yet clear. Model licensing and fine tuned simulators for gaming and robotics partners were the stated targets.
product_category: Interactive video world models
market_need_then: Interest in world models for games and robot training was rising in late 2024, driven by Oasis and Genie 2. Evidence of paying demand for Lucid itself was not found.
outcome_analysis: Lucid built a technically notable fast Minecraft world model in 2024 and joined YC in Winter 2025 with three people. No funding or exit has been found, and a Roblox post of June 2026 says cofounder Alberto Hojel joined Roblox in late 2025, so the company's current activity and the founder split are unclear. The story is still open, with strong competition from better funded world model labs.

name: Lucidic AI
tags: AIOps; Developer Tools; SaaS; Automation; AI
one_liner: Reimagining how Machines Learn
long_description: Lucidic is trying to find a new paradigm to teach models. The last decade made models intelligent, but intelligence is not the same as experience. Humans do not get better by memorizing thousands of examples; we build learning systems around ourselves: skills, memories, critique, practice, tools, and guidance. And every person learns differently because every task is different. Lucidic brings that idea to AI agents by training a custom learning system for each agent, so it learns what to remember, what skills to build, when to ask for help, and how to improve from experience. The model provides the intelligence, Lucidic gives it a way to learn.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises running AI agents in production who want lower cost per task
problem: Agents do not improve from experience; teams struggle to debug, test and train them from production data.
business_model: Enterprise B2B platform sold by demo (pricing not public)
product_category: AI agent training, evaluation and optimization
founder_names: Abhinav Sinha; Andy Liang; Jeremy Tian
market_need_then: Launch HN (2025-07) said observability users naturally wanted evaluation; demand evidence is anecdotal.
outcome_analysis: Lucidic launched as agent observability in July 2025 and by 2026 pitched agent training with enterprise logos on its site and a SOC badge. Funding is not public, so success is unclear; a crowded observability market pushed a repositioning toward training.

name: Lucis
tags: Telehealth; Digital Health; Health & Wellness; AI
one_liner: Function Health for Europe
long_description: Think Function Health for Europe. We combine medical expertise and AI to transform regular blood testing into actionable insights to help people live healthier, longer.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: European consumers paying for preventive blood testing memberships
problem: People lack regular, interpretable blood biomarker testing; Lucis turns tests into doctor reviewed action plans.
business_model: Annual membership with biomarker panels and AI coach (site shows 199 euros per year; FrenchWeb reported 490 euros)
product_category: Consumer preventive health testing
founder_names: Max Berthelot; Baptiste Debever; Max G.
market_need_then: Function Health style memberships had proven US demand and Europe lacked equivalents; Lucis reports over 10,000 users per press.
outcome_analysis: Lucis copied a proven US model for Europe, raised an $8.5M seed in December 2025 and a $20M Series A in May 2026, and reports over 10,000 users. Speed of fundraising and execution are strong signals, while regulation, pricing and US entrants are the main risks.

name: Lumari
tags: B2B; Manufacturing; Supply Chain; Operations; AI
one_liner: AI Digital Workers for Supply Chain
long_description:
Lumari is the world's first AI-powered procurement automation platform purpose-built for direct materials and supply chain execution. 

Backed by Y Combinator, Lumari is a well-funded startup that deploys 100s of always-on AI agents that run sourcing workflows, manage RFQs, expedite purchase orders, and coordinate supplier communication end-to-end -- compressing cycle times and giving teams full visibility into active orders, RFQs, and supplier performance.

Founded by engineers from Google, Tesla, Amazon, and Stripe who have built and scaled supply chain systems serving millions of users. 

Built to operate directly on top of existing tools and ERP systems, Lumari helps procurement teams move faster, eliminate operational bottlenecks, and build more resilient supply chains. No rip-and-replace, no supplier onboarding. Lumari handles the manual chase: quote follow-ups, PO confirmations, delivery status updates, and risk escalation.

Lumari helps companies from Fortune 500s to fast-growing startups automate work from sourcing to delivery, streamline supplier communication and order management, and bring full visibility to their procurement operations.

To learn more check out https://lumari.ai/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Procurement and supply chain teams at manufacturers buying direct materials (robotics, industrial equipment, medical devices, biotech instruments, automotive).
problem: Procurement staff spend their time chasing RFQ quotes, PO confirmations and delivery updates by email and spreadsheet instead of sourcing.
business_model: B2B SaaS for AI procurement agents layered on ERP, email and Excel (pricing not public)
product_category: AI agents for procurement and supply chain execution
market_need_then: Direct materials procurement is run on email and spreadsheets. The company's site cites customers OFS, Carbon Robotics and Ultima Genomics reporting faster RFQ handling (customer reported).
outcome_analysis: Lumari is a very early Spring 2025 YC company with named industrial customers on its site and ex Google, Stripe and Tesla founders. No funding round, exit or distress is publicly documented as of November 2026, so the outcome is unknown and early.

name: Luminal
tags: AIOps; Developer Tools; Cloud Computing; AI
one_liner: Making AI run fast on any hardware.
long_description:
Luminal builds an ML framework and compiler that generates GPU code.
Our stack 10x's model speed while simplifying deployment and cutting idle GPU costs

Github: https://github.com/luminal-ai/luminal
Discord: https://discord.gg/APjuwHAbGy
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI engineering teams, research labs and startups that run their own models and want faster, cheaper GPU inference.
problem: Most teams using their own models reach only a fraction of GPU utilization, wasting compute spend, and hand tuning CUDA kernels is slow.
business_model: Open source compiler plus usage-based serverless inference cloud and licensed on-prem
product_category: ML compiler and inference infrastructure
founder_names: Joe Fioti; Matthew Gunton; Jake Stevens
competitors_at_founding: Nvidia CUDA toolchain; Baseten; Together AI
market_need_then: Felicis states most teams reach only 10 to 20 percent GPU utilization and neocloud GPU spend was growing fast; the Show HN launch drew developer interest in search-based compilation.
outcome_analysis: Luminal turned an open source search-based compiler into a YC Summer 2025 company and raised a 5.3M seed led by Felicis in November 2025, riding the demand for cheaper GPU inference. Founders have Intel, Amazon and Apple backgrounds. A later round is reported but not verified, so the trajectory is positive but early.

name: LunaBill
tags: Generative AI; Health Tech; Healthcare; Healthcare IT; AI
one_liner: AI Voice callers for healthcare billing teams
long_description:
LunaBill is building AI Voice callers for healthcare billing teams. Insurance claim follow-up calls account for the 80% of the daily workload of a healthcare billing team, with each call averaging 30 minutes.

Since our launch in July we are now at $764K in contracted ARR, of which $428K is live revenue and the rest will go live by January 2026. Our customers see a 10x increase in claims followed up per biller in the first week and we have converted 100% of pilots to paying customers. We have automated 50,000+ calls and signed partnerships with top healthcare systems in the country.

The founders have known each other for over a year. Suhail is a 2x founder, with 3+ years of experience building in healthcare including operating a medical billing company with 200+ healthcare clients. David founded Skiesoft, Taiwan’s biggest healthcare AI scribe company, used by thousands of healthcare professionals. He also worked as a data scientist at UCSF, building models to audit medical-coding accuracy.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hospitals and revenue cycle management firms whose billing teams chase insurance claims by phone.
problem: Claim follow-up calls make up most of a billing team's workload and each call takes around 30 minutes.
business_model: Percentage of net collections recovered, nothing upfront (company site)
product_category: AI voice agents for healthcare revenue cycle
market_need_then: Company reports 764K contracted ARR (428K live) after a July 2025 launch and 100 percent of pilots converting; one customer reports days in AR falling from 45 to 7 (all company reported).
outcome_analysis: LunaBill launched in July 2025 and reports 764K contracted ARR within months, with founders who ran medical billing operations. Funding is not verified and funded competitors such as SuperDial exist, so strong early traction is company reported and the outcome is still open.

name: Lunavo
one_liner: Lunavo is the AI assistant for carriers.
long_description:
We build AI that runs carrier operations.

Lunavo is the AI assistant for carriers. It plugs directly into their existing toolstack, understands their processes, and monitors all incoming data and requests. Lunavo runs end-to-end backoffice operations, handling repetitive tasks, resolving issues autonomously, and escalating only what matters.

Lunavo helps carriers scale operations without scaling headcount.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Trucking carriers and freight forwarders in Germany that run dispatch and back office on a TMS
problem: Carrier back offices spend headcount on repetitive order entry, document handling, quoting, invoice checks and exception emails.
business_model: B2B software subscription for AI agents sold to carriers, pricing not stated
product_category: AI agents for logistics back office
market_need_then: Back office staffing cost in logistics and the arrival of capable LLM agents in 2025. The company claims paying customers in Germany, per a job post, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Lunavo is a Fall 2025 company with two founders and no public funding or exit yet. Its founders combine logistics operating experience with applied AI, which suggests founder market fit, but there is too little evidence for a firm outcome view. The main risks are TMS vendors adding the same features and the breadth of integrations.

name: MOVEdot
one_liner: AI Agents for Hardware Engineering
long_description: Our agents run hardware engineering tasks that normally take hours or days in just a few minutes, allowing engineers to process 100x more data and information. Our platform allows hardware engineers to orchestrate agents for tasks such as analyzing failures across entire test campaigns, pulling the right data and KPIs from their databases, checking how conditions (like temperature or load) affect performance and reliability, and then document findings in reports and dashboards.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hardware and automotive engineering teams, starting with motorsport teams, then OEMs and suppliers.
problem: Engineers spend hours or days analyzing failures across test campaigns and pulling data and KPIs from separate systems and simulation tools.
business_model: Enterprise software platform (moveOS), deployable in the customer's cloud; pricing not public
product_category: AI agents for hardware and automotive engineering data
market_need_then: YC page says the company closed a 30K first deal within two weeks of a proof of concept with Tractian; website lists racing teams such as Arrow McLaren as customers.
outcome_analysis: MOVEdot sells AI agents to motorsport and automotive engineers, a niche where the founders worked for about a decade. Early customers are named on its site. Funding is unverified and no exit or distress is reported, so the outcome is unknown.

name: MSPilot
tags: Generative AI; B2B; No-code; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Turn AI adoption into a recurring revenue line.
long_description:
Make AI your next recurring revenue line.

MSPilot helps Managed Service Providers deploy, govern, and monetize AI agents across their entire client base. Author an agent once, roll it out to your whole book, and bill for every token - with markup.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Managed service providers (MSPs) that want to govern and resell AI to their small business clients.
problem: MSP clients use unmanaged AI tools (shadow AI) and MSPs have no control layer or way to bill for AI usage.
business_model: B2B SaaS for MSPs with usage billing and markup on tokens
product_category: AI governance and agent platform for MSPs
market_need_then: Company site claims 11 MSP logos as customers; no independent demand evidence found.
outcome_analysis: MSPilot is a three person Fall 2025 YC company selling an AI control plane to MSPs, from founders with a prior coding assistant that reached 1.5M installs. No funding, exit or distress is verified, and the founders also list OpenBuilder, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Macadamia
one_liner: AI Agents for Complex Engineering Projects
long_description:
Macadamia builds AI agents for complex engineering projects. 
They automate both engineering & business processes, to automate away all low-leverage work.
It integrates with all engineering data sources, technical documentation, and third-party software tools.
Macadamia serves customers in mechanical engineering, manufacturing, and construction.
regions: Netherlands; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering firms in industrial construction, manufacturing and mechanical engineering
problem: Engineers spend much time on low-leverage work such as drawing checks, cross-referencing P&IDs with equipment lists, cost estimates and data entry.
business_model: Enterprise software selling AI agents as roles (per agent or contract); pricing not found
product_category: AI agents for engineering and back-office workflows
market_need_then: Engineering firms carry heavy documentation and checking workloads and industrial software had little automation; evidence is the company's own positioning, no independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Macadamia is an early Winter 2025 YC company still listed Active with a team of two. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found. Public information is limited to YC pages, job posts and its site, so there is no verified traction, and any assessment of its outcome rests on thin evidence.

name: MadeThis
one_liner: The autonomous business platform
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Solo founders, creators and small businesses wanting to launch and run a business without technical staff.
problem: Starting a business needs a site, incorporation, payments, marketing and operations work that small founders cannot cover.
business_model: Subscription with tiered plans (task limits, number of businesses, domains)
product_category: AI agents that launch and run small businesses
market_need_then: YC page claims over 20,000 businesses launched in 100 days and 100,000s generated (company reported, unverified).
outcome_analysis: MadeThis claims fast user growth for an AI business launching platform in Fall 2025, but no funding, revenue or exit is verified and similar tools were already shipping. The record is too early to judge the outcome.

name: Magnetic
one_liner: AI Tax Preparer for CPA firms
long_description:
Magnetic scans client documents - from handwritten charity notes to excel spreadsheet Schedule Cs to multi-state K-1s - and enters them into tax software automatically, saving hours of tedious data entry. 

The accounting profession is facing a massive talent shortage, as graduates choose different professions and the old guard begins to retire. As a result, CPA and tax preparation firms are awash in clientele, but unable to keep up. At many firms, phones go unanswered, clients are "fired", and websites are taken down, as the existing workforce tries to handle the grueling 80 hour+ weeks necessary to push through tax season to the April 15th deadline.

We built this because a former colleague who owns her own tax firm asked us to automate her workload, and we quickly realized the massive opportunity. Thomas brings deep domain expertise as the former Head of Product at Keeper (YC W19), where he built tax engine automation systems and an OCR form scanning system that outperformed everything else on the market. At Keeper, he leveraged early access to OpenAI's LLMs (well before ChatGPT) to build systems that automated the entire tax filing process, allowing a tiny team of CPAs to process thousands of returns with near zero busy work. Patrick was the first engineer at FunCraft, shipping multiple mobile games with 1M+ downloads and building scalable shared codebases. We've worked together since 2017, including co-leading multiple teams at Zynga as PM & Tech Lead respectively.

The opportunity is massive - there are 80M US personal tax returns filed via professionals annually, in a $2B outsourcing market where individual CPA firms currently pay $100k-$1M per year for inferior services. We're positioned to capture significant market share by offering better accuracy & document coverage, instant processing, and superior user experience.

We've built this kind of software before, we've worked together for years (and even lived together), we've built products to $10M ARR before, and we have the grit to outwork anyone in this space.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: CPA and tax preparation firms that outsource or struggle to staff 1040 return preparation.
problem: A talent shortage leaves firms unable to keep up with returns; manual data entry from client documents consumes the work.
business_model: Per return pricing in credits by complexity, with AI drafting and licensed EA or CPA review
product_category: AI tax return preparation for accounting firms
market_need_then: Company cites 80M US personal returns prepared by professionals and a 2B outsourcing market; a firm owner asked them to automate her workload (YC description).
outcome_analysis: Magnetic moved from document scanning to an AI drafted, human reviewed 1040 service with a 10 dollar accuracy guarantee reported in June 2026. Founders come from Keeper and Zynga. Funding evidence is thin and competitors are well established, so the outcome is still open.

name: Magnitude
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Run open models as fast as your hardware allows
long_description: Magnitude is an open source inference engine that tunes its kernels on your hardware to find the fastest way to run each model. It's over 2x faster than Ollama and works on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, or just a CPU. One click connects it to the agent you already use (Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, and more)
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and agent users who run open models locally on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD or CPU.
problem: Local inference engines are not tuned to each machine, so open models run slower than the hardware allows.
business_model: Open source (Apache 2.0) desktop app and engine; monetization not stated
product_category: Local inference engine for open models
market_need_then: Original browser agent launched on Show HN in mid 2025 and claimed 94 percent on WebVoyager; the inference pivot launched 2026-09-30 claiming over 2x faster than Ollama (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Magnitude began as an open source browser agent in the Summer 2025 batch and by September 2026 had shifted to a local inference engine, facing entrenched open source runtimes. No funding or exit is verified, so the outcome is unknown and the repeated pivots are the main signal.

name: MangoDesk
one_liner: Long-horizon RL environments
long_description: We help AI become better at real-world workflows through production-grade RL environments.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI labs and AI product teams that need custom evals, post-training data and RL environments for specific real-world workflows
problem: Teams improving AI models on specific use cases lack production-grade evals and training environments, and building annotation pipelines with expert annotators by hand is slow.
business_model: B2B services plus software: generated annotation and eval pipelines with a vetted expert annotator pool; pricing not public
product_category: RL environments, evals and human data tooling for AI training
market_need_then: In 2025 AI labs were increasingly buying RL environments and expert data to train agents, and press in September 2025 described heavy investor interest in the category.
outcome_analysis: MangoDesk is a two-person YC Summer 2025 company that moved from a launch pitch of custom evals and human data to a pitch of long-horizon RL environments. It sits in a crowded and fast-moving category where well-funded rivals and Scale AI entered in 2025. The company claims an oversubscribed seed but discloses no amount or investors, and no outcome events were found, so its trajectory cannot be judged yet.

name: Manufact
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Cloud infrastructure for MCP servers and Claude / ChatGPT plugins.
long_description:
Manufact is the MCP cloud platform to get your product ready for Claude Connectors marketplace, ChatGPT / Codex plugins store and any AI agent that supports MCP.
We're the team behind mcp-use SDK, the open-source framework for building MCP Apps with 10k github stars and 10M+ downloads across python and typescript.

It's the fastest and most complete solution for production-ready MCP servers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies that build MCP servers and apps for Claude, ChatGPT and other agent clients
problem: Teams shipping MCP servers need hosting, deployment, analytics, evals and marketplace submission tooling to get production-ready across clients.
business_model: Open-source SDK (mcp-use) with a paid cloud platform for MCP deployment, analytics and evals; pricing not captured
product_category: MCP cloud platform and developer infrastructure
market_need_then: MCP adoption by Claude and ChatGPT in 2025 created demand for deployable servers and marketplace-ready plugins; the SDK passed millions of downloads by early 2026.
outcome_analysis: Manufact grew out of the open-source mcp-use SDK, which gave it developer distribution before the YC Summer 2025 batch. It rode the 2025 MCP adoption wave and raised a $6.3M seed led by Peak XV in February 2026 on the strength of SDK downloads and early customers such as AgentMail. The risk is that hosting is commoditized by larger platforms, but no negative outcome has been reported.

name: Maritime Fusion
one_liner: Fusion reactors for ships
long_description:
Maritime Fusion is building fusion reactors for ships and off grid energy markets. En route on this endeavor we’re commercializing High Temperature Superconducting (HTS) cable technology for power distribution while advancing the physics basis of our HTS tokamak to decarbonize global shipping. 

Breakeven fusion is coming soon, but the first-of-a-kind (FOAK) reactors will be costly, high maintenance, and have low capacity factors, leading to 5–10x higher electricity cost on the grid. Maritime Fusion is pursuing the most widely accepted approach to fusion, the tokamak, but specifically designed for the marine environment where the challenges that arise between breakeven and a commercially viable energy source are alleviated. The market we're targeting requires 15x less power, lower up-time, and costs the same as alternative fuels but without any emissions. Since fusion does not use highly radioactive fuels or materials – unlike fission – we sidestep the vast majority of regulatory challenges and safety risks associated with nuclear energy. Our team brings over a decade of industry and research experience in plasma physics, nuclear engineering, and electrical engineering with backgrounds at SpaceX, Tesla, Columbia University, and University of Pennsylvania.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Commercial shipping operators of very large vessels, militaries with mobile vessels, and off-grid or islanded energy users
problem: Shipping has few decarbonization options at scale, and first-of-a-kind fusion plants on the grid would be costly, so the founders target ships where low power and downtime are tolerable.
business_model: Develop and sell fusion reactors to shipping and off-grid customers; near term revenue from HTS cable technology for power distribution
product_category: Fusion energy hardware (HTS tokamak) and superconducting cable
competitors_at_founding: Commonwealth Fusion Systems; Proxima Fusion; Helion; Ulstein THOR
market_need_then: Shipping faces emissions rules and weak options, with hydrogen and ammonia having density and safety drawbacks per the founders; fusion investment was also rising in 2025.
outcome_analysis: Maritime Fusion picked a niche inside fusion where low power density and downtime are acceptable, and its founders bring SpaceX and Tesla hardware experience plus plasma physics. It raised a $4.5M seed in November 2025 led by Trucks VC with Paul Graham and YC. The physics and magnet risks remain large, and the first ship deployment is targeted around 2032, so success is still unproven.

name: MarkIt
tags: Workflow Automation; Compliance; Consumer Products; AI
one_liner: Compliance that makes products ready for global markets.
long_description: MarkIt is an AI-powered regulatory compliance platform that helps consumer brands launch products in new markets. We review formulations, packaging, and supporting documents against local regulations, identify compliance gaps, and provide the exact changes, regulatory references, and market-ready labels needed before launch. We are initially focused on cosmetics and food products entering the U.S., replacing weeks of manual work across regulatory consultants, spreadsheets, and disconnected vendors with one actionable compliance workflow.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Consumer brands and product teams, initially cosmetics and OTC products, launching in new markets
problem: Brands review formulations, packaging and claims against local rules through consultants and spreadsheets over weeks before launching in a new market.
business_model: B2B SaaS compliance workspace per product review; pricing not public
product_category: AI regulatory and label compliance for consumer products
market_need_then: US cosmetics companies faced new FDA rules (MoCRA) and brands entering markets faced label and ingredient rules; the company positions manual consultant work as the pain.
outcome_analysis: MarkIt is a very young Fall 2025 YC company with a small team building AI compliance checks for consumer product launches. No funding amount, customers or outcome events are verifiably public, and the crowded field of label compliance vendors and YC peers makes the wedge competitive. The evidence is too thin to say whether it will stall or succeed.

name: Mastra
one_liner: The Javascript framework for building AI agents, from the Gatsby devs
long_description: Mastra is the easiest way to build a production AI application, built by the team that brought you Gatsby. We provide a complete set of AI primitives: workflows for complex operations, agents for autonomous decisions, RAG for knowledge integration, and evals for quality & accuracy. Mastra is open-source, modular, and built in Typescript for product developers. You can deploy Mastra on any cloud, and it gives you a straightforward syntax to solve the hardest problems building with AI: human-in-the-loop workflows, agent memory and tool selection, and output quality.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Product developers and companies building AI agents and workflows in TypeScript
problem: Building production AI applications needs agents, workflows, memory, RAG, evals and observability, and most frameworks were Python-first.
business_model: Open-source framework (Apache 2.0) with paid hosted platform and enterprise features
product_category: AI agent framework and platform
founder_names: Sam Bhagwat; Abhi Aiyer; Shane Thomas
