outcome_analysis: Mastra pairs founders who already scaled the open-source Gatsby framework with the 2025 surge in agent building. It grew quickly by open source and free distribution of its book, with named usage at Replit, SoftBank and others, raised a $13M seed in October 2025 and a $22M Series A led by Spark Capital in April 2026. The main risk is overlap with LangChain and Vercel.

name: Maximal
one_liner: Truckload Planning at Machine Precision
long_description:
Maximal is building autonomous systems to plan and move the world's freight.

Our first product is a context-aware algorithmic load planning platform for full truckload (FTL) carriers. Our agents plug into a carrier's existing ERPs and communication channels, using that context to generate holistically optimized load plans. The result: carriers earn more revenue-per-mile while spending less time planning.

Our founding team
* grew up in 3PLs and trucking companies
* studied the math behind transportation science at Cornell, Columbia, and USC
* developed the technology that optimizes Amazon's distribution and fulfillment center network
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Asset-based full truckload carriers and fleets
problem: Carriers plan loads manually or with basic TMS tools, losing revenue per mile and spending planner time that algorithmic planning could save.
business_model: B2B software and agents for carriers with pilot-first pricing
product_category: Logistics AI: load planning, dispatch automation
market_need_then: Truckload carriers run thin margins and the company claims planners spend large time on manual planning; TMS vendors added AI planning in late 2025, indicating demand.
outcome_analysis: Maximal is a three-person YC Summer 2025 company with founders who know trucking and optimization and a site that lists several carrier customers, though no funding is verifiable. It faces TMS vendors and Optym shipping AI planning in the same months, so the wedge depends on execution and integrations. No outcome event has been reported, so the story is still open.

name: Mayflower
one_liner: AI plug-in that automates HR immigration screening and compliance
long_description: Mayflower is building an AI-powered HR plug-in that automates immigration screening, eligibility checks, and compliance for global candidates. The platform parses documents, classifies visa pathways, and generates attorney-ready forms. By integrating directly with existing HR systems, Mayflower helps companies surface only compliant candidates, reduce legal risk, and streamline the international hiring process.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: HR teams and employers hiring international candidates
problem: Screening candidates for visa eligibility and compliance is manual and creates legal risk when hiring across borders.
business_model: B2B SaaS plug-in for HR systems; pricing not public
product_category: AI immigration screening and compliance for HR
market_need_then: Employers face legal exposure when hiring global candidates and the company cites manual screening; SHRM coverage describes workplace immigration technology as booming.
outcome_analysis: Mayflower is a two-person Fall 2025 YC company building an HR plug-in for immigration screening. No verified funding, customers or outcome events are public, and larger mobility and legal vendors are adding similar AI tools. There is not enough evidence to judge whether it will stall or succeed.

name: Mbodi AI
one_liner: Industrial Robots that Learn and Operate Like Humans
long_description:
Teach robots new skills through natural language and run reliably in production in minutes.

Mbodi combines generative AI and agent orchestration, turning everyday language and quick demos into precise, reliable robot actions for industrial automation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Industrial and logistics operators deploying collaborative robots, initially for picking and packing, with ABB Robotics as a channel partner
problem: Industrial robots need slow, brittle programming and downtime for each new task, so Mbodi lets operators teach skills with language and short demonstrations.
business_model: B2B robot software and agents sold with partners such as ABB; pricing not public
product_category: Embodied AI and robot skill learning for industrial automation
market_need_then: Industrial robots remain hard to reprogram while generative AI advanced; the founders cite brittle code and long deployment cycles as the pain.
outcome_analysis: Mbodi has early traction signals: an ABB commercialization agreement after ABB's AI Startup Challenge, a pharma pilot reported in 2026 and the Automate 2026 Startup Challenge win. Its funding is not verifiable from primary sources, and well-funded robot foundation model players raise the competitive bar. The story is still early and no failure or exit has been reported.

name: Mecha Health
tags: Machine Learning; Computer Vision; Health Tech; Healthcare; AI
one_liner: Foundation models to automate x-ray analysis for radiologists
long_description:
Mecha Health builds foundation models to automate x-ray analysis for radiologists. We take medical images and process them using proprietary models to produce accurate draft medical reports. Our first model was built in less than two months, and beat Microsoft, Google, and OpenAI on clinical accuracy metrics. On top of that, it’s two orders of magnitude smaller and trained with a quarter of the data.

We are partnering with the largest privately owned radiology practice in the US and a multinational tele-radiology company to provide them with their own foundation model, enabling their radiologists to go from reading 1 scan per hour to 1 scan every 5 minutes. By charging on a per scan basis, x-ray report generation represents a 40B+ market opportunity.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Radiology practices and tele-radiology companies that pay per scan for draft x-ray reports
problem: Radiologists spend most of their time drafting reports for routine x-rays, which limits throughput. Mecha builds foundation models that turn images into draft reports for radiologist review.
business_model: Usage-based per scan pricing, with a custom foundation model per large radiology customer
product_category: Medical imaging AI, radiology report generation
founder_names: Ahmed Abdulaal; Hugo Fry; Ayodeji Ijishakin; Nina Montaña Brown
market_need_then: Radiologist shortage and growing scan volume. The company claims a 40B plus per scan opportunity and cites partnerships with the largest privately owned US radiology practice and a multinational tele-radiology firm (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Mecha is active and early. A four person team of UCL researchers and a physician built a radiology foundation model, joined YC in Winter 2025 and announced a 4.1M seed in November 2025 led by Valia Ventures. The main risks are regulatory clearance, large lab competition and proving per scan revenue beyond two pilot partners, none of which has resolved yet.

name: Mentra
tags: Hardware; Consumer; Open Source; AI; AR
one_liner: Building the open source smart glasses operating system.
long_description: Mentra is building the open source operating system for smart glasses. The smart glasses hardware is finally ready, so we're building the OS and app store to power the next computing platform.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Smart glasses developers and enterprise frontline teams buying camera glasses and the MentraOS software
problem: Each smart glasses maker ships a closed software stack, so developers rebuild apps per device. Mentra offers one open source OS and app store that runs across glasses.
business_model: Hardware sales (Mentra Live glasses) plus open core software with paid cloud plans and an app store
product_category: Smart glasses operating system and hardware
market_need_then: Smart glasses hardware matured by 2024 and 2025 (Ray-Ban Meta, Even Realities G1), but developers lacked a cross device OS. The company cites interest from hundreds of companies per a secondary source.
outcome_analysis: Mentra is active and early. It raised an 8M seed announced in June 2025 from YC, Toyota Ventures, the Amazon Alexa Fund and well known angels, shipped MentraOS 2.0 and then Mentra Live glasses in 2026. It positions toward enterprise frontline use. Main risks are hardware economics and Meta and Google dominating the glasses platform, and no later round was found.

name: Mercura
one_liner: AI quote & order processing for technical distributors & manufacturers
long_description:
Mercura is the AI platform for quote and order processing for technical distributors and manufacturers: it reads incoming requests, matches every line item to the right product and turns them into ERP-ready quotes and orders.

Requests arrive as e-mails, PDFs, scans, Excel lists, bills of quantities and GAEB tenders. Sales teams review every quote before it goes out, and the result is written straight into their ERP. Built for distributors and manufacturers in HVAC and plumbing, electrical, building materials, building services and industrial supplies.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Technical distributors and manufacturers in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, building materials and industrial supplies
problem: Sales teams manually read emails, PDFs, scans and tenders, match each line to a product and key it into the ERP, so quotes take days. Mercura automates this with human review.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for quote and order processing integrated with the customer ERP
product_category: Vertical AI for quoting and order entry
founder_names: Lukas Bock; Stefan Zheng; Sean Sdahl; Hai Dang
market_need_then: Distributor sales teams handle high volumes of unstructured requests. The company cites customers cutting quote time from 2 days to 2 hours (self reported) and the YC pitch is quotes in minutes not days.
outcome_analysis: Mercura is active. A Munich team with an insider CEO from the trades built an AI quoting product, was profitable before raising any outside capital per company information, and announced a seed of about 1.8M euros in January 2026 from TQ Ventures and SignalFire. It claims 80 plus customers in 20 plus countries. The open question is whether it can scale against ERP and CPQ vendors that moved into AI quoting in 2026.

name: Mesh
one_liner: Eliminating accrual spreadsheets for faster month-end
long_description:
Month-end shouldn’t be a race against the clock.

For most mid-to-enterprise finance teams, accruals are a manual bottleneck. Chasing missing invoices and manually updating spreadsheets can eat up 4+ days of every month-end close.

Mesh changes the timeline. We automate 90% of the accruals process by capturing real-time usage and service signals directly from your AP inbox, Slack, Teams, and historical journals. We turn fragmented data into audit-ready outputs, so you can stop guessing and start closing.

See how top teams are accelerating their close by 4+ days at www.usemesh.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mid size to enterprise finance and accounting teams that close books monthly
problem: Accruals need chasing missing invoices and updating spreadsheets, which can take 4 plus days of month-end close. Mesh pulls usage and service signals from AP inbox, Slack, Teams and journals to produce audit ready accruals.
business_model: B2B SaaS for finance teams
product_category: AI accounting automation, accruals
market_need_then: Finance teams report accruals as a manual bottleneck. The company claims accruals consume 4 plus days of close and that its customers close faster.
outcome_analysis: Mesh is active and early with a three person team led by two former Carta accounting automation builders. No funding announcement was found, so outcome cannot be judged. The wedge is real but crowded, with close automation vendors and larger platforms adding accrual agents, and the generic name overlaps with Mesh Payments.

name: Mesmer
one_liner: We build software factories for engineering teams
long_description:
Mesmer builds software factories for engineering teams. Keeping a team at the state of the art with agents has become a full-time job, and the target keeps moving. We do that job for our customers: we're always finding the biggest bottleneck in how their team ships and fixing it in their factory.

We're repeat founders and CTOs in Berlin, backed by YC, GFC and 468 Capital.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Engineering organizations and CTOs at growth stage software companies
problem: Teams struggle to keep up with fast changing AI coding tools and to find their real delivery bottleneck. Mesmer first reported on engineering work and now ships fixes into customer codebases as pull requests.
business_model: B2B services plus software, monthly improvement cycle per customer with demo led sales
product_category: Engineering intelligence and agentic engineering services
founder_names: João de Paula; Sergio Oliveira Bergmann; Lucas Silva
market_need_then: AI coding tools changed how engineering teams work in 2025, and the company says leaders lack visibility. Launch coverage claims 70M lines of code reviewed and 10 plus live customers (secondary source, unverified).
outcome_analysis: Mesmer is active. Repeat founders from Origin Financial launched in YC Spring 2025 as Cursor for CTOs, claimed fast early traction and later shifted from reporting to hands on engineering fixes. Backers per the YC page are YC, GFC and 468 Capital but no round size is confirmed. The risk is that analytics vendors and AI coding tool makers absorb the offering.

name: Meteor Labs
one_liner: We provide hedge funds with information they can trade on
long_description:
Meteor Labs is a research company focused on providing a granular view of the data center supply chain.

We track upstream of the major data center buildout to understand the OEMs winning the market, the bottlenecks, and supply chain links.

Our expertise in browser agents and AI helps us source this information from esoteric public filings across the web.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hedge funds, private equity and infrastructure investors, consultants and equipment makers buying data center supply chain research
problem: Investors lack granular, early data on data center buildout bottlenecks such as generators, power equipment, memory and project delays. Meteor Labs extracts it from public filings with browser agents.
business_model: Subscription research and data product sold to investors
product_category: Alternative data, data center supply chain intelligence
competitors_at_founding: Perplexity Comet; The Browser Company Dia
market_need_then: In 2025 the AI browser category was heating up, and later AI data center buildout drove investor demand for supply chain data. The company's site cites coverage of 500 plus US data center projects (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Meteor Labs is active with two founders. The YC Summer 2025 launch was an agentic browser covered by GeekWire, and the company now sells data center supply chain research to investors with notes published in October 2026. No funding round or revenue was verified, so no outcome verdict is possible, and the pivot reason and date are not public.

name: Method
one_liner: Agents that improve
long_description: Method turns repeated work into workflows your coding agent can run, check, and improve.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and startups using coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) who want repeatable, checked workflows
problem: Coding agents patch single cases, drop instructions or write brittle checks. Method turns a repeated task into a workflow with checks and run records so the agent can improve it.
business_model: Freemium developer tool: free plan, 500 USD per month Startup plan, open source CLI
product_category: Developer tooling for agent workflows
market_need_then: Coding agent use exploded in 2025. The company argues agents fail at consistent repeated work. No customer evidence found.
outcome_analysis: Method is listed as active with a team of one and no verified funding. The YC listing combines Method with an earlier or parallel product, Zenobia Pay, and the current site sells an agent workflow tool. With no revenue, customers or round found, and an unclear pivot, no outcome judgment can be made beyond the high copy risk from agent vendors.

name: Metis
one_liner: Infrastructure to build reliable agents
long_description: We build infrastructure enabling AI agents to reliably perform complex tasks in production
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Enterprises and AI labs deploying agents in production
problem: AI agents fail on complex multi-step tasks in production and companies lack tooling to train and evaluate them on their own data.
business_model: Enterprise software and services for agent post-training, private beta
product_category: AI agent infrastructure and post-training
founder_names: Aryan Shah; Aayush Sheth; Marcus Yearwood
market_need_then: In 2025 companies were moving agents into production and complaining about reliability, which drove demand for evaluation and agent training tools. No customer evidence for Metis was found.
outcome_analysis: Metis joined YC in Summer 2025 as a thirteen person team building agent reliability infrastructure and later described itself as an agent post-training lab. The YC directory lists it as acquired but no acquirer, date or terms were found in two searches. With no public cause or deal facts, no success or failure factors are asserted.

name: Metorial
one_liner: Agentic infrastructure to power AI-native companies.
long_description: Metorial gives every employee, agent, and AI client in your company one place to connect tools and skills. Governance, access control, and tracing included.
regions: Austria; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers building AI agents and companies that want governed access to tools via MCP
problem: Connecting agents and AI clients to many tools through MCP needs hosting, auth, access control and logging. Metorial provides an open source gateway with one URL, SSO, role based access and tracing.
business_model: Open core with cloud usage plans: free Dev, 250 USD per month Scale, custom Enterprise
product_category: AI agent infrastructure, MCP gateway
market_need_then: MCP adoption surged through 2025 and developers needed hosting and security for servers. The YC launch and Show HN (2025-10-14) pitched Vercel for MCP.
outcome_analysis: Metorial is active and early. Two long time friends who ran Valicit launched an open source MCP platform from YC Fall 2025, got Forbes and Hacker News attention, and later repositioned toward an enterprise MCP and skills gateway. No funding round was confirmed from a primary source, and a crowded field of funded MCP infrastructure startups is the main risk.

name: Mimos
one_liner: The growth OS for plaintiff-side law firms
long_description:
Plaintiff-side law firms compete in some of the most expensive search ad markets to acquire high-intent leads, but the path from click, call, or form fill to signed retainer is still fragmented. Disconnected intake workflows, slow response times, and disconnected spend-to-case data makes it hard to know what is actually working.

Mimos automates their growth and intake playbook:
1. Generate Qualified Leads: Our agents manage Google Ads, Local Services Ads, Google Business Profile, and other high-intent acquisition channels.
2. Convert Faster: Every lead flows into a CRM built for intake, triage, follow-up, and handoff from inquiry to signed retainer.
3. Close the Loop: We connect spend, lead source, intake actions, and signed-case outcomes so firms know what to scale, pause, or fix.

The result: more qualified leads, less wasted spend, and more signed cases.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Plaintiff-side personal injury and employment law firms, plus agencies and MSOs that run several firms
problem: Plaintiff firms pay heavily for search ad leads, but the path from click or call to signed retainer is fragmented, with slow intake and no link between spend and signed cases.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus managed ad acquisition for law firms
product_category: Legal growth and intake software
market_need_then: Plaintiff firms buy expensive high intent search leads and lose cases to slow response and poor spend tracking, per the company's launch pitch. Independent demand data was not found.
outcome_analysis: Mimos is an active two person YC S25 company with no reported exit, shutdown or layoffs. It appears to have moved from answer engine optimization for regulated firms to a plaintiff law firm growth and intake product, where well funded intake specialists and legal CRMs are already shipping AI features. No traction numbers or priced rounds are public, so the outcome is unknown.

name: MindFort
tags: Developer Tools; Cybersecurity; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Autonomous Security Swarms
long_description:
MindFort is a security swarm platform that makes it easy for teams to run continuous security testing across all their applications and services. Our fully autonomous agents powered by our in-house models that can find, exploit, and patch complex vulnerabilities in web applications at massive scale. 

MindFort swarms use the same principles as human penetration testers to understand their target and figure out the best ways to work together to exploit it.

While security teams were already behind with legacy tools and processes, AI coding is make the problem worse. AI generates code far faster than human teams can secure it; MindFort can match that speed and scale. Our agents will become critical as organizations scale up development with AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Security teams at companies shipping web applications, buying continuous automated penetration testing
problem: AI assisted coding ships code faster than human security teams can test it, and scanners give many false positives.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for autonomous pentesting agents
product_category: AI autonomous penetration testing
founder_names: Brandon Veiseh; Akul Gupta; Sam (last name not listed)
market_need_then: Founders cite AI coding outpacing security review. Pentest budgets are large and manual testing is slow, but figures here are company claims.
outcome_analysis: MindFort is a young company that raised a reported seed of about 3 million dollars in April 2026 led by Soma Capital after the Spring 2025 batch. The founders bring offensive security and AI research backgrounds and the market tailwind of AI generated code is real. The main risk is crowding by better funded autonomous pentest rivals, so the outcome is still open.

name: Minerva
one_liner: AI native financial institution
long_description: We’re making financial services fast and affordable for everyone, starting with accounting.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and midsize businesses and accounting firms that need bookkeeping, reconciliation and tax filing
problem: Small businesses find accounting slow and expensive. Minerva offers an AI accountant that automates bookkeeping, reconciliation and tax filing, sitting on top of existing ledgers.
business_model: Tech enabled accounting service, subscription pricing (exact pricing not found)
product_category: AI accounting and financial services
market_need_then: Small business accounting is costly and slow; the company claimed accountants would be largely replaced within about a decade (May 2025 coverage). Independent demand data not collected.
outcome_analysis: Minerva is an active five person YC Spring 2025 company still hiring a financial controller. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found. It competes against well funded AI accounting players, and its funding is unclear, so there is not enough evidence to call the outcome either way.

name: Minimal AI
one_liner: AI Agents for E-commerce Customer Support
long_description: Minimal AI makes it easy for e-commerce brands to build and manage AI support teams that resolve 90%+ of tickets while increasing revenue.
regions: Netherlands; Europe
target_customer: E-commerce brands, many on Shopify, that run customer support through helpdesks such as Zendesk and Gorgias
problem: E-commerce support teams drown in repetitive tickets. Minimal AI builds AI agents that resolve tickets end to end across email, chat, WhatsApp and social and take actions in Shopify and similar systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI support agents
product_category: AI customer support agents for e-commerce
market_need_then: E-commerce brands handle large volumes of repetitive tickets; the company claims 80% lower cost per ticket and up to 90% automation (company claims, not independently verified).
outcome_analysis: Minimal AI went through YC Summer 2025 and raised a reported $3.6M seed in March 2026, with named customers and a LangChain case study showing early production use. It faces both helpdesk incumbents and well funded AI vendors, so the main risk is competition. No exit or shutdown found; the outcome is still open.

name: Miniswap
one_liner: The Marketplace for Complex Hobbies
long_description:
Miniswap a marketplace for complex hobbies, starting with Warhammer.

In hobbies as complex as Warhammer, finding what you want on general marketplaces is a huge pain. Filters don't work, free-form listings mean that products are regularly misidentified, and piles of counterfeit junk crowd search results. 

Miniswap saves hobbyists from this chaos with its catalogue of more than 20,000 unique miniatures. Sellers match their listings against Miniswap's catalogue giving buyers more information and structure as they shop.

The global market for tabletop games is estimated to be worth $20B in 2025 and Warhammer alone is projected to grow to $3B by 2030. By capturing the market in this untapped niche, Miniswap is strongly positioned to bringing greater transparency, simplicity, and connectivity into adjacent verticals.

Miniswap's founding team merges deep domain knowledge with elite programming expertise and years of experience in business consulting and startups. Co-founders Zak and Will met while studying together at Cambridge, bonded over their love of Warhammer and early modern history. They have been best friends ever since.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Warhammer hobbyists who buy and sell miniatures, starting with Games Workshop products
problem: General marketplaces misidentify miniatures, have weak filters and are crowded with counterfeits. Miniswap matches listings to a catalogue of more than 20,000 miniatures so buyers can search by attributes.
business_model: Marketplace take rate
product_category: Niche hobby marketplace
competitors_at_founding: eBay; Facebook Marketplace and groups; Wargame Trader
market_need_then: Hobbyists complain about misidentified listings and counterfeits on general marketplaces; the YC launch post reports 1,000 sign-ups and over $40k of listed inventory in four weeks.
outcome_analysis: Miniswap is an active two person YC Fall 2025 company that raised a reported $3.5M seed in December 2025 and has early community traction. The founders are lifelong Warhammer players, which gives domain insight. The outcome depends on building marketplace liquidity against eBay and Facebook; no exit or failure found.

name: Minro
one_liner: Identify churn risk and stay close to users at scale
long_description:
Minro helps companies stay close to their users as they scale.

Today, most startups have thousands of product events flowing through tools like PostHog, but still have no real understanding of who their users actually are, which users are quietly about to churn, or what outreach actually brings them back. Founders care deeply about their users, but staying close to them becomes operationally impossible very quickly.

Minro plugs directly into a company’s analytics stack and turns product activity into living customer intelligence. We enrich every user with context like their company, role, LinkedIn/GitHub/Twitter, background, and likely use case, currently matching users to the correct online identity with ~80% accuracy starting from just name + email.

We then identify which users are most likely to churn based on behavioral patterns, persona similarity, and historical retention signals, and help founders proactively reach out before those users disappear. Minro drafts highly contextual founder-style outreach, tracks which conversations actually convert into retention, and continuously improves the system over time.

The result is a customer intelligence and retention layer that helps companies understand their users better, build stronger relationships, and reduce churn before it happens.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Startups and SaaS teams that track product events in tools like PostHog
problem: Founders cannot stay close to thousands of users. Minro enriches each user with identity context, predicts churn risk from behavior and drafts founder style outreach to retain them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription
product_category: Customer intelligence and churn prevention
market_need_then: Startups collect product events but lack user context; the need is asserted in the company's pitch and one customer quote, with no independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Minro is an active two person YC Fall 2025 company with no public funding, exit or shutdown. It sells a churn and outreach layer into a market where established customer success vendors all added AI agents. With no traction numbers public, the outcome cannot yet be judged.

name: Misprint
one_liner: Misprint is building Robinhood for Pokemon cards
long_description:
Misprint is an all-in-one marketplace that solves the biggest pain point in the collectibles world: opaque pricing. Collectors, investors, and hobbyists currently rely on scattered data from auction houses, online forums, and reseller platforms, making it difficult to know the true value of their items. Misprint streamlines the process by combining accurate pricing analytics with a seamless buy/sell marketplace, making it easier than ever to understand and monetize collectible assets.

Existing marketplaces lack robust, real-time analytics because accurate valuations require deep expertise in both the collectibles domain and advanced pricing algorithms. Misprint’s unique blend of insider trading card knowledge and machine learning allows us to fill this gap.

Building these pricing models requires extensive data infrastructure, deep domain expertise, and cutting-edge ML. Recent surges in the trading card market show that collectors crave transparent valuations.

The global collectibles market is worth tens of billions of dollars. Eva has experienced the scale of this industry firsthand, generating $500k ARR within three months of taking her Pokemon card-selling side hustle full-time. With additional segments like sports cards, comics, and emerging collectible categories, the growth runway is immense.

Co-founders Eva and Jon have been best friends since Exeter, combining finance expertise, a passion for collectibles, and mathematical rigor. By merging Goldman Sachs-level financial analytics with top-tier mathematical talent, Misprint is uniquely positioned to become the go-to platform for fair, transparent pricing in the collectibles space.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pokemon card collectors, investors and sellers, especially graded and sealed products
problem: Collectible pricing is opaque and scattered across auction houses and forums. Misprint combines pricing analytics with a bid and ask marketplace.
business_model: Marketplace take rate
product_category: Collectibles marketplace and pricing
market_need_then: Collectors complain of opaque prices; the founder reports $500k ARR from her own card selling in three months (company claim). Trading card demand was rising per the company pitch.
outcome_analysis: Misprint is an active four person YC Winter 2025 company whose CEO built a card selling business before founding it, a strong domain fit. No funding amounts, exit or shutdown are public. It competes against TCGplayer, eBay and Whatnot, so liquidity is the central risk and the outcome is still open.

name: Mixy
one_liner: Make mashups without knowing how to DJ
long_description:
Live out your DJ dreams with Mixy, the mind-blowing music app that lets you mash-up any song in seconds.

⁕ Add your songs
⁕ Instantly blend vocals and beats
⁕ Play and share your mashup anywhere

There’s no limit to your imagination!

⁕ Launched to #1 in Music on June 19th
⁕ 1.5M users in 3 months
⁕ 15M mashups made and growing
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Consumers who want to make and share music mashups without DJ skills, paying by subscription
problem: Making mashups needs DJ skills and tools. Mixy blends vocals and beats of any songs in seconds on an iPhone.
business_model: Consumer subscription app
product_category: Consumer music creation app
market_need_then: Strong consumer pull shown by usage: the YC page reports 1.5M users in 3 months and a #1 Music ranking on 2025-06-19, with 350k pre-orders from TikTok prototypes per Know Your Meme coverage.
outcome_analysis: Mixy launched an iOS mashup app on 2025-06-19 after a TikTok prototype campaign, reached the top of the Music chart and reports 1.5M users and about $20k MRR in the YC listing. The founders have a long consumer app history. The open risks are music licensing and platform dependency; no exit or shutdown found.

name: Miyagi Labs
one_liner: AI tutors for exam prep
long_description:
Miyagi Labs is an AI-powered exam preparation platform built to unlock human intelligence and democratize world-class education globally. We provide students with an elite AI tutor, hyper-personalized study analytics, and an infinite engine of rigorous practice material tailored to exam material.

We currently support major standardized exams across North America, Europe, Africa, and Asia, including the SAT, ACT, and NYC SHSAT (US), the UTME (Nigeria), the KCSE, KJSEA and KPSEA (Kenya), the NEET and CAT (India), and the YKS (Turkey).

We’re building the platform we wish we had when studying for exams. We envision a world where students anywhere can come to Miyagi to receive personalized, world-class AI tutoring designed to unlock their full potential.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Students preparing for standardized exams such as SAT, ACT, SHSAT, UTME, KCSE, NEET and YKS
problem: Students lack affordable personalized tutoring and endless tailored practice material for high-stakes exams.
business_model: Consumer subscription for AI tutor, question bank and practice exams
product_category: AI exam preparation and tutoring
market_need_then: Large exam-taking populations in several countries and the arrival of capable LLMs; the company's site claims 150K+ students.
outcome_analysis: Miyagi Labs joined YC in Winter 2025 with a YouTube to course tool and now sells an AI tutor for exam prep across several countries, with a mobile app and claims of 150K students. Funding appears small and unverified, and incumbents like Khan Academy plus general chatbots are the main threat. It is too early to call the outcome.

name: Moby Analytics
one_liner: AI financial auditors
long_description: At Moby Analytics, we provide the first AI agentic platform built for financial auditors. Auditors easily create and deploy AI agents to automate audit workflows. No code, just prompts and domain expertise.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Audit firms and financial advisors that work in Microsoft Excel
problem: Auditors repeat manual testing, ledger analysis and statement tie-outs. Moby provides AI agents inside Excel that automate these tasks with every figure linked to its source for review and sign off.
business_model: B2B SaaS per user licence, Essential plan about 348 EUR per user per year, custom enterprise plan from 50 licences
product_category: AI audit automation
founder_names: Dimitri Kassubeck; Thomas Rapilly; Clement Sengelen
market_need_then: Founders ran a data analytics agency that trained hundreds of auditors before building the product (YC launch post), showing direct exposure to demand; independent spend data not collected.
outcome_analysis: Moby Analytics is an active YC Spring 2025 company selling an Excel add-in to auditors, listed on Microsoft AppSource with published pricing. It shares its category with DataSnipper, which shipped agents with Microsoft later in 2025. Funding is only reported by aggregators and no exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is still open.

name: Modelence
one_liner: Production infrastructure on autopilot
long_description:
You built your product in a weekend and deployed to Vercel, Supabase, Railway or AWS. Now you need to figure out how to pick the right region, scale to multiple instances, add monitoring and alerts, and who to ping when something breaks… and you don't have a cloud engineer.

We spent a decade at our previous startup (CodeSignal), building a $500M platform while scaling to millions of users and customers like Meta & Netflix. Now we're standardizing how web applications are operated in production, so developers can build reliable production apps without becoming cloud infrastructure experts.

Modelence is a production cloud that's designed for enterprise-grade apps, abstracting away the infrastructure layer:
- Deployments & hosting
- Background jobs and persistence
- File storage, real-time data and networking
- Monitoring and alerts

Platforms like Vercel and Supabase are easy to start with, but most companies that start getting real customers eventually need a persistent backend where processes can run beyond just a few minutes at a time, unlike pure serverless. And low-level cloud platforms like AWS are meant to be operated by cloud engineers and are too complicated for engineers who want to focus on product rather than infra. Modelence is your managed backend infrastructure, built on decades of our experience operating web apps in the cloud.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Small teams and startups that built an app quickly (often AI-assisted) and need production hosting, jobs, storage and monitoring without a cloud engineer
problem: Teams that ship a prototype on Vercel, Supabase, Railway or AWS then struggle to run it in production with regions, scaling, monitoring and alerts.
business_model: Managed cloud platform with a free hobby tier and paid usage and resource plans; open source web framework as the funnel
product_category: Developer infrastructure, managed backend cloud
market_need_then: Vibe coding and AI-assisted app building in 2025 produced many prototypes that need production operations; the company cites the gap between simple serverless and complex AWS.
outcome_analysis: Modelence is active and raised a $3M seed in January 2026 led by YC after its Summer 2025 batch. Founders with a decade at CodeSignal give credible infrastructure experience and the vibe coding wave created demand, but strong incumbents such as Vercel, Supabase and Railway make defensibility the main open question.

name: Monarcha
one_liner: Turn maps into data
long_description:
Monarcha is an AI-powered georeferencing platform built for mining, infrastructure, and land intelligence teams. It turns scanned maps, plats, and land documents into accurate, queryable spatial data in seconds.

Aligning historical maps, plats, and survey drawings to real-world coordinates is tedious work. Most teams either hire specialists or skip it entirely, leaving critical spatial data locked in documents.

Monarcha lets users upload any document and get a fully georeferenced, queryable GIS layer in 90 seconds or less.

Want to learn more? Check out monarcha.ai
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mining, infrastructure and land intelligence teams (as launched in 2025)
problem: Scanned maps, plats and survey drawings must be aligned to real coordinates by hand or by specialists, leaving spatial data locked in documents.
business_model: B2B SaaS (pricing not found)
product_category: AI georeferencing and GIS platform
market_need_then: YC page says teams hire specialists or skip georeferencing. No dated spend data found.
outcome_analysis: Monarcha is a two person Summer 2025 company that launched an AI georeferencing product for mining and land teams. By late 2026 its own site describes a large tabular model for enterprise data and lists georeferencing as a separate product, which suggests a repositioning, though no source explains it. No verified funding or outcome is public, so there is not enough evidence to judge success or failure.

name: Monte
one_liner: Specialized Models for Agents
long_description: Monte is an applied research lab building products for model post-training and continual learning.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies that want proprietary models trained on their own data and workflows
problem: Generic frontier models underperform on company specific work; teams lack the tooling to build training environments, post-train open-weight models and keep retraining from production traces.
business_model: Applied research lab selling a model post-training platform with hands on partnership
product_category: Model post-training and continual learning infrastructure
market_need_then: Demand for custom agents and enterprise adoption of open-weight models, plus a wave of RL environment startups in the same YC batch, signaled interest in post-training tools.

name: MorphoAI
one_liner: Software tool for designing robots and machines
long_description:
MorphoAI builds hardware foundation models for mechanical engineering. Our GPU-accelerated design models that let engineers generate and explore hundreds of complete mechanical assembly designs in minutes, accelerating the invention of new hardware. Our models learns from a company’s prior CAD designs and generate editable assemblies from engineering requirements, incorporating standard and custom components and manufacturing constraints. This enables companies to design and ship the next generation of their hardware faster and better than competition.

The models can generate assemblies with up to 500 parts in minutes, including a full bill of materials. Engineers can explore 100s of design options at the beginning of a project and refine and validate the outputs within their existing CAD.

MorphoAI’s technology builds on research conducted by its team at MIT and Harvard, with support from ARIA, the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency with a GBP 2.5M grant. Its customer list includes companies like ABB and other large OEMs in robotics and automation, electric, power and grid, consumer electronics, and industrial equipment. 

Ayna and Andy, the co-founders, met during their time at Harvard and started this in 2024. Our founding team is built of a prof. of ECE and robotics at Carnegie Mellon, Forbes u30 serial hardware entrepreneur, and an ex. Amazon Robotics scientist. Between them, they have written 65+ papers on algorithms for hardware design during their PhDs at Harvard and MIT. The team at large holds PhDs from Imperial, TU Wein, UCL and has worked across computational geometry, computer vision, ML, optimization, simulation, and the CAD space.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Mechanical and robotics engineering teams at large OEMs in robotics, automation, power and grid, consumer electronics and industrial equipment
problem: Designing mechanical assemblies and robots is slow and manual; engineers explore few options early in a project.
business_model: Enterprise software licensing for generative hardware design models integrated with customer CAD (pricing not public)
product_category: Generative AI for mechanical engineering and CAD

name: Moss
one_liner: Real-time semantic search for Conversational AI
long_description:
Moss is building the real-time semantic search runtime for conversational and multimodal AI. Our system enables voice agents, copilots, and chat interfaces to retrieve, reason, and respond in sub-10 ms, delivering the responsiveness that makes AI interactions feel truly natural.

If you’ve ever built a conversational or voice AI product, you’ve felt the lag. That moment when an agent pauses and the illusion of intelligence breaks. The bottleneck is almost always retrieval. Each query hops across networks and databases, adding delay and cost. Moss eliminates that gap by keeping retrieval close to where the agent runs.

Moss runs natively across browsers, mobile devices, and servers with an optimized vector index built in Rust and WebAssembly. It enables teams to build AI products that feel instant, contextual, and adaptive. The experiences that sustain engagement and unlock new kinds of interaction. For our customers, this translates into tangible business value: stronger user retention, higher conversion, and entirely new product categories made possible by real-time understanding. Moss is already powering production pilots across voice AI and developer platforms, achieving sub-10 ms retrieval and 70–90% token savings compared to traditional pipelines.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

business_model: Developer platform with SDKs and a hosted index service, usage and plan based pricing (details not public)
product_category: Developer infrastructure, on-device and edge semantic search runtime
market_need_then: Voice AI adoption in 2025 made retrieval latency visible; the company reports 6 enterprise design partners and 3 paying customers on its YC page (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Moss is active after Fall 2025 with a five person team and early design partners in voice AI. It targets a real latency problem with an on-device runtime, but verified funding is missing and established vector database vendors are strong, so its trajectory is still undetermined.

name: Multifactor
one_liner: Zero-trust authentication, authorization, and auditing for AI agents
long_description:
The agentic era is here, but its foundation is dangerously insecure. A growing number of high-profile "AI agent gone rogue" security incidents make headlines each week.

As enterprise adoption of agentic software has far outpaced the development of applicable cybersecurity solutions, CISOs have loudly voiced a growing need for verifiable, fine-grained security controls on complex multi-agent systems. That's why we built Multifactor.

Multifactor offers best-in-class authentication, authorization, and auditing technologies for agentic systems, allowing users to securely and revocably share online accounts with agents while maintaining fine-grained permissions and a detailed event history. We are doing for AI security what Cloudflare did for web security, Okta did for identity security, and Wiz did for cloud security: defining the category.

A world-class "account manager" that allows agents to securely use online accounts on your behalf is just the start—our early enterprise partners include companies using AI agents to manage $7.5+ billion manufacturing supply chains, where the consequences for lapses in security are severe. Our patented AI security technology seamlessly integrates with existing agentic software to thwart attacks like prompt injection, so CISOs and end users alike can breathe a sigh of relief, without slowing the pace of AI adoption.

business_model: Free consumer password and account manager, planned developer API access and enterprise plan
product_category: Identity and access security for AI agents
market_need_then: Rapid enterprise adoption of AI agents in 2025 and security concerns about agents using accounts; the company cites CISO demand and early partners in supply chain manufacturing (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Multifactor is active and announced a $15M seed in December 2025 led by Nexus Venture Partners, soon after Fall 2025. Founders with CIA and NASA cryptography backgrounds and a rising AI agent security need drove a large early raise, while Okta, CyberArk and password managers are the main threat.

name: Nessie
one_liner: The shared context layer for recursive companies.
long_description:
Knowledge work is being restructured by AI. Strategy happens in Claude. Research happens in ChatGPT. Building happens in Claude Code and Codex. Meetings get recorded, notes get written, agents run for hours and leave behind traces nobody reads. The people defining the next decade of work are already thinking with AI every day. But none of that thinking compounds. Every session starts from zero. The reasoning behind decisions, the context behind strategies, the evolution of ideas across hundreds of conversations - all of it evaporates.

Nessie is the infrastructure that makes it permanent. We auto-sync AI conversations and agent traces across every major provider - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, and more - alongside meetings, notes, and email from tools like Granola, Read AI, Plaud, and Obsidian. Everything a team produces with AI flows into one place and compounds over time.

Nessie turns that raw, heterogeneous data into an ontology: the live state of a company. Not a static schema but a continuously updated record of what the company knows, what it has decided, who owns what, and how its thinking has evolved, kept current as new work flows in. It is queryable from any agent through our CLI, MCP connector, and plugins, shareable across a team with real permissions, and deployable on-prem for organizations that need it.

Then the loop closes. Once a company’s state is legible to its agents, every agent run becomes training signal: which skills worked, which failed, which workflows keep repeating. Nessie feeds that signal back as reviewable improvements to the skills, prompts, and processes the team runs on. This is what makes a company recursive: its agents get better from its own history, the people working with them get better too, and the compounding never stops.

Where we are going: the AI-native organization runs thousands of agents that are powerful but amnesiac. Nessie is the layer that gives them, and the humans steering them, a shared memory. Science has journals, law has case law, software has git; AI-native knowledge work has had nothing. We are building it.

Founded by two Yale CS grads and former Amazon engineers in San Francisco. Backed by BoxGroup, Pioneer Fund, Y Combinator, Precursor, and more.

https://nessielabs.com

target_customer: Skilled nursing facilities and multi-facility post-acute operators that own or rent beds, wheelchairs and oxygen concentrators

product_category: AI equipment and asset management for post-acute care

name: Notte
one_liner: Browser infra for AI agents: sessions, auth, proxies, payments
long_description: Notte is cloud browser infrastructure for AI agents. regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need to operate real websites
problem: Agents need reliable cloud browsers with sessions, proxies, stealth, CAPTCHA solving, logins and payments to run web tasks in production.
business_model: Usage-based API and platform for browser infrastructure
product_category: Browser infrastructure for AI agents
market_need_then: AI agents that browse the web were a fast-growing use case in 2025. The company claims 20,000 developers and 1,000 organizations (self-reported).

name: Novaflow
one_liner: The AI data analyst for biology labs
long_description:
Novaflow is the AI data analyst for biology labs.

Bioinformatics data analysis is a time-consuming and expensive process for scientists. With Novaflow, life scientists can upload experimental data, ask questions in plain English, and get instant, publication-ready plots, giving them results in minutes instead of months.

Researchers at leading institutions like UCSF, Mount Sinai, UC Berkeley, and Harvard are already using Novaflow in their labs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Life science researchers and biology labs at universities and institutes
problem: Bioinformatics analysis is slow and expensive, leaving experimental data waiting on analyst backlogs for months.
business_model: B2B SaaS for labs (pricing not found)
product_category: AI data analyst for biology labs
market_need_then: The Show HN launch and company site describe users at UCSF, Mount Sinai, UC Berkeley and Harvard (self-reported). Analysis backlogs are the stated pain.
outcome_analysis: Novaflow is a Summer 2025 YC company with a team of four that launched in July 2025 via a Show HN post and is listed as Active. name: Novoflow

long_description: Novoflow deploys AI agents that operate on any medical practice’s EHR to automate its biggest operational bottlenecks. Deployment takes weeks and does not require staff to change how they work. Built for healthcare providers and hospitals.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Medical practices and hospitals with operational bottlenecks such as scheduling, calls and no-shows
problem: Practices lose time and revenue to manual front and back office work inside EHR systems that lack modern interfaces.

market_need_then: Clinics suffer no-shows and understaffed front desks. The YC page claims the voice agent answers every call and books directly in the EHR. No independent demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Novoflow is a Spring 2025 YC company that sells computer-using and voice agents to medical practices and is listed as Active with six people. The company site names its investors without amounts, and trackers report a seed of about 3.1M in late 2025 that no company post confirms. No exit or shutdown was found and EHR vendors launched competing agents during 2025.

name: Nox Metals
one_liner: Supplying America's Industrial Base
long_description: Nox Metals is an AI-powered metals supplier powering modern American manufacturing at scale. We are building automated factories that turn raw metal into production-ready material faster, cheaper, and more reliably than legacy service centers.

target_customer: American manufacturers, including aerospace and defense firms, that buy aluminum plate and bar

business_model: Metals distribution and processing with online instant quotes and automated cutting
product_category: Tech-enabled metals service center
market_need_then: The company cites long lead times and phone based quoting at legacy service centers. Customer logos on its site include Boeing, Blue Origin, Sikorsky and Stoke Space (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Nox Metals joined YC in Summer 2025, grew to a reported team of 64 by the directory snapshot and announced an 11.5M seed in June 2026 led by Hyperion, with a listed customer base in aerospace and defense. name: Nozomio

name: Nucleo
one_liner: The first Agentic platform for Oncology
long_description:
We help oncologists and radiologists extract insights from CT scans to support tumor characterization and treatment.

The hospitals we work with include Stanford Hospital, Cedars-Sinai, UCI Health, and Weill Cornell.

target_customer: Hospitals, oncologists and radiologists who pay for automated measurement of CT and MRI scans

market_need_then: Oncology imaging review is labor intensive; the company cites partnerships with Stanford, Cedars-Sinai, UCI Health and Weill Cornell as demand evidence (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Nucleo is an early stage Fall 2025 company with two research-heavy founders from Stanford, Apple and Politecnico di Milano, selling to hospitals. No funding round beyond YC, no exit and no shutdown were found. The main open risks are clinical validation, FDA clearance and slow hospital sales cycles.

name: Null Labs

long_description: We provide defense companies with simulation infrastructure to train and validate autonomous systems.

target_customer: Defense contractors and autonomy programs building maritime, aerial, ground and counter-UAS systems

product_category: Simulation and synthetic data for defense autonomy

No funding beyond aggregator figures, no exit and no shutdown were found. The market is attractive but crowded with well funded simulation vendors.

name: Nuntius

name: Oki
one_liner: The memory computer for your digital life.
long_description:
Your life’s context, in one device. Oki Home is a memory computer that grows with you, keeping your data and personal intelligence on hardware you own.

A future of limitless, personalized tokens for every consumer.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Originally startup leaders wanting daily progress reports; now consumers who buy a private home AI device
problem: Leaders lose visibility as teams grow and information scatters; the later pivot targets people who want their personal data and AI to stay on hardware they own.
business_model: Originally SaaS reports; now hardware sales (Oki Home with a removable Memchip, reservations open)
product_category: Personal AI hardware (memory computer), earlier workplace AI reporting
market_need_then: Engineering leaders wanted cross-tool visibility; coverage dated July 2025 framed the pain as information scattering as startups grow.
outcome_analysis: Oki entered YC in Winter 2025 with a workplace reporting tool, then pivoted to a private home AI computer sold on reservation. No funding beyond aggregator claims, no exit and no shutdown were found. Hardware execution, shipping timelines and pricing changes are the key risks, with delivery now listed for 2027.

name: Okibi
one_liner: Turns products into CLIs and agents into customers
long_description:
Okibi generates a CLI from any product's codebase, so AI agents can use it the way people do.

Agents are becoming software's next customers. When one comes to a product to do a task or purchase and finds no doorway in, it moves on to the competitor whose CLI lets it through. Okibi turns products into CLIs and agents into customers.

DoorDash, Mercury, Gusto, Ramp, and 30+ other companies have already launched first-party agent CLIs. Okibi is how every product gets one.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software companies that want AI agents to use their product (CLI generation); originally non-technical operators building agents
problem: Agents hitting a product with no usable interface move on to a competitor; MCP servers and raw APIs are weaker for agents than a CLI, according to the company.
business_model: SaaS tiers: Free, Pro (200 USD per month or 150 annual per the site), Enterprise custom
product_category: Developer tools, CLI generation for AI agents
market_need_then: In mid 2025 no-code agent builders were crowded; the CLI direction rides the later shift to agents as customers, per the YC description.
outcome_analysis: Okibi is the second YC company from the SigmaOS founders. It launched as a no-code agent builder in July 2025 and has since repositioned around generating CLIs for agents. No sourced funding beyond aggregator claims, no exit and no shutdown were found. The company is early and its defensibility depends on staying ahead of agent platforms and product vendors.

long_description: Omnara is an open-source, model-agnostic control plane for managed agents. One API to deploy, run, and control them. Self-host it, or use our managed cloud.

name: OnDeck AI
tags: Machine Learning; SaaS; Computer Vision; B2B; Video
one_liner: Analyze any footage, without training a model
long_description:
OnDeck is the infrastructure layer that makes Vision Language Models accessible and scalable for enterprise. Our model, Perception-0, let organizations instantly find any object, behavior or event, in any footage, without needing to train a model or collect any training data.

The Pain: Creating vision models usually takes months: collecting training data, training, then deployment.  Worse yet: 
+ it’s often impossible to get enough data for a specific task, and 
+ even the best cv models struggle to generalize across diverse camera setups, workflows and environments. 

To overcome these blockers, we bet early on the power of VLMs and built a vision engine that can generalize across any task and doesn’t need any training data. We published a NeurIPS workshop paper showing our new methods with VLMs beat traditional CV even at niche tasks. Now, our model Perception-0 beats the best VLMs including Gemini at long video understanding.

Our current customers include:
- National Defense Organizations
- Robotics Research
- Security cameras
- Behaviour analysis for port monitoring
- Off-shore oil & gas monitoring
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises, defense agencies, robotics teams and security operators that need to search and analyze large volumes of video footage
problem: Finding objects, behaviors or events in hours of footage usually requires training custom models; OnDeck offers a vision language model that does this without training.
business_model: Enterprise API and deployment (cloud or on-prem), pilots such as a reported 160K USD Singapore military pilot (company claim)
product_category: Video understanding and vision language models
market_need_then: Original fisheries monitoring had regulatory driven demand for video review; the current pivot targets defense and enterprise video, with a reported Singapore Ministry of Defence pilot.
outcome_analysis: OnDeck began as a Vancouver fisheries monitoring startup in 2022 and rebranded in 2025 into a general video understanding company, entering YC in Summer 2025. It reports a defense pilot and benchmark lead, but those are company claims. No verified funding, exit or shutdown was found, and competition from video AI specialists and frontier labs is strong.

name: OneStop
one_liner: The local social network: what's going on a few blocks from you.

regions: United States of America; America / Canada

No funding, exit or shutdown was found. The core challenge for hyperlocal social apps is reaching density in a small area and keeping it, and no evidence of traction was found.

name: Onlook
tags: Developer Tools; Design; Design Tools; AI
one_liner: The Developer tool for Designers
long_description:
Onlook is the fastest way for anyone to craft exceptional experiences in code. We built an open-source, visual editor for code that merges design, development, and AI.

Since launching, Onlook hit #1 on Hacker News, was the #1 trending repo on GitHub–twice– and has earned over 26,000 GitHub stars.

Founded by Daniel Farrell, a designer of 10+ years and former Head of Growth, and Kiet Ho, an ex-Amazon and ex-ServiceNow engineer, Onlook is on a mission to finally solve the gap between design and development.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Product designers and design-minded developers at startups who want to edit a real React and Next.js codebase visually instead of handing off mockups
problem: Designers work in mockup tools and hand off to engineers, so the shipped product drifts from the design. Onlook lets designers change the real code through a visual canvas and AI.

product_category: Open-source visual editor for code (design to code, AI developer tool)

outcome_analysis: Onlook is active and had no reported exit, shutdown or layoffs in searches. It rode the AI code editor wave with an open source launch that reached the top of Hacker News and GitHub trending, and it built a large star count quickly. Funding is thin in verified sources, with only aggregator figures, so the commercial outcome is unproven. The main risks are forks and well-funded prompt-to-app tools.

name: OpenIntake

long_description: OpenIntake boosts law firm revenue by converting callers into clients 24/7.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Law firms, especially contingency fee practices, that lose potential clients when calls go unanswered

No priced round beyond aggregator entries was found, and the market is crowded with answering services and AI voice vendors that raised money in 2025. Its prospects depend on law firm distribution and integrations rather than technology.

Compensation, headcount, and budgeting in one platform.

name: Operand

name: Optifye.ai

Optifye deploys AI cameras in factories to monitor operator productivity & SOP adherence in real-time.

We work with 5 out of the 10 largest autocomponent manufacturers in India!

name: Opusense AI
one_liner: AI for Field Inspection Reports
long_description:
Opusense AI automates field report writing for construction field inspectors. Instead of typing up notes at the end of the day, inspectors can now walk a site, speak observations aloud, snap photos, and let our AI assistant generate a detailed, organized report on-site and in real time.

Combined, the founding team has over 15 years in the construction industry. Writing up these field reports used to take up at least 20% of the week. With Opusense, we cut that time by 5x. Our team combines deep construction experience with technical expertise, Roya has a PhD in civil engineering, and Michael has worked at multiple construction tech startups.

Why hasn’t this been done before? Construction is slow to adopt new tech, and reporting is messy, photos, voice notes, and field notes all live in silos. Turning that into a clear, structured report requires real insight into how inspectors work and what clients need. Only now, with advances in AI, can we process unstructured data adequately to generate high-quality reports in real time.

The opportunity is massive. Every inspection firm and contractor is struggling with documentation. Manual reports slow them down, create inconsistencies, and delay handoffs. We believe AI can do this better, and Opusense is proving it.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Construction field inspectors, engineering and architecture review firms, general contractors and facility owners
problem: Inspectors spend a large share of their week typing field reports after site visits. Opusense turns voice notes, photos and typed notes into formatted reports on site.
business_model: B2B SaaS mobile and web app (pricing not found)
product_category: AI field inspection reporting for construction and facilities
market_need_then: The YC page says the founders' combined experience exceeds 15 years and report writing took at least 20% of the week; claims are self-reported. Construction documentation was slow to digitize.
outcome_analysis: Opusense is an active two person YC Spring 2025 company with founders who include a former site inspector. The company says it is live with multiple North American firms. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding beyond YC is unverified, and construction platforms have added similar AI features since.

name: Orange Slice
one_liner: Agentic sales enrichment spreadsheet
long_description: Orange Slice is a spreadsheet where every column is TypeScript—and AI writes it for you. Describe what you want in chat ("find the CEO's LinkedIn and get their email"), and we generate the code, create the columns, and run it across thousands of rows. Our fully-typed SDK has 100+ enrichments built in: LinkedIn, contact info, company data, web scraping, AI research. Columns automatically execute in dependency order. No workflow builders—just describe it or code it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B sales, RevOps and growth teams that build prospect lists and enrich leads
problem: Finding the right prospects and enriching them takes stitched-together vendors and manual work. Orange Slice offers a spreadsheet where AI writes TypeScript columns that pull from many data vendors, plus sequencing and signals.
business_model: Usage-based credits, free to start per the company site
product_category: Sales data enrichment and GTM agent platform
market_need_then: Sales teams were already spending on enrichment tools like Clay. The company site claims over 1,000 companies and 9.5M paid lookups (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Orange Slice is active and says it raised a $5.3M seed after YC, with Product Hunt and usage claims on its site. No exit, shutdown or layoffs found. It competes against much larger, well-funded Clay and Apollo, so durable advantage is unproven.

name: Orbital Operations
one_liner: High Thrust Space Vehicles for Satellite Defense
long_description:
Orbital Operations is developing a high thrust, reusable space vehicle for satellite defense. We protect critical satellites, like GPS and Military communication satellites, from adversarial threats, like China and Russia.

Our vehicle will use the exact same propulsion systems that launch vehicles have used for decades by implementing a cryogenic management system. This will give us over 100x the thrust or current in-space propulsion.

Ross and I have over 15 years of combined aerospace experience across NASA, Aerojet Rocketdyne, SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Relativity Space. We’ve worked side by side for more than 3.5 years developing propulsion systems, turbomachinery, and building our own respective engineering teams.

We are currently working on the first demo of our unique cryo management system and intend to launch an operational vehicle by 2027.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US Space Force and defense organizations needing maneuverable satellite protection, plus commercial orbital logistics
problem: Satellites cannot maneuver quickly because in-space propulsion is low thrust. Orbital Operations is building a high-thrust, reusable LH2/LOx vehicle with cryogenic management to protect satellites.
business_model: Government contracts and awards (defense), later commercial orbital logistics
product_category: Space propulsion and orbital vehicles for defense
market_need_then: Space Force interest in maneuverable and defensive satellites is growing; a SpaceWERX award and an NASA support letter are cited by the company and press.
outcome_analysis: Orbital Operations raised an $8.8M seed in August 2025 led by Initialized Capital after YC and reports a SpaceWERX award and a later DoD demo award headline. Founders come from SpaceX, Blue Origin and Relativity. No exit or shutdown was found. The key risk is technical: the cryo vehicle demo and capital for hardware.

name: Orchid
one_liner: A personal EA in your iMessage
long_description:
Orchid is an executive assistant that lives in iMessage. It texts you your day each morning, drafts your replies, and books your meetings. You approve, it handles the rest.

If you've ever wished for a world-class EA, come talk to us.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Busy professionals and founders who want an executive assistant they can text, paying a monthly subscription
problem: Inbox triage, calendar coordination, scheduling and follow-ups eat time that most people cannot hand to a human executive assistant.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer subscription (Orchid's own comparison page lists a plan from $29.99 per month, unverified marketing claim)
product_category: AI personal executive assistant delivered over iMessage and SMS
market_need_then: Interest in AI agents that act on email and calendar was rising in early 2025 and the same founders had just built the Zero open source email client, indicating inbox pain. No sourced spend or usage figures for Orchid itself.
outcome_analysis: Orchid is active with a three person team as of the YC listing. No funding round, shutdown or acquisition was found in public sources, so the outcome is open. The team's pivot from the Zero email client toward a messaging assistant and a viral 2026 ad suggest strong attention-seeking distribution, while thin defensibility and large platform and funded competitors such as Poke are the main risks.

name: Osmosis

name: Perseus Defense
one_liner: America's Golden Dome for Drones
long_description:
Perseus Defense is building a mass-manufactured Counter UAS solution for the Department of Defense and Department of Homeland Security. Current solutions are one-to-one, too dangerous for use on U.S. soil, and orders of magntiude more expensive than the threats they defeat. Our self-guided missile platform is man-portable and multi-domain capable. It senses, engages, and eliminates threats with drastically reduced cost per engagement over existing kinetic solutions. 

Solving this critical national security problem requires understanding complex DoD needs along with actual rocket science including aerodynamics, guidance, navigation, control, and much more. Jason and Steve met at Penn State while they pursued their PhD and MS in aerospace engineering, respectively. Their past experiences designing space helicopters for NASA, making Boeing airliners land autonomously, controlling swarms of unmanned autonomous systems, teaching aerospace engineering at Stanford, winning multiple ONR and DOE engineering competitions, and founding an international drone competition makes them the perfect team to create transformative solutions protecting our service members. 

"If you build this, it will be mandatory equipment for every truck, boat, and convoy in the U.S. Military. We're talking thousands of units." - Former DoD Procurement Officer

The White House just released Executive Order, "Unleashing American Drone Dominance" which adds billions of dollars, government support, and streamlined regulations to enable the development of our product. 

Traction: 
Jason and Steve used more than 100 end-user interviews across the DoD and DHS to shape the product to something of critical need to both boots on the ground and DoD purchasers. In 8 short weeks following a strict 2-week design-build-test cycle, the team has gone through 4 major guided missile iterations with over 30 live-fire flight tests. They were invited to Ft. Hood to present their platform to the 1st Cavalry Division, and also briefed the Pentagon and U.S. congressmen on current U.S. vulnerabilities to advanced drone technology.  Perseus Defense is actively standing up cooperative research agreements with U.S. Army DEVCOM's Applied Research Laboratory, Aviation and Missile Center, Armaments Center, and High Performance Computing Modernization Program.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US Department of Defense and Department of Homeland Security buyers of counter-drone systems
problem: Small drones threaten troops and US sites, and existing interceptors are one-to-one, costly or unsafe for use on US soil.
business_model: Hardware sales of man-portable launchers and low-cost guided interceptors to government customers
product_category: Counter-UAS guided micro-missile
market_need_then: The company cites a 2025 White House executive order on drone dominance, cost-per-engagement problems with existing kinetic defenses, and more than 100 end-user interviews across DoD and DHS.
outcome_analysis: Perseus raised a reported $6M seed within weeks of Demo Day by pairing aerospace PhD founders with a timely counter-drone need and fast live-fire iteration. It showed hardware at Fort Hood and Yuma in 2026, but no confirmed government contract was found, so the next test is converting demos into funded programs against Anduril and RTX.

name: Perspectives Health

America is facing an addiction and mental health crisis, but the treatment programs trying to solve the problem are faced with administrative burden, staff shortages, and pressure from payers. 

We work with treatment programs to incorporate AI that reduces administrative burden, prevents insurance denials, and helps directors run their program better.

Our agents analyze charts to prevent insurance denials, complete documentation and insurance paperwork to save staff time, and sift through historical data to find opportunities for improvement.

name: PgDog
one_liner: Scaling engine for PostgreSQL
long_description:
PgDog is an application for sharding PostgreSQL. It understands SQL and can distribute queries automatically between databases. It's built for managed databases, like AWS RDS, and doesn't require any changes to application code or schema.

In addition to sharding, PgDog is a load balancer and pooler, so it can act as a replacement for PgBouncer, RDS Proxy, and other Postgres scaling products. It brings the simplicity and performance of HTTP load balancing to the database.

Built from the experience of sharding Postgres at Instacart during peak growth in 2020, PgDog is the answer to the old question: does Postgres scale? It does now.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering teams running large PostgreSQL databases on managed services such as AWS RDS
problem: Postgres is hard to scale horizontally. Sharding usually means rewriting the application or schema.
business_model: Open source core with commercial offering (license and pricing not stated on the site)
product_category: PostgreSQL sharding, pooling and load balancing proxy
market_need_then: The founder reports sharding Postgres at Instacart in 2020, and the company's customer logos include Coinbase, Ramp and Modal. A podcast notes many investors were backing Postgres sharding.
outcome_analysis: PgDog turned the founder's Instacart sharding experience and the PgCat open source project into a Postgres scaling proxy, collected named startup customers, and raised a $5.5M seed in June 2026, about a year after its Spring 2025 batch. The risk is that Multigres and other funded entrants compete for the same sharding wedge.

name: Pickle

long_description: Pickle is the personal AI agent network for Asia. Instead of building another chatbot or an overcrowded super-app, Pickle replaces daily life administration with an "invisible super-app" powered by autonomous background tool execution—handling restaurant bookings, store phone calls, delivery tracking, administrative paperwork, and local payments without user micromanagement. Because every user gets a dedicated agent with persistent memory and local context, Pickles naturally connect with one another: coordinating schedules between friends, exchanging local recommendations, and delegating shared errands. Starting with Korea and Japan, Pickle integrates deeply with local messaging (Kakao, LINE), local identity, and payment rails to become the default consumer execution layer across 670M people in Asia.

Most kids' screen time is broken: passive, algorithmic content designed to keep kids watching, not growing. Pixley is the antidote.
