name: Playgent
one_liner: Sandboxes for AI agents
long_description:
When enterprise agents fail in production, the conditions that caused the failure are critical: user state, data, tool calls, and context. Without a way to recreate these conditions, teams can't fix what broke.

Playgent provides infrastructure to create high-fidelity sandbox environments for AI agents. Our environments come packaged as a single MCP url where tool calls are mocked, authentication is abstracted away, and test data can be initialized via natural language or JSON specifications.

Teams can use Playgent to reproduce production failures in safe, scoped environments that accurately reconstruct state. Finally, export runs as OTel traces from Playgent's environment to plug directly into your observability tools or RL pipelines.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams building and testing enterprise AI agents, and later AI labs that need finance focused training environments
problem: When enterprise agents fail in production teams cannot recreate user state, data, tool calls and context to fix them. Playgent provides sandbox environments that reproduce those conditions.
business_model: B2B infrastructure sold as sandboxes and RL environments, usage or contract based
product_category: AI agent testing sandboxes and RL environments
market_need_then: In 2025 AI labs and enterprises began paying for RL environments and agent testing infrastructure, covered by TechCrunch in September 2025, and agent failures in production were a recurring pain.
outcome_analysis: Playgent is a two person Summer 2025 company that started with agent sandboxes for reproducing failures and now presents itself as a builder of finance RL environments. No funding, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is open. The category is crowded and fast moving, with funded rivals and AI labs building in house.

target_customer: Robotics researchers and humanoid-robot companies that need dexterous hands and human hand-manipulation data
problem: Humanoids lack hands dexterous enough for contact-rich manipulation; simple grippers fail on non-rigid objects and teleoperation does not scale or capture touch and pressure.
business_model: Hardware sales of dexterous robot hands (ProHand) plus a data-collection glove (ProGlove)
product_category: Robotics hardware: dexterous hands and tactile data capture
market_need_then: Humanoid robot makers were building their own hands because grippers and teleoperation were insufficient, and Tesla's Optimus program showed hands were a major engineering bottleneck, which created demand for dexterous hands and training data.
outcome_analysis: Proception is an early-stage company that raised an $11M seed led by First Round in June 2026, shortly after settling a year-long Tesla trade-secret suit and starting to ship its first ProHand units. Founder-market fit is strong, since the CEO led electronics on Optimus, and humanoid robotics funding gave a tailwind. Risks are the Tesla legacy, hardware execution, and low-cost Chinese hand makers that already ship at scale; it is too early to call an outcome.

name: Proliferate
one_liner: Do your life's work with agents
long_description: We're a dense, small team in SF building the open source platform for working with agents.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software teams that want company-specific background coding agents they can self-host
problem: Teams want agents with their own sandboxes, secure access to internal services and event triggers. Proliferate offers an open-source, MIT-licensed, self-hostable platform with multiplayer sessions and live previews.
business_model: Open source core with a hosted cloud tier using usage-based credits (per aggregator snippet)
product_category: Background agent platform, developer tools
market_need_then: Coding agents were spreading in 2025, and teams wanted autonomous background runs; evidence of demand for self-hosted versions is the company's own positioning.
outcome_analysis: Proliferate is an active solo-founder open-source company, formerly Keystone, in a crowded coding-agent market where Cursor and others shipped background agents during 2025. No outcome event was found, and funding is unconfirmed, so the trajectory is unclear.

name: Promptless
tags: Developer Tools; Generative AI; SaaS; B2B; AI
one_liner: An AI teammate that automatically updates your customer-facing docs
long_description:
Docs are integral to a great customer experience, but managing them is a challenging, multi-team effort. The most successful companies recognize that fantastic docs drive adoption and bad ones cause customers to churn. Promptless is used by fast-growing startups and Fortune 500 enterprises alike to automatically update docs based on feature releases, support tickets, internal Slack conversations, and more.

Promptless is designed to be flexible—it can integrate with any docs platform, be triggered automatically from many workflows, and can pull in context from any internal knowledge source.

With Promptless, documentation becomes a strategic advantage for growth, not a bottleneck or a liability.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software companies, from startups to Fortune 500, with customer-facing docs that fall behind product releases
problem: Docs go stale as products change across teams. Promptless drafts doc updates from code changes, support tickets and Slack, and a human reviews before shipping.
business_model: B2B SaaS; pricing not stated in sources
product_category: AI documentation maintenance, developer tools
market_need_then: Docs quality drives adoption and churn per company copy; the Launch HN post in February 2025 and named customers like Vitess and Runpod show early use. Demand evidence is mostly the company's own.
outcome_analysis: Promptless is active with a five person team and a customer list including open-source projects and startups. Aggregators suggest only about $500K raised, which is unconfirmed. It expanded into agent instruction tuning, while docs platforms like Mintlify moved into automation, so competition grew after launch.

name: Propolis
one_liner: Hands off QA via intelligent browser agents.
long_description: Propolis simulates real users via swarms of autonomous browser agents that test for you.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software teams that ship web products and need QA
problem: Manual and scripted QA is slow and brittle, and bugs reach users because teams cannot test every flow.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for autonomous browser agent testing
product_category: AI software testing
market_need_then: Agentic AI products are nondeterministic and hard to test with scripts, and Datadog framed quality as a continuous signal. Two person teams had little QA capacity.
outcome_analysis: Propolis went from YC Spring 2025 to an acquisition by Datadog announced in January 2026, less than a year after its batch. A two person team with Palantir and Airtable backgrounds built autonomous QA agents as testing for agentic software became urgent, and Datadog bought the capability and team rather than waiting. Deal terms are not public.

name: Prox
one_liner: Air-breathing hypersonics for scale.
long_description:
Parity is a moving target. Every advance in offense prompts a response in defense, and every response starts another race. The West cannot take military superiority for granted. It has to keep building, fielding, and improving technology at scale.

We believe hypersonics at scale can be the West's ultimate equalizer. Our mission is to give the United States and its allies the capacity to close capability gaps and sustain credible deterrence as threats evolve.

Prox is developing a stand-in attack weapon platform powered by solid-fuel ducted ramjet propulsion (SFRJ), with repeatable production at the center of the effort.

Based in Hawthorne, California.
useprox.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Unclear: YC directory says defense buyers (hypersonic weapons); the same page's launch post says third-party logistics providers; 2026 coverage says manufacturers of complex physical products
problem: Directory text: building solid-fuel ramjet stand-in attack weapons at production scale. Launch post: automating carrier claims and operations work in logistics with AI agents.
business_model: Unclear (defense hardware per directory; AI agent software per launch post)
product_category: Unclear: air-breathing hypersonics vs AI agents for operations/support
market_need_then: For the logistics version, the launch post cites a first deployment at ShipBob automating lost-in-transit carrier claims; for the defense version, the directory cites deterrence needs with no data.
outcome_analysis: Prox is a Fall 2025 YC company, so there is no outcome yet. Its public descriptions conflict: the directory text describes a hypersonic ramjet weapon program in Hawthorne, while the same page carries a launch post about AI agents for logistics claims with ShipBob, and 2026 coverage says technical support AI for manufacturers. No funding amount is confirmed. The record can only say it is early, small and unclear in its direction.

name: QFEX
one_liner: 24/7 Global Stock Exchange
long_description:
QFEX is the 24/7 exchange for traditional financial markets.

We let you trade US equities, commodities and FX pairs with (or without) leverages of up to 100x. On QFEX, UX comes first: brokerless market access, seamless integration with traditional payment rails, and ultra-efficient Perpetual Futures offered over all asset classes. Trading has never been simpler, cheaper or fairer than with QFEX.

Founded by Quants and Engineers from Citadel & Tower Research who saw an opportunity to make markets how they always should have been, QFEX will eventually replace the entire $100 billion exchange and clearing industry.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Traders wanting 24/7 leveraged access to US equities, indices, commodities and FX via perpetual futures
problem: Traditional markets close nights and weekends and trade through brokers. QFEX offers a brokerless 24/7 exchange with perpetual futures over traditional assets.
business_model: Exchange trading and clearing fees (inferred from exchange model; fee schedule not opened)
product_category: 24/7 exchange, perpetual futures on traditional assets
market_need_then: Retail demand for off-hours trading and perpetual futures was shown by crypto venues and Coinbase's 2025 moves; founders cite experience at Tower and Citadel.
outcome_analysis: QFEX raised a $9.5M seed at a reported $95M valuation led by General Catalyst in March 2026, helped by founders with Tower, Citadel and Cambridge pedigrees. No shutdown or acquisition was found. Crowding by Coinbase, Kraken and One Trading and licensing risk are the main threats.

name: QualGent
one_liner: AI Mobile App Quality Assurance Tester
long_description:
QualGent is an AI Mobile App Quality Assurance Tester that mimics a real human, helping teams catch bugs and ship faster - without hiring more QA testers. One customer reached #3 in the Education category on the App Store by improving app quality with QualGent.

Mobile bugs hurt: crashes kill ratings, broken checkouts drive churn. QualGent helps teams scale QA effortlessly and avoid Sonos-level disasters.

The idea for QualGent was born from the founders’ experience leading engineering teams at Google across Android XR, Stadia, Quick Share, and foldable devices where shipping to billions of users meant constantly facing the painful trade-off between moving fast and maintaining quality. With prior research experience at Nvidia, Maryland, and Berkeley, the team saw a clear opportunity: use AI to scale QA.

QualGent’s vision is to close the loop on software creation. As AI enables engineers to code 100x faster, QualGent eliminates the next bottleneck—software verification—unlocking truly scalable, end-to-end software development.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mobile app teams (founders, product, QA and engineering leaders) and coding agents needing device verification
problem: Mobile bugs hurt ratings and checkout conversion, and QA does not scale with AI-accelerated coding. Teams trade speed against quality.
business_model: B2B SaaS and managed testing (AI agents plus optional human testers)
product_category: AI mobile app QA and testing
market_need_then: AI coding tools were speeding up shipping in 2025 so verification became the bottleneck; founders cite their experience with quality versus speed at Google.
outcome_analysis: QualGent joined YC in Spring 2025, launched on Product Hunt, expanded into a closed-loop QA platform with TrustLoop and DevLoop, and was still publishing in 2026. Funding is unclear and the QA agent space is crowded, so its position remains unproven.

name: Quantstruct
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; API; Automation; AI
one_liner: AI documentation engineer – test & autoimprove stale product docs
long_description:
Quantstruct automatically creates and improves product documentation, implementation guides, and changelogs for API & SDK products, web-based enterprise software, and internal applications.

Quantstruct identifies gaps in your knowledge base based on each product release or unfulfilled customer query. It uses multiple AI agents to search existing knowledge sources, test existing docs for validity and style guidelines, and clicks, scrolls, and uses enterprise software through a web browser to generate docs with embedded screenshots and video recordings. Quanstruct is available as a cloud service to start, targeting technical writers, content writing, professional services, and product teams.

Traditional generative AI tools risk hallucinating critical API & SDK fields, even with RAG based approaches. Purely agent-based approaches risk providing unpredictable output that can diverge from desired documentation processes. Finally, no company’s review and publishing workflow is the same. Quantstruct is the easiest way to onboard and customize AI agents to continuously improve your documentation based on your customer needs and product evolution. https://quantstruct.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: API and SDK companies, enterprise software vendors and internal product teams with technical writers
problem: Product documentation goes stale after each release and generic AI tools hallucinate API fields, while manual upkeep is slow.
business_model: B2B SaaS cloud service for documentation teams
product_category: AI documentation agents for developer and enterprise software
market_need_then: Fast release cycles and AI-related API change make stale docs common; YC page names Vapi (W21) as a customer, which is a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Quantstruct entered YC in Winter 2025 as a two person team from Moveworks and Replit building AI agents to keep product documentation current. Public evidence is thin: only an aggregator-listed pre-seed and a launch post. By late 2026 its own website describes hotel housekeeping robots instead, which suggests a pivot, but no source confirms the timing or reason, so the outcome is still unresolved.

name: Quotain
one_liner: AI sales roleplay built from your real deals
long_description: Quotain is AI sales roleplay software for revenue teams. Reps practice the calls they need to win against AI buyers built from your playbook, CRM context, and past calls, from cold calls and discovery to negotiations, buying committees, and screen-share demos. Every session is scored against your methodology, and reps retry the exact moment that slipped. Managers see who is ready and what to coach. Try a free practice call at quotain.com.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Revenue teams and sales managers who want reps to practice calls before live deals
problem: Reps rehearse poorly and managers cannot see readiness. Quotain simulates AI buyers built from the playbook, CRM context and past calls, scores sessions and shows coaching priorities.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat: Starter $50 and Pro $100 per seat per month with 7-day trial
product_category: AI sales roleplay and coaching
market_need_then: Vendor comparison pages show a crowded roleplay category, indicating spend on sales training, though those pages are mostly vendor blogs and undated.
outcome_analysis: Quotain is an active two person New York company selling AI sales roleplay in a crowded category with funded rivals. Public pricing and a MCP integration exist, but funding is unverified and no outcome event was found, so its trajectory is unclear.

name: Radius
tags: Developer Tools; Design; Design Tools; AI
one_liner: Code and browse in the same place
long_description: Radius is a browser where developers can orchestrate agents from their tabs. Ship 100x from a single place where agents can see, navigate, and act on your workspace.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software developers who run coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor Agent and want them next to their PRs, docs, terminals and localhost servers
problem: Developers juggle coding agents, terminals and browser tabs in separate windows, and the agents cannot see or act on the browser workspace.
business_model: Free macOS browser using the user's existing agent subscriptions; no paid model found
product_category: Developer browser for agent orchestration
market_need_then: Rapid adoption of coding agents in 2025 created demand for tools that coordinate several agents in parallel next to the browser context developers already use. No hard spend figures found.
outcome_analysis: Radius is a very young Fall 2025 company that moved from an AI front end IDE to a developer browser in under a year and renamed twice. No funding, traction or exit is public. The wedge sits in a space where Cursor and Anthropic ship agent management features quickly, so competition and differentiation are the main open questions.

name: Rally
one_liner: Financial OS for Modern Fleets
long_description:
Rally is a financial platform for businesses that operate vehicle fleets. We're starting in Europe, where over €1 trillion is spent annually on fuel, charging, maintenance, and other fleet expenses - most of it still running on legacy networks built in the 1960s.

We set a new standard for fleet finance by streamlining payments and automating workflows across bookkeeping, credit, and driver payroll, helping real-world businesses like delivery services, construction crews, and service technicians stay in control and operate efficiently.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Businesses that operate vehicle fleets such as delivery services, construction crews and service technicians, starting in Europe (Germany and Spain per a trade report)
problem: Fleet spend on fuel, charging and maintenance runs on legacy networks from the 1960s, with manual bookkeeping, credit and driver payroll.
business_model: Fleet payment card and finance platform, likely interchange and credit based; not stated by a source
product_category: Fleet fintech
market_need_then: Company states over 1 trillion euros is spent yearly on fleet fuel, charging and maintenance in Europe, mostly on legacy networks. Not independently verified.
outcome_analysis: Rally is an active Winter 2025 company with a five person team in Berlin selling fleet finance to European operators. A trade press piece shows live customers and UK expansion plans, but no verified funding, revenue or exit exists in public sources, so the outcome is still open. Established fleet card issuers and newer entrants make competition the main risk.

name: Ralo
one_liner: AI-Native Mortgage Broker
long_description: Ralo is the first AI-native mortgage broker. We use AI to remove layers of overhead and pass the savings back to borrowers. Our customers get rates more than half a point below the national average, save tens of thousands of dollars over the life of their loan.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US home buyers and refinancers who want lower mortgage rates, currently in Texas, California and Colorado where Ralo is licensed
problem: Mortgage brokerage carries heavy human overhead and hidden fees that raise borrower costs.
business_model: Licensed mortgage broker earning origination compensation, using AI to cut cost and pass savings to borrowers
product_category: AI-native mortgage brokerage
market_need_then: Mortgage origination costs are high and borrowers overpay; Ralo claims rates more than half a point below the national average (company claim, unverified).
outcome_analysis: Ralo raised 2.9M seed money after a Spring 2025 batch and publicly launched in June 2026 with licenses in three states, and reports funding over 8M of Texas mortgages. Founders with Google and Goldman Sachs experience give it product credibility, but it is small and faces incumbents adding AI, so its outcome is still open.

name: ReJot
one_liner: We turn complex API integrations into drop‑in full‑stack libraries
long_description:
ReJot is building Fragno to let API companies go from simply exposing an API to offering drop-in integrations that work out of the box.

Fragno is an open‑source framework for packaging backend endpoints, data storage patterns, and frontend utilities into reusable building blocks. API providers ship full integrations, not just low‑level SDKs and docs.

Customers configure rather than write code, so integrations are both much faster to launch and far more consistent across customers.
regions: Netherlands; Europe
target_customer: API companies that want to ship drop-in full-stack integrations (backend routes, storage, frontend hooks) instead of only SDKs and docs
problem: Most SDKs only wrap API calls, so developers still write webhook handlers, data persistence and frontend hooks themselves.
business_model: Open-source framework (MIT) with a likely commercial layer; no pricing found
product_category: Developer tools, open source integration framework
market_need_then: API providers want faster, more consistent integrations; evidence is the founders' pitch and Hacker News launch comments, no spend data.
outcome_analysis: ReJot is a two person Amsterdam team that launched a sync engine at YC in early 2025 and then shifted to the Fragno open source framework, shown on Hacker News in October 2025, with its homepage now featuring another product. No verified funding or traction exists, so the outcome is open, and the adoption dependency on API providers is the main risk.

name: Reacher
one_liner: We automate creator marketing for the world's largest brands
long_description:
Reacher is an AI-powered platform that automates creator marketing workflows—from discovery and outreach to campaign management and content strategy—making marketing teams 10x more productive. 

We handle the manual tasks so brands can focus on building relationships with creators while centralizing their operations in one platform to manage creators on TikTok Shop, Instagram, and YouTube.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Brands and agencies selling on TikTok Shop that run creator and affiliate programs
problem: Creator marketing on TikTok Shop is manual: finding creators, outreach, sample management and reporting run on spreadsheets.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for TikTok Shop affiliate software, plus a separate creator network
product_category: Creator marketing automation for TikTok Shop
market_need_then: TikTok Shop brands need creator affiliates at scale; Reacher claims 1,000 to 3,000 brands (inconsistent on its own site, self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Reacher grew from a 2024 start to a ten person team with thousands of claimed brand customers and TikTok Shop partner status after the Summer 2025 batch. Evidence is self reported and dependence on TikTok platform rules is a clear risk, so the outcome is still open.

name: RealRoots
one_liner: IRL friendship app for women
long_description: Real friendships, made in real life. Answer a few questions, and we'll match you into IRL hangs with women you'll actually click with. Made for women, by women.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Women, 21 and older, in US cities who want new in-person friendships
problem: Adult women struggle to make close friends in a new city, and friendship apps rarely lead to meetups.
business_model: Consumer subscription for curated group experiences (commitments of a quarter, a year or longer per YC page)
product_category: IRL friendship matching app for women
market_need_then: Rising interest in friendship apps in 2024 and 2025, shown by Bumble buying Geneva and Pie's 11.5M raise; loneliness demand is qualitative here.
outcome_analysis: RealRoots is an active Summer 2025 company with a seven person team and CEO and CPO from Cambly and Brilliant. It sells curated group friendships to women in a field where Bumble and Pie compete and where Hey VINA shut down. Funding and traction are not verified, so the outcome is open.

name: Rebolt
one_liner: Agentic AI for aircraft maintenance
long_description: Rebolt is the AI operating platform for aircraft maintenance. Its agents work on top of the maintenance and engineering (M&E), ERP systems and OEM portals operators already run, performing the work of engineers and planners. Works for Base, Line, Engines, and Components maintenance teams.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Aircraft maintenance and engineering teams (base, line, engines, components) at operators; at YC time, companies wanting internal AI apps
problem: Aircraft maintenance engineers and planners spend hours per finding on work across M&E systems, ERPs and OEM portals; the company says resolution drops from 2 to 6 hours to 15 minutes.
business_model: Enterprise software for MRO operators; pricing not found
product_category: Agentic AI for aircraft maintenance
market_need_then: Aviation maintenance labor shortages and heavy documentation; evidence here is the company's own claims and MRO events, no independent spend data.
outcome_analysis: Rebolt entered Winter 2025 as a company OS for internal AI apps and now positions itself on aircraft maintenance, a narrower regulated market with clear spend. No verified funding, named customers or exit is public, so the outcome is open; the early pivot and thin evidence are the main uncertainties.

name: Rebulk
one_liner: AI-native software for managing rail and bulk operations.
long_description:
Rebulk builds AI-native software for rail, transload, and bulk operations. We help teams manage railcars and trucks, transloading, maintenance, yard switching, railcar tracking, bulk inventory, documents, customer reporting, and billing.

Much of this work still runs on spreadsheets, paper tickets, phone calls, and disconnected legacy systems. That means teams spend too much time entering the same information twice, tracking down paperwork, figuring out where railcars and inventory are, and putting together reports by hand. Rebulk brings that work into modern software built around how each business actually operates.

We’ve lived this problem, and we know how to build for it. Warren previously led product at a Series A supply chain software startup, where he worked closely with companies moving and managing bulk commodities. Cole was engineer #3 at Tropic, helping scale it from seed to Series B, and later led engineering at an AI startup.

Rebulk runs operations at Venezia Transport, Usher Transport, Cicada Logistics, McDonald Farms, and TransloadX across transloading, rail maintenance, switching, railcar tracking, and bulk inventory.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Shippers, railroads, transloaders, carriers, plants and merchants running rail and bulk operations
problem: Rail, transload and bulk work runs on spreadsheets, paper tickets, phone calls and disconnected legacy systems, so data is entered twice and inventory is hard to see.
business_model: B2B SaaS across operations, tracking and finance modules; says no onboarding fee and no billing until go-live
product_category: AI-native software for rail and bulk operations
market_need_then: Operators run on paper and spreadsheets; the company's customers include Venezia Transport, Usher Transport and TransloadX, and a Cargill pilot is reported by Startland News.
outcome_analysis: Rebulk moved from transcription to bulk inventory scanning and then to a full rail and bulk operations suite, with paying customers, a Cargill pilot and a 1.2M pre-seed from Kansas City investors. Founders with supply chain experience help, but it is tiny, in a niche market with older transload software vendors, so the outcome is still open.

name: Red Barn Robotics
one_liner: A Roomba for weeds on a farm.
long_description: We are building an autonomous robot to precisely eliminate weeds and leave crops untouched. Despite $100 billion being spent annually on weed control, weeds still cost the US economy $46B/year. Weeds steal sunlight and nutrients from crops, forcing farmers to choose between higher costs and lower yields. Moreover, many farms still rely on hand labor to control weed growth. The process is slow, expensive, and increasingly difficult due to constant labor shortages (1 out of every 5 US farm positions go unfilled each year). Our robot nicknamed the Field Hand is able to automate one of the worst jobs on a farm and will help healthily feed the world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Specialty and row-crop farms that pay for intra-row weeding, today done by hand labor
problem: Weeds in the crop row cost farmers yield and labor, and hand weeding is slow, expensive and hard to staff.
business_model: Robot-as-a-service weeding: a consultation, a custom weeding plan, robot operations and regular service through the growing season (pricing not public)
product_category: Agricultural robotics, autonomous weeding
founder_names: Adam Iseman; Ilya Kelner; Alex Neff
market_need_then: The YC description cites about $100 billion a year spent on weed control and a farm labor gap where one in five US farm positions goes unfilled; these figures are company claims.
outcome_analysis: Red Barn Robotics is an early company that is still active as of late 2026, with no reported shutdown, acquisition or layoffs. Its outcome is not yet determined: it competes with better funded laser weeding firms, and public information about customers and revenue is absent.

name: Redapto
one_liner: Intelligence that moves the world
long_description: Redapto builds the intelligence that runs the real world, closing the gap between understanding and execution. By combining real-time context, specialized AI agents, and adaptive orchestration, Redapto takes ownership of complex, mission-critical operations from end to end. Acting as an always-on operational brain, it coordinates across people and systems, improves every decision, and grows more capable with every task.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Operations teams in manufacturing, logistics, energy and defense (current site); early press described customer-interaction teams
problem: Critical operations run across disconnected people and systems; Redapto aims to coordinate them with governed AI agents under human oversight.
business_model: Enterprise agentic AI platform (Redapto OS); pricing not public
product_category: Agentic AI platform for operations
market_need_then: In 2025 enterprises were broadly adopting AI agents; no Redapto-specific demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Redapto is a very young company, active as of late 2026 with no reported shutdown or sale. Its December 2025 pre-seed was small and its positioning shifted from customer-interaction AI in early coverage to operations for physical industries on its current site, so its outcome is not yet determinable.

name: Reditus Space
one_liner: Reusable Satellites
long_description:
We are making reusable satellites for zero-g manufacturing & Hypersonic Technology Development. 
Our first orbital recovery mission is set to launch in Q4 2026.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Aerospace and defense programs needing hypersonic reentry testing, and pharma, materials, semiconductor and optics firms wanting microgravity manufacturing
problem: Getting products and test articles back from orbit and hypersonic flight is costly and one-time; reusable spacecraft aim to make it repeatable.
business_model: Microgravity and reentry as a service on reusable ENOS spacecraft
product_category: Reusable reentry satellites
competitors_at_founding: Varda Space Industries; Inversion Space; Outpost
market_need_then: Defense interest in hypersonic test targets and reentry testing plus emerging microgravity manufacturing demand; Dawn Aerospace announced a propulsion supply deal in March 2025.
outcome_analysis: Reditus Space has raised a $7.1M seed and built its ENOS vehicle, with the first flight pushed from early 2026 into later 2026 and the vehicle shipped to Vandenberg by July 2026. Founders with NASA and Space Force backgrounds fit the market, but outcome depends on a successful first reentry.

name: Refresh
one_liner: Training gyms for computer use and software engineering work
long_description: Building RL environments for coding and computer use.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and enterprises that need RL training environments for coding and computer use
problem: Training agents on computer use and software engineering requires high fidelity, verifiable simulated environments that labs do not want to build themselves.
business_model: Custom RL environments sold to labs and enterprises (pricing not public)
product_category: RL environments for AI agent training
market_need_then: In 2025 AI labs were reported by TechCrunch to be investing heavily in RL environments to train agents, creating demand for third-party suppliers.
outcome_analysis: Refresh is an early RL environment vendor, active as of late 2026 with job listings reported by a directory and no news of shutdown or sale. Public funding and customer data are absent, and the segment has become crowded with larger funded entrants, so its trajectory is unknown.

name: Relaw
one_liner: AI Legal OS
long_description: Relaw powers leading AI-native law firms.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and mid-size consumer-facing law firms (estate planning, elder law, PI, family, immigration)
problem: Law firms stitch together separate tools for intake, practice management, billing and drafting.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, Standard plan from 269 USD/month billed annually
product_category: AI-native legal practice management
market_need_then: Law firm demand for AI tools was visible in 2025 (several YC legal AI companies funded); no Relaw-specific demand figures found.
outcome_analysis: Relaw is a Fall 2025 YC company with two people selling an all-in-one AI legal operating system to small law firms. Public information is thin: no funding announcements, customer counts or revenue were found, so it is too early to judge success or failure. The model rides the legal AI wave but faces Clio and well funded AI-native entrants.

name: Relling
one_liner: deploying the first billion robots for manufacturing
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Specialty manufacturers, with a focus on the defense industrial base, per a job posting
problem: Manufacturers struggle to deploy robots on varied tasks; Relling builds a deployment layer combining classical motion control with learned manipulation in hybrid robotic cells.
business_model: Deployed robotic cells in manufacturing operations (commercial terms not public)
product_category: Industrial robotics and physical AI deployment
market_need_then: Robotics startup funding was reported at $6 billion in the first seven months of 2025 per Crunchbase data, and defense industrial base reshoring created manufacturing demand; Relling-specific demand evidence was not found.
outcome_analysis: Relling is a very young company, active as of late 2026 and hiring per directories, with no coverage of customers, funding or setbacks. Its stated focus on defense-related manufacturing is a plausible wedge but there is no public evidence yet of traction, so the outcome is undetermined.

name: Remedy
one_liner: AI Agents for Pharmacies
long_description: Streamline prescription refills, reduce workload, and enhance patient care with intelligent automation.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: Independent and chain pharmacies
problem: Pharmacy staff spend much of their day on phone calls and data entry for prescription refills instead of patient care.
business_model: B2B SaaS for pharmacy AI voice and data entry agents
product_category: Healthcare voice AI
founder_names: Vishnu Sreenivasan; Nikhil Devaraj; Sai Mandhan
market_need_then: Pharmacies were short staffed and refill calls are a repetitive load, which several 2025 vendors targeted.
outcome_analysis: Remedy joined YC in Fall 2025 as a two person team building AI agents for pharmacy refills. The YC directory marks it acquired, yet two searches found no acquirer, date or news, and a founder is listed as former. With no public cause the outcome is unexplained and no factors are recorded.

name: Revise Robotics

Our first product is an AI-enabled robotic system that integrates with these facilities to assess and refurbish hundreds of laptops a day without any human intervention. name: Rimba
one_liner: Streamlining Data Capture to Report Creation for Heavy Industries
long_description:
Rimba integrates fragmented data — PDFs, Excel files, time-series, IoT sensors, equipment telemetry, and system performance data — to complete a workflow, such as populating a database, running analytics, and creating a report. 

Our software streamlines the entire journey from data capture to report creation for the physical world, starting with heavy industries such as renewables, oil & gas, supply chain, and chemicals. 

Legacy systems don't communicate, and critical operational data remains siloed. Rimba bridges that gap by connecting data from fragmented systems and structures — ERPs, SCADA, SharePoint, email, and more — to automate workflows, classify inputs, transform data, and improve data monitoring.

name: Risely AI
one_liner: AI agents that automate administrative work across college campuses.
long_description:
Risely’s AI agents will form the new operating system for universities, improving retention, staff productivity, and efficiency. Our platform integrates directly into existing university systems (SIS, LMS, CRM), learns each institution’s unique workflows, and deploys specialized AI agents. This dramatically reduces the $735 billion universities spend annually on administrative labor, expands staff capacity without increasing headcount, and improves the student experience.

This hasn't been done before because university workflows require nuanced, autonomous judgment, exactly what agentic AI was designed to solve. Our team uniquely combines deep expertise in higher education, enterprise-scale AI, and regulated enterprise sales.

Sadia previously built Salesforce’s Education Cloud from scratch, creating the core Student Information System widely used across higher education. She deeply understands university operations and maintains trusted relationships with hundreds of higher-ed CIOs and Provosts.

Danial was one of DoorDash’s earliest engineers, where he architected and scaled complex systems from zero to billions of transactions, including their search, recommendation, and Voice AI platforms. He knows how to build robust AI solutions that reliably perform at enterprise scale. 

Shahryar was a GM at Airwallex, where he built the entire Americas business from 0 to 1 and drove 11x revenue growth.  He’s also a master closer, single-handedly securing over $17M in enterprise deals at NerdWallet.  He’s a relentless startup executor with deep expertise launching and scaling go-to-market machines in highly regulated industries.

We launched six weeks ago and are already at $8k MRR, growing 55% week-over-week -- one of the fastest ramps ever in higher ed. Universities urgently need solutions that expand labor capacity and efficiency, especially as they face unprecedented budget pressure and staffing shortages.

With unmatched buyer access, deep technical expertise, and rapid early traction, we are perfectly positioned to own this enormous market.

problem: Universities spend heavily on administrative labor and lose students to avoidable attrition because data sits in separate SIS, LMS and CRM systems and staff are overloaded.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS sold to institutions, agent modules by function (advising, registrar, retention, admissions)

name: Riviera
one_liner: AI Employees for Hotels
long_description:
Riviera builds AI Employees for Hotels. Our first agent is a hotel phone receptionist that lets hotels spend less time answering phone calls and more time helping customers. Our system handles front-desk inquiries, in-room dining orders, and reservations. It answers every question instantly and in any language, 24/7.

We are solving a problem that older phone systems and IVRs can't: customers hate not being able to talk to someone immediately, but most travel businesses can’t dedicate additional staff to manage phone lines. Voice AI has always seemed out of reach because the technology infrastructure in the travel industry is often fragmented, with reservation systems, loyalty programs, and in-house operations software that weren’t designed with voice AI in mind. Riviera addresses this by integrating seamlessly with existing software providers and using human-sounding voice models that are highly trained on data specific to each business type and department.

Hotels spend hundreds of billions annually on staffing and risk losing potential revenue when phone lines are overwhelmed or callers hang up. By enabling them to handle unlimited calls, day or night, Riviera unlocks additional revenue and eases labor challenges.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: Hotel phone lines are overwhelmed and staffed thinly; legacy IVRs frustrate callers and lose bookings.
business_model: B2B SaaS in three tiers (Boutique, Property, Portfolio) with a 14 day free trial
product_category: Voice AI receptionist for hospitality

market_need_then: Hotels cannot staff phones around the clock and callers hang up; the company claims hotels lose revenue when lines are overwhelmed (company claim, no external data found).

name: Roark
one_liner: Test, monitor, and improve your voice agents
long_description:
Roark helps teams test, monitor, and improve their voice agents.

Voice AI is exploding, but reliability is still the #1 challenge. Teams spend hours manually testing agents and still miss failures. In the last 6 months, Roark has processed over 10M minutes of calls, powering monitoring and simulation for teams across the Voice AI ecosystem (including YC companies).

We close that gap by combining:

 📊 Monitoring & Evaluation - 40+ built-in metrics (latency, instruction-follow, sentiment, etc.), custom dashboards, alerts, and the ability to define your own. Up to 15 speakers with automatic speaker identification.
 🎭 Simulations & Personas - end-to-end phone/WebSocket simulations for inbound and outbound agents, with configurable personas (accents, languages, speech & behavior profiles). Define tests as conversations with a graph-based approach, so you can easily branch into edge cases and variants.
 🔁 Full lifecycle loop - failed calls automatically become repeatable tests, so every failure makes your agent stronger.

Roark is the missing QA layer for Voice AI - helping teams ship agents they can trust.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams building and operating voice AI agents (including YC companies)
problem: Voice agent teams test calls by hand and miss failures; reliability is the top blocker to production.
business_model: Usage based B2B SaaS for voice agent QA, simulation and monitoring
product_category: Voice AI testing and observability
market_need_then: Voice AI adoption was growing and teams reported reliability as the main problem; the company says it processed over 10M call minutes in six months (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Roark is an active Winter 2025 company in voice agent QA. It benefits from the growth of voice AI and has integrations with major voice frameworks, but it faces funded rivals such as Hamming and Coval. Funding is only visible in aggregators and no exit or shutdown was found, so it has stalled or succeeded in no confirmed way yet.

name: Rocketable
one_liner: The AI Maximalist Software Holding Company
long_description:
Rocketable is building a large portfolio of wildly profitable software businesses by acquiring existing products and replacing human teams with AI agents.

Today’s foundation models already possess enough intelligence to automate most of the tasks required to run a profitable software business. In the functions where agents aren’t yet intelligent enough to replace humans, they will be soon.

When every human function required to operate a software product has an AI agent equivalent, the next step will be within reach: operating an entire company with a team of AI agents instead of humans.

But superintelligent agents within each function won’t be enough. To operate a software company with 0 human employees, the agents will need to be directed towards common goals, integrated to collaborate across functions, tuned with feedback loops connected to product metrics, and trained to make resource allocation decisions.

We are creating the tools needed to replace the entire org chart of a software company with a team of AI agents. We are developing these tools by owning the products that we automate, because we know from 10+ years of experience building automated systems with AI/ML that integration is the key to unlocking superhuman performance.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Owners and sellers of small profitable software products, and its own customers once acquired
problem: Many small software businesses run with human teams for tasks AI agents could do; the company wants to acquire them and replace the org chart with agents.
business_model: Software holding company that acquires products and operates them with AI agents
product_category: AI operated software holding company
market_need_then: The founder says he began experimenting in 2023 after buying a small business on Acquire.com; the thesis rests on foundation models automating most software company tasks (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Rocketable is an active Winter 2025 company that raised a reported 6.5M seed in 2025 and has public thesis writing, but no verified completed acquisitions turned up in search. Its outcome depends on acquiring and profitably operating software with agents, which is unproven; no shutdown or exit was found.

RowFlow replaces clunky web forms with natural conversations that run over text, slack, or wherever your users are. Our platform increases your form’s response rates while cutting your internal overhead in half. 

With RowFlow, you can take any existing form and instantly convert it into an AI-powered conversation. New flows launch in minutes and reach respondents over your preferred channel or embedded chat. We guide the exchange, follow up automatically, and return clean structured data without extra work from your team.

Forms power billions of business interactions yearly. Whether it’s forms for client intake, registrations, compliance, feedback, or surveys, they all follow the same painful pattern: low conversion, messy data, and frustrated users. Teams have long tolerated forms only because there's been no scalable alternative for collecting structured information from people - until now. Our goal is for RowFlow to become the new default way for how organizations collect user data in an AI-first world.

name: SF Tensor
one_liner: Infrastructure for AI labs to focus on research.
long_description:
AI researchers should be pushing the boundaries of what's possible with new architectures and training methods. Instead, they waste weeks configuring cloud infrastructure, debugging distributed systems, and optimizing their GPU code. We know because we lived it: While training our own models across thousands of GPUs earlier this year, we spent more time fighting our infrastructure than doing actual research.

That's why we're building two things. First, Elastic Cloud: a managed platform that automatically finds the cheapest GPUs across all providers, handles spot instance preemption, and cuts compute costs by up to 80%. Second, automatic kernel optimization that makes training code run faster by modeling hardware topology, often beating hand-tuned implementations.

The problem is that getting high performance across different hardware is genuinely hard. NVIDIA's CUDA moat exists because writing fast kernels requires deep expertise. Most teams either accept vendor lock-in or hire expensive kernel engineers. Our goal is to break the CUDA moat.

The compute bottleneck is the biggest constraint on AI progress. NVIDIA can't manufacture enough GPUs, and their monopoly keeps prices astronomical. Meanwhile, AMD, Google, and Amazon are shipping capable alternative hardware that nobody uses because the software is too hard. We're breaking that moat. If we succeed, anyone will be able to train state-of-the-art models without thinking past their PyTorch code.

problem: Researchers waste weeks on cloud setup, distributed training and kernel tuning; GPU costs are high and CUDA creates vendor lock-in.

product_category: AI training infrastructure and GPU compiler

market_need_then: GPU scarcity and cost, CUDA lock-in and the growth of AI training created demand; a December 2025 interview reports $41K usage revenue in two weeks after launch (single source).

Surveys ask people what they think they’ll do. Focus groups ask a handful of people to explain behavior they often don’t understand themselves.

The output is not another dashboard. It’s a prediction of what will happen, which segments will drive it, and what decision is most likely to win.

name: Scalar Field
one_liner: Your Agentic Trading Desk — Building the next era of agentic…
long_description:
We’re building the agentic trading desk for the new operating system of markets.

I used to be a trader at Tower Research and Goldman Sachs, and I’m building Scalar Field with my co-founder Ramakant, who led engineering teams at Microsoft.

We’ve both spent our careers at the intersection of finance and technology, and we’re using that experience to rethink how markets are analyzed, tested, and traded in the age of agents.

Scalar Field is built around a simple belief: over the next few years, agents will not just help people research markets — they will actively participate in them.

They will monitor news, parse filings, track sentiment, test hypotheses, rebalance portfolios, and execute trades. They will turn ideas into strategies, and strategies into live portfolios.

But today’s financial infrastructure was not built for that world.

Terminals are dashboards. Backtesting tools are fragmented. Execution systems are separate. Market data is hard to unify. And most platforms still assume the human is the only decision-maker.

Scalar Field changes that.

We’re building an agentic trading platform where users can create financial agents that research data, backtest strategies, monitor market events, and trigger trades when specific conditions are met.

The long-term vision is agentic ETFs: portfolios created, managed, and rebalanced by agents around any idea, narrative, event, or market signal.

Scalar Field lets users go from thesis to backtest to live portfolio in one place.

It is infrastructure for the agentic trading era.

problem: Terminals are dashboards, backtesting and execution tools are fragmented and market data is hard to unify for agent driven trading.

product_category: agentic trading platform

product_category: Expert STEM training and evaluation data
market_need_then: Labs shifted demand toward STEM experts in 2025 and reportedly pay over 125 USD per hour per Handshake's CEO; frontier models scoring near zero on the hardest problems is the company's own claim.
outcome_analysis: Sciloop is a Fall 2025 YC company, Active with a team of six, selling Olympiad level math and physics problems to AI labs. No customers are named and funding figures vary by aggregator, so traction is unverified. It enters a market where Mercor, Handshake, Turing and Surge were already large, so its edge depends on elite problem quality.

name: Scoop
one_liner: Automating regulatory submissions for life sciences
long_description: We’re building AI agents that speed up drug trials by automating the manual consolidation and document prep required for every IND submission. Today, biotechs spend months stitching together reports from contractors and internal teams just to file and get to their first-in-human trial.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Biotechs, pharma companies and CROs preparing IND submissions for first-in-human trials
problem: Biotechs spend months stitching together reports from contractors and internal teams to assemble an IND submission. Scoop drafts modules from study reports, CMC data and protocols and checks consistency across the dossier.
business_model: B2B SaaS for regulatory submission drafting (pricing not public)
product_category: AI regulatory document automation for life sciences
market_need_then: The YC description says biotechs spend months consolidating contractor and internal reports to file an IND. A December 2025 industry guide notes sponsors remain responsible for what they file, so AI is positioned as drafting support.
outcome_analysis: Scoop is an active Fall 2025 company with two founders, one of whom has direct IND and clinical trial experience from Corestem and Genentech. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news exists. Weave Bio had already launched a competing IND drafting product in 2024, so the open question is whether source-cited drafting wins customers against it. Funding is not public beyond the YC deal.

name: Scott AI
one_liner: The planning layer for teams that build with coding agents
long_description:
Coding agents made writing code fast. But 6 engineers in a room will probably still disagree on what needs to be built.

Scott AI is a planning workspace where engineering teams align on what to build before their coding agents start building it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams that build software with coding agents
problem: Coding agents make writing code fast, but engineers on a team still disagree about what to build. Scott is a planning workspace where teams align on a spec before agents start coding.
business_model: B2B SaaS for engineering teams (free trial download, demo for teams; pricing not found)
product_category: Spec and planning workspace for AI coding agents
market_need_then: Agent coding speeds up implementation, so alignment on what to build becomes the bottleneck for multi-engineer teams, according to the YC description. The spec-driven tooling wave of 2025 shows vendor attention to the same pain.
outcome_analysis: Scott AI is an active Fall 2025 company with a CEO from Coinbase and a CTO with startup and Stanford AI training. No acquisition or shutdown news was found. It entered a crowded spec-driven development category where AWS and GitHub shipped products in 2025, so outcomes depend on whether a neutral team planning layer beats bundled vendor features. Funding beyond the YC deal is not public.

name: Scout
one_liner: AI-powered student information system for K-12 schools
long_description:
The student information system (SIS) is the core system of record in every K-12 school. It tracks students, attendance, grades, schedules, staff, and more - kind of like the ERP for schools.

Legacy SIS providers do just about that, and not much more. School districts layer dozens of tools on top of their SIS to fill in the gaps.

Scout is an AI-powered student information system that automates school- and district-wide busywork, from day-to-day operations like attendance tracking to annual compliance reports. Our mission is to help school districts run like high-performing organizations, enabling them to provide high-quality, personalized instruction to every student.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: K-12 schools and districts, starting with California and Oregon independent study, charter and personalized learning programs
problem: Legacy student information systems store records but leave schools to bolt on dozens of tools for attendance, enrollment and compliance. Scout automates that busywork, including audit packets and state reporting.
business_model: B2B SaaS per school or district (pricing not public)
product_category: AI-native student information system
market_need_then: Schools layer many tools on a legacy SIS and juggle annual compliance reports, according to the YC page. The company says it targets California and Oregon independent study programs where attendance and work sample audits are heavy.
outcome_analysis: Scout is an active Winter 2025 company serving California and Oregon independent study schools, with named school testimonials on its site. No acquisition or shutdown news was found, and a software engineer job post suggests it was hiring. Incumbent PowerSchool added AI assistants on top of its SIS rather than replacing it, which leaves room for an AI-native system of record. Funding beyond the YC deal is not publicly confirmed.

name: Selfin
one_liner: Institutional liquidity across prediction markets
long_description: Bring us risk. We’ll find the market. Institutional liquidity for event-driven exposure across prediction markets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies with revenue exposed to a single event (airlines, AI and GPU businesses, sports clubs), per the current site
problem: Risks that insurance and futures do not cover leave CFOs exposed to single events. Selfin sources institutional market makers to create event contracts on regulated prediction market venues.
business_model: Brokerage or intermediary fees on event contracts (not stated); the company says it is registering as an introducing broker with the NFA
product_category: Prediction market liquidity and event risk hedging
market_need_then: The current site points to corporate exposure to single events that insurance and futures miss. 2026 trade press describes corporate hedging with event contracts as emerging but limited by basis risk, liquidity and settlement questions.
outcome_analysis: Selfin is an active Fall 2025 company that appears to have pivoted from an AI personal finance bank to institutional event contracts on prediction markets. Founders have aerospace, quant and consulting backgrounds. Nothing was found on funding, traction or outcomes. The market it chose grew fast in 2026, with Kalshi raising $1B, but Kalshi and others also court institutions directly.

name: SellRaze
one_liner: The fastest way to sell online.
long_description:
SellRaze is an AI-powered selling assistant that helps anyone sell anything in seconds. Point your camera at any item and we'll identify it, price it, and create an engaging listing across multiple marketplaces, including our own.

Each day, more than 2,500 items are added to SellRaze, representing over $326,000 in inventory value.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individual resellers and casual sellers listing secondhand goods on marketplaces
problem: Creating listings across multiple marketplaces is slow and manual.
business_model: consumer/prosumer app (subscription implied, not confirmed) plus own marketplace
product_category: AI listing and cross-posting tool
market_need_then: Cross-listing across Poshmark, eBay and Mercari is an established paid category (multiple 2025 comparison guides). YC launch post claims 200,000+ signups; site claims 600,000+ sellers (company claims).
outcome_analysis: SellRaze (Fall 2025, Active) shows fast self-reported user growth for a seven-person team, with a seed from YC, Pioneer Fund and Tekedia Capital per aggregators, but no independent traction or priced round was verified. It sells into a crowded crosslisting category where marketplaces and incumbents add AI listing features, so differentiation on listing speed alone may be hard; the outcome is not yet visible.

name: Semble
one_liner: Takeoffs, design, and field work. Powered by AI.
long_description:
Takeoffs, design, and field work. Powered by AI. Mark up plans. Organize documents. Collaborate on PDFs. Keep crews moving.

Jonathan and Ethan met studying computer science at Stanford. Jonathan worked at Convergint, one of the world's largest building system integrators.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Building system integrators and contractors (fire, HVAC, plumbing, security) that do takeoffs, design and field work
problem: Integrators mark up plans, organize documents and do takeoffs and design by hand. Semble uses AI to speed takeoffs, design and field coordination.
business_model: B2B SaaS for contractors and integrators (pricing not found)
product_category: AI software for building systems design and takeoffs
market_need_then: Takeoff, design and field work in building systems are labor heavy; the company's own pitch is that AI can speed them. No dated demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: Semble is an active Fall 2025 company founded by two Stanford classmates, one of whom worked at the integrator Convergint. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found. Funding beyond the YC deal is not confirmed, and no traction data is public. AI takeoff tools from other vendors expanded through 2025 and 2026, so differentiation will depend on the building systems focus.

name: Semiotic
one_liner: Studio-Grade Design at Scale
long_description:
Semiotic builds AI design agents. We’re starting with agents that build landing pages for fast‑growing startups. 

Existing AI website builders didn't make creating websites easier—they made creating ugly websites easier. So, companies choose between blue-purple gradient slop or agencies with 3-month waitlists and $100k minimums.

You don't have to choose anymore. 

Start a project: semiotic.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Fast-growing startups that need studio-quality landing pages
problem: AI website builders make ugly pages easier while agencies have long waitlists and $100K minimums. Semiotic builds AI design agents that produce landing pages at studio quality.
business_model: Project-based or subscription design service delivered by AI agents (pricing not found)
product_category: AI design agents for landing pages
market_need_then: The YC page claims $78,000 in revenue in the first four weeks after launch (company stated, unverified). Agency costs and waitlists named in the description are the demand signal.
outcome_analysis: Semiotic is an active Fall 2025 company claiming $78,000 revenue in its first four weeks. No acquisition or shutdown news was found. Founders combine a brand design background with AI research at Columbia. The category was crowded by 2025 launches such as PageAI and Framer add-ons, so quality of output is the bet. Funding beyond the YC deal is not confirmed.

name: Sennu AI
one_liner: We turn traditional companies into AI companies
long_description: Sennu AI builds AI systems that fundamentally transform how your business operates
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises and Salesforce consulting and development teams

business_model: B2B software and services, pricing not found
product_category: Enterprise AI agents, Salesforce developer tools
market_need_then: Large Salesforce developer and consulting ecosystem with code review needs; the founders grew up around Salesforce consulting per YC page.
outcome_analysis: Sennu AI joined YC in Winter 2025 with two founders from Brex and Confluent and launched Salesforce code review, QA testing and a sales agent. A separate profile says it now helps enterprises deploy Claude, which suggests a broadening of scope. No funding, customer or outcome news was found, so the outcome is open.

name: Serafis
one_liner: Deep intelligence for private markets
long_description: Serafis is building the AI knowledge graph for market intelligence, starting with the information frontier. Trusted by top investors ($70B+ AUM) and the largest global consulting firms.

target_customer: Institutional investors (claims $70B+ client AUM) and large consulting firms

business_model: B2B SaaS/data product with web platform, REST API, MCP server and data warehouse feed (pricing not public)
product_category: AI market-intelligence knowledge graph
