name: Sherpa Labs
one_liner: Frontier Data
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying benchmarks, data products and expert network access (per the company site)
problem: Frontier models need high quality, hard to source data and evaluations. Sherpa Labs sells benchmarks, data products and an expert network.
business_model: Data and evaluation sales to AI labs (pricing not found)
product_category: Frontier AI training data and benchmarks
market_need_then: The site says its backers include angels from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, which implies lab interest. No dated market data was gathered because the competitor search found nothing from early 2025.
outcome_analysis: Sherpa Labs is an active Winter 2025 company led by one founder with data science and quant research experience, including a role at Surge. It appears to have moved from an agentic data science team to selling frontier data and benchmarks. No acquisition or shutdown news was found. Funding and traction are not public, so its path in a crowded data vendor market is unknown.

name: Shor
one_liner: International payroll, built for founders
long_description:
Shor is international payroll, built for founders. Hire your first international employee or contractor at startup speed. Set up on one call, run payroll the same week.

Pay contractors and employ full-time team members through Shor's EOR across the world. Localized contracts, automatic compliance, and same-day local-currency payouts at a flat FX margin. No setup fees, no lock-ins.

Backed by Polychain Capital, Founders Capital, and Goodwater, among others.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startup founders hiring their first international contractors and employees
problem: Hiring abroad requires localized contracts, compliance and local currency payouts that are slow and expensive. Shor offers contractor payments in 150+ countries and employer of record in about 70 markets with a disclosed FX margin.
business_model: Per person monthly fees ($19 contractor, $299 EOR, about $50 to $60 own entity) plus a 2% FX margin, per the company site
product_category: International payroll and employer of record
market_need_then: Founders hiring abroad face setup time, legal cost and FX fees; the YC launch positions Shor as the fastest and cheapest option. Competitors such as Rise show demand for stablecoin payroll in 2025.
outcome_analysis: Shor is an active Summer 2025 company that launched international payroll and EOR in 2025 with stated backing from Polychain Capital, Founders Capital and Goodwater, though amounts are not public. The CEO's Founders Brew community gives a distribution channel. No acquisition or shutdown news exists. Deel and others added stablecoin payouts by 2026, so the wedge faces strong incumbents.

name: SigmanticAI
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; B2B; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: The Cursor for Chip Design - Delivering Silicon-Ready Chip Designs…
long_description:
SigmanticAI is building an AI-native hardware development assistant that automates the entire RTL design flow, from natural language to synthesizable HDL and testbenches, inside a seamless VSCode fork. Powered by fine-tuned Verilog LLMs, reinforcement learning, and real compiler feedback, SigmanticAI iteratively refines code until it compiles and passes synthesis, no matter how complex the design. It’s like the Cursor for HDL design. 

In addition to code generation, SigmanticAI can generate token-level annotations and onboarding documents to accelerate ramp-up for new engineers. With support for both cloud and on-prem deployment, it integrates with existing EDA tools to dramatically reduce debug time, improve collaboration, and accelerate hardware design across teams
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Chip design and verification engineering teams (RTL, FPGA, ASIC)
problem: Writing and verifying RTL and testbenches is slow and manual.
business_model: Developer tool installed via pip and a VS Code fork; pricing not found
product_category: AI assistant for chip design and verification (EDA)
market_need_then: Chip design labor shortage and LLM progress; YC launch post reports first paying customer and conversations with Northrop Grumman, SciEngines and Quadric engineers.
outcome_analysis: SigmanticAI is a Summer 2025 YC company of two Berkeley-trained founders with hardware and ML backgrounds, building an AI assistant for chip design. It is Active, reports a first paying customer, but funding beyond an aggregator-listed $500K is unknown and it is too early to judge a success or failure outcome.

name: Sim
one_liner: Build autonomous AI agents for enterprise systems
long_description: Sim is a platform to build autonomous AI agents for enterprise systems. Teams connect their integrations and Sim builds a knowledge graph of company data and processes; from there, they work with Sim to build and monitor the AI agents and workflows that run production systems.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering and operations teams at companies that build and run AI agents and workflows, plus individual developers using the open source project
problem: Building reliable AI agent workflows required boilerplate code and opaque framework abstractions. Sim offers a visual canvas where the workflow is explicit.
business_model: Open source core with hosted freemium tiers (Free, Pro, Max, Enterprise); prices not shown on the site
product_category: AI agent workflow builder and workspace
market_need_then: Spring 2025 saw rapid interest in agent builders; the founders cited frustration with boilerplate-heavy frameworks, and the open source repo attracted thousands of GitHub stars within months.
outcome_analysis: Sim grew from an April 2025 Show HN open source launch to a $7M Series A in November 2025 led by Standard Capital, with company reported adoption of about 60,000 developers and over 100 production companies. The open source distribution and the agent boom helped it, while the forkable licence and crowded visual builder market remain risks. It is active with no exit.

name: Sira
one_liner: AI Native Rippling for Deskless Workers
long_description:
Sira is the AI-powered platform for managing time tracking, scheduling, payroll, and HR — purpose-built for hourly teams.

Our intelligent agents handle the manual, time-consuming tasks for you — like calling workers to fill open shifts, detecting timesheet anomalies, and streamlining payroll processing.

With Sira, businesses stay organized, compliant, and focused on what really matters — while we take care of the team.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and mid-size businesses with hourly deskless workers, such as security, cleaning, landscaping and valet companies
problem: Existing time, scheduling and payroll tools are built for desk workers and need tech savviness; managers spend hours chasing timesheets and filling shifts.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat (YC launch post mentioned a 25% per-seat discount)
product_category: AI HR, payroll and workforce management for hourly teams
market_need_then: Hourly teams use clunky tools designed for desk workers per the YC launch post; Intuit's own later launch indicates the segment's size.
outcome_analysis: Sira is an early-stage company that raised a reported $3.4M seed in November 2025 and lists a customer base of security, cleaning, landscaping and valet firms. The CEO's Intuit workforce background fits the problem, but Intuit launched a competing AI workforce suite in May 2026. Outcome is still open and no exit or distress was found.

name: Sixtyfour
one_liner: Intelligence Infrastructure on People and Entities
long_description: Sixtyfour deploys AI agents that investigate people and companies across the open and dark web, official records, proprietary databases, and unstructured sources. We resolve identities, map entity relationships, and surface risk signals for teams where data quality is essential.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Go-to-market, risk and compliance teams that need verified data on people and companies
problem: Contact and entity data from databases is incomplete; teams need agents that research open web, records and proprietary sources and resolve identities.
business_model: Usage-based API and platform subscription for data enrichment and research agents
product_category: AI agent data enrichment and entity intelligence
market_need_then: Sales and risk teams relied on static data vendors; a customer case study claims Apollo found contacts for about 25% of accounts versus 75% with Sixtyfour (vendor claim).
outcome_analysis: Sixtyfour is an early-stage company from the Spring 2025 batch with a 12 person team and an API product used by sales and risk teams. The only funding found is an unverified aggregator-reported $500K pre-seed, so its fundraising trajectory is unknown. It is active with product releases through November 2026 and no exit.

name: Slashy
tags: Productivity; Enterprise Software; Automation; Email; AI Assistant
one_liner: Cursor for Email
long_description: Slashy is an AI-native email client for founders and operators. It drafts replies in your voice from your sent mail, triages your inbox, tracks follow-ups, keeps your calendar in the inbox, and can be run from iMessage, Slack, or an AI agent through its MCP server. Slashy works with Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook.com, and Microsoft 365, on web, Mac, and iOS.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Founders and operators with heavy email loads, on Gmail, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365
problem: Inbox triage, replying and follow-up tracking consume hours; Slashy drafts in the user's voice and tracks follow-ups.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat (one review reports about $25 per seat monthly billed annually; reviews disagree)
product_category: AI native email client
market_need_then: Email overload is a long-standing pain; the 2025 agent wave made voice-matched drafting feasible.
outcome_analysis: Slashy entered YC as Dash AI, an AI website builder, and rebranded to Slashy in January 2026 around an email client. Listings report 1,000 active organizations by March 2026 and a June 2026 Product Hunt launch, but a co-founder reportedly left in June 2026 and the market is crowded with Gmail, Outlook and Superhuman. Funding beyond a $500K pre-seed is unclear.

name: Socratix AI
one_liner: AI coworkers for fraud and compliance teams.
long_description:
Socratix builds AI coworkers for fraud and compliance teams so that humans don't have to spend their days drowning in alerts and spreadsheets.

Today, fraud and risk teams at fintechs and banks are overwhelmed. Analysts jump between tools, manually stitch together context, and make judgment calls under pressure, often for hundreds of alerts a week. Too much of their work is slow, repetitive, and error-prone. We're here to change that. 

Socratix gives fraud and risk teams AI coworkers that investigate alerts in real time, replacing manual reviews with fast, explainable decisions. Socratix agents plug into existing workflows and reason across signals just like human analysts to help teams reduce fraud losses, minimize false positives, and scale operations without scaling headcount.

We've seen this problem firsthand. At DoorDash, Riya helped save $30M+ a year by building smarter fraud detection and investigation tooling, and at Unit21, she built products for analysts that made them 3X faster. We're able to build and sell enterprise-grade software. At Cruise, Satya built scalable AI systems powering petabyte-scale data, and at LinkedIn, he built enterprise products from 0 to 1 generating $50M+ in incremental revenue. Now, the two of us are teaming up to eliminate the manual toil in fraud and compliance.

We're obsessed with fraud, LLMs, real-world automation, and the messy edge cases traditional ML has trouble handling. We believe that every fraud analyst should have an AI coworker - and the future of fraud will involve combining human-level reasoning with machine-speed execution.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Fraud, financial crimes and compliance teams at banks, credit unions and fintechs
problem: Analysts drown in alerts and stitch context across tools by hand; reviews can take a full day.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software, agents integrated into existing fraud stacks
product_category: AI agents for fraud and compliance operations
market_need_then: Fraud teams face high alert volume and false positives; founders cite hundreds of alerts per week per team and first hand experience at DoorDash and Unit21.
outcome_analysis: Socratix raised a $4.1M seed led by Pear VC in October 2025, shortly after its Summer 2025 YC batch, with founders from DoorDash, Unit21, Cruise and LinkedIn. It names bank and fintech case studies and presented at Finovate Spring 2026. It is early, active and without exit, and faces better funded fraud platforms adding agents.

name: Solidroad
one_liner: AI agents for CX teams, starting with training and QA.
long_description:
Solidroad builds AI agents for CX teams, starting with training and QA. Solidroad agents train human reps in a simulated environment, and evaluate their performance in live customer channels.

By starting with training and QA, our agents learn how humans learn, and their performance can be compared directly with human reps. This enables us to prove the value of the rest of the agents on our roadmap.

Since launching last summer, we’ve reduced onboarding times by 50% at several of the world’s largest outsourced contact centres/BPOs like PartnerHero and Tech Mahindra, and improved go-live CSAT at Crypto.com by 3% (now above 90% CSAT).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Customer experience and contact centre teams, including BPOs, that train and quality check support agents
problem: Manual QA reviews a tiny share of interactions and training is slow; Solidroad simulates conversations to train reps and scores live interactions.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS
product_category: AI training and quality assurance for customer experience teams
market_need_then: Contact centres review a small sample of conversations manually and BPOs need fast onboarding; Solidroad reports halving onboarding time at BPOs.
outcome_analysis: Solidroad moved from a $1.2M angel round in July 2024 to a $6.5M seed led by First Round in June 2025 and a $25M Series A led by Hedosophia in April 2026. Named enterprise customers include Crypto.com, Ryanair and ActiveCampaign. Expansion from training into QA of all interactions drove the larger round.

name: Solva
one_liner: Building the new superintelligence for insurance
long_description: Insurance is 13% of US GDP and we’re building the infrastructure to change how the world handles risk
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Insurers and MGAs (claims AI at launch); by 2026 businesses wanting to offer their own insurance via a licensed platform
problem: Claims handling is repetitive and wrongful payouts are costly; Solva checks policy terms against evidence with AI agents.
business_model: B2B software for carriers and MGAs; later a full-stack licensed insurer model
product_category: AI for insurance claims and insurance infrastructure

market_need_then: Insurance claims handling is labor intensive; the YC launch pitched 'Harvey for insurance'. Direct demand evidence was not found.

Funding details conflict between sources, though a SEK 57M seed with First Round and SV Angel is reported. The model change and licence-heavy path make the outcome uncertain with no exit.

name: Sorce
one_liner: Tinder for jobs
long_description: Tinder for Jobs. Swipe right, AI applies on your behalf.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individual job seekers (consumer), often free users with paid swipe tiers
problem: Applying to jobs is slow and repetitive; Sorce lets users swipe right and an AI agent fills the application on the employer's site.
business_model: Consumer subscription (one reviewer cites $15 per week for unlimited swipes); earlier a 15% recruitment commission was paused
product_category: Consumer AI job search and auto-apply app

Funding disclosed is small, with only Founders Inc. and angels named and no amount. Reviews are mixed on reliability and pricing, so durable retention is unproven.

name: Soren
one_liner: The AI Transformation Company
long_description:
Soren is an AI-native engineering firm that helps traditional businesses put AI to work.

We combine world-class engineering talent with AI-powered delivery to modernize legacy systems, build intelligent software, and solve complex business problems.

By pairing human expertise and judgment with the speed and efficiency of AI, we deliver better technology, faster and at a fraction of the cost of traditional engineering firms.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Established small, midsize and enterprise businesses in legal, finance, healthcare, logistics, government and nonprofits that want AI built into their workflows
problem: Traditional businesses lack the engineering talent to modernize legacy systems and put AI to work, and traditional engineering firms are slow and expensive.
business_model: Services: AI-native engineering firm selling embedded engineering projects and ongoing support
product_category: AI engineering services and consulting
market_need_then: Companies were under pressure to adopt AI in 2025 but lacked in-house engineers. The company's site cites case studies for a 250 person law firm, a private equity firm and a 200 person scholarship fund.
outcome_analysis: Soren is an active Fall 2025 YC company run by a single named founder. No exit, shutdown or layoff news was found. The positioning appears to have moved from AI evals and private AI infrastructure for regulated industries (YC launch listings) to a general AI transformation engineering firm, with the date of that shift unknown. Outcome is too early to judge and no priced round was found.

name: Sourcebot
one_liner: Helping humans and AI agents understand massive codebases
long_description:
Sourcebot is an open source code understanding platform for massive codebases. We’re used by thousands of engineers in some of the largest companies in the world, including NVIDIA, Red Hat, Wikimedia, and Arista Networks.

Understanding code, not writing it, is the primary bottleneck for large engineering teams. For developers, this means onboarding onto complex codebases faster. For AI agents, it means getting the necessary code context to minimize hallucinations and maximize cohesion within the wider codebase.

Sourcebot solves this by giving developers and AI agents the ability to regex search across millions of lines of code instantly, as well as ask questions across thousands of repos using any flagship reasoning model. Being open source and on-prem, we can get deployed in enterprises within minutes before other tools even get approval.

We met a decade ago at McGill University and have been building together full time for over 2 years. We’ve personally felt the pain of understanding large codebases while working at Microsoft, EA, Ubisoft, Google, and Meta.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams at large companies with big self-hosted codebases, plus AI coding agents that need code context
problem: Understanding code, not writing it, is the bottleneck for large engineering teams, and AI agents lack context across many repositories.
business_model: Open core (fair source) self-hosted software: free tier up to 5 users, Pro at 20 USD per user per month billed yearly, custom Enterprise
product_category: Code search and code understanding for developers
market_need_then: Large companies needed to search millions of lines across many repos and AI agents needed codebase context. The company says NVIDIA, Red Hat, Wikimedia and Arista engineers use it, and its site quotes a Red Hat security engineer.
outcome_analysis: Sourcebot started as an open source Sourcegraph alternative in September 2024 and joined YC in Fall 2025, then added AI Ask and MCP features for agents around October 2025. A search result says it moved to a fair source license in March 2026, which would narrow the open source positioning. It is active with named enterprise users, but no priced round or revenue figure is public.

name: Specific
one_liner: The cloud platform built for coding agents
long_description: Specific lets your coding agent write code and build the infrastructure to deploy it. Connect your favorite coding agent and start building immediately. Run `specific dev` to get a full local environment running in seconds. Run `specific deploy` to go to production on our scalable cloud platform in minutes.
regions: Sweden; Europe
target_customer: Developers and AI coding platforms (for example Natively) whose coding agents need a backend and cloud deployment
problem: Coding agents can write code but need infrastructure, databases, auth and deployment that they can provision themselves.
business_model: Usage-based cloud platform and backend as a service for coding agents
product_category: Cloud platform and backend infrastructure for AI coding agents

outcome_analysis: Specific is an active two person Stockholm company from YC Fall 2025 that offers a cloud platform driven by coding agents. It shows early usage through Neon (over 10,000 databases) and a Natively partnership, but no priced round is public. Crowded agent backend competition and a generic name are the main risks, and the outcome is still open.

name: Specific Labs
tags: Generative AI; Reinforcement Learning; B2B; AI
one_liner: Real World Environments and Data for AI
long_description: Specific builds enterprise environments and datasets representative of work inside real-world businesses. The next frontier of AGI is bottlenecked by data that is hard to access, and we make that easier.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI labs and enterprises that need realistic enterprise environments, codebases and datasets for training and evaluating agents
problem: Frontier AI progress is bottlenecked by hard to access data from real businesses.
business_model: Dataset licensing and evaluation benchmark as a sales channel (per press commentary)
product_category: AI training data, environments and benchmarks
market_need_then: AI labs were spending heavily on training environments and evaluation data in 2025. The company launched Real-SWE on 2026-09-12 and coverage in the trade press followed.
outcome_analysis: The company entered YC in Fall 2025 as Bear, a generative engine optimization product with 60 plus customers, and later became Specific Labs selling real world enterprise environments and datasets for AI. Real-SWE in September 2026 brought press attention. Funding is not verified and the pivot is too recent to judge whether the data business works.

name: Splash Inc.
one_liner: Autonomous patrol-boats for National Security
long_description: Splash is developing the next generation of autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to provide National Security and defend critical assets such as oil rigs and shipping terminals. Our long-term vision is to make traditional naval vessels obsolete by creating a fleet of low-cost and versatile boats which will be able to dominate the seas. Our expertise in mass manufacturing, engineering and quickly scaling operations will make this vision a reality.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: National security and defense buyers (navies, coast guards) plus operators protecting oil rigs, shipping terminals and harbors
problem: Crewed naval patrol vessels cost tens of millions of dollars, so critical maritime assets are hard to defend at scale.
business_model: Hardware sales of autonomous surface vessels plus command and control software and mission payload modules
product_category: Defense autonomous surface vessels
market_need_then: Navies were seeking low cost uncrewed vessels, and defense tech funding for maritime autonomy grew in 2024 and 2025, with Replicator style programs. The company later demonstrated resupply of USS Essex at RIMPAC 2026 (reported July 2026).
outcome_analysis: Splash joined YC in Winter 2025 as a two founder maritime autonomy startup and by July 2026 had a fielded Typhoon USV that completed a reported first autonomous resupply of a US warship at RIMPAC. It then added an Airstrike Pack payload (2026-08) and is preparing the larger Tempest. Funding is not verified in primary sources, so capital strength relative to well funded rivals is unknown.

name: Spotlight Realty
one_liner: AI powered brokerage reducing residential rental commissions in NYC…
long_description: We are a full-service sell-side residential brokerage that lists and markets your properties. We also screen and schedule tenants showings with our AI agent for a third of the normal commission.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: NYC landlords, property managers and sellers who list rentals
problem: Traditional brokerage rental commissions are high, and after the FARE Act landlords must pay the broker fee and handle tours, applications and screening.
business_model: Brokerage commission, about 4 percent of rent (about a third of the typical rate), with an AI agent handling inquiries and scheduling
product_category: AI powered residential real estate brokerage
founder_names: Raymond Allie; Jake Phelan; Aryan Sharma
market_need_then: The FARE Act (June 2025) barred landlords from passing broker fees to tenants, pushing landlords to look for cheaper leasing. The Real Deal in August 2025 named Spotlight as one discount entrant.
outcome_analysis: Spotlight Realty is a Summer 2025 YC company that began serving NYC rentals in June 2025, just as the FARE Act changed who pays broker fees. It undercuts brokers at 4 percent with an AI agent. It is active with no exit or shutdown news, but there is no verified funding or revenue and the legal future of the FARE Act is uncertain.

name: Spott
tags: SaaS; B2B; HR Tech; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: AI-native ATS/CRM for recruiting firms
long_description:
Spott is the first AI-native ATS/CRM for recruiting & staffing firms. We built Spott because existing recruitment platforms require extensive manual work, are clunky to use, rely on fragmented add-ons, and are not designed for AI adoption.

Spott combines everything recruiting firms need, from a full ATS & CRM to AI agents across the entire workflow, into one AI-native solution. It enables recruiters to focus on what matters most and close more placements.
regions: Belgium; Europe
target_customer: Recruiting and staffing agencies (permanent, executive search, contract, temp and RPO)
problem: Recruiters lose time to manual logging and clunky ATS tools that store data without using it, and legacy platforms cannot support AI natively.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat (comparison pages list about 149 USD per user per month)
product_category: AI native ATS and CRM for recruiting firms
founder_names: Lander Degreve; Manu Vanderveeren; Samuel Smeys
market_need_then: The founders saw agencies losing time to manual logging while consulting for them. Customers named on the site migrated from Bullhorn, Loxo, Vincere, JobAdder and others.
outcome_analysis: Spott started in November 2024, pivoted during YC from a report writer to a full AI native ATS, raised a 3.2M seed and then a 21M Series A led by Balderton in September 2026. The company says ARR passed 1M euros by about February 2026 and 500 plus agencies use it. These are company claims and the later growth rests on a crowded market with several AI native rivals.

name: Stamp
one_liner: The AI Secretary for Email and Calendar.
long_description:
Stamp is the first AI Native inbox. It's more than an email client, though -- it's like your second brain.

Stamp can respond to emails in your voice, organize your inbox to filter out the noise, keep track of action items, and automate essentially every task you're doing manually in your inbox today.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Professionals and teams who spend heavy time in email and calendar
problem: Email and calendar admin consumes hours of knowledge workers' time and inbox tools do not act on their behalf.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer SaaS subscription with a 30 day free trial
product_category: AI native email client and AI secretary
market_need_then: Heavy email load and LLM drafting made AI inbox tools a hot category in early 2025. The product launched on YC with a year of free access for signups within one week (2025-02).
outcome_analysis: Stamp is a one person Winter 2025 YC company building an AI native email client that later repositioned as an AI secretary for email and calendar with mobile apps. There is no exit or shutdown news. It competes with Gmail, Superhuman, Shortwave and Fyxer in a category where incumbents added AI features quickly, and no verified funding or revenue was found.

name: StarSling
one_liner: Agent-native GitHub Actions runners
long_description: Drop-in Ubuntu runners plus AI agents that open optimization PRs for your workflows. StarSling Runners continuously improve your CI to make it up to 10x faster and 13x cheaper.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams that run CI on GitHub Actions and pay per runner minute
problem: GitHub Actions hosted runners are slow and relatively expensive, and CI workflows rarely get optimized after they are written.
business_model: usage-based per minute runners, plus review runners and enterprise contracts
product_category: Developer tools, CI runners with AI agents
market_need_then: Teams complained about GitHub Actions cost and speed and a market of third party runner vendors had formed by 2024 and 2025, as the competitor sources show.
outcome_analysis: StarSling is active and early. Experienced founders with a prior exit raised a reported $3M pre-seed with Bessemer and Y Combinator in 2026 while selling into a crowded market of faster CI runners, so its edge depends on the AI agent layer rather than the runners themselves. No outcome beyond fundraising is public yet.

name: Steinmetz
one_liner: Next-Generation Power Electronics
long_description:
Steinmetz is building the next generation of American power electronics. The next generation of great machines — electric vehicles, robotics, aerospace, and industrial systems — depends on power electronics that are lighter, cheaper, more efficient, and built at real scale.

We push the Pareto frontier of power electronics through multi-disciplinary design. We're the OEM that customers actually appreciate.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: OEMs building electric vehicles, robotics, aerospace and industrial systems that buy traction inverters and motor controllers
problem: Power electronics such as inverters are heavy, costly and inefficient, and limit electric machines.
business_model: Hardware sales of inverters and custom power electronics to OEMs
product_category: Power electronics hardware, traction inverters
market_need_then: EV, robotics and industrial makers were pushing for denser, cheaper power electronics, and the founders cite power density as the limiting factor in the YC launch post.
outcome_analysis: Steinmetz is an active early hardware company founded by two Waterloo mechatronics engineers with Tesla and Neuralink experience. It is shipping a 500 kW inverter per its website, but no verified funding or customer data is public, so the outcome cannot be judged yet.

name: Stellon Labs
one_liner: Building tiny frontier AI models that run on edge devices
long_description: Stellon Labs is an AI research lab that is building tiny frontier AI models that can run on edge devices like smartphones, wearables and embedded systems. Our first open source model, KittenTTS, is a super-tiny text-to-speech model, that got 8K Github stars and 45K model downloads within 2 weeks of launching.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and device makers who need small AI models that run on phones, wearables and embedded hardware, plus API customers
problem: Frontier AI models are too large to run on edge devices, so small high quality models are needed for local speech and other tasks.
business_model: Open source models with paid hosted APIs
product_category: Edge AI models, text to speech
market_need_then: KittenTTS reached 8K GitHub stars and 45K model downloads in two weeks per the YC page, which shows developer demand for tiny local models.
outcome_analysis: Stellon Labs is active. Its open source KittenTTS drew fast developer attention at launch and the company is adding a larger speech model and paid APIs, but no verified funding is public and the open source model limits defensibility.

name: Stillwind
one_liner: PCB component librarian
long_description: Stillwind is a fractional librarian for startups. Customers give us the parts they want to put into designs and we give them footprints, symbols and 3d models made from the manufacturers datasheet.
regions: Switzerland; Europe
target_customer: Hardware startups and electronics teams that design PCBs in KiCad or Altium
problem: Building correct footprints, symbols and 3D models from manufacturer datasheets is slow and error prone work for PCB designers.
business_model: Service subscription for custom PCB library parts, with a free trial
product_category: Electronics design services, PCB component libraries
founder_names: Linus Meierhöfer; Hannes Furmans; Josef Zoller
competitors_at_founding: SnapEDA (now SnapMagic Search); SamacSys Component Search Engine; Ultra Librarian
market_need_then: PCB library creation is a recurring cost for design teams, and existing providers sell build on request services, which indicates paid demand.
outcome_analysis: Stillwind is active in Zurich with three ETH Zurich founders in a service business against established free and paid libraries. The YC pages suggest the same founders earlier ran Augento, an AI fine tuning product, but no pivot date or reason is sourced, and no funding or outcome is public.

name: Stockline
one_liner: AI-native ERP for food wholesalers
long_description:
Stockline is an AI-native ERP for food wholesalers. Our agents eliminate human labor for repetitive tasks, starting with order entry. 

Our goal is to replace clunky software with the next generation of ERPs, built with AI employees at their core.

Team is 2 Polytechnique alums who dropped out of Stanford and MIT. 
Mariem is daughter of the fish industry and Moncef started coding and building softwares at 13.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Food wholesalers and distributors, starting with fish wholesalers, that take orders by WhatsApp, SMS, email and phone
problem: Wholesale order entry is manual and repetitive, with orders arriving across many channels and keyed into legacy ERPs.
business_model: B2B SaaS ERP with AI agents, with on-site onboarding
product_category: Vertical AI ERP for food distribution
market_need_then: Food distribution relies on manual order entry from chat and phone, and a funded vendor already sold AI order capture in 2025.
outcome_analysis: Stockline is active and early. One founder grew up in the fish wholesale business, which gives domain insight, but a funded competitor already sold AI order entry and no verified funding or customers are public.

name: Stormy
one_liner: Stormy runs the office so your crew can run the work.
long_description: Stormy runs the office so your crew can run the work. Every call answered, day or night. Every quote followed up until it is a yes or a no. Jobs booked, crews scheduled, parts tracked, invoices sent and collected. Marketing that brings the work in, and an AI agent for every person on your team — all working from the same job record. Built for the shops that keep physical things running: forklift and heavy equipment service, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, roofing, logistics and yards.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small service businesses such as HVAC, plumbing, roofing and equipment service shops (YC page); the company website in 2026 describes a physical AI lab building a robot Workcell
problem: Service shops lose work to missed calls, slow quotes and manual back office tasks. The earlier influencer marketing product targeted manual creator outreach.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: AI agents for business operations
market_need_then: The launch posts framed influencer marketing as running on spreadsheets and manual DMs, and the product won Product Hunt Product of the Day on 2025-08-18.
outcome_analysis: Stormy changed direction at least twice. It began with desktop agents, moved to an influencer marketing agent that won Product Hunt in August 2025, and the YC page describes service business AI while the 2026 website describes a physical AI lab. Funding reports conflict and no outcome is public.

name: Structured AI
one_liner: The AI drawing review platform for architects and engineers.
long_description:
Structured AI is the most advanced AI-powered QA/QC platform for drawing packages, working across both PDF drawings and native Revit models. Architects and engineers use our platform to make every drawing set leave the office with certainty. 

Our AI agents learn your firm's standards, apply the relevant codes, and read every page of a set, then return a clear list of what's wrong, where it sits, and how to fix it. Run compliance reviews across thousands of pages in minutes, chat with your drawings for sourced answers, build custom checks in plain English, compare versions, overlay disciplines, and close out comments - all within a single platform, with a full audit trail on every finding.

For decades, the last line of defense on a drawing set has been a red pen at the end of a deadline week. But buildings have outgrown the red pen. A modern set runs thousands of drawings, and the errors hiding between them threaten quality and safety, not just cost. What manual review misses resurfaces as RFIs, change orders, and field rework, paid for in time, margin, and reputation.

Structured AI catches those errors before they leave the office, capturing the judgment of your best reviewer once and applying it everywhere.

Better drawings build a better world. #GetStructured
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Architecture and engineering firms that review drawing sets before they go to contractors
problem: Drawing packages run to thousands of sheets and manual review misses errors that return later as RFIs, change orders and field rework.
business_model: B2B SaaS
product_category: AI QA and QC for construction drawings and Revit models
founder_names: Raymond Zhao; Issy Greenslade; Brandon Abreu Smith
market_need_then: Drawing errors cause rework and change orders, and incumbents moving to acquire drawing review AI in 2025 shows demand.
outcome_analysis: Structured AI is active. Its Oxford founders raised a reported $4.2M seed led by FCVC in June 2026, a few months after the YC batch, with a strategic tie to engineering firm Syska Hennessy. It faces an incumbent that bought AI drawing review technology and other funded startups.

name: Subimage
one_liner: The Open-Core Security Graph
long_description:
Subimage builds maps of your infrastructure to give you visibility on what assets you have and how they relate to each other. This enables any security team to deeply understand their environments and reduce risk.

Subimage is a managed offering built around the Cartography open-source project, and is founded by members of Cartography's original team.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Security teams that need an inventory of cloud and on-prem assets and how they relate
problem: Security teams lack visibility into what assets they have and how they connect, which makes risk hard to reduce.
business_model: Open core, managed SaaS built around the Cartography open source project
product_category: Cloud security graph, asset inventory
market_need_then: Security teams already use Cartography in production (the founder cites 70 plus companies on LinkedIn), which shows demand for asset graphs.
outcome_analysis: SubImage is active and raised a $4.2M seed in November 2025. Its founders created Cartography at Lyft, which gives distribution among security engineers, but it competes with well funded proprietary cloud security graphs. No later outcome is public.

name: Sublingual
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Daily productivity tracker
long_description: Our desktop app helps teams stay focused on shipping.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Subtrace
one_liner: Zero code network tracer
long_description: Subtrace is a zero-code network tracer. It's like having an inspect element button for your whole infra: when you start a process with Subtrace, you'll see every HTTP request coming in and going out in realtime. Under the hood, it uses BPF to make this possible without any root privileges or code changes. We have ~2.5k stars on Github.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Backend and infrastructure engineers at software teams running Docker or Kubernetes services
problem: Seeing the HTTP requests flowing in and out of a service normally requires code changes, sidecars or root-level packet capture setup. Subtrace offers a request inspector for a whole process without code changes.
business_model: Open source tool with a hosted dashboard; paid tier details not confirmed
product_category: Developer tools, network observability
market_need_then: Developers regularly need request-level debugging in containers, and a Show HN post framed the tool as Wireshark for Docker containers in early 2025, drawing community discussion including privacy concerns.
outcome_analysis: Subtrace is an active two person team that joined YC in Winter 2025. No outcome event was found in searches. It earned open source traction (about 2.5k GitHub stars per YC) and press from InfoQ, but the commercial path against eBPF observability incumbents is unproven, so no success or failure factors are assigned yet.

name: Sureform
one_liner: Real-world company data for frontier AI
long_description: Sureform help companies monetize their internal operational data by turning it into training signal for frontier AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Operators of physical workplaces such as hotels, warehouses and restaurants, paid to supply task data to robotics labs and frontier AI developers
problem: Robotics and world-model labs need real-world task data, and workplaces hold it but have no way to capture and sell it. Sureform connects the two.
business_model: Data marketplace and collection service; revenue from selling captured data to AI labs
product_category: AI training data for robotics and world models
market_need_then: Robot foundation model and world model labs were hungry for real-world manipulation data in 2025, per the company's launch framing on its YC page.
outcome_analysis: Sureform is an active small team from Spring 2025 collecting real-world human data for robotics labs. No funding, outcome event or traction figure was found in public sources, so no success or failure factors are assigned and the outlook is unknown.

name: Swerve

long_description: Play stories in your own words. Swerve is AI fiction that unfolds around what you say and do.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Adult consumers on iPhone who want interactive AI fiction and character chat
problem: Existing AI story tools forget context or lean on heavy filters; Swerve offers stories that unfold around what the user says and does, later adding AI video with friends.
business_model: Consumer freemium subscription and in-app purchases (Pro listed at 12.49 USD, Lite at 3.99 USD by secondary sources)
product_category: Consumer AI entertainment, interactive fiction
market_need_then: AI companion and story apps had strong engagement in 2025 per one review headline, though the same piece flagged market limits; AI Dungeon alternatives roundups show users shopping for better memory and fewer filters.
outcome_analysis: Swerve is a two person team from Winter 2025 with robotics-industry backgrounds that built a consumer AI fiction app. No funding, outcome event or verified traction was found. The category is crowded and easy to copy, so the outlook is unproven and no factors are assigned.

name: Sygaldry Technologies
one_liner: quantum-accelerated AI servers
long_description: We’re building quantum-accelerated AI servers so organizations building AI can exponentially speed up training and inference. And we’re making tools for AI researchers to integrate quantum capabilities into AI models and workflows.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Organizations that train and run large AI models in data centers, plus AI researchers wanting quantum tools
problem: AI training and inference cost and speed are limited by classical hardware. Sygaldry aims to add fault-tolerant quantum accelerators to AI servers to speed up existing AI algorithms.
business_model: Hardware servers for AI data centers plus software tools; no revenue disclosed
product_category: Quantum computing hardware for AI infrastructure
founder_names: Chad Rigetti; Idalia Friedson; Michael Keiser
market_need_then: AI compute demand and data center buildout were surging in 2025, and quantum hardware makers were courting AI use cases, but production advantage on AI workloads remained unproven.
outcome_analysis: Sygaldry joined YC in Spring 2025 led by the founder of Rigetti Computing and raised 34M seed in August 2025 and 105M Series A in March 2026. Founder track record in quantum hardware and AI data center demand explain the fast fundraising. The technology is unproven, so execution risk remains high.

name: Synthio Labs

Founders with McKinsey and pharma consulting background and a timing tailwind from voice AI support the early traction; no failure signals found.

name: TectoAI

name: Tegore
one_liner: Your new AI-powered math tutor.
long_description:
Tegore follows K-12 school curriculum to design courses like Algebra I & Algebra II. In addition to working with high schools in the Bay Area to design the best in-classroom experiences, Tegore is developing the corresponding consumer product, a Duolingo for Math.

Each lesson in Tegore follows a lesson plan (e.g. Polynomial Long Division), and the content is delivered with voice / interactive visuals, and checks students' understanding by using dialectic teaching.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Middle and high school students and the schools and teachers who assign math courses; consumer app planned
problem: Students need personalized math help aligned to school curriculum. Tegore pairs an AI tutor with curriculum-based lesson plans, voice and interactive visuals.
business_model: School partnerships plus a planned consumer subscription product (Duolingo for Math); pricing not found
product_category: K-12 AI math tutoring, edtech

outcome_analysis: Tegore is an active one person company from Spring 2025 building an AI math tutor aligned to K-12 curriculum with school pilots. No outcome event or verified funding was found. Strong incumbents exist in AI tutoring, so the outlook is unproven and no factors are assigned.

name: TensorPool

The YC directory marks it acquired and an investor post says OpenAI hired the three founders through an acquisition in September 2026, so the exit looks like a team led deal on infrastructure skill. name: Tergle

name: Tesora
one_liner: Frontier AI for Actuaries
long_description:
Tesora builds frontier AI agents for actuaries at P&C carriers, reinsurers, and MGAs. The agents handle the assembly, pulling the data, running the method, and deploying the rater, while you review the work and make every call. We deploy inside the stack you already run, on your infra and under your IT team's control, with no shared servers and nothing to rip out. Your data never trains our models, or anyone else's. We treat this as a partnership so we stay hands-on until the work is live and holding up in production. That standard runs through our security posture too: SOC 2 Type II certified, with a full audit trail behind every change.

The part of the job that matters is actuarial judgment, and we automate everything around it so you get back to the work only you can do. Built by AI technologists and actuaries who want to see this exist and backed by Y Combinator & other top investors.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Actuarial teams at P&C carriers, reinsurers, MGAs, captives and actuarial consultancies

product_category: AI agents for actuarial and insurance pricing work

name: Text.ai
one_liner: Alfi - your group chat with social skills to bring friends closer
long_description:
We're building the first group chat with social skills.

While everyone else is stuck with boring individual chatbots, we've cracked the impossible: Alfi reads the room, understands each person, and creates custom intelligence for every group chat.

Alfi is your new social friend. The one who remembers everything, plans effortlessly, and keeps the crew together.

Here's what that looks like:

- Book restaurants together, with Yelp built in, directly in the chat. No more "where should we go?" spirals. Reserve instantly.
- Create images with your friends: drop your crew into funny hats, wild scenes, anything you can dream up. Multiplayer image gen, first of its kind.
- Social calendar: upcoming hangs, all in one place. Everyone on the same page.
- Group Wrapped: who's the chattiest? Top inside jokes? Now you'll know.
- Reminders & Memory: Alfi remembers your spots, your preferences, and nudges you to actually hang out.

We're in the middle of a quiet shift. Gen Z is leaving broadcast social media. They're retreating to group chats, smaller, more intentional and personal spaces where they're honestly themselves.

But group chats are also where plans go to die. Someone has to be "the planner" or nothing happens.

We believe the group chat is the real social network. Where the funniest moments and real conversations happen in real time. With Alfi, we hope to bring you together more expressively, a lot more often.

This technology will bring humanity closer than it's ever been before. Not replace connection, deepen it. That's the future we're building toward.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Gen Z and young adult consumers who coordinate plans in group chats
problem: Group chats are where plans stall. Alfi sits in the chat to plan, book, remind and generate images together.
business_model: Consumer app, monetization not stated in sources found
product_category: Consumer social AI assistant for group chats
founder_names: Rushi Shah; Paras Maniar; Prahar Patel
market_need_then: The company argues Gen Z is moving from broadcast social media to private group chats. This is a thesis from the company, not independent data.
outcome_analysis: Text.ai is active after Spring 2025 YC. It launched Alfi on Product Hunt in January 2026 and in June 2026 the company claimed over 500,000 users, an unverified company figure. Funding is small and partly undisclosed. No shutdown or acquisition found. OpenAI's later group chat launch is a risk to the wedge.

name: The Context Company
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Analytics; Monitoring; AI
one_liner: Find what's losing you customers and money in your AI agent and fix it
long_description:
We analyze every conversation between your customers and your AI agent to find what's losing you customers and money. Then we help ship the fix and prove it worked.

Nobody on the team can read every conversation once an agent is in production. TCC does, and turns them into patterns tied to the accounts they affect: where customers get stuck, what they wish the agent could do, and where it's spending more than it needs to.

Engineers ask about a pattern from their IDE through our MCP, get the conversations and traces behind it down to the tool call or prompt that went wrong, ship the fix, and benchmark cost and quality before and after. Product sees what customers are actually trying to do with the agent and where it falls short, broken out by topic and account, which becomes the backlog for what to build next. Customer success sees which accounts the agent is struggling with before the customer says anything, and steps in with the full conversation on hand.

Any agent framework, a few lines of code. If you're running an agent in production or about to launch, ping us.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams running AI agents in production, from developers on a free plan to enterprises needing HIPAA support
problem: Teams cannot see where production agents fail or what users actually ask. The product turns agent conversations into patterns, alerts and reports.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with free Developer, Pro and Enterprise tiers
product_category: AI agent observability and conversation analytics
market_need_then: Production AI agents were spreading quickly in 2025 and teams needed ways to find silent failures. Evidence comes from observability roundups, not spend data.
outcome_analysis: The Context Company is an active two person Fall 2025 YC company in a crowded agent observability market. The only confirmed money is a reported 500K from YC in December 2025. No acquisition or shutdown is reported. Early traction claims rest on one named customer case study on its own site.

name: The Hog
one_liner: Real-time web intelligence API for AI agents and GTM teams
long_description:
One API to search, enrich, and monitor the web.

An agent is only as good as the data it runs on. Most agents and GTM tools today are stuck pulling stale, fragmented data from a dozen different providers, which caps how good their output can ever be. We unify all of it behind one API.

One credit-based API covers people data, company data, web search, deep research, news, social signals, and web scraping. Multi-provider waterfall logic routes each call to the best source and falls back automatically, so you get one integration and one bill instead of stitching together Clay, Apollo, Exa, Tavily, and a handful of others.

We're building the data layer that agents and GTM teams plug into to find, understand, and reach their customers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI agent builders and B2B go-to-market teams needing people, company, web and social data
problem: Agents and GTM teams stitch together many data providers. The Hog offers one pay-per-call API for web, people, company and social intelligence.
business_model: Usage-based API with credits and a free tier of 500 calls per month per a third-party profile
product_category: Web intelligence API and AI go-to-market tooling
market_need_then: Agent builders needed live web and people data in 2025, shown by funding into Exa, Tavily and Firecrawl. Evidence for The Hog's own demand is not found.
outcome_analysis: The Hog is a two person Fall 2025 YC company selling a data API to agents and GTM teams. Positioning shifts between a web intelligence API and an AI demand generation command center across sources. No funding, traction, acquisition or shutdown is verified, so the outcome cannot yet be judged.

name: The Prompting Company
one_liner: We help products get discovered & used by AI agents.
long_description:
The Prompting Company helps companies get discovered and used by AI agents.

We help companies with two things:
- Discovery: We find the exact questions your customers ask AI, analyze whether your product shows up, and improve how AI systems describe and recommend you.
- Usability: We test whether AI agents can actually use your product, including finding the right docs, performing the right workflows, and completing tasks on behalf of users.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software, developer tool and infrastructure companies (plus some larger enterprises) that want AI assistants and coding agents to find, cite and correctly use their product
problem: Buyers increasingly ask ChatGPT and other AI tools which product to use, and products that AI systems do not know or cannot operate lose discovery and signups. Companies lack tooling to see how AI describes them and to make docs and workflows usable by agents.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services: AI visibility audits, a monitoring and content hosting platform, and an agent experience testing product
product_category: Generative engine optimization and agent experience
founder_names: Kevin Chandra; Michelle Marcelline; Albert Purnama
market_need_then: In 2025 AI assistants became a discovery channel and the founders told TechCrunch most growth on websites was coming from AI bots rather than people. Brands wanted to know whether ChatGPT mentioned them, which created fast demand for visibility tooling.
outcome_analysis: The company is a young repeat founder team that rode the 2025 shift toward AI search and raised a 6.5 million dollar seed about four months after starting, with named software customers. No shutdown, sale or layoffs were found, so the outcome is still open. Its main risk is a crowded category where better funded rivals and SEO suites compete on the same visibility metrics.

name: Third Chair

long_description:
Third Chair works with IP rightsholders to enforce and monetize their rights, supported by an on-demand network of top lawyers to step in when you need them.

The biggest media and entertainment companies like Universal Music Group in the world rely on Third Chair to enforce their intellectual property, unlock licensing revenue, and accelerate deal flow.

ThirdLayer is the learning and alignment layer for enterprise AI. We continuously ingest and structure messy organizational context, complex operational processes, and siloed, permission-sensitive data, then grade agents against the outcomes each company cares about. Every interaction becomes feedback that helps agents improve over time.

Companies use ThirdLayer to power their internal agents or embed it into the AI products they’re building. We give agents the context, evaluations, and learning loops they need to stay aligned with each organization and deliver better outcomes with every run.

name: Ticket Wallet
one_liner: AI-optimized ticket resale
long_description:
Ticket Wallet is an AI-powered resale platform for season ticket holders and brokers.
We automate pricing, listing, and distribution across all major marketplaces.

Today, most tickets are still sold manually: spreadsheets, guessing prices, and listing on one site at a time. The biggest brokers outsource pricing to teams in the Philippines… 

We built Ticket Wallet because we lived this. Truman has been flipping tickets for the last 5 years. Ryan built pricing software after seeing the mess first-hand. We’ve turned that pain into a product.

Since launch, we’ve onboarded $3M+ in ticket inventory, signed up 100+ paying sellers, and started working with pro teams. We charge 10% per ticket sold. This is our wedge into the $26B resale market.

Other platforms cost you money. We make you more of it.

outcome_analysis: Ticket Wallet is active and growing after Spring 2025. A CEO who resold tickets for years paired with a machine learning co-founder, launched a take-rate product, and reportedly raised a $6M seed in July 2025 led by Seven Seven Six. Team size reached about 20. Traction numbers are self-reported. Risks are marketplace access and rules on resale, but no failure signals were found.

name: Tinfoil
tags: Developer Tools; Security; Privacy; Cloud Computing; AI
one_liner: Encrypted AI with verifiable privacy
long_description:
Tinfoil makes it easy to make your AI workloads secure and provably private. You get the privacy of on-prem deployments, while running on the cloud. It's like end-to-end encrypted messaging but for your AI applications. 

We’ve built a full-stack platform on top of the latest NVIDIA GPUs offering confidential computing capabilities, meaning that you don’t have to trade off performance for privacy. We integrate a suite of recent advances in secure hardware technologies, in particular NVIDIA’s confidential compute mode available on Hopper and Blackwell. When combined with Tinfoil’s software stack, companies can prove their security claims like "we can't see and don’t log your queries.” Tinfoil guarantees that all data always stays private and cannot be accessed by anyone other than the end user -- not even by Tinfoil or the cloud provider it’s processed on. Everything can be made end-to-end encrypted and private with Tinfoil. 

The founding team combines deep academic and industry experience in security and Internet protocols. Tanya was previously a systems engineer at Cloudflare, where she built Internet security protocols used by billions, and contributed to the Workers AI platform. Jules and Sacha hold PhDs from MIT, where they worked on secure hardware, cryptography, and privacy technologies. Jules has also worked at NVIDIA on their confidential computing team. Tinfoil was born from our personal frustration with the false choice between access to powerful AI and the massive data privacy implications of deeply integrated AI.

AI is a universal tool that becomes part of our personal lives and business workflows. In the process, it needs access to all personal, private, and proprietary data. Right now, the only solutions are data processing agreements (i.e., "pinky promises"), band-aids like PII redaction that don't work in practice, or AI locally/on-prem, which doesn't scale. Tinfoil promises to unlock significantly deeper AI adoption and integrations by making it easy to obtain true privacy, just as TLS on the Internet enabled e-commerce to flourish by securing credit cards on the network.

Today we offer several self-serve products: 

- A consumer-facing chatbot that keeps your chats end-to-end encrypted and provides zero-access inference with powerful open-source models like Kimi, Gemma, and GLM. You can try it out for free: https://chat.tinfoil.sh

- A developer-friendly API that allows you to build AI applications where all user data is kept private and we as the inference provider cannot see any of the prompts. Our SDKs make sure that all relevant security measures are checked for you before even sending a single byte of data. Learn more:https://docs.tinfoil.sh 

- An advanced confidential computing platform we call Tinfoil Containers that allows you to secure any Docker application. We make it easy to deploy your own logic and applications inside secure enclaves and prove to the world what code is running inside. This enables attested workloads and publicly verifiable privacy policies for sensitive applications. Learn more: https://tinfoil.sh/containers
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers, enterprises and consumers who need AI inference where even the provider cannot see prompts
problem: Using powerful cloud AI requires trusting providers with private data; on-prem does not scale and redaction or contracts are weak guarantees.
business_model: Usage-based API and containers plus a $20 per month consumer chat subscription
product_category: Confidential computing for AI inference
founder_names: Tanya Verma; Jules Drean; Sacha Servan-Schreiber
market_need_then: Companies were blocked from sending private data to AI providers; Tinfoil's site lists customers such as DuckDuckGo and universities and claims SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance, all self-reported.
outcome_analysis: Tinfoil is active with a five-person team from Spring 2025, led by founders with cloud security and MIT secure hardware backgrounds, offering a chat app, inference API and containers. Funding is not verifiably known and no exit has occurred. The privacy-for-AI trend and customers like DuckDuckGo suggest early traction, but that comes from the company's own site.

name: Topological

long_description:

Our technology is accelerating the engineering workflow with AI and scales design and optimization to identify the ideal designs for complex problems given their physical constraints with enhanced speed and performance. 

Our first model, UToP-v1, is a SOTA topology optimization model that understands physics, geometry, and manufacturability. It can generate the most efficient design given a problem’s physical requirements. It has <5% compliance error and is 1930x faster than current methods. We're reimagining mechanical engineering and computational design with precision spatial AI.

The headline speed claim is unverified and the model competes with CAD incumbents, so the outcome is unknown at this stage.

name: Tornyol

Because these drones are so cheap and fast, we will lower the cost of mosquito control by 100x which will enable the eradication of mosquitoes from cities, saving more than a million people each year from Malaria, West Nile, Dengue, etc.

market_need_then: Funds spend heavily on expert networks and research; the founders cite analyst experience. The company claims 125 plus fund contributors and 2,000 plus tickers, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Trata began in Winter 2025 with a founder who was a hedge fund analyst plus two technical co-founders, which gives it founder market fit for selling to funds. It remains active with six people and a new trata.com domain. No exit or shutdown was found, and funding is visible only in conflicting aggregators, so its eventual outcome is unknown.

name: Trava
tags: Generative AI; B2B; Compliance; Logistics; Supply Chain
one_liner: AI agents for global trade compliance
long_description: Trava is building AI agents for global trade compliance. Importers lose billions each year to duty overpayments and filing errors. Trava audits customs entries and automates classification to help importers protect margins and stay compliant at scale.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US importers that pay customs duties
problem: Importers overpay duties and misclassify goods as tariff rules change, and recovering refunds is manual.
business_model: B2B software audits and classification tools, pricing not found; early access
product_category: Trade compliance AI
market_need_then: The founder cites over $200B of US duties paid in 2025 amid shifting tariff rules, company claim; tariff turbulence raised audit demand.
outcome_analysis: Trava is a one person Winter 2025 YC company aimed at customs duty audits for US importers during a period of tariff turbulence. No exit or shutdown was found. Funding is not publicly reported and the site shows early access products, so traction cannot be judged and competitors such as Caspian arrived in July 2025.

name: Trelium
tags: B2B; Workflow Automation; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: AI Agents for Enterprise Wide Operations
long_description: Trelium lets enterprise teams build AI agents in simple English to automate back-office work. We serve companies handling custom and bulk operations, including distributors, suppliers, and decorators across the print, merch, and apparel industries, automating workflows like order entry, purchase order creation, PO-invoice matching, order-status follow-ups, and many more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Mid-market and enterprise operations teams, especially promo, print and apparel distributors, suppliers and decorators
problem: Back-office work such as purchase order entry, invoice matching and order follow-ups is manual and spread across tools without APIs.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform for building AI agents, hosted tiers not found
product_category: Enterprise AI workflow agents
market_need_then: Distributors in promotional products described using AI automation for order entry in a September 2025 ASI article; manual order work was a known pain.
outcome_analysis: Trelium joined YC in Fall 2025 after rebranding from Questom and shifting from sales agents to back-office operations for promo and apparel firms. Its site lists seven customers, and the YC page lists a team of eleven. No exit or shutdown was found, funding is only a CB Insights convertible note estimate, and the outcome remains open.

name: Trim
one_liner: A foundation model for physics.
long_description: Trim is building a general intelligence AI model that can simulate real-world physical systems evolving over time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Not clearly stated; example uses are autonomous vehicle planning, gravitational wave detection and engineering simulation
problem: Traditional physics simulation is slow and expensive; Trim wants a learned model that simulates physical systems in near constant time.
business_model: Not stated; research stage with open source trim-transformer package
product_category: Physics foundation model and simulation AI
market_need_then: Engineering simulation is a large spend and physics AI attracted funded startups, though Trim itself shows no named customers.
outcome_analysis: Trim is a three person Winter 2025 YC research company building a foundation model for physics, led by a physicist founder. It stays active, with no exit or shutdown found. Its ambitious technical bet and open source architecture come with no disclosed customers or verified funding, so its outcome is unknown.

name: Tweeks.io
one_liner: Lovable for Chrome Plugins
long_description: Make websites work exactly how you want
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individual web users who want to change how websites look and work
problem: Websites have clutter and missing features, and writing userscripts is a barrier for ordinary users.
business_model: Freemium browser extension with paid plans for higher limits and advanced features
product_category: AI browser extension and userscript manager
market_need_then: Userscript managers had a long running user base; the Chrome Web Store listing shows about 10,000 users and the site claims 25k plus people.
outcome_analysis: Tweeks started as a side project by two MIT graduates and went through YC in Winter 2025 under NextByte, launching in October 2025 per its changelog. Its user base is modest and the idea is easy to copy, and no exit or shutdown was found. Funding is unverified, so the outcome is open.

name: TwentyTwo
tags: Synthetic Biology; Biotech; Compliance; Security; AI
one_liner: AI infrastructure for biosecurity
long_description: AI is making biology easy to engineer. Life-saving drugs and therapies are accelerating, but so is the ability for bad actors to create a pandemic. TwentyTwo is working on the defensive stack to prevent the next pandemic.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: DNA synthesis providers, biotech firms and AI x bio model developers needing biosecurity screening
problem: AI makes biology easier to engineer, raising misuse risk; defenders lack tooling for customer screening, functional sequence screening and model safeguards.
business_model: B2B biosecurity infrastructure (customer screening module live; pricing not public)
product_category: Biosecurity AI infrastructure
founder_names: Evan Seeyave; Harmon Bhasin; John Wang
market_need_then: A May 2025 US executive order called for verifiable nucleic acid screening (per a secondary source, not checked against the order); sources note customer screening standards are less mature than sequence screening.
outcome_analysis: TwentyTwo, a three-person Summer 2025 biosecurity team, was acquired by LatchBio on 2026-06-29, about a year after the batch, with undisclosed terms. No funding round was found, so it is unclear whether this was a soft landing or a strategic exit. The founders' SecureBio evaluation background and a policy tailwind on screening fit the story, but the sources do not give traction or customers.

name: Uncommon Therapeutics
one_liner: A Disease Focused Biotech, Building Multiple Billion Dollar Drugs
long_description: Our founder Noah, an experienced tech entrepreneur, was directly impacted by a severe genetic disease when his daughter was diagnosed with Rett Syndrome, a disease that afflicts 1 in 10,000 girls. Using an innovative polytherapy strategy, we’ve successfully improved her quality of life, and have designed new therapeutics that each could be worth billions and together could deliver a cure.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Rare disease patients, starting with Rett syndrome; eventual buyers are payers and partners
problem: Rett syndrome has few treatments and rare disease drug development is slow and expensive.
business_model: Biotech drug developer with a polytherapy strategy, no revenue
product_category: Rare disease therapeutics (gene editing, ASO, small molecules)
competitors_at_founding: Acadia Pharmaceuticals (trofinetide); Taysha Gene Therapies; Neurogene
market_need_then: Rett affects about 1 in 10,000 girls per the company and only one drug had been approved by 2023; parents and advocates drive demand.
outcome_analysis: Uncommon Therapeutics is a two person Winter 2025 YC biotech built around a founder whose daughter has Rett syndrome and a scientist with neurology drug discovery experience. It claims three candidates working in patient cells, funded by about $1M so far per YC. No exit or shutdown was found and public funding data is thin, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Units
one_liner: Units builds full-stack AI education infrastructure.
long_description:
Units lets ambitious students graduate high school in 1 year instead of 4 with real accredited diploma credits, plus a portfolio of real-world work, not just a transcript, to produce kids that are irreplaceable by AI.

We're rebuilding school for a post-AGI world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Ambitious high school students and their parents, who pay per accredited credit; also teachers via the founder's earlier grading tool
problem: Traditional high school takes four years and delivers a transcript; Units offers AI-led mastery lessons and accredited credits so students can finish faster and build a portfolio of real work.
business_model: Free lessons, paid accredited credits at $1,000 per official Ontario credit (per the company site)
product_category: AI-native online high school
market_need_then: Parents and students were questioning the value of school in an AI era and Alpha School drew heavy press in 2025; the company frames it as rebuilding school for a post-AGI world. No Units-specific demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Units is an early stage, one person company from Spring 2025 that is still active. No outcome events, shutdown or acquisition were found in a search. Its fate depends on whether paid credits sell, and whether it can differentiate from Alpha School style models.

name: Unsiloed AI
one_liner: API for parsing multimodal unstructured data
long_description:
AI teams spend 6+ months building document workflows, yet fewer than 10% ever reach production. Generic LLM parsers and OCR collapse on multimodal documents with text, tables, images, and charts. Poor parsing and suboptimal chunking cripple RAG pipelines and downstream automation. Unsiloed AI has built state-of-the-art vision models which serves as the infrastructure layer for turning unstructured data into structured, queryable, and LLM-ready assets.

Our APIs are already parsing hundreds of thousands of documents for startups and NASDAQ-listed enterprises, powering vertical AI solutions across industries. On public benchmarks, Unsiloed AI consistently outperforms solutions from LlamaIndex, Gemini, Mistral, and Unstructured.io among others.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI teams and enterprises (banks, NASDAQ-listed firms, startups) building RAG and document workflows
problem: Generic LLM parsers and OCR fail on multimodal documents (text, tables, charts, images), which cripples RAG pipelines.
business_model: usage-based API (plus on-premise deployment option)
product_category: document parsing / unstructured data API
market_need_then: YC page claims AI teams spend 6+ months on document workflows and under 10% reach production (company claim, unverified). Peer funding in 2025 (Extend $17M in June 2025; Reducto Series A with Benchmark) shows investor demand for document parsing.
outcome_analysis: Too early to judge: Unsiloed AI joined YC in Fall 2025 and is Active with two founders. No priced round was verified (aggregators disagree at roughly 0.5M to 1M, one outlier 7.5M). It sells a parsing API into a crowded document-AI space where Reducto, Extend and LlamaParse are better funded, so whether benchmark claims turn into durable revenue is not yet visible.

name: Uplane
one_liner: Replace marketing agencies with AI
long_description:
Uplane replaces marketing agencies with AI. We generate hundreds of ads with matching landing pages and steer the ad spend across channels like Meta, Google, LinkedIn and others. By connecting to CRM and ERP data, Uplane learns what drives profits and continuously improves campaigns.

Companies waste billions on bad ads, mismatched landing pages, and poor budget allocation. Uplane fixes this by replacing a patchwork of agencies, spreadsheets, and siloed tools with one self-improving system. The result: Higher ROAS for enterprises and effortless, expert-level marketing for SMBs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies spending about 100K USD or more a month on digital marketing (enterprise and growth brands), and SMBs wanting expert-level marketing
problem: Companies pay agencies and juggle spreadsheets and siloed tools for ads, landing pages and budget allocation; Uplane generates ads and landing pages and steers spend across channels using CRM and ERP data.
business_model: Annual fee B2B software with managed-service option (per press report)
product_category: AI marketing and ad automation
founder_names: Julius Körfgen; Marvin Abdel-Massih; Lukas Vollmer
market_need_then: Companies spend heavily on agencies and ad platforms; the company claims customers such as AG1 and Kalshi saw 20 to 50 percent ROAS gains (company claims, not independently verified).
outcome_analysis: Uplane, a Fall 2025 company, raised a reported 4.5M USD seed in April 2026 and grew to a listed team of 26 in its first year. Founders combine paid marketing operating experience with engineering, and AI made agency replacement plausible. The risk is crowded AI ad tooling and platform-owned automation.

name: Uplift AI
one_liner: Foundational Voice Models for regional languages
long_description:
We build Voice Models for regional languages (like Urdu, Bengali, Greek etc) and make them available through simple APIs and SDKs.
