Its only visible signals are a founder with Scale and Anthropic experience and a list of angel backers tied to AI and consumer companies. Nothing supports a verdict on success or failure yet.

name: s2.dev
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; API; Infrastructure; Databases
one_liner: API for unlimited, durable, real-time streams
long_description:
S2 is an API for durable streams. We make working with streaming data dead simple and reliable.

The more we worked on data systems, the more we felt like there was a missing building block. The seamless experience of object storage simply did not exist for durable streams – so we set out to fix that!

S2 reimagines streams as an unlimited and access-controlled web resource. Like if Kafka and S3 had a baby.

- Building agents? Use granular streams to persist context in real time, make workflows auditable, and coordinate between agents.

- Publishing fast-moving data? Streams support high fanout and can be accessed directly over the internet, so they are a great fit for broadcasting real-time feeds.

- Sandboxing? Emit to per-instance streams, and read history or live events just as easily.

- Local-first and multiplayer experiences? Propagate updates reliably and efficiently.

Stop dealing with clusters, and start streaming.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents, real-time feeds, sandboxes and local-first apps
problem: Durable streaming data needs Kafka-style clusters; there was no object-storage-like serverless primitive for ordered durable streams.
business_model: Usage-based cloud API with open-source self-hostable s2-lite
product_category: Serverless streaming data infrastructure
founder_names: Shikhar Bhushan; Stephen Balogh; Dwarak Govindparthiban
market_need_then: Agent workloads and real-time apps increased demand for persisted event streams; Kafka operational burden was a known pain point in the launch discussion.
outcome_analysis: S2 launched its streaming primitive in late 2024, joined YC in Fall 2025 and announced a 3.85 million dollar Accel-led seed in February 2026 with general availability. Founders with Etsy, Facebook and Confluent infrastructure experience, an open-source local version and demand from agent workloads support the story. Cloud providers shipping similar services is the main later risk.

name: sieve
one_liner: AI + human review to solve data cleaning - accessible via API or Excel
long_description:
sieve solves data cleaning for hedge funds and investment firms by letting them get clean data in four lines of code. Currently, their data pipelines have conditions that raise for human review, which literally send an email to engineers with data that needs to be reviewed. We provide an API that integrates directly into their existing pipeline - instead of raising for human review, they can send all the same information to our API and get clean, high-quality data back.

By using our AI agents built specifically for financial data collection, along with expert-in-the-loop review, we provide our clients with clean, validated data at a scale and level of quality that wasn't achievable before.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hedge funds and investment firms with data pipelines needing human review
problem: Pipeline exceptions emailed to engineers for manual cleaning are slow and costly; sieve returns clean data via API or Excel.
business_model: usage/API pricing with expert-in-the-loop review (pricing not found)
product_category: Financial data cleaning and extraction API
market_need_then: Hedge funds run manual data-cleaning steps; sieve's own claims of 100% match to hand-collected data and 60-70% lower cost are company statements.
outcome_analysis: sieve joined YC in Spring 2025 as a two-person team and is listed Active. Its only traction claims (multi-million dollar ARR, profitable, per the YC profile) are unverified company statements and no funding round was confirmed, so the outcome cannot yet be classified beyond early stage.

name: stagewise
one_liner: The makers of Klex Bots, your own team of digital coworkers.
long_description:
stagewise is building Klex Bots, autonomous AI coworkers that can take on real work inside companies.

Unlike traditional AI assistants, Klex Bots don't need to be prompted for every task. They operate continuously, maintain their own memory and workspaces, and use the same tools and systems as human employees. They can execute complex, multi-step tasks independently, collaborate with other bots or humans, and can use multiple sandboxes/computers depending on configuration.

Our Klex Cloud platform makes it easy for businesses to deploy and manage these digital coworkers securely, using their preferred AI models and infrastructure, hosting agents either in cloud or on custom infrastructure.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: Software engineers and companies adopting AI coding agents; later businesses deploying autonomous AI coworkers
problem: Frontend developers had to describe UI elements to coding agents by hand; later, teams want autonomous agent workers.
business_model: Open core (AGPLv3 core) with commercial cloud inference and enterprise offerings
product_category: Developer tools: browser toolbar, agentic IDE, AI coworkers
market_need_then: AI coding agents were growing fast in 2025 and the toolbar attracted 4,800 stars and 130,000 downloads soon after launch according to a launch-era announcement.
outcome_analysis: stagewise grew from an open source browser toolbar into a frontend agent in July 2025, then an open-source agentic IDE, and now the Klex Bots digital coworker product. The open source repo drew over six thousand stars quickly, which is the main traction signal, but public funding beyond an unverified 500 thousand dollar aggregator figure was not found and the product direction has shifted repeatedly.

name: stratify
tags: B2B; Design; Consumer Products; AI; Conversational AI
one_liner: AI agents that help you understand your customers' needs
long_description:
Stratify is the AI-powered user researcher that discovers the why behind every decision, click, and preference.
Our platform uses agentic workflows that instantly recruit participants, conduct user interviews, analyze responses, and provide actionable insights.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Product, design and research teams at companies that run user research
problem: User research is slow and costly to recruit, interview and analyze.
business_model: B2B SaaS (pricing not found)
product_category: AI user research platform
market_need_then: Teams wanted faster qualitative insight, and AI interview startups were raising seed rounds in 2024 and 2025.
outcome_analysis: Stratify launched its AI user researcher in May 2025 as a two person Stanford team. No funding announcement, customer figures or outcome news were found, and the market is led by better funded rivals. There is not enough public evidence to call it a success or a stall.

name: superglue
one_liner: AI agents that run ERP implementations for consultants
long_description:
superglue is a platform for ERP implementation teams at VARs, advisory firms and systems integrators. Each client implementation is a project in superglue, and its AI agents do the hands-on work across the whole project: the project plan from the kickoff, data assessment, fit-gap, configuration, data mapping and migration, testing, cutover and the integrations that run after go-live.

The agents execute the work in the client's systems, they don't just list what needs doing. Consultants review every change and sign off before anything reaches production. Approved migration scripts run the same way every time, with no AI at run time, and every run is logged.

superglue works with NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica, SAP and about 140 other systems, and reads legacy sources such as QuickBooks Desktop, Sage 50 and 100, Dynamics GP, databases and files.

A Sage value-added reseller running 40 Sage Intacct implementations cut migration and configuration hours per project by 80%. superglue is SOC 2 Type II, offers EU data residency, and can be self-hosted.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: ERP implementation teams at VARs, advisory firms and systems integrators (earlier, developers needing API integrations)
problem: ERP implementations and API integrations require slow manual data mapping, migration and configuration.
business_model: B2B SaaS, cloud or self-hosted
product_category: AI agents for ERP implementation (originally open-source integration proxy)
market_need_then: Integration code was costly to build per API, and open-source plus LLM approaches drew developer interest at the W25 launch.
outcome_analysis: superglue started in Winter 2025 as an open-source LLM-based integration proxy and moved to AI agents for ERP implementation firms, winning a Sage Intacct marketplace listing and an accounting partnership by 2026. Funding is not credibly verified, though aggregators show about 500 thousand dollars with YC, so strength of the fundraising story is unknown.

name: throxy
one_liner: Vertical AI agents running B2B outbound on autopilot, with human SDRs
long_description:
throxy builds custom vertical AI agents and pairs them with human SDRs and ultra personalised email sequences to book meetings for B2B software companies selling into traditional industries (e.g. manufacturing, logistics, construction, supply chain)

Outbound is broken. Generic automation gets ignored and decision-makers in legacy sectors are hard to reach. Most of your TAM isn't even on LinkedIn, and tools like Clay, Apollo, and ZoomInfo only cover about 65% of the market. throxy fixes this by running bespoke, fully managed outbound systems for software sales teams trying to crack these industries. We use proprietary scraping tools to map your entire addressable market, then combine AI agents with human experts to deliver hyper-personalised email campaigns and human cold calling that is consistently generating six-figure qualified pipelines.

Since 2023, throxy has powered outbound for B2B software companies, from industrial SaaS to fintech providers, replacing the need for internal SDR teams or stacks of tools with a solution that outperforms on both speed and quality. Today, we have a team of 55 across London and Cape Town, booking on average 8 to 12 qualified meetings per month per client, with some clients seeing 20+ in their first weeks after we doubled down on human-led cold calling.

AI handles the data: building custom databases, scoring leads against your ICP, and personalising outreach at scale. Humans handle the conversations: real cold calls, real emails, real relationships. That's the difference between us and every AI SDR on the market.

Our founding team has built AI at JP Morgan, scaled businesses from age 14, and led enterprise sales from Seed to Series D. We're not just automating outbound, we're redefining what sales execution looks like for software companies selling into traditional industries.

throxy is the "AI SDR" purpose-built for the sectors software forgot.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: B2B software companies selling into manufacturing, logistics, construction and other traditional industries
problem: Decision makers in legacy sectors are hard to reach with generic outbound tools.
business_model: Managed outbound service, pay per qualified meeting
product_category: Outsourced AI plus human SDR outbound
founder_names: Arnau Ayerbe Garcia; Pablo Jimenez de Parga Ramos; Bergen Merey
market_need_then: Founders cite that Clay, Apollo and ZoomInfo cover about 65 percent of the market and that outbound to legacy sectors is hard; AI SDR vendors raised heavily in 2024 and 2025.
outcome_analysis: Throxy built a managed outbound business since 2023, reported about 1.5 million dollars of ARR at its September 2025 6.2 million dollar Base10-led seed, and grew to a large team by 2026. The pay-per-meeting model and niche focus on traditional industries are the main drivers; later growth data is limited to company claims.

name: truthsystems
one_liner: Automatically blocking risky behavior with real-time governance agents
long_description:
Truth Systems provides a compliance agent to govern the use of generative AI. It translates operational policies into intelligent, real-time guardrails that monitor every AI interaction. This empowers companies to proactively block non-compliant actions and align access to AI tools with user competency. By eliminating the risks and operational blind spots associated with uncontrolled AI adoption, our platform enables enterprises to fully leverage the technology's potential without compromising security. 

We are establishing the new standard for AI governance, building a future where every professional can innovate safely and confidently.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Law firms and regulated enterprises using generative AI
problem: Firms cannot enforce policies and client guidelines on staff use of generative AI.
business_model: B2B SaaS for law firms (pricing not found)
product_category: AI governance and compliance agent (Charter, Alexandria gateway)

outcome_analysis: Truth Systems launched Charter in August 2025 with about 1 million dollars, then raised a 4 million dollar seed in October 2025 led by Gradient with strong legal tech and venture backers. Law firm traction (two firms and about 1,500 attorneys per YC) and Stanford Law ties support its story, but customer revenue is not public.

name: /dev/fast
one_liner: /dev/fast is the AI-native code forge
long_description:
/dev/fast is the AI-native code forge. We're building Whiteboard, an open-source canvas for thoughtful software design.

The Whiteboard app is designed to give you confidence in your code. Critique interactive visualizations, diffs, and agent traces, all from one interface. 

Learn more at https://dev.fast
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineering teams that use coding agents and need to review AI-generated code and agent traces
problem: Coding agents produce large diffs that humans struggle to review and trust. Engineers need visual, architecture-level ways to critique code, diffs and agent trajectories.
business_model: Open-source desktop apps (Whiteboard, Review) with a hosted version listed as coming soon; monetization not stated
product_category: Developer tools, AI code review and software design canvas

outcome_analysis: The company is active in its first year after the Winter 2026 batch. It shipped an open-source Whiteboard beta and a Review app, gained early GitHub attention, and faces strong competition from funded AI code review tools. No exit, shutdown or confirmed round has been found, so the outcome is still open.

name: 0.security
tags: B2B; Open Source; Cybersecurity; Enterprise; Defense
one_liner: The autonomous cybersecurity team
long_description:
0.security builds an autonomous offensive security team that finds and fixes vulnerabilities as fast as AI writes code and before attackers exploit them.

We've found and fixed dozens of previously unknown vulnerabilities (0-days) in government software across multiple countries and in software running on 3+ billion devices. Today we work with EY (Ernst & Young), leading tech companies and defense organizations.

Our AI agents hack into any software, verify every vulnerability they find, and ship the fix. They run 24/7 across the full stack, from web apps and dependencies down to operating systems and the Linux kernel.

We offer two products: 0cloud, where developer teams connect their repos and get security handled 24/7 at the speed of their coding agents, and our open-source harness, which we deploy & run for tech companies, enterprises and critical infrastructure providers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software and security teams at tech companies, enterprises and defense or critical infrastructure organizations
problem: AI coding agents ship code faster than security teams can audit it, and attackers can use AI to find bugs too. Companies need continuous vulnerability finding and fixing that keeps pace.
business_model: Open-source harness deployed and run for enterprises, plus a paid continuous testing product (0cloud) that opens fix pull requests, with a credit offer of 50 free PRs
product_category: AI offensive security and automated vulnerability remediation
market_need_then: AI generated code is increasing the volume of unaudited software, and reports in 2026 describe models exposing vulnerabilities faster than teams patch them.
outcome_analysis: The company is in its first months after the Fall 2026 batch. It claims real kernel vulnerabilities and an open-source launch, and lists enterprise and defense relationships, but no round, revenue or exit is verified. Direct competitors have raised far larger rounds, so the outcome is open.

name: 10x Science
one_liner: The AI-native platform for next-generation protein characterization.
long_description:
10x Science develops frontier AI models with deep memory to redefine how scientists understand and engineer biology across the life sciences, starting with drug development.

AI-powered drug discovery is flooding the pipeline with new candidates faster than ever. But before any of them can advance to the clinic, scientists must deeply characterize the protein therapeutic to understand whether it will work. Today, that process takes months of manual, error-prone analysis that cannot keep pace with discovery. Our AI-native platform automates it, giving drug developers the confidence to advance the right candidates and stop the wrong ones early.

We have strong commercial traction with enterprise pharma customers. Our founding team built the field of next-generation protein characterization out of Carolyn Bertozzi's Nobel laureate lab at Stanford. Collectively, we have 18+ years of collective domain expertise, 47+ scientific publications, and a 2x YC Founder. We move at the highest velocity and are positioned to lead the next generation of modern AI development in the life sciences.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Pharma and biotech teams doing protein characterization (mass spec and related analytics)
problem: Analyzing protein characterization data takes months of manual work as AI generates more drug candidates.
business_model: B2B SaaS / AI analysis platform for enterprise pharma
product_category: AI for proteomics and protein characterization
founder_names: David Roberts; Andrew Reiter; Vishnu Tejus
market_need_then: The company says it has enterprise pharma customers onboarding and claims large time savings; TechCrunch (Apr 2026) frames AI producing more drug candidates than can be characterized. Company claims, not independently verified.
outcome_analysis: 10x Science, founded in 2025 out of a Stanford lab and in YC W26, raised a $4.8M seed led by Initialized Capital in April 2026 and is Active. It is only months old at the time of research, so no outcome exists; founder domain fit and an early pharma pipeline are the sourced strengths and are not yet proof of product-market fit.

name: 21st
one_liner: UI building blocks for the agentic internet
long_description:
21st.dev is the largest React component registry for AI applications, used by 2M developers 
We provide the building blocks to create agent-powered apps: UI components, agent templates.

business_model: Freemium component registry with paid membership for unlimited copies, 21st AI add-on, and an agents SDK with usage billing
product_category: React component registry and AI agent infrastructure

name: 6thSense
one_liner: Nervous System for Physical AI

target_customer: Robotics and physical-AI companies training dexterous manipulation models

name: 83 Sciences

long_description: 83 Sciences uses AI to mine discarded experimental data and drive scientific breakthroughs. Working alongside labs, we discover the materials that will power the new Industrial Revolution.

name: 9 Mothers
one_liner: Counter Drone Systems. $1.6m sales. We delivered for the DoW.
long_description:
We have sold $1.6m of systems to the DoW. Multiple systems delivered to the DoW.

Our first product - EDDA - is a counter drone system - small, low power, low cost fully autonomous-capable. It's designed to be used on vehicles, bases, or carried - to stop group 1 suicide drones. We have multiple contracts, sales, etc.

We have 3 more products with demand in various stages of development.

More details at https://9mothers.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

outcome_analysis: The company claims 1.6M in sales to the Department of War, delivered systems, Army testing in August 2026 and a radar integration partnership, which shows early product market fit in a drone-driven demand surge. Founders previously built and ran a YC software company. Funding amounts are unverified, so the capital story is unknown.

name: AICE

name: ANORIA
one_liner: The first wearable that reads your emotions to enhance your EQ.
long_description: We've spent decades tracking everything. Sleep. Recovery. Steps. All proxies for how we feel. Performance is 90% mental. And yet no one has built the feedback loop for our emotions. We close that loop by designing a device that understands how you feel, tells you why, and what you can do about it. Emotional intelligence becomes trainable, so you can better connect and create with those around you.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: People track sleep, recovery and steps but have no feedback loop for emotions. ANORIA is a bracelet that infers emotional state from biometric and audio signals and gives a Flow Score built from energy, mood and focus.

name: ARC Prize Foundation
one_liner: AI benchmarks that measure general intelligence and inspire new ideas
long_description:
ARC Prize builds AI benchmarks that measure general intelligence. Our benchmark, ARC-AGI, has been used by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and xAI.

Founded by Mike Knoop and Francois Chollet, we inspire open source artificial general intelligence (AGI) research through benchmarks (the ARC-AGI series), global competitions, research grants, community, and content, we exist to guide researchers, industry, and regulators on the path to AGI.

We believe that AGI requires more than just scaling up existing AI models. It demands a fundamental shift towards systems capable of genuine fluid intelligence, the ability to adapt to novel challenges and solve problems efficiently, much like humans do.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: AI labs, researchers and regulators who use or cite the ARC-AGI benchmarks; funded by donors and sponsors rather than customers
problem: Existing AI benchmarks saturate and do not measure fluid intelligence, so the field lacks a durable test of progress toward general intelligence.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by donations, with prize money and benchmark evaluations; no revenue model stated
product_category: AI benchmarks and research competitions (nonprofit)
founder_names: Greg Kamradt; Mike Knoop; Francois Chollet
market_need_then: Frontier labs lacked a benchmark that resisted scaling, and the ARC Prize 2024 competition ran from 2024-06-11 to 2024-11-10 with a pool above 1M, drawing wide participation.
outcome_analysis: The foundation turned a one-off prize into a nonprofit that runs the ARC-AGI benchmark series, with frontier lab adoption, a 2 million dollar 2026 prize on Kaggle and press from launches. Funding sources are not public in what was found, and criticism about overselling the benchmark and disputes over evaluations remain.

name: AbInitio Bio
one_liner: The Intelligence layer for Drug Manufacturing
long_description: Abinitio Bio builds foundation models for biomanufacturing, validated against wet lab data. Our first model, Echo, predicts manufacturing outcomes more accurately than standard models, and any pharma or CDMO can adapt it to their own workflow instantly. By making process decisions that take 6-18 months today in hours, we help teams avoid the cost of delay on a single program.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

business_model: Enterprise software and models licensed to pharma and CDMOs, adaptable to each customer's workflow (pricing not public)
product_category: AI foundation models for biologics manufacturing and process development
market_need_then: The company states process decisions take 6 to 18 months today. Several funded startups (ChemT, Basetwo) target AI for biomanufacturing, which indicates active investor interest.
outcome_analysis: AbInitio Bio is a Spring 2026 YC company with two founders, a first model called Echo and no verified revenue or customers. It is too early to judge an outcome; the main questions are whether Echo's accuracy claims hold up against wet lab data and whether pharma and CDMO buyers will adopt it. No shutdown or acquisition has been reported.

name: Acyclic Labs
tags: Swarm AI; Open Source; Data Engineering; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Benchmarks, RL envs and infra for scaling agent swarms
long_description:
We’re building the foundations of agent swarms that can materially accelerate all work: benchmarks to measure model capabilities, models trained to coordinate thousands of agents, RL environments to improve them, and infrastructure that can put a datacenter’s worth of compute behind a single conversation within seconds.

Both founders graduated top 10% from Cambridge. Ram is a published ML researcher and Varun worked at the frontier of parallel programming languages and shipped enterprise multi-agent systems at Palantir and Tracelight. We realised that agents were good enough to solve most use cases. So why couldn’t we run thousands of them at once and finish hours of work in minutes?
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and engineering teams that want to run agent swarms at scale
problem: Agents are good enough for most use cases, but running thousands of them in parallel and coordinating them to finish hours of work in minutes lacks benchmarks, training environments and infrastructure.
business_model: Open source infrastructure plus managed platform, training data and RL environments sold to labs, and a benchmark (SwarmBench)
product_category: Agent swarm infrastructure, RL environments and benchmarks
market_need_then: Reports in 2026 describe heavy lab demand for RL environments and roughly 20 seed to Series A environment startups, with consolidation expected.
outcome_analysis: Acyclic Labs is a Fall 2026 YC company with two Cambridge graduates in London and no disclosed funding. The outcome is open; success depends on whether SwarmBench and the open source infrastructure gain adoption among labs before frontier labs and better funded RL environment vendors absorb the niche.

name: Adalat AI
one_liner: AI OS transforming courts, accelerating justice

problem: Indian courts face huge backlogs and a shortage of stenographers; clerical work such as typing depositions slows every case.
business_model: Nonprofit-style justice technology provided to courts, funded by grants and philanthropic capital; YC listing shows it as a company
product_category: Legal tech: court speech-to-text transcription and case workflow

It is funded by grants and philanthropy, not venture rounds, so growth rests on government adoption rather than commercial sales.

name: Adialante
one_liner: Cancer screening without barriers
long_description:
We know how to improve cancer outcomes by 8x-10x: you catch it early. 

MRI is the most robust and powerful cancer-detection tool in the world, yet systems cost millions to purchase, take months to install, and require high levels of technical skill to operate. We've redesigned MRI from the ground up with new physics, algorithms, and hardware, all to bring cancer screening to the entire world. 

Our mobile MRI is an imaging clinic on wheels. No equipment to buy, no infrastructure needed. For a flat per-scan fee, any medical site can offer MRI cancer screening. Starting with prostate cancer. Then everything else.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Medical clinics (starting with urology) that pay a flat per-scan fee
problem: MRI cancer screening needs multimillion dollar systems and expert operation, so most sites cannot offer it.
business_model: Owned mobile MRI units with flat per-scan fee (service model)
product_category: Mobile compact MRI for cancer screening

outcome_analysis: Adialante is a Spring 2026 company still pre-clearance, with no FDA approval reported and its first units expected in clinics around Q4 2026. Its story rests on a hard technical and regulatory path, grant support and letters of intent; it is too early to assign outcome factors.

name: Adside.ai
one_liner: AI agency that manages paid ads on Meta, Google, LinkedIn, etc.
long_description: We're Robin Choy and Guillaume Miara, founders of Adside (adside.ai). We're building Adside, a swarm of agents that manages ads on Meta, Google and LinkedIn, etc. We’re building the service we wished we had in our previous B2B marketing software company that we sold earlier this year.

product_category: AI agents for paid advertising management

The market is crowded with funded agentic ad tools and native platform AI, so the outcome depends on execution and distribution; no result is known yet.

name: Advanced Metal Research
one_liner: Machine intelligence for American Welding
long_description:
America does not just need more welders. It needs welding knowledge that can scale.

The American Welding Society projects 320,500 new welding professionals will be needed by 2029, with about 80,000 jobs to be filled annually from 2025 to 2029. More than 157,000 current welding professionals are approaching retirement. Welders are only a small share of the skilled-trades workforce, but welding accounts for an outsized share of projected capability demand. 

The market calls it a labor shortage. AMR sees a learning bottleneck.

We are building American-made robotic welding cells that combine computer vision to provide real-time seam tracking and post-weld inspection to turn welding from a scarce manual process into a closed-loop manufacturing system that learns from every weld as it happens.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US manufacturers and fabricators with welding labor shortages, plus federal buyers and technical schools
problem: The American Welding Society projects 320,500 new welders needed by 2029 while many welders near retirement; welding knowledge does not scale.
business_model: Hardware sales of robot arms and weld cells plus paid welding intelligence software skills; open source controller
product_category: Robotic welding cells with computer vision
founder_names: Angus Muffatti; Julian Fried; Stephen Lin
market_need_then: AWS workforce projections of 320,500 new welders by 2029 and about 80,000 openings a year, as quoted by the company.
outcome_analysis: Advanced Metal Research is a Spring 2026 YC company that went from selling a welding cell concept to shipping its own robot arm and open source controller. It faces a far better funded rival in Path Robotics, so the result depends on cost, American-made positioning and the data advantage from learning on every weld. No outcome is known yet.

name: Aemon
one_liner: The Forward-Deployed AI Research Engineer
long_description:
Aemon is the first autonomous research engineer that delivers state-of-the-art solutions to your engineering problems. It generates, tests, and evolves thousands of approaches at machine speed to discover optimal solutions beyond what human experts can find.

Aemon already set a new world record on an NP-hard math optimization problem with <$10 of compute, beating the previous record set by Google DeepMind in 2025.

Ray and Richard (twin brothers) dropped out of UWaterloo and UIUC to build Aemon. They published at top AI conferences like ICLR and EMNLP before turning 20.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering and R&D teams with a measurable evaluation metric for a hard optimization problem
problem: Solving hard engineering problems requires expert researchers to try many approaches by hand; an autonomous system can generate, test and evolve thousands of approaches cheaply.
business_model: Forward-deployed AI research service sold by demo and engagement (pricing not public)
product_category: Autonomous AI research and optimization engineer
market_need_then: AlphaEvolve in 2025 showed LLM driven discovery could beat human records, and open source clones drew developer interest, indicating demand for the approach.
outcome_analysis: Aemon is a Winter 2026 YC company founded by twin brothers who dropped out of university and who claim a record on circle packing for under 10 USD of compute. Open source and DeepMind competition is strong, so the result depends on turning benchmark wins into paid engineering engagements. An aggregator lists a pre-seed in March 2026, unverified; no outcome yet.

name: Aernata
tags: Carbon Capture and Removal; Alternative Fuels; Climate; Energy
one_liner: Making clean fuels out of CO2.
long_description:
Aernata is an American chemicals company producing clean fuel from industrial emissions.

We're starting by converting CO2 to methanol for synthetic fuel production.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Industrial CO2 emitters and synthetic fuel and chemical buyers needing methanol
problem: Industrial CO2 emissions have little economic use, and e-methanol costs more than fossil methanol.
business_model: Chemicals producer selling clean methanol made from captured industrial CO2 (details not public)
product_category: CO2 to methanol clean fuel production
competitors_at_founding: Oxylus Energy; Aerleum; European Energy Kasso plant
market_need_then: E-methanol is promoted for shipping decarbonization, but sources note it remains much costlier than fossil methanol due to electricity costs.
outcome_analysis: Aernata is a Spring 2026 YC company with two repeat founders from finance and crypto backgrounds aiming to make methanol from industrial CO2. Little public information exists. Competing efforts have more funding and operating plants, and e-methanol cost remains the central risk; no outcome is known yet.

name: Aerogen Systems
one_liner: Modernizing Chip Manufacturing Infrastructure
long_description:
We are building the future of chip manufacturing.

Chips are more advanced than ever, and the features inside them keep getting smaller. But the cleanroom infrastructure supporting their manufacture has not scaled at the same pace. Intel, TSMC, Samsung, and others spend billions building and operating massive cleanrooms, only to isolate their most advanced wafers from the surrounding facility as much as possible.

We think that architecture is backwards. Instead of making the entire building cleaner, why not make the machinery itself as clean as possible?

Talos is our proprietary tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor equipment and continuously destroys airborne molecular contaminants before they reach the wafer. Instead of fighting contamination by constantly flooding tools with ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos keeps the environment inside the machine 10–100x cleaner, without the massive purge-gas bill.

Talos is powerful on its own, but it is also the foundation for a much bigger vision: the Cleanpipe.

The Aerogen Systems Cleanpipe is an ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Rather than relying on a billion-dollar cleanroom to protect every cubic foot of factory space, Cleanpipe creates a controlled environment only where cleanliness actually matters: around the wafer.

Talos cleans the tools. Cleanpipe connects them. Eventually, we delete the cleanroom and build more advanced chips, at greater scale, with radically less infrastructure. With cleanpipes connecting tools, chip fabs can exist anywhere.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Semiconductor equipment makers and fabs
problem: Fabs spend billions on cleanrooms and ultra-high-purity nitrogen purges, yet airborne molecular contaminants still reach wafers as features shrink.
business_model: Hardware units installed inside process tools (Talos), with a planned fab interconnect (Cleanpipe); pilot program
product_category: Semiconductor contamination control hardware
market_need_then: Entegris and AAF describe AMC as an invisible threat to yield; fabs spend heavily on cleanrooms and nitrogen purge, per the company.
outcome_analysis: Aerogen Systems is a Summer 2026 YC spinout of University of Michigan aerospace research that won the university's Demo Day top prize and a Fuel grant. It is piloting Talos in semiconductor tooling and has no disclosed venture funding. The outcome depends on equipment partner pilots and proving lab claims in fabs; unknown for now.

name: Agency Tool Company
tags: Developer Tools; Robotics; Automation; Infrastructure; Self-Driving Vehicles
one_liner: Reliable infrastructure to build, deploy and manage real-world robots.
long_description:
Agency Tool Company ships software to robots in the field 20x faster than a Docker pull with ATC Deploy, sending only the bytes that changed and resuming when the network drops. Deployment tooling is the connection between the lab & the field that continually bottlenecks robotics scaling and lacks a strong robotics-native solution. Deploy is live today with 3 launch partners across ag, construction, and logistics robotics.

Our second product, ATC Build, offers embedded-compute as a CI service so devs can run tests and validate their software on the actual target hardware. Build supports the Nvidia Jetson lineup, Raspberry Pi, and a number of other embedded platform targets.

Jack Morrison and Davis Foster founded and sold Scythe Robotics after deploying hundreds of autonomous mowers across the country; Agency Tool Company is building the robotics deployment platform across hardware and software they wish they had.

Learn more at https://agencytool.com
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Robotics companies deploying fleets of field robots (agriculture, construction, logistics) and their software and operations teams
problem: Shipping software to robots in the field is slow and brittle over poor networks, and embedded CI needs real target hardware. Deployment tooling is the gap between lab and field.
business_model: Developer infrastructure SaaS (OTA deploy and fleet management, hosted embedded CI); pricing not found
product_category: Robotics developer tools and deployment infrastructure

name: Ageospatial
one_liner: Physical intelligence for every decision with Geospatial AI.
long_description:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.

name: Ailit
tags: Hardware; Transportation; Energy; Electric Vehicles; AI
one_liner: Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.
long_description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype, and it’s being prepared to move a locomotive on battery power in the coming days.

name: Alt-X
one_liner: Building the best venue for private markets exposure.
long_description:
Alt-X is building the AI-native liquidity layer for private markets.

Private markets have created trillions of dollars in value, yet remain fragmented, illiquid, and inaccessible. While public markets benefit from exchanges, market makers, brokerages, and data infrastructure, private markets still rely on brokers, spreadsheets, and manual workflows to connect buyers and sellers.

Alt-X uses AI to automate the core functions required to make private assets liquid. We streamline diligence, valuation, investor matching, and transaction execution, reducing the friction that makes private-market transactions slow, expensive, and opaque today.

Our initial focus is venture-backed secondaries. We source opportunities from founders, employees, and early investors while building a network of accredited investors seeking exposure to the world's most valuable private companies. Over time, we believe every private asset—from startup equity to private credit and alternative investments—will require modern liquidity infrastructure.

Building trusted infrastructure for private markets is difficult. Transactions involve complex diligence, fragmented information, transfer restrictions, and significant compliance requirements. Alt-X is focused on creating systems that can support real transactions at scale, not just marketplace listings.

Ryan Samadi (Stanford CS/AI, former Citadel commodities trader) and Michael Wachsman (Cornell CS, infrastructure engineer) are building Alt-X because they believe ownership of innovation should be more liquid, transparent, and accessible. Today, Alt-X has sourced over $1.5 million in transaction opportunities and assembled a network of 40 accredited investors representing hundreds of millions of dollars in investable assets.

Our mission is to democratize ownership of innovation by building the financial infrastructure that private markets have never had.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Venture secondary buyers and sellers and accredited investors; an Excel plugin also targets real estate underwriters
problem: Private market transactions rely on brokers, spreadsheets and manual diligence, making them slow, costly and opaque.
business_model: Marketplace for venture secondaries (take rate not stated) plus an Excel AI modeling tool
product_category: Fintech, private markets liquidity and AI financial modeling
market_need_then: PitchBook estimated US VC secondaries traded about $106.3B in 2025, and companies stayed private longer, creating demand for liquidity.
outcome_analysis: Alt-X is a Winter 2026 company whose two Stanford and Cornell computer science founders pitch AI infrastructure for private markets, with the CEO coming from Citadel. name: Altair Health
one_liner: Stripe for medical billing
long_description:
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions.

That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. 

Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay.

We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot.

Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on. And to the Health Insurers' "Delay, Deny, Defend", we say "Predict, Prevent, Prevail".

name: Archgen Labs

Stacking compute vertically shortens connections and reduces the energy and delay of moving data. But it also makes heat harder to remove. Our tools help engineers optimize placement, timing, and temperature together so they can build faster, more power-efficient 3D chips.

Our GPU-accelerated placement engine ranked first in the Hudson River Trading macro-placement challenge. LayerTherm, our thermal analysis tool, predicts chip temperatures roughly 5,000× faster than conventional simulation in our benchmarks, helping engineers explore more designs and identify hotspots earlier. Newton, our AI chip design engineer, automates work across placement, routing, design-rule fixes, and timing closure.

We’re working with GlobalFoundries on 3D chip development, targeting our first tapeout in 2027.

name: Arlo Industries
one_liner: Track drones and missiles without radars - Accurate, Passive, Scalable
long_description:
Arlo Industries is building a network of sensors that precisely tracks stealthy drones and aerial threats better than radars.

This capability does not exist yet because traditional radars are built on past war doctrines designed to protect single, centralised assets. Modern warfare, however, demands wide-area, persistent coverage that is both passive and economically scalable. By utilising a mesh architecture, Arlo Industries unlocks unprecedented asymmetric economics. The network is fundamentally built to scale: the cost of adding sensors grows linearly, but the tracking accuracy increases exponentially, delivering highly resilient, persistent coverage for a fraction of the cost of legacy systems.

Deo founded Arlo Industries after spending over 6 years in the Israeli defence ecosystem, where he lived through multiple conflicts and experienced the Iron Dome and other systems in action against ICBMs and the infamous Shahed drones. Learning exactly how these defence systems could be improved after a Shahed exploded close to his apartment, he built Arlo Industries around the core philosophy that conflict should be concise & precise.

The people behind Arlo1 includes a PhD in drones and autonomy and military experts.

Arlo Industries has actively showcased this technology directly to Ukrainian militaries on the frontlines, as well as to operators across Europe and the USA.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Military and defense buyers in Ukraine, Europe and the USA needing wide-area tracking of drones and cruise missiles

business_model: Hardware sensor network plus software sold to defense customers (pricing not stated)

outcome_analysis: Arlo Industries is a Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. name: Armature

We call this Agent-Led Growth (~coding agents GEO for dev tools).

And once agents use your product, Armature shows you what users do with it through AI, with self-serve MCP analytics and evals that catch regressions before your users see them.

name: Armorer Labs
one_liner: Continuous security verification for AI in regulated industries
long_description:
Armorer helps companies in regulated industries ship their own AI systems faster and keep them secure in production.

Most security tools flag an issue and file a ticket. Armorer assesses your agent and simulates attacks to find the real issues. Then it creates a verified fix that stops the attack without breaking the business, ready for your approval in about 4 hours.

In production, Armorer checks every agent action in milliseconds, with no GPU needed. It detects malicious behavior such as prompt injection, goal hijacking and data leaks, then allows, holds or denies the action.

Armorer's detection models beat every other detector we tested on six public benchmarks. Armorer is 22% more accurate than JEV while being 88x faster, so users won't feel the delay.

We spent years building and evaluating AI security systems together at AWS, including its first customer-facing AI security agent, which scaled to 100k+ customers. Armorer is backed by Paul Vixie, an internet pioneer inducted into the Internet Hall of Fame in 2014.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering and security teams in regulated industries (finance, food delivery, healthcare) that deploy their own AI agents
problem: Security tools flag AI agent issues and file tickets, but teams in regulated industries need verified fixes and runtime checks of every agent action without slowing the business.
business_model: B2B SaaS for agent security assessment, fix verification and runtime protection (Armorer Guard), sold by demo
product_category: AI agent security and runtime guardrails
market_need_then: Enterprises were deploying agents in 2026 and security standards (OWASP Agentic Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, NIST AI RMF) were being mapped; a Just Eat Takeaway engineering director is quoted as a customer, but counts and revenue are not given.
outcome_analysis: Armorer Labs is a Fall 2026 YC company that is active with two ex AWS founders. It targets a fast growing need for agent security in regulated firms but faces many funded guardrail vendors and cloud incumbents. No exit, funding round or revenue figure is verified, so the outcome is unresolved.

name: Arzana
one_liner: Adaptive AI built for manufacturers
long_description:
Arzana trains custom models on manufacturers' operational data to automate their quoting, order entry, invoicing, and other repetitive office work. We've saved our customers over $1.5M in avoided staff costs.

In the future, we'll expand into shop-floor automation, sending instructions to machinery and robots to produce the orders that our office agents processed. By 2035, we aim to fully automate 10,000 American factories.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and mid sized discrete manufacturers (machining, molding, stamping, fabrication, packaging) that run ERP and email heavy back offices
problem: Manufacturers burn skilled staff time on quoting, order entry, scheduling and AP/AR work inside legacy ERP systems and inboxes.
business_model: B2B SaaS of custom built AI agents per shop, with more agents added over time
product_category: AI back office agents for manufacturing
market_need_then: Manufacturing back offices were heavily manual and ERP vendors were adding AI in 2025; customers quoted on the company site report faster quoting, though figures are self reported.
outcome_analysis: Arzana is an active Spring 2026 YC company founded in 2025 that sells custom AI agents to manufacturers and shows 14 customer logos. It competes with several YC and venture funded quoting startups and ERP vendors adding AI. Funding is not verifiably documented, so the trajectory is still open.

name: Asakana
one_liner: Automating away manual admin for food distributors: texts to ERP
long_description: Restaurants send orders to food distributors by email, text, and photo. Someone at the distributor retypes every one of them into the ERP. Asakana does that entry instead: orders land in the ERP already entered, and anything unclear goes to a person before it goes in. Live at US seafood distributors today, returning 40%+ of order-desk time to selling. Founded by a seafood distributor and a Gemini builder.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Food distributors, starting with US seafood distributors, whose order desks retype restaurant orders into an ERP
problem: Restaurants send orders by text, email, phone, photo and handwritten note, and distributor staff retype them into the ERP, tying up sales reps and order desks.
business_model: B2B SaaS that reads orders and automates order entry and related sales workflows, integrating with the distributor's ERP
product_category: AI order entry for food distribution
market_need_then: Distributor order desks were manual and the YC page claims 40 percent or more of order desk time returned to selling at live seafood customers; no independent customer evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Asakana is an active Fall 2026 YC company with a founder who worked in seafood distribution and a CTO from Google AI. It is live at seafood distributors but competes with several funded rivals. Funding and revenue are not verified, so the outcome is unresolved.

name: Ascenix
one_liner: Custom software for senior care facilities.
long_description:
Ascenix is building one custom interface for running senior homes. We combine reusable building blocks into workflows tailored to each home's existing processes, from incident reporting to reimbursement. Homes get custom software without hiring an engineering team.

Living in a retirement home convinced us that the best way to improve residents' lives is to improve the systems staff rely on. As the older population grows, care teams need more time and resources. Repetitive reporting, missed reimbursement, and compliance problems take those away. Disconnected products that solve each of these individually add costs and leave staff moving information between systems.

Our building blocks gather information from EHRs like PointClickCare and other sources, process it, apply rules, and produce reports, tasks, or emails. Incident reporting and reimbursement reviews usually come from two separate vendors. Ascenix builds both from the same blocks, in one interface, so data isn't stuck in silos. Homes start with their biggest bottleneck and add workflows as priorities change.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Senior care and long term care operators (nursing and retirement homes) in Canada and the US
problem: Care homes run on fragmented vendors and manual reporting for falls, incidents, compliance and reimbursement review, and staff lose hours to documentation and miss funding.
business_model: B2B SaaS, custom workflows built on reusable blocks over EHR data, replacing multiple vendors with one system
product_category: Workflow automation and analytics for senior care
market_need_then: Care homes face documentation burden and compliance risk; a case study customer (Responsive Health Management) reports an 80 percent cut in manual fall analysis time, and the founders report live use in 55 facilities, both company stated.
outcome_analysis: Ascenix is an active Fall 2026 YC company from Toronto with a seven person team and reported customers across nine named care providers. Its founders immersed themselves in a retirement home, which gives strong founder market fit. Funding is undisclosed and the main risk is EHR incumbents, so the outcome remains open.

name: Asendia AI
one_liner: AI recruiters for staffing agencies
long_description: Asendia AI replaces the top-of-funnel recruiter. Our AI agents clone each agency's best human recruiter: their knowledge base, screening logic, outreach style, and judgment, then run the full workflow across phone, SMS, WhatsApp, and email, 24/7. A req comes in; by the time a recruiter sits down, Asendia has already sourced, screened, and drafted submittals. Staffing is a $200B+ industry where speed is the entire margin.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Staffing and recruiting agencies (Bullhorn-style ATS users)
problem: Top-of-funnel recruiting work (sourcing, screening, outreach, drafting submittals) is slow and manual and limits placements per recruiter.
business_model: B2B SaaS for agencies (pricing not found)
product_category: AI recruiting agents for staffing
market_need_then: Staffing agencies compete on speed; the company cites a 200B USD industry. The only dated demand evidence found is a May 2026 trade-press interview about doubling placements with agentic AI.
outcome_analysis: Asendia AI is a Spring 2026 YC company selling AI recruiter agents to staffing agencies, with a ten-person team. No verified funding or traction is public, and no outcome exists yet. It enters a category where Alex and Juicebox raised large rounds within the prior year, so differentiation by cloning each agency's best recruiter is the stated bet.

name: Aseon Labs
one_liner: Robotic pitstops for self-driving cars
long_description:
Aseon Labs builds robotic pitstops for self-driving cars.

Autonomous vehicles can drive themselves, but they still rely on humans and centralized depots for charging, cleaning and servicing multiple times per day. As fleets scale, the operational layer makes up 70% of the cost of the service and is of the largest barrier to uptime, profitability and market expansion.

Aseon Pods are robotic micro-depots that can be deployed directly within operating zones, bringing fleet servicing to where demand exists. By eliminating unnecessary depot trips and automating routine operations, Aseon helps autonomous fleet operators increase uptime, reduce reset cost by 50% and unlock scale.

Founded by the team behind Pushme, which deployed 5,000 mobility infrastructure locations across 40 cities before its acquisition by TIER-Dott, Aseon is funded and building product in Redwood City for pilot deployment with major autonomous vehicle operators.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Robotaxi and autonomous vehicle fleet operators and automotive OEMs
problem: Autonomous fleets spend a large share of miles and time driving to depots to charge, clean and inspect vehicles; the company says about a third of vehicles are offline for servicing at any time.
business_model: Hardware plus service: robotic micro depots (Aseon Pods) deployed in operating zones for pilot customers
product_category: Robotic servicing pods for autonomous vehicle fleets
market_need_then: Robotaxi fleets were scaling in 2026 and deadhead miles and depot space were widely discussed; Aseon says pilots are underway with AV operators, but no named customers exist.
outcome_analysis: Aseon Labs, from the Pushme team that sold to TIER-Dott, emerged from stealth in May 2026 and announced a $10M seed led by Crane Venture Partners in June 2026. Repeat founders with hardware and fleet operations experience gave it fast funding, but pods are still prototypes and no customer is named. Outcome is open.

name: Ashr
tags: Deep Learning; Generative AI; Reinforcement Learning; Data Engineering; AI
one_liner: Enterprise post-training, monitoring, and continual learning platform
long_description:
Ashr Manifold is a self-contained model training, hosting, observability, and continual learning platform for purpose-built open-weight models. 

Startups can use Manifold to post-train and manage fleets of continuously improving open-weight models without having a dedicated research team or infrastructure. Ultimately, this reduces operating costs and allows a greater degree of control over proprietary company knowledge.

Enterprises can use Manifold to encode institutional judgements and priorities into open-weight models, reduce token costs, and manage every level of the AI life cycle, from data curation, to model serving on weights and infrastructure they own.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Growth stage startups, research teams and enterprises that want custom open weight models without an in house ML team
problem: Teams want models tuned to their own data and workflows but lack the research staff to curate data, post train, evaluate and serve open weight models.
business_model: Platform plus forward deployed engineering for post training, hosting, monitoring and evals (Ashr Manifold), customers own the weights
product_category: Post training and continual learning platform for custom models
market_need_then: Open weight models were improving and enterprises wanted owned models; a customer quote claims a tripling of browser agent performance on EHR workflows at 20 clinics, which is self reported.
outcome_analysis: Ashr is an active Winter 2026 YC company with two founders that moved from agent testing toward a post training platform. It lists named customers such as Novoflow and academic users, but funding and revenue are not public. Large model platforms are encroaching, so its path is still unclear.

name: Asim
tags: Deep Learning; Hard Tech; Hardware; Robotic Process Automation; Robotics
one_liner: Enable robots to operate safely in the real world.
long_description:
Asim is building standardized benchmarks for physical intelligence, helping robotics companies understand their robots’ capabilities and safety limits before deployment.
We test real robots under changing physical conditions, varying shape, weight, friction and material, to identify where performance breaks down and give engineers actionable feedback.

Our four founders include three PhD researchers, two specializing in robotics, with backgrounds at Sony and NASA JPL and two RoboCup@Home championship wins.

Our ambition is to become the standard robotics teams use to measure progress and assess readiness for deployment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robotics companies and robot foundation model developers that need standardized, repeatable evaluation of physical performance and safety before deployment
problem: There are few standardized real world benchmarks for robots under changing conditions such as object shape, weight and friction, so teams cannot see where performance breaks down or what safety risks exist.
business_model: Benchmarking and evaluation services for robot makers, pricing not stated
product_category: Physical intelligence benchmarks and robot safety evaluation
founder_names: Douglas Tilley; Raphaël Lafargue; Tristan Lecourtois; Maëlic Neau
market_need_then: Physical AI funding grew fast in 2026 while real world evals barely existed, as multiple sources including Robocurve say; no customer or pilot is named for Asim.
outcome_analysis: Asim is a Fall 2026 YC robotics benchmark startup with four academic founders and no public funding or customers. Strong research credentials fit the evaluation niche, but competitors Robocurve and PhAIL started earlier and the commercial model is unproven. The outcome is open.

name: Asimov
one_liner: Real-world human movement data for humanoid robots
long_description: Asimov collects real-world human movement data from households and businesses to train humanoid robots. Unlike factory datasets that capture the same tasks in the same environments, we deliver the full diversity of real human environments, thousands of hours a day to leading labs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Frontier robotics and humanoid labs that buy training data
problem: Humanoid robot models need diverse real world human movement data, while factory datasets repeat the same tasks in the same places.
business_model: data sales to robotics labs; paid contributors and partner businesses record tasks with Asimov collection kits
product_category: physical AI training data
market_need_then: Robotics labs were seeking egocentric human video at scale in 2026, with NVIDIA research using tens of thousands of hours of human video.
outcome_analysis: Asimov is an early stage W26 company selling human movement data to robotics labs, with a creative side business running a cleaning company whose cleaners wear its kits. It has YC, Robinhood Ventures and angel backing, no disclosed round size, and no outcome yet, so any forecast rests on a hot physical AI data market with growing competition.

name: Assemble
one_liner: Autonomous IT Delivery
long_description: Assemble accelerates IT teams by performing development work inside core enterprise systems like ERP, CRM, and HRIS. Our agents help IT teams scope dependencies, build logic, and validate changes across your systems.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: IT and business systems teams at scaling companies that run ERP, CRM and HRIS platforms such as Salesforce, SAP, Workday and NetSuite
problem: IT teams have backlogs of change work inside core business systems, and each change needs dependency mapping, logic building and validation.
business_model: enterprise software subscription for autonomous agents (pricing not published)
product_category: AI agents for enterprise systems administration and IT delivery
founder_names: Aliyan Ishfaq; Shaurnav Ghosh; Shrish Janarthanan
competitors_at_founding: Salesforce Agentforce Operations; SRE.ai; Workday Admin Agent
market_need_then: IT teams carry change backlogs and vendors were all shipping agentic features in 2026, indicating spend and demand, though the YC page gives no customer evidence.
outcome_analysis: Assemble is a four person Summer 2026 company with Stanford AI founders building agents that change enterprise systems. No funding or customers are public, and the major suite vendors and a funded YC peer already target similar work, so the outcome will depend on trust, integrations and speed against incumbents.

name: Aster
one_liner: Automating open-ended research.
long_description: Aster is the first autonomous research lab — thousands of AI research agents orchestrated in parallel toward a single goal. We're on a mission to automate open-ended research: research that defines its own problems before it can answer them. The future doesn't wait to be defined by benchmarks. Neither do we.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Research teams and AI labs that want automated research; products named on the site are Inference, Roadmap and Plans (pricing)
problem: Research is limited by human researcher time; Aster aims to run thousands of AI research agents in parallel on open-ended problems that define their own questions.
business_model: research automation platform and products; pricing plans listed but details not found
product_category: autonomous AI research lab
market_need_then: Autonomous science drew investor funding in early 2026, as seen in a 14M seed at Autoscience and a 45M round at an unnamed Singapore lab reported by Semafor.
outcome_analysis: Aster is a one person Spring 2026 company led by a former Magic researcher, with a published paper and claimed benchmark records but no public customers or confirmed funding. It competes with funded autonomous research startups and with frontier labs, so its path depends on turning claimed speed into repeatable discoveries.

name: Astraea
one_liner: AI Operating System for Clinical Development
long_description: Astraea automates clinical trial biometrics from raw study inputs to FDA-ready outputs. The platform handles data normalization, CDISC mapping, SDTM, ADaM, TFLs, QC, and revision workflows in one auditable system, helping Phase II/III sponsors reduce months of manual programming and data management into automated, reviewable execution.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Phase II and III clinical trial sponsors and their biometrics, data management and statistical programming teams
problem: Turning raw clinical study data into FDA-ready submission outputs (CDISC mapping, SDTM, ADaM, tables, listings, figures, QC) takes months of manual programming.
business_model: Enterprise software deployed inside the sponsor's environment with forward-deployed engineers
product_category: AI clinical trial biometrics automation
competitors_at_founding: Saama; Narrativa Dataset Voyager; Clymb Clinical
market_need_then: Sponsors spend months on manual biometrics programming; 2026 vendor and conference material (PharmaSUG, Cytel, Saama) shows active demand for AI in statistical programming with human oversight.
outcome_analysis: Astraea is a Spring 2026 company that is still active and only weeks old at the time of research, so there is no outcome yet. Its early signals are a two person technical founding team, a focused regulated niche, and a crowded field of AI SDTM and ADaM vendors, so the main open question is whether it wins sponsor trust faster than established players.

name: Async
one_liner: AI agents that run businesses
long_description: Async builds AI agents that run businesses.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Service businesses such as law firms, clinics and real estate firms (YC listing and company customer stories)
problem: Small businesses lose time on lead intake, follow-up, document processing, research and back-office work that agents could run continuously.
business_model: B2B AI agent platform, pricing not found
product_category: AI agents for business operations

outcome_analysis: Async is an active two person company selling AI agents to service businesses, and no outcome event has occurred. The risks visible now are a crowded agent market with weak defensibility and a generic name, while its traction claims on its own site remain unverified.

name: Atlas Discovery

one_liner: AI-native pharma company
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: Biomedical knowledge is too large for humans to search, so drugs that could treat rare diseases go unfound and small markets are ignored because development economics do not work.
business_model: Pharma company model: AI-found drug repurposing programs taken into clinical trials, with data partnerships and possible licensing (company describes data partnerships, biology models and autonomous research agents)
product_category: AI drug discovery and repurposing

competitors_at_founding: Every Cure; Harvard TxGNN research model; Perceptic; Helical

No failure or exit is reported.

name: Atlia
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
tags: Real Estate; Proptech; Big Data; AI
one_liner: The AI-native property management company for short-term rentals
long_description: We use AI agents to manage short-term rental properties by running operations completely autonomously. We cut traditional human management fees in half so owners take home 20% to 30% more revenue. And we operate with near-zero boots-on-the-ground so we can scale nationwide with software margins and at venture speed in a traditionally physical industry.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Owners of short-term rental properties such as Airbnbs who want to outsource management
problem: Traditional short-term rental managers charge 20 to 35 percent of revenue and rely on many local staff; owners want lower fees and less hassle.
business_model: Full-service property management for a flat percentage of booking revenue (website states 10 percent), with AI agents running operations and local operators supervising
product_category: AI-native short-term rental property management
market_need_then: Owners complain about 20 to 35 percent management fees (company claim); the company reports managing about 80 properties at batch time.
outcome_analysis: Atlia is a two person Summer 2026 company at the earliest stage, with about 80 managed properties reported at batch time and no exit. Its fee advantage is easy for crowded AI property management rivals and incumbents to match, so it must prove unit economics from real operations, which is why no success or failure factors are assigned yet.

name: Atomarine
one_liner: Floating nuclear powered data centers at sea.
long_description: We are building nuclear power delivery ships to power our floating compute barges at sea. Our systems are fully standalone, have better cooling, and avoid all the resource competition that leads to local community opposition. Our centralized manufacturing allows us to deploy anywhere on Earth, four times faster than on land.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI operators and data center developers needing fast, large scale power and compute capacity
problem: AI compute is limited by access to power and by local opposition and slow permitting on land.
business_model: Shipyard-built floating compute barges of 75 to 100 MW paired with power vessels, sold or leased as compute campuses
product_category: Offshore data center and power infrastructure
competitors_at_founding: Bluecore Energy; Nautilus Data Technologies; ABS and Herbert Engineering study; Karpowership and Mitsui O.S.K. Lines
market_need_then: AI data center demand outstripped grid power and local siting in 2025 and 2026; the company cites community opposition on land.
outcome_analysis: Atomarine is a two person Summer 2026 company that attracted unusual press and a reported $19M seed after Demo Day. Its pitch is nuclear, but the first product is gas powered with a 2028 pilot target, so the central risk is regulatory and technical. No exit or failure has occurred; success factors are not assigned until deployment.

name: Atrisa
one_liner: AI Agents for Analog Circuit Design
long_description: AI Agents to build, debug and automate analog circuit design
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Analog and mixed-signal chip design teams at semiconductor companies
problem: Analog circuit design is manual, slow and depends on scarce experts; engineers spend long cycles on topology choice, simulation and debugging.
business_model: Enterprise software for analog design teams (demo request, likely per seat or contract; pricing not public)
product_category: AI agents for analog circuit design (EDA)
founder_names: Sayan Mitra; Rithik Jain; Atman Kar
market_need_then: Analog design remains a manual bottleneck in chip development and expert engineers are scarce; multiple startups raised money for it in 2025 and 2026.
