outcome_analysis: Autoresearch, Inc. is a Summer 2026 company with three people and two founders from Reducto, DynamoAI and Discord. It claims strong benchmark results on Karpathy's autoresearch task in its launch post, which are unverified. The idea rides a new public technique, so success depends on customer results and speed more than defensibility.

name: Autostep
one_liner: The P&L for knowledge work
long_description: Autostep maps how work happens across a company for humans and agents, finds repetitive tasks and bottlenecks, and ranks them by cost and impact. Then it fixes them by building agents inside existing tools, changing the process, or finding the right software.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies with knowledge workers that want to measure and fix repetitive work, including with AI agents
problem: Companies do not know where employee and agent time goes, so repetitive tasks and bottlenecks go unmeasured.
business_model: B2B software with a desktop app (pricing not public)
product_category: Task mining and operational intelligence for AI agents
market_need_then: Enterprises were buying process intelligence and trying to price AI agent ROI; the company cites a 10 person team finding $100K plus of waste (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Autostep is a one person Spring 2026 company, so no outcome exists yet. It enters task mining where Celonis and Skan are established, and its angle is pricing both human and agent work and then building the fix. Reported revenue growth is unverified and survival depends on raising a seed round and hiring.

name: Autumn
one_liner: The people-intelligence company.
long_description:
Autumn builds research agents that answer questions about people and companies at scale. These AI agents are powered by a live index of over 1 billion people, 100 million companies, and state-of-the-art web research tools. Autumn is already in production with enterprise teams at Brex, Rippling, PostHog across sourcing, enrichment, and identity-verification workflows.

We are a small, highly-technical team. Our vision is to be the search engine that agents use when they need to understand people, their networks, and professional lives.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Go to market, recruiting and identity verification teams at enterprises
problem: Teams need current answers about people and companies at scale for sourcing, enrichment and verification.
business_model: Usage based B2B research agents and API (pricing not public)
product_category: People and company research agents
market_need_then: Sales and recruiting teams spend heavily on enrichment data, and Proxycurl's 2025 shutdown left demand for replacements.
outcome_analysis: Autumn is a four person Winter 2026 company with no outcome yet. It claims production use at Brex, Rippling and PostHog, which is unverified. The risks are crowded enrichment vendors, data access constraints, and a name shared with other startups that muddies discovery.

name: Auxos
one_liner: Simulations of real people for market research
long_description:
Auxos builds AI customer twins for marketing, product, and research teams to test their hypotheses at scale. We work with companies to create 1:1 replicas of their customers by sourcing and interviewing real people in their ICP, allowing us to accurately model how they behave and make decisions. 

Currently, market research is too slow and expensive to use on anything but the biggest decisions. Surveys and panels cost a fortune and it takes weeks to recruit, moderate, and gather insights.   

Auxos provides a 24/7 available customer panel that can give population-scale insights in minutes. The day-to-day decisions surrounding product, pricing, and positioning can now be validated with the same rigor that used to be reserved for the big ones.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Marketing, product, consumer insights and research teams
problem: Surveys and panels are slow and expensive, so only big decisions get validated.
business_model: B2B research platform (pricing not public)
product_category: AI customer twins for market research
founder_names: Ashton Daniel; Jerry Wu; Kerry Lu
market_need_then: Market research is costly and slow; synthetic research drew over $1.5B in venture funding by one estimate.
outcome_analysis: Auxos is a three person Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. The founders have strong engineering and consulting backgrounds but it competes with Aaru and Simile, which raised far larger rounds. Accuracy proof and enterprise sales will decide it.

name: Avea Robotics
one_liner: The human-in-the-loop system for robots
long_description: We built the fastest software to control robots from anywhere in the world. We make it possible for robotics companies to keep their robots at 100% uptime, and intervene instantly when a failure occurs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robotics companies that need to teleoperate and supervise deployed robots
problem: Deployed robots fail in the field and need a human to step in instantly to keep uptime high.
business_model: B2B software platform (Sentinel) for teleoperation and fleet operations
product_category: Robot teleoperation and fleet operations software
market_need_then: Humanoid and field robot makers in 2026 needed teleoperation both to recover from failures and to collect training data; Sentinel's own site frames a learning loop that turns field data into training data.
outcome_analysis: Avea Robotics joined YC in Spring 2026 with two founders and shipped the Sentinel teleoperation platform, launched publicly on June 1, 2026. By its own site it is now part of Foundry Robotics, which announced a $100M Series A and the Avea purchase in late October 2026. Terms are undisclosed, so whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing is not known.

name: Aviern
one_liner: Unmanned cargo airplanes
long_description: Aviern makes unmanned cargo airplanes for commercial operations and defense logistics. In 2 months we built our own scaled aircraft that taxis, takes off, flies and lands fully autonomously and are working on a larger 50lb aircraft.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Air cargo integrators (FedEx, UPS, DHL feeder programs), shippers and defense logistics
problem: Moving cargo to small airports and remote sites with crewed aircraft is costly.
business_model: Autonomous cargo airline and aircraft operator (model not final)
product_category: Unmanned cargo aircraft
market_need_then: FAA proposed Part 108 rules and the eIPP program were opening a path for unmanned operations; integrators run feeder networks.
outcome_analysis: Aviern is a five person Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. It claims an autonomous scaled prototype built in two months. It faces heavily funded rivals such as Reliable Robotics and long certification timelines, so progress depends on funding and milestones in 2027.

name: Avoca Systems
one_liner: The AI operating system for radiology networks
long_description: Avoca is the AI patient access platform built for radiology. It integrates with a network’s existing systems and operational knowledge to automate calls, online scheduling, faxes, e-referrals and patient communications, from referral through to results and follow-up. Unlike generic scheduling tools, Avoca understands the clinical, operational and resource constraints behind every radiology booking, helping providers capture more demand, reduce administrative work and fill more scan capacity.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Radiology networks and imaging clinics
problem: Radiology bookings, referrals and calls are manual, causing call abandonment and missed appointments.
business_model: Success based pricing per the company site
product_category: AI patient access for radiology
market_need_then: 24% of outpatient imaging appointments are missed per a 2025 study cited by RamSoft; company claims call abandonment fell from 30% to 2%.
outcome_analysis: Avoca Systems is a six person Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. It reports live use in more than 250 clinics (company claim) and strong compliance certifications, which suggests early traction in Australia, but it expands into the US against agentic competitors.

name: Avoice
one_liner: AI-native workspace for AEC
long_description:
Avoice is an all-in-one, AI-native platform for running an architecture practice. It covers the whole arc of a project: pricing and proposals to win the work, research and schedules in early design, specifications and QA/QC checks through documentation, contract particulars and preliminaries at tender, then RFIs, submittals, instructions, certificates and valuations through construction, and the compliance record at handover. Timesheets, fees, financials and invoicing run alongside, with Xero and QuickBooks.

Specification is the most-used part of the platform. Avoice drafts coordinated, tender-ready specifications from a practice's own drawings, schedules and office masters, then checks them back against those drawings. Work that normally takes weeks takes an afternoon.

Practices in the UK, US, Australia and New Zealand use Avoice, from boutique studios to firms of several hundred people. It integrates with Revit and ArchiCAD.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Architecture and engineering practices
problem: Practices spend time on specifications, QA, RFIs and admin using separate tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per practice
product_category: AI workspace for architecture practices
market_need_then: Small firms lack large back offices; company claims 250 plus practices and $300M of projects on platform.
outcome_analysis: Avoice is a Winter 2026 company with no outcome yet, with claimed traction in 250 plus UK and international practices and architecture trade press coverage. The founders sold an edtech startup before this one. Risks are incumbents and a small market.

name: Axelrod
one_liner: Hotels that run themselves
long_description: Autonomous software for hotels that takes over all front-of-house and back-of-house tasks with zero integrations, running operations better than your staff would. Axelrod is trusted by Michelin Key awarded and Marriott hotels and is live across 3 continents.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Boutique and luxury hotels
problem: Hotels run many manual front and back of house tasks across PMS, POS and RMS systems.
business_model: B2B software and agents for hotels (pricing not public)
product_category: Autonomous AI agents for hotel operations
founder_names: Adrian Lucas Tariel Stoica; Saman Sayahpour
competitors_at_founding: Operto; AI Hospitality Group; TrustYou AI Agents
market_need_then: Hotel operators were adopting agentic AI in 2025, with Mews publishing a report in Nov 2025.
outcome_analysis: Axelrod is a two person Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. It claims use at Michelin Key hotels across continents, which is unverified. Competition is already active in hotel agents and traction is the key risk.

name: Axiomat
one_liner: We make AI that never hallucinates.
long_description:
Axiomat makes it impossible for AI agents to make mistakes when querying a company’s data. It formally verifies that the agents’ queries are correct before employees or customers rely on the answers. 

It is becoming increasingly important for companies to rely on AI without the need for humans to manually check the answers. This has created a need for systems which can guarantee correctness without limiting the agent’s capabilities. Axiomat provides the infrastructure to prove that answers are correct, starting with data queries and analysis. It brings mathematical guarantees to the agents working with your data.

The team brings direct experience solving AI hallucinations through Ethan’s work as an Applied Scientist at AWS, where he worked on formally verifying AI responses. They also bring research experience in AI, LLMs, and formal methods from EPFL, the University of Toronto, and Georgia Tech.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies that want AI agents to query their own data and need the answers to be provably correct before employees or customers rely on them
problem: AI agents that query company data can return wrong answers, so humans must check them by hand. Axiomat formally verifies the agent's queries against a logical model of the business so correctness is guaranteed.
business_model: B2B SaaS data layer, pricing not public
product_category: Verified AI data layer and semantic layer for agents
founder_names: Ethan Kharitonov; Jack Naimer; Elad Perlman
market_need_then: Companies increasingly want agents to answer data questions without manual checking, and hallucinated answers block adoption. This is the YC page and company description claim; no independent spend data was found.
outcome_analysis: Axiomat is an Active Fall 2026 YC company of three founders with formal methods and AI research backgrounds. No funding, customers or press were found, so no outcome can be judged. Its main risk will be whether verified queries beat semantic layers that incumbents already sell, and the confusable name beside Axiomatic AI and Axiom Math.

name: AxionOrbital Space
one_liner: Foundation models for 24/7 Earth Observation
long_description:
AxionOrbital Space builds foundation models that enable continuous visibility through clouds and darkness. Legacy optical satellites are rendered useless 70% of the time by weather and night cycles, while Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) produces data that is unintelligible to humans and breaks standard vision pipelines.

We solve this by translating raw radar backscatter into analysis-ready optical imagery in real-time. Our proprietary architecture uses deterministic one-step diffusion to transform complex radar signals into clear, photorealistic images. This enables persistent, 24/7 situational awareness for defense, commodities trading, and disaster response, guaranteeing visibility even when the sky is blocked.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Defense, commodities trading and disaster response users who need continuous Earth observation imagery through clouds and darkness
problem: Optical satellites are blocked by weather and night, while radar (SAR) imagery is hard for humans and standard vision pipelines to use. The company translates SAR backscatter into analysis-ready optical imagery in near real time.
business_model: Foundation model and imagery API, pricing not public
product_category: Earth observation foundation models (SAR to optical translation)
market_need_then: Weather and darkness limit optical imagery, per the company page, and SAR demand is growing among defense and commodities buyers. No dated customer evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: AxionOrbital Space is an Active Winter 2026 YC company with two technical founders and a launched model called ORION in January 2026. No verified funding, customers or independent benchmark were found, so no outcome can be judged. Key risks are unproven demand and large EO players with foundation model efforts.

name: Axis
one_liner: An AI Copilot for Trading Desks
long_description:
Axis is building an AI Native Trading System, allowing a trader to deploy models that monitor and analyze relevant markets and strategies. We've chosen commodities as our first market.
Commodities make up a third of global goods exports, and physical commodities traders decide the movement and storage of metals, agricultural products, and energy across the globe. They trade in public markets and bilateral OTC agreements. Engaging in these markets is complexing, covering derivatives positioning, refinery data, storage inventory, import/exports, geopolitical events and more. Axis is building an AI driven analytical layer for these markets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Physical commodities trading desks (metals, agriculture, energy) that trade in public markets and bilateral OTC deals
problem: Commodity traders must track derivatives positioning, refinery data, storage, trade flows and geopolitics across many sources. Axis builds an AI native layer where a trader deploys models that monitor and analyze markets and strategies.
business_model: B2B software for trading desks, pricing not public
product_category: AI research and trading platform for commodities
market_need_then: Physical commodities are a third of global goods exports per the company, and the YC page describes trading desks needing faster analysis across fragmented data. No dated spend figures found.
outcome_analysis: Axis is an Active Winter 2026 YC company of two ex quant trading founders targeting commodities desks. No verified funding, customers or press were found, so the outcome is open. Risks are a generic name, a small team and established analytics vendors such as Sparta.

name: Axonnic
one_liner: Creating human skill at robot scale
long_description: Axonnic is building the missing data layer for dexterous robotics. Our wearable EMG technology captures human intent, effort and force directly from muscle activity as people demonstrate physical tasks. By revealing the physical signals that video cannot capture, Axonnic gives AI models the data they need to learn more precise and dexterous behaviour. Beyond robotics, this creates a foundation for new forms of human–computer interaction in which technology can understand and respond directly to human movement and intent.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Robotics companies and manufacturers that need dexterous, force aware human demonstration data to train robot policies
problem: Video demonstrations miss the force and effort of human hands, limiting dexterous robot learning. Axonnic records skilled workers with a forearm EMG sleeve plus video and hand tracking to capture those signals.
business_model: Data and training service for robot policies, pricing not public
product_category: Robotics training data via wearable EMG
market_need_then: Robotics labs are seeking dexterous manipulation data; the company reports a letter of intent from a European manufacturer for force sensitive sewing and a construction pilot. No paying customers are named.
outcome_analysis: Axonnic is an Active Fall 2026 YC company with Oxford founders and four named backers but no disclosed amounts. It has a letter of intent and a construction pilot, no paying customers named, and direct EMG rivals launching at the same time. Outcome is open.

name: Balance
one_liner: Full-Stack AI Accounting
long_description: Balance is an AI accounting firm that helps SMBs close their monthly books. Our agents do the work of an in-house finance hire, reconciling books in real time and flagging issues before they become problems.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: SMBs and startups in the UK and Denmark that need monthly bookkeeping, VAT, accounts and tax handled
problem: Small businesses need accurate monthly books but cannot afford an in house finance hire. Balance runs bookkeeping with AI agents while its accountants review and sign off every entry.
business_model: Subscription accounting firm, plans from 500 GBP per month per the site
product_category: AI native accounting firm
founder_names: Mathias Løvring; Gus Levinson; Emil Munk
market_need_then: SMBs struggle to hire finance staff and want real time books. The company reports 60 plus customers growing 40 percent monthly in a YC job post, and the site later says 150 plus companies.
outcome_analysis: Balance is an Active Winter 2026 YC company that reports a GV led seed and fast customer growth in the UK and Denmark. It is early, so the outcome is open. Its human reviewed model differs from software only rivals but faces Xero, Digits and Pilot, and a generic name.

name: BaseFrame
one_liner: Detect what AI can automate for your team
long_description:
Most teams want to plug in AI but don't know where to get started. BaseFrame's desktop app finds exactly what to automate for each employee using the historic data on their computer. 

Instead of relying on screen recording or generic AI demos, we use the existing history of how work gets done across email, docs, Slack, calendar, browser, and files to identify the highest-value automations. We use local models so that your sensitive data doesn’t have to leave your system. 

Once you find a set of automations, send them off to your automation tool of choice and share them with your team so that everyone can get productivity boosts.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams and knowledge workers who want to find what AI can automate in their own work
problem: Teams want to adopt AI but do not know where to start. A desktop app uses local models over email, docs, Slack, calendar, browser and file history to find the highest value automations per employee.
business_model: Desktop software for teams, pricing not public
product_category: AI automation discovery
market_need_then: Companies are pressed to adopt AI but lack guidance on where; the task mining market is described as about 2 billion USD in 2025 by a vendor roundup. No dated customer evidence for this product.
outcome_analysis: BaseFrame is an Active Winter 2026 YC company with two founders. Sources disagree on its product, showing automation discovery and a hardware design copilot, and it appears to have moved to a new product, Clam, in February 2026. Funding beyond the YC deal was not found, so the outcome is open.

name: Baud
one_liner: AI chips for ultra-fast training and inference
long_description: Novel AI hardware built from first principles to let companies train, fine-tune, and deploy frontier models with orders of magnitude better performance than incumbents
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies and labs that train, fine tune and serve frontier AI models and want lower compute cost
problem: Training and running frontier models is very expensive. Baud proposes an arithmetic format without multiplications, an ASIC architecture for it and a compiler from PyTorch models.
business_model: AI compute cluster access and chips, early design partner program
product_category: AI accelerator chips
market_need_then: AI chip startups raised about 15B USD in the first nine months of 2026 per a market blog, showing intense demand, though that source is unverified.
outcome_analysis: Baud is an Active Summer 2026 YC company with an experienced ASIC architect and a serial ML founder. It has an emulated demo and a design partner program but no disclosed funding. Chip startups need large capital and face NVIDIA, Etched and Cerebras, so the outcome is open.

name: BayMachines
one_liner: Air-gapped compute for defense contractors
long_description: BayMachines deploys on-prem, air-gapped GPU containers for defense teams to run and fine-tune AI locally. We support defense technology companies serving the DoW and special operations, with deployments built to support CMMC and NIST 800-171 requirements.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Defense technology companies and contractors serving the Department of War and special operations that must run AI on premises
problem: Defense teams cannot send sensitive data to cloud AI and need compliant local compute. BayMachines sizes, configures and installs air gapped GPU systems built to support CMMC and NIST 800-171.
business_model: Hardware and managed deployment sales (AI Box, GPU Server, Private Cluster)
product_category: On premise air gapped AI compute for defense
market_need_then: Defense teams need local AI under CMMC and ITAR rules, and cloud use is restricted for sensitive data. The site lists five logos it does not label as customers.
outcome_analysis: BayMachines is an Active Spring 2026 YC company with seven staff selling air gapped GPU systems to defense teams. Founders were not found on its YC page or site, no verified funding exists, and several turnkey rivals sell the same thing, so the outcome is open.

name: Bayworks
one_liner: Intelligence that keeps America’s vehicles running
long_description:
Bayworks captures how expert technicians fix cars and uses that knowledge to guide every technician through diagnosis and repair in real time, and to automate the admin work that follows.

This knowledge grows with every repair captured, across every car model and technician. Next, it will guide robots through the same repairs.

In four months, we have gone from zero to nearly seven figures in cARR, across 6 dealership groups including a top-50 US dealer ($3Bn annual revenue), and have powered over 50,000 repairs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US car dealership groups, specifically fixed operations and service departments that employ repair technicians
problem: Dealerships lack enough skilled technicians, repairs are not standardized, and technicians spend time on admin such as warranty write-ups. Expert repair knowledge stays in technicians' heads.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to dealership groups, likely contract based (company reports contracted ARR); pricing not public
product_category: AI repair guidance and service workflow automation for automotive dealers
market_need_then: The company says over a million cars a day need repair in the US and there are not enough technicians. Its site claims 80+ dealerships and the YC page claims nearly seven figures in cARR across 6 dealer groups (company claims, unverified).
outcome_analysis: Bayworks is a Fall 2026 company only months old, so there is no outcome yet. It reports fast early traction with dealer groups, a technical founding team from Indian fintech and voice AI, and a clear shortage of technicians as the pain, but also faces dealer software incumbents launching technician AI in 2026.

name: Beacon Health
one_liner: AI Employees for Primary Care
long_description:
Beacon Health (YC W26) is building AI employees that double revenue for primary care practices while also reducing the total cost of care.

Primary care is the primary source of care for over 200M Americans, but physicians don’t have the bandwidth to manage their patient panels. 

Beacon Health builds AI employees that automate tedious background workflows - preventative screenings, prior authorizations, referrals, and risk adjustment. We handle these workflows from start to finish, directly in their EHR.

We’re on a mission is to bring joy back to primary care.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent physician associations, ACOs and primary care practices with risk-based or value-based contracts
problem: Primary care physicians lack bandwidth for background workflows such as screenings, prior authorizations, referrals and risk adjustment coding, which costs practices revenue and quality scores.
business_model: B2B software that sells AI agents operating inside the practice EHR; pricing not public
product_category: AI agents for primary care administrative workflows
market_need_then: Physicians lack bandwidth for panel management; CMS rules effective 2026 push faster prior authorization decisions, and value-based contracts reward quality gap closure and risk adjustment coding. A first customer, an IPA with about 40,000 patients, went live per the YC page.
outcome_analysis: Beacon Health is a Winter 2026 company with no outcome yet. It has a founder with firsthand primary care exposure and a technical co-founder, an early live deployment at an IPA, and a policy tailwind, but it competes with far better funded workflow automation platforms.

name: Bear
one_liner: AI-native accounting firm.
long_description: Bear (formerly Last Accounting Company) is a full-stack AI accounting firm. We sell the same service (bookkeeping, tax filings, etc.) as a traditional accounting firm, but underneath agents handle everything and a certified accountant signs off. Our service is faster, cheaper, and fully integrated, allowing our clients to focus on what matters, not accounting admin.
regions: Finland; Europe
target_customer: Startups and small and mid-size businesses in Finland, Europe and the US that need bookkeeping, payroll and tax filings
problem: Traditional accounting firms are slow and costly for routine bookkeeping and filings; founders want books kept current and queryable without admin work.
business_model: Accounting services firm with AI agents doing the work and certified accountants signing off; fixed monthly fee
product_category: AI-native accounting services (full-stack accounting firm)
market_need_then: AI-native accounting drew large funding in 2026 (Basis, Accrual), showing demand for automating bookkeeping. The company's Finnish site claims more than 20 client companies (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Bear is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. It renamed from the longer Last Accounting Company, has technical Finnish founders with financial data infrastructure experience, and sells a service rather than software, but faces heavily funded AI accounting competitors.

name: BeeSafe AI
one_liner: Frontier AI Defenses for Social Engineering Attacks
long_description:
BeeSafe AI is building the frontier model layer for social engineering defense. Cyberattacks have moved from code to conversation: attackers now use AI to carry out long-term, trust-based manipulation across SMS, voice, email, and social platforms, often inside encrypted channels where defenders cannot see, detect, or stop them.

BeeSafe changes that by deploying undercover AI agents that engage attackers directly, expose hidden infrastructure, and convert live adversarial conversations into actionable intelligence. Each engagement adds to BeeSafe's proprietary dataset of real attacker behavior and trains foundational models that continually learn about counter-persuasion, deception, and manipulation in the wild.

BeeSafe is starting in financial crime, where banks already value our data against Authorized Push Payment (APP) fraud and money laundering, but the opportunity is far broader. The same data and models that uncover mule networks today can protect consumers, secure enterprises, and strengthen governments against the next generation of AI-powered social engineering attacks tomorrow.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Financial services and crypto firms, telecoms and government agencies fighting authorized push payment fraud, money mules and scam infrastructure
problem: Trust-based scams and mule accounts move money faster than defenders can map them; manual undercover work does not scale.
business_model: B2B fraud intelligence platform (early access); pricing not public
product_category: Anti-scam AI agents and fraud intelligence
founder_names: Daniel Spokoyny; Ariana Mirian; Nikolai Vogler
market_need_then: Authorized push payment fraud and scam losses are a growing concern for banks, telecoms and governments; the company claims thousands of real scammer conversations and mule accounts mapped and use by financial services and government (company claims).
outcome_analysis: BeeSafe AI is a Winter 2026 company with no outcome yet. The founders are three security and AI PhDs who published research on engaging scammers, which gives strong founder market fit, while competitors such as Apate and Netcraft pursue similar scam baiting, so differentiation and sales into banks will decide results.

name: Belvedir
one_liner: Autonomous AI Model Training
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies running AI agents and LLM apps in production that want cheaper private models trained on their own traces and logs
problem: Teams pay high inference costs for general models; building custom models needs data cleaning, RL environments, training and deployment work most teams lack.
business_model: Usage-based: charges per token by hosting multiple LoRA adapters on shared clusters
product_category: Autonomous custom model training and deployment platform (SDK plus API)
competitors_at_founding: OpenPipe; Applied Compute; Thinking Machines Tinker
market_need_then: Inference cost and model quality pressure on agent builders; the founder reports 10 live companies and 10x lower cost claims (company claims, unverified).
outcome_analysis: Belvedir is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. A solo founder with prior YC experience at Traverse and RL environment work reports ten live customers, but the trace to custom model loop is crowded with funded competitors and platform vendors.

name: Bernard
one_liner: AI employees that run home appliance repair companies
long_description:
Bernard builds AI employees for home and commercial appliance servicers. They work across phone, text, email, warranty feeds, and existing systems to manage customer communication, scheduling, and dispatch, carrying each job through diagnosis, parts preparation, technician handoff, and follow-up. At the center is Pre-ID, which combines the exact appliance and its symptoms with repair history, similar completed visits, manufacturer guidance, and parts data to produce a diagnosis, ranked parts, and follow-up questions. Technicians arrive prepared with the right parts, helping servicers complete more repairs on the first visit.

We’re building the world’s most efficient appliance servicers, creating happier customers and a more connected appliance ecosystem.

Learn more at https://bernardhq.com/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Home and commercial appliance repair servicers, including large authorized service companies
problem: Appliance servicers lose revenue on missed calls, slow scheduling and technician visits made without the right parts diagnosed in advance.
business_model: B2B software (AI employees) for service companies, integrated with existing field service management systems; pricing not public
product_category: AI phone, scheduling, dispatch and parts pre-identification for appliance repair
market_need_then: Appliance servicers face technician shortages, missed calls and low first-time fix rates; the company says it is live with some of the largest authorized service companies (company claim, no numbers).
outcome_analysis: Bernard is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. It targets a narrow vertical with a founding team combining operations and fraud engineering experience and a team of nine, but generic AI dispatch and voice products compete for the same buyers.

name: Beyond Reach Labs
one_liner: Space solar arrays that grow to the size of a football field in orbit
long_description:
At Beyond Reach Labs we are building solar panels for Space that grow from the size of a dining table to a football field in orbit.

Mitch and Pele met 13 years ago as freshmen at UPenn studying mechanical engineering. Mitch recently got his PhD at Carnegie Mellon working with NASA on kilometer-scale deployable structures, and Pele spent seven years at SpaceX leading Dragon parachute engineering, safely returning astronauts from space.

The collective satellites today use around 20MW, roughly the output of a datacenter on earth, but by 2030 there is a demand for over 10GW, a 500x increase, largely driven by orbital datacenters, space stations, and lunar outposts.

If you want more power, your only option is to launch larger solar panels, which quickly become fragile or impractically expensive. As a result, power constraints already determine whether missions or industries can exist at all.

But at Beyond Reach Labs we have introduced a new class of deployable solar panels giving satellites 10x more usable power without increasing launch mass or volume. This works because our patented deployable design changes geometry in space, allowing for us to reach 10x longer while remaining rigid.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Satellite manufacturers and operators, space station and orbital infrastructure builders that need large amounts of solar power per launch mass and volume
problem: Satellite power is limited by how large a solar array can fit in a launch vehicle and by structural vibration of long arrays; larger platforms such as orbital infrastructure need far more power.
business_model: Hardware sales of deployable solar arrays (Flarewing S, M and L) and thermal radiators, quoted per project
product_category: Deployable space solar arrays and radiators
market_need_then: Orbital infrastructure and data center concepts need far more power per launch; the company reports letters of intent from space companies totaling over $175M (company claim) and unveiled the Flarewing line in August 2026.
outcome_analysis: Beyond Reach Labs raised a $10M seed in July 2026 after YC Winter 2026, opened a Brooklyn facility in September 2026 and unveiled Flarewing in August. Founders with NASA, SpaceX and deployable structure research backgrounds and a patented design support the technical moat, but flight proof is still ahead (demo targeted for Q2 2027).

name: Bidflow
one_liner: Revolutionizing the Construction Industry
long_description: More coming soon...
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Electrical contractors that estimate and bid jobs (per YC launch listing as summarized by search results)
problem: Electrical estimating is slow and document heavy, which limits how many jobs contractors can bid.
business_model: Likely B2B software for contractors; model and pricing not stated in any source opened
product_category: AI copilot for electrical estimating and bidding
market_need_then: Electrical contractors do manual takeoff and quoting; incumbents' AI releases show demand. No traction figures for Bidflow are public.
outcome_analysis: Bidflow is a Winter 2026 company whose public footprint is thin: the YC page says more is coming and the website says the company is rebuilding. There is no sourced traction, so no outcome can be judged, and the generic name and crowded AI estimating field are noted risks.

name: Billow AI Labs
one_liner: AI-native Accounting Firm that's killing Deloitte
long_description:
Billow handles the work of Accounting and FP&A FTEs keeping teams compliant and audit-ready. We work within existing stacks (NetSuite, Coupa, and 80+ other systems) and complex spreadsheets, chasing down information and coordinating approvals across stakeholders. 

Built by repeat founders; Joan built and exited an accounting/ERP platform (45,000 businesses in 4 years) and Phil built Bloomberg's financial “brain” data infrastructure, and as CTO of a trading platform ($1B in volume). Advisors include CFOs, controllers, auditors from publicly-traded biopharma, and a Big-4 Accounting firm.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Finance and accounting teams at venture-backed and mid-market companies (including biotech) that use NetSuite, Dynamics 365 or QuickBooks
problem: Month-end close, reconciliations, accruals and FP&A reporting consume many accounting FTEs and outside-firm hours. Billow runs this recurring work inside existing systems with human CPA oversight.
business_model: AI accounting services and software sold to finance teams, with CPA oversight, free trial offered
product_category: AI accounting and FP&A automation
market_need_then: Finance teams spend heavy FTE time on manual close work and outside accounting firms; investor money was flowing into AI accounting in 2025 and 2026. The company says it reached partnerships with Series B to D companies within three months (launch post, company claim).
outcome_analysis: Billow is a Summer 2026 company that is active and too young for an outcome. Its strengths are repeat founders with accounting and finance data backgrounds and a strong tailwind in AI accounting. Its main risk is a crowded field of heavily funded competitors, and no round has been confirmed.

name: BioDelivera
tags: Gene Therapy; Drug Delivery; Therapeutics; AI; Biotechnology
one_liner: Programmable drug delivery precisely targets only diseased cells
long_description: BioDelivera has developed proprietary GCV™, a drug delivery platform designed to travel through the body and selectively target diseased cells while sparing healthy ones. GCVs can carry genetic medicines, DNA, RNA, small molecules, or combinations of these at the same time. BioDelivera has demonstrated efficacy in tumors, muscle, and brain and is expanding to additional tissues. The company’s mission is to enable cures for every patient, across every disease.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Biopharma and genetic medicine developers needing tissue-specific delivery of DNA, RNA or small molecule payloads
problem: Delivering genetic medicines to only diseased cells while sparing healthy tissue is a major bottleneck. BioDelivera builds Guided Chimeric Vehicles (GCV) intended to solve it.
business_model: Drug delivery platform, likely partnering or licensing with therapeutics developers (not stated)
product_category: Drug delivery and gene therapy platform
market_need_then: Targeted delivery is widely described as the main bottleneck for genetic medicines, and investors in 2026 say they want programmable, redosable delivery scaffolds (venture firm thesis post).
outcome_analysis: BioDelivera is a Fall 2026 company that is active and too new for an outcome. It targets a recognized bottleneck in genetic medicine with a two-person team, and it faces well-capitalized delivery competitors. No funding beyond the YC deal could be confirmed.

name: BioStack Platforms
one_liner: Real world training envs for healthcare AI models
long_description:
BioStack is building the data engine for healthcare and drug discovery AI. The bottleneck is not models. It is access to high-quality biological data. Clinical and experimental data is fragmented, unstructured, and locked inside hospitals, labs, and CROs, while generating new data is slow and expensive. BioStack fixes this with proprietary clinical and preclinical data pipelines that turn real biomedical workflows into ML-ready training environments.

We structure longitudinal multimodal data across imaging, EHR, and experimental assays, then package it for post-training and reinforcement learning so models can learn how research and care actually happen. Instead of static datasets, BioStack gives AI labs workflow-aligned data and environments that improve reasoning, decision-making, and real-world performance in biology and medicine.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI labs, biotech startups and human-data companies that need healthcare and preclinical datasets and RL environments
problem: Healthcare and drug discovery AI is limited by access to high-quality clinical and experimental data locked in hospitals, labs and CROs. BioStack sources, structures and annotates it and builds simulation environments.
business_model: Data and RL environment sales to AI labs and biotech (project and dataset based)
product_category: Healthcare AI training data and RL environments
competitors_at_founding: Archangel Health; Appen and other data vendors
market_need_then: AI labs were buying domain-specific data and RL environments in 2026; the company reported 17 customers and prospects including top AI labs at launch (YC launch post, company claim).
outcome_analysis: BioStack raised a reported $9.5M seed about months after its Spring 2026 YC batch, with Peak XV leading according to YourStory. It is active and early. Its team has biomedical research and AI lab credibility, and demand from AI labs is the tailwind; competition from data vendors is the main risk.

name: Bizmark
one_liner: OpenClaw for manufacturers
long_description:
Hey YC! We're Bizmark. I (Rodrigo) grew up in a factory, watching my mum run everything through Excel and email.

That’s why we’ve built Otto, the OpenClaw for manufacturers.

In a few days, he learns from your systems and spreadsheets to take over repetitive work in procurement, quoting, and production planning. 

Otto is live at multiple factories, bringing in $108k in annual recurring revenue. Last month, he worked the equivalent of 9 full-time employees.

I did CS at UChicago and built a distribution business from 0 to $60M.

My cousin and cofounder Oscar did CS at Stanford and deployed AI for the US Air Force, Amazon, and the factories of Johnson & Johnson and Intel.

There's a quarter of a million manufacturers in the US, making this a $25B market.

In 5 years, they will all run on Otto-pilot.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Manufacturers, distributors and retailers that make, move or sell physical goods
problem: Operating decisions such as procurement, production planning, labor scheduling and revenue operations are made across disconnected data. Bizmark unifies the data, applies forecasting and optimization, and runs agents to execute decisions.
business_model: Enterprise software and deployment for operating decisions (pricing not stated)
product_category: AI operating system for physical industries
competitors_at_founding: Keychain (KeychainOS); Lyzr; Siemens Industrial AI Operating System
market_need_then: Manufacturers rely on legacy ERP and spreadsheets for planning; 2026 coverage shows a wave of funded AI ERP and operations startups, indicating demand and investor interest.
outcome_analysis: Bizmark is a Summer 2026 company, active and too new for an outcome. It targets a large physical-industry market with a technical founding pair and an unusual cousin team, but faces funded AI ERP rivals and incumbents. No funding beyond YC is confirmed.

name: Blinka
one_liner: Banking for US companies operating globally
long_description:
Blinka is banking for US companies operating globally.

Our customers incorporate in the US but run their operations, teams, and vendors from other countries. They use Blinka as their primary operating account.

With Blinka, companies can:

- Open a USD business account without being in the US.
- Send money abroad without the usual 4–5% FX fees.
- Earn yield on treasuries.
- Issue global corporate cards with 1.5% cash back and 0 international fees.
- Manage their financial operations with our AI tools.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US-incorporated companies operated from abroad, especially Latin American startups
problem: Foreign-run companies struggle to get US dollar accounts, payments, cards and treasury. Blinka provides USD accounts, cross-border transfers, cards and yield on idle cash through partner banks.
business_model: Fintech banking platform (not a bank) earning on payments, cards and treasury products
product_category: Cross-border business banking
market_need_then: Colombian press reports more than 150 businesses in accounts opened or applications and over US$10M processed in the first two months (outlet claims); foreign-owned LLCs are commonly rejected by US neobanks per comparison guides.
outcome_analysis: Blinka is a Fall 2026 company with early traction claims in Latin American press and no confirmed outside round. It is active and too new for an outcome. Its risks are dependence on partner banks and competition from neobanks that serve foreign founders.

name: Bloomy
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Education; eLearning; Personalization; AI
one_liner: AI-native learning for every school
long_description: Bloomy is the best way to teach anything in school. We provide schools with an AI-native academic system comprising core and supplemental curriculum, AI teaching, and assessment to help K-12 students learn faster. Backed by the founders of Clever.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: K-12 schools, homeschool families and ESA/EFA-funded families
problem: Students move on without mastering skills. Bloomy diagnoses gaps, sets personalized paths and uses a Socratic AI tutor (BloomyBot) with a mastery gate before advancing.
business_model: Monthly or annual subscriptions for families, plus school partnerships
product_category: AI mastery learning for K-12
market_need_then: Strong K-12 interest in AI tutoring and ESA/EFA school choice funding; the founder reports pilot students growing about 2x faster than national average (company claim). The HN launch drew 81 points and 85 comments.
outcome_analysis: Bloomy is a Summer 2026 solo-founder company that is active and too young for an outcome. A former teacher and consultant founded it with early pilots and an HN launch, but it lacks a technical co-founder, public efficacy data and a clear moat in a crowded AI tutoring market.

name: Boat
one_liner: The best cloud VMs for billions of agents
long_description:
**Problem**

Humans used to need laptops to do their work. Now they prompt agents instead, and those agents need computers too: always-on, in large quantities, and with unlimited capabilities. 

Building and maintaining that yourself is far from trivial.

**Solution**

Boat provides powerful, simple, permissive Ubuntu VMs in the cloud. In a sandbox, an agent can work for long periods on code or on knowledge work like legal, research, reporting, and auditing.

**Why Boat and not any other cloud VM?**

1. It is ready out of the box: every sandbox ships with a desktop, chrome, languages, docker, snapshots, and templates, plus a CLI, SDK, API, and control pane for your fleet.
2. It is permissive and paradigm agnostic: any number of agents can use any number of sandboxes. Agents can run inside or use sandboxes as an external tool.
3. It is expertly crafted: we manage everything from the individual CPU to the orchestration software, which makes sandboxes stable, persistent, scalable, and secure.
4. It is the best performance and price in town: our CPUs rank first on HPC benchmarks, and sandboxes are typically 9x to 18x cheaper than other leading sandboxes.

**Further notes**

Sandboxes are hosted in Europe, which keeps prices low, and more regions are coming. Unless compliance requires it, agents don't notice the region they run in.
regions: France; Europe; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Developers and companies running AI agents that need persistent Linux sandboxes
problem: AI agents need full, persistent machines with SSH, Docker and desktop access rather than ephemeral containers. boat sells Ubuntu VM sandboxes with snapshot forking.
business_model: Usage-based cloud VMs, pricing from $20 per month after a 7-day trial per a directory listing
product_category: Cloud sandboxes for AI agents
competitors_at_founding: E2B; Daytona; Fly.io Sprites; Sail Research Sailboxes
market_need_then: Agent builders adopted sandboxes widely in 2025 and 2026; a testimonial from Theo Browne (t3.gg) says boat unblocked his agents, and the site lists customers such as Tella, Morph and Squad (unverified).
outcome_analysis: boat is a Fall 2026 Paris company that is active and too young for an outcome. It sells VM sandboxes into a fast-growing agent market but competes with well-funded rivals, and no round beyond YC has been confirmed.

name: Booko
one_liner: Dynamically pricing the whole economy.
long_description: Booko helps businesses that sell bookable time slots make more money by dynamically pricing their time. Unlike physical inventory, unsold time slots disappear forever, yet most time-slot-based businesses still rely on static pricing. We integrate with existing booking systems to adjust prices and incentives based on historical utilization, availability, and demand. Early customers see ~20% revenue uplift by selling time that would have otherwise gone unsold.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Owners of businesses that sell bookable time slots such as fitness studios, golf simulators, med spas, museums and tours
problem: Unsold appointment slots are perishable revenue. Booko forecasts demand per slot and sets prices between owner-chosen floor and ceiling, working inside existing booking systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS pricing engine, likely revenue-based or subscription (pricing not published)
product_category: Dynamic pricing for service businesses
market_need_then: Fitness and service operators face empty off-peak slots, and incumbents publish guides on dynamic pricing; Booko reports about 20 percent revenue lift for early customers (company claim) and 98 locations across 22 countries as of November 2026.
outcome_analysis: Booko is a Winter 2026 company that is active and too new for an outcome. Founders with pricing experience from Joby launched in early 2026 and report broad deployment, but incumbents already sell dynamic pricing in booking software and no funding beyond YC is confirmed.

name: Boxes.dev
one_liner: A better place to run your coding agents.
long_description: Close your laptop again. Run Claude Code and Codex on unlimited parallel cloud computers from your laptop, phone, and terminal. Bring your own subscription, start agents from Slack and Linear, and manage an agent swarm by letting your agents coordinate their work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineers and teams who already pay for Claude Code or Codex and want to run many agents in parallel
problem: Coding agents tie up a laptop and one local environment. Running many in parallel needs isolated machines with the full dev environment, which is slow to set up by hand.
business_model: Per seat SaaS tiers ($19 to $249 per user per month) with included box-hours and usage overage at $0.40 per box-hour; users bring their own agent subscription
product_category: Cloud development environments for AI coding agents
market_need_then: Launch coverage (Show HN, Product Hunt in June 2026) frames running agents locally as the pain. Demand evidence beyond launch upvotes was not found.
outcome_analysis: Very early company in the Fall 2026 batch, so no outcome exists yet. Strengths are a repeat founder pair with an earlier YC company and a tailwind from heavy use of coding agents. The risk is that model labs and code platforms ship their own cloud agent environments, which would commoditize the wedge.

name: Brumby
tags: Reinforcement Learning; Drones; Computer Vision; Agriculture
one_liner: Robot Cowboys that Herd Cattle with AI Drones
long_description:
Brumby builds autonomous drones that herd cattle.

On command, our drones fly to a paddock, position themselves around the mob, and move them where they need to go. What used to take a full day of helicopters, motorbikes, and horses now runs on a schedule.

We work with some of the largest cattle ranches in the world. While the drones are herding, they're also estimating animal weights, measuring grass biomass, monitoring water levels, and flagging sick animals. We're building physical AI that lets a grazier manage thousands of head across millions of acres from their phone.
regions: Australia; Oceania; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Large cattle ranches and graziers in Australia, expanding to US ranchers
problem: Mustering cattle takes helicopters, motorbikes, horses and a full crew for a day. The company claims drones can do it on a schedule at roughly half the cost.
business_model: Pilot rollout with waitlist and free on-site demo; pricing not published
product_category: Autonomous drones and AI for livestock mustering and pasture monitoring
market_need_then: Large Australian stations spend heavily on helicopters and labor for mustering, and labor is scarce. Pilot farms covering about 700,000 hectares were reported lined up in Queensland and NSW in early 2026.
outcome_analysis: Active and early. The founder grew up on a cattle station, which gives unusual domain insight and access to pilot ranches. A 19 year old founder raising a YC led pre-seed with pilots across Queensland and NSW is a strong start, but revenue is not public and pricing is unpublished. Hardware, regulation of drone flight and US expansion are the main risks.

name: Bubble Lab
one_liner: The intelligence layer for communities and events.
long_description: Bubble Lab is the all-in-one platform for running professional communities and events. From member data and operations to automations and billing, everything in one place. Try it now or book a demo!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Operators of professional communities, member clubs and event series
problem: Community operators stitch together separate tools for event applications, payments, email, member data and automations, and have little insight into who attends.
business_model: SaaS tiers from $99 to $1,499 per month plus 1% of payments processed, with an MCP access add-on
product_category: Community and event operations platform with AI enrichment and matchmaking
market_need_then: Organizers of paid communities and clubs pay for several tools. The site cites named customers such as Our Third Place and Founders on Tap, but the demand evidence is company supplied.
outcome_analysis: Early stage with no public outcome. The product has paying plan tiers and named community customers on its site, but funding, revenue and retention are unknown. The main risk is that event and community platforms add AI enrichment and matchmaking themselves.

name: Burt
one_liner: AI teammates for logistics
long_description:
We're building for the people that keep the world moving. 

Freight brokers and forwarders operate on razor-thin margins in a relationship-driven business — yet most of their teams spend the majority of their day on manual, repetitive work.

We help freight brokers and forwarders build AI teammates that handle their repetitive, manual tasks so teams have time to focus on customers, carriers, and growing the business.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Freight brokers and freight forwarders
problem: Brokerage teams spend most of the day on manual work such as quoting, load building, carrier sourcing, appointment scheduling, tracking and paperwork, on thin margins.
business_model: B2B AI agents sold per deployment; pricing not published
product_category: AI teammates for freight brokerage operations
market_need_then: Freight brokerage is relationship driven with thin margins and heavy manual email and phone work, and funded startups were raising for the same problem in 2024 and 2025.
outcome_analysis: Early and active with no public outcome. The CEO grew up in a logistics family and both founders built agent and data systems at a YC company. The market is crowded with funded competitors such as Vooma and Augment, so execution and integration depth will decide the result. Funding is not public.

name: Button Computer
one_liner: The tiny computer built for voice AI.
long_description: We’re launching a small hardware device: a button that you clip to your shirt. You press it to talk to AI, and it responds instantly.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Consumers who want a screenless, privacy focused voice AI device
problem: Phones and earlier AI wearables are slow, always listening or awkward for quick voice questions. Button aims for a press to talk device that answers in about half a second.
business_model: Hardware sale ($179 listed, $229 regular) plus optional Button AI Pro subscription at $7.99 per month, or bring your own API key
product_category: Consumer AI hardware wearable
competitors_at_founding: AI pendants and pins (Friend, Plaud, Limitless, Bee)
market_need_then: Early AI wearables such as Humane's pin failed, but pendants returned at CES 2026. Button's preorders and launch press exist, but sales volume is unknown.
outcome_analysis: Preorder stage with first US shipments listed for 15 December 2026, so there is no outcome yet. Strengths are founders who worked on Vision Pro hardware and a simple privacy story. The main risks are hardware execution, the poor record of earlier AI wearables, and big platforms entering the category.

name: ByteAsk
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: The AI coding agent for C and C++
long_description: ByteAsk is an AI coding agent built for C and C++, the code that runs trading systems, cars, chips, and operating systems. It does not stop at a diff that looks right. ByteAsk builds, debugs, and tests every change with the real toolchain until the change holds. If the compiler, the debugger, or the tests can catch it, then ByteAsk catches it too. It runs from the terminal or inside VS Code, Neovim, and Emacs, and is available fully on-prem.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: C and C++ engineering teams in trading, embedded, automotive, silicon and systems software
problem: General coding agents work from source text and ignore build configuration, so changes often fail to compile or hide memory and threading bugs. C++ teams need agents that build, test and run sanitizers before review.
business_model: Free plan plus enterprise plan with on-prem and air-gapped deployment; bring your own model keys; prices not published
product_category: AI coding agent for C and C++
market_need_then: C++ remains central in trading, embedded and systems code, and teams there are strict on correctness and data privacy. Founders came from trading firms and spoke at CppCon per the YC page.
outcome_analysis: Active and very early. The founders already built and sold LawSutra AI to Manupatra, came from trading and infrastructure engineering, and raised a YC and Entrepreneur First led pre-seed in September 2026. The main risk is that Copilot, Claude Code and Codex add build-aware C++ workflows, narrowing the niche.

name: Byteport
one_liner: Global upload acceleration for 1GB-100TB files.
long_description: Founded in 2025, Byteport is a technology company that builds mission-critical network infrastructure for robotics, satellite, AI, and enterprise applications all over the world. Businesses of every size—from new startups to public companies—use our software to accelerate file transfer online.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprises moving large data over hard networks: satellite and ground stations, drone fleets, robotics, AI clusters, media and defense
problem: TCP based transfers are slow and fragile over long, lossy or non-IP links. Byteport sells a UDP based protocol it says is far faster and lossless.
business_model: Software subscription: Growth plan $500 per month ($425 annual) and custom enterprise pricing, plus custom network builds
product_category: High speed data transfer protocol and software (DART)
market_need_then: Satellite, robotics and AI cluster operators move large volumes over poor links, and alternatives to Aspera are widely discussed. Direct demand evidence for Byteport, such as named customers, was not found.
outcome_analysis: Early and active with no public outcome. The CEO's CERN experience moving collider data fits the problem, and the product is priced from $500 per month. Funding and customers are unconfirmed and the performance claims are inconsistent, so traction is the key unknown.

name: COACH
tags: SaaS; B2B; Sales; Sales Enablement; AI
one_liner: The AI Coach for in person sales reps.
long_description:
85% of all sales still happen face-to-face. Coach is how those get closed.
Our AI turns in-depth sales conversation analysis into company knowledge and personalized coaching to help reps close more deals.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies with in-person field sales teams in retail, home improvement, door-to-door, alarm systems and roofing
problem: Field reps are not recorded like phone reps, so managers cannot coach most conversations. COACH records meetings from the phone and gives each rep feedback after every conversation.
business_model: B2B SaaS for sales teams, sold by demo; pricing not published
product_category: AI sales coaching for in-person sales
founder_names: Mathieu Perez; Thomas Perez; Nicolas Sebag
market_need_then: Field teams lacked recorded conversations to coach from. A 2026 survey cited in a guide found one in three field sales teams had adopted no AI tool, though an AI coach trial cited by Whatfix showed no gain over no coaching.
outcome_analysis: Active and early with no public outcome. The founders previously built a field sales company, which gives domain access, and company-provided profiles claim about $500K ARR and French enterprise customers. These figures are not independently confirmed, and Rilla and Quantified already compete in in-person coaching.

name: CONUS
one_liner: Medical Device Platform for Hospitals
long_description:
CONUS structures fragmented medical device information for surgeons. We combine manufacturer documentation, hospital protocols and medical research in one place, giving surgeons and MedTech teams reliable answers across products and procedures through search and source-backed AI.

We already work with leading manufacturers including Johnson & Johnson, Stryker and Zimmer Biomet, and since launching six months ago we’ve gone live in 27 hospitals, with 49 more onboarding.

Long term, hospitals will use CONUS to source and order surgical devices across manufacturers.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Surgeons, hospitals and medical device manufacturers (MedTech sales, field service and quality teams) in orthopaedics and trauma surgery
problem: Surgeons cannot easily find reliable answers about implants and procedures because manufacturer documentation, hospital protocols and medical literature are scattered across many sources.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to hospitals and to MedTech manufacturers; longer term a sourcing and ordering layer for surgical devices (stated direction, not yet operating)
product_category: Medical device knowledge platform with source-backed AI search
founder_names: Vincent Paffrath; Maximilian Becker; Alexander Schulz
competitors_at_founding: Johnson & Johnson MedTech Polyphonic; Stryker SmartHospital Platform
market_need_then: Hospitals handle many implant systems whose instructions sit in separate manufacturer documents; the company reports live use in 27 hospitals and 49 more onboarding, self reported on the YC page.
outcome_analysis: CONUS is an active Fall 2026 YC company with early traction reported by the company itself: live in about 27 German and European hospitals and co-founded with five chief physicians in trauma surgery and orthopaedics, which gives clinical access. No funding round, exit or failure has been reported publicly. The main risks are that manufacturers build their own platforms and that general AI tools commoditize search.

name: Cajal
one_liner: Scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery
long_description:
Cajal (YC W26) is massively scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery. We deploy superhuman AI mathematicians to high-impact applied domains, starting with quantum computing and finance.

We do this with Lean - a framework that allows us to formally verify any mathematical statement, grounding AI in truth and validating the tools discovered by our systems.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and research institutes (datasets, evals, RL environments) and compute heavy firms needing provably correct optimized code
problem: AI generated math and code are hard to trust; Cajal uses Lean to formally verify results and optimized routines.
business_model: Sells verified proof datasets, benchmarks and RL environments to AI labs; product Tau offers verified code speedups with demo requests
product_category: Formal verification and AI for mathematics
market_need_then: Frontier labs were buying verifiable data and RL environments, and formal verification startups drew funding in 2025 and 2026, but customer evidence for Cajal itself was not found.
outcome_analysis: Cajal is a two person company from the Winter 2026 batch with no verified funding, customers or exit yet. It operates in a hot area where Harmonic and others raised large rounds, and its early signal is the Tau product and open source Talos, so an outcome view is premature.

name: Caladh
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Drones; Maritime; Defense
one_liner: Anti-drone defense for the maritime domain
long_description: Caladh protects critical maritime infrastructure from drone attacks above and below the waterline.  Our systems detect, track, and defeat unmanned systems so they can't get near the assets they want to disrupt.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Defense and government operators and owners of critical maritime infrastructure such as subsea cables, pipelines, ports and naval assets
problem: Cheap aerial and underwater drones can threaten maritime infrastructure, and existing counter-drone tools mostly address the air domain.
business_model: Hardware systems sold to defense and infrastructure customers, likely government contracts (not stated)
product_category: Maritime counter-drone defense hardware (non-kinetic)
competitors_at_founding: D-Fend Solutions EnforceAir2 Maritime; Babcock, Frankenburg and ACUA Ocean; Robin Radar Systems
market_need_then: Defense buyers sought maritime counter-drone solutions in 2026: the Defense Innovation Unit solicited counter-drone USV solutions in July 2026 and analysts describe drone threats moving to the maritime domain.
outcome_analysis: Caladh is an active Fall 2026 YC company run by a solo founder with a PhD and DARPA experience in underwater drone detection, strong founder market fit for a hard technology problem. No funding, exit or failure is publicly reported. The Irish word for a landing place suits the maritime focus, but the sources do not state the name's origin. Risks are long defense sales cycles and being a single founder company.

name: Callab AI
one_liner: Human-centered AI for contact centers.
long_description:
Callab AI is a human-centered customer engagement platform for enterprise contact centers. It lets teams deploy AI agents that handle inbound and outbound conversations across voice, chat, and messaging, while human agents and supervisors stay in control of every interaction.

The platform has two sides. The AI side lets teams build, deploy, and evaluate voice and text agents using a shared knowledge base, embedded evaluations, post-call analysis, data extraction, batch calling, and call transfer. The human side provides a dialer and a live supervision dashboard, from which a person can watch any AI conversation in real time, step in, and hand it back without the customer repeating a word.

Every agent retains memory across channels, so a customer who called yesterday and writes today is recognized and picked up where they left off. The system learns from each human intervention and improves in the direction the team chooses.

Callab AI runs on its own carrier-grade telephony stack and connects natively to Cisco, Mitel, Avaya, SIP trunks, and on-premises PBX systems. Enterprises can adopt it without migrating to the cloud first. The platform maintains SOC 2 controls and serves customers in financial services, healthcare, hospitality, and retail.

Key features:

- AI voice and text agents: Agents handle inbound and outbound conversations across phone, chat, and messaging from a single configuration.

- Live human supervision: Supervisors watch any AI conversation in real time and take over without the customer repeating a word.

- Persistent memory: Every customer's full context is retained across channels and over time.

- AI builder: Teams design, test, and deploy agents without engineering support.

- Embedded evaluations: Every conversation is scored continuously, so performance is measured rather than assumed.

- Self-improving agents: Agents learn from human interventions and get better with every conversation.

- Post-call analysis and data extraction: Every conversation becomes structured, searchable records.

name: Caution
one_liner: Hosting platform for software you can't afford to have hacked
long_description:
Caution is a hosting platform for software you can't afford to get hacked. It simplifies and extends confidential compute, and lets developers deploy workloads to secure enclaves in minutes and give customers, auditors, and counterparties cryptographic proof that production is running the exact reviewed source code, build, configuration, and runtime - not an opaque binary controlled by a cloud operator or internal admin.

Confidential computing hardware exists, but the tooling is too fragmented and incomplete for most teams to use well. Today, attestation often proves only that a binary has a certain hash; it does not prove what source code produced that binary. Building the missing deployment, reproducibility, and verification layer requires specialized security engineering and often locks teams into one cloud or hardware stack. Caution turns that into a simple git-based workflow that builds reproducible enclave images, provisions infrastructure, and lets anyone independently verify what is running.

We built Caution after years securing high-risk systems through Distrust, where we worked with hedge funds, custodians, blockchain teams, cloud platforms, and critical grid operators on systems responsible for more than $600B in assets. Again and again, the same problem showed up: teams running mission-critical infrastructure could not reliably prove what was executing in production.

As AI, fintech, healthcare, and regulated data collaboration move into the cloud, "trust us" is no longer enough. Caution is a general-purpose platform: if it runs on a server, it can run verifiably on Caution. We're starting where trust failures cost the most, but we believe verifiable compute will become the default way software runs, the same way HTTPS became the default way it's served. Infrastructure you can verify, not trust.

name: Chamber
one_liner: The AIOps Agent for ML Teams
long_description: Chamber puts your AI infrastructure on autopilot, and saves your machine learning engineers hours of manual effort. Our agents continually monitor, detects failures, provide root-cause analysis, resolve issues, and optimize AI workloads and scale across clouds. It operates like an autonomous infrastructure team, helping save your research and engineers hours each day, and debugging workload performance issues. Your ML teams move faster, infra waste drops, and GPU bottlenecks disappear.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: ML and AI infrastructure teams running GPU clusters
problem: ML engineers lose hours to failed training jobs, idle GPUs and unhealthy nodes. Chamber agents monitor GPU workloads, diagnose failures, fix them and reclaim idle capacity.
business_model: B2B SaaS for GPU infrastructure operations, installed in the customer environment (Helm install shown on site)
product_category: AIOps agents for ML and GPU infrastructure
