name: ChampionEffect Inc.
one_liner: An AI coach for every employee!
long_description:
ChampionEffect is an AI Coach that teaches AI to every employee at a company, in Slack and Teams.

The Coach helps with a new AI concept, a new workflow, or any tool. It jumps on a call and walks you through the work, just like a coworker would. It points to the top use cases in your industry and tailors everything to your company’s needs and tools. Every time someone does a walkthrough with the Coach, it learns how real work gets done at the company and uses that knowledge with other coworkers.

Before this, we ran a YC company (Cambly) that taught English to millions of professionals and generated $100M+ in revenue. Now we’re using what we learned to teach millions about AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies that want every employee, in roles from sales to engineering, to adopt AI tools and workflows
problem: Employees do not know how to apply new AI tools to their daily work. An AI coach in Slack and Teams walks each person through workflows, learns how real work gets done and shares that across coworkers.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to companies (call-booking sales motion); pricing not stated
product_category: AI adoption coaching for employees
market_need_then: Companies were pushing AI adoption in 2026 and many vendors sold AI coaching inside Slack and Teams; the YC page cites the founders' experience teaching millions of English learners.
outcome_analysis: ChampionEffect is an active Fall 2026 company by two Cambly veterans who scaled a YC company to a reported $100M revenue. No exit, shutdown or funding was found. Founder track record is the main strength; the main risk is a crowded AI coaching market with established vendors.

name: CharacterQuilt
one_liner: Computer use agents to deploy enterprise marketing campaigns
long_description:
CharacterQuilt builds computer use agents to deploy enterprise marketing campaigns. 

Marketers today don’t actually do much marketing at all.

Today, over 80% of time spent on launching a marketing campaign is actually ops work: tweaking automation flows in Pardot, configuring audiences in LinkedIn, or wiring HTML emails in Marketo. 

What’s crazy about enterprise marketing is companies pay agencies millions of dollars just to deploy campaigns in their systems — and they still have to wait weeks for each one.

CharacterQuilt is AI infrastructure for marketing teams: a brain that learns your brand, and agents that operate your existing tools. Marketing campaigns that used to take 3 agencies, 10 tools, and 6 weeks are now being built, designed, and deployed from CQ in an hour.

Customers submit a brief like they would send to a human teammate or marketing agency, and they get back fully designed and deployed campaigns.

Teams like 1upHealth, ABC Fitness, and Emplifi use us to:

1-) Build segments/audiences faster
2-) Create on-brand creative (AI is terrible at staying on-brand)
3-) Deploy campaigns automatically into HubSpot, WordPress, LinkedIn etc. 

We replicate your brand guidelines, deeply understand past campaigns, and work inside your systems.

If you run demand gen or lifecycle at a B2B/B2C company and want to ship campaigns faster, send us a brief and we’ll build it in 15 minutes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Demand generation and lifecycle marketing teams at B2B and B2C companies, and the agencies they pay to deploy campaigns
problem: Over 80% of campaign time is ops work in tools like Pardot, Marketo and LinkedIn. CharacterQuilt agents take a brief, create on-brand creative and deploy the campaign inside the customer's existing tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services replacing agency campaign deployment; pricing not stated
product_category: Computer use agents for marketing operations
market_need_then: Companies pay agencies for weeks of campaign deployment work; the company names 1upHealth, ABC Fitness and Emplifi as users (company claim on the YC page).
outcome_analysis: CharacterQuilt is an active Spring 2026 company with a research-heavy CEO and a growth-focused CMO from Bloomreach. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found. A job listing claims fast growth in the batch, but funding is unverified. Platform vendors and funded marketing AI rivals are the main risk.

name: Chasi
one_liner: AI Revenue Engine for the Equipment Industry
long_description:
Chasi deploys AI agents that help equipment dealers sell more, respond faster, and maximize fleet utilization - 24/7.

One-third of the cost to build and maintain the physical world goes to equipment, yet fleet utilization across the industry often sits below 60%. Billions in assets sit idle while dealers drown in phone calls, emails, and manual data entry. Missed quotes, slow follow-ups, and disconnected systems mean lost revenue every day.

Chasi plugs into a dealer's existing stack to deploy AI agents that handle sales, rentals, and service requests around the clock. The result: faster response times, higher utilization, and stronger margins, without adding headcount. We automate the busywork so teams can focus on what actually grows the business: customer relationships.

Akash Pavan and Sarman Aulakh have built tractors, race cars, and robots, and previously led AI deployments at Tesla, Boeing, and Cummins, where they saw firsthand how much operational value gets left on the table in equipment-heavy industries. Chasi is live across equipment businesses in the US and Europe.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Equipment dealers and rental companies selling, renting and servicing construction, agricultural and industrial equipment
problem: Dealers miss quotes and follow-ups, and fleet utilization often sits below 60 percent. Chasi agents handle sales, rental and service requests around the clock inside the dealer's existing systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI agents sold to dealers
product_category: AI agents for equipment dealers and rental
market_need_then: Equipment is a large share of build and maintenance cost, utilization is low, and dealers rely on phone and email work; a customer, Premier Equipment Solutions, selected Chasi in July 2026.
outcome_analysis: Chasi is an active W26 company with industrial AI deployment backgrounds. It signed Premier Equipment Solutions for a pilot across Northeast compact equipment dealerships (reported July 2026). No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is unverified, and DMS vendors adding agents are the main competitive risk.

name: ChemPilot.ai
tags: Robotics; Workflow Automation; Aerospace; Advanced Materials; Defense
one_liner: Discover novel defense related materials/molecules.
long_description:
ChemPilot accelerates the discovery and development of next generation defense materials using AI and data from our automated wet lab. Developing a new material today takes 10+ years of trial and error. We compress that to months by screening for what can actually be made, then closing the loop: every lab result feeds back into the models so the next round is faster and smarter.

Sam, Ofir and Maor spent two years researching these materials at the Technion lab of our CSO, Prof. Alon Grinberg Dana (former MIT postdoc), working directly with defense primes and government R&D agencies. Together we bring chemical engineering, computational chemistry and AI, plus the production systems to put them to work. ChemPilot spun out of that research.

The West’s defense and dual-use industrial base runs on materials with fragile, sole-source and often adversarial supply chains. Demand for new capability is surging, and materials still take decades to develop. We’re building a new kind of chemical prime: one that can discover, develop and ultimately manufacture the materials the West needs, securely, fast and at cost.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Defense primes, aerospace companies, government R&D agencies and chemical companies needing new or domestically sourced materials
problem: Developing a new material takes over ten years of trial and error, and defense supply chains rely on fragile, sole source or adversarial suppliers.
business_model: Materials discovery and development contracts, with an aim to manufacture materials later
product_category: AI and automated wet lab materials discovery for defense
founder_names: Sam Cogan; Ofir Simhi; Maor Goldman
market_need_then: The company points to surging defense and dual use demand and fragile supply chains for materials. The batch is Fall 2026, with reported large funding for AI materials discovery as supporting context.
outcome_analysis: ChemPilot joined YC in Fall 2026 as a team of three that spun out of Technion defense materials research, and no outcome exists yet. Strengths are founders with domain and software exits behind them and a stated first autonomous lab, while risks include well funded AI materials competitors and the long cycle of defense procurement.

name: Chert
one_liner: iMessage infrastructure for business
long_description: Chert provides the infrastructure for businesses to automate conversations over iMessage. We’re already working with B2C startups, customer experience teams, and sales teams to reach end users through trusted and conversational messaging.

outcome_analysis: Chert is a two person Spring 2026 YC company that launched in May 2026 with a Twilio for iMessage pitch in an already crowded niche. It is too early for an outcome; the open risks are dependence on non official iMessage access, competitors with SOC 2 and longer track records, and the thin moat.

name: Chronicle Labs

long_description: Chronicle Labs is a staging environment for enterprise AI agents: we capture every event the agent sees in production and backtest it, so customers can safely test new behaviors without breaking anything.

name: Cignara

long_description: Cignara automates the entire revenue cycle - sales and support - across voice and chat - for Fortune 500-scale companies. It is too early for an outcome, so the main question is whether enterprise sales traction outpaces Sierra, Decagon and PolyAI.

name: ClaimKit

name: Clara
one_liner: AI primary care doctor
long_description:
Clara is an AI primary care and longevity practice from the team that founded and grew Circle Medical to $100M in revenue.

Our mission at Clara is to add one billion years of healthspan to humanity. We do this with an AI with deep clinical knowledge, coupled with the ability to sift through medical data to detect trends and patterns that could be missed.

Unlike Claude or ChatGPT, Clara can see your medical data and then act. Chat with Clara as you would a doctor and Clara can help with you make sense of symptoms, get medication refills, order and understand labs, and achieve health goals. Medical recommendations are preliminary until one of our human medical providers in the loop reviews and approves them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Individual patients, often longevity minded, paying membership tiers of $25, $50 and $150 per month without insurance
problem: Primary care is hard to access and fragmented across labs, prescriptions and wearables; patients lack a continuous clinician that sees all their data.

product_category: AI primary care and longevity practice

outcome_analysis: Clara is led by the Circle Medical team and raised a reported $12M pre-seed around its June 2026 launch, unusually large for the stage. It is too early for an outcome. Success factors cited reflect founder domain depth and a quick launch; the risks are AI medical regulation and well funded rivals.

name: Clean
one_liner: Revenue intelligence for agents and sales teams.
long_description:
Agents can run outreach on their own now.

In manufacturing, insurance, defense and banking, buying runs on a clock. Every deal has a transaction window almost nobody can see. Reach out before it opens and nobody answers. After it closes, the deal's gone.

Clean finds that window and gives agents and sales teams the strategy to win the deal.

We're building the revenue intelligence every sales agent will run on.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Sales teams and sales agents selling into manufacturing, healthcare, legal, fintech, insurance and tech infrastructure
problem: Buying decisions in these industries happen in short windows that sellers cannot see, so outreach arrives too early or too late.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API data and signals for revenue teams (pricing not found)
product_category: revenue intelligence and sales signal data
founder_names: Pavan Kumar Naguvanahalli Yashavantha; Tejas Gupta; Pratham Patel; Clarissa Saputra

outcome_analysis: Clean is a Fall 2026 YC company with four founders selling dated buying signals to sales teams. It is too early for an outcome. Company claims of reply rates and contract wins are unverified, and established intent data vendors are the main competition.

name: Click
one_liner: Managed Agents API
long_description:
Click is the Managed Agents API you can use with any model. Send a task with an API call, and Click runs the agent and streams back results. 

Click gives you the entire agent stack over an API, with no infrastructure to manage. Sessions are created with everything the agent needs - a sandbox, browser, and web search. Agents run on a harness with the latest innovations, like deferred tool discovery to support 1000s of tools, and Code Mode to use tools with scripts.

Ask your coding agent about useclick.ai/reference!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies building products on AI agents who do not want to run agent infrastructure
problem: Running production agents requires sandboxes, browsers, tool management and long running execution that most teams do not want to build.
business_model: usage-based API with tiers and bring your own model keys
product_category: managed agents API and agent infrastructure
market_need_then: Agent builders needed hosted infrastructure; the launch of Anthropic's managed agents shows labs saw the same need in April 2026.
outcome_analysis: Click is a one person Summer 2026 YC company selling a model agnostic managed agents API, launched shortly after Anthropic shipped a managed agents product. It is too early for an outcome. The main risk is that model labs absorb the wedge, while bring your own key flexibility is the differentiator.

name: CoArena
tags: AIOps; Machine Learning; Reinforcement Learning; Data Labeling; AI
one_liner: The biggest crowdsourced benchmark for Computer-Use
long_description: CoArena is a live arena where anyone can use the world's top computer-use models racing two of them on the same real computer task and judging which one did it better. Every battle becomes something the AI labs can't build themselves, an honest test of their agents on real work, and the data to make them better.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI labs and agent builders who buy computer-use evaluation data and datasets; the arena itself is free for public users who judge battles

product_category: AI evaluation, crowdsourced benchmark and data labeling for computer-use agents

No exit, shutdown or layoff reports exist, so it is too early to judge success or failure. The key uncertainty is whether labs will pay for the resulting data.

name: Codag
one_liner: The AI gateway for cheaper, faster, permissioned agents.
long_description:
Codag compresses tool call outputs before agents read them, which reduces token spend by  20-30% while retaining output accuracy.

Govern and see analytics on agent dollars across all model providers and internal agents.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams running coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex who pay for tokens and want spend governance
problem: Coding agents read large tool outputs such as logs, test runs and file trees, which burns tokens and money. Teams also lack visibility into agent spend across providers.
business_model: Usage-based credits (about 0.05 dollars per credit, Team plan 499 dollars per month, custom enterprise)
product_category: AI gateway and context compression for coding agents
market_need_then: Agent token bills were a visible pain in 2026, with many write-ups and tools on cutting coding agent token costs.
outcome_analysis: Codag is a solo-founder Summer 2026 company and still active. It targets agent token cost, a real 2026 pain, but faces open source tools and vendor built-in limits. No exit, shutdown or layoff reports exist, so the outcome is open and depends on whether governance and analytics give it a paid edge over simple compression.

name: CodeWisp
one_liner: Anyone can create real games with AI
long_description:
CodeWisp lets anyone build and publish web games using plain-English prompts.

Traditional game development requires learning complex engines, managing assets and code, and following rigid workflows, making it slow and inaccessible for most people.

With CodeWisp, users describe the game they want. CodeWisp generates the game’s code, structure, and assets, and users can refine it with follow-up prompts. This makes it possible to go from idea to a playable web game in minutes, without prior game-development experience.

CodeWisp also makes Petlings: Merge & Battle, a free pet merge game for iPhone and iPad: https://playpetlings.com/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Beginners and hobbyists who want to make and publish web games without coding, plus mobile game players via its own Petlings game
problem: Traditional game development needs engines, assets and code, which blocks most people from making games.

product_category: AI game creation platform
market_need_then: The YC launch post reports 2,000 plus weekly active creators and 17,000 plus games made, a company claim. Demand for no-code creation of games was visible in the many prompt-to-game tools in 2026.
outcome_analysis: CodeWisp is a Winter 2026 company with a solo listed founder and three staff, still active. It reports early creator traction and also ships its own mobile game. No exit, shutdown or layoff reports exist. Outcome is open and depends on whether creators and players stay in a crowded AI game tools market.

name: Cofia

name: Collar

name: Confluence Labs
one_liner: AI models that learn from experience
long_description:
While modern AI excels in any area you can collect a lot of data for, it struggles in areas where data is sparse or costly to attain. Designing new molecules, discovering new physics, and engineering new materials are all domains where collecting data is extremely costly. 

We dream of a world where AI accelerates research in all of these domains and creates a more abundant future for humanity, but the current technology is not there. That’s why we started Confluence Labs. 

We are building AI that can design highly effective experiments in data-sparse domains and learn maximally from the data it already has.

name: Congruent
one_liner: AI native radars for self-driving cars
long_description: At Congruent, we build radars for end-to-end autonomous systems. The most advanced autonomous systems are trained as a single neural network from raw sensor data to navigation actions. For a sensor to be included in these pipelines sensor stacks requires two key properties: access to raw sensor data and a high-fidelity sensor simulator. Current automotive radars have neither, they output heavily processed point clouds and no raw radar simulator exists for driving scenes. Congruent solves both problems: a radar architecture that exposes raw data, paired with a world model based radar simulator. Radar is the only depth sensor at a price point that scales to every car on the road and works in all weather conditions. Congruent is building the radar compatible with the training architectures that will make mass-market vehicles autonomous.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Autonomous vehicle developers training end-to-end neural driving stacks

outcome_analysis: Congruent is an active W26 company with no exit, shutdown or layoffs found. The CEO previously led autonomy at a radar company, which gives founder market fit, and end-to-end driving is a tailwind. Hardware cost and capital needs are the main risks.

name: Conifer
one_liner: Intelligent decisions for critical AI operations
long_description: AI now runs on a market of hundreds of models and providers that changes constantly, each with its own price, strengths and failure modes. Agents also act faster, and on more information, than people can meaningfully review. Conifer builds the decision layer between agents and the people in charge. Our gateway puts 240+ models from 28 providers behind one key, with 99.99% uptime. Our router picks a model for each request by weighing the task against its cost, and Parallax reviews the code agents write.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams running AI agents and coding agents that use many model providers
problem: Hundreds of models and providers with changing prices and failure modes, and agents act faster than people can review. Conifer is a gateway and router that picks models by task and cost, plus a reviewer for agent-written code.

product_category: LLM gateway, router and agent code review

name: Constellation Space
one_liner: AI operating system for mega-scale satellite networks.
long_description:
Constellation Space is building the autonomous infrastructure layer for the next generation of space networking. As satellite constellations rapidly scale from hundreds of nodes to tens of thousands, traditional ground-based orchestration fundamentally breaks down. ConstellationOS bridges this gap by providing zero-intervention network handoffs, predictive thermal load-balancing, and sub-second optical routing.

Our founding team spent years building and operating satellite systems at SpaceX, Blue Origin, and NASA. We started Constellation to solve the problem we kept running into: reactive monitoring doesn't scale.

We are building the sub-second routing protocols and hyperscale load-balancing infrastructure that will manage the future of off-world telecommunications and compute. 

hello@constellation-io.com

name: Corvera
tags: SaaS; Consumer; B2B; Data Engineering; AI
one_liner: The AI sales agent for CPG brands
long_description:
Corvera (YC W26) is the AI sales agent for CPG brands. We turn the data a brand already has into the actions its sales team takes today.

A CPG brand sells into tens of thousands of independent US stores through dozens of distributors, and works that base with a handful of people. CLEAN Cause, a $20M yerba mate brand, covers 21,000 stores through 46 distributors with a four-person sales team. The accounts worth a call are not capped by headcount. The team is.

CLEAN Cause now runs its daily sales decisions on Corvera: 5,000 queries in 40 days across 12 users, $250K of opportunities surfaced within days, and a 7x return on the analysts they would otherwise hire.

With Corvera in place, every sales rep starts the morning with:
- The stores to act on today, ranked and priced, with the reason on the row,
- The outreach already drafted to the right contact at the right distributor, and
- The follow-up booked, logged, and measured against the goal it was set to move.

All from the distributor feeds, retailer portals, and ERP data they already have, resolved into one context layer - without a data team, and without handing their sales to a broker.

We’re founded by Chris (2x Founder; ex-CEO at Better Nature; Forbes 30U30), Dirk (ex-Google Data & AI Lead), and Matthew (ex-Head of Product at Rosemark; Princeton MEng in CS).

To date, we’ve raised $6.2M and are backed by YC, firstminute capital, 6 Degrees Capital, 20VC, Rebel Fund, Duke Capital Partners, and more. Our ICP is US CPG brands doing $20M+ in retail revenue through UNFI, KeHE and DSD distributors. We sell to VPs of Sales and CEOs.

The incumbents prove the scale. Brokers take 5-12% of a $350B US independent grocery market, and Advantage Solutions, a publicly traded company, does $3.5B in annual revenue.

Our mission is bold: to enable the next generation of unicorn CPG brands to be run by teams of less than 10 people.

Our vision is even bolder: to give every CPG brand the coverage of a full sales team at a fraction of the headcount, and displace the broker network that covers the US independent channel today.

Visit www.corvera.ai to learn more!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US and UK consumer packaged goods brands with 20M dollars or more in retail revenue selling through UNFI, KeHE and DSD distributors
problem: CPG brands receive fragmented sell-out data from distributor and retailer portals and ERPs. Corvera unifies it and turns it into daily ranked sales actions for reps.
business_model: B2B SaaS for CPG brands; pricing not published
product_category: AI sales and operations agent for CPG

outcome_analysis: Corvera joined YC in Winter 2026 and announced a 4.2 million dollar seed round led by 6 Degrees Capital in May 2026. A CEO who built the Better Nature food brand gives founder market fit with CPG buyers. Its focus moved from back office operations to sales actions. We're scaling in solar, expanding in data centers, and building lunar construction robotics under contract with NASA.

name: Covera

Every hour spent on manual quoting is an hour not spent selling. Across tens of thousands of brokers, that's billions in revenue left on the table.

Covera runs it end to end, with AI workflows connected to the AMS, the inbox and 100+ carrier portals. It fits the way brokers already work, so their teams can focus on advising clients and closing business.

In 3 months, Covera went live with 90+ brokers in the US and Europe. Brokers now go from a client's email to a quote in 3 minutes, instead of hours.

name: Crosslayer Labs
one_liner: Protect, monitor and defend your Internet presence
long_description: Crosslayer Labs detects impersonation attacks on websites and APIs. We provide "outside-in" monitoring of customer infrastructure, comprehensively discovering and monitoring all Internet dependencies, including DNS, BGP, TLS certs, Javascript. We correlate signals from different layers of the Internet stack to identify attack patterns. Our alerts are actionable and contain root cause analysis/remediation recommendations. Our founding team is world renowned for previously inventing the MPIC standard adopted by all the major CAs including Google, Apple, Amazon. The MPIC standard is securing over 700 million websites via the issuance of over 3 billion digital certificates, and is now a global internet standard that protects every single HTTPS connection.

name: Cumulus Labs
one_liner: The Fastest Multimodal Inference OS
long_description:
Cumulus Labs lets engineering teams ship AI in production without needing a dedicated ML platform team. Right now, companies building AI products are forced to stitch together separate vendors for routing, observability, evaluation, fine-tuning, and inference. This fragmented approach is brittle, expensive, and is a common reason enterprises fail with AI.  

We replace that entire stack with a single unified platform. Developers can keep their existing code while instantly upgrading to a unified platform that handles routing, semantic caching, continuous shadow evaluation, simulated data, and one-click fine-tuning. 

Behind the platform is Ion, our proprietary inference engine running on a custom NVIDIA Grace GPU fleet. Ion uses in-house custom GPU kernels to deliver 30 to 50 percent more throughput than standard vLLM or SGLang, giving our customers SOTA inference economics.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

Funding is unverified (aggregators suggest about 500K USD from YC and others; a 63M USD figure is implausible). Performance claims are self-reported and the market has funded incumbents, so no outcome can be assessed yet.

name: Current
one_liner: Run hundreds of coding agents and stay in control
long_description:
Current is an opinionated way to work with your coding agents. It lets you run hundreds of agents while staying in control.

The problem with running agents in parallel isn't their intelligence. It's your attention. You end up scrolling walls of text and tool calls, looking for answers you'd already been given.

So Current drops the chat entirely and focuses on your agents' outputs, not their inputs. Everything is an issue, from a quick fix to a big project with sub-issues. You write it, and your agents pick it up and deliver.

When they're done, they notify you and show you what they made: a report, a chart, a before and after video, or an interactive app that shows their work. You review the work, not how they got there. Comment and the agent goes back to work. Approve and it merges.

Current is built with Current. It's free on Mac, Windows, Linux and iPhone, and works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and many more agents.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software developers who run many coding agents in parallel
problem: Running agents in parallel overwhelms attention because developers scroll through chat and tool calls instead of reviewing finished work.
business_model: Free desktop and iPhone app; monetization not shown, pricing section lists no plans
product_category: Developer tools, coding agent management
competitors_at_founding: Conductor; Vibe Kanban; Cursor cloud agents
market_need_then: By 2026 roughly all developers used AI workflows per newsletters, and many guides compared tools for running multiple agents, showing demand for orchestration.
outcome_analysis: Current is a single-founder Spring 2026 company in the crowded coding agent management category. It is free with no disclosed traction. The main risk is that model vendors and IDEs absorb parallel agent review, while its angle is reviewing outputs rather than chats.

name: Cyclon

With one touch, you can spin up AI agents to control your phone or handle tasks in the background. AI isn’t just inside an app - it’s the phone itself.

name: DAIVIN!
one_liner: Tankless Dive Gear - Breath Autonomy at Sea, Land & Space
long_description: DAIVIN! builds tankless dive gear that unlocks breath autonomy in extreme environments. Starting from underwater environment our mission is to remove the need for dangerous, heavy and bulky oxygen tanks in space, air and on land and replace them with water!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Divers first, then users of breathing gas in aviation, land and space environments
problem: Oxygen tanks are heavy, bulky and dangerous; the company aims to generate breathable gas from water by electrolysis.
business_model: Hardware sales of wearable dive gear; no pricing disclosed

name: Daqstra
one_liner: AI-native test infrastructure layer for hardware companies
long_description: Daqstra is the AI-native orchestration layer for physical R&D. It saves engineers in Aerospace, Energy and Robotics hundreds of man hours managing test infrastructure by connecting fragmented test hardware, bringing live and historical test data into one place, and by giving engineers an API to orchestrate their entire test setup. We enable teams to spend less time rebuilding test infrastructure and more time improving the hardware they test.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: Engineers spend hundreds of hours building and managing fragmented test hardware infrastructure and lose test data across runs.
business_model: B2B software for test infrastructure, with edge, cloud hub and API; pricing not shown; early pilots
product_category: Test infrastructure orchestration for physical R&D

outcome_analysis: Daqstra is a Summer 2026 company from UC San Diego rocket engine testing, with early aerospace programs and a pilot. Funding is undisclosed. Competition from Nominal and incumbent vendors is the main risk, while founders' hands-on test experience is the main strength.

name: Databuddy
tags: B2B; Analytics; Data Engineering; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: AI Data Analyst for fast-growing teams
long_description:
Databuddy gives you your very own data analyst, always watching over your data, combining all your context to investigate and paint a full picture on every product issue that emerges in real-time; conversion drops, user frustration and churn.

It makes your product better without needing to have you look at a dashboard and spend hours figuring out the why. one click to install or switch from any dated analytics provider.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Early-stage startups and developers without a dedicated data person, paying from $9.99 a month
problem: Small teams cannot afford analysts or hours spent in dashboards to learn why conversion drops or users churn, and legacy analytics tools are heavy or privacy-invasive.
business_model: Freemium SaaS, free to 10,000 events a month then usage-tiered plans from $9.99 a month
product_category: Cookieless product and web analytics with an AI analyst (Databunny) and MCP server

outcome_analysis: Databuddy is active and only months old. A solo founder reached YC Fall 2026 with an open source, cookieless analytics product, early launch traction on Product Hunt and X, and a small round of roughly $560K. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found. The main risks are a crowded market with PostHog and Plausible and thin defensibility, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Datoric
tags: Machine Learning; Robotics; Data Labeling; AI
one_liner: The training data R&D engine for physical AI
long_description:
Datoric develops custom datasets for robotics, treating research, collection, verification, and production as one continuous process. We work closely with frontier model teams to turn emerging limitations and model failures into testable data hypotheses, and run exclusive collections for specific data methods based on results.

Data is collected through private invite-only applications separated by modality, customer, and trust level. Every submission remains linked to the contributor, device, task, session, consent, rights, and processing history that produced it, giving our internal QA and fraud models the context to detect problems that may appear legitimate in the finished file. 

Once a collection method is validated, we scale it up as a solution to the model failure and it also becomes a reusable data recipe for future custom projects or independently collected, rights-cleared data products.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI and robotics model teams buying custom training data
problem: Robotics and physical AI models fail for lack of trustworthy, well-provenanced real-world data such as egocentric video, UMI demonstrations and teleoperation.
business_model: Custom data collection projects plus reusable rights-cleared data products
product_category: Training data for robotics and physical AI
market_need_then: Robotics labs were buying large volumes of egocentric video in 2026, with reports of foundation models pretrained on over a million hours of first-person video.
outcome_analysis: Datoric is a two-person company in a hot physical AI data market, claiming nearly seven figures of revenue in 30 days in its launch post and over 300,000 contributors. No outcome events were found. Funding is unknown. Risks are crowded vendors and customer concentration, so the story is unresolved.

name: Dawn Industries
one_liner: Automatic Diagnosis & Fix for Industrial Automation Cells
long_description: VIM connects to the entire cell: PLCs, robots, CNC machines, sensors. When a cell faults, VIM finds the cause, stages the fix, and the operator approves with one click. When a part drifts, VIM catches it seconds after the cut, inside the machine, and recommends the correction. Recovery drops from 30 minutes to under two, saving more than $15,000 per fault in large factories.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Factories running PLC, robot and CNC automation cells
problem: When an automation cell faults, recovery takes about 30 minutes and costs thousands per fault; parts also drift unnoticed.
business_model: Enterprise software (VIM) sold to manufacturers, pricing not found
product_category: Industrial AI fault diagnosis and recovery
market_need_then: The company claims faults cost over $15,000 each in large factories and recovery takes 30 minutes; independent verification was not found.
outcome_analysis: Dawn Industries is a months-old company with a staged-autonomy product (read-only, then one-click approval, then unattended recovery) aimed at a costly factory pain point. No outcome events or verified funding were found. Safety requirements and incumbent controls vendors are the main risks, so the outcome is open.

name: Dayjob
one_liner: AI Scheduling for Short Haul Trucks
long_description: Dayjob does AI Scheduling for Short Haul Trucks. Our scheduling agent plugs into existing ERPs and continuously re-optimises routes in real time - handling new jobs, driver changes, and exceptions automatically. Customers in waste management see 8%+ efficiency gains from day one.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Skip hire and waste collection operators running short-haul truck fleets
problem: Dispatchers plan routes manually and lose margin on mismatched trucks and jobs, especially when jobs and drivers change during the day.
business_model: B2B SaaS scheduling agent integrated with existing ERPs, pricing not found
product_category: AI scheduling and dispatch for waste logistics
market_need_then: Operators claim margin loss from poor scheduling; Dayjob's site claims 11% revenue gain and 25% less admin time, which are unverified company claims.
outcome_analysis: Dayjob is early, targeting UK skip hire operators and expanding to the US per a YC launch page. Founders previously built an ERP for e-waste recyclers, a plausible domain edge. No outcome events were found and funding is unconfirmed, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Decawork
one_liner: Training company-specific models that approve AI actions.
long_description:
An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Access decisions need to adapt in real time as the agent works, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rules or have people manually approve every step.

We train small, company-specific models that approve AI actions in real time. They consider the company’s policies and interests, the agent’s current task, and its past actions to decide whether each proposed action should be allowed. Access is specific to the task at hand and reassessed as the agent works.

Companies will rent intelligence from AI labs or run open-source models to power their agents. They’ll own the models that keep their entire AI workforce acting in their interests. Decawork is building those models.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies deploying internal AI agents, buyers in IT and security
problem: Static access rules and manual approvals cannot judge whether an agent's action fits its current task.
business_model: B2B software that trains company-specific approval models, pricing not found
product_category: AI agent authorization and governance
market_need_then: Analysts expected a wave of agent runtime authorization products in 2026 as enterprise agents spread.
outcome_analysis: Decawork is a months-old AI agent control startup with a clear thesis but heavy incumbent competition from identity vendors launching the same runtime authorization in 2026. No outcome events were found and funding is unconfirmed, so its result is unknown.

name: Decent

long_description: Decent is a health insurance brokerage for small businesses. We compare every way to cover your team, show what each one costs, and then keep improving your plan all year. We're paid by insurance companies, so we're free to you.

You give us a problem and we ship a working AI product in the same afternoon.

name: DeepMark
one_liner: A live watermark inside AI voice that survives phone calls
long_description: DeepMark is the authentication layer for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we embed a compact, machine-readable ID directly into the audio, not in metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The ID resolves to a trust record, so a bank, a call center, or the person on the line can verify in real time who the agent is.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Voice AI providers, banks and call centers that need to prove an AI voice agent's identity, plus media platforms needing content provenance

business_model: Platform license to voice AI providers plus verification services
product_category: AI voice watermarking and authentication

A pre-YC platform license and a Deepgram integration suggest early commercial pull, while Resemble AI and Digimarc remain direct rivals and funding is not verified.

name: DeepReach Inc.
tags: Hardware; Machine Learning; Robotics; Computer Vision; AI
one_liner: Network for Physical AI Data Business
long_description:
Physical AI — robots and world models — is bottlenecked on one thing: diverse,
real-world data at massive scale showing how humans actually do work in the
physical world. It was never written down, and you can't buy it, because no one
has ever captured it. Only real local experts, the people who do this work every
day, can produce data this authentic and valuable.

DeepReach builds the network that reaches them. We design and manufacture
wearable stereo capture devices, then place them with local data partners who
run collection as their own business — in warehouses, workshops, farms, kitchens
and repair shops. They own the local relationships; we supply the hardware, the
software platform, the quality pipeline and the payments. Anyone can run a data
business.

That structure is what produces diversity. Instead of thousands of hours inside
one environment, we deliver hours spread across thousands of environments —
which is what actually makes robot policies generalize.

475 devices in the field and 100+ data partners are live across 7 countries, adding new
partners every week. They've collected nearly 150,000 clips in the past three
months, with volume roughly doubling month over month. Our data is in production
with multiple frontier model and robotics companies, and we're scaling to
10,000+ devices across 50 countries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and robotics companies buying real-world human task data; local data partners who run collection businesses
problem: Robot policies need diverse real-world data showing how people do physical work, which cannot be bought because it was never captured.
business_model: Data sales to AI labs; hardware and platform supplied to local data partners who are paid per qualified hour
product_category: Physical AI egocentric data network with wearable capture devices
competitors_at_founding: Human Archive; Claru; General Intelligence Labs
market_need_then: Physical AI labs are data constrained; company claims several million dollars in contracts with frontier labs and robotics firms and 475 devices and 100 plus partners in 7 countries (self-reported, inconsistent figures on the YC page).
outcome_analysis: DeepReach is an active Summer 2026 company claiming early commercial traction with frontier labs through a distributed partner model. The claims are self-reported and internally inconsistent, funding is not verified, and egocentric data is a crowded field, so the outcome is open.

name: Definite
one_liner: Connect operational data with finance to see what drives the numbers.
long_description:
Definite connects operational data with finance so businesses that make, move, build or operate things can see what each production run, load and job actually cost.

These businesses already record a lot: production runs, shipments, job sites, equipment hours, work orders. Finance records the same business in a different shape. Operating systems track activity by site, line, or day. The ledger tracks it by entity, account, and month. Both sets of records exist, but the link between an operating decision and its financial effect usually lives in spreadsheets and in a few people's heads.

So questions that should be routine take days. What happens to cash if one plant adds a shift? How does a change in throughput or staffing flow into the forecast? Which operating changes actually moved the numbers last quarter?

Definite connects to existing operational and financial systems read-only. Models propose how operational records map to financial ones and explain what they find. Deterministic rules perform the calculations and checks, so results trace back to the source records they came from. 

Definite started in a plant office an hour from campus, watching a controller rebuild the same spreadsheet she rebuilds every month to tie her production system to her ledger. The three of us met at the University of Waterloo and had each spent our careers on a version of that join. Gurshabd built wallet policy and approval controls at BitGo, where proving customer assets matched the ledger was still done by hand. Farhan built recommendation systems for Instagram Reels at Meta, joining billions of raw events to the numbers the business reported. Mazin built trading systems at Optiver, then agents for financial analysts at Boosted.ai, where analysts would not act on a number they could not trace. In finance that work is at least funded. In companies that make and move things, nobody had built it at all.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Finance teams at companies that make, move, build or operate things, such as manufacturers and logistics firms
problem: Operating records (production runs, shipments, work orders) and the ledger describe the same business in different shapes, so linking operating changes to financial results lives in spreadsheets.
business_model: B2B software connecting read-only to operational and financial systems; pricing not found
product_category: AI ontology layer linking operational data to finance
founder_names: Gurshabd Singh Varaich; Mazin Al-Ani; Farhan Ur Rehman
market_need_then: Founders describe controllers rebuilding the same spreadsheet monthly to tie production systems to the ledger; a 2026 guide identifies job costing and WIP valuation as poorly handled by general AI finance tools.
outcome_analysis: Definite is an active Fall 2026 company of three Waterloo engineers with fintech and trading backgrounds, so no outcome has occurred. The founders' narrative of watching a controller rebuild a spreadsheet is a real pain, but the name collides with an unrelated funded company and the niche is adjacent to fast-moving AI ERPs.

name: Degla Inc
one_liner: The fully autonomous intelligence layer in the sky.
long_description:
Degla AI builds autonomy software that enables drones to understand spoken instructions, reason onboard, and adapt as the mission unfolds. Once you’ve expressed your intent, the system owns the problem.

An operator can say, “Find the missing hiker wearing a red sweater.” The drone plans the mission, interprets what it sees, and adjusts its flight as new information emerges. The operator sets the objective and the aircraft handles the execution.

At the core is an onboard vision-language model that interprets what the drone sees, understands the operator’s intent, and guides mission planning, execution, and adaptation. Running locally on NVIDIA Jetson, it makes mission decisions without relying on cloud inference.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Drone operators in search and rescue and disaster response
problem: Drones need a skilled pilot or manual mission planning; operators want to state intent in speech and have the aircraft plan and adapt.
business_model: Autonomy software for drones, pricing not found
product_category: Drone autonomy with onboard vision-language model
market_need_then: Search and rescue demand and active 2026 research on language-grounded aerial autonomy; the company gives no traction numbers.
outcome_analysis: Degla is an active Fall 2026 company with a single named founder and a two person team, so no outcome exists yet. The idea of onboard language-driven drone autonomy is technically hard and the field has well funded players, so progress depends on demonstrating reliable real flights.

name: Denta
one_liner: Fortune 500 Dental Benefits
long_description: Fixing health insurance by giving the buying power back to the individual.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Employers buying dental benefits for employees, with employees as card users

Sources disagree on whether it started as dental practice management or as a benefit card, which suggests an early repositioning, and the main hurdle is winning employers away from established carriers.

name: Deploy
one_liner: The generalist robot deployment company.
long_description: Deploy's core belief is that robots should be useful. Getting a generalist robot to do real work is fundamentally the same problem across industries. We build everything between the model and the task to bring generalist robots to the businesses that actually need them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

business_model: Robots as a service: customers pay for completed work or a station with guaranteed throughput, no capital expenditure
product_category: Robot deployment service for warehouse tasks

outcome_analysis: Deploy is a two person Fall 2026 company with no verified funding and no public customers, so there is no outcome yet. It is competing in warehouse robots as a service against better funded players, and its early public notes stress remote human intervention as a design choice. The key uncertainty is whether intervention rates fall enough for the per station economics to work.

name: Derya
tags: AIOps; Logistics; Supply Chain; Procurement; Automation
one_liner: AI Brokers for Industrial Trade
long_description:
Derya deploys supply chain automations for startups, SMEs, and enterprises that fulfil their entire supply chain function, from prospecting and procurement to distribution of goods.

Our mission is to rebuild the supply chain from the ground up, turning one of the world’s hardest coordination problems into an AI native system that moves commodities by being integrated into both the supply chain infrastructure and the customer. We work across robotics, commodities, and food & beverages companies; procuring goods and managing various operation functions for them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

product_category: AI supply chain and freight forwarding automation

outcome_analysis: Derya is an active Summer 2026 company that raised about $1.1M from YC, 212 and an angel in mid 2026. Founders bring maritime software and shipping legal experience, which fits the freight wedge. It faces several YC freight AI peers, so winning depends on operational execution in hardware supply chains rather than technology.

name: Didit
one_liner: Infrastructure for identity and fraud.
long_description: One API for KYC, KYB, AML, authentication, biometrics, and fraud — powered by 1,000+ data sources, 200+ signals, and in-house AI models. Global coverage. Integrate in minutes, pay as you go. Start free at business.didit.me.

It claims 1,500 customers, growth over 30% month over month and profitability, all self reported. Success so far rests on aggressive pricing and a free tier in a crowded market, so durability depends on whether those economics hold.

name: Dipole Labs
one_liner: AI-controlled optical switching for AI clusters
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hyperscalers and neoclouds building large AI training and inference clusters
problem: Electrical packet switching inside AI data centers wastes power, adds latency and heat; optical circuit switching keeps traffic in light but needs fast, reliable switches and control software.

product_category: Optical circuit switching hardware for AI clusters

It enters a field where nEye, Salience Labs and iPronics have raised far more. Its prospects depend on proving a reliable switch and securing foundry and design partner commitments.

name: Discovered Materials
one_liner: AI scientists to discover materials for the semiconductor industry.
long_description:
We use AI to discover new materials for the semiconductor industry - specifically datacenters and fabs. Finding novel materials today takes 10+ years of lab work. We aim to compress that timeline to months, using a swarm of AI agents.

Akash completed his PhD at Stanford on material discovery for semiconductors. The materials he discovered for nanoscale interconnects have been adopted into the roadmaps of Intel and TSMC. Advaith was the founding applied scientist at Persona AI (acquired by Luma Labs), where he built long horizon autonomous agents for major telecom and crypto companies.

Power consumption and heat release from AI chips is doubling every year. The semiconductor industry needs new materials to keep this exponential going -  Discovered Materials will help find them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Semiconductor makers, datacenter chip designers and fabs needing new materials, initially for heat management
problem: Discovering and validating new chip materials takes over ten years in the lab; the bottleneck is finding candidates that can be synthesized and tested quickly.
business_model: AI agent platform for materials discovery with in house lab validation; customer revenue model not stated
product_category: AI materials discovery for semiconductors
competitors_at_founding: CuspAI; Periodic Labs; Radical AI; SandboxAQ
market_need_then: AI chip heat flux is a pressing problem (the company cites about 140 W per square centimeter) and chip makers need new materials; skeptics note no AI discovered material has yet had commercial impact.
outcome_analysis: Discovered Materials, previously Matforge, raised a $9M seed announced 2026-08-10 led by Lightspeed India Partners with YC and Peak XV, soon after its Spring 2026 batch. Founders combine AI research and Stanford materials science. It competes with far better funded AI materials rivals, so the test is whether lab validated results reach customers, not whether candidates can be generated.

name: Dispatch
one_liner: Satellites for Manufacturing in Space
long_description:
Dispatch is building refurbishable reentry vehicles that host and return payloads for companies making ultra-high-value materials (semiconductors, biotech, and pharma) that can only be manufactured in space. Right now, these companies have no practical way to manufacture and get their products back to Earth. We solve this bottleneck.

We just returned from the Mojave Desert testing our first full-scale reentry heat shield designed to protect the satellite as it returns from space at Mach 20+, built in an apartment for 100x cheaper than competitors. To test, we held it behind a rocket engine to simulate the forces of atmospheric reentry. IT WORKED! Watch here - https://youtu.be/dhlQmnIoptg

To scale, we anchor permanent infrastructure in orbit - building high power Autonomous Space Stations designed from day one for "lights-out" manufacturing serviced by the reentry vehicles.

name: Donkey
one_liner: The AI-native trading company: factory prices, delivered, one number
long_description:
Donkey is the AI-native trading company. Upload a buying list and we land the whole container at one locked, delivered price, tariffs included. You buy from Donkey: one contract, one company responsible for everything between the factory floor and your door. Our own people check the cartons before the factory gets paid, and the balance is due when the goods are accepted at your dock.

Small businesses buy imports through three or four middlemen, each adding 15 to 30 points, because none of them can fill a container on their own. Big enough to buy pallets, never big enough to buy the box. Quotes float with freight, FX and tariffs and live 15 to 30 days.

A trading company is rooms of people on the phone with factories, forwarders and brokers. Donkey runs that as one engine. It finds the real factory behind the customs record, stacks duty line by line, packs the container on weight and cube, and returns one number that holds from signature. Next comes the shared container: small buyers fill one box together at container prices, and every container earns better factory terms for the next one.

Team in San Francisco and Wuhan, English and Mandarin. If your business buys pallets of anything imported, send us your buying list.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

business_model: Trading company: buys from factories and resells at one locked delivered price, margin on goods
product_category: AI-native import trading and sourcing
market_need_then: Small importers face stacked middleman markups and volatile tariffs in 2025 and 2026, so a locked all-in price is a clear pain point. Demand evidence is the founder's claim, not independent data.
outcome_analysis: Donkey is a Summer 2026 YC company with five people and no reported exit or distress. It sells a risky, working-capital heavy trading model to small importers while Alibaba and AiDeliv launched AI sourcing tools in 2026. Too early to judge success or failure.

name: Doomersion

Gen-Z doomscrolls 2.5-3 hours a day, and if we bake immersion into that by only showing them viral videos in another language that are matched to their level, we can make the optimal language learning method addictive for people. Hence the name, doomersion.

The app gained ~15k downloads in the first two weeks, and power users spend ~3+ hours daily on the app. Feel free to download and try it yourself!

name: Drafted
one_liner: Design your home instantly with AI
long_description:
Drafted is building multimodal generative models for residential architecture and spatial design.

The product allows users to design homes by combining sketches and direct spatial input to generate coherent floor plans and elevations that can be explored in both 2D and 3D. Users can define footprints, lot boundaries, room placement, relationships, room programs, and square footage constraints that persist across generations and iterative design exploration, then export CAD, PDF, and other files into the rest of the home design and construction process.

⁃ In the past month, we've had 120k users come to the site, generating 325k+ floor plans through socials and word-of-mouth. 
⁃ A team of 9, made up of researchers from Stanford, Autodesk, Brown, Adobe, and Architects from WeWork, Atmos, and design families
⁃ Raised $17.5M from investors such as Buckley Ventures (Josh Buckley), YC (Aaron Epstein), Patrick Collison, Evan Moore, Convective Capital (Bill Clerico), Ben Silbermann, Jack Altman, Samsung, Starship Ventures, Charlie Songhurst, Ryan Tedder, Moses Moody, Alex Blania, and Kevin Mahaffey

name: Dream

long_description:
Dream makes AI cameras that catch damage teams miss. Car dealerships, equipment rental companies, fleets, and more move expensive assets in and out all day, and undocumented damage is a costly leak.

Dream cameras are simple to set up and work automatically. Each vehicle or machine that passes is photographed from every angle, identified, and reconstructed into a complete condition record. On return or intake, Dream instantly flags new dents, scrapes, and changes your team might miss, giving one source of truth for every asset's condition over time.

Ryland worked at X/xAI and built aerial damage-detection vision at Vexcel Imaging. Alexander worked at AWS and trained edge-camera models deployed in the wild across Africa and India to detect poachers.

So far, we've hit 40-50% lower latency than existing neoclouds.

name: Dualizer

Dualizer builds AI-powered, physics-based process simulation and digital twins to design and scale chemical processes and optimize existing plants. We help engineering teams identify bottlenecks, increase yield and throughput, and reduce energy and production costs—improving plant efficiency and profitability.

The platform combines AI reasoning, our proprietary deterministic simulation and optimization engine, and physics-informed machine learning. Engineers can build, calibrate, and refine models through conversation, starting from a diagram, available data, or an engineering objective. Calculations account for thermodynamics, material and energy balances, equipment behavior, and operating constraints, enabling teams to optimize interconnected equipment and operating conditions across a plant.

Equipment sizing and costing, 3D layout planning, and techno-economic analysis connect process improvements to plant-level decisions. Teams can accelerate new process scale-up, debottleneck operating plants, and continually refine operating strategies as production targets and plant conditions change. Dualizer makes rigorous simulation and optimization an ongoing capability for improving industrial productivity and profitability throughout a plant’s life.

name: Egoist Machines
tags: Hardware; Personalization; Privacy; Consumer Products; AI Assistant
one_liner: Your personal context, securely portable across every AI app.
long_description:
Egoist Machines is building infrastructure for a world where your personal context belongs to you, rather than to the apps and AI companies you use. Today, every assistant and consumer app builds its own version of you. We think that architecture is backwards. Your context should live with you, persist across products, and be available to any model, app or agent you choose.

AI Passport is the first layer of that infrastructure. It brings the context you generate across AI assistants and everyday apps into one portable profile you control. Tell ChatGPT something and Claude can already know it, for example. Switch to a new product and it can understand you from the first interaction, without the new company needing to own the underlying data.

Apps integrate through Sign in with AI Passport, requesting only the context they need for a specific purpose and duration. Users can see what is being accessed and revoke that access later. Underneath, we have built our own memory infrastructure for fast, compact per-user retrieval and permissioned access.

We are distributing AI Passport directly to consumers through first-party products, while integrating it into consumer applications with existing distribution. Every new product that uses Passport gives users another reason to maintain their context there, and every additional Passport holder makes the context layer more useful to developers.

The next step is to build a true Egoist Machine: an intelligent system whose memory, incentives and actions are governed by the individual it represents. We call it Digital Domovoy, the hardware extension of AI Passport. Instead of your most personal context ultimately living on somebody else's servers, it lives and is processed locally on hardware you control. AI Passport becomes the permission layer between that private local context and the cloud models and internet services you choose to use.

Our North Star is the Egoist Machine: an intelligent system whose memory, incentives and actions are governed by the individual it represents.

business_model: Consumer product plus B2B2C integrations; Domovoy hardware planned at a $199 reservation and $2,999 starting price
product_category: Personal context and memory layer, with planned local hardware

outcome_analysis: Egoist Machines is an Active Summer 2026 company that announced a $3M seed round and public launch of AI Passport in October 2026. Founders have Cambridge, OpenAI and security backgrounds. The risk is platform capture, since assistants are adding their own memory and import tools.

name: Elimentary
one_liner: Agents that run middle/back-office operations for Private Capital
long_description:
Elimentary’s is building AI agents that can run middle/back-office operations for private capital managers, starting with structured credit. Most private capital managers focus primarily on sourcing and capital deployment. Meanwhile post-investment operations receive step-child treatment. While AUMs have increased exponentially over the last decade, operations continue to be painfully supported by humans using spreadsheets and emails. Things have started to break leading to investment write-offs, fines, penalties, and sometimes lost LP relationships. 

Our agents can run these operations (borrowing base calcs, cracking loan tapes, NAV calculations, etc.) end to end autonomously. For one of our customers, our agents cut a 20-hour ops process to 30 minutes. It saved 90% of the manual hours, translating to $150k in annual savings.

name: Elite
one_liner: Healthcare AI
long_description:
Elite builds AI voice agents that run the front office for healthcare practices. Elite answers every patient call instantly and finishes the job inside the practice's EHR: scheduling, triage, referrals, refills, eligibility, intake, and billing, across voice, SMS, and web, around the clock.

Front offices are drowning in phone volume, so patients wait on hold, calls go unanswered, and staff get pulled away from care. Elite picks up every call, resolves the routine ones end to end, and escalates anything complex to the team with full context. It ships knowing the scheduling protocols of 18 specialties and writes back to more than 19 EHRs including Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, and ModMed. There is no rip-and-replace, it goes live in days, and every resolved patient interaction is what we charge for.

Our starting point is healthcare. The mission is to rebuild the critical industries America runs on, including government, finance, insurance, and manufacturing, by deploying AI agents into the slow, manual workflows at their core.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Healthcare practices that want phone and patient access work handled by AI voice agents

outcome_analysis: Elite is an active Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. The company site now frames the business as a multi-industry software rebuild with healthcare coming soon, which suggests the focus may still be shifting.

name: Elithia
tags: Health Tech; B2B; LegalTech; Insurance; AI
one_liner: Agents for the medical review behind every claim
long_description:
US workers' compensation paid out $64.1 billion in 2023. Personal injury, malpractice, and other insurance claims add billions more. Behind every one of these claims sit thousands of pages of medical records, and a clinician spends hours or days reading them to reconstruct what happened to the patient.

Elithia is building agents to do this work.

Our agents reconstruct patient histories, reason across conflicting evidence, and produce defensible analyses, with every finding cited to the original record.

We've sold to physician expert witnesses and medical-legal firms, turning thousands of pages into court-ready chronologies an expert can verify in minutes. Next: TPAs and insurers, where the same review sits behind every injury claim.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Physician expert witnesses and medical-legal firms, next TPAs, insurers and law firms handling injury claims
problem: Clinicians spend hours or days reading thousands of pages of records to reconstruct a patient history for a claim. Elithia agents build cited, verifiable timelines.

The founder's quant finance background and early sales to physician experts and medical-legal agencies are the main signals. The medical chronology market already had funded players, so the wedge into insurers and TPAs will matter.

name: Elyra
one_liner: AI Reservation System for Restaurants
long_description:
Elyra is an AI reservation system for restaurants. Instead of missing 40% of incoming phone calls and taking days to reply to emails, leaving over $100,000 in bookings on the table every year, restaurants get AI agents that answer every call and email instantly, 24/7, connected to a reservation system that optimizes table placements in real time so empty seats get filled with the right guests.

Felix and Alan met in primary school in Stockholm and have been building things together ever since.

We launched with a single restaurant and within weeks they hit record occupancy, bookings they used to miss were suddenly being captured automatically, and empty Tuesday nights started filling up. Today we power top restaurants groups. 

There are over 1 million restaurants in the US and Europe alone. The average restaurant loses $100K+ a year to missed calls and slow email replies. At our current pricing, that's a $10B+ market opportunity, and we're the only system that handles the call, the email, and the table allocation in one place.
regions: Sweden; Europe
target_customer: Restaurants and restaurant groups, starting in Sweden
problem: Restaurants miss a large share of calls and reply slowly to email, losing bookings. Elyra answers calls and emails with AI and optimizes table allocation.

product_category: AI reservation and guest communication system for restaurants
market_need_then: The company claims restaurants miss 40% of calls and lose $100K a year; figures are self-reported. A Swedish feature says the founders found the idea when nobody answered at a restaurant.
outcome_analysis: Elyra is an active Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. Childhood friends with engineering and business training built a restaurant AI system and report restaurant group customers in Stockholm. Voice reservation competitors already existed, so differentiation through table allocation and email handling is the open question.

name: Emdash
one_liner: One app for all your coding agents
long_description:
Emdash brings Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents into one app.

Run agents in parallel on your own infrastructure, Emdash Cloud or locally. Start tasks from Slack, Linear or GitHub, and let agents keep working after you close your laptop. Access sessions from web, desktop or mobile.

Share environments, skills, MCP servers and secrets across your team, with centralized access and spend controls. Bring your existing AI subscriptions and cloud commitments. No lock-in.

The category was crowded and exposed to coding agent vendors, so monetizing teams is the key question.

long_description: Enact creates the physical environments to benchmark and hill climb robotics models on high-value tasks. We find where robots fail, and fix them with our in-house training loop.

name: End Close
one_liner: AI powered reconciliation for high-volume payments companies
long_description:
End Close builds automatic reconciliation for payments companies like fintechs, marketplaces, banks and payroll companies. Reconciliation helps companies track every dollar and resolve every exception, ensuring they have no money loss, can report audit ready financials, and stay compliant.

Sean (CEO) spent the last 6 years building the reconciliation org at Modern Treasury (S18), processing a trillion dollars in payments across 40 banks with 99.995% automation. Fast growing companies like Modern Treasury are forced to build a solution in-house or buy a legacy solution. End Close provides a modern reconciliation system that works with a company's existing stack and is managed by AI agents.

Exception handling is where 99% of the manual work happens today, payment ops teams spend hours gathering context across various data sources to investigate each ticket. End Close provides an AI ops agent that connects to a company's data warehouse, invoicing platform and payment processors to triage and resolve issues without human intervention.

Legacy providers only provide reconciliation for month end close applications. End Close continuously reconciles with developer friendly APIs, allowing teams to integrate real time payments data within their products to create product experiences for customers like faster balance top-ups, instant trading etc. 

New payment rails and agent-to-agent payments are increasing online transaction volumes, making reconciliation a growing challenge for companies. David (CTO and 2nd time YC founder) most recently built these kinds of high-scale ingestion pipelines when starting and leading error tracking at PostHog (W20), the fastest growing product in the company's history.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: High-volume payments companies such as fintechs, marketplaces, banks and payroll companies
problem: Payment ops teams spend hours gathering context to resolve reconciliation exceptions, and legacy tools only reconcile at month end, so companies build in-house or buy slow systems.
business_model: B2B software, pricing quoted per customer based on transaction volume and integrations
product_category: AI payments reconciliation
competitors_at_founding: BlackLine and Trintech (Adra, Cadency); Modern Treasury; Numeric
market_need_then: Company says exception handling is where most manual payment ops work happens, and new payment rails and agent payments raise volumes. The need is vendor-stated.
outcome_analysis: End Close is a very young Winter 2026 company with two founders who built reconciliation at Modern Treasury and error tracking at PostHog. No exit or distress has been reported and no outcome can be judged yet; the main risks are crowded AI reconciliation competition and low defensibility of the agent layer.

name: Enjamb Labs
one_liner: The AI Workforce for Biopharma
long_description:
We've worked with 130 life science companies, preclinical through phase 3, to deploy AI securely inside the systems they already work in.

Pharma runs on decades of closed software like Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, and SAS. None of it has an AI layer or speaks MCP, so agents cannot reach the systems where the work lives.

Enjamb is that layer. Our agents run on top of existing systems and data, with no migration, and they reach the lab systems and internal tools no other AI touches. They learn how a team works, then do the work in Slack, in Teams, and in the systems themselves, across preclinical research, clinical evidence, trial design, statistical programming, and regulatory submissions.

This is AI tailored for how medicine gets made.

name: Eos AI
one_liner: Autonomous OS for healthcare
long_description:
Eos helps clinics turn their data into actionable insights to identify more eligible patients and early care interventions.

We harmonize historical data across all systems to create standardized patient data distributions, acting like a translation layer between different applications. Then we build a centralized index over it: a compressed representation that lets petabytes of raw data stay where it is while allowing us to search and reason across it as one system.

Instead of treating the visit or document as an isolated instance, we can look at it as a continuous story. We can predict how a case will resolve, trigger the required approvals and actions, and do so while reducing staff workload and recovering hospital revenue.

name: Evardi
one_liner: Agents that engineer the grid edge
long_description: At least 94% of US outage minutes start on the distribution grid, and most utilities are blind between the substation and the meter. Evardi builds a live model of a utility’s network from data it already has, matching every meter to its transformer and using virtual meters to show load and solar on every transformer. On top of that model, our AI agents do the engineering work utilities need at the grid edge: checking switching orders, finding outages after extreme weather and planning for new load from DERs and data centers. Because the model sees every transformer, it will also help utilities decide when new wires are really needed, and how distribution load can free up transmission for new data centers. We’re working with utilities across the globe that together serve over 10 million customers.

name: Evergrove

On average, our customers see a 40% increase in workflow completion, 10x decrease in cycle times, and >60% reduction in cost.

We think voice agents are the starting point for solving slow and fragmented care coordination in this market. Companies that manage an injured worker's care rely on short-staffed contact centres and archaic methods of info exchange: phone, fax, and email. Every delay along the path of care leads to slower rehab of the injured worker, lower throughput for providers, and higher expense for the insurer/employer.

name: Executor

Executor.sh is an MCP gateway that allows you to sign in once to all of your integrations and use them with any client.

We enable you to connect your agents to anything (MCP, GraphQL, OpenAPI) so regardless of what you're trying to connect agents to you're able to.

If you're trying to scale agents to access all of your production services, data, etc, you need Executor as a unified management layer.

name: Exosat
tags: Space Exploration; Satellites; Aerospace; Telecommunications; AI
one_liner: Building a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink
long_description:
Exosat is building thousands of low-cost communication satellites to provide a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. By designing our satellites with zero ITAR/EAR-controlled content, we can leverage manufacturers anywhere in the world to produce our satellites at under a tenth of the cost and launch them from other nations to bypass capacity bottlenecks and access equatorial orbits. 

We're starting off by selling connectivity to device OEMs and network operators, but will eventually use the distributed compute across our constellation to run low-latency inference for robots and autonomous vehicles in remote and rural areas anywhere on the planet.

We've already signed hundreds of millions in LOIs to work with operators across Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, booked our first satellite launch next year, and hold an 11,000 satellite filing with the ITU to build the largest comms network outside of the U.S. and China.
