name: Expanse
one_liner: Twice the work from the GPUs you already own
long_description:
Expanse delivers compute certainty. Its software predicts exactly what every AI workload needs before it runs, so organisations can do more with the GPU infrastructure they already own, privately and on their own hardware.

Every AI breakthrough begins with a compute decision, and today that decision is a guess. Ask for too little and the job dies hours in. Ask for too much and the hardware sits reserved and idle while other work waits. Expanse replaces the guess with evidence, before a single GPU is committed.

We're four engineers who ran and managed GPU clusters at some of the world's largest quantitative hedge funds, following earlier research at national supercomputing scale. This was the tool we always wanted, so we built it.

name: Fabraix
one_liner: The world's frontier hacker of AI agents.
long_description:
Fabraix builds state-of-the-art AI red-teaming agents that continuously detect security vulnerabilities in customer-facing AI. Our product, Nyx, has already found vulnerabilities in agents at dozens of Fortune 500 companies. 

AI agents can change more often than teams can test them. A new model, prompt, tool, permission, or data source can change what an agent does, even when the application code stays the same. And AI is also increasing how much software companies produce and how often it changes. We built Nyx to automate the work required to red-team AI agents. It is multi modal by design and interacts with the target indirectly through controlled replicas of SaaS products and websites that we maintain, placing malicious payloads in webpages, documents, files, messages, and tool outputs to test how an agent behaves under different conditions.

We're also the team behind ACE (Adversarial Cost to Exploit), a benchmark that measures AI security in terms of how much it costs attackers to break an AI system; providing a game-theoretic framework to understand how motivated a rational attacker would be in exploiting the system.

name: Faraday
tags: B2B; Manufacturing; Enterprise Software; AI; Industrial
one_liner: Industrial aOS coordinating humans, agents, and machines
long_description:
Industrial and legacy enterprises still rely on people to coordinate disconnected layers of systems. Automating this work has required an FDE services approach in the past, because so much of it is bespoke and company specific.

Faraday is a self-improving platform that take on this operational work. It connects to their existing software and machines and automatically builds RL environments around each company’s workflows and data. Each job the agents do is checked against those environments, and the results are used to train them. The agents get better on their own with no additional work.

Continuous learning turns each company’s expertise into a compounding asset. Completed work, corrections, and employee feedback improve the agents, and those improvements carry into future jobs. The business preserves its knowledge while becoming more capable over time.

As these agents take on more workflows, Faraday will be the shared runtime coordinating work between humans, agents, and robots across the business.

product_category: Industrial AI agent platform and operations software

name: Fire Wallet
one_liner: Fire Wallet is a privacy-first crypto wallet designed to just work,…
long_description:
🔥FIRE WALLET 🔥

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JeXDDegwhgA

TL;DR: Fire Wallet is a fast, end-to-end encrypted, non-custodial stablecoin wallet with built-in payment processing and fiat on/off ramps, built by the team that created MobileCoin, the cryptocurrency inside Signal.

Hey Bookface! We're Josh, Michael, and Manny and we're building Fire Wallet!

🔥Why we built this

Most wallets and payment processors don’t work FOR you. They're slow, route your payments in the way that earns them the most, and they leak your financial life to anyone asking. Worse: every single one hold the keys to your money.

We believe your financial tools should act in your interest and, frankly, that your money should be yours.

 🔥What Fire does

Multi-chain, non-custodial, end-to-end encrypted wallet. 
Your keys, your money, your assets: you are in full control of your funds at all times. 
Least Cost Routing. Every swap and payment takes the cheapest path, not the one that pays a middleman the most.
Self-sovereign payment processing. Send an invoice straight from the wallet. Get paid from your web checkout. No middleman.
Easy fiat on/off ramps. Move stablecoins to USD and back without the pain.
Built for agentic commerce. Manage per-agent sub-wallets for agentic workflows.
Encrypted by default. Protecting you from bad actors and surveillance capitalism.

🔥Early traction

Signed our first major LOI with @Trustboop (founded by Justice Laub of Drone Racing League and Rob Rhinehart of Soylent).

Onboarding our first enterprise customer in ecommerce packaging and marketing, doing about $1.5M/month in volume. They've connected us to 10 more companies in the same vertical at similar volume, roughly a $100M/yr GMV opportunity.

🔥Why us

Josh and Manuel led the creation of MobileCoin, the cryptocurrency in Signal Messenger: $100M+ raised, $1.16B peak valuation, $4B+ peak coin market cap, acquired in 2026. They understand what it takes to build a cryptographic business.

Michael runs product and design. He's an internationally exhibited artist with two published art books, and he builds beautiful products.

Manuel runs operations and orchestrates systems that actually work at scale.

🔥Asks

Intros to businesses moving $1M+/month in payments, especially cross-border, ecommerce, and DTC, who want lower fees and more control over their funds.

Strategic partners in fintech and payments interested in integrating our infrastructure.
Tell us what's broken. Reply here or email founders@fire.co.

We're looking for our first 100 customers. If that's you or someone you know, we'd love to talk.

name: Floracene
tags: Health Tech; Medical Devices; Digital Health; Enterprise Software; Healthcare IT
one_liner: Vibecode + deploy HIPAA-compliant internal tools, no eng team needed
long_description:
Floracene lets any healthcare operator describe the internal tool they need and deploy it in one click - connected to production data, with read and write access scoped by the user. Think Lovable or Retool, except purpose-built for the needs of healthcare business that has no engineering team.

The bottleneck in healthcare isn't building anymore. Anyone can vibecode an 80% solution in an afternoon, custom to their own workflow, with people already on staff. The tool then dies locally on the builder’s computer, because IT (correctly) won't let anyone deploy a tool touching PHI without first-class authentication and permissioning. Our first customer had multiple employees who had each built useful tools and dashboards locally, but couldn’t actually share these with coworkers or connect to their core practice data. Within weeks of implementing Floracene, they were able to consolidate their BI tooling into Floracene and shipped 4 net-new to production.

A staggering ~$200B is spent on administrative software in healthcare every year in the US. Tens of thousands of those companies still run core operations on spreadsheets, and we're at the top of the first inning of AI adoption.

Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.

name: Foaster
one_liner: AI infrastructure for consulting teams to run engagements with agents
long_description:
Foaster is building the AI infrastructure for consulting teams to run engagements with agents.

Consultants will soon direct more intelligence than any firm could ever hire. As agents take on entire workstreams, consultants will guide their work, build trust with clients, and lead change. This intelligence explosion will expand what a firm can deliver: deeper investigations, bigger problems, and entirely new types of engagements.

Foaster builds and operates the AI infrastructure behind these engagements. Our Forward Deployed Engineers configure and deploy Foaster around each firm’s methods, knowledge, and workflows, in the firm’s environment or on-premise at its clients. Once deployed, consultants run their engagements on Foaster, while our dedicated team maintains the infrastructure and advances its capabilities through applied research and benchmarking on real consulting work.

Each engagement builds a knowledge graph of the client that can be reused and extended in future work. Approved lessons strengthen the firm’s methods, while advances in models expand its capabilities. Over time, each firm builds its own intelligence layer, grounded in its expertise and the organizations it serves.

We developed this approach by running more than 20 consulting engagements ourselves during our time at Y Combinator. Using AI-led interviews at scale and autonomous process mapping, our agents investigated organizations in far greater depth than a human team could. But they could not automate the human side of an engagement: building trust, navigating difficult decisions, and leading change. So we are now bringing that technology to consulting teams.

one_liner: Keeping contractors on the job site, not behind a desk.
long_description:
Foreman is the all-in-one AI-powered project management platform built for construction contractors and the trade industry.
Today, contractors run complex businesses on a patchwork of tools that were never designed for construction — estimates in spreadsheets, plans in email, proposals copy-pasted from old Word docs, photos scattered across phones. Nothing talks to anything else, and the admin work never stops.
Foreman replaces that patchwork with a single platform that manages the full lifecycle of a construction job, from first estimate to final invoice. Contractors upload plans, photos, or a project description, and Foreman's AI instantly generates structured takeoffs, scoped estimates, and professional proposals — in minutes, not hours. From there, every customer record, document, permit, photo, change order, and conversation lives in one place, organized around the job.
The result: contractors spend less time buried in admin and more time building. They bid faster, manage jobs with less chaos, and close projects cleanly — without duct-taping five tools together to do it.

name: Frontier Computing
one_liner: Frontier grows scalable biological brains as an ML training substrate
long_description:
Frontier is first to grow biological brains at scale, serving biological neural nets with substrate-level colocation of memory and compute, enabling highly cost effective training of large parameter count models.

While academia has traditionally been limited to ~1M neurons in vitro, Frontier has built a pathway to scale to 100M+ neurons by circumventing traditional scaling challenges in biological culture, demonstrating this strategy's functionality by training a biological brain using this scaling primitive to play Frogger.

Frontier is now growing exascale compute clusters to produce substrates capable of long-horizon language reasoning while operating at much higher sample efficiencies than traditional architectures, and collocating memory with compute to enable significantly larger parameter counts than would be tractable for training within traditional compute clusters.

Its scale and learning claims come from its own pages and have no independent verification, and rivals Cortical Labs and FinalSpark already sell or rent access. There is no exit or failure to explain yet.

name: Frontrunner
one_liner: Engineer your GTM
long_description:
Frontrunner lets GTM teams describe the work they need done and deploy agents that run it, connected to their existing tools and data. Our customers are building agents for everything from inbound lead routing to signal-based outbound and multi-touch attribution. Think Cursor for GTM: the place to engineer your revenue factory. 

GTM engineers and rev ops teams spend their days stitching tools together; and fielding requests from sales and marketing. Each campaign has its own version of who the customer is, what makes a lead qualified, and which signals matter. When the business changes, someone has to update that logic everywhere. Even teams that can build their own tools end up depending on the person who built them to keep everything running.

Not only does Frontrunner give those agents a shared understanding of your ICP, customers, and gtm motion, but persists that shared understanding automatically when business context changes so that it remains in sync. Sales and marketing build, run, and manage agents against that shared context, using the tools they already know. As prospects move from first touch to closed deal, the results feed back into how agents target, qualify, and engage the next account. Your revenue factory gets smarter with every cycle, optimizing for conversion across the full sales journey.

Our customers range from AI native startups to agencies running GTM for their clients to established businesses supporting large sales teams. They use Frontrunner to turn their best plays into agents their whole team can use.

name: GRU Space
one_liner: Moon Hotel -> The Intergalactic Construction Company of Earth
long_description:
GRU Space is building permanent lunar infrastructure to make humanity interplanetary within our lifetime, starting with the first hotel on the Moon. In just 6 weeks, we built the world's first Moon factory: patent-pending hardware that turns lunar regolith into bricks and inflates modular pressurized habitats designed to withstand lunar temperature and pressure extremes. 

Our first mission lands on the Moon in 2027 to demonstrate in-situ brick manufacturing and habitat deployment. A second mission lays the hotel's foundation inside a lunar cave, and a third opens the first lunar hotel, targeted for 2032. 

We don’t stop at Moon hotels. GRU’s long-term plan:

1. Build the first hotel on the Moon. GRU solves off‑world surface habitation.
2. Become the Moon Base Company of America: build roads, mass drivers, warehouses, and physical infrastructure.
3. Repeat on Mars and build the first cities there.
4. Own property on the Moon and Mars as these economies grow.
5. Reinvest profits into resource utilization systems on the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and beyond—reaching our final form: Galactic Resource Utilization.

GRU Space is backed by investors in SpaceX and Anduril, is part of Nvidia's Inception program, and our launch generated 1B+ views across 60+ countries, earning invitations to the White House, Senate, and Pentagon.

outcome_analysis: GRU Space is an active Winter 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its launch generated large press attention and deposit-based demand signaling, which helped awareness. The core challenges are extreme technical difficulty, dependence on third-party landers, long timelines to 2032, and doubts that the deposits represent real demand.

name: Gamgee
one_liner: Curing cancer. Starting with dogs.
long_description:
​Gamgee began with Rosie, founder Paul Conyngham’s dog. After surgery, chemotherapy and immunotherapy failed, Rosie was given months to live. Paul used AI and genomic analysis to identify targets in her tumour, then worked with scientists at UNSW to produce what is believed to be the first fully computationally designed mRNA cancer vaccine delivered to a dog. Following treatment, several tumours shrank significantly and her quality of life improved

Gamgee is building an end to end platform for personalised mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs. We sequence a dog’s tumour and healthy DNA, identify mutations unique to its cancer, and design a vaccine that teaches the immune system what to attack. We manage the entire process- from vet intake and tissue collection through genomic analysis, vaccine production, treatment and response monitoring

​We are now turning that one off effort into a repeatable clinical system. Gamgee is running clinical trials in Australia, working with vets, oncologists and specialised laboratories, and accepting cases globally. Our goal is to make personalised cancer treatment accessible to every dog that needs it- and use each case to improve the treatment for the next

product_category: Veterinary biotech, personalized mRNA cancer vaccines
market_need_then: Strong emotional and press pull from the Rosie story and growing pet cancer spending; evidence base is thin and the company itself says it is seeking funding for a more rigorous study.
outcome_analysis: Gamgee is an active Summer 2026 company with a 4M seed led by Founders Fund announced 2026-08-17, so no outcome yet. Its strengths are a compelling founder story with wide press and top tier investors. Its main uncertainty is clinical evidence: a single case, a planned trial in Australia and a market already served by approved canine immunotherapies.

name: GatherHQ
one_liner: Applied AI for Enterprise GTM (3X founders, 10X growth, backed by ANT)
long_description:
Gather's long horizon agent serves enterprise GTM teams by continually interviewing real buyers and turning what it learned into content that drives pipeline and simulations that predict customer behavior.

More than 65 enterprise marketing teams, including Envoy, Eclypsium, Cover Genius, Fortinet, CoStar, Bagel Brands, and Family Express, use Gather to continually fight AI slop and create original on-brand, third-party validated thought leadership, reports, ebooks, and campaign content.

The value of that research compounds. Every interview adds to a foundation of quantitative, qualitative, and voice data from over 300,000 real interviews across customers, with thousands added monthly. Our models use that understanding to predict how buyers will respond to messaging, pricing, and market shifts. Each answer includes supporting evidence and a confidence level. When confidence is low, Gather automatically runs new research.

Gather starts by replacing research firms and content agencies, and we aspire to build the real-time customer understanding layer that enterprises will use to drive decisions.

Built by the team that created Cooliris (acquired by Yahoo) and Pulse (acquired by Gartner), and ran Gartner Peer Insights.

name: Glen
one_liner: Institutional Learning Layer for Every Agent in Your Company
long_description:
Glen is the layer that unifies every agent your company runs. Glen pulls in agent sessions from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, plus Slack messages, GitHub prs, tickets, docs and calls. When a new agent picks up a task, Glen finds relevant prior context and injects it in the agents context window to steer it, producing knowledge work that is significantly higher quality, faster and cheaper.

Glen does more. You can query the original agent behind any line of code, or search every session your org has ever run. It distills what your team does into skills and surfaces the right one automatically. Agents work multiplayer, picking up the style and context of whoever else is on the file. Transcripts are unified across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, so you can hand a session from one to another mid-task. And Glen can also double as a company brain, from Slack, in app, or by just installing Glen on any agent.

We’re building toward a future where memory is no longer the missing piece of intelligence. A future where every agent maintains a lossless and continuous thread of institutional experience enabling the era of the compounding organization and fully unsupervised digital labour.

product_category: Agent memory and institutional context layer

outcome_analysis: Glen is a one person company in the Summer 2026 batch with early design partners and no public funding. The bet is that shared memory across agents matters, but memory is a crowded space and platform vendors may absorb the feature.

name: Gojiberry AI
one_liner: AI Go-To-Market agents for B2B teams
long_description:
Gojiberry is building the AI GTM team for B2B companies.

We start with outbound: Gojiberry finds buyers showing intent, enriches them, reaches out, follows up, handles replies, and books qualified meetings.

Companies use Gojiberry to replace the old way of doing outbound: buying tools, hiring SDRs & agencies, testing lists, writing messages, and guessing what works. Gojiberry turns it into one AI team that finds buyers and books meetings.

Every campaign makes Gojiberry smarter. It learns which buyers convert, which signals matter, which messages get replies, and which actions create revenue. Over time, Gojiberry uses what works across similar companies and industries to help every new customer get better results from day one.

Long term, Gojiberry will become the system that finds every revenue opportunity and acts on it: outbound leads, website visitors, inbound leads, old CRM leads, replies, meetings, CRM updates, new campaign ideas, and account expansion.

The goal is to make every B2B company able to run a high-performing GTM team without hiring one.

We grew from $0 to $2.5M ARR in 10 months, are growing 30% MoM, profitable, and used by 2,000+ customers.

Customers get 2-5x more positive replies than traditional outbound.

Graphide CI runs your CI 10-20× faster than GitHub runners on enterprise deployments, and our 24/7 agents optimize the CI itself, not just the machines. For teams with big CI bills that haven't been optimized, we cut costs 70%+ and take over the ongoing work of optimizing CI, so you can focus on your product.

We're faster and cheaper because we own both the hardware and the optimizations and configs that run on it, which lets us do what owning only one could not. A graph of the codebase runs only the tests each change can reach, and we run your tests in parallel, so your CI is limited only by the length of your longest test. Our agents then tune machines, caches and test splits as you add more tests and code over time. We also patch the tests themselves, fixing flakes and adding our own libraries so they run faster and more reliably.

Coding agents now write more code than teams can check, making verification the new bottleneck. CI is where we start, but we also cover the rest of the verification stack. Our PR review agent runs the old and new code in live environments, finding bugs and proving them by writing tests (50% more bugs found than Greptile on our benchmarks, with 35% fewer false positives). Our visualizer shows data flows and graph-based diffs so you can understand a PR in seconds.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams with large, unoptimized GitHub Actions CI bills
problem: CI is slow and expensive, and AI coding agents produce more code than teams can verify, making verification the bottleneck.
business_model: Fixed monthly price per org for CI runners quoted from usage; AI PR review at $1 per pull request after 10 free
product_category: CI runners and AI code review
market_need_then: Teams complain about GitHub hosted runner cost, and runner vendors report migrations cutting cost to a quarter in one anecdote. AI generated code raises review load.
outcome_analysis: Graphide is a Fall 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. It enters a crowded GitHub Actions runner market with funded rivals and adds an AI review product, so it must differentiate on its graph based test selection and agent tuning rather than raw runner speed.

name: Graphify Labs
one_liner: Shared Understanding of Codebase for Agents and Developers
long_description:
Graphify is a Knowledge Graph control plane for enterprise software. The open-source tool has 116K+ GitHub stars and 6.5M+ downloads, and is used in production by engineers at Shopify, Datadog, JP Morgan, American Express, Harvey, Automation Anywhere, and Vanguard.

On top of that graph, our enterprise layer reviews every pull request and formally verifies each code change: it proves the new behavior matches the old, or hands back the exact input that breaks it. That makes it built for the changes teams fear most, like refactors, framework upgrades, and large-scale migrations, where you need proof that nothing broke, not a guess.

The graph updates itself as the code changes and keeps context instead of forgetting it, so your whole team and their coding agents work from one shared, always-current view of the codebase instead of a thousand private threads.

It runs entirely inside your perimeter, fully air-gapped on-premise or self-hosted in your own cloud, so no code or data ever leaves your environment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Enterprise engineering organizations and developers using AI coding agents
problem: Coding agents and developers lack a shared, current understanding of large codebases, and risky changes like migrations need proof that nothing broke.
business_model: Open source core (free), hosted free tier, per seat Pro and Teams, enterprise self hosted tier
product_category: Codebase knowledge graph and formal verification for code changes
market_need_then: AI coding assistants spread widely in 2025 and 2026 and developers adopted a free graph tool quickly: the company blog says it passed 100,000 GitHub stars within 117 days of the first commit.
outcome_analysis: Graphify Labs is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. A solo founder's weekend open source project hit over 100k GitHub stars quickly, giving unusual distribution. The open question is converting free developer use into enterprise revenue while lookalike tools and coding assistants compete.

name: Gravy
one_liner: Agents that move money, trade stocks, and file taxes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

product_category: AI personal finance agent

name: GrayPass
one_liner: Verify the expected person is still in control before sensitive…
long_description:
Login tells you who signed in. GrayPass helps apps check who’s behind sensitive actions and whether they’re authorized before those actions go through.

It combines identity, device and session context with behavioral signals like typing rhythm, cursor movement and scrolling. Before a sensitive action goes through, GrayPass evaluates that evidence against your team’s policy and returns a decision: allow, challenge, hold or deny. Your app enforces the decision.

This applies to actions like exporting sensitive data, changing admin permissions or allowing an AI agent to act on someone’s behalf. Allowed actions receive short-lived, signed proof tied to the exact action and your app.

Your existing login and authentication stack stays in place.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Software companies that need to protect sensitive in app actions such as data exports, admin changes and AI agent actions
problem: Login proves who signed in but not who is behind a sensitive action later in the session, especially with session hijacking and AI agents acting for users.
business_model: B2B API priced by evaluation request (pricing not published; request evaluation)
product_category: Pre-action authorization and behavioral biometrics
market_need_then: Analysts say passkeys push attackers toward session hijacking, raising value of continuous checks, and AI agents acting for users create new authorization questions. Market size estimates are around $3 to 4 billion for 2026.
outcome_analysis: GrayPass is a Fall 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. Two very young founders target post login authorization, a space with strong incumbents in behavioral biometrics. Reported traction (900,000 sessions, $50,000 revenue) is company claimed and unverified.

name: Grep AI
one_liner: Self-improving agents that automate your growth bottlenecks
long_description:
Grep AI is the fastest way to create, optimize, and deploy agents for tedious, complex operational work that slows down your business. Our self-improving agents learn from every run, making them smarter and cheaper as you scale. IG.com a global retail brokerage used our agents to review compliance alerts and now 80% of their customers onboad without manual intervention, doubling first trades and propelling them to a FTSE 100 company. 

Customers including Airwallex, Worldpay, Citizens Bank, FV Bank and Shopmonkey have used our agents to automate over 250,000 of operational work across compliance, onboarding, underwriting, corporate due diligence, document verification, merchant categorization, market and competitive research, rev ops and much more.

We founded Grep AI after experiencing firsthand how manual workflows can prevent a business from growing when we ran the platform team at Brex. We're now on a mission to rid businesses of tedious, repetitive so their employees can focus on the most high leverage tasks that matter.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Financial services firms, fintechs and other enterprises with heavy operational workloads such as compliance, onboarding and underwriting
problem: Manual operational workflows like KYC, KYB and compliance review slow businesses down and are costly to staff.
business_model: Managed platform for building and running AI agents, sold to enterprises (pricing not published)
product_category: AI agents for operations and compliance
market_need_then: In 2023 fintech compliance teams faced heavy manual KYC and KYB review. The founders ran platform and data teams at Brex and saw the bottleneck first hand.
outcome_analysis: Parcha raised a $5M seed in 2023 as a pre revenue Brex founder team, then widened into Grep, a general agent platform with named enterprise customers like Citizens Bank, Airwallex and Worldpay. It joined YC in Fall 2026 and has no outcome yet. No Series A was found.

name: Greypoint Industries
one_liner: Building drone swarms that hunt hidden enemies.
long_description: We build LEGION, a drone swarm that identifies, geolocates, and tracks every emitter on the battlefield using the enemy’s own radio signals. LEGION enables our warfighters to precisely track previously obscured targets like jammers, command posts, and drone operators so they can proactively respond to threats instead of reacting to them.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Military forces (warfighters) needing to locate enemy emitters such as jammers, command posts and drone operators
problem: Battlefield emitters are hard to find and track, so forces react to threats instead of anticipating them.
business_model: Defense hardware and software contracts (a first contract was announced by the CEO in June 2026 per a profile)
product_category: Defense drone swarms and RF emitter geolocation
founder_names: Darcy Zhang; Nic Chu; Jordan Khoo; Steven Xu

outcome_analysis: Greypoint is a Summer 2026 YC defense startup with no outcome yet. A four person team with defense and sensing backgrounds sells a drone swarm for emitter tracking, a technically hard field with funded rivals. Defense contract timing will decide its progress.

name: Grip
one_liner: Robots for waste manipulation
long_description: Grip is a robotics company building intelligent robotic systems for waste and recycling. We are starting with organic waste, where removing contaminants from messy, constantly changing streams remains difficult and highly manual. Our technology combines learning-based manipulation and custom hardware to identify and pick objects, learning from real-world operating data, including every successful and failed grasp, to become more reliable and adaptable over time. This helps waste operators reduce manual sorting, recover more valuable material, lower contamination, and deploy automation flexibly across facilities. Over time, Grip aims to expand beyond organics and build the intelligent manipulation layer for trash in general, making waste processing and the circular economy more efficient and scalable.
regions: Switzerland; Europe
target_customer: Waste and recycling operators, starting with organic waste facilities
problem: Removing contaminants from messy, changing organic waste streams is manual and difficult to automate.
business_model: Robotic systems sold to waste operators (hardware; pricing not published)
product_category: Learning based robotic manipulation for waste sorting
market_need_then: Operators struggle with contamination in organics and manual sorting; AMP is pairing organics sorting with biochar, signaling market interest.
outcome_analysis: Grip is a Summer 2026 YC robotics startup with no outcome yet. Two ETH linked robotics engineers target organic waste sorting, a harder niche than standard recycling where AMP reports unpredictable results. Success will depend on grasp reliability in real facilities.

name: Grocalo
one_liner: AI brain for creators that runs their social content
long_description:
Grocalo (S26) is an AI brain that runs content for creators. We understand their audiences, using video understanding and deep platform analytics to bottle up the taste behind each creator and personalize and distribute content to creator specific audiences.

Grocalo generated 2B views and gained 4M followers for our creators in the last 2 months. Some of our clients include Jimmy O. Yang (Comedian, 11M followers), King Bach (72M followers), Leenda Dong (28M followers), Steven He (30M followers), Sheena Melwani (18M followers), and Jeannie Mai (TV host, 6M followers).

Content should be personalized and data-driven. We’ve developed the most advanced AI brain replicating viral content for any given audience.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Social media creators and personalities (clients named include comedians, TV hosts and influencers with up to 72M followers)
problem: Creators struggle to produce, personalize and distribute data driven content across platforms.
business_model: Invite only service for creators (pricing not published)
product_category: AI content operations for creators
market_need_then: Creators publish across many platforms and tool roundups in 2026 show heavy AI tool use. The company claims 2B views and 4M followers gained for clients in two months (unverified).
outcome_analysis: Grocalo is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. It pairs a finance background CEO with a repeat YC technical founder and claims large creator clients, but sells into a crowded tool category where a related AI creator suite already retreated.

name: Gutgutgoose
one_liner: We sequence your gut and build the probiotics it’s missing
long_description:
Most data companies pay for their data. Ours pays for itself.
Customers send us a stool sample. We sequence it, build a metabolic model of that gut, and simulate whether each probiotic strain has an open niche it can colonize. We formulate the best candidates, then re-sequence 90 days later to see what actually took hold and what changed. Each cycle gives us the baseline gut, the intervention, and the outcome. At scale, the endgame is models that predict chronic disease years before symptoms.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers who want gut health improvements and will pay a monthly subscription for personalized probiotics
problem: Off the shelf probiotics are built for an average gut. Gutgutgoose sequences a customer's stool sample, models which probiotic strains have an open niche to colonize, formulates a custom blend and re-sequences later to check what took hold.
business_model: Consumer subscription (about $93 to $183 per month) with at-home sequencing and a retest, plus a 180 day money-back guarantee
product_category: Personalized probiotics and microbiome sequencing
competitors_at_founding: Viome; Floré; Ombre (formerly Thryve); Tiny Health
market_need_then: Consumer demand for gut health testing is visible in many 2026 comparison guides, while a 2026 review notes scientific doubt about microbiome supplement claims. Early traction reported on the YC page: 20 of 50 attendees at an endometriosis event joined the waitlist.
outcome_analysis: Gutgutgoose is an active Summer 2026 company, so there is no outcome yet. The case for it is a data loop that pays for itself through subscriptions and founders with biology and modelling depth. The risks are scientific proof that strain-level prediction works, crowded personalized probiotic competitors and consumer acquisition cost. No funding beyond the standard YC deal was verified.

name: HABU
one_liner: Like Crosby, but for real estate development
long_description:
HABU is an AI-native real estate development firm that helps real estate investors deploy capital to build housing faster, at lower cost, and with higher yield. 

We're building an internal AI-native operating system that completes 90%+ of development tasks at 95% faster processing speeds while delivering the same outcomes customers expect externally: high yield, low risk projects. We're selling the outcome, not the inputs to the outcome. 

Developers are service providers for white-collar investors: they find land, construct buildings, and operate and sell them for a profit. Our customers don't care how the projects are sourced or managed, only that they are completed on time and produce the forecasted returns. 

We use agentic workflows, geospatial analysis and mapping, and development-specific workflow automation to manage the end-to-end process. The result is 5x more projects per FTE compared to a non-AI developer, 20% faster project schedules, and 10-15% lower total project costs. 

We're *not* long term property owners, strictly the service provider (fee/merchant developer).

$160B was deployed into multifamily in 2025 and $534B into commercial real estate overall. Developers naturally have high operating margins and we are building to be the most operationally and capital efficient developer in the country. 

Starting first with multifamily in Phoenix and then expanding nationally.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Institutional and white-collar real estate investors who want multifamily housing built without running a developer themselves
problem: Development is slow, labor heavy and fragmented. HABU acts as the fee or merchant developer, using AI workflows to find land, build, operate and sell multifamily projects faster and cheaper.
business_model: Fee and merchant real estate development services for investor capital, not SaaS and not long-term ownership
product_category: AI-native real estate developer
market_need_then: The company cites $160B deployed into multifamily in 2025 and a housing shortage thesis. These are company-stated figures. Developers are described as service providers to investors.
outcome_analysis: HABU is an active Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its edge is a CEO with real development experience paired with a Meta-trained AI lead, selling outcomes to investors instead of software. The main uncertainties are whether AI really cuts cost and schedule by the claimed 10 to 20 percent, access to capital partners and the cyclical, capital heavy nature of development.

name: HERA
tags: B2B; Design; Design Tools; Manufacturing; Industrial
one_liner: Agents for Industrials
long_description: At Hera, we build physical AI tools that help heavy engineering teams bring products to market up to 20× faster. Today, we work with manufacturers of data center ancillary equipment, renewable energy systems, robotics, heat exchangers, power plants and pressure vessels.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering and quality teams at manufacturers of pressure vessels, aerospace, semiconductor, medical device and custom machinery parts
problem: Reviewing 2D mechanical drawings for GD&T, tolerance stack-ups and standards compliance takes a day or more per drawing and misses errors that scrap parts. HERA automates the review against ASME Y14.5 and ISO.

name: HEVN, inc
one_liner: Cross-border payments for exporters of physical goods.
long_description:
HEVN is a B2B financial platform built for global commerce. We solve the last-mile problem in cross-border payments by working with licensed local payment service providers and settling transactions through domestic payment rails instead of relying on international bank transfers.

HEVN helps importers and exporters move money between jurisdictions with fewer intermediaries and faster, more predictable settlement.

A team that already scaled a crypto wallet to 15 million users brings product and audience skills, which may lower acquisition cost. The risks are heavy compliance dependence on partners, a crowded field adding stablecoin accounts in 2026 and regulatory exposure in several jurisdictions.

name: Haladir
one_liner: Operational Intelligence for Global Logistics
long_description: Haladir builds advanced AI decision intelligence systems for logistics. Our systems are built for warehousing, fulfillment and transportation operations, deciding with AI and optimization solvers what happens today and what changes over time, from one site to the whole network. Today's AI brought intelligence. The next frontier is judgement.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: 3PLs and fulfillment providers, distributors, manufacturers and brands running warehouses and transportation; also frontier AI labs buying RL environments
problem: Logistics operations make constrained planning decisions across WMS, TMS and ERP systems that generic LLMs handle poorly and legacy optimizers handle rigidly.
business_model: Enterprise software (planning and execution agents) plus data and RL environments for AI labs
product_category: AI decision intelligence for logistics

It is too recent for a success or failure verdict; the open questions are customer adoption versus established warehouse software vendors and AI logistics startups.

name: Halmos Labs
tags: AI-powered Drug Discovery; Auto Commerce; Swarm AI; Biotech; Automation
one_liner: Rebuilding drug development for automation
long_description:
The drug development pipeline is built around humans. Other AI biotech companies build automation around the established infrastructure. Halmos Labs rebuilds the infrastructure around automation. The central bottleneck is access to experiments. Halmos Labs platform physicalvalidation.com connects agents to biolabs across the globe in days rather than weeks. 

Using physicalvalidation.com, Halmos research agent is continuously designing drugs and has so far designed and tested a new mRNA cancer vaccine and a new antibiotic with results December 10th.
regions: Sweden; Europe
target_customer: Biotech and pharma R&D teams and AI agents that need fast access to wet-lab experiments
problem: Drug development is built around human steps, and access to experiments is the bottleneck. Halmos Labs connects agents to biolabs worldwide through its Physical Validation platform and designs experiments with many coordinated agents.
business_model: B2B platform: marketplace and software for agent-driven experiment design and lab access (pricing not stated)
product_category: AI experiment design and automated drug development infrastructure
founder_names: Mattias Akke; Linus von Ekensteen Lofgren; Linus Sarud
competitors_at_founding: Ginkgo Cloud Lab; Amazon Bio Discovery
market_need_then: Experiment access is cited as the bottleneck; two NeurIPS 2026 workshop papers by the team show research traction, and 2026 coverage describes AI designing and running thousands of experiments.
outcome_analysis: Halmos Labs is an active Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. Founders with published ML research and a thesis that automation needs rebuilt infrastructure target a real bottleneck. The risks are very large competitors with their own labs, unverified drug results and a team of three in a capital heavy field.

name: Harbor
one_liner: AI-native CRO for clinical trial operations
long_description:
Harbor is building an AI-native contract research organization (CRO) for clinical trials. We started with an AI-native system of record for clinical trial data (electronic data capture system), grew the software business to seven trials and ~$187k in contracted software revenue over the next twelve months, then expanded into full-service trial execution and signed our first CRO contract worth $1.93M over three years.

Clinical trials consume 45% of all new drug and device development spend. While some of that goes to software, sites, and patients, the largest line items are services: project management, monitoring, data management, site coordination, source verification, query resolution, record reconciliation, and analysis.

Today, drug and device companies outsource clinical operations to legacy CROs and their massive teams, which is why the CRO market is $82B annually. Harbor delivers the regulated services companies buy from legacy CROs, but built around our AI-native system of record from day one. Our software already automates the core data workflows: study build, data capture, query generation, monitoring, signing, and database lock. Because we own the system of record, we can expand into the surrounding service workflows: site contracting and billing, subject engagement and retention, statistics, reporting, and more.

We built Harbor because we lived through the problem. Albert spent four years in clinical trials and regulatory strategy at a medical device startup, taking an unproven wearable from first-in-human trials to FDA authorization. Nate brings the technical depth, having built scalable software at Google and Ramp and served as employee #1 at a previous YC startup.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Drug and medical device sponsors that run clinical trials
problem: Clinical trials rely on legacy EDC software and large CRO teams. Harbor sells an AI-native EDC and is expanding into full-service trial execution built on that system of record.
business_model: EDC software contracts plus full-service CRO contracts (company states a $1.93M three year CRO contract)
product_category: AI-native EDC and contract research organization
market_need_then: Company cites clinical trials as 45% of new drug and device development spend and an $82B CRO market. Its own early traction: seven trials and about $15.6k monthly software revenue per the YC launch post.
outcome_analysis: Harbor is an active Spring 2026 company with early revenue it states at $187k contracted software revenue and a $1.93M three year CRO contract, both company-reported. The CEO's clinical and FDA background and a CTO from Google and Ramp fit the problem. Risks include incumbents' AI features, long regulated sales cycles and the shift from software to a services business.

name: Hebbian Robotics

long_description: Hebbian Robotics builds open source foundational infrastructure for Physical AI to develop robots that extend what humanity can do, for the benefit of the communities they serve.

problem: Robot training data is messy and hard to search and quality check at scale. Hebbian Robotics ships open source infrastructure (the HFlow SDK) and APIs for processing and verifying physical AI data.

Strong engineers and an open source launch in August 2026 give it a developer-led distribution path, but funded rivals like Encord and Foxglove already serve robotics data teams and an open source SDK is easy to copy, so monetization is the key question.

name: Hedge
one_liner: AI-Native insurance company
long_description: Hedge is an AI-Native specialty insurance company. We help insurance brokers find faster, cheaper, and better coverage for their customers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Licensed retail insurance brokers placing hard-to-place commercial accounts in the excess and surplus market
problem: Wholesale E&S placement is slow and manual. Hedge uses AI to get brokers quotes faster and cheaper, starting at the wholesale layer with plans to add underwriting.
business_model: Wholesale brokerage commissions on placed policies (Taven Insurance Services LLC, doing business as Hedge Specialty)
product_category: AI-native wholesale insurance brokerage

name: Helios Intelligence
tags: Health Tech; Consumer; Diagnostics; Health & Wellness; AI
one_liner: At-home molecular body test: 1,000+ biomarkers from a drop of blood
long_description:
Helios is building a molecular body test from a single drop of blood. Our at-home test measures more than 1,000 biomarkers and turns them into a living model of the body—designed to show what is happening now, surface risk earlier, and become more useful with every test.

By combining longitudinal molecular data with labs, wearables, health records, and outcomes, we are building toward a world model of human biology. Our goal is to simulate all of human health and use that intelligence to help people perform, recover, and live longer.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Health-conscious consumers who would buy an at-home blood test and ongoing biomarker tracking
problem: Routine blood panels measure few biomarkers and are taken rarely, so people cannot see molecular change in the body early. Helios wants one drop of blood to yield more than 1,000 biomarkers.
business_model: Consumer at-home test kits, likely repeat purchase or subscription (pricing not disclosed)
product_category: At-home molecular diagnostics and AI health model
market_need_then: The company's own pitch is earlier risk detection and personal performance tracking. No dated demand evidence was found beyond the pitch.
outcome_analysis: Helios is an active Fall 2026 YC company with five people and no shipped product, so no outcome exists yet. Its strength is founder market fit: two Harvard faculty with prior diagnostics exits. The main risks are the technical difficulty of a one drop, 1,000 biomarker assay and the regulatory and validation path for a consumer test.

name: Hemlock
one_liner: Force + contact dynamics collected at scale for training physical AI.
long_description: At Hemlock, we equip workers around the globe with EMG wearables to generate force/contact-annotated egocentric video data to give physical AI models a sense of touch from human data. Force + contact dynamics, collected at scale.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robotics and physical AI labs that buy training data with force and contact labels
problem: Video-only robot training data carries no force or touch information. Hemlock records worker hand activity with EMG wearables to add force and contact labels.
business_model: Data foundry selling annotated egocentric datasets to physical AI developers
product_category: Physical AI training data and EMG wearable hardware
market_need_then: Robotics labs were buying large volumes of human video in 2026, and one source cites Skild noting that video lacks force and torque. Hemlock claims adding its data raised egg pick-and-place success tenfold on Pi0.5, a company claim reported by Fondo.
outcome_analysis: Hemlock is an active one-person Fall 2026 YC company selling force-labelled egocentric data for robots, so no outcome exists yet. The idea rides a real data scarcity in physical AI, but a solo founder, crowded data vendors and the need to prove buyers pay for force labels are the open questions.

name: Hesper AI
one_liner: AI Claims Investigator for Insurance
long_description:
Hesper AI builds AI agents that investigate P&C insurance claims end to end.

Hesper’s agents read the claim file, detect tampered documents, verify facts, check coverage, flag inconsistencies, and produce an audit-ready case file in minutes, so insurers can check every claim. 

We work with Claims and SIU orgs at Carriers, MGAs and TPAs,
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Claims and SIU organizations at P&C carriers, MGAs and TPAs
problem: Insurers can only investigate a small share of claims, so fraud and errors slip through. Hesper agents investigate each claim end to end and produce an audit-ready file.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to insurance claims teams (pricing not disclosed)
product_category: AI claims investigation for property and casualty insurance
market_need_then: A 2026 trade article says automated tools now make 45% of SIU referrals while SIU staffing grew about 0.5% in 2024, per the Coalition Against Insurance Fraud. That implies investigator capacity is the bottleneck.
outcome_analysis: Hesper is an active Fall 2026 YC company of three people with no public traction figures yet. Founders have Nanonets sales and engineering experience in document AI, which fits the product. The key risk is a crowded 2026 AI claims market where incumbents already ship agentic investigation.

name: Hessian
one_liner: Forward-deployed AI Agents
long_description: Hessian is the platform for automating business operations with AI agents. We forward deploy on-site to map the work, and build the agents on our platform to run it end-to-end. Unlike off-the-shelf tools that don't know your business, you get a partner that owns the software and operates it every day. Why now? Coding agents have matured to the point where, combined with our engineering judgment we've built across a decade of shipping production systems, we can scale forward-deployed engagements with minimal headcount. Furthermore, our FDE agents and tooling will accelerate how quickly we automate workflows on our platform. We're already saving our customers hundreds of hours a month. Trillions of dollars a year are spent on knowledge work, and we're building the standard for how every company deploys, operates, and governs the AI agents that do it.

name: Hlabs
one_liner: US-Made Parts for Robots
long_description:
HLabs is making an industrial supply chain for building robots in the USA including electronics and actuators, with a focus on in-house manufacturing.

Robotics is going to be one of the largest industries the world has ever seen. Teams have to buy what they can from overseas and then build everything else in house just to get something to move. HLabs is producing a plug and play set of robotic primitives to accelerate the early development and then working with larger scale production robots for bespoke designs.

Early customers span across household robotics, humanoids, robot arms, quadrupeds, and defense.

Hlabs is founded by Paul, a second time YC founder who also participated in the W21 batch with Mystic. He ran Mystic as CEO for 6 years.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robotics builders: household robotics, humanoid, robot arm and quadruped teams, plus defense customers, who want US-made electronics and actuators
problem: Robot teams must buy parts overseas and build the rest in house just to get something moving. HLabs sells a plug and play set of US-made robotic primitives to speed early development.
business_model: Hardware product sales (preorders of boards, motors and actuators) plus bespoke design work for larger production robots
product_category: Robotics components: compute boards, wireless modules, motor controllers, motors and actuators
market_need_then: US robot teams depend on China for parts. Policy moved against Chinese robot imports in 2026 and distributors such as RoboStore pivoted to US production, indicating demand for domestic supply. HLabs customer traction is not independently verified.
outcome_analysis: HLabs is an active W26 company with a solo second time YC founder selling US-made robot electronics and actuators. It rides a 2026 policy shift away from Chinese robot imports, but scale, cost against Chinese suppliers and capital are open risks. No outcome events were found.

name: Hop Aero

long_description: Hop Aero is building rocket cargo vehicles that deliver to contested environments hundreds of miles away in minutes. Our rockets fly point-to-point into the most austere locations at hypersonic speeds. Hop Aero's goal is to provide the U.S. and allies the asymmetric advantage that deters a future major conflict.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Hoplite

No outcome events found.

name: Hopper

We are building the inference layer for voice. Voice agents are latency-sensitive and differentiated enough to warrant a focused inference player, similar to Fal (inference for video) or Sail Research (inference for long horizon agents).

Before this our team wrote megakernels at Meta Reality Labs and ran inference at Salient (a16z-backed voice startup)
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies running latency sensitive voice agents, and developers wanting cheap coding model access
problem: Voice agents need very low latency inference across speech to text, language model and text to speech. Hopper tunes and serves open models on customers' production calls.
business_model: Usage-based inference and post-training services; the company site also sells monthly coding plans from 20 to 200 dollars
product_category: Inference cloud for voice AI
market_need_then: Growth of voice agents in 2026 with latency as a key complaint; Salient's 60M dollar Series A (per the YC page) indicates the sector's funding.
outcome_analysis: Hopper is a two person F26 company from IIT Madras founders with voice inference experience, selling latency optimized open model inference for voice agents. Competition from Deepgram, Cartesia and gateways is strong and funding is undisclosed. No outcome events found.

name: Hub Labs

name: Hubble

Today, a person’s health history is scattered across disconnected systems, leaving patients and the people helping them to piece it together. We’re building a future where one authorization unlocks a more complete record, regardless of where someone received care.

Our founders previously built healthcare and AI products at Grow Therapy and Amazon One Medical, and we’re backed by Y Combinator, Madrona, and Basis Set. We’re building our team in Seattle, with the opportunity to work directly with the founders and shape how people access and use their health information.

outcome_analysis: Hubble is an active S26 company with founders from Grow Therapy and Amazon One Medical, self-reporting early customers and 2.8M in backing from YC, Madrona and Basis Set. Records retrieval has funded rivals such as Metriport, so execution and integrations will decide results. No outcome events found.

name: Hundred
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Machine Learning; Computer Vision; Industrial
one_liner: 100% automated inspection for precision hardware parts
long_description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

Designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Precision hardware manufacturers and contract manufacturers of device components (phones, watches, laptops)
problem: Manual inspection under microscopes misses roughly 15 percent of defects, and traditional machine vision cannot keep up with fast design changes. Hundred scans a whole tray of parts for sub-100 micron defects.
business_model: Benchtop inspection station hardware plus software
product_category: Automated visual inspection for precision parts
founder_names: Erica Diaz; Imani Gosserand; Iris Liao
market_need_then: Defects cost US discrete manufacturers an estimated 45 billion dollars a year per the YC page; manual microscope inspection is still common.
outcome_analysis: Hundred is a three person F26 company led by a hardware engineer from Meta, Google and Magic Leap, with a software and ML team, building tray-level inspection. No funding beyond YC is public, and it faces established inspection vendors. No outcome events found.

name: Hyper

long_description: Hyper is a shared brain that plugs into all information flowing inside a company, creates a self-maintaining knowledge graph, and makes your AI employees better and ultimately saves people time. Our in-house memory system scores at or above SOTA on most public benchmarks, and we've built a custom eval suite to measure our precision/recall metrics. In the last 12 days since launch, we've gotten top 5 / top 12 on hacker news & product hunt, onboarded 50+ teams, grown 0 to 1k MRR, and are scoping paid design pilots with co's like Razorpay and Snorkel AI. Our whole lives we've packaged hardcore engineering into beautifully simple products, and that's how we’ll win this platform shift.

name: HyperProbe
tags: AIOps; Developer Tools; SaaS; DevOps; AI
one_liner: AI engineer that debugs and fixes production incidents in realtime
long_description:
With tools like Cursor and Claude Code, writing software is no longer the bottleneck. Debugging is. Agents cannot fix production crashes using logs and traces that were sized for human eyeballs. The gap is missing data.

HyperProbe allows agents to debug live software autonomously. Our SDK drops non-breaking probes straight into running services to read exact variable states from memory at the moment of failure, instead of reasoning backwards from flat logs.

Zero redeploys. Under 1% CPU overhead. Automatic PII redaction.

We turn 4-hour production war rooms into 10-minute automated resolutions. As agents write and operate more of the world's software, HyperProbe is the runtime observability layer that lets them understand what they built.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering and on-call teams running production services in Node.js, Java and Python, and teams using coding agents
problem: Production incidents are debugged from logs and traces that lack variable state, so war rooms last hours. HyperProbe places read-only probes in live services to capture exact state for agents and humans.
business_model: B2B SaaS with SDK and MCP server, POC-led sales (pricing not found)
product_category: AI on-call agent and runtime observability for production debugging
market_need_then: Coding agents made code cheap and shifted the bottleneck to debugging. Customers quoted on the site are Indian engineering teams (CheQ Digital, Housing.com), and the company claims time to root cause falls from hours to under 10 minutes (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: HyperProbe is a Summer 2026 spinout from the founders' earlier startup HyperTest, with a team of 8 and a strong technical angle on read-only runtime probes. No funding round, exit or distress was found. The main risk is Lightrun and observability incumbents occupying the same wedge, so the outcome is too early to call.

name: IMPACT Drones
one_liner: Air Defense as a Service for Civilian Infrastructure.
long_description: IMPACT builds autonomous interceptor drones that ship in sealed containers. The box sits at the site it protects, data centers, power grids, airports, bases, with no crew on the pad. When sensors cue a hostile drone, an interceptor pierces its own frangible lid, launches, and rams the target, guided by onboard vision that keeps working when GPS is jammed. Legacy effectors cost $1M+ per shot against $30k threats; ours cost less than the threat and scale with the swarm, the same class of interceptor already downing Shahed drones over Ukraine. Sites subscribe to protection instead of buying missiles, hardware, reloads and monitoring included: Air Defense as a Service. 180M+ USD in signed letters of intent.

market_need_then: Shahed-class drones were hitting infrastructure and governments were buying cheap interceptors. The company cites 180M+ USD in signed letters of intent, which are non-binding and self-reported; pilots were planned from Q3 2026.
outcome_analysis: IMPACT is a two-person Summer 2026 defense hardware startup that launched Air Defense as a Service on 2026-08-04 and drew trade press. name: Ignition Benefits

We have rebuilt the sales and back office to be AI-first. This market represents about $500B of market cap, and those businesses have not fundamentally changed in over 50 years. While scaling Plated, I wore every HR hat from doing payroll myself, to managing a PEO, to eventually hiring an employee benefits broker on our way to 1,500 employees. We wasted over $4M on benefits over 5 years, and I'm building Ignition to help companies under 200 employees avoid making my mistakes.

name: Illume Labs
tags: Generative AI; Health Tech; Biotech; Health & Wellness; AI

long_description: Illume is a 24/7 AI personal health & longevity companion that connects your wearables, blood panels, and genomic data to text you personalized and actionable insights. We pull in your health data and fuse it into one secure model. You get daily text updates on what changed, what it means, and what to do next; conversational health Q&A like "What should I do to improve my bloodwork?"; cross-data trend detection that catches patterns individual platforms miss; and a full platform to dig deeper, explore your health data, and text your Illume agent anytime. We're 3 MIT grads & friends, with experience at Windsurf, MIT CSAIL, Eli Lilly, & the Broad Institute.

name: Imperfect

one_liner: Adaptive training coach for runners, cyclists, and triathletes
long_description: An adaptive training coach to help runners, cyclists, and triathletes set and achieve goals. It adapts your training, recovery, and nutrition to how your body is actually responding.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: recreational and competitive runners, cyclists and triathletes who pay for coaching
problem: Generic training plans are rigid and do not adapt to real-life constraints or how the athlete's body is responding.
business_model: consumer subscription app (pricing not found)
product_category: AI endurance-sports training coach (consumer health and fitness)

name: InLoop Robotics
one_liner: Robotic arms that pick and pack your orders.
long_description:
We are building AI-native fulfillment powered by robotics.
Warehouses without human labor that get better, faster, and cheaper with every order.

Most robotics companies wait until their system is perfect before deploying. We don't. We ship imperfect policies into real warehouses, detect failures in real time, recover automatically when we can, and bring in a remote human operator when we can't.

Every failure becomes training data. Every intervention makes the system better. The result is a fulfillment system that continuously learns from production.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: E-commerce and logistics warehouses that pick, pack and kit orders
problem: Warehouse picking is manual labor that robots rarely handle reliably. InLoop ships imperfect policies into real warehouses, recovers automatically and calls a remote human operator when it cannot, turning failures into training data.
business_model: Robots as a service: monthly rental covering bimanual hardware, software updates and remote support, with no upfront cost (per aggregator profiles)
product_category: AI-native robotic fulfillment with teleoperation fallback
market_need_then: Warehouse labor automation demand and rapid progress in robot learning models. The YC listing and aggregator profiles mention paid pilots in customer warehouses from March 2026, which is self-reported and not verified.
outcome_analysis: InLoop Robotics is a small Spring 2026 robotics startup with machine learning founders from Bosch and BMW and research ties. It sells robots as a monthly service and reports paid pilots. No verified funding, exit or distress was found; the outcome is too early to judge amid well-funded picking vendors.

name: IncidentFox
one_liner: AI SRE agent that triages, coordinates, and fixes production incidents
long_description: AI SRE agents that automatically learn each customer’s system so they work just like an in-house engineer.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering and on-call teams at software companies that run production systems and use PagerDuty, Datadog or Grafana
problem: Investigating production incidents is slow and painful because engineers must work out what is happening across many tools before they can fix anything. On-call load causes alert noise and burnout.
business_model: Open core (Apache 2.0) with hosted SaaS and on-prem or VPC deployment; pricing not stated
product_category: AI SRE agent / AIOps incident response
market_need_then: On-call pain and alert noise are widely discussed, and AI SRE became a funded category in 2025, with Resolve AI reported at a $1B valuation in December 2025. The company's own pitch cites 85 to 95 percent alert noise reduction, a self reported claim.
outcome_analysis: IncidentFox is an active Winter 2026 company with two founders from Roblox infrastructure and no verified outside funding beyond YC. It entered a category that had already attracted multiple funded rivals by late 2025, so its outcome depends on whether an open core, chat native approach wins pilots against better capitalized competitors. It is too early to judge success or failure.

name: Index Law
one_liner: Your company's AI lawyer
long_description:
Index Law is building Mike-1, a superhuman AI lawyer*! Mike is an AI legal agent that gives every business the capabilities of a world-class legal team. 

Unlike traditional legal AI tools that help lawyers work faster, Mike gets legal work done directly for your business. It understands your business, reviews and negotiates contracts, handles corporate matters, and brings in vetted human lawyers when specialist expertise is needed.

Your documents, agreements, signatures, and legal history live in one workspace. Mike remembers your business and becomes more useful with every matter.

We're starting with contracts and corporate work for startups and growing businesses. Early customers have turned around contracts in under an hour and received quotes up to 80% below traditional law firm alternatives.

Our ambition is to make legal services work like software: instantly accessible, deeply personalized, and capable of handling increasingly complex work.

Try Mike: https://usemike.com

*Note: Mike-1 is an AI legal agent, not a licensed or practicing lawyer. Qualified human lawyers provide legal advice and representation where required.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startups and growing businesses that need contracts and corporate legal work
problem: Legal work is slow and expensive for small companies, and existing legal AI tools mostly help lawyers rather than doing the work for the business.
business_model: AI legal agent sold to businesses, with vetted human lawyers brought in for specialist work; the company says early customers received quotes up to 80 percent below law firms. Exact pricing not stated.
product_category: AI legal agent / legal services platform
market_need_then: Legal tech raised billions in early 2026 according to trade coverage, and trade press noted that broad horizontal legal automation pitches were harder to fund because they look like they compete with Harvey, Legora and frontier labs. Startups face real cost pain on routine contracts.
outcome_analysis: Index Law is a Fall 2026 YC company with a single named founder whose earlier AI education company reportedly hit legal trouble. It targets a crowded legal AI market where heavily funded leaders exist, and the site says former UK deputy prime minister Dominic Raab has joined. Nothing public yet shows traction, so the outcome cannot be judged.

name: Induction Labs
one_liner: Building intellectually curious AI
long_description:
We are scaling foundation models that are curious about the world.

We’ve seen general intelligence appear exactly once, and its hallmark has been curiosity: a dissatisfaction with what we already know about the world, an ability to learn from world experience, and a disposition to share knowledge with other individuals. Across generations, these human traits have built modern science, technology, and culture.

We think superintelligence will come from models that work the same way: learning from their own observation, updating as they go, growing what they know. These models will start from what humanity knows and discover past us.

We believe that scaling curious intelligence is a defining problem of our time. If solved, we will live to see a new era of technological advances, scientific understanding, and human flourishing.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI labs that want their models to learn to do research; earlier descriptions also mention computer use model customers
problem: Frontier models lack open ended curiosity and the ability to learn from world experience. The company builds research environments and models that learn from observation to address this.
business_model: Research and environments partnership with AI labs, plus foundation model development; pricing not stated
product_category: Foundation models / research environments for AI labs
market_need_then: Labs and agent builders want models that can operate computers and do research. Computer use was an active frontier area in 2025, and the company positions itself as supplying environments and models to labs.
outcome_analysis: Induction Labs is a Summer 2026 YC company that began around 2025 with a computer use model focus and now describes itself as building curious AI and research environments for labs. Public evidence of funding, customers or results is thin, so no outcome can be assessed beyond the stated pivot in positioning.

name: Infera

long_description: Describe an experiment in plain English, and Infera turns it into a validated, instrument-ready run across the equipment your lab already uses. Infera handles the protocol logic, vendor-specific scripts, data, inventory, and institutional knowledge in one system. An AI-native compiler for the lab: one system from intent to execution.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Academic and industry research labs that run multiple instruments from different vendors
problem: Scientists lose time writing vendor specific instrument scripts and moving data by hand. Infera turns plain English protocols into validated runs on existing equipment.
business_model: B2B software for labs (protocol compiler, data reader, desktop research environment, agent evaluations); pricing not stated, labs book a consultation
product_category: Lab automation software / AI lab operating system
market_need_then: Labs run many instruments with vendor specific software, and interest in AI agents that drive wet labs was growing in 2026. A YC listing says it runs pilots with Boston area academic labs and cores.
outcome_analysis: Infera is a Spring 2026 YC company with two technically strong founders building software that drives lab instruments from natural language. It reports pilots with local academic labs but no named customers or verified funding, so the outcome is unknown and depends on integration depth and lab adoption.

name: Inflection Space Systems

long_description: Inflection is building the industrial capacity to manufacture tens of thousands of spacecraft per year for next generation commercial and government space applications. Imagine a factory that looks like an Amazon fulfillment center instead of a NASA clean room.

target_customer: Satellite operators and payload customers for data infrastructure, telecommunications and imaging missions
problem: Spacecraft are built one at a time in clean rooms, which limits volume and raises cost. Inflection aims to build the industrial capacity to make tens of thousands of standardized spacecraft per year.
business_model: Hardware sales of a standardized spacecraft platform with volume pricing; the site lists 1.5M per unit for one unit falling to 700K per unit at 100 units
product_category: Standardized spacecraft bus manufacturing
market_need_then: Demand for satellites for data infrastructure, telecom and imaging was growing, and the company is recruiting payload customers for a 2028 launch. No named customers are public.

name: Inkbox
one_liner: Give agents a computer with their own email, phone, iMsg, and WhatsApp
long_description: Give your agents a computer to run on, with their own email, phone, iMessage, and WhatsApp. Each agent runs next to its communication channels, so it never misses a reply, and sleeps when idle, so customers don’t pay for downtime.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need their own email, phone, iMessage, WhatsApp and a persistent cloud computer
problem: Agents cannot easily receive replies, confirmations and calls or stay reachable, so builders stitch together separate services. Inkbox gives each agent an identity and communication layer plus a cloud computer that sleeps when idle.
business_model: Usage-based developer API and platform for agent inboxes, phone numbers and compute
product_category: Agent identity and communication infrastructure
founder_names: Ray Liao; Dima Vremenko; Alex Wilcox
