name: InstaAgent
one_liner: Scale marketing campaigns across hundreds of personas
long_description:
InstaAgent helps B2C companies scale a single campaign across hundreds of specific audiences on Meta and TikTok, each with its own content, voice, and targeting. Traction: $1M Ann. Run Rate in 10 months.

From one brief, we create personalized creatives, distribute them through paid channels and niche social accounts, and use performance data to learn what works, scale winners, and improve every campaign.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2C brands and marketers that run paid campaigns on Meta and TikTok
problem: Brands run one campaign for a broad audience, while each audience responds to different content, voice and targeting. InstaAgent runs one brief across hundreds of audiences and scales the winners.
business_model: Marketing platform and managed distribution sold to brands; pricing not stated
product_category: AI marketing and ad personalization platform
market_need_then: Brands spend heavily on paid social and want more creative variants. The company reports 500+ clients, 1M ARR after 10 months and enterprise sales cycles closing in under a month, all self reported.
outcome_analysis: InstaAgent is a Spring 2026 YC company that reports 1M ARR after 10 months, 500+ clients and recognizable brand logos, which is traction well ahead of most batch peers if accurate. It competes with funded creative tools and with platform AI features, so growth quality and retention will decide the outcome.

name: InstaBox

long_description: Full Linux VMs for long-running agents.

target_customer: Developers and companies running long lived AI agents that need a full Linux machine
problem: Agents need full computers with persistent disks, desktop access and browsers rather than short lived code sandboxes. InstaBox provides Firecracker microVM Linux machines per agent.
business_model: Usage-based cloud compute with subscription tiers: Free, Pro 20 per month, Builder 100, Team 500 and Enterprise, plus charges for vCPU, memory, storage and egress
product_category: Cloud computers and sandboxes for AI agents

outcome_analysis: InstaBox is a Spring 2026 YC company selling Linux cloud computers to AI agents in a crowded sandbox market. Its YC page carries bios tied to InsForge, so the team relationship is unclear, and no funding, customers or traction are public. The outcome cannot be judged.

name: Instinct
one_liner: Trade with superhuman instinct
long_description:
Capital allocation is becoming a more important part of individual economic life.
Finance is moving toward a global, onchain, 24/7 future with thousands of markets trading at once.

The asset management industry is built around the scarcity of financial expertise and the cost of organizing people around capital. 

Institutions cover global markets by employing analysts, researchers, and quants around the clock. 

AI turns this organizational capacity into software.

Instinct is building the harness for this transition.

Instinct is a proactive team of agents that searches thousands of markets, investigates opportunities, and operates 24/7. The individual becomes the portfolio manager, Instinct becomes the investment firm operating around them.

As institutional advantages become widely accessible, the edge concentrates in each trader’s worldview, judgment, and bets. 

The first one-person investment firm managing $1 billion will emerge within two years.

It will run on Instinct.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Individual retail and semi-professional traders in crypto and onchain markets, paying through trading fees
problem: Covering thousands of markets around the clock needs analysts and quants that an individual trader cannot afford. Instinct packages that research and monitoring as a team of AI agents.
business_model: Trading platform with per-trade fees (the site advertises about $1 on a $10,000 trade); agents and research tools bundled
product_category: AI trading agents and trading app
market_need_then: Onchain perpetuals volume was growing (Hyperliquid open interest reported above $10 billion by mid-2026) and AI agent tooling made 24/7 automated research feasible. Evidence of paid demand for Instinct itself was not found.
outcome_analysis: Instinct is a Winter 2026 company with a five person team and no disclosed outcome. It has launched a waitlist for AI trading agents aimed at traders who want an investment-firm toolset. The main risks visible today are a crowded field of Hyperliquid agent products and name confusion with a different Instinct that raised far more money.

name: Insurf
tags: Health Tech; Healthcare; Insurance; Automation; AI
one_liner: The AI-Native Decision Layer for Health Insurance
long_description: Insurf is the AI-native data and decision layer for health insurance. Our model Surely identifies the lowest-cost coverage for anyone, saving individuals, families, and companies thousands per employee. Our product Inveto collects the data from hospitals and clinics that informs Surely.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Employers moving to ICHRA, families and individuals choosing plans, and clinics handling prior authorizations and denial appeals
problem: People choose health plans by sticker premium rather than full-year cost, and clinics lose time and revenue to prior authorizations and denials. Insurf prices plans by county and drafts source-cited appeals.
business_model: B2B and B2C health insurance software; product lines Surely (plan cost engine) and Inveto (clinic appeals), pricing not found
product_category: Health insurance decision and prior authorization software

market_need_then: The launch post cites a 2028 shift away from auto-renewing plans and growth of ICHRA; denial rates and appeal overturn rates (company cites 80.7 percent for appealed Medicare Advantage denials, methodology not found) drive clinic demand.

It pairs an employer and consumer plan pricing model with a clinic appeals tool that it says is live in Texas, Georgia and California. name: Intelligence Factory
one_liner: Human Intelligence for Robots
long_description:
Robotics is the new paradigm. With hardware converging, Intelligence is the biggest bottleneck. Our world was built for humans and we're giving robots the ability to reason and act like us. 

The way we learn any task - by seeing, doing, and feeling - is how we train robots. We're building general intelligence that works on any robot and fits seamlessly within our world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robot makers and operators (warehouses, grocery stores, data centers) who need manipulation models
problem: Robot hardware is converging but manipulation intelligence is the bottleneck. The company trains models on human demonstrations captured with custom gloves in data factories and retargets them to different robots.
business_model: Foundation models for manipulation sold or deployed to robot operators; pricing not found
product_category: Robot manipulation foundation models and human demonstration data
competitors_at_founding: MANUS (data gloves) and its customers such as Mimic Robotics; Sunday Robotics skill capture glove
market_need_then: Humanoid and dexterous robot hardware investment grew through 2025 and 2026 and teams reported a data bottleneck for dexterous hands (ICRA 2026 coverage by a glove vendor, so a vendor view).
outcome_analysis: Intelligence Factory is a Spring 2026 company with about ten people according to YC and strong robotics founders. It has no verified funding or revenue, so its outcome is open. The main questions are whether its glove-collected human data beats rivals and whether customers beyond early warehouse and data center pilots appear.

name: Interfaze
one_liner: AI model built for high accuracy deterministic tasks
long_description:
Interfaze is an AI model built on a new architecture that merges specialized DNN/CNN models with transformers for tasks that require deterministic output and high consistency like Document intelligence, Object detection, Classification, Audio understanding and more.

Interfaze outperforms large lab models like Gemini flash, Claude Sonnet and the GPT-5.4 mini series

Architecture paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04101
Full open benchmarks: https://interfaze.ai/leaderboards
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies that need consistent, verifiable output for OCR, extraction, classification and speech tasks
problem: General LLMs are inconsistent on tasks like document OCR and structured extraction. Interfaze merges specialist DNN and CNN models with a transformer to give repeatable output with confidence scores and bounding boxes.
business_model: Usage-based API (OpenAI-compatible) plus an open-weight Lite model under Apache 2.0
product_category: AI model for deterministic document, vision and audio tasks
founder_names: Yoeven D Khemlani; Harsha Vardhan Khurdula
market_need_then: Developers building document and extraction pipelines complained about LLM inconsistency; ABBYY and others were also marketing hybrid deterministic plus generative document AI in 2026, a sign of demand.
outcome_analysis: Interfaze is a Spring 2026 company that appears to continue the earlier JigsawStack developer API business under a new name and architecture. It has published a paper, benchmarks and an open-weight Lite model, but no named customers or verified funding. The outcome is open and depends on whether benchmark gains hold against fast-moving lab models.

name: Inth
tags: Developer Tools; Compliance; Web Development; Trust & Safety; AI
one_liner: Privacy and consent infrastructure that ships with your code
long_description:
Inth brings together consent management, continuous privacy monitoring and AI-assisted investigation. It follows changes from code to production so engineering, marketing and legal teams can see what their sites and codebases are doing, verify their controls and get problems fixed.

We're the team behind c15t, our open-source (Apache-2.0) consent framework with millions of downloads, rebuilt in v3 to run on any framework and on the server. We also maintain an open library of privacy enforcement cases, and we've completed our SOC 2 Type 2 audit.

Backed by Y Combinator and Vercel. Start at inth.com
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Engineering, marketing and legal teams at companies that must manage web consent and privacy compliance
problem: Consent banners and privacy controls drift from the code that ships, and compliance tools slow sites down. Inth ships an open-source consent framework with hosted monitoring and AI-assisted investigation.
business_model: Open-core: open-source c15t framework plus a paid hosted control plane (consent management, monitoring)
product_category: Consent management and privacy compliance infrastructure
market_need_then: Privacy regulations and enforcement cases keep producing consent requirements; the YC page cites c15t with over 2 million npm downloads, which is evidence of developer demand.
outcome_analysis: Inth grew from the open-source c15t consent library, which reports millions of downloads and conference visibility, into a broader privacy monitoring company in April 2026. It is a three person Spring 2026 team with SOC 2 Type 2 done and Vercel backing noted by YC. Outcome is open; adoption by developers is the clear strength, monetization and competition from large vendors the risk.

name: InventoryQuant
one_liner: We automate the inventory process in insurance
long_description: We automate inventory and contents processing for insurance and insurance-adjacent industries, including public adjusters, restoration contents, and insurance companies. We also handle various inventory and estimate adjacent processes that cost many billions of dollars a year and thousands of years of man hours.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Public adjusters, restoration contents firms and insurers who build contents inventories for claims
problem: Contents inventories for insurance claims are typed in by hand line by line. InventoryQuant turns video or audio walkthroughs into priced line items and submission-ready inventories.
business_model: B2B SaaS for claims professionals, pricing not found
product_category: Insurance contents inventory automation
market_need_then: The company says contents work is manual and costs thousands of man hours; one law firm testimonial on its site says it saved days, which is a vendor-chosen quote. 2025 launches by competitors show insurer demand.
outcome_analysis: InventoryQuant is a one person Winter 2026 company building contents inventory automation for insurance claims. It has one named customer testimonial and no verified funding or revenue. The outcome is open, with the founder's AI credibility an asset and the crowded contents-claims field and solo staffing the main risks.

name: Invertix
one_liner: AI agents that operate energy plants and datacenters
long_description:
Invertix builds AI that helps energy companies run Power Plants Autonomously.
We believe Power Plants and Datacenters will be autonomously developed and operated.
We are building that AI layer.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0uDH6pMn5OE

Critical Infrastructure is a $10 trillion market.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Utilities, energy asset owners, O&M companies and data center operators (Altenia, Terna and TotalEnergies named on its site)
problem: Operating power plants involves triaging alarms, dispatching technicians and reporting across fragmented SCADA and work order systems.
business_model: Enterprise deployments with forward deployed engineers building AI agents inside customer systems
product_category: AI agents for energy plant operations

name: Isengard Industries Inc
one_liner: Mass-produced AI strike systems and Counter-UAS
long_description:
Isengard Industries is not another drone company.

We build sovereign production: the means for allied nations to make precision-strike and counter-drone systems by the thousand, on their own soil, at a fraction of what the primes charge.

We call it Weapons of Mass Production. The Arsenal of Democracy, rebuilt for the drone age.

More to come, and only where it helps. You know how to reach us.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Allied governments and militaries (U.S. Army, Ukrainian units, Middle East and other allies) buying strike drones, counter-UAS and production cells
problem: Allied nations lack cheap, domestically produced precision-strike and counter-drone systems at volume. Isengard supplies designs, autonomy software, tooling and supply chain so partners run local production cells.
business_model: Defense hardware sales plus licensed production cells and tooling for allies
product_category: AI strike drones, counter-UAS and distributed munitions manufacturing
market_need_then: Ukraine war evidence of cheap drones beating costly defenses and a Pentagon drone dominance program (reported aim of 340,000 low-cost drones by 2028) created demand; company claims $10M revenue and a $350M pipeline (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Isengard is a Summer 2026 company run by a founder who previously scaled Terminal Autonomy, with a closed seed round announced in August 2026, claimed U.S. and Ukrainian customers and a 30 person team. Strong demand tailwinds and founder market fit support it. Product claims are self-reported and amounts undisclosed, so outcome is open.

name: Janeen
one_liner: Prior auths and benefits investigation for infusion clinics
long_description:
Janeen is built for infusion clinics. We handle prior authorizations and benefit investigations from start to finish (actually though!).

Biologics are expensive medications that cost $80-$150K+ per year per patient, and often need to be administered in specific settings called infusion clinics. Medical providers buy these drugs up front to secure pricing deals and safer inventory - they are reimbursed for the cost of the medications through the patients’ insurance. 

Current medical workflows aren't built for infusion clinics. Inventory, storage, transport, and billing is still managed through paper and excel spreadsheets. And because they’re so expensive, these specialty medications are denied by insurers at a rate of 37% each year. When they are denied, when workflows fail, or patients are infused before paperwork is cleared, providers don’t get reimbursed for the medication and are left covering the costs. Ruma Care solves this so clinics get paid, patients get treated faster, and care teams spend less time fighting forms. 

We work with clinics across the country and have removed 95% of all manual labor in the process.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Infusion clinics (rheumatology, headache, other biologic administering practices) that pay for prior authorization and benefits investigation work
problem: Biologics cost $80K to $150K+ per patient per year and are often denied; paper and spreadsheet workflows leave clinics unreimbursed. Janeen handles benefits investigation, prior authorization submission, insurer calls and appeals end to end.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services per clinic, pricing not found; free Formulary Navigator tool as lead generation
product_category: Prior authorization and benefits investigation automation for infusion clinics
founder_names: Meng Fei Shen; Christina Lee Huang
market_need_then: The company cites 37 percent annual insurer denial of specialty medications and clinics paying for drugs upfront; the founder's patient experience and live clinic use in California and Nevada support need (company claims of 50 percent lower denials).
outcome_analysis: Janeen, formerly Ruma Care, is a Winter 2026 company with five people and reported live use in infusion clinics in California and Nevada. Founder market fit is notable since a co-founder is a former biologics patient. Funding is not verified from a primary source and larger vendors are entering infusion, so the outcome is open.

name: Jcode
one_liner: High performance coding agents
long_description: Jcode is a high-performance coding-agent harness that makes it possible for developers to scale up multi-agent/swarm workflows. It's built from the ground up with a different architecture to solve the memory bottleneck (it's 20x more memory efficient than Claude Code) that has kept agent swarms from going mainstream. It has 20K GitHub stars, and throughputs $1mil per month of inference spend
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Professional and hobbyist software developers who run several AI coding agents in parallel, plus enterprises via an Enterprise tier
problem: Existing coding-agent harnesses use a lot of memory per session, which limits how many agents a developer can run at once in swarm style workflows.
business_model: Open-source (MIT) terminal agent with desktop and iPhone apps in beta and an Enterprise offering; pricing not published on the site
product_category: Developer tools, AI coding agent harness
market_need_then: Developers were adopting terminal coding agents in 2026 and reported memory and process overhead when running many sessions; the company claims throughput of about 1 million dollars of monthly inference spend through the tool, which is self reported.
outcome_analysis: Jcode is a Summer 2026 solo founder company with fast open source traction and a memory efficiency pitch, still active with no exit. It is very early, so the outcome is unknown. The main risks visible now are that the code is MIT licensed and copyable and that Anthropic, OpenAI and others compete directly in the same product category.

name: Jinba
one_liner: Automate enterprise workflows through chat
long_description:
Jinba lets enterprise teams vibe-code AI workflows instead of drag and drop. Describe what you need in plain language, and your whole company can start using it immediately. No engineers required. Enterprise-grade permissions, audit logging, and on-prem deployment built in. We serve 40,000 enterprise users at major financial institutions.

Build something your colleagues want.
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Large enterprises, especially banks and manufacturers in Japan, where non-engineer staff build internal AI workflows
problem: Enterprise teams want to automate workflows with AI but drag and drop builders need engineers and lack enterprise controls.
business_model: B2B SaaS with credit based workflow execution tiers, an enterprise plan and on-prem or private cloud deployment
product_category: Enterprise AI workflow automation platform

name: Juno
one_liner: AI Health Assistant for Chronic Illness
long_description:
Juno is an AI personal health assistant for the 1B+ people living with chronic illness.

Launched in October, Juno now supports 300,000+ patients globally.

target_customer: Adults living with chronic illness such as fibromyalgia, long Covid and endometriosis, paying via an optional Pro subscription

name: Kailash Labs
one_liner: A factory for small and specialized video reasoning models
long_description:
The world generates petabytes of video every day, and almost none of it is readable to machines.  Frontier VLMs that can unlock this (like Gemini) are too expensive to run at the volume real industries have, too generic for any single task, and can't be deployed on-prem where sensitive video lives.

We are building an auto vision factory: take video plus a customer's objective, distill a frontier model, and post-train a small open model that is SOTA on that one task and serve it blazingly fast. Our first product, Marlin, is a 2B-parameter open-weights video VLM that matches Gemini-2.5-flash on dense captioning and temporal grounding at a fraction of the cost.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Companies with large volumes of video such as robotics, security and industrial monitoring teams that find frontier video models too expensive
problem: Frontier video language models can read video but are too costly or slow to run at industrial volume, so most video stays unreadable to machines.
business_model: Custom distilled small video models per customer task plus an open weights model, Marlin; commercial terms not published
product_category: Small specialized video reasoning models
market_need_then: Video volume is large and frontier video models are costly at scale, per the company; no independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Kailash Labs is a two person Fall 2026 company in Bengaluru building small video reasoning models; it is active with no exit, and it is too early to judge. The YC page and the company website describe different offerings (video models versus robot workcells), which is an unresolved inconsistency.

name: Kairos Health
one_liner: AI front desk that fills every chair for dental practices
long_description:
Kairos Health automates patient engagement for dentists by handling phones and insurance.

Kairos plugs into a dental practice's software, calls patients who are overdue for care, and books them directly into the schedule. It also answers every inbound call 24/7 and verifies insurance.

Our mission is to put practice operations on autopilot and keep every chair filled.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Dental and orthodontic practices, paying for an AI front desk
problem: Dental front desks miss calls, fail to recall overdue patients and spend time on insurance verification, leaving chairs empty.
business_model: B2B SaaS per practice for AI voice and text patient engagement integrated with dental practice management software
product_category: AI receptionist for dental practices

outcome_analysis: Kairos Health is an active Fall 2026 company started by Rice and Georgia Tech students, one of whom grew up in her mother's dental practices, and it reports quick early growth. There is no exit. The main risk is that the dental AI receptionist market is crowded with funded startups and incumbents already bundling similar features.

name: Kairox Systems
one_liner: Autonomous drones that fly and swim
long_description:
Kairox Systems combines the speed of aerial drones and the stealth of underwater drones into one vehicle. We can look for mines in a strait, fly out of the water to inspect a coastline, and then engage maritime threats in one go. 

Joel, Alex, and Jorge all met at MIT. After conversations with warfighters and drone researchers, they decided to create a vehicle unlike any before: A long-range vehicle that is truly amphibious, low-cost enough for one-way swarms, can operate fully autonomously, and can be repurposed on the front lines. Engaged with the Marine Corps and validated with end users across the U.S. and allied militaries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Government and defense buyers such as program offices, special operations units and labs evaluating multi-domain unmanned systems
problem: Mine detection and coastal inspection need both air speed and underwater stealth, which normally requires separate vehicles.
business_model: Hardware sales and contracts to defense customers for the Tempest hybrid drone
product_category: Hybrid aerial and underwater autonomous drone
founder_names: Joel Santiago-Baretti; Jorge Cavazos; Alex Rice
competitors_at_founding: Naviator (Rutgers hybrid quadcopter); Exail K-STER and REMUS class UUVs
market_need_then: Navies were buying mine countermeasure drones and testing multi-domain unmanned systems in 2025 and 2026 exercises; the company cites a 50 km range and 1 lb payload for Tempest (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Kairox Systems is a three person, all MIT, Fall 2026 hard tech company building an amphibious drone for defense. It is active with no exit and little public data, so the outcome is unknown. The key risks are hardware cost and defense sales cycles rather than direct competition.

name: Kanopy
one_liner: Computer vision operating layer for physical infrastructure
long_description: Video to automatically identify risks and condition on power lines, pipelines, rail, and other types of infrastructure over hundreds of miles at once.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Electric utilities, pipeline and rail operators that inspect long infrastructure corridors
problem: Inspecting power lines and similar assets over hundreds of miles is slow and manual, and vegetation clearances and condition risks are found late.
business_model: B2B software that turns video from drones, vehicles or phones into 3D models and risk reports; pricing not published
product_category: Computer vision for infrastructure inspection and vegetation management
market_need_then: Utilities invest in wildfire and outage prevention and vegetation management; 2026 trade coverage describes airborne LiDAR and satellite AI deployments, which indicates budget exists. No customer data for Kanopy found.
outcome_analysis: Kanopy is a two person New York company in Fall 2026 selling video based infrastructure inspection to utilities. One founder spent years advising utilities at McKinsey and the other has computer vision and robotics experience, which fit the problem. It is active with no exit and almost no public coverage, so the outcome is unknown.

name: Kara
one_liner: Making Diamond Semiconductors
long_description:
Kara is building diamond semiconductors. 

We begin with growing ultra-high purity diamond wafers for advanced hardware. Used in data centers, spacecrafts, RF systems, and quantum hardware, our diamond moves heat up to 5× better than copper, helping critical systems run cooler, faster, and more reliably. 

Diamond has spent centuries as a symbol. We are turning it into infrastructure.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI accelerator packaging teams, aerospace and defense electronics makers, data-center thermal teams, RF/GaN and quantum hardware groups
problem: High-power chips are limited by how fast they shed heat; copper is nearing its thermal limit as power density rises.
business_model: Hardware materials: custom diamond heat spreaders, plates, submounts and wafers sold under pilot agreements and purchase orders
product_category: Engineered lab-grown diamond for thermal management, later semiconductors
market_need_then: AI chip power density is rising and thermal throttling is a documented bottleneck; diamond conducts heat about five times better than copper (YC page, press).
outcome_analysis: Kara was founded in 2026 and joined YC in Summer 2026 with two founders, one a fifth-generation diamond industrialist and one a diamond quantum systems engineer. It is producing samples under pilot agreements; no verified funding, customer or outcome is public, so any judgement of success or failure is premature.

name: Kebra
one_liner: AI For The Skilled Workforce
long_description:
Kebra builds AI for skilled technicians.

Kebra guides technicians in the field in real time, documents their job, and automatically handles hours of back-office work; from dispatching technicians to filing warranty claims and managing inventory.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Field service and skilled trades companies (home services, HVAC and similar) that employ technicians; the company says it works with field operations firms in Florida, Pennsylvania and California
problem: Technicians document jobs poorly, which leaves the back office doing hours of manual work on dispatch, warranty claims and inventory.
business_model: B2B SaaS for field service companies (pricing not public)
product_category: AI operations layer for field service
competitors_at_founding: ServiceTitan Atlas; Housecall Pro, Jobber, Zuper, ServiceMax, Salesforce Field Service

outcome_analysis: Kebra is a Summer 2026 company with two founders from Microsoft and Arista backgrounds, so no outcome exists yet. A search for acquisition, shutdown or layoffs found nothing. The main risks visible today are incumbents such as ServiceTitan shipping Atlas in September 2025, and the need to prove accuracy across messy field data.

name: KelAI
one_liner: The AI Quant: Autonomous Alpha Engine for Funds and Traders.
long_description:
Founded by former WorldQuant portfolio manager & head of event driven systematic strategies Jeremie Cohen, KelAI is building the autonomous alpha engine for hedge funds, traders and institutional investors. 

Investment teams now have more data, tools and compute than ever, but research still runs across siloed systems and inefficient workflows. KelAI turns that fragmented process into a compounding AI-native engine that continuously finds, tests and validates trading signals at a pace no human team can match.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hedge funds, systematic traders and institutional investors
problem: Investment research runs across siloed systems and slow workflows, so finding, testing and validating trading signals is limited by human team capacity.
business_model: B2B software and signals for funds (pricing not public)
product_category: AI quant research agents for finance
market_need_then: Funds have more data and compute than before but research workflows stay fragmented, and AI agents for institutional research were attracting seed and Series A funding in 2026.
outcome_analysis: KelAI is a Spring 2026 company that announced a $5M seed in July 2026 led by Frst, Y Combinator and Robinhood Ventures, with signals reportedly live at an institutional investor since October 2025. The founder's WorldQuant and Millennium background fits the buyers. No exit or distress was found, and rivals such as Pinegap, AgentSmyth and Itoflow (pre-seed, August 2026) are raising in the same space.

name: Keres
one_liner: Kill the drone, keep the jet. Reusable unmanned interceptors.
long_description: Keres (KAIR-eez) builds reusable unmanned jet interceptors for air defense. The Garmur launches on cue, closes at jet speed, positively identifies and kills drones and cruise missiles, then lands to fly again. It gives commanders a fighter-class response at a fraction of the cost.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US military and air defense commanders (government buyers)
problem: Defending against drones and cruise missiles with fighter jets or expensive missiles is too costly; the company wants a fighter-class response at a fraction of the cost.
business_model: Defense hardware sold to government customers (contracts not public)
product_category: Reusable unmanned jet interceptors for air defense
market_need_then: Counter-UAS startups raised over $1.2B across 15 verified rounds between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026 per one tracker, showing demand for low cost interceptors against drones and missiles.
outcome_analysis: Keres is a Fall 2026 company with an Air Force pilot CEO and a CTO who led production operations at Boom, so it is too early for an outcome. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. The key risks are the hardware difficulty for a three person team and well funded counter-drone competitors raising large rounds in mid 2026.

name: Keyframe Labs
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; B2B; API; AI
one_liner: Bring AI to life with the world's best interactive avatars
long_description: We build human foundation models. Our first family of models powers lifelike avatars that interact with users in real time, enabling AI agents and applications to go beyond text and voice with just a few lines of code. State-of-the-art realism with ultra-low latency at scale.

target_customer: Developers and enterprises adding real-time video avatars to AI agents (roleplay, recruiting, telehealth, customer support)

name: Khotan (formerly Pollinate)
one_liner: FDE as a platform for rebuilding critical operations in software.
long_description:
Khotan is the platform for forward-deployed engineers to rebuild operations as software and maintain them. It combines your context with the infrastructure harnesses need to deploy, share, and maintain each application.

Across procurement, supply chain, finance, and operations, we’ve rebuilt the systems businesses cannot afford to get wrong.

Learn more at khotan.com
regions: Australia; Oceania
target_customer: Mid-sized and large businesses with procurement, supply chain, finance and operations workflows
problem: Critical operations run on brittle or off-the-shelf software; Khotan lets forward-deployed engineers rebuild them as maintained custom applications on the company's own data.
business_model: B2B software platform with forward-deployed engineering (pricing not public)
product_category: Forward-deployed engineering platform, custom procurement software
market_need_then: Forward-deployed engineer job postings grew sharply in 2025 per a research teardown, and AI makes bespoke software cheaper to build; evidence of Khotan-specific demand is not public.
outcome_analysis: Khotan is a two person Brisbane founded company that joined YC in Winter 2026 after two earlier rejections and renamed itself from Pollinate. It is too early for an outcome. The only reported capital is the roughly $500K initial funding at YC admission. The main risk is a crowded forward-deployed engineering field where Palantir and AI labs already operate.

name: Kimpton
one_liner: Live Evaluation Arenas for Financial Work
long_description:
In investment management, every decision gets graded. The market prints the answer on a date known in advance, and nobody gets to argue with it.

Kimpton is financial AI that answers to reality. Kimpton OS is the AI-native operating system for investment teams: it does the research and hands PMs structured trades. EarningsBench is a public benchmark where models forecast quarterly earnings before companies report and the reported numbers do the scoring. Koliseum is the set of point-in-time financial environments we build from that work, for labs to train and evaluate models on.

The whole industry is fighting underperformance. Active managers trail their benchmarks, and capital keeps bleeding into passive. AI was supposed to fix that, but it hasn't. Funds either stitch together a dozen point tools or babysit general agents all day, and neither gets them to the trade.

Kimpton OS goes straight to it. It ingests a fund's mandate, strategy, and positions, connects to the institutional data the fund already runs on, and returns a structured trade proposal built for that fund. It's built to disagree, because consensus is poison for investment decisions. Instead of telling a PM what they want to hear, it surfaces the breaches and risks they'd otherwise miss.

That same work is how we grade AI. Static benchmarks leak into training data. Simulations reward what their authors imagined. A forecast sealed before the outcome exists and scored when the company reports can't be rehearsed or backdated. We started in markets because they're the one place reality answers on schedule.

We're two ex-Goldman engineers and an ex-SpaceX engineer. We left to start our own quantitative systematic hedge fund, raised $10M from a family office at 21 and 22, and scaled it to $35M over four years. We learned to trust live results over historical fit. We built Kimpton inside that fund, then productized the stack.

We're live with our first institutional client, a $3.3B manager. Our first market is fundamental equity funds from $1B to $10B, and the labs that need to know whether their models can do this work.
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Fundamental equity funds with $1B to $10B in assets (Kimpton OS) and AI labs that need finance training and evaluation environments (Koliseum, EvalRouter)
problem: Active managers trail benchmarks and funds stitch together point tools or babysit general agents; AI labs lack evaluation that cannot be rehearsed or backdated.
business_model: B2B software for funds plus data and evaluation environments sold to AI labs (pricing not public)
product_category: Financial AI research OS and live evaluation benchmarks
founder_names: Jack Zumwalt; Mauricio Ortiz; Adrian Del Bosque
market_need_then: The company points to active managers trailing benchmarks and capital moving to passive funds, and to labs needing non leaking evaluations; its founders report a live first client managing $3.3B.
outcome_analysis: Kimpton is a Spring 2026 company built by three engineers who ran a quantitative fund and productized its stack. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. Its early signals are a live institutional client reported by the company and a public benchmark, while risks are heavily funded finance AI incumbents and a name that collides with a hotel brand.

name: Kinect
one_liner: The AI revenue platform for D2C brands
long_description:
Kinect builds AI agents that know your brand, your catalog, and your customers. On your site, they sell every visitor — running the conversation, adapting product pages in real time to each customer segment, picking the right recommendation for the question being asked. The agent picks up on what each shopper actually wants from how they ask, what they hesitate on, what they compare, and what objection makes them bounce. 

We take all of a brand's data and make a structured catalog, brand voice, fit notes, return reasons, segment-level nuance — all so the Kinect agents truly can speak about a brand. When an agent describes the brand, the version it describes is the one you'd want them to, not whatever it guessed from a public catalog scrape. We expose this data as well in the form of agent storefronts, letting every other AI talk about your brand in the way you would want too.

We're building for human shoppers today and the AI agents that shop and discover for them. Either way, the entire website needs to get a lot smarter and personalized. 

Two surfaces. One layer. Built for scaling DTC ecommerce brands.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Direct-to-consumer ecommerce brands
problem: Brand sites show the same pages to every shopper and lose conversions; AI agents can sell and personalize.
business_model: B2B SaaS AI agents for ecommerce
product_category: AI revenue platform for D2C
market_need_then: AI-referred ecommerce traffic is surging (Shopify's Q1 2026 data cited AI-referred sessions up more than 8x and orders about 13x year over year per a retail roundup), creating demand for storefronts that sell to humans and to AI agents. Company reports 11 live customers (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Kinect is a Spring 2026 YC company founded in 2026 by two ex-Reevo, Google Commerce and Anduril engineers, still Active with two people, so no exit or failure exists. It sells AI agents to D2C brands in a market where Shopify and funded rivals like Wizard were already launching agentic shopping features, and in a search-confusing name shared with Microsoft's Kinect. Reported funding is an unverified pre-seed of about $500K, consistent with the YC deal; traction numbers are company-reported.

name: Kinro

long_description: We help small business owners get the right coverage.

product_category: Autonomous insurance brokerage

It claims licenses in 30 states, 15 carrier appointments and a signed $1M enterprise sale at YC entry. No shutdown or layoff news was found, while funded AI brokerage rivals like Cara and WithCoverage raised rounds in early 2026.

name: Kita
tags: Fintech; Computer Vision; Lending; Emerging Markets
one_liner: Underwrite borrowers around the world in minutes
long_description:
In emerging markets, open finance is still nascent. Most of the population is traditionally unbanked, banking APIs don’t exist, and a borrower’s financial history lives in documents: e-wallet records, bank statements, utility bills, and more. Because this data is unstructured, credit and risk teams are forced into manual review. This slows decisioning, increases costs, and caps lending volume. 

Kita is the AI platform for global lending operations. We help lenders in emerging markets automate application completion, document verification, and underwriting from messy financial documents — using AI to extract fraud-checked data and localized risk signals that power faster, better credit decisions.

Under the hood, Kita is a learning engine. We link document-level signals to repayment outcomes, allowing our models to continuously improve fraud detection and risk assessment over time. This creates a compounding advantage for lenders as their distinct underwriting decisions feed back into the system.

We’re Carmel and Rhea. We met before Stanford and have been building together ever since. Carmel is from Manila, is a repeat founder, and spent three years in product at Apple. Rhea has a research background in computer vision and received the highest honor in Stanford Computer Science. Together, we combine deep local context with strong technical execution to build the infrastructure that expands access to credit in emerging markets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Lenders and fintechs in emerging markets
problem: Borrower financial data lives in unstructured documents, forcing manual credit review.
business_model: B2B SaaS AI underwriting platform
product_category: AI lending operations / document-based underwriting
market_need_then: Open finance is nascent in emerging markets and borrower history sits in unstructured documents such as e-wallet records and bank statements (YC launch post, Mar 2026). Kita reports over $130M in loan volume processed for lenders in the US, Southeast Asia and Latin America (American Bazaar, Aug 2026, company-sourced).
outcome_analysis: Kita is a Winter 2026 YC company that launched publicly in March 2026 and announced a $4.5M seed led by BoxGroup in August 2026, about five months after the batch. Founder-market fit is the visible strength: a CEO from Manila and a computer-vision CTO selling to emerging-market lenders, with reported production use in the Philippines, Indonesia, Mexico and the US. It is still early and active, so no exit or failure exists; the data (loan volume, files processed) is company-reported and not independently verified.

name: Kiwi
one_liner: Kiwi is your GTM agent's favorite data engineer.
long_description: While engineering teams have become fully AI-native, GTM teams have fallen behind. Teams struggle with continuous enablement of their teams, keeping context, agent skills, and connectors up to date with shifting GTM states and strategies, as well as accuracy, when operators can't trust their agents because the data is incomplete, inconsistent, or unreliable. With Kiwi, every agent is self-improving, and cites the SQL query and data snapshot pulled from the Kiwi GTM brain used to produce every output. Kiwi enables GTM teams to be fully AI-native.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: RevOps, BizOps, sales and marketing teams that run AI agents on go-to-market data
problem: GTM teams cannot trust AI agents because the data is incomplete, inconsistent or stale, and keeping agent context and skills up to date is manual.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform for building GTM agents on a synced data layer (pricing not public)
product_category: GTM data layer and agent platform
market_need_then: The CEO says she spent about 20 hours a week reviewing agent work and that conversations with more than 100 companies shaped the product (per a launch article dated October 2026); GTM agent startups raised sizable rounds in 2025 and 2026.
outcome_analysis: Kiwi is a Fall 2026 company with two founders from Chalk AI, Plaid and Jane Street backgrounds who launched in October 2026. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news exists. It enters a crowded GTM agent market where Reevo, Default, Alta and HockeyStack have all raised large rounds, so differentiation rests on its cited and replayable data layer.

name: Klaimee
one_liner: Liability insurance for AI Agents. You deploy agents, we cover you.
long_description:
Klaimee is the first insurance for your AI agents. It covers what traditional E&O and cyber explicitly carve out, so you can deploy agentic AI at scale with real peace of mind.
Built for companies deploying agentic AI, self-serve from day one.

The problem: AI agents are taking actions autonomously buying, emailing, modifying sensitive data. AB 316 already holds deployers liable. EU AI Act enforces in August. Cyber and E&O insurance are excluding AI claims. Companies shipping agents have zero coverage and no third-party proof their agent is safe. Enterprise legal asks "who pays if your agent breaks something?" and there's no good answer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
We built the answer. Critical-category risk evaluation, certification, financial guarantee, liability insurance and the documentation enterprise procurement needs to sign off.

Team: Ines (ex-General Manager at SafetyWing, grew insurance product from $5M to $60M revenue, 5 years launching insurance products from scratch and structuring a TokioMarine MGA into its own carrier) + Julien (AI software engineer + corporate strategy, enterprise compliance).

We understand how insurance works, what enterprises require, and why startups can't wait 6 months for either.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies deploying agentic AI who need liability cover and proof of safety for enterprise procurement
problem: Traditional E&O and cyber policies exclude AI agent claims, so companies shipping agents have no coverage and no third party proof that an agent is safe.
business_model: Insurance premiums plus certification and financial guarantee fees, self-serve; website lists pricing from about $22,200 per year for early-stage AI products
product_category: AI agent liability insurance and certification
market_need_then: The company cites California AB 316 holding deployers liable, the EU AI Act enforcement in August, and insurers excluding AI claims; enterprise legal teams ask who pays when an agent fails.
outcome_analysis: Klaimee is a young company that announced a $5.5M seed in July 2026, a few months after its Spring 2026 YC batch. Its CEO has direct insurance product experience from SafetyWing, and regulation and carve-outs in existing policies give it timing support. No outcome exists yet, and competitors AIUC, Armilla and Mount are in the same space.

name: Klarify
one_liner: AI Agent for Therapists
long_description:
Klarify handles every job a therapist does other than the therapy itself, from clinical notes and treatment plans to insurance claims and finding new clients.

Therapists hold the world together. They also run businesses, file insurance claims, write letters, fill forms, supervise new grads, and do hours of paperwork every night. 

Practice management software has existed for decades. It records what therapists do. It can't actually do any of it.

Klara is the AI at the heart of Klarify. She handles notes, treatment plans, clinical letters, insurance claims, between-session resources, supervision prep, and finding new clients.

Nearly 12,300 therapists use Klarify today.

Our mission is to empower therapists, not replace them. So they can focus on the one thing only a human can do. Be present with their client.
regions: Canada; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Solo and small practice therapists and counsellors in the US, Canada and other English speaking markets
problem: Therapists spend large amounts of unpaid time on notes, treatment plans, letters and insurance claims. Klarify's agent Klara drafts these.
business_model: Per therapist SaaS subscription with a free tier and paid plans from 16 to 71 dollars per month
product_category: AI scribe and practice assistant for therapists
market_need_then: Therapist documentation burden is widely discussed and company estimates therapists lose 1,000 to 2,500 dollars per month in missed reimbursement, a company claim from a launch press release.
outcome_analysis: Klarify is a Spring 2026 company with a public launch on June 30, 2026 and claims between 6,000 and 12,000 therapists using it. Usage claims conflict across sources and funding is unverified. It faces established scribe competitors, so its outcome depends on distribution among solo therapists and its added agent features.

name: Klaus AI
one_liner: Fast and Safe OpenClaw on the cloud

name: KugelAudio
one_liner: Kugel is an on-prem Voice AI model supporting 30+ languages
long_description: Kugel is an enterprise-ready TTS model, available on-prem, with a focus on 30+ languages and low latency.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Enterprises and voice agent builders needing low latency multilingual text to speech with EU hosting or on-prem deployment

product_category: Text to speech, voice AI infrastructure
