Crowded competition from ElevenLabs and Mistral is the main risk.

name: Kuli
one_liner: AI coworker for marketing teams at the largest consumer brands
long_description:
Kuli is an AI coworker for marketing teams at the world's largest consumer brands. Our agent watches all videos across social media, learns the brand's context and helps them turn signals from billions of social videos into winning campaigns without increasing headcount.

Previous platforms gave marketers databases to search through and a CRM. Kuli actually watches the content. Marketers at team like Disney, Nivea and PostHog use it to scout creators, run analysis on trends and competitor strategies, and analyse what makes their campaign perform better.

For 10 years, influencer marketing meant more tools, more tabs, more spreadsheets. Kuli replaces all of that with one single agent you orchestrate. One marketer with Kuli does what a $50K/month agency bills for manual tasks.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Marketing and influencer teams at large consumer brands
problem: Creator marketing relies on many tools and manual video review; marketers cannot watch the volume of social video to scout creators and spot trends.
business_model: B2B SaaS, demo led sales; pricing not published
product_category: AI agent for influencer and creator marketing
market_need_then: Brands spend heavily on creator marketing; the company claims one marketer replaces about $50K per month of agency manual work (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Kuli is a one to two person Spring 2026 Paris company selling a video watching agent to big consumer brands, with claimed named customers such as Disney, Nivea and PostHog. There is no verified funding or outcome yet. Strong early customer claims help, but established influencer platforms already sell AI discovery.

name: Kyten Technologies
one_liner: Custom Aerospace-Grade Battery Packs
long_description:
Kyten Technologies is building a factory to manufacture custom aerospace-grade battery packs. 
100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites are being built in the US, but the legacy supply chain can't keep up. 
During our six years at Starlink, we put 5,000+ battery packs into space. Now, we're bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the entire industry.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: LATO
one_liner: Predict how market participants behave
long_description:
LATO is the agent-native research and simulation system that lets investors and companies test any thesis. Funds managing $400bn+ use LATO, including General Atlantic, Hg, Generation, NEA and Verdane, along with their portfolio companies.

We’re backed by leading funds including Y Combinator, Air Street Capital and Axiom Partners. Our angels include Paul Graham and co-founders of Vercel, ElevenLabs, Snowflake and Rogo. LATO was founded by a former private equity investor and an AI/ML engineer.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Investors (funds, private equity) and companies doing commercial due diligence
problem: Commercial diligence needs many expert and customer interviews and documents analyzed over weeks; LATO agents run interviews and build a live market simulation in hours.
business_model: B2B subscription or per study for investors; pricing not published
product_category: AI market research and simulation for investors
market_need_then: Funds pay heavily for expert calls and diligence; YC page claims funds managing over $400bn use LATO (company claim).
outcome_analysis: LATO is a two person Summer 2026 San Francisco company with a founder from growth private equity, backed by YC, Air Street and Axiom plus notable angels. Outcome is unknown. The finance background gives distribution into funds, while AlphaSense and expert networks already sell similar diligence.

name: Lab0
one_liner: AI FDEs to make your B2B SaaS Go Live in Days, not Months
long_description:
Enterprise software implementation is broken,  and it has been for decades. 
Every rollout, whether it's a traditional ERP or a new AI system, requires months of manual integration, configuration, and tuning done by armies of system integrators and forward-deployed engineers. 
Lab0 builds agentic systems that automate this layer, compressing months-long implementations into weeks.
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Enterprise software vendors and system integrators implementing ERP and SaaS platforms
problem: Enterprise software rollouts take months because discovery, configuration, testing and hypercare need large implementation teams.
business_model: B2B, sold to software vendors and integrators; pricing not published
product_category: AI agents for enterprise software implementation
founder_names: Onkar Borade; Lakshya Gupta; Sujay Srivastava
market_need_then: Constellation notes heavy implementation burden for enterprise AI; Lab0 claims rollouts cut from six months to about 10 days and works with Adobe (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Lab0 is a Spring 2026 Bengaluru company with IIT founders and an Emergent alumnus selling AI implementation agents to software vendors and integrators. No verified funding or outcome exists yet. Faster rollouts address a real pain, but large vendors are building the same service.

name: Lamb Labs
one_liner: Lightning fast chips with hardcoded AI models
long_description: Lamb Labs is building Model Processing Units (MPUs), custom AI chips that hardcode LLM weights directly into silicon. Rather than adapting general-purpose processors to run AI models, we're rethinking how LLMs are implemented in hardware to make inference dramatically faster and more energy-efficient.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies running LLM inference who want faster, more energy-efficient hardware
problem: General-purpose processors run LLMs inefficiently; Lamb Labs hardcodes model weights into silicon.
business_model: Hardware sales (custom AI chips, MPUs); not sourced
product_category: AI inference semiconductors
market_need_then: Demand for faster, cheaper LLM inference is evident from the funding of similar chip startups in early 2026 (Taalas, MatX raised 500M per SiliconANGLE Feb 2026 headline); Lamb Labs own performance figures (20,000 tokens/s target, 63x intelligence per watt) are unverified company claims.
outcome_analysis: Lamb Labs is a Summer 2026 company a few months old with only an FPGA prototype and unverified performance targets, so there is no outcome to explain yet. The key uncertainty is whether a hardwired-weights approach can reach silicon while Taalas, which shipped HC1 in February 2026 with much larger funding, is ahead.

name: Lamina Labs
one_liner: Near-real-time video infrastructure for LLMs
long_description:
Lamina Labs is building infrastructure for near-real-time structured video generation.

Most AI video is built for cinematic clips. Lamina is built for useful videos that break down ideas, workflows, and AI answers. Our first product, Simi, turns prompts and documents into whiteboard-style explainer videos in seconds
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: L&D, education, onboarding, creators, small business and developers who need explainer videos
problem: Making explainer videos is slow and costly; Simi turns prompts and documents into narrated whiteboard videos in seconds, via app and API.
business_model: Freemium subscription ($19.99 per month for 6,000 credits) plus usage API
product_category: AI generated whiteboard explainer video
competitors_at_founding: Golpo AI; Animaker AI Whiteboard Video Maker; VideoScribe
market_need_then: Training and education teams need fast video; the founders pitch Simi as a visualization layer for AI answers.
outcome_analysis: Lamina Labs, a two person MIT founded Spring 2026 company, announced $4.8 million on July 30, 2026 after Demo Day, which is a strong early raise for its stage. Simi has a priced product and API, but several whiteboard video generators already exist, so differentiation on speed and cost matters.

name: Lance
one_liner: AI Agents That Run Hotel Operations.
long_description:
Autonomous AI agents that answer calls, close sales, and run operations, so your team can focus on guests. Trusted by some of the top hotel groups in the US, supporting 50+ hotels across brands like Marriott, Hilton, and Hyatt

Built on advanced Computer Use Agent technology, Lance agents can navigate your existing hotel software, make real-time decisions, and handle complex multi-step tasks.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hotel groups and operators (front desk, sales and operations teams) at brands such as Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt properties
problem: Hotels lose bookings and staff time to unanswered calls, messages, RFPs and manual work orders across legacy property systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI agents (receptionist, sales) plus tablet ops hub
product_category: Vertical AI agents for hospitality operations
founder_names: Caleb Chan; Gavin Brennen; Gatik Trivedi
market_need_then: Hotels face high front desk turnover and missed calls; company claims 50+ hotels using it (self reported on YC page).
outcome_analysis: Lance is an early stage W26 company that reported a 5 million dollar seed in April 2026 and claims 50+ hotels across major brands. It benefits from the timing of capable voice and computer-use models and founders with product and exit experience, but the hotel AI receptionist space is crowded and the traction claim is self reported, so the outcome is still open.

name: Lantern AI
tags: Human Resources; Recruiting; HR Tech; Talent Acquisition; AI
one_liner: Agentic Recruiting Platform for Enterprise
long_description:
Lantern is the agentic recruiting platform for enterprise.
Traction: $1M ARR, 30% MoM growth, 230% NDR. Clients include Hyatt, Baker McKenzie, Crypto.com, etc. 

Lantern runs on: 
(1) World People Model, a live talent graph of a billion professionals that knows who’s exceptional, reachable, and about to move
(2) Company Hiring Model, which learns your taste from every hiring decision you’ve ever made

Together, our agents plug into your existing systems and run the whole workflow: sourcing, application review, AI interviews, meeting intelligence, and analytics, under universal context. 

Lantern also launched OpenRouter for People (people.lantern.md), an agent-native infrastructure to empower agents to find, research, outreach to anyone in the world (3000 sign-up & $80k Annualized Run Rate in 25 days).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprise recruiting and talent teams
problem: Recruiting tools are fragmented across sourcing, review, interviews and scheduling; Lantern shares hiring context across agents that can run on or replace an ATS.
business_model: B2B SaaS; company reports $1M ARR in October 2026
product_category: Agentic recruiting platform
market_need_then: Company reports 30 percent month over month growth, 270 percent net dollar retention and clients including Hyatt and Crypto.com (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Lantern AI reached a reported $1M ARR by October 2026 within weeks of its Fall 2026 batch, with founders who ran recruiting startups before. Outcome is open. Growth claims are strong, but the market is crowded and the name is generic.

name: Lark
one_liner: AI agents that automate workflows for distributors
long_description:
Lark deploys AI agents for distributors to automate purchasing, demand forecasting, inventory monitoring, sales operations, and data analysis.

Our agents connect to the ERP, CRM, email, spreadsheets, and other software your team already uses. They forecast demand, prepare purchase orders, flag inventory issues, update sales records, and answer questions using your business data. Together, these agents can run a distributor’s entire operation.

We handle setup and tailor each agent to your workflows, business rules, and approval limits, so your team can automate recurring work while staying in control.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Wholesale and industrial distributors
problem: Distributors run on manual purchasing, forecasting, order entry and inventory spreadsheets across ERP and email; Lark agents automate these with approvals and audit logs.
business_model: B2B SaaS for distributors; pricing not published
product_category: AI agents for distribution operations
market_need_then: Site cites one customer, Interline Hardware, with 60 hours per week saved and 20 percent leaner inventory (company claims).
outcome_analysis: Lark is a two person Fall 2026 company by a repeat YC founder, selling agents to distributors with one named customer and reported savings. There is no outcome yet. Name confusion with ByteDance's Lark is a real discoverability cost.

name: Latent
one_liner: Stop AI agent mistakes by reading the model’s mind
long_description:
Latent is a control layer for AI, built on interpretability. It reads signals inside a model as it works and checks every answer and agent action in milliseconds. Then it lets the output through, holds it, re-asks a stronger model, or sends it to review with the reason attached.

Reading the model is far cheaper than running a second LLM, so it can check every step. Latent stops 99% of rule-breaking agents before they act, against 69% for a frontier LLM judge.

It works with self-hosted and API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, runs hosted or in your own cloud, and calibrates to your traffic with every review.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams running AI agents or LLM features in regulated industries (healthcare, finance, insurance, legal)
problem: LLM judges and human review are costly and miss agent mistakes; teams need cheap per-step checking of answers and actions.
business_model: Usage-based API and gateway, hosted or in customer cloud (pricing not found)
product_category: AI control layer using model interpretability
market_need_then: Enterprises deploying agents in 2026 pay for LLM judges and review; the company claims 600x lower cost than an LLM judge (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Latent is a one-person Fall 2026 YC company with strong research credentials and bold self-reported benchmarks but no public customers or funding yet. Its main risks are competing interpretability startups, labs offering similar monitoring, and unverified performance claims.

name: Lattice Health
one_liner: Monitoring and governance for deployed medical imaging AI
long_description: Lattice Health monitors deployed medical imaging AI so hospitals can tell whether each model is still working, tracking agreement with the radiologist's read, drift, and performance across patient groups. It observes rather than controls and produces the evidence teams need for safety, governance and compliance.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hospitals and health systems that run third party medical imaging AI in production (radiology leadership, CMIOs, AI governance leads)
problem: Once an imaging AI model is live in a hospital, few teams can show whether it still agrees with radiologists, has drifted, or performs evenly across patient groups. Governance and compliance teams need evidence of continuous monitoring.
business_model: B2B software sold to health systems, pilot first; pricing not public
product_category: Clinical AI monitoring and governance
market_need_then: The YC launch post cites FDA, ONC and ACR expectations for continuous post deployment monitoring. A 2026 ACR practice parameter and an RCR monitoring document (March 2026) and a Stanford HAI brief (May 2026) all call for monitoring of deployed clinical AI.
outcome_analysis: Lattice Health is a Spring 2026 company with a single founder and no public customers, funding or outcome yet. The timing tailwind from FDA, ONC and ACR monitoring expectations is real, but a solo founder faces hospital sales cycles and professional society programs.

name: Laurence
one_liner: The frontier operating system for marketers
long_description:
Grow e-commerce revenue across Amazon, DTC, and more with a platform that understands your profits, CACs, CPAs, and TAMs across all channels. Built for the marketers of tomorrow.

Live for Amazon Sponsored Ads and DSP; in beta preview for Meta Ads; Google Ads, ChatGPT Ads, and more in development.

Advertising today is like trading in the 1980s pits: archaic, manual, and iterative guesswork. Humans update bids and keywords with noisy, delayed data using simple if-else rules that both break at scale and ignore stochasticity.

Laurence advertises like modern hedge funds trade markets: custom-fit statistical models that calculate expected profit per click from margin, conversion rates, and CPCs combined with modeling organic sales per rank and per-product LTV.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: E-commerce brands and agencies that spend on Amazon Sponsored Ads and DSP, expanding to Meta and other ad channels
problem: Marketers adjust bids and keywords by hand or with if-else rules on noisy, delayed data; Laurence replaces this with statistical models of expected profit per click.
business_model: B2B SaaS / software that manages ad spend (pricing not found)
product_category: AI advertising optimization for e-commerce (Amazon ads first)
market_need_then: Agencies are said to charge $5,000 to $50,000 a month for ad management (founder on a Fondo podcast); YC page claims $10M in live ad spend managed. Company claims, not verified.
outcome_analysis: Laurence is a Winter 2026 company with two technical founders from big-tech ML and quant trading, selling profit-driven Amazon ad automation. It is active with 12 people and claims $10M in managed ad spend, but no outside funding or customer press was found, so it is too early to say whether it succeeds. The main risk is a crowded Amazon PPC tooling market plus Amazon's own agentic ad tools.

name: LegalOS
one_liner: The AI-Native Immigration Law Firm
long_description:
LegalOS is an AI-native immigration law firm that combines cutting-edge technology with 40+ years of legal expertise.

We’ve studied 12,000 successful petitions to design our process - which allows us to deliver top-quality visa applications in as quickly as 48 hours. Our specialized AI agents draft petition narratives, compile evidence, and anticipate USCIS objections - work that traditionally takes attorneys weeks, if not months.

Every case is reviewed and signed by licensed immigration attorneys with 40+ years of experience, so companies get both speed and reliability. We support O-1, H-1B, L-1A, L-1B, TN, EB-1A, EB-1C, and EB-2 NIW petitions.

Our unique approach works. We’ve filed dozens of visa applications and have a 100% approval rate so far.

The U.S. processes 1M+ work visas annually—a market where incumbents still operate on fax machines, email, and 1990s case management software. We're building the modern immigration law firm.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Startups, enterprises and high skill individuals needing US work visas and green cards (O-1, H-1B, L-1, TN, EB-1, EB-2 NIW)
problem: Immigration petitions take attorneys weeks or months and incumbents use legacy tools. LegalOS drafts narratives and evidence with AI and attorneys review and sign.
business_model: AI enabled immigration law practice, per case fees (government fees extra); prices not published
product_category: Legal services, immigration
founder_names: Matthew Asir; Rachel Asir; Claire Jutabha
market_need_then: The company cites more than 1M US work visas a year and slow, manual legacy processes. Founders grew up in a family immigration practice and the company lists startup clients such as Arc Prize on its site.
outcome_analysis: LegalOS is a Winter 2026 company still active with early traction (dozens of filings claimed). Founders have family immigration practice experience, which helps credibility, but competition is crowded and funding facts are unverified.

name: LemonLime
one_liner: Fully automated growth for small business
long_description:
LemonLime runs fully automated sales and marketing for small businesses.

Every morning, LemonLime finds you new leads and drafts personalized outreach, prepares branded content, and identifies untapped sales & marketing opportunities.

All you have to do is click send.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Small and medium businesses that want sales and marketing done for them
problem: Small businesses lack time and staff to find leads, write outreach and produce content. LemonLime finds leads each morning, drafts outreach and content, and asks the owner only to approve.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription; pricing page exists but figures not captured
product_category: AI sales and marketing automation for SMBs
market_need_then: Small businesses have limited marketing staff; 2026 roundups describe many AI sales agents aimed at SMBs, indicating demand and crowding.
outcome_analysis: LemonLime is a Summer 2026 company, active, with no confirmed funding or customers. Its main public moment is a July 2026 hiring stunt that drew heavy criticism; whether it hurts or helps depends on later execution in a crowded SMB category.

name: Letter
one_liner: The world's first coding agent, IDE & infra for growth engineering.
long_description: The Letter Company issues autonomous pull requests to scale websites, agent experiences, and so much more. Today, we solve modern issues like agentic conviction, inbound conversion, SEO, GEO, etc. However, we believe as agents become more truth-seeking, spammy marketing strategies will fall apart in favor of benchmark and evidence-based messaging. These are engineering problems that only a purpose-built coding agent can solve.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software and marketing teams that want autonomous pull requests to improve website conversion, SEO and AI search visibility
problem: Growth work such as conversion, SEO and generative engine optimization is really engineering work that marketers cannot ship alone. Letterpress-1 is a coding agent that opens pull requests for it.
business_model: Software subscription; pricing page exists but figures not captured
product_category: Coding agent for growth engineering
market_need_then: Rapid growth of AI search made SEO and GEO urgent for marketers in 2026, and Profound reached a $1B valuation in February 2026.
outcome_analysis: The Letter Company is a Fall 2026 company so there is no outcome yet. It targets a hot category, AI search driven growth work, with a coding agent approach, but faces well funded measurement players and general coding agents.

name: Levocred AI
one_liner: AI Workforce for lenders
long_description: Levocred AI build AI employees for lenders including credit funds, fintechs, credit unions & banks to automate operations like servicing/collections, underwriting, back-office tasks etc.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Credit funds, fintech lenders, credit unions and banks
problem: Lenders run servicing, collections, underwriting, monitoring and compliance reporting with manual back office work. Levocred builds AI employees that draft IC memos, answer questions on the loan book in Slack and test compliance certificates.
business_model: Usage based AI workforce (company says scale with tokens, not headcount); prices not public
product_category: AI back office automation for lenders
market_need_then: Private credit grew and funds need operations staff; a 2026 Apex survey and industry guides discuss AI in private credit operations. Company claims one customer, Pier Asset Management, and $1B+ running through the product (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Levocred is a Summer 2026 company, active, claiming live production use at credit funds. Founders come from credit fund operations, which fits the buyer. No outcome yet; competition from funded private credit AI vendors is the main risk.

name: Lexius
one_liner: AI for Corporate Security Cameras
long_description:
Lexius turns existing security cameras into an AI security guard that detects, documents, and alerts incidents like shoplifting and slip-and-falls.

Millions of locations already have cameras but no intelligence. Replacing them costs $50K to $100K per site. Lexius upgrades every camera instantly, no rip and replace, no new hardware.

Real-world camera systems are messy, fragmented, and decades old, and AI breaks on low-quality CCTV. The hard part isn’t the model, it’s making unreliable systems work at scale with accuracy high enough for real decisions.

Lexius starts with security and liability, and becomes the operating system for physical spaces.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Grocery and retail chains with existing cameras, loss prevention and store operations teams
problem: Retailers lose money to missed scans and theft and cannot afford to replace cameras at $50K to $100K per site. Lexius adds AI to existing cameras and matches video to the register log.
business_model: B2B software per store; pricing not public, free trials in stores reported
product_category: Computer vision for retail loss prevention
market_need_then: The ECR 2026 self checkout loss report found missed scans in roughly 1% to 4.8% of transactions; Lexius shows logos such as Erewhon and Pak'nSave on its site and a Marino's Market case study.
outcome_analysis: Lexius is a Winter 2026 company, active, with retail logos and a narrowed checkout wedge. No outcome yet. Competition from Everseen and Scandit and the hard messy CCTV problem are the main risks, while store trials show early pull.

name: Libra Robotics
tags: Hard Tech; Robotics; Construction; Energy; AI
one_liner: The robot workforce for infrastructure of the AI era
long_description: Infrastructure faces rapid expansion and labor shortages. Today, robots struggle to scale to meet customers’ high-mix work needs. Libra builds AI that engineers robots for new tasks across embodiments. We go from each new infra task to field-deployable robots 10x faster. Today, our robots are working on solar farms and piloting in data centers. Contractors pay for completed work as a service, not robots.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Contractors building solar farms and data centers
problem: Infrastructure builds face labor shortages and robots struggle with high mix work. Libra builds AI that engineers robots for new tasks and sells completed work as a service.
business_model: Robots as a service, contractors pay for completed work (pay per watt reported for solar)
product_category: Construction and infrastructure robotics
market_need_then: Solar and data center build outs face labor shortages; AES framed Maximo as installing at half the cost, and Planted Solar raised $31.8M to build solar for data centers with robots.
outcome_analysis: Libra Robotics is a Fall 2026 company (a Fondo post calls it Summer 2026, a conflict) with robots on solar sites and data center pilots. Strong robotics founders fit the problem, but capital intensity and funded rivals are the main risks. No outcome yet.

name: Light Anchor
one_liner: AI-native growth agency for consumer brands
long_description:
Light Anchor (YC P26) is an AI-native growth agency for consumer brands.

Consumer brands have always been limited by the speed of humans: hiring, coordinating, and sleeping. AI agents that now run operations end-to-end break all those constraints, making a new kind of consumer business possible: one capped by compute, not headcount.

Today, Light Anchor operates 7 brands, all run by AI agents on a shared platform that compounds with every new brand launched. The vision is thousands of consumer businesses, operating with little to no human intervention.
regions: South Korea; East Asia
target_customer: Consumer brands, mostly Korean beauty and e-commerce brands, that pay for AI run growth and operations
problem: Consumer brands are limited by human hiring and coordination speed. Light Anchor runs ads, storefronts, AI search visibility and research with AI agents on a shared platform and also operates its own AI run brands.
business_model: Performance fee of 5 to 15 percent of revenue the agents create, with pilot first and no retainer (company site)
product_category: AI native growth agency and AI run consumer brands
market_need_then: The company claims eight client brands and sample reports showing weekly sales for one serum brand, all self reported; Korean e-commerce brands entering global markets supply demand.
outcome_analysis: Light Anchor is a Spring 2026 company that raised pre-YC seed money from Krew Capital and ASQ and a YC investment, and runs AI agents for several brands. No outcome yet. Risks are agency style services that scale with revenue share and dependence on ad platforms.

name: LightSprint
one_liner: Software factory for product teams
long_description:
Lightsprint is a collaborative software factory for product teams to plan visually, preview live and ship with an army of cloud agents. Your whole team, including non-engineers, can now ship end to end reliably.

The company is founded by Ben Ong, an AI investor who previously scaled AI products at SEA Group (NYSE: SE) and Temasek ($300B fund), Benedict Chan who was VP Engineering at Chainlink and CTO at BitGo (NYSE:BTGO), and Heng Hong Lee who built Facebook Messenger in 2013 and was Director of Engineering at Fazz (YC S17).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Product teams at software companies, including PMs, designers and ops staff who want to ship code changes with engineering approval
problem: Non engineers cannot safely change production software and agent tools are single player. Lightsprint gives a shared cloud workspace where teams plan visually, preview live and ship pull requests through cloud agents that engineering approves.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat, free plan and Pro at 40 dollars per seat per month, with bring your own model keys
product_category: Collaborative AI software development platform
founder_names: Ben Ong; Benedict Chan; Heng Hong Lee
market_need_then: By early 2026 commentary described PMs and designers opening pull requests with coding agents, but prototypes were not production ready, creating demand for governed workflows.
outcome_analysis: Experienced founders from BitGo, Facebook and Temasek joined YC in Spring 2026 and raised a 6.1 million dollar seed led by 645 Ventures in October 2026, reporting more than 100 companies using the product since an April start. It is early and active with no shutdown or sale found. The main risk is that coding agent vendors absorb the non engineer collaboration wedge.

name: Limnion
one_liner: Telemetry storage for the agentic era.
long_description: Limnion is building an open-standards telemetry storage platform for observability at scale, including agentic workflows. Siglake is the open-source project that sits at the heart of it, designed around OTel, Parquet, and Iceberg. No proprietary storage, no vendor lock-in.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Engineering and platform teams that run observability at scale, including teams monitoring AI agent workflows and wanting telemetry in their own object storage
problem: Telemetry volumes are growing fast, and proprietary observability storage is costly and locks customers in. Limnion offers open-standards storage so data stays in the customer's own object store.
business_model: Open-source core (Siglake, Apache 2.0) with planned commercial BYOC platform and anomaly detection layer
product_category: Observability and telemetry storage
founder_names: Todd (surname not stated in sources opened)
competitors_at_founding: Imply Lumi Loglake; Altinity open observability stack (ClickHouse with Iceberg, Parquet, OpenTelemetry); OpenObserve
market_need_then: Observability cost and lock-in complaints, plus growing telemetry from agentic systems, drove vendors to move telemetry into open lakehouse formats in 2026.
outcome_analysis: Limnion is a brand new Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its site lists array.vc, Foundation Capital and Y Combinator as backers without amounts. The open source Siglake project and the founder's long observability career are strengths, while established vendors already sell competing lakehouse telemetry products.

name: Limrun
one_liner: Extend cloud sandboxes with iOS, Android and more
long_description:
Coding agents in the cloud don't work for majority of teams who require native capabilities; they lack XCode for iOS, Emulator for Android, Unity for game development teams. We are on a mission to cloudify every local development utility so that regardless of where it runs, your agent can compose an ideal set of capabilities on the fly so you don't need to run it on your laptop.

Today, we provide remote services such as XCode, iOS & Android simulators to enable coding agents running in any sandbox to be able to build and iterate over mobile apps, too.

Replit, Rork, Momentic, Minitap and more agent companies have built mobile development and testing experiences on Limrun platform. Coconote (Quizlet), SorceJobs (W25) and more companies with mobile apps use Limrun with their cloud agents, merging PRs without having to check out the code locally.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Teams building cloud coding agents and mobile app tools, such as app builders and testing startups
problem: Coding agents run in Linux sandboxes and cannot build or test iOS apps, which need Xcode and the iOS Simulator. Limrun provides remote Xcode, iOS Simulator and Android Emulator.
business_model: Usage based pricing split between idle time and build time
product_category: Developer infrastructure, cloud mobile simulators for AI agents
market_need_then: Cloud coding agents cannot run local simulators, a limitation noted in Expo's docs. Customers named by Limrun include Replit and Rork, a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Limrun is a Spring 2026 company led by a solo founder with strong infrastructure credentials and named customers among agent builders. Funding is unverified and the category drew several rivals within months, including Expo, so the outcome depends on staying the default simulator layer for agent platforms.

name: Linzumi
one_liner: Team chat to command all your company's coding agents
long_description:
Linzumi is the chat your engineering team uses to direct dozens of AI coding agents.

Kick off work, review it, ship it. All from chat.

See every agent's work. Unblock the agents that need you from your laptop, your phone, the coffee line. Your teammates see it too.

Every decision your team makes compiles into a source of truth - what to build, why it changed, how your agents should act. That same source generates new work and verifies completed work.

Deliberative alignment, repurposed from aligning LLMs to aligning companies.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Software engineering teams running many AI coding agents who want shared visibility and control
problem: Teams running dozens of coding agents lose track of their work and decisions; Linzumi puts agents inside team chat channels so work can be started, reviewed and unblocked together.
business_model: SaaS subscription: free personal tier, company tier listed at 100 USD per month
product_category: Team chat for AI coding agents
market_need_then: Coding agents were spreading quickly in 2026, and teams needed shared coordination around them.
outcome_analysis: Linzumi is an early Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. The founder previously sold OneGraph to Netlify and worked at OpenAI on alignment, which fits the agent coordination wedge. The main risk is that chat and model vendors ship competing agent channels, as Slack did in August 2026.

name: Liquid Energy
tags: Hard Tech; Solar Power; Energy; AI
one_liner: Self contained solar-powered AI inference modules: the NanoDC
long_description:
Liquid Energy delivers the most scalable and cost effective inference. Our compute is hosted in our proprietary data center modules that we call NanoDC - the Nano Data Center. 

NanoDC is engineered to be rapidly deployable and scalable without traditional bottlenecks like power, permitting, and supply chains. Using NanoDC, Liquid Energy is able to provide the most efficient and sustainable way to scale compute to meet global AI demand.

We have 20 units and have spent the last year in building the supply chain and manufacturing, because of that we have an ability to manufacture 2 MW/month. Over the next year we will scale that up to 20MW per month.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: AI companies and operators buying inference capacity who cannot wait for grid power, permitting and data center construction
problem: Power, permitting and supply chains bottleneck new AI data centers. Liquid Energy ships factory built solar powered modules (NanoDC) that it says go from contract to first token in under eight weeks.
business_model: Inference compute sold from owned modular solar data centers (hardware plus compute as a service)
product_category: Modular solar powered AI inference data centers
founder_names: Sid Ravikumar; Sajan Khosa; Arsh Sekhon
market_need_then: AI inference demand was constrained by power and data center build times in 2026, driving interest in rapidly deployable off grid compute.
outcome_analysis: Liquid Energy is an early Fall 2026 hardware company with no outcome yet. It claims 20 units built and 2 MW per month of capacity, but coverage mostly repeats company claims. Funding is unknown beyond Y Combinator, Nvidia Inception and Velocity affiliations, and competitors such as Rune and Crusoe are better funded.

name: Litmus
one_liner: Evals for humans
long_description:
At Litmus, we’re building evals for humans and redefining how talent is evaluated. Teams like Mercor, Wispr, Composio, Neo Scholars, Astranis, and more are already using Litmus to build their technical teams.

Every company in the world will soon be powered by neo-humans (agent assisted people). But building evals to measure neo-human performance is unexplored and difficult. It requires systematically benchmarking neo-human capabilities and failure modes across all sectors of knowledge work, developing reproducible environments that test neo-human performance on complex tasks, and designing causal attribution frameworks over execution trajectories to identify and validate reproducible action sequences and decision patterns that lead to successful outcomes.

At Litmus, we’re solving this problem. We deliver hiring insights to companies by capturing how candidates use tools, reason, and make decisions in their interviews, giving agentic graders the evidence to evaluate candidate skillset and predict job performance.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and tech companies hiring engineers who want to see how candidates work with AI tools
problem: Standard coding tests no longer show how candidates perform when using AI tools. Litmus generates async assessments from a company's own repos and tickets and grades the process and output.
business_model: B2B SaaS with custom pricing; integrates with Ashby, Greenhouse and Lever
product_category: Technical hiring assessments
market_need_then: AI tools made leaked-question coding tests less informative, and hiring teams sought new signals; company reports 3,000 assessments evaluated and about 60k USD ARR.
outcome_analysis: Litmus is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. It reports early traction with companies like Mercor and Astranis and about 60k USD ARR per its YC page. The risks are well funded incumbent assessment vendors and a name shared with several other Litmus and Lytmus companies.

name: Locke
one_liner: The First AI Government Affairs Firm.
long_description:
Locke is the first AI-native government affairs firm.

We pair elite lobbyists and political talent with our own AI systems, helping companies lobby policymakers and win government contracts.

Locke's team comes from The White House, Congress, and the Pentagon.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Early stage and growth companies in defense, healthcare, GovTech and other sectors that need lobbying, regulatory monitoring and government sales help
problem: Companies need to influence policymakers and win government contracts, but traditional firms split Hill, agency and procurement work across expensive separate teams. Locke pairs in-house lobbyists with an AI system (LockeOS).
business_model: Professional services firm (retainers) powered by proprietary AI software
product_category: AI-native government affairs and lobbying firm
market_need_then: Reported AI related lobbying spending rose in 2026, and companies sell to government at growing scale; company reports over 500K USD run rate six weeks after launch (its own statement).
outcome_analysis: Locke is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. The founder's White House and policy background and a reported 500K USD run rate within weeks (company statement) support founder market fit. Risks are the services heavy model, regulation of lobbying work and competing AI native policy startups such as Fed10.

name: Luca IQ
one_liner: API-first tax engine for CPA firms and developers
long_description: Luca IQ is an API for deterministic tax calculation and an IRS Authorized e-filing engine - the foundation for accounting firms and fintechs building on tax.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: CPA and accounting firms, plus fintechs and developers building on tax calculation
problem: Tax software for accounting firms is dated and fragmented. Luca IQ offers a deterministic tax calculation engine, workflow platform and IRS authorized e-filing, also via API.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage based API sold through CPA and tax firms
product_category: Tax engine and e-file platform
market_need_then: CPA firms depend on legacy tax software, and AI tools raised demand for API based tax engines; the company says it keeps a waiting list of firms.
outcome_analysis: Luca IQ is a Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its early win is IRS e-file approval for Form 1040 announced August 2026, which supports a regulatory position. Open questions are funding, scale through a first filing season and competition from April, Instead and incumbents.

name: Lucent
one_liner: AI that automatically improves products from user behavior
long_description: Lucent is an AI product manager that automatically improves products based on how users behave. We use AI to watch and understand user sessions and detect bugs and UX issues.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Startups and product teams with web or app products that already record session replays
problem: Nobody has time to watch session replays, so bugs and UX problems go unnoticed. Lucent uses AI to watch every replay and surface bugs, with reports routed to Slack or Linear.
business_model: Usage based SaaS (free tier of 400 sessions processed)
product_category: AI session replay analysis
market_need_then: Teams generate far more replays than humans can watch; Lucent reports use by 30+ YC companies including Reducto, Julius and Finta.
outcome_analysis: Lucent is a Winter 2026 company with no outcome yet. It raised a reported pre-seed in October 2025 and claims use by 30+ YC companies. The main risk is that session replay incumbents add AI analysis, making the wedge easy to copy.

name: Luel
one_liner: Turning everyday words and actions into usable training data.
long_description: Luel is a sourcing and licensing platform for rights-cleared multimodal training data at scale. We work with frontier AI teams to provide high-quality bespoke data collections and off-the-shelf datasets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and AI teams buying rights-cleared multimodal training data
problem: AI teams need licensed, consented video, audio and action data with provenance. Luel runs a two sided marketplace and collection engine delivering audit ready data within days.
business_model: Marketplace and bespoke data collection, licensing fees from AI buyers, payouts to a contributor network
product_category: AI training data marketplace
market_need_then: Frontier labs faced copyright pressure and needed licensed, consented multimodal data; Bloomberg Law reported licensing startups blooming amid legal battles.
outcome_analysis: Luel is a Winter 2026 company with no exit. It announced a 31.2M USD seed led by Lightspeed on May 15, 2026, a large early raise tied to demand for licensed AI training data. Competition from Troveo, Protege and established vendors, and unverified traction claims, are the open risks.

name: Lumeria
tags: Consumer Health Services; Health Tech; Health & Wellness; Skincare; AI
one_liner: Oura Ring for Skin
long_description: The Lumoscope is a multispectral camera that clips onto your phone and scans your skin at home with the same light used in clinics. You see what a mirror can't: a breakout days before it surfaces, and wrinkles changing over time. Our software then reads that history, connects flare-ups to causes you'd never suspect, and matches products to what your own data shows works.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers with acne, eczema or aging concerns who buy a phone attachment plus an app subscription-style coaching service
problem: People cannot see skin changes that happen below the surface or track causes of flare-ups over time, so product choices are guesswork.
business_model: Consumer hardware (Lumoscope phone clip, preorder price reported at 199 to 329 USD) plus AI app (Lumi)
product_category: Consumer skin imaging hardware and AI skin health app
competitors_at_founding: Perfect Corp skin analysis (software and hardware guides)
market_need_then: Large consumer skincare spend and an existing market of skin analysis apps; founder Guo cites personal eczema experience. No independent demand data found; the company claims a 24 hour first batch sellout per a Chinese-language article (unverified).
outcome_analysis: Lumeria is an active Summer 2026 company at preorder stage, so there is no outcome yet. The launch drew trade press and a founder audience, but a third-party directory says no FDA record exists and questions the hardware claims, and no funding round has been confirmed beyond YC, so credibility and delivery of the shipments expected in September and October 2026 are the open risks.

name: Lumius
one_liner: Fast, smart, accessible 3D ultrasound that anyone can use
long_description:
Ultrasound today is still mostly 2D. Clinicians have to imagine the 3D anatomy in their head while also moving the probe at the same time. This makes procedures like vascular access hard to learn and perform consistently, especially for beginners. ~50% fail on their first attempt. Hospitals also spend millions each year on 2D ultrasound training. Meanwhile, existing 3D ultrasound devices can cost >10× as much.

Lumius is building fast, smart, and accessible 3D ultrasound systems to eliminate this 2D guesswork. Our technology shows a clear, real-time 3D view of what’s inside the body. It works over a large volume, not just a thin slice. The device is also affordable, compact, and portable.

We are starting with vascular access, especially central line. Future use cases include blood clot detection, tumor diagnosis, and biopsy guidance. Our long-term vision is a universal 3D ultrasound platform that brings easy-to-use, real-time imaging to a wide range of clinical and eventually consumer applications.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hospitals and clinicians performing vascular access, especially central line placement, and ultrasound training programs
problem: 2D ultrasound forces clinicians to imagine 3D anatomy while moving the probe; about half of beginners fail on a first central line attempt and existing 3D devices cost over ten times as much.
business_model: Medical device sales (3D ultrasound system with AI and mixed reality guidance)
product_category: 3D and wearable ultrasound medical devices
market_need_then: Central line placement has a high first attempt failure rate among beginners per the company; hospitals spend heavily on ultrasound training. Demand evidence is company stated.
outcome_analysis: Lumius is an active Spring 2026 company with no exit. It is a Duke spinout selected by Y Combinator in March 2026 and still raising a seed round as of June 2026 according to a report found in search; the product is not FDA cleared, so the main risks are regulatory timing, hardware cost targets and incumbent response.

name: Lux Foods
tags: Cellular Agriculture; Robotics; Manufacturing; Agriculture; Biotechnology
one_liner: Crops engineered for premium fruit, grown without sunlight.
long_description: Lux Foods engineers ultra-compact plants that produce mostly fruit, then grows them on sugar with 90% less light. We design the biology and hardware together to make robotic farming easier. Starting with cherry tomatoes, we’re building year-round production of flavorful, nutritious, pesticide-free fruit near the people who eat it. Our tomatoes have been grown on the International Space Station, and now we're taking this technology to Earth.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Chefs, grocery buyers and distributors seeking premium fresh fruit year round near cities
problem: Indoor farming is dominated by lighting cost; growing fruit crops without sunlight and with far less light could make local year round production viable.
business_model: Produce sales from company-run robotic indoor farms, starting with cherry tomatoes
product_category: Cellular agriculture and indoor farming (sugar-fed engineered plants)
market_need_then: Lighting is the main cost of indoor farms per industry press, and consumers pay premiums for flavorful local fruit; NASA's Deep Space Food Challenge showed institutional interest in light-independent food production.
outcome_analysis: Lux Foods is a Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its credibility rests on the UC Riverside lab record in NASA's Deep Space Food Challenge and the 2022 Nature Food result, while the central commercial risk is that yield and cost at scale are not yet demonstrated and no funding beyond YC is public.

name: Lyon
tags: Machine Learning; Finance; Data Science; Big Data
one_liner: Foundation models on enterprise event data.
long_description:
Lyon builds private foundation models for banks, fintechs, funds, brokers and payments companies, turning their own data into better predictions.

These models apply the transformer technology behind large language models to transaction histories, loan records and customer activity. They learn relationships across events and over time that manually engineered features can miss, producing richer signals for existing models and new applications.

The same model can support fraud detection, credit default prediction, loss given default estimation and product recommendations. Lyon develops and deploys each institution’s model, with software to keep it current and integrate its predictions into existing systems.

At a consumer fintech with tens of millions of users, a Lyon model trained on tens of billions of transactions delivered a 112% relative improvement in default prediction PR-AUC over the fintech’s existing tree-based model.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Banks, fintechs, funds, brokers, insurers and payments companies with large event datasets
problem: Hand-engineered features miss patterns across transaction histories; institutions want better fraud, credit and churn predictions without sending data outside their cloud.
business_model: Custom private foundation model development and deployment per institution plus software to keep it current
product_category: Enterprise foundation models on event and transaction data
market_need_then: Banks and fintechs spend heavily on fraud and credit models; transaction foundation models were a visible 2025 to 2026 theme in industry articles (Thoughtworks, Fintech Wrap Up).
outcome_analysis: Lyon is a two person Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. The thesis matches a real industry trend, and the claimed fintech result is strong, but it competes with in-house efforts at large payments firms and has no confirmed funding beyond YC, so customer concentration and sales cycles with regulated institutions are the main risks.

name: Madrone
one_liner: Hyper-efficient coolers for data centers
long_description: Madrone builds cooling systems for data centers. In Texas, where most new sites are, Madrone can cool using 30% less power and water, thanks to novel dew-point cooling technology.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data center operators and hyperscale builders in hot regions, starting with Texas
problem: Up to 40 percent of data center power goes to cooling, and chillers and cooling towers consume large amounts of power and water.
business_model: Hardware sales of modular dew-point cooling systems for new builds and retrofits
product_category: Data center cooling hardware
market_need_then: AI data center buildout in 2025 to 2026 is straining power and water, and Texas has many new sites; an Uptime Institute April 2026 briefing argues dry cooling can match evaporative performance, so the claimed water advantage may be contested.
outcome_analysis: Madrone is an active Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. The market pull from AI data center growth is strong, but the technology is not novel, incumbents are well resourced, and no installations or pilots were found in public sources, so proving the claimed 30 percent savings in the field is the key milestone.

name: Magma
one_liner: Monetize your agent's traces.
long_description: We enable companies monetize their agents' traces.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies that build AI agents and want revenue from their agent interaction data; buyers are AI labs
problem: Agent traces contain valuable training signal but companies have no safe way to anonymize, package and license them.
business_model: Revenue share on licensing of anonymized agent traces and derived training environments to AI labs
product_category: AI training data and RL environment licensing
market_need_then: Frontier labs spend heavily on training data and RL environments; a 2026 market map says about 50 vendors compete and buyers are building in house.
outcome_analysis: Magma is a one person Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. The idea has a clear buyer set and a recent precedent for licensing agent records, but a solo founder, no public customers or licensing deals, and strong incumbent data vendors make supply acquisition and lab willingness to pay the main risks.

name: Maingen
one_liner: Simulating Agents Running Industrial Companies
long_description: Maingen builds simulations for industrial operations ($5 trillion slice of the US economy) so frontier labs can train models that actually run power plants, factories, and datacenters.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs that train models to operate industrial systems (company says it is already working with frontier labs, none named)
problem: Models lack realistic simulated environments of industrial operations (power plants, factories, solar portfolios, datacenters) in which to learn to run them.
business_model: Bespoke RL environments and benchmarks sold to AI labs (pricing not public)
product_category: RL training environments / industrial simulation
competitors_at_founding: Bespoke Labs; Mechanize / Fleet AI / HUD / Veris AI / Plato; Scale AI, Surge AI, Mercor, Turing
market_need_then: Labs were buying RL environments in 2026 (Epoch AI interview study cited by a trade outlet). Industrial deployment demand is claimed by the company ($5T slice of US economy) but no independent evidence of paying industrial customers was found.
outcome_analysis: Maingen is a two-person Summer 2026 company that is still early. It has a public benchmark (SolarBench) and says it works with frontier labs, but no named customers, rounds or exit were found, so no verdict on success or failure is possible yet. The main risks are a crowded RL environment market and weak defensibility.

name: Mango Medical
one_liner: Foundation models for planning orthopedic surgery
long_description: Mango Medical builds agentic surgical planning AI for orthopedic surgery. We deliver surgeon-ready plans in minutes instead of days. 8-figure LOI from a top orthopedic company. Pursuing FDA 510(k) clearance. We're building a future where every surgery follows a personalized plan.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Orthopedic implant companies and surgeons who need surgical plans, starting with total shoulder arthroplasty
problem: Preoperative orthopedic planning takes days of manual work; the company delivers plans from CT scans and X-rays in minutes.
business_model: API and software for surgical planning sold to implant companies and providers, pending FDA 510(k) clearance
product_category: Agentic AI surgical planning for orthopedics
competitors_at_founding: Precision AI planning software; Smith+Nephew Coriograph shoulder planning
market_need_then: Surgeons and implant companies depend on slow planning services; the company claims an 8 figure LOI from a top orthopedic company, which is unverified and unnamed.
outcome_analysis: Mango Medical is an active Winter 2026 company with no exit. It reports a large unnamed LOI and has a named investor in Tekedia Capital, but regulatory clearance is still pending and cleared plus incumbent shoulder planning products already exist, so converting the LOI and getting 510(k) clearance are the key milestones.

name: Manicule
one_liner: AgentRel — Devrel For Agents
long_description:
Manicule does AgentRel. We get companies discovered and used by AI agents. Think DevRel, rebuilt for a world where agents make all the decisions. 

Our software tracks how often AI recommends your product; our team handles the strategy, documentation, technical content, and distribution that help developers and coding agents use it. Customers include Agentmail, Greptile, Reducto, and Mastra.

Naman has been doing fractional DevRel since 13. Shreyans started building at 14 and was Supermemory’s founding engineer. We met in high school and have built multiple startups together since.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Developer tool and AI infrastructure companies that want to be discovered and used by AI agents
problem: AI coding agents now choose which tools developers use, and companies have no visibility into or strategy for how agents recommend them.
business_model: Services retainers for strategy, docs, content and distribution plus agent visibility tracking software
product_category: Agent relations (DevRel and generative engine optimization for AI agents)
market_need_then: Developer tool firms report agents influencing tool choice; Grit Daily and the site cite a Supermemory case study claiming 90 percent more traffic in three months (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Manicule is an active Spring 2026 company that raised a 1.3 million dollar seed in October 2026 and lists named developer tool customers. Founder fit is strong because both founders did DevRel and startup engineering early, but the model is service heavy and overlaps with funded visibility trackers, so scaling beyond founder led delivery is the main test.

name: Manifold
tags: Hardware; Warehouse Management Tech; Robotics; Logistics; Supply Chain
one_liner: Drop-in robotic labor that works on Day 1
long_description:
The US Warehouse industry spends $75bn on labor each year. Yet, only 10% of US warehouses have any form of automation, because existing robotics are too expensive and hard to integrate. 

Manifold deploys autonomous robots that handle picking, loading / unloading, and palletizing — priced by pick. Integration in hours. No upfront costs. No retrofitting. No need to rebuild the operation around the robot. 

Our mission is to make it easy for any warehouse to adopt robotics.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US warehouse and distribution operators that move cases by hand and have not automated
problem: Most US warehouses have no automation because existing robotics cost too much and are hard to integrate, so labor stays the main cost. Manifold sells robot labor priced per pick with no upfront cost.
business_model: robotics as a service, usage-based pricing per pick
product_category: warehouse robotics (case picking, truck loading and unloading, palletizing)
market_need_then: The company cites $75bn of annual US warehouse labor spend and only 10 percent of warehouses with any automation, which are its own figures from the YC page.
outcome_analysis: Manifold is a two person Summer 2026 company that has just launched, so there is no outcome yet. It pairs a technical founder with robotics control research and a supply chain operator, and sells robot labor per pick to remove upfront cost. The main risks are hardware execution and well funded warehouse robotics rivals that launched case picking in 2026.

name: Mantis
one_liner: Digital Twins of humans
long_description: Mantis is a digital twin company that combines LLMs with high-fidelity physics simulations in order to convert rare and difficult-to-access human behavior data into predictive models.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharma, biotech, clinical trial designers and healthcare providers that need predictive models of human physiology and behavior
problem: Rare and hard to access human behavior and physiology data limits prediction in medicine. Mantis combines LLMs with physics simulation to build digital twins that fill the data gap.
business_model: B2B platform where customers request scoped predictions from digital twins, pricing not stated
product_category: digital twins of humans for healthcare and biomedical research
market_need_then: Medicine suffers from data availability gaps for rare conditions and trial populations, and coverage in 2025 and 2026 shows steady investment in healthcare digital twins.
outcome_analysis: Mantis is a Winter 2026 company with a single founder that raised a reported seed of about 7.4 million dollars led by Decibel. There is no exit or failure signal. The story so far rests on a hard research problem, a planned rare disease pilot, and a founder with biomedical startup experience, while validation with paying customers is still unproven.

name: Mantle
one_liner: The pit crew for machines and robots.
long_description:
Mantle is a full-stack field service company that deploys, fixes and maintains machines for the companies that build them. We're not a marketplace or software tool, we own uptime directly to provide better, more reliable service without burdening your engineers on support calls. 

$500B+ a year is spent to keep machines running in the US, we're coming for all of it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robot and machine manufacturers that need field deployment, repair and maintenance for their installed fleets
problem: Companies that build machines and robots get pulled into support calls and uptime problems at customer sites. Mantle owns field service and uptime directly so engineers do not have to.
business_model: full stack field service contracted by machine makers, pricing not stated
product_category: field service for robots and industrial machines
market_need_then: The company claims 500 billion dollars a year is spent keeping machines running in the US, its own figure. Robot makers hiring field service staff in 2026 shows the support burden is real.
outcome_analysis: Mantle is a Fall 2026 company with no public traction, site or funding data yet. Both founders have built and sold or scaled earlier ventures in physical operations, which gives it founder market fit for a services business. The key uncertainty is whether robot makers outsource service or build their own teams, as 2026 job postings suggest some are doing.

name: Maquoketa Research
one_liner: Automated LiveOps for Game Studios
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: The YC directory says game studios (LiveOps automation). The founders' launch post and directories describe defense buyers of one way attack drone guidance, so the real customer is unclear.
problem: The directory one liner is automated LiveOps for game studios. The launch post describes terminal guidance modules for one way attack drones, so the stated problem conflicts with the launch material.
business_model: unclear, no pricing found
product_category: conflicting: game LiveOps software per directory, defense drone guidance per launch post and directories
founder_names: Evan Yeager; David Muchow; Aidan Williams
market_need_then: For the drone reading, a government program to buy large numbers of low cost one way attack drones signals demand. For the LiveOps reading, game studios use live events to retain players, but no demand evidence specific to the company was found.
outcome_analysis: Maquoketa Research is a Spring 2026 company with a five person team and no public outcome. The founders show technical depth and one has a large Roblox revenue result, but the directory description and the launch post disagree about the product. Nothing about customers, funding or traction could be verified, so no success or failure factors are assigned.

name: Marble
one_liner: The autonomous back-of-house for restaurants.
long_description:
Marble is the first AI-native operating system for the restaurant back-of-house. 

Restaurants, cafes and bars still run on a patchwork of disconnected point solutions, spreadsheets, clipboards and tribal knowledge, which costs the industry billions each year in stockouts, food waste, and lost profit. 

Marble replaces that entire stack with one system. Computer vision and voice AI capture real-time inventory levels 90% faster than manual counts, ML models forecast item-level demand at 97% accuracy, and AI agents run dozens of end-to-end workflows autonomously, from procurement and invoice reconciliation to scheduling, food prep, menu engineering, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Multi-unit restaurant groups, cafes and bars in the US and Canada
problem: Restaurant back of house runs on disconnected tools, spreadsheets and clipboards, causing stockouts, waste and lost profit. Marble replaces the stack with one AI system for inventory, ordering, scheduling and finance.
business_model: B2B SaaS, pricing not stated
product_category: AI restaurant back of house operating system
market_need_then: The company says restaurants lose billions a year to stockouts, food waste and lost profit. One founder grew up in a family restaurant business and the company shows an A&W case study, which is a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Marble is a Summer 2026 company with a three person team and no exit. The founders pair restaurant operating experience with applied AI engineering, and the site names several restaurant customers. The main risk is that established restaurant software vendors added AI features in spring 2026, so winning depends on speed and integration depth.

name: Marengo
one_liner: AI-Native Engineering Firm designing Data Centers
long_description:
Marengo is the AI-native engineering firm automating engineering design, starting with data centers. We’ve generated $70K in revenue in our first month, with $4M in contracts to deliver.

Marengo is backed by YC, Exor, Future Planet Capital, undisclosed $2B AUM family office, and other top-tier investors.

Our team includes the former President & CEO of Saipem America ($3B+ P&L), former President of Exyte's Advanced Technology Facilities GBU ($6B+ P&L) and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data center developers and hyperscale operators that need site due diligence, feasibility, concept design and FEED and permitting engineering

business_model: engineering services firm, project fees, with a one site pilot offer
product_category: AI-native engineering design services for data centers

name: Maritime
one_liner: The managed cloud for AI agents.
long_description: Maritime is a fully managed cloud platform for startups selling AI agents. regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Startups that sell AI agents and need to run many of them in isolated persistent environments

name: Marker

name: Markov
tags: Reinforcement Learning; Data Labeling; Data Engineering
one_liner: The data lab for engineering and computer-use AI.
long_description:
Markov is the data lab for engineering and computer-use AI. We capture real work from domain experts and craft high-fidelity datasets and RL environments.

We built the most complex tasks and RL environments sourced through manufacturing experts proficient in AutoCAD, SOLIDWORKS, CATIA, Revit, Siemens NX and more. Our computer-use datasets are action-labelled, narrated and sourced from domain experts in design and enterprise software.

We work with frontier AI labs and we've built over 10,000 CAD environments and collected over 500,000 hours of computer-use data. Our open-source datasets have 800,000+ downloads on Hugging Face.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying training data and RL environments for engineering and computer use agents
problem: Models lack high fidelity examples of expert work in CAD and enterprise software, which are hard to source at scale.
business_model: Data sales to AI labs (datasets and RL environments), with open source datasets for visibility
product_category: Expert workflow data and RL environments for AI
market_need_then: Labs were buying RL environments heavily in 2025 and 2026 and TechCrunch covered Silicon Valley betting on environments to train agents in September 2025.
outcome_analysis: Markov is a Summer 2026 data company selling expert workflow datasets and CAD RL environments to labs. It reports sales of 15,000 hours and large open downloads but no verified funding; the market is crowded with funded vendors, so it is too early to judge an outcome.

name: Martini
tags: Generative AI; Entertainment; Design Tools; Video; Media
one_liner: AI Video Production for Professionals
long_description:
Martini is a collaborative, AI-native platform for professional filmmaking in the era of generative media.
By integrating the best generative models into professional workflows, we enable world-class creatives to harness generative AI as a legitimate medium for film.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Professional filmmakers, studios, agencies and indie creators producing AI-assisted video
problem: Generative video work is scattered across many models and tools with no shared workspace, provenance tracking or cost control, which makes professional collaboration messy.
business_model: SaaS subscription with a free tier, paid plans from $15 per month and extra credits for some generative models; bring-your-own fal API key
product_category: AI-native collaborative video production workspace
competitors_at_founding: Runway; Google Flow; LTX Studio; Higgsfield
market_need_then: Generative video models proliferated through 2025, and professionals wanted a workflow that fits editing tools (XML export), shared review and cost control. Evidence is the product framing on the YC page and the July 2026 No Film School coverage; no sourced spend data.
outcome_analysis: Martini is a Winter 2026 YC company that is still active and very early, so no outcome exists yet. It pairs a cinematographer CEO with a former Supabase growth engineer and sells a collaborative workspace on top of third-party video models. The main risks are model-platform bundling by Runway or Google and thin defensibility, while the distribution through professional film events and a free tier are early positives. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found in an outcome search.

name: Mass Magnetics
tags: Hard Tech; Robotics; Drones; Manufacturing; Defense
one_liner: USA-made magnetics for robotics and defense.
long_description:
Mass Magnetics turns recycled rare-earth scrap into high-performance permanent magnets, made in America. The materials we supply are the backbone of electric motors, sensors, speakers, hard drives, and electronics.
Our process enables DFARS-compliant magnets for defense, aerospace, and industrial manufacturers who demand domestic supply without compromising on quality.
Operations in Greater Boston, MA (Greentown Labs) and Columbus, IN.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Defense, aerospace and industrial manufacturers needing DFARS-compliant domestic permanent magnets
problem: US magnet supply depends on China; domestic, compliant magnets for motors in robotics and defense are scarce.
business_model: Manufacturer selling permanent magnets made from recycled rare-earth scrap
product_category: Recycled rare-earth permanent magnet manufacturing
market_need_then: Heavy policy and defense focus on US rare-earth supply in 2025 and 2026 and a reported recycling rate of about 1 percent of rare earth magnets globally.
