The market tailwind is strong policy attention on domestic rare earth supply, but funded competitors such as Noveon and Cyclic Materials are already ahead on scale.

name: Masterpiece
one_liner: Working capital for data companies training frontier AI
long_description:
We believe AI will be one of humanity’s next great masterpieces. Building it will require financial infrastructure as ambitious as the companies creating it. We're founders backed by Y Combinator building the financial rails underpinning the AI data economy.

Masterpiece provides short term working capital to data vendors that sell training data, evaluation work, and reinforcement learning environments to frontier AI labs.

A major financing gap exists in this market. Data vendors often need to pay contributors and fund operations before a lab has completed QA, accepted the work, and paid the invoice. This creates a 30 to 90 day cash gap between when vendors incur costs and when they receive payment. Legacy invoice lenders have little visibility into how to underwrite these assets.

Masterpiece closes that gap by advancing capital against high quality lab contracts and invoices. Vendors can use the capital to scale delivery, pay contributors, and fund growth, then repay masterpiece when the lab payment arrives.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Data vendors that sell training data, evaluation work and RL environments to frontier AI labs
problem: Data vendors must pay contributors and fund operations 30 to 90 days before a lab finishes QA and pays the invoice, and legacy invoice lenders cannot underwrite these receivables.
business_model: Short-term invoice-backed lending funded by a credit-fund warehouse facility and a stablecoin liquidity pool; revenue from loan yield
product_category: Specialty fintech: receivables financing for the AI data economy
competitors_at_founding: Legacy invoice lenders and factoring firms
market_need_then: AI data vendors such as Mercor, Surge and others grew fast in 2025 and 2026 (a search result cites Mercor at over $2B annualized gross revenue in mid 2026, with conflicting figures), and a 30 to 90 day payment lag creates a working capital gap according to the company.
outcome_analysis: Masterpiece is a Spring 2026 YC fintech that is active and pre-outcome. The YC page claims $65m in signed LOIs, $200k of loans and a $10m warehouse facility, but none of this was confirmed by an outside source. The wedge is real if AI data vendors keep growing, though unit economics, credit losses and the crypto funding leg are untested.

name: Maven
one_liner: Payments for Conversational Agents
long_description: We enable AI chat and voice agents to collect payments through a single API call, handling card processing and PCI compliance across all payment gateways
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Builders and operators of AI voice and chat agents in commerce, restaurants, healthcare, home services, insurance, travel, salons and collections
problem: AI agents cannot safely take card payments mid-conversation without pulling the builder's stack into PCI scope.
business_model: Usage-based payments API (pricing not found)
product_category: Payments infrastructure for conversational agents
competitors_at_founding: Telnyx Voice Payments API; Twilio Agent Assisted Pay
market_need_then: Voice AI agents were being deployed for ordering, scheduling and collections in 2025 and 2026, and payment capture inside the call is a gap needing PCI handling; evidence is competitor products and vendor guides.
outcome_analysis: Maven is a Winter 2026 YC company that is active and pre-outcome. It sells one API call for taking payments inside voice and chat agents. The wedge is real but exposed to Twilio, Telnyx and the voice-agent platforms that it integrates with, and there is no public traction data. Distribution through Vapi and Retell integrations is the early lever.

name: Maywood
one_liner: The first finance-compliant proactive AI that runs 24/7
long_description:
Maywood is the first finance-compliant proactive AI that runs 24/7, working across your network, pipeline, and active processes, running constantly in the background and surfacing things you'd otherwise miss. It tracks relationships and sector context to flag when a target is gearing up for a process (and drafts the outreach in your voice), watches network activity across LinkedIn, news, and conference follow-ups, and surfaces where active processes stand, including what's at risk since you last looked.

It also auto-updates CRMs and trackers and creates meeting briefs that includes relationship history, recent activity, deal context, external research, talking points that can pull from internal and external data sources. Dealmakers interact with it over email, Teams, or the platform itself.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Senior dealmakers (managing directors and partners) at investment banks and other finance firms
problem: Dealmakers miss signals across relationships, news and active processes, and spend junior time on CRM updates, briefs, decks and diligence Q&A.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software for finance firms (pricing not found)
product_category: Proactive AI agent for finance and M&A
founder_names: Drake Goodman; Kent Goodman; Esteban Vizcaino
market_need_then: Banks were adopting AI for analyst work in 2025 and 2026, shown by Rogo's funding and customer list at Rothschild, Jefferies, Lazard and Moelis per search coverage.
outcome_analysis: Maywood is a Winter 2026 YC company with a three-person founding team from Blackstone, BCG, Balyasny and MIT, still active. It launched its Maverick agent and announced data partnerships with S&P Global (July 2026) and PitchBook (September 2026). Strong founder-market fit for finance is offset by heavily funded competitors, so the outcome is open.

name: Melty
one_liner: Mashup any game
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Gamers who want AI-made game mashups and mods, and AI researchers who need programmable games for RL and evals
problem: Combining or modifying games is technically hard for players, and RL researchers lack customizable game environments.
business_model: Free consumer launcher plus B2B tools for RL and evals (Melty Gym, Net, MCP); pricing not found
product_category: Game mashup launcher and programmable game environments
market_need_then: AI mashup clips went viral in 2026 (Decrypt, Minecraft inside Elden Ring demos), and the YC page claims 3.5K mashups played by 170K players.

It gained viral attention with game mashups but drew backlash over terms of service and installer behavior, and it is repositioning toward RL and eval environments. No outcome exists yet; platform and IP risk are the main threats.

name: Memoir
one_liner: AI in your calls
long_description:
Memoir is an AI teammate that joins your video calls, listens like everyone else, and only talks when you talk to it.

A founder is on a sales call. The customer asks what a pilot would look like. Instead of promising to send something over, the founder says, "Memoir, draft this up." A few seconds later there's a page in the chat with the plan they just talked through. Everyone opens it, and they go through it together before anyone hangs up. Afterward, Memoir can help the founder follow up on what they promised, with one click.

Most calls end with a list of things people said they'd do, and it takes days to do them. Agents already do real work in our email, our browsers and our code. They've become extensions of us. But on calls, most of them still just take notes.

We're starting with technical founders on the sales and design calls they run in Google Meet. But we want every call to work like that one. Eventually everyone will bring their own agents to a call, and those agents will work together the way the people do.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Technical founders running sales and design calls on Google Meet; the launch post also pitches an AI CMO for software companies
problem: Calls end with action items that take days to complete, and AI note-takers only record; separately, software teams ship faster than they can market.
business_model: SaaS subscription (pricing not found)
product_category: AI teammate for video calls (pivoted from AI CMO for software companies)
market_need_then: AI agents became common in email, browsers and code in 2025 and 2026 while calls still produced only notes; evidence is the YC launch post, not independent demand data.
outcome_analysis: Memoir is a Spring 2026 YC company with two technical founders who met at IMC Trading, still active and pre-outcome. It has already changed direction at least twice, which signals searching for a wedge. Its calls product competes with Google and note-taker incumbents and is in private testing, so the odds depend on finding a distinct use case.

name: Memory Store

One memory for your team's agents. 

Turn every meeting, Claude session, and Slack chat into context your team and agents share.

It has real agent-infrastructure experience and a clear per-seat price. The category is crowded, with funded rivals and at least one competitor shutting a company-brain product, so defensibility against labs and incumbents is the open question.

name: Mendelia

product_category: AI back office automation for patient access

product_category: AI data analyst for consumer brands

name: Metalcraft

product_category: RL environments and evaluation data for biology

name: Meteoric
one_liner: Drones that clear clouds over solar farms and weaken hurricanes
long_description: Meteoric is building drones that clear clouds over solar farms and ultimately weaken severe storms and hurricanes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Operators of utility-scale solar farms

product_category: Weather modification drones for solar

It has strong press attention but unverified performance claims and heavy technical and FAA regulatory risk, so the outcome cannot yet be judged. No funding beyond YC is public.

name: Micora
one_liner: Micro-grids in a box deploying industrial power autonomously in weeks
long_description: Micora re-designed the process of building solar farms to optimize speed to power generation and portability. The product suite combines a palletized solar block, a containerized energy storage system, and low-cost autonomous robots that deploy a solar farm on-site in days to weeks – and pack it back up when needed.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Industrial sites needing temporary or remote power, such as those otherwise using diesel generators
problem: Getting power to industrial sites quickly is slow; solar farms take long to build and diesel needs fuel deliveries.
business_model: Hardware sales or lease of palletized solar blocks and containerized storage, plus robotic deployment (inferred from product page)
product_category: Portable solar plus storage microgrids and deployment robots
founder_names: Ashten Akemoto; Chris Choo; Frederik (Fredy) Mareels
competitors_at_founding: Terabase Energy; Charge Robotics; LONGi BLOCK

It enters a field where Terabase, Charge Robotics and large manufacturers already ship automated or portable solar, so differentiation on deployment speed and portability will decide whether it raises beyond the YC deal.

name: Milliray
one_liner: Technology to detect and track small drones
long_description:
We make radars that can see small drones.

As drones evolve faster than air defenses, detection has fallen behind. Even $50 drones now present a major threat to airports, critical infrastructure, and front-line defense.

We solve this by building high-frequency radar systems, designed from the ground up to detect even the most challenging low-signature targets. This allows us to identify and track nano drones like no other solution, letting you know what's truly in your airspace.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Airports, critical infrastructure operators, defense forces and venues needing to detect small drones
problem: Cheap small drones are hard for conventional radar to see, leaving airports, infrastructure and front lines exposed.
business_model: Sale of radar sensor hardware and systems to defense and infrastructure buyers
product_category: Millimeter-wave radar for counter-drone detection
founder_names: Matthew Moore; Thomas Doherty; Jordina Frances de Mas
market_need_then: Drone threats to airports and the front line were rising, defense funding for counter-UAS grew, and counter-UAS startups raised over $1.2B between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026 per one tracker.
outcome_analysis: Milliray, formerly DroneTector, is a Winter 2026 company from a St Andrews radar group with academic and defense program support. It is early with no verified round, selling into a hot counter-drone market where radar rivals raised very large rounds, so its outcome depends on field proof and defense procurement.

name: Minicor
one_liner: Scalable windows desktop automations
long_description:
Minicor connects AI startups to legacy desktop apps that have no API. Reliably, quickly and at scale.

Describe a workflow and get an API endpoint. Each call triggers a self-healing desktop automation on a Windows VM. On-prem, cloud, or Citrix. Build through your coding agent via our MCP.

Complete with the observability tools to manage your customer relationship: full video replay of every automation, granular logging, and slack enabled alerts.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: AI startups that sell into industries run on legacy Windows desktop software with no API (healthcare, logistics, finance and similar)
problem: AI products cannot go live because customers' systems of record are desktop apps without APIs, and scripted automations break often.
business_model: Usage-based API and platform for self-healing desktop automations on Windows VMs
product_category: Desktop automation infrastructure for AI companies
market_need_then: AI startups selling to healthcare and logistics need access to desktop systems without APIs; the company reports 2.5M executions run and named customer logos on its site.
outcome_analysis: Minicor raised a $3.8M seed in October 2026, months after its Spring 2026 batch, led by IA Ventures with YC and Paul Graham. Its founders have legacy-integration experience and it shows customer logos and usage, but rivals like Cyberdesk and incumbent RPA vendors make defensibility the key question.

name: Mirabelle
one_liner: Your own chef at home
long_description:
We build the personal robot chef.

Mirabelle cooks fresh meals on demand, so you can eat well every day without spending hours in the kitchen.
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Home consumers who want fresh cooked meals without spending time cooking
problem: People want to eat well daily but cooking takes hours.
business_model: Consumer hardware sale with preorder deposits
product_category: Countertop home cooking robot
market_need_then: Demand shown by Posha's sold-out first batch in 2025 and Mirabelle's own deposit preorders; no Mirabelle sales figures found.
outcome_analysis: Mirabelle is a Winter 2026 consumer hardware startup with preorders and first home tests planned for late 2026. There is no outcome yet; the main risks are hardware execution and an existing funded rival, Posha, while founders have shown consumer growth in a prior app.

name: Mireye
one_liner: Search Engine for the Physical World
long_description:
AI agents are starting to act in the real world, but they can't reliably understand it. 

Every fact about a place has its own silo: land in GIS maps, power in utility portals, people in census tables, policy in county PDFs. All built for humans, none for agents. Underneath, the data is fragmented across thousands of sources, unstructured and complex.

Mireye is building the infrastructure that powers agents to make decisions and act in the real world. One API and MCP to connect agents to the physical world with accurate data enrichment, signals and tools.

Our mission is to index every inch of the earth, and make it as queryable as the web.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need facts about physical locations, such as land and site selection teams
problem: Facts about places are scattered across GIS, utility, census and county sources built for humans, so agents cannot reliably use them.
business_model: Usage-based API and subscription (per parcel and per page pricing, paid plans from $49 a month)
product_category: Geospatial data API and MCP for AI agents
market_need_then: Agents acting in the real world need cited location facts; first customers reportedly used it to source off-market land for data centers, a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Mireye is a Summer 2026 company with a live API, a Launch HN thread and a first-time repeat founder who sold an earlier startup. No funding is public, and parcel data vendors already ship MCP servers, so traction from agent builders will decide the outcome.

name: Mirrors
tags: Developer Tools; SaaS; B2B; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: The guidance system for production AI agents
long_description: Mirrors gives developers the infrastructure to control what production AI agents are told, and when. Today that lives in long prompts and skills the agent may never open, so agents keep breaking rules they've already been given. With Mirrors, a developer writes a rule once and defines where it applies, and Mirrors delivers it at that step of the run and measures whether it helped. It works with any agent framework and any model. As agents take on more of a company's work, what they're told becomes how the company runs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams running production AI agents
problem: Rules for agents live in long prompts and skills the agent may never open, so agents repeat mistakes already corrected.
business_model: Usage-based SaaS with a free tier and Growth plan at $299 a month plus $0.005 per turn
product_category: Runtime guidance infrastructure for AI agents
market_need_then: Teams add instruction after instruction to prompts after each failure; a launch write-up cites a design partner agent with 75 errors on one task despite a prompt rule.
outcome_analysis: Mirrors joined YC in Fall 2026 and has only a launch article and a product site as evidence. It addresses a real pain for agent builders but sits in a crowded guardrail space where rivals have been acquired, so there is no outcome yet.

name: Miso Labs
one_liner: Emotive foundation voice models
long_description: Miso Labs is building the world’s most emotive foundation models for voice. Our goal is to pass the voice Turing test.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies building voice agents and voice products, including enterprises that want on premises models
problem: Text to speech output sounds robotic and flat in conversation. Miso Labs wants voice models with emotion and low latency good enough to pass a voice Turing test.
business_model: Open weight models with a planned paid API and enterprise support and on premises hosting contracts

name: Moonshot
one_liner: agents for the rest of us
long_description:
We want to bring AI agents to a billion people.

To do this, we believe it needs to be 1. proactive and 2. personal. A billion people already carry the right device, but none of them have the right connector.

Moonshot is personal intelligence that lives on your iPhone and listens to you 24/7. It continuously builds up a greater understanding of you through constantly listening and building context. It just pays deep attention, the way a good friend does. Through this, Moonshot monitors your conscious and subconscious life, figuring out what you need before you know, reminding you about open loops, identifying life and emotional trends before you recognize it, and covering a lot more of what we gloss over in daily life.

For fifty years, software has waited to be asked. We think tools are just good enough to flip this, and the next great software will provide value before asking for something first. We're doing it through Moonshot.

Our thesis is simple: you're only living half your life. The half that you actively remember. The other half just evaporates into your subconscious: what you said, felt, promised, and forgot. It's the more interesting half, and until now nothing could catch it, making it not actionable.

Moonshot catches your subconscious half and understands you well enough to take actions on your behalf.

Take life personally.

The iOS app is designed around ambient listening and clear user control. Short microphone chunks are sent securely to Moonshot's private transcription service and deleted when transcription finishes. Text and selected context can be sent through Moonshot's server to a model when the app needs to understand a moment. Nothing leaves without your yes. The privacy policy explains every data path, stored copy, permission, and deletion control in detail.

Moonshot is in early access. Join the waitlist to hear when access opens, read more about the team and product on the About page, or use the Contact page for a direct written response from the Moonshot team.

Let's make it a Moonshot.

tags: Deep Learning; Hard Tech; Remote Work; AI; ML

long_description:
Ndea is building frontier AI systems that blend intuitive pattern recognition and formal reasoning into a unified architecture.

# AI for Scientific Advancement

Unlike all life before us, humanity's ascent is a story of ingenuity, not just biological evolution. Our progress has been driven by the curiosity to acquire knowledge, the ability to pass it on, and an intrinsic drive to innovate. We build technology which gives us leverage beyond our biology.

We stand at the top of a knowledge and technology colossus that we collectively created over the past ten thousand generations. Scientific progress has helped us overcome burdens that long defined human life — famines, plagues, and widespread illiteracy. Science will continue to redefine the boundaries of the human condition.

Today, the acceleration of scientific progress hinges on one factor: AI capable of independent invention and discovery. This capacity is the gateway to advancements beyond our wildest imagination.

# A New Research Lab

We're starting Ndea — an AI research and science lab. The name - like 'idea' with an 'n' - is inspired by the Greek concepts ennoia (intuitive understanding) and dianoia (logical reasoning), capturing our first goal to merge deep learning with program synthesis.

Ndea is entirely focused on developing and operationalizing AGI to realize unprecedented scientific progress in our lifetime for the benefit of all current and future generations.

Building AGI alone is a monumental undertaking, but our mission is even bigger. We're creating a factory for rapid scientific advancement — a factory capable of inventing and commercializing N ideas.

From our vantage point today, we see many 'known' frontiers like self-driving vehicles, drug discovery, sustainable energy, robotics, and space exploration. While AGI will benefit all of these, the most exciting adventure lies in the 'unknown'. AGI promises discoveries and progress we cannot imagine today.

Nori aims to solve the robotics data bottleneck. By deploying affordable robots to customers around the world, we can gather the diverse data required to train the next generation of generalist robotic policies. Every user of Nori makes Nori smarter.

Since launching 6 weeks ago we have already deployed our first robot and have over $440k+ in sales.

We can bring general-purpose robotics to homes and businesses that could never afford it before. There are 132.7 million households and 8.4 million employer business locations in the U.S. At $1,688 per robot, selling just one Nori to 0.5% of them represents a $1.2B market opportunity in the U.S. alone.

name: Nxtcure Labs
one_liner: Engineering the future of Cancer Drug Discovery
long_description:
NxtCure Labs is an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster. We are reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery.

About 2 million Americans are diagnosed with cancer every year. Science has never moved faster, new immunotherapies, targeted drugs and cancer vaccines arrive every year. But roughly 90% of cancer drugs fail in clinical trials, and about 80% of trials run late. The breakthroughs exist. The way we test them is stuck in the last century.

NxtCure is building autonomous clinical trials. Before a single patient enrolls, we run the trial thousands of times on digital twins. Each virtual patient is a system of coupled differential equations that track how a drug moves through plasma, tumor and heart, and how the tumor grows, shrinks or fights back. The parameters are fit to real trial data, so every twin behaves like real biology. Across thousands of simulations we can calculate the odds that a dose will hit its endpoints, and fix the protocol before it costs anyone time, money or hope.

Then 13 AI agents run the trial. Each one owns a stage: drafting the protocol, ranking sites, pre-screening patients, forecasting drug supply, watching for adverse events, predicting dropout, cleaning data and writing the final report. As real data comes in, the twins update and flag problems weeks before a human would see them.

In 2025, the FDA laid out how computer simulation can take its place. Soon a cancer drug will run through thousands of simulated trials before it ever touches a lab, and reach patients years faster. We’re building that future.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: Most cancer drugs fail in trials and many trials run late. The company runs trials with AI agents and uses simulated patient models to test protocols before enrolment.
business_model: Full-service CRO fees per trial, software-enabled
product_category: AI-native contract research organization (oncology)

market_need_then: Sources cite roughly 90% oncology drug trial failure and frequent delays, and an FDA signal on simulation from 2025 per the company description. Capital is flowing into clinical AI per 2026 industry coverage.

SMB Bench is a step toward our longer-term goal of having AI as an independent economic actor.

name: OS3
one_liner: Affordable, intelligent humanoid robots built to deploy at scale
long_description:
OS3 is building the platform that makes intelligent robots accessible to every business.

Today, robotics is constrained by two fundamental bottlenecks: hardware is too expensive to deploy at scale, and robots are difficult to train because high-quality robotics data is scarce and costly to collect. 

We built OS3 to solve both.

Our two-person team designed and a US-made mobile humanoid robot for a fraction of the cost of commercial alternatives. On the intelligence side, instead of relying on expensive robot-generated training data, we trained our own video-action model on 150,000 hours of real-world video spanning more than 2,000 tasks. Every deployed robot feeds new experience into our reinforcement learning pipeline, self improving robot fleet over time.

This creates a robot that can be deployed across industries to automate repetitive, physical work without requiring a new robot or training pipeline for every task. Our robots are already deployed in hotels, with customers now expanding the platform into biotech, hospitals, and data centers, including a wet lab at Stanford.

Our mission is to do for robotics what Apple did for personal computing: take technology that was once expensive, specialized, and inaccessible and make it powerful and usable at massive scale. We’re building toward a world with billions of intelligent robots, and OS3 is the platform that makes that possible.

name: OctaPulse
one_liner: OctaPulse builds computer vision and robotics for fish farms and…
long_description:
OctaPulse is building the robotics layer for seafood production. Aquaculture is the fastest-growing food sector and already produces more seafood than commercial fishing, yet the people who breed and process fish still make thousands of decisions a day with almost no data about the fish in front of them, and much of the most important work is still done by hand, one fish at a time.

We put cameras where fish are already handled, turn every image into measurements, and give farms and plants the tools to act on them. Today that is two products: Phenotyping, which measures every fish for shape, size and condition and links it to its family for breeding decisions, and Digital Twin, which places cameras on processing lines and farm sites onto the floor plan with live views, automatic counts and a built-in AI assistant.

The same per-fish measurements are the foundation for Plant Robotics: robot cells that handle whole fish on the processing line, working alongside the people there. Fish are wet, slippery, soft and never the same twice, which is exactly why this work is still manual and why it needs measurement-driven robots built for food plants rather than rigid grippers and tabletop demos. We are now selecting processing plants for the first pilots on real lines.

We signed a 6-figure paid pilot with the largest trout producer in the United States, and every deployment adds labeled images to a proprietary multi-species dataset that improves our models across species and becomes the brain for autonomous seafood production.

name: One Robot
one_liner: World models for robot evals and training.
long_description:
One Robot builds simulation environments that are realistic to see and realistic to interact with, so robotics teams can train and evaluate robot policies without being bottlenecked by robot time.

Today, improving a VLA often means more real-world hours: setting up the scene, running trials, resetting, and repeating. This loop is slow, expensive, and hard to scale. For example, material handling and manufacturing assembly tasks, models need far more training and evaluation data than teams can collect in the real world.

We use task-specific data to build world model-based simulation environments for hard manipulation tasks (for example, textiles and box folding). These environments help teams run more training and evals, find failure modes faster, and accelerate iteration on action policies with less dependence on real-world data collection and robot availability.

name: Ontora
one_liner: AI agents that interviews every employee to hand context to AI tools.
long_description: Ontora is an AI Agent that interviews every employee to map how work actually gets done and identify bottlenecks. Consultants spend months doing this manually; Ontora does it in hours.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Enterprise leaders planning AI transformation
problem: Mapping how work really gets done takes consultants months; Ontora agents interview employees to discover processes and prioritize AI opportunities.
business_model: AI transformation service and platform sold to enterprises
product_category: AI process discovery
founder_names: Leon Iwanowitsch; Maximilian Arnold; David Korn
market_need_then: Founders say company knowledge is mostly unwritten; one customer example, Pilot Group, scoped six AI initiatives from over 200 employee conversations in two weeks (company site).
outcome_analysis: Ontora is a Spring 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. The founders bring consulting, Porsche and prior exit experience, which fits an enterprise sales motion, while process mining incumbents and consultancies are strong alternatives.

name: Ooak Data
one_liner: We turn company data into training data
long_description: Ooak Data turns internal company data into a training ground where AI agents can be tested on real work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying agent training data, and companies licensing their internal work history
problem: Agents trained on simulated tasks lack real work; Ooak turns licensed anonymized company workflows into digital twin environments for training.
business_model: Data licensing to labs with revenue share style purchases from companies
product_category: RL environments from enterprise data
market_need_then: Analysts in 2026 describe heavy frontier lab demand for RL environments; one lab leader publicly doubted the startup category.
outcome_analysis: Ooak Data is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. Its differentiator is licensed real company workflow data, which is hard to collect, but it competes with funded environment startups and with data vendors in a crowded 2026 market.

name: OpEra
tags: Logistics; Manufacturing; Supply Chain; Operations; AI
one_liner: The AI decision engine for factories, warehouses and fleets
long_description: OpEra Technologies is the AI decision engine for factories, warehouses and fleets. Companies with physical operations make thousands of decisions every day, and we help their teams make the best one at every step from production to delivery: (1) Planning: how much to make, buy and stock. (2) Scheduling: what runs when, and who works on what. (3) Allocation: which warehouse or store gets each order. (4) Routing: boat, plane or truck, and which route each one takes. Founded out of MIT's Operations Research Center.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Operations teams at companies with factories, warehouses and fleets
problem: Physical operations make thousands of planning, scheduling, allocation and routing decisions; OpEra builds custom optimization engines that re-plan when conditions change.
business_model: B2B software, custom optimization engines via pilots (pricing not stated)
product_category: AI decision engine / operations research for supply chain
market_need_then: Self-reported results from pilots (38% lower delivery cost for a retailer, 54% fewer unfulfilled orders for a marketplace), unverified; founders say they met on a delivery routing project for a major retailer.
outcome_analysis: OpEra is a Fall 2026 YC company founded by two MIT Operations Research Center graduates, still in pilots, so no outcome exists yet. The only sources are the YC page and launch post plus a Dealroom profile. The main risk visible is that established optimization vendors exist; no dated evidence about them was gathered.

name: Opalite Health
one_liner: Helping Healthcare Providers Speak Any Language
long_description:
Opalite makes it easy for healthcare providers to communicate with non-English speaking patients. We’re built to work inside existing clinical workflows, so providers can communicate in real time without waiting for an interpreter or delaying care. 

Opalite is available instantly, 24/7, and replaces traditional interpretation services with software that’s more reliable and saves millions of dollars per year.

We've built a voice AI system that is the safest, most compliant, and most accurate medical interpreter in the world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Hospitals, health centers, home health organizations, telehealth programs and clinics that pay for interpretation services for non-English speaking patients
problem: Providers wait for human interpreters or use slow phone and video services when treating patients who do not speak English, which delays care and costs hospitals large sums each year.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage-based AI interpretation sold to provider organizations as a replacement for per-minute human interpretation services
product_category: Healthcare voice AI, real-time speech-to-speech medical interpretation
competitors_at_founding: GLOBO Language Solutions (GLOBO KAI); Artisight; Vocality Health; No Barrier
market_need_then: Hospitals pay per minute for human phone and video interpreters, with long waits at the point of care. The company's own site cites one customer that halved interpretation costs. Demand from the AI interpreter wave of 2025 is visible in multiple launches.
outcome_analysis: Opalite is an active Winter 2026 company with no exit and no confirmed funding round. Its path depends on whether hospital buyers trust AI interpretation more than human services, on accuracy tooling, and on competition from several startups and incumbents that launched AI interpreters in 2025. Too early for a verdict.

name: Open Actuation
tags: Hard Tech; Robotics; Drones; Manufacturing; Electronics
one_liner: Quick-turn, purpose-built motors & actuators for all
long_description:
We design and manufacture high-mix drone motors and robotic actuators in LA.

DJI, Apple, and Ford don't settle for OTS components. Likewise, the teams that win the Western robotics market will build seamless machines from tightly integrated software and hardware. 

Open Actuation designs motors and actuators around your robot's unique form factor and mission - then we rapidly bring them to life with proprietary software and tooling geared for high-mix machining and assembly. We've designed and built motors for top drone OEMs and can assemble thousands of motors per month at our first factory in LA.

We're doing for motion components what 3D printing has done for structural components. This enables hardware teams to build and iterate at the speed of software so they can create elegant, reliable, ROI-positive robots and win massive markets.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Drone OEMs and robotics hardware teams that need custom motors and actuators in small to mid volumes
problem: Off-the-shelf motors and actuators do not fit custom robot form factors, and imported components face supply and FCC restrictions, so US hardware teams wait long for custom parts.
business_model: Build-to-order manufacturing of motors and actuators with an online actuator configurator, plus drone motor product lines
product_category: Hard tech, electric motors and robotic actuators manufacturing
market_need_then: The FCC's December 2025 action on foreign-made drone components, including motors, created demand for domestic motors, as covered in trade press in 2026.
outcome_analysis: Open Actuation is an active Fall 2026 company with no exit, no verified funding and almost no press. Its tailwind is domestic drone motor demand after the December 2025 FCC action, while funded rivals such as Westmag and Atlas Motion entered the same gap in 2026. Too early for a verdict.

name: OpenCrawl
one_liner: Multiplayer for your coding agents.
long_description: OpenCrawl lets your coding agents search each other’s histories and talk to each other, across laptops and cloud coding environments. It’s open source and self-hostable. YC companies get 200M tokens of session data ingested free per month, no credit card required.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams that use several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) across laptops and cloud sandboxes
problem: Coding agents do not share what they learned, so teammates' agents repeat investigations and lose context across machines.
business_model: Open source core with a usage-based cloud, priced per million ingested agent-session tokens after a free monthly allowance
product_category: Developer tools, shared memory and messaging for coding agents
competitors_at_founding: Stash (Fergana Labs); Augment Code Cosmos; MemNexus
market_need_then: Teams running multiple coding agents in 2026 need shared context; many launches of team memory tools in 2026 show demand.
outcome_analysis: OpenCrawl is an active Fall 2026 company with no exit or reported funding. Founders have data infrastructure and GTM agent backgrounds from Pocus and Sigma, but the shared-memory-for-coding-agents space was crowded by mid 2026. Too early for a verdict.

name: OpenHack
one_liner: Always-on AI security engineer
long_description: OpenHack is an always on AI Security Engineer. OpenHack understands your business, system design and developer intent like a real security engineer. It ingests all this context to find the hardest vulnerabilities through AI codebase scanning, AI pentesting and Supply Chain Security. It verifies and prioritizes vulnerabilities automatically, and filters out false positives like a real security engineer drastically reducing overhead.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Startups and enterprises, including healthcare and finance, that want automated security review of code and live apps
problem: Security teams are short-staffed and drowned in false positives from scanners; OpenHack aims to find and verify real vulnerabilities like a human security engineer.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI codebase scanning, AI pentesting and supply chain security
product_category: DevSecOps, AI pentesting and vulnerability management
market_need_then: AI-generated code and AI-assisted attackers raised demand for automated pentesting in 2026, shown by large rounds for rivals.
outcome_analysis: OpenHack is an active solo-founder Fall 2026 company with no reported funding or exit. It sells into a crowded, well funded AI pentesting market and shares its name with a May 2026 open source tool from Hadrian, which may hurt search visibility. Too early for a verdict.

name: OpenLake Technologies
tags: Generative AI; SaaS; Big Data; Infrastructure
one_liner: OpenLake lets companies deploy models that improve in real time
long_description:
OpenLake is an applied AI research lab serving over 100 billion tokens a day. We train models on your company’s datasets and live user conversations, turning your domain expertise into a competitive advantage for your products. 

Our latest model, Ultra R1, is available on the OpenLake platform. Get started today.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies that want models trained on their own data and live user conversations, served by an inference platform
problem: Deployed models stop improving after launch; OpenLake trains models on company datasets and live conversations so they improve in real time.
business_model: Usage-based inference platform and applied research services
product_category: Generative AI infrastructure, inference and continual learning
market_need_then: Industry essays in 2026 argue deployed models stop learning, and investors funded several continual learning startups.
outcome_analysis: OpenLake is an active Fall 2026 company with no funding or exit found. It claims heavy usage with a two-person team, which could not be verified, and competes with funded continual learning startups. Too early for a verdict.

name: OpenRelay
one_liner: Distributed, hardware-agnostic AI inference
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: AI application builders, robotics, voice assistant and batch inference users who need cheap, low-latency inference across GPUs and other accelerators
problem: Inference is expensive and tied to specific hardware and clouds; OpenRelay routes requests across a distributed network by cost, latency and availability.
business_model: Usage-based inference API on a distributed network of compute sites
product_category: AI infrastructure, distributed hardware-agnostic inference
market_need_then: Demand for cheaper inference was strong in 2026; the company reports over 5 trillion tokens a month and over 10M USD annualized revenue (company claims) within five months.
outcome_analysis: OpenRelay raised a 10M USD seed announced November 12 2026, shortly after Summer 2026, and claims over 10M USD annualized revenue within five months (company claims). Experienced infrastructure founders and strong demand for cheaper inference support this, while funded inference clouds make the position contestable. Too early for an exit verdict.

name: OpenScaffold
one_liner: Superagent for Deployment Teams
long_description:
OpenScaffold is building AGI for every deployment team.

The result is a custom scaffold that is autonomously harnessed for each deployment, drawn from customer discovery, business objectives, past deployments, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Forward deployed, solutions and implementation engineers and deployment leads who take customers live with software
problem: Deployment teams do customer discovery, scoping and build work by hand; OpenScaffold agents read customer calls, emails and tickets and brief coding agents.
business_model: B2B SaaS with free signup; pricing not stated
product_category: AI agents for software deployment and implementation teams
market_need_then: Forward deployed engineering was described as the fastest-growing role at AI startups in 2026, with many open roles at companies like Sierra, which signals deployment labor demand.
outcome_analysis: OpenScaffold is an active Fall 2026 company with no funding or exit found. It targets deployment teams, a role in rapid growth, but it has no named customers and faces crowded agent tooling. Too early for a verdict.

name: OpenSpec
one_liner: Plan mode for complex features
long_description:
OpenSpec is an open-source, spec-driven framework. We help developers plan complex features by creating lightweight spec documents that serve as durable context for their coding agents.

With 20k+ GitHub stars, we’re one of the leading spec-driven frameworks, used by thousands of developers and teams to plan and ship with the coding agent of their choice.

Our philosophy is simple: keep planning lightweight and iterative, and match how software actually gets built, messy, evolving, and real, without dragging teams into rigid, bureaucratic workflows.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and teams using coding agents who want lightweight specs as durable context
problem: Coding agents lose context on complex features; OpenSpec provides spec documents that keep humans and agents aligned.
business_model: Open source MIT framework from Fission AI; monetization not stated
product_category: Developer tools, spec-driven development framework for coding agents
market_need_then: Coding agent adoption in 2025 created a context problem; several spec tools launched at once, which indicates demand.
outcome_analysis: OpenSpec grew rapidly as an open source project, reporting over 265,000 monthly developers and 66.2k stars (company claims), and Thoughtworks placed it in Trial in November 2026. Its risk is monetization and large vendors with competing spec tools. No exit; no verified funding.

name: OpenTag
tags: AIOps; B2B; Workflow Automation; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Model Agnostic AI coworker in Slack
long_description: OpenTag is an AI coworker in your Slack with full context on your company. It answers questions and takes real work off your plate. It also keeps your wiki up to date automatically, so knowledge never goes stale.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams that work in Slack (and later Microsoft Teams) and want an AI agent with company context to answer questions and do tasks
problem: Company knowledge is scattered and wikis go stale, and employees spend time on repetitive requests that an agent with full context could handle inside the chat tool they already use.
business_model: SaaS subscription for a model-agnostic Slack agent with integrations; pricing details not confirmed
product_category: AI coworker agent in Slack, enterprise knowledge and workflow automation
founder_names: Tony Kam; Shelden Shi; Wilson Nguyen
market_need_then: Companies were adopting AI agents in chat tools in 2026, and the launch of Claude Tag and roundups of alternatives show active demand for Slack-native agents.
outcome_analysis: OpenTag is an Active company from the Summer 2026 batch, too early for an outcome. It enters a crowded space weeks after Anthropic launched Claude Tag, so its edge rests on being model agnostic and on team execution, and the founders have shipped a prior YC company together. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found.

name: OpenVector
one_liner: AI that turns any camera to an autonomous worker with real-time vision
long_description: OpenVector transforms any existing camera into an automated 24/7 workforce without requiring new hardware. We've built the world's fastest vision-language model inference engine that allows users to simply describe a task in plain English and automatically build a custom AI vision model to monitor their feed. When it detects an important physical event—like a stalled production cycle, a safety violation, or a waiting customer—it operates a computer just like a human to take immediate action. It integrates with legacy systems, makes calls, sends emails, updates a POS/CRM, or triggers webhooks in real time. OpenVector enables any camera to do real work.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Businesses with existing camera systems (industrial, retail, safety) that want to turn video feeds into automated actions
problem: Existing cameras only record, so people must watch feeds or write custom vision models to detect events such as stalled production, safety violations or waiting customers.
business_model: Hosted video language model API plus a hardware station; the pre-order station was listed at 449 USD per month or 6,499 USD up front
product_category: Computer vision, vision language model inference and video agents
market_need_then: Large installed base of passive cameras and fast progress in vision language models in 2026 created demand for natural language camera monitoring.
outcome_analysis: OpenVector is an Active Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its bet is a technically deep, fast video language model engine from a founder with published vision research, aimed at a large installed base of cameras. Main risks are incumbents in video analytics and open source models narrowing its speed lead. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.

name: OpenWork
one_liner: The open source alternative to Claude Cowork
long_description: OpenWork is a desktop app that lets people connect to their existing skills, MCPs, and agents. Users can download the app for free, try it with over 50+ model providers, and easily share their setup with their team.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Knowledge workers and teams who want an AI desktop agent that works on local files with their choice of model provider
problem: Closed agent apps such as Claude Cowork lock users to one model vendor and keep files and setups in the vendor's cloud; teams want an open, shareable setup of skills, MCPs and agents.
business_model: Free open source desktop app with paid add-ons (MCP Gateway, AI Gateway, Cloud App) and a Team plan listed at 10 USD per user per month
product_category: Open source AI agent desktop app, developer and enterprise tooling
market_need_then: Interest in Claude Cowork and complaints about vendor lock-in drove demand for open, model agnostic alternatives; the Show HN post and fast GitHub growth in 2026 show developer pull.
outcome_analysis: OpenWork is an Active Spring 2026 company with strong early open source traction, reported by its YC launch post as 14k GitHub stars and over 150k downloads within three months. It rides the shift to agent desktop apps, but faces vendor-built rivals and a licensing trust question. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.

name: Operon
one_liner: Agentic data layer for manufacturing & process industries.
long_description:
Operon is the data intelligence layer for heavy industry. We ingest the messy documents a plant runs on (P&IDs, schematics, datasheets, scans) and turn them into one structured, queryable model of the facility.

On top of it, engineers query their plant in natural language and build agentic workflows for safety, compliance, and design.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Owner operators, EPC firms and mechanical contractors in energy, chemicals and process industries, and private equity portfolio companies
problem: Plant knowledge is trapped in P&IDs, schematics, datasheets and scans, making safety, compliance and design work slow.
business_model: Enterprise deployments with a down payment covering the full cycle and engineers on site for the first month
product_category: Industrial data layer and AI agents for plant documents
competitors_at_founding: SymphonyAI IRIS Foundry; Acuvate DiagramIQ; AVEVA P&ID and Hexagon SmartPlant P&ID
market_need_then: Heavy industry runs on legacy drawings; the company claims 2.8M average annual savings, unverified, and says about 20 clients, some proofs of concept, per a secondary report.
outcome_analysis: Operon is a Summer 2026 company led by a young solo founder selling a plant data layer to process industries. It reports around 20 clients and a quick pre seed per secondary press, but no verified funding; incumbents and data vendors make it too early to assign an outcome.

name: Orca Aerospace
one_liner: AI spacecraft operators that live onboard the vehicle
long_description: At Orca, we are focused on creating the future of spacecraft operations by moving control onto the vehicle. By allowing AI models to control the satellite using deterministic tooling, we are able to achieve the same holistic, high-quality decisions on "what" to do to carry out a mission while maintaining the safety of systems that decide "how" to execute it.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Satellite and spacecraft operators, including government and defense customers and orbital compute operators
problem: Spacecraft are operated from the ground with limited contact windows, so missions stall between passes and during communication gaps; onboard AI could keep them moving if it can be kept safe.
business_model: Software licensing and contracts for onboard autonomy software; a contract with a planned orbital data center operator is reported but its value is an upper bound
product_category: Onboard spacecraft autonomy software, AI operators with deterministic planners and guardrails
competitors_at_founding: Shield AI with Sedaro; AstroForge; Boeing onboard AI prototype; EraDrive
market_need_then: Growing satellite counts, communication gaps and demand for autonomy, plus orbital compute plans, created interest in onboard operators; a reported deal with an orbital data center company shows early demand.
outcome_analysis: Orca Aerospace is an Active Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. Founders with deep guidance and control experience are building onboard AI operators with safety guardrails, and a reported deal to fly on a planned orbital data center fleet suggests early pull. The risks are long space timelines, safety assurance and primes working the same idea. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.

name: Orchestra
one_liner: Self-optimizing neocloud that cuts LLM costs by 100x
long_description:
Orchestra is an inference cloud. We capture your AI work traces, train smaller models, and automatically deploy them (only when they outperform the expensive model you are currently paying for).

Instead of renting the same frontier model forever, your AI infrastructure gets faster, smarter, and cheaper every time it runs.

Suppose your product uses Claude for a repetitive legal workflow.

Orchestra observes successful production runs, learns the specific tools and judgment required for that workflow, and trains a specialized open-weight model.

Once that model matches or beats Claude on a held-out evaluation, Orchestra starts routing production traffic to it.

As more work is completed, the model keeps improving.

We started Orchestra because we believe every company using AI should be accumulating intelligence, not accumulating API bills.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies with high volume, repetitive LLM workloads who pay frontier model API bills and want cheaper specialized models
problem: Teams keep paying frontier model prices for repetitive tasks; training and safely deploying smaller models from their own traces is hard to do and verify.
business_model: Usage-based inference cloud and routing platform that captures traces, trains open-weight models and serves them
product_category: AI inference cloud, model routing, evaluation and distillation
market_need_then: Rising LLM API bills in 2026 and published cost reductions from distillation created demand; one independent review noted the 100x claim was unproven while a route ran about 5x faster than a frontier model.
outcome_analysis: Orchestra is an Active Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. A two person team with deep ads and ML infrastructure experience is selling cost savings on LLM bills, with a site claiming 97.8 percent cost reduction on one example. Direct rivals already distill from traces, and an independent review called the 100x claim unproven, so execution speed and customer proof will decide. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.

name: Ordo Labs
one_liner: Regulated lab software, rebuilt around AI agents
long_description:
Ordo is rebuilding lab software for the AI era.

The next generation of lab software will be a workforce scientists direct. We’re building it for regulated labs.

Our agents analyze instrument data, apply each lab’s quality rules and draft source-linked reports. We have paid pilots and have cut a 40-hour post-analysis workflow to four hours, including scientist review.

Our ambition is for labs to grow their capacity by deploying agents, without multiplying manual work.

Agents do the work, scientists sign.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Regulated labs such as bioanalytical, GMP pharma and biologics, preclinical safety and ISO/IEC 17025 testing labs
problem: Scientists in regulated labs spend a large share of project time on manual data checks and report drafting; the company cites manual data work as 40 percent of project time.
business_model: B2B software subscription for lab teams, with paid pilots reported; pricing not found
product_category: AI agent software for regulated laboratory data analysis, quality checks and reporting
founder_names: Sebastian Apelgren; Kristina Hoang; Adam Tovatt
competitors_at_founding: Expert Intelligence; Scispot; Benchling and Sapio Sciences
market_need_then: Labs face heavy manual QC and reporting work; the company cites paid pilots in the US and Europe and a 40 hour workflow cut to four hours, while funding of several competitors in 2026 shows investor demand.
outcome_analysis: Ordo Labs is an Active Fall 2026 company with paid pilots and no outcome yet. The team pairs pharma software and engineering backgrounds and targets a regulated niche where trust, validation and audit trails matter. Funded competitors and incumbents are adding agents, so deep lab workflow fit is the edge to watch. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.

name: Organizely
tags: Logistics; Manufacturing; E-commerce; Supply Chain; AI
one_liner: A New AI-Native ERP for American Manufacturers 🇺🇸
long_description:
Organizely helps American manufacturers use AI to lower production costs. 

Factories depend on three resources: materials, equipment, and labor. Costs rise unexpectedly when components are missing, machines go down, or staffing doesn’t match demand. We experienced this firsthand while owning and operating a factory in the U.S. for six years. As we scaled, it was expensive to resolve factory-wide bottlenecks quickly and it became harder to stay competitive on price. 

Other companies are trying to layer AI agents on top of legacy ERPs to do logistics work, but the underlying data architectures limit how much those agents can understand and do. So we’re building a new ERP from the ground up for the era of AI. 

Organizely is an AI-native ERP with AI reasoning and machine learning algorithms embedded throughout for a single intelligent platform that can model, predict, and act. We natively automate all core manufacturing workflows including demand planning, raw material tracking, machine maintenance, and production scheduling. 

Organizely continuously improves over time, suggesting new ways for manufacturers to reduce costs and produce more with their existing facilities and teams. It's the whole factory solved. 

We’ve deployed to factories across six U.S. states and now we’re bringing AI to all factories across America. 🇺🇸
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: American small and mid-size manufacturers
problem: Factories lose money when materials are missing, machines go down or staffing mismatches demand, and legacy ERPs with AI agents bolted on cannot reason over the underlying data.
business_model: B2B SaaS ERP (pricing not found)
product_category: AI-native ERP for manufacturing
founder_names: Christian Santos; Matthew Weiss; Lisa Mengotto
market_need_then: Founders cite their own six years running a US factory; the company reports one named customer (Kinetic Labs) with a self-reported 22% higher operating margin.
outcome_analysis: Organizely is a Fall 2026 YC company with no history to judge yet. Its edge is founders who ran a factory themselves and a claim of deployments in six states, but the only named customer is the founders' own prior company, and the AI-ERP field already has several funded rivals, so early traction needs independent customers.

name: Orgo
one_liner: Computers for Agents
long_description: Orgo is the simplest way to give your AI employees their own secure, persistent cloud computers. Over 1000 teams use Orgo to run AI workers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and teams building and running AI agents or AI workers that need persistent cloud desktops
problem: Agents that use computers need secure, persistent desktops they can see and control that keep running after logout; building and managing those environments is a burden for teams.
business_model: Usage and subscription plans for cloud desktops; the changelog lists paid plans at 29, 99 and 399 USD per month
product_category: Cloud computers and sandboxes for AI agents, developer infrastructure
founder_names: Spencer Kinney; Nick Vasilescu; Tiger Wang
market_need_then: Growth of computer-use agents created demand for persistent desktops; the company reports over 1000 teams using it by the Fall 2026 batch (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Orgo is an Active Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. It claims over 1000 teams using its cloud desktops and has paid plans, which suggests early product pull. The category is crowded with funded sandbox vendors and cloud platforms, so differentiation on persistence and ease of use will matter. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.

name: Origami Robotics
one_liner: Manipulate Anything Robot
long_description: We are building a "manipulate anything" model with the robot hardware that embodies it. We designed a hand-based data-collection device and a high DOF, direct drive robotic hand that match each other exactly, enabling us to eliminate embodiment gap and collect real-world data and deploy it directly. We want to scale real world manipulation data by deploying our devices "in the wild" like manufacturing factories, logistic centers to collect Tesla like data, use these data to train our model and then provide automation solutions to these industries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robotics and physical-AI labs buying dexterous hands and data-collection gloves; later factories and logistics operators
problem: Robot manipulation lacks data and hardware that match human hand dexterity (embodiment gap).
business_model: Hardware sales (robot hand, gloves) to fund data collection and a manipulation model; later automation sales
product_category: Dexterous robot hands and robot-learning data gloves
market_need_then: Physical-AI labs need dexterous hardware and demonstration data; the company claims early hand sales including Amazon (launch post, unverified).
outcome_analysis: Origami Robotics is a W26 company with a five-person team selling a dexterous robot hand and data-collection glove, with a plan to move from hardware sales to data collection and a general manipulation model. Funding is unverified, with conflicting reports of $500K and $12.5M, and no outcome exists yet, so the record is a snapshot of a very early company.

name: Origin
one_liner: AI and Data for Cancer Therapeutics
long_description:
We produce patient-derived cancer datasets for licensing to pharmaceutical and AI companies. Our data comprises matched spatial transcriptomics, H&E and clinical labels. We operate our own laboratory, where samples are processed. Samples are sourced from leading biobank / hospital networks.

As R&D workflows increasingly rely on frontier AI systems, we believe there is critical need for real world datapoints so that findings translate in the clinic.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pharmaceutical and AI drug discovery companies that license patient-derived oncology datasets
problem: Cancer drug and AI models lack matched real patient tumor data (spatial transcriptomics, H&E images and clinical outcomes), so trial response is hard to predict.
business_model: Data licensing to pharma and AI companies, with models built on proprietary data
product_category: AI and patient-derived cancer data for therapeutics
market_need_then: AI drug discovery firms increasingly cite a shortage of real patient data; Noetik's GSK deal and Tempus's licensable data library show pharma spending on spatial oncology data.
outcome_analysis: Origin is a Winter 2026 company still at an early stage, building a patient-derived oncology data engine to license to pharma and AI firms. No outcome, funding round or partnership is publicly verified yet, so there is no success or failure story to attribute. The key open questions are whether it can secure biobank access and customers before better funded players such as Tempus and Noetik close the data gap.

name: Orikata Bio PBC
tags: Machine Learning; SaaS; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: A multiplayer discovery workspace for human and agentic scientists
long_description:
A new agent, tool, or generative model alone doesn’t solve the whole problem for most research questions. Someone still has to assemble the data, work out which methods to use and get the tools and datasets working together. We’re building Noto, a multiplayer discovery workbench for human and agentic scientists, to bring everyone's favorite frontier models, agents, tools, and scientific models into one shared workspace, so that you can focus on making your next discovery, rather than wrestling with your Python environment or finding GPUs.

Plan an experiment, work with its generated data, run an analysis or model, maybe even train a new model, and keep the results in the notebook. We designed Noto so that the inputs, code, methods and results stay connected across local and hosted compute. Both people and agents need to see how a result was produced and build on it. Biology is where we’re starting, with the workbench being built for more general research across many scientific disciplines.

Available now: our first biological analysis tools, hosted model inference, and an initial agent interface. Free usage is available within limits, alongside paid model runs and individual and team plans. Researchers can run sequence and structure analyses and hosted scientific models without provisioning GPUs or maintaining each model’s dependencies.

In development: the full multiplayer notebook and wider agent workflows and integrations.

Orikata Bio Public Benefit Corporation, or Orikata Bio PBC, is the company. We work under two brands: Orikata Bio for biological discovery and Megure Labs for scientific software.

Biological discovery with Orikata Bio

We’re developing Ibuki, a world-model family for biology, to learn how evolution, sequence, structure and function relate and use those relationships to understand and engineer living systems. We’re pretraining our own protein language models, and developing coordinate and multimodal models for prediction, inverse folding, alignment and generative design. Proteins are our starting point; DNA, RNA, small molecules, and other biological modalities are part of the longer-term direction.

Along the way, we assembled Umi, with over 100 billion unique protein sequences, and Sora, with nearly two billion protein structure records. Having that much data only helps if we can organize it, compare it and find the biology relevant to a particular question. We’re building the full-corpus embedding, indexing and customer access that will bring more of those collections into research workflows.

Our key insight was that the fixed substitution tables used to compare biological sequences are the simplest example of a neural network. Replacing them with contextual substitution operators lets us learn how positions correspond, from reference alignments and directly from molecular geometry. Hikoboshi (open source) turns those learned relationships into tools for sequence and structure alignment, search, clustering and many other evolutionary analysis pipelines.
GitHub: https://github.com/orikata-bio/hikoboshi

Scientific software with Megure Labs

Learning those relationships meant making the alignment calculation itself trainable. Orihime (open source), our differentiable-alignment and structured-attention library, lets neural networks learn through scientific algorithms on CPUs and GPUs. It supplies the training machinery behind our learned alignment methods.
GitHub: https://github.com/megure-labs/orihime

Running the models efficiently is its own problem. Hataya (private evaluation), our inference engine and compiler for scientific models, turns trained models and their dependencies into standalone CPU and GPU programs, carrying the exact weights, identity and verification evidence with them. We’re building it to make both our models and public scientific models cheaper to run, including through Noto’s hosted service.

Kaname coordinates long-running agent work across every model provider: tasks, compute, permissions, retries and the record of what happened. We’re bringing that coordination and provenance into Noto’s research workflows so work can continue across people, agents and machines.

Researchers can start with a single analysis or hosted model run today. Noto is where we’re bringing them together so an analysis or model run can become part of a continuing research project, with the data, methods and results kept alongside it.

name: Papaya
tags: AIOps; Developer Tools; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Continuously improve the quality of your AI agents.
long_description:
Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Engineers don't have time to continually improve the agents they've shipped — the context bloat, overly chatty subagents, and broken tool calls sit in production traces nobody reads, quietly hurting agent efficiency. With Papaya they connect their agent directly via SDK, get actionable recommendations on how to improve quality, latency, and cost, and the ones they approve are pushed to production as pull requests.

Papaya runs 200+ research-backed analyses across context, prompts, prompt caching, subagents, and tool calls. Every recommendation is ranked by impact and comes with the production runs that produced it — typically a 20%+ quality improvement on the first workflow analysis.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: Agent teams lack time to review production traces for context bloat, chatty subagents and broken tool calls that hurt quality, latency and cost.
business_model: B2B SaaS with SDK integration (pricing not found; first analysis free)
product_category: AI agent optimization / agent observability
founder_names: Macy Mody; Niyaz Puzhikkunnath; Faiz Vadakkumpadath
market_need_then: Production agents are widespread in 2026 and observability platforms cover tracing, but comparisons say few tools turn traces into code-level fixes.
outcome_analysis: Papaya joined YC in Fall 2026, so no outcome exists yet. The site claims two named customers and 1.1M conversations analyzed, all self-reported. The team is experienced but faces well-known observability vendors that may add the same recommendation loop. No outcome factors are assigned until later events.

Pavoot replaces this fragmented workflow with a single AI system that keeps every attendee, interaction, conversation, and follow-up connected in one place, making relationship-driven growth scalable.

name: Perit.AI
one_liner: Expert-collected voice, egocentric and RL training data for frontier…
long_description:
Perit is a training-data company for frontier AI labs. Everything we deliver is recorded, transcribed, labelled and graded by people who actually do the job: ex-contact-centre QA leads, claims handlers, ward clerks and shopkeepers, recruited for the sector and locale each program needs.

What we deliver:

- Voice and speech data: 4,000+ hours of audio delivered across 9 locales, transcribed verbatim and word-aligned, with 95%+ QA-sample accuracy.
- RL environments and benchmarks: speech-to-speech RL environments plus coding and RL task sets, currently 100 RL tasks per week and scalable to 2,000.
- Embodied data for robotics: egocentric video, depth, teleoperation and handheld-gripper demonstrations recorded in real homes, shops and workplaces.
- Data collection and annotation: video, image and text collected to spec, and annotation of any data type on our own Foundry workspace.

Every batch ships with a quality report, consent references and a reviewer chain. We work with almost all frontier labs and have quickly gotten past $9M in revenue.

Founded by 2x YC founders Kshitij Dixit (Zeo, YC W20) and Poorva Dixit (ex-Google Cloud AI, Uber, Atlassian), with a deep IIT network of researchers at top labs.

name: Piris Labs

long_description: Up to 80% of the most advance AI compute chips sits idle because of slow networking. Piris Labs builds photonic based networking solutions to enable fast, scalable, and low cost AI workload execution infrastructure.
