name: Plek AI
one_liner: The AI company brain for PE value creation
long_description:
Plek is the AI company brain for private equity value creation. Upload an employee census, and Plek maps every person to a taxonomy of 50,000 jobs and 250,000 tasks, down to the time each task takes. It then analyzes spans and layers, org structure, footprint, compensation, functional fragmentation and AI exposure in parallel, and reconciles overlapping levers employee by employee so every dollar is traceable.

What takes a performance improvement team 6 to 8 weeks takes Plek under a minute. At a 3,600-person company, Plek found $30M in annual EBITDA levers, matching what a global PE advisory firm found in six weeks. Funds and advisories use Plek from due diligence to exit to run org value creation scenarios, from the platform or from their own AI agents via MCP.

Plek grew out of the MIT Work Analytics Lab, founded by CEO Pierre Bouquet during his MIT PhD. Long-term, Plek becomes the Celonis of the workforce: it continuously monitors the org and flags value creation levers as they appear.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Private equity funds and advisory firms running organizational value creation in due diligence through exit
problem: Org and workforce analysis for PE takes a performance improvement team 6 to 8 weeks; Plek maps a census to tasks and sizes EBITDA levers in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS for PE funds and advisories, accessible via platform and MCP
product_category: AI workforce analytics for private equity
market_need_then: Advisory firms charge for 6 to 8 week analyses and PE firms are pressed to show AI-driven value (PwC, KPMG and FTI commentary in 2026); company claims four pilots and a deployment at a $2B fund.
outcome_analysis: Plek is a Fall 2026 YC company, so no outcome exists yet. The founders bring research credentials from the MIT Work Analytics Lab and a clear wedge in PE value creation at a time when funds want AI evidence. Open questions are customer conversion from pilots, whether advisory firms become partners or rivals, and the absence of any disclosed funding.

name: Plena Health
one_liner: Plena is the AI operating system for specialty medical practices
long_description: Plena is the AI operating system for specialty medical practices. We automate the administrative workflows that keep clinics running — referrals, fax intake, scheduling, procedure compliance, and collections — end to end, across all the systems a practice already uses. Unlike point solutions that cover a slice of the problem, Plena becomes the operating layer across the entire practice, connecting the systems, teams, and workflows that keep it running. In 10 months we've grown 17x and crossed seven figures in committed ARR across six specialties and eight states, with 80% of growth through word of mouth.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Specialty medical practices (six specialties in eight states claimed)
problem: Clinics lose time and revenue to manual referrals, fax intake, scheduling, procedure compliance and collections spread across many systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS and automation with annual or multi-year contracts
product_category: AI operating system for specialty practice administration
market_need_then: Self-reported traction: 17x growth in 10 months, seven figures committed ARR, 80% of growth by word of mouth. Specialty practice back office pain is documented in trade coverage.
outcome_analysis: Plena Health is a Spring 2026 YC company with self-reported fast growth and committed ARR above one million dollars. Founders with clinic exposure and a no-migration approach support early traction, but the wedge overlaps with Tennr and others. No exit or shutdown signal exists yet.

name: Ploid
one_liner: The people data company for the agent era
long_description:
Ploid is the AI-native people data infrastructure for developers and companies building products, workflows, and agents around people.

We've built an index of 2B+ people across professional and social sources, giving developers one API to search for people, enrich profiles, find emails and phone numbers, resolve identities, and retrieve up-to-date information from across the web. Unlike traditional people databases built around static records, Ploid combines its massive people index with real-time retrieval and identity resolution, delivering fresh, reliable information whenever it's needed. From sales and recruiting to customer intelligence, trust and safety, and AI agents, Ploid replaces fragmented data providers with a single infrastructure layer.

2B+ people. One API. Built for AI.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies building sales, recruiting, trust and safety and agent products that need people data
problem: People data is spread across fragmented providers with static records; builders want one API with fresh, resolved identities.
business_model: Usage-based API plus web app, CLI and MCP server (pricing page exists, details not seen)
product_category: People data and search API
market_need_then: Agent builders need people lookup; the 2025 Clearbit enrichment shutdown and Proxycurl closure opened demand for replacements, per roundup guides.
outcome_analysis: Ploid is a two-person Fall 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. It targets a crowded enrichment market but benefits from recent exits of Clearbit and Proxycurl. Key risks are data sourcing legality, accuracy claims that are self-reported, and well-funded competitors.

name: Plover Labs
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Enterprise; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Enable enterprises to ship agent code without human review
long_description:
Plover Labs is building toward a future where AI agents write, ship, and maintain most of a company's software. We make it possible for agents to own real engineering roles, not just suggest code for someone else to approve.

Coding models keep getting more capable, but enterprise adoption lags behind AI-native startups because enterprises don't yet trust agent output. Each codebase has conventions, history, and failure modes that a general-purpose model doesn't know. We learn those continuously from the code, how the team works, and the mistakes agents make. Then we fix the codebase and add merge gates that use deterministic verifiers instead of another model's judgment, so the same mistake can't ship twice. As the gates build up, agents can be trusted with more of the work.

We have five-figure monthly contracts with Series C companies Envoy and Fieldguide. At Fieldguide, we tripled PRs per engineer in one quarter, with the same headcount and PR size.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Enterprise engineering teams adopting AI coding agents
problem: Enterprises do not trust agent-written code because each codebase has conventions and failure modes general models do not know, so humans remain bottlenecked on review.
business_model: Enterprise contracts (five-figure monthly with two customers per YC page)
product_category: Codebase-specific intelligence and merge gates for coding agents
market_need_then: Reports in 2026 say agent output outpaces human review; Vercel published that 58% of PRs in its largest monorepo merge without human review. Company cites 3x PRs per engineer at Fieldguide.
outcome_analysis: Plover Labs is a two-person Fall 2026 YC company with early enterprise contracts. It is too early for an outcome. The thesis that verified gates let agents ship without review is timely, but model vendors and review tools are entering the same space.

name: Ploy

regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote

name: Pluto
one_liner: LinkedIn for agents
long_description:
Resumes made careers readable. LinkedIn made them filterable. Pluto makes them searchable.

Professionals spend 10 minutes talking to Pluto's voice agent about what they've done, what they're great at, and what they want next. Pluto turns that into a structured picture of who someone actually is, capturing the competency and intent that resumes and LinkedIn don't.

When companies and AI agents go looking to hire, Pluto makes the right people discoverable.

27K+ professionals have shared their career context with Pluto, and 50+ companies, including Mercor, Warp, and Rho, use it to find and reach the right people. Long-term, we're building the LinkedIn for agents.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies and AI agents that hire (50 to 100+ companies per YC posts); professionals use it free
problem: Resumes and LinkedIn profiles do not capture competency and intent; a voice conversation can produce a structured, searchable career picture.
business_model: Free for professionals; paid access for hiring companies (pricing not seen)
product_category: AI voice agent for career profiles and talent discovery
founder_names: Sahil Seth; Maki Potamianos; Tony Xavier
market_need_then: Hiring teams and agents need richer candidate context; company reports 27K+ professionals and 50+ companies (100+ in an earlier launch post), including Mercor, Warp and Rho.
outcome_analysis: Pluto is a Summer 2026 YC company with a five-person team and claimed traction of tens of thousands of professionals plus dozens of hiring customers. It is too early for an outcome. Supply of profiles is the asset, while copyability and LinkedIn are the main threats.

name: Pocket
one_liner: Take Notes in the Real World
long_description: Pocket is a Y Combinator W26 company building a premium hardware plus software product in the AI voice recorder space. We are obsessed with quality and speed. We are scaling very fast in the US and now European markets and building a device experience that can become the category leader.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Professionals, founders and creators who want in-person conversations and phone calls recorded, transcribed and summarized without a screen

product_category: AI voice recorder hardware plus software

It reports 130,000 units sold and closed an $11M seed led by Accel in June 2026, about three months after the W26 batch. The risks are a crowded field led by Plaud, thin technical moat and hardware margin pressure, but no shutdown, layoff or acquisition was found.

name: Polemos Industries
one_liner: AI-guided ballistic missiles, built for mass manufacturing
long_description:
Precision strike is rationed. Forces see more targets than they can afford to hit.

Polemos builds AI-guided ballistic missiles and the compact launchers that fire them, designed for mass manufacturing. Our launchers form a strike network wired into the recon drones already in the sky: a drone geolocates a target, the nearest launcher fires, and a guided round lands in seconds.

Short range, no wasted kilometers, no modified trucks. Built on production lines that already exist, so output scales when it matters most.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Military forces and defense buyers seeking low-cost precision strike
problem: Precision strike is rationed because each round is expensive, so forces see more targets than they can afford to hit.
business_model: Hardware sales of missiles and launchers to defense customers (stated intent, no contracts found)
product_category: Defense hardware, guided short-range ballistic missiles and launchers
market_need_then: US and allied forces are pursuing cheaper strike munitions; the Army has an Affordable High Speed Strike effort and a Low-Cost Containerized Missiles program per 2026 coverage (search results, TWZ and DTR).
outcome_analysis: Polemos joined YC in Fall 2026 with a three-person team and no public funding, customers or press. Its idea sits in a hot defense niche with funded rivals such as Castelion, so its path depends on a working prototype and government access. It is too early to call; no shutdown or acquisition was found.

name: Polymath

long_description: Polymath is a data lab focused on improving long-horizon agent capabilities and alignment. We build reinforcement learning environments for recursive self-improvement (RSI) and long-horizon software engineering.

name: Pomerado
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Workflow Automation; API; AI
one_liner: Turn any website into an MCP for your agents, in minutes
long_description:
Pomerado turns any website into an API / MCP in minutes. Connect your agents to legacy portals, consumer websites, and internal tools. 

Why Pomerado:
    • 7x faster than browser agents on customer workflows
    • 100x cheaper than browser agents
    • Self healing, deterministic APIs
    • Universal website coverage
    • Hosting, authentication, and permissions handled

Customers can use us to:
    • automate back office workflows on legacy systems (ERP, EHR, CRM)
    • speed up customer integrations for forward deployments
    • connect enterprise assistants to internal tools
    • supercharge personal assistants with fast and reliable browser use

We’re ex-McKinsey and Scale AI. We drove enterprise agent deployments at F500s and orgs like the Mayo Clinic. We saw how legacy systems block agent development and AI transformations; Pomerado turns those systems into AI-native components automatically.

problem: Browser agents are slow, costly and brittle, and many systems (ERP, EHR, CRM) have no API. Pomerado turns any website into a hosted API or MCP server.
business_model: Freemium usage-based: Free (100 calls per day), Premium $50 per month, custom Business tier; open-source core
product_category: Developer tools, website to API and MCP for agents

outcome_analysis: Pomerado is a two-person Fall 2026 company with Scale AI and McKinsey backgrounds and an open-source product with early GitHub interest. name: Poth Labs

long_description: Poth is an agentic research platform that connects to your company data, creates hypotheses about what might be causing problems, and validates them using both existing data and adaptive user feedback.

name: Prana
one_liner: An AI primary care doctor in your pocket
long_description:
Prana replaces the reactive, 15-minute annual physical with continuous, proactive care. We connect to your medical records and wearables to watch for "clinical drift," catching subtle declines in health that human doctors miss between visits.

Most AI health apps are just chatbots. Prana is a full-stack medical provider. Our AI acts as a always-on physician that watches your data, explains your labs, and manages your prescriptions.

Safety & Scale: We automate 90% of the "grunt work" (history taking, logistics, triage) so our human doctors can focus purely on high-leverage decisions. This allows us to offer 24/7 physician care for a fraction of the cost of traditional care.

The Team:
 - Meer Patel (CEO): JHU BME. Deferred Brown Medical School to build Prana because code scales better than appointments.
- Vishvam Rawal (CTO): Ex-Quant. Building high-frequency data infrastructure for health signals.
- Sanjit Menon (CHO): Graduating MD Candidate. Deep clinical expertise to ensure our models practice good medicine.

Traction: Live in beta with early users.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers wanting low-cost, always-on primary care guidance and physician visits
problem: Primary care is reactive and limited to short visits; Prana connects medical records and wearables to catch gradual decline and automates routine work so doctors focus on key decisions.
business_model: Consumer: free AI chat plus a flat $39 doctor visit with no subscription (per site)
product_category: AI primary care, telehealth
founder_names: Meer Patel; Vishvam Rawal; Sanjit Menon
market_need_then: Consumers were already using AI health tools at scale in 2025, shown by Doctronic's reported 1 million users and $20M raise.
outcome_analysis: Prana is a four-person W26 company with a mix of engineering, quant and clinical founders, live in beta with a free chat and $39 visits. Its model closely resembles Doctronic, which is better funded. No verified funding, shutdown or acquisition was found, so the outcome is open.

name: Praxis
one_liner: AI agents that run law firm operations.
long_description:
At Praxis, we’ve built AI agents that run law firm operations, from first inquiry to paid invoice. Agents do the admin end to end, and the lawyer supervises and approves every step. Firms reply in minutes, onboard clients in days instead of weeks, and spend their time practicing law.

Lawyers spend 62% of their day on admin nobody pays for: intake, conflict checks, chasing documents, engagement letters, follow-ups, billing. Every hour on admin is an hour a client waits, and clients go to the firm that answers first. One law firm owner shared: “Every month we lose 3-5 clients, $10k each, because we’re 3 paralegals to handle the process, it’s too slow.”

We’re live with law firms across the US.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: Lawyers spend most of their day on unpaid admin such as intake, conflict checks, document chasing and billing, and slow replies lose clients.
business_model: B2B SaaS for law firms, pricing not published (early access)
product_category: Legal operations AI agents
competitors_at_founding: Eve; Lawmatics QualifyAI; Clio Grow AI

outcome_analysis: Praxis is a two-person Fall 2026 company with a strong go-to-market founder from Gorgias and an AI engineer. It says it is live with US law firms but has no public funding or press beyond a Fondo write-up. Competition from incumbent practice management tools is intensifying, so the outcome is open.

name: Preload

Designing and iterating a multimodal hardware stack (currently ego + tactile gloves + EMG) to collect rich and scalable datasets for physical AI. Also interested in how we can use this technology to advance surgery.

About us:
Prescience is building a new healthcare system for America. We train AI systems to: create, operate, insure, and deliver healthcare for employer health plans. Prescience Time Machine – an AlphaGo-like system – steers patients towards “Move 37 health trajectories” that deliver dramatic cost savings for employers. Rishab Jain and Aditya Jain, M.D. are serial entrepreneurs and brothers from Harvard & Harvard Medical School with backgrounds in machine learning and medicine. We believe abundant intelligence will bring an opportunity to fundamentally rebuild the $4.5T healthcare industry around proactive (prescient) health and wellness.

It is too early for an outcome: no priced round beyond a possible YC standard deal, no exit and no independent traction data were found, so nothing supports success or failure factors yet.

name: Prized
one_liner: A cloud devbox that feels local
long_description:
Prized is a cloud development environment that feels local on your Mac. 

Developers get a dedicated, persistent machine with their repos, dependencies, and tools already configured. 

Files sync into a real local folder, remote ports appear on localhost, and terminals persist through tmux, so developers and coding agents can keep working even after the laptop closes. 

Machines can be resized or cloned as workloads grow, without rebuilding the development environment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software developers and teams running AI coding agents who need persistent cloud machines
problem: Coding agents stop when a laptop closes and local setups are hard to share. Prized gives each developer a persistent cloud Linux machine that syncs to a local folder.
business_model: Subscription plans from $10 to $1,000 per month plus usage billing for sandboxes (per the company site)
product_category: Cloud development environments and agent sandboxes
market_need_then: Coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex became mainstream and teams want them to keep running when a laptop closes. Several vendor comparison posts in 2026 show demand for agent sandboxes.
outcome_analysis: Prized is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. Both founders worked at Gander, which Archer Aviation acquired, but the devbox space is crowded and easy to copy, so winning will depend on developer experience and distribution. A YC launch page also frames it as an internal tool builder, so the positioning is unsettled.

name: Probe
tags: Machine Learning; SaaS; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: The Agent-Native Research Stack
long_description:
Probe is building the agent-native research stack.

Our goal is simple: help AI/ML teams run better experiments, faster. We believe research will drive progress and everyone deserves to have their own personalized lab that iterates faster than ever before. 

Probe brings core research tools, shared context from past experiments, and visibility into each run together in one platform. Helping teams spend less time setting up infrastructure, supervising agents, catching teammates up and more time testing ideas.

Built for helping research labs experiment faster while keeping every researcher and agent aligned, and helping AI/ML teams setup a research capability without building a lab’s infrastructure first.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI and ML research teams and labs that run many experiments with coding agents
problem: Teams lose context between experiments and spend time on infrastructure, supervising agents and catching teammates up. Probe logs runs, metrics and decisions so agents build on past work.
business_model: Software platform for teams; pricing not stated
product_category: Experiment tracking and research workspace for AI agents
founder_names: Ashwarye Yadav; Mahit Namburu; Richard Wei
market_need_then: Coding agents began running research experiments in 2026, and roundups note the tools to observe and debug agents have diverged from classic experiment tracking.
outcome_analysis: Probe is a Spring 2026 YC company still operating with no outcome yet. The three Berkeley founders have ML infrastructure experience, but the category has entrenched trackers and open source options, so Probe must win on agent native workflows and shared context to raise.

name: Prodigy Research
tags: Reinforcement Learning; Finance; Investing; Trading; AI
one_liner: Training the world's best AI model for quantitative finance.
long_description: Prodigy is the frontier AI trading research lab. We've trained the world's best foundation model for quantitative finance. We've already achieved more than 100% returns in live trading over the course of our YC batch, doubling our capital while major indices were flat. Our founders previously worked on a trading desk at Jane Street, trained frontier AI models at Google DeepMind and shipped cutting-edge AI at Apple to billions of customers. Join us as we use AI to solve the market.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Not clear; the company trades its own capital in live markets and presents no customer product
problem: Build a foundation model for quantitative finance that trades autonomously and captures alpha.
business_model: Proprietary trading with an AI research lab framing; no API or subscription presented (per Runtime Wire)
product_category: AI quantitative trading research lab
market_need_then: Reports in May 2026 found most AI trading bots in live tests were losing money, so demand for a model that works is real but unproven. The company's 140 percent return claim is its own and unverified.
outcome_analysis: Prodigy Research is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. The founders bring trading desk and frontier AI experience, but its main evidence is a self reported 140 percent return with no method published, so the next test is whether it can show verified performance or raise outside capital.

name: ProjectX
one_liner: Agent native workspace for heavy parallel workflows on the web
long_description:
Every computer ever made forces you to do one thing at a time. One cursor. One keyboard. One Hardware. One app in focus. Fifty years. Nobody questioned it.

We did. We started over.

We built InfinityOS, a fundamentally new computer OS on the cloud from ground up.

Infinity runs every app in its own independent computer -- own GPU, own input, own environment. Windows and Linux in the same session. Humans and agents working side by side. No concurrency ceiling. Cold start in seconds. runs on the browser of any device..
regions: India; South Asia; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Users and teams running heavy parallel workflows and AI agents on the web, including those on low powered devices
problem: Computers run one app in focus on one machine. Infinity runs each app on its own cloud computer with its own GPU so humans and agents can work in parallel from any browser.
business_model: Cloud computing platform accessed by browser; pricing not found
product_category: Cloud native operating system for agents (Infinity)
founder_names: Rounak Adhikary; Bishal Karmakar; Sourya Majumder
market_need_then: Press in 2024 framed Infinity as bridging the digital divide for people with low powered devices; by 2026 the pitch shifted to agent workspaces as agents drive parallel work.
outcome_analysis: ProjectX began in 2022 as a student led cloud OS project in Kolkata, drew Google Cloud support in 2024, and joined YC in Spring 2026 with a pitch reframed around AI agents. Reported funding is small and conflicting, and its outcome is not yet known, so the YC batch and agent positioning are the main tests.

name: Proprio Robotics
one_liner: Robots to maintain and assemble data centers
long_description: Proprio Robotics is building state-of-the-art physical intelligence to automate the entire data center lifecycle—from buildout to maintenance to decommissioning. There are currently 400,000 unstaffed data center technicians positions in the United States alone, which means the massive compute needs of AI are being bottlenecked by labor constraints. Proprio is solving this by building robots that do it instead, and is deploying data center maintenance robots starting Q1 2027.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data center operators and builders facing technician shortages
problem: Data centers lack technicians (the company cites 400,000 unstaffed positions in the US) which bottlenecks AI compute. Proprio builds robots for buildout, maintenance and decommissioning.
business_model: Robots deployed in data centers, starting Q1 2027 per the company; pricing not stated
product_category: Physical AI robots for data center operations
competitors_at_founding: Exclaim Robotics; Darwin Robotics; Watney; Boost Robotics
market_need_then: AI data center buildout in 2026 is constrained by labor, and Meta publicly tested robot technicians; several startups raised pre-seed rounds for the same wedge.
outcome_analysis: Proprio Robotics is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. The timing tailwind from the data center labor shortage is clear, but the team is one or two people attempting research grade manipulation against better funded rivals, so a working deployment in Q1 2027 is the milestone to watch.

name: Proto
one_liner: The product designer's coding agent
long_description: Designers are no longer drawers, but builders. Yet their canvas based design tools are still built for drawing, and the coding agents they’re using are built for engineers. Proto is a coding agent with all the capabilities of Claude Code, but rebuilt from scratch for designers, with features like Midjourney’s rapid idea exploration, and Figma’s first class sharing.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Product designers at software companies who want to build working prototypes with a coding agent
problem: Designers are moving from drawing to building, but canvas design tools are made for drawing and general coding agents are made for engineers.
business_model: Software subscription for a designer-focused coding agent (pricing not published; early access alpha)
product_category: AI coding agent and IDE for designers
competitors_at_founding: MagicPath; Figma Make; Lovable; Magic Patterns
market_need_then: The YC page and site argue designers are becoming builders. Evidence of demand is the number of 2026 design to code tools and comparison articles; no usage data for Proto was found.
outcome_analysis: Proto joined YC in the Fall 2026 batch as a two person team building a coding agent for designers. It is too early for an outcome. The wedge is real but crowded, with MagicPath, Figma Make and Lovable already serving designers, so the open question is whether a designer-native agent with strong sharing and idea exploration can beat those and the general coding agents.

name: Prototyping.io
one_liner: Autonomous manufacturing for mechanical parts
long_description: Prototyping.io turns CAD designs into real mechanical parts through an AI-driven manufacturing system. We analyze designs for manufacturability and automate production workflows to deliver high-quality parts faster and at lower cost.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware and engineering teams that order custom mechanical parts from CAD files
problem: Ordering CNC machined parts still runs through phone calls and PDFs across thousands of shops, making quotes and delivery slow and costly.
business_model: Manufacturing service: AI quoting and production planning, revenue per part ordered
product_category: AI enabled on demand manufacturing for mechanical parts
market_need_then: Competitor marketing and the company's own launch page describe thousands of local and offshore shops still quoting by phone and PDF, and tariff driven interest in domestic sourcing; no independent demand data was retrieved.
outcome_analysis: Prototyping.io joined YC in Spring 2026 with a CAD to CNC part pitch and was reported to have raised a seed of $6.2M, with one outlet saying it paused hiring after plans changed. YC lists it as Acquired, but no buyer, date or press coverage of a deal was found, and its own site still takes early access sign ups. The outcome is therefore unverified.

name: ProvenMetal
one_liner: AI-native electronics manufacturing for the American industrial base
long_description:
ProvenMetal manufactures the fastest circuit boards in the United States.

Domestic circuit board manufacturing is slow and expensive, and while reshoring is happening, the supply chain isn't there yet.

We automate the bottlenecks - part procurement, DFM review, and assembly - delivering circuit boards in days instead of weeks.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware engineering teams, robotics and drone companies and defense electronics teams needing US-made circuit boards quickly
problem: Domestic circuit board manufacturing is slow and expensive, and over half of lead time goes to quoting, DFM review and part sourcing rather than manufacturing.
business_model: Manufacturing service: instant quote, sourced BOM and assembled boards routed to US fab and assembly partners
product_category: Electronics manufacturing (PCB fabrication and assembly orchestration)
market_need_then: Reshoring and defense demand: a trade article in the results says domestic fabricators fell from over 2,000 to around 145, and the founders say they spent 90 percent of their time assembling boards by hand before building the service.
outcome_analysis: ProvenMetal is a Summer 2026 YC company that pivoted from an energy management idea to fast US-made circuit boards. It is too early for an outcome. The pain is real and defense and reshoring tailwinds help, but CircuitHub is well funded and the service depends on partner fabs, so defensibility rests on speed and relationships.

name: Proximitty
one_liner: AI operating system for commercial loans
long_description:
Proximitty is the AI operating system for commercial loans - we build regulator-grade AI agents that ingest and parse documents, spread financials, automate loan operations and track covenants.

We help FDIC-insured banks and fintechs underwrite faster and scale their loan books without scaling costs.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: FDIC-insured banks, credit unions and fintech lenders running commercial loan books (C&I, CRE, SBA)
problem: Commercial loan underwriting and servicing is manual: analysts collect documents, spread financials and track covenants by hand, so loan books cannot scale without headcount.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software with AI agents; pricing not published, about three week deployment per company site
product_category: AI agents for commercial lending operations
market_need_then: Banks face rising loan volumes and analyst costs; the founders cite a fintech customer that cut a loan servicing team from 15 people to 2 (company-sourced claim).
outcome_analysis: Proximitty is a Winter 2026 YC company with two founders from fintech and security backgrounds selling AI agents to banks. It reports early seed funding from YC, CRV, Cohen Circle and Uphonest. It is too early for an outcome; the key questions are bank sales cycles and whether a well-funded rival like Casca wins the commercial lending workflow.

name: PumpGTM
one_liner: Find and engage with desperate buyers across LinkedIn, Email, and X
long_description:
Your favorite AI's favorite GTM tooling

We connect your LinkedIn, Email, and X and find you leads and get you sales while you sleep
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: B2B startups and sales teams that want outbound leads across LinkedIn, email and X
problem: Founders and small sales teams struggle to find buyers who are actively looking and to run multichannel outreach without stitching several tools together.
business_model: Subscription from $75 per month per LinkedIn account plus done-for-you plans ($1,740 setup, $2,980 to $5,640 per month)
product_category: AI outbound sales and lead engagement
market_need_then: Founder-led outbound is a widespread need; the product grew out of the internal system the founder used to acquire customers for his other company, per one aggregator.
outcome_analysis: PumpGTM is a Spring 2026 YC company that productized the outbound system its founder used for another startup. It is too early for an outcome. The market is crowded with LinkedIn and email outreach tools, so it must win on results and the done-for-you offer rather than technology.

name: Q2Q
one_liner: We help private equity teams find acquisition targets faster
long_description:
Q2Q is the AI-native outbound engine for deal sourcing. Tell us the types of companies you want to buy, and we'll get qualified meetings booked for you. 

You can think of Q2Q as your personal team of AI interns. You give us your buying criteria, and we'll go out and find companies, write personalized emails, and get first calls booked with business owners for you. As the human in the loop, you'll approve messages before we send. Q2Q handles the sourcing work so you can focus on evaluating great deals.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Qlo
one_liner: Legora for commercial insurance carriers
long_description:
Qlo builds AI agents to run commercial insurance underwriting. We start by fully automating the operational work around risk decisions, become the system of record, and earn autonomy workflow by workflow toward the autonomous AI underwriter.

We’re rebuilding underwriting infrastructure from the ground up so human underwriters and AI agents can share the same accounts, rules, documents, permissions, and workflow state. 

We believe every commercial insurance program will eventually be built and operated end to end by AI agents on Qlo.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Commercial insurance carriers, MGAs and program administrators handling many submissions
problem: Commercial underwriting is full of operational handoffs (intake, rating, endorsements, document processing) that slow quotes and cap how many submissions underwriters can handle.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software with AI agents and an AI-native system of record; pricing not published
product_category: AI agents for commercial insurance underwriting
market_need_then: Insurers want faster quoting and more throughput; Qlo's site claims 3x primary quote throughput (company claim). Founder previously sold into commercial insurance and got an acquisition offer from a public insurer, showing buyer interest.
outcome_analysis: Qlo is a Summer 2026 YC company building underwriting agents for commercial insurers. The founder has insurance marketplace experience, which helps with distribution to MGAs. It is too early for an outcome. The main risk is that better funded underwriting platforms already ship similar agents.

name: Quippy
one_liner: Helps build social skills through daily practice
long_description: Quippy is a daily practice app for your social life. You run short, realistic practice conversations, like pushing back on a boss or talking during a first date, and get line-by-line feedback on what landed and what backfired. The curriculum adapts to each person's patterns, reshaping itself around their weak spots, ensuring steady improvement in the conversations that matter most.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Consumers who want to improve social and conversation skills (dating, work, everyday situations)
problem: People lack a safe, repeatable way to practice hard conversations out loud and get specific feedback.
business_model: Consumer subscription app (pricing not found)
product_category: AI social skills practice app
market_need_then: The number of 2026 social skills practice apps and Duolingo's Video Call with Lily show demand for spoken AI practice; no Quippy user data found. A podcast notes the open question of whether users return without external pressure.
outcome_analysis: Quippy is a solo-founder Fall 2026 YC consumer app for practicing conversations. The founder has Duolingo and Luvu product experience, which fits a habit-based app. It is too early for an outcome. The category filled with similar apps in 2026, so retention and brand will decide it.

name: Quivly AI
one_liner: AI agents that run onboarding, adoption, and renewals
long_description: Quivly is the agentic workspace for everything after the sale. Our agents turn kickoff calls into launch plans, chase blockers, catch risk and expansion signals, and have the full account story ready at renewal. With Quivly, companies are able to take their customers live in 7 days instead of 30, and then grow revenue from these customers by 4.3x on avg.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Post-sales teams (customer success, forward deployed and customer engineers) at companies with usage-based pricing
problem: After a deal closes, onboarding, adoption and renewals are handled manually across CRM, billing and support tools, so launches take weeks and expansion and risk signals are missed.
business_model: B2B SaaS with AI agents; pricing not published
product_category: AI agents for post-sales and customer success
market_need_then: Usage-based pricing is spreading (the CMU spotlight, reflecting company messaging, says 85 percent of software companies have or plan it), making account health and expansion tracking more urgent.
outcome_analysis: Quivly is a Fall 2026 YC company founded in 2024 by two experienced product and fintech operators, selling post-sales agents. It is too early for an outcome. The incumbents all added agents in 2026, so Quivly must differentiate on usage-based pricing customers and execution speed.

name: Quotient Labs
one_liner: Use Claude Code at 47% less cost in one line of installation.
long_description:
You should only be paying frontier model prices for top-shelf reasoning. But 88% of your token bill is just tool I/O.
 Quotient Labs runs on top of Claude Code to reduce token spend, compress context, and optimize tool calls while preserving output quality. Same models, same workflow, no changes to how you work. Benchmarked 47% less cost on real, multi-step developer workflows, with no quality loss.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and teams that are heavy users of Claude Code
problem: About 88 percent of a Claude Code token bill is tool input and output, so users overpay for non reasoning tokens.
business_model: Developer tool subscription at $20 per month or 10 percent of savings generated
product_category: AI developer tools, token cost optimization
competitors_at_founding: Compresr (YC W26); The Token Company (YC W26); Edgee
market_need_then: Claude Code costs are large for heavy users; the company reports 34 to 51 percent savings (average 47 percent) in its own benchmarks, while a third party benchmark found 19 percent for one tool of this type.
outcome_analysis: Quotient Labs is an active Winter 2026 company selling a Claude Code cost saver with a witty product brand. No verified funding exists beyond an unconfirmed $125K seed on one aggregator. The outcome is open, and the main risks are Anthropic shipping native savings and several YC peers building the same tool.

name: RASPIRE
one_liner: Autonomous Runtime Security
long_description: RASPIRE is the first line of defense for applications against AI-powered fraud attacks, API abuse, and runtime threats. Unlike code scanners and pentesting tools that identify vulnerabilities before release, RASPIRE operates like a security expert running inside applications, monitoring, detecting, and blocking attacks 24/7 in real time. All without writing a single line of code.
regions: Egypt; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Mobile engineering and security teams at banks, fintechs, healthtech and e-commerce companies
problem: Mobile apps are attacked at runtime through tampering, hooking, API abuse and AI-powered fraud, and protecting them normally needs SDK integration and code changes.
business_model: B2B security platform; protections applied to compiled APK or IPA builds with no SDK; pricing not published
product_category: Mobile runtime application self-protection (RASP)
market_need_then: Banks and fintechs face rising mobile fraud and compliance pressure (OWASP MASVS, PCI DSS). The founders cite 16 customers and 25 apps in third party profile (yespress); company site claims 20M+ end users protected.
outcome_analysis: Raspire is a Cairo-based Spring 2026 YC company selling no-code mobile runtime security, founded by two offensive security practitioners. It is too early for an outcome. It reports early customers in banking and fintech, but must prove it can displace established shielding vendors.

name: RATLOG
one_liner: Reusable heavy-lift rockets
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: Commercial and institutional satellite operators and agencies that need heavy-lift launch capacity in Europe, booked and paid by the kilogram
problem: Europe has little available or affordable heavy-lift launch capacity, and the company argues Ariane 6 is expensive and scarce.
business_model: Launch services sold per kilogram of payload capacity, with launch reservation agreements as the early commercial instrument
product_category: Reusable heavy-lift launch vehicle and rocket engine
founder_names: Charlie Weise; Paul Kunhart; Felix Kelm; Matty Driesnack
competitors_at_founding: Isar Aerospace; Ariane 6; Rocket Factory Augsburg
market_need_then: European institutional customers lack independent heavy-lift options; company claims over 400 million dollars in launch reservation agreements, which is self-reported and not binding purchase evidence.
outcome_analysis: RATLOG is a Fall 2026 YC company with an active status and no outcome yet. The signals so far are a small German grant, a first hot-fire, and self-reported launch reservations; the long timeline to a 2029 or 2030 launch means capital and technical execution are the main open risks.

name: REV1
one_liner: Claude Code for Mechanical Engineers
long_description:
REV1 is Claude code for mechanical engineers, starting with automating the process of turning 3D designs into 2D manufacturing drawings – which is more than 25% of all of what a mechanical engineer does - our software does it in minutes. 
Compressing hours of work into minutes while delivering consistent, higher quality results.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mechanical engineers and hardware teams that produce manufacturing drawings from 3D CAD
problem: Turning 3D designs into annotated 2D manufacturing drawings with GD&T consumes more than 25 percent of a mechanical engineer's time.
business_model: B2B software sold on demo basis, pricing not public
product_category: AI engineering drawing and GD&T automation
market_need_then: Drawing creation is a recognized time sink for mechanical engineers; company cites over 25 percent of working time. No independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: REV1 is a Winter 2026 YC company that is still active with a two person team. The founders come from Apple and Tesla hardware work, which fits the problem, but competitors target the same drawing automation wedge and no outcome is public yet.

name: Radley
one_liner: The AI-native radiology practice
long_description:
Radley is the first AI-native radiology practice. We're acquiring a radiology practice bringing Radley to $4.6M in annualized revenue and rebuilding it with agents from the ground up.

Radiology is already in crisis: there aren't enough radiologists to interpret 1 in 6 medical scans. In 10 years, that gap is growing to 1 in 3 - 246M scans a year.

From past experience, we know that point solutions won’t cut it. While there is demand (we have $2.2M in contracts to prove it), bottleneck isn't just software, it's outdated systems and slow, inefficient operations. That's why we own the full stack, clinical and operational, end to end.

We met at Carbon Health as we scaled operations 31x and expanded to 100+ clinics. Now we're rebuilding radiology.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Hospitals and imaging centers that outsource radiology reads
problem: There are too few radiologists to read all scans, and operations around reading are slow and outdated.
business_model: Owned radiology practice charging per read, using AI to draft reports that radiologists sign
product_category: AI-native radiology practice
competitors_at_founding: Epsilon Health; Harrison.ai (Frontier Radiology); Rad AI
market_need_then: Company states 1 in 6 scans lacks a radiologist and the gap grows to 1 in 3 within ten years, and claims 2.2M dollars in contracts and 4.6M annualized revenue via an acquisition; all self-reported.
outcome_analysis: Radley is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. Founders scaled Carbon Health operations, which fits the full-stack approach, but the model depends on closing a practice acquisition and competing with funded AI-native practices and incumbents.

name: Rainbrand
one_liner: The brand layer for agents.
long_description:
Rainbrand is the brand layer for agents. It turns a brand’s identity, guidance, and assets into shared context that agents and products can use. That context evolves with the brand, alongside the tools where it is created and managed.

Starting with websites, social media, and files, Rainbrand develops and maintains versioned brand context. Through MCP or the API, connected agents and products can retrieve and update that context, then apply it to images, websites, slides, video, copy, and other brand work.

We’re an ai infra company making brand as operable as software.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies and AI product builders who need agents to produce on-brand output
problem: Agents and AI tools lack structured, current brand context, so generated content drifts from the brand.
business_model: B2B SaaS with MCP and REST API access
product_category: Brand context infrastructure for AI agents
market_need_then: Founder's earlier launch as Bloom reportedly drew 15K signups in December 2025 per its YC page as relayed by search; no paying demand data found.
outcome_analysis: Rainbrand, formerly Bloom, is a Spring 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. It reports early viral signups and a roughly one million dollar pre-seed, but several brand tools already ship MCP access, so differentiation and monetization are the open questions.

name: RamAIn
one_liner: RamAIn - AI Employees with a computer to perform business tasks just…
long_description: RamAIn Employees join your team just like a human. Teach them to work across systems just like a new hire and watch them work autonomously to do the work 24/7.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Enterprises with legacy software and web portals that lack APIs, such as lenders, marketplaces and healthcare billing firms
problem: Back-office work lives in systems without APIs, so it needs people or brittle RPA scripts.
business_model: Enterprise subscription for AI employees assigned to defined processes
product_category: Computer-use AI agents for process automation
market_need_then: Enterprise pages cite no-API legacy systems as the main automation obstacle; RamAIn claims customers such as a national mortgage lender, unnamed and self-reported.
outcome_analysis: RamAIn is a Winter 2026 YC company still active with a small team. Founders have strong research credentials and claim enterprise customers, but computer use agents were a crowded category by 2025 and no funding or outcome is public.

name: Rapidfolio
one_liner: AI-native back-office for banks and fintechs
long_description:
Rapidfolio helps banks and fintechs fully automate back-office workflows like fraud investigations, KYB/KYC and loan underwriting, with accuracy and auditability.

Built by fintech founders and operators, Rapidfolio is on a mission to ensure banks and fintechs scale their customer base without adding another back-office head count.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Banks and fintechs with manual compliance and risk back offices
problem: Fraud investigations, KYB and KYC checks and underwriting require growing back-office headcount.
business_model: B2B SaaS automating back-office workflows, pricing not public
product_category: AI back-office automation for financial institutions
market_need_then: Banks and fintechs carry large manual KYB, fraud and underwriting queues; the company shows named customers and case results that are vendor-provided.
outcome_analysis: Rapidfolio is a Summer 2026 YC company with named early customers and repeat founders who previously built and sold a fintech. It faces funded agentic compliance competitors and incumbent AI launches, and no funding or outcome is public.

name: Rasyn
one_liner: Making chemicals 100,000x faster
long_description:
We build foundational AI models for chemistry. Almost nothing you buy is a single chemical. Products like datacenter coolant, GPU thermal paste, paint, and glue are formulations, which are mixtures of around ten ingredients each, and demand for them has grown quickly because of AI and EVs.

Designing a new formulation is essentially a search problem, because there are more possible mixtures than anyone could ever test, and none of them can be predicted in advance. As a result, bringing a single formulation to market today takes three to five years of trial and error in a lab.

Our models predict how a mixture will behave far faster than the standard methods used today, which lets us design new formulations in weeks rather than years, at a fraction of the cost. To prove this, we used them to invent three chemicals that never existed before, including a PFAS-free coolant for datacenters, and we have since synthesized and patented all three.

We are already working with some of the largest manufacturers to design formulations for them, and we are building our own lab to generate the data that will train our next models.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Large manufacturers of industrial chemicals and formulations such as coolants, thermal paste, paints and adhesives
problem: Developing a new formulation takes three to five years of lab trial and error because the search space of mixtures is vast.
business_model: Custom formulation design projects for manufacturers, with in-house lab and models
product_category: AI foundation models for chemistry and formulation design
founder_names: Ansh Tiwari; Ayush Chauhan; Daood Hashmi
competitors_at_founding: Citrine Informatics; Periodic Labs; Orbital Industries
market_need_then: AI data centers and EVs raised demand for new coolants and formulations; company says it works with large manufacturers, unnamed.
outcome_analysis: Rasyn is a Summer 2026 YC company with no public outcome. Its pivot from a chemistry copilot toward owning formulation design and a lab aims at more defensible data, but competitors with much larger funding operate in the same area.

name: Rational
one_liner: First Zero-human Accounting Firm
long_description: Rational is building the first accounting firm with no humans. It's entirely run by our AI employees, who go from client intake to doing the books to filing with the IRS. We secure 90% cost reduction, 24/7 support, and an overall seamless experience for businesses.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Startups, businesses and accounting firms that outsource bookkeeping and tax
problem: Accounting is labor intensive and expensive, with slow turnaround for bookkeeping and filings.
business_model: AI-run accounting services and AI employees sold as a service
product_category: AI accounting firm
market_need_then: Accounting is a large spend with talent shortages; Botkeeper's failure shows risk. Inside Public Accounting reports design partners including a Fortune Global 500 company.

name: Raven

name: RealPact
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: AI-native OS for Real Estate Brokerages
long_description:
RealPact builds AI agents that handle the paperwork behind real estate transactions. They find property records like deeds, tax records, permits, parcel data, and MLS information, then use that data to fill out contracts, organize documents, track deadlines, and help brokerages close deals faster.

We are starting by automating transactions and will expand into other parts of brokerage operations. Much of the software used across the real estate industry is outdated. We currently sell to brokerages in New Hampshire and are expanding quickly.

name: Reason Machines

Reason runs autonomous cloud agents with a frontier harness on cost per task.

name: Reconero

name: Redoubt Insurance

name: Reific
tags: Generative AI; Machine Learning; Reinforcement Learning; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time
long_description:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. AI has learned to reason over text and code. But most of what matters in the real world shows up as numbers that change every second: a heartbeat, a gearbox, a GPU cluster. No human can track thousands of signals at once, but AI should be able to.

In our environments, data streams in on a clock while the agent works, and every action is graded by what actually happened. Most AI training today teaches models to match human experts. We treat human performance as the floor. Each environment comes from real, de-identified records, in three task families: personal agents, industry, and science & compute.

Today, even the best frontier model averages under 50% on each family. Training an open model on our environments raised its full-solve rate on unseen tasks by 54% (from 25.6% to 39.5%), with no loss on general benchmarks. Our mission is to build the infrastructure that keeps AI climbing the frontier, long past human level in the real world.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs that train agents with reinforcement learning, buying licensed or custom RL environments and data licenses
problem: Most RL training teaches models to match human experts on text and code, but much real-world signal is numeric streams that change over time. Labs lack graded environments where data arrives on a clock and actions are scored against what actually happened.
business_model: License RL environments, build custom environments, and license data (usage terms not published)
product_category: RL environments and evals for frontier AI labs
competitors_at_founding: HUD; Bespoke Labs; Mechanize, Prime Intellect, Plato, Fleet AI
market_need_then: Frontier labs were investing heavily in RL environments by 2026 according to an investor note, and reports describe a growing set of YC-backed environment startups with strong revenue.
outcome_analysis: Reific is a one-person Fall 2026 company active in the RL environment market that frontier labs were funding heavily. Its edge is real streaming records plus a researcher founder, but defensibility is thin because labs can build in-house and several funded vendors exist. No outcome exists yet, so these factors are provisional.

name: Rex
one_liner: AI operations partner for enterprise order-to-cash
long_description:
Rex is a managed AI service for AR and order-to-cash. AI agents and finance experts run the work that delays payment, from collections, portals, disputes and remittances to the shared AR inbox, so cash keeps moving.

Order to cash is a $60B outsourced function because the work is too messy for traditional automation. Every customer has different context, exceptions do not follow clean rules, and the next step is often buried in emails, portals, handoffs, or someone’s memory. Rex agents run continuously in the background and resolve work to SLA standards so cash keeps moving. We're live with pre-IPO tech companies, managing  >$500m in receivables from F100 companies, cutting manual follow-up cycles from weeks to hours.

We founded Rex after spending four years building Sequence, an a16z-backed finance ops platform, from zero to Series A — where we saw firsthand that at-scale, O2C still runs on manual labour.

Rex is the #1 winner of the Vercel AI Accelerator out of 2,500 teams, selected by Guillermo Rauch and leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Browserbase and more.

product_category: AI operations service for accounts receivable and order to cash
market_need_then: The company says order to cash is a 60B USD outsourced function. It reports managing over 500M USD in receivables and a 12 day DSO improvement at a customer, both company reported and unverified.
outcome_analysis: Rex is an active Summer 2026 company. Founders spent four years at Sequence, an order to cash platform, which gives them domain insight. It won the Vercel AI Accelerator and has a named customer in Synthesia, though funding amounts are undisclosed. Well funded AR startups compete, so execution decides the outcome.

name: Rhizome AI
one_liner: Agent Platform for Life Sciences
long_description:
It takes 500,000 days of office work to bring a drug to market. We want to make it 5. To get there, we need agents doing most of the work. 

Today, our research agent is the best way to know what the FDA thinks. Users ask a question and get an answer backed by up to 1,000 documents, where each statement has a citation. 

It’s the best because we have the best retrieval engine. We’ve tuned it on our life science-specific dataset, and we find what others miss.

As more teams use Rhizome, we gain more data on what regulatory professionals actually need, which makes retrieval even better. This flywheel is how we become the retrieval engine that powers all human and agent work in life sciences.

Chetan started his career as a research engineer, but quickly realized he enjoyed building more than research. He joined EvolutionaryScale as their sole founding product engineer, launching their developer-scientist platform and scaling to tens of thousands of users and billions of API calls. He was also #16 at Instabase helping banks with document processing, closing $7m as the technical closer.

Agents can do magical things today, but most in life sciences only use them to edit emails. Agents are missing the context they need to 100x the number of drugs we can bring to market. Rhizome AI is focused on that critical problem.

We study how models learn and represent knowledge, and build systems that put that research to work. Our work spans model routing, evaluations, post-training, and physical AI.

Earned intelligence.

name: RightNow

Run the best open models at full speed per token, or with reserved capacity, dedicated deployments and batch at half price. For enterprises, we optimize your own models down to the kernel

name: Rindler
one_liner: The IDE for Tokenmaxxers
long_description:
We build Maxxwell, a desktop app for people who run several coding agents at once.

Past two or three sessions, you become the bottleneck. Every session asks you something, most of it small, and you spend the day answering instead of deciding. It is also hard to tell which sessions are making progress, which are stuck on something trivial, and which have quietly started building the wrong thing.

Maxxwell puts every session in one window and marks each one working, idle, or waiting on you. On top of that sits an orchestrator, a real coding-agent session of its own that reads the others and reports back. You talk to it instead of to twelve terminals. It tells you what landed, what it decided for you, and what actually needs your call.

Every worker is your own tool, unmodified. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent run in real terminal sessions you can attach to and take over at any point
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

business_model: Free desktop app and CLI (Maxxwell) where users bring their own agent subscriptions or API keys; monetization not stated
product_category: Developer tools, multi-agent coding orchestration desktop app

market_need_then: Heavy use of parallel coding agents in 2026 created a supervision bottleneck, and many open source orchestrators appeared at the same time, showing the pain is widely felt.
outcome_analysis: Rindler is a two person MIT team in the Summer 2026 batch that, per the YC page, launched with a web-to-API product for agents but now sells Maxxwell, a free multi-agent coding desktop app. No outcome exists yet. The wedge is real but crowded with open source orchestrators and exposed to the agent vendors adding native supervision.

name: Rise Reforming
tags: Hard Tech; Smart Waste Management; Alternative Fuels; Renewable Energy; ClimateTech
one_liner: We turn waste gases into supply-secure chemicals
long_description:
Geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters frequently expose the vulnerability of the American chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.

We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas.

We're hiring for a senior chemical process engineer. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rise-reforming/jobs/wJ9Q9nv-senior-chemical-process-engineer
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Operators of wastewater plants, farms and landfills with stranded biogas, and buyers of DME and methanol
problem: About 60% of US biogas is wasted in low margin uses or flared while chemical supply chains stay centralized and fossil dependent.
business_model: Modular container-sized units that convert biogas on site into DME and methanol, sold or operated per site; commercial terms not public
product_category: Hard tech, modular biogas to chemicals reforming
founder_names: George Rose; Lucas Zubillaga; Jona van Oord
market_need_then: Supply chain shocks and geopolitical events exposed chemical industry fragility; biogas is flared or underused and DME is used as aerosol propellant and propane additive.
outcome_analysis: Rise Reforming is an active early hard tech startup from three University of Chicago molecular engineers. It has a working pilot container, a conditional DME offtake agreement and a pre-seed, and is raising a larger round for the first plant. The main risks are scale up, capital intensity and well funded modular competitors, none of which has resolved yet.

name: Robby
one_liner: AI agents that grow revenue for home services businesses
long_description:
Robby is an AI growth engine for home services businesses that uncovers revenue opportunities and collects additional data from every technician visit. Our AI combines customer and third party data to generate dozens of new leads every day, and then arms the technicians with talking points to increase close rates, giving GMs a single command center to manage and drive revenue. We have several paying customers that are each uncovering 6 figures in additional revenue opportunities every week. On our first day of launch, we helped close $40k in new business within an hour.

Our team has spent the last few months riding along with dozens of technicians and shadowing every position in the office to best understand the industry. We're also studying for the EPA 608 exam to become certified technicians ourselves.

Vineet and Feroze have both built critical products and infra at prominent startups (Ironclad, Porter, Affinity, Uber, Cloud Health Systems). Joe previously consulted PE firms on software acquisitions and led home services growth projects at Bain. We all met at Harvard Business School, and dropped out to work on Robby full-time.

name: Robocurve
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Robotics; Open Source; AI
one_liner: Evals for robots
long_description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI labs and robot makers that need independent evaluation of models controlling real robots
problem: There is no neutral, reproducible way to measure what frontier AI models can do when controlling physical robots.
business_model: Independent evaluations and benchmarks for labs, plus open source tooling; revenue model not stated
product_category: AI and robotics evaluation, public benefit corporation
competitors_at_founding: Berkeley, Stanford and NVIDIA real robot evaluation platform; AGIBOT World Challenge 2026; RoboBench
market_need_then: Physical AI models were multiplying in 2026 with mostly self reported results, creating demand for neutral measurement.
outcome_analysis: Robocurve raised a $10M seed led by Initialized Capital in September 2026, shortly after its Summer 2026 batch, on the strength of a credible AI safety researcher founder and an open source framework with wide installs. It is early; the risk is monetizing a neutral evaluator and keeping independence from labs that pay.

name: Rodeo Robotics
one_liner: Robots for vehicle maintenance.
long_description:
Rodeo Robotics (YC F26) automates vehicle maintenance so shops can get vehicles back to work at lower cost.

Co-founders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they helped OEMs like Toyota and General Motors deploy autonomy in the real world and saw firsthand how much hands-on work it takes to keep fleets running.

They’re now applying their experience to the $600B US maintenance market. The average vehicle is getting older and needs more maintenance, but shops struggle to recruit new technicians to replace experienced workers as they retire. This leaves shops turning away work and customers waiting longer for service.

Rodeo builds robots that inspect vehicles, diagnose problems, and perform services, starting with routine maintenance like oil and tire changes. Their robots use AI models specialized for multi-step vehicle maintenance tasks and operate autonomously for 96% of execution time on their initial tasks.

No financing or outcome is public. Hardware difficulty and funded tire robot rivals are the main uncertainties.

long_description:
Roma is the to-do list that does itself. Two of our three founders have been through YC before: Jan built Loom (W12, acquired by Dropbox) and Tobi built Senic (S13, acquired by Gira).

Most of the work we do starts and ends with a task. So we're rebuilding something everyone already uses: the to-do list that becomes your everyday assistant, the one place that already knows everything you need done.

name: RonanRx Inc.
one_liner: Full Stack Pharmaceutical Company for Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s
long_description:
RonanRX is a full-stack pharmaceutical company, starting with personalized peptides and GLP-1s.

In our first 10 weeks, we went from having no pharmacy to being licensed in 33 states. Since launch, we’ve grown 50% week over week.

We manufacture the medications ourselves, sell directly to patients, and eliminate the layers of middlemen that make prescription drugs more expensive.

What makes this possible is AI.

Traditional pharmaceutical companies are built to manufacture one drug for millions of people. RonanRX is purpose-built to personalize treatment for each patient: different biology, different response, different dose.

Patients come directly to RonanRX or through doctors using our platform. Every patient completes our medical intake, meets with a licensed doctor through our telehealth platform, and receives a personalized prescription when appropriate. From there, we manufacture the medication ourselves and deliver it directly to the patient.

Labs, wearables, medical history, treatment response, and other health data feed back into the platform so doctors can continuously refine treatment over time.

Before AI, doing this for every patient at scale was impossible.

We didn't invent the demand we are seeing. 80 Million people are on a GLP-1 and millions more are using Peptides. We're building a better way to manufacture, personalize, prescribe, and deliver them.

Our founders have built and exited multiple companies, raised more than $100M, built a $50M U.S. medical manufacturing business, and spent years developing peptide therapeutics at companies including Eli Lilly and AbbVie.

We’re just getting started with peptides and GLP-1s. Next comes hormone therapy and the rest of personalized medicine.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: GLP-1 and peptide treatment is standardized and expensive, with many intermediaries between manufacturer and patient. RonanRx wants to personalize dose and regimen per patient and sell directly.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer telehealth plus pharmacy fulfillment, cash pay subscriptions for compounded medications
product_category: Telehealth and personalized compounded pharmaceuticals
competitors_at_founding: Hims & Hers; Ro; Henry Meds; Fridays and TrimRx
market_need_then: The company says 80 million people are on a GLP-1 and millions use peptides. Third-party roundups in 2026 show heavy consumer demand for cheaper cash-pay GLP-1 access, though pricing and compounded supply were shifting.
outcome_analysis: RonanRx entered YC in Summer 2026 and is too young for an outcome. Its own copy claims licensing in 33 states within 10 weeks and 50 percent weekly growth, and an aggregator lists 541K ARR in September 2026, but none of this is independently verified. The main risks visible in 2026 sources are FDA scrutiny of compounded GLP-1 marketing, shrinking compounded supply and a crowded cash-pay telehealth field.

name: Routant
one_liner: Last mile deployment and connectivity for Agents as a Service
long_description: AI agents won’t stay inside the companies that build them. The most valuable agents will work across company boundaries, inside customers’ private systems. In those environments, intelligence is no longer the barrier to deployment. Trust and access are. Routant is the zero-trust access layer for this new agentic world. Vendors integrate once, while customers retain governance over every deployment, deciding what agents can access and which actions need human review, with a complete audit trail of every action.

name: RouterPlus
one_liner: Marketplace for AI inference: the right model at the best price
long_description:
RouterPlus is a marketplace for AI inference. We find the right AI model for a team's product, then get it served at the team's scale, at the best price.

Most teams that run AI in production pay for a top model on every task, when a cheaper model can do most of the work. The same model can also cost twice as much depending on which provider runs it, and many providers fail at peak traffic.

RouterPlus tests models on a team's own traffic and recommends one. Providers then compete for the workload. We check that the chosen provider can hold the team's real peak, and we keep a second provider ready as a backup. Teams call the model through one API.

Our largest customer runs 3 million agent conversations a day on RouterPlus.
regions: India; South Asia

problem: Most teams pay for a top model by default. RouterPlus finds the right model for a team's workload from its own evals and traffic, then gets it served at scale at the best price.
business_model: Inference marketplace and routing layer, providers compete for the customer's workload, fee schedule not published

market_need_then: Roundups in 2026 list many OpenRouter alternatives and describe provider-agnostic failover and latency-aware routing becoming default expectations, showing real demand for model selection and price control.
outcome_analysis: RouterPlus is a Fall 2026 YC company with no public outcome yet. It claims a large customer at 3 million conversations a day and 25 percent lower P95 latency after switching models, but these are company figures. It competes with OpenRouter, which raised 113M in May 2026, so differentiation through workload-specific evals and provider competition is the open question.

name: RunAnywhere
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Inference research at the frontier. Faster, cheaper frontier models…
long_description:
Inference research at the frontier. We make frontier open models faster and cheaper on Wally.

We're RunAnywhere (YC W26). You can use frontier open models like GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and MiniMax M3 on Wally today. Wally has an OpenAI-compatible API and the wally CLI, with zero data retention by default, and it works with OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and Cline. Tell your agent: set up https://runanywhere.ai/SKILL.md

Our engineers and AI agents build the kernels and the serving stack for each chip. For AWS Trainium, trnRT is our open-source (Apache-2.0) LLM inference engine; Aman Swar and Sanchit Monga's post covers serving GLM-5.3-Flash on one Trainium2 box: https://runanywhere.ai/blog/glm-5-3-flash-trainium2-nki-megakernels

For on-device AI, the open-source RunAnywhere SDKs share a C++ core across Swift, Kotlin, React Native, Flutter, TypeScript and C++.

We publish how we measured each result. Happy to help any YC founder running coding agents, long-context workloads or on-device models.

long_description: Runtime is building a simulation-based robot policy that needs no fine-tuning or teleoperation.

target_customer: Robotics builders and physical AI labs that need robot policies and simulation evaluation
problem: Robot policies usually need per-task fine-tuning and teleoperation data. Runtime.si builds policies that explore in simulation and act in the real world without them, and evaluation infrastructure for physical AI.
business_model: Robot policy and simulation evaluation platform, early access, pricing not published
product_category: Simulation based robot policies and evaluation
founder_names: Chen Peng; Yim Ying; Liam Zhong
competitors_at_founding: Genesis AI; NVIDIA Cosmos; Physical Intelligence
