It faces very well funded simulation and robotics model players, so results on its benchmarks will decide traction.

name: Ryhla
tags: Solar Power; Climate; Energy; Renewable Energy; Infrastructure
one_liner: Faster power grid connection for your projects
long_description: Ryhla develops proprietary models that replicate the distribution power grid and learn what gets a project connected. We work with solar/battery, EV charging and small data center developers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers of solar, battery storage, EV charging and small data center projects of roughly 1 to 50 MW that need distribution grid interconnection approval
problem: Interconnection applications to distribution utilities are often rejected or delayed because developers cannot see feeder capacity. Developers pick sites blind and re-file.
business_model: B2B software and analysis service sold to project developers (pricing not public)
product_category: Grid interconnection modeling software
competitors_at_founding: Piq Energy; Nira Energy; Pearl Street Technologies (Enverus)
market_need_then: Interconnection queues are a widely reported bottleneck for solar, storage and data center projects in 2026, and developers see low approval rates (YC page says 20 to 40 percent typical, company claim).
outcome_analysis: Ryhla joined YC in Fall 2026 and is active with two founders and no disclosed funding. The founders researched grid intelligence at Stanford, which fits the problem, and interconnection delays are a growing pain. No outcome news exists yet, so the story is too early to judge.

name: Rystic
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: Test agents and code changes in high-fidelity simulated environments
long_description:
Staging environments and test sandboxes don't scale for development with AI.

Rystic is building the verification layer for software written by AI. We give every change a deterministic simulated environment, populated with local, stateful simulators of APIs like Slack, Stripe, GitHub, and PostHog. Control everything about your dependencies, from the clock to injected faults, and use our harness for integration tests or agent evals.

With simulation testing, every change is evaluated quickly in its own private world, where you can measure its impact on other systems. We're building the next step forward in software testing, one that scales with your agents instead of holds them back.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams building or testing AI agents and AI written code that integrate with third party APIs
problem: Staging environments and vendor sandboxes are slow, shared and non deterministic, so teams cannot safely test agents and code changes against Slack, Stripe, GitHub and similar services.
business_model: Developer tools subscription for local API simulators and a test harness (pricing not found)
product_category: Developer tools, simulation testing for AI agents
competitors_at_founding: Archal; WireMock Cloud cleanroom; Veris AI
market_need_then: AI agents with write access cause incidents in shared environments; the founders cite an agent flooding CI runners with pull requests (Fondo blog). Funded competitors in agent simulation show investor demand in 2025 and 2026.
outcome_analysis: Rystic is a two person Fall 2026 YC company that launched local API simulators for agent testing. Founders have infrastructure experience at Roblox and Google. Demand is rising with AI written code, but competitors are numerous and no outcome has occurred yet, so the story is too early to call.

name: SE3 Labs
one_liner: Real-World RL Environments for Physical AI
long_description:
We build real-world RL environments for robots. Starting with tasks from industry partners, we test policies on real robots and identify where they fail. We use those failures to decide what data to collect and curate for the next policy update.

Next, we're setting up physical sandboxes at partner sites, so policies can train on the exact tasks and conditions they'll face in deployment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robot foundation model and policy developers, and industry partners with robot tasks, who need real world evaluation and training data
problem: Robot policies are hard to evaluate and improve without real robots, so failures in deployment are found late. SE3 Labs tests policies on real robots and uses failures to decide what data to collect.
business_model: Services and data for robot policy evaluation and reinforcement learning on physical sandboxes (pricing not found)
product_category: Real world RL environments for physical AI
founder_names: Mark Chen; Conan Yu; Paige Xu
competitors_at_founding: Robocurve (YC Summer 2026); RL Environment as a Service; Runtime.si (YC Fall 2026)
market_need_then: Robot foundation model teams in 2026 are raising large rounds for data pipelines and evaluation, and many startups address policy evaluation, showing demand.
outcome_analysis: SE3 Labs is a three person Fall 2026 YC company selling real world RL environments for robots. It has no disclosed funding, and its name collides with a Munich spatial AI company that raised a seed in June 2026. Both naming confusion and well funded evaluation rivals are risks, but there is no outcome yet.

name: STASIS
tags: Hardware; Sports Tech; Consumer Health Services; Health & Wellness
one_liner: The WHOOP for 16 billion eyes
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers and athletes who want continuous eye based health and performance tracking from wearable smart glasses
problem: People track sleep and strain with wrist wearables, but the eyes are an untapped signal. STASIS pitches smart glasses that read eye signals as a WHOOP style tracker.
business_model: Consumer hardware, likely device sales with possible subscription (not confirmed by sources)
product_category: Eye tracking smart glasses for health and wellness
competitors_at_founding: AdHawk Microsystems; Carolina Instruments; Soma Reality
market_need_then: Wearable health tracking is a large category (WHOOP raised 575 million USD in 2026 per press), and eye signals for fatigue and cognition are an active research area.
outcome_analysis: STASIS is a two person Fall 2026 YC hardware company pitching eye based health tracking glasses. Founders have bioengineering and hardware backgrounds, but no funding, product traction or outcome information is public, so no success or failure story can be told yet.

name: Saccade
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Machine Learning; B2B; Healthcare
one_liner: World's Earliest Test for Alzheimer's Biomarkers
long_description:
Alzheimer's testing today is bottlenecked around the onset of symptoms, when the damage is already done. Current treatments, including the FDA-approved drugs released in 2024, don't reverse the disease; they only slow it down. Earlier detection means earlier intervention.

Eye movement changes linked to Alzheimer's surface sooner than any other biomarker, up to 15 years before symptoms appear.

We deliver a 15-minute VR assessment delivered to patients in longevity clinics:
• Tasks: patients perform visual tasks designed by neurologists to trigger a distinct oculomotor response in people with Alzheimer's or on its path
• Hardware: our patent-pending attachment connects to any VR headset on the market and captures these eye movement patterns.
• Analysis: the patterns are compared against our ML model to produce a risk analysis.

Once classified, patients can access new interventions, such as the FDA-approved drugs. They're also referred to longevity practices, neurology practices or both, depending on their stage of decline.

Testing for the earliest biomarkers allows the earliest possible intervention. In some cases, that slows the disease enough that patients outlive the onset of symptoms and never face memory loss in their lifetime.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Longevity clinics, neurology practices and consumers seeking early Alzheimer's risk screening via eye movement testing
problem: Alzheimer's testing happens around symptom onset. Eye movement changes may appear years earlier, and Saccade offers a 15 minute VR assessment with a headset attachment to capture them.
business_model: B2B to clinics for assessments plus a consumer wellness test and at home blood panel (pricing not found)
product_category: VR eye tracking diagnostic and wellness screening
competitors_at_founding: Olleyes VR exam (UC Davis pilot); Max Planck Institute VR pupillometry trial
market_need_then: FDA approved Alzheimer's drugs in 2024 slow progression, which raises demand for earlier detection, per the company description.
outcome_analysis: Saccade is a Fall 2026 YC company with one named founder offering a VR eye movement test. A Fondo article of October 2026 says it is in local clinics with no published validation or accuracy data, and the company calls the product investigational. It is too early for an outcome.

name: Saffron
one_liner: Helping your company find 10x engineers.
long_description:
Saffron allows companies to quickly evaluate how well software engineers use AI to code. 

The way engineers write code has fundamentally changed, but the way companies evaluate them hasn't. Saffron gives teams full visibility into how candidates use AI agents to build, debug, and ship real features on an actual codebase. 

Saffron was founded by Robert Chondro (formerly MIT and Jane Street), Jerry Yao (Stanford and Jane Street), and Kazuma Choji (Harvey Mudd, published in NeurIPS and ICML), and is backed by Y Combinator (P26) and Afore Capital.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering hiring teams that want to measure how candidates use AI coding agents
problem: Engineers now write code with AI agents, but hiring tests still assess unaided coding. Saffron lets candidates build features in a real repository with Claude Code and scores the session.
business_model: B2B SaaS assessment platform with demo led sales (pricing not found)
product_category: HR tech, AI native technical assessments
founder_names: Robert Chondro; Jerry Yao; Kazuma Choji
market_need_then: AI coding agents changed daily engineering work in 2025 and 2026, so employers question unaided coding tests; incumbents responded with AI assisted formats.
outcome_analysis: Saffron is a three person Spring 2026 YC company selling AI native engineering assessments, backed by YC and Afore Capital. The founders have Jane Street and strong CS backgrounds, but CodeSignal, HackerRank and CoderPad shipped similar features first. No outcome exists yet, so the key risk is incumbent copying.

name: Salem Robotics Inc
tags: Hard Tech; Robotics; Energy; Defense; Industrial
one_liner: Deploying robots to replace workers in hazardous spaces
long_description: Our software turns any robot we deploy into an everyday independent worker at your facility. They are able to walk sites, handle instruments, overcome obstacles, collect measurements, and generate auditable compliance records, replacing hours of mandatory manual surveys and inspections. Built by Los Alamos robotics veterans and deterministic-manipulation researchers, we started in nuclear and are already expanding to other hazardous industries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Nuclear facilities and other hazardous industrial sites (oil and gas, chemical, biological, space) that run recurring radiation surveys and inspections
problem: Mandatory manual surveys in hazardous areas expose workers and consume hours. Salem software turns existing or supplied robots into autonomous inspectors that produce auditable compliance records.
business_model: Software for robots plus turnkey robot deployments, contract based (pricing not found)
product_category: Autonomy software for industrial inspection robots
competitors_at_founding: Boston Dynamics Spot; ANYbotics ANYmal; DEEP Robotics
market_need_then: Nuclear sites such as Sellafield already deploy robot dogs for inspection, and decommissioning and survey regulation create recurring manual work. The company reports active contract scoping in nuclear and oil and gas.
outcome_analysis: Salem Robotics is a two person Summer 2026 YC company with founders who deployed robots at Los Alamos, a strong fit for nuclear inspection. Funding amounts are conflicting on aggregators and unconfirmed, and no outcome exists yet. The main risks are slow nuclear sales cycles and robot makers moving into software.

name: Salus
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; API; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: Guardrails to validate your agent's actions before they execute
long_description:
Your agent processed a refund without looking up the order ID, costing you thousands. You only found out three hours later from a support ticket. Evals, output scoring, and observability can reduce the likelihood of mistakes like these occurring - but there's no solution that inspects and prevents an action as it’s about to execute. Salus does that.

We’ve built an API that wraps around your agent and checks its actions at run time, blocking incorrect ones and providing immediate feedback to guide retries.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Teams deploying AI agents that take state changing actions such as refunds or updates
problem: Agents make costly mistakes, such as refunding without checking the order ID, and evals or observability find them only after the fact. Salus checks actions before they execute.
business_model: Usage based API and developer tooling (pricing not found)
product_category: AI agent runtime guardrails
competitors_at_founding: Guardrails AI; Lakera (Check Point); NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails
market_need_then: Companies shipping agents in 2026 report costly wrong actions, and many vendor comparisons list runtime action validation as a gap beyond content screening.
outcome_analysis: Salus is a two person Winter 2026 YC company selling runtime checks for AI agent actions. It is active, with no confirmed funding amount, and faces vendors and security firms already in guardrails. Nothing indicates an outcome yet, so the story is early.

name: Samora AI
one_liner: Multilingual voice agents that outperform humans
long_description:
Samora runs multilingual voice operations for organizations with high-volume calling without requiring engineering teams, call centers, or AI expertise.

Many important tasks still depend on phone calls, including customer support, outreach, follow-ups, screening, and intake. But voice AI often fails in production because real callers interrupt, go off-script, switch languages mid-sentence, and speak in local dialects. Teams also worry about safety and compliance, especially when an agent can accidentally make the wrong promise.

Samora solves this with voice agents that sound local and follow strict rules. Samora agents handle inbound and outbound calls, collect information, and update internal systems like CRMs, ticketing tools, and ATS platforms. When a call becomes sensitive or uncertain, the agent hands off to a human. It can also follow up over WhatsApp, SMS, or email when needed.

With Samora, teams get:
1. Voice agents that work in real conversations, including dialects and code-switching
2. Strict safety controls so agents don’t make unauthorized offers, discounts, or promises
3. Calls that result in completed actions, system updates, and safe human handoff
regions: Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Organizations with high-volume calling (support, collections, outreach, screening, intake), including enterprises, NGOs and government programs in multilingual markets such as India
problem: Voice AI often fails in production because real callers interrupt, go off-script, switch languages mid-sentence and speak in dialects, and teams fear agents making unauthorized promises.
business_model: Managed voice agent service, sold by demo, pricing not published
product_category: Multilingual conversational voice AI agents
founder_names: Kartik Sawhney; Vineeth Kumar; Shakul Raj Sonker
market_need_then: Large call volumes in support and collections, plus demand for local-language voice in India and similar markets. The company reports customers including UNICEF and Signify and over 1M calls handled (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Samora is an active early-stage company from YC Winter 2026 with no reported exit or layoffs. Its edge is multilingual and dialect-aware voice with managed operations and safety rules, aimed at markets such as India, where founders have prior accessibility and AI work. No priced funding round is public, so the stronger test of traction is still ahead.

name: Saudara AI
one_liner: AI Native Sourcing Broker For Overseas Manufacturing
long_description:
Saudara AI is an AI sourcing broker connecting American brands with vetted overseas factories.

US brands import $3T in goods a year and lose billions to ghost suppliers, hidden fees, and blown deadlines. The factories that actually deliver sit behind decades-old relationships outsiders can't break into. We were born into them.

Every deal runs through a real human broker, supercharged by AI that handles sourcing, quoting, QC, logistics and vendor financing. 10x faster, at a fraction of the cost.

Sourcing is the largest broken market in global trade. We're the on-ramp.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US brands (initially apparel and textile) importing from overseas factories, starting with Indonesia
problem: US brands lose money to ghost suppliers, hidden fees and missed deadlines, and the reliable factories sit behind long-standing personal relationships outsiders cannot access.
business_model: Sourcing brokerage (commission per deal, assumed from description; vendor financing also mentioned) with AI-assisted human brokers
product_category: AI-enabled cross-border sourcing broker / global trade marketplace
market_need_then: Company cites about $3T of US goods imports a year and complaints about ghost suppliers and hidden fees; it reports sourcing $900K+ for 40+ brands in about 5 months (company-reported, via a search summary of an aggregator page).
outcome_analysis: Saudara AI is a two-person Spring 2026 company with an aggregator-reported $500K pre-seed and company-claimed early GMV, so there is no outcome to explain yet. Its distinguishing feature is founder-market fit through family ties to Indonesian textile manufacturing, but the sources provide no independent traction or competition evidence.

name: Savant
one_liner: Company brain every AI-native enterprise runs on
long_description: Savant is the company brain every AI-native enterprise runs on. We plug into the tools you already use, capture the written knowledge / undocumented procedures, and serve them to your employees and agents at decision time.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI-native enterprises whose employees and AI agents need undocumented company procedures and context at decision time
problem: Operating knowledge is scattered across tools and people, so employees and AI agents lack the policies, workflows and judgment needed to act correctly.
business_model: Enterprise software sold by demo, pricing not published
product_category: Enterprise knowledge and operational memory layer for agents
market_need_then: Companies deploying AI agents need grounded context, and Glean reporting $300M ARR in May 2026 shows enterprise spend on context.
outcome_analysis: Savant is a very young company from YC Spring 2026 with no reported funding round amount, exit or layoffs. It targets a crowded enterprise context market led by Glean, so the main open questions are differentiation and enterprise sales traction, neither of which is public yet.

name: Sazabi
one_liner: AI-native observability and security platform
long_description: The AI-native observability and security platform for fast-moving engineering teams. Backed by tastemakers from the world's top AI companies: Vercel, Graphite, Daytona, Browserbase, LangChain, Mastra, Replit, and more.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Fast-moving engineering teams, especially those shipping with AI coding tools, who pay for production log monitoring
problem: Traditional observability is dashboard heavy and complex. Sazabi bets that logs alone, tied to code, can power detection, root cause analysis and fixes.
business_model: Usage-based SaaS tiers: Hobby $50, Startup $200, Growth $1,000 per 30-day cycle, custom enterprise
product_category: AI-native observability and security
market_need_then: AI coding tools increase shipped code and incidents, and engineers complain about dashboard complexity and cost; customers report fast root cause times (self-reported case studies).
outcome_analysis: Sazabi raised an $8M seed within months of YC Spring 2026, led by J2 Ventures, Village Global and YC with many developer tool angels, on the thesis that logs plus coding agents can replace dashboard heavy observability. A founder with a decade in infrastructure and an AI coding tailwind helped, while Datadog and funded AI SRE rivals are the main risk. No exit or layoffs reported.

name: Scheduling Wizard
one_liner: Logistics infrastructure to modernize healthcare operations
long_description:
Scheduling Wizard is building the logistics infrastructure to modernize healthcare operations. Hospitals still rely on manual workflows to manage staffing, patient flow, and core operations, contributing to $760B in annual inefficiency.

20 departments across 16 hospitals already outsource their physician scheduling to us, powered by our internal Scheduling Programming Language and AI-driven workflows. We work with Mass General, Johns Hopkins, UT Southwestern, UCSF, and many others.

We are actively onboarding new clients and expanding into patient triaging and provider management systems, working with partner departments at UCSF and other leading institutions. Scheduling Wizard aims to bring healthcare operations into the future by reducing administrative burden and improving clinical care coordination. Our goal is to create the AI-native administrative layer in healthcare operations.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hospital departments, residency (GME) programs and provider groups that outsource physician call, clinic and block scheduling
problem: Residents and attending physicians spend hundreds of hours a year on scheduling, and legacy tools display schedules rather than generate them.
business_model: Service plus software for outsourced physician scheduling, pricing not published
product_category: Healthcare operations and scheduling logistics
founder_names: Samuel Oberly; Zachary Dermody; Abdelrahman Hamimi
market_need_then: Physician scheduling is manual and time consuming; the founders heard this directly from a Johns Hopkins doctor. Company reports 20 to 30+ departments across many hospitals (self-reported, counts vary by source).
outcome_analysis: Scheduling Wizard is an active YC Winter 2026 company with named academic medical customers and a services-first wedge in physician scheduling, expanding to triage and care coordination. No exit or layoffs reported, and funding beyond YC is not public, so traction is only self-reported so far.

name: Scope
one_liner: We help software companies get discovered and used by AI agents
long_description:
Scope is the system companies use to measure and improve how agents discover, interact and use their product.

As more products gets used through AI agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and similar agents, agents are starting to influence which tools get chosen, how they get set up, and whether they keep getting used. Most companies still cannot see that process clearly.

We run real workflows across agents and show teams when the agent picks them versus a competitor, where it breaks, where docs or product surfaces confuse the agent, and what to change to get better results and a better agent experience.

I started Scope after working on interpretability research for closed-source models at Princeton and later as an ML engineer in GEO/AEO. I kept seeing the same pattern: these systems were shaping real product discovery and usage, but companies had very little visibility into what the model was actually doing.

We are starting with products that agents can directly interact with, especially APIs, infra products, CLIs, and MCP servers.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software companies with API, infrastructure, CLI and MCP-server products that want agents to pick and use them
problem: Coding agents increasingly choose and configure developer tools, but vendors cannot see when agents pick a competitor, where they fail, or which docs confuse them.
business_model: B2B software (agent experience platform), pricing not found
product_category: Agent experience analytics / agent-facing GEO
market_need_then: Per the Fondo interview, the founder spoke with about 15 companies and roughly 12 said they would pay for a working product; the earlier GEO product had revenue but a unicorn prospect doubted its budget.
outcome_analysis: Scope is a Spring 2026 YC company with one founder and a pivot from GEO to measuring how coding agents discover and use developer tools. Public evidence is only the YC page and one podcast interview, which claims millions of logged agent runs and interest from about 12 of 15 companies. Funding is unverified and no outcome exists yet; the main risks are a crowded, well-funded GEO field and a generic name.

name: Seeing Systems
one_liner: Modular AI-Commanded Drones for Defence
long_description:
We engineer inexpensive, autonomous strike drones designed to operate in the most contested combat environments on Earth!

By combining true hardware modularity with an agentic control system that lowers cognitive load on operators, we enable faster upgrades, broader adoption, and more than 2x reduction in lifecycle cost.

Our customers and partners include the UK Royal Marine Commandos, several other units in the UK, and 4 other NATO forces, and we are currently shipping prototypes for iterative feedback.

Think of us as Anduril, but with worse weather, and better banter.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: NATO-aligned militaries, starting with UK units, buying low-cost strike, reconnaissance and training drones
problem: Contested battlefields need cheap, modular, jam-resistant drones; existing systems are expensive and hard to adapt.
business_model: Hardware sales of drones plus swarm control software, to defence customers
product_category: Defence drones and swarm software
founder_names: Alexander Le Maitre; Matthew Le Maitre
market_need_then: Fibre-optic and low-cost FPV drones reshaped the Ukraine war and drove NATO demand; the company reports collaboration with UK Royal Marines and prototype shipments to Ukraine (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Seeing Systems is an active YC Winter 2026 drone maker riding strong defence demand from the Ukraine war. Two brothers with hardware and Jane Street software backgrounds report UK and NATO interest, but funding and customers are not independently verified, and the low-cost drone field is crowded. No exit reported.

name: Sentient OS
one_liner: On-device AI that knows your entire life and does your work overnight.
long_description:
Truly personal AI requires running inference on your life, every day. In the cloud, that’s expensive and a privacy nightmare. On your own chip, it’s free and private.

Our custom inference stack, built on a LiteRT-LM fork, runs on Macs with just 8 GB of RAM. Every night, Sentient’s on-device models process your emails, messages, Granola transcripts, files, and more, building a rich personal knowledge base on your Mac.

Your projects, conversations, commitments, and preferences. Context you’d never have the time to type into a chatbot.

That understanding powers three ways to get work done:

Sidekick: click your Mac’s notch and say “finish this for me.” It already has your context and gets to work across your apps and browser with its own cursor, while you keep working.

Proactive intelligence: wake up to work already prepared. The reply you forgot, drafted. The subscription renewing tomorrow, caught. The report you promised, ready for review. Sentient waits for your approval before acting.

Double Tap: two taps, two seconds, and the reply you would have written appears, drafted from your personal context and writing style. Just review and send.

Open source and built with privacy at its core. Over 30 enterprises use Sentient already.

Our alpha reached 4,000+ users in its first week with $0 marketing. Our launch was the top post of the month on r/macapps.

We’ve raised over $1 million with participation from Y Combinator (F26), Afore, Pioneer Fund, and a16z speedrun’s scout fund.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mac users (free consumer app) and enterprises paying for work integrations and support
problem: Personal context is scattered across email, messages, notes and files, so assistants lack the context to draft replies or finish tasks.
business_model: Free open-source app, revenue from enterprise plans for work integrations and support
product_category: On-device personal AI agent for macOS
market_need_then: Rewind's Mac capture shutdown in December 2025 left a gap in local memory tools, and users showed interest on Reddit; company claims 10,000+ users (inconsistent with 4,000+ on the YC page).
outcome_analysis: Sentient OS is a YC Fall 2026 company that launched an open-source on-device Mac assistant in late October 2026, after Rewind's Mac capture ended. It has early user interest and young founders with open-source credibility, but no verified revenue, and large platform players are the main risk. No exit or layoffs reported.

name: Sentrial
one_liner: Datadog for Agent Reliability
long_description:
Sentrial is the monitoring platform for AI products in production. 

When your AI product/agent loops indefinitely, hallucinates, or frustrates users, Sentrial detects it in real-time, diagnoses the root cause, and recommends specific fixes. We provide the monitoring, evaluation, and debugging infrastructure that traditional tools weren't built for, so teams iterate based on production reality, not just offline evals.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams running AI agents in production
problem: Agents loop, hallucinate, misuse tools or frustrate users silently, and teams lack monitoring that finds failures and turns them into tests.
business_model: Usage-based SaaS by trace volume: Developer $10, Startup $450 per month, custom enterprise
product_category: AI agent observability and continual improvement
market_need_then: Agents moving into production create demand for monitoring; the Hacker News launch got modest attention (about 17 points) and the company claims early MRR that I could not verify.
outcome_analysis: Sentrial is an active YC Winter 2026 company of two Berkeley founders building agent monitoring in a very crowded observability field. It has public pricing and an HN launch but no verified revenue or priced round, and no exit or layoffs are reported. Its main challenge is differentiating from LangSmith, Arize and Datadog.

name: Sequence Markets
one_liner: Low-latency execution across crypto, prediction, and tokenized assets
long_description:
Sequence Markets lets traders execute across crypto exchanges, prediction markets, and tokenized-asset venues from one system.

We built proprietary low-latency infrastructure and routing software so users can package one market view into one trade with the speed, access, and transparency execution requires.
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Active traders and trading firms executing across crypto exchanges, prediction markets and tokenized-asset venues
problem: Liquidity is fragmented across venues and a best displayed quote may not fill large orders; traders lack one system to route and execute across them.
business_model: Execution platform via terminal, API, SDK and MCP; pricing not published
product_category: Low-latency multi-venue trade execution infrastructure
market_need_then: Prediction market and perps volume is growing and liquidity is split across venues; the company reports 150+ signups in its first week (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Sequence Markets is an active YC Winter 2026 company building cross-venue execution for crypto, prediction and tokenized assets, led by a CEO with exchange and fund trading experience. Traction is only self-reported and funding beyond YC is not public. No exit or layoffs reported; competition from River Markets and others is the main risk.

name: Servo7
one_liner: Container unloading robots for warehouses
long_description:
We deploy robots in warehouses to automate the most demanding job in logistics: unloading loose-loaded containers.

Our customers include 3PLs (CEVA, Stord), distributors (DHL, PostNL) and many more logistics companies.
regions: Netherlands; Europe
target_customer: Third party logistics providers and distributors that unload loose loaded shipping containers at warehouse dock doors
problem: Unloading loose loaded containers by hand is physically punishing, hard to staff and slow, and fixed automation usually needs the facility redesigned.
business_model: Robot deployments for warehouses, commercial terms not public
product_category: Robotics, container unloading automation
competitors_at_founding: Boston Dynamics Stretch; Pickle Robot; Anyware Robotics
market_need_then: Container and trailer unloading is described by trade press as one of the hardest warehouse jobs, and large buyers such as DHL and UPS signed multi unit robot orders in 2025.
outcome_analysis: Servo7 joined YC in Winter 2026 and is a very early company with no exit and no public failure. The YC page says customers include CEVA, Stord, DHL and PostNL, but no primary announcement confirms this, and a directory notes no named case studies. It enters a market where Boston Dynamics, Pickle and Anyware were already shipping, so its path depends on execution speed and pilot conversion.

name: Shepherd Robotics
one_liner: Robots for high skilled labor powering AI infrastructure
long_description: Shepherd Robotics builds general purpose robots for skilled physical work across AI infrastructure and advanced manufacturing. Our robots are powered by robot foundation models and use modular, flexible hardware designed to adapt to different environments and tasks. We train our systems on a combination of real world and simulation data so they can learn complex manipulation skills and generalize across workflows. We also provide integration into customers’ existing workflows, starting with data center construction and operations, electrical manufacturing and testing, and electronics manufacturing, where traditional automation struggles with variability, dexterity, and changing environments.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data center builders and operators, and electrical and electronics manufacturers needing skilled manual work

name: Shire Intelligence

Shire knows what is happening in the room, so wait-time quotes, staffing, and pricing run on real turn times.

name: Sidekick
tags: SaaS; B2B; Manufacturing; AI Assistant; Industrial
one_liner: AI agent that manages manufacturing operations over text
long_description:
Sidekick is an AI agent that runs custom manufacturing operations over text. Workers text a problem, photo, video, or voice memo and get an answer from the shop's own documents. It reads live machine data and acts on its own: flagging issues before they become downtime, opening and routing work orders, and placing purchase orders. No app, no login.

These shops run on tribal knowledge: a handful of veterans know how every job is set up, and they are retiring. Sidekick learns from every message it handles, so answers outlive the people who gave them, and shops run 15% more jobs with the same crew. Sidekick captures it as a byproduct of the work, in an industry that was never documented.

The no app SMS design lowers adoption friction in shops, while a generic name and many AI assistant rivals make differentiation and enterprise sales the main risks.

Employees open a link and speak in their own language. The agent asks follow-up questions, and teams compare problems across sites and departments. We’ve completed 10,000+ employee interviews and signed one of the world’s top three consulting firms.

We’re building the context layer and operating system for strategy teams: combining employee knowledge with company data to understand operations, improve processes and put decisions into action. The same context will guide AI agents as they take over work, so the company keeps what it learns.

name: Sparkles
one_liner: Make everyone on your team an engineer
long_description:

name: Squid
one_liner: AI agents for power grid planning  🦑
long_description:
We believe the electricity grid is the most important machine on Earth. If we want electrification to move fast, the teams planning and operating networks need software that is as modern as the challenge.

Our thesis is simple. Better decisions come from one unified, trusted network model. When everyone works from the same model, planning becomes consistent, assumptions are visible, and progress stops getting lost in spreadsheets and static reports.

Squid is AI powered grid planning in your browser. We have spent years inside National Grid, Octopus Energy, and AWS, building and learning what breaks. Now we are building what we wished existed.

outcome_analysis: Squid is a Winter 2026 London company founded by an ex-National Grid and Octopus Energy team, with a live pilot at National Grid DSO and certifications claimed, so no outcome yet. The founders have clear domain access, but large vendors such as Schneider and IFS Copperleaf were shipping AI planning tools in 2025, and the amount raised is unknown.

name: Standard Physics
one_liner: Fast Physics Simulations for Rapid Design and Real Time Control
long_description:
Standard Physics (formerly Inviscid AI) builds AI that does real physics. Most AI tools approximate physical behavior and get it wrong in ways engineers can’t see. Ours run actual numerical solvers, so the results are accurate enough to make real engineering decisions on.

We have three products built on one engine.

Reynolds runs computational fluid dynamics for you. An engineer describes the flow in plain language, and Reynolds writes the OpenFOAM case, builds the mesh, runs the solver, and returns the figures, the numbers, and a case they can rerun. It’s open source.

Archimedes searches the design itself. Swarms of agents try thousands of layouts in parallel, simulate each one through Reynolds, keep what the physics rewards, and redraw the search space when the best answer was never in the original plan. We sell it as outcome-based engineering: customers pay for a better design, not for compute.

Inviscid AI (now a product!) points the same engine at a running building. It holds a data center within its thermal limits in real time, computed continuously from live telemetry. Our platform optimizes airflow patterns and ventilation strategies to eliminate dead zones, improve air distribution, and reduce the load on mechanical systems. On the energy side, we minimize HVAC power consumption, reduce cooling costs, and lower overall operational expenses while maintaining optimal thermal comfort and indoor air quality. 

We work with hardware startups and engineering teams on data center cooling, drones, energy systems, piping, and electronics. Reynolds earns engineers’ trust in daily use, and Archimedes and Inviscid AI turn that trust into large contracts.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

business_model: outcome-based engineering for design search, open-source core simulator, and software for data center thermal control
product_category: AI-driven physics simulation (CFD)
market_need_then: Simulation setup is slow and expert-driven, and data center cooling demand was rising. No customer evidence for this company is public.
outcome_analysis: Standard Physics (formerly Inviscid AI) joined YC in Winter 2026 as a two-person team and is Active. - Founders/Recruiting send 100s of AI-generated messages to hire the same talent - this is spam.

This has to stop.

In 1 month, 10k talent / 60 companies / 100 intros.

name: Stilta
one_liner: Agentic AI for intellectual property
long_description:
Stilta builds agentic AI software for intellectual property, starting with patent litigation. Whether challenging or enforcing a patent, leading IP law firms and in-house IP teams use Stilta for source-backed, auditable analysis.

Innovation drives the world's most important breakthroughs, but the tools that protect it haven't kept pace. Patent attorneys do high-stakes work with a process still built on manual document review and disconnected point solutions. Generative AI helps with drafting, but it doesn't deliver the trust and transparency that legal-grade work demands - no sources, no traceability, no audit trail. Stilta takes a different approach. We use agentic AI to run search and analysis at a scale manual methods can't match, with every output source-backed, referenced, and auditable. Until recently, this wasn't technically possible.

We're four engineers from McKinsey/QuantumBlack who built and deployed AI systems at some of the world's largest organizations. With Stilta, we're equipping the people who protect the world's most valuable ideas with tools that match the stakes.

A drop-in module that integrates with existing Ardupilot, INAV and PX4 flight controllers, with demonstrated satellite-independent autonomous flight and GPS handoff.

name: Super Powers Mobility (SPM)
tags: Energy Storage; Unmanned Vehicle; Manufacturing; Electric Vehicles; Electronics
one_liner: The highest performance modular battery packs for mobility/vehicles
long_description:
We started off building the highest performance, 470 volt electric off-road vehicles but we realized our ultra power dense battery packs are useful for mobile and stationary energy storage and power export, for military and consumer use cases. We develop battery packs, power electronics, and traction powertrain systems for vehicles.

For the majority of 2026 we were marketing our electric off-road vehicles, but we pivoted to selling our high performance battery packs and power export capabilities in the month of September. We went from having $769,000 in consumer pre-orders (possibly low conversion rate to sales) to $421,815 in realized revenue in 1 month, with a $792,000 qualified pipeline. 

Our tech is so compelling because the safety and layout of high voltage battery packs has only been mastered by large, well funded OEM companies who have brought it in-house. name: Superlog

long_description:

When something breaks, Superlog groups the errors into a single incident, investigates with full context (logs, traces, recent deploys, past Slack threads), and posts one mergeable PR in Slack. You merge it, ignore it, or open it as a Claude Code session and modify it.

Telemetry is vendor-neutral, so you keep every log, trace, and metric we install, even if you leave.

name: Superserve
one_liner: Virtual machines for long-running agents
long_description:
Superserve gives every AI agent its own computer in the cloud. Each one is an isolated VM that starts in under 50ms, sleeps between turns, and picks up exactly where it left off, for hours, weeks or indefinitely.

Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run one app for many users. Agents flip that. Each agent needs its own isolated machine where it can write and run code, use tools and work on its own for long stretches. Everything it produces has to persist the whole time, the way your laptop keeps your work.

That means agent computers have to be stateful, secure and cheap to run. For agents that talk to customers, they also have to start, sleep and wake almost instantly.

Fast - Machines start in under 50ms, either cold or from a template with your repo and dependencies already loaded. You don't need to keep a pool of servers running and waiting.

Persistent - Paused machines keep their full memory and disk state at zero compute cost. They can resume or fork from that exact state. Pausing and resuming is fast enough that a machine can sleep between inference calls and wake on the next turn. Agents can run Docker, databases, browsers or any other service inside.

Secure - Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You can program the rules for what traffic can come in and go out, and they're enforced at the network boundary where the agent can't reach them. API secrets are handled at the network layer too, so they never enter the machine. Every action is logged for audits.

Teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, and eval or RL training environments use Superserve to give every agent session or rollout its own machine, with no infrastructure to manage.

We run 100K+ machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.

name: Sutrix

Paying research teams at 10+ institutions cut data prep by 80% going from months per study to weeks.

name: Synara

Synara is the AI monitoring station for the cameras that are already installed. It needs no new hardware and watches day and night. It understands far more than intruders: falls, guns, fights. And it owns the response. Synara verifies incidents in seconds, talks intruders down on site or sends police a verified alarm, then coordinates with officers on who’s on site and where people are safe, until the insurance claim is resolved.

Because AI does the watching, monitoring becomes drastically cheaper and more accurate. Synara sells through security integrators under their own brand, so every camera they’ve installed becomes recurring revenue.

name: Taan.ai

long_description:

If the scene is tense for 10 seconds and then turns happy, the music changes at that exact moment. You get back a fully mixed .mp4. Agents and apps call Taan through our API, so any video tool can add scored, synced music with one call.

name: Tarifflo Inc.
one_liner: Supply chain compliance and cost savings
long_description:
Tarifflo is the modern ABI, built for the AI agent era.

Legacy ABI software was built for people keying entries into screens. Tarifflo is built for code and agents. Every part of customs work is an API call: create entries from documents, classify every line to HTS, fill PGA records, apply Chapter 99 duties, transmit to CBP and track status through liquidation.

Your agents can file customs. Connect Claude or any MCP client and it prepares full entries using the same API. You review and approve, and Tarifflo files under your own filer code. Developers get REST and webhooks. Everyone gets one key, one meter and one bill.

Under it all is the same engine: live tariff intelligence covering every HTS code, Chapter 99 program, exclusion and rate change. The duty you file going forward is as right as the duty we audit looking back. 1 in 8 products we audit is overpaying, and if you overpaid on past entries we find it and file for your refund.

product_category: Customs compliance and trade automation API
market_need_then: The 2025 and 2026 tariff changes, Chapter 99 duties and IEEPA refunds created heavy demand for classification and refund recovery. Press in March 2025 framed Tarifflo as helping firms navigate a trade war landscape.
outcome_analysis: Tarifflo started as a Utah State student startup, won a $20K prize in March 2025 and joined YC in Summer 2026. A licensed customs broker as CEO and the tariff turbulence of 2025 and 2026 are tailwinds. It faces funded classification rivals. Outcome is still open as of November 2026.

name: Tasklet
one_liner: Agents that own the work
long_description:
AI chatbots can answer questions, but they can't do your work — they aren't connected to your tools, can't take actions, and stop running when you close the tab. Meanwhile, knowledge workers are still spending most of their day switching between dozens of SaaS apps, manually stitching together workflows that should be automated.

Tasklet is the AI agent that actually does the work. It connects to every tool you use — via thousands of built-in integrations, any HTTP API, or MCP servers — and takes real actions on your behalf: pulling reports, updating CRMs, triaging emails, processing data, and more. When it needs a UI, it generates one on the fly. When it needs to crunch numbers or do bulk operations, it writes and runs code in a cloud sandbox. When it needs to interact with a website that doesn't have an API, it uses a real browser. And because it runs in the cloud 24/7, you can set up triggers to have it take ongoing responsibility for workflows — not just do something once, but handle it going forward.

The product is deliberately simple: a chat interface where you talk to an extremely capable agent. But underneath that simplicity is a cloud-native agent runtime, best-in-class context engineering, a universal connections layer, and multi-model support that keeps us on the frontier as AI improves. 

We think legacy SaaS is being unbundled by agents, and Tasklet is the operating system that ties it all together.

name: Teaflask
one_liner: Make your product AI native by tomorrow.
long_description:

Calling a model is the easy part of shipping an in-product agent. The hard part is everything around it: streaming, crash recovery, scaling, guardrails, interfaces that match the product, and knowledge that stays current as the code changes. Teaflask handles all of it with no backend changes, and gives product teams visibility into how their users actually use the product.

name: TensorTest
one_liner: Evals, RL environments and training data for creative tasks

TensorTest (formerly Ritivel) builds evaluations, reinforcement-learning environments, and expert training data for AI labs developing creative agents, starting with video editing.

We offer labs private evaluations to identify where their models fail, training environments that use our verifier’s scores as rewards, and expert-created training data, including professional editing demonstrations, preference pairs, and grading rubrics. These offerings connect evaluation to training: identify what an agent gets wrong, provide feedback on its attempts, and supply examples of better work.

Our team comes from IIT Bombay and has trained language models and built agentic systems at Microsoft Research.

name: Tilo
tags: Developer Tools; Open Source; Infrastructure; AI
one_liner: The Microsoft of the AI era: the operating system for AI agents.
long_description:
Tilo gives AI agents one shared computer. Today every agent gets its own virtual machine and works by screenshots and clicks, which is slow, expensive and brittle. Agents that work together have to describe what they did to each other in messages.

Tilo is a Linux-based operating system built for agents as users. Every app exports typed actions that agents call over MCP while people use the same actions as buttons, on the same live state. Many agents work in one workspace at once and read each other's work instead of messaging about it. Every change is attributed and can be undone, and irreversible actions need permission. Because state and interface are separate, agents can generate an app's entire UI on demand.

On the same multi-app task with the same model, agents on Tilo were about 29× cheaper and 90× faster than computer use, which failed. A small model on Tilo did it for about 1/10,000 of the frontier model's cost. In our scale test, 50 agents worked in one shared workspace on a single laptop, at about 60 MB of memory per agent. Tilo runs headless, in our cloud, or as a desktop, and you can open any workspace from the browser.

business_model: Open source Linux operating system with a hosted cloud and desktop offering; pricing not stated
product_category: Operating system for AI agents
market_need_then: Computer-use agents were known to be slow and expensive, and MCP had become the common interface, but commentary in 2026 argued no true AI operating system existed yet.
