market_need_then: Interest in agent swarms and AI for science rose through 2026, with frontier lab research and well-funded startups, but paying demand for Topos's specific offer is not shown.
outcome_analysis: Topos is an active Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. Two Harvard math dropouts are attempting research-grade agent swarms against frontier labs doing similar work. No funding beyond YC is public and no press was found.

name: Torus
tags: Construction; Energy; Enterprise Software; AI; Industrial
one_liner: Superintelligence for Infrastructure
long_description:
Torus lets engineering firms and project owners build infrastructure 10x faster to reindustrialize America and the West. 

We're working with multiple Fortune 500 companies to build critical infrastructure including data centers and critical energy installations.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: EPC and AEC engineering firms and project owners producing plant, substation and building engineering packages
problem: Engineering packages (P&IDs, line lists, datasheets, one-line diagrams, calculations) are drafted by hand and kept consistent manually, which slows infrastructure delivery.
business_model: B2B enterprise software for engineering firms, managed cloud or sovereign deployment
product_category: AI agentic engineering software for capital infrastructure projects
market_need_then: ENR 2026 Top 500 reporting says design firm revenue rose 7.4% to $158.7B driven partly by data center work, implying engineering capacity strain. The company cites one unnamed major US EPC measuring 9.7x output per engineer hour, a vendor claim.
outcome_analysis: Torus joined YC Summer 2026 with a team of 8 and an established founder pair, one of whom previously ran a YC S21 company. No outcome exists yet as of November 2026. No shutdown, layoff or acquisition coverage was found. The main risks are name confusion with other Torus firms, incumbents building in house, and unproven customer claims.

name: Totalis
one_liner: derivative layer for prediction markets
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Retail prediction market traders who want parlay style combined bets, and apps building on the exchange
problem: Prediction markets offer single outcome bets, so traders cannot combine several outcomes into one payout without a venue's own parlay feature.
business_model: Exchange and derivative layer earning from combo trading, with market makers pricing combos
product_category: Prediction market derivatives (parlays, structured products)
competitors_at_founding: Kalshi Combos; Polymarket Combos; Crypto.com combo betting
market_need_then: Sports style parlays drove large volume on Kalshi after 2025-09, showing retail demand for multi-leg bets, though Bloomberg reported net customer losses on them.
outcome_analysis: Totalis raised a $500K seed paid in USDC and launched parlay trading in spring 2026, gaining crypto press. No shutdown, hack or regulatory action was found as of November 2026. It faces large venues that already ship combos, plus sector wide legal risk, so its outcome is open.

name: Touchmark
one_liner: Market for future inference capacity
long_description: Buy tokens over a time window from the provider of your choice at a price fixed today - 10-30% off the on-demand price. If your plans change - resell your reserved capacity to another buyer.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Commercial buyers of AI inference tokens and commercial inference providers in the wholesale capacity market
problem: Inference prices are floating and capacity cannot be reserved or resold at a fixed price, so buyers overpay and providers cannot sell forward.
business_model: Marketplace for forward and reserved inference capacity, buyers pay no fees per company site
product_category: AI compute and inference forward market
competitors_at_founding: CME Group with Silicon Data; ICE with Ornn
market_need_then: Reported reserved GPU contract prices rose while spot fell (single secondary source), and a 2026-03 arXiv paper proposes token futures, indicating interest in hedging inference cost.
outcome_analysis: Touchmark is a two person YC Summer 2026 company that launched a forward inference market around 2026-08-14 with Wafer as first provider. It has early institutional backers listed on its site. No failure signals were found. Exchange incumbents entering compute futures and the need for liquidity are the main open risks.

name: TovenAI
one_liner: AI agents for compliance at institutional trading firms
long_description:
TovenAI builds a platform of AI agents that handle manual, data-intensive work for compliance teams at institutional trading firms, with six agents currently live. Our customers range from specialist firms to large global institutions, with our agents supporting multiple compliance workflows at a top-10 institutional brokerage.

With prebuilt connectors to more than 30 systems—including Bloomberg, Cloud9, and NICE Actimize—firms can onboard to our platform and evaluate results using their own data in less than a week.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Compliance teams at institutional trading firms and brokerages
problem: Compliance analysts manually review alerts, communications and trades, most of which are false positives, which is slow and costly.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS, AI agents sold to compliance teams
product_category: AI compliance and surveillance agents (regtech)
market_need_then: Compliance teams drown in false positive alerts; the company claims about 70% are auto cleared, a self reported figure. Fintech press in 2026-09 described the old compliance stack as unsustainable.
outcome_analysis: TovenAI is a two person YC Summer 2026 company with six agents live and a claimed deployment at a top-10 brokerage. No outcome events were found as of November 2026. Regulated buyers mean long sales cycles; early backers are listed but amounts are unknown.

name: Traceforce
one_liner: CrowdStrike for AI Agents
long_description:
AI apps such as ChatGPT and Claude have become part of everyone's daily workflow, but they introduce new security risks that traditional security tools weren't built to handle. Security teams at companies from startups to Fortune 500s, are struggling to keep up.

Traceforce gives a company’s security team visibility of how AI apps are being used across company’s devices, and the ability to detect and prevent security breaches and unsafe actions as early as possible.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Enterprise security teams
problem: AI apps such as ChatGPT and Claude create new security risks that traditional tools do not see; Traceforce gives visibility and prevention on company devices.
business_model: B2B SaaS (endpoint agent)
product_category: AI agent and AI app security
market_need_then: Security teams are struggling with AI app usage (company statement); launch post claims pilots, unverified.
outcome_analysis: Traceforce is a Summer 2026 YC company with two technical founders from Clumio; too early for an outcome. Launch post claims deployment on 3,000+ devices and 40+ pilots, unverified, and no funding was confirmed.

name: Tracer
one_liner: Combining open-source AI models for better answers at lower cost
long_description:
Tracer is an AI research lab building more capable and efficient AI through model coordination. We research adaptive inference, ensembling, and systems in which multiple open-source models work together to produce capabilities beyond any single model.

Our work spans reasoning, code, research, and agentic systems, with the goal of making advanced intelligence more accessible and economical.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and companies running chat, code and agent workloads who want frontier-like quality at lower inference cost
problem: Frontier models are expensive; no single open model matches them, so teams overpay or accept lower quality.
business_model: Usage-based OpenAI-compatible API (Echo), plus research outputs
product_category: Multi-model coordination and adaptive inference
market_need_then: Routing startups saw a funding boom in 2026 and cost pressure on frontier models pushed demand for cheaper open-weight setups.
outcome_analysis: Tracer is a solo founder YC Summer 2026 lab that launched Echo on about 2026-07-23, claiming Claude Fable level results at a third of the cost using open models. Benchmarks are self reported and no failure signals exist as of November 2026. Heavily funded routers and the founder being alone are the key risks.

name: Traverse
one_liner: On a mission to keep the future in human hands.
long_description:
Humans control the future because we are the most intelligent species on Earth. We believe AI will soon change that, and that our control is at risk. As a research lab, we study AI alignment and model psychology to ensure these systems have our best interests at heart. We post-train models for companies on the same principle, so that the models they rely on are their own and act in their interest. 
We are a small team of researchers and engineers, and we’re hiring!
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying post-training data and RL environments, and companies wanting custom post-trained models
problem: Frontier training needs data for ambiguous, taste dependent tasks that is hard to verify; companies also want models that act in their own interest.
business_model: B2B services: post-training and data research for labs and companies
product_category: AI alignment research and post-training data lab
market_need_then: Frontier labs spend heavily on post-training data; sources describe demand for RL environments and expert data in 2026 and Traverse was hiring research roles in 2026-07.
outcome_analysis: Traverse is a Winter 2026 YC lab, small and still hiring in mid 2026. Its positioning shifted between alignment research and a data lab for frontier labs depending on the source. No shutdown or acquisition was found as of November 2026. Funding is undisclosed, so traction is unclear.

name: Travo
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Real estate private equity, developers and brokers who need ownership, pricing, zoning and operating data
problem: Real estate data is fragmented across web sources, emails and calls, and incumbent databases are costly.
business_model: Data platform subscription (pricing not stated)
product_category: Real estate data infrastructure
founder_names: Clarence Chen; Alexander Calafiura; Michael Dalva; Ashwin Sriram
market_need_then: Press describes CoStar as expensive for smaller firms, a gap Travo targets with AI aggregation. The launch post says the team first tried real estate private equity agents and decided the underlying data was the missing piece.
outcome_analysis: Travo is a Winter 2026 YC company that pivoted from private equity workflow agents to a real estate data platform. No shutdown or acquisition was found as of November 2026. Funding is unknown and the field is crowded with incumbents, so its outcome is open.

name: Trellis
one_liner: Agents that run short-term rental operations end-to-end
long_description:
Trellis is building toward a new hospitality platform: one that does not just help guests find homes, but actually operates them with agents. 

Our first wedge is short-term rental property managers, replacing their fragmented stack across guest messages, tasks, cleaners, maintenance, vendors, and owner updates with agents that run operations end-to-end. 

In two months, we’ve grown to $500k ARR across 35 customers and 3000 listings, growing around 15% week over week, with one customer already running day-to-day operations with no human involved.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Vacation rental property management companies with 20 or more units and a property management system
problem: Short-term rental operations run across fragmented tools for guest messages, cleaning, maintenance, vendors and owner updates, needing large human teams.
business_model: B2B SaaS, single plan scaling with property count
product_category: AI agents for short-term rental operations
market_need_then: Hostaway reported over 70% of vacation rental managers use AI tools in some form, while a 2026-06 poll found only 7% had reached autonomous agents, indicating room for end to end agents.
outcome_analysis: Trellis, a Spring 2026 YC company, reports fast growth from founders with short-term rental experience (self reported $500k to $614k ARR within about two months). No shutdown found as of November 2026. The main risk is PMS platforms like Guesty shipping their own agents.

name: Trepo
one_liner: The agentic grocery shopper that knows what you have and need.
long_description:
Trepo is building agents that shop for you, starting with groceries.

To know what your household needs, a shopper has to understand what happens at home. Today, that information is scattered across cupboards, receipts, recipes, and the people living there, leaving one person to remember what’s running low, what needs using, and what’s for dinner.

Our Kitchen Assistant and connected app help households track their food, decide what to cook, and use what they already have. A shared device lives in the kitchen, where groceries are unpacked, meals are prepared, and leftovers are saved. That makes it easy to keep Trepo informed as those things happen, giving our agents the context to understand what your household needs and buy it for you.

We’re starting with food. Our ambition is a home that knows what it has, what it needs, and what to do next.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Households that buy groceries and cook at home, paying for a kitchen device and a subscription
problem: One person in a household has to remember what food is running low, what needs using up and what to cook, because the information is scattered across cupboards, receipts and recipes.
business_model: Consumer hardware preorder ($99 device) plus subscription (Food Club, $9.99 per month after three months)
product_category: Consumer smart kitchen assistant and agentic grocery shopping
competitors_at_founding: Grocery AI (Pocket Labs); Gravitas Kitchen; Uber Eats agentic grocery shopping; Instacart Clementine
market_need_then: Households carry a mental load of tracking food and waste. The company sells a $99 preorder device with the pitch that you do not have to keep it all in your head. No independent demand evidence was found.
outcome_analysis: Trepo is an active Fall 2026 YC company with two founders, a $99 preorder kitchen device and no disclosed funding. No outcome exists yet. The founders have hardware and brand marketing backgrounds, while Instacart and Uber Eats were already shipping agentic grocery tools in 2026.

name: Trident
one_liner: Autonomous offensive security agents. The best defense is offense
long_description:
Trident is the standard for modern day security. its an agentic pentester that chains vulnerabilities together like a real attacker mapping verified attack paths across AWS, Azure, GCP, web apps, and APIs. Run AI attacks and get fixes.

Get started today: tridentsecurity.io
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Startups and engineering teams that need continuous penetration testing of web apps, APIs and cloud accounts
problem: Traditional pentesting is periodic and slow. Teams want verified attack paths across cloud and apps with proof and fixes, continuously.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for continuous agentic pentesting and PR review
product_category: AI offensive security and pentesting
market_need_then: Security teams face periodic pentests that miss fast shipping code. The category drew large 2026 funding rounds, signalling buyer demand. Trident says it found critical issues at startups and three unicorns (company claim).
outcome_analysis: Trident is an active Summer 2026 YC company with a four person team and no disclosed funding. It sells an agentic pentester into a category where XBOW, Horizon3 and RunSybil had already raised large rounds, so execution speed and customer proof will decide its path. No outcome exists yet.

name: Trope
one_liner: AI FDE that deploys custom AI agents into ERPs
long_description: Trope deploys custom AI agents into ERPs for mid-market companies. Every ERP is heavily customized, so useful agents need custom deployment too. Trope’s AI FDE learns each business and ERP, then builds and deploys agents, turning the last mile from services into software.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Mid-market companies running heavily customized ERPs, plus ERP vendors, resellers, systems integrators, advisory firms and private equity firms
problem: Every ERP is heavily customized, so generic AI agents do not fit and each deployment needs custom engineering. Trope tries to turn that last mile from services into software.
business_model: Software plus delivery for ERP agent deployment; the YC launch page describes fixed-fee implementation delivery
product_category: AI agents for ERP implementation and customization
market_need_then: Trade press in 2026 describes ERP implementation as slow and consulting-heavy, with change requests becoming consulting engagements, and vendors racing to add execution-layer AI.
outcome_analysis: Trope is a Summer 2026 company with two engineer founders and no outcome yet. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff reporting was found. The thesis rests on ERP customization being a services bottleneck, while ERP vendors are acquiring agent startups, so the outcome is still open.

name: TrueMile
tags: AIOps; Machine Learning; Logistics; Data Science
one_liner: The AI-native trucking company
long_description:
TrueMile is building an AI-native trucking company. We run our own fleet, using agents to find freight, plan loads, and coordinate drivers and brokers.

Our goal is to reduce empty miles, improve truck utilization, and lower the cost of moving goods. Operating the fleet ourselves lets us connect each decision to its outcome on the road and improve how we work.

We’re starting with human drivers. As autonomous trucks become available on our routes, we intend to put them to work within an established freight network.

Founder Harpreet Dhaliwal started running his family’s trucking business at 19 and has generated more than $7M in trucking revenue. The tools he built for that operation became TrueMile.

For recurring truckload freight and partnerships: harpreet@truemile.ai
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Shippers with recurring truckload freight, served by TrueMile's own fleet
problem: Trucks run empty miles and underused because dispatch, load planning and broker coordination are manual and fragmented.
business_model: Asset based trucking carrier using AI dispatch; revenue from freight hauled
product_category: AI-native trucking carrier and dispatch software
founder_names: Harpreet Dhaliwal; Daniyar Abykhanov; Mouha Mansour
market_need_then: Empty miles and thin margins are persistent trucking pain. TrueMile claims AI-selected loads earned 17% more per mile than market for dry vans over four months (company claim via Fondo).
outcome_analysis: TrueMile is an active Fall 2026 YC company that tests AI dispatch on its own trucks. It has a strong founder market fit story but no disclosed funding and no outcome yet. Funded dispatch startups like Datatruck were already selling AI tools to carriers in 2026.

name: TryNearby
tags: Restaurant Tech; Marketing; Creator Economy; SMB
one_liner: Local creators for local businesses
long_description: TryNearby connects local businesses with creators who live nearby. Restaurants subscribe monthly and automatically get booked visits from local creators who film, edit, and post a review to the local algorithm. This creates a steady stream of content that compounds into discovery on TikTok, Instagram, and increasingly AI search. Over 100 restaurants and thousands of creators are on the platform across Southern California, with AI agents handling matching, booking, and every creator conversation.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Local restaurants paying a monthly subscription (about $399) for creator visits and posts
problem: Independent restaurants need steady local discovery on TikTok, Instagram and AI search but cannot manage creator outreach, booking and content themselves.
business_model: SMB subscription with creators booked by AI agents
product_category: Local creator marketing marketplace for restaurants
founder_names: Yousef Abdelfattah; Obaida Albaroudi; Ahmad Ibrahim
competitors_at_founding: Storytime Marketplace; Bestie Bite; Peppr Grow; TikTok Must Eat
market_need_then: Restaurants shift marketing to short form video and AI search. TryNearby claims 120+ paying restaurants, 2,500+ videos, 35M views and 90% monthly retention (company claims on YC launch post).
outcome_analysis: TryNearby is an active Summer 2026 YC company with a five person team and a founder with creator economy experience from FaZe Clan. It claims fast subscription growth and high retention in Southern California. No funding is verified and no outcome exists yet.

name: Tsenta
tags: Marketplace; Consumer; Recruiting; HR Tech; AI
one_liner: AI career agent that finds matching jobs & applies on your behalf
long_description:
Tsenta is an AI career agent that matches you with jobs, applies automatically, and gets you the best offers on the market.

We grew to ~$3M Annualized in three months. 

We built it after manually applying to over 3,000 jobs ourselves, so that candidates would always have someone on their side.

Today, more than 90,000+ job seekers trust Tsenta to automate their job search.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Job seekers, especially students and early career, paying a monthly plan for automated applications
problem: Applying to jobs means retyping the same resume data into dozens of forms. Candidates want matching, tailored applications and tracking done for them.
business_model: Consumer subscription by application volume ($19, $39, $99 per 30 days; first 25 free)
product_category: AI job application agent
market_need_then: Job seekers face high application volume. The founders applied to over 3,000 jobs by hand. Company claims 90,000+ users and about $3M annualized in three months, which conflicts with the launch post figure of 45,000+ users.
outcome_analysis: Tsenta is an active Summer 2026 YC company founded by two Rose-Hulman students who report quick consumer growth. The auto apply market was already crowded and easy to copy, so durability depends on interview outcomes and retention. No outcome exists yet.

name: Turnstone
one_liner: The best model-agnostic Grokbot alternative
long_description:
Turnstone is the best model-agnostic Grokbot alternative. Run persistent Agents on your Mac with the AI subscriptions or API keys you already have

On Turnstone, you can connect multiple AI subscriptions / API keys in one place, and build a team of agents just like you would on Grokbot. 

When a subscription runs out, your Agent can automatically move to another connected subscription with available capacity. You can switch between accounts and model providers within an agent, and its conversation and context persists.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Knowledge workers and prosumers with existing AI subscriptions who want persistent agents on a Mac
problem: Persistent AI agents get stuck when a subscription runs out and are tied to one provider. Users want one place to run agents across their subscriptions and keys.
business_model: Free Mac app with a planned hosted Turnstone Cloud at $49 per month
product_category: Local first AI agent desktop app
market_need_then: Demand for persistent personal agents grew in early 2026 around open source tools like OpenClaw, and users juggle multiple AI subscriptions. No independent traction data found.
outcome_analysis: Turnstone is an active Winter 2026 YC company with two Berkeley founders and a free Mac app that runs agents across existing AI subscriptions. Backers named on its site have no amounts. Model labs ship competing agent products, so no outcome can be called yet.

name: Twolabs
one_liner: RL environments for underexplored domains.
long_description:
We build verifiable reinforcement-learning environments, evaluations, and proprietary training datasets to improve frontier AI models and robot policies.

We focus on complex, underexplored domains where high-quality training data is scarce and existing models fall short.

Our long-term goal is to develop self-improving training infrastructure that can autonomously generate increasingly challenging tasks, evaluate performance, and continuously advance model capabilities toward recursive self-improvement.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Frontier AI labs and robotics teams buying RL environments, evaluations and training data; earlier launch targeted nursing homes with caregiving robots
problem: High quality verifiable training environments and data are scarce in complex domains where models and robot policies fall short.
business_model: Sales of RL environments, evals and datasets to AI labs (launch post also pitched caregiving robots)
product_category: RL environments and robot training data
market_need_then: AI labs demanded more RL environments from 2025, with TechCrunch reporting heavy lab interest in September 2025. A source estimates multi hundred million spend by labs; not independently verified.
outcome_analysis: Twolabs is an active Spring 2026 YC company. The YC launch post describes caregiving robots while the current site sells RL environments, which signals a shift in positioning. No verified funding exists and the environment market was crowded with funded startups.

name: UXDuck
one_liner: Build better drones. Run better missions.
long_description:
Starting with a modern interface for drones that users can build on and adapt. 

Works with planes, copters, rovers, boats and submarines.

Try it in 5 seconds with simulated drones - https://uxduck.com/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Drone developers and operators building on ArduPilot and custom firmware
problem: Drone ground control tools are dated and hard to extend. Teams want a modern interface to simulate, tune, plan and fly many vehicle types.
business_model: Open core software, monetization not stated
product_category: Drone ground control station and simulator
market_need_then: Defense and commercial drone volume rose, and the founder's prior startup scaled to over 1,000 drones. The company claims 500 hours of simulated flight; no independent demand data found.
outcome_analysis: UXDuck is an active Fall 2026 YC company run by a solo founder with defense drone experience at Helsing and a stealth startup. It has an open source core and no disclosed funding. No outcome exists yet and adjacent drone software companies raised in 2026.

name: Ultrasonium
one_liner: Metal manufacturing, faster, cheaper, and more versatile.
long_description:
The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, and robots, are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous.

Ultrasonium has invented a new manufacturing method to make these critical parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. 

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can't be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has built and innovated some of the most complex engineering systems known to man: quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and novel aerospace alloy processing methods.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Aerospace, defense, energy and compute hardware makers that need complex metal parts; early NSF grant text also names small machine shops, research institutions and dental or medical device makers.
problem: Complex metal geometries cannot be machined or cast, and the advanced alternatives are slow, expensive and hazardous. Ultrasonium claims a new method that is 15x faster and 75% cheaper.
business_model: Manufacturing of finished metal parts (hardware, possibly machines); exact model not stated
product_category: Metal additive manufacturing using acoustic molding and a physical AI control layer
founder_names: Jack Qiu; Hunter Brown; Chris Carter; Alexander Urbanski
market_need_then: Domestic manufacturing capacity for aerospace, energy and compute is described by the company as a national priority; complex metal parts are hard to cast or machine.
outcome_analysis: Ultrasonium is an active Summer 2026 company with an NSF SBIR Phase I grant and a team with national lab and metal printing backgrounds. It is too early for an outcome; the key risk is whether the acoustic process scales beyond feasibility into production parts.

name: Unifold
one_liner: Multi-chain deposit and payment infrastructure
long_description:
Launch crypto deposits in minutes. 

Unifold is a developer-first API + SDK that makes it easy for any app to accept on-chain deposits – across any chain and token – with less than 10 lines of code. We handle the full deposit flow so teams can ship faster and give users a smooth experience that actually works.

If you’re building a consumer-facing on-chain product and want best-in-class deposits (or want to support more chains fast), we’d love to work with you.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumer facing on-chain apps such as prediction markets, perpetual exchanges, DeFi protocols and fintechs that need to accept crypto deposits.
problem: Accepting deposits across many chains and tokens is complex for app teams, involving routing, gas and compliance. Unifold offers an API and SDK that handles the full deposit flow.
business_model: Developer API and SDK, likely usage based; pricing not found
product_category: Crypto deposit and payment infrastructure
founder_names: Timothy Chung; Hau Chu; Quang Huynh
market_need_then: Growth of prediction markets and consumer on-chain apps in 2026 created demand for simple multi chain deposits; the team points to live deposits during Super Bowl LX (secondary source).
outcome_analysis: Unifold is an active Winter 2026 company with founders who previously built and sold Streambird to MoonPay. It has a Robinhood Ventures investment announced August 2026 and early prediction market traction, though no outcome can be judged yet; routing competitors are the main risk.

name: Unisson
one_liner: AI agents that automate B2B software implementation
long_description:
Unisson is building trusted AI subject-matter experts for teams that are responsible for customer deployments (technical customer success, implementation, sales engineering). Within 20 minutes, our agents learn to use any product and can be used by teams in Slack, text, or email. Our agents gather requirements and context from existing tools enabling them to handle complex tasks like customer health audits, onboarding, product administration, and custom integrations. 

With Unisson, customer-facing teams have 24/7 access to an AI SME, allowing them to scale and save thousands of hours.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B software companies' technical customer success, implementation and sales engineering teams.
problem: Customer deployments need subject matter experts and handoffs that slow onboarding. Unisson agents learn a product quickly and complete onboarding, audits and integrations tasks.
business_model: B2B SaaS with usage based custom pricing per a third party review
product_category: AI agents for software implementation and customer success
market_need_then: Implementation and onboarding delays are a known pain for B2B software; many onboarding tools were being marketed as AI native in 2026.
outcome_analysis: Unisson is an active two person Winter 2026 company with founders from Ambient.ai and Chef Robotics. No funding beyond aggregator figures or customer traction was verified, so no outcome can be assessed; crowded onboarding tooling is the main risk.

name: Uno Wallet
one_liner: The AI mobile wallet that replaces Apple Pay
long_description:
We are changing the way that people pay...
Founded by:
Saket Joshi: www.linkedin.com/in/saket-dattatray-joshi/
Mordi Shadpour: www.linkedin.com/in/mordi-shadpour/
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: iPhone users with multiple rewards credit cards who pay by tap.
problem: Users do not know which card earns the most rewards at each purchase. Uno is a wallet that picks the card automatically at tap to pay.
business_model: Consumer app; monetization not found (rewards or interchange likely but not sourced)
product_category: Consumer AI mobile wallet
market_need_then: Rewards optimization apps proliferated in 2026, indicating demand among points enthusiasts.
outcome_analysis: Uno Wallet is a two person Spring 2026 company with an early access iPhone wallet and no verified funding or traction. Heavy platform dependence on Apple and existing card picking apps make the path uncertain, but no outcome has occurred.

name: Userlens
tags: Productivity; Enterprise Software; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Let agents talk to your customers
long_description:
Companies today are growing faster than ever with smaller teams. The best AI-native companies don’t just need more users - they need more of their users becoming power users. Userlens makes it possible for lean teams to drive product adoption proactively, at scale.

Userlens is building the AI product adoption expert. Our goal is to help every user at every company get more value from the product they already use.

Most teams still rely on onboarding flows, lifecycle emails, support docs, and reactive CSM outreach. Userlens breaks that ceiling. Lumi watches how users actually use your product, spots when they’re ready for the next feature, workflow, or habit, and nudges them at exactly the right moment.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: B2B SaaS product led growth and customer success teams.
problem: Lean teams struggle to turn users into power users and spot churn. Userlens's agent Lumi watches usage and nudges users toward features at the right moment.
business_model: B2B SaaS; free for 3 months for YC companies, pricing otherwise not found
product_category: AI product adoption and customer success agent
market_need_then: Smaller teams seek automated adoption and churn prevention; customer logos such as Quartr and Smartly are shown on the site (self reported).
outcome_analysis: Userlens is an active Spring 2026 company led by the Wudpecker founders, who report self stated customers such as Quartr and Smartly. Funding beyond the earlier Wudpecker pre-seed is not verified, and incumbents with AI features are the main threat. No outcome yet.

name: VOYGR
one_liner: The real-world intelligence and action layer
long_description:
VOYGR is a better maps API every agent and AI app will need. Google says '4.2 stars, open till 10 – VOYGR knows the chef left, wait times doubled, and locals moved on. Our intelligent local search combines accurate place data with fresh web context – news, articles, and events. We expand beyond 10-15 map attributes into infinite, queryable place profiles, enabling agents to reason and act in the real world.

Maps are no longer browsed – LLMs/agents use them to reason and act. 20M+ apps/websites, up to 40% of search queries, and 20% of LLM prompts need local context. 
10-15 attributes per place are not enough for AI. Places change constantly - restaurants close, hours change, businesses move. LLMs struggle with semantic queries “Specialty coffee shops in SF with Wi-Fi, popular with YC founders”. Agents cannot reliably “parse half the internet” - they need real-world ontology

We’re experienced builders in maps, search, and ML to solve this. Vlad knows this space inside and out – he worked on the Google Maps APIs GTM, plus firsthand customer experience from building in ridesharing and travel. Yarik has spent over a decade leading ML/search teams at Apple, Google, and Meta. 

Google Places alone is a $XXB/Yr monopoly. Agents turn it into a transactional layer opportunity for local commerce and ads.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: AI app and agent developers, mapping, retail, real estate, ad and KYB companies needing fresh place data.
problem: Maps expose 10 to 15 attributes per place and go stale. VOYGR builds richer, continuously validated place profiles and a PlaceCall API so agents can phone businesses.
business_model: Usage based data and API (validation, enrichment, PlaceCall); first 250 calls free
product_category: Place intelligence API for AI agents
competitors_at_founding: Google Places API; Foursquare Places API; Brave Place Search API
market_need_then: Agents increasingly use maps data and need fresher context; the company cites 20M plus apps needing local context (self reported).
outcome_analysis: VOYGR is an active Winter 2026 company whose CEO led Google Maps API go to market and whose CTO led search and ML teams. It has Overture Maps and RepRally as early users per aggregators; no verified funding or outcome yet, and Google plus open data providers are the main competitive pressure.

name: ValCtrl
one_liner: ValCtrl is building the only intelligent prediction market
long_description: ValCtrl is building the intelligent prediction market: users type any public, resolvable belief about the future, ValCtrl structures it, prices it, and lets them trade it. Today’s prediction markets only support pre-listed questions, leaving user beliefs fragmented across venues, contract wording, rules, and proxy markets. ValCtrl’s world model maps typed beliefs to relevant market signals, evaluates basis risk, prices the claim, and moves toward model-priced liquidity where ValCtrl can take the other side with risk and compliance controls. We are starting from hard belief-to-market queries and building toward a market where anything that can be resolved can be priced.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Forecasters, investors, operators and founders who want to trade beliefs about the future on prediction markets.
problem: Prediction markets only list pre-written questions. ValCtrl lets users type any resolvable belief, then structures, prices and lets them trade it.
business_model: Trading venue and market maker taking the other side of trades with risk controls; revenue not stated
product_category: AI prediction market
market_need_then: Prediction market volume and funding surged in 2026 (Kalshi $1B round, a $35M fund backed by Kalshi and Polymarket CEOs per press).
outcome_analysis: ValCtrl is an active two person Spring 2026 company with no verified funding, founder backgrounds or launch traction. It enters a fast growing but competitive prediction market field where regulation and resolution wording are key risks; no outcome yet.

name: Valence
one_liner: Unified prediction markets trading platform
long_description: Valence is a unified trading platform for prediction markets. We provide infrastructure to aggregate and execute contracts across Kalshi, Polymarket, and other platforms, surface arbitrage and mispricing opportunities in real time, and give systematic traders the API and backtesting tools they need to build and execute data-driven strategies on anything.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

name: Valgo
one_liner: Insurance risk layer for autonomy
long_description:
Insurers struggle to price autonomous systems because the historical data simply doesn't exist. Your car insurance draws from over 30 billion claims records, but autonomous trucks and robots have nearly zero. Valgo is the risk quantification platform that closes that gap. We are building probabilistic models of routes, tasks, and environments from the bottom up. We output a simulated loss estimate that insurers need to price coverage. Valgo is the foundational layer that gives insurance providers confidence to properly price autonomy risk.

Our team combines expertise in risk estimation for autonomy with deep experience in the insurance industry. Sydney and Robert are Stanford PhDs with leading expertise in safety of physical AI systems. Sydney wrote the textbook on validating safety-critical systems and teaches the course at Stanford. Robert spent 7 years at MIT Lincoln Laboratory on the core team that designed and validated an FAA-certified aircraft collision avoidance system, now a worldwide standard. Jon is a Sloan Fellow from the Stanford GSB and an actuary who spent over 12 years in insurance leadership and led over $5 billion in M&A as head of corporate development for one of the largest insurers in Asia-Pacific.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Insurers, reinsurers and brokers pricing coverage for autonomous trucks, robots and other physical AI, plus the autonomy companies seeking cover.
problem: Autonomous systems have almost no claims history, so insurers cannot price them. Valgo builds probabilistic simulations of routes, tasks and environments that output loss estimates.
business_model: B2B software and risk models sold to insurers; pricing not found
product_category: Risk quantification for autonomy insurance
founder_names: Robert Moss; Sydney Katz; Jon Qian
market_need_then: Insurers lack claims data for autonomy, and an S&P Global article from February 2026 describes insurers retreating from AI risk.
outcome_analysis: Valgo is an active Winter 2026 company whose founders combine Stanford autonomy safety research and insurance M&A experience, backed by Floodgate, Menlo Ventures (Anthology Fund) and Y Combinator per its own site. Amounts and customers are undisclosed, so no outcome can be judged.

name: Vector Legal
one_liner: A premier AI-native law firm & legal operating system for Startups.
long_description:
A modern solution for Startup legal.

Vector combines premier lawyers/paralegals (averaging 13+ years of experience) + custom-built AI, so our clients get world class startup legal service at a fraction of Big Law rates. See our client testimonials - https://www.vectorlegal.com/testimonials.

Services: fundraise & priced rounds | customer contracts and commercial contracts | international flips | complex formations | grow your team | agentic data rooms | e-signatures | cap table management | legal health checks | mergers & acquisitions | co-founder separations | dissolutions.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Venture-backed startups from pre-seed through Series B that need corporate, fundraising and commercial legal work
problem: Startups overpay Big Law for routine legal work or get slow, inconsistent help from cheap providers. Vector pairs experienced lawyers with AI first drafts to cut fees.
business_model: Hybrid law firm (hourly at about half Big Law rates, outcome-based pricing, fractional general counsel retainers) plus the VectorOS software platform
product_category: AI-native law firm and legal operating system
market_need_then: Startups spend heavily on legal fees and founders complain about Big Law cost. Generative AI made first-pass drafting cheap in 2025 and 2026, and YC backed multiple AI-native law firms in the Winter 2026 batch.
outcome_analysis: Vector is a Winter 2026 company that raised a $5.19M seed in July 2026 led by Base10, soon after demo day. Founder market fit is clear, with a lawyer from Fenwick and YC Legal paired with an Ironclad AI engineer. The main risks are crowding by other AI-native law firms and the law firm model's operating leverage, which commentary in 2026 compared to Atrium LTS. No failure has been reported.

name: Veeza AI
one_liner: AI tourist visa agent for people with weak passports.
long_description: Billions of people need tourist visas to travel the world. We use AI agents to prepare applications, verify documents, secure appointments, and handle the visa process end to end.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Travelers holding passports that require tourist visas, mainly Egyptian and Global South passport holders, paying per application
problem: Tourist visa applications involve heavy paperwork, document checks and scarce appointment slots for holders of weak passports.
business_model: Per-application service fees (itemized) with AI preparation, human expert review and optional appointment booking packages; also seeking distribution partners such as travel agencies
product_category: AI visa application agent
competitors_at_founding: Atlys; iVisa and HelloGov AI; VisaHQ
market_need_then: Large numbers of travelers from weak-passport countries need tourist visas, with documented friction in paperwork and appointments. Founder cites personal experience traveling on two passports.
outcome_analysis: Veeza AI is a Fall 2026 company that launched publicly on 2026-10-19 and was seeking distribution partners a day later. No outcome data exists yet. Its main challenge is that funded incumbents such as Atlys already sell AI-assisted visa applications, so its edge rests on founder insight into weak-passport travelers and local distribution in Egypt.

name: Vela
one_liner: AI Recruiting Coordinator for Executive Search
long_description:
Scheduling one interview panel takes a dozen emails. Then someone moves a call and you start over. 

Vela is an AI Scheduling Coordinator that handles it end to end. Just CC Vela on the thread like you would a person. It reaches out, finds times that work for everyone, chases the people who don't reply, reschedules when things change, and confirms. Over email, SMS, and WhatsApp, at any hour your candidate happens to respond.

No dashboard. No new workflow. Your team works the way it already works, without the scheduling.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Executive search and recruiting firms and enterprise recruiters that coordinate interview panels
problem: Scheduling one interview panel takes many emails and reschedules. Vela is CC'd on the thread and handles outreach, follow-ups, rescheduling and confirmation over email, SMS and WhatsApp.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for recruiting scheduling coordination (pricing not found)
product_category: AI recruiting scheduling agent
founder_names: Gobhanu Sasankar Korisepati; Saatvik Suryajit Korisepati
market_need_then: GoodTime reported talent teams spend about 38% of their time on coordination (company-reported). Executive search coordination is multi-party and manual.
outcome_analysis: Vela is a Winter 2026 company still operating in late 2026 with active job postings and a reported team of 15. Aggregators report a roughly $500K seed but no verified round exists in primary sources. It faces fast copying by funded incumbents like GoodTime and Joveo, so its niche in executive search is the main differentiator. No outcome yet.

name: Veltha
one_liner: AI native TPA starting with workers comp
long_description:
Veltha is the AI native TPA starting with workers comp. We handle claim for insurance providers end to end.

Learn more at https://veltha.ai
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Insurance carriers and third party administrators handling regulated claims, starting with workers compensation and crop insurance
problem: Adjusters spend hours per claim gathering records, analyzing causation and checking statutes. Veltha claims to compress about six hours of work into about ten minutes.
business_model: AI-native TPA and claims decisioning for insurers, per-claim services (pricing not found); the company website separately describes per-document pricing for a mortgage back office offering
product_category: AI claims adjudication and TPA
market_need_then: Workers compensation claims are manual and rule bound; trade coverage in 2026 argued TPAs face pressure from carriers automating simple claims or buying AI-native capability.
outcome_analysis: Veltha is a 2026 YC company with a two-person ex-Palantir team and early trade coverage in September 2026. No verified funding or outcome is public. Its website at the time of research described a mortgage back office offering rather than workers compensation claims, which suggests a possible repositioning that sources do not explain. It faces a heavily funded AI-native TPA competitor launched in June 2026.

name: Velum Labs
one_liner: The OS for data quality across any stack
long_description:
Velum is the operating system for data quality. Velum automatically monitors and enforces data quality across a company's data stack, so bad data never reaches dashboards. We turn data quality from a manual task into infrastructure that runs itself.

Data trust you can prove. From the pipeline to the boardroom.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Data teams at companies (reported regulated fintechs) that need automated data quality monitoring; the current website instead targets developers using coding agents
problem: Bad data reaches dashboards because quality checks are manual. Velum positioned itself as an operating system that monitors and enforces data quality across the stack.
business_model: B2B software (pricing not found); website now describes RouteKit, a local tool that routes coding tasks to the best model
product_category: Data quality, later AI model routing for coding
market_need_then: Data quality monitoring is a mature category with several funded vendors, indicating real spend; AI use raised the cost of bad data.
outcome_analysis: Velum Labs is a Winter 2026 two person team that has changed positioning at least twice, from a privacy firewall to data quality and then to a coding model router on its current site. No verified round is public and no outcome yet. The data quality category already had funded rivals, which may explain the repositioning, but no source states the reason.

name: Ventura
one_liner: AI Workforce for Distributors and Manufacturers
long_description: Ventura builds the AI workforce for distributors and manufacturers, starting with quoting and order entry. It plugs into your existing ERP, follows your SOPs, and learns your team's tribal knowledge - getting smarter with every completed task.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Industrial distributors and manufacturers whose sales and order desks handle quoting and order entry in an ERP
problem: Reps spend time re-keying quotes and orders from emails, PDFs and calls into ERP systems. Ventura drafts quotes and orders for human review and submits them to the ERP.
business_model: B2B SaaS for AI quote-to-cash workflows (pricing not found)
product_category: AI agents for distribution quoting and order entry
market_need_then: Distributors rely on manual re-keying into ERPs; trade press in 2026 described AI moving into the distributor order desk. Founder Collins reportedly embedded with a $2bn distributor at Harvard to build AI sales automation.
outcome_analysis: Ventura is a Winter 2026 company with a two person team that pairs a distribution-industry founder with an ML engineer. No verified funding, traction or outcome is public. The market drew several competitors in 2026, so execution speed and ERP integrations will decide the result. No outcome yet.

name: Verdant
one_liner: AI Agents to Make Local Gov Efficient
long_description:
Verdant sells AI agents to local government to make them more efficient. We're starting with permitting, the highest-volume workflow in local government that requires judgment. 

Many startups fail to sell to government, but not us - we've processed 200+ applications and gone from 0 to 4 paid deployments across 4 states with an average close time of 4 weeks.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Local governments (cities and counties) that run permitting and planning, buying modules per agency
problem: Permitting is the highest volume, judgment-heavy workflow in local government and agencies use one-size-fits-all software. Verdant provides intake, plan review and markup, hearings and ordinance research configured to each agency.
business_model: B2B software and AI agents sold to local government by module (pricing not found)
product_category: GovTech permitting and planning software
market_need_then: Cities were adopting AI to speed housing permitting in 2026 and HUD offered grants for automated permitting. Founders report interviewing 200+ local government staff who named permitting as painful.
outcome_analysis: Verdant is a Summer 2026 company whose YC page reports 200+ processed applications and four paid deployments in four states with a four week average close time (company-reported). The founders have government backgrounds, which helps with a hard buyer. No verified funding is public and no outcome yet. Risks include funded AI permitting competitors and slow public sector procurement.

name: Verdex
one_liner: AI Verification for Insurance
long_description: Verdex is an AI insurance adjuster. We use data streams like satellite imagery to verify claims, allowing insurers to process it immediately and save billions of dollars. We are currently helping insure over 11% of all American farmland.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Crop insurers and insurance carriers that settle agricultural claims, starting with US crop insurance
problem: Verifying crop claims normally needs field visits. Verdex uses satellite imagery and other data streams so insurers can verify and settle claims from the desk.
business_model: B2B software for insurers (pricing not found)
product_category: AI claims verification using satellite imagery
competitors_at_founding: EarthDaily; Descartes Labs and Planet Labs; ESA EO-INSURE
market_need_then: Crop insurance claims depend on field visits and manual adjusting; insurers and claims vendors in 2026 were adopting satellite and drone based loss verification.
outcome_analysis: Verdex is a Winter 2026 two person team of Dartmouth graduates claiming to help insure over 11% of US farmland, a company-sourced figure that is unverified. No verified funding or outcome is public. Strengths are a focused crop insurance wedge and satellite expertise; risks are a thin public presence, limited insurance experience on the team and established satellite analytics vendors.

name: Verdict Machine
one_liner: AI cybersecurity for financial institutions' digital assets
long_description:
Verdict Machine uses AI to understand each financial institution's complete on-chain environment, assess its cyber risk and generate tailored controls. The same live model powers transaction prevention, continuous cyber diligence, security posture and cost-efficient wallet screening. Before execution, Verdict Machine evaluates proposed transactions against the institution's active policies.

In our first weeks, we started POCs with asset managers and digital-asset infrastructure providers whose systems move billions of dollars every week for financial institutions. We're now in active evaluations with digital-asset teams at some of the world's largest banks.

The founding team launched and led blockchain security at Check Point (NASDAQ: CHKP).
all_locations: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
regions: Israel; Middle East and North Africa
target_customer: Banks, asset managers and digital-asset infrastructure providers that hold or move on-chain assets
problem: Financial institutions moving digital assets lack a live model of their on-chain exposure, so cyber risk, vendor and protocol diligence and pre-execution transaction checks are manual or fragmented.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for risk assessment, policy generation and transaction screening, pricing not public
product_category: Blockchain security and on-chain risk platform for institutions
founder_names: Dan Danay; Isaac Grossman; Liran Kogan
competitors_at_founding: Hypernative; Blockaid; Fireblocks with Chainalysis and Elliptic
market_need_then: The July 2026 EU deadline for continuous on-chain monitoring cited by Hypernative, plus bank interest in digital assets, creates compliance demand. The company reports proofs of concept and bank evaluations, which are its own claims.
outcome_analysis: Verdict Machine is an active Summer 2026 company with no exit and no reported shutdown, so the outcome is open. Its strongest asset is founder market fit, since two founders launched blockchain security at Check Point and one founded keyTango, but incumbents already sell pre-transaction screening and funding is not publicly confirmed.

name: Verdun
one_liner: The world's most advanced security monitoring service
long_description:
Traditional security camera monitoring is vaporware. Your sites aren't actually being protected. 

A monitoring center's video alarm queue is managed by operators who are flooded by alarms during peak activity - meaning it often takes 20+ minutes for them to even see your alarm.

When you call an airline and get placed on hold for a long time only for an offshore operator to tell you he can't solve your problems, this is the security equivalent. 

We've built the world's most advanced monitoring center run by AI agents identify threatening behavior and context before escalating to our highly trained professional operators to dispatch guards and police.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Multi-site businesses with security cameras (car dealership groups, retail, truck yards) and security dealers and integrators
problem: Video alarm queues at monitoring centers are flooded at peak times, so real threats can wait 20 or more minutes before a human sees them.
business_model: Subscription monitoring service with AI triage and human operators
product_category: AI-assisted remote video monitoring
competitors_at_founding: Ambient.ai; Spot AI Remote Security Agent; Actuate
market_need_then: Verdun cites alarm queues taking 20 or more minutes at peak (company claim). The IPVM and Fondo coverage of the launch indicate trade press interest, though traction numbers were not disclosed.
outcome_analysis: Verdun is an active Fall 2026 company with no exit or shutdown reported. The CEO previously scaled Actuate and raised venture rounds in the same market, which is strong founder market fit, but Ambient.ai and Spot AI already sell comparable AI plus human monitoring and Verdun has not disclosed funding or traction.

name: Veriad
one_liner: AI operating system for advertising
long_description: Veriad is building marketing agents for enterprises to run advertising campaigns end-to-end in-house.
regions: United Kingdom; Europe
target_customer: Enterprise marketing and compliance teams that run advertising in-house
problem: Enterprises spend heavily on advertising and need each ad checked against brand and legal rules, which is slow and manual.
business_model: B2B SaaS, pricing not public
product_category: AI marketing agents and ad compliance
market_need_then: The company cites about $1T yearly ad spend and $100B wasted on non-compliant or ineffective ads (its own claim). Funded competitors in 2025 show investor demand for ad agents.
outcome_analysis: Veriad is an active Winter 2026 company with two founders, no reported exit and no confirmed funding beyond a single aggregator listing. The story is too early to classify; the main risk is that well funded ad agent startups and the ad platforms already offer end to end automation.

name: Vernius Systems, Inc.
tags: Hard Tech; Drones; Radar; Aerospace; Defense
one_liner: Mass-deployable radars for air defense
long_description:
We make mass-deployable radars for unmanned systems. Our first product is Archimedes, a radar seeker that finds and locks onto targets, enabling autonomous intercept on any drone. We have over $580M in LOIs for Archimedes, across some of the largest defense primes in Ukraine, the EU, and the Middle East.

Seekers are the most critical and costly component in every autonomous interceptor. Developing a radar seeker takes a 200+ person team at Raytheon and hundreds of millions of dollars. Archimedes is 100x cheaper than existing radar seekers on the market - and is the first product to make it feasible to deploy radars on every drone.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Defense primes, drone and interceptor makers and military units in Ukraine, the EU, the US and the Middle East
problem: Radar seekers for autonomous interceptors cost six figures per unit and take large teams to build, which makes them uneconomic against cheap drones.
business_model: Hardware sales of radar seekers and ground radars, with LOIs from defense customers
product_category: Low-cost radar seekers for counter-UAS
founder_names: Arthur Nguyen-cao; Hisham El-Halabi; Joe Gonzalez
competitors_at_founding: Cambridge Aerospace; Boeing Ultra Low-Cost Seeker
market_need_then: Shahed-class drone attacks and the US Army low-cost interceptor competition (June 2026) create demand for cheap seekers. The CEO reported $500M in non-binding LOIs and a 45-unit sale to a special forces unit, company statements not independently verified.
outcome_analysis: Vernius is an active Summer 2026 company with no exit. It reports fast field testing in Ukraine, a 45-unit sale and large LOIs, helped by wartime demand for cheap interceptors and a team with RF and defense experience, but the claims are unverified and well funded rivals and primes are building low-cost seekers.

name: Verno
one_liner: AI engineering industrials like chip fabs, refineries and power plants
long_description: Every refinery, chip fab and power plant is built from thousands of engineering documents that are supposed to agree, and engineers still keep them in sync by hand. Verno is AI for how the physical world gets built. An engineer describes a change, and Verno edits the P&ID in the native CAD file, carries the change through line lists and other downstream documents, and checks every one against engineering rules before the engineer approves it. On drawings already issued for construction, it has caught errors like one tank with three different design pressures across three documents. We're starting with process EPCs in oil and gas, chemicals, semiconductors, pharma, and food and beverage, then expanding into water and power.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: Process EPC firms and owner-operators in oil and gas, chemicals, semiconductors, pharma and food and beverage
problem: Engineering documents such as P&IDs and line lists must agree across a plant project, and engineers keep them in sync by hand, which causes errors.
business_model: B2B enterprise software, single-tenant deployment available, pricing not public
product_category: AI for engineering drawings and documents (P&ID editing and checking)
market_need_then: The company says it caught a tank with three design pressures across three documents on issued drawings. Several vendors were digitizing P&IDs in 2025 and 2026, which suggests demand.
outcome_analysis: Verno is an active Fall 2026 company that is only weeks old, with no exit, no found funding and no press. The team has relevant ML experience from Blue Origin and Asurion but no stated plant engineering background, and the outcome cannot be classified yet.

name: Versine
tags: Fintech; Consumer; Consumer Finance; Neobank; AI
one_liner: Let your agents send and receive money. We're Venmo for agents.
long_description:
Versine lets your agents send and receive money. We’re Venmo for agents.

Connect it to ChatGPT, Claude, Muse or your own agent through our MCP. Then send your agent a dinner receipt and it splits the bill. Tell it “if I don’t run 10k tomorrow, pay Jake $10” and it checks Strava and pays out if you miss. It can also pay invoices that land in your inbox, or split rent and utilities with your roommates every month. 

Recipients don’t need an account: they get a link to cash out to their bank.

Banking and payout services are provided by licensed partners.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: US consumers who use AI assistants and want them to send and receive money, plus developers
problem: AI agents cannot safely move money on a user's behalf, so tasks like splitting bills, paying invoices or conditional payouts stay manual.
business_model: Consumer payments app with partner banking, balances held as USDC; revenue model not stated
product_category: Agent-first consumer payments (MCP wallet)
founder_names: Harshith Latchupatula; Vishnudev Poil; Param Thakkar
competitors_at_founding: Coinbase x402; Stripe machine payments; Skyfire
market_need_then: Agent payment protocols from several major players in 2025 and 2026 signal demand, but consumer demand for agent-sent money is unproven. Examples on the site are splitting bills, rent and allowances.
outcome_analysis: Versine is an active Fall 2026 company with no exit and no confirmed funding. The founders have payments and infrastructure experience from Stripe, Databricks and Amazon, but Stripe, Coinbase and others already ship agent payment rails, so the outcome cannot be judged yet.

name: Vespin
one_liner: An inbox for your coding agents
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers who run several coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex
problem: People running many coding agents must watch each one for questions or handoffs; an inbox that only surfaces what needs attention reduces that load.
business_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0) app; monetization not stated
product_category: Developer tools, coding agent inbox and orchestration
market_need_then: Several orchestrator tools and roundups in 2026 show many developers running parallel coding agents. Willingness to pay is unclear because leading tools are free or open source.
outcome_analysis: Vespin is an active Spring 2026 company with no exit and no confirmed funding. It is released free and open source by the team behind Stage, so it may serve as distribution for the code review product; competition and the shutdown of Vibe Kanban suggest weak monetization, but it is too early to classify.

name: Vestris
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate
one_liner: The FICO score for homes
long_description: With the government pushing to make title insurance optional on refinances, lenders are starting to take on title risk. Vestris gives every property a risk assessment, like a credit score for homes, so lenders know what they're lending against and homeowners know where their property stands.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Title agencies and processors; homeowners preparing to sell or refinance as a direct buyer of the score
problem: Title processing is manual back-office work, and lenders taking on title risk as title insurance becomes optional on refinances lack a standard property risk assessment.
business_model: Software for title agencies plus a $200 per property Vestris Score sold to homeowners
product_category: AI title processing and property title risk scoring
market_need_then: The FHFA and Fannie Mae title waiver pilot, expanded in 2025 with a second vendor, moves title risk to lenders, which the company cites as its opening. Title insurers oppose the program, so the policy outcome is uncertain.
outcome_analysis: Vestris is an active Summer 2026 company with no exit and no confirmed funding. A regulatory shift toward optional title insurance on refinances is a tailwind and the founders have title shop exposure, but incumbent data advantages and policy uncertainty make the path unproven.

name: Vexo
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Hardware; Productivity; Conversational AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: An AI bracelet that remembers your day and acts before you ask.
long_description: Vexo is an Always listening AI bracelet. that remembers everything you say and hooks up to your existing AI agents that you can control from your wrist.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Consumers and prosumers who already use AI assistants and want hands-free capture and action from the wrist
problem: People forget what was said during the day and cannot easily hand conversation context to their AI agents. Vexo records speech and triggers actions in connected apps.
business_model: Consumer hardware sale at $199 per band, no subscription listed on the product page
product_category: AI wearable bracelet with voice memory
founder_names: Haris Malik; Farqaleet Kiani; Vikram Narra
competitors_at_founding: Sandbar Stream Ring; Bee wristband; Limitless Pendant
market_need_then: Strong investor and press attention to AI wearables in 2025 and 2026, with several funded launches. Consumer demand for always listening devices is unproven and privacy concerns are visible.
outcome_analysis: Vexo is a Fall 2026 company that has just listed a $199 AI bracelet for shipment in January 2027. It is too early to judge an outcome. The wedge is crowded and incumbents have been buying wearables rivals, so execution and distribution will decide the result.

name: Viraj Aero
one_liner: Next generation gas turbines for data centers & aviation
long_description:
Viraj Aero builds gas turbines that deliver both power and cooling water for data centers. It needs no grid connection and no water pipeline.

Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patented system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks.

We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions.

We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: Aircraft engine makers and light aviation OEMs first, then data center operators needing off grid power and cooling water
problem: Steam injection raises turbine efficiency and cuts NOx but needs water that aircraft cannot carry. Viraj recovers water from exhaust. The same loop supplies power and cooling water to data centers without a grid or water pipeline.
business_model: Engine and genset hardware sales plus development work with engine makers, not fully specified in sources
product_category: Steam injected gas turbines for aviation and onsite power
competitors_at_founding: ProEnergy PE6000; Boom Superpower turbine; FTAI Power
