name: Visibl Semiconductors
tags: Hard Tech; Enterprise; Enterprise Software; Semiconductors; AI
one_liner: Custom silicon for power electronics
long_description:
Visibl Semiconductors makes custom silicon accessible to hardware companies, starting with power electronics. We are an AI-native custom-silicon design partner that cuts ASIC development cost and timeline on mature nodes, helping teams deliver better performance and lower BOM cost.

We work with data-center and AI-infrastructure power, motor drives, industrial automation and robotics, industrial power supplies and conversion, battery systems and e-mobility powertrains, EV charging, solar, energy storage, grid power, HVAC, heat pumps, and appliances.

V1 boards built from off-the-shelf parts are great for getting to market quickly, but scaling to v2+ volume requires optimizing cost, size, and manufacturability. Visibl folds those parts into custom silicon built around the product: a simpler BOM, reclaimed board space, fewer supply constraints, and automation-ready assembly.

We manage the full path from architecture and design through verification, fabrication, packaging, and production-ready silicon, working alongside hardware teams so they do not need an in-house chip team.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware companies in EV charging, motor drives and energy storage that need custom chips without building a chip team
problem: Custom silicon is costly and slow for small hardware companies. Visibl positions as an AI native design partner that cuts ASIC cost and timeline on mature nodes, starting with power electronics.
business_model: Design services and partnership from specification to production silicon, with an AI coordination layer for chip design
product_category: AI native custom silicon design partner
market_need_then: Investors poured money into AI chip design startups in 2025 and 2026, and edge silicon interest returned per SemiEngineering. Small hardware firms still lack access to custom chips. Visibl's own demand evidence was not found.
outcome_analysis: Visibl Semiconductors is a Winter 2026 YC company with a team of three and no verified funding. The position is crowded with far better funded AI chip design startups and incumbent EDA vendors. No outcome is visible yet, and the early signals are a thin public footprint and no named customers.

name: Volaren
one_liner: The personal investing agent that comes to you
long_description:
Volaren is the personal investing agent that comes to you. It knows why your portfolio moved, suggests your next idea, and trades it for you. 

Connect your bank accounts & brokerage and Volaren tells you what changed and why, answers any question about your money, and turns any idea into a trade. You can copy the moves of famous investors, politicians, proven strategies and themed baskets in a tap, or set up your own AI agents to watch the market and act within the limits you choose. 

Everything works from the app, the web or a simple text, so managing your money feels like texting a portfolio manager who never sleeps.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Retail investors and small funds who hold brokerage and bank accounts and want an AI agent to explain and act on their portfolio
problem: Individuals find portfolios hard to monitor and trades hard to act on. Volaren connects accounts, explains why money moved, and turns ideas into trades with user approval.
business_model: Consumer subscription: free tier with 100 credits a month, paid tier at $12 per month
product_category: AI personal investing agent
competitors_at_founding: Public.com AI agents; Robinhood Cortex and agentic trading; Composer; eToro
market_need_then: Retail interest in AI trading tools rose through 2026 as brokerages shipped agents and MCP servers. The company says over 2,500 funds and retail traders use the product, which is its own claim.
outcome_analysis: Volaren launched in November 2026 with a roughly $1M raise from YC and Afore Capital. The agentic investing space was already entered by large brokerages earlier in 2026, so its edge depends on speed, cross broker aggregation and RIA status. It is too early to judge an outcome.

name: Voltair
one_liner: Autonomous Drones for Earth Observation
long_description:
Voltair is building the world's first globally distributed network of autonomous drones for Earth observation.

Power utilities are the perfect first customer. Aging infrastructure and extreme weather drive the need for millimeter-scale inspection data on the power grid. Utilities spend tens of billions of dollars every year just looking at their own equipment. Autonomous drone fleets will enable utilities to inspect 7 million miles of infrastructure more frequently, quickly, and accurately. Our long-range, weatherized flying robots work with charging pads installed directly on utility poles. Each new pad unlocks 1000 square miles of coverage.

With a charging network deployed on the power grid, we can serve existing multi-billion dollar data markets in road, rail and telecom inspection at 10x lower prices while enabling entirely new applications in hyperlocal weather monitoring, forestry, construction, search & rescue, and insurance.

We envision a future in which drone "instances" are requested on-demand through our platform, enabling any application builder to serve these critical markets without ever operating their own hardware.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Electric utilities, with road, rail and telecom inspection as later customers
problem: Utilities need frequent, high quality inspection data over large areas, and drones normally need a crew and a return trip to charge. Voltair deploys long range fixed wing drones that recharge on pads on utility poles or at substations.
business_model: Drone hardware and charging network sold to utilities, with a long term plan for on demand drone capacity for app builders
product_category: Autonomous drone network for infrastructure inspection
founder_names: Ronan Nopp; Hayden Gosch; Avi Gotskind; Warren Weissbluth
market_need_then: Utilities were adopting docked drones for substation inspection in 2025 and wildfire risk raised demand for line monitoring. Voltair's own site names no customers.
outcome_analysis: Voltair is a Winter 2026 YC company with four named founders and prototype drones. Funding is unverified and no customer is named, so traction is unclear. Docked drone vendors already sell to utilities, so its self charging network must show a clear range and cost edge to win.

name: Voquill
one_liner: The agentic OS for medical labs
long_description:
Voquill is the modern AI-native operating system for medical labs. This software manages the entire workflow of the lab (accessioning, workflow, reporting, coding, compliance, and revenue) and contains modern agentic AI tools to help each step. For example, pathologists can write reports 20% faster through our voice AI coworker.

Incumbent lab operating systems are old, don't scale with how modern labs work, and can’t integrate existing AI solutions. As a result, labs are either building their own or paying millions for band-aid solutions and consultants. We're building an agentic platform to manage every aspect of the lab and displace the billions spent on legacy management systems.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Pathology and medical laboratories, starting with pathologists who sign out cases at large reference labs
problem: Incumbent lab operating systems are old and cannot integrate modern AI, so labs build their own tools or pay for expensive consultants. Voquill sells an AI native lab operating system whose first product is voice AI for writing pathology reports.
business_model: B2B SaaS for labs; first product a voice AI coworker for pathologists, with revenue cycle management listed as coming soon
product_category: Lab information system and clinical voice AI
founder_names: Michael Gibson; Henry Habib; Josiah Saunders
market_need_then: Labs complained that legacy lab systems cannot integrate AI. Voquill reports 25 or more pathologists onboarded in about four weeks, saving roughly 20 percent of daily case writing time (company reported). Labs also face revenue leakage on coding.
outcome_analysis: Voquill is a Spring 2026 company with founders who came from Techcyte, a digital pathology vendor, which gives unusual domain access to large labs. It starts with a voice AI wedge and aims to replace the lab operating system, a very large but crowded and slow selling market. There is no outcome yet, so no failure factors are recorded.

name: Vorelios
one_liner: AI that can engineer anything
long_description: Vorelios is a research lab developing AI that understands physics and engineers autonomously, from an objective to the system that achieves it. We want to turn humanity's greatest ambitions into tractable engineering problems, accelerate the technologies that transform civilization, and discover the ones no one has imagined yet.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Engineering teams that run fluid, thermal and structural simulation for product design
problem: Physics simulation takes hours or days per design. Vorelios builds AI models that predict fluid, thermal and structural behavior of a geometry in seconds and uses them to improve designs autonomously.
business_model: Not stated on the company site; research lab positioning with no pricing or customers shown
product_category: AI physics surrogate models for engineering design
market_need_then: Engineering simulation is slow and costly, and investors funded physics AI heavily in 2025 and 2026. Vorelios shows no customer evidence on its own page.
outcome_analysis: Vorelios is a two person Fall 2026 YC lab with teenage founders from the University of Florida and no public customers or funding details. Physics AI is a hot and well funded field, so the company must show model accuracy and a first customer to compete. It is too early to judge an outcome.

name: Vorflux
tags: Developer Tools; B2B; Enterprise Software; AI
one_liner: A cloud-based AI coding agent for teams
long_description:
Vorflux is a cloud-based AI coding agent for teams that takes work from an idea, ticket, or message through planning, implementation, review, testing, and a pull request.

Its harness coordinates parallel agents, uses different models for planning and adversarial review, and retains codebase knowledge across sessions. Each team's repository and full stack run on dedicated compute, where QA agents test the application in a real browser and record video evidence.

Vorflux connects to tools such as GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Slack, Figma, and Jira, as well as cloud infrastructure and observability tools. Teams can bring their own models, with tasks routed to the best-value model. Vorflux also helps teams set up the harness and work through their first backlog.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Software engineering teams that want AI agents to take work from ticket to pull request and run recurring ops tasks
problem: Engineering teams spend time on triage, review, CI repair and routine tasks. Vorflux runs cloud AI agents, called AutoBots, that act as always on coworkers in Slack and GitHub style workflows.
business_model: SaaS with usage credits or customers' own model plans and API keys
product_category: Cloud AI coding agent and team agent platform
founder_names: Prasanna Sankar; Haritha Elango; Anant Nag
competitors_at_founding: Cursor Cloud Agents; Devin (Cognition); OpenAI Codex cloud; Tembo
market_need_then: AI coding adoption was high in 2026 and teams were moving to async cloud agents. Vorflux lists ten named customer teams on its site, as a company claim.
outcome_analysis: Vorflux raised a $15M seed in July 2026 on the strength of a founder who co-founded Rippling and two Databricks engineers, soon after the founder wound down 0xPPL in June 2026. It joined YC in Fall 2026. The agent market is crowded with model labs and well funded tools, so the outcome depends on customer traction that is not yet public.

name: Vouch
one_liner: Personal wealth manager for 100M+ Indian professionals
long_description:
Vouch is the new-age wealth manager for India’s young and ambitious professionals, with no minimums. India’s wealth industry is antiquated: great help starts at Rs 5 crore, and everyone else is left with a local agent or a trading app. Vouch’s AI agents, trained by experienced wealth managers, are filling the void: they plan your money, act on it once you approve, and keep it on track.

Indians are getting wealthier and moving that wealth into markets: $2.37 trillion in new financial wealth by 2030, and stocks and mutual funds up from 2% to 15% of household savings since 2012. At Vouch, we're starting with mutual funds before growing into the one place this burgeoning, new India manages its money.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: Salaried professionals in India who hold mutual funds and want an AI wealth manager
problem: Indian investors hold mutual funds without ongoing checks on whether they are on track. Vouch reads holdings through MF Central, monitors daily, flags issues and proposes changes that need the user's approval.
business_model: Licensed mutual fund distributor earning from fund houses, with a planned fee based investment adviser registration
product_category: AI personal wealth manager for India
competitors_at_founding: Wealthy.in; TIFIN MyFi; PowerUp Money; 5paisa AI mutual fund platform
market_need_then: India's mutual fund industry assets were Rs 82.64 lakh crore at the end of September 2026 per AMFI via a press report, and AI wealth tools were being funded and launched. Vouch shows no customer count.
outcome_analysis: Vouch is a Fall 2026 YC company with a solo founder who has Jane Street and Robinhood experience and is preparing an app launch in India subject to licensing. The market is attracting well funded rivals and fund house tools. It is too early to judge an outcome.

name: Voxel Energy
tags: Hardware; Solar Power; Energy; Renewable Energy; AI
one_liner: Energy independent data centers with solar and repurposed batteries.
long_description:
The best grid connection is no grid connection. Voxel builds vertically integrated energy generation and storage systems for data centers that bypass utility connection delays. 

By leveraging the vast supply of second-life EV batteries and our novel DC microgrid architecture, Voxel generates datacenter power on site and drastically reduces system cost and time-to-power.
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: Data center developers and AI compute operators that cannot wait for utility grid interconnection
problem: Utility connection delays of years block new data centers. Voxel sells prefabricated on-site solar and storage power systems that avoid the grid.
business_model: Vertically integrated energy systems and modular off-grid data center power, sold per project
product_category: Off-grid power systems for data centers (solar plus second-life EV battery storage)
founder_names: Casey Spencer; Max Pfeiffer; Evan Schmidt
market_need_then: AI data center demand outpaced grid interconnection in 2025, and the company cites utility delays as the bottleneck.
outcome_analysis: Voxel is an early stage company still pre-commercial as of late 2026. It rides the AI data center power shortage and has founders with Tesla, EV and data center construction backgrounds. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found. Public evidence of customers or deployed projects is missing, and a similar solar plus second-life battery system already existed from Crusoe and Redwood.

name: Voyager
one_liner: Open harness for video and other creative work.
long_description:
Most AI tools are built for coding. Voyager is designed to get the best creative results from models like Opus, Astra and DeepSeek.

It comes bundled with free motion graphics, music and video editing tools - or, it can drive Blender, DaVinci Resolve, After Effects, Ableton and 100+ others.

From the team behind Moda (moda.app, 100k+ users).
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Video editors, motion designers, musicians and creative professionals who want AI agents to drive their creative tools
problem: Most AI agents target coding. Creative work spans many apps and models, and Voyager gives agents one harness to control them.
business_model: Freemium desktop app with monthly credits, or bring your own Claude or ChatGPT account
product_category: Desktop AI agent harness for creative work
founder_names: John Holliman; Anvisha Pai; Ravi Parikh
market_need_then: Agentic tools were booming in coding in 2026 and a16z published on agentic video editing; creative professionals had no equivalent harness.
outcome_analysis: Voyager is a Fall 2026 company from repeat founders behind Moda and Dover, launched as a desktop app in October 2026. It is too new for an outcome. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. The main risk is that creative app vendors build native agent control, as DaVinci Resolve did in 2026.

name: Vyra
one_liner: Personal video editing agent for shortform content
long_description: Instead of making users learn a timeline, we let them upload footage, describe what they want, and get back a polished edit in minutes.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Short-form creators, UGC teams and non-editors who want edited video without learning a timeline
problem: Editing short-form video on a timeline is slow. Vyra turns raw footage and a text prompt into a finished edit.
business_model: Subscription, $24 to $129 per month, with credits and a free trial
product_category: AI video editing agent
competitors_at_founding: Adobe Quick Cut; Overlap AI; AI Video Cut
market_need_then: Short-form video demand is high and editing is a bottleneck; the YC page claims over 40M views on Vyra-edited content.
outcome_analysis: Vyra is a two person Fall 2026 company with founders who edit video and have an audience. It is too new for an outcome. No shutdown or acquisition news was found. It faces a crowded field of agent editors and incumbents shipping similar features, so its edge depends on creator distribution.

name: Waddle Labs

target_customer: Robotics teams and developers who want to program robot arms with natural language prompts

product_category: LLM agent API for robot control code

name: Wakeshift
one_liner: The Wake-up Call for AI Agents
long_description: Wakeshift gives MCP servers real-time events that wake up agents in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, without polling or harness-specific code. You add the SDK once. Wakeshift handles every harness.

market_need_then: Open Claude Code issues in 2026 request external wake signals and push notifications from MCP servers, and an MCP Triggers and Events working group was chartered in March 2026, showing real demand.
outcome_analysis: Wakeshift is a Spring 2026 YC company from a repeat founder with a prior acquisition. It is too new for an outcome. The main risk visible in sources is that MCP Events standards and agent harness vendors may provide the wake feature natively.

name: Walter
one_liner: AI Employee for Manufacturing Operations
long_description: Walter is an AI employee for manufacturing operations.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Packaging and industrial manufacturers running SAP, Dynamics 365 or Oracle ERP
problem: Manufacturing back offices spend hours entering purchase orders, ordering from suppliers and catching pricing errors by hand. Walter does this as an AI employee inside the ERP, email and Teams.
business_model: B2B software subscription, demo led sales
product_category: AI document and order automation for manufacturing operations

name: Wato
one_liner: The control point for AI agents at work.
long_description: Wato gives AI agents shared memory, reusable workflows, connected tools, and living artifacts so work compounds across a team instead of disappearing into chat threads. Teams use Wato to give every agent access to trusted company context and turn useful runs into knowledge the next agent can build on.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Companies whose teams use AI agents and need shared memory, permissions and audit across them
problem: Work done with AI agents stays trapped in individual chats. Wato gives agents shared team memory, reusable workflows, approved tools and traceable cloud sessions.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (pricing not disclosed on the pages opened)
product_category: Shared AI agent workspace and control layer
competitors_at_founding: Basic Memory Teams; Claude and ChatGPT team plans
market_need_then: Companies adopting coding and work agents in 2026 needed governance, shared context and audit logs; evidence is the product positioning, not measured demand.
outcome_analysis: Wato is a two person Spring 2026 company building a shared workspace for AI agents. It is too new for an outcome and no shutdown or acquisition news was found. The main risk is that model vendors and memory tools ship the same shared memory and governance features.

name: Waybill
one_liner: Agentic procurement & inventory for deep tech teams.
long_description:
Hardware teams burn weeks on procurement. An engineer needs a part. Someone emails five distributors, chases quotes, gets an approval, wires the money, tracks a shipment across three carriers, clears customs, and then nobody knows where the box is or what's actually on the shelf.

Waybill runs that entire loop. Send us a part, a spec, or a BOM. We source it, pull quotes, route approvals, pay the supplier, handle freight and customs, track it to your dock, and keep your stock count updated. 

Take your supply chain for granted.

Built by a team that's seen it at LAT Aerospace and WareIQ (YC S20).
regions: India; South Asia
target_customer: Deep tech and hardware teams that buy parts and components, including across borders
problem: Hardware procurement means chasing suppliers, quotes, freight, customs and inventory by hand. Waybill runs it from request to stock under one approval and one payment.
business_model: Managed procurement service, likely a margin or fee on orders (not stated on the pages opened)
product_category: Agentic procurement and inventory for hardware
market_need_then: Hardware teams, especially in India, lose time to fragmented procurement and import paperwork; the company page claims end to end handling, evidence of demand is not independently shown.
outcome_analysis: Waybill is a three person Summer 2026 company from Bengaluru automating hardware procurement. Founders have operations and supply chain backgrounds from LAT Aerospace and WareIQ. It is too new for an outcome and no shutdown or acquisition news was found. Funded rivals such as Cofactr and Reframe make execution and supplier access the key variables.

name: Wayco
one_liner: AI operator for medlegal cases
long_description: Wayco is building a unified data intelligence layer for medical treatment of legal cases. From the first intake to instant settlement.

problem: Injury claim intake, medical record gathering and attorney matching are slow and costly. Wayco runs 24/7 AI intake and builds the case file from first call to settlement.
business_model: Lead and case referral to partner law firms (participating attorneys pay), plus AI intake for firms
product_category: AI operator for medical legal cases and legal intake
market_need_then: Intake and client acquisition costs in personal injury law are high; the founder pitch targets 24/7 intake in English and Spanish. Direct demand evidence beyond the pitch was not found.
outcome_analysis: Wayco is a five person Winter 2026 company founded by a 19 year old solo founder that raised a pre-seed in January 2026 per press. It is too early for an outcome and no shutdown or acquisition news was found. Legal advertising rules, attorney supply and better funded rivals such as Supio are the main risks.

name: Wealor
one_liner: AI-native platform for wealth managers
regions: France; Europe
target_customer: Registered investment advisers, multi-family offices, trust companies and tax and estate planning firms
problem: Wealth managers keep client data scattered across conversations, financial documents, tax and legal records and custodial systems, so operational work is manual.

product_category: AI operations platform for wealth management
market_need_then: Wealth firms were adopting AI heavily in 2026, with multiple platforms and Anthropic announcing RIA focused AI products, which signals spend and demand.

name: Whitespace
one_liner: AI Operating System for Wholesale Distribution
long_description:
Whitespace builds AI agents that run the entire operation of supply chain businesses, starting with wholesale distributors. We give them self-improving AI agents that learn their business and do work like inventory planning and customer service.

We're building towards a world where all supply chain operations run through our agents, and all physical goods purchases can happen across businesses without human touch.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Wholesale distributors, starting with industrial, building materials and textile distributors
problem: Distributors run inventory planning, purchasing and customer service by hand across ERPs and inboxes.
business_model: B2B SaaS for distributors, sits on top of the existing ERP
product_category: AI agents for supply chain operations
market_need_then: Distribution industry research cited by Modern Distribution Management shows 400 plus distributors investing in AI, indicating demand.
outcome_analysis: Whitespace is an early Summer 2026 company selling AI inventory planning to wholesale distributors. Two named customers appear on its site and a third party reports ARR growth during the batch, but there is no verified funding or exit. Differentiation against established planning vendors adding AI will decide the outcome, and the founders have supply chain and AI backgrounds.

name: Wideframe
one_liner: AI coworker for video editors to ship more video faster
long_description:
Wideframe is an AI coworker for video editors. It automates the searching, labeling, organizing, and sequencing of footage so editors can ship videos faster.

Why is this important? Well, it turns out that editors spend 3x more time preparing footage than actually editing.

One agency said we will save their editors 10 hours per week. Another organized an entire documentary worth of footage in hours rather than weeks. He had 2,500+ videos, 500+ audio clips, across >2.5 TB of files and our agent handled them effortlessly.

Users link footage to Wideframe and then our Agent acts like an Assistant Editor to handle work like searching, labeling, organizing, and sequencing footage. Wideframe works with footage across local filesystems and cloud providers. We also supports Adobe Premiere Pro (.prproj) roundtrip. Our robust integrations are important so that Wideframe can work with source footage all the way through to delivering Premiere Pro projects to editors.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Professional video editors, agencies and post production teams using Adobe Premiere Pro
problem: Editors spend far more time preparing footage than editing it.
business_model: Subscription, $100 per month with team pricing
product_category: AI assistant editor for footage prep
market_need_then: Company says editors spend about three times longer on preparation than editing, and an agency reported saving about 10 hours weekly (company claims, not independent).
outcome_analysis: Wideframe is a Winter 2026 company building an AI assistant editor for footage preparation with a paid Mac app. Early traction signals include a Product Hunt launch and named testimonials, but funding is unverified and there is no exit. Competition from other AI editors is dense, and the paid only model targets professionals.

name: Wingman Law
one_liner: AI-native personal injury law firm
long_description: Wingman Law is an AI-native personal injury law firm. Attorneys lead a team of AI agents to recover compensation for people injured in accidents. We are solving the human bottle neck in personal injury.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Bay Area people injured in accidents, who pay on contingency
problem: Injury victims face low insurer offers and slow, labor heavy casework.
business_model: Contingency fee personal injury law firm run by attorneys directing AI agents
product_category: AI native law firm
market_need_then: Large personal injury market; tool vendors raised large rounds in 2025 and 2026, showing demand for AI in the field.
outcome_analysis: Wingman Law is a Fall 2026 AI native personal injury firm with a lawyer led founding team. No funding or case results are public, and a trade article notes no published outcome data. The model competes for cases against established firms and depends on legal marketing and operations more than software.

name: WonderTx
tags: AI-powered Drug Discovery; Generative AI; Biotech
one_liner: Extrapolative AI to unlock First-in-Class drugs
long_description:
We’re an AI-native biotech, working on replacing needles with pills. Many drugs, like insulin or Ozempic, are wonderful except you have to inject them. We discover new molecules that you can take as a pill instead. Because the pills operate on biology which has been shown to be effective in people, rather than merely in animal models of disease, we avoid what has historically been the single biggest risk in drug discovery.  This should dramatically increase our probability of success.

There’s $200B of treatable diseases and validated human biology without a pill because discovery programs lack a tractable chemical starting point. This is a zero-shot inference problem, because these targets have no training data, so LLMs and other historical interpolative AI approaches are insufficient. Instead, we are building our own extrapolative frontier models that reason beyond their training data. Most critically, we have repeatedly validated our platform on both our own and partner programs. On 4 biologically- and structurally-diverse targets where we had zero training data, we successfully picked binders that were validated experimentally, with confirmation ranging from primary screen hits to crystallographic structures.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Fully Remote
target_customer: Pharma partners and eventually patients, via oral small molecule drugs
problem: Many disease targets lack a chemical starting point, so drugs for them are injectables or do not exist.
business_model: Drug discovery biotech (internal pipeline, likely partnerships)
product_category: AI native biotech
market_need_then: Company reports experimentally validated binders on 4 targets with no training data (own claim).
outcome_analysis: WonderTx is a Summer 2026 AI biotech led by an Atomwise co-founder. Only company claims about validated binders exist, with no verified funding or exit. Drug discovery timelines are long, so success depends on capital access, which a founder track record can help.

name: Wondering
tags: AI-Enhanced Learning; Education; Consumer; AI; AI Assistant
one_liner: Duolingo for learning anything
long_description:
Wondering turns anything you want to learn, from LLMs to quantum mechanics to product design, into a path of three-minute lessons with visuals, podcasts, and interactive exercises.

name: ZeroSettle
one_liner: iMessage API for businesses and AI agents
long_description:
ZeroSettle is an iMessage API. Each customer gets a dedicated phone number that sends and receives real iMessages from their own code or AI agent. Plans start at $49/month.

Developers send and receive messages through a REST API and webhooks. AI agents connect through our MCP server, which works with Claude, ChatGPT, Grok and Cursor. name: herdr
one_liner: building the open agent runtime
long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.

product_category: Agent runtime and terminal multiplexer for coding agents

Horizontal connects the people, software and machines that run production.

Agent workloads are moving from ephemeral to always-on. A coding agent working on a hard feature runs 6-8 hours. Auto-research agents run for days. machine0 is the environment in which these agents run.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Developers and teams running long-lived coding or research agents that need persistent cloud VMs, including GPU machines
problem: Agents running for hours or days need full persistent machines they can create and manage themselves, which hyperscaler consoles and ephemeral sandboxes serve poorly.
business_model: usage-based per-minute VM billing with prepaid credits
product_category: cloud compute for AI agents
competitors_at_founding: Fly.io Sprites; E2B; Modal; Daytona and Freestyle
market_need_then: Agent workloads were moving from ephemeral to long running per the company, and a crowded set of sandbox vendors in 2026 shows active demand. Its Launch HN post exists but traction figures were not found.
outcome_analysis: machine0 is a Summer 2026 solo-founder company with no outcome yet. It targets persistent agent compute in a market with funded sandbox vendors and hyperscalers moving in, so differentiation and distribution are the open questions. The founder has prior YC and infrastructure experience per the YC page.

name: o11
tags: Developer Tools; Fintech; SaaS; B2B; AI
one_liner: OpenRouter wallet for paid goods and services
long_description:
o11 helps your AI agents access apis, tools, and other paid goods and services. Instead of hacky computer use, managing credit card permissions, assigning each agent a new email, we handle all the hard parts of accessing the paid web. o11 has zero markup and gives teams better prices, easy checkout, and full auditability when purchasing with AI agents. 

The o11 wallet gives your AI agents access to the paid world.

target_customer: Teams and developers whose AI agents need to buy APIs, tools and other paid services with spending controls and audit trails

product_category: agentic commerce wallet

outcome_analysis: o11 is an active Winter 2026 company that moved from a finance-focused office-app agent to an agent payments wallet. It has no exit and no verified round. The site lists notable backers, and the wedge faces large players such as Stripe that entered in 2026. Outcome is not yet determinable.

name: primitive

name: rekursiv.ai
one_liner: Scale AI scientists whose own breakthroughs accelerate the next.
long_description:
We're scaling self-improving AI scientist teams to ideate/experiment/discover, generating new knowledge autonomously. Their discoveries reduced ARC-1/2 costs by 10,000× while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy and yielded material advances on combinatorial ML problems.

We believe that AI is bounded not by compute, but ideas. Scaling to millions of sessions of discovery enables leveraging its own discoveries and presents a novel training source capable of ushering a new era of self-reliant foundational models.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada; Remote; Partly Remote
target_customer: AI labs and research teams that want autonomous AI scientist teams to work on benchmark and research problems as a service
problem: Progress in AI is limited by the supply of good research ideas and experiments; the company wants fleets of AI scientists to generate and test them at scale.
business_model: access to AI scientist teams as a service (third-party profile; not confirmed by the company)
product_category: autonomous AI research systems
competitors_at_founding: Periodic Labs; Sakana AI (The AI Scientist); FutureHouse and Edison Scientific
market_need_then: AI labs were investing heavily in AI scientists in 2025 and 2026, with large rounds at Periodic Labs and others, but paying customers for a third-party service are unproven.
outcome_analysis: rekursiv.ai is a Summer 2026 company with strong research founders per the YC page and ambitious but self-reported benchmark claims. It has no exit and no verified funding round. Its outcome depends on turning AI scientist output into paid demand against frontier labs and well-funded rivals.

name: screenpipe

long_description: Screenpipe records and learns how people in your company work and turns it into a searchable memory, documents, and AI agents. Model agnostic and data is stored on your device and/or where your team choose, source available.

name: shortkit
one_liner: Media infra for consumer apps
long_description:
ShortKit lets any consumer app launch a TikTok-grade media expereinces. 

Michael, spent 6 years at YouTube building the infrastructure that powers YouTube Shorts. Neil, prev. scaled a SaaS company from 0 to $6M ARR as employee #1. 

We handle the full media stack, starting with short form video - client SDKs, video infrastructure, rec systems, and monetization - so product teams don't have to.

target_customer: Media publishers and consumer app companies that want TikTok style short video inside their own apps
problem: Building vertical video feeds with smooth playback, recommendations and ads takes a dedicated video engineering team. ShortKit offers SDKs and managed infrastructure.

product_category: Short-form video SDK and infrastructure
market_need_then: Publishers such as news and sports brands want short video in their own properties. Evidence is the company's own pitch; no independent demand data was found.
outcome_analysis: ShortKit is a two person Winter 2026 company. No verified funding, customer or revenue figures exist, so the outcome is open. Its main asset is a founder with Shorts infrastructure experience, set against a technically heavy product and well resourced video infrastructure vendors.

name: shotwell.ai
one_liner: Annotations for robotics data
long_description: Shotwell AI is building the data QA layer for dexterous robotics. We work with teams collecting teleoperation and egocentric data to provide dense semantic annotation and validate task adherence. This lets teams compress feedback loops from weeks to hours and iterate on models much faster.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Robotics labs, deployment companies and data vendors that collect teleoperation and egocentric data

name: smol machines
one_liner: Ship software faster with portable, self contained virtual machines.
long_description:
Smol machines solve the problem of "but app works on my machine" by shipping the machine.

Smol machine enables devs to ship a lightweight virtual machine with any software, similar to how Electron ships an entire browser with the web app.

target_customer: Developers and agent builders who run untrusted or model-generated code, or ship software with its environment, and want isolated microVMs

name: tash

long_description:
tash is building the investment platform for sports and trading cards. We create professionally constructed portfolios of iconic, investment-grade cards, giving investors exposure to the asset class without the hassle of selecting, buying, storing, and selling individual cards.

Trading card investing remains fragmented, opaque, and difficult to access. tash is building the infrastructure to make the asset class simpler, more transparent, and professionally managed. We are currently pursuing SEC qualification to launch regulated investment offerings backed by trading cards.

It has four founders with finance backgrounds, and its path depends on SEC Regulation A qualification and broker-dealer partners. name: tday.com
one_liner: AI that turns your product into on-brand marketing content
long_description: tday automatically turns a software company's product into on-brand marketing creative. Connect your product and git repo, and tday generates polished launch videos, social graphics, and ads, the content a team would normally spend hours making in a design tool or pay a freelancer for. tday then publishes the creative and measures how it performs across your social and ad channels, closing the loop from what you ship to what you post.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada

problem: Small software teams spend hours in design tools or pay freelancers for marketing content for each release.

The outcome is unknown; crowded demo-video tools and thin defensibility are the visible risks, while the founders' repeated founder experience is the visible strength.

name: transload
one_liner: Measure freight with security cameras
long_description:
transload helps logistics companies measure shipments using the security cameras they already have. A pallet, a couch, a tire – we capture its true size as it moves through the warehouse.

For our customers, 15% of shipments turn out to be bigger than what the sender claimed. Catching those differences is worth ~$50k per site per month in rebillings and improved trailer utilization.
regions: Germany; Europe
target_customer: LTL trucking carriers and cross-docking warehouse operators that bill by freight dimensions
problem: Shipment dimensions declared by senders are often wrong, so carriers lose revenue in rebillings and trailer space. Dedicated dimensioning stations are costly and slow the dock workflow.
business_model: B2B software per site using existing CCTV cameras (pricing not stated in sources)
product_category: Computer vision freight dimensioning
founder_names: Julius Scheel; Nils Boerner; Jago Wahl-Schwentker
competitors_at_founding: CubiScan dock dimensioners; Mettler Toledo laser dimensioning; vMeasure
market_need_then: NMFTA moved LTL classification to a density based system on 2025-07-19, making accurate dimensions more valuable. Founders spoke to over 50 trucking companies and one customer found dimension errors in about 10% of checked shipments (company stated).
outcome_analysis: transload is a Spring 2026 YC company that is active. A founder with family access to LTL trucking and a computer vision team pivoted from forklift routing to dimensioning after customer interviews. No verified funding or exit exists, and NTEP certification is still pending, so no outcome can be assigned yet.

name: twentyfour26
tags: Hard Tech; Hardware; Manufacturing; AI; Industrial
one_liner: Building Autonomous Factories in America, Starting with On-Demand CNC…
long_description:
At twentyfour26, we are developing standardized manufacturing cells that bring machines, tooling, workholding, and inspection under a single system. Our models are being developed to interpret CAD designs, plan machining strategies, select tooling and setups, and operate the machines.

We're already manufacturing components for hardware companies in and around the Bay Area, with turnaround times as fast as ~48 hours. Operating our own machines allows us to develop and deploy automation against real production workloads.

Our goal is to make manufacturing 100 different designs as easy as manufacturing 100 units of the same design.

From individual components to complete assemblies, we want to abstract the entire manufacturing infrastructure into an API.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Hardware companies in the San Francisco Bay Area that need small batches of machined parts quickly
problem: Prototype and low volume CNC parts take long to quote and make, and each new design needs manual setup.
business_model: On-demand CNC parts service with instant software quoting, aiming to become manufacturing as an API
product_category: AI enabled on-demand CNC manufacturing
market_need_then: Hardware startups need fast machined parts. The company says it already makes parts for Bay Area hardware firms with turnaround near 48 hours.
outcome_analysis: twentyfour26 is a Fall 2026 YC company with two founders and an operating shop, so it is far too early for an outcome. Competition from funded AI manufacturing firms is heavy, and the pivot from software to a shop is a capital intensive path.

name: Asterline

long_description: Asterline is a quantitative trading firm that builds automated systems to exploit pricing inefficiencies in prediction markets. We built proprietary backtesting infrastructure to rapidly discover, validate, and deploy new strategies at scale.

name: Colony
one_liner: Long-range drone network for world data collection
regions: Canada; America / Canada
target_customer: Operators of pipelines, power transmission lines, highways, rail and construction sites that need geospatial survey data
problem: Collecting survey and inspection data over long linear assets is slow and costly with crewed aircraft and short range drones. Colony builds long range autonomous VTOL aircraft that collect geospatial data at scale.

product_category: Long range autonomous drones for geospatial data
founder_names: Rad El Gharbi; Igor Martins; Adam Walker

name: DataNode

long_description: DataNode is building the structuring data layer for event risk. Our engine combines prediction markets with traditional derivatives to quantify and risk assess any event exposure and build a priced, tailored hedge, even before a market for it exists.

name: LinkLane

Anyone can get a quote and book instantly, while our AI agents find the carrier, negotiate the rate, and manage every load from pickup to delivery. Trucking is a nearly $1 trillion market still run by call centers of brokers working the phones. We're bringing the Amazon experience to freight, making shipping cheaper and easier for every business.

name: Lucebox
one_liner: Self-improving inference workstation
long_description: Lucebox makes workstations for local AI inference. They're private, always-on machines that arrive with Lucebox's inference engine installed and tuned, so developers point Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode on their own hardware. Lucebox is building toward a new category of self-improving personal AI computers that learn from the work you do every day, training small models on your own context until they're faster and better than the cloud at your tasks. The engine is open source, with 2.9K stars on GitHub and 95K+ downloads on Hugging Face.
regions: Italy; Europe
target_customer: Developers and small teams who want to run coding agents and open models locally for privacy and without per-token fees

product_category: Local AI inference workstation and open source inference engine
competitors_at_founding: NVIDIA DGX Spark; Framework Desktop and other Strix Halo mini PCs
market_need_then: Open models improved and Strix Halo class hardware made local inference practical in 2025 and 2026. Lucebox cites 2.9K GitHub stars and 95K+ Hugging Face downloads as demand signals (YC page, self-reported). Memory price increases raised hardware costs in 2026.
outcome_analysis: Lucebox is a Winter 2027 hardware and open source company with a two person team that opened direct orders for its Zero 495 workstation in September 2026. Its open source traction and AMD partnership are early positives, but the hardware is commodity and NVIDIA and mini PC makers compete, so the outcome is not yet known.

name: Memorable

It targets a clear and growing pain, the cost of agents re-planning tasks, with early design partners, but competes with funded memory startups and with agent platforms that can ship the same feature.

name: Render
one_liner: AI CMO that puts marketing on autopilot
long_description:
Render is an AI CMO that runs a business's marketing on autopilot.

We're at $1.7M ARR, growing 100% month over month, with 1,000+ paying businesses.

Render makes the ads, launches the campaigns, and improves them every day. It covers Meta, Google and YouTube ads, cold email, direct mail, and TV commercials. Most small businesses can't afford a marketing team, and agencies charge thousands a month to run one or two channels. Render runs all of them for a fraction of the price. Owners connect their accounts and set a budget, and Render does the rest.

It sells into a crowded AI small business marketing field, and no funding or exit news was found, so the outcome is open.

name: Rote
one_liner: AI-native insurance department for auto body shops
long_description: Rote handles the entire negotiation lifecycle between shops and insurance companies to help them recover thousands of dollars in denied claims. Shops today lose millions per year because they lack the resources to negotiate with insurance companies that undervalue repair costs. Rote's agents recover denied revenue by taking shop estimates and referencing technical repair data to autonomously file and defend shop claims.
regions: United States of America; America / Canada
target_customer: Independent and small auto body and collision repair shops
problem: Shops lose large sums to denied or undervalued insurance claims because they lack staff and technical repair data to negotiate with insurers.
business_model: Likely a fee or share of recovered claim revenue, not published
product_category: AI agents for insurance claim negotiation in collision repair
market_need_then: Trade press in 2025 and 2026 covers AI adoption in body shops and shop concerns about insurer payments; the company states shops lose millions per year to underpaid claims (self-reported).
outcome_analysis: Rote is a Winter 2027 company founded by two Cornell students with Apple and Toyota experience, selling AI negotiation of denied claims to body shops. There is no public funding or traction data, and the estimating incumbents may add similar features, so any outcome is unknown at this stage.

name: Tesser
one_liner: Seamless cloud dev environments
long_description:
Tesser is a cloud development runtime that lets developers run multiple dev environments in parallel without overloading their laptops.

Our CLI moves workloads like servers, builds, tests, and typechecking to isolated cloud machines while developers continue using their existing editors and coding agents. Tesser handles provisioning, networking, and port forwarding. Teams can access each other's environments through our gateway, share live previews, and run Tesser on our infrastructure or their own cloud (BYOC).
regions: Unspecified
target_customer: Software developers and teams running coding agents in parallel
problem: Running several dev environments or agent worktrees in parallel overloads laptops and collides on ports.
business_model: Developer tool / cloud runtime, hosted or bring-your-own-cloud (pricing not found)
product_category: Cloud development runtime
market_need_then: Parallel coding agents increase local resource contention; no dated demand evidence beyond the founders' pitch was found.
outcome_analysis: Tesser is a Winter 2027 company, so no outcome exists. It sells a CLI that moves dev servers, builds and tests to isolated cloud machines. The founders have startup and developer-tool experience, but the category is crowded and no traction or funding is public.

name: Vibe Robotics
one_liner: Robotics workforce for hotels
long_description:
Vibe Robotics builds robots for the work nobody should have to repeat.

We’re starting in hotels. Every day, housekeeping teams move linens between floors, restock carts, and fold stacks of laundry before the next guests arrive. It’s physical work that has to get done every shift.

Our first robot, Vibe 01, folds a hand towel fully autonomously in 23.8 seconds. It learned from just a few hundred human demonstrations. We’re piloting Vibe 01 at a Hilton property and working with hotels under the Marriott, Hilton, and IHG brands to bring it to more locations.
